     VTA's own DID: 0.2 declares no code for "a create cannot re-identify
     this node", and its serviceDidNotPermitted now means only the switch,

  3. An unresolved placeholder is reported in templateVarsInvalid's

  5. Setup's own key-role identity is recorded as class service; the service

title: vti-trust-task-server-v0.10.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-sdk**: ResolvedMethods declarations and the VTI-KEY-009 refusals ([#2672](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2672))

* feat(vta-sdk): resolvedMethods declarations and the VTI-KEY-009 refusals

  The VTI specification now admits did:webs as an optional, alpha method
  for a node's durable identity (dtgwg-vti-spec#121). A node acts as an
  identity of an optional method only toward a peer whose verified current
  DID document declares it resolves that method, in a top-level
  resolvedMethods member (VTI-KEY-008); otherwise it sends nothing and
  fails with methodNotDeclared. A party that cannot rely on material
  without resolving a method it does not resolve refuses it with
  unsupportedDidMethod (VTI-KEY-009).

  - vta_sdk::resolved_methods: the required methods, what this build
    resolves and declares, the lenient reader of a peer's declaration,
    require_declared (the sending-side rule) and declare (with the JSON-LD
    term VTI-KEY-008 fixes).
  - The VTA declares did:webs in every document it mints, and so do the
    built-in templates for the nodes this workspace runs (vtc-host,
    room-host, dtg-witness, ballot-box). Templates for software outside it
    declare nothing.
  - Receive side: a proof by a DID of a method this party does not resolve
    is refused as DiProofError::UnsupportedDidMethod before any resolver is
    asked, and answered proofInvalid with details.reason
    unsupportedDidMethod and the method (the VTA, the shared Trust Task
    spine, the VTC).
  - Typed errors end to end: AppError::{MethodNotDeclared,
    UnsupportedDidMethod}, VtaError::{MethodNotDeclared,
    UnsupportedDidMethod}, read back from a Trust Task rejection and a REST
    body. The spine's app_error_to_reject also gains the NoMatchingProtocol
    arm it lacked (it answered internalError).

  Not breaking: DiProofError, AppError and VtaError are non_exhaustive.
  The documents the VTA mints and the four templates gain resolvedMethods
  and a further @context entry, which a DID-document consumer ignores.

  The sending-side check at the outbound seams follows separately; no
  node's own identity can be did:webs yet.



### Fixed

- **vta**: A did:webs node acts toward any peer; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008) ([#2697](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2697))

* fix(vta,vtc)!: a did:webs node acts toward any peer; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008)

  Each party chooses its own identity method and still works with every
  other: a did:webs client talks to a did:webvh service, and a did:webs
  node reaches any peer. dtgwg-vti-spec#123 makes did:webs a required
  method every node resolves, with the key-role designation extension
  (VTI-KEY-003); a node never requires a peer to use a particular durable
  method (VTI-KEY-001); VTI-KEY-008, the resolvedMethods declaration gate,
  is withdrawn with its methodNotDeclared refusal; VTI-KEY-009 keeps only
  the receiving side.

- **vtc-service**: Keep no copy of a token-bearing response for redelivery ([#2677](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2677))

The Trust Task spine records each successful response so that a redelivery
  of the same document `id` gets the first result back. Responses carrying a
  bearer secret are left out of that record. That list had invite claim codes,
  invitations and the event-stream grant, but not session tokens. So a
  redelivered `auth/authenticate/0.3` or `auth/refresh/0.2` got the recorded
  tokens back without the handler running: no single-use challenge check, no
  refresh rotation or reuse detection, no audit row. The tokens also stayed in
  the record for the acceptance window.

  Now also unrecorded (a redelivery is answered `204`):
  - `auth/authenticate/0.3`, `auth/refresh/0.2` (access and refresh tokens)
  - `vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3`, `vtc/install/claim/passkey/finish/0.1`
    (setup session token)
  - `vtc/auth/recognise/0.3` (cross-community access token)
  - `backup/initiate-export/0.1`, `backup/initiate-import/0.1` (transport token)

### Added

- **vtc**: A VTC can take a level-1 did:webs as its own DID ([#2698](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2698))

* feat(vta-sdk): vtc-host-classical, the VTC template a level-1 did:webs can carry

  A level-1 did:webs holds one key-state signing key, and CONVENTIONS.md 0.2
  §9.2 refuses vtc-host's second (post-quantum) signing slot as keyAlgorithm and
  forbids a VTA to drop what a template describes; the template keys block has no
  optional slot (vta/did-templates/* 3.1). So a did:webs VTC (VTI-KEY-001) names a
  template that does not ask for the key: vtc-host-classical, vtc-host less the
  pq-signing slot, its verification method and its assertionMethod reference.

  two cannot drift (pinned by a test rendering both). The §9.2 check is
  unchanged: vtc-host stays refused, every other refusal stands.

  service supplied whole as a variable (SERVICE_TSP, SERVICE_DIDCOMM) keeps the
  placeholder, because a whole-value substitution is not substituted again, and
  was refused under did:webs as "not a fragment".

title: vti-voting-v0.17.0
body:
### Fixed

- **voting-service**: Resolve a signer on the HTTPS door only where the box knows it ([#2676](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2676))

The HTTPS binding proves no sender, and verifying a request's proof resolves
  the DID its verification method names. Only casts were held to a did:key, so
  a signed read or trustee step could name any DID and have the box fetch it,
  per request.

  - The proof's verification method must be the issuer's before anything is
    resolved (it was compared after verifying).
  - A did:key or did:peer signer resolves with no I/O, on any binding.
  - Any other signer is resolved on the HTTPS door only when `[communities]
    allowed` names it, or the election the request names, held here, lists it
    as its community, an auditor or a trustee. Otherwise `permissionDenied`,
    before any fetch. TSP and DIDComm are unchanged: the transport proved the
    sender, which must be the issuer.
  - A community's or a trustee's request (register, close, cancel, trustee
    steps, authorize) is refused `expired` once older than the VTI acceptance
    window (VTI-OPS-024: ten minutes plus a minute's skew). Casts keep their
    current rule.

  beside the versions already pinned.

  Hosts (room-host and the VTC, through vti_rooms): rooms/records/list/0.7 is
  served beside 0.5 and 0.6. `order: newestFirst` returns rows in descending
  version, each cursor continuing downward; `sinceVersion` stays a lower bound,
  tombstones and `lastPrune` are as oldest first, and the commitment, count and
  head are over the whole room. A cursor is bound to its order (`v<N>` oldest
  first, `n<N>` newest first) and refused with the declared `invalidCursor`
  under the other (Order item 5). `vti_rooms::storage::list_records_page_in`
  takes a `RecordOrder`; `list_records_page` is unchanged (oldest first).
  Records are keyed by key, not version, so both orders sort the room in memory,
  which is no more than every page already pays for its uncached whole-room
  commitment; a version index belongs with a cached commitment.

title: vti-common-v0.64.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-sdk**: ResolvedMethods declarations and the VTI-KEY-009 refusals ([#2672](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2672))

* feat(vta-sdk): resolvedMethods declarations and the VTI-KEY-009 refusals

  The VTI specification now admits did:webs as an optional, alpha method
  for a node's durable identity (dtgwg-vti-spec#121). A node acts as an
  identity of an optional method only toward a peer whose verified current
  DID document declares it resolves that method, in a top-level
  resolvedMethods member (VTI-KEY-008); otherwise it sends nothing and
  fails with methodNotDeclared. A party that cannot rely on material
  without resolving a method it does not resolve refuses it with
  unsupportedDidMethod (VTI-KEY-009).

  - vta_sdk::resolved_methods: the required methods, what this build
    resolves and declares, the lenient reader of a peer's declaration,
    require_declared (the sending-side rule) and declare (with the JSON-LD
    term VTI-KEY-008 fixes).
  - The VTA declares did:webs in every document it mints, and so do the
    built-in templates for the nodes this workspace runs (vtc-host,
    room-host, dtg-witness, ballot-box). Templates for software outside it
    declare nothing.
  - Receive side: a proof by a DID of a method this party does not resolve
    is refused as DiProofError::UnsupportedDidMethod before any resolver is
    asked, and answered proofInvalid with details.reason
    unsupportedDidMethod and the method (the VTA, the shared Trust Task
    spine, the VTC).
  - Typed errors end to end: AppError::{MethodNotDeclared,
    UnsupportedDidMethod}, VtaError::{MethodNotDeclared,
    UnsupportedDidMethod}, read back from a Trust Task rejection and a REST
    body. The spine's app_error_to_reject also gains the NoMatchingProtocol
    arm it lacked (it answered internalError).

  Not breaking: DiProofError, AppError and VtaError are non_exhaustive.
  The documents the VTA mints and the four templates gain resolvedMethods
  and a further @context entry, which a DID-document consumer ignores.

  The sending-side check at the outbound seams follows separately; no
  node's own identity can be did:webs yet.

- **rooms**: A room may turn off its watch signals' randomised delay (rooms/signal-delay/set 0.1, info 0.4, create 0.3, owner/register 0.3) ([#2667](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2667))

* feat(rooms)!: a room may turn off its watch signals' randomised delay (rooms/signal-delay/set 0.1, info 0.4, create 0.3, owner/register 0.3)

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1084. A room's signal delay (randomised, the default, or none) is stored on the host's room record (absent = randomised, no migration) and applied by RoomWatches::fire from the room, never the watch request. Both hosts serve rooms/signal-delay/set/0.1 (admin, idempotent, audited), rooms/create/0.3 and rooms/info/0.4 beside create 0.2 and info 0.3. The VTA serves rooms/owner/register/0.3, passing recordRetention and signalDelay through to create 0.3 and refusing hostRefused on a host that does not take it. pnm rooms signal-delay show|set, pnm rooms owner register --chat; the VTC console shows the setting.



### Fixed

- **vta**: A did:webs node acts toward any peer; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008) ([#2697](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2697))

* fix(vta,vtc)!: a did:webs node acts toward any peer; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008)

  Each party chooses its own identity method and still works with every
  other: a did:webs client talks to a did:webvh service, and a did:webs
  node reaches any peer. dtgwg-vti-spec#123 makes did:webs a required
  method every node resolves, with the key-role designation extension
  (VTI-KEY-003); a node never requires a peer to use a particular durable
  method (VTI-KEY-001); VTI-KEY-008, the resolvedMethods declaration gate,
  is withdrawn with its methodNotDeclared refusal; VTI-KEY-009 keeps only
  the receiving side.

- **vtc-service**: Passkey ceremonies expire and are bounded, and a sign-in naming a subject answers alike whether or not it is enrolled ([#2693](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2693))

In-flight WebAuthn ceremony state (`vti_common::auth::passkey::store`)
  had no expiry and no bound. A sign-in challenge stayed redeemable however
  old it was; the browser's 60 s timeout is advisory only. Every
  unauthenticated start wrote a row that nothing removed.

  Ceremony state now:
  - carries an `expiresAt` five minutes out (`CEREMONY_TTL_SECS`). A take
    or read of a lapsed row answers `None`, and the take deletes it exactly
    once. Rows written before this change are treated as lapsed.
  - is swept by the retention task in the console's and the member
    portal's passkey keyspaces, together with the portal registration pin
    and the revocation target pin. Each delete is conditional on the row
    being unchanged, so a row a finish has just taken is never deleted a
    second time.
  - is counted per owner. That is the authenticated DID that started it, or
    one shared anonymous owner for an unauthenticated sign-in. The bounds:
    8 pending per DID (429), 1,000 pending anonymous sign-ins (503) and
    2,000 in all per keyspace (503). Lapsed rows are swept before a start
    is refused. `store_registration_state` and `store_auth_state` take the
    owner; `store_pending` / `take_pending` / `get_pending` /
    `sweep_expired_ceremonies` are new.

  `POST /v1/auth/passkey-login/start` with a `subject` and no session
  refused a subject without passkeys (403) and challenged one with
  passkeys (200). It now answers 200 for both. An unenrolled subject gets a
  stand-in credential set derived with HMAC-SHA256 from the subject under a
  community-held random key. The set is stable per subject, goes through
  the same webauthn-rs start, and is stored as a ceremony that no
  authenticator can finish. `passkey-login/finish` answers every failure
  before a registered credential is found with the same 401 body ("passkey
  authentication failed"). The detail is logged.

  A `429` from the Trust Task door's pre-verification ceiling for
  documents claiming a known signer now reports the anonymous limiter's
  name and message, so it no longer says whether the named DID is known.

- **vta-service**: Outbound Trust-Task REST sends dial only vetted peer endpoints, through the guarded client ([#2687](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2687))

* fix(vta-service)!: outbound Trust-Task REST sends dial only vetted peer endpoints, through the guarded client

  A REST send's URL comes from the recipient's DID document, which whoever
  controls that DID writes, and the recipient of a room task is named by the
  caller. `Outbound::send_rest` posted to it with the ordinary REST client
  (timeouts and same-origin redirects only), so the endpoint could name a
  loopback or private-network service, the reply was read with no size limit,
  and a reply that was not JSON was copied into the error the caller saw. The
  push transport (`vti_common::trust_task_push::RestPushTransport`) had the
  foreign-fetch client but no URL check, and that client's resolver never sees
  an IP-literal host.

  - vta-sdk: `http::guard_peer_endpoint(url, policy)`. `https://` is decided by
    `guard_foreign_url`. `http://` passes only for an exact loopback host, and
    only with the private-endpoint opt-in. Userinfo is refused unechoed.
  - vta-service: `send_rest` (now `send_rest_to`, taking the policy) checks the
    URL with `guard_peer_endpoint` under `EndpointPolicy::process_default()` and
    sends through `foreign_fetch_client_for` with the same policy (no proxy, no
    redirects, a resolver that refuses non-public answers). The 30 s total
    request budget is kept. The reply is read under a 4 MiB cap
    (`read_body_capped`). A reply that is not JSON is reported by status, size
    and parse position; its text goes to the debug log only.
  - vti-common: `RestPushTransport::new` takes a `RestEndpointGuard`, run on each
    URL before it is dialled; a refusal is `MessagingError::NoEndpoint`. The VTA
    and VTC pass `guard_peer_endpoint` and build the client for the same policy.

  Behaviour changes: loopback and private-network peers (room hosts, DID
  hosting, push recipients) are reached only with `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`
  (the data-rooms quickstart already sets it); a peer's redirect is no longer
  followed; a reply over 4 MiB is refused; a non-JSON reply's body is no longer
  in the error.

title: feat(ts, ts-gen)!: type generated schema constants as JSON Schema instead of literal types
body:
Every generated TypeScript module used to emit `PAYLOAD_SCHEMA` and `RESPONSE_PAYLOAD_SCHEMA` with `as const`. That made each `.d.ts` carry the whole schema again as a deeply readonly literal type, and nothing reads that type: the runtime takes schemas as `unknown` (`SpecPolicy.payloadSchema`, `PayloadValidator.validate`, `prunePayload`). Both generators now annotate the constants as `{ readonly [key: string]: unknown }`. That covers `scripts/build-ts-bindings.mjs` for the prebuilt modules and `trust-tasks-ts-gen/src/emit.ts` for consumer-side generation. Each generator was changed on its own, as CLAUDE.md requires. `SPEC.payloadSchema` and `RESPONSE_SPEC.payloadSchema` pick up the same type. `TYPE_URI`, `RESPONSE_TYPE_URI` and the `SPEC` objects are still `as const`.

I used an index signature rather than `Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>` because some specs (`vtc/registry/records/list` 0.1 and 0.2) generate their own interface named `Record`, which shadows the global one. The annotation is written inline instead of importing a named type from the runtime. A module generated by `trust-tasks-ts-gen` therefore still compiles against an older `@openvtc/trust-tasks` that does not export such a type.

Three readers of the TypeScript module text now accept the annotated form: `scripts/check-bindings-conformance.mjs` (`tsSchemaConst`), `scripts/check-bundles.mjs` (`tsConst`) and `trust-tasks-ts-gen/scripts/equivalence.mjs` (`cutSchema`). The comment in `trust-tasks-ts/scripts/api-compat.mjs` about the schema mask is updated too.

Size of `@openvtc/trust-tasks`, from `npm pack --dry-run`, before and after:

- unpacked size: 101,449,186 B to 42,581,606 B
- `.d.ts` total (1,575 files): 69,113,286 B to 9,839,534 B
- tarball size: 8,191,148 B to 3,545,445 B
- `dist/acl/grant/0.3/payload.d.ts`: 136,655 B to 5,945 B

This changes the declared types of public constants, so it is a TypeScript API break for `@openvtc/trust-tasks`. A consumer that relied on a schema's literal type (for example `typeof PAYLOAD_SCHEMA["properties"]["x"]`) no longer compiles. The output of `trust-tasks-ts-gen` changes the same way, so the title scopes the `!` to both `ts` and `ts-gen`. Run locally with this title, `npm run api-compat` passes: the changed constants are reported as breaks declared by the `ts` scope.

Checks run locally:

- `npm run build-ts-bindings` regenerates the prebuilt modules.
- The Rust, Go and Dart generators produce no diff.
- `npm run check-bindings` passes.
- `npm run build`, `npm run build-bundles` and `npm run check-bundles` pass (1,385 schema pairs agree with the TypeScript modules).
- The `trust-tasks-ts` tests pass (252), and so does `npm run smoke`.
- The `trust-tasks-ts-gen` tests pass (30), and `npm run equivalence` reports the modules equivalent.
- `examples/consumer-app-ts` runs `npm run all` successfully.
- `trust-tasks-ts-proof`, `-tsp` and `-capability-client` build and pass their tests against the in-tree core.

The `src/` and source-map part of this issue landed in #1227. Splitting out a separate runtime package was declined, so this PR finishes the issue.

Closes #1107.

feat(ts, ts-gen)!: type generated schema constants as JSON Schema instead of literal types (#1236)

* feat(ts, ts-gen)!: type generated schema constants as JSON Schema instead of literal types

Both TypeScript generators (scripts/build-ts-bindings.mjs and trust-tasks-ts-gen) now emit PAYLOAD_SCHEMA and RESPONSE_PAYLOAD_SCHEMA as `{ readonly [key: string]: unknown }` instead of `as const`. The literal type repeated every schema in full in each declaration file, and nothing reads it at the type level: the runtime takes schemas as `unknown`. title: vta-sdk-v0.88.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A VTC can take a level-1 did:webs as its own DID ([#2698](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2698))

* feat(vta-sdk): vtc-host-classical, the VTC template a level-1 did:webs can carry

  A level-1 did:webs holds one key-state signing key, and CONVENTIONS.md 0.2
  §9.2 refuses vtc-host's second (post-quantum) signing slot as keyAlgorithm and
  forbids a VTA to drop what a template describes; the template keys block has no
  optional slot (vta/did-templates/* 3.1). So a did:webs VTC (VTI-KEY-001) names a
  template that does not ask for the key: vtc-host-classical, vtc-host less the
  pq-signing slot, its verification method and its assertionMethod reference.
  It is derived from vtc-host when loaded, not shipped as a second file, so the
  two cannot drift (pinned by a test rendering both). The §9.2 check is
  unchanged: vtc-host stays refused, every other refusal stands.

  The §9.2 service rule reads a `{DID}#…` id as the DID's own fragment: a
  service supplied whole as a variable (SERVICE_TSP, SERVICE_DIDCOMM) keeps the
  placeholder, because a whole-value substitution is not substituted again, and
  was refused under did:webs as "not a fragment".

- **vta**: Provision an integration as a did:webs ([#2695](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2695))

The template var DID_METHOD=webs routes provision-integration's mint to
  create_did_webs: level 1, class `service` (VTI-KEY-192), shaped by the
  template with every CONVENTIONS.md 0.2 §9.2 check and refusal, gated by
  `[dids] webs_service_dids`, and published at WEBVH_SERVER (required: a
  did:webs has no serverless mode) on WEBVH_DOMAIN under WEBVH_PATH. No wire
  member is added to provision/integration/0.3: the method is a template var,
  as DID_METHOD=scid already was. A build without `webs` refuses the selection
  by name.

  The bundle stays SealedPayloadV1::TemplateBootstrap. Its keys are the
  key-state key and the designated X25519 key agreement key under the ids the
  did:webs document gives them (<did>#<CESR key>), config.did_document is the
  document the stream derives, and the stream itself rides a new
  TemplateOutput::WebsKeriCesr in place of a did.jsonl. It is emitted only for
  a did:webs, so every webvh/did:key/did:peer bundle is byte-identical; an
  opener that predates the variant refuses such a bundle by name. TemplateOutput
  becomes #[non_exhaustive] (breaking for vta-sdk Rust callers matching it
  exhaustively).

  Integration side: ProvisionResult(V2)::webs_keri_cesr,
  ProvisionResultV2::integration_secrets_bundle and
  DidKeyMaterialV2::secrets_bundle (the bundle a host service stores, led by
  the key its document lists for authentication);
  DidSecretsBundle::trust_task_signing_key_for picks that key by role
  (VTI-KEY-150) rather than the first Ed25519. vti-witness and
  vti-voting-service setup take `did_method = "webs"`, store keys by the
  bundle's ids and write no did.jsonl.

  build_did_secrets_bundle (what room-host fetches) now holds exactly the keys
  a did:webs document lists, led by its authentication key: it used to include
  the KERI pre-rotated successor (<did>#pre-rotation-<sn>), handing a service
  the key that controls the identifier's next rotation. ExportDeps gains
  `webs_ks` (breaking for vta-service).

- **vta**: A did:webs template's resolvedMethods is ignored, not refused ([#2691](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2691))

trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1170 (closing #1164) made a template's
  resolvedMethods member ignored, as @context is, in vta/webs/_shared/0.2
  §9.2: a did:webs node declares did:webs by using it, and the derivation
  renders no declaration of further methods (VTI-KEY-008). The checker
  follows, so VTI's node templates (dtg-witness, did-host-*, room-host,
  ballot-box) are now usable with vta/webs/dids/create/0.2; vtc-host is
  still refused, for its post-quantum second signing key.

- **vta**: Serve vta/webs/dids/create/0.2 — DID classes, did:webs service DIDs, templates ([#2689](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2689))

Pin vta/webs/dids/create/0.2 beside 0.1 (0.1 is now marked superseded
  upstream and stays served) and serve it.

  - Every 0.2 create states a DID class (relationship | persona | service,
    VTI-KEY-190 – 193), which WebsDidRecord now keeps (`didClass`, serde
    default; a 0.1 create records none and none is inferred). Setup records
    this VTA's own did:webs identity as `service`.
  - A level-1 did:webs service DID is enabled separately from creation by
    the new `[dids] webs_service_dids` (default false,
    VTA_DIDS_WEBS_SERVICE_DIDS), the name the specification's example uses;
    off refuses `service` with serviceDidNotPermitted (CONVENTIONS 0.2 §1.1).
  - didClassConflict (§1.2): a persona/relationship DID made primary of a
    context whose primary is a service DID (this VTA's own DID, or a service
    did:webs it created) — details.requiredClass "service"; a service DID
    replacing a persona did:webs primary. The MAY rule is implemented too:
    a template whose kind names only a node (mediator, dtg-witness,
    push-gateway, trust-registry, vtc-host, room-host, ballot-box,
    did-host-*) under a class other than service.
  - DID templates (§9): template/templateContext/templateVars resolve
    context → global → built-in (the webvh resolver), variables are checked
    (templateVarsInvalid with missing/unknown), and the document is checked
    against §9.2 by a new pure checker in vta-sdk
    (`did_templates::webs::{check_key_shape, map_webs_document}`, returning
    the first failing reason and the JSON Pointers it refused, or the
    designations). The template is rendered and checked once with
    placeholder keys before any key is derived, then again with the real
    DID and keys after the inception: create_did_webs now computes the
    inception (and so the AID and DID) before writing the designations, and
    still publishes before recording anything (R2.1).
  - `resolvedMethods`, carried by VTI's node built-ins, is refused as
    documentMember as §9.2 is written (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1164);
    the fix, should the specification honour it, is one line in
    DOCUMENT_MEMBERS, and a test pins today's behaviour. `ai-agent` and
    `room` are representable today.
  - SDK: TASK_VTA_WEBS_DIDS_CREATE_0_2, retry-safety Keyed,
    VtaClient::create_did_webs_classed, fixes for the new codes.
    pnm webs create gains --class (sends 0.2; without it, 0.1), --template,
    --template-context and --var.

  Specification choices (conservative readings):
  1. 0.2 with didClass service and setPrimary on the context holding this
     VTA's own DID: 0.2 declares no code for "a create cannot re-identify
     this node", and its serviceDidNotPermitted now means only the switch,
     so it is the framework's permissionDenied. 0.1 still answers
     serviceDidNotPermitted.
  2. A templateContext the caller may not act in is permissionDenied
     (CONVENTIONS §8), not a silent fall-through to the global scope.
  3. An unresolved placeholder is reported in templateVarsInvalid's
     details.missing (the details schema has only missing and unknown).
  4. #1164: the specification's own dtg-witness example is refused under
     §9.2 as written.
  5. Setup's own key-role identity is recorded as class service; the service
     switch gates level-1 service DIDs only (key roles are not this family).
  6. A context provisioned for a VTC, VTN or host service carries no marker,
     so §1.2 item 1's second case is not refused (gap documented in
     docs/02-vta/did-webs.md).

  The designated aliases of a did:webs also carry its did:web twin and
  did:keri form (affinidi-did-webs designates them, as for 0.1), beyond the
  specification's example responses.

  Also fixes two clippy findings on this stack (Option::replace in role-key
  rotation, an item after a test module in webs_store).

- **vta**: A VTA whose own DID is a key-role did:webs — setup, first-boot self-registration ([#2679](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2679))

* feat(vta)!: create a key-role did:webs, and keep this VTA's own DID from being deleted

  S6 slice 2 (docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md §4, decision 2):
  a node's durable identity is a key-role identity (VTI-KEY-070,
  VTI-KEY-173), so create can mint one.

  - CreateDidWebsParams::key_roles: two more Ed25519 keys, each on its own
    path, designated as the attestation and operational role keys, and the
    independently derived X25519 key as the messaging key, through the
    did:webs key-role extension; the key event log's own key is in no
    relationship (VTI-KEY-071, VTI-KEY-184). Each role key's record is
    named by the id its document gives it, so the VTA finds it by role.
  - WebsDidRecord and CreateDidWebsResult carry the attestation and
    operational key ids.
  - delete refuses this VTA's own DID (permissionDenied): a node's identity
    is retired by re-identifying it.

  Off by default: personas and relationship DIDs are minted as before. The
  wire does not expose it yet (vta/webs/dids/create/0.2's didClass, S7);
  setup will (slice 3).

  Breaking (vta-service): new fields on WebsDidRecord (serde-defaulted) and
  CreateDidWebsResult.

- **rooms**: A live watch while a conversation is open (rooms/watch 0.2, rooms/keys/watch 0.2) ([#2671](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2671))

* feat(rooms)!: a room may turn off its watch signals' randomised delay (rooms/signal-delay/set 0.1, info 0.4, create 0.3, owner/register 0.3)

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1084. A room's signal delay (randomised, the default, or none) is stored on the host's room record (absent = randomised, no migration) and applied by RoomWatches::fire from the room, never the watch request. Both hosts serve rooms/signal-delay/set/0.1 (admin, idempotent, audited), rooms/create/0.3 and rooms/info/0.4 beside create 0.2 and info 0.3. The VTA serves rooms/owner/register/0.3, passing recordRetention and signalDelay through to create 0.3 and refusing hostRefused on a host that does not take it. pnm rooms signal-delay show|set, pnm rooms owner register --chat; the VTC console shows the setting.

- **vta**: A VTA authenticates with its authentication key, and can resolve itself as a did:webs ([#2675](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2675))

S6 slice 1 (docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md §4): the plumbing
  a did:webs VTA identity needs, with nothing changed for a did:webvh VTA,
  whose authentication and signing key are both #key-0.

  - SelfKeys gains the authentication key: a key-role identity's
    operational key (VTI-KEY-072), which is the key every request,
    response and DIDComm sender of this VTA proves with (proofPurpose
    authentication). The VTA's resident key at boot, the offline CLI
    bridge's signer, vta status's DIDComm profile and the operational-
    secret fallback now load it; attestation artefacts (credentials, the
    VtaAuthorization VC, room-owner registration) keep the signing
    (attestation) key. load_vta_issuer_secret_from_store takes the SelfKey
    to load.
  - A did:webs VTA preloads its own document into the resolver from the key
    event log it stores; readiness probes did:webs over the network and
    names its keri.cesr URL.
  - didcomm_light and url_from_did handle did:webs;
    vta_sdk::resolved_methods::is_durable_identity is webvh, scid or an
    optional durable method (did_scid::is_durable keeps meaning "has a
    webvh log").

  Breaking (vta-service): DIDCommBridge::signing_only and
  preload_self_did_document take the webs keyspace;
  load_vta_issuer_secret_from_store takes a SelfKey; SelfKeys has an
  authentication field.

- **vta-sdk**: ResolvedMethods declarations and the VTI-KEY-009 refusals ([#2672](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2672))

* feat(vta-sdk): resolvedMethods declarations and the VTI-KEY-009 refusals

  The VTI specification now admits did:webs as an optional, alpha method
  for a node's durable identity (dtgwg-vti-spec#121). A node acts as an
  identity of an optional method only toward a peer whose verified current
  DID document declares it resolves that method, in a top-level
  resolvedMethods member (VTI-KEY-008); otherwise it sends nothing and
  fails with methodNotDeclared. A party that cannot rely on material
  without resolving a method it does not resolve refuses it with
  unsupportedDidMethod (VTI-KEY-009).

  - vta_sdk::resolved_methods: the required methods, what this build
    resolves and declares, the lenient reader of a peer's declaration,
    require_declared (the sending-side rule) and declare (with the JSON-LD
    term VTI-KEY-008 fixes).
  - The VTA declares did:webs in every document it mints, and so do the
    built-in templates for the nodes this workspace runs (vtc-host,
    room-host, dtg-witness, ballot-box). Templates for software outside it
    declare nothing.
  - Receive side: a proof by a DID of a method this party does not resolve
    is refused as DiProofError::UnsupportedDidMethod before any resolver is
    asked, and answered proofInvalid with details.reason
    unsupportedDidMethod and the method (the VTA, the shared Trust Task
    spine, the VTC).
  - Typed errors end to end: AppError::{MethodNotDeclared,
    UnsupportedDidMethod}, VtaError::{MethodNotDeclared,
    UnsupportedDidMethod}, read back from a Trust Task rejection and a REST
    body. The spine's app_error_to_reject also gains the NoMatchingProtocol
    arm it lacked (it answered internalError).

  Not breaking: DiProofError, AppError and VtaError are non_exhaustive.
  The documents the VTA mints and the four templates gain resolvedMethods
  and a further @context entry, which a DID-document consumer ignores.

  The sending-side check at the outbound seams follows separately; no
  node's own identity can be did:webs yet.

- **rooms**: A room may turn off its watch signals' randomised delay (rooms/signal-delay/set 0.1, info 0.4, create 0.3, owner/register 0.3) ([#2667](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2667))

* feat(rooms)!: a room may turn off its watch signals' randomised delay (rooms/signal-delay/set 0.1, info 0.4, create 0.3, owner/register 0.3)

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1084. A room's signal delay (randomised, the default, or none) is stored on the host's room record (absent = randomised, no migration) and applied by RoomWatches::fire from the room, never the watch request. Both hosts serve rooms/signal-delay/set/0.1 (admin, idempotent, audited), rooms/create/0.3 and rooms/info/0.4 beside create 0.2 and info 0.3. The VTA serves rooms/owner/register/0.3, passing recordRetention and signalDelay through to create 0.3 and refusing hostRefused on a host that does not take it. pnm rooms signal-delay show|set, pnm rooms owner register --chat; the VTC console shows the setting.

- **rooms**: Open a conversation at its newest records (rooms/records/list 0.7, rooms/keys/browse 0.5) ([#2668](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2668))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1088.

  Pins rooms/records/list/0.7 and rooms/keys/browse/0.5 in vti-specs-rooms,
  beside the versions already pinned.

  Hosts (room-host and the VTC, through vti_rooms): rooms/records/list/0.7 is
  served beside 0.5 and 0.6. `order: newestFirst` returns rows in descending
  version, each cursor continuing downward; `sinceVersion` stays a lower bound,
  tombstones and `lastPrune` are as oldest first, and the commitment, count and
  head are over the whole room. A cursor is bound to its order (`v<N>` oldest
  first, `n<N>` newest first) and refused with the declared `invalidCursor`
  under the other (Order item 5). `vti_rooms::storage::list_records_page_in`
  takes a `RecordOrder`; `list_records_page` is unchanged (oldest first).
  Records are keyed by key, not version, so both orders sort the room in memory,
  which is no more than every page already pays for its uncached whole-room
  commitment; a version index belongs with a cached commitment.

- **vta**: A member's room read marker, kept by their VTA and shared across their devices (rooms/keys/read-marker 0.1, keys/list 0.3) ([#2665](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2665))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1086.

  Pins rooms/keys/read-marker/set 0.1, rooms/keys/read-marker/moved 0.1 and
  rooms/keys/list 0.3 (beside 0.2) in vti-specs-rooms. Only the three new
  versions are added to the lock; the existing pins keep their digests.

- **vta**: Serve vta/webs/dids/*/0.1; pnm webs; VtaClient did:webs methods; docs ([#2564](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2564))

* feat(vta)!: did:webs operations refuse in the codes the tasks declare; setPrimary, additional services, admin gate

  The did:webs operations return `WebsError`: a declared refusal (`WebsRefusal`:
  methodDisabled, serverNotFound, hostDoesNotHostWebs, domainNotServed,
  pathRefused, serviceDidNotPermitted, notFound, versionConflict, noChange,
  serviceIdConflict, deactivated, publishRefused) or any other `AppError`, so the
  Trust Task slice answers with the code the task declares instead of reading it
  from a message. A host's refusal is sorted by the code the host sent.

  Create resolves the domain before incepting (`WebsHost::resolve_domain`, which
  refuses one the host does not serve), takes `setPrimary` (refused as
  serviceDidNotPermitted on the context holding this VTA's own DID, VTI-KEY-001)
  and further designated services. Update, rotate and delete require the admin
  role, as their webvh counterparts do. `WebsDeps::from_app_state`; a borrowed
  host is a `WebsHost`.

- **vta**: Create, get and list did:webs DIDs (operation layer; no wire yet) ([#2561](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2561))

Step 4 of docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md, without the Trust Task
  handlers: the vta/webs/dids/* family is being specified, and the handlers will
  call these operations.

  - `webs` keyspace (vta-keyspaces): in ALL and BACKED_UP (a restored VTA must
    be able to continue the key event log); purged with its context
    (context_delete_effect Purged, and the purge is real:
    webs_store::purge_context, read on `contextId` alone so it runs without the
    feature); Orphaned for a DID deletion until vta/webs/dids/delete exists.
    `Keyspaces::webs` is not feature-gated, since a gated field changes the
    struct for every crate that builds one once any crate enables it.
  - `webs_store`: one WebsDidRecord per DID (the published keri.cesr, the
    ControllerState, the signing, successor and key agreement key ids).
  - `operations::did_webs::create_did_webs`: KeyMint and context gates; refused
    unless `[dids] webs_enabled` (new, default false, VTA_DIDS_WEBS_ENABLED);
    Ed25519 signing, X25519 key agreement and one pre-rotated successor derived
    under the context's base as did:webvh's are; KERI v2 inception (kt 1, nt 1)
    through affinidi-did-webs create_controlled; designated #didcomm and #tsp
    through this VTA's mediator; published to the did-hosting server as
    `method: "webs"` at slot `{path}/{AID}`, then (R2.1) key records and the
    row. The DID is computed as the host builds it, and a host that answers
    with another DID leaves nothing recorded. `get_did_webs` / `list_did_webs`.
  - `WebvhHostClient::publish_webs` and a `WebsHost` seam the operation is
    tested through.
  - vta-service feature `webs` (default on, not in vta-enclave), with
    affinidi-did-webs 0.12 (`create`), affinidi-keri 0.7, keri-core 0.7,
    keri-crypto 0.7. `affinidi-keri` brings LMDB (heed) that the controller
    path does not use; making it optional upstream is a follow-up.
  - Census entries: one raw seed access in did_webs/mod.rs (fresh keys at
    allocated paths), and two `mnemonic` slot paths that are not BIP-39.



### Changed

- **vta,vtc**: A node finds its own keys by role in its own DID document ([#2670](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2670))

A node addressed its own keys by fragment: `{did}#key-0` (signing),
  `#key-1` (key agreement), `#sealed-transfer-0`. That numbering is what one
  minting path gives a did:webvh, not a property of DIDs: a did:webs names each
  key by itself, and a key-role identity by its role's key (VTI-KEY-150). The VTC
  already read its ids from its document for messaging, yet registered its
  secrets under `#key-0`/`#key-1`, so on any other method the two never met.

  - `vta_sdk::node_keys::NodeKeyIds::from_document`: signing, authentication,
    key agreement and sealed-transfer ids from a node's own document, by
    `keyRoles` (attestation / operational / messaging) where the document has
    them, else by relationship (and the `sealed-transfer-0` assertion method a
    VTA's own did:webvh publishes). `conventional` is the did:webvh fallback.
  - `vta_service::self_keys`: the VTA's keys, each a key record id and a
    verification method, from its own document read from its own store (webvh
    log, did:webs key event stream; never resolved). Used by `init_auth`,
    `find_vta_key_paths`, the status trust-ping, the credential issuer key, the
    provision-integration VC and sealed-transfer keys, the offline CLI signer,
    and the VTA-as-room-owner key. `did:key` keeps its own shape.
  - VTC: startup and the status trust-ping register the secrets under the ids
    `vtc_key_ids` reads from the document (now through `node_keys`), and room
    files take the key agreement id it lists (`VtaStorage::with_key_agreement_id`,
    `#key-1` unless set).

  Nothing a did:webvh peer sees changes: a VTA's own did:webvh document, as the
  creation path renders it, gives exactly `#key-0`, `#key-1` and
  `#sealed-transfer-0` (tested), and a node whose document it does not hold falls
  back to them. A did:webs key-role document is read by role (tested).



### Fixed

- **vta**: A did:webs node acts toward any peer; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008) ([#2697](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2697))

* fix(vta,vtc)!: a did:webs node acts toward any peer; withdraw the resolvedMethods gate (VTI-KEY-003, VTI-KEY-008)

  Each party chooses its own identity method and still works with every
  other: a did:webs client talks to a did:webvh service, and a did:webs
  node reaches any peer. dtgwg-vti-spec#123 makes did:webs a required
  method every node resolves, with the key-role designation extension
  (VTI-KEY-003); a node never requires a peer to use a particular durable
  method (VTI-KEY-001); VTI-KEY-008, the resolvedMethods declaration gate,
  is withdrawn with its methodNotDeclared refusal; VTI-KEY-009 keeps only
  the receiving side.

- **vti-witness**: Bound witness sessions and the work one submission can cause ([#2682](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2682))

* fix(vti-witness): bound witness sessions and the work one submission can cause

  An identity that admits any opener (`allowed_parties` unset, the default)
  refused new sessions once `max_open` were open, and a session stayed open for
  its whole TTL. Openers with fresh DIDs could therefore hold every slot and keep
  members out by reopening. A submission's presentation was verified credential
  by credential, each resolving its issuer's DID, with no limit on how many
  credentials it carried. A failed submission left the session open, so the same
  session could be submitted to any number of times.

  - Opening: besides the per-opener cap, at most `max_open_per_party` open
    sessions may name one party as the counterparty. At `max_open`, an identity
    with no allow-list closes its oldest open sessions to make room. One with an
    allow-list still refuses (`witness/session:refused`, same message).
  - Submitting: a presentation carries at most 8 credentials, refused before any
    is resolved. Only credentials that could count are resolved and verified: the
    submitter's relationship credential, or a membership credential from an
    accepted community naming the holder. Any other credential is ignored, not
    resolved. The independence check still covers every credential.
  - After 3 submissions whose presentation does not verify, the session is
    closed (`SessionRecord.failed_submits`, defaulted for stored rows).

  Behaviour changes: a full open identity closes its oldest session rather than
  refusing; a second session naming the same counterparty is refused at the
  default per-party cap; a presentation with more than 8 credentials is
  refused; an extra credential that could not count no longer fails the
  presentation; a session closes after 3 failed submissions.

- **vta-service**: Outbound Trust-Task REST sends dial only vetted peer endpoints, through the guarded client ([#2687](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2687))

* fix(vta-service)!: outbound Trust-Task REST sends dial only vetted peer endpoints, through the guarded client

  A REST send's URL comes from the recipient's DID document, which whoever
  controls that DID writes, and the recipient of a room task is named by the
  caller. `Outbound::send_rest` posted to it with the ordinary REST client
  (timeouts and same-origin redirects only), so the endpoint could name a
  loopback or private-network service, the reply was read with no size limit,
  and a reply that was not JSON was copied into the error the caller saw. The
  push transport (`vti_common::trust_task_push::RestPushTransport`) had the
  foreign-fetch client but no URL check, and that client's resolver never sees
  an IP-literal host.

  - vta-sdk: `http::guard_peer_endpoint(url, policy)`. `https://` is decided by
    `guard_foreign_url`. `http://` passes only for an exact loopback host, and
    only with the private-endpoint opt-in. Userinfo is refused unechoed.
  - vta-service: `send_rest` (now `send_rest_to`, taking the policy) checks the
    URL with `guard_peer_endpoint` under `EndpointPolicy::process_default()` and
    sends through `foreign_fetch_client_for` with the same policy (no proxy, no
    redirects, a resolver that refuses non-public answers). The 30 s total
    request budget is kept. The reply is read under a 4 MiB cap
    (`read_body_capped`). A reply that is not JSON is reported by status, size
    and parse position; its text goes to the debug log only.
  - vti-common: `RestPushTransport::new` takes a `RestEndpointGuard`, run on each
    URL before it is dialled; a refusal is `MessagingError::NoEndpoint`. The VTA
    and VTC pass `guard_peer_endpoint` and build the client for the same policy.

  Behaviour changes: loopback and private-network peers (room hosts, DID
  hosting, push recipients) are reached only with `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`
  (the data-rooms quickstart already sets it); a peer's redirect is no longer
  followed; a reply over 4 MiB is refused; a non-JSON reply's body is no longer
  in the error.

- **status-list**: Bound every size read from a fetched Bitstring Status List ([#2674](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2674))

* fix(status-list): bound every size read from a fetched Bitstring Status List

  A fetched BitstringStatusListCredential is someone else's document, and
  the VTC sized its decode from it: `credentialSubject.statusSize` was taken
  as the list length, unbounded, and handed to the decoder, which allocates
  in proportion. In W3C Bitstring Status List v1.0 `statusSize` is the bits
  per entry, on the BitstringStatusListEntry (§2.1), not a list length — so
  a list carrying the conformant `"statusSize": 1` was also read as a
  one-entry list and refused for any index past 0.

  vtc-service (`recognition::verify`, used by recognise, join presentation
  and invitation checks):
  - The bit is read by `read_status_bit`, which bounds everything before
    decoding: the index (at most 4,194,304 entries, checked before the fetch
    too), the `encodedList` length, and the decoded length, which is the
    larger of `index + 1` and the spec minimum of 131,072 entries. Nothing
    the list declares sizes a buffer.
  - A list shorter than 131,072 entries, or than the index, is refused
    (§3.2 steps 9 and 10).
  - `statusSize` on an entry, or on a list, must be 1: the reader supports
    only 1-bit entries, which §1.3 allows. Anything else is refused rather
    than read as one bit.
  - A multibase `u`-prefixed `encodedList` (§2.2) is now read.

  The same reads elsewhere:
  - vta-sdk `vetting::status`: `MAX_STATUS_LIST_BITS` is now 1 << 22 (was
    1 << 26), since the decoder allocates about a byte per entry read; an
    entry whose `statusSize` is not 1 reads as Unknown.
  - vta-vault `status`: the resolver-supplied list size and `encodedList`
    length are bounded before decoding, the index is checked against the
    size first, and an entry whose `statusSize` is not 1 is refused.
  - vti-vtn: `VtnClient::get_url` reads the body under a 2 MiB cap
    (`MAX_FETCHED_BODY`) instead of buffering it whole; `StatusChecker`
    refuses an index past the end of the list (it read as clear) and an
    entry whose `statusSize` is not 1. `Bitstring::len_bits` is new.

  Behaviour changes: entries declaring `statusSize` other than 1 are
  refused (status Unknown / error) everywhere; in vtc-service a list
  carrying `statusSize: 1` is now read in full, one carrying any other
  value is refused, and a list longer than 131,072 entries is read past
  that point (it used to be read only to the first 131,072); indexes past
  4,194,304 are refused in vtc-service and vta-sdk; vti-vtn's checker
  errors on an out-of-range index instead of reporting Valid.

- **vta-sdk**: Did:webs is resolved over the network, though not a durable node identity ([#2560](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2560))

`is_network_resolved` named did:web, did:webvh and did:scid:vh:1, so a
  did:webs, whose key event log is fetched from its host, was treated as
  resolvable offline: the host session never probed it. It is now network
  resolved. `is_durable` is unchanged: VTI-KEY-001 does not name did:webs for a
  node's durable identity.

  Step 2 of docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md.

title: vti-specs-vta-v0.9.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Serve vta/webs/dids/create/0.2 — DID classes, did:webs service DIDs, templates ([#2689](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2689))

Pin vta/webs/dids/create/0.2 beside 0.1 (0.1 is now marked superseded
  upstream and stays served) and serve it.

  - Every 0.2 create states a DID class (relationship | persona | service,
    VTI-KEY-190 – 193), which WebsDidRecord now keeps (`didClass`, serde
    default; a 0.1 create records none and none is inferred). Setup records
    this VTA's own did:webs identity as `service`.
  - A level-1 did:webs service DID is enabled separately from creation by
    the new `[dids] webs_service_dids` (default false,
    VTA_DIDS_WEBS_SERVICE_DIDS), the name the specification's example uses;
    off refuses `service` with serviceDidNotPermitted (CONVENTIONS 0.2 §1.1).
  - didClassConflict (§1.2): a persona/relationship DID made primary of a
    context whose primary is a service DID (this VTA's own DID, or a service
    did:webs it created) — details.requiredClass "service"; a service DID
    replacing a persona did:webs primary. The MAY rule is implemented too:
    a template whose kind names only a node (mediator, dtg-witness,
    push-gateway, trust-registry, vtc-host, room-host, ballot-box,
    did-host-*) under a class other than service.
  - DID templates (§9): template/templateContext/templateVars resolve
    context → global → built-in (the webvh resolver), variables are checked
    (templateVarsInvalid with missing/unknown), and the document is checked
    against §9.2 by a new pure checker in vta-sdk
    (`did_templates::webs::{check_key_shape, map_webs_document}`, returning
    the first failing reason and the JSON Pointers it refused, or the
    designations). The template is rendered and checked once with
    placeholder keys before any key is derived, then again with the real
    DID and keys after the inception: create_did_webs now computes the
    inception (and so the AID and DID) before writing the designations, and
    still publishes before recording anything (R2.1).
  - `resolvedMethods`, carried by VTI's node built-ins, is refused as
    documentMember as §9.2 is written (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1164);
    the fix, should the specification honour it, is one line in
    DOCUMENT_MEMBERS, and a test pins today's behaviour. `ai-agent` and
    `room` are representable today.
  - SDK: TASK_VTA_WEBS_DIDS_CREATE_0_2, retry-safety Keyed,
    VtaClient::create_did_webs_classed, fixes for the new codes.
    pnm webs create gains --class (sends 0.2; without it, 0.1), --template,
    --template-context and --var.

  Specification choices (conservative readings):
  1. 0.2 with didClass service and setPrimary on the context holding this
     VTA's own DID: 0.2 declares no code for "a create cannot re-identify
     this node", and its serviceDidNotPermitted now means only the switch,
     so it is the framework's permissionDenied. 0.1 still answers
     serviceDidNotPermitted.
  2. A templateContext the caller may not act in is permissionDenied
     (CONVENTIONS §8), not a silent fall-through to the global scope.
  3. An unresolved placeholder is reported in templateVarsInvalid's
     details.missing (the details schema has only missing and unknown).
  4. #1164: the specification's own dtg-witness example is refused under
     §9.2 as written.
  5. Setup's own key-role identity is recorded as class service; the service
     switch gates level-1 service DIDs only (key roles are not this family).
  6. A context provisioned for a VTC, VTN or host service carries no marker,
     so §1.2 item 1's second case is not refused (gap documented in
     docs/02-vta/did-webs.md).

  The designated aliases of a did:webs also carry its did:web twin and
  did:keri form (affinidi-did-webs designates them, as for 0.1), beyond the
  specification's example responses.

  Also fixes two clippy findings on this stack (Option::replace in role-key
  rotation, an item after a test module in webs_store).

- **vti-specs-vta**: Pin vta/webs/dids/{create,get,list,update,rotate-keys,delete}/0.1 ([#2562](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2562))

The level-1 did:webs family (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1082), so the VTA
  can serve it: generated payload and response types under
  vti_specs::vta::webs::dids::*. Nothing serves or sends them yet; the handlers
  land with the operation layer (docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-in-the-vta.md,
  step 4 wiring).

title: ci: list a long set of changed inputs without failing on a closed pipe
body:
The `changed-paths` action from #1228 printed the changed inputs with `echo "$changed" | head -50` under `set -o pipefail`. When more than 50 inputs changed, `head` closed the pipe, `echo` failed with a broken pipe, and the step failed instead of deciding to run the job. #1236 (about 1,400 regenerated TS modules) hit it in all three TS sibling jobs.

The list is now printed with `sed -n '1,50p'`, which reads all its input, followed by a count of the lines left out. Tested locally under `set -uo pipefail` with 50,000 lines. Part of #1141.

title: feat(messaging/mux): admin-list, admin-revoke and admin-revoke-all for operators
body:
This adds three administrator tasks for DID multiplexing, all 0.1 (draft):
`messaging/mux/admin-list`, `messaging/mux/admin-revoke` and `messaging/mux/admin-revoke-all`.

## Why

The Affinidi mediator carries many member DIDs on one connection under grants each member signs. Today only the parties to a grant can see or end it:
- `messaging/mux/list` and `messaging/mux/revoke` serve the principal and the member only.
- `messaging/mux/revoke-all` needs a statement signed by the member DID.

An operator has no way to cut off a lost or compromised device, or to act for a DID's controller who has lost its keys. The mediator design (`mediator-did-multiplexing-design.md` §7.8) calls for an admin client that can list grants by principal or DID, revoke them, and bump a DID's epoch, with every admin action reported with reason `admin`.

## The tasks

The naming follows the registry's `admin-` sibling pattern (`auth/passkey/admin-list`, `vtc/members/admin-remove`). Each task requires a proof and `issuedAt`.

- **`admin-list`** (read-only)
  - **Who may call it:** `admin`, `rootAdmin` or `mediator`, as for `mux/connections`.
  - **Request:** filter by `principal`, `member` or both. At least one is required, so one request cannot dump the whole delegation graph. Paged with `cursor` and `limit`.
  - **Response:** an `AdminGrantView` per grant: id, both DIDs, state, effective scope and expiry, the epoch it was signed under, and `signedAt`. With `member`, the response also carries that DID's current `epoch`.
  - **No signed statements.** As with `mux/connections`, statements go only to the grant's two parties, through `mux/list`.
- **`admin-revoke`** (destructive)
  - **Who may call it:** `admin` or `rootAdmin` only.
  - **Root admins are protected.** An `admin` is refused with `messaging/mux/admin-revoke:protectedAccount` when any selected grant's member or principal is a `rootAdmin` account. The wording follows `messaging/account/remove`. A `rootAdmin` may revoke any grant.
  - **Selectors:** `principal`, `member`, both, or `member` plus `grantIds`. A grant id is unique only on its member's record, so `grantIds` is refused without `member`.
  - **Bounded work:** one request revokes at most `limit` grants (at most 500) and returns an exact `remaining` count. The client repeats the request until `remaining` is 0. Every revoked grant is listed, so the response is never a truncated list.
  - **Effects:** the same as `mux/revoke`.
    - Members are detached synchronously.
    - Replay floors are raised.
    - Each principal gets a `detached` event and a durable `grantsRevoked` notice, both with reason `admin`.
- **`admin-revoke-all`** (destructive)
  - **Who may call it:** `admin` or `rootAdmin` only. It has the same root-admin protection, with code `messaging/mux/admin-revoke-all:protectedAccount`.
  - **Request:** `{ did, epoch }`. The admin names the current epoch, so a replayed request does nothing once the epoch has moved, just as with the member's own revoke-all statement.
  - **Results:**
    - An earlier epoch succeeds with `epochAdvanced: false`.
    - A later one is refused with `epochMismatch`, which carries the current epoch.
    - Two more codes: `unknownAccount` and `contended`.
  - **Effects:** the same state change as `mux/revoke-all`. Grants become `epochRevoked` and the DID's session attaches end. It is reported with reason `admin` instead of `epochBumped`, so a principal can tell an operator's action from the member's.

**No shared-schema change.** `DetachReason`, `MemberChangeReason` and the `grantsRevoked` notice already carry `admin`.

Bindings are regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart. `npm run validate`, `check-bindings`, `check-published-schemas`, the Rust `messaging` conformance tests, `go build ./...` and `dart analyze lib/specs/messaging` pass.

## Questions for reviewers

- **The member DID gets no notice of an admin revoke.** `mux/notice` 0.1 sends `grantsRevoked` to principals only. The member sees the change through `mux/list`. Should a later notice version tell the member too?
- **`mediator` may call `admin-list` but not the two destructive tasks.** We think that matches intent: the service may read, and an operator decides what to end. Is that the right split?
- **`admin-list` requires a filter.** There is no "list every grant" form. Is anyone relying on one?
- **No `show` task.** `admin-list` explains why it has no sibling: a grant is reached through its member or its principal, and both filters exist.

## Implementation

The Affinidi mediator will implement these behind its existing mux store and add them to the admin client and console. This closes the "Admin grant revoke and epoch bump" item in the design's "Not built" list.

Adds three administrator tasks (0.1, draft) for DID multiplexing, the
operator side of the mediator design's §7.8:

- messaging/mux/admin-list: list stored grants by principal DID, member
  DID or both (one is required), paged, in every state, without the
  signed statements; with `member`, the member's current epoch.
- messaging/mux/admin-revoke: revoke grants of other accounts by
  principal, member, both, or member + grantIds; a bounded batch per
  request (`limit`), with an exact `remaining` count; synchronous detach,
  replay floors raised, detached events and grantsRevoked notices with
  reason `admin`.
- messaging/mux/admin-revoke-all: advance a member DID's epoch without
  its signature, naming the current epoch so a replay is inert; same
  state change as revoke-all, reported with reason `admin`.

admin-list admits the admin, rootAdmin and mediator account types, as
messaging/mux/connections does. The two destructive tasks admit admin and
rootAdmin only, and refuse an admin whose target member or principal is a
rootAdmin account with <slug>:protectedAccount, as messaging/account/remove
protects root admins. No shared-schema change: DetachReason,
MemberChangeReason and the grantsRevoked notice already carry `admin`.

title: feat(messaging/monitor): opt-in mux membership events (event 0.3, subscribe 0.2)
body:
This adds `messaging/monitor/event` 0.3 and `messaging/monitor/subscribe` 0.2 (draft). With them, a traffic-monitor subscription can opt in to mux membership events: a member DID attached to or detached from a principal's mux connection, with the reason.

## Why

The Affinidi mediator carries many member DIDs on one `didcomm-mux` or `tsp-mux` connection. The mediator design (`mediator-did-multiplexing-design.md` §7.8) asks the monitor to show "attached/detached per member, with reason". Today it cannot:
- `MonitorEvent` is "one observed step in the life of one message".
- `TrafficStage` is a closed enum.

Attach and detach are changes to a connection, not steps of a message.

## The change

- **A separate event shape.** `MonitorMembershipEvent` is a new def with these members:
  - `occurredAt`
  - `change`: `attached` or `detached`
  - `principal`, `member`
  - `wire`: `didcomm` or `tsp`, the values `mux/connections` uses
  - `source`: `grant` or `attach`
  - `reason`: reuses `MemberChangeReason`
  - `sessionId`, optional

  It carries metadata only. It never carries a message, a signed statement, a nonce, a scope or key material. `MonitorEvent` and `TrafficStage` are unchanged.
- **A separate array.** `event` 0.3 adds an optional `membership` array and a `membershipDropped` count. `events` and `dropped` keep their 0.2 meaning. Producers emit one membership event per member change they report in `mux/event`.
- **Opt-in.** `subscribe` 0.2 adds an optional `membership` filter (`dids`, `changes`, `wires`, `sources`). Its presence is the opt-in, so no subscription receives membership events without asking. It also adds `traffic: false`, for a tap that wants membership events only.
  - The response echoes the effective `membership` filter. If it is absent, the subscriber gets no membership events.
  - A non-admin sees only changes it is party to, using the same narrowing rule as for traffic.
- **Both versions declare `extends`.** `event` 0.3 extends 0.2, and `subscribe` 0.2 extends 0.1. A consumer of the old version still reads the new documents. Nothing that links to the old versions goes stale. A 0.1-only mediator ignores `membership` and answers without it, which the subscriber can see.
- **Shared schemas, additive and in place.**
  - `MembershipChange`, `MonitorMembershipEvent` and `MembershipFilter` are added to `messaging/_shared/0.3/mediator-ops`.
  - `MuxWire` is added to `messaging/mux/_shared/0.1`.
  - `check-published-schemas` confirms both edits are additive.

Bindings are regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart. `event` 0.2 and `subscribe` 0.1 now carry the superseded deprecation note. `npm run validate` passes, including both `extends` checks. `check-bindings`, `check-published-schemas`, the Rust `messaging` conformance tests, `go build ./...` and `dart analyze lib/specs/messaging` also pass.

## Questions for reviewers

- **Shared schema in place, or a new version?** The new defs are added to `mediator-ops` 0.3 and `mux/_shared` 0.1 in place. That is allowed for new `$defs`, and `connectionFull` was added to `mux/_shared` 0.1 the same way. The alternative is a `mediator-ops` 0.4 that copies 0.3. We chose in place to avoid a near-duplicate file.
- **Traffic events stay on by default in `subscribe` 0.2.** Our rule is "nothing by default, everything opted into". Membership events follow it. Traffic events do not, because turning them off by default would break `extends: "0.1"`. Making traffic opt-in too would need a version that does not extend 0.1.
- **The two arrays are not interleaved.** Each is in observation order, and a client merges them by `occurredAt`. Is that enough, or should there be one ordered array?
- **`sessionId` is optional and `grantId` is omitted.** Should either change?

## Implementation

The Affinidi mediator will emit these from the place it already sends `mux/event` attached/detached events. This closes the "Monitor attached/detached stages" item in the design's "Not built" list.

title: trust-tasks-cli-v0.2.0
body:
### Documentation

- Fix drifted counts, release runbook, licences and stale examples across the four libraries ([#1224](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1224))

* docs(getting-started): move the worked example to acl/grant/0.3 and stamp issuedAt with issued_at_now()

  The example pinned acl/grant/0.2, superseded by 0.3, and stamped issuedAt
  with chrono::Utc::now(), the full-precision form #970 removed from the
  libraries. The TS consumer example wrote toISOString() milliseconds into
  document fields the same way. The dependency snippet now uses cargo add,
  so it cannot name a stale version, and §4.4 describes the shared version
  group instead of versions from 0.14.



### Fixed

- **rs,build,cli,codegen**: Review fixes — declared guard code, SchemaValidator, keyword slugs, generate --lang rs, registry hints, docs.rs ([#1215](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1215))

* fix(rs): declared acl/revoke code in the guard, a caching SchemaValidator, docs.rs metadata

  - guards::acl::reject_last_authority returns acl/revoke:lastAuthorityProtected,
    the code every acl/revoke version declares (was snake_case); new
    LAST_AUTHORITY_PROTECTED constant, pinned to the generated declarations ([#1093](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1093)).
  - validate::SchemaValidator: a PayloadValidator compiling each schema once,
    cached by the schema text's address and confirmed against its content;
    validate_value and check_details use a shared one; prune_payload reuses a
    parsed-schema cache; PayloadPolicy::accept_unvalidated() ([#1091](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1091)).
  - docs.rs builds trust-tasks-rs with validate + acl and the facade with its
    non-spec features, and trust-tasks-rs / trust-tasks-https enable doc_cfg
    under docsrs, without which the docs.rs build cannot compile ([#1106](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1106)).

- **cli**: Refuse a plain-http registry unless it is on loopback or --allow-http-registry is given ([#1203](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1203))

A registry's index supplies the digests a pin records, so over plain http
  anything on the network path could choose both the digests and the bundles
  they name. Sources were already https-only; the registry now is too, with
  a loopback exception for local mirrors and tests and an explicit
  --allow-http-registry flag. The https agent refuses http redirects.

  with chrono::Utc::now(), the full-precision form #970 removed from the
  libraries. The TS consumer example wrote toISOString() milliseconds into
  document fields the same way. The dependency snippet now uses cargo add,
  so it cannot name a stale version, and §4.4 describes the shared version
  group instead of versions from 0.14.



### Fixed

- **rs,ts,go,dart**: The in-memory replay guard refuses when full instead of dropping live records ([#1163](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1163))

* fix(runtime): the in-memory replay guard refuses when full instead of dropping live records

  InMemoryReplayGuard (Rust, TypeScript, Go, Dart) made room for a new id by
  dropping the least-recently-used record, whether or not that record was
  still inside its retention window. A document whose record was dropped that
  way was then accepted again inside its window, with nothing logged.

  - When every slot holds a live record, a claim for a new id now fails
    (Rust ReplayGuardError, TS ReplayGuardFullError, Go ErrReplayGuardFull,
    Dart ReplayGuardFullException), which the pipeline answers `unavailable`
    (retryable). Records whose window has closed are reclaimed first; a
    record is never dropped to make room. Duplicates and conflicts are still
    recognised while full.
  - The default capacity is 100 000 live records (was 10 000), documented as
    a ceiling on distinct documents per retention window, and exported as
    DEFAULT_REPLAY_CAPACITY / DefaultReplayCapacity / defaultReplayCapacity.
  - TypeScript, Go and Dart gain the expiry horizon Rust already had
    (`expiryHorizonMs` / `ExpiryHorizon` / `expiryHorizon`, 30 days in the
    consequential policy): a stated expiresAt bounds the acceptance window in
    place of the maximum age, up to issuedAt + horizon, and the retained
    record's expiry is clamped to the same instant, so a producer can no
    longer pin a record indefinitely with a distant expiresAt.

- **runtime**: Digest item 11 over the received document, and check envelope types and nesting depth ([#1171](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1171))

* fix(runtime)!: digest item 11 over the received document, and check envelope types and nesting depth

  Item 11's duplicate-execution digest is now taken over the document as
  received wherever a pipeline holds it, so two documents under one id that
  differ only in a member the payload type does not model, or in the spelling
  of a timestamp, are an idConflict rather than a duplicate:

  - Go ConsumeInbound digests ConsumeOptions.Received when set.
  - Dart consumeInbound digests `received` whenever it is passed (it did only
    for a forward read), and the HTTPS server, DIDComm and TSP consumers pass it.
  - Rust consume_inbound / consume_dispatched digest the received JSON under
    ProofPolicy::VerifyReceived, with or without a proof; the HTTPS server
    digests the body. New received_document_digest.

  TypeScript consumeInbound now checks the envelope before anything reads it:
  member types (string id/type and string-valued optional members, object
  payload/proof/ceremony, @context string/array/object) and a nesting bound of
  128 levels, refused malformedRequest and addressed only from string members.
  validateEnvelope and MAX_NESTING_DEPTH are exported.

  Dart consumeInbound refuses a document nested beyond maxNestingDepth (128)
  with malformedRequest instead of overflowing the stack, and the new
  parseTrustTaskDocument decodes a received value without throwing, returning
  a malformedRequest reason for a mistyped member.

  Shared vectors in fixtures/consume/item11-digest.json run in all four
  runtimes.

title: trust-tasks-proof-v0.38.0
body:
### Documentation

- Fix drifted counts, release runbook, licences and stale examples across the four libraries ([#1224](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1224))

* docs(getting-started): move the worked example to acl/grant/0.3 and stamp issuedAt with issued_at_now()

  The example pinned acl/grant/0.2, superseded by 0.3, and stamped issuedAt
  with chrono::Utc::now(), the full-precision form #970 removed from the
  libraries. The TS consumer example wrote toISOString() milliseconds into
  document fields the same way. The dependency snippet now uses cargo add,
  so it cannot name a stale version, and §4.4 describes the shared version
  group instead of versions from 0.14.



### Fixed

- **proof,ts-proof,go-proof,dart-proof**: Follow the JCS cryptosuites' @context rule in all four proof backends ([#1233](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1233))

Signers copy a document's @context into the proof (eddsa-jcs-2022 /
  ecdsa-jcs-2019 section 3.3.1 step 2). Verifiers hash the proof
  configuration as received, and refuse a proof whose @context is not
  exactly the document's (section 3.3.2 step 4, held to equality because a
  ProofVerifier returns no verified document). The Dart verifier no longer
  lets ssi copy the document's @context into the configuration, which made
  it refuse what the other three signers emit. Documents without @context
  get byte-identical proofs. Six shared vectors in fixtures/proof pin the
  behaviour in every library.

- **rs,ts,go,dart,proof,ts-proof,go-proof,dart-proof**: Refuse out-of-range timestamp fields instead of rolling them over ([#1210](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1210))

issuedAt and expiresAt, and a proof's created, are now read with every
  field range-checked after the shared pattern: month 1-12, a day the month
  has, hour 0-23, minute and second 0-59 (no leap second), and an offset of
  at most 23:59 (14:00 for a proof's dateTimeStamp, as for expires).

  Before, the four runtimes disagreed on the same bytes. TypeScript's
  Date.parse read 2026-02-30 as 2 March and 24:00 as the next day; Dart's
  DateTime.tryParse rolled 2026-13-45T25:61:61Z over into 2027 and took any
  offset; Rust's chrono read :60 as a leap second and accepted a space for
  the T; Go's time.Parse accepted +24:00 and +23:60. In the TypeScript proof
  verifier a regex-valid but unparseable created (month 13) gave NaN, which
  never compares later than the clock-skew horizon, so it was accepted.

  New shared vectors: fixtures/consume/timestamps.json, run by all four
  runtimes, and five correctly signed created-* proof vectors.

- **https,proof**: Verify client response proofs as received, hold error responses to them, and bound DID resolution by default ([#1204](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1204))

* fix(https,proof)!: verify client response proofs as received, hold error responses to them, and bound DID resolution by default

  HttpsClient verified a response's proof over the parsed and re-serialised
  document, so a valid signature over, for example, an issuedAt written with
  +00:00 was refused. It now verifies over the body exactly as received, as
  the server already does.

  With a response verifier configured, a trust-task-error response is now
  returned as TrustTaskError only when its proof verifies and its issuer and
  recipient match the configured VIDs. Otherwise it is returned as the new
  ClientError::UnverifiedErrorResponse, which keeps the document for
  diagnostics but marks it as unattested. ClientError is now non_exhaustive.

  HttpsServer with a verifier and no explicit DID-method choice now accepts
  did:key only (DEFAULT_ALLOWED_DID_METHODS). allowed_did_methods widens it;
  the new allow_any_did_method lifts it. A server without a verifier is
  unchanged.

  CachedDidResolver now gives every resolution a deadline
  (DEFAULT_RESOLUTION_TIMEOUT, 10 s, with_timeout) and refuses a DID naming
  localhost or a loopback, private-network or link-local address before the
  client is called (allow_private_hosts opts out). with_host_filter adds a
  caller-supplied host allow-list.

- **go-proof, ts-proof, dart-proof**: Check proofPurpose and expires, and sign with authentication by default ([#1168](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1168))

* fix(go-proof, ts-proof, dart-proof)!: check proofPurpose and expires, and sign with authentication by default

  The Go, TypeScript and Dart proof verifiers accepted any non-empty
  proofPurpose, including keyAgreement, and none of the four read a proof's
  expires. They now apply the rule trust-tasks-proof (Rust) already applies
  (SPEC §4.7.3):

  - proofPurpose must be authentication, assertionMethod,
    capabilityInvocation or capabilityDelegation; keyAgreement and any other
    value are malformedProof.
  - Dart's withResolver path checks that the issuer's DID document lists the
    exact verificationMethod under the relationship proofPurpose names (by
    absolute reference, relative fragment, or embedded), defines it under
    verificationMethod, and names the issuer as its controller. The document
    is resolved once per verification and shared with ssi.
  - expires, when present, must be a dateTimeStamp (Z or an explicit offset)
    that has not passed; no clock-skew allowance. All four runtimes.
  - The Go, TypeScript and Dart signers default proofPurpose to
    authentication, as the Rust signer does, and refuse a purpose naming no
    signing relationship.
  - TypeScript verifies Ed25519 with RFC 8032 decoding ({ zip215: false }),
    as Go, Rust and Dart do.

  Three shared vectors (fixtures/proof) are correctly signed and must fail in
  every runtime: proofPurpose keyAgreement, an unrecognised proofPurpose, and
  a passed expires.

- **proof, ts-proof, dart-proof, dart-didcomm, ceremony**: Bound multibase decoding of unauthenticated values ([#1167](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1167))

* fix(proof, ts-proof, dart-proof): bound base58 decoding of proofValue and did:key

  The Rust, TypeScript and Dart proof verifiers decode a proof's proofValue
  and its did:key multikey with base58btc decoders whose cost grows with
  the square of the input length, and they do so before any signature is
  checked. A 1 MiB value took about 50 s per field in trust-tasks-proof
  (release build), and would take minutes in the Dart package and in the
  TypeScript package on @scure/base 2.0-2.3 (2.4 refuses over 4096
  characters itself).

  Each verifier now refuses a base58btc value longer than 175 characters
  before decoding it, or one that decodes to more than 128 bytes - the
  bounds the Go module adopts in #1166. The largest value any of them reads
  is a 96-byte P-384 signature; a did:key multikey is at most 51 bytes;
  175 = ceil(128 * log 256 / log 58).

  Nothing that could verify before is refused: a value over the bounds
  always decoded to more bytes than any supported key or signature.
