title: Key assurance levels for service DIDs, chosen by the operator and judged by verifier policy; DID classes; threshold recovery custodians (#82)
body:
Key assurance levels for service DIDs, chosen by the operator and judged by verifier policy; DID classes; threshold recovery custodians (#82)

* Key assurance levels for service DIDs, chosen by the operator and judged by verifier policy; DID classes; threshold recovery custodians (VTI-KEY-146 to VTI-KEY-149, VTI-KEY-190 to VTI-KEY-201, VTI-KEY-205, VTI-KEY-206, VTI-KEY-210 to VTI-KEY-221)

Key roles were all-or-nothing: a node identity without them was
non-conformant and its credentials refused, and every key-role identity needed
an external recovery key. This makes the protection a choice the operator
makes and a verifier judges.

- DID classes (VTI-KEY-190 to 193): relationship DIDs (one key is normal, any
  method), persona DIDs (one key or passkeys; `keyRoles` marks only
  `authenticator`), and service DIDs (VTA, VTC, VTN, registry, host services,
  mediator, integration).
- Key assurance levels (VTI-KEY-194 to 201): 1 single key, 2 role-separated
  (VTA holds attestation and update keys, which may be derived and backed up),
  3 recoverable (generated, in no backup, recovery custodian, witness). Every
  level is conformant; each verifier's policy sets the minimum per use. The
  level is declared in a top-level `keyAssurance` member, and at level 3 names
  the recovery commitment; a verifier caps it at what the document and
  history show, and treats a lowered level as level 1. What stays
  self-asserted is listed.
- Custody (VTI-KEY-110 to 119) states its level; the recovery key is
  mandatory at level 3 only. Recovery custodians (VTI-KEY-205, 206): a
  separately held key, a second VTA, or a threshold custodian.
- Threshold custody (VTI-KEY-210 to 221): FROST(Ed25519, SHA-512) [RFC 9591],
  t-of-n with 2 <= t < n, dealerless key generation [FROST20], participants
  in distinct boundaries with no subject approving at t of them, per-
  participant checks, single-use nonces, identifiable abort, Trust Tasks over
  TSP or DIDComm, refresh, no fallback below t, no reconstruct-then-sign;
  SHOULD NOT hold an attestation key.
- VTI-KEY-129 becomes a MUST at level 3 and also refuses a lowered level.
  VTI-KEY-181: the recovery key authorizes its own replacement; the quorum is
  for a lost recovery key and for raising to level 3. VTI-KEY-180: creating a
  level-2 identity needs a bound step-up as a SHOULD.
- VTI-KEY-146 to 149 replace "non-conformant, replace and deactivate" with
  level 1 being conformant, in-place raising by one entry with fresh keys, and
  no lowering. VTI-KEY-201 judges an artefact by the level at which its key is
  bound, which a raise keeps to one level per key.
- Appendix F.6 re-filed: the single-key rows move to VTI-KEY-196's SHOULD,
  and the custody rows say which level they block.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(keys): VTI-KEY-147 settles the old key with SHOULD retire / MAY keep as operational; VTI-KEY-196 lets a service's kind set a default level and a floor

A raise is a custody change, not evidence of compromise, so forcing the
replaced key out forced a re-issue operators did not need. The level-1 key
may stay as the operational key, the custody it already had; it can never
become attestation or update, and VTI-KEY-201 keeps everything it signed a
level-1 artefact. An implementation SHOULD default a new service DID to the
level recommended for its kind, and MAY let a template set a floor.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(keys): the threshold custodian is a condition over whole keys; FROST dropped (VTI-KEY-210–221 revised)

After review: a threshold custodian is n members, each a recovery custodian
of kind 1 or 2 in its own protection boundary holding one whole recovery key,
of which t (2 ≤ t < n) must authorize. Every member's key is committed in the
history; keyAssurance.recoveryCommitment names every commitment and t
(VTI-KEY-197); a verifier and a witness count only distinct committed members
(212) and require at least t proofs on a recovery or replacement entry (215);
membership changes are a replacement of the commitment by t members (218);
any algorithm the method admits, post-quantum included (219). A threshold
signature scheme is no longer a threshold custodian (220): it hid the group
behind one key at the cost of a DKG, single-use nonces, refresh and
ceremonies, with no post-quantum form, and nothing the recovery key does
needs it. VTI-KEY-199 item 3 and VTI-KEY-181 updated; term, references
(Verifiable Conditions, informative) and consideration 25 revised.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(rooms)!: room hosts hold every read to the purposes its chain grants (VTI-ACL-110)
body:
A room's authority credential may now state purposes (dtg-credentials 0.14,
DTG context v2), and a host serving a read holds the request to them
(`rooms/records/get/0.4`, *Purpose of use*).

- vti-rooms: `purpose::ChainPurposes` and `PurposeDecision`; `VerifiedChain.purposes`
  (a new public field), `AuthorizedAction::purposes` and `admit_purpose`; get/0.4 is
  dispatched, with `blob_tasks::get_v4_purpose` and `read_purpose_refused`.
- vti-rooms-dtg: `DtgChainVerifier` fills `purposes` from the verified chain, whose
  chain rule (a link may not widen its parent's purposes, VTI-ACL-107) dtg-credentials
  applies. A scope this build does not know grants nothing.
- room-host and vtc-service serve `rooms/records/get/0.4`. A purpose the chain does not
  grant, or none where it lists several, is refused with `purposeNotGranted` after the
  chain verifies and before any record is read. get/0.2 and 0.3 cannot name a purpose and
  are decided as naming none (`permissionDenied` where the chain lists several).
- The served read's purpose, or `unstated`, is recorded: `RoomOperationData.purpose`
  (vti-common, a new public field) at the VTC, the room operation log line at room-host
  (VTI-ACL-106).

Breaking: `VerifiedChain` and `RoomOperationData` gain a public field.

The VTA does not yet write purposes into the credentials it issues
(`rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.3`); that follows, and closes Appendix F's
VTI-ACL-110 row.

## Tests
- room-host `vti_acl_110_a_read_is_held_to_the_purposes_its_chain_grants`: real signed VACs stating one, two or no purposes, through get/0.4 and get/0.3.
- vtc-service `vti_acl_110_get_0_4_is_held_to_the_chain_purposes`.
- vta-service: `read_0_3_is_held_to_the_callers_purposes` now sees get/0.4 served; `read_0_3_falls_back_to_get_0_3_on_a_host_without_get_0_4` keeps the fallback covered.
- Full pre-push suite locally: workspace nextest, doc tests, vtc nextest (3675 passed), clippy, fmt, cargo deny.

title: feat(messaging/mux): connectionFull detach reason; didcomm-mux subprotocol binds a DIDComm socket
body:
Closes two gaps in `messaging/mux/*/0.1` that implementing the mediator surfaced. The specs are drafts, so there is no version bump.

## A connection with no room for a grant

Nothing told a principal that a valid grant was not carried because its connection already held `maxDidsPerConnection` members. This happened both on connect and when a grant was stored while connected. The principal saw `stored` and no `attached` event, and had to infer the rest.

- New `DetachReason` / `MemberChangeReason` value **`connectionFull`**: the grant is valid and stays stored, but this connection had no room for it.
- `event` producer rule 4: on connect, valid grants the connection has no room for are listed in the `detached` event with `connectionFull`. Which grants fill a connection is up to the mediator, and SHOULD be stable across connects.
- `event` producer rule 5 and `grant` rule 5: a grant stored while the principal is connected, which the connection has no room for, is reported `detached` / `connectionFull`. `attachedNow` is `true` only when some connection took the member.

## How a DIDComm socket becomes a mux connection

The event spec left this to "the transport". It now defines a `didcomm-mux` WebSocket subprotocol, next to `tsp-mux`:

- The client offers `didcomm-mux`. The mediator selects it only when it implements mux and has it enabled.
- An older mediator may echo an unknown token, so selection alone proves nothing. The client treats the connection as mux only after `ready`, and reports no member reachable before then.
- Delivered frames are the members' own messages, routed by recipient. DIDComm refusals are already in-band, so a DIDComm socket gets no `refused` event.
- A mediator MAY keep accepting a provisional token it shipped before this binding existed. The Affinidi mediator used `affinidi-mux` before release. A client MUST NOT offer such a token.

`attach`'s definition of a mux connection now points at both bindings.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart) for the new enum value.

Implementation: the Affinidi mediator (connection-full reporting, `didcomm-mux`) and SDK (`didcomm-mux`) follow.

title: fix(vta-sdk): PurposeScope refuses `any` carrying purposes, and a duplicate purpose
body:
An internally tagged enum let the unit variant ignore extra members, so
{"scope":"any","purposes":[...]} parsed as any, and the listed variant's set
folded a duplicate purpose silently (VTI-ACL-100). Payloads of the acl tasks
are held to the schema before they are parsed, but a stored entry and an SDK
response are not; parse through a strict wire form instead. Found writing the
same type for dtg-credentials (OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#44).

Tests: `vti_acl_100_an_empty_list_is_refused` gains both cases. Locally, 885 ACL, memory, room and purpose tests pass, plus clippy `-D warnings` and fmt.

title: feat!: a VAC states purposes of use, and verify_chain holds a chain to them
body:
DTG Core Credentials' Purposes of Use (trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#84): an
optional credentialSubject.purposes on a VAC, any or a non-empty list, under
context v2. verify_chain enforces the chain rule (a link stating none takes its
parent's; a wider link is WidensPurposes) and reports the effective purposes.
The member was refused outright before: the VAC subject denies unknown fields,
so no verifier using this library could read a VAC carrying it. Breaking: new
public fields on CredentialSubjectAuthority and VerifiedAuthority, and a new
AuthorityError variant.

See the CHANGELOG entry for the full surface. Tests: `authority_chain::purposes` covers seven cases (none stated grants `any`, narrowing, inheritance, widening refused, `modelTraining` only from a root naming it, refusal at issue, and context `v2` required with an empty list refused), plus the `PurposeScope` unit tests including the strict parse. Locally: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --all-features` (232), `--no-default-features`, and `cargo package --locked`.

The release that publishes this is a separate `chore(release)` PR. VTI then pins it to check `rooms/records/get` 0.4 against chain purposes, and writes them in `rooms/owner/issue-authority` 0.3.

title: Let a VAC state the purposes its subject may use what it obtains for
body:
Adds an optional `purposes` member to a VAC's `credentialSubject`, beside `authority`. It says what the subject may use content obtained under the authority **for**, so the VTI specification's purpose of use (VTI-ACL-100 – VTI-ACL-110) can apply to authority carried by a credential (VTI-ACL-110) as it already does to authority carried by an access control entry.

**What changes (`spec/body.md`, `CONTEXT.md`)**
- **Schema:** `credentialSubject.purposes` (OPTIONAL) is `{"scope":"any"}` or `{"scope":"listed","purposes":[...]}`, with a non-empty list naming each purpose once. Absent means `any`. This is the shape trust-tasks `acl/_shared/0.3` `PurposeScope` defines.
- **New section, *Purposes of Use*:**
  - Purposes are registered names (personalisation, taskExecution, analytics, modelTraining) or absolute IRIs, compared exactly. An unrecognised purpose equals only itself.
  - `any` never includes `modelTraining`.
  - **Along a chain:** a link with no `purposes` inherits its parent's, and a link stating wider purposes than its parent invalidates the chain. The verifier reports the leaf's effective purposes.
  - **Verification:** a content-disclosing operation that names a purpose is refused unless the effective purposes grant it. A single listed purpose applies when none is named. Under a list of several, naming none is refused. The refusal discloses no content and is distinct from an authority refusal. Which operations count, and the audit record, are left to the VTI requirements rather than restated.
- **Attenuation:** a new MUST NOT in the attenuated-VAC list, and the purposes check added to the chain-verification sentence.
- **Example:** the agent attenuation example now narrows its agent to `taskExecution` beneath a root that states none. The root example is unchanged, so its digest, which the agent example cites as `parent`, still holds.
- **Security Considerations:** item 23, on purposes widened along a chain or read as wider than stated.
- **CONTEXT.md:** the VAC entry mentions `purposes`.

**Judgement calls**
- **Context:** `v1` is byte-frozen and every term is `@protected`, so the member needs context `v2`. *Context Versions* now says a VAC stating `purposes` lists `v2`, and a credential without it may keep `v1`. An editor's note says `v2` (v1 plus `purposes`, with its own `scope`/`purposes` scoped inside so the protected `authority.scope` is not redefined) is not yet published, and leaves its digest to be added when the registry publishes it. **Publishing `v2` is a registry change this PR depends on.**
- **The VTI specification's** purpose registry and verifier obligations are cross-referenced, not copied.

**Why now / what follows**
- OpenVTC/dtg-credentials 0.13 declares the VAC subject `deny_unknown_fields`, so today every verifier using it refuses a VAC carrying `purposes`.
- After this lands and `v2` is published, dtg-credentials needs a release that reads `purposes` and enforces the chain rule.
- Then VTI room hosts check `rooms/records/get/0.4` against it (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1076), and the VTA's `rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.3` writes the member.

**Checks:** `npm run render` succeeds. Its one warning (dangling definitions) and `npm run healthCheck` (4 passed, 1 failed, 4 warnings) give the same result on unmodified `main`.

title: Let a VAC state the purposes its subject may use what it obtains for (#84)
body:
Let a VAC state the purposes its subject may use what it obtains for (#84)

* Let a VAC state the purposes its subject may use what it obtains for

A VAC gains an optional credentialSubject.purposes: {"scope":"any"} or a
non-empty listed set of registered purposes or absolute IRIs, absent meaning
any, any never including modelTraining. A link without purposes inherits its
parent's; a link stating wider purposes than its parent makes the chain
invalid. A verifier holds a content-disclosing operation that names a purpose
to the chain's effective purposes, as the VTI specification holds an access
control entry's (VTI-ACL-100 – 110).

The member needs context v2, which the registry has not published; an
editor's note says so.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* Hold every disclosing operation to a VAC's purposes, as VTI-ACL-103 - 105 do

The Verification paragraph was conditioned on the request naming a purpose,
then ruled on requests that name none, and said nothing of a request naming
none under `any`. State it as the VTI specification does: every operation that
discloses content is held to the chain's effective purposes, a chain stating
none grants `any` (never modelTraining), a request naming none is read as the
single listed purpose, refused under several, and served unstated under `any`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* Fix the links the Spec-Up-T health check finds broken

The v0.3 proposal draft was removed from dtgwg-cred-tf (#38), so its four
links now point at the last commit that holds it. www.trusttasks.org does not
resolve; trusttasks.org does. .gitignore states .env, .env.* and

title: feat(rooms): the key holder holds every opening to the caller's purposes (VTI-ACL-102)
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1076 at the VTA, as #2539 did for
agent memory.

Opening a room record discloses it, so it is purpose-bound (VTI-ACL-102). New
versions rooms/keys/open/0.3, read/0.3 and file-key/0.3 carry the purpose the
caller will use what it opens for (`purposeOfUse` on file-key, where `purpose`
already means seal or open). The purpose is judged against the caller's stored
ACL entry before anything is decrypted or the host is asked; one not granted is
`purposeNotGranted`, disclosing nothing (VTI-ACL-103, -104). The earlier
versions, still served, name none: served under `any` or a single listed
purpose, refused as `taskFailed` under an entry listing more. Only a key to
open a file is held to a purpose; a sealing key discloses nothing. Every
opening's audit row records its purpose, served or refused (VTI-ACL-106).

read/0.3 passes a named purpose to the host as rooms/records/get/0.4's, and
asks get/0.3 of a host that answers unsupportedType.

Not yet: room authority credentials stating purposes (VTI-ACL-110). A VAC has
no such member until trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#84 defines one, and
dtg-credentials 0.13 refuses a VAC that carries it, so a chain grants `any`
and the caller's entry is what narrows. issue-authority/0.3 is not pinned, and
no host serves get/0.4 yet.

The purpose helpers move from the memory handlers to trust_tasks::helpers.
The signing test state now seeds the super admin's ACL entry, as a running VTA
always has one.

## Tests
- `open_0_3_is_held_to_the_callers_purposes`
- `file_key_0_3_holds_an_opening_key_to_its_purpose_and_not_a_sealing_one`
- `read_0_3_is_held_to_the_callers_purposes`: refused before the host is asked, and audited both ways. A granted purpose goes to the host as get/0.4, falling back to get/0.3.
- Conformance witnesses for the three new URIs.
- Locally: 7211 of 7212 VTA-side tests passed. The one failure, `vti_08_context_create_fits_half_a_default_worker_stack`, failed under load and passes on its own, both on this branch and on main. Also passing: VTC 3674, doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt and cargo-deny.

body:
Moves the cache SDK's minimum to 0.8.48, which brings `affinidi-did-webs` 0.10.0 (affinidi-tdk-rs #997) and, with it, affinidi-keri 0.6.

What it changes for VTI's `did:webs` resolution:
- **Rotations:** they verify in keripy. A v1 rotation no longer carries `c`, and the resolver refuses one that does, as keripy does.
- **Thresholds:** thresholds of 10 or more are hex.
- **keri 0.6:** reads KERI v2 (`docs/05-design-notes/did-webs-keri-v2.md`).

**Lockfile:** only the did-webs chain moves: did-webs 0.10.0, keri-core and keri-crypto 0.6.0, did-scid 0.4.4, affinidi-tdk 0.37.3. The diff is version and checksum lines only, and no other lockfile contains did-webs.

**Checks, run locally:**

- vtc-service and vtc-client: 3674 passed;
- doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt and cargo-deny: clean.

title: docs(design-notes): v2 registries checked against keripy: a fresh UUID per update, and keripy reads a withheld revocation as issued
body:
Two findings from the v2 registry fixtures in affinidi/affinidi-keri-rs#20 (built by keripy 2.1.0-dev1 b70986f), recorded under P5 in `did-webs-keri-v2.md`:

- **A fresh UUID per update.** With public mode's empty UUID, a re-issue's BLID collides with the first issuance's, and keripy refuses it. VTI writes a fresh UUID for every update.
- **A withheld revocation.** keripy resolves a credential as issued when the stream leaves out its anchored revoking update. P5's 'every anchored registry event must be present' rule exists for this; keri-core's new `registry` module enforces it for v1 and v2.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.13
body:
### Added

- **acl**: Purpose of use on grants and on memory reads (AclEntry 0.3; vta/memory put/delete/list 0.3, get 0.2) ([#1074](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1074))

* feat(acl): purpose of use on grants and on memory reads (AclEntry 0.3; vta/memory put/delete/list 0.3, get 0.2)

  An access-control entry says who may do what, where and until when, but not
  what for. An agent granted a read of its principal's memory can use the content
  for anything, and nothing records the use it intended. The VTI specification
  now requires the purpose (VTI-ACL-100 – 110, trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#115);
  these are the wire shapes.

  acl/_shared/0.3 — AclEntry 0.3 adds one REQUIRED axis, `purposes`:
  `{"scope": "any"}` or `{"scope": "listed", "purposes": [...]}` with at least
  one `Purpose` — a lowerCamelCase name registered in the VTI purpose registry
  (personalisation, taskExecution, analytics, modelTraining) or an absolute IRI
  such as a DPV purpose. `any` never grants `modelTraining`. Delegated purposes
  are a subset of the granter's. CONVENTIONS.md §8a maps a 0.2 entry onto 0.3
  (`any`, the authority it already held, now stated) and §12 states the rules.

  acl tasks on AclEntry 0.3: grant/0.3, update/0.3, show/0.3, revoke/0.3,
  change-role/0.3, list/0.4. New errors on grant and update: `purposeOutsideDelegator`
  (purposes wider than the granter's) and `purposeRefused` (policy will not grant
  a purpose, refused by name, never dropped). update/0.3 replaces `purposes`
  wholesale; narrowing it is an audited privilege reduction. `purposes` is never
  redacted by show or list. No `extends`: a REQUIRED member on the entry cannot
  be added to a version a 0.2 consumer still reads.

  vta/memory put/0.3, delete/0.3, list/0.3, get/0.2 (each `extends` its
  predecessor) add an optional `purpose` (`MemoryPurpose`, new in
  vta/_shared/0.1/memory-record, a reference to acl's `Purpose`) and a
  `purposeNotGranted` error that discloses nothing and is distinct from
  `contextForbidden`. A recall, and a listing with values, is purpose-bound:
  refused for a purpose the entry does not grant, or for none under an entry
  listing several, and audited with its purpose either way. A write is not
  purpose-bound, but a conflict that returns `currentValue` is: the value is
  withheld unless the request's purpose is granted.

  Data rooms (a room authority credential's `purposes`, VTI-ACL-110) are a
  follow-up.

  Samples in other specs that named the superseded acl versions now name the new
  ones, with `purposes` on every embedded entry; prose links were moved by
  `npm run fix-stale-references`.



### Specifications

- **rooms**: Purpose of use on room reads and authority credentials (VTI-ACL-102, -110) ([#1076](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1076))

* spec(rooms): purpose of use on room reads and authority credentials (VTI-ACL-102, -110)

  Room content a key holder releases to its caller is purpose-bound, as agent
  memory is (vta/memory/get 0.2), and a room's authority credential may state
  the purposes it grants.

  - rooms/keys/open 0.3, rooms/keys/read 0.3: optional `purpose`; refused with
    `purposeNotGranted` where the caller's entry, or the principal's authority
    over the room, does not grant it. read passes it to the host.
  - rooms/keys/file-key 0.3: the same as `purposeOfUse` (`purpose` already

title: spec(rooms): purpose of use on room reads and authority credentials (VTI-ACL-102, -110)
body:
Closes the rooms gap recorded in the VTI specification's Appendix F (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#116), following `vta/memory`'s purpose model (#1074).

**New versions**, each `extends` its predecessor:
- `rooms/keys/open/0.3` and `rooms/keys/read/0.3` add an optional `purpose`. A request whose purpose isn't granted is refused with `purposeNotGranted` (details `purposeNamed` / `purpose`, as `vta/memory/get` 0.2). The granted purposes are those both the caller's ACL entry and the principal's room authority grant. `read` passes the purpose on to the host.
- `rooms/keys/file-key/0.3` adds the same as `purposeOfUse`, because `purpose` already means seal or open. Only `open` is purpose-bound.
- `rooms/records/get/0.4` adds an optional `purpose`. The host holds a read to the purposes the presented chain states (VTI-ACL-110), and a chain that states none grants `any`.
- `rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.3` adds an optional `purposes` (`PurposeScope` from `acl/_shared/0.3`), stated in the credential. Absent means `any`.

**In place, additive:** `rooms/_shared/0.2` gains `RecordPurpose` only. The chain rule is in `rooms/owner/issue-authority/0.3`, *Purposes along a chain*: a link that states no purposes takes its parent's, and a link that states wider ones is refused whole (VTI-ACL-107). Putting it in `AuthorityPresentation`'s shared description changed a TypeScript interface every version shares, which is an API break.

**Judgement calls:**
- `browse` returns metadata only, so it isn't purpose-bound.
- `present` is left alone. It mints presentations rather than opening anything, and an attenuated link's purposes follow the chain rule above.
- Where the VAC carries `purposes` in the credential itself is for DTG Core Credentials (dtgwg-cred-spec) to pin down. This PR states only that the issued credential states them.
- No `!` in the title, per the repo rule.

**Local checks:** validate, check-bindings, check-published-schemas (additive), build-bundles and check-bundles (1362), check-withdrawal-readiness, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate`, TS 126/126, `go build` and `go vet`, `dart analyze --fatal-infos`. All four bindings are regenerated.

title: feat(acl)!: purpose of use on ACL entries and memory reads (VTI-ACL-100 – 110)
body:
Closes #2120 for the VTA's ACL and agent memory.

ACL entries state `purposes`: `any`, or a non-empty list of registered
purposes (personalisation, taskExecution, analytics, modelTraining) or
absolute IRIs (VTI-ACL-100, -109). Entries written before purposes existed
are rewritten to `any` at boot, before anything is served (VTI-ACL-101).
`any` never grants modelTraining (VTI-ACL-105).

The VTA now serves acl/{grant,show,update,change-role,revoke}/0.3 and
acl/list/0.4 in place of 0.2 / list 0.3. Approval rules naming a 0.2
version move to 0.3 at boot (RETIRED_TASK_TYPES), so no gate fails open.
A grant or amendment may state only purposes the writer's own stored entry
grants (`purposeOutsideDelegator`, VTI-ACL-107); narrowing purposes is
audited as a privilege reduction. A hand-off successor inherits the marked
entry's purposes. The VTC stays on acl 0.2: it serves no purpose-bound
operation.

Every memory read is purpose-bound (VTI-ACL-102): get, list returning
values, and a conflict that would hand back the current value. New
versions vta/memory/{put,delete,list}/0.3 and get/0.2 carry `purpose`; a
purpose the caller's stored entry does not grant is refused with
`purposeNotGranted`, disclosing nothing (VTI-ACL-103, -104). The older
versions, still served, read as naming no purpose: served under `any`
(recorded as unstated) or a single listed purpose, refused as `taskFailed`
under an entry listing more. Every read's audit row records its purpose,
served or refused (VTI-ACL-106).

SDK: `PurposeScope` (vta_sdk::acl), `CreateAclRequest::purposes`,
`UpdateAclRequest::purposes`, `AclEntryResponse::purposes()`, and
memory_{get,list_page,put_versioned,delete_versioned}_for taking a purpose.
pnm: `acl create --purposes`, `acl update --purposes / --purposes-any`,
`memory recall --purpose`.

Not yet: room record reads and room credentials (VTI-ACL-102, -110), and
VTI-ACL-107 on entry-writing paths outside the ACL tasks — both recorded in
the specification's Appendix F (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#116).

Breaking: new public fields on vti_common::acl::AclEntry,
vta_sdk::client::{CreateAclRequest, UpdateAclRequest},
vta_service::operations::acl::{CreateAclParams, UpdateAclParams}; new
parameters on vta_cli_common::commands::{acl::cmd_acl_create,
acl::cmd_acl_update, memory::cmd_memory_recall} and
VtaClient::roll_over_handoff; ACL tasks 0.2 no longer served by the VTA.

## Tests
- `acl_purposes_are_stated_and_bounded_by_the_writer`: grant and update at 0.3 over the trust-task surface, covering empty list refused, `modelTraining` not delegable under `any`, a list never delegating `any`, and narrowing.
- Memory: `vti_acl_104_…`, `vti_acl_103_…`, `vti_acl_105_…`, the listing with and without values, a write naming an ungranted purpose refused before writing, and a conflict disclosing only for a granted purpose. Audit rows carry `purpose=`.
- `vti_acl_101_every_entry_comes_to_state_its_purposes` (boot migration), and the `PurposeScope` unit tests.
- Local: nextest 7209 (VTA side) and 3674 (VTC), doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, cargo-deny.

title: fix(mux/grant): unknown-key rule fails closed on direct authentication; no exemption for a grant without recorded keys
body:
Prose only in `messaging/mux/grant/0.1`; no schema or digest change.

A security review of the mediator implementation found that the rule as written could be switched off. The spec said an active grant stored without recorded key-agreement keys gives no basis for comparison, and that a direct DIDComm authentication does not fire the rule while one exists. One such grant, for example one stored while the resolver was down, therefore exempted every grant on the DID.

Changes:
- **A grant is never stored without its key-agreement keys.** If the member DID cannot be resolved to read them, the grant is refused with `messaging/mux:didUnresolvable`. An empty set means the document listed none, so that DID's first key-agreement key is unknown.
- **The comparison is with the keys every active grant recorded together.** A grant that recorded none no longer exempts the others.
- **Direct authentication fails closed.** The mediator MUST apply the rule, commit any suspension and detach its members before the authentication succeeds. If it cannot, it MUST refuse the authentication as retryable. A DID with no active grants is not affected.

Implementation: affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator branch `fix/mux-unknown-key-fail-closed`.

title: feat(chat/direct): a message from one person to another, rewritable by its author (chat/direct/message/0.1)
body:
## What

Adds **`chat/direct/message/0.1`** (draft, category `chat`). It is a person-to-person message that its author can rewrite. It also adds the shared component **`chat/direct/_shared/0.1/direct.schema.json`**. All four libraries are regenerated.

This is the first of a short series that answers discussion #1013, "A Trust Task type for a message from one person to another". It covers the interop board's `write` scenario.

- **One task, rewritten under the same `messageId`.** The author mints a fresh 43-character `messageId`, then sends the message again with a greater `revision` to:
  - **edit** it (`editedAt` is required on every revision after the first);
  - **withdraw** it (an empty `body`, which leaves a tombstone);
  - **react** with a message of `kind: reaction`, which names its target in `inReplyTo`.
- **Error codes.**
  - `notAuthor`: a rewrite by anyone but the authenticated original author.
  - `revisionConflict`: the same revision arrives again with a different payload.
  - `rewriteInvalid`: a rewrite changes `kind`, `writtenAt`, or a reaction's `inReplyTo`.
  - Stale revisions and unknown `messageId`s are handled silently. This avoids a state oracle (SPEC §12.6).
- **Two separate dedup layers.** SPEC §7.2 item 11 still dedups by document `id`. Separately, (author, `messageId`, `revision`) absorbs a new attempt (§8.4) that carries an identical payload.
- **Schema.** `additionalProperties: false`. The revision and reaction rules are a top-level `oneOf` with two branches (first revision / rewrite). The Rust generator's existing compound-`not` pass drops that `oneOf` from the typify copy, so it is enforced at runtime, as for the other `oneOf` schemas. typify does not support `if`/`then`.
- **`payload.invalid-examples.json`** has 10 fixtures:
  - revision 1 with `editedAt`;
  - revision 1 with an empty `body`;
  - revision 2 without `editedAt`;
  - a reaction without `inReplyTo`;
  - a `messageId` of the wrong length;
  - an unknown member;
  - an extra member in `inReplyTo`;
  - a non-`Z` `writtenAt`;
  - `revision: 0`;
  - a bare `ext` key.
- **`website/assets/data.js`**: only the `chat` category blurb changes, so that it names both `chat/direct/*` and `chat/message`. No taxonomy change is needed: `chat` is already in the meta-schema enum and in `TT_CATEGORIES`. The slug is not reserved, and the existing Rust `chat` feature covers it.

## Why this shape

- **Its own namespace, not an extension of `chat/message/0.1`.** That spec is the bridge's agent-to-platform chain. Its authority, its proof requirement (`REQUIRED`), its parties and its retention (`durable`) all differ, so an `extends` could not keep its promises.
- **Groups stay in `rooms/*`.** With pairwise identifiers, a group built by fanning out 1:1 messages cannot name its members to each other.

## Proof and carriage

`proofRequirement: OPTIONAL`, with a normative carriage rule:

- A producer **MUST** send these documents only over a binding mode whose binding specification permits omitting `proof` under SPEC §9.1.1.
- It **SHOULD NOT** fall back to a mode without that allowance; it waits or tells its user instead.
- A present proof is still verified (§7.2 item 7).

The spec names no bindings. Which modes qualify is left to each binding's own text.

## Alignment with rooms

The content vocabulary is the one in `rooms/_shared/0.1` (`SealedRecordBody`). `kind`, `writtenAt` and `editedAt` are **`$ref`'d directly** from `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json` (`RecordKind`, `RecordWrittenAt`, `RecordEditedAt`), so their patterns cannot drift. The bundle's `defOrigins` names the rooms component. The spec applies the named rooms rules (*Edits*, *What a new version keeps*, *Withdrawing a message*, *Replies*, *Reactions*, *Counting reactions*, *A reaction's value*, *Nothing answers a reaction*, *When it was written*), with host times mapped to the consumer's receipt instants.

| `chat/direct/message` | rooms | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` (required) | `RecordKind` (optional) | `$ref`; stricter |
| `body` (≤16384; empty = withdrawn on a rewrite) | `body` | same rules; stricter bound |
| `writtenAt` / `editedAt` | `RecordWrittenAt` / `RecordEditedAt` | `$ref`; `editedAt` required on revision ≥ 2 |
| `inReplyTo` → `{messageId}` | `RecordReference {key, version?}` | same rules; no host version |
| edit / withdraw / react = rewrite of the same id | same | aligned; the word "retract" is kept out (it is a curator act in rooms) |
| `messageId` (author-minted) | record `key` | kept: there is no host location |
| `revision` (author-set) | `version` (host-set) | kept: there is no host |
| author = authenticated issuer; non-author rewrite refused | signed `author`; non-author rewrite shown as the new author | kept (stricter) |
| `ext` | — | kept; dropped on import |
| no `title`/`tags`/provenance/`roomProfile` | present | omitted; a direct message is a strict subset |

The cost of the `$ref` is that `chat/direct` follows the lifecycle of `rooms/_shared`. `rooms/_shared/0.1` and `0.2` define these four definitions byte-identically. A container-neutral content component that both families reference would be the longer-term option, and that is for the rooms owner.

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- **Binding text.** Each binding would say what its sender authentication gives a holder of the envelope. That is deferred.
- **`chat/direct/receipt/0.1`.** Delivered/read receipts, opt-in by the reader. When it lands, `related` here gains it.
- **`knownImplementations`** for both tasks, after the first interop run.
- **`chat/direct/message/0.2`.** An optional `file` aligned with the rooms `FileManifest`, `extends: "0.1"`.
- **Canonical framework repo** (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec), not here:
  - **C1:** a way for a specification to say its documents are meant to be non-transferable, so that "SHOULD NOT include a proof" can be said without weakening §4.7.2.
  - **C2:** an informative §13 item on this kind of carriage.
  - **C3:** only if pursued, an in-band authentication construction that does not conflict with §4.7.3 item 1.
- **For the rooms owner:** an import provision, so that history imported from a 1:1 is not flagged as backdated.

## Other notes for review

- **`targetFrameworkVersion` is `0.6.0`.** The build has no `specs/_framework/0.7` envelope schema yet, and the scaffolder chose 0.6.0.
- **The acceptance window (30 days) is guidance.** It is stated as a SHOULD in Security & Privacy, for offline composition and mediated delivery.
- **No version bumps, CHANGELOG entries or `SPEC.md` edits.** `rooms/*` and `chat/message` are untouched.

## Testing

All commands were run locally under `nice -n 10`.

- `npm run validate`: passes. `TT_STRICT_SECURITY_PRIVACY=1 npm run validate` also passes. Casing, wire conventions, stale references and the free-text bound all report 0 non-conforming.
- `npm run build`: passes. The six request examples and two error examples validate against the envelope schema.
- Libraries regenerated with `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, `npm run build-ts-bindings`, `npm run build-go-bindings` and `npm run build-dart-bindings`. All four succeed; the drift is committed.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four libraries agree across 1341 specs.
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: passes (new versions only).
- `npm run check-withdrawal-readiness`: passes.
- `npm run build-bundles && npm run check-bundles`: 1335 bundles verified. The new bundle's `defOrigins` names `rooms/_shared/0.1`.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features chat`: passes. With `--features "chat validate" --test conformance chat::direct`, all 7 tests pass: the 6 examples and `rejects_invalid_examples`.
- `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-rs --lib --test conformance --no-default-features --features "chat validate" -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `trust-tasks-ts`:
  - `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` passes;
  - `npm test` passes (126/126);
  - `npm run smoke` passes.
- `trust-tasks-go`:
  - `go build ./...` passes;
  - `go vet` on `./specs/chat/...` and `./trusttasks/...` passes;
  - `go test` on `./trusttasks/...`, `./smoke/...` and `./specs/chat/...` passes;
  - `gofmt -l specs/chat` reports nothing.
- `trust-tasks-dart`: `dart analyze --fatal-infos lib/specs/chat test` finds no issues. `dart test test/smoke_test.dart` passes.
- Not run locally:
  - the full `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`;
  - workspace-wide clippy;
  - the API-compatibility jobs.

title: feat(acl): purpose of use on grants and on memory reads (AclEntry 0.3; vta/memory put/delete/list 0.3, get 0.2)
body:
Wire shapes for purpose of use (VTI-ACL-100 – 110, trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#115). Implementation tracking: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2120.

An access-control entry says who may do what, where and until when, but not
what for. An agent granted a read of its principal's memory can use the content
for anything, and nothing records the use it intended. The VTI specification
now requires the purpose (VTI-ACL-100 – 110, trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#115);
these are the wire shapes.

acl/_shared/0.3 — AclEntry 0.3 adds one REQUIRED axis, `purposes`:
`{"scope": "any"}` or `{"scope": "listed", "purposes": [...]}` with at least
one `Purpose` — a lowerCamelCase name registered in the VTI purpose registry
(personalisation, taskExecution, analytics, modelTraining) or an absolute IRI
such as a DPV purpose. `any` never grants `modelTraining`. Delegated purposes
are a subset of the granter's. CONVENTIONS.md §8a maps a 0.2 entry onto 0.3
(`any`, the authority it already held, now stated) and §12 states the rules.

acl tasks on AclEntry 0.3: grant/0.3, update/0.3, show/0.3, revoke/0.3,
change-role/0.3, list/0.4. New errors on grant and update: `purposeOutsideDelegator`
(purposes wider than the granter's) and `purposeRefused` (policy will not grant
a purpose, refused by name, never dropped). update/0.3 replaces `purposes`
wholesale; narrowing it is an audited privilege reduction. `purposes` is never
redacted by show or list. No `extends`: a REQUIRED member on the entry cannot
be added to a version a 0.2 consumer still reads.

vta/memory put/0.3, delete/0.3, list/0.3, get/0.2 (each `extends` its
predecessor) add an optional `purpose` (`MemoryPurpose`, new in
vta/_shared/0.1/memory-record, a reference to acl's `Purpose`) and a
`purposeNotGranted` error that discloses nothing and is distinct from
`contextForbidden`. A recall, and a listing with values, is purpose-bound:
refused for a purpose the entry does not grant, or for none under an entry
listing several, and audited with its purpose either way. A write is not
purpose-bound, but a conflict that returns `currentValue` is: the value is
withheld unless the request's purpose is granted.

Data rooms (a room authority credential's `purposes`, VTI-ACL-110) are a
follow-up.

Samples in other specs that named the superseded acl versions now name the new
ones, with `purposes` on every embedded entry; prose links were moved by
`npm run fix-stale-references`.


## Out of scope
- **Data rooms**: `purposes` on a room authority credential and a `purpose` on room reads (VTI-ACL-110) come in a follow-up PR.
- `acl/swap-key/0.1` still returns an AclEntry 0.1 and is unchanged.

## Checks run locally
- `npm run validate`: 1363 specs; no stale references; 23 declared extensions checked.
- `npm run check-bindings`: Rust, TS, Go and Dart agree.
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: 23 released files changed only additively.
- `npm run build-bundles` + `check-bundles`: 1357 bundles verified.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs` (acl, with `-D warnings`): pass. Conformance tests for acl+vta: 589 pass; vtc+rooms+auth+vault: 1143 pass.
- trust-tasks-ts `npm test`: 126 pass. `go build ./...`: ok. `dart analyze` on the new modules: no issues.

title: ci(dependabot): hold webauthn-rs at 0.5 until 0.6 verifies Ed25519
body:
webauthn-rs-core 0.6 swapped OpenSSL for RustCrypto and stubbed out Ed25519: every OKP key is refused with `COSEKeyEDUnsupported`, at registration and at authentication. The VTC install flow requires an Ed25519 passkey, which becomes the admin's `did:key`, and every Ed25519 passkey already enrolled would stop verifying.

Once #2532 and #2535 are combined and ported so they build, **360 vtc-service tests fail**, all with `passkey registration failed: ED25519 and ED448 keys are not supported by this implementation`.

This holds `webauthn-rs*` at `< 0.6`, and 0.5 patches still come through. The port is on `wip/webauthn-0.6-port`. It is the `Base64UrlSafeData` → `Vec<u8>` change, plus `passkey_storage_compat`, a test showing that passkeys stored by 0.5 load under 0.6 with the same IDs and keys and are rewritten byte-identical. That branch is ready to land once upstream verifies Ed25519 again.

title: feat(acl): purpose of use on grants (VTI-ACL-100 – 110)
body:
An entry says who may do what, where and until when, but not what for. An
agent granted a read of its principal's memory, or of a room, can use the
content for anything, and nothing records the use it intended.

An entry now states `purposes`: `any`, or a non-empty list of purposes,
each a name registered in the new Appendix H (personalisation,
taskExecution, analytics, modelTraining) or an absolute IRI such as a DPV
purpose. Every request for a purpose-bound operation (a read of agent
memory, opening a room record, a conflict that returns content) names the
purpose it is for; the node refuses one the entry does not grant,
distinguishably from an access refusal, and records the purpose in the
audit row of every such read, served or refused.

- Absence is not a grant (VTI-ACL-008): an implementation writes `any`
  on every entry that predates this before serving a purpose-bound
  operation under it.
- `any` never grants `modelTraining`; it must be named (VTI-ACL-105).
- Delegated purposes are a subset (VTI-ACL-107); policy may refuse a
  purpose at write time, by name (VTI-ACL-108).
- A data room's authority credential may state `purposes` with the same
  meaning; one that does not grants `any` (VTI-ACL-110).
- VTI-VTA-044: an agent's entry SHOULD state the purposes its task needs.

Appendix H (Acknowledgements) becomes Appendix I.

Implementation tracking: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2120.

Release notes

Sourced from regorus's releases.

regorus-v0.14.0

Added

  • (compiler) [breaking] support fixed-arity host-await builtins (#857)
  • (bindings) expose compiled program builtin names (#853)

Fixed

  • (number) reject non-finite arithmetic results (#845)
  • (engine) keep query loop hoisting out of the shared compiled policy (#849)
  • (rvm) stop after compiling the final hoisted output loop (#850)
  • (number) reject non-finite values at supported ingress boundaries (#840)
  • (rvm) omit undefined values from set accumulation (#841)

Other

  • Fix ARM function naming in arity errors and enhance compile-error tests (#867)
  • Fix handling of quoted digit path segments in Azure Policy (#866)
  • Enhance Azure Policy tests for evaluation errors and short circuits (#865)
  • Preserve memory budgets across suspendable execution (#830)
  • fix dependency audits and vulnerable zip dependency (#844)
  • (deps) bump the github-actions group with 7 updates (#839)

Added

  • Expose compiled RVM builtin names through the C FFI and Program.GetBuiltinNames() in C#.

Changed

  • [breaking] Registered RVM HostAwait builtins now require a declared input arity and pass new calls to host handlers as ordered arrays; host responses remain unwrapped. The C# HostAwaitBuiltin(string) constructor was removed, a source and CLR binary break, and public Rust Compiler::alloc_register now returns Result<Register, SpannedCompilerError>; the registered-builtin API signature is unchanged. Explicit __builtin_host_await calls and previously compiled programs keep their raw payloads, which may themselves be arrays and cannot be identified by shape. Deploy a matching program/handler/native/managed bundle or provide application-owned legacy routing; no runtime handshake or universal compatibility handler is provided. New managed code with an older size-aware native library may have its count ignored and is unsupported. Roll back the matching prior package/handler/program bundle together.
  • [breaking] Float-promoting arithmetic now raises numeric overflow in <operation> instead of producing NaN or infinity, regardless of strict-builtin-error mode. Unlike OPA's wide-exponent arithmetic, finite results outside the binary64 range are rejected.

Release notes

Sourced from aws-lc-rs's releases.

aws-lc-rs v1.19.0

What's Changed

  • Add AES OFB, CFB8, and CFB1 modes by @​lokeswarivejju in aws/aws-lc-rs#1259
    • Adds OperatingMode::OFB, OperatingMode::CFB8, and OperatingMode::CFB1 for AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 through both the one-shot and streaming cipher APIs.
  • Add an on-demand AWS-LC self-test API by @​Elvrarin in aws/aws-lc-rs#1262
    • Adds aws_lc_rs::try_fips_self_test(), allowing applications to re-run all AWS-LC cryptographic algorithm self-tests without calling the sys crate through unsafe FFI. This does not re-run the module integrity test.
  • Add Keccak-256 digest support behind "unstable" feature flag by @​fabrice102 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1266
    • Adds aws_lc_rs::unstable::digest::KECCAK256 and KECCAK256_OUTPUT_LEN behind the unstable feature for use with the existing digest::digest and digest::Context APIs.
  • Add configurable RSA-PSS salt lengths by @​PaulDance in aws/aws-lc-rs#1267
    • Adds RsaPssSaltLength::{Digest, Max, Custom} and with_pss_salt_length builders on RsaSignatureEncoding and RsaParameters, covering signing and verification for both message and precomputed-digest APIs.
  • Implement Clone for signing key pairs by @​JakeHuneau in aws/aws-lc-rs#1277
    • rsa::KeyPair, EcdsaKeyPair, Ed25519KeyPair, and PqdsaKeyPair can now be cloned directly rather than wrapped in an Arc.
    • Clones share the immutable, reference-counted EVP_PKEY; key material is not duplicated, and a clone remains usable after the original is dropped.

Upstream AWS-LC

  • aws-lc-sys v0.47.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.12.0 (previously v5.11.0).
  • aws-lc-fips-sys v0.14.4 updates its bundled AWS-LC FIPS 4.2.0 snapshot with recent FIPS 4.x backports.

Build Improvements

  • Lower the minimum system-installed AWS-LC version to 4.2.0 by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1268
    • The default aws-lc-sys system-library path now accepts AWS-LC 4.2.0 or newer, previously 5.7.0, allowing use of a FIPS 4.x system library.
    • Enabling the unstable feature requires AWS-LC 5.7.0 or newer because unstable APIs currently include Keccak-256. Bundled-source builds are unaffected.
  • Share cc compiler detection across builds by @​johncarmack1984 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1273
    • Reuses compiler detection results across the main library build and compiler feature probes, reducing repeated compiler invocations during cold builds.

Issues Being Closed

  • Implement Clone for rsa::KeyPair -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1260
  • Expose AWS-LC FIPS on-demand self-test -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1261
  • Add a way to specify the RSA-PSS salt length -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1263

title: fix(vtc): a member can add a passkey with a hardware key when their DID is long
body:
Hi Glenn,

Thanks for all the work on VTI. I ran into a bug while adding a passkey in the member portal, and this started as my attempt at a small fix. It now includes your follow-up commits (a708b13ba, 55327b668).

## The problem

On the member portal, adding a passkey with a YubiKey failed with "Passkey creation was cancelled". The PIN was accepted, but the touch prompt never appeared. The same key worked on other VTCs.

The cause is the name we send to the authenticator. `register_start` passes the member's whole DID as WebAuthn `user.name` and `user.displayName`. A `did:webvh` is about 95 bytes, and this key rejects a `user.name` longer than 64 bytes. CTAP2 only requires authenticators to accept 64. The key answers `CTAP1_ERR_INVALID_LENGTH` before asking for a touch, and Chrome turns any such CTAP error into a generic `NotAllowedError`, which is where the "cancelled" message comes from.

## How I checked

I took the exact options the portal returns and ran them against the key directly (python-fido2) and through `navigator.credentials.create` in Chrome. Only the name changed between runs:

| `user.name` | CTAP result | Chrome |
|---|---|---|
| 95 bytes (the DID) | `INVALID_LENGTH` (0x03), no touch prompt | `NotAllowedError` |
| 64 bytes | OK | not run |
| 65 bytes | `INVALID_LENGTH` | not run |
| 59 bytes (output of the original version of this PR) | OK | OK |

A long `displayName` on its own was accepted; only `user.name` is limited. PIN, `credProtect`, `userVerification: required` and the algorithm list were identical in every run.

Environment: YubiKey 5 series, firmware 5.7.4, Chrome 156 on Linux. I only tried this one key, so other keys may behave differently.

## The change (current head)

- `vti_common::auth::passkey::AuthenticatorName` is the only way to build a name for an authenticator (`for_did`, `from_label`, `for_did_or_label`), and it is bounded to 64 **bytes**. `vti_common::auth::passkey::start_passkey_registration` is the one place a registration starts. The VTC wrapper, the three VTC DID-named paths (member portal, admin passkeys, step-up redeem), the VTC install ceremony and the VTA passkey-VM enrolment all go through it.
- Naming rules:
  - `did:webvh` / `did:tdw`: `<host:path> (<last 6 chars of SCID>)`, e.g. `dids.example.org:example-member-000001 (000000)`. If host+path doesn't fit it keeps both ends joined by `…`.
  - Any other DID: unchanged if 64 bytes or less, otherwise first 40 bytes + `…` + last 21 bytes.
  - VTA operator-supplied label: used as given; if over 64 bytes, `…` plus its tail.
  - All cuts are on char boundaries. The same name is applied to `user.name` and `user.displayName`.
- The VTA's old `display_name_for` is removed. It capped at 64 characters, not bytes, and its long branch produced 66 bytes, so it had the same bug.
- The private copy of `authenticator_name` in `step_up_passkey.rs` is removed.

The name is display only. The account is still identified by `user.id` and this service's own record, as before.

Behaviour changes to be aware of: a webvh name now carries a SCID fragment and shows host+path rather than the first-40/last-16 form, so names differ from what the step-up flow showed before, and from what the VTA produced.

## Testing

- CI is green on the current head.
- Glenn reports vtc-service + vtc-client 3598/3598, vti-common and vta-service passkey tests, workspace clippy `-D warnings` and doc tests all passing locally.
- YubiKey check on the current head (55327b668): I ran a local test VTC built from this head and added a passkey from Chrome with the same YubiKey. It worked: the touch prompt appeared and the passkey registered. The server returned `user.name` and `user.displayName` of `first.example.com:members:alice (2bwPSE)` (40 bytes) for an 88-byte `did:webvh`, where the original code sent all 88. This used the repo's `TestVtc` harness with a wallet-proven member session, not the real wallet sign-in, and not a deployed community portal.
- I have **not** run it against a deployed portal such as the one where I first hit the bug; that is still open.
- Test gaps I'd like covered (also requested in my comment above): `did:webvh:<scid>:` with an empty tail and `did:webvh:<scid>` with no colon; host+path of exactly 64 and 65 bytes; exact-output assertions for 2-byte and 3-byte characters; and one test that the options returned by the three DID-named call sites carry the short name.

## Open questions

- Over-length webvh with a long host: the host head is capped at about 26 bytes, so hosts longer than that are cut inside the host. Is that acceptable?
- An over-long VTA `label` keeps its tail; for free text, keeping the head may read better.

Thanks for taking a look.

Brendan

title: fix(messaging/mux): direct authentication is compared with keys of its own relationship; grantsExpiring for every unrenewed grant
body:
Two fixes to the draft `messaging/mux` specs, found while implementing them in the Affinidi mediator. Both are prose-only: no schema, binding or digest changes.

## 1. Unknown-key rule: compare like with like (`grant/0.1`)

The rule compared "the DIDComm authcrypt sender key" with "the verification methods that signed [the member's] active grants". Authcrypt proves a `keyAgreement` key, while grants are signed with `authentication` keys. The two sets hold different keys, so taken literally **every direct login of a member DID suspends all its grants**.

The known keys are now two sets, both read from the active grants:
- **Signing keys:** the `authentication` methods that signed the grants. These are compared with grant and attach signatures, and with the TSP sender VID's signing key.
- **Key-agreement keys:** the member's `keyAgreement` methods recorded, by key material, when each grant was stored. These are compared with the DIDComm authcrypt sender key.

So a member that already logs in directly with a key it listed when it granted doesn't suspend its own grants. A key added since then (a new controller's key, or a rotation) is unknown. That matches the rule's intent: it detects a hand-over.

## 2. `grantsExpiring`: the mediator can't see a renewal opt-in (`notice/0.1`)

Producer rule 5 said to send `grantsExpiring` "only for grants whose renewal the application did not opt into". That opt-in is client-side and never reaches the mediator. The rule now says:
- send it for every grant past about 75% of its lifetime that is still active and not replaced;
- the notice MAY be stored lazily: at the principal's next authentication or connection, or on a periodic check while it's connected;
- it is never stored for a grant that is expired, revoked, suspended or replaced.

The consumer rule now says a client that renews a grant itself discards the notice for it.

Both are draft specs, so this changes them in place without a version bump.

title: fix(vta-service): app-state refuses a context id that is not a context path
body:
Application state is stored as `app:{context}:{namespace}:{key}` (and the
`appv:`/`appc:`/`appt:` siblings). Its prefixes are unambiguous only
because neither a context id nor a namespace contains `:`. The namespace
was checked; the context id was not, and access does not imply a
well-formed id: an unrestricted admin may name any context, including
`acme:x`, whose rows then sit under `acme`'s prefix, where `acme`'s
listings read them and `acme`'s purge erases them.

Every app-state operation now checks the context id against the context
path grammar (`validate_context_path`) before touching the store: get,
get_many, put, put_many, delete, list, reap and purge. Memory already did
this for its own calls (#2115); this moves the rule to the store so every
caller inherits it.

The tombstone sweeper skips, with a warning, any rows written under such
an id before this change, rather than stopping the sweep of the rest.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

## Tests
- New: `a_context_id_that_is_not_a_context_path_is_refused` — put, get, list and purge refuse `acme:x`, `acme:openvtc`, empty, leading-slash and empty-segment ids, and `acme`'s own row is untouched.
- Local: workspace nextest (7191 passed), doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt. `vtc-service` does not depend on `vta-service`.

title: fix(pnm): rooms put writes provenance on open rooms, and rooms read shows it
body:
`pnm rooms put` refused --basis, --confidence, --cite-*, --purpose,
--use-note and --valid-until on an `open` room, on the belief that the key
holder's `rooms/keys/act` would not carry them. It signs the cleartext the
producer built, unaltered (act Recipient item 6), and `rooms/records/put`
0.3 and later accept these members in an open room's cleartext. So an
open-room write now carries them, and gets `basis: declared` by default
as a sealed write already does (`rooms/records/put/0.5` Producer item 9:
a writer SHOULD set `basis`). No room profile governs them.

The members are built once (`RecordProvenance::members`) and checked
against the specification before anything is sent; sealed bodies take the
same values, so both tiers spell them alike.

`pnm rooms read` now shows the basis and expiry line `pnm rooms get`
shows, marked unsigned on an open room. Both name their keys, which is the
explicit request on which a reader shows an expired record, marked
(`RecordValidUntil`).

Closes #2117.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

## Tests
- New unit tests in `vta-cli-common`: open and sealed writes carry the same provenance members; unstated provenance adds nothing; invalid provenance is refused before sending.
- Local: workspace nextest (7193 passed), doctests, vtc-service/vtc-client (3674 passed), clippy `-D warnings`, fmt.

Changelog

Sourced from @​openvtc/trust-tasks's changelog.

0.28.19 — 2026-11-06

Added

  • vtc/badges: Member badges — community badges backed by groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos, Open Badges credentials (vtc/badges/*/0.1) (#1052)

  • feat(vtc/badges): member badges — community badges backed by groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos, Open Badges credentials (vtc/badges/*/0.1)

    A new family for the VTI Community Badges chapter (VTI-BDG-001 – 095): pictures with a name a member earns, holds and shows on their directory card.

    • A community badge is backed by a community group: create creates the group as vtc/groups/create does, its managers are the badge's owners, its members the holders; requests reuse vtc/groups/join and requests/decide, owners reuse managers/add and remove. The shared Group record gains an optional badgeId (additive).
    • An award is an offer until its recipient accepts (awards/offer → mine/accept or mine/decline); mine/accept issues the badge credential as the group's DID first and records the membership after. mine/accept states the credential profile: an Open Badges 3.0 OpenBadgeCredential with the community as the Achievement's creator and endorser, one evidence entry per award; short-lived with no status inside the community, long-lived with a slot in the community's own status set where holders may show it outside.
    • Hidden is portal-only (mine/hide, mine/show): walls, holders/list and counts leave a hidden holder out; awards/list shows owners the hidden mark.
    • Kudos badges (kudos/give, kudos/list): given by any member to any other within per-giver limits, each giving an award of its own; promote turns one into a community badge.
    • settings/show and settings/update hold the community's switches and limits.
    • images/upload and images/get mirror the directory's picture pipeline.

0.28.18 — 2026-11-05

Added

  • vtn/registry: Check a party against the network's trust registry through the network, and the registry status for administrators (#1050)

vtn/registry/check/0.1 lets anyone ask a network to ask its trust registry whether a party is published as its member, returning the registry's own signed answer verbatim, so a verifier with no DIDComm or TSP session (a browser, or a registry that serves no HTTPS) can still check the registry rather than take the network's word for it. Unreachable is indeterminate, never not a member.

vtn/registry/status/0.1 lets an administrator read the registry, the writer and whether it is connected, the last reconcile, and every record compared with what the entries project (ok, missing, stale, wrong).

  • vta/collection: Settings/show and settings/set — collection by default per trust context, stored and changed at run time (#1049)

Collection by default was one operator setting, off unless enabled (VTI-NTF-093). The VTI specification withdraws that in favour of a setting of each trust context, enabled unless disabled there (VTI-NTF-094 – VTI-NTF-098):

title: vtc-service-v0.27.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A member can rotate onto a did:webs (VTI-MEM-041, VTI-KEY-003) ([#2517](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2517))

Member rotation accepted did:key, did:webvh and did:scid. It now accepts
  did:webs. A did:webs document has no `#key-0`: its keys are the KERI key
  state's, identified by their CESR encoding, all in `authentication`. The
  document resolves only when the key event log verifies (VTI-LNK-052), so the
  new-DID signature is accepted from any key the document authorises for
  authentication (at most 16 are tried), each through the same purpose and
  controller check as the did:webvh path (VTI-MEM-041). A ConditionalProof2022
  entry is skipped; it is not a key.

  Re-pins vtc/members/rotate/0.1, which gained `did:scid` and `did:webs` in
  its response `method` enum in place (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1064).
  That also fixes rotation onto a did:scid, whose successful reply
  (`method: "did:scid"`) failed the published schema and reached the member
  as an internal error.

- **vtc**: The badge picture builder finds icons by meaning, and browses them all ([#2511](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2511))

Find an icon matches lucide's tags as well as names ("insect" finds the
  bug, "prize" the trophy), names first; Browse all icons opens every icon
  in a dialog with the same search, uncapped. Tags come from lucide-static
  0.469.0 (ISC, dev dependency pinned to lucide-react's release), bundled
  only into the lazy badge-icons chunk.

- **vtc**: A member's badge wall says when each badge was earned ([#2502](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2502))

wall/show already answers since and latestAt; the portal used them only
  to sort. A tile now reads "Earned <date>", or "Since <date>" for a badge
  held more than once with the latest in its title.

- **vtc**: The community issues the badge credential, named (VTI-BDG-060, 064, 080) ([#2501](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2501))

A verifier outside the community knows the community, not a badge group's
  DID, and the embedded endorsement never named the group. The community
  now signs the OpenBadgeCredential: issuer and the Achievement's creator
  are its named Profile (DID, name, public url); credentialSchema names the
  OB3 JSON Schema; evidence dates are to the second in UTC, with no
  unregistered urn:vtc id. No endorsement is embedded, the group's VAC no
  longer rides with the offer, and the registry record names the community.
  The console's badge details show the group's DID and the issuer's, each
  to copy or scan.

- **vtc**: The badge picture builder searches lucide's whole icon set ([#2499](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2499))

Sixteen icons are still offered first; *Find an icon* searches all of
  lucide's (about 1,500) by name, every word of the search in the name,
  showing at most 60 at a time. The whole set is its own chunk (about
  104 kB gzipped), loaded only when someone searches. The picture is made
  and sent as before (VTI-BDG-050).

- **vtc**: Authorize another key from the console through the wallet, for an administrator whose identity lives in their VTA ([#2498](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2498))

`cnm access authorize-key` signs the `auth/signing-key/authorize/0.1` a key
  such as vtc-mcp's needs to act with an administrator's standing, but only with
  a key `cnm` holds. An administrator whose identity is a persona in their VTA
  had no way to sign it, so their assistant could not act for them, and a
  step-up the assistant hit could not be answered from their wallet (it names
  `cnm`'s key as the subject).

  Console signing keys → Authorize another key builds the same document — the
  named did:key, the identity, `scope: console`, an optional label, the
  delegation's expiry (1 – 30 days) — usable for an hour, and has the wallet
  sign it as the identity. Nothing is sent from the console: the authorization
  is copied or downloaded and given to the key's holder, which enrols itself
  with `auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2` (`vtc_enrol_signing_key`). The VTC's checks
  are unchanged (single-use, only the named key, terms exactly the enrolment's,
  not signed by a delegated key). The console refuses a non-did:key, an
  out-of-range expiry, the identity itself and this browser's own key before
  asking the wallet, and warns against reusing a key across communities.

  vtc-mcp's `vtc_enrol_signing_key` now points at the console as well as `cnm`;
  its operator page, README, skill and the console guide say how, and the
  "not built yet" items for it and for the wallet step-up reader (plugin #427)
  are gone.

- **vtc-mcp**: Warn when an agent key is reused at a second community; say why one key per community (VTI-KEY-005, VTI-KEY-006) ([#2495](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2495))

* feat(vtc-mcp): warn when an agent key is reused at a second community; say why one key per community (VTI-KEY-246)

  A community records every DID that signs in to it, enrols as an approver or
  holds a delegation. Two communities that hold the same one can tell that one
  person stands behind both by comparing their records, and neither can see the
  reuse from its own. Only the key holder can.

  - vtc-mcp keeps an owner-only local note of the communities each agent DID

    ~/.local/state/vtc-mcp; DIDs only). A key pointed at a second community is

    warns and never refuses; --no-key-reuse-check turns it off.
  - docs/03-vtc/admin-access.md §3.1a and vtc-mcp.md §2.7: use a different
    approver, administrator and agent key at each community. The VTA browser
    plugin already mints one approver per community; keys carried by hand are
    the risk.
  - The console's approver panels, the /admin/enrol-approver page and
    `vtc admin enrol-approver` say the same in one line.

The mockups' builder for members without artwork: a banner (with the badge's

- **vtc**: Badge claim codes for events and the automatic badge counts (VTI-BDG-015, 025 – 027) ([#2494](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2494))

Phase 4 of member badges, from the chapter (dtgwg-vti-spec #108) and the wire
  (trust-tasks-tf #1059), pinned here.

  Claim codes (`vtc/badges/claims/{create,list,withdraw,redeem}/0.1`,
  `badges::claims`):
  - An owner (or `vtc.badges.admin`) issues a code for a community badge with a
    label, a time (at most 90 days ahead) and a claim limit. The code is 256 bits
    from the CSPRNG, answered once; the community keeps only its SHA-256 digest
    (`bcdig:`), the record (`bclaim:`, indexed by badge) and a marker per member
    who redeemed it.
  - A member redeeming it is admitted as on an approved request (VTI-BDG-024):
    the claim is reserved - counted and marked under the badges lock - before the
    credential is issued, and released if the key holder fails, so a limit is
    never exceeded; then `credential::issue_with_new_award` issues the badge
    credential with a new accepted award (giver = the code's issuer) as evidence,
    offers it, and records the membership. Unknown, expired, exhausted,
    withdrawn and retired-badge codes answer `codeInvalid` alike;
    `alreadyClaimed` and `alreadyHeld` refuse a second claim.
  - Withdrawing stops a code; claims made stand. Retiring a badge withdraws its
    codes. `claims/list` never answers a code.

  Rule counts (VTI-BDG-015): an automatic badge's rule may read
  `kudosReceived`, `ideasSelected` and `electionTickets` with `atLeast` and
  `count`. `groups::check_badge_rule` admits them; `check_rule` (any other group)
  refuses them. `badges::rule_counts` counts from the community's own records at
  each recompute - accepted kudos awards, selected ideas by proposer entry,
  tickets by the member's current DID (never whether a ballot was cast).
  Accepting kudos, selecting an idea and issuing a ticket kick the dynamic
  sweeper (VTI-DIR-072).

- **vtc**: Badge groups published to the trust registry as issuers the community recognises (VTI-BDG-080) ([#2491](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2491))

Where the community publishes to a trust registry, each active community badge's
  group is published as one TRQP authorization record under the community's
  authority: `{entity: the group's DID, action: issue, resource: the badge's
  Achievement id}` - the identifier every credential of the badge names - with
  `context: {kind: "vtcBadgeIssuer", badgeId}`. An outside verifier asks the
  registry whether the community stands behind the issuer of a badge, and the
  community's status set whether the award still stands. The record never carries
  the badge's name or picture, so a badge kept inside is not described to the
  world (VTI-BDG-050). Kudos badges have no group and are not published.

- **vtc**: Hand a delegated key's step-up to the person's wallet (VTI-LNK-125 – VTI-LNK-131) ([#2490](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2490))

A key a person delegated, such as their assistant's over vtc-mcp, can
  redeem an operation-bound step-up but must never make one (VTI-APV-015).

- **vtc**: A holder shows a badge award outside the community — share, unshare, the verification location and the baked picture (VTI-BDG-070, 071) ([#2489](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2489))

* feat(vtc): a holder shows a badge award outside the community — share, unshare, the verification location and the baked picture (VTI-BDG-070, 071)

  Serves `vtc/badges/awards/share/0.1` and `unshare/0.1` (pinned in #2487) and
  answers the holder's own awards on `vtc/badges/show/0.1` (`myAwards`,
  trust-tasks-tf #1057, refreshed here).

  Sharing is the holder's own choice, award by award, for a badge marked
  `shareableOutside`:

  - `badges::share`: a 256-bit token generated for the share and derived from
    nothing (`bshare:<token>` -> award, `Award.shared` with the locations and
    `since`); a repeat share answers the same locations; `unshare` discards the
    token, revokes nothing, and a later share answers new ones.
  - What is served is the holder's credential exactly as issued: each time
    `credential::issue` signs one in the outside regime it is kept at
    `bcred:<badge>:<entry>`, so a repeat award or a renewal is served at the same
    location (share item 10). A holder whose credential predates that is issued
    it again on their first share (outside the lock, as every issue is).
  - `GET /badges/shared/<token>`: the credential (`application/vc+ld+json`) to a
    verifier; to a browser, a page saying what the community verifies of it
    (issued by it, in its validity period, its slot in the community's
    revocation list clear), with its own CSP. `GET .../image.png`: the badge's
    picture as a PNG with the credential baked into an `iTXt` chunk
    (`openbadgecredential`, Open Badges 3.0 baking). Unauthenticated,
    parent-root, let through the host-surface gate; neither names another
    holder or a count (VTI-BDG-071).
  - A share ends with `unshare`, a take-back (`awards/revoke`), retiring the badge
    and the holder's departure (`badges::on_departure`); `share::resolve`
    re-checks the award, the token and the badge on every request, so a stopped
    share answers the same `404` as a token never issued.
  - Refusals as declared: `badgesOff`, `notFound` (unknown, another's and not
    accepted alike), `notShareable` (`insideOnly` | `kudos` | `retired`),
    `publicLocationUnavailable` (no `public_url`).
  - `settle_after_revoke`'s re-issue is factored out as `reissue`, which now
    re-reads each award under the badges lock before recording the credential on
    it, so it never writes back a stale award (and its share) over a newer one.

- **vti-specs-vtc**: Pin vtc/badges/awards/{share,unshare} 0.1 (badges shown outside, VTI-BDG-070) ([#2487](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2487))

* feat(vti-specs-vtc): pin vtc/badges/awards/{share,unshare} 0.1 (badges shown outside, VTI-BDG-070)

  Pins the two tasks from trust-tasks-tf #1054: a holder shows an accepted award

  #1054 also added `AwardShare` and the optional `Award.shared` to

  (awards/{list,offer,revoke,withdraw}, kudos/{give,list}, mine/{accept,decline,list});
  `trust-tasks update` takes their new bytes. Additive: no field VTI sends today
  changed.

  vti-mcp-common's guard census classifies `share` and `unshare` as mutating, as

  Nothing serves the two tasks yet; the handlers follow.

- **vtc**: The public Achievement document and picture of a badge shown outside (VTI-BDG-050, 051, 071) ([#2484](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2484))

A badge its holders may show outside now has its two public artefacts at
  the stable locations its credentials name, served to any Open Badges
  verifier without authentication:

  - `GET /badges/<badgeId>`: the Achievement document
    (`application/ld+json`), with the community as creator and the
    community's endorsement, as the credentials embed it.
  - `GET /badges/<badgeId>/image`: the badge's picture, the community's own
    re-encoding.

  Both are parent-root routes beside the identity logs and pass the
  host-surface gate on every host (`badges::public::is_badge_artefact_path`).
  They name no holder and no count (VTI-BDG-071). A badge kept inside the
  community answers the same 404 as an unknown one: its picture stays
  members-only through vtc/badges/images/get (VTI-BDG-050). The credential of
  a shareable badge now names its picture by that public location; an
  inside badge's still names it by digest.

  Sharing an award (vtc/badges/awards/share|unshare, the verification page
  and the baked image) follows once those tasks are published
  (trust-tasks-tf #1054).

- **vtc**: Badges shown outside — the long-lived credential in the community's status set, and the community's endorsement embedded (VTI-BDG-060 – 063) ([#2482](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2482))

The outside credential regime for member badges, and the one piece of
  VTI-BDG-060 the first build left out.

  - `shareableOutside` is accepted on `create` and `promote` for a community
    badge (refused on a kudos badge as before) and fixed from then on. Such a
    badge's credential is long-lived (`settings.credentialValidDays`, default
    730) and carries a `credentialStatus` slot in the **community's** own
    revocation list — the set every community credential uses, allocated at
    random — one slot per badge and holder (`bslot:<badge>:<entry>`), reused by
    every re-issue and renewal. Never a set of the badge's or the group's own
    (VTI-BDG-062, VTI-CRD-014). The list's credential is the community's while
    the badge credential's issuer is the group: the W3C Bitstring Status List
    Recommendation compares no issuers and says the two "might differ".
  - The bit is flipped when the holder's last award is taken back, when the
    badge is retired, and when the holder departs (VTI-BDG-063:
    `credential::{revoke_holder, revoke_all_holders, revoke_departed}`); an
    inside-only credential still lapses with its renewal.
  - Every badge credential now embeds the community's Open Badges 3.0
    `EndorsementCredential` of the Achievement, signed by the VTA as the
    community on first need and kept on the badge (VTI-BDG-060), so an outside
    verifier sees who stands behind the issuer from the credential alone.
  - Console: "May be shown outside" on the new-badge form and on promotion;
    the credential's life in the settings.

  Sharing an award outside (`awards/share|unshare`, the public verification
  page and the baked image) is the next phase and needs the Trust Task family
  first; this build issues the credential such a badge needs.

- **vtc**: Member badges in the console and the member portal (VTI-BDG-001 – 095) ([#2479](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2479))

The pages over the vtc/badges/* 0.1 family #2477 serves.

  Console (Community → Badges, `plugins/badges.tsx` over `lib/badges.ts`):
  every badge the administrator or owner may see; the settings — on or off,

  Portal (`#/badges`, `members/Badges.tsx` over `members/badges-api.ts`):

  A member's directory card shows their wall, pinned first, with the kudos
