title: fix(vtc): election records change under one write lock, and an end in flight is not asked twice
body:
fix(vtc): election records change under one write lock, and an end in flight is not asked twice

Every change to a stored election was a read, a change and a write of the whole
record, with nothing between writers - and several held a record across a call
to the ballot box and wrote it back whole (`cancel`, `deliver_registration`).
Three writers run at once in practice: a task handler, a board's closing in the
background (VTI-BRD-006) and the elections sweeper's tick. Whichever wrote last
erased what the others had written. Observed: a board closed while the sweeper
was keeping a checkpoint lost the election's `pendingEnd`, so the election was
never ended and stayed open for voting with nothing left to retry it; and a
close racing a checkpoint lost the final board head, which a deleted board's
tombstone must keep (VTI-BRD-008).

- `elections::store::update` applies a change to the record as stored now,
  under one write lock held only from the read to the write - never across a
  call to the ballot box (R1.3). Every writer in `elections` uses it and sets
  only the fields it decided; `store::put` is left for a record nobody else can
  be writing.
- An end in flight holds a lease: `record_end` and `request_end` make the
  pending end due one backoff later, so the sweeper retries only an attempt
  that never answered, and one election is never ended twice at once.

Found as the intermittent CI failure of
`board_tasks::vti_brd_008_a_deletion_waits_for_the_final_head` (#2486) on
#2487. Under load (`--stress-count 40 --test-threads 16`) the board deletion
tests failed about one run in six before and pass 40/40 after; the test
helper now reports the record it gave up on.

title: feat(vtc): the public Achievement document and picture of a badge shown outside (VTI-BDG-050, 051, 071)
body:
## What

The first part of phase 3b of member badges (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-badges.md`): the **public artefacts of a badge its holders may show outside** (VTI-BDG-051), at the stable locations its credentials already name since #2482.

| Route | Answers |
|---|---|
| `GET /badges/<badgeId>` | The Achievement document (`application/ld+json`): name, description, criteria, the community as `creator`, the community's `EndorsementCredential`, the picture by its public location |
| `GET /badges/<badgeId>/image` | The picture, the community's own re-encoding (`directory::images::get` over `badge_images`) |

## Invariants

- **Unauthenticated and foreign-protocol**: Open Badges verifiers fetch these over plain HTTPS, so they are parent-root REST routes beside `/.well-known/did.jsonl`, `/room-dids/…` and `/group-dids/…`, outside the `/v1` mount and its Trust Task door, and let through the host-surface gate on every host (`badges::public::is_badge_artefact_path`, beside `is_group_did_log_path`).
- **No holder, no count** (VTI-BDG-071): neither artefact carries anything about who holds the badge.
- **Inside badges stay inside** (VTI-BDG-050): a badge not marked `shareableOutside` answers the same `404` as an unknown or malformed id, so its picture is shown only to active members through `vtc/badges/images/get`.
- The credential of a shareable badge now names its picture by the public location; an inside badge's still names it by `urn:sha256:`.

## Tests

`tests/it/badges.rs`: a shareable badge's Achievement document and picture are served with the right types, the document names the community as creator and the picture by its public location and nothing about holders; an inside badge and an unknown id are both `404` at both routes; the shareable badge's credential names the public picture, the inside one's the digest. Unit test on the path gate.

## Next

`vtc/badges/awards/share|unshare` (specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1054): once released and pinned, the verification page and the baked image per award, at unguessable locations.

title: Add the step-up trigger-link flow: a delegated key's refused operation, approved from the person's wallet (VTI-LNK-125 – VTI-LNK-131)
body:
## Why

A person's assistant can act for them with a key they delegated, as the VTC's MCP bridge does. Such a party can redeem an operation-bound step-up (VTI-APV-015), and must never make one.

Today the step-up request reaches only that party, inline in the refusal. That party cannot gather the person's factor. It also cannot pass the request to the person's wallet, because the inline request carries no proof. So every step-up-gated act is out of reach for a delegated key.

## What

- **The `step-up` flow** (`/vti/flow/step-up/0.1`) is added to the registry (VTI-LNK-046). The note that step-up would be named later is removed.
- **VTI-LNK-125 – VTI-LNK-131** cover the flow:
  - The expiry is at most the hand-off's own expiry, and at most 300 seconds.
  - The service issues a handle only in the inline refusal, to the party that sent the operation. It answers each handle once.
  - That party is the link's producer, and shows the link only to the subject.
  - The reader acts only for a service already in its records, and only for the subject's identity there.
  - The reader verifies the service's signed request and recomputes the binding from the returned operation. It shows the operation itself.
  - The reader answers as the subject, directly to the service, never through the link's producer.
- **New reasons:** `not-in-records`, `not-the-subject` and `binding-mismatch` map to `invalid`. `step-up-gone` maps to `expired`.
- **VTI-APV-015** now states that the caller is the subject the operation acts as. A delegated key redeems the subject's re-authentication but never makes it. A node may deliver the challenge to the subject's own agent.
- **Examples:** a `step-up` link and its outcomes are added.

The Trust Task used is `auth/step-up/requests/show/0.1`, in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1056.

`npm run render` completes cleanly.

title: fix(vtc): a board is deleted only once its closed elections' final heads are kept (VTI-BRD-008)
body:
fix(vtc): a board is deleted only once its closed elections' final heads are kept (VTI-BRD-008)

Closing a board ends its elections in the background: `elections::ops::close`
records the election closed, then reads the ballot box's final board head.
`vtc/boards/delete` counted the election ended as soon as it read `closed`, so a
deletion in that moment kept a tombstone without the final head - the one a
voter checks a receipt against once only the tombstone is left.

A closed or tallied election now counts as ended for a deletion only once its
pending end is settled and its final head is kept; a cancelled one as before.
The sweeper keeps the head on its next pass, so the window is short and a
deletion inside it answers `electionsRunning`.

This was the cause of the intermittent CI failure of
`vti_brd_009_a_tombstone_is_read_by_members_until_it_is_removed`: its one
sweeper pass could settle the pending end and return before keeping the head,
and the deletion then raced the background close. The tests now run the sweeper
until the head is kept, and a new test holds the refusal.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.8
body:
### Added

- **vtc/badges**: Awards/share and awards/unshare — a holder shows an award outside the community (vtc/badges/awards/{share,unshare}/0.1) ([#1054](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1054))

* feat(vtc/badges): awards/share and awards/unshare — a holder shows an award outside the community (vtc/badges/awards/{share,unshare}/0.1)

  The two tasks the VTC badges design note lists for showing a badge outside
  the community (VTI-BDG-070 – 072), completing the vtc/badges/* 0.1 family.

  - `vtc/badges/awards/share/0.1`: the holder of an accepted award of a badge
    the community marked `shareableOutside` asks, and the community answers the
    public locations it serves the award at — a verification location that
    answers the credential exactly as issued with its status, and a baked image
    where it serves one. Locations are the community's, unguessable (≥ 128
    bits, never derived from the award), idempotent on a repeat, and disclose
    no other holder nor a count (VTI-BDG-071). They stop serving on unshare,
    take-back, retire and departure. Codes: badgesOff, notFound (unknown,
    another member's, not accepted — alike), notShareable (insideOnly | kudos
    | retired), publicLocationUnavailable.
  - `vtc/badges/awards/unshare/0.1`: stops it; the locations answer as ones
    that never existed; idempotent; not a revocation. Codes: badgesOff,
    notFound.
  - `_shared/0.1/badge.schema.json`: `AwardShare` and the optional
    `Award.shared` (verificationUrl, bakedImageUrl?, since) — additive.

  Both are acts of the member: a portal key the member authorized for
  `vtc/badges` under auth/oob/grant/0.3 may sign them (VTI-BDG-095).

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.19`) | `0.10.18` → `0.10.19` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.28` → `0.9.29` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(vtc-mcp): report a delegation made in an earlier run, and read a home-relative authorization path
body:
Two defects found by the first live run of `vtc-mcp` against a test community (`first-vtc`), where a delegated bridge key enrolled, read the access list and groups, and defined and retired a directory field.

- **`vtc_status` forgot the delegation across restarts.** `delegationOf` was set only by an enrolment in the same run, though the delegation lives at the community and the bridge kept acting with it. The bridge now asks `auth/signing-key/list` at start-up and records the identity of its own **active** delegation. An unenrolled key is refused by the community and nothing is recorded. Verified live: a fresh bridge reports the existing delegation over TSP.
- **`vtc_enrol_signing_key` could not read `~/…`**, the path its own suggested `cnm` command writes. It now expands a leading `~/`.

Tests: +2 (home-relative path expansion; a delegation learnt at start — own active key recorded, another key's / a revoked one / a refusal not). 29 bridge tests pass; clippy clean.

title: feat(vtc-mcp): act as yourself — wallet sign-in for members, a signing-key delegation for administrators
body:
The bridge signs in as **you**, through your wallet, the way the member portal and the operator console sign you in — so your own assistant acts with your standing instead of an enrolled agent entry. No new ACL row, no duplicate member or role.

## How it works

The bridge keeps running with its own key (`vtc-mcp --mint-did-key`, enrolled nowhere). It becomes the *starter* of the trigger-link sign-in (`auth/oob/*`):

1. `vtc_sign_in` (audience `member`, or `admin`) opens a request signed by the bridge's key and returns the trigger link.
2. You open it in the browser holding your wallet, or scan it; the wallet shows the community, the starter (`vtc-mcp/<version>`) and a match number.
3. `vtc_sign_in_finish` answers with the same match number to compare, then with the session once you approve. `vtc_sign_in_cancel` withdraws a request; `vtc_status` reports `signedInAs`.

What redeem yields is the community's existing behaviour, unchanged:

- **member**: the portal's delegation is armed for the bridge's key, so it signs the portal's task families (directory, boards, badges, …) as you until the grant's expiry, with your standing read fresh on every call.
- **admin**: a console session for the bridge's key, so `auth/whoami` answers for it.

## What lands

- **`vtc-client`**: `signin` — the portal's sign-in config (refused when it names another community), the trigger link (contract C1), request, redeem polls with the match number, cancel; always over the HTTPS door, presenting the portal's origin and naming the starter, as the portal page does; `VtcError::SignIn`. A session client now keeps its own key for that door (admin verbs still go over the session).
- **`vtc-mcp`**: the three tools (`src/signin.rs`), `signedInAs` in status, docs (operator page §3.0 and §11, README, skill, `CLAUDE.md`).
- **`vti-mcp-common`**: the starter's three `auth/oob` steps are `ReadOnly` — nothing happens without the person's approval, and a `--read-only` bridge still needs to sign in to read as them. The approver's steps are unchanged.
- **Fix, from phase 3**: the bridge now enables the SDK's `acl-setup` (and `crypto-provider`), as `cnm` and `vta-mcp` do. Without it a freshly minted `did:key` has no mediator ACL, and the mediator silently drops the message types it was not told to accept — the bridge would connect and then hear nothing.

## Administrators: a signing-key delegation (second commit)

An administrator's assistant gets the administrator's full standing the way the operator console's key does — a signing-key delegation of the identity (`auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2`), authorized by the identity's own signed `auth/signing-key/authorize/0.1`. No specification change: this is the enrolment the console already uses, with the signature produced by `cnm` instead of the in-page wallet.

1. `vtc_enrol_signing_key` with no arguments answers with the bridge's DID and the command to run.
2. `cnm access authorize-key <bridge-did> --label vtc-mcp --expires 30d --out <file>` signs the authorization offline with the profile's administrative key. It states its own `expiresAt` (an hour by default) so it survives the hand-off, and is single-use.
3. `vtc_enrol_signing_key` with the file: the bridge refuses an authorization for any other key before sending, then enrols with exactly the authorized terms plus the authorization.

No access-control entry is created. The key acts with the administrator's standing read at every call, expires within 30 days, is listed and revoked on its own, and never answers a step-up or signs a `task-consent/decision`. `vtc_status` reports `delegationOf`.

## Not built (operator page §11)

- **An administrator whose identity lives only in a wallet**, with no `cnm` profile: nothing outside the console's own page signs the authorization yet. The fix is a console action that signs the same authorization for a key you name.
- **Step-up through the wallet**, for authority-changing acts, and **approving someone else's action**: both need the person's own factor, which a delegated key never has. The bridge reports the refusal; the console, wallet or `cnm consent approve` finish it.
- An `admin` wallet sign-in is a console session only, and idles out (15 minutes by default).

## Tests

Second commit: `cnm` +2 (the authorization is the identity's signed terms, schema-valid, alive for the hand-off; refusals for a non-`did:key` and for the identity itself); `vtc-mcp` +1 (the enrol tool names the command, refuses another key's authorization unsent, and sends the terms plus the authorization signed by the bridge's key). 27 bridge and 150 `cnm` tests pass.


`vtc-client` +2 (the trigger link and encoding; audience and code reading). `vtc-mcp` +2 over a scripted loopback community: a sign-in opens as the portal would (config, request signed by the bridge's key with the portal origin, user agent and audience), returns the match number once, then the session, and status reports it; a declined sign-in clears the request, and a portal naming another community is refused before a request opens. 26 bridge and 67 client tests pass; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are green.

Not yet exercised against a live community or wallet.

title: feat(notifications): vta/notifications/deposit, vtc/notifications/{list,show,relay}, and relay-depth, proof-purpose and withdrawal fixes
body:
Follow-up to #1012, implementing trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#95 (VTI-NTF-006, 025, 034, 047, 054 – 056, 070 – 074), from what the first implementation (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2397) found.

## New tasks

| Task | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `vta/notifications/deposit/0.1` | A client that receives a notify/relay for a DID whose keys its VTA holds (a persona DID whose mediator socket the client holds) hands it to the VTA **exactly as received** (opaque `document`, proof intact). The VTA verifies it exactly as a direct delivery, applies its acceptance policy to the party that delivered the document and **never** the depositing client, keeps one record per originator + `notificationId`, and answers `{notificationId, revision}` whatever it did. Gated by standing in `contextId`; retry class 2; `notAddressedHere`, `documentInvalid`. |
| `vtc/notifications/list/0.1`, `show/0.1` | A community's administrators read the notifications addressed to the community (`vtc.notifications.read`): `mayRelay`, `relayDisclosure`, relay decisions (selection + count, never who). |
| `vtc/notifications/relay/0.1` | An administrator's relay decision (`vtc.notifications.relay`, qualified `group:<id>`): `recipients` = `allMembers` / `group`+`groupId` / `role`+`role` (`dependentSchemas`, not if/then/else); refused with `disclosureNotAcknowledged` (details carry the statement) until acknowledged; never to the community, the originator or an earlier relayer; later revisions follow without a new decision. `destructive` (irreversible disclosure); step-up/consent left to community policy per SPEC §7.3 item 13. Errors: `notificationUnknown`, `notRelayable`, `lapsed`, `disclosureNotAcknowledged`, `groupUnknown`. |

Shared: `vtc/notifications/_shared/0.1/received-notification.schema.json` (`groupId` `$ref`s the groups' `GroupId`).

## Fixes to `notifications/notify/0.1` and `notifications/relay/0.1` — prose and examples only

Both are released (trust-tasks-rs-v0.36.9), so nothing their generated types or bundles see changes: no schema, `proofRequirement`, error code or bound. The bundles carry no prose, so pinned digests are unaffected. `check-published-schemas` passes.

- **Relay depth:** producer item 2 said "MUST NOT relay a relay that already carries three relays (so that its own would make more than four)", which forbade the fourth relay the consumer accepts. It now says a relayer may relay only where its relay makes at most four in all. This only permits what consumers already accept, so no new version.
- **Proof purpose:** notification and relay proofs carry `authentication` with the operational key (VTI-NTF-006 / VTI-KEY-081/082); the examples said `assertionMethod`. Consumers verify the relationship the proof names (SPEC §4.7.3) and read it as authorship only. VTI-KEY-107 applies to the relay received, not to forwarded layers.
- **Withdrawal** keeps the period of the revision it replaces (example updated); **VTI-NTF-005** re-checked for each revision issued, except a withdrawal; the election informative note covers an early close.
- **No relay back** to the originator or an earlier relayer (strengthens producer item 4).
- Pointers to `deposit` and the VTC tasks; corrected the relay size rationale (five layers, not four).

## Local validation

`npm run build`, `npm run validate`, `check-bindings` (all four agree), `check-published-schemas`, `build-bundles` + `check-bundles`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, TS `tsc` + `npm test` + `smoke`, `go vet` + `go test`, `dart analyze --fatal-infos` + `dart test`, `check-sibling-core-ranges`, `check-dart-packages` — all green. Rust, TS, Go and Dart regenerated.

title: feat(rooms): a member's name in a room, as a memberProfile record
body:
## What

A reader showing a quote, or who reacted, has the author's DID and no name for it. This adds
`rooms/_shared/0.3/member-profile.schema.json`: a member writes its own name for itself, in one
room, as a record of `kind: memberProfile` with the name in `title`.

## Why a record in the room

- A room author is a persona DID held for that room alone.
- The community directory is addressed by entry identifier, and only administrators may look an
  entry up by DID (`vtc/directory/entries/show/0.1`, consumer item 2), so that the directory does
  not answer whether a DID is a member.
- A room may belong to no community, and a `private` room's host must not learn who its members are.
- `rooms/_shared/0.2` `RoomProfile` names the room, not its members; DID documents carry no name;
  `persona/contact` petnames are the reader's own, for contacts it already has.

The audience for the name is the room's members, so the name lives where they already read:
sealed from the host on `attributed` and `private` rooms, as the room's own profile is.

## Design

- **No new task, and no change to existing schemas.** On the sealed tiers the record is an ordinary
  `SealedRecordBody` (`kind`, `title`, optionally `writtenAt` / `editedAt`); on an `open` room it is
  ordinary `cleartext` with an empty `body`. `rooms/keys/seal/0.3` seals it as is, and hosts store
  it like any other record. `MemberProfileRecord` is `SealedRecordBody` plus constraints;
  `MemberProfileCleartext` is the open-room form; `MemberName` is the name itself: one line, no
  control characters, at most 64 code points, and an empty value withdraws the name.
- **Gated like the other record members.** A reader that knows `kind` but not `memberProfile` would
  show the record as a note. So a writer may write one only once the room profile's
  `recordMembers` lists both `kind` and `memberProfile`, which this component defines as a new
  value. The *Turning them on* order applies.
- **Reading.** A name applies only to its record's `author`, only in that room. It comes from the
  most recently stored current version (by `bodyStoredAt`, else `updatedAt`). A rewrite by another
  member never names the original author. A `memberProfile` record is never shown as a note,
  message or reaction, and never counted.
- **Showing.** The reader's own petname for the DID comes first, then the member's name in this
  room, then a shortened DID. A name is a self-assertion and is never shown as verified. Names that
  collide after NFC and case folding, or that match a petname for a different DID, must be shown
  so the authors can be told apart.
- **Finding.** There is no fixed location. On an `open` room `rooms/records/list/0.6` rows carry
  `kind`, and on the sealed tiers names are found as records are opened. A member SHOULD write its
  name again (same key, new version) after the epoch advances, so that readers of a room whose
  history starts at each member's join can see it.

## Judgement calls

- One member, `title`, carries the name. Avatars and pronouns are left out: an avatar is a file a
  reader fetches, and nothing else was asked for.
- No derived record key (unlike `RoomProfileStatement`). A key derived from the storage key needs
  the key holder to compute it, which means new key-holder tasks. Discovery by reading avoids them,
  and the cost is the re-write after an epoch advance.
- A new shared-schema version rather than a new `SealedRecordBody` member. Released versions are
  left as they are.

## Checks

- `npm run validate`: passes (1292 specs, 169 shared schemas).
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: 0 changed spec files; only new files are added.
- Bindings regenerated (Rust codegen + `cargo fmt`, TS, Go, Dart). `npm run check-bindings`: all
  agree. The TS, Go and Dart outputs build (`tsc`, `go build` / `go vet`, `dart analyze
  --fatal-infos`). Rust codegen produced no diff.
- The schema was exercised with ajv. A valid body passes. A body carrying `body`, a multi-line
  name, a 65-code-point name, or a different `kind` fails. The open form accepts only an empty
  `body`.

title: feat(vtc/networks): 0.2 on vtn/* tasks, and vtc/networks/deliver/0.1
body:
## Why

The vtc/networks/* 0.1 family is a community's admin API for its memberships in Verifiable Trust Networks. Since it was written, the VTN moved onto vtn/* Trust Tasks (#1020). A community now talks to a network only with vtn/* tasks it signs as itself, and checks each network answer's authentication proof against the network's DID. That change does three things to this family:

- servesRole/1 is retired. A group's registration is now the community's signed vtn/groups/register request itself, and the network's groupRegistered/1 acceptance binds it by digest (SHA-256 over the JCS form of the request, proof included).
- A community group's relay endpoint used to be a REST path per group taking { envelope }. It is now the community's Trust Task endpoint.
- The network needs a Trust Task to deliver broadcasts to that endpoint. This PR adds it as vtc/networks/deliver/0.1.

## What changed

- vtc/_shared/0.7/network-membership.schema.json: a copy of 0.6 with the same shape. Only three RegisteredGroup descriptions change:
  - registration is the signed vtn/groups/register request as the network accepted it.
  - acceptance is the groupRegistered/1 VSC carrying the registration's digest.
  - endpoint is the Trust Task endpoint where broadcasts arrive as vtc/networks/deliver.
- vtc/networks/join/0.2:
  - Reads its own entry with vtn/entries/show and the roles with vtn/roles/list.
  - Registers each group with vtn/groups/register and verifies the acceptance against the digest of the request as sent.
  - Reads the offer with vtn/membership/offer and acknowledges with vtn/membership/acknowledge.
  - Every request is signed as the community for authentication and addressed to the network DID the administrator named. The community verifies each answer's proof by that DID.
- vtc/networks/groups/register/0.2: the registration is the signed vtn/groups/register request, and the endpoint is the Trust Task endpoint.
- vtc/networks/leave/0.2: the repudiation goes out with vtn/membership/repudiate. After departing, the community refuses vtc/networks/deliver from that network.
- vtc/networks/repudiate/0.2: reads the listing with vtn/entries/show and repudiates with vtn/membership/repudiate.
- vtc/networks/list/0.2 and show/0.2: records follow _shared/0.7.
- vtc/networks/evidence/0.2: links[].registration is the signed request, which is the pair a network checks for vtn/rooms/pass.
- Every example's servesRole VSC is now a signed vtn/groups/register request document. Every relay endpoint is now https://community.example.org/v1/trust-tasks.
- Request shapes, response shapes, error codes, parties and proof requirements are all unchanged. None of the 0.2 versions declares extends, because the meaning of registration changed. Each spec has a "Changes from 0.1" section.
- New vtc/networks/deliver/0.1:
  - The network is the issuer. It must hold an acknowledged membership from the community and must sign the document for authentication.
  - The payload is { role, envelope } and reuses vtn/_shared/0.1 Envelope.
  - The response is only { status: delivered | duplicate }. It deliberately carries no member count, so the network does not learn the group's size.
  - Error codes: notMember, roleUnregistered, envelopeInvalid.
  - A delivered envelope is passed on unchanged to each group member as vtc/networks/notice.
- vtc/networks/notice stays at 0.1 because its contract does not change. One prose sentence now names vtc/networks/deliver as how the envelope arrives, and deliver is added to related.
- The vtn/memberships/* mirror specs link to vtc/networks/* 0.2. These edits are from npm run fix-stale-references.
- Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated.

All 0.1 versions remain published.

title: spec(rooms): a removed member can rejoin — prior group state is a prior membership, not a join, corrected in place
body:
## The defect

`rooms/keys/welcome/0.1` § *Joining twice is refused, not merged* required a recipient holding group state for `roomId` for the member the invitation names to answer `alreadyJoined`, and ended "Leaving and rejoining is a removal followed by a fresh invitation, not a second Welcome".

A member removed by a commit **keeps** its group state: `rooms/keys/open/0.2` and `rooms/keys/file-key/0.2` answer `unknownEpoch` with reason `removed` and `removedAtEpoch` from exactly that state. Read literally, the MUST therefore refuses the fresh-invitation Welcome the same paragraph says rejoining uses. `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.4` (*Re-admitting someone removed*) and `rooms/owner/revoke/0.1` (*Re-admitting a party*) both describe re-admission as fresh credentials plus a new leaf. An implementation following the literal text (the VTA) can never re-admit a removed member of an attributed room.

A second instance of the same contradiction sat in welcome's *Retention*: "MUST discard it on removal". That contradicts the `removed` reason in open/file-key and file-key's "Removal is forward-only".

## The rule

**`rooms/keys/welcome/0.1`**
- *Joining twice is refused, not merged*: `alreadyJoined` is for **current** group state, meaning state with no processed removal after it.
- New *Rejoining after a removal*: state from which a processed commit removed the member is a **prior membership**, not a join. A recipient holding only prior memberships MUST process a Welcome under a valid, unconsumed invitation as a first join, and MUST keep each prior membership, unmerged, for records sealed under the epochs it covers. A member may have several, one per removal, each covering `[join epoch, removal epoch)`. They never overlap, so at most one state covers any epoch.
- *Retention*: removal is forward-only. Prior state is kept for epochs before the removal, subject to the room's epoch floor (`rooms/epoch/prune/0.2`).
- `alreadyJoined` meaning updated to match.

**`rooms/keys/open/0.2`** (*Conformance*, `unknownEpoch` meaning)
- The record's epoch `E` chooses the state. Use the current state when `E` ≥ its join epoch, otherwise the prior membership covering `E`. If `E` falls between a removal epoch and the next join epoch, or at or after the last removal epoch with no current state, the answer is `unknownEpoch` / `removed` with that `removedAtEpoch`. This replaces "has no way to choose". The rule that an oracle never retries under another member's state stands, and now also covers the member's other states.
- `removed` / `notDelivered` / `beyondChain` are scoped to the state `E` chose. `removed`'s range is bounded above by the next join epoch.

**`rooms/keys/file-key/0.2`** (mirrors open: item 3, item 4, `unknownEpoch` and `noGroup` meanings, *Removal is forward-only*)
- `open` uses the same epoch-chosen state. An oracle holding only prior memberships answers `seal` with `noGroup`, because it has no current epoch to seal under.

**`rooms/owner/group/remove/0.4`** (*Re-admitting someone removed*)
- One sentence pointing at welcome's rule: the key holder joins by the new Welcome and keeps the removal's state as a prior membership, which is not `alreadyJoined`.

`rooms/owner/revoke/0.1` is unchanged. Its re-admission text covers credentials only and was already consistent.

## Why in place

There is no wire change: no member, error code, reason or `details` field is added or removed. All four specifications are `status: draft`, and SPEC §5.2 says an editorial change to a `draft`, such as rewording prose, is made in place and MUST NOT mint a new version. This is a correction of a self-contradiction: welcome/0.1 already said rejoining is a fresh invitation, and open/file-key 0.2 already assumed a removed member keeps its state. The amendment makes the MUSTs agree with that.

`check-published-schemas` passes: 4 changed spec files, all released in `trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.2`, all changed additively (prose/descriptions only). The regenerated bindings change only the error-code doc comments in three Rust modules. TS, Go and Dart came out byte-identical.

## Validation

- `npm run validate`: 1276 specs validated, 0 non-conforming (stale references, wire conventions, casing, framework links all clean)
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, `npm run build-ts-bindings`, `build-go-bindings`, `build-dart-bindings`: regenerated. Only 3 Rust doc-comment diffs.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree; ERROR_CODES match
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: every released file changed only additively
- `npm run build`: OK


## Follow-up: a removal the key holder never saw (b89abe59b)

A member that was idle when it was removed never applies the removing commit. It also cannot fetch that commit afterwards, because the host serves `rooms/epoch/commits` under a `read` grant that the removal withdrew. Under the rule above, its key holder would answer the re-admitting Welcome with `alreadyJoined`.

- **welcome 0.1**: the recipient recognises a prior membership in either of two ways:
  - from a removal it processed; or
  - from a Welcome whose ratchet tree no longer contains the member's earlier leaf, matched by signature key or leaf node and never by identifier.

  It processes the Welcome without keeping the result.
  - If the leaf is still present, the answer is `alreadyJoined`, and the recipient consumes neither the invitation nor the KeyPackage.
  - If the leaf is absent, the held state becomes a prior membership whose removal epoch is not yet known.

  A recipient MUST NOT wait for or fetch the removing commit, and a client is not required to apply commits first. The recipient MAY later apply commits to that prior state to fix r.
- **open 0.2 and file-key 0.2**: until the removing commit is applied to that state, an epoch above h and below the next join is `notDelivered`, with that state's `heldEpoch`. It is never `removed` before then. Once the commit is applied, the epoch is handled as a known removal.

This is still not a wire change, so it is an in-place draft correction. `validate`, `check-bindings`, `check-published-schemas` and `build` all pass. Of the regenerated bindings, only the Rust `alreadyJoined` doc text changes. The implementation is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2441.

title: spec(rooms): a record's kind, replies and reactions — notes, messages and reactions on every tier
body:
Requested by Keyring: [`berkmancenter/keyring-wallet` docs/upstream/2026-11-rooms-findings.md](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/blob/167f3a0dccb571e02fb2ac7664a9b985e56a18fd/docs/upstream/2026-11-rooms-findings.md), finding 2. Rooms have no record kind for a message, so a chat-style client's messages read as untitled notes everywhere else, and nothing lets two clients agree on a reply or a reaction.

**Draft:** this is a proposal for review, Keyring's especially. The second revision answers [Keyring's review](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1027#issuecomment-6631928554) item by item; see *Response to Keyring's review* below.

## What changes

### `rooms/_shared/0.1` and `0.2`: `SealedRecordBody` (in place, additive)

The two shared versions define `SealedRecordBody` identically, and both are changed identically. There are four new optional members, `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt` and `editedAt`, and new `$defs`: `RecordKind`, `RecordReference`, `RecordWrittenAt`, `RecordEditedAt` and `RecordMetadataV3`.

- **`kind`** (`RecordKind`) is an open, lowerCamelCase string, not an enum. It defines `note`, `message` and `reaction`. Absent means `note`. A reader MUST show a kind it doesn't know as a note.
- **Untitled records.** A reader that keeps a conversation apart from a library MAY treat a record with no `kind` and no `title` as a message. If it does, it shows such records in the same conversation as `kind: message`, and renders their body as plain text. A reader that shows one as a note renders markdown.
- **What `body` is.** On a `message`, `body` is plain text, and readers MUST NOT render it as markup. On a `reaction`, it is the reaction's value. On a note, or on a kind the reader doesn't know, it is markdown.
- **`inReplyTo`** (`RecordReference`, `{key, version?}`) names another record of the same room.
  - A reply stays visible when its target is unavailable, including when the target was withdrawn.
  - A reader says that a target has changed only when its **content** changed: every body member except `proof`, the location and `editedAt`. A version number alone never counts, because curation moves the version but never touches the body.
- **`writtenAt`** is the author's signed claim of when the record was written. It is kept across edits, and it is compared with the host's **`createdAt`** (below), not `updatedAt`, because edits and curation move `updatedAt`.
  - **Future check:** more than five minutes after `createdAt` is implausible. It falls back to `updatedAt` where there is no `createdAt`.
  - **Backdating:** a `writtenAt` more than 24 hours before `createdAt` MUST be ordered by `createdAt`, and the reader MUST show that it arrived later than it claims. Without `createdAt`, readers fall back to the existing MAY.
  - Messages without `writtenAt`, and unverifiable placeholders, are ordered by `createdAt`, else `updatedAt`.
- **`editedAt`** (new) is signed and set by the writer on every version after the first. It is absent on the first version. Readers show "edited" from it, never from `version`.
- **What a new version keeps.** A new version MUST keep `kind`, and a reaction's new version MUST keep `inReplyTo`. A reader holding an earlier version MUST refuse a version that changes either one.
- **Reactions:**
  - **Values.** A value is normalised to NFC, then U+FE0E and U+FE0F are removed, and only then is it measured or compared. The limit is 64 code points after normalisation, on one line, meaning no line terminators. A value that is empty or only whitespace is empty, and an empty value withdraws the reaction.
  - **One per author, value and target.** A writer SHOULD reuse the key of its existing reaction with the same value and target. Withdrawing means withdrawing every such record.
  - **Who can withdraw.** A withdrawal counts only when the empty version comes from the reaction's author, judged against the version the reader holds.
  - **Removed members.** A removed member's reactions keep counting until a curator retracts them. A member who returns under a new DID counts as a different author.
  - Nothing may target a reaction (unchanged).
- **Withdrawing a message.** The author writes a new version with an empty `body` and no `file`. Readers show the message as withdrawn, or not at all, and its replies stay.
- **Tombstones.** A reader uses the kind and the place in the conversation from the version it held before. If it held none, the tombstone appears in no conversation and in no reaction count. An `open` room's tombstone keeps none of the new members, consistent with put/0.5 *Retention*.
- **An author whose DID does not resolve.** "The DID did not resolve (or is deactivated)" is now a separate case from "the signature is wrong".
  - For an unresolvable DID, a reader MAY show a placeholder that says the author can't be verified. The placeholder is ordered by `updatedAt`, so replies still anchor to it, and it shows none of the content.
  - A wrong signature is still refused.
- **When a writer may use the members.** The members are gated by `recordMembers`, and `editedAt` is gated with the others.
  - Rule (1), "an old reader refuses them", holds only for conforming readers. Non-conforming readers exist, which is why readers ship first.
  - A writer MAY rely on a profile it resolved within the room's current epoch.
- **Turning them on.**
  - Deciding that a room's readers are ready is an out-of-band decision by the room's owner or a curator.
  - Rollout order:
    1. Readers, including profile readers.
    2. **The owner's key holder**, which re-writes the profile after a removal and so MUST accept `recordMembers` before any profile carries it.
    3. On the sealed tiers, the key holders that seal for the room's writers (`rooms/keys/seal/0.3`).
    4. The profile.
  - There is no default for new rooms yet. The profile is set with `rooms/keys/profile/write` on sealed tiers, or with `rooms/records/put` at `room-profile` on `open`. Both need `curate` or `admin`.

### `RoomProfile.recordMembers` (in place, additive)

The defined values are now `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt` and `editedAt`. The description gains the out-of-band decision, the rollout order, how the profile is set, and the epoch freshness rule.

### `rooms/records/put/0.5` (extends 0.4, new in this PR)

- `cleartext` gains `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt` and `editedAt`.
- Producer rules now cover keeping `kind` and a reaction's `inReplyTo` on a rewrite, setting `editedAt`, withdrawals, and reaction-key reuse.
- The host still stores these members as received. The one exception: **on an `open` room only**, a host MAY refuse, with the standard `permissionDenied`, a new version of a record whose current `kind` is `message` or `reaction` when its author is not the record's original author. The original author's own rewrites and withdrawals are still accepted. On `attributed` and `private` the host MUST NOT try: `kind` is sealed and must not be copied into the clear, so the reader-side rules are the defence there.
- Host item 16: the host records when it stored a record's first version and keeps it across every version and curation. That time is served as `createdAt`.
- Security & Privacy says plainly that a reader seeing a record for the first time cannot detect a replacement by another member on tiers where the host does not check authorship.
- *Retention* says what an `open` tombstone keeps.

### `rooms/keys/seal/0.3` (new, extends 0.2)

The schema is identical to 0.2. Under `signAsPrincipal`, a 0.3 key holder MUST accept a body that carries `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt` or `editedAt`, or a `file` whose manifest carries `width`, `height` or `preview`. A 0.2 key holder refuses any of these with `bodyInvalid`. This is the same type-URI argument as put/0.5: `trust-task-discovery` can now answer whether a key holder will seal these members.

### `rooms/records/list/0.6` (new)

Each row is a `RecordMetadataV3`: `RecordMetadataV2` plus four members.
- `kind`, **on `open` rooms only**, where the host reads the body anyway. It is omitted on a tombstone, on a record that has none, and on every sealed tier.
- `createdAt`, **on every tier**: when the host stored the record's first version. Neither edits nor curation change it. A host MUST set it and keep it. For records stored before the host kept it, the host omits it rather than guessing, and readers fall back to `updatedAt`.
- `createdBy`, **on `open` and `attributed` only, never on `private`**: the author of the first version, as the host recorded it (put/0.5 Host item 17). Readers use it to apply the rewrite-by-another-member rules to records they see for the first time.
- `bodyStoredAt`, **on every tier**: when the host stored the body the current version carries, i.e. the time of the `rooms/records/put` that wrote it. Curation leaves it unchanged, and for the first version it equals `createdAt`. Readers verify the author's proof against the DID document as it stood at this time.

It is a new version rather than an in-place change, because `RecordMetadataV2` is closed and the family keeps each listing's shape fixed. It does not declare `extends`, because the build refuses a renamed row type.

### `rooms/records/get/0.3` (new, extends 0.2)

Adds `createdAt`, `createdBy` and `bodyStoredAt` to the single-record read. None is committed, so a reader removes all three from the leaf preimage, as it already removes `blobs`. It is minted for consistency: `rooms/keys/read/0.2` can pass on only what the host serves, and a reader that reads one record directly needs the same metadata a listing gives.

### `rooms/keys/browse/0.4` (new)

Rows are `RecordMetadataV3`, passed through from `rooms/records/list/0.6`. Each row can carry `kind` (open rooms), `createdAt`, `createdBy` and `bodyStoredAt`, and `blobs` is carried as well.

### `rooms/keys/read/0.2` (new)

- **`createdAt`, `createdBy` and `bodyStoredAt`** are added beside what 0.1 returns, passed through from `rooms/records/get/0.3`.
- **Batch form.** `keys` is a list of up to **32** keys, answered in `results`: one entry per key, in order, each with its own record or its own error. One key's failure never fails another.
  - Each failed key carries the code and `details` it would have had if read alone.
  - Refusals that concern the whole request (`notAMember`, `permissionDenied`, `malformedRequest`) are still a single `trust-task-error`.
  - The new `notAttempted` code (retryable) lets the key holder stop when a response would exceed its size or time budget.
  - Repairs run once per batch, not once per key.
- **Why 32:** it is about one screen of a busy conversation, and it bounds what one request can ask of a key holder: each key is a host request, a trace check and possibly a repair. A body can be up to 1 MiB, so `notAttempted` covers the size case that a count alone can't.

### `rooms/keys/act/0.11` (extends 0.10, new in this PR)

The table adds `rooms/records/put/0.5` (`write`), `rooms/records/list/0.6` (`read`) and `rooms/records/get/0.3` (`read`). `rooms/keys/*` tasks are addressed to the key holder rather than a host, so they are not in the table. Act and seal are consistent: act never opens or signs a sealed body, so on the sealed tiers a member's own client uses `rooms/keys/seal/0.3` to sign and seal, then act to complete the put. The worked example now names `seal/0.3`.

### `FileManifest` (`rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json`, in place, additive)

Optional `width` and `height` (positive integers, in pixels, always together) and `preview`: a JPEG, PNG or WebP image of at most 8 KiB, base64url-encoded. All three are advisory, and a reader checks them against the bytes when it fetches the file. A reader renders a preview only as a raster image it decodes itself, never as SVG and never as a link.

On sealed tiers the manifest is inside the sealed body, so the host learns nothing from them. On `open` they are in the clear, carried with put/0.5. They are gated by `recordMembers` (values `width`, `height`, `preview`). `FileManifest` gained `fileKey` the same way in put/0.4.

### More reader rules in `SealedRecordBody`

- **Which DID document.** A reader verifies the current version's proof against the author's DID document as it stood at the host's `bodyStoredAt`, not at the proof's own `created`.
  - A key rotated away after that time still verifies; one rotated away before it does not.
  - For a DID method with history (did:webvh `versionTime`), the reader resolves the document as of that time.
  - For a method without history, it uses the current document. A proof that fails there is shown as the placeholder (author can't be verified, content not shown), never silently dropped.
  - Without `bodyStoredAt`, the reader uses the current document.
  - put/0.5 Security & Privacy: a key rotated away before `bodyStoredAt` can't sign a version that verifies, so a compromised old key can't backdate or edit past its rotation.

- **The record's original author.** Readers use `createdBy` to apply the rewrite-by-another-member rules to a record they see for the first time.
- **Changing a reaction.** A new version of a reaction with a different non-empty value changes that author's reaction.
- **Ordering.** A reader MAY order a conversation by `createdAt`, the order the room received its records, instead of by `writtenAt`.
- **Reaction display.** The normal form of a reaction value is for measuring and comparing only. A reader MAY show the fully qualified form, with U+FE0F.
- **Captions.** A `message` with a `file` and an empty `body` is a photo or a file with no caption.
- **URLs.** A reader never follows a URL by itself. It MAY offer to open one after the member explicitly asks and confirms.

### Reference updates

Current specs that named a superseded version now link `rooms/records/list/0.6`, `rooms/keys/read/0.2` or `rooms/keys/browse/0.4`. These are link changes only, made by `fix-stale-references`.

## Response to Keyring's review

1. **Untitled records:** applied, as a MAY.
   - Your question: **the member portal and the browser plugin will show both in one conversation**, untitled no-kind records and `kind: message` records together.
2. **Turning the members on:**
   - (a) Conforming vs non-conforming readers: applied.
   - (b) Out-of-band decision: applied.
   - (c) `rooms/keys/seal/0.3`: added. Act never signs a sealed body, so it needs no matching change beyond naming seal 0.3.
   - (d) No default; the profile is set with `rooms/keys/profile/write` (sealed) or `rooms/records/put` at `room-profile` (open): applied.
   - (e) Epoch freshness: applied.
   - (f) Owner's key holder in the rollout order: applied.
3. **Rewrites by another member:**
   - Applied: (a) keep `kind`, and a reaction keeps `inReplyTo`; (b) readers holding an earlier version refuse a change; (c) the Security & Privacy statement. Withdrawing a reaction requires the reaction's author.
   - Host refusal: an `open` room's host MAY refuse another author's new version of a message or reaction (`permissionDenied`). `attributed` and `private` can't, because `kind` is sealed.
4. **Deleting:** applied. This covers message withdrawal, tombstones, and what an `open` tombstone keeps.
5. **Cost:** `kind` is now in `open` listings (`rooms/records/list/0.6`).
   - Batch read: `rooms/keys/read/0.2` takes up to 32 keys and answers each one separately.
6. **Replies and changes:** applied. "Content" is defined, and curation never counts as a change.
7. **Edits:** applied. `editedAt` is gated by `recordMembers`.
8. **Reaction values:** applied. NFC, then U+FE0E and U+FE0F removed, then a 64 code point limit; no line terminators; whitespace-only counts as empty.
9. **Duplicate reactions:** applied. A writer reuses the key, and a withdrawal covers every matching record.
10. **Backdating:** applied against a host-stamped `createdAt` (list/0.6), with a 24-hour MUST. The five-minute future check also moves to `createdAt`.
11. **Unresolvable author DIDs:** applied. The placeholder shows no content.
12. **Reactions after removal:** applied.
13. **Plain text:** applied. A message is plain text, a note is markdown, a reaction's body is its value, and an unknown kind is shown as a note, so markdown. An untitled record shown as a message is plain text; one shown as a note is markdown.

## Out of scope here (answers to Keyring's questions)

- **How a member learns of new records.** Nothing in the rooms family does this today, and `notifications/notify` is not a per-record signal. A content-free "room changed" signal is a candidate follow-up.
- **Where a member's name comes from.** Rooms define none. Community rooms can use the community's member directory. A room-level answer is a follow-up.

## Design decisions (kept)

1. The sealed-tier members are added to `_shared` in place, following the precedent of provenance and `validUntil`.
2. `kind` is an open string with a lowerCamelCase pattern.
3. One reference member, `inReplyTo`, serves both replies and reactions. Nothing may target a reaction.
4. The reaction value goes in `body`.
5. The room's profile (`recordMembers`) gates the new members; `editedAt` joins them.
6. `writtenAt` is kept across edits; `editedAt` marks an edit.

## Checks

`npm run validate`, `npm run check-bindings`, `npm run check-published-schemas` and `npm run build` pass. The Rust, TS, Go and Dart libraries are regenerated.

title: feat(trust-task-discovery): publish 0.4, a responder advertises the horizon up to which it honours a stated expiresAt
body:
SPEC §7.2 (Bounding the record) applies a consumer's maximum age only where a
document states no expiresAt, and since trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (#1021)
validate_freshness does so, honouring a stated expiry up to the policy's
expiry_horizon. discovery 0.3 cannot describe that: its window "governs
issuedAt only" and its responder refuses any document past
issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds + clockSkewSeconds, whatever expiresAt it states. A
responder that honours an expiry could only advertise a narrower window than
it applies, and a producer could not learn that stating an expiry keeps a long
delivery acceptable.

- specs/trust-task-discovery/0.4: acceptanceWindow gains an optional
  expiryHorizonSeconds (whole seconds, at least 1), and the spec defines a
  document's acceptance end: issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds without an expiresAt;
  the earlier of expiresAt and issuedAt + expiryHorizonSeconds with one; and,
  where the window carries no horizon, the earlier of expiresAt and
  issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds, which is what a 0.3 window says.
  - Responder: MUST NOT advertise a horizon wider than it applies, nor one at
    all if it applies its maximum age whatever expiresAt states.
  - Discoverer: send bounds follow the acceptance end. MAY state an expiresAt
    within the horizon, no later than it will pursue delivery, instead of
    issuing a chain of new attempts; a new attempt carries it unchanged.
    Absent a horizon, it MUST assume the maximum age applies to every
    document.
  - AcceptanceWindow is closed in 0.3, so an added optional member is a MINOR
    increment (§5.2): a new version, not an edit.
  - Response-side invalid examples: a zero horizon, a duration string, and a
    fractional entry-level horizon.
- trust-tasks-rs: DiscoveryRegistry::respond_to_v0_4 is the current answer.
  acceptance_window_from reads the policy's expiry_horizon, and
  expiry_horizon() sets one by hand. respond_to_v0_3 moves to
  discovery/superseded.rs and states the window without the horizon (narrower
  than applied, which 0.3 permits).
- trust-tasks-https: enable_discovery answers 0.4, and 0.3 beside 0.2 and 0.1.
- trust-tasks-dart-https: enableDiscovery answers 0.4. Dart's FreshnessPolicy
  has no horizon, so its window states none, which says the maximum age
  applies to every document. 0.3 moves to the superseded block.
- Examples and tests that named the 0.3 types use 0.4.
- Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart). 0.3 is superseded.

Follows from #1021 and trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#96 (VTI-OPS-024,
VTI-OPS-028, VTI-TRN-048), whose implementation in
OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure states delivery deadlines as expiresAt.

## Tests
- New: `the_expiry_horizon_is_advertised_from_the_policy`, `a_0_3_response_states_the_window_without_the_horizon` (rs); `answers 0.3 in 0.3, with the window` (dart-https); the window tests now run against 0.4
- trust-tasks-rs + trust-tasks-https: 2562 passed; doctests; workspace clippy `-D warnings`; fmt
- dart-https: 62 passed; `dart analyze --fatal-infos` clean in dart, dart-https, dart-tsp, dart-didcomm
- go vet + go test; `npm run build`, `check-bindings`, `check-published-schemas`, `check-bundles`
- TypeScript not compiled locally (no tsc installed); left to CI

title: feat(vtc/boards): community boards — propose ideas, leave notes, vote on each accepted idea through its own election (vtc/boards/*/0.1)
body:
## What

Thirteen Trust Tasks implementing the VTI **Community Boards** chapter (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#98, VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080):

| Area | Tasks |
|---|---|
| Boards | `create`, `update`, `list`, `show` |
| Ideas | `ideas/propose`, `ideas/update`, `ideas/withdraw`, `ideas/decide` (accept opens an election from the board's template), `ideas/select` |

title: spec(vta/collection): category notifications, a disabled reason, and the 24-hour lease
body:
Follow-up to #1023, which was merged before this commit reached it. It applies the decisions taken on trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#97 (VTI-NTF-080, 082, 083 and the new VTI-NTF-093).

- **Category**: `messaging` changes to `notifications` for `vta/collection/{claim,release,list}/0.1`.
- **Collection by default is behind an operator setting (VTI-NTF-093)**, off unless the operator enables it.
  - `NotCollectedReason` gains `disabled`, appended after `limit` and `conflict`: the operator has not enabled collection by default.
  - While the setting is off, the VTA still grants, renews, releases and lists claims, so clients can adopt claims before an operator turns collection on.
  - `notCollectable` and the scope of `list` now refer to the identifiers VTI-NTF-080 names whether or not the setting is on.
  - A claimant's release resumes the VTA's collection only where the setting is on.
- **Lease sizing (claim)**: a producer SHOULD request `86400` seconds and renew at half the granted period. The VTA's stated maximum SHOULD NOT exceed thirty days.

`vta/collection/*` has not been in a `trust-tasks-rs` release yet, so these edits are in place. The enum value is appended.

## Local validation

`npm run validate` and `npm run build` pass. `check-bindings` reports all four bindings agree. `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features vta --test conformance -- collection` passes 6 tests. Rust, TS, Go and Dart are regenerated.

title: feat(rooms): rooms/watch and rooms/changed — a content-free signal that a room has moved
body:
## What

A member's client learns that a room has new records only by polling `rooms/records/list` with
`sinceVersion`. This adds two tasks:

- **`rooms/watch/0.1`** (member → host). The member names an `address` DID and the version it has
  read the room to. The request is authorized by an `AuthorityPresentation` conferring `read`,
  exactly as a listing is. The same request re-arms or cancels the watch.
- **`rooms/changed/0.1`** (host → address). A one-way signal that the room has moved past that
  version: `roomId` and `latestVersion`, nothing else.

## Why nothing existing fits

- `notifications/notify/0.1` tells a party that a thing exists which it may take part in. It is a
  durable, revisioned inbox record, governed by an acceptance policy and a kind registry, and it is
  not a per-change signal. A host also keeps no roster, so it has no list of members to notify.
- `push/wake/0.2` is the doorbell. Its triggers are the device's mediator and its VTA, as
  provisioned by `device/set-wake`. A room host is not one, and should not hold a device's wake
  handle.

These tasks connect the two. The signal is an ordinary Trust Task document for the address, so it
waits in that address's mediator queue, and the existing queue-driven wake rings the device. No new
wake path is added.

## Design

- **One signal per arming.** A watch fires once and disarms, and the member re-arms after reading.
  However busy the room or however long the device sleeps, a watch puts at most one signal in the
  queue and causes at most one wake. A misdirected watch costs its address one document.
  `sinceVersion` closes the gap between the member's last listing and arming: the host signals at
  once if the room is already past it.
- **Nothing about the change.** The host sends the same signal for a put of any kind, a curation, a
  retraction, a prune or a profile write. It never carries or varies anything by what changed, and
  waits a short randomised interval before sending. The address's mediator sees a document for the
  address, and the push gateway and push service see a contentless wake.
- **Sealed tiers.** The host never sees `kind`, so a reaction fires a watch exactly as a message
  does. Both specs say this. `rooms/changed` has a *What a reader does with a signal* section: list
  from the watermark, learn each changed record's kind (from the row on `open`, through the key
  holder on sealed tiers), and count as unread only messages that are new to the reader, not the
  member's own, and current. New is judged by key, or by `createdAt` against the reader's read
  marker, so a back-dated message still counts. Reactions, edits, curations, notes and profile
  records are never unread messages. The reader alerts only on what it found, with wording taken
  from the records it opened.
- **One-way.** `rooms/changed` has no `#response`, since a reply would tell the host when the
  device woke.
- **A watch grants nothing.** It is host state, never consulted for authorization, never shown to
  anyone, and forgotten when it fires, is cancelled, lapses (at most 30 days, and never past the
  presentation's validity) or is revoked. It does not move with the room.
- **`private` rooms.** The address must be a DID used for nothing else. Re-arming the same address
  links one member's reads over time, although without saying who the member is. The spec says
  so, and suggests a fresh address per arming, or polling, for members to whom that matters.

## Judgement calls

- Re-arm after each signal rather than a lease with a rate limit. This costs one request per wake
  cycle, and in return bounds the mediator queue and the wake count without the host learning
  whether a signal was read.
- `open` rooms get the same signal, with no kind filter, even though their host could filter. The
  signal stays one shape on every tier, and a filter can be added later as an optional member.
- `latestVersion` is included. It lets a reader skip a signal it has already caught up past, and
  tells the address nothing a listing would not.

## Checks

- `npm run validate`: passes (1294 specs). No warnings name either new spec.
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: 0 changed spec files; only new files are added.
- Bindings regenerated (Rust codegen + `cargo fmt`, TS, Go, Dart). `npm run check-bindings`: all
  four agree.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`: passes (conformance 3628/3628).
  The first run failed two `rooms/watch` example tests, because a top-level `not` clause made the
  Rust generator drop `sinceVersion` and `cancel`. The clause is gone, and the rule is now stated in
  prose: a host ignores `sinceVersion` and `leaseSeconds` on a cancel.
- `npm run build-bundles && npm run check-bundles`: 1288 bundles verified.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `tsc`, `go build` / `go vet`, `dart analyze --fatal-infos`: clean.

title: spec(vtc/elections): a deleted group's DID is never a member party (VTI-VOT-029)
body:
## What

`vtc/elections/show/0.6`, `vtc/elections/list/0.5` and `vtc/elections/tickets/issue/0.3` defined a **member party** as a `roll.memberOf` that is "neither the community's own DID nor one of its groups". After a group is deleted its DID is no longer one of the community's groups, so read literally the definition put a deleted group's election on the member-party presentation path, where a holder of an unexpired credential that group issued could read it.

[VTI-VOT-029](https://trustoverip.github.io/dtgwg-vti-spec/) forbids that. Such an election is shown, and confirmed to exist, only to a holder of `vtc.elections.manage`, and the deleted group's identifier is never treated as a party outside the community.

## Wording

- **show/0.6 item 1**: adds "An election whose `credential` roll names a group the community no longer holds is seen only by a caller holding `vtc.elections.manage`, with or without a presentation (VTI-VOT-029)."
- **show/0.6 item 8.3**: the member-party test is now "`roll.memberOf` neither the community's own DID nor the DID of one of its groups, *as the community's records stood when the election was created*", and adds "A group the community has deleted since is still one of its groups here, never a member party: its election is answered as item 1 says, and a presentation of a membership credential the group issued shows it to nobody (VTI-VOT-029)."
- **show/0.6 `presentation` description**: "a party other than the community and its groups *that is itself a member of the community, never a group the community has since deleted (VTI-VOT-029)*".
- **list/0.5 item 1**: adds "Where `roll.memberOf` is a group the community no longer holds, the election is shown to no caller but one holding `vtc.elections.manage`, who is the one to cancel it: the deleted group has no members in the community's records, and its DID is never read as a member party's (VTI-VOT-029)."
- **list/0.5 payload description**: adds "nor one whose credential roll names a group the community has deleted to any caller but an administrator (VTI-VOT-029)".
- **tickets/issue/0.3 item 3**: the same "as the community's records stood when the election was created, so that a group the community has since deleted is never one (VTI-VOT-029)" in its member-party definition. Item 6.2 already answers a manager `rollUntrusted` for a deleted group, as VOT-029 requires.

## Versioning

This is an in-place change, with no new version folders. All three are `status: draft`, and CONTRIBUTING-SPECS "Version rules" says rewording a description in a draft happens in place. These versions are in `trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.2`, and a released version may still gain a description in place. No member, type, enum, bound, `proofRequirement` or error code changes. `check-published-schemas` passes: 5 changed spec files, all released, all additive. The generated Rust, TS, Go and Dart modules change only in their embedded description text.

## Checks run locally

`npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings`, `check-published-schemas`, all four generators (no drift), and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features vtc --test conformance` (656 passed).

title: fix(dart): keep trust_tasks' CHANGELOG.md under pub.dev's 256 KiB limit
body:
pub.dev refuses a `CHANGELOG.md` over 262144 bytes. `trust-tasks-dart/CHANGELOG.md` was 303894, so every `trust_tasks` publish since 0.9.11 failed ("`CHANGELOG.md` exceeds the maximum content length") and pub.dev is still at 0.9.10.

Knock-on effects: `tag-dart` for `trust_tasks_didcomm` / `trust_tasks_https` verifies against pub.dev's 0.9.10, which lacks trust-task-discovery 0.4, so it fails; and `release-pr` does not run after a failed publish, so no Release PR has opened since #1028.

- Entries for 0.8.29 and earlier move to `trust-tasks-dart/CHANGELOG-archive.md`, excluded from the package by a new `.pubignore`. `CHANGELOG.md` keeps 0.9.x (79 KB) and links the archive. The release script inserts at the first `## ` heading, which is unchanged.
- New `dart.yml` job `changelog-size` fails any `trust-tasks-dart*/CHANGELOG.md` over 230000 bytes.
- `dart pub publish --dry-run` lists `CHANGELOG.md (76 KB)` and not the archive.

After merge, `trust-tasks-dart-v0.9.23` (never published) is re-pushed at the merge commit, whose pubspec is still 0.9.23, so pub.dev publishes it.

title: spec(rooms): memberProfile — names near the head, look-alike names, before a name is found, several records by one author
body:
Addresses the four points in Keyring's review of #1035: https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1035#issuecomment-6646548218

All changes are to the `MemberProfileRecord` description in `specs/rooms/_shared/0.3/member-profile.schema.json`; no member, type, bound or `$ref` changes. Go and Dart bindings are regenerated (they carry the description as doc comments); Rust and TypeScript are unchanged.

## Versioning

`rooms/_shared/0.3` is amended in place. It was merged in #1035 after the last release, `trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.2` (a644a4270), so it is in no released library, and RELEASING.md / CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md allow a version merged since the last release to be fixed in place. No task schema `$ref`s this component, so it is in no registry bundle and no `by-digest` path changes. `check-published-schemas` passes: 1 changed spec file, 0 of them released. The change is description-only, which the gate would accept on a released version as well.

## The four points

1. **Writer guidance: keeping names near the head.** New paragraph *Near the room's head*: a member that writes any record to the room, a reaction included, SHOULD write its name record again (same key) when the `version` that write was assigned exceeds its `memberProfile` record's current `version` by more than 500. The number 500 is the largest page `rooms/records/list/0.6` returns (its maximum `limit`), so a reader that has listed the 500 versions before the earliest record it shows finds the name of every author who follows the rule. The distance is fixed rather than left to each writer because a reader can bound how far back it reads only if every writer bounds the same distance. It is counted in versions because every put reports one and a reader's `sinceVersion` counts them. It costs at most one record per writing member per 500 room versions. A new paragraph, *Writing it again*, covers both re-write triggers (this one and the existing epoch-advance one). It writes the name rule 2 currently gives the member's own author, not a name a device remembers. It keeps `writtenAt` and sets no new `editedAt`. A withdrawn name is not re-written. A client may do it on its next write, and one version satisfies both triggers.

2. **Look-alike names.** *Showing a name* now says a reader SHOULD apply the collision rule (show something that tells the authors apart) where two names are equal by their UTS #39 `skeleton()`, applied after NFC and case folding. The existing MUST for equality after NFC and case folding is unchanged. The skeleton is for comparing only and is never shown. Readers on different confusables data versions may disagree on a pair, which changes only which names they tell apart.

3. **Before a name is found.** New paragraph: until a reader finds a name it shows the next step of the order (petname, else a shortened DID). It MAY update a shown author when it later finds the name, or finds it changed or withdrawn, and SHOULD then update every place it shows that author. It MUST NOT show a guessed name: one from another room or DID, a directory, a DID document or a credential, one inferred from content, or a placeholder that reads as a name. A name found earlier in this room by rule 2 and kept is not a guess.

4. **Several name records from one author.** "Most recent wins" is the whole rule. Rule 2 gains a tie-break (equal times: greater `version`). A new paragraph, *Several records by one author*, says every record whose current version is by the author is weighed, whatever its key. A reader MUST NOT prefer the first record it met or set a later key aside. Reasons:
   - The name does not depend on reading order, so readers holding the same records agree whether they read from the start or back from the head.
   - A reader that opens only recent pages, which point 1 is designed for, can settle a name. A first-key rule would need the whole room to know no older record exists.
   - It fits rule 3. A rewrite of another member's record is the rewriting member's claim about themselves, and it is weighed like any other version by that member, by when the host stored it, not by whether the reader happened to see it first.

## Checks (run locally on this branch)

- `npm run validate`: 1295 specs, 169 shared schemas, pass
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: 1 changed spec file, 0 released, pass
- codegen (Rust, then `cargo fmt --all` as CI does), `build-ts-bindings`, `build-go-bindings`, `build-dart-bindings`, then `npm run check-bindings`: all four agree, pass
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`: 3906 passed, 0 failed
- `npm run build-bundles` + `npm run check-bundles`: 1289 bundles verified
- TypeScript: `tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (126 pass, 0 fail), `npm run smoke`, pass
- Go: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, pass
- Dart: `dart analyze --fatal-infos` (no issues), `dart test` (152 passed)

`rooms/watch`, `rooms/changed` and `rooms/keys/act` are not touched.

title: feat(vtn/registry): check a party against the network's trust registry, and registry status
body:
Two `vtn/*` read tasks for a network that publishes its membership to a trust registry. The registry in question may speak DIDComm or TSP only, with no HTTPS.

**`vtn/registry/check/0.1`.** Anyone asks the network to ask its registry whether a party is published as its member.
- The network queries the registry (the one its DID's `TrustRegistry` referral names) for the party under its own authority.
- It returns `member`, `listed`, and the registry's own answer document verbatim as `answer`, signed by the registry. A verifier can then check the answer came from the registry, rather than take the network's word.
- `reachable: false` (with a `reason`) is indeterminate, never "not a member" (VTI-REG-012).
- `noRegistry` when the network publishes to none.
- Proof is optional: the answer is what the registry already publishes.

**`vtn/registry/status/0.1`.** An administrator reads:
- the registry, how the network writes to it, and whether that transport is connected;
- the last reconcile (`put`, `deleted`, `failed`, `blocked`);
- when the registry answers, every record compared with what the entries project: `ok`, `missing`, `stale` or `wrong`.

It changes nothing and does not reconcile. `noRegistry` when there is none.

Generated: Rust (with conformance tests), TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass, and so do the conformance tests for both.

Consumer: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network (the VTN's `nnm registry`, the landing page's Check membership, and `nnm verify` against a DIDComm-only registry).

title: feat(vtc/networks/preview): read a network before joining it
body:
`vtc/networks/preview/0.1`: an administrator reads a Verifiable Trust Network before joining it.

A network invites a community with a URL and the DID to expect there. Before `vtc/networks/join/0.2` signs anything, the administrator needs to know what the network is, which roles they must assign a group to, and whether it really lists the community. The console can't fetch that itself: its policy keeps the browser on its own origin. So the community reads it server-side and answers.

**Request:** `{ url, network? }`. `network` is optional: an administrator who typed only a URL can still look.

**Response:**
- the network's own profile: `{ network, url, name, description?, owner?, framework? { iri, version }, roles: [{ name, required, description? }] }`;
- where the community stands with it: `listed`, `entryState?` (the network's state for the entry), `notListedReason?` and `membershipState?` (the community's own record).

`listed` is `true` only when the network's entry carries a listing that verifies as the network's, names the community with `lists/1`, and lists it as a `VTC`. That is the same check `join` makes. Not listed is a field, not a refusal.

**Errors:**
- `vtc/networks/preview:networkUnreachable` (retryable);
- `vtc/networks/preview:networkMismatch`: a DID other than `network`, or an answer not signed by the DID it answers as.

**Gating:** administrator standing only, no step-up; `sideEffects: none`. Its only request to the network is the community's own `vtn/entries/show`, the read `join` already makes.

Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass locally, as do the `vtc` conformance tests.
