title: feat(rooms/keys): rooms/keys/watch and rooms/keys/changed, and act 0.12 lists rooms/watch
body:
## What this adds

A wallet whose member keys are held by its VTA (its key holder) can now get the `rooms/changed` signal from #1036. Three changes, all new versions or new tasks. No released version is edited.

| | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **`rooms/keys/watch/0.1`** (new) | client → key holder. The key holder arms `rooms/watch/0.1` at one host, for one or more rooms, **as the member** (its own presentation and signature), at an **address the key holder controls** and uses for that one watch only. It returns `armed` / `expiresAt` per room, or the reason it was refused. | The wallet can't present as the member, and it has no address a host can reach. This task does both on the wallet's behalf. |
| **`rooms/keys/changed/0.1`** (new) | key holder → that client, one-way. Carries `roomId`, `member`, `host`, `latestVersion` and nothing else. | Passes the host's signal on: one per arming, constant shape, no address, no content. |
| **`rooms/keys/act/0.12`** (`extends: "0.11"`) | adds `rooms/watch/0.1` (`read`, presentation inserted) to the closed table, plus Producer item 6 on the `address`. | Lets a client that receives at an address of its own arm the watch as the member. |

The push binding (`bindings/push/0.1`, draft) gains one informative paragraph in §4. It names the intended mobile-wallet shape and adds no requirement.

## How it works

1. The wallet sends `rooms/keys/watch` to its VTA with `member`, `host` and `rooms[{roomId, sinceVersion}]`.
2. For each room, the VTA mints a presentation conferring exactly `read`, granted to the member, the same way `act` inserts one. It then sends `rooms/watch/0.1` signed by the member, with a dedicated address of its own: never the VTA's DID, the member's, the caller's or another watch's.
3. The host sends `rooms/changed` to that address once. The VTA checks that the sender is the host it armed at, that the room matches and that the watch is still armed. It then sends one `rooms/keys/changed` to the caller and forgets the watch.
4. The wallet reads the room through the VTA (`rooms/keys/browse` / `read`), applies `rooms/changed`'s reader rules, and re-arms with `rooms/keys/watch`.

**Re-arming.** Re-arming a watch that has not fired keeps its address, so it replaces the host's watch instead of adding a second one. Any arming after a signal is a new watch with a **new address**. The key holder forgets a watch once it fires, so it has no old address left to reuse. As a result, one address's re-arming times never form a member's reading pattern, on any tier, and the VTA does not need to know the tier.

**What the VTA records.** One record per armed watch, holding only: caller, member, room, host, the address and its receiving key material, and when the watch lapses. It does **not** keep watermarks, signalled versions, signal times, or a history of addresses. It forgets the record when the watch fires, is cancelled or lapses (at most 30 days), when the caller's standing is withdrawn, or when it no longer holds the member's credentials for the room. It may log arm/cancel for the member's own audit.

**Authorization.** The entitlement is the same as `act`'s: acting as the member. Delegates are refused (`permissionDenied`). `member` is always named and must be a DID the key holder holds keys for, for its own principal, that the caller may act as; anything else gets `memberNotPrincipal`, and the key holder never picks a member for the caller. Standing in the room is the room's decision, made from the presentation.

## Keyring's review of #1036 ([comment](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1036#issuecomment-6646548855))

1. **An `act` version that lists `rooms/watch`.** Added: `rooms/keys/act/0.12`, row `rooms/watch/0.1` → `read`, presentation inserted. A cancel takes the same presentation. The `address` is the one member of the document that belongs to the producer, so the new Producer item 6 limits it. It must be a DID the producer receives at and uses only for watches. It must not be the identifier the producer authenticates to its key holder with, the key holder's DID or the member's. On a `private` room it must also be used for that one watch only. A client with no such address must not use this row and uses `rooms/keys/watch` instead.
2. **Which address a phone names.** The intended shape is **(a) its agent**, through `rooms/keys/watch`. The agent arms the watch at an address of its own (not its own DID, which would tell the host which agent serves the member). It passes the signal on to the phone with `rooms/keys/changed`, which waits in the phone's mediator queue and wakes it like any other document. **(b)**, a DID the phone holds behind its own mediator, is possible through `act/0.12` but is not the intended shape for a wallet whose keys are at its agent. This is stated in `rooms/keys/watch` (Abstract), in `act/0.12` (*Which address a phone names*), and informatively in the push binding §4.
3. **Several rooms at one host in one request.** Added at the key holder: `rooms/keys/watch` takes up to 64 rooms at one host and answers per room. The batching **stops at the key holder**. No multi-room `rooms/watch` is added. On a `private` room, presentations are zero-knowledge precisely so that a host cannot link one member's reads, and a request or an address covering several rooms would tell the host that one party reads all of them. `rooms/watch` forbids the host to make that link. So each room is armed with its own request, presentation and address. A phone woken for several rooms needs no batched signal: its mediator coalesces the queued `rooms/keys/changed` documents into one wake (`push/wake` producer item 4).
4. **Records stored before `createdAt`.** `rooms/keys/changed/0.1` (*What a reader does with a signal*) says: such a record has only `updatedAt`, which moves on an edit, so a reader that keeps no copy counts an edit of an old message as unread. This is accepted: it is bounded to old records, it errs toward showing something, and a reader that keeps a copy tells the two apart by key.
5. **Phones on `private` rooms.** Stated plainly in `act/0.12` (*Changes from 0.11*) and in `rooms/keys/watch` (*Correlation*): polling with `rooms/keys/browse` is the expected choice for a phone on a `private` room, unless its agent watches for it with `rooms/keys/watch`, which bears the cost of a fresh address per arming instead of the phone.

## Alternatives rejected

- **`act` only, with the VTA's own DID as the address.** `act` is stateless and never sends (Recipient item 7), so the VTA would not know whose signal arrived or where to send it. The VTA's own DID would also reach the host, which `rooms/keys/browse`/`read` forbid, and it would be one address shared by every watch, which breaks `rooms/watch` Producer item 2 on `private` rooms.
- **`act` plus a separate "allocate me an address" task.** That makes three tasks instead of two. The address would leak to the client, and the VTA would hold a forwarding record not tied to the host's arming.
- **Passing the signal on through `notifications/notify` and the held store (`vta/notifications/*`, deposit).** Held notifications are durable records the client lists. They don't push to the wallet, they would add retention to a transient signal, and they model "a thing exists you may take part in", signed by an originator for relay, which is a different kind of thing. Deposit runs the other way (client → VTA).
- **`sync/event`.** A closed vault/ACL/policy event union, with per-consumer `seq`, maintainer retention of 30 days or more and retried delivery. That is the opposite of one transient signal per arming.
- **`push/wake` alone.** Contentless, so the wallet would not learn which room changed. It is reused implicitly: the `rooms/keys/changed` document waiting in the queue is what the mediator wakes the device for. The key holder **SHOULD NOT** add a wake of its own, because one per signal would show the gateway how often the member's rooms move.
- **Forwarding `rooms/changed/0.1` itself to the wallet.** Its parties and consumer rule ("act only when it comes from the host you armed with") don't fit a key-holder hop. It also lacks `member`, which a wallet needs when one VTA holds two members of a room.

`task-consent/granted` is the precedent for the delivery path: a fire-and-forget VTA → client document, delivered at the mediator where the client collects from its agent.

## Checks

Run locally on this branch:

- `npm run validate`: passes (1298 specs). Wire conventions, casing, stale references (0) and free-text bounds are all clean.
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: passes. No released spec file changed.
- Regenerated Rust (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`), TS, Go and Dart bindings, and committed the result.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree (1298 specs; error codes and size bounds match).
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets`: 3919 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`: ok.
- `npm run build-bundles` + `npm run check-bundles`: 1292 bundles verified.
- `trust-tasks-ts`: `npm run build` ok; `npm test` 126/126.
- `trust-tasks-go`: `go build`, `go vet` and `go test ./...` ok.
- `trust-tasks-dart`: `dart analyze`, no issues.

title: feat(vtc/badges): awards/share and awards/unshare — a holder shows an award outside the community (vtc/badges/awards/{share,unshare}/0.1)
body:
## What

The two tasks the `vtc/badges` family reserved for showing a badge outside the community (the VTC badges design note's "Outside" row; VTI Community Badges chapter VTI-BDG-070 – 072):

- **`vtc/badges/awards/share/0.1`** — the holder of an accepted award of a badge the community marked `shareableOutside` asks; the community answers the public locations it serves the award at: a **verification location** (the credential exactly as issued, with its status in the community's own set, for any Open Badges verifier) and, where it serves one, a **baked image** (the badge's picture with the credential baked in). The locations are the community's to choose, unguessable (a token of at least 128 bits, never derived from the award, the badge, the holder or the credential), the same on a repeat, and disclose no other holder and no count (VTI-BDG-071). They stop serving on unshare, when the award is taken back, when the badge is retired and when the holder departs; a stopped location answers as one that never existed. Codes: `badgesOff`, `notFound` (unknown, another member's and not-yet-accepted answer alike), `notShareable` (`details.reason`: `insideOnly` | `kudos` | `retired`), `publicLocationUnavailable` (no public origin; retryable).
- **`vtc/badges/awards/unshare/0.1`** — stops it. Idempotent; not a revocation. Codes: `badgesOff`, `notFound`.

Both are acts of the member: a member portal key authorized for `vtc/badges` under `auth/oob/grant/0.3` may sign them (VTI-BDG-095), as the other holder tasks of the family.

## Shared schema

`specs/vtc/badges/_shared/0.1/badge.schema.json` gains `AwardShare` and the optional `Award.shared` (`verificationUrl`, `bakedImageUrl?`, `since`) — additive to the released 0.1 (an optional member and a new `$defs` entry), so every library takes it as a patch.

## Consumer

VTI implements both in `vtc-service` once this is released and pinned, together with the public artefacts the chapter requires (the Achievement document and picture of a shareable badge, VTI-BDG-051; the verification page and baked image, VTI-BDG-070) as declared REST exceptions, since Open Badges verifiers speak HTTPS.

## Checks

`npm run validate` passes with the warnings it had before (none from these specs). Both specs carry the Security & Privacy section with its four sub-headings, declare `issuedAtRequirement: REQUIRED`, and come with invalid-examples.

title: feat(vtc): badges shown outside — the long-lived credential in the community's status set, and the community's endorsement embedded (VTI-BDG-060 – 063)
body:
## What

Phase 3a of member badges (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-badges.md`): the **outside credential regime** (VTI-BDG-062/063) and the **community's endorsement embedded in every badge credential** (the part of VTI-BDG-060 #2477 left out).

## The outside regime

- `shareableOutside` is accepted on `vtc/badges/create` and `vtc/badges/promote` for a community badge and fixed from then on (a kudos badge is still refused it; `update` still refuses it as fixed at creation).
- Such a badge's credential is long-lived — `settings.credentialValidDays`, default 730 — and carries a `credentialStatus` slot in the **community's** own revocation list, the set every community credential uses, allocated at random. One slot per badge and holder (`bslot:<badgeId>:<entryId>` in the `badges` keyspace), reused by every re-issue and renewal, so a repeat award or a renewal never takes a second slot. Never a set of the badge's or the group's own (VTI-BDG-062, VTI-CRD-014).
- **The open question is settled**: the status list credential is the community's while the badge credential's issuer is the group. The W3C Bitstring Status List v1.0 Recommendation (May 2025) compares no issuers in its validate algorithm and states the two "might differ" (§2.2 and the note after §3.2). Recorded in the design note.
- The bit is flipped on three paths (VTI-BDG-063): the holder's last award taken back (`settle_after_revoke`), the badge retired (`handle_retire`, after the group's own one bit), and the holder's departure (`ceremony::execute`, beside the groups' and badges' departure hooks). An inside-only credential keeps lapsing with its renewal; nothing changes for it.

## The endorsement

Every badge credential's Achievement now carries `endorsement: [<EndorsementCredential>]`: an Open Badges 3.0 `EndorsementCredential` whose subject is the Achievement, signed by the community's VTA **as the community** (`keys/sign-document` with the community's key) on first need and kept on the badge (`Badge.endorsement`), so later issues sign once, as the group. An outside verifier sees who stands behind the issuer from the credential alone (VTI-BDG-064's first way); the community's authority credential to the group says the same.

## Console

"May be shown outside" on the new-badge form and on a kudos badge's promotion; the credential's life (30 – 3650 days) in the settings page.

## Tests

`tests/it/badges.rs`: a badge shown outside is created and shown as `outside`; accepting signs the endorsement as the community and then the credential as the group, embedding it signed, with a status slot and the community's life; a repeat award re-issues in the same slot with no second endorsement; taking one award back leaves the bit clear, taking the last back sets it; retiring sets another holder's; departure sets what the member still holds; an inside-only badge gets no status and still embeds the endorsement. The refusal tests move off `shareableOutside` (now accepted) to another `settingsInvalid` cause. Unit tests on the document builder cover the status and the endorsement.

## Docs

`docs/03-vtc/badges.md` (*The credential*: both regimes), the crate guide's badges entry, the design note's status, phases and the settled question.

feat(vtc): badges shown outside — the long-lived credential in the community's status set, and the community's endorsement embedded (VTI-BDG-060 – 063) (#2482)

The outside credential regime for member badges, and the one piece of
VTI-BDG-060 the first build left out.

- `shareableOutside` is accepted on `create` and `promote` for a community
  badge (refused on a kudos badge as before) and fixed from then on. Such a
  badge's credential is long-lived (`settings.credentialValidDays`, default
  730) and carries a `credentialStatus` slot in the **community's** own
  revocation list — the set every community credential uses, allocated at
  random — one slot per badge and holder (`bslot:<badge>:<entry>`), reused by
  every re-issue and renewal. Never a set of the badge's or the group's own
  (VTI-BDG-062, VTI-CRD-014). The list's credential is the community's while
  the badge credential's issuer is the group: the W3C Bitstring Status List
  Recommendation compares no issuers and says the two "might differ".
- The bit is flipped when the holder's last award is taken back, when the
  badge is retired, and when the holder departs (VTI-BDG-063:
  `credential::{revoke_holder, revoke_all_holders, revoke_departed}`); an
  inside-only credential still lapses with its renewal.
- Every badge credential now embeds the community's Open Badges 3.0
  `EndorsementCredential` of the Achievement, signed by the VTA as the
  community on first need and kept on the badge (VTI-BDG-060), so an outside
  verifier sees who stands behind the issuer from the credential alone.
- Console: "May be shown outside" on the new-badge form and on promotion;
  the credential's life in the settings.

Sharing an award outside (`awards/share|unshare`, the public verification
page and the baked image) is the next phase and needs the Trust Task family
first; this build issues the credential such a badge needs.

body:
Bumps [aws-lc-rs](https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs) from 1.18.2 to 1.19.0.
Release notes

Sourced from aws-lc-rs's releases.

aws-lc-rs v1.19.0

What's Changed

  • Add AES OFB, CFB8, and CFB1 modes by @​lokeswarivejju in aws/aws-lc-rs#1259
    • Adds OperatingMode::OFB, OperatingMode::CFB8, and OperatingMode::CFB1 for AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 through both the one-shot and streaming cipher APIs.
  • Add an on-demand AWS-LC self-test API by @​Elvrarin in aws/aws-lc-rs#1262
    • Adds aws_lc_rs::try_fips_self_test(), allowing applications to re-run all AWS-LC cryptographic algorithm self-tests without calling the sys crate through unsafe FFI. This does not re-run the module integrity test.
  • Add Keccak-256 digest support behind "unstable" feature flag by @​fabrice102 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1266
    • Adds aws_lc_rs::unstable::digest::KECCAK256 and KECCAK256_OUTPUT_LEN behind the unstable feature for use with the existing digest::digest and digest::Context APIs.
  • Add configurable RSA-PSS salt lengths by @​PaulDance in aws/aws-lc-rs#1267
    • Adds RsaPssSaltLength::{Digest, Max, Custom} and with_pss_salt_length builders on RsaSignatureEncoding and RsaParameters, covering signing and verification for both message and precomputed-digest APIs.
  • Implement Clone for signing key pairs by @​JakeHuneau in aws/aws-lc-rs#1277
    • rsa::KeyPair, EcdsaKeyPair, Ed25519KeyPair, and PqdsaKeyPair can now be cloned directly rather than wrapped in an Arc.
    • Clones share the immutable, reference-counted EVP_PKEY; key material is not duplicated, and a clone remains usable after the original is dropped.

Upstream AWS-LC

  • aws-lc-sys v0.47.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.12.0 (previously v5.11.0).
  • aws-lc-fips-sys v0.14.4 updates its bundled AWS-LC FIPS 4.2.0 snapshot with recent FIPS 4.x backports.

    • The default aws-lc-sys system-library path now accepts AWS-LC 4.2.0 or newer, previously 5.7.0, allowing use of a FIPS 4.x system library.

  • Share cc compiler detection across builds by @​johncarmack1984 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1273
    • Reuses compiler detection results across the main library build and compiler feature probes, reducing repeated compiler invocations during cold builds.

title: docs(vtc): the vtc-mcp operator page, the vtc-community skill, and --mint-did-key
body:
Phase 6 of the `vtc-mcp` design note (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-mcp.md`, #2470) — the last.

## What lands

- **The operator page, `docs/03-vtc/vtc-mcp.md`**, the sibling of `docs/02-vta/vta-mcp.md`: what the bridge exposes (the tools, the guide resources, the prompts, with the annotation and pinned-slug tests named); the security model — four layers and which one is load-bearing, the gap the local guard closes, *parked is an outcome*, *deciding is vouching* (why `vtc_actions_decide` always asks the human and why an `approver` entry is the usual shape), what the bridge does not protect you from; the two identity rungs with the enrolment recipe (`--mint-did-key`, then `cnm access grant` as an approver, a narrowed moderator, or a one-group manager; a member's persona bundle); transport selection and why an advertised session is never replaced by HTTPS; hardening flags and recipes; observability and degraded mode; host configuration; a worked example of a new group that parks on a `grants` binding and is approved by a second administrator's assistant; troubleshooting; what this is not.
- **The Claude Code skill**, `vtc-mcp/skills/vtc-community/SKILL.md`: how an assistant works through the bridge — start with status, whoami and supported tasks; read the catalog's schema before a call; the prompt-or-tool table for the six jobs; parked is not failed; read the guide first; identifiers and the ballot rule.
- **`vtc-mcp --mint-did-key`**: mints the dedicated agent's Ed25519 `did:key` on the machine that runs the bridge and prints the DID (to hand to an administrator) and the key (to keep as `VTC_MCP_AGENT_KEY`), so no key is ever handed from one person to another. The CSPRNG and encoding are the SDK's own (`getrandom`, raw seed base58btc).
- `docs/README.md` rows, the crate's README and `CLAUDE.md`, and the design note marked **implemented** with its phase table complete.

## Tests

One new test: a minted `did:key` reconstructs from its key, two mints differ, and the flag parses. The bridge's 24 tests, `cargo clippy -p vtc-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the workspace clippy and `cargo fmt --check` are green.

## After this

The programme in #2470 is complete. Follow-ups recorded in the note's open questions: whether the dedicated-agent rung deserves a built-in `agent` role ceiling, and moving `cnm`'s own transport selection onto `VtcClient::connect_resolved`.

title: feat(vtc-mcp): the six workflow tools and the action-list tools
body:
Phase 5 of the `vtc-mcp` design note (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-mcp.md`, #2470): the workflow tools and the action-list tools.

## What lands

**Six workflow tools** — `group_setup`, `board_create`, `election_create`, `room_open`, `member_admit`, `admin_grant` — as thin orchestrators (`vtc-mcp/src/workflows.rs`). Each sends the steps of one of the prompts' workflows in order, **every step through the same guard and recorder as a `vtc_call` and under its own Trust Task URI**, so `--read-only`, `--deny` and `--confirm` apply per step exactly as they would to the assistant sending it by hand. A flow **stops at the first step that does not complete** — refused by the community, parked for other administrators, refused by the local policy, or declined by the operator — and returns how far it got, step by step with each step's answer, so the assistant carries on with `vtc_call` or `vtc_actions_show`. A step's payload is the task's own JSON (schema-checked by `send_task`); the tool derives only the identifiers later steps need (`groupId`, `boardId`, `roomId`, `electionId`) from the answers. `board_create` and `election_create` check the ballot box against the community's trusted list before creating; `admin_grant` reads the subject's entry first and stops if one exists, and when the grant parks it reads the action so the report says who approves.

**Four action-list tools.** `vtc_actions_list` and `vtc_actions_show` (the action's summary re-derived from the payload that would run and verified against it, with the match code, and whether this identity may decide). `vtc_actions_decide` approves or denies as this identity, as a `task-consent/decision` signed with its own key — and **always asks the operator** through the host, shown the verified summary and the match code to compare with the requester's, whatever `--confirm` says; a host that cannot ask gets a refusal, never an unconfirmed decision. `vtc_actions_cancel` cancels an action this identity requested. `task-consent/decision` is placed `Sensitive` in the shared table.

Plumbing: the workflow tools live in their own `#[tool_router]` merged into the handler; `begin` takes an optional host peer so a step can be exercised without one (a step that needs confirming is then refused, never run unconfirmed).

Docs: `vtc-mcp/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the design note's phase table.

## Tests

Seven in `workflows.rs`, beside the sixteen from before: every workflow URI is pinned; a group is set up step by step over a scripted loopback community and the report lists the four steps with the reason carried onto each appointment; a refused create stops the flow with nothing more sent; a read-only bridge refuses the first step locally before anything is sent, and a step needing confirmation with no host is refused; an untrusted ballot box stops a board before the create; a grant to an existing entry is stopped locally; a decision is never sent without the operator (the show is sent, the decision is not, and the refusal carries the verified title and the match code). `cargo clippy` on the three MCP crates and the workspace with warnings as errors, and `cargo fmt --check`, are green.

## Not in this PR

Phase 6: the operator page `docs/03-vtc/vtc-mcp.md`, a worked example, and a Claude Code skill wrapping the same prompts.

title: feat(vtc): member badges in the console and the member portal (VTI-BDG-001 – 095)
body:
## What

The console plugin and the member-portal pages for **member badges**, over the `vtc/badges/*` 0.1 tasks #2477 serves (design: `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-badges.md`; chapter VTI-BDG-001 – 095). With this, phase 1 of the programme is complete end to end.

## Console — *Community → Badges*

`admin-ui/src/plugins/badges.tsx` over `admin-ui/src/lib/badges.ts`. Shown to holders of `vtc.badges.admin`, `vtc.groups.manage` (an owner's qualified grant) or `vtc.config.admin`.

- **List**: every badge the administrator or owner may see, with a notice when the community has badges off.
- **Settings** (`vtc.config.admin`, bound step-up through `postSignedWithStepUp`): on/off, who may make a kudos badge (nobody, chosen roles and groups, every active member), the kudos limits, pins, offer expiry, `membersMayRequest`, `automaticBadges`. Nothing the community wrote (`updatedAt`) is sent back.
- **New badge** (`vtc.badges.admin`): name, description, criteria, picture (uploaded through `vtc/badges/images/upload` with the portal's own `prepare`/`toBase64Url`), repeatable, requestable (disabled when the settings forbid it), listed, who sees its holders, an automatic rule (the groups' `RuleEditor`, only when the settings allow), owners.
- **One badge**: summary and edit; give to chosen members or to everyone in a group (`awards/offer`, the skipped ones named); requests for it and its owners, which are the badge group's requests and managers through `@/lib/groups`; every award with its state, hidden mark, giver and note, withdrawn or taken back with a reason; a kudos badge's givings and its promotion; retire (step-up for a community badge).

Every act is signed by the console key, never a portal key (VTI-BDG-095). Nothing here parks in the action list.

## Portal — `#/badges`

`admin-ui/src/members/Badges.tsx` over `admin-ui/src/members/badges-api.ts`, signed by the portal's delegated key through `send`.

- **Your badges**: the offers waiting, each accepted or declined (a decision surface rendered inside `Protected`); the wall with order, pins, hide/show again and who sees it; hidden badges; every badge to browse; the kudos badges the member made.
- **One badge**: picture, description, criteria, owners (named through the directory as the member sees it), who holds it (projected and hidden-aware, as the task answers), asking its owners for it (`vtc/groups/join` on `badge.groupId`, withdrawn with `vtc/groups/leave`), giving a kudos badge to a member found in the directory.
- **Make a badge** (`#/badges/new`): a kudos badge with a picture uploaded from the browser.
- **A member's card** shows their wall (`WallSection` in `Directory.tsx`), pinned first, with the kudos total where the community shows it, and lets another member give them a kudos badge from there.
- **Home**: a Badges tile and an attention line for offers waiting (`badgesStatus`, `badgesAttention`).

When the community has badges off every page shows one line and nothing else.

## Wire

- `Badges*01Payload` / `Badges*01Response` wrappers for all 24 tasks in `vta_sdk::openapi` (with the census checks), listed in `routes::openapi_spec`; `openapi.json` regenerated with `UPDATE_OPENAPI=1`, `wire.ts` with `npm run wire:generate`; aliases in `wire-types.ts`.
- The 24 badge tasks listed among the console's spine-dispatched tasks in `tests/it/trust_task_manifest.rs`, so `every_admin_ui_task_is_enforced_by_a_route` holds.
- The four badge listings pinned in `list-limits.json` (200 each, from the schemas), their call sites in `list-limits.test.ts`. The badge Type URIs are spelled out in full in both API modules because the census matches the literal.

## Tests

- `plugins/Badges.test.tsx`: the list and its gates, badges off, defining a badge after an upload, offering to chosen members and taking an award back with a reason, saving the settings with a reason and without `updatedAt`.
- `members/Badges.test.tsx`: offers accepted and declined, the wall arranged (pin, order, visibility, hide), badges off, one badge with its holders and a request to its owners, not-found, the home status.
- `Portal.test.tsx` routes; the list-limit census over the new call sites.

## Docs

`docs/03-vtc/badges.md` (*In the member portal and the console*), the crate guide's badges entry, the design note's status.

title: feat(vtc-mcp): the community's guides as resources and one prompt per workflow
body:
Phase 4 of the `vtc-mcp` design note (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-mcp.md`, #2470): the VTC knowledge an assistant needs, shipped with the bridge as MCP resources and prompts.

## What lands

- **Ten guide resources**, `vtc://guide/{groups, boards, elections, rooms, rooms-quickstart, admission, lifecycle, vetting, directory, admin-access}`: the workspace's own `docs/03-vtc/*.md`, embedded with `include_str!` at build time. One source of truth, pinned to the binary's own version; a guide moved or renamed breaks the build.
- **Six prompts**, one per multi-step job — `setup-group`, `create-board`, `run-election`, `open-data-room`, `admit-member`, `grant-administration`. Each renders an ordered brief: the preconditions (who must hold what, what must be configured), the tasks to send in order with what to put in each, which steps **park** on the community's action list and who approves (group authority bindings, binding elections, referred admissions, authority-conferring grants, admin invites), what the member sees afterwards, and the guides to read first. Optional arguments (`name`, `subject`, `role`, …) fold in what the operator already said. The content is drawn from the guides themselves — a prompt links the guide rather than restating it.
- **`every_slug_a_prompt_names_is_pinned`**: every task a prompt names, in a step or in backticks anywhere in its text, is held to `vti_specs::schema_index`, so a prompt cannot send the assistant after an operation `vtc_call` would refuse.
- The server declares the `prompts` capability, lists and renders them, and lists and serves the guides as `text/markdown` resources; the instructions tell the assistant when to reach for a prompt.
- Docs: `vtc-mcp/README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, the design note's phase table.

## Tests

Four in `guides.rs` (the pinned-slug census; every prompt names real guides and every guide is real and reachable; names are unique and the six are present; rendering folds in arguments and marks parked steps), beside the twelve from phase 3. `cargo clippy -p vtc-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are green.

## Not in this PR

Phase 5 (the six workflow tools and `vtc_actions_show` / `vtc_actions_decide`), phase 6 (the operator page `docs/03-vtc/vtc-mcp.md` and a Claude Code skill wrapping the same prompts).

title: feat(vtc): member badges — the vtc/badges/* 0.1 family, badges backed by badge groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos (VTI-BDG-001 – 095)
body:
## What

Phase 1 backend of **member badges** (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-badges.md`, #2469): the 24 pinned `vtc/badges/*` 0.1 tasks (#2473) served on the dispatch spine, per the VTI Community Badges chapter (VTI-BDG-001 – 095, trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#105).

## How it is built

- **A community badge is a badge group.** `create` mints the group exactly as `vtc/groups/create` does and records `badge_id` on it; owners are its managers, holders its members, requests and owners reuse the groups' tasks, `retire` deletes the group. A badge group never carries authority (`bindings/add` refuses it) and is left out of `vtc/groups/list` and the shared-groups audience.
- **An award is an offer until accepted.** `awards/offer` and `kudos/give` record `offered`; `mine/accept` has the VTA sign an Open Badges 3.0 `OpenBadgeCredential` as the group's DID (the community as the Achievement's `creator`, one `evidence` entry per award) **before** the membership is recorded. `groups::credential::issue` branches to the badge credential for any group with `badge_id`, so admission by request, by rule and renewal issue the same profile.
- **Hidden is portal-only.** `badges::Prefs` holds hidden, pins, order and wall visibility; walls, `holders/list` and counts leave a hidden holder out; `awards/list` shows owners `hidden: true`.
- **Kudos** within the community's limits (every giving counts whatever its later state); `promote` turns a kudos badge into a community badge and offers every holder.
- **Settings** behind `vtc.config.admin` and a bound step-up; a community badge's `retire` takes the step-up too. Holder tasks accept the portal's delegated key (`vtc/badges` joins `PORTAL_SIGNING_SCOPE`); owners' and administrators' tasks never do.
- New: keyspaces `badges` and `badge_images` (backed up), capability `vtc.badges.admin`, audit event `BadgeChanged`, departure and sweep hooks, `directory::images::collect_except` so the badge picture store reuses the directory's collector.

## Scope

Inside-only credential regime: `create` refuses `shareableOutside` until the community-owned status set is served (phase 3). Console and portal pages are the next PR; this PR serves the tasks and documents them (`docs/03-vtc/badges.md`, the crate guide's flow entry).

## Tests

`vtc-service/tests/it/badges.rs`: settings on/off and the step-up, a community badge backed by a group (and absent from the groups list), offer → accept issues the Open Badge as the group then records the membership, repeat awards append evidence, decline and withdraw record nothing, hidden is portal-only, take-back ends the membership, kudos limits and the administrator's view, arranging and pins, retire deletes the group and keeps the holder's record. The refusal tests drive every code the 24 specifications declare (70 witnessed in `error_code_census`; retire's two key-holder codes are baselined, since deleting a badge group asks the VTA nothing). Plus unit tests on the records, the arrangement and the credential document.

title: feat(vtc-mcp): a VTC as MCP tools, over the transport its DID document advertises
body:
Phase 3 of the `vtc-mcp` design note (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-mcp.md`, #2470): the community bridge itself.

## What lands

**`vtc-client`: `VtcClient::connect_resolved`.** Connects as a `SessionIdentity` — a `did:webvh` secrets bundle (a member's persona) or an Ed25519 `did:key` — over the transport the community's DID document advertises, matched on service type: TSP (the TSP leg of the one mediator socket for a bundle), else DIDComm, else signed documents over the `VTCRest` endpoint. A session the community advertises that cannot be opened is `VtcError::NoTransport`, never a silent downgrade to HTTPS; `TransportChoice::Rest` is the operator's explicit way to do that for a diagnosis. `SessionIdentity` has a hand-written `Debug` that never prints the key.

**`vtc-mcp`** (`publish = false`), a stdio `rmcp` server that is a native Trust Task client — every tool call is one signed document sent in-process; it never runs `cnm`/`pnm` and never reads a CLI's stored login:

- `vtc_list_operations` — the catalog of every pinned request Type URI, read from `vti_specs::schema_index` (description, payload schema, declared error codes), with each entry's risk class, this bridge's policy decision and, once the community has been asked, whether it serves the task. Slug globs narrow it; `detail: "full"` adds the schema and codes.
- `vtc_call` — any pinned operation by Type URI, through `VtcClient::send_task` (unpinned refused, payload schema-checked first). A parked write (`VtcError::Parked`) is returned as a successful result with `status: "parked"` naming the action: nothing failed, nothing is resent.
- `vtc_supported_tasks` (discovery 0.4, cached for the catalog), `vtc_whoami` (`auth/whoami`, with the community's reason when it does not answer for this key), `vtc_status`.
- Resources `vtc://status`, `vtc://operations`, `vtc://calls/recent`.
- The identity ladder: rung 1 `--agent-secrets` (bundle), rung 2 `--agent-did` + `--agent-key`; both is an error, half of rung 2 is an error naming the missing field, neither serves degraded so `vtc_status` can say so. There is no rung that replays an operator's login.
- Every call goes through the shared guard (`Guard::node = "VTC"`) and recorder from `vti-mcp-common`; a few community-shaped identifiers (`groupId`, `boardId`, `electionId`, `subject`, …) are added to the redactor's safe keys.

Workspace wiring: members, default-members, `Dockerfile.nitro`, the crate map, layout and count in `CLAUDE.md`; `vtc-mcp/{README,CLAUDE}.md`; the design note's phase table.

## Tests

- `vtc-mcp` (12): the tool set; annotations against the shared classifier; the catalog is exactly the pinned index with risk and policy, narrowed by glob, `full` carrying schema and codes, a read-only bridge denying `groups/create` and allowing `groups/list`; degraded status; a call signed and posted over loopback HTTP with its answer returned; a refusal carrying the community's document and an unpinned URI sending nothing; the parked outcome; the ladder (no rung, half a rung, two rungs, an inline bundle); the defaults.
- `vtc-client` (+3): a `did:key` signs as itself; a bundle signs with `#key-0` and refuses without an Ed25519 key; the advertised-transport summary.

`cargo clippy -p vtc-client --all-targets` with and without `--features tsp`, the three crates' tests, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and the Nitro-copy and version-requirement scripts are green.

## Not in this PR

Phase 4 (the guide resources and workflow prompts), phase 5 (workflow tools and the action-list tools), phase 6 (the operator page). `cnm`'s own transport selection still has its copy of the TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS logic; moving it onto `connect_resolved` is a follow-up, since `cnm`'s `auto` falls back to HTTPS with a warning where the bridge refuses.

title: refactor(vta-mcp): share the guard and call recorder through vti-mcp-common, classifying every pinned Trust Task
body:
Phase 2 of the `vtc-mcp` design note (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-mcp.md`, #2470): what the MCP bridges share moves out of `vta-mcp` so the coming `vtc-mcp` does not copy it.

## What lands

- **`vti-mcp-common`** (`publish = false`): `guard` (the risk classifier, allow/deny slug globs, `--read-only`, confirm levels) and `observability` (stderr start/finish lines, the redacted ring, the owner-only JSONL audit file), moved with `git mv` from `vta-mcp`. `Guard::node` names the node in a confirmation prompt (`Approve destructive VTA operation …`); `init_tracing` takes the bridge's tracing target.
- **One classification table for every pinned Trust Task.** A new census in the shared crate holds every pinned request Type URI in `vti_specs::schema_index` to an override or a known verb. That surfaced about 170 tasks from the `vtc/*`, `rooms/*`, `vtn/*`, `voting/*`, `witness/*`, `git-ns/*`, `credential-exchange/*` and `auth/*` families the table had never seen; each is now placed, with its reason in the comment. Highlights: authority-conferring `add`/`decide`s (group managers and bindings, board facilitators, join decisions, direct admission, role set, admin invites, vetter grants, endorsement issue) are `Sensitive`; the community's exports, backup chunks and `policy/activate` are `Sensitive`; `close`, `certify`, `leave`, `withdraw`, `cast`, `suspend`, `repudiate`, `prune` are `Destructive`; a member's own badge wall actions stay `Mutating`.
- **`vta-mcp`** depends on the shared crate and keeps what is the VTA's alone: its tools and annotations (still asserted against the shared classifier), the connect ladder, and its own census over the VTA dispatch table (`src/census.rs`, through the shared helper, because that table carries the unpinnable framework specifications). No behaviour change for its tools; its 16 tests pass unchanged.
- Docs: `vti-mcp-common/{CLAUDE,README}.md`, the crate map and layout in the workspace `CLAUDE.md`, `vta-mcp/CLAUDE.md`, and the design note's phase table.

## Checks

`cargo test -p vti-mcp-common -p vta-mcp`, `cargo clippy -p vti-mcp-common -p vta-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `scripts/check-workspace-version-reqs.py` are green.

title: feat(vtc-client): send any pinned Trust Task by Type URI, report the transport, and discover what a community serves
body:
Phase 1 of the `vtc-mcp` design note (`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-mcp.md`, #2470): the generic, session-first sender an MCP bridge drives, in `vtc-client`.

## What lands

- **`VtcClient::send_task(type_uri, payload)`** — the one sender behind every admin verb, named by Type URI. Over the mediated session when the client holds one (TSP leg when enabled, DIDComm otherwise); signed with the operator's key and posted to the document endpoint only without one.
  - A Type URI `vti_specs::schema_index` does not pin, or a `#response` URI, is the new `VtcError::UnpinnedTask` and nothing is sent. `None` from the index means "not pinned", never "nothing to check".
  - The payload is validated against the pinned schema before sending; the declared error codes (so a declared `notFound` is `VtcError::NotFound`) and the response size bound come from the same index.
- **`VtcClient::discover(patterns)`** — `trust-task-discovery/0.4`, answered as the generated `Response`; `vtc_client::supported_type_uris` flattens it to bare URIs.
- **`VtcClient::transport()`** — which leg a call takes (TSP / DIDComm / HTTPS), for the bridge's status tool.

This is what reaches the families that have no typed method and no `cnm` command: `vtc/groups/*`, `vtc/directory/*`, `vtc/notifications/*`.

## What was dropped from phase 1

The note had listed a retry-safety classification for the VTC families. That was wrong: the VTC's receive pipeline claims every document's `id` before dispatch and answers a redelivery with the recorded response, uniformly, so a retry is safe by resending the same document (which the SDK's session retry does). `vta_sdk::retry_safety` is the VTA's own dispatch-side policy over `ALL_URIS`, not a place for `vtc/*` rows. The note is updated.

## Tests

Eight in `vtc-client/src/send.rs`: unpinned, `#response` and schema-refused calls send nothing (unroutable base); no key is `NotAuthenticated`; a pinned task is signed, posted to `/trust-tasks` with the right `type`, `issuer`, `recipient` and `proof`, and its response payload returned; a declared `notFound` is typed; discovery sends 0.4 and flattens both entry forms; the transport accessor. The two wire tests run against a loopback HTTP/1.1 responder.

`cargo clippy -p vtc-client --all-targets -- -D warnings` with and without `--features tsp`, `cargo test -p vtc-client`, and workspace clippy are green.

title: feat(vtc/badges): member badges — community badges backed by groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos, Open Badges credentials (vtc/badges/*/0.1)
body:
## What

A new family, `vtc/badges/*` 0.1 (24 tasks), for the VTI Community Badges chapter (VTI-BDG-001 – 095, trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#105): pictures with a name a member earns, holds and shows on their directory card. The community's gamification layer, carrying no authority.

Plus one additive member on the shared `Group` record, `badgeId`, so a group that backs a badge says so.

## The model

| Group | Tasks |
|---|---|
| Settings | `settings/show`, `settings/update` |
| Definitions | `create`, `update`, `retire`, `promote`, `list`, `show` |
| Pictures | `images/upload`, `images/get` |
| Awards (owners) | `awards/offer`, `awards/withdraw`, `awards/revoke`, `awards/list` |
| The holder | `mine/list`, `mine/accept`, `mine/decline`, `mine/hide`, `mine/show`, `mine/arrange` |
| Walls | `wall/show`, `holders/list` |
| Kudos | `kudos/give`, `kudos/list` |

- **A community badge is backed by a community group.** `create` creates the group exactly as `vtc/groups/create` does; owners are its managers, holders its members. Requests reuse `vtc/groups/join` and `requests/{list,decide}`; owners reuse `managers/{add,remove}`. No new request or owner tasks.
- **An award is an offer until accepted.** `awards/offer` records offers; `mine/accept` issues the badge credential as the group's DID first and records the membership after; `mine/decline` records nothing.
- **The credential** (stated in `mine/accept`): an Open Badges 3.0 `OpenBadgeCredential`, issuer the badge group, the community as the Achievement's `creator` with its endorsement embedded, one `evidence` entry per award. Inside the community: short-lived, renewed, no status (VTI-DIR-085's terms). Where holders may show it outside: long-lived, with a slot in the community's own status set.
- **Hidden is portal-only.** Owners (`awards/list`) still see every holder, marked hidden.
- **Kudos** are given by any member to any other within per-giver limits; each giving is an award of its own.

## Companions

- Design note: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2469.
- Chapter: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#105.

`npm run validate` passes.

title: Community Badges chapter: badges backed by groups, awards accepted by the member, kudos, Open Badges credentials (VTI-BDG-001 – 095)
body:
## What

A new chapter, **Community Badges** (`spec/12d-vtc-badges.md`, VTI-BDG-001 – 095): badges are pictures with a name a member earns, holds and shows on their directory card. The community's gamification layer, carrying no authority.

Registers `vtc.badges.admin` in Appendix C.3, and the chapter in `specs.json` and `STRUCTURE.md`.

## The model

- **A community badge is backed by a community group** (VTI-BDG-010 – 014): owners are its managers, holders its members, a request is a request to join, an automatic badge is a dynamic group, retiring deletes the group.
- **An award is an offer until accepted** (VTI-BDG-020 – 024): nothing is admitted, issued or shown before the member accepts; declining records nothing.
- **The holder's control** (VTI-BDG-030 – 033): hidden is portal-only; who sees a member's badges is the member's setting, never wider than the directory shows the card; holder lists go through the directory projection.
- **Kudos** (VTI-BDG-040 – 044): given by any member to any other within per-giver limits, each giving counted, never a credential; promotable to a community badge.
- **Credentials** (VTI-BDG-060 – 064): a badge group issues an Open Badges 3.0 credential in place of a group membership credential. Inside the community: short-lived, no status, on VTI-DIR-085's terms. Where holders may show it outside: long-lived, with a status in the community's own status set, which the community alone changes (VTI-CRD-014 holds because the set is the whole community's).
- **Outside** (VTI-BDG-070 – 072): the holder's choice per award; nothing public lists holders.
- **Registries** (VTI-BDG-080): badge groups projected as recognised issuers.

## Companion changes

- Design note: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-badges.md`.
- Trust Tasks: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf `specs/vtc/badges/*/0.1`, branch `feat/vtc-badges`.

The note proposes vtc-mcp: one generic vtc_call catalogued from the pinned vti-specs-vtc / vti-specs-rooms bundles (description, schema, error codes, policy), an identity ladder (member persona over DIDComm/TSP, dedicated agent entry, cnm session) that never falls through, the local guard and recorder extracted from vta-mcp into a shared crate, approvals surfaced as a parked outcome, and VTC knowledge shipped as MCP resources (the docs/03-vtc guides) and prompts for groups, boards, elections, data rooms, admission and administration, with workflow tools over the same guard. title: feat(web): verify signatures in the browser; verified relayed registry answers count as direct
body:
Operator feedback: a relayed registry answer that arrived over DIDComm/TSP and whose proof verifies is as good as a REST fetch of the same record, so the page shouldn't treat it as weaker.

**Page**
- New `verifyProof`: checks eddsa-jcs-2022 proofs in the browser (WebCrypto Ed25519 + the page's JCS), resolving the signer's `did:webvh` log from its host (`did:key` inline). It checks the key's purpose. With a proof set (Ed25519 + ML-DSA), the Ed25519 proof decides. The page reads the latest log state only; `nnm verify` also checks the hash chain.
- Applied to the network's answer, the three credentials, and the relayed registry answer. Each row says *signature verified in this browser*, *does not verify* (fail), or *not checked here* (why; unknown, not fail).
- **Relayed registry answer:** if the signature verifies, the row reads *the registry's signed answer, relayed by this network; signature verified*, and the answer counts the same as a direct one. If it doesn't verify, the answer is discarded (indeterminate).
- **Refusals:** a refusal now shows its real reason. `unsupportedType`/`permissionDenied` means "add this network's DID to the registry's ADMIN_DIDS". The contradictory "(answer is signed…)" suffix no longer appears on a failure.

**CSP:** `connect-src 'self' https:` (was `'self'` plus the registry's query origin), since signers' DID hosts are arbitrary.

**nnm verify:** it already rejects a relayed answer whose signature doesn't verify; the wording now says *the registry's signature verified* instead of *weaker than asking directly*.

**Checked:**
- In headless Chrome against live data from vtn.openvtc.net: the network answer, listing, grant and acknowledgement all verify in the browser.
- The live registry refusal (`unsupportedType`) shows the ADMIN_DIDS hint.
- The JS verifier was also checked in Node against the live registry's signed answer.
- fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.6
body:
### Added

- **vtn/registry**: Check a party against the network's trust registry through the network, and the registry status for administrators ([#1050](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1050))

vtn/registry/check/0.1 lets anyone ask a network to ask its trust registry whether a party is published as its member, returning the registry's own signed answer verbatim, so a verifier with no DIDComm or TSP session (a browser, or a registry that serves no HTTPS) can still check the registry rather than take the network's word for it. Unreachable is indeterminate, never not a member.

  vtn/registry/status/0.1 lets an administrator read the registry, the writer and whether it is connected, the last reconcile, and every record compared with what the entries project (ok, missing, stale, wrong).

- **vta/collection**: Settings/show and settings/set — collection by default per trust context, stored and changed at run time ([#1049](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1049))

Collection by default was one operator setting, off unless enabled
  (VTI-NTF-093). The VTI specification withdraws that in favour of a setting of
  each trust context, enabled unless disabled there (VTI-NTF-094 – VTI-NTF-098):

  - vta/collection/settings/show/0.1: a party with standing in a context reads
    its setting, who last changed it and when, and whether the VTA's operator
    has suspended collection by default everywhere (VTI-NTF-096).
  - vta/collection/settings/set/0.1: a party with administrative authority over
    the context (VTI-ACL-022) enables or disables it; stored, audited, applied
    before the answer — disabling closes the VTA's connections first
    (VTI-NTF-095). Answers the setting and whether it changed.
  - _shared/0.1 gains a CollectionSetting definition (new $defs entry), and the
    `disabled` reason is re-described: the context's own setting, or the
    operator's suspension (VTI-NTF-097, VTI-NTF-098). No enum value changes.
  - claim/list/release 0.1 prose and an error-code meaning now cite the
    per-context setting instead of VTI-NTF-093 (description edits only).

  The setting is not folded into list's response: it belongs to the context,
  not an identifier, and an added member in that released response would be
  refused by every existing client's additionalProperties: false.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat: write and read a DIDComm-only trust registry over the network's own session
body:
The VTN's trust registry speaks DIDComm and TSP only, with no HTTPS. #27 projected membership but wrote nothing, and #26/#27 read the registry over HTTPS, which this registry doesn't serve. This makes both work.

**Writes over the network's own DIDComm session.**
- Configured with `[messaging] mediator_did`, and `request_timeout_secs` for how long to wait for each answer.
- The session is `vti_common::host_session`'s, the one the witness and ballot box run, now with outbound requests (#2465). `vtn` holds one socket at the mediator as its DID, reconnects with backoff, and closes it on shutdown.
- `registry::MessagingWriter` replaces `NoWriteTransport` when configured. It sends `registry/record/put/0.3` and `delete/0.2`, and lists with `query/0.3` under this network's authority.
  - Each request names the registry as `recipient`, carries `issuedAt`, and is signed for `authentication` by the network's key: what the registry checks before it takes a write from a DID in `ADMIN_DIDS`.
  - A `delete` that finds nothing counts as success.
- The record now carries `recordType: "authorization"`, which the registry requires (#27 left it out).
- **The syncer:**
  - waits for the session before its first reconcile, which is the backfill, and reconciles again on each reconnect;
  - retries an incomplete reconcile after 30 s, backing off to 10 minutes, instead of waiting `sync_interval_secs`.
- **`vtn setup`:** `[messaging]` in the setup file fills the template's new `SERVICE_DIDCOMM` slot (a `DIDCommMessaging` service; `#key-1` is already the X25519 key) and writes `[messaging]`. `[messaging]` needs a provisioned `[identity]`; its keys come from the `[secrets]` store.

**Relayed reads** (`vtn/registry/check` and `vtn/registry/status`, specified in TF #1050 and pinned in VTI #2465):
- **`vtn/registry/check`** (anyone, unsigned): the network asks the registry over its session and returns `member` and `listed`, plus the registry's own signed answer verbatim. `reachable: false` is indeterminate.
- **`vtn/registry/status`** (administrators): the writer, `connected`, the last reconcile, and every record against the projection: `ok`, `missing`, `stale` or `wrong`.
- **`nnm registry status | check | records`:** asked directly when the profile has a `queryUrl`, otherwise relayed through these tasks. `check` says whether the relayed answer is signed by the registry's DID.
- **Landing page (Check membership, Verify):** with no `queryUrl`, the page relays and says so: "relayed by this network; the answer is signed by the registry's DID", or "take it as the network's word".
- **`nnm verify`:**
  - with no query URL it relays, and counts the answer only when the registry's signature on it verifies against the registry's DID, resolved independently, reading the records itself;
  - an answer the registry did not sign is indeterminate;
  - the report says "relayed by the network: weaker than asking directly".

**Also:**
- Onto the current VTI crates: `vti-vtn` 0.7, `vti-common` 0.60, `vta-sdk` 0.84, `vti-trust-task-server` 0.6, `vti-oob-server` 0.5, `vti-secrets` 0.33. No code changes were needed.
- The registry assumption is renumbered **A23** (#27 reused A22), and its text now says how records are written.
- Docs: `docs/trust-registry.md` (*Writes*: config, the DID service to add, mediator ACL, keys; *Checking records*: direct vs relayed), `docs/verifying.md`, README, both example tomls.

**Tests:**
- `records_are_written_as_signed_trust_tasks_over_the_session`: a registry behind the session seam checks every request as the Affinidi registry does (recipient, issuer, signature, `ADMIN_DIDS`, own authority, `recordType`). Not an admin: refused and reported. Admin: the backfill writes, and a departure deletes.
- `the_registry_is_checked_and_read_through_the_network`: unsigned check, the registry's answer verified, and admin status rows `ok`/`missing`; a non-admin gets `permissionDenied`.
- `without_a_registry_the_registry_tasks_say_so`.
- `a_relayed_registry_answer_counts_only_when_the_registry_signed_it` (nnm verify).
- The setup mediator test, and the served-task census (35 tasks).
- fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass locally.

Not run: against a live mediator and registry. `host_session` is the session the witness and ballot box run in production, but the outbound path is new.

Approvals are the one thing left open: required_approving_review_count is 0, so a pull request must be opened but need not be approved, and the unattributed-Copilot-approval setting is inert at a count of zero. The README records what raising the count to one would have cost against the 24 pull requests merged so far.

title: vti-rooms-v0.32.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: The VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head ([#2461](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2461))

* feat(rooms)!: the VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head

  rooms/keys/watch/0.1, rooms/keys/changed/0.1 and rooms/keys/act/0.12
  (trust-tasks-tf #1040), pinned in vti-specs-rooms (act 0.8-0.11 are now
  marked superseded upstream, so their uses carry allow(deprecated)).

  The VTA serves rooms/keys/watch/0.1: up to 64 rooms at one host, one
  outcome per room. A delegate is refused permissionDenied, a member the
  VTA holds no authentication key for that the caller may act as is
  refused memberNotPrincipal (details.member), a room named twice is
  malformedRequest. Each room is its own rooms/watch/0.1 at the host,
  completed as act/0.12 completes one (presentation narrowed to read,
  granted to and signed by the member), with an address of the VTA's
  own: a did:peer:2 minted for that one watch from fresh keys, whose
  only service is DIDCommMessaging at the VTA's mediator. A re-arm of an
  unfired watch keeps its address; every other arming takes a new one.
  Per room: notAMember, actionNotHeld, limitReached (the VTA's own bound:
  64 per member, 64 per caller, 256 in all; a VTA with no mediator holds
  none), hostUnreachable, or hostRefused with the host's code unaltered.

  The record (operations::room_key_watch, keyspace room_key_watches,
  encrypted at rest, excluded from backup) is Recipient item 6's list and
  nothing else: caller, member, room, host, address and its keys, lapse.
  messaging::watch_addresses holds one mediator connection per address
  and runs the sweep. A rooms/changed at an address is passed on only
  when DIDComm authcrypt proved the watch's host as sender, it names the
  watch's room, and the watch has not lapsed; the watch is forgotten
  before the pass-on is sent. rooms/keys/changed carries roomId, member,
  host and latestVersion only, signed by the VTA, through the push path
  task-consent/granted uses, without a doorbell (Producer item 5) and
  with a deadline of one attempt window, so an accepted push is never
  re-sent (Producer item 4). A watch is also forgotten when cancelled,
  at its lapse (never later than the host's expiresAt, 30 days at most),
  when its caller loses standing to act as the member, and when the
  member's credentials for the room are gone. rooms/changed addressed to
  the VTA's own DID matches no watch and is dropped.

  rooms/keys/act/0.12 is served beside 0.8-0.11; its table adds
  rooms/watch/0.1 (read). A watch whose address is the caller's DID, the
  VTA's or the member's is refused malformedRequest (Producer item 6;
  Recipient item 6).

title: vti-common-v0.61.0
body:
### Added

- **vti-common**: Host sessions send Trust Tasks and await their answers ([#2465](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2465))

* feat(vti-common): host sessions send Trust Tasks and await their answers (host_session::Requester)

  A host service reached through its own mediator session (the witness, the
  ballot box, and now the VTN) could only answer. `IdentitySession::with_requester`
  hands it a `Requester` that sends a signed Trust Task document to a DID over
  DIDComm, authcrypted as the identity in the binding envelope, and waits for the
  answer. The waiter is registered under the request document's `id` before the
  send. An inbound envelope completes it when its DIDComm `thid` or its document's
  `threadId` names that id and it comes from the DID the request went to; it is
  then not dispatched to the `Responder`. A send is "handed to the mediator",
  never "delivered": no answer within the window is `RequestError::Timeout`, and
  no live session is `NotConnected`. DIDComm only; TSP requests are not sent yet.

title: feat(collection)!: collection by default is a stored setting of each trust context, with an off-only operator suspension (VTI-NTF-094 – 098)
body:
Implements dtgwg-vti-spec #103 (chapter 05a: VTI-NTF-093 withdrawn; VTI-NTF-094 – 098) and trust-tasks-tf #1049 (`vta/collection/settings/{show,set}/0.1`, `CollectionSetting` in `_shared/0.1`).

## What changes

- **Per-context setting (VTI-NTF-094).** Collection by default is stored per trust context in the `collection` keyspace (`context-setting:<contextId>`). A context with no record is **enabled**. A context's setting applies to that context alone and is not inherited by ancestors or descendants. It is backed up, survives a restart, and is purged when the context is deleted (#2419 purge set).
- **`vta/collection/settings/set/0.1` (VTI-NTF-095).** Needs administrative authority over the context (VTI-ACL-022): a context admin of it or of an ancestor, or a super-admin. Every other party gets `permissionDenied`, including one with standing.
  - Disabling writes the record, then closes every connection the VTA holds for the context's identifiers before it answers. Each close runs under that identifier's lock, and the collector's `may_open` re-reads the suspension and the context's setting under the same lock.
  - Enabling clears the context's VTI-NTF-085 conflicts and kicks the collector. It does not wait for connections to open (Consumer item 4).
  - Setting the value already held answers `changed: false` and touches nothing, `changedBy` included. Retry class 2.
- **Audit and show (VTI-NTF-096).** Each change is audited (`collection.setting.enabled` / `collection.setting.disabled`) before it is applied, and the change is refused if the audit cannot be written. `settings/show/0.1` (standing in the context, retry class 1) answers the setting, `changedBy` and `changedAt`, and `suspendedByOperator`.
- **Disabled contexts (VTI-NTF-097).** Claims are still served while a context is disabled. `list` gives the `disabled` reason when the context is off or the operator has suspended collection.
- **Operator suspension (VTI-NTF-098).**
  - `[collection] collect_by_default` is replaced by the off-only `[collection] suspend`. The tenant overlay's `collection.suspend` can only engage it: a `false` there leaves the baked value.
  - The suspension is read at boot. Engaging or lifting it is audited at that boot (`collection.suspended` / `collection.suspension_lifted`).
  - It never changes a context's setting, and nothing enables a context whose setting disables it. Lifting it clears conflicts in enabled contexts, as enabling does.
- **Retired key.** `collect_by_default` is warned about and ignored, not refused. It still loads, `AppConfig::validate` names the replacement, and the overlay accepts it and ignores it the same way. Its old default (`false`) was written into deployed configs by our own docs, and refusing it would stop a working VTA over a value that no longer means anything. The retired `setting` row is dropped at boot.
- **Upgrade backfill (user-approved).** Collection is now on by default, so the first boot of this release records as provisioned every `did:webvh` that the VTA's own records show `provision/integration` minted before `provisioned:` existed. It does this before the collector opens anything. Two kinds of record count as evidence:
  - a `key.secret_export` audit row on the `provision-integration` channel;
  - a key record labelled the way provisioning labels them (`<holder did:key> signing key` / `key-agreement key`).

  The backfill runs once (`backfill:provisioned`) and is audited once (`collection.provisioned_backfilled`). An identifier that neither record identifies stays a candidate, and the docs tell operators to use `exclude`.
- **Client side.** Adds the `TASK_VTA_COLLECTION_SETTINGS_{SHOW,SET}_0_1` constants, `VtaClient::collection_settings_{show,set}` (+ `_json`), retry classes, and `pnm collection status|enable|disable --context <ctx>`. `status` shows the setting, who changed it and when, the suspension, and counts by collector and reason. vta-mcp needed no change: the verb census classifies `show` and `set` already.
- **Pins.** Adds `settings/show/0.1` and `settings/set/0.1`. The claim and list 0.1 bundles are re-pinned (`trust-tasks -C vti-specs-vta update`) because #1049 changed their descriptions in place.

## Why `!`

Published, non-`#[non_exhaustive]` or field-removing changes:
- `vta_config::CollectionConfig::collect_by_default` and `TenantCollectionOverlay::collect_by_default` are removed in favour of `suspend`.
- `CollectionControl::{new, enabled, set_enabled}` become `new(suspended)` / `suspended()`.
- `PlanInputs.enabled` is replaced by `disabled_contexts` + `suspended`.
- `record_setting` is replaced by `record_suspension`.

Behaviour change: collection by default is now **on** for every context.

## Tests

- **Engine** (`operations/collection_tests.rs`): on by default with no record; disable closes the context's connections (and only that context's) before answering; enable resumes, including after a conflict; a same-value set is a no-op and moves no `changedBy`; authority (non-admin with standing refused, ancestor admin allowed, other-context admin refused, super-admin allowed, unknown context `NotFound`); not inherited in either direction; the suspension overrides everything, never enables, changes no setting, and is audited once per change; persistence across a store reopen; purge drops the setting; backfill by audit row and by label, run once.
- **Handlers**: show and set through the handlers, with schema-checked answers.
- **Config**: retired key loads with no effect; the overlay is off-only.
- **Conformance**: witnesses for both tasks. `spec_pin_census`, the retry-safety census and the vta-mcp verb census pass.

## Follow-up (spec repo)

Close the Appendix F.3 *(observed, re-filed)* entry for VTI-NTF-094 – VTI-NTF-098 once this merges.

## Cross-service pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — `settings/set` holds a per-context lock and each identifier's lock across `CollectingSession::close` (the ATM's graceful_shutdown), the same as a claim grant already does; required by VTI-NTF-095 ("before it answers")
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — no remote effect; audit row is written before the record (process dies after the audit: the row overstates; dies after the record: the next collector pass applies it)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — set is RetrySafe (sets a state)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — a failed backfill is retried each pass, collecting nothing meanwhile
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — generated types from the pinned bundles; no JS consumer of these tasks yet
- [ ] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — DEVIATION, by specification: VTI-NTF-094 makes collection on unless disabled, so absent `[collection] suspend` means collecting. The rationale is in the spec (silent non-collection is the failure that reports nothing)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers (R5 above)
```

title: feat(collection)!: collection by default is a stored setting of each trust context, with an off-only operator suspension (VTI-NTF-094 – 098) (#2467)
body:
feat(collection)!: collection by default is a stored setting of each trust context, with an off-only operator suspension (VTI-NTF-094 – 098) (#2467)

dtgwg-vti-spec #103 withdraws VTI-NTF-093 (one operator setting, off unless
enabled, read from configuration at boot) in favour of VTI-NTF-094 – 098, and
trust-tasks-tf #1049 adds the operations.

- VTI-NTF-094: collection by default is a setting of each trust context,
  stored in the `collection` keyspace (`context-setting:<contextId>`), enabled
  for a context that has no record, applying to that context alone and not to
  its ancestors or descendants. It is backed up, survives a restart and is
  purged with its context.
- VTI-NTF-095: `vta/collection/settings/set/0.1` changes it, for a party with
  administrative authority over the context (VTI-ACL-022: an admin whose act
  scope covers it, so a context admin of it or an ancestor, or a
  super-admin). Disabling writes the record and closes every connection the VTA
  holds for the context's identifiers, each under its identifier's lock, before
  answering; the collector re-reads the setting under the same lock before it
  opens one. Enabling clears the context's VTI-NTF-085 conflicts and starts the
  collector. The value already held answers `changed: false` and changes
  nothing. Retry class 2.
- VTI-NTF-096: each change is audited (`collection.setting.enabled` /
  `collection.setting.disabled`) before it is applied, and refused if it
  cannot be; `vta/collection/settings/show/0.1` answers the setting, who last
  changed it and when, and whether the suspension is in force, to any party
  with standing in the context. Retry class 1.
- VTI-NTF-097: while disabled, nothing unclaimed is collected there and claims
  are still served; `list` gives `disabled` for a disabled context or a
  suspended VTA.
- VTI-NTF-098: `[collection] collect_by_default` is replaced by the off-only
  `[collection] suspend` (tenant overlay: `collection.suspend`, which can only
  engage it). It never changes a context's setting and nothing enables a
  context whose setting disables it. Engaging or lifting it is audited at the
  boot that applies it (`collection.suspended` /
  `collection.suspension_lifted`); lifting clears conflicts in enabled
  contexts.

The retired `collect_by_default` key is not refused: it loads, is ignored
whatever its value, and `AppConfig::validate` warns naming the replacement
(the tenant overlay accepts and ignores it the same way). Its old default,
`false`, was written into deployed configurations by the docs, and refusing it
would stop a working VTA for a value that means nothing now.

Upgrade backfill: since collection is now on by default, the first boot of this
release records as provisioned for another party (VTI-NTF-080 item 2) every
`did:webvh` the VTA's own records show `provision/integration` minted before it
wrote `provisioned:` — a `key.secret_export` audit row on the
`provision-integration` channel, or a key record labelled the way provisioning
labels them — before the collector opens anything. It runs once
(`backfill:provisioned`) and is audited once
(`collection.provisioned_backfilled`). What neither shows stays a candidate;
the docs tell operators to use `[collection] exclude`.

Client side: `TASK_VTA_COLLECTION_SETTINGS_{SHOW,SET}_0_1`,
`VtaClient::collection_settings_{show,set}` (+ `_json`), retry classes, and
`pnm collection status|enable|disable --context <ctx>`.

The claim and list 0.1 bundles are re-pinned: their descriptions changed in
place in #1049.

BREAKING CHANGE: `vta_config::CollectionConfig::collect_by_default` and
`TenantCollectionOverlay::collect_by_default` are replaced by `suspend`;
`CollectionControl::{new, enabled, set_enabled}` become
`CollectionControl::{new(suspended), suspended}`; `PlanInputs.enabled` becomes
`disabled_contexts` + `suspended`; `record_setting` becomes
`record_suspension`. Collection by default is now on for every context, where it
was off unless the operator enabled it.

feat(vtn/registry): check a party against the network's trust registry through the network, and the registry status for administrators (#1050)

vtn/registry/check/0.1 lets anyone ask a network to ask its trust registry whether a party is published as its member, returning the registry's own signed answer verbatim, so a verifier with no DIDComm or TSP session (a browser, or a registry that serves no HTTPS) can still check the registry rather than take the network's word for it. Unreachable is indeterminate, never not a member.

vtn/registry/status/0.1 lets an administrator read the registry, the writer and whether it is connected, the last reconcile, and every record compared with what the entries project (ok, missing, stale, wrong).

title: feat(vti-common): host sessions send Trust Tasks and await their answers
body:
A host service reached through its own mediator session (`vti_common::host_session`: the witness, the ballot box) could only answer. The VTN needs to *ask*: its trust registry takes `registry/record/put` and `delete` only over DIDComm or TSP.

- `Requester`, handed to a session with `IdentitySession::with_requester`. While the session is live, `request(peer, document, timeout)`:
  - sends a signed Trust Task document to `peer` over DIDComm, in the binding envelope, authcrypted as the identity;
  - waits for the answer.
- **Correlation:**
  - a waiter is registered under the request document's `id` **before** the send, so a fast answer is never lost;
  - an inbound envelope completes it when its DIDComm `thid` or its document's `threadId` names that id **and** it comes from the DID the request went to;
  - an answer is not dispatched to the `Responder`; anything else is handled as before.
- **Errors:** `NotConnected`, `NoId`, `Send`, and `Timeout` (retryable). A send that returns is "handed to the mediator", never "delivered" (R1.1).
- DIDComm only; TSP requests are not sent yet.
- No behaviour change for a session without a requester. The witness and ballot box build unchanged.

Tests (unit): correlation by `thid` and by `threadId`; another sender, an unknown thread or a non-envelope is not an answer; no session gives `NotConnected`; no `id` gives `NoId`.

title: feat(vta/collection): settings/show and settings/set — collection by default per trust context, stored and changed at run time
body:
Companion to trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#103, which withdraws VTI-NTF-093 (an operator setting, off unless enabled) and replaces it with VTI-NTF-094 – VTI-NTF-098: collection by default becomes a stored setting of each trust context, enabled unless a context administrator disables it, and changed at run time.

## New tasks

- **`vta/collection/settings/show/0.1`**: a party with standing in the context reads the `CollectionSetting`. That is `collectByDefault`, `suspendedByOperator`, and `changedBy` / `changedAt`, which appear together or not at all. Retry class: first.
- **`vta/collection/settings/set/0.1`**: a party with administrative authority over the context (VTI-ACL-022) sets `collectByDefault`. The VTA stores the value, audits the change and applies it before it answers; disabling closes the VTA's connections first. The response carries `setting` and `changed`. Retry class: second (it sets a state). `issuedAtRequirement: REQUIRED`, `errorCodes: []`.

## Changes to released 0.1 (all additive or description-only; `check-published-schemas` passes)

- `vta/collection/_shared/0.1` gains a new `$defs` entry, `CollectionSetting`, which uses `dependentSchemas` and no `if`/`then`/`else`. The `disabled` reason in `NotCollectedReason` is re-described: it now means the context's own setting is off, or the operator has suspended collection. **No enum value is added or changed.**
- `claim`, `list` and `release` 0.1: their prose, and the `claim:notCollectable` meaning, now cite the per-context setting instead of VTI-NTF-093. `list` adds `settings/show` to `related`.

## Why the setting isn't folded into `list`'s response

The setting belongs to the context, not to any identifier in it. Also, `list/0.1`'s response is released with `additionalProperties: false`, so a new member there would be refused by every existing client's schema.

## Checks run locally

`npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings`, `npm run check-published-schemas`, `npm run check-bundles` all pass. All four bindings are regenerated. `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features vta,validate --test conformance collection`: 17 passed, including the new request/response examples and the invalid-example fixtures for both requests and responses.
