Collection by default was one operator setting, off unless enabled
(VTI-NTF-093). The VTI specification withdraws that in favour of a setting of
each trust context, enabled unless disabled there (VTI-NTF-094 – VTI-NTF-098):

- vta/collection/settings/show/0.1: a party with standing in a context reads

  before the answer — disabling closes the VTA's connections first

- _shared/0.1 gains a CollectionSetting definition (new $defs entry), and the

  operator's suspension (VTI-NTF-097, VTI-NTF-098). No enum value changes.
- claim/list/release 0.1 prose and an error-code meaning now cite the
  per-context setting instead of VTI-NTF-093 (description edits only).

The setting is not folded into list's response: it belongs to the context,

title: Make collection by default a stored setting of each trust context, enabled unless disabled, changed at run time by a context administrator (VTI-NTF-094 – VTI-NTF-098)
body:
VTI-NTF-093 made collection by default one setting of the VTA's operator, disabled unless enabled, and in practice read from configuration at boot. That is hard to manage: the operator does not know which clients a principal runs, a change needs a restart, and a run-time patch is lost when a TEE restarts. Clients now claim before they collect (OpenVTC 0.7 and later), so the default can be on, with the conflict back-off (VTI-NTF-085) as the safety net.

## What changes

- **VTI-NTF-093 withdrawn**, with a note. Its identifier is not reused.
- **VTI-NTF-094**: collection by default is a setting of each trust context. It is enabled unless disabled there, applies to that context only (not to its ancestors or descendants), is stored so it survives a restart (a TEE's included), and takes effect without a restart.
- **VTI-NTF-095**: a party with administrative authority over the context (VTI-ACL-022: a context administrator of it or of an ancestor, or a super-administrator) changes it through the catalogue's operation, and every other party is refused. The change takes effect when it is answered. Disabling stops collection and closes the VTA's connections before the answer. Enabling starts collecting, including for identifiers the VTA stopped for after a conflict. Setting the value already held changes nothing.
- **VTI-NTF-096**: every change is audited. Any party with standing in the context can read the setting, who last changed it and when, and whether an operator suspension is in force.
- **VTI-NTF-097**: while the setting is disabled, the VTA collects for no unclaimed identifier, and claims are still granted and listed (the old VTI-NTF-093 behaviour, now per context). It is a SHOULD to disable it while a client collects without claiming.
- **VTI-NTF-098**: an operator MAY suspend collection by default for every context at once. The suspension only turns collection off: it never changes a context's setting and cannot turn collection on. Suspending and lifting it are audited.
- VTI-NTF-080 now refers to the per-context setting. Also updated: the plain-terms paragraph, the chapter's list of operations, the conformance note and the STRUCTURE.md row. The F.3 entry is re-filed against VTI-NTF-094 – VTI-NTF-098, because the implementation still ships the operator switch, off by default.

## Why a context administrator, not standing alone or super-admin only

A claim decides for one identifier and one client, so standing in the context is enough for it. This setting decides for every identifier and every client in the context at once. Turning it off leaves the personas of every browser-only client there with nobody collecting for them. That is administering the context (VTI-ACL-022). Making it super-admin only would hand the decision back to the operator, who does not know which clients a principal runs.

## Why only an off switch for the operator

An operator still needs an incident stop, for example when a mediator fails, that does not depend on every principal acting. Because the operator can only turn collection off, there is exactly one place that turns it on, the context's setting. An operator who could also turn it on could override a principal's decision to turn it off.

## Companion

Trust Tasks: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf — `vta/collection/settings/show/0.1` and `vta/collection/settings/set/0.1` (PR linked in a comment below).

title: vtc-service-v0.25.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc-service**: Preview a network before joining it — vtc/networks/preview/0.1, the console's join form and cnm networks preview ([#2464](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2464))
- **elections**: Check a vote after close against the head the community kept (VTI-VOT-053) ([#2460](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2460))

The VTA kept each receipt and could check it against a head and an
  inclusion proof, but nothing ever handed it either after close. Now:

  - VTA: vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list/0.1 returns the receipts kept for an
    election, whole, and the ballot box recorded at registration.
    vta/pcs/voter/read/0.7 also signs vtc/elections/tombstones/show/0.1, so a
    member can read the heads a community keeps once the election's board is
    deleted (VTI-BRD-009). voter/receipt answers notIncluded for a head too
    small to hold the cast before it looks at a path (consumer item 7.2), as
    the ballot box gives no inclusion proof for one.
  - vta-sdk: pcs_voter_receipts_list(_json); pcs_voter_read_json sends 0.7 only
    for a tombstone read, so list and show keep working against an older VTA.
  - pnm elections verify <id>: reads the head the community kept at close
    (show, or the tombstone on electionUnknown), lists the receipts, fetches
    each cast's voting/board/inclusion from the ballot box over its own
    connection, unsigned, and has the VTA check it. A cast the head omits is
    printed in red and the command fails.
  - Member portal: "Check my vote in my wallet" on a closed or tallied
    election, for a wallet that offers checkVote. The wallet answers in its
    own window; the page is told nothing.
  - Docs: pcs-engine.md step 7, elections.md.

  Pins vta/pcs/voter/read 0.7 and vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list 0.1 from the
  Trust Task PR's registry build (read 0.2/0.3/0.6 take its new deprecation
  notes); lock reset to trusttasks.org.

- **boards**: Appoint a board's facilitators (VTI-BRD-090 – 093) ([#2459](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2459))

Serves vtc/boards/facilitators/{add,remove,list}/0.1. Any facilitator of a board
  appoints an active member to facilitate it: a resource grant of vtc.boards.manage
  at board:<boardId> on the member's own entry, beside their role, delegated by and
  bounded to the signer's own holding, so a member with no administrative role can
  run one board and nothing else. A facilitator steps down; only a holder of
  vtc.boards.manage unqualified ends someone else's appointment. When the appointer
  departs or stops facilitating the board, the appointment goes to an
  acl.grants.review item (boardGrants) and is withdrawn on decline or at the
  deadline; deleting the board withdraws every appointment to it. Every change is
  audited as BoardChanged by entry, never DID.

  The grant/review/withdraw machinery of group managers moves to
  acl::appointment and now serves both kinds; ResourceGrant::confers answers
  vtc.boards.manage for the exact board only.

    own window; the page is told nothing.
  - Docs: pcs-engine.md step 7, elections.md.

  Pins vta/pcs/voter/read 0.7 and vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list 0.1 from the
  Trust Task PR's registry build (read 0.2/0.3/0.6 take its new deprecation
  notes); lock reset to trusttasks.org.

- **rooms**: The VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head ([#2461](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2461))

* feat(rooms)!: the VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head

  rooms/keys/watch/0.1, rooms/keys/changed/0.1 and rooms/keys/act/0.12
  (trust-tasks-tf #1040), pinned in vti-specs-rooms (act 0.8-0.11 are now
  marked superseded upstream, so their uses carry allow(deprecated)).

  The VTA serves rooms/keys/watch/0.1: up to 64 rooms at one host, one
  outcome per room. A delegate is refused permissionDenied, a member the
  VTA holds no authentication key for that the caller may act as is
  refused memberNotPrincipal (details.member), a room named twice is
  malformedRequest. Each room is its own rooms/watch/0.1 at the host,
  completed as act/0.12 completes one (presentation narrowed to read,
  granted to and signed by the member), with an address of the VTA's
  own: a did:peer:2 minted for that one watch from fresh keys, whose
  only service is DIDCommMessaging at the VTA's mediator. A re-arm of an
  unfired watch keeps its address; every other arming takes a new one.
  Per room: notAMember, actionNotHeld, limitReached (the VTA's own bound:
  64 per member, 64 per caller, 256 in all; a VTA with no mediator holds
  none), hostUnreachable, or hostRefused with the host's code unaltered.

  The record (operations::room_key_watch, keyspace room_key_watches,
  encrypted at rest, excluded from backup) is Recipient item 6's list and
  nothing else: caller, member, room, host, address and its keys, lapse.
  messaging::watch_addresses holds one mediator connection per address
  and runs the sweep. A rooms/changed at an address is passed on only
  when DIDComm authcrypt proved the watch's host as sender, it names the
  watch's room, and the watch has not lapsed; the watch is forgotten
  before the pass-on is sent. rooms/keys/changed carries roomId, member,
  host and latestVersion only, signed by the VTA, through the push path
  task-consent/granted uses, without a doorbell (Producer item 5) and
  with a deadline of one attempt window, so an accepted push is never
  re-sent (Producer item 4). A watch is also forgotten when cancelled,
  at its lapse (never later than the host's expiresAt, 30 days at most),
  when its caller loses standing to act as the member, and when the
  member's credentials for the room are gone. rooms/changed addressed to
  the VTA's own DID matches no watch and is dropped.

  rooms/keys/act/0.12 is served beside 0.8-0.11; its table adds
  rooms/watch/0.1 (read). A watch whose address is the caller's DID, the
  VTA's or the member's is refused malformedRequest (Producer item 6;
  Recipient item 6).



### Fixed

- **room-host**: Sign every answer as the host, and run a room watch end to end through a real mediator ([#2463](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2463))

* fix(room-host): sign every answer as the host, and run a room watch end to end through a real mediator

  A member's VTA believes only an answer signed by the host it addressed
  (`ReplyTrust::SignedByRecipient`; SPEC §7.3 item 7, VTI-KEY-106), but
  `room-host` answered unsigned over HTTP, DIDComm and TSP alike. So every
  success it returned to a VTA was refused as "bytes, not evidence": a VTA
  could not arm `rooms/watch` at a standalone host at all (`hostUnreachable`),
  nor run any other room task whose answer it acts on. `room_key_watch_tests`
  and `room_profile_tests` never saw it because their fixtures sign the host's
  answers themselves.

  `HostState` now takes an answer signer, and `dispatch` signs every answer it
  gives — refusals included, and the DIDComm binding's `identityMismatch` — once
  the host has one. `didcomm::serve` sets it from the host's identity (its
  Ed25519 key under its own DID). An HTTP-only host with no identity answers
  unsigned, as before.

  Found by `tests/e2e/tests/room_key_watch.rs`, new here: `rooms/keys/watch/0.1`
  and `rooms/keys/changed/0.1` through a real `TestMediator` — a VTA on its
  production inbound loop and address supervisor, a room host serving over the
  mediator and HTTPS, and a wallet with its own TSP session. It proves that the
  mediator takes a session for a VTA-minted `did:peer:2` watch address nobody
  registered, routes the host's `rooms/changed` to it (also when sent before
  the address's connection opened: held, then delivered when it connects), and
  carries exactly one `rooms/keys/changed` on to the wallet, with nothing for a
  second write that was not re-armed.

  What it also shows, recorded in data-rooms.md rather than changed: a watch
  address gets only the mediator's `global_acl_default`, and the shipped
  `DENY_ALL,LOCAL,SEND_MESSAGES,RECEIVE_MESSAGES` lets it connect but not
  receive (an empty allowlist, no RECEIVE_FORWARDED, no self-change bit), so the
  host's signal is refused there; and the VTA reaches a host only over HTTPS,
  because the `rooms/watch` it sends is the member's and DIDComm/TSP would
  authenticate the VTA instead.

  `MockVta` gains `start_with_transports_using` (configure the embedded
  mediator), `configure_messaging`, `start_watch_addresses` and
  `mediator_inbox_count`; `test_support::seed_room_membership` seeds a member's
  room credentials.

title: feat(elections): check my vote after close, in the wallet's own window (VTI-VOT-053)
body:
Wallet side of VTI-VOT-053: `elections.checkVote` from the portal opens a wallet window that lists the VTA's receipts, reads the closing head from `vtc/elections/show` (or the tombstone via `vta/pcs/voter/read/0.7`), fetches each inclusion proof from the ballot box on the wallet's own connection, and has the VTA check it. A cast the head omits is shown first, as a warning. The page always gets `{}`, so it never learns whether the member voted; a membership is presented only if the member already chose to for that election.

Core: `pcsVoterReceiptsList`, `fetchInclusion`, `closingCheckpoint`; `pcsVoterReceipt` takes optional evidence.

**Merge after** OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2460 is merged and released: every voter read now goes as `vta/pcs/voter/read/0.7` (the lock pins one version per task), which only that VTA serves. `voting/board/inclusion/0.1` is pinned.

title: feat(elections): check my vote after close, in the wallet's own window (VTI-VOT-053) (#420)
body:
feat(elections): check my vote after close, in the wallet's own window (VTI-VOT-053) (#420)

* feat(elections): check my vote after close, in the wallet's own window (VTI-VOT-053)

A page's window.vtaWallet.elections.checkVote({ hostDid, electionId }) asks
the wallet to check the member's vote once voting has closed. The member's
VTA lists the receipts it keeps (vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list/0.1); the
wallet reads the head the community kept at close from vtc/elections/show,
or, once the election's board is deleted, from its tombstone through
vta/pcs/voter/read/0.7 (VTI-BRD-009); it asks the ballot box for each cast's
voting/board/inclusion proof from its own connection, unsigned, with the
receipt's token; and the VTA checks each (vta/pcs/voter/receipt). The
answer is shown only in the wallet's window. A cast the head omits is said
first, as a warning. The page is answered {} whatever happened, so it never
learns whether the member voted.

A membership already presented for the election is presented again to read
it; none is newly presented for a check. A ballot box the wallet may not
reach is asked nothing, and the window says to allow it.

core: pcsVoterReceiptsList, fetchInclusion, closingCheckpoint, and evidence
on pcsVoterReceipt; pcsVoterRead signs tombstone reads with read/0.7 while
list and show stay on 0.6 for older VTAs. Pins read 0.7 and receipts/list
0.1 from the Trust Task PR's registry build; task surface resynced (243).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(elections): every voter read on read/0.7; pin voting/board/inclusion/0.1

The lock pins one version of a task and the built-bundle check holds the
extension to it, so list and show move from read/0.6 to 0.7 with the
tombstone read; the wallet now needs a VTA that serves read 0.7. The
inclusion read the wallet sends to the ballot box is pinned.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: vta-keyspaces-v0.34.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: The VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head ([#2461](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2461))

* feat(rooms)!: the VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head

  rooms/keys/watch/0.1, rooms/keys/changed/0.1 and rooms/keys/act/0.12
  (trust-tasks-tf #1040), pinned in vti-specs-rooms (act 0.8-0.11 are now
  marked superseded upstream, so their uses carry allow(deprecated)).

  The VTA serves rooms/keys/watch/0.1: up to 64 rooms at one host, one
  outcome per room. A delegate is refused permissionDenied, a member the
  VTA holds no authentication key for that the caller may act as is
  refused memberNotPrincipal (details.member), a room named twice is
  malformedRequest. Each room is its own rooms/watch/0.1 at the host,
  completed as act/0.12 completes one (presentation narrowed to read,
  granted to and signed by the member), with an address of the VTA's
  own: a did:peer:2 minted for that one watch from fresh keys, whose
  only service is DIDCommMessaging at the VTA's mediator. A re-arm of an
  unfired watch keeps its address; every other arming takes a new one.
  Per room: notAMember, actionNotHeld, limitReached (the VTA's own bound:
  64 per member, 64 per caller, 256 in all; a VTA with no mediator holds
  none), hostUnreachable, or hostRefused with the host's code unaltered.

  The record (operations::room_key_watch, keyspace room_key_watches,
  encrypted at rest, excluded from backup) is Recipient item 6's list and
  nothing else: caller, member, room, host, address and its keys, lapse.
  messaging::watch_addresses holds one mediator connection per address
  and runs the sweep. A rooms/changed at an address is passed on only
  when DIDComm authcrypt proved the watch's host as sender, it names the
  watch's room, and the watch has not lapsed; the watch is forgotten
  before the pass-on is sent. rooms/keys/changed carries roomId, member,
  host and latestVersion only, signed by the VTA, through the push path
  task-consent/granted uses, without a doorbell (Producer item 5) and
  with a deadline of one attempt window, so an accepted push is never
  re-sent (Producer item 4). A watch is also forgotten when cancelled,
  at its lapse (never later than the host's expiresAt, 30 days at most),
  when its caller loses standing to act as the member, and when the
  member's credentials for the room are gone. rooms/changed addressed to
  the VTA's own DID matches no watch and is dropped.

  rooms/keys/act/0.12 is served beside 0.8-0.11; its table adds
  rooms/watch/0.1 (read). A watch whose address is the caller's DID, the
  VTA's or the member's is refused malformedRequest (Producer item 6;
  Recipient item 6).

title: fix: the trust graph checks a member's acknowledgement
body:
The trust graph showed a member's acknowledgement (its `MembershipCredential` back to the network) as `unchecked`. `vti_vtn::graph::export` only knows this network's own status lists. The acknowledgement and any repudiation are issued by the listed party, so it left them `unchecked`.

- `Network::graph` now checks those party-issued credentials with the network's `StatusChecker`, the one that already checks member VMCs and room-pass chains:
  - against the party's own Bitstring Status Lists, verified as signed by the party;
  - cached for `status_cache_seconds`.
- A credential with no `credentialStatus` is `valid`, as `StatusChecker::check` defines: its validity window is its control. The live First VTC acknowledgement is one of these.
- A list that can't be fetched, or isn't signed by the party, stays `unchecked` (logged), never `valid`.

Test: the lifecycle test in `network_api.rs` now asserts the acknowledgement edge is `valid`.

title: v0.7.0
body:
### Added

- **Collection claims before a persona connects** (VTI-NTF-080 – 084, `vta/collection/claim/0.1`,
  `vta/collection/release/0.1`). A persona's mediator permits one connection, and your VTA can
  collect its messages too, so this app now connects a persona whose keys your VTA holds only
  once the VTA grants it the claim, asked for twenty-four hours. It renews the claim at half
  time and closes the connection two minutes before the claim ends unless the renewal landed.
  When a persona stops for good, its connection closes first and the claim is released after.
  If another of your apps holds the claim, your VTA refuses it, or the VTA cannot be asked, the
  persona stays disconnected, the activity log says why, and the claim is asked again later.
  A claim released from elsewhere disconnects the persona before it ends. A persona your VTA
  never collects for, or a VTA too old to take claims, connects without one. A BIP32 account is
  unchanged. `openvtc repos …` opens a VTA session to make the claim.
- **Elections put to the members of a party you belong to, and the notifications that tell
  you of them.** A notification (`notifications/notify`, `notifications/relay`, VTI-NTF-054)
  addressed to one of your personas is handed to your VTA exactly as it arrived
  (`vta/notifications/deposit/0.1`) — every one, with no filter of this app's own — and its
  sender is answered with the receipt the task defines, the same whatever your VTA does with
  it. When your VTA cannot be reached the notification is neither handed over nor answered, so
  its sender delivers it again. Nothing is opened, and nobody else told, because one arrived.
  A community's Elections panel now also lists, under **Told of**, the elections your VTA holds
  a notification of that concern that community — held by it, or put to its members by another
  community — shown only as notified (who holds it, its identifier, whom it is put to, its
  period) until you open it (VTI-NTF-063). Opening one reads it from the community holding it,
  first presenting nothing; if that community shows it only to those who present a membership
  of the party it is put to, the panel says what presenting shows before your VTA presents
  anything, and only **y** presents (VTI-VOT-015, VTI-VOT-016).
- **Credential rolls.** An election whose roll is the holders of a membership credential for
  one DID (`roll.rule: credential`) shows whose credential admits a voter, and warns that
  taking a ticket shows the community your membership of that party (VTI-VOT-090). **t** finds
  the membership credential that party itself issued you in your VTA's vault, and your VTA signs
  the claim with its presentation (`vta/pcs/voter/register/0.5`'s `membershipCredential`,
  VTI-VOT-025); this app carries it unchanged. The community's new refusals — no presentation,
  membership not proven or revoked, the roll's party no longer trusted, and `indeterminate`
  when it could not complete a check (nothing recorded: try again later, VTI-VOT-018) — are
  said in words. The Elections panel now speaks `vtc/elections/list/0.5`, `show/0.6` and
  `tickets/issue/0.3`, and `vta/pcs/voter/register/0.5`, `read/0.6`, `vote/0.4` and
  `vote-encrypted/0.5`: it needs a community on VTI's vtc-service 0.19 and a VTA on vta-service
  0.71.
- **Get back to the hidden-vetting key a community bound you to.** A vetter whose VTA derived
  a new PCS key (its vetter engine record was replaced) was refused enrolment for good with
  `identifierRebound`, told to "vet from the install that enrolled first" — wrong now the key
  lives in the VTA, and revoking and re-granting the vetter role did not help, because the
  community binds a member to one key. Now that refusal starts a check: enrolment is held, the
  community is asked which key it bound (`vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1`), and the
  VTA is asked to restore it (`vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1`); restored (or already held),
  enrolment is asked again once. If the VTA cannot find the key, the Hidden vetting view says
  to ask an admin of the community to reset your hidden-vetting key, then follows the reset —
  "Reset: waiting for vetter/2026-10 to retire" — and enrols with your current key once it
  opens. A key held in another of your contexts, an engine bound to another member DID, and an
  engine that already holds the community's credentials are each said in their own words.
  **r** on the Hidden vetting view checks again from the top. Needs a community serving
  `pcs-binding/show/0.1` and a VTA serving `vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1`.
- **Vote in a community's elections.** Press `e` on an active community to see its
  elections — voting open first, then those issuing tickets, upcoming, and closed — and
  whether you hold a ticket. Opening one shows what you are told before taking part: the
  schedule, who runs the ballot box (with a warning when it is the community's own
  operator), who can read the board, whether a later vote replaces an earlier one, and that
  a vote can be proven to someone who demands it. **t** takes a ticket: your VTA builds the
  blinded request (`vta/pcs/voter/register/0.3`), OpenVTC signs it as your persona and sends
  it to the community (`vtc/elections/tickets/issue/0.1`), and the VTA takes the community's
  blind signature (`vta/pcs/voter/accept/0.1`). **v** votes: with no ticket held it takes
  one and stops — come back later, so the ticket and the vote cannot be paired by time — and
  with one held it opens the ballot (single and multiple choice, ranking, scores, free text,
  leaving optional questions blank), checks it against the election's rules, and on **y**
  has your VTA seal it under a key made for that vote alone (`vta/pcs/vote/0.3`, or
  `vta/pcs/vote-encrypted/0.4` for a sealed or encrypted election). OpenVTC then sends the
  cast to the ballot box itself, over its advertised HTTPS door after a random pause of up to
  20 s, checks that the receipt is signed by the ballot box and answers this cast, and has
  the VTA keep it (`vta/pcs/voter/receipt/0.1`). The community never sees a ballot, a cast
  or a receipt; the ballot box never sees who you are. A cast whose answer was lost is resent
  unchanged (**r**), never rebuilt. An election may release written answers after fewer
  than 10 ballots (as few as 1, VTI-VOT-065); then the election, the ballot and the
  confirmation all say "Written answers are released once N ballots are counted. Below 10,
  a written answer may identify who wrote it." (VTI-VOT-090). Needs a VTA serving
  `vta/pcs/voter/register/0.3`, `vote/0.3` and `vote-encrypted/0.4` (vta-service 0.70)
  and a community serving `vtc/elections/list/0.3` and `show/0.3`.
- **Repositories in nested GitLab groups.** A repository may now be named
  `<forge>/<owner>/<group>/…/<repo>` (up to GitLab's 20 levels of subgroups), so
  cloning, the workspace layout, remote matching and signing set-up work for
  `gitlab.com/group/sub/repo`. github.com, bitbucket.org and codeberg.org, which
  have no nested groups, still take exactly `<owner>/<repo>`. Listing them in the
  Repos panel needs a community that answers `git-ns/view/0.6`.
- **Onboarding without the TUI.** Subcommands named after the TUI's panels take an
  account from nothing to signed commits in a script: `setup --vta-did` creates the
  account against a VTA (`--context`, `--wait`, `--unlock-code-file`);
  `community join <vtc>` joins a community and waits for the verdict (`--persona` or
  `--new-persona`, `--wait`, `--invitation`); `repo list`, `repo clone <resource>
  [--dir]` and `repo sign [path] [--persona]` list and clone the repositories a
  persona may see (`--community`) and make a checkout sign its commits as the
  persona. Each holds the profile lock as the TUI does.
- **A community's data rooms, the same everywhere you reach them.** Press `o` on an
  active community to see every data room it has offered this persona, and where
  each stands: offered, joined, accepted but not finished, needing re-admission, or
  removed. OpenVTC keeps no record of its own: it reads the community's
  (`vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1`) beside your VTA's (`rooms/keys/list`), as the
  member portal and `pnm rooms memberships` do, so a room accepted in the portal shows
  as joined here and the other way round. **⏎** accepts an offer — the VTA stores its
  credentials, gives the KeyPackage (`rooms/keys/key-package/0.2`), and joins from the
  Welcome — and finishes an acceptance begun on another surface rather than starting a
  second one; a Welcome another surface already handed over reads as joined. Needs a
  VTA (it holds the rooms' keys) serving `rooms/keys/key-package/0.2` for an
  interrupted acceptance to be finishable elsewhere, and a community serving
  `vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1`. See [`docs/community-rooms.md`](docs/community-rooms.md).
- **Have a relationship witnessed.** Press `w` on a relationship, name a witness,
  and your VTA does the witnessing (`vta/witness/{open,present,accept}/0.2`): it
  signs every document as the relationship DID and presents the VRC you issued
  (and, only if you choose, your membership credential), while OpenVTC carries the documents to the witness on
  that DID's own connection (DIDComm, or TSP where both sides advertise it) and
  hands the answers back. The witness's answers are verified as its own before they
  are used; a refusal is explained, never handed back. The resulting witness
  credential is stored at your VTA and listed on the relationship. By default only
  the VRC is presented and the witness learns nothing of who you are. Presenting
  your community membership is an explicit choice for that one witnessing (**Tab**
  on the prompt, off every time it opens, never remembered); the prompt says the
  witness will learn which community member is behind the relationship, and the VTA
  then links the two in the submission's `memberPresentation`. Needs a VTA that
  serves the witness tasks at 0.2 (`vta-service` 0.62 or later); not available to a
  BIP32 account.
- **A witnessing whose record was lost is rebuilt from the VTA.** At start, after
  the account-state sync, OpenVTC reads the VTA's stored witness credentials
  (`vta/witness/list/0.1`) and rebuilds any witnessing it holds a VWC for that
  this device never kept — a crash between the VTA storing it and the record being
  saved — for relationships the account still holds. A rebuilt witnessing is only
  listed and offered; it is never presented on its own.
- **Issued relationship credentials are stored in the VTA's credential vault** on
  connect, where witnessing presents them from. Only credentials the vault does not
  hold are stored.
- **A personhood assertion can present witness credentials you choose.** None is
  included by default: when the persona has witnessed relationships, `P` lists them
  (other party, witness, date, digest) and says what the community learns from each;
  you include them one by one, or all of them only through a separate confirmation
  for that assertion. Each included VWC carries its outcome evidence in the
  assertion's `outcomeEvidence` (`vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.2`, at most 16),
  which a community needs beside a VWC to count it.
- **What a community's member directory would show about you, before you join.**
  Requirements are asked as `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.4`, falling back to 0.3
  (then 0.2) when a community refuses the version. When the manifest carries a
  `directoryDisclosure`, the join review says it in plain sentences before anything
  is sent: what a new card shows, the most you could show, what admins or
  credentials write, how you can be found, and for how long. Every audience is the
  widest it can reach (`public` reads as "anyone, outside the community too");
  labels are the community's own text, shown as text. The statement's
  `statementDigest` is kept with the join record. A malformed statement stops the
  join; a manifest without one says nothing about a directory.

- **Choose how setup reaches your VTA.** When the VTA advertises more than one
  transport, the PNM step of `openvtc setup` has a Transport row: **Tab** cycles
  between Automatic (TSP, then DIDComm, then REST) and each advertised transport on
  its own. Automatic moves on only when a transport fails to connect; once the VTA
  has acted on the request, a lost reply is final, so picking the transport up front
  is the way round a mediator that drops replies (#501).

### Security

- **No PCS key is held on the device any more.** Hidden vetting runs on the
  person's VTA (`vta/pcs/*`, VTA 0.60 or later): it holds each applicant and
  vetter key, and builds every enrolment request, token draw, attestation and
  admission proof. OpenVTC carries what the VTA builds to the community and the
  other member, and keeps only what the VTA says it holds — enrolled labels,
  token counts, the metadata of each attestation. Keys an earlier version kept
  in the protected config are dropped the first time this version loads it.

### Changed

- **A received notification's sender is answered with your VTA's receipt** (VTI-NTF-054,
  VTI-NTF-055). The receipt is the one the VTA answers the hand-over with, the same whether it
  held the notification or declined it. This app no longer verifies the notification itself to
  decide whether to answer, so the answer cannot differ from the one your VTA gives when it
  collects the persona's messages itself. A notification the VTA refuses (not addressed to one
  of your personas, or one it could not have accepted) is not answered, and its sender delivers
  it again.
- vta-sdk 0.80, did-git-sign 0.33, affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45 and
  trust-tasks 0.37.
- **Onto the VTI 0.78 stack:** `vta-sdk` 0.78, `did-git-sign` 0.30 (the same
  signer, rebuilt on that line) and `trust-tasks-rs` 0.36.2; `affinidi-tdk` 0.36 and
  `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.44 are unchanged. The test `MockVta` moves to
  `vta-service` 0.70, with `vti-voting` 0.7 and `vti-vetting-pcs` 0.11 beside it.
- **Personhood assertions are sent as `vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.2`**, the
  only version a community on `vtc-service` with VTI #2147 serves, with or without
  witness credentials. `openvtc_core::personhood::assert_personhood` takes the
  outcome evidence as its own argument instead of an `ext`, and
  `openvtc_core::witness::personhood_ext` / `WITNESS_EXT` are replaced by
  `personhood_evidence`. On `vta-sdk` 0.70, `vta-service` 0.62, `trust-tasks-rs`
  0.31.12 and `did-git-sign` 0.22.
- **Hidden vetting goes through your VTA.** Enrolling, drawing tokens, taking in
  a vetter's attestation, building the join's proof and attesting are VTA calls,
  run off the screen's loop; answers from a community or a vetter that the VTA
  must take in are queued (and survive a restart) until it has them. A vetting
  request under a hidden criterion waits for the VTA to create the application.
  **One-time cost of the upgrade:** a vetter enrolled by an earlier version
  enrols again under a key the VTA holds — a community that refuses
  (`identifierRebound`) has to let it re-enrol — and an application under way
  starts its hidden vetting again, since its attestations were bound to the old
  key. Each is said once on the Vetting page.
- The attestation a vetter sends is now the `vetting/attestation/0.1` shape the
  specification states (`suite`, `token { label, serial, shown }`); the earlier
  flat shape is no longer sent.
- **Trust Task types are generated from pinned specs, at their latest versions.**
  `openvtc-core` generates `openvtc_core::specs` at build time (`trust-tasks-build`
  0.1, from `openvtc-core/trust-tasks.{toml,lock}` and the vendored bundles) instead
  of using `trust-tasks-rs`'s deprecated prebuilt modules; `trust-tasks-rs` 0.35 is
  the runtime only. Every task is sent at its latest version: joins as
  `manifest/0.4` and `submit/0.3`, `vta/witness/list/0.2`, `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.4`,
  git-ns `view/0.6`, `drift/resolve/0.4`, `repo/create/0.4`, `right/{grant,revoke}/0.4`,
  `persona/profile/compose/1.1`, `persona/attribute/promote/1.1`,
  `persona/world/put/1.1`, `vta/webvh/agent-name/list/1.1` and
  `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.2`; through `vta-sdk`, `keys/list/0.2`,
  `vta/app-state/list/1.1`, `vault/credentials/get/0.2` and the ACL tasks at
  `acl/*/0.2` and `acl/list/0.3`. Needs a VTA and community on a VTI release that
  serves them: `vta-service` 0.67 and `vtc-service` 0.15 or later. On `vta-sdk`
  0.75, `vti-vetting-pcs` 0.8, `did-git-sign` 0.26, `affinidi-tdk` 0.36,
  `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.44 and `trust-tasks-rs` 0.36, which deprecates the
  prebuilt types `vta-sdk` still hands back (the vetting model, rooms, persona);
  the workspace allows `deprecated` until the SDK moves. A rebuild and the health
  check read every page of a context's keys rather than the first 500. Device access looks up the DID's
  existing entry before granting, because `acl/grant/0.2` merges a grant into an existing
  entry (re-asserting or widening it) rather than refusing it; a revoke of an entry that is
  already gone (`acl/revoke:subjectNotPresent`) still counts as done. A community's manifest is now kept as `vta-sdk`'s
  `manifest/0.4` type (`vetting::protocol::Manifest`) rather than carried into the
  0.2 shape; vetting requirements saved by an earlier version still load.

### Fixed

- **A persona whose keys the VTA refuses is no longer called a network blip.** When
  the VTA answered `forbidden`, `notFound` or `gone` for a persona's key, the startup
  report said "this looks temporary" and to restart once connectivity was back,
  which can never help. That happens, for example, when a VTA context is deleted and
  recreated under the same id, and synced account state brings the old personas back
  without their keys. The report now says the VTA refused the keys to this account
  and that a restart won't change it. It names the usual cause and says what to do.
  An unreachable VTA is still reported as temporary.

- **A setup over REST keeps the VTA's DIDComm mediator.** A REST bootstrap
  saved the account with no mediator even when the VTA's DID document advertised
  one, so the first persona then refused with "your VTA did not advertise a DIDComm
  mediator". The advertised mediator is now kept, on the dev `OPENVTC_VTA_URL`
  route too where the DID resolves. The refusal now also names the other cause, an
  account set up over REST by an earlier OpenVTC, and says to reconnect it (#501).
- **A lost provisioning reply is no longer reported as "VTA unreachable".** When
  the VTA got the provisioning request but its reply never arrived, setup said to
  retry as-is, which the VTA then refused because the one-time grant was spent.
  It now says the grant must be re-granted, and how to find and delete the unusable
  admin entry the VTA created (`pnm acl list`, labelled `openvtc`) (#501).
- A VTA that advertises only TSP is no longer refused at the enter-DID step as
  advertising "neither a REST endpoint nor a DIDComm mediator".

### Removed

- The `openvtc-vetting-pcs` crate and the `zkp_reference_flow` example. The
  engine lives in VTI (`vti-vetting-pcs`); its end-to-end run is
  `openvtc-core/tests/hidden_vetting_onboarding.rs`, against an in-process VTA.
- The join's fallback to `manifest/0.3`/`0.2` and `submit/0.2`, and the
  key-package 0.1 fallback for a room offer. A community or VTA that refuses the
  current version is reported as such. A pending join saved by an earlier version
  still loads.

- **Onto the VTI 0.68 stack:** `vta-sdk` 0.68, `trust-tasks-rs` 0.31,
  `affinidi-tdk` 0.26, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.36 and `did-git-sign` 0.20
  (the same signer, rebuilt on that line). No behaviour change. The test
  `MockVta` moves to `vta-service` 0.60, the first VTA that serves the
  hidden-vetting engine tasks (`vta/pcs/*`).

title: pnm-cli-v0.56.0
body:
### Added

- **elections**: Check a vote after close against the head the community kept (VTI-VOT-053) ([#2460](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2460))

The VTA kept each receipt and could check it against a head and an
  inclusion proof, but nothing ever handed it either after close. Now:

  - VTA: vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list/0.1 returns the receipts kept for an
    election, whole, and the ballot box recorded at registration.
    vta/pcs/voter/read/0.7 also signs vtc/elections/tombstones/show/0.1, so a
    member can read the heads a community keeps once the election's board is
    deleted (VTI-BRD-009). voter/receipt answers notIncluded for a head too
    small to hold the cast before it looks at a path (consumer item 7.2), as
    the ballot box gives no inclusion proof for one.
  - vta-sdk: pcs_voter_receipts_list(_json); pcs_voter_read_json sends 0.7 only
    for a tombstone read, so list and show keep working against an older VTA.
  - pnm elections verify <id>: reads the head the community kept at close
    (show, or the tombstone on electionUnknown), lists the receipts, fetches
    each cast's voting/board/inclusion from the ballot box over its own
    connection, unsigned, and has the VTA check it. A cast the head omits is
    printed in red and the command fails.
  - Member portal: "Check my vote in my wallet" on a closed or tallied
    election, for a wallet that offers checkVote. The wallet answers in its
    own window; the page is told nothing.
  - Docs: pcs-engine.md step 7, elections.md.

  Pins vta/pcs/voter/read 0.7 and vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list 0.1 from the
  Trust Task PR's registry build (read 0.2/0.3/0.6 take its new deprecation
  notes); lock reset to trusttasks.org.

- **rooms**: The VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head ([#2461](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2461))

* feat(rooms)!: the VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head

  rooms/keys/watch/0.1, rooms/keys/changed/0.1 and rooms/keys/act/0.12
  (trust-tasks-tf #1040), pinned in vti-specs-rooms (act 0.8-0.11 are now
  marked superseded upstream, so their uses carry allow(deprecated)).

  The VTA serves rooms/keys/watch/0.1: up to 64 rooms at one host, one
  outcome per room. A delegate is refused permissionDenied, a member the
  VTA holds no authentication key for that the caller may act as is
  refused memberNotPrincipal (details.member), a room named twice is
  malformedRequest. Each room is its own rooms/watch/0.1 at the host,
  completed as act/0.12 completes one (presentation narrowed to read,
  granted to and signed by the member), with an address of the VTA's
  own: a did:peer:2 minted for that one watch from fresh keys, whose
  only service is DIDCommMessaging at the VTA's mediator. A re-arm of an
  unfired watch keeps its address; every other arming takes a new one.
  Per room: notAMember, actionNotHeld, limitReached (the VTA's own bound:
  64 per member, 64 per caller, 256 in all; a VTA with no mediator holds
  none), hostUnreachable, or hostRefused with the host's code unaltered.

  The record (operations::room_key_watch, keyspace room_key_watches,
  encrypted at rest, excluded from backup) is Recipient item 6's list and
  nothing else: caller, member, room, host, address and its keys, lapse.
  messaging::watch_addresses holds one mediator connection per address
  and runs the sweep. A rooms/changed at an address is passed on only
  when DIDComm authcrypt proved the watch's host as sender, it names the
  watch's room, and the watch has not lapsed; the watch is forgotten
  before the pass-on is sent. rooms/keys/changed carries roomId, member,
  host and latestVersion only, signed by the VTA, through the push path
  task-consent/granted uses, without a doorbell (Producer item 5) and
  with a deadline of one attempt window, so an accepted push is never
  re-sent (Producer item 4). A watch is also forgotten when cancelled,
  at its lapse (never later than the host's expiresAt, 30 days at most),
  when its caller loses standing to act as the member, and when the
  member's credentials for the room are gone. rooms/changed addressed to
  the VTA's own DID matches no watch and is dropped.

  rooms/keys/act/0.12 is served beside 0.8-0.11; its table adds
  rooms/watch/0.1 (read). A watch whose address is the caller's DID, the
  VTA's or the member's is refused malformedRequest (Producer item 6;
  Recipient item 6).

title: cnm-cli-v0.50.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc-service**: Preview a network before joining it — vtc/networks/preview/0.1, the console's join form and cnm networks preview ([#2464](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2464))
- **boards**: Appoint a board's facilitators (VTI-BRD-090 – 093) ([#2459](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2459))

Serves vtc/boards/facilitators/{add,remove,list}/0.1. Any facilitator of a board
  appoints an active member to facilitate it: a resource grant of vtc.boards.manage
  at board:<boardId> on the member's own entry, beside their role, delegated by and
  bounded to the signer's own holding, so a member with no administrative role can
  run one board and nothing else. A facilitator steps down; only a holder of
  vtc.boards.manage unqualified ends someone else's appointment. When the appointer
  departs or stops facilitating the board, the appointment goes to an
  acl.grants.review item (boardGrants) and is withdrawn on decline or at the
  deadline; deleting the board withdraws every appointment to it. Every change is
  audited as BoardChanged by entry, never DID.

  The grant/review/withdraw machinery of group managers moves to
  acl::appointment and now serves both kinds; ResourceGrant::confers answers
  vtc.boards.manage for the exact board only.

title: vti-specs-vtc-v0.6.2
body:
### Added

- **vtc-service**: Preview a network before joining it — vtc/networks/preview/0.1, the console's join form and cnm networks preview ([#2464](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2464))
- **boards**: Appoint a board's facilitators (VTI-BRD-090 – 093) ([#2459](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2459))

Serves vtc/boards/facilitators/{add,remove,list}/0.1. Any facilitator of a board
  appoints an active member to facilitate it: a resource grant of vtc.boards.manage
  at board:<boardId> on the member's own entry, beside their role, delegated by and
  bounded to the signer's own holding, so a member with no administrative role can
  run one board and nothing else. A facilitator steps down; only a holder of
  vtc.boards.manage unqualified ends someone else's appointment. When the appointer
  departs or stops facilitating the board, the appointment goes to an
  acl.grants.review item (boardGrants) and is withdrawn on decline or at the
  deadline; deleting the board withdraws every appointment to it. Every change is
  audited as BoardChanged by entry, never DID.

  The grant/review/withdraw machinery of group managers moves to
  acl::appointment and now serves both kinds; ResourceGrant::confers answers
  vtc.boards.manage for the exact board only.

title: vti-specs-vta-v0.5.2
body:
### Added

- **elections**: Check a vote after close against the head the community kept (VTI-VOT-053) ([#2460](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2460))

The VTA kept each receipt and could check it against a head and an
  inclusion proof, but nothing ever handed it either after close. Now:

  - VTA: vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list/0.1 returns the receipts kept for an
    election, whole, and the ballot box recorded at registration.
    vta/pcs/voter/read/0.7 also signs vtc/elections/tombstones/show/0.1, so a
    member can read the heads a community keeps once the election's board is
    deleted (VTI-BRD-009). voter/receipt answers notIncluded for a head too
    small to hold the cast before it looks at a path (consumer item 7.2), as
    the ballot box gives no inclusion proof for one.
  - vta-sdk: pcs_voter_receipts_list(_json); pcs_voter_read_json sends 0.7 only
    for a tombstone read, so list and show keep working against an older VTA.
  - pnm elections verify <id>: reads the head the community kept at close
    (show, or the tombstone on electionUnknown), lists the receipts, fetches
    each cast's voting/board/inclusion from the ballot box over its own
    connection, unsigned, and has the VTA check it. A cast the head omits is
    printed in red and the command fails.
  - Member portal: "Check my vote in my wallet" on a closed or tallied
    election, for a wallet that offers checkVote. The wallet answers in its
    own window; the page is told nothing.
  - Docs: pcs-engine.md step 7, elections.md.

  Pins vta/pcs/voter/read 0.7 and vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list 0.1 from the
  Trust Task PR's registry build (read 0.2/0.3/0.6 take its new deprecation
  notes); lock reset to trusttasks.org.

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.37.4` → `0.37.5` | patch |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.16`) | `0.10.15` → `0.10.16` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.25` → `0.9.26` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

Now: - VTA: vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list/0.1 returns the receipts kept for an election, whole, and the ballot box recorded at registration. vta/pcs/voter/read/0.7 also signs vtc/elections/tombstones/show/0.1, so a member can read the heads a community keeps once the election's board is deleted (VTI-BRD-009). voter/receipt answers notIncluded for a head too small to hold the cast before it looks at a path (consumer item 7.2), as the ballot box gives no inclusion proof for one. - vta-sdk: pcs_voter_receipts_list(_json); pcs_voter_read_json sends 0.7 only for a tombstone read, so list and show keep working against an older VTA. - pnm elections verify : reads the head the community kept at close (show, or the tombstone on electionUnknown), lists the receipts, fetches each cast's voting/board/inclusion from the ballot box over its own connection, unsigned, and has the VTA check it. A cast the head omits is printed in red and the command fails. - Member portal: "Check my vote in my wallet" on a closed or tallied election, for a wallet that offers checkVote. The wallet answers in its own window; the page is told nothing. - Docs: pcs-engine.md step 7, elections.md. Pins vta/pcs/voter/read 0.7 and vta/pcs/voter/receipts/list 0.1 from the Trust Task PR's registry build (read 0.2/0.3/0.6 take its new deprecation notes); lock reset to trusttasks.org.
## `vti-specs-vtc`
## [0.6.2](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-specs-vtc-v0.6.1...vti-specs-vtc-v0.6.2) — 2026-11-05 ### Added - **vtc-service**: Preview a network before joining it — vtc/networks/preview/0.1, the console's join form and cnm networks preview ([#2464](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2464)) - **boards**: Appoint a board's facilitators (VTI-BRD-090 – 093) ([#2459](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2459)) Serves vtc/boards/facilitators/{add,remove,list}/0.1. Any facilitator of a board appoints an active member to facilitate it: a resource grant of vtc.boards.manage at board: on the member's own entry, beside their role, delegated by and bounded to the signer's own holding, so a member with no administrative role can run one board and nothing else. A facilitator steps down; only a holder of vtc.boards.manage unqualified ends someone else's appointment. When the appointer departs or stops facilitating the board, the appointment goes to an acl.grants.review item (boardGrants) and is withdrawn on decline or at the deadline; deleting the board withdraws every appointment to it. Every change is audited as BoardChanged by entry, never DID. The grant/review/withdraw machinery of group managers moves to acl::appointment and now serves both kinds; ResourceGrant::confers answers vtc.boards.manage for the exact board only.

A rooms/changed at an address is passed on only when DIDComm authcrypt proved the watch's host as sender, it names the watch's room, and the watch has not lapsed; the watch is forgotten before the pass-on is sent. rooms/keys/changed carries roomId, member, host and latestVersion only, signed by the VTA, through the push path task-consent/granted uses, without a doorbell (Producer item 5) and with a deadline of one attempt window, so an accepted push is never re-sent (Producer item 4). A watch is also forgotten when cancelled, at its lapse (never later than the host's expiresAt, 30 days at most), when its caller loses standing to act as the member, and when the member's credentials for the room are gone. rooms/changed addressed to the VTA's own DID matches no watch and is dropped. rooms/keys/act/0.12 is served beside 0.8-0.11; its table adds rooms/watch/0.1 (read). A watch whose address is the caller's DID, the VTA's or the member's is refused malformedRequest (Producer item 6; Recipient item 6).

title: feat(vtc-service): preview a network before joining it
body:
The console's Join form can now show the network before anything is signed. It shows the network's name, owner, governance, DID and required roles, and whether the network lists this community. Until now that was learned only by trying to join. Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1047, live on trusttasks.org.

**`vtc/networks/preview/0.1`** `{ url, network? }`, pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`:
- `networks::preview` fetches the profile at `url` and checks it answers as `network` when one is given.
- It reads the community's own entry there with `vtn/entries/show`, through the same verified listing check `join` uses (`own_listing`, now `own_entry`, which also returns the entry's state).
- The answer: the network's name, description, owner, framework and roles, plus `listed`, `entryState`, `notListedReason` and the community's own `membershipState`.
- Not listed is an answer. `networkMismatch` and `networkUnreachable` are the declared refusals.
- `vtc.config.admin`, no step-up: a read, with nothing signed to the network but that one read.

**Console** (Community → Networks → Join a network):
- It previews as soon as there is an `https` URL, 400 ms after typing stops.
- A card shows the network.
- The DID the network answers as fills an empty DID field, and each required role gets a group row.
- When the network does not list the community, or it is already a member, the form says so and Join is disabled.
- A required role added between the preview and the join is still caught by the existing `roleUnassigned` row.

**CLI:** `cnm networks preview <url> [--network <did>]`.

**Wiring:** `DISPATCHED_URIS`, conformance `checked!`, the error-code census (both codes, `a_preview_reads_the_network_and_where_the_community_stands`), the console task allowlist in `trust_task_manifest`, the `vta-sdk` OpenAPI schemas, the snapshot and `wire.ts`. `docs/03-vtc/networks.md` covers the task, the console and the CLI.

**Tests:**
- `vtc-service` `--test it`: 1380 pass, including the new preview test (listed, no DID given, mismatch, unreachable, not listed, after joining, and a non-admin refused).
- `vtc-service` lib: 2173 pass.
- Console: lint, typecheck, build and 1544 tests pass, including two new ones: the card, the DID filled and the role row added; and Join disabled when the network does not list the community.
- `cnm-cli` tests pass; clippy is clean (`-D warnings`) on `vtc-service`, `vta-sdk` and `cnm-cli`.

title: fix(room-host): sign every answer as the host, and run a room watch end to end through a real mediator
body:
## Summary

`tests/e2e/tests/room_key_watch.rs` (new) runs `rooms/keys/watch/0.1` → `rooms/keys/changed/0.1` through a real `TestMediator`. It sets up a VTA on its production inbound loop and address supervisor, a `room-host` serving over the mediator (`didcomm`) and HTTPS, an open room whose member persona the VTA holds, and a wallet with its own TSP session.

**What the test proves:**
- The mediator accepts a session for a VTA-minted `did:peer:2` watch address that nobody registered.
- The mediator routes the host's `rooms/changed` to that address. This includes a signal sent **before** the address's connection opened: the mediator holds it (checked in its inbox) and delivers it when the supervisor connects.
- The wallet receives exactly one `rooms/keys/changed` with the right `roomId`, `member`, `host` and `latestVersion`, signed by the VTA and without the address. A second write without re-arming produces no signal.

**The bug it exposed (fixed here):** `room-host` never signed its answers. A member's VTA only believes a reply signed by the host it addressed (`ReplyTrust::SignedByRecipient`; SPEC §7.3 item 7, VTI-KEY-106). Every success a standalone host returned was therefore refused, so arming a watch failed with `hostUnreachable`. The in-crate `room_key_watch_tests` and `room_profile_tests` didn't catch this because their fixtures sign the host's answers themselves.

`HostState::set_answer_signer` and `dispatch` now sign every answer, including refusals and the DIDComm binding's `identityMismatch`. `didcomm::serve` sets the signer from the host identity's Ed25519 key. An HTTP-only host with no identity still answers unsigned. A unit test pins the signing.

**Findings recorded (docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md), not changed:**
- A watch address gets only the mediator's `global_acl_default`. The `mediator.toml` default `DENY_ALL,LOCAL,SEND_MESSAGES,RECEIVE_MESSAGES` lets it connect but not receive: the access list is an empty allowlist, `RECEIVE_FORWARDED` is not granted, and there is no self-change bit. On that default the watch arms, the address connects, and the mediator refuses the host's signal (`e.p.delivery.refused`). The test uses `MODE_EXPLICIT_DENY,LOCAL,SEND_MESSAGES,RECEIVE_MESSAGES,RECEIVE_FORWARDED`, the least a self-registered DIDComm receiver needs.
- The VTA can reach a host only over HTTPS to arm a watch. `rooms/watch` is issued by the member, and DIDComm or TSP would authenticate the VTA as the sender instead (`identityMismatch`). A host the VTA arms watches at must therefore advertise `TrustTaskHTTPS`.

**Harness additions (`vta-service` `test-support`):**
- `MockVta::start_with_transports_using`, to configure the embedded mediator
- `configure_messaging`
- `start_watch_addresses`, which is joined on shutdown
- `mediator_inbox_count`
- `test_support::seed_room_membership`

## Test plan
- [x] `room_key_watch` e2e passes 6× under `cargo test` and 2× under nextest (≈7–15 s per test)
- [x] With the host's signer removed, arming fails with "the reply … is unsigned" (the bug reproduces)
- [x] `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 7053 passed
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`
- [x] `cargo test -p room-host --features didcomm`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the same for `room-host --features didcomm`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- vtc-service / vtc-client not run: they depend on none of the changed crates

title: feat(did-management/stats/set-resolution): choose a slot's statistics resolution
body:
Adds `did-management/stats/set-resolution/0.1`, which chooses how much statistical detail a DID hosting service keeps over time for one slot.

## Why

A hosting service keeps a coarse series (hourly or daily) for every slot, and a fine one only for its busy slots, chosen by traffic. This task lets someone override that choice for one slot:

- **An owner** can keep less about their own DID: `coarse`, or `off` (totals only). They can also return the slot to `auto`, the service's own choice.
- **An administrator** can set any level for any slot, including `fine`, which keeps the finest series whatever the slot's traffic and outside the service's cap. It spends the operator's capacity, so only an administrator may set it.

The spec names levels, not bucket widths. A caller sees the width in `stats/timeseries`'s `bucketSeconds`.

The first implementation is affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#332 (merged): the override and its authorisation ship there behind an offline CLI, and will be exposed as this Trust Task once the spec lands.

## Shape

- **Request:** `mnemonic` (required), `domain` (optional), `resolution` (`auto | fine | coarse | off`).
- **Response:** `resolution`, `previousResolution`, `changed`, plus:
  - `tier` (`fine | coarse | off`): what the service actually keeps;
  - `tierReason` (`override | policy | traffic`): why.

  `tier` is how a caller tells "not recorded" (`off`) from "not resolved", since both read as empty buckets in `stats/timeseries`.
- **Errors:** `set-resolution:notFound` for both a missing slot and someone else's, as in `stats/get`, so the code can't be used to enumerate slots. `permissionDenied` for an owner asking for `fine`. `did-management:unknownDomain`.
- **Classification:** `mutating`, consequential. Proof and `issuedAt` are REQUIRED, because the resolution is set rather than advanced and a replayed old document would undo a later setting. `discloses: metadata`: `fine` because of `traffic` says the slot is busy.

## Checks

- `npm run validate`: 1,296 specs validate.
- Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart). `npm run check-bindings` reports all agree.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features --test conformance set_resolution`: 6 passed, covering the 9 invalid-example fixtures.

title: feat(boards): appoint a board's facilitators (VTI-BRD-090 – 093) (#2459)
body:
feat(boards): appoint a board's facilitators (VTI-BRD-090 – 093) (#2459)

Serves vtc/boards/facilitators/{add,remove,list}/0.1. Any facilitator of a board
appoints an active member to facilitate it: a resource grant of vtc.boards.manage
at board:<boardId> on the member's own entry, beside their role, delegated by and
bounded to the signer's own holding, so a member with no administrative role can
run one board and nothing else. A facilitator steps down; only a holder of
vtc.boards.manage unqualified ends someone else's appointment. When the appointer
departs or stops facilitating the board, the appointment goes to an
acl.grants.review item (boardGrants) and is withdrawn on decline or at the
deadline; deleting the board withdraws every appointment to it. Every change is
audited as BoardChanged by entry, never DID.

The grant/review/withdraw machinery of group managers moves to
acl::appointment and now serves both kinds; ResourceGrant::confers answers
vtc.boards.manage for the exact board only.

Also: vtc-client's boards checked() now validates vtc/boards/delete, which it
refused client-side before ("is not a vtc/boards task"), so `cnm boards delete`
never reached the community.

- cnm boards facilitators add|remove|list
- console: a Facilitators card on the board page (shared EntryName component)
- docs: boards.md "Appointing facilitators", design note, CLAUDE.md
- test: vti_brd_090_a_member_appointed_facilitator_runs_the_board_until_removed

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |

| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.37.3` → `0.37.4` | patch |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.15`) | `0.10.14` → `0.10.15` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.24` → `0.9.25` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(web): wallet sign-in fills the number in a browser wallet, and starts by itself
body:
The landing page's wallet sign-in now behaves like the VTC console's.

- **The number fills itself in a browser wallet.** The match number's element carries `data-oob-request-id` and `data-oob-match-number` (sign-in contract C11, as the VTC's `WalletSignIn`). When the code is clicked on this page, the wallet browser extension reads them and fills the number in; only a phone wallet asks for it to be typed. The page posts nothing to the extension, and nothing comes back. The attributes are cleared when the sign-in ends.
- **A code without a click.** A members-only or admins-only page shows a sign-in code as soon as it loads, unless the visitor is signed in already. "Sign in with a wallet" stays for starting again after a decline or cancel.
- **Codes renew.** An unscanned code that runs out is replaced, as the VTC does. While the tab is hidden it is replaced when the tab returns. A code that ends within 10 seconds of being made (a wrong clock, a network dropping requests) ends instead of looping.
- **Polls survive blips.** A dropped connection, a 5xx or a rate limit is retried on the same request, not shown as a failed sign-in.
- **Approval end.** When the approval ends, the page signs out by itself and, on a restricted directory, shows a fresh code.
- **Wording.** The steps say a wallet in this browser fills the number in.

Checked in headless Chrome with stubbed answers: the code appears with no click, and the number element carries both attributes. The extension itself wasn't exercised.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.3
body:
### Added

- **rooms/keys**: Rooms/keys/watch and rooms/keys/changed — a key holder watches rooms for its member's wallet; act 0.12 lists rooms/watch ([#1040](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1040))

A wallet whose member keys are held by its key holder cannot present as
  the member and has no address a host can reach, so it could not use
  rooms/watch ([#1036](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1036)).

- **did-management/stats/set-resolution**: Choose a slot's statistics resolution ([#1041](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1041))

An owner can keep less statistical detail over time for their own DID (coarse, or totals only), or return it to the service's own choice; an administrator can set any level for any slot, including always keeping the finest series. Bindings regenerated.

- **vtc/elections**: Read a deleted board's election tombstone ([#1037](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1037))

vtc/elections/tombstones/show/0.1 (new): an active member or a holder of vtc.elections.manage reads the tombstone the community keeps of an election on a deleted board (VTI-BRD-009) — identifier, manifest digest, ballot box, and each kept board head with the ballot box's signed voting/board/head document as received — so a voter's agent can still check a receipt against the community's record (VTI-VOT-053). No tombstone and an unreadable one are both electionUnknown. Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

- **rooms**: Rooms/watch and rooms/changed — a content-free signal that a room has moved ([#1036](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1036))

A member who wants to know a room has new records polls
  rooms/records/list with sinceVersion. rooms/watch/0.1 lets it instead
  name an address DID and the version it has read to; the host sends one
  rooms/changed/0.1 to that address the first time the room moves past
  it, then disarms until the member re-arms after reading.

  The signal carries the room and its latest version only, the same
  whatever changed, and is one-way. It reaches a sleeping device through
  the address's mediator queue and the existing push/wake doorbell, so the
  mediator, push gateway and platform push service learn that something
  arrived and nothing of the room. One signal per arming bounds the queue
  and the wake count however busy the room is.

  On the sealed tiers the host never sees a record's kind, so a reaction
  fires a watch as a message does. rooms/changed states how a reader
  decides unread after listing: new message keys, not its own, current;
  reactions, edits, curations and notes are never unread messages, and an
  alert is raised only on what was found.

  A watch is host state that grants nothing and does not move with the
  room. On a private room the address must be used for nothing else.

- **vtc/networks**: 0.2 on vtn/* tasks, and vtc/networks/deliver/0.1 ([#1033](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1033))

vtc/networks/{join,leave,list,show,repudiate,evidence,groups/register} 0.2 reach the network only through vtn/* Trust Tasks signed as the community; a group's registration is the community's signed vtn/groups/register request (servesRole retired) and its endpoint the community's Trust Task endpoint (vtc/_shared/0.7). New vtc/networks/deliver/0.1: a network delivers a broadcast envelope to the community's registered group. 0.1 remains published.

- **vtc/boards**: Delete a closed board, and end its voting when it closes ([#1032](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1032))

- vtc/boards/delete/0.1 (new): a board manager (vtc.boards.manage
    unqualified, with a bound step-up) deletes a closed or archived board
    whose elections have all closed or been cancelled (`notClosed`,
    `electionsRunning`). Removes the board, ideas, notes and each
    election's content; each election keeps a tombstone — identifier,
    manifest digest, kept board heads — for the community's tombstone
    retention (default twelve months, may be unbounded, zero keeps none).
    Answers counts and when the tombstones go (VTI-BRD-007, VTI-BRD-008).
  - vtc/boards/update/0.1: closing a board ends its voting (VTI-BRD-006):
    elections open for voting are closed early, so the count is final;
    those not yet open are cancelled; those that cannot close early run
    on. The response gains an optional `closing` summary. A template
    that does not allow closing early is `templateInvalid` (VTI-BRD-030).
  - vtc/boards/create/0.1: the same template rule; examples in create,
    show, list and update now allow closing early.
  - Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.



### Specifications

- **vtc/elections**: A deleted group's DID is never a member party (VTI-VOT-029) ([#1039](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1039))

vtc/elections/show/0.6, vtc/elections/list/0.5 and
  vtc/elections/tickets/issue/0.3 defined a member party as a
  `roll.memberOf` that is "neither the community's own DID nor one of its
  groups". Once a group is deleted its DID is no longer one of the
  community's groups, so read literally the definition let the election
  fall onto the member-party presentation path, where a holder of an
  unexpired credential the deleted group issued could read it.
  VTI-VOT-029 forbids exactly that: such an election is shown, and
  confirmed to exist, only to a holder of `vtc.elections.manage`, and
  the deleted group's identifier is never treated as a party outside
  the community.

  The member-party test is now decided by what `roll.memberOf` was when
  the election was created; show item 1 and list item 1 say a deleted
  group's election is seen only by a manager; show item 8.3 says a
  presentation of the group's credential shows it to nobody. The
  payload descriptions of show and list say the same.

  Description and prose only: every schema is otherwise unchanged, as
  CONTRIBUTING-SPECS "Version rules" allows in place for a released
  draft version.

- **rooms**: A record's kind, replies and reactions — notes, messages and reactions on every tier ([#1027](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1027))

* spec(rooms): a record's kind, replies and reactions — notes, messages and reactions on every tier

  A room had one kind of record, so a chat-style client's messages read as
  untitled notes in every other client, and nothing let two clients agree
  on a reply or a reaction (Keyring, berkmancenter/keyring-wallet
  docs/upstream/2026-11-rooms-findings.md, finding 2).

  SealedRecordBody (rooms/_shared 0.1 and 0.2, identically) gains two
  optional members, in place and additively, as provenance did:

  - `kind` (RecordKind): an open, lowerCamelCase set — `note`, `message`,
    `reaction` defined. Absent means note; a reader shows a kind it does
    not know as a note and never refuses a record for its kind.
  - `inReplyTo` (RecordReference): another record of the same room, by
    key and optionally the version answered. A reader resolves it only
    against records it can already read, shows a reply whose target is
    unavailable as such, and fetches nothing because of it.

  Reactions are records of kind `reaction` carrying their target in
  `inReplyTo` and a value of at most 64 characters on one line in `body`;
  one per author, value and target; withdrawn by rewriting the same key
  with an empty body. Edits are what they already were: a new version
  under the same key — nothing is added, and a version by another author
  is never shown as the earlier author's edit. A file record's `body` is
  its caption, which a reader SHOULD show.

  Readers that predate the members refuse them by rule (1), so a writer
  SHOULD NOT write them until its room's readers accept them — and the
  spec says plainly a writer cannot check that: a sealed body carries no
  schema version and members publish no reader capabilities.

  rooms/records/put/0.5 (extends 0.4) adds `kind` and `inReplyTo` to an
  open room's closed `cleartext`; the host stores and serves them and
  never acts on them. rooms/keys/act/0.11 (extends 0.10) adds put/0.5 to
  its table. Libraries regenerated.

- **rooms**: A removed member can rejoin — prior group state is a prior membership, not a join, corrected in place ([#1031](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1031))

* spec(rooms): a removed member can rejoin — prior group state is a prior membership, not a join, corrected in place

  rooms/keys/welcome 0.1 required a recipient holding group state for
  `roomId` for the member to answer `alreadyJoined`, and in the same
  paragraph said rejoining is "a removal followed by a fresh invitation".
  A member removed by a commit keeps its group state — rooms/keys/open 0.2
  and rooms/keys/file-key 0.2 answer `unknownEpoch` with reason `removed`
  from it — so the MUST refused the very Welcome the paragraph said
  rejoining uses, and a removed member could never be admitted again.
  rooms/owner/group/remove 0.4 and rooms/owner/revoke 0.1 both describe
  re-admission as fresh credentials plus a new leaf. Welcome's Retention
  section also said to discard the state on removal, contradicting the
  `removed` reason and file-key's "removal is forward-only".

  - welcome 0.1: state from which a processed commit removed the member is
    a prior membership. A recipient holding only prior memberships MUST
    process a Welcome under a valid, unconsumed invitation and MUST keep
    each prior membership, unmerged, for records sealed under the epochs
    it covers (subject to the epoch floor). `alreadyJoined` is for current
    state only. Prior memberships cover [join epoch, removal epoch) and
    never overlap.
  - open 0.2: the record's epoch chooses the state — current when E is at
    or after its join epoch, else the prior membership covering E; E in a
    gap between a removal and the next join is `unknownEpoch` / `removed`
    with that `removedAtEpoch`. Never a retry under another state.
  - file-key 0.2: the same selection for `open`; a principal holding only
    prior memberships answers `seal` with `noGroup`.
  - group/remove 0.4: re-admission points at welcome's rule.

  No wire change: no member, code or reason added or removed. All four
  specifications are `draft`, so the prose correction is made in place
  (SPEC §5.2). Regenerated bindings change only error-code doc text.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.23` → `0.9.24` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.
