title: feat(rooms): open rooms learn of changes through the member's VTA, and members' names follow the amended reading rules
body:
## Summary

Two specification changes are implemented here: watching rooms through the member's VTA (trust-tasks-tf #1040, served by VTI #2461), and the memberProfile reader and writer amendments (trust-tasks-tf #1038).

### Watching (`rooms/keys/watch/0.1`, `rooms/keys/changed/0.1`)

- **Pins.** Both tasks are pinned and generated. `task-surface.json` is resynced from vta-sdk 0.83.0 at VTI origin/main, and the recorded coverage count goes from 242 to 244.
- **Core (`rooms/watch.ts`).**
  - `roomsKeysWatch` checks that the answer echoes the member and host, with one outcome per room in the order asked.
  - `parseRoomsKeysChanged` accepts a signal only from the wallet's own VTA, as the transport proved it, and only with the closed schema's payload.
  - `RoomWatcher` gathers requests per VTA, member and host, with at most 64 rooms per request. Each arming takes one signal. It re-arms only after a read and cancels on release. A release during arming is cancelled once the answer says the watch was armed. Refusals are quiet and are retried only after a delay. A lapse at `expiresAt` makes the pane read again.
  - `unreadMessages` and `latestMessageTime` follow `rooms/changed/0.1` step 4.
- **Extension.**
  - The offscreen inbound dispatch routes `rooms/keys/changed` beside `task-consent/granted` and forwards it to the console (`RUNTIME_ROOMS_KEYS_CHANGED`). The console takes a signal only from `offscreen.html`, and only for a watch it armed (`manager/room-watch.ts`).
  - The records pane now refreshes incrementally. It lists from the watermark and batch-reads what changed. A `lastPrune` past the watermark triggers a full rebuild.
  - The pane keeps a read marker in `chrome.storage.local`, shows an unread count, and raises one OS notification with fixed, content-free words when the console is hidden.
  - Polling is the fallback: every 60 s when no watch covers the room, and every 10 min while one is armed.

### Members' names (`rooms/_shared/0.3` memberProfile)

- **Rule 2 for several records by one author.** The most recently stored version wins, and a tie goes to the greater version. Reading order does not affect the result.
- **Rewrites.** A version one member wrote over another's record is now the writer's own claim. Before, it named nobody.
- **Look-alike names.** UTS #39 `skeleton()` comparison tells them apart. It runs over Unicode's `confusables.txt` 16.0.0, generated in full by `scripts/sync-confusables.mjs` and pinned by SHA-256.
- **Before a name is found.** An author is shown as their petname or a shortened DID. The pane no longer shows a name taken from the author's DID document.
- **500-version rewrite.** `rewriteMemberNameAsMember` writes the name again after a console note, curation or file put that lands more than 500 versions past the member's name record. It uses the same key and name, keeps `writtenAt` and sets no new `editedAt`. It replaces the version read and is gated on the room's `recordMembers`.

## Notes for review

- **Confusables data.** No npm confusables package is both maintained and a direct UTS #39 `skeleton()` implementation, so the full Unicode data is generated and digest-pinned instead. The data is about 72 KB and lives under the `rooms` subpath only.
- **No toolbar badge.** The background's toolbar badge comes from durable state (approvals, offers). Unread counts are per open pane and in memory, so they are shown in the pane and through the notification instead.
- **Portal writes.** Portal writes (`window.vtaWallet.rooms.putNote` and `putFile`) do not do the 500-version rewrite. The wallet holds none of the room's records there, and the spec has the rewrite use the name rule 2 gives from the records the client holds.
- **`rooms/keys/act`.** The pin stays at 0.11. VTI still serves it, and this change does not need 0.12.

## Tests

- core: new `rooms.watch.mjs` and `rooms.confusables.mjs`; `rooms.member-name.mjs` extended (rule 3, tie-break, order independence, skeleton, no guessing, near-the-head writer).
- extension: new `rooms-watch.render.test.mts` (arm after read, signal → refresh from watermark → re-arm, ignored senders, unread and notification without content, refusal → polling, cancel on close); `room-files.test.mts` extended (offscreen rewrite after note/curate, not within 500, gate holds).
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (all workspaces, 0 failures), `check-task-versions.mjs`, and every post-test step in `ci.yml` (bundle assertions, package, zip checks) pass locally.

title: feat(rooms)!: the VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head
body:
Implements two merged rooms specifications in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf:

- **trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1040** (a67bf811): `rooms/keys/watch/0.1`, `rooms/keys/changed/0.1`, `rooms/keys/act/0.12`
- **trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1038** (83716be9): `rooms/_shared/0.3` memberProfile, amended in place (rule 2 tie-break, re-write near the head)

Builds on #2457 (`rooms/watch`, `rooms/changed` at both hosts) and #2452 (`act/0.11`).

## VTA

**`rooms/keys/watch/0.1`** (`trust_tasks::room_key_watch`). Accepts up to 64 rooms at one host and returns one outcome per room, in the order given.
- Requests refused as a whole:
  - a delegate gets `permissionDenied`;
  - a `member` the VTA holds no `authentication` key for, or that the caller may not act as, gets `memberNotPrincipal` with `details.member`;
  - a room named twice gets `malformedRequest`.
- Each room gets its own `rooms/watch/0.1`, presentation and address. The request is completed as `act/0.12` completes one: the presentation is narrowed to `read`, granted to the member and signed by the member.
- Per-room refusals: `notAMember`, `actionNotHeld`, `limitReached`, `hostUnreachable`, and `hostRefused` with the host's code unaltered.
- `limitReached` here is the VTA's own bound: 64 per member, 64 per caller and 256 in all.

**Addresses.** Each address is a `did:peer:2` minted per arming from fresh keys, using the existing `operations::did_peer` construction. Its only service is `DIDCommMessaging` at the VTA's mediator DID.
- The address is never the VTA's DID, the member's or the caller's, and it is never shown to the caller.
- A re-arm of a watch that has not fired keeps its address. Every other arming takes a new one.
- `messaging::watch_addresses` holds one mediator connection per address, in the same shape as the collector's per-persona sessions, and runs the sweep.

**Record.** `operations::room_key_watch` keeps exactly what Recipient item 6 lists: caller, member, room, host, address and its keys, and the lapse time.
- Stored in keyspace `room_key_watches`, which is encrypted at rest and excluded from backup.
- `Debug` is written by hand.
- The DID-delete and context-delete censuses are classified.

**Signal.** A `rooms/changed` at an address is passed on only when all of these hold:
- DIDComm authcrypt proved the watch's `host` as the sender;
- it names the watch's room;
- the watch has not lapsed.

The watch is forgotten **before** the pass-on is sent. `rooms/keys/changed/0.1`:
- carries `roomId`, `member`, `host` and `latestVersion` and nothing else, and is signed by the VTA;
- goes out on the push path `task-consent/granted` uses (`step_up::push_to_device_with`);
- sends no doorbell (Producer item 5);
- has a deadline of one attempt window, so a push the delivery layer accepted is never re-sent (Producer item 4).

A `rooms/changed` addressed to the VTA's own DID matches no watch and is dropped.

**Removal.** A watch is forgotten when:
- it fires;
- it is cancelled;
- it lapses: never later than the host's `expiresAt`, and 30 days at most;
- the caller loses standing to act as the member: the ACL entry is gone, narrowed, or now a delegate's;
- the member's credentials for the room are gone.

The sweep runs every 30 s and on every change.

**`rooms/keys/act/0.12`** is served beside 0.8–0.11. Its table adds `rooms/watch/0.1` (`read`). As Recipient item 6 says, the VTA does not read, check or change `address`, `sinceVersion` or `leaseSeconds`; Producer item 6 (which DID the address may be) binds the client and is enforced by `pnm rooms watch --via-host`.

**Classifications:**
- `retry_safety`: `RetrySafe`.
- Operation budget: `keys/watch` is charged the heaviest weight. Signals at an address are charged to the bound for senders without standing.
- Also covered: the dispatch class, conformance rows, the policy subject (`/member`), the vta-mcp guard and the keyspace censuses.

## SDK and pnm

**SDK:** `VtaClient::{room_watch, room_watch_cancel, room_act_v0_12}`, `unsigned_room_request_v0_12`, `room_changed_signal`.

**`pnm rooms watch`** now asks the VTA by default.
- `--room` can be repeated.
- `--member` is optional. Without it, pnm uses the one member `rooms/keys/list` names, or, for an open room with `--host`, the member `rooms/info` completes as.
- A VTA without `rooms/keys/watch` gets an error that names `--via-host` or polling.

**`--via-host --address`** arms the host's watch through `act/0.12`. It refuses an address that is the client's own DID, the VTA's or the member's (Producer item 6) before anything reaches the host, and falls back to the #2457 present-and-sign path for a VTA that predates 0.12.

**memberProfile:**
- Rule 2's tie-break (on equal stored time, the greater `version` wins) is in `vti_rooms::member_profile::Names` and in pnm's own-record pick, so the name no longer depends on reading order.
- After `rooms put` and `rooms file put`, pnm writes the name again over the same key when the write's version is more than 500 past the name record's.
  - It keeps `writtenAt`, adds no `editedAt`, and never re-writes a withdrawn name.
  - It looks one page back before reading the whole room.

## Decisions where the specification is silent or loose

- **The address advertises DIDComm only, not TSP.** A did:peer address cannot take part in a TSP relationship without more machinery; the host already picks DIDComm by service type.
- **A VTA with no mediator answers every room `limitReached`.** It has no address it could receive at, and the specification's guidance for a room the key holder cannot watch is to poll.
- **A failed re-arm.** If the host cannot be reached, the existing record is kept, since the earlier arming may still be in force. If the host refuses, the record is forgotten.
- **A cancel the host refuses still forgets the watch here,** because the caller asked for it gone.
- **On a withdrawal, the host's watch is not cancelled.** Recipient item 7 says the VTA SHOULD cancel at the host, but that needs the member's credentials for a caller that may no longer use them, or credentials that are gone. The host forgets the watch at its own lease.
- **Rooms in one request are armed one after another.**
- **The audit row** names the host and the counts armed and cancelled. It never names a room or an address (item 6's MAY).
- **memberProfile rule 3 with "Several records by one author".** A version another member rewrote is weighed as that member's claim, and never as the original author's. #2457 had it name nobody.
- **`TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_CHANGED_0_1` is not in `ALL_URIS`.** The VTA sends it and serves nothing under it.
- **Act 0.8–0.11 bundles changed with this pin.** Upstream now marks them superseded, so their uses carry `allow(deprecated)`.

## Tests

The end-to-end tests run against a real room host, using the `room_profile_tests` fixtures. The host's `rooms/changed` is handed to the VTA's address receiver in-process, where a mediator would carry it.

- arm through the VTA, put at the host, the VTA receives the signal, passes one `rooms/keys/changed` to the caller (four members, signed, schema-valid, no address), forgets the watch, and drops a replay;
- re-arming keeps the address until the watch fires, then takes a new one;
- cancel, and a cancel of a watch that is not held, which asks nothing of the host;
- `limitReached`, from the VTA's own bound and from having no mediator;
- `memberNotPrincipal`, a room named twice, and per-room `notAMember`;
- a signal from the wrong sender or for the wrong room is dropped;
- the sweep forgets a lapsed watch and one whose caller lost standing;
- `act/0.12` completes a watch that the real host arms, passing `address` (including the caller's, the VTA's and the member's DID), `sinceVersion` and `leaseSeconds` through unaltered; `act/0.11` refuses `rooms/watch` with `typeNotActable`.

Unit tests cover pnm's item 6 check, the 500-version rule, the version tie-break in either order, the act 0.12 table, address minting and the redacted `Debug`.

### Results
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 7023 passed, 23 skipped
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: 8 passed, 0 failed (30 ignored)
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3606 passed, 1 skipped
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`: 3 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. The three `vta-service` feature-matrix clippies from CI are also clean: `rest`; `setup,keyring,rest,tsp,cli-synthesis`; `setup,keyring,rest,didcomm,cli-synthesis`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

Not exercised: a live mediator carrying a signal to a minted address. Nothing here has run against a live mediator.

## Breaking
- `vta_service::server::AppState` gains `room_key_watches`.
- `vti_rooms::member_profile::Names::offer` takes the version and no longer takes `created_by`.

feat(rooms)!: the VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head (#2461)

* feat(rooms)!: the VTA watches rooms for its clients (rooms/keys/watch, rooms/keys/changed), act/0.12, and memberProfile's tie-break and rewrite near the head

rooms/keys/watch/0.1, rooms/keys/changed/0.1 and rooms/keys/act/0.12
(trust-tasks-tf #1040), pinned in vti-specs-rooms (act 0.8-0.11 are now
marked superseded upstream, so their uses carry allow(deprecated)).

The VTA serves rooms/keys/watch/0.1: up to 64 rooms at one host, one
outcome per room. A delegate is refused permissionDenied, a member the
VTA holds no authentication key for that the caller may act as is
refused memberNotPrincipal (details.member), a room named twice is
malformedRequest. Each room is its own rooms/watch/0.1 at the host,
completed as act/0.12 completes one (presentation narrowed to read,
granted to and signed by the member), with an address of the VTA's
own: a did:peer:2 minted for that one watch from fresh keys, whose
only service is DIDCommMessaging at the VTA's mediator. A re-arm of an
unfired watch keeps its address; every other arming takes a new one.
Per room: notAMember, actionNotHeld, limitReached (the VTA's own bound:
64 per member, 64 per caller, 256 in all; a VTA with no mediator holds
none), hostUnreachable, or hostRefused with the host's code unaltered.

The record (operations::room_key_watch, keyspace room_key_watches,
encrypted at rest, excluded from backup) is Recipient item 6's list and
nothing else: caller, member, room, host, address and its keys, lapse.
messaging::watch_addresses holds one mediator connection per address
and runs the sweep. A rooms/changed at an address is passed on only
when DIDComm authcrypt proved the watch's host as sender, it names the
watch's room, and the watch has not lapsed; the watch is forgotten
before the pass-on is sent. rooms/keys/changed carries roomId, member,
host and latestVersion only, signed by the VTA, through the push path
task-consent/granted uses, without a doorbell (Producer item 5) and
with a deadline of one attempt window, so an accepted push is never
re-sent (Producer item 4). A watch is also forgotten when cancelled,
at its lapse (never later than the host's expiresAt, 30 days at most),
when its caller loses standing to act as the member, and when the
member's credentials for the room are gone. rooms/changed addressed to
the VTA's own DID matches no watch and is dropped.

rooms/keys/act/0.12 is served beside 0.8-0.11; its table adds
rooms/watch/0.1 (read). A watch whose address is the caller's DID, the
VTA's or the member's is refused malformedRequest (Producer item 6;
Recipient item 6).

Classified: retry_safety (watch and act/0.12 RetrySafe), operation
budget (watch charged the heaviest weight; signals at an address to
the bound for senders without standing), dispatch class, conformance
rows, the policy subject (/member), the vta-mcp guard, the keyspace
backup, DID-delete and context-delete censuses.

SDK: VtaClient::{room_watch, room_watch_cancel, room_act_v0_12},
unsigned_room_request_v0_12, room_changed_signal. pnm rooms watch now
asks the VTA (repeat --room; --member, else the one rooms/keys/list
names); --via-host --address arms the host's watch through act/0.12,
falling back to the earlier present-and-sign path for a VTA that
predates it.

memberProfile (rooms/_shared/0.3, trust-tasks-tf #1038): rule 2's
tie-break - of two versions stored at the same time the greater version
wins - in vti_rooms::member_profile::Names and in pnm's own-record pick,
so the name never depends on reading order; a version another member
rewrote is weighed as that member's claim. After rooms put and rooms
file put, pnm writes the member's name again over the same record when
the write's version is more than 500 past it, keeping writtenAt and
adding no editedAt, and never for a withdrawn name.

Breaking: vta_service::server::AppState gains room_key_watches;
vti_rooms::member_profile::Names::offer takes the version and no
longer takes created_by.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rooms): act/0.12 relays rooms/watch without checking its address

rooms/keys/act/0.12 says the recipient does not read, check or change
address, sinceVersion or leaseSeconds (Recipient item 6); Producer item
6, which says which DID the address may be, binds the producer alone.
The VTA no longer refuses a rooms/watch whose address is the caller's,
the VTA's or the member's DID: it completes it with the three passed
through unaltered, which the test now asserts.

The producer keeps item 6: pnm rooms watch --via-host refuses an
address that is the client's own DID, the VTA's (from the session, else
the client) or the member's, before anything reaches the host
(forbidden_watch_address).

title: feat(web): invite from the landing page
body:
An administrator who signs in on the landing page with their wallet can now invite a community or network there, as `nnm invite` does.

**Scope.** A wallet-approved browser key now also signs `vtn/listings/create`, `list` and `show` as its approver (`tasks::oob::SIGNING_SCOPE`).
- The scope is the same for every approver; each task still checks the approver's standing. So only an administrator's sign-in lists anyone, and a member's key is refused as before.
- Suspending, removing, broadcasts and memberships stay with the NNM, signed by the administrator's own key.
- The wallet shows the wider scope when it asks for approval. A key approved before this change keeps its old scope until it signs in again.

**Invite tab.** It appears once the signed-in key may read listings (a `vtn/listings/list` probe).
- The form takes the party's DID, kind, name, site, description and tags.
- It lists the party, or reuses an entry that is still waiting for acknowledgement.
- It shows the invitation to send: network URL and DID, the roles that need a group, and how to accept. For a community with a site, that is the console link `<site>/admin/networks?join=…&network=…`, which opens the VTC console's Join page (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2458). "Copy invitation" copies it as text.

**Docs.** A13, `docs/trust-tasks.md` and the README say what the scope covers now.

**Test.** `an_administrators_page_key_invites_and_a_members_does_not`:
- an administrator's page key lists and shows a community, but cannot remove it;
- a member's page key cannot list anyone.

Checked in headless Chrome with stubbed answers (the form, the invitation and the console link).

title: vtc-service-v0.24.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc-service**: Join a network from the console's Networks page or cnm networks ([#2458](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2458))

The community side of Verifiable Trust Network membership (vtc/networks/*/0.2) had no
  caller: no console page and no cnm command sent join, leave or repudiate.

  - Console: Community → Networks (/admin/networks, vtc.config.admin) lists the
    memberships with their credentials (the network's listing and grant, the community's
    acknowledgement or repudiation, the registered groups), and joins, leaves or rejects a
    listing through the console's operation-bound step-up. A network's invitation links to
    /admin/networks?join=<network url>&network=<network DID>. A roleUnassigned refusal adds
    a row for the role; only groups with a DID of their own are offered.
  - cnm networks list | show | join <url> --network <did> [--group role=groupId]... |
    leave | repudiate, through cnm's step-up hand-off.
  - join, repudiate and leave now run every check that would refuse them before asking for
    the step-up (join_preflight, repudiate_preflight, leave_preflight), so a join that
    cannot succeed costs the administrator no passkey gesture (VTI-APV-015).
  - vta-sdk exposes the vtc/networks/{list,show,join,leave,repudiate}/0.2 schemas to the
    OpenAPI document, so the console's wire types are generated, not written by hand.

- **portal**: Put notified elections on the home page; read the wallet's error codes first ([#2456](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2456))

The home page's *Needs your attention* read only the community's own
  election list, so an election the member was notified of (VTI-NTF-063),
  one put to a member party's members (VTI-VOT-015), never appeared there.

  - `actionableNotified` keeps the notified elections the community does
    not list (deduplicated by `notifiedOnly`), whose notice still stands
    (a withdrawn one cannot be opened, VTI-NTF-024) and whose voting
    period, where the notice states one, has not closed. The home page
    reads them from the same `member-elections` query as the Elections
    page, names them by identifier only, counts them on the Elections
    tile, and links them with `electionHref`, so the election page still
    takes `memberOf` from the standing notice, never from the link.
  - `refusalKind` and `declinedInWallet` read the `code` a wallet puts on
    its page-facing error first: the Trust Task codes `electionUnknown`
    and `indeterminate` (`REFUSAL_BY_CODE`), and the wallet's own codes
    for what the member decided in its window (`WALLET_OUTCOME_BY_CODE`,
    `declined` for now, the name the wallet's room offers already use).
    An error with no code, or one these tables do not know, is read by
    its words as before, so older wallets keep working.

- **rooms**: Members' names in a room (memberProfile), and rooms/watch with its rooms/changed signal on both hosts ([#2457](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2457))

A member's name in a room (trust-tasks-tf #1035, rooms/_shared/0.3
  member-profile): a record of kind `memberProfile` whose `title` is the
  name. `vti_rooms::member_profile` holds the writer's and reader's rules
  (MemberName: one line, no controls, at most 64 code points after NFC;
  empty or white space withdraws; MemberProfileRecord /
  MemberProfileCleartext shapes; `Names`, which takes per author the most
  recently stored version and refuses a rewrite by anyone but the original
  author). `record_members::used` names `memberProfile` for a body of that
  kind, so the writer's rule asks for `kind` and `memberProfile` listed;
  the SDK's copy (`RECORD_KIND_VALUES`, `MEMBER_PROFILE_KIND`) is pinned
  equal by the existing test. No host, seal or act change: a key holder
  seals the body unchanged, as the schema says. `pnm rooms name set|clear`
  writes the record (seal/0.3 + act/0.11 on sealed tiers, put/0.5 on open),
  over the member's existing name record when it holds one; `pnm rooms
  list|get|read` show a name record as a name, never a note, and an
  author's name beside their DID.

  rooms/watch/0.1 and rooms/changed/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #1036), pinned in
  vti-specs-rooms. `vti_rooms::watch` is the host-neutral half both hosts
  call: authorized as a listing (`read`), with the task's chainTooDeep and
  subjectBindingMissing; one watch per room and address in its own
  keyspace (host state, never backed up, never consulted to authorize);
  lease 7 days by default, 30 at most, never past the presentation's
  first credential lapsing (`VerifiedChain::valid_until`, new);
  addressUnreachable when the address offers no transport the host
  speaks; limitReached past 1024 per room or 16 per member. After any
  successful room task the room's watches past their watermark are
  removed under one lock and signalled once, after a 2-6 s randomised
  delay, with the room and its latest version only; a watch whose
  presentation the held revocation list withdraws never fires. room-host
  signals over its mediator session (TSP before DIDComm, by service type);
  the VTC over `PeerTasks::send_one_way`, signed as the community. Neither
  sends REST or retries.

title: feat(rooms/keys): rooms/keys/watch and rooms/keys/changed — a key holder watches rooms for its member's wallet; act 0.12 lists rooms/watch (#1040)
body:
feat(rooms/keys): rooms/keys/watch and rooms/keys/changed — a key holder watches rooms for its member's wallet; act 0.12 lists rooms/watch (#1040)

A wallet whose member keys are held by its key holder cannot present as
the member and has no address a host can reach, so it could not use
rooms/watch (#1036).

rooms/keys/watch/0.1: the client asks its key holder to arm rooms/watch at
one host for one or more rooms, as the member, at an address the key
holder controls and uses for that one watch only. Each room is its own
host request, presentation and address: batching stops at the key holder,
so a host never sees one party reading several rooms.

rooms/keys/changed/0.1: the key holder passes the host's signal on to the
client that armed the watch, once per arming, with the room, member, host
and latest version and nothing else, then forgets the watch.

rooms/keys/act/0.12 adds rooms/watch/0.1 (read) to its table for a client
that receives at an address of its own, and says which address it may be.

The push binding gains an informative note on the intended mobile-wallet
shape.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc-service): join a network from the console's Networks page or cnm networks
body:
The community side of Verifiable Trust Network membership (`vtc/networks/*/0.2`) has had no caller: no console page and no `cnm` command sent `join`, `leave` or `repudiate`. So a community a VTN listed had no practical way to accept. This adds both, reusing the existing tasks unchanged. `join` already is the credential exchange: it verifies the network's listing, registers the community's groups for the network's roles, signs the acknowledgement of the network's offer, and verifies the grant the network returns.

## Console: Community → Networks

`/admin/networks`, for `vtc.config.admin`:
- **Memberships:** lists them (`vtc/networks/list/0.2`). Each one opens with `show`: its credentials (the network's listing and grant, the community's acknowledgement or repudiation), and the groups registered for each role.
- **Join a network:** takes the network URL and DID. A network's invitation links straight here: `/admin/networks?join=<network url>&network=<network DID>`, both percent-encoded.
  - Pick a group for each of the network's roles. Only groups with a DID of their own are offered.
  - When the network requires a role the form leaves out, the `roleUnassigned` refusal names it, and the form adds a row for it.
  - Sent through the console's operation-bound step-up (`postSignedWithStepUp`).
- **Leave** and **Reject listing**, each with a confirmation and an optional audit reason.

## `cnm networks`

```
cnm networks list
cnm networks show <network-did>
cnm networks join <url> --network <did> [--group <role>=<groupId>]...
cnm networks leave <network-did> [--reason …]
cnm networks repudiate <url> --network <did> [--reason …]
```

Writes go through cnm's existing step-up hand-off (`git::send_change`). Refusals name what to do.

## Server: check before asking for the gesture

`join`, `repudiate` and `leave` asked for the bound step-up first and only then contacted the network, so a join that would fail (no group for a required role, not listed yet, wrong DID) still cost the administrator a passkey gesture. With the role refusal, each attempt cost one.

They now run every check that would refuse them first: `networks::{join,repudiate,leave}_preflight`. As the console's step-up flow expects, a refusal is shown with no gesture. The writes check everything again after the gesture, since any of it can change in between. New test: `a_join_that_would_fail_asks_for_no_step_up`.

## Wire types

`vta-sdk`'s `openapi` exposes the `vtc/networks/{list,show,join,leave,repudiate}/0.2` payloads and responses. `vtc-service` adds them to the OpenAPI document, so the console's types are generated (`openapi.json`, `wire.ts`), not written by hand. Census updates:
- `list-limits.json` and its test;
- `trust_task_manifest` `SPINE_DOCUMENT_TYPES`.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client -p vta-sdk`: 4917 passed, 4 failed. The four failures are member-portal bundle tests that also fail on a clean `origin/main` here when the bundle build is skipped (`VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`).
- `cargo nextest run -p cnm-cli`: 148 passed.
- admin-ui: `npm run lint` (wire check and tsc) clean, `vitest` 1536 passed, `npm run build` ok.

Pairs with the VTN's `nnm invite`, which lists a community and prints the deep link above.

title: spec(vtc/elections): a deleted group's DID is never a member party (VTI-VOT-029) (#1039)
body:
spec(vtc/elections): a deleted group's DID is never a member party (VTI-VOT-029) (#1039)

vtc/elections/show/0.6, vtc/elections/list/0.5 and
vtc/elections/tickets/issue/0.3 defined a member party as a
`roll.memberOf` that is "neither the community's own DID nor one of its
groups". Once a group is deleted its DID is no longer one of the
community's groups, so read literally the definition let the election
fall onto the member-party presentation path, where a holder of an
unexpired credential the deleted group issued could read it.
VTI-VOT-029 forbids exactly that: such an election is shown, and
confirmed to exist, only to a holder of `vtc.elections.manage`, and
the deleted group's identifier is never treated as a party outside
the community.

The member-party test is now decided by what `roll.memberOf` was when
the election was created; show item 1 and list item 1 say a deleted
group's election is seen only by a manager; show item 8.3 says a
presentation of the group's credential shows it to nobody. The
payload descriptions of show and list say the same.

Description and prose only: every schema is otherwise unchanged, as
CONTRIBUTING-SPECS "Version rules" allows in place for a released
draft version.

title: feat(nnm): invite a community or network
body:
The VTN side of inviting a community.

- `nnm invite <did> [--kind community|network] [--label …] [--console <vtc url>] [profile args]`:
  - lists the party (`vtn/listings/create`), unless it is listed already;
  - then prints the invitation for its administrator: the network URL, the network DID, the roles it must assign a group to, and how to accept.
- **How to accept:**
  - A community accepts in its operator console (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2458), or with `cnm networks join`. With `--console` (default: `--url`, or the URL on its entry), the invitation is a direct link: `<console>/admin/networks?join=<network url>&network=<network DID>`.
  - A network accepts with `nnm memberships join <url>`.
- Accepting is the existing exchange, unchanged:
  1. the community's `vtc/networks/join` verifies the network's listing credential;
  2. it registers its groups and signs the acknowledgement;
  3. it verifies the membership grant the network issues back.

Tests:
- `nnm-cli` `invite_tests`: the link encoding, and the invitation's roles and accept line.

title: fix(dart): keep trust_tasks' CHANGELOG.md under pub.dev's 256 KiB limit (#1042)
body:
fix(dart): keep trust_tasks' CHANGELOG.md under pub.dev's 256 KiB limit (#1042)

pub.dev refuses an upload whose CHANGELOG.md exceeds 262144 bytes. trust-tasks-dart's had reached 303894, so every trust_tasks publish from 0.9.11 to 0.9.23 failed and pub.dev stayed at 0.9.10. The tag-dart checks for trust_tasks_didcomm and trust_tasks_https then failed against that old release, and the failed publish held back the Release PR for every language.

Entries for 0.8.29 and earlier move to CHANGELOG-archive.md, which .pubignore keeps out of the package; CHANGELOG.md keeps the 0.9.x entries (79 KB) and points to the archive. A new Dart CI job fails any Dart package's CHANGELOG.md over 230000 bytes, before a publish can.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(web): redesign the VTN landing page
body:
A cleaner landing page. Only `vtn-service/web/index.html` changes. Every element id and every behaviour the script relies on is kept: the sign-in flow, sign-out, directory, graph, filters and copy buttons. Still no external assets; the icons are inline SVG data URIs, which the CSP already allows (`img-src 'self' data:`).

- **Top bar:** a small "Verifiable Trust Network" mark, with the signed-in state as an account chip on the right (a green dot, the approver truncated with the full DID on hover, "Sign out").
- **Header card:** name, description, then owner, governance and DID as chips. The DID is truncated with its full value on hover, and Copy still copies all of it.
- **Stats:** one compact segmented row instead of four large cards, 2×2 on phones, muted when every count is 0.
- **Members-only notice:** a lock icon, a short heading and line, and a primary "Sign in with a wallet" button.
- **Wallet sign-in:** two columns on wide screens, the QR in a white padded frame beside three numbered steps (scan, approve, enter the number). The match number is in a highlighted box, the status has a spinner while waiting (static under `prefers-reduced-motion`), and the actions row is Open in wallet / Copy link / Cancel. The raw link is under "Show the link". One column on phones.
- **Directory:** search with an icon; filters as pill segmented controls that wrap; entries as rows in one card, with kind and state badges. Not-acknowledged rows get a warn-coloured edge. The empty state has an icon.
- **Graph and footer:** the graph panel and legend restyled; the footer smaller and muted.
- Dark mode uses the same token approach (`:root` plus `prefers-color-scheme`), extended with `--border-strong`, `--faint`, `--accent-hover` and `--on-accent`.

Checked in headless Chrome against stubbed responses, at 1280px and at 390px (in an iframe, since a headless window won't go narrower than about 500px): signed-in directory, members-only sign-in with the match number, no horizontal scroll on phones. `node --check` passes on the script; fmt, clippy and `cargo test --workspace` pass.

title: fix(web): signed-in bar layout, and a sign-out that ends the delegation
body:
After a wallet sign-in, the "Signed in as …" bar overlapped the header's DID line. Its `margin-top: -10px` pulled it up into the header, and the approver's DID, shown bold in proportional type, ran across it.

- The bar sits below the header (`margin-top: 14px`) as a bordered strip, in the page's own tokens, so it works in dark mode too.
- An approver with no display name is shown as a DID in the page's mono `.did` style, which wraps anywhere. A display name stays bold.

**Sign-out.** "Sign out" only dropped the key from IndexedDB, without waiting for the delete to commit before reloading, so it could come back signed in. The network also kept the key's delegation until it ran out.

- The network answers `auth/revoke-session/0.2` `{ all: true }` (or `subject` naming the key), signed by the browser key itself. A delegation never covers `auth/*`, so this is the key acting for itself. It drops the key's delegation and answers `revokedCount` 1, or 0 when there is none. `all: false` is refused as malformed, as the task says.
- "Sign out" sends that, then forgets the key, waiting for the IndexedDB write to commit before reloading. Storing the key after sign-in waits for its commit too.
- The test `a_wallet_approves_the_page_key_for_reads_only` now signs out at the end: the directory is closed to the key again, and a second revoke answers 0.

title: feat(rooms): check room record proofs against the author's DID document as of bodyStoredAt
body:
Room record bodies are now checked against the author's DID document as it stood at the host's `bodyStoredAt` (`SealedRecordBody`, *Which DID document*). This uses `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` 0.14, which resolves did:webvh and did:scid:vh:1 with `versionTime` (OpenVTC/vti-didcomm-js#35). #416 left `resolveDidAt` unwired because the resolver could not do this yet.

## Resolving as of a time

`resolveDidDocumentAt(did, at)` is in `@openvtc/pnm-core/did`, file `did/resolve-at.ts`:

- **did:webvh / did:scid:vh:1**: runs the same host guard as a current resolution first (`assertResolvableWebvhHost`, or `assertResolvableScidHost` for a DID URL with `src`). Then calls `resolve(did, { versionTime: at })` and returns `didDocument`.
- **No document at `at`**: answers `null` when the instant is before the DID's first entry. The library signals this with `code: "E_DID_VERSION_NOT_FOUND"`, and the match is on the code, never on the message.
- **Any other method**: answers `undefined`, which keeps today's behaviour. did:key and did:peer documents never change.
- **Memo**: `memoResolveDidDocumentAt()` answers each DID and instant once, for one render or batch. A historical lookup skips the resolver's cache and re-fetches and re-verifies the whole log.

The function is in `did`, not in `didcomm/index.ts` next to `resolveDidDocument`. The host guard lives in `did`, and `did` and `didcomm` are the same layer, which `tests/package.module-boundaries.mjs` does not let import each other.

## Verifying a record body

`verifyRecordBody` (`rooms/record-body.ts`):

- `ResolveDidAt` may now answer `null`, meaning the author had no document at that instant. That is refused as `signature`, not shown as a placeholder.
- A thrown error with `code: "E_DID_VERSION_NOT_FOUND"` is treated the same way, so another `resolveDidAt` implementation gets the same result.
- A proof that fails against the document as of `bodyStoredAt` is refused, as before.
- The placeholder (`authorUnverifiable`) now applies only when `bodyStoredAt` is absent or the method keeps no history.
- The contract comments are updated to match.

## Callers

- **File engine** (`getRoomFile`): passes `resolveDidAt` with get/0.3's `bodyStoredAt`. The new optional `RoomFileContext.resolveDidAt` lets a caller share one memo across files.
- **Offscreen room-page bridge** (`readView`): passes `resolveDidAt`. Its fourth parameter is now `{ resolveDid?, resolveDidAt? }`, replacing a bare `resolveDid`.
- **Console records pane** (`rooms-records.tsx`): one `memoResolveDidDocumentAt()` per listing, shared by every read in it.

## Tests

- `core/tests/did.resolve-at.mjs` (new):
  - webvh, scid DID URL and bare scid resolve with `versionTime`;
  - did:key, did:peer and did:web answer `undefined` without resolving anything;
  - the host guard refuses before any resolve;
  - the library's `DidVersionNotFoundError` gives `null`, matched on the code (an error with the same words but no code is rethrown);
  - a resolution with no document throws;
  - the memo is hit once per DID and instant, a new memo asks again, and a failure is kept for the batch.
- `core/tests/rooms.record-body.mjs`: an author history (created, then rotated) through `memoResolveDidDocumentAt` with the library's error class:
  - a proof made before the rotation verifies as of its `bodyStoredAt` and is refused when stored after it;
  - a proof made with a key not yet active at T is refused, even though the current document lists that key;
  - a T before the DID's creation is refused without consulting the current document, whether `null` is returned or the coded error is thrown; the same words without the code give the placeholder;
  - three records by one author at one T cost one resolution.
- `extension/tests/room-page.test.mts`: `readView` checks against the document as of `bodyStoredAt` and refuses a `null` history.

The tests inject the resolver at `resolveDidDocumentAt`'s `resolve` seam. They do not build signed webvh logs; the library's own tests cover log verification with `versionTime`.

Local results (Node 24, `npm ci` in a fresh worktree):

- `npm run lint`: clean
- `npm run build`: clean
- `npm test`: tsp-js 123/123, core 1260/1260, extension 1502/1502, demo-rp 6/6, reviewer-demo 9/9
- `node packages/extension/scripts/check-task-versions.mjs`: OK, 444 task URIs at their pinned versions
- Every other CI `verify` step run locally (single-bundle worker and console, content script, confinement checks, no rooms task in page-reachable bundles, Web Store zip): pass

Raises `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` to `^0.14.0`. The lockfile changes only that package.

title: feat(extension): page bridge errors carry a machine-readable code
body:
## What

Every `window.vtaWallet.*` rejection — `elections`, `rooms` (including `rooms.getFile` / `rooms.putFile`), `directory`, `git` and the top-level methods — is now an `Error` named `VtaWalletError` with the existing human `message` **unchanged** and a stable, machine-readable `code`. Portals (VTI #2447's `refusalKind` / `declinedInWallet`) can switch on `code` instead of matching message text (R3.7).

Contract: [`docs/page-bridge-errors.md`](docs/page-bridge-errors.md) (linked from the README). Source: `packages/extension/src/page-error.ts`.

## Where a code comes from

1. **Trust Task error code** of the refusing community / room host / member's agent, by its local part: `vtc/elections/show:electionUnknown` → `electionUnknown`; standard codes (`indeterminate`, `permissionDenied`) as they are. The election refusals the wallet rewrites into words keep the community's code.
2. **Wallet code** (`WALLET_ERROR_CODES`): `invalidCall`, `originNotPermitted`, `notConnected`, `walletLocked`, `hostPermissionRequired`, `identityUnknown`, `identityAmbiguous`, `declined`, `notShared`, `offerNotListed`, `offerInProgress`, `membershipNotHeld`, `credentialNotHeld`, `disclosureExceeded`, `rollChanged`, `timedOut`, `unreachable`, `walletUnavailable`, `unclassified`.
3. **Rooms work code** (`ROOMS_WORK_CODES`, from pnm-core's `RoomOfferErrorCode` / `RoomFileError`) for offer acceptance and file transfers.

`takeTickets`' per-election `failed` entries carry `code` too. `vote` is unchanged: whatever the member did in the ballot window, the page hears `{ ticketTaken: false }`, and a cast's failure never reaches the page.

## How

- The offscreen document answers every page channel with `pageFailure(e)`, which reads the code off the error (refusal classes, `OobRefusedError`, `CastRefusedError`, `VtaClientError.details.code`, `e.client.timeout` / `network`, `WalletLockedError`) while its class is still known — never off the message.
- Each gate (`elections-page.ts`, `room-page-background.ts`, `directory-page.ts`, `git-page.ts`) names the code of every refusal it raises; its refusal class now extends `PageRefusal` and requires one.
- The background, the content script and the page-world provider forward a code only when it is a single camelCase name (`/^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,63}$/`), else `unclassified`, so nothing but a fixed name can reach the page — no credential, no choice, no persona detail (VTI-NTF-063, VTI-VOT-090).
- Room offers' internal codes `noOffer` / `busy` are renamed `offerNotListed` / `offerInProgress`; `declined` keeps its name and is now the code for every "the member said no in the wallet".

## On `declined`

`declined` was chosen to match the room offers' existing name and the parallel VTI portal PR (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2456). It is the one wallet code that shares a name with a pinned extended code (`auth/oob/redeem:declined`, `vetting/request:declined`); both mean "refused to go on with the request" and neither answers on a page channel. Documented in the contract. Every other wallet code was checked against all 741 local error codes declared by the task bundles VTI pins: no collision. A test holds the wallet codes disjoint from the §8.3 standard codes.

## Tests

- `tests/page-error.test.mts` — code extraction per error class, sanitising, doc tables == `WALLET_ERROR_CODES` / `ROOMS_WORK_CODES`, disjointness from standard codes.
- `tests/page-error-bridge.test.mts` — content script + provider in one happy-dom window: `VtaWalletError` shape on every channel, unclassified for missing/non-name codes, `walletUnavailable` when the worker does not answer, room-file `failed` and closed-port codes.
- Gate tests (elections, rooms, directory, git) and offscreen elections tests assert the code of each refusal path.

`npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (all workspaces) and `check-task-versions.mjs` pass locally, as do the CI bundle assertions.

## Follow-up

VTI #2447's portal matcher can switch to `e.code` (`electionUnknown`, `indeterminate`, `declined`) and drop the message matching; the wallet and the portal cut over together.

title: feat(rooms): members' names in a room (memberProfile) — read, shown and written
body:
Implements members' names in a room (trust-tasks-tf #1035, `rooms/_shared/0.3/member-profile`), reader and writer, against VTI #2457. Covers `rooms/watch` / `rooms/changed` (trust-tasks-tf #1036) too: they are not wired, for the reasons given below.

## Reading (`@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms`)

New module `rooms/member-name.ts`; `assembleRoomRecords` applies its rules.

- A `memberProfile` record is never shown as a note, message or reaction, and is never counted. A reply to one, or a reaction on one, finds no target.
- An author's name comes from the version of their own name record that the host stored most recently, by `bodyStoredAt`, else `updatedAt`. It gives no name when that version:
  - is empty or white space,
  - has been retracted,
  - was refused (signature, or the wrong shape for a name).
- A version written by anyone but the record's original author names nobody. The original author is taken from the held version, else from `createdBy`.
- A name applies only to its author, and only in that room. `names` is returned per `assembleRoomRecords` call, which covers one room.
- The shape follows `MemberProfileRecord` / `MemberProfileCleartext`:
  - kind and title;
  - `writtenAt` and `editedAt` at most;
  - no `body` on the sealed tiers, and an empty one on an open room;
  - a `MemberName` of one line, no control characters, and at most 64 code points both as written and after NFC.

## Showing (records pane)

- Each author is shown by, in order:
  1. the member's own contact petname (`persona/contact/list/1.1`, read across the console's contexts);
  2. the author's name in this room, in quotes, labelled as their own claim and never beside a check mark;
  3. the agent name or shortened DID, as before.
- A DID fingerprint is shown when two authors' names match after NFC and case folding. The same applies when a room name equals a petname held for a different DID.
- Names appear on record authors, on reply quotes ("In reply to Venue by “Alice”") and on who reacted.
- The signature line names the DID rather than a claimed name.

## Writing

- **Set my name in this room** reads the room's profile through the member's agent. If `recordMembers` does not list both `kind` and `memberProfile`, it says so and offers no save.
- The write is a new `name` open on the room-files port, run by the offscreen document as the member (`writeMemberNameAsMember`). It reads the profile again and refuses before anything is sealed or sent.
- **Sealed tiers:** the body is `kind` + `title`, signed and sealed by the agent as the member.
- **Open rooms:** the write is the cleartext of `rooms/records/put/0.5` with an empty body.
- The member's own name record is written over (`expectedVersion` = the version read), never doubled. An empty name withdraws it.
- `writtenAt` and `editedAt` are written only where the profile lists them.

## Pins

| Task | From | To | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rooms/keys/seal` | 0.2 | 0.3 | 0.3 is the version that seals a body carrying `kind` |
| `rooms/records/put` | 0.4 | 0.5 | 0.5's cleartext carries `kind`; 0.5 is 0.4 plus those members |

- Every seal and put moves with these pins. The VTA serves seal/0.3, and both room-host and the VTC serve put/0.5.
- `RecordReference` now aliases the generated type.
- `task-surface.json` is resynced from vta-sdk 0.82.0 (VTI `origin/main`).

## `rooms/watch` / `rooms/changed`: not wired

- **No address to receive a signal.** `rooms/changed` goes to a watch `address` whose DID document advertises a transport the host speaks. The wallet's mediator sessions are:
  - the holder's `did:key`, which has no service,
  - the approver,
  - the onboarding ephemeral.

  A persona's keys, `keyAgreement` included, live only at the VTA. So nothing could deliver to the wallet, and a host would answer `rooms/watch:addressUnreachable`. This is the same gap already recorded for notification deposit.
- **The watch request would be signed by the wallet's key.** `rooms/keys/act/0.11` does not relay `rooms/watch`, so the client presents through `rooms/keys/present` and signs with its own key, as `pnm rooms watch` does. On a member's path here that would make the host take the wallet's key as the member.
- **What is missing:** a watch address the VTA holds for its member, plus a way for the VTA to pass the signal to the wallet. The VTA already accepts `rooms/changed` to its own DID, logs it and keeps nothing.
- **Effect here:** listing stays on demand. No watch or changed version is pinned. CLAUDE.md records this.

## Tests

- `packages/core/tests/rooms.member-name.mjs`:
  - each reader rule (1–4), plus a deciding version that is refused;
  - shape refusals;
  - display order, collisions, petname collisions and inert text;
  - the writer's gate: refused with nothing sealed or sent; a bad name refused before any read;
  - the sealed body, the open cleartext at put/0.5, and writing over the member's own record.
- `packages/extension/tests/rooms-records.render.test.mts`:
  - the name record is hidden;
  - the author is shown by name in quotes;
  - the reply quote names the author;
  - a petname comes first;
  - colliding names get fingerprints;
  - the gate message;
  - the editor is offered where the profile permits.

Run locally: `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (all workspaces green), `node packages/extension/scripts/check-task-versions.mjs`, and every CI bundle assertion plus the Web Store package and upload checks.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new fetch. Profile, contact and record calls go through the existing senders.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): nothing local is written. A name write is create-only, or replaces the version read.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): the only retry is the existing bounded re-seal in `writeSealedAsMember`.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): none added.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound is untouched.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): generated types from the pinned bundles. The new bridge message is internal.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): a profile that is absent or unreadable permits no name.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): a room name is never shown as verified, and the check mark stays on the DID's signature.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a lost reply leaves at most the record written; the next write finds it and replaces it.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: feat(rooms): members' names in a room (memberProfile) — read, shown and written (#418)
body:
feat(rooms): members' names in a room (memberProfile) — read, shown and written (#418)

A room's author is a per-room persona DID; trust-tasks-tf #1035
(rooms/_shared/0.3/member-profile) lets a member name themselves in a room
with a record of kind `memberProfile` whose `title` is the name.

Reading (`@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms`, `member-name.ts` and
`assembleRoomRecords`): a name record is never a note, a message or a
reaction and counts in nothing; a reply to it or a reaction on it finds no
target. Each author's name is the one the version of their own name record
the host stored most recently gives (bodyStoredAt, else updatedAt) — none
where it is empty or white space, retracted, refused or the wrong shape —
and a version written by anyone but the record's author names nobody. A
name applies to its author, in that room only.

Showing (records pane): the member's own contact petname first
(`persona/contact/list/1.1`, every context), then the author's name in this
room, in quotes and never beside a check mark, then the DID. Two authors
whose names match after NFC and case folding, or a room name equal to a
petname for another DID, carry a fingerprint of the DID. Names are shown on
authors, on reply quotes and on who reacted. The signature line names the
DID, not the claimed name.

Writing: "Set my name in this room" in the records pane, a `name` open on
the room-files port, run by the offscreen document as the member
(`writeMemberNameAsMember`). It reads the room's profile through the
member's agent and refuses before anything is sealed or sent unless
`recordMembers` lists both `kind` and `memberProfile`; the pane says so
when the control opens. A sealed tier's body is kind and title, signed and
sealed by the agent as the member; an open room's is the cleartext of
rooms/records/put/0.5 with an empty body. The member's own name record is
written over, never doubled; an empty name withdraws it.

Pins: rooms/keys/seal 0.2 -> 0.3 (the version that seals a body carrying
`kind`) and rooms/records/put 0.4 -> 0.5 (the version whose cleartext
carries it); every seal and put moves with them. `RecordReference` is now
the generated type. task-surface.json resynced from vta-sdk 0.82.0.

rooms/watch and rooms/changed (trust-tasks-tf #1036) are not wired: the
wallet holds no DID a host could send rooms/changed to (its sessions are the
holder's did:key, the approver and the onboarding ephemeral), and the watch
request is signed by the client's own key, which a member's path here must
not do. Recorded in CLAUDE.md beside the notification-deposit gap.

title: feat(portal): put notified elections on the home page; read the wallet's error codes first
body:
Follows #2447.

The home page's *Needs your attention* read only the community's own election list, so an election the member was notified of (VTI-NTF-063) — such as one put to a member party's members (VTI-VOT-015) — never appeared there.

**Home page**
- `actionableNotified` (`home-status.ts`) keeps the notified elections the community does not list (deduplicated through `notifiedOnly`), whose notice still stands (a withdrawn one cannot be opened, VTI-NTF-024) and whose voting period, where the notice states one, has not closed.
- They come from the same `member-elections` query key as the Elections page, are named by identifier only (the page knows nothing else of them), are counted on the Elections tile ("N you were told about"), and are linked with `electionHref` — so the election page still takes `memberOf` from the standing notice in the shared list, never from the link.

**Refusal detection**
- `refusalKind` and `declinedInWallet` read the `code` on the wallet's page-facing error first (the companion plugin PR, OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin `feat/page-error-codes`, adds it):
  - `REFUSAL_BY_CODE`: the Trust Task codes `electionUnknown`, `indeterminate`.
  - `WALLET_OUTCOME_BY_CODE`: the wallet's own codes for what the member decided in its window. The wallet's names are not settled yet; `declined` is assumed for now, the name the wallet's room offers already use. A new one is a row in this table.
- An error with no code, or with one neither table knows, is read by its words as before, so older wallets keep working.

**Tests**: vitest for the home-page attention/status (standing, withdrawn, closed, undated, dedupe against the list, no audience in the item, link = `electionHref`) and for code-first detection (code beats words, wallet-local vs community codes, fallback for no/unknown code, prototype keys, rendered refusal and decline).

**Docs**: `docs/03-vtc/elections.md`, `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md`, `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md` (*Elections in the portal*).

Checked locally: `npm run lint`, `npx vitest run` (1529 passed), `npm run build`, `npm run build:members`.

title: feat(did-webvh): resolve a did:webvh as of a versionTime (#35)
body:
feat(did-webvh): resolve a did:webvh as of a versionTime (#35)

`resolve(did, { versionTime })` (the resolver, `didWebvh.resolve`,
`didWebvh.resolveLog`, and did:scid:vh:1 through its log) returns the
document of the last log entry whose `versionTime` is at or before the
instant, per did:webvh v1.0. The whole log is verified first exactly as a
current resolution verifies it — SCID, hash chain, every entry's proof
under the update keys in force, pre-rotation and witness thresholds — and
only then is the entry chosen.

An instant before the DID's first entry throws `DidVersionNotFoundError`
(`code: "E_DID_VERSION_NOT_FOUND"`), so a caller can tell "the DID did not
exist then" from "the DID does not resolve".

didwebvh-ts 2.8's own `versionTime` selector is not used: it compares
strictly, so an instant equal to an entry's `versionTime` selects nothing,
and once it has selected an entry it swallows any later failure in the
walk, which also skips the witness checks that run after it.

A resolution with `versionTime` bypasses the resolver cache in both
directions, and neither advances nor is checked against a did:scid source
book: an earlier version is the right answer as of its own time, not a
stale mirror.

title: feat(rooms)!: members' names in a room (memberProfile), and rooms/watch with its rooms/changed signal on both hosts
body:
Implements two rooms specifications from trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf:

- **#1035** (6e643738), `rooms/_shared/0.3/member-profile.schema.json`: a member's name in a room.
- **#1036** (35bd1510), `rooms/watch/0.1` and `rooms/changed/0.1`: one content-free signal when a room moves. Both are pinned in `vti-specs-rooms` with `trust-tasks add` from the deployed registry.

## Members' names (`memberProfile`)

- `vti_rooms::member_profile` holds the writer and reader rules:
  - `MemberName`: one line, no control characters, at most 64 code points after NFC. An empty name, or one that is only white space, withdraws it.
  - The `MemberProfileRecord` and `MemberProfileCleartext` shapes.
  - `Names`: for each author, the name from the version the host stored most recently, by `bodyStoredAt` and else `updatedAt`. A rewrite by anyone other than the original author names nobody.
- `record_members::used` returns `memberProfile` for a body of that kind, so the writer's rule now requires `kind` **and** `memberProfile` in the profile's `recordMembers`. The SDK's copy (`RECORD_KIND_VALUES`, `MEMBER_PROFILE_KIND`) is held equal to `vti-rooms` by the existing pin test.
- No changes to hosts, `seal` or `act`. The schema says a key holder seals the body unchanged, and `seal/0.3` already accepts it. Profile reads and writes already accept any `recordMembers` value matching the pattern, so `pnm rooms profile set --record-members …,memberProfile` works as it is; only its help text changes.
- `pnm rooms name set <NAME>` and `pnm rooms name clear` write the record:
  - sealed tiers: `seal/0.3` + `act/0.11`;
  - open rooms: `put/0.5` cleartext with an empty `body`.
  - If the member already holds a name record, the command writes a new version of it. Otherwise it creates one, create-only, so a retry still leaves a single record. On sealed tiers, finding the existing record means opening the member's records through the VTA.
- `pnm rooms list`, `get` and `read` never show a name record as a note. They show a name beside its author's DID as "calls themselves …".

## Watch and changed

- `vti_rooms::watch` is the host-neutral half that both `room-host` and the VTC call.
- **Authorization:** exactly as a listing (`read`). It also returns the task's own `chainTooDeep` and `subjectBindingMissing` codes.
- **State:**
  - one watch per room and address, in a new `room_watches` keyspace;
  - host state only: never consulted for authorization, and excluded from VTC backup;
  - `addressUnreachable` when the address has no transport the host speaks.
  - `limitReached` past 1024 watches per room or 16 per member.
- **Lease:** 7 days by default, 30 days at most. It never runs past the first credential in the presentation lapsing (new `VerifiedChain::valid_until`).
- **Repeats and cancels:** repeating the same arming request returns the same answer. Cancelling a watch the host does not hold returns `armed: false`.
- **Firing:**
  - After any successful room task, both hosts check the room's watches. That covers put, curate, prune, profile write, a mirror pull on room-host, and the arming itself.
  - A watch past its watermark is removed under one lock and signalled once, after a randomised 2–6 s delay. The signal carries only the room and its latest version.
  - A watch whose presentation the held revocation list withdraws never fires.
- **Transport:**
  - `room-host` sends over its mediator session (TSP, then DIDComm, chosen by service type).
  - The VTC sends through the new `PeerTasks::send_one_way`, signed as the community.
  - Neither host falls back to REST or retries a signal.
- **Member side:**
  - `VtcClient::{watch, cancel_watch}` and `pnm rooms watch --room … --host … --host-did … --address <DID> [--since N] [--lease 7d] [--cancel]`.
  - The request is presented for the client and signed by it, as `prune` is: `rooms/keys/act/0.11`'s closed table does not list `rooms/watch`.
- **VTA as the address:** a VTA accepts `rooms/changed/0.1` from a sender with no ACL entry (a counterparty task), logs it at `debug` and returns nothing. No consumer on the VTA reads a room in response yet.
- **Registrations:** `retry_safety` (`rooms/changed/0.1`: `ReadOnly`), VTA conformance witness, vta-mcp verb census, `ROOMS_DISPATCHED_URIS` and the vti-rooms registry check.

## Breaking

`vti_rooms::authz::VerifiedChain` gains a public field, `valid_until`.

## Tests

- `vti-rooms`: `member_profile` and the record-members rule; `watch` covers fire-once, already-past, no watermark, cancel, lease bound, unreachable address and the declared codes.
- `room-host` and `vtc-service`: end to end, one signal per arming after two puts.
- `vta-cli-common`: how a name is shown.

title: feat(service): deliver broadcasts to communities as vtc/networks/deliver
body:
Builds on the published VTI release from OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2448: `vti-specs-vtc` 0.6, `vti-vtn` 0.5, `vti-common` 0.58, `vta-sdk` 0.82, `vti-trust-task-server` 0.4, `vti-oob-server` 0.3 and `vti-secrets` 0.31.

A network now delivers a broadcast to a member community's group as a Trust Task, `vtc/networks/deliver/0.1`, instead of posting a bare `{ envelope }` to its inbox. This closes A15's "until `vtc/networks` 0.2". The specs are trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1033.

- **`broadcast.rs`:**
  - A community's group gets `vtc/networks/deliver`, signed by this network, at the endpoint it registered (now its `/v1/trust-tasks`). The role is the one the envelope's last hop names.
  - The answer must carry the community's valid proof (`vti-vtn` verifies every answer).
  - `delivered` and `duplicate` map to receipts. A refusal below 500 is final, and anything else is queued for retry, as before.
  - Member networks still get `vtn/relay/deliver`.
- **New dependency:** `vti-specs-vtc`, for the `vtc/networks/deliver` types.
- **Docs:** A15 now describes both deliveries, and notes that a group registered under `vtc/networks` 0.1 named a REST inbox that no longer exists and must be registered again. The README and step 5 of `trust-tasks.md` are updated.
- **Tests:** the cascade tests' community inboxes are now Trust Task endpoints. Each checks it was sent `vtc/networks/deliver` for `admins`, records the envelope, and answers a `#response` signed by the community; the refusing inbox answers a `trust-task-error`. The nested broadcast and retry-queue tests pass through them. fmt and clippy are clean, and all 24 tests pass against the #2450 branch.

title: vtc-service-v0.23.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Hosts serve put/0.5, list/0.6 and get/0.3 and record createdAt, createdBy, bodyStoredAt ([#2451](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2451))

Stage 2 of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1027, the room host side, on room-host and
  the VTC's community room host.

  - Serve rooms/records/put/0.5 beside 0.3 and 0.4. An open room's cleartext may carry
    kind, inReplyTo, writtenAt and editedAt, and its file width, height and preview; each
    is held to its schema (vti_rooms::record_members::check) and stored as received
    (Host item 14).
  - Record the host's createdAt and createdBy (first version only, never moved; createdBy
    on open and attributed only) and bodyStoredAt (every put, never a curation) on every
    put version (Host items 16-17). Rows stored earlier read with all three absent.
  - Serve rooms/records/list/0.6 (RecordMetadataV3: kind on open only, absent on a
    tombstone) and rooms/records/get/0.3 beside list/0.5 and get/0.2. None of the new
    get/0.3 members is committed; the leaf is unchanged.
  - Host item 15 (a MAY): on an open room, refuse with permissionDenied a new version of
    a message or reaction by anyone but its original author. On by default; off with
    room-host --allow-rewrites-by-others or the VTC's [rooms] refuse_rewrites_by_others.
  - vtc-client asks get/0.3 and list/0.6 and falls back on unsupportedType; a mirror
    keeps its primary's record times.

- **vtc**: Vtc/networks 0.2, and broadcasts as vtc/networks/deliver ([#2450](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2450))

A community pins vtc/networks/* 0.2 (a registration is the signed
  vtn/groups/register request; a group's endpoint is the community's Trust
  Task endpoint) and takes a network's broadcasts as
  vtc/networks/deliver/0.1 at /v1/trust-tasks, signed by the delivering
  network, instead of the REST route /v1/networks/relay/{group_id}.

- **rooms**: Record kinds, replies and image previews at the VTA — serve rooms/keys/seal/0.3 and act/0.11, carry recordMembers ([#2449](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2449))

The first stage of trust-tasks-tf #1027: a record says what it is to a
  reader (kind), what it answers (inReplyTo), when it was written and edited
  (writtenAt, editedAt), and a file can carry an image's width, height and
  preview. A room's profile lists which of these its writers may use
  (RoomProfile.recordMembers).

  Pinned in vti-specs-rooms beside the versions already pinned:
  rooms/keys/seal/0.3, rooms/keys/act/0.11, rooms/records/put/0.5,
  rooms/records/list/0.6, rooms/records/get/0.3, rooms/keys/browse/0.4 and
  rooms/keys/read/0.2. Every bundle referencing rooms/_shared was re-vendored:
  #1027 changed SealedRecordBody, RoomProfile and FileManifest in place.



### Fixed

- **rooms**: A member removed from a room can be admitted again ([#2441](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2441))

* fix(rooms): a member removed from a room can be admitted again

  Group state with a removal recorded is a prior membership, not a join
  (rooms/keys/welcome/0.1, rooms/keys/open/0.2; trust-tasks-tf #1031).
  `join` refused every Welcome once group state existed, and a removal
  keeps the group state, so a re-admitted member's VTA refused the new
  Welcome and nothing sealed after the removal ever opened for it.

  `join` now accepts a Welcome when a removal is recorded: the ended group,
  its join epoch and its removal epoch move into a `room-prior` list, the new
  group becomes current, its join epoch is kept in `room-joined`, and the
  removal row is cleared, in one conditional batch. `alreadyJoined` stays
  for current state with no removal.

  Opening goes by the record's epoch: at or above the current join epoch,
  the current group; within a prior membership's [join, removal), that
  membership's group and links; between a removal and the next join,
  `removed` with that removal's epoch; below the first join, `beyondChain`.
  This holds for open_record (and so keys/open, read, browse and act's
  opens), file-key, and the profile location and walk. A member removed and
  not yet re-admitted has no current epoch: sealing, file-key-to-seal and a
  profile write answer noGroup, and act answers notAMember.

  `forget` discards prior memberships and the join epoch; the epoch floor
  drops a prior membership wholly below it and the rest's rungs at or below
  it (rooms/epoch/prune/0.2). The welcome handler's spent-invitation check
  answers alreadyJoined only for a current membership.

    get/0.3 members is committed; the leaf is unchanged.

    a message or reaction by anyone but its original author. On by default; off with
    room-host --allow-rewrites-by-others or the VTC's [rooms] refuse_rewrites_by_others.

    keeps its primary's record times.

- **rooms**: Record kinds, replies and image previews at the VTA — serve rooms/keys/seal/0.3 and act/0.11, carry recordMembers ([#2449](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2449))

The first stage of trust-tasks-tf #1027: a record says what it is to a
  reader (kind), what it answers (inReplyTo), when it was written and edited
  (writtenAt, editedAt), and a file can carry an image's width, height and
  preview. A room's profile lists which of these its writers may use
  (RoomProfile.recordMembers).

  Pinned in vti-specs-rooms beside the versions already pinned:
  rooms/keys/seal/0.3, rooms/keys/act/0.11, rooms/records/put/0.5,
  rooms/records/list/0.6, rooms/records/get/0.3, rooms/keys/browse/0.4 and
  rooms/keys/read/0.2. Every bundle referencing rooms/_shared was re-vendored:
  #1027 changed SealedRecordBody, RoomProfile and FileManifest in place.

- **rooms**: A member removed from a room can be admitted again ([#2441](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2441))

* fix(rooms): a member removed from a room can be admitted again

  Group state with a removal recorded is a prior membership, not a join
  (rooms/keys/welcome/0.1, rooms/keys/open/0.2; trust-tasks-tf #1031).
  `join` refused every Welcome once group state existed, and a removal
  keeps the group state, so a re-admitted member's VTA refused the new
  Welcome and nothing sealed after the removal ever opened for it.

  `join` now accepts a Welcome when a removal is recorded: the ended group,
  its join epoch and its removal epoch move into a `room-prior` list, the new
  group becomes current, its join epoch is kept in `room-joined`, and the
  removal row is cleared, in one conditional batch. `alreadyJoined` stays
  for current state with no removal.

  the current group; within a prior membership's [join, removal), that
  membership's group and links; between a removal and the next join,

  opens), file-key, and the profile location and walk. A member removed and
  not yet re-admitted has no current epoch: sealing, file-key-to-seal and a
  profile write answer noGroup, and act answers notAMember.

  drops a prior membership wholly below it and the rest's rungs at or below
  it (rooms/epoch/prune/0.2). The welcome handler's spent-invitation check
  answers alreadyJoined only for a current membership.

title: feat(elections): read a deleted board's election tombstone (VTI-BRD-009) (#2455)
body:
feat(elections): read a deleted board's election tombstone (VTI-BRD-009) (#2455)

A deleted board's elections each keep a tombstone (VTI-BRD-007/008),
but nothing served it, so no voter could check a receipt against the
community's kept heads once the board was gone (VTI-VOT-053).

`vtc/elections/tombstones/show/0.1`: an active member or a holder of
vtc.elections.manage reads it — identifier, manifest digest, ballot
box, each kept board head with the ballot box's signed
voting/board/head document as received, deletedAt and removeAt. The
tombstone is looked up only for such a reader; no tombstone, an
unreadable one and a removed one are all `electionUnknown`. Nothing the
board held is carried.

- vtc-client: `elections_tombstone`; cnm: `elections tombstone <id>`.
- Pins vtc/elections/tombstones/show/0.1.
- docs/03-vtc/boards.md, elections.md.

Adds VTI-BRD-009: while a VTC keeps a deleted board's election tombstone (VTI-BRD-008), it shows it to any active member and any holder of `vtc.elections.manage` — election identifier, manifest digest, ballot box, and each kept board head with the ballot box's signed document as received — so a voter can still check a receipt after the board is gone. body:
Show a deleted board's tombstones to the members they concern, so a voter can still check a receipt (VTI-BRD-009) (#101)

While a VTC keeps a tombstone (VTI-BRD-008) it shows it to any active member and any holder of vtc.elections.manage: the election's identifier, manifest digest, ballot box, and each kept board head with the ballot box's signed document as received. An unknown election and an unreadable one are answered the same way, and nothing VTI-BRD-007 forbids keeping is carried. Without it a tombstone checks nothing (VTI-VOT-053).

On by default; off with room-host --allow-rewrites-by-others or the VTC's [rooms] refuse_rewrites_by_others. - vtc-client asks get/0.3 and list/0.6 and falls back on unsupportedType; a mirror keeps its primary's record times. - **vtc**: Vtc/networks 0.2, and broadcasts as vtc/networks/deliver ([#2450](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2450)) A community pins vtc/networks/* 0.2 (a registration is the signed vtn/groups/register request; a group's endpoint is the community's Trust Task endpoint) and takes a network's broadcasts as vtc/networks/deliver/0.1 at /v1/trust-tasks, signed by the delivering network, instead of the REST route /v1/networks/relay/{group_id}. - **rooms**: Record kinds, replies and image previews at the VTA — serve rooms/keys/seal/0.3 and act/0.11, carry recordMembers ([#2449](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2449)) The first stage of trust-tasks-tf #1027: a record says what it is to a reader (kind), what it answers (inReplyTo), when it was written and edited (writtenAt, editedAt), and a file can carry an image's width, height and preview. A room's profile lists which of these its writers may use (RoomProfile.recordMembers). Pinned in vti-specs-rooms beside the versions already pinned: rooms/keys/seal/0.3, rooms/keys/act/0.11, rooms/records/put/0.5, rooms/records/list/0.6, rooms/records/get/0.3, rooms/keys/browse/0.4 and rooms/keys/read/0.2. Every bundle referencing rooms/_shared was re-vendored: #1027 changed SealedRecordBody, RoomProfile and FileManifest in place. ### Fixed - **rooms**: A member removed from a room can be admitted again ([#2441](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2441)) * fix(rooms): a member removed from a room can be admitted again Group state with a removal recorded is a prior membership, not a join (rooms/keys/welcome/0.1, rooms/keys/open/0.2; trust-tasks-tf #1031). `join` refused every Welcome once group state existed, and a removal keeps the group state, so a re-admitted member's VTA refused the new Welcome and nothing sealed after the removal ever opened for it. `join` now accepts a Welcome when a removal is recorded: the ended group, its join epoch and its removal epoch move into a `room-prior` list, the new group becomes current, its join epoch is kept in `room-joined`, and the removal row is cleared, in one conditional batch. `alreadyJoined` stays for current state with no removal. Opening goes by the record's epoch: at or above the current join epoch, the current group; within a prior membership's [join, removal), that membership's group and links; between a removal and the next join, `removed` with that removal's epoch; below the first join, `beyondChain`. This holds for open_record (and so keys/open, read, browse and act's opens), file-key, and the profile location and walk. A member removed and not yet re-admitted has no current epoch: sealing, file-key-to-seal and a profile write answer noGroup, and act answers notAMember. `forget` discards prior memberships and the join epoch; the epoch floor drops a prior membership wholly below it and the rest's rungs at or below it (rooms/epoch/prune/0.2). The welcome handler's spent-invitation check answers alreadyJoined only for a current membership.
