title: feat(portal): show notified elections and open them as the party's member
body:
## Summary

The wallet (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin #411) now answers `window.vtaWallet.elections.list` with `{ elections, notified }`, `notified` being the member's held election notifications from this community (VTI-NTF-063), and accepts `memberOf` on `show` / `takeTicket` / `vote`. The portal's Elections page still read the old shape and never passed `memberOf`, so an election put to another party's members (VTI-VOT-015) could not be opened from the portal.

- **Both wallet shapes** (`wallet-elections.ts`): `electionListOf` normalises `{ elections, notified }`, `{ elections }` and a bare array; `walletElections()` returns a wrapper whose `list` is always `{ elections, notified }`, so Home and Boards (same query key) keep working. Of a notification only `electionId`, `audience`, `status`, `votingOpensAt`, `votingClosesAt` are kept — anything else a wallet sends is dropped (NTF-063).
- **The list**: notified elections the community does not list are shown in their own section ("You were told about these"), one per election; a listed election that was also notified gets a "you were told about this" mark instead (de-duplicated). A withdrawn notice is shown without a way to open it.
- **memberOf pass-through**: the election page takes `memberOf` from the audience of a notification still standing (VTI-NTF-024) and passes it to `show`, `takeTicket` and `vote`. The wallet asks the member in its own window before presenting the credential that party issued (VTI-VOT-016, 090); the page presents nothing and sees no credential or choice. The read waits for the list so the first `show` already names the party.
- **Older wallet**: it reports no `notified`, so no `memberOf` is ever sent — a wallet before credential rolls refuses the field (`show takes no \`memberOf\``).
- **Refusals in words**: the community's `electionUnknown` (same answer whether the election does not exist, is not open to the member, or is put to a party whose membership was not shown — VTI-VOT-015/025) and `indeterminate` (a check it could not complete; nothing recorded) are explained, matching both the wallet's wording and a bare code. Declining in the wallet to show a membership is a status with "Ask my wallet again", not an error.
- Docs: `docs/03-vtc/elections.md`, `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md`, `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md` (*Elections in the portal*).

Spec: dtgwg-vti-spec 05a VTI-NTF-024, VTI-NTF-063; voting VTI-VOT-015 – 018, 025, 090.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run` — 121 files, all pass, including new tests for both wallet shapes, the NTF-063 field filter, dedupe, memberOf pass-through to show/ticket/vote (and none for a withdrawn notice or an older wallet), and the `electionUnknown` / `indeterminate` / declined wording.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:members`.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`, default and with `vetting-pcs,voting` (the bundle is embedded by `build.rs`).

No Rust changes.

title: feat(rooms): rooms/watch and rooms/changed — a content-free signal that a room has moved (#1036)
body:
feat(rooms): rooms/watch and rooms/changed — a content-free signal that a room has moved (#1036)

A member who wants to know a room has new records polls
rooms/records/list with sinceVersion. rooms/watch/0.1 lets it instead
name an address DID and the version it has read to; the host sends one
rooms/changed/0.1 to that address the first time the room moves past
it, then disarms until the member re-arms after reading.

The signal carries the room and its latest version only, the same
whatever changed, and is one-way. It reaches a sleeping device through
the address's mediator queue and the existing push/wake doorbell, so the
mediator, push gateway and platform push service learn that something
arrived and nothing of the room. One signal per arming bounds the queue
and the wake count however busy the room is.

On the sealed tiers the host never sees a record's kind, so a reaction
fires a watch as a message does. rooms/changed states how a reader
decides unread after listing: new message keys, not its own, current;
reactions, edits, curations and notes are never unread messages, and an
alert is raised only on what was found.

A watch is host state that grants nothing and does not move with the
room. On a private room the address must be used for nothing else.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(rooms): a member's name in a room, as a memberProfile record (#1035)
body:
feat(rooms): a member's name in a room, as a memberProfile record (#1035)

A room's author is a per-room persona DID, and nothing a reader may use
maps it to a name: the community directory is addressed by entry, never
by DID; a room may belong to no community; a private room's host must
not learn who its members are.

rooms/_shared/0.3/member-profile.schema.json defines a member's name as
a record the member writes into the room: kind `memberProfile`, the name
in `title` (MemberName: one line, at most 64 code points, empty
withdraws). It is an ordinary SealedRecordBody on the sealed tiers and
ordinary cleartext on an open room, so no task, host or key holder
changes. Writers may use it only once the room profile's recordMembers
lists `kind` and `memberProfile`. Readers prefer their own petname for
a DID, then the member's name in this room, then a shortened DID, and
distinguish authors whose names collide.

No released schema is edited; room.schema.json stays at 0.2.

title: feat(rooms): show room records by the #1027 reading rules
body:
## What

Implements the reader side of `SealedRecordBody` at `rooms/_shared/0.2` as dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1027 defines it (merged as 565f8d32), in the console's records pane (`manager/panes/rooms-records.tsx`) and in the record views the page bridge builds (`room-page-offscreen.ts`).

## Reading a body (`rooms/record-body.ts`)

- `verifyRecordBody` accepts `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt` and `editedAt` with the schema's shapes (lowerCamelCase kind ≤ 64; `RecordReference`; RFC 3339 UTC `Z`), and a profile's `recordMembers`. A profile record carrying any of the new members is refused, as before for the others.
- **Which DID document.** The proof is checked against the author's document as it stood at the host's `bodyStoredAt`, where the new `resolveDidAt` option can resolve it then. A proof that fails against that document is refused. Where it cannot be had (a method without history, no `bodyStoredAt`, or no such resolver), the current document is used, and a proof that fails there comes back as `RecordBodyError` with `placeholder: true` (`authorUnverifiable`). An author whose DID does not resolve is `authorUnresolvable`, also a placeholder. A placeholder shows nothing of the record.
- A `did:key` (or `did:peer` 0/2) document cannot change, so a failing proof against one is refused, not shown as a placeholder.
- A proof whose verification method belongs to a DID other than `author` is refused before anything is resolved.

## Showing a room (`rooms/record-view.ts`, new)

`assembleRoomRecords(inputs, { now })` is a pure function. It takes what reading each key produced (verified content, refusal, placeholder, tombstone, unreadable, profile), plus any earlier version the reader holds, and returns what a reader shows:

- **Kind**: `message` → message; no kind and no title → message (*Untitled records*); `note` and every unknown kind → note. Never refused for its kind. A new version that changes the kind of the version held is refused, alone.
- **Replies**: always shown. `replyTo.available: false` when the target was never written, is withdrawn, retracted, expired, refused, a placeholder or unopened. Nothing is fetched to resolve one. A target is said to be "edited since" only from `editedAt` after the reply's `writtenAt`, and never just because its version moved.
- **Nothing answers a reaction**: a record naming a reaction in `inReplyTo` is shown nowhere and counted as no reaction.
- **Reactions**: shown beside their target, never as rows. Values are NFC with U+FE0E/U+FE0F removed, at most 64 code points, one line; an empty or White_Space value withdraws. They count once per author, value and target. Only the reaction's author withdraws it: an empty version by someone else leaves the held version counting. A new version that moves a reaction to another target is refused. No reaction is shown on a target that is not available, and expired or retracted reactions count as nothing.
- **Withdrawn messages**: an empty body and no file, from the message's own author (by the version held, else the host's `createdBy`), shows as withdrawn with nothing of any version. From anyone else it is a rewrite.
- **Tombstones**: a retracted record the reader held keeps its place as "retracted". One the reader held nothing of is in no conversation and no count.
- **writtenAt**: ordering is by `writtenAt`, then key. A record without one is ordered by `createdAt`, else `updatedAt`, else the read time. A claim more than five minutes after `createdAt`/`updatedAt`/read time is implausible, and so is a rewrite that changes it: those are ordered by the host's time and their claimed time is not shown. A claim more than 24 hours before `createdAt` is ordered by `createdAt` and shown as arriving later than it claims.
- **editedAt**: shown as edited. One before `writtenAt`, or more than five minutes after `updatedAt`, is shown as edited but without a time. An edit is never inferred from `version`. A version by someone other than the record's author is shown as their rewrite.
- **validUntil**: records at or past it are left out of `records` and returned in `expired`.

## The console's records pane

- Lists with `rooms/keys/browse/0.4`, then reads every listed record in batches of 32 with `rooms/keys/read/0.2` (`roomsKeysReadMany`, new; keys answered `notAttempted` are asked again). Previously it opened the newest five and waited for clicks on the rest. Replies, reactions and conversation order need every record.
- Verifies each sealed body with the host's `bodyStoredAt`, then hands everything to `assembleRoomRecords` and draws the result. Shows "In reply to …" / "In reply to a record that is not available", reaction chips with counts, withdrawn and retracted rows, "author not verified" placeholders, "edited", the late-arrival note, rewrites by another author, and a "Show expired records" toggle. Retracted records the pane held nothing of are only counted.
- Every body is drawn as plain text, and nothing in one is a link the pane follows.
- Remembers the versions it showed across refreshes, so the rules that compare with a held version apply.
- *Edit* is offered only on a record carrying none of `kind`, `inReplyTo` and `writtenAt`. The note editor does not write them, and a rewrite must keep them.

## The page bridge

`readView` passes `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt`, `editedAt`, `createdAt` and `createdBy` through to the view, and verifies against `bodyStoredAt`. An expired record comes back as `expired: true` with nothing of its content. An unverifiable author comes back as `authorUnverified: true`, again with nothing of the content, instead of an error. Listing rows gain `createdAt`, `createdBy` and `kind`.

## Versions

The plugin moves to `rooms/keys/browse/0.4`, `rooms/keys/read/0.2`, `rooms/records/list/0.6` and `rooms/records/get/0.3`. Every request made as the member is completed by `rooms/keys/act/0.11`, a superset of 0.10's table. These replace browse/0.3, read/0.1, list/0.5, get/0.2 and act/0.10, which are unpinned. VTI serves all of them (VTI #2449, #2451, #2452). The file engine reads a record at get/0.3 and checks its body against `bodyStoredAt`. `task-surface.json` is resynced from vta-sdk 0.81.0 (VTI origin/main), and the relay-budget list names read/0.2 and browse/0.4.

There is no fallback to the older versions on `unsupportedType`. This repo's CLAUDE.md rules out compatibility folds ("the plugin and the VTA cut over together"), and CI's `check-task-versions.mjs` fails a bundle that names a version other than the pinned one.

## Tests

- `core/tests/rooms.record-view.mjs` (new, 35 tests): one or more per rule above, including NFC/VS16 normalisation, the 64-code-point and line-terminator bounds, per-author counting, withdrawal only by the author, kind and target changes refused, tombstones with and without a held version, and the five-minute, 24-hour and rewrite rules for `writtenAt` and `editedAt`.
- `core/tests/rooms.record-body.mjs`: the new members' accepted and refused shapes, `recordMembers`, and the `bodyStoredAt` cases (verifies with a rotated key against the document as of then; refused against that document; placeholder without it, or when it cannot be had; unresolvable author; did:key refused; a foreign verification method refused before resolution).
- `core/tests/rooms.reads.mjs` (new): browse/0.4, read/0.2 single and batch (32 per request, in order, sealed-at per key, a misordered answer refused, `notAttempted` retried and bounded), list/0.6 and get/0.3.
- `core/tests/rooms.file-engine.mjs`: reads at get/0.3 through act/0.11.
- `extension/tests/rooms-records.render.test.mts`: one batch read; reactions beside the target and not counted on a missing target; reply to an unavailable target; reply naming its target; withdrawn; edited; late arrival; expired hidden and shown on request. Existing tests moved to the new versions.
- `extension/tests/room-page.test.mts`: new members reach the page; expired and unverifiable-author records carry nothing of their content.

Local results (Node 24, `npm ci` in a fresh worktree):

- `npm run lint`: clean
- `npm run build`: clean
- `npm test`: tsp-js 123/123, core 1227/1227, extension 1495/1495, demo-rp 6/6, reviewer-demo 9/9
- `node packages/extension/scripts/check-task-versions.mjs`: OK, 444 task URIs at their pinned versions
- file-key confinement, no rooms task in page-reachable bundles, single-bundle background and console: pass

## Not done here

- The wallet's resolver (`@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js`) does not yet resolve did:webvh as of a time (`versionTime`). So the pane and the page bridge pass no `resolveDidAt` today. A did:webvh proof that fails against the current document is shown as the placeholder; it is never shown as valid. `resolveDidAt` is where that resolver plugs in.
- Writing `kind`, replies and reactions from the wallet (gated by the room profile's `recordMembers`).

title: feat(rooms)!: the VTA serves rooms/keys/browse/0.4 and the rooms/keys/read/0.2 batch; the SDK and pnm write kinds, replies and reactions
body:
The third and last stage of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1027 (merged as 565f8d32), after #2449 (the VTA's seal/0.3 and act/0.11, the pins) and #2451 (hosts serve put/0.5, list/0.6, get/0.3 and record `createdAt`, `createdBy`, `bodyStoredAt`). Every URI here was pinned by #2449.

## The VTA

- **Serves `rooms/keys/browse/0.4`** beside 0.3. It lists with `rooms/records/list/0.6`, asks again with list/0.5 when the host answers `unsupportedType` (only before the first page, since a cursor belongs to its version), and passes the `RecordMetadataV3` rows through exactly as served. Host failures are browse/0.4's declared `hostRefused` / `hostUnreachable`, and a principal holding nothing the room issued is `notAMember`. browse/0.3 is unchanged.
- **Serves `rooms/keys/read/0.2`** beside 0.1, in the new `trust_tasks/room_read.rs`, which now answers 0.1 too, so the two can't answer a record differently:
  - It fetches with `rooms/records/get/0.3` and passes `createdAt`, `createdBy` and `bodyStoredAt` through as served. A host that answers `unsupportedType` is asked get/0.2, and the rest of the request goes straight to get/0.2.
  - `key` is answered as 0.1 answers it, plus the host's times.
  - `keys` (1–32, unique) is answered with `results`, one entry per key in request order. Each key gets its own `rooms/records/get`, checks and verdict.
  - A key's `error` is taken from the refusal document a single read of that key would have produced: same code, same `details`. `retryable` is the value the spec declares for the code.
  - Whole-request refusals are one `trust-task-error`: `malformedRequest` (both or neither of `key`/`keys`, more than 32, a repeated key) and `notAMember`.
  - **`notAttempted`.** Keys are begun in order. A key is begun only while the answered entries are under **512 KiB** and less than **15 s** have passed. A key that was begun is always answered with its record or its own error, never `notAttempted`; every key not begun gets `notAttempted` (retryable).
  - **Repairs once per batch.** Every key is fetched and opened first. Then at most one catch-up (to the highest epoch any key needs) and one chain extension (down to the lowest) run through `room_catch_up::repair`, under its per-member lock, and the keys waiting on them are opened again.
  - `ReadResult` is closed and has no `ext`. So what a single read says in `ext` (`roomProfile`, `sealedAt`) is said once at the response level, by key: `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].roomProfile: [keys]` and `.sealedAt: {key: version}`.
  - Opening is unchanged, prior memberships (#2441) included.
- Dispatched as `[Mutating Secret true]`, the spec's `sideEffects: mutating` (a repair changes this VTA's key state). Both URIs are in `vta_sdk::trust_tasks` (`ALL_URIS`), classified `RetrySafe` in `retry_safety`, in the outbound budget list, and have conformance entries. The error-code census baseline shrinks by four: the browse 0.3 and read 0.1 codes are now witnessed through their 0.4/0.2 twins.

## The SDK (`vta-sdk`)

New in `client::rooms_records`; the old methods are kept:

- `room_browse` (browse/0.4, falls back to 0.3).
- `room_read` (read/0.2 `key`, falls back to 0.1).
- `room_read_batch` (read/0.2 `keys`). A VTA without 0.2 is read key by key with 0.1, its refusals put in the same per-key shape.
- `room_seal_as_principal_v0_3` (seal/0.3, falls back to 0.2 only for a body using none of the governed members).
- `room_act_v0_11` and `unsigned_room_request_v0_11`.
- **The writer gate.** `room_check_record_members(room, host, member, body)` reads the room's profile only when the body uses a governed member, and refuses with the new typed `VtaError::RecordMembersNotPermitted { room_id, refused, listed, unresolved }`. It has a `suggested_fix`. `VtaError` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new variant is additive.
  - `room_record_members` caches per (room, host, member) for the room's current epoch, which it reads from `rooms/keys/list`. An `open` room has no epoch, so it is read every time.
- `room_read_batch` waits 60 s: the VTA's 15 s budget, plus the key in hand and one repair.

## The CLI (`pnm rooms`)

- `put --kind K`, `put --reply-to KEY[@VERSION]`, and `put KEY --react VALUE --to KEY[@VERSION]` (a record of kind `reaction`, whose body is the reaction).
  - Shapes are checked locally (`vti_rooms::record_members::check`), then against the room's profile.
  - A refusal prints the fix: `pnm rooms profile set --room … --host-did … --record-members <listed + refused>`. Nothing is written.
  - **`writtenAt` is set automatically** whenever the profile lists it (this needs `--host-did`, which the VTA uses to find the profile).
- `read KEY... --room R --host-did D` is a batch read through the VTA. More than 32 keys are split into requests. Sealed bodies are verified as `get` verifies them, and a refused one is reported for its key.
- Default sends move to the new versions with fallback:
  - `get` asks get/0.3 (and prints the host's times, `kind` and `inReplyTo`), falling back to get/0.2.
  - `list` (and the head lookup before a sealed write) asks list/0.6, falling back to list/0.5.
  - `put` asks put/0.5 through act/0.11, falling back to put/0.3 through act/0.10 when the VTA lacks act/0.11 or the host answers `unsupportedType`. The fallback is used only for a record that asked for no governed member; an automatic `writtenAt` is dropped rather than failing the write.
  - Sealed bodies are sealed with seal/0.3.
- `vtc_client::rooms::body::SealedRecordBody` gains `kind`, `in_reply_to`, `written_at` and `edited_at`, checked by `record_members::check`. It is `deny_unknown_fields`, so without them `pnm rooms get` refused every sealed record carrying one.

## Judgement calls

1. **Budgets: 512 KiB and 15 s, checked before beginning a key.** The response is then at most the budget plus one record, and one record is what a single read already returns. A screen of messages is a few KiB a record, so 32 fit many times over. What the bound stops is 32 records of a mebibyte each. 15 s leaves room under the SDK's 60 s for the key in hand and one repair, which can wait 20 s (`REPAIR_WAIT`).
2. **Keys are read sequentially, not concurrently.** A key in flight when the budget runs out has been read and must be answered, so with concurrency the bounds would hold only approximately. Repairs are serialised anyway.
3. **"At most once per batch" is one catch-up and one chain extension**, each aimed at the most demanding epoch among the keys that need it. A batch whose keys need different prior-membership states gets the repair the chosen key's epoch selects; the others answer `cannotOpen` with the reason. Asking again repairs them.
4. **read/0.2 is dispatched `Mutating`, as its spec declares.** read/0.1 stays `None`, which already diverges from its own spec (`mutating` too). I didn't change 0.1's class in this PR because that would change how existing approval rules treat it.
5. **notAMember**: 0.2 and browse/0.4 answer a principal with no credentials from this room (the oracle's `NotFound`) with the declared code. 0.1 and browse/0.3 keep the refusal they always gave.
6. **The SDK keeps its own copy of the writer's rule**, `record_members_used` / `record_members_permitted` and the two member lists. `vta-sdk` can't depend on `vti-rooms`: `vti-rooms` depends (optionally) on `vti-common`, which depends on `vta-sdk`, and cargo counts optional edges as cycles. `vta-service/tests/it/room_record_members_gate.rs::the_sdk_governs_exactly_the_members_vti_rooms_does` pins the two equal.
7. **Scope item 3, the VTA's other host calls, is not moved.** The profile lookup reads a profile record (`get/0.2`) and its timing window is defined on `updatedAt`. The head lookups (profile write's version prediction, `room_owner`'s anchor) read only `headVersion`/`dataCommitment`, which list/0.6 serves identically. None of them consumes a member 0.3/0.6 adds, so moving them would only add a fallback round trip at older hosts. The `allow(deprecated)` comments now say so.
8. **MCP (`vta-mcp`)** has no read or browse tool of its own. Both go through `vta_call`, whose guard classes `rooms/keys/read` and `rooms/keys/browse` as `Sensitive` by slug, whatever the version. The new fields pass through unchanged, so nothing needed adding, and the guard rules are untouched.
9. **pnm puts sealed records with put/0.5 too**, except a record naming `blobs` (file records), which stays on put/0.3 whose blob handling every host serves.

## Nothing the spec ruled out

The batch is the spec's. Two points where the spec is silent, handled as above: where a batch puts what a single read says in `ext` (response-level, by key), and the precise reading of "each repair at most once per request" (call 3).

## Breaking

- `vtc_client::rooms::body::SealedRecordBody` gains four public fields. It isn't `#[non_exhaustive]` and the crate is published.
- `vta_cli_common::commands::rooms::cmd_rooms_put` takes a new `RecordThread` argument.

Additive: `VtaError::RecordMembersNotPermitted` (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`), new SDK methods and constants, `pnm rooms read`.

## Tests

`vta-service` `trust_tasks::room_profile::tests`, against a real `room-host` on loopback. The fixture now logs every type the host receives and can act like a host that predates get/0.3 and list/0.6:

- `read_0_2_answers_each_key_on_its_own_in_order`: a record with its times, `hostRefused` for a missing key with the host's code, no single-record members at the top, one get/0.3 per key.
- `read_0_2_of_one_key_passes_the_hosts_times_through`: and read/0.1 carries none.
- `read_0_2_falls_back_to_get_0_2_once_per_request`: get/0.3 asked once, then get/0.2 for every key.
- `read_0_2_answers_keys_past_its_bound_not_attempted`: retryable, no details, the host never asked.
- `read_0_2_refuses_a_malformed_batch_whole`: 33 keys, a duplicate, `[]`, both, neither. 32 is accepted.
- `a_batch_repairs_once_and_opens_every_record`: a member behind by a commit and joined late reads five records. Exactly one `rooms/epoch/commits` and one `rooms/epoch/chain` request; every record opens.
- `a_record_that_will_not_open_fails_only_its_own_key`: `cannotOpen`/`notDelivered` with its epoch beside a readable record, and the same code when read alone.
- `read_0_2_and_browse_0_4_name_their_refusals`: `notAMember`, `hostUnreachable` (per key in a batch, retryable), `hostRefused`.
- `browse_0_4_passes_list_0_6_rows_through_and_falls_back_to_0_5`: `kind`, `createdBy`, the times; fallback rows carry none; browse/0.3 unchanged.
- `messages_replies_and_reactions_round_trip_through_a_batch_read`, end to end on an open room:
  - the owner writes a profile with `recordMembers: [kind, inReplyTo, writtenAt]`;
  - the writer's rule permits the three and refuses `editedAt`;
  - a message, a reply and a reaction are written with put/0.5 through act/0.11, and one read/0.2 batch returns each with its `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt`, `createdBy` and host times.

The SDK gate:

- `vta-service/tests/it/room_record_members_gate.rs` (loopback transport):
  - refuses an unlisted member with the typed error;
  - allows a listed one;
  - reads no profile for a body using none;
  - reads the profile once per epoch and again when the epoch moves;
  - permits nothing with no `recordMembers`;
  - pins the SDK's lists to `vti-rooms`'.
- `vta-sdk` unit tests for `check_record_members`.

The CLI:

- `pnm-cli`:
  - `rooms_put_takes_a_kind_a_reply_and_a_reaction`, including the rejected combinations: no body; `--react` without `--to`; `--to` without `--react`; a body with `--react`; `--kind` with `--react`.
  - `rooms_read_takes_several_keys_and_the_host_did`.
- `vta-cli-common`: `a_record_thread_is_the_bodys_kind_and_in_reply_to` and `a_refused_record_member_prints_the_profile_command`.

Run locally (macOS, default features):

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6987 tests run, 6987 passed (2 slow), 23 skipped
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: passed (0 failed)

- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`: passed (0 failed)

title: feat(rooms)!: hosts serve put/0.5, list/0.6 and get/0.3 and record createdAt, createdBy, bodyStoredAt
body:
The second stage of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1027 (merged as 565f8d32), after #2449: the **room host side**, on `room-host` and the VTC's community room host, with the shared logic in `vti-rooms`. Every new URI was already pinned by #2449.

## What the hosts do now

- **Serve `rooms/records/put/0.5`** beside 0.3 and 0.4. An `open` room's `cleartext` may carry `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt` and `editedAt`, and its `file` may carry `width`, `height` and `preview`. The payload is validated against the 0.5 schema, and each member is checked by `vti_rooms::record_members::check`. The cleartext is then stored exactly as received and never acted on (Host item 14), so there is no rewrite check and no `recordMembers` check. On the sealed tiers the host sees ciphertext only, so nothing changes there. Shared code: `blob_tasks::{put_v5_parts, put_v5_as_v0_1}`.
- **Record `createdAt`, `createdBy` and `bodyStoredAt`** (Host items 16–17), in `storage::put_record`, so every host and every put version records them:
  - The first version sets `createdAt` and `createdBy`, and every later put copies them from the stored record. A curation, retraction included, never touches them. `createdBy` is the author the host authenticated, and is recorded only where the tier discloses an actor: `open` and `attributed`, never `private`.
  - Every put sets `bodyStoredAt`. A curation leaves it alone.
  - Whatever a caller puts in these fields is overwritten. They are the host's metadata, never the writer's.
  - Storage: three `Option` fields on `vti_rooms::Record`, with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if)]`. Old rows read with all three `None`, and no migration rewrites anything. After an edit, an old row still has no `createdAt`/`createdBy` (the first version was never timed, so it is not guessed), but it does get a `bodyStoredAt`.
- **Serve `rooms/records/list/0.6`** (rows built by `Record::metadata_v3`, i.e. `RecordMetadataV3`) and **`rooms/records/get/0.3`** (`blob_tasks::get_v3_response`), beside list/0.5 and get/0.2, which are unchanged.
  - On list/0.6, `kind` is read from the stored `cleartext.kind`, on `open` only. It is absent when the record has none and on a tombstone, and it is never defaulted.
  - On both, `createdBy` is withheld on `private`, decided again from the room's visibility at read time.
  - None of these members is in `CommittedRecord`, so the leaf, the root and the trace are exactly get/0.2's.
- **Host item 15, the optional open-room refusal**: `blob_tasks::rewrite_by_other_refused`. On an `open` room, a new version of a record whose current `cleartext.kind` is `message` or `reaction`, from anyone other than its recorded `createdBy`, is refused with the standard `permissionDenied`. The check runs under the record-write lock (`prepare_record`'s guard), so it judges the record the write replaces, and it refuses before anything changes. It never fires on `attributed`/`private`, on a tombstone, on a first version, or on the original author's own rewrites (the withdrawal included).
- **Advertised and dispatched**:
  - room-host: `route`, `is_consequential` (get/0.3 and list/0.6 are reads).
  - VTC: the dispatcher registrations and `AS_RECEIVED_URIS` for put/0.5. `served_uris()` feeds discovery, sizes and the censuses.
  - `vti_rooms::wire::ROOMS_DISPATCHED_URIS` and the conformance test that pins each constant to its generated `TYPE_URI`.
- **Clients**:
  - `vtc-client`'s `get_record` / `list_records` ask get/0.3 and list/0.6 first, and ask again at get/0.2 and list/0.5 when the host answers `unsupportedType`.
  - A `room-host` mirror (which pulls through `vtc-client`) keeps the primary's `createdAt`/`createdBy`/`bodyStoredAt` from get/0.3. It never uses its own arrival time, and stores none when the primary served none.

## Judgement calls

1. **The open-room refusal is on by default.** The spec makes it a MAY and says nothing about a default. Readers defend against such a rewrite either way, but on `open` the host reads the body anyway, so the refusal costs nothing and protects readers that predate the reader rules. To turn it off: `room-host --allow-rewrites-by-others`, or the VTC's `[rooms] refuse_rewrites_by_others = false` (absent means on).
2. **The refusal applies to every put version, not only 0.5.** Item 15 is about "a new version of a record", and the record's kind lives in its stored cleartext. A 0.3/0.4 put that overwrote another member's message would otherwise go around it.
3. **A record with no recorded `createdBy` is never refused.** Item 15 names the original author as "the author it recorded for the record's first version (item 17)". A record stored before this change has none, and guessing one from the current `author` would be supplying a value item 17 forbids.
4. **The times are recorded on put/0.3 and 0.4 writes too.** Items 16–17 are host behaviour ("It knows which task wrote each version, so it does this on every tier"), and list/0.6 and get/0.3 serve them for every record, whatever wrote it.
5. **`bodyStoredAt` stays on a tombstone**, unchanged by the retraction, as the `RecordMetadataV3` description says of every curation.
6. **A record re-put after retraction keeps its original `createdAt`/`createdBy`.** The key still holds the record (a tombstone), so the put is a new version, not a first one. After a purge or a prune the row is gone, and the next put is a first version again.
7. **The VTA's host calls are not moved.** The VTA reads records from hosts for `rooms/keys/browse/0.3`, `rooms/keys/read/0.1`, the profile lookup and `room_owner`'s head check. None of those responses can carry the new members: browse/0.3's rows are `RecordMetadataV2`, and passing list/0.6 rows through would break its own response schema. Moving them belongs with browse/0.4 and read/0.2 in stage 3. Nothing they consume changed: list/0.5 and get/0.2 serve exactly what they did.

## Breaking

`vti_rooms::Record` (published, not `#[non_exhaustive]`) gains `created_at`, `created_by` and `body_stored_at`. Every struct literal outside the crate must name them. `vtc-service`'s `RoomsConfig` gains `refuse_rewrites_by_others`.

## Tests

- `vti_rooms::storage::record_times_tests`:
  - `createdAt`/`createdBy` are set once and stay the same across an edit by another member, a pin, a demotion and a retraction, on `open` and `attributed`.
  - `bodyStoredAt` moves on each put and on no curation.
  - A writer-supplied value is overwritten.
  - `createdBy` is never recorded or served on `private`.
  - An old row (raw JSON without the members) serves none of them, and after an edit still has no `createdAt`/`createdBy`.
  - list/0.6 `kind` appears on `open` only, is absent when not carried, and is absent on a tombstone. 0.5 rows are unchanged.
  - get/0.3: removing the spec's listed members from the response gives the committed record, so the leaf hash is unchanged and its trace verifies against the root.
- `vti_rooms::blob_tasks`: the item 15 rule (another author refused; own rewrite, first version, other kinds, tombstone, unrecorded author and sealed tiers all accepted). put/0.5 accepts the new members and stores the cleartext as received. It refuses each bad shape (kind case, empty, length, type; `inReplyTo` without `key` or with an unknown member; non-instant `writtenAt`; non-UTC `editedAt`; an unknown member).
- `room-host` and `vtc-service`, end to end through dispatch:
  - put/0.5 is served back by list/0.6 and get/0.3, and list/0.5 and get/0.2 carry none of the new members.
  - A malformed member is `malformedRequest`, and nothing is stored.
  - The refusal: on by default, `permissionDenied` with nothing changed (also via put/0.4 on room-host), and off via the switch or config.

Run locally (macOS, default features):

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6966 tests run, 6966 passed, 23 skipped
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3603 tests run, 3603 passed (1 leaky), 1 skipped
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`: passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

## Follows

Stage 3: the VTA's `rooms/keys/browse/0.4` and `rooms/keys/read/0.2`, which will read list/0.6 and get/0.3. Then the SDK's and pnm's default sends move to put/0.5.

title: feat(vtc)!: vtc/networks 0.2, and broadcasts as vtc/networks/deliver
body:
A community now speaks `vtc/networks/*` 0.2 and takes a Verifiable Trust Network's broadcasts as a Trust Task, `vtc/networks/deliver/0.1`, at its `/v1/trust-tasks`. Before, broadcasts came in at a REST route, `POST /v1/networks/relay/{group_id}` with a bare `{ envelope }`. The specs are trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1033, now live on trusttasks.org.

**Why:** the VTN moved onto `vtn/*` Trust Tasks, and the community already talks to it that way (#2422). Two things were left over:
- the 0.1 specs still described a group's registration as a `servesRole` credential, which VTN retired;
- the community's intake was the last REST route a network used.

0.2 changes what `registration` and `endpoint` mean: the registration is the signed `vtn/groups/register` request, and the endpoint is the community's Trust Task endpoint. With `deliver`, a network reaches a community the same way it reaches a member network.

**`vti-specs-vtc`**

- Pins `vtc/networks/{join,leave,list,show,repudiate,evidence,groups/register}` at 0.2 instead of 0.1, and adds `vtc/networks/deliver/0.1`. `notice` stays at 0.1.

**`vtc-service` networks**

- **`vtc/networks/deliver/0.1`:** a new handler in `network_tasks`, backed by `networks::deliver(state, deliverer, role, envelope)`. It replaces `networks::relay`. The deliverer is the task's verified signer. In order, it:
  1. refuses with `vtc/networks/deliver:notMember` unless the deliverer is a network this community has an acknowledged membership in;
  2. refuses with `vtc/networks/deliver:roleUnregistered` unless a group is registered for `role` there;
  3. verifies the envelope, at most 8 hops, and refuses with `vtc/networks/deliver:envelopeInvalid` unless its last hop is the deliverer's and addressed to that group;
  4. drops a repeated message id as `duplicate`;
  5. otherwise pushes `vtc/networks/notice/0.1` to the group's active members and answers `delivered`.

  The answer carries no member count, so the network doesn't learn the group's size.
- **Registered endpoint:** every group registers `<public_url>/v1/trust-tasks` (`DELIVERY_PATH`) instead of `<public_url>/v1/networks/relay/<group id>`.
- **Removed:** the REST route, `routes/networks.rs`, and its entries in `REST_EXCEPTIONS` and `GOVERNED_UNAUTH`. `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `src/lib/wire.ts` are regenerated.
- **Consequence:** a group registered under 0.1 points at a route that no longer exists, so the community has to register it again. `docs/03-vtc/networks.md` says so.
- **0.1 is dropped:** nothing in VTI sends `vtc/networks/*/0.1`, so the 0.1 pins are removed rather than kept alongside 0.2.

**Tests**

- Unit: `a_broadcast_is_delivered_once_and_only_by_the_network` adds an unregistered role and an envelope whose last hop is another network's. After leaving, a delivery is `notMember`.
- New integration test, `deliveries_are_taken_only_from_a_joined_network_for_a_registered_role`: a fake network signs real `vtc/networks/deliver` tasks through the spine and drives each declared code, then `delivered` and `duplicate`. It also checks the registered endpoint. It is the witness for the three new codes in the error-code census.
- The conformance census includes `deliver`, using the spec's own example. The shared sample is `_shared/0.7`.
- Results:
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` is clean;
  - `vtc-service` passes 2170 and 1376 tests;
  - the `vti-specs` and `vti-specs-vtc` tests pass;
  - `npm run wire:check` passes.

**Follow-up:** OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network delivers to communities with this task once it's released (it needs `vti-specs-vtc` for the types). That branch passes all its tests against this one.

title: feat(rooms)!: record kinds, replies and image previews at the VTA — serve rooms/keys/seal/0.3 and act/0.11, carry recordMembers
body:
The first stage of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1027 (merged as 565f8d32): a record's kind, replies, reactions, when it was written and edited, and an image's size and preview. This PR covers the VTA's side, plus the pins every later stage needs.

## Pins (`vti-specs-rooms`)

Added beside the versions already pinned, which stay pinned because old clients still send them:

- `rooms/keys/seal/0.3`, `rooms/keys/act/0.11`
- `rooms/records/put/0.5`, `rooms/records/list/0.6`, `rooms/records/get/0.3`
- `rooms/keys/browse/0.4`, `rooms/keys/read/0.2`

`trust-tasks update` also re-vendored every bundle that references `rooms/_shared` (act 0.8–0.10, browse 0.3, file-key, open, profile read/write, read 0.1, seal 0.2, welcome, get 0.1–0.2, list 0.1–0.5, put 0.1–0.4). #1027 changed `SealedRecordBody`, `RoomProfile` and `FileManifest` in place, so those bundles changed too. Superseded versions still in use are marked `#[allow(deprecated)]` with a reason.

## What the VTA does now

- **Serves `rooms/keys/seal/0.3`** beside 0.2. Under `signAsPrincipal` it accepts `kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt`, `editedAt`, and a `file` carrying `width`, `height` or `preview`. Each one is checked against its schema; the checks live in the new `vti_rooms::record_members::check`. 0.2 still refuses all of them with `bodyInvalid`, as the 0.3 spec says a 0.2 key holder does. That refusal is how `trust-task-discovery` tells a writer which key holder accepts them.
- **Serves `rooms/keys/act/0.11`** beside 0.10. Its table adds `rooms/records/put/0.5` (`write`) and `rooms/records/list/0.6` and `rooms/records/get/0.3` (`read`). It is otherwise completed as 0.10 is, with the `cleartext` signed unaltered.
- **Body allow-lists.** `BODY_MEMBERS` in `trust_tasks/room_act.rs` and `operations/room_profile.rs` now know the four new members. The profile reader lists them among the members a profile record must not carry, so a record carrying them at a profile location reads as `notProfile` rather than `malformed`.
- **`FileManifest`.** `vti_rooms::files::FileManifest` gains `width`, `height` and `preview` (`FilePreview`). It is `deny_unknown_fields`, so without them every reader built on it would refuse a manifest that uses them.
- **`RoomProfile.recordMembers`.** The profile reader accepts a profile that carries it. Before this change it would have read such a profile as `malformed`, and the owner's re-write after an advance would have dropped it. The reader now also holds the profile to its full JSON Schema (`recordMembers` is a non-empty set, which the generated type alone does not enforce), and `profile/write` refuses a profile its readers would refuse. `carry_before_advance` / `rewrite_after_advance` carry `recordMembers` through unchanged.
- **CLI.** `pnm rooms profile set --record-members kind,inReplyTo,…` and `--no-record-members`, through the SDK's `room_profile_write`. `pnm rooms profile show` prints the list. cnm has no profile command, so there is no cnm twin to update.
- Both new Type URIs are pinned, classified in `vta_sdk::retry_safety` (`RetrySafe`, as their predecessors), listed in `ALL_URIS`, dispatched, given conformance entries, and act/0.11 is in the policy gate's subject resolution.

## Judgement calls

1. **No `recordMembers` gate on the VTA's seal or act.** `rooms/keys/seal/0.3` Recipient item 3 says the key holder "MUST NOT refuse it for carrying `kind`, … which it does not check against the room's `recordMembers`". `rooms/keys/act/0.11` says the same about the writes it completes: "that is the writer's rule (`rooms/records/put/0.5` Producer item 11)". The only body the VTA itself authors is the room profile, which may not carry these members at all. So there is no VTA write path where the spec lets the gate apply. The writer's rule is `vti_rooms::record_members::permitted` (absent, empty or unresolvable profile → none permitted), which has tests. It is for the client writer, and wires in when pnm/the SDK start sending these members.
2. **`rooms/keys/read` does not refuse a body with unknown members.** Neither read/0.1 nor read/0.2 gives the key holder a refusal for an opened body, and neither declares an error code for one. Their only codes are `notAMember`, `hostUnreachable`, `hostRefused`, `cannotOpen` and (0.2) `notAttempted`. The spec puts rule (1) on the reader the plaintext is handed to. Inventing a code, or overloading `cannotOpen` with a new `details.reason` that consumers "MUST act on", would be an unregistered divergence. Because the members were added to `SealedRecordBody` in place, every body that uses them is a valid body anyway. If the key holder should apply rule (1), the next step is a spec change: for example, a `bodyInvalid` code on `rooms/keys/read` and `browse`. read/0.1 behaviour is unchanged.
3. **The carry-through test runs on an admission and a renewal, not a removal.** All three call the same `carry_before_advance` / `rewrite_after_advance`. The room-profile fixture cannot drive a removal: on `attributed` the host refuses the room-signed withdrawal, because the fixture's signing key isn't the room DID's key; on `private` an admission needs a subject binding the fixture doesn't mint.
4. **seal/0.2 now inspects `file`** for the three governed manifest members and refuses them. Before this PR it did not look inside `file`. This follows the 0.3 spec's account of a 0.2 key holder.

## Follows in later PRs

- The host side, in room-host and vtc-service: serve `rooms/records/put/0.5`, `list/0.6` and `get/0.3`, and record and serve `createdAt`, `createdBy` and `bodyStoredAt`.
- The VTA's `rooms/keys/browse/0.4` and the `rooms/keys/read/0.2` batch read.
- Moving the SDK's and pnm's default sends to seal/0.3, act/0.11 and put/0.5, with the writer gate (`record_members::permitted`) applied by pnm against the resolved profile.

## Breaking

`vti_rooms::files::FileManifest` gains three public fields, and `vta_cli_common::commands::rooms_custody::ProfileEdit` gains one. Neither struct is `#[non_exhaustive]`, and both crates are published. The generated `vti-specs-rooms` types are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so their new fields are additive.

## Tests

- `vti_rooms::record_members`: each member's shape, accepting the valid forms and refusing each invalid one. Covers `kind` (open lowerCamelCase set, at most 64 characters), `inReplyTo` (`{key, version?}`), `writtenAt`/`editedAt` (UTC only), `width`/`height` (1–1048576), and `preview` (JPEG/PNG/WebP only, at most 8192 bytes decoded, closed). Also tests the writer's rule `permitted`.
- `trust_tasks::room_act`: seal/0.3 accepts and signs, unaltered, each body 0.2 refuses `bodyInvalid`. seal/0.3 refuses each malformed member and an unknown one.
- `operations::room_act`: act/0.11's table.
- `operations::room_profile`: a profile with `recordMembers` is accepted as signed; malformed `recordMembers` reads as `malformed`; a profile record carrying a new member reads as `notProfile`.
- `trust_tasks::room_profile`: `recordMembers` is carried through two advances.
- `rooms_custody`: `--record-members` sets, carries over and drops the list, and the result parses as a `RoomProfile`.

Run locally before pushing (macOS, default features):

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6946 tests run, 6946 passed, 23 skipped
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3598 tests run, 3598 passed, 1 skipped
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`: passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `trust-tasks -C vti-specs-rooms check`: 72 pinned task versions match the lock

title: fix(rooms): a member removed from a room can be admitted again
body:
Two defects from Keyring's rooms report (https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/blob/167f3a0dccb571e02fb2ac7664a9b985e56a18fd/docs/upstream/2026-11-rooms-findings.md). The second one follows up #2424.

The spec amendment for the first is still in flight in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf as draft trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1031 (rooms/keys/welcome/0.1, rooms/keys/open/0.2, file-key/0.2). This PR implements the rule as drafted there, including its commits b89abe59b, 80a9a6e26 and 9ca2d9502: a removal is recognised from the re-admitting Welcome when the member's VTA never processed it (section 1a below).

## 1. A member removed from a room could not rejoin it

`join` returned `alreadyJoined` whenever group state existed. `apply_commit` keeps the group state on a removal so that older records still open. Together these meant a re-admitted member's VTA refused the new Welcome, and nothing sealed after the removal ever opened for that member. The removal-row clearing in `join` could not be reached after a real removal.

**The rule (rooms/keys/welcome/0.1, rooms/keys/open/0.2):** group state with a removal recorded is a *prior membership*, not a join.

- **join**: accepts a Welcome when a removal is recorded. In one conditional `Batch`, it does all of the following:
  - moves the ended group, its join epoch and its removal epoch into `room-prior/<room>/<persona>`, a list with one entry per removal, so repeated removals pile up;
  - stores the new group as current;
  - records the new join epoch in `room-joined/<room>/<persona>`;
  - clears the REMOVED row and the consumed KeyPackage.

  `alreadyJoined` still applies to current state with no removal recorded, or when a concurrent Welcome won the batch.
- **Opening uses the record's epoch E:**
  - E ≥ the current join epoch: the current group.
  - E in a prior membership's [join, removal): that group, with its own links.
  - E between a removal and the next join: `removed`, with that removal's epoch. This holds even when a backfill reached the current chain that far.
  - E below the first join: `beyondChain`.

  This applies to `open_record*` (so keys/open, read, browse and act), `file_key`, `profile_location` and `profile_locations`.
- **Sealing always uses the current group.** A member that has been removed and not yet re-admitted has no current epoch. `seal_record`, file-key-to-seal and the profile write location all answer `noGroup`, and `keys/act` answers `notAMember`.
- **forget** discards the prior list and the join epoch.
- **Epoch floor** (rooms/epoch/prune/0.2): drops a prior membership once all its epochs are below the floor, and drops the remaining memberships' rungs at or below it.
- **Legacy migration** needs no change. The per-room build wrote neither row, and `room-prior` only exists alongside a group that a legacy row never overwrites.
- **Welcome handler:** the spent-invitation check answers `alreadyJoined` only for a *current* membership.

Docs: `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` (*Remove a member*, and the `removed` reason).

## 1a. A member removed while idle (review follow-up)

Section 1 treated group state as a prior membership only when a REMOVED row existed, and that row is written only when this VTA applies the removing commit. A member that was idle when removed never applies it, and cannot fetch it afterwards, because the host refuses commits to a withdrawn member. Its VTA reached re-admission holding stale state at some epoch h with no removal recorded, and `join` still answered `alreadyJoined`.

**The rule (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1031, welcome/0.1 *Rejoining after a removal*): the Welcome is the evidence.** There is no network step, and the client does not have to apply anything first.

- **join**: when current state exists and no removal is recorded, the VTA processes the Welcome in memory and stores nothing yet. It then looks in the Welcome's ratchet tree for the held state's own leaf, matched by **signature key**, not by DID (the re-admitted leaf has the same DID under a new key). `RoomGroup::has_leaf_with_signature_key` and `GroupSnapshot::signature_public_key` are new in vti-rooms.
  - **Leaf still present**: `alreadyJoined`. Nothing from the Welcome is kept and the KeyPackage is not consumed.
  - **Leaf absent, and the Welcome is later than the held epoch**: the held state moves into `room-prior` with `removedEpoch` unknown. The rest of the switch is the same as in section 1, in one conditional batch that also requires the REMOVED row to still be absent.
  - **A Welcome for another MLS group** (different group id; spec 80a9a6e26 and 9ca2d9502, *Same group, whatever the evidence*): `welcomeInvalid` (`JoinError::WelcomeForAnotherGroup`). This applies on both paths, with or without a REMOVED row, and is checked before anything is written, so nothing is consumed or changed.
  - **No Welcome to inspect** (no KeyPackage, an expired one, or a Welcome that does not process): `alreadyJoined` as before, and nothing is discarded.
- **A prior membership with an unknown removal** covers its join epoch up to the next join.
  - For E ≤ h, records open.
  - For E in (h, j), the answer is `notDelivered` with `heldEpoch` set to the prior's held epoch. It is never `removed` before the removing commit has been applied.
- **Repair** (`room_catch_up::repair`): `room_groups::repair_state` now chooses the state by the record's epoch, under the same per-member lock. Catch-up then applies the host's commits to that prior state with `apply_prior_commit`, until `RoomKeyError::Removed { epoch }` fixes r. After that the membership is handled as a known removal: E < r opens, and E in [r, j) is `removed`.
  - `apply_prior_commit` never advances a prior state to the next join epoch, and it writes conditionally on the `room-prior` row it read.
  - Sealing still uses only the current group.
- **Epoch floor and profile walk**: both bound an unknown removal by the next join epoch and by the epoch the prior state holds.

**The host serves a re-admitted member the commits it needs.** Both `room-host` and `vtc-service` handle `rooms/epoch/commits/0.1` the same way. `authz::authorize(.., Action::Read, now)` checks the presentation as of now, and the revocation list withdraws only credentials with `validFrom < revokedAt`, so the fresh credentials pass. `storage::commits_since` then returns every commit above any `sinceEpoch`, with no bound by the credential's `validFrom`. Commits are deleted only by `purge_room_rows`, and an epoch prune drops rungs, not commits. So commits from before the new credentials' `validFrom` are served.

## 2. `community_renewal::held()` disagreed with the VTA

When there were several credentials of one type, `held()` refused and said the VTA "acts on the room with none of them". That stopped being true with #2424. `held()` now uses `room_oracle::current`'s rule: the latest `validFrom` among those in force. On a tie it names the vault ids and says to archive the one not meant (`pnm cred-vault archive <id>`). The choice is a pure `choose`, covered by unit tests. The vtc-service CLAUDE.md line that described the old behaviour is corrected.

## Tests

- `room_groups::readmission_tests` (sealed room, real MLS):
  - admit, seal, remove, seal while out, re-admit, seal;
  - while out: seal, file-key-to-seal and profile seal are refused;
  - after re-admission: the pre-removal record opens, the out-of-membership record is `removed`, and the post-readmission record opens;
  - file-key gives the same answers;
  - after a backfill, the gap is still `removed` and epoch 1 is `beyondChain`;
  - a second Welcome is `alreadyJoined`;
  - two removals pile up, and the profile walk skips the gaps;
  - the epoch floor prunes the first prior membership;
  - `forget` clears all prior state.
- `room_owner_group::a_member_removed_from_an_attributed_room_is_admitted_again_and_reads_on`: the owner's VTA runs `remove/0.4` on an attributed room (withdraw, then advance) and then `add/0.3`. The member's VTA processes the removal and joins again. The test asserts every case in the brief, plus `forget`.
- `vtc-service/tests/it/community_rooms.rs::a_member_removed_from_an_attributed_room_can_be_admitted_again`: the community-side flow on an attributed room. The VTC harness's VTA is scripted and holds no MLS group, so the member's key-holder half of this is covered by the vta-service test above, not here.
- `community_renewal::tests::{the_credential_chosen_is_the_latest_in_force, a_tie_names_the_vault_ids_and_says_archive}`.
- Section 1a, sealed room with real MLS:
  - `room_groups::readmission_tests::a_member_that_never_applied_its_removal_is_admitted_again_by_the_welcome`:
    - the owner renews (3) and removes (4); the member applies neither, and the Welcome at 5 is accepted with the removal epoch unknown;
    - the record at h = 2 opens, and the post-readmission record opens;
    - records at 3 and 4 are `notDelivered`, with held = 2 for both keys/open and file-key;
    - `repair_state` targets the prior membership;
    - for the commits applied to the prior state: a gap is refused, and a replay is a no-op;
    - after the renewal is applied, epoch 3 opens and epoch 4 is `notDelivered` with held = 3;
    - after the removal is applied, r = 4, epoch 4 is `removed` (also via file-key), and no more commits apply;
    - the profile walk is `[5, 3, 2]`.
  - `room_groups::readmission_tests::a_welcome_that_still_holds_the_members_leaf_is_already_joined_and_consumes_nothing`: a second leaf is added while the first is still in the tree. The result is `alreadyJoined`, `holds_key_package` is still true, the held group is unchanged, and there is no prior membership.
  - `room_owner_group::a_member_removed_while_idle_from_an_attributed_room_is_admitted_again_and_reads_on`: the sibling of the attributed-room test, where the member skips the removal commit. It runs `remove/0.4` and then `add/0.3`, and the Welcome is accepted. Epoch 3 is `notDelivered` with held = 2 until the removal commit is applied to the prior state, and then `removed`. The before and after records open, and a second Welcome is `alreadyJoined`.
  - `room_groups::readmission_tests::a_welcome_for_another_group_retires_nothing`: another group, at a higher epoch, adds the member. The Welcome is refused as `WelcomeForAnotherGroup`, the KeyPackage is still held, and the group, join epoch, prior list and REMOVED row are unchanged.
  - `room_groups::readmission_tests::a_removed_member_is_not_admitted_to_another_group`: with a removal recorded, another group's Welcome is refused. The group row, the removal row, the join epoch and the KeyPackage are unchanged, and no prior membership is created. The room's own group then re-admits the member.
  - `vti-rooms` `mls::leaf_recognition_tests`: a leaf is recognised by its signature key, not by the member's DID.
  - **The host round trip is driven at the operations level.** The test owner's mock host does not serve `rooms/epoch/commits`, so the tests hand `apply_prior_commit` the owner's own commits, the same way `room_catch_up` hands it what the host serves.

Local results (after section 1a):

- `cargo nextest run -p vta-service`: 2338 passed, 1 skipped
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3598 passed, 1 skipped (without `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD`)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

title: fix(rooms): a member removed from a room can be admitted again (#2441)
body:
fix(rooms): a member removed from a room can be admitted again (#2441)

* fix(rooms): a member removed from a room can be admitted again

Group state with a removal recorded is a prior membership, not a join
(rooms/keys/welcome/0.1, rooms/keys/open/0.2; trust-tasks-tf #1031).
`join` refused every Welcome once group state existed, and a removal
keeps the group state, so a re-admitted member's VTA refused the new
Welcome and nothing sealed after the removal ever opened for it.

`join` now accepts a Welcome when a removal is recorded: the ended group,
its join epoch and its removal epoch move into a `room-prior` list, the new
group becomes current, its join epoch is kept in `room-joined`, and the
removal row is cleared, in one conditional batch. `alreadyJoined` stays
for current state with no removal.

Opening goes by the record's epoch: at or above the current join epoch,
the current group; within a prior membership's [join, removal), that
membership's group and links; between a removal and the next join,
`removed` with that removal's epoch; below the first join, `beyondChain`.
This holds for open_record (and so keys/open, read, browse and act's
opens), file-key, and the profile location and walk. A member removed and
not yet re-admitted has no current epoch: sealing, file-key-to-seal and a
profile write answer noGroup, and act answers notAMember.

`forget` discards prior memberships and the join epoch; the epoch floor
drops a prior membership wholly below it and the rest's rungs at or below
it (rooms/epoch/prune/0.2). The welcome handler's spent-invitation check
answers alreadyJoined only for a current membership.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc): renewal picks the community's room credential as the VTA does

`held()` refused when the community's VTA held more than one credential
of a type from a room, saying the VTA acts on the room with none of them.
Since #2424 `room_oracle::current` picks the latest `validFrom` among
those in force and refuses only a tie. `held()` now applies the same rule
(a pure `choose`, unit-tested) and on a tie names the vault ids and says
to archive the one not meant (`pnm cred-vault archive <id>`).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rooms): a member removed while idle can be admitted again — the Welcome is the evidence

The previous commit treated group state as a prior membership only when a
REMOVED row existed, and that row is written only when this VTA applies the
removing commit. A member idle when it was removed never applies it, and
cannot fetch it afterwards: the host serves `rooms/epoch/commits` under a
`read` grant the removal withdrew. Its VTA met the re-admitting Welcome
holding stale state at some epoch h with no removal recorded, and `join`
still answered `alreadyJoined`.

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1031 as amended
(rooms/keys/welcome/0.1 *Rejoining after a removal*, rooms/keys/open/0.2,
rooms/keys/file-key/0.2): a removal is recognised by a removal processed OR
by a Welcome whose ratchet tree no longer holds the member's earlier leaf.

- join: with current state and no removal recorded, the Welcome is
  processed in memory without storing anything, and its tree searched for
  the held state's own leaf by its signature key (never the DID, which the
  re-admitted leaf shares). Still there: `alreadyJoined`, nothing kept, the
  KeyPackage not consumed. Absent (and the Welcome later than the held
  epoch): the held state moves into `room-prior` with its removal epoch not
  yet known, and the rest of the switch is as before, in one conditional
  batch that also requires the REMOVED row still absent. No Welcome to look
  in (no KeyPackage, an expired one, one that does not process) is
  `alreadyJoined` as before, with nothing discarded.
- PriorMembership.removed_epoch / removed_at are optional. Such a
  membership covers its join epoch up to the next join; an epoch above the
  one it holds is `notDelivered` with that state's `heldEpoch`, never
  `removed`, until the removing commit is applied to it.
- repair_state / apply_prior_commit: a read's repair (`room_catch_up`) now
  chooses the state by the record's epoch, under the same per-member lock,
  and applies the host's commits to a prior membership until the removing
  one fixes its removal epoch (`RoomKeyError::Removed`); from then on it is
  a known removal. Never advanced to the next join epoch; written
  conditionally on the `room-prior` row read. Sealing still uses only the
  current group.
- The epoch floor and the profile walk bound an unknown removal by the
  next join epoch and by the epoch the state holds.
- vti-rooms: `RoomGroup::has_leaf_with_signature_key` and
  `GroupSnapshot::signature_public_key`.

The host's commit endpoint (room-host and vtc-service) authorizes the
presentation as of now and serves every commit above any `sinceEpoch`,
keeping commits until the room is purged — so a re-admitted member's fresh
credentials reach commits from before their `validFrom`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rooms): a Welcome for another MLS group retires no membership

`join`'s absent-leaf path read a Welcome whose ratchet tree lacks the held
state's leaf as evidence of a removal the member never saw. A Welcome for a
different MLS group has none of that state's leaves by construction, so it
would have retired current state on no evidence.

Per trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1031 (80a9a6e26, rooms/keys/welcome/0.1
*Rejoining after a removal*): before an absent leaf counts, the Welcome's
MLS group id must equal the held state's. Otherwise `join` answers
`JoinError::WelcomeForAnotherGroup`, which the welcome handler refuses as
`welcomeInvalid`, before anything is written: no invitation or KeyPackage
consumed, no state changed.

- vti-rooms: `RoomGroup::group_id` and `GroupSnapshot::group_id`.
- Test `readmission_tests::a_welcome_for_another_group_retires_nothing`:

title: spec(rooms): a record's kind, replies and reactions — notes, messages and reactions on every tier (#1027)
body:
spec(rooms): a record's kind, replies and reactions — notes, messages and reactions on every tier (#1027)

* spec(rooms): a record's kind, replies and reactions — notes, messages and reactions on every tier

A room had one kind of record, so a chat-style client's messages read as
untitled notes in every other client, and nothing let two clients agree
on a reply or a reaction (Keyring, berkmancenter/keyring-wallet
docs/upstream/2026-11-rooms-findings.md, finding 2).

SealedRecordBody (rooms/_shared 0.1 and 0.2, identically) gains two
optional members, in place and additively, as provenance did:

- `kind` (RecordKind): an open, lowerCamelCase set — `note`, `message`,
  `reaction` defined. Absent means note; a reader shows a kind it does
  not know as a note and never refuses a record for its kind.
- `inReplyTo` (RecordReference): another record of the same room, by
  key and optionally the version answered. A reader resolves it only
  against records it can already read, shows a reply whose target is
  unavailable as such, and fetches nothing because of it.

Reactions are records of kind `reaction` carrying their target in
`inReplyTo` and a value of at most 64 characters on one line in `body`;
one per author, value and target; withdrawn by rewriting the same key
with an empty body. Edits are what they already were: a new version
under the same key — nothing is added, and a version by another author
is never shown as the earlier author's edit. A file record's `body` is
its caption, which a reader SHOULD show.

Readers that predate the members refuse them by rule (1), so a writer
SHOULD NOT write them until its room's readers accept them — and the
spec says plainly a writer cannot check that: a sealed body carries no
schema version and members publish no reader capabilities.

rooms/records/put/0.5 (extends 0.4) adds `kind` and `inReplyTo` to an
open room's closed `cleartext`; the host stores and serves them and
never acts on them. rooms/keys/act/0.11 (extends 0.10) adds put/0.5 to
its table. Libraries regenerated.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(rooms): writtenAt, nothing answers a reaction, and the room's profile says which record members its writers may use

Resolves the open questions on this proposal:

- SealedRecordBody gains `writtenAt` (RecordWrittenAt, RFC 3339 UTC),
  also in put/0.5's open-room cleartext: set by the author, kept
  unchanged across edits so `version` alone marks revisions. Readers
  order messages by it, then by key; without one, by the host's
  updatedAt. It is the author's claim: a reader treats one later than
  the host's updatedAt (or the read instant) by more than five minutes,
  or an edit that changes it, as implausible — ordered by updatedAt and
  its time not shown. OPTIONAL on a note; a message or reaction SHOULD
  carry it.
- A writer MUST NOT name a reaction in `inReplyTo`; a reader that finds
  one MUST ignore the naming record. A reader's rule: no host enforces
  it, and on the sealed tiers none could.
- RoomProfile gains `recordMembers`: the optional body members the
  room's writers may use. A writer MUST NOT write `kind`, `inReplyTo` or
  `writtenAt` unless the room's current profile lists it; absent means
  none. Set by a curate/admin member once the room's readers, profile
  readers included, accept them. This replaces the SHOULD NOT and the
  "a writer cannot check" text. RoomProfile is referenced by $ref from
  rooms/keys/profile/{read,write}/0.1, so the member is added in place,
  additively, with no new task version.

Libraries regenerated.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(rooms): answer Keyring's review — editedAt, withdrawals, tombstones, reaction values, seal/0.3 and list/0.6

SealedRecordBody (rooms/_shared 0.1 and 0.2, in place, additive):
untitled no-kind records MAY join a conversation as messages; a message's
body is plain text; editedAt marks edits; a new version keeps kind and a
reaction's inReplyTo; messages are withdrawn by an empty version from
their author; tombstones place by what the reader held; reaction values
are NFC-normalised without VS15/VS16, 64 code points, one line;
duplicate reactions reuse a key; only the author withdraws; removed
members' reactions keep counting; an author whose DID does not resolve
MAY be shown as an unverifiable placeholder; a reply's target changed
only when its content did. recordMembers gains editedAt, the out-of-band
readiness decision, the rollout order with the owner's key holder, and
epoch freshness.

rooms/keys/seal/0.3 accepts the new members under signAsPrincipal, so
trust-task-discovery can say a key holder will seal them.
rooms/records/list/0.6 serves kind on open rooms (RecordMetadataV3).
rooms/keys/act/0.11 adds list/0.6. put/0.5 gains editedAt and the
rewrite, withdrawal and replacement rules.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(rooms): host-stamped createdAt for backdating, open-room host refusal of another author's rewrite, plain text for untitled messages

rooms/records/list/0.6 rows (RecordMetadataV3) gain createdAt on every
tier: when the host stored the record's first version, unchanged by
edits and curation, omitted for records stored before a host kept it.
Readers compare writtenAt with it: more than five minutes after is
implausible, and more than 24 hours before MUST be ordered by createdAt
and shown as arriving later than it claims; without it they fall back
to updatedAt and the existing MAY. put/0.5 Host item 16 records it.

put/0.5 Host item 15: on an open room a host MAY refuse, with the
standard permissionDenied, a new version of a message or reaction by
anyone but its original author. attributed and private cannot: kind is
sealed and must not be copied into the clear, so the reader rules are
the defence there.

An untitled record without kind that a reader shows as a message has
its body rendered as plain text; shown as a note, markdown.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(rooms): createdBy, image size and preview, reaction change, arrival order; get/0.3, browse/0.4 and read/0.2 with batch reads

RecordMetadataV3 gains createdBy: the author of the record's first
version as the host recorded it, on open and attributed only (put/0.5
Host item 17). Readers use it to apply the rewrite-by-another-member
rules to a record they see for the first time.

rooms/records/get/0.3 adds createdAt and createdBy (not committed).
rooms/keys/browse/0.4 passes RecordMetadataV3 rows through from
list/0.6. rooms/keys/read/0.2 passes createdAt and createdBy through from
get/0.3 and reads up to 32 keys in one request, each answered on its own
(notAttempted when the recipient's response bound is reached).
rooms/keys/act/0.11 adds get/0.3.

FileManifest gains optional width, height and an 8 KiB raster preview,
advisory and gated by recordMembers. A new non-empty value on a
reaction changes it; a reader MAY order by createdAt; a reaction's
normal form is for comparing only; a message with a file and no body
has no caption; a reader follows a URL only when the member asks and
confirms.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(rooms): verify a version's proof against the author's DID document at the host's bodyStoredAt

RecordMetadataV3, rooms/records/get/0.3 and rooms/keys/read/0.2 gain
bodyStoredAt on every tier: when the host stored the body the current
version carries. A curation leaves it unchanged; for the first version it
equals createdAt. put/0.5 Host item 16 records it; it is not committed.

SealedRecordBody reading rule (2) verifies the current version's proof
against the author's DID document as it stood at bodyStoredAt — resolved
as of that time for a method with history, the current document
otherwise or when bodyStoredAt is absent, where a failing proof is shown
as the unverifiable-author placeholder, never dropped. A key rotated away
before bodyStoredAt cannot sign a version that verifies.

FileManifest drops the dependentRequired on width/height, which the
published-schemas check refuses on a released shape; the pairing is
prose.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat: verify network answers (vti-vtn answer proofs)
body:
Builds against the VTI crates from release #2438: `vti-vtn` 0.4, `vti-common` 0.57, `vta-sdk` 0.81, `vti-trust-task-server` 0.3, `vti-oob-server` 0.2 and `vti-secrets` 0.30. `vti-specs-vtn` 0.2 and `vti-specs-core` 0.4 already match.

The network already signs every Trust Task answer for `authentication`. With OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2439, `vti-vtn`'s client verifies that signature, and here every client the VTN and the NNM use does.

- **`vtn-service`:**
  - `Network::client` verifies through the network's own resolver. That covers answers from a parent network (memberships), a member network (`vtn/relay/deliver`) and federated search.
  - `VtaKeyResolver` is now a re-export of `vti_vtn::resolve::VmKeyResolver`, the shared copy of what this crate kept.
- **`nnm`:**
  - Every admin command checks that the answer is signed by the network DID recorded in the profile.
  - New global `--resolver-url`. Without it, `nnm` resolves DIDs directly, as `vtn` does when `resolver_url` is unset.
- **Docs:** `trust-tasks.md` says answers are signed and verified, that an unsigned refusal is still a refusal, and that an answer authenticates only itself.
- **Tests:**
  - The cascade tests' client verifies with `VtaKeyResolver::offline()`. So the nested-network tests now check real signed answers between networks.
  - fmt and clippy are clean, and all 23 tests pass.
