title: vtc-service-v0.22.0
body:
### Added

- **rate-limit**: VTA and VTC limits run on affinidi-rate-limit ([#2414](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2414))

* feat(rate-limit)!: VTA and VTC limits run on affinidi-rate-limit

  The per-IP limits and the trusted-proxy client-address rule now come from
  affinidi-rate-limit, the crate the mediator, the DID resolver cache and the
  DID hosting service use, rather than three separate copies of the rule.

  - vti-common's TrustedProxyKeyExtractor delegates to the crate's
    ClientIpExtractor. Its constructor now returns a Result: a range covering
    every address (0.0.0.0/0, ::/0) is refused.
  - The VTA's limiters run on the crate with the same quotas, runtime quota
    swaps and 429 contract.
  - The VTC's unauthenticated limiter is the crate's layer, sharing one
    budget with the Trust Task admission limits, which also run on the crate.

  Behaviour changes. An X-Forwarded-For chain from a trusted proxy that
  cannot be read (a malformed entry, more than 64 entries) is refused with
  400 instead of being charged to the proxy, which gave its sender a second
  bucket and hid a misbehaving proxy. trust_xff_cidrs refuses 0.0.0.0/0 and
  ::/0 at load, on the VTA and the VTC. The VTC's sign-in and room limiters
  refuse a new address once 10,000 are live, where they used to sweep and
  grow. The VTC's unauthenticated 429 no longer carries tower_governor's
  informational x-ratelimit-after header; Retry-After is unchanged.

- **boards**: Closing a board ends its voting; delete closed boards, keeping tombstones for a set retention (VTI-BRD-005 – 008) ([#2444](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2444))

Closing a board (open → closed, or straight to archived) now ends the
  voting on it (VTI-BRD-006): each idea's election open for voting is
  closed early, so its count is final; one not yet open, or not yet
  registered, is cancelled and its idea not selected; one whose manifest
  does not allow closing early runs on, and the close answers which
  (`closing.runningToClose`). The board is stored closed first; each end
  is recorded on its election (`ElectionRecord::pending_end`) before the
  ballot box is asked, asked at once in the background, and retried by
  the elections sweeper — its one retry owner — until answered. The
  facilitator's request never waits for the ballot box. A closed board
  opens no election (VTI-BRD-005). Every board election is opened with
  `allowEarlyClose: true`, and a template stating `false` is
  `templateInvalid` (VTI-BRD-030); the console and `cnm boards init`
  starter templates allow it.

  `vtc/boards/delete/0.1` (VTI-BRD-007, VTI-BRD-008): vtc.boards.manage
  unqualified and a step-up bound to the request, spent only after every
  check passed; a board that is open is `notClosed`, one with an election
  still running `electionsRunning`. Audited before anything goes. Removes
  the board, its ideas and notes, and each election's record and ticket
  rows; each election keeps a `Tombstone` — identifier, manifest digest,
  kept board heads, never title, roll or tickets — for
  `[boards] tombstone_retention` (days, default 365; 0 keeps none;
  "forever"). The sweeper removes tombstones past their retention.

  - cnm: `boards delete <id> --reason`, `boards close` prints how the
    voting ended; refusals print the fix (close first, which elections
    run, the passkey gesture).
  - console: "Close and end voting", the closing summary in the toast,
    and "Delete board" (closed boards, board managers only) with the
    title typed, a reason, and the bound passkey gesture.
  - vtc-client: `boards_delete`. vta-sdk: the delete schemas in OpenAPI.
  - Pins vtc/boards/delete/0.1 and the updated vtc/boards/update/0.1.
  - docs/03-vtc/boards.md: closing, archiving, deleting, retention.

- **console**: Group elections by the board they came from ([#2445](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2445))

A community board opens one election per accepted idea, so a busy board
  buries the community's own polls in a flat list. The console's Elections
  page and the member portal's now show stand-alone elections first, then
  one collapsible group per board, headed by its title, the count and (in
  the console) a stage summary such as "1 taking tickets · 1 voting", with
  a link to the board. Rows in a board's group show the idea's title
  without the generated identifier. The console adds a filter: all
  elections, stand-alone only, or one board.

  No wire change. An election a board opens is named
  `board.<boardId>.<ideaId>` (VTI-BRD-031); `lib/election-origin.ts`, a
  pure helper both bundles import, reads that and nothing else, so an id
  that only resembles it stays stand-alone. Titles come from
  `vtc/boards/list` — the console's signed read, the portal's own. A board
  the list does not name is "Deleted board" in the console and "A board
  no longer shown" in the portal (an archived board is hidden from
  members, not deleted); when the list cannot be read at all, each board
  is named by its identifier ("Board ff-8cTg0…") and the page still
  renders. The portal adds nothing about tickets or votes (VTI-VOT-001).

- **portal**: A cleaner member home with live status per service ([#2440](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2440))

The member portal's home had grown into a grid of uneven cards, each a
  paragraph and a button. It is now:

  - one profile header: picture, greeting, status, role, member since, how
    the member signed in, their DID (copyable) and what other members see
    of their card;
  - "Needs your attention": open voting, tickets not yet taken, boards
    taking proposals, room offers waiting, a card with no name - each a
    link to where the member acts on it, shown only when there is one;
  - uniform tiles for Members, Groups, Boards, Elections, Data rooms and
    Repositories, each with a live status line;
  - passkeys under "Sign-in and security".

  Every status is read with the same query (key and function) as the page
  its tile opens, so the page shows what the tile said without asking
  again. Nothing on the home page prompts the wallet: it calls only the
  wallet's `rooms.list`, `rooms.offers` and `elections.list`, which never
  open a window. A passkey session, which holds no delegated key, is told
  to sign in with the wallet rather than shown an error.

- **vti-vtn**: Verify the network's proof on every Trust Task answer ([#2439](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2439))

A client accepts a #response only with the network DID's valid
  authentication proof (ClientError::Unverified otherwise), and sends no
  task without a resolver (VtnClient::verifying). New `resolve` feature:
  VmKeyResolver, the purpose-checking DID resolver the VTC, the VTN and
  the NNM share. The VTC verifies every network answer; an unverified one
  is a mismatch.

- **discovery**: Answer trust-task-discovery 0.4 and advertise the expiry horizon ([#2437](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2437))

The VTA, the VTC and the witness answer trust-task-discovery/0.4
  (trust-tasks-tf #1030, trust-tasks-rs 0.37.2). Its acceptance window carries
  the thirty-day expiry horizon up to which a stated expiresAt is honoured
  (VTI-OPS-028), so a sender can state an expiry within it instead of issuing a
  new attempt every max_age (VTI-TRN-047).

  AcceptanceWindow gains expiry_horizon. VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW sets it to
  EXPIRY_HORIZON, and freshness_policy applies it, so the advertised horizon is
  the applied one by construction. Each node's test reads the horizon back out
  of its own answer and checks it against the spine's policy.

  The superseded 0.3 is still answered, with the same list and a window without
  the horizon, for the clients that still ask it (the SDK, the console and the
  git-ns bridge probe).



### Fixed

- **portal**: Offer a board vote by the idea's election, not the board's window ([#2446](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2446))

#2433 held the vote button back until the board's `voting.opensAt`. But an
  idea's election keeps the window it was registered with: an idea accepted
  before a facilitator brought the board's voting window forward still
  opens on its old date, and the board then reads "Voting" while the
  member's VTA refuses the cast as `notOpen`.

  The portal now reads whether voting is open from the idea's own
  election (`election.state`): `registered` / `registration` take tickets
  but no ballot. The date shown is the board's `voting.opensAt` while that
  is still ahead; otherwise "Voting on this idea hasn't opened yet", since
  the board does not carry the election's own window.

- **console**: Theme deciding pages, keep only their decision surfaces out of reach ([#2442](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2442))

vtc/community/theme/show/0.1 client item 2 requires every surface on which
  a person decides, approves, declines, consents, signs or is warned to be
  isolated from the theme. The console met it by isolating four whole pages
  (Actions, Join requests, Members, Repos), so their headers, filters, tables
  and empty states were drawn in the default look on a themed page: a box of
  another colour from the breadcrumb down, and a list with nothing to decide
  on it isolated anyway.

  The isolation now sits on the decision surfaces themselves:

  - Actions: each action card (verified summary, match code, the decision).
  - Join requests: the vetting card and the Decide card.
  - Members: the add-member form, entries without a membership, removed
    members; on a member, notes, step-up passkeys, approver devices, the
    vetter role and admin actions.
  - Repos: every form dialog and the signing dialog, and the break-glass and
    departed-grant warnings.

  Confirm dialogs, banners and the step-up page were already isolated. The
  page around a surface takes the theme. That is safe because the theme
  profile admits colours, fonts, borders, radii and gradients only - no
  position, z-index, margin or content - so a themed ancestor cannot cover,
  move or relabel an isolated surface.

  `Protected` gains a `card` ground: the card's colour, rounded to the
  console's `.card` and laid out as a grid, so a protected card shows no
  square corners and fills a stretched row. While a community theme is drawn,
  a protected card is outlined and marked "Protected area - standard look,
  not the community theme", from inside the isolation so no theme can hide
  it; without a theme nothing is marked.

  Fixes, both found while moving the boundary:

  - A protected surface ignored a pinned light / dark. The production build
    lowers light-dark() into custom-property toggles that the re-scoped
    :root rule resets to light inside the isolation, and only [data-theme]
    flips them back - so Dark pinned on a light OS drew every protected
    surface light (on main: the Actions, Join requests, Members and Repos
    pages, and every confirm dialog). The isolation's root now mirrors
    <html data-theme>, followed live. Tests and the dev server never lower
    light-dark(), which is why nothing caught it.
  - Protected portals its children a render after it mounts, so a useModal
    above it ran before the dialog existed and never moved focus in. The
    Repos dialogs wrap their surface in Protected instead.

title: spec(rooms): a removed member can rejoin — prior group state is a prior membership, not a join, corrected in place (#1031)
body:
spec(rooms): a removed member can rejoin — prior group state is a prior membership, not a join, corrected in place (#1031)

* spec(rooms): a removed member can rejoin — prior group state is a prior membership, not a join, corrected in place

rooms/keys/welcome 0.1 required a recipient holding group state for
`roomId` for the member to answer `alreadyJoined`, and in the same
paragraph said rejoining is "a removal followed by a fresh invitation".
A member removed by a commit keeps its group state — rooms/keys/open 0.2
and rooms/keys/file-key 0.2 answer `unknownEpoch` with reason `removed`
from it — so the MUST refused the very Welcome the paragraph said
rejoining uses, and a removed member could never be admitted again.
rooms/owner/group/remove 0.4 and rooms/owner/revoke 0.1 both describe
re-admission as fresh credentials plus a new leaf. Welcome's Retention
section also said to discard the state on removal, contradicting the
`removed` reason and file-key's "removal is forward-only".

- welcome 0.1: state from which a processed commit removed the member is
  a prior membership. A recipient holding only prior memberships MUST
  process a Welcome under a valid, unconsumed invitation and MUST keep
  each prior membership, unmerged, for records sealed under the epochs
  it covers (subject to the epoch floor). `alreadyJoined` is for current
  state only. Prior memberships cover [join epoch, removal epoch) and
  never overlap.
- open 0.2: the record's epoch chooses the state — current when E is at
  or after its join epoch, else the prior membership covering E; E in a
  gap between a removal and the next join is `unknownEpoch` / `removed`
  with that `removedAtEpoch`. Never a retry under another state.
- file-key 0.2: the same selection for `open`; a principal holding only
  prior memberships answers `seal` with `noGroup`.
- group/remove 0.4: re-admission points at welcome's rule.

No wire change: no member, code or reason added or removed. All four
specifications are `draft`, so the prose correction is made in place
(SPEC §5.2). Regenerated bindings change only error-code doc text.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(rooms): a Welcome whose tree lacks the member's earlier leaf is evidence of a removal

#1031 let a removed member rejoin only when its key holder had processed
the commit that removed it. A member idle at its removal never applies that
commit, and cannot fetch it afterwards: a host serves `rooms/epoch/commits`
under a `read` grant the removal withdrew. It reaches the re-admitting
Welcome holding stale state at some epoch h that no processed commit ended,
and so answered `alreadyJoined` — the case #1031 set out to fix.

- welcome 0.1: a recipient recognises a prior membership by a removal it
  processed OR by the Welcome itself. It processes the Welcome without
  keeping the result and looks in its ratchet tree for the member's earlier
  leaf, identified by that leaf's signature key or leaf node, never by the
  member's identifier (the re-admitted leaf names the same member under a
  new key). Still in the tree: `alreadyJoined`, keeping nothing and
  consuming neither the invitation nor the KeyPackage. Absent: the member
  was removed at some r, h < r <= j, and the state is a prior membership
  whose removal epoch is not yet known. A recipient MUST NOT wait for or
  fetch the removing commit before joining, and a client need not apply
  commits first. Such a membership covers its join epoch through h for
  certain; the recipient MAY apply commits to it until the removing one
  fixes r.
- open 0.2, file-key 0.2: until the removing commit is applied to that
  state, an epoch above h and below the next join is `notDelivered` with
  that state's `heldEpoch`, never `removed`; once applied, it opens below r
  and is `removed` in [r, next join), as for a known removal.

No wire change: no member, code or reason added or removed. All three
specifications are `draft`, so the correction is made in place (SPEC
§5.2). The regenerated Rust binding changes only `alreadyJoined`'s doc text.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(rooms): a Welcome for another MLS group is no evidence of a removal

The absent-leaf rule in welcome 0.1 *Rejoining after a removal* read the
Welcome's ratchet tree as evidence that the held state ended. A Welcome for
a different MLS group has none of that state's leaves by construction, so
it would retire current state on no evidence at all.

- welcome 0.1: before treating an absent leaf as a removal, the recipient
  MUST check that the Welcome is for the same MLS group (equal group ids).
  Otherwise it answers `welcomeInvalid`, keeps nothing the Welcome formed,
  changes nothing it holds, and consumes neither the invitation nor the
  KeyPackage. `welcomeInvalid`'s meaning names the case.

No wire change: the code already exists; only its description grows. The
spec is `draft`, so the correction is made in place (SPEC §5.2). The
regenerated Rust binding changes only `welcomeInvalid`'s doc text.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(rooms): a re-admitting Welcome must be for the member's own group, whatever the evidence

80a9a6e26 required equal MLS group ids only where the evidence of a removal
was the Welcome's own tree. A removal the recipient processed is no reason
either to take a Welcome for another group as the room's current group.

- welcome 0.1 *Rejoining after a removal*: a new paragraph, *Same group,
  whatever the evidence*. Under either piece of evidence, before the held
  state becomes a prior membership and the Welcome's group the current
  state, the recipient MUST check the group ids are equal; otherwise it
  answers `welcomeInvalid`, keeps nothing the Welcome formed, changes
  nothing it holds, and consumes neither the invitation nor the KeyPackage.
  The absent-leaf bullet now points at it.

No wire change, and no binding change: `welcomeInvalid`'s meaning already
names a Welcome for another group. Draft, corrected in place (SPEC §5.2).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: vta-config-v0.34.0
body:
### Added

- **rate-limit**: VTA and VTC limits run on affinidi-rate-limit ([#2414](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2414))

* feat(rate-limit)!: VTA and VTC limits run on affinidi-rate-limit

  The per-IP limits and the trusted-proxy client-address rule now come from
  affinidi-rate-limit, the crate the mediator, the DID resolver cache and the
  DID hosting service use, rather than three separate copies of the rule.

  - vti-common's TrustedProxyKeyExtractor delegates to the crate's
    ClientIpExtractor. Its constructor now returns a Result: a range covering
    every address (0.0.0.0/0, ::/0) is refused.
  - The VTA's limiters run on the crate with the same quotas, runtime quota
    swaps and 429 contract.
  - The VTC's unauthenticated limiter is the crate's layer, sharing one
    budget with the Trust Task admission limits, which also run on the crate.

  Behaviour changes. An X-Forwarded-For chain from a trusted proxy that
  cannot be read (a malformed entry, more than 64 entries) is refused with
  400 instead of being charged to the proxy, which gave its sender a second
  bucket and hid a misbehaving proxy. trust_xff_cidrs refuses 0.0.0.0/0 and
  ::/0 at load, on the VTA and the VTC. The VTC's sign-in and room limiters
  refuse a new address once 10,000 are live, where they used to sweep and
  grow. The VTC's unauthenticated 429 no longer carries tower_governor's
  informational x-ratelimit-after header; Retry-After is unchanged.

title: cnm-cli-v0.47.0
body:
### Added

- **boards**: Closing a board ends its voting; delete closed boards, keeping tombstones for a set retention (VTI-BRD-005 – 008) ([#2444](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2444))

Closing a board (open → closed, or straight to archived) now ends the
  voting on it (VTI-BRD-006): each idea's election open for voting is
  closed early, so its count is final; one not yet open, or not yet
  registered, is cancelled and its idea not selected; one whose manifest
  does not allow closing early runs on, and the close answers which
  (`closing.runningToClose`). The board is stored closed first; each end
  is recorded on its election (`ElectionRecord::pending_end`) before the
  ballot box is asked, asked at once in the background, and retried by
  the elections sweeper — its one retry owner — until answered. The
  facilitator's request never waits for the ballot box. A closed board
  opens no election (VTI-BRD-005). Every board election is opened with
  `allowEarlyClose: true`, and a template stating `false` is
  `templateInvalid` (VTI-BRD-030); the console and `cnm boards init`
  starter templates allow it.

  `vtc/boards/delete/0.1` (VTI-BRD-007, VTI-BRD-008): vtc.boards.manage
  unqualified and a step-up bound to the request, spent only after every
  check passed; a board that is open is `notClosed`, one with an election
  still running `electionsRunning`. Audited before anything goes. Removes
  the board, its ideas and notes, and each election's record and ticket
  rows; each election keeps a `Tombstone` — identifier, manifest digest,
  kept board heads, never title, roll or tickets — for
  `[boards] tombstone_retention` (days, default 365; 0 keeps none;
  "forever"). The sweeper removes tombstones past their retention.

  - cnm: `boards delete <id> --reason`, `boards close` prints how the
    voting ended; refusals print the fix (close first, which elections
    run, the passkey gesture).
  - console: "Close and end voting", the closing summary in the toast,
    and "Delete board" (closed boards, board managers only) with the
    title typed, a reason, and the bound passkey gesture.
  - vtc-client: `boards_delete`. vta-sdk: the delete schemas in OpenAPI.
  - Pins vtc/boards/delete/0.1 and the updated vtc/boards/update/0.1.
  - docs/03-vtc/boards.md: closing, archiving, deleting, retention.

title: fix(rooms): verify every record the records pane shows
body:
## What

The console's records pane (`manager/panes/rooms-records.tsx`) now verifies every sealed record it opens before showing any of it, following `SealedRecordBody`'s *Reading* rule (`rooms/_shared/0.2/room.schema.json`):

- the author's proof, for `assertionMethod`;
- the signed room, key and version — the version the agent reports the body opened at (`ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].sealedAt`) for a curated record, else the record's own;
- on an attributed room, that the host's author (from the read, and from the listing for the same version) is the signer.

A body that fails shows none of its content, only that it could not be verified and which check failed. "The signed record" and "Signed by …" appear only when verification succeeded, and the author shown for an opened record is the verified signer (the host's record on an open room), never an unchecked body member. The host-listing verdict (Merkle trace / count / prior roots) keeps its own wording, separate from the author check.

## The verifier and its member list

- The pane reuses `verifyRecordBody`. It moved from `rooms/files.ts` into `rooms/record-body.ts` and is exported from `@openvtc/pnm-core/rooms`, because the console may not import `rooms/files` (its `rooms/keys/file-key` URI is confined to the offscreen bundle by CI). `rooms/files` re-exports it, so the offscreen document and file engine are unchanged.
- The allow-list now matches the released `SealedRecordBody` members exactly (`RECORD_BODY_MEMBERS`): `basis`, `confidence`, `evidence`, `validFor`, `validUntil` and `roomProfile` were added beside the existing nine, each with the schema's shape checks; a profile record carrying a record's members is refused. Draft members from trust-tasks-tf #1027 (`kind`, `inReplyTo`, `writtenAt`, `editedAt`) are not added. Provenance types come from the generated `rooms/records/put/0.4` module.
- `signRecordBody` writes the new members.
- `readView` (`room-page-offscreen.ts`) now checks against the sealed-at version too (`readSealedVersion`), so a curated record reads there as well.

## Tests

- `packages/core/tests/rooms.record-body.mjs`: the allow-list against each released member (an accepted value and the values the schema refuses), draft members refused, profile exclusivity, `signRecordBody` round trip, `readSealedVersion`.
- `packages/extension/tests/rooms-records.render.test.mts`: a valid record shows "signed" with the signed author; a bad proof, an unsigned body, a mismatched host author, a mismatched listing author, and a body signed for another key, version or room each show no content; a curated record verifies at its sealed-at version; a record carrying provenance members reads. Existing render tests now use signed bodies.
- `rooms-record-actions.render.test.mts`: notes are signed by `did:key` identities so the pane can verify them.

Local results (Node 24, cold `npm ci`):

- `npm run lint`: clean
- `npm run build`: clean
- `npm test`: tsp-js 123/123, core 1171/1171, extension 1485/1485, demo-rp 6/6, reviewer-demo 9/9
- `node packages/extension/scripts/check-task-versions.mjs`: OK, 444 task URIs at their pinned versions
- CI's bundle assertions (run locally after build + package): 13/13 pass

title: fix(rooms): verify every record the records pane shows (#415)
body:
fix(rooms): verify every record the records pane shows (#415)

The console's records pane read `rooms/keys/read` bodies without verifying
them, labelled any sealed body "The signed record", and fell back to the
body's `author` member when the host gave none. It now applies the
`SealedRecordBody` Reading rule (rooms/_shared/0.2) before showing any member
of a sealed record: the author's proof for assertionMethod, the signed room,
key and version (the version the agent reports the body opened at, for a
curated record), and on an attributed room that the host's author, from the
read and from the listing, is the signer. A body that fails shows none of its
content and says it could not be verified; "signed" is said only of a body
that passed, the author shown is the verified signer, and the author check is
worded apart from the host-listing verdict.

The pane reuses `verifyRecordBody`, moved to `rooms/record-body` so the
console can import it without `rooms/files` (whose file-key URI is confined to
the offscreen bundle); `rooms/files` still re-exports it. Its member list now
matches the released `SealedRecordBody` exactly: `basis`, `confidence`,
`evidence`, `validFor`, `validUntil` and `roomProfile` are accepted with the
schema's shape checks, and a profile record carrying a record's members is
refused. `readView` in the page bridge now verifies against the sealed-at
version as well.

* feat(rate-limit)!: VTA and VTC limits run on affinidi-rate-limit

  The per-IP limits and the trusted-proxy client-address rule now come from

    ClientIpExtractor. Its constructor now returns a Result: a range covering
    every address (0.0.0.0/0, ::/0) is refused.
  - The VTA's limiters run on the crate with the same quotas, runtime quota
    swaps and 429 contract.
  - The VTC's unauthenticated limiter is the crate's layer, sharing one
    budget with the Trust Task admission limits, which also run on the crate.

  Behaviour changes. An X-Forwarded-For chain from a trusted proxy that
  cannot be read (a malformed entry, more than 64 entries) is refused with
  400 instead of being charged to the proxy, which gave its sender a second
  bucket and hid a misbehaving proxy. trust_xff_cidrs refuses 0.0.0.0/0 and
  ::/0 at load, on the VTA and the VTC. The VTC's sign-in and room limiters
  refuse a new address once 10,000 are live, where they used to sweep and
  grow. The VTC's unauthenticated 429 no longer carries tower_governor's
  informational x-ratelimit-after header; Retry-After is unchanged.

- **discovery**: Answer trust-task-discovery 0.4 and advertise the expiry horizon ([#2437](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2437))

The VTA, the VTC and the witness answer trust-task-discovery/0.4
  (trust-tasks-tf #1030, trust-tasks-rs 0.37.2). Its acceptance window carries
  the thirty-day expiry horizon up to which a stated expiresAt is honoured
  (VTI-OPS-028), so a sender can state an expiry within it instead of issuing a
  new attempt every max_age (VTI-TRN-047).

  AcceptanceWindow gains expiry_horizon. VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW sets it to
  EXPIRY_HORIZON, and freshness_policy applies it, so the advertised horizon is
  the applied one by construction. Each node's test reads the horizon back out
  of its own answer and checks it against the spine's policy.

  The superseded 0.3 is still answered, with the same list and a window without
  the horizon, for the clients that still ask it (the SDK, the console and the
  git-ns bridge probe).

title: feat(service): every vti-secrets backend (keyring by default)
body:
`vtn` was built with no `vti-secrets` backend features, so only `plaintext` and `encrypted_file` worked. `backend = "keyring"`, which `vtn-setup.example.toml` suggests, failed because keyring wasn't compiled in, and so did every cloud backend. Now every `vti-secrets` backend can be built into `vtn`, set up the way the VTC does it.

**`vtn-service` features**

| Feature | `backend` |
|---|---|
| `keyring` (**default**) | `keyring`: macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, Windows Credential Manager |
| `aws-secrets` | `aws` |
| `gcp-secrets` | `gcp` |
| `azure-secrets` | `azure` |
| `vault-secrets` | `vault` |
| `k8s-secrets` | `kubernetes` |
| `tpm` | a TPM key-encryption key for `encrypted_file`. Linux only, needs the system `libtss2`. |
| `all-secrets` | all of the above except `tpm` |

- **Always built in:** `plaintext` (dev only, with `allow_plaintext = true`) and `encrypted_file`. `config_seed` is still refused by `vtn setup`.
- **Keyring at startup:** `vtn` registers the OS credential store before opening any secret store. It uses `vta_sdk::keyring_init::warn_store_unavailable("vtn")`, as `vtc` and `vta` do. A host without a credential store, like a headless Linux server, still starts with a warning; only `backend = "keyring"` then fails.
- **Lockfile:** `smallvec` is pinned to 1.15.2, as in VTI's lockfile. `kube` 4.2 depends on `serde-saphyr`, which requires `smallvec` below 1.16, so `k8s-secrets` can't resolve otherwise. The lockfile now also records every optional backend's dependencies (about 1,700 lines). A default build compiles only keyring, and D-Bus was already in the build through `affinidi-tdk-common`.
- **Docs:** the README has a new "Where the keys are kept" section: a table of backends, the build feature each needs, and `cargo install --path vtn-service --features all-secrets`. `vtn-setup.example.toml` lists the alternatives, with `encrypted_file` and plaintext shown as examples.
- **CI:** a new clippy step builds `vtn-service --features all-secrets`.

**Checks**

- clippy is clean for the default features, `--no-default-features`, `--features all-secrets` and the workspace.
- `cargo deny check` passes with all features. Its one warning (an ignored advisory that no longer matches) is already there on main.
- fmt is clean and all 24 tests pass.
- Not tested: actually storing a seed in each cloud backend.

The board is stored closed first; each end is recorded on its election (`ElectionRecord::pending_end`) before the ballot box is asked, asked at once in the background, and retried by the elections sweeper — its one retry owner — until answered. Removes the board, its ideas and notes, and each election's record and ticket rows; each election keeps a `Tombstone` — identifier, manifest digest, kept board heads, never title, roll or tickets — for `[boards] tombstone_retention` (days, default 365; 0 keeps none; "forever"). The sweeper removes tombstones past their retention. - cnm: `boards delete --reason`, `boards close` prints how the voting ended; refusals print the fix (close first, which elections run, the passkey gesture). - console: "Close and end voting", the closing summary in the toast, and "Delete board" (closed boards, board managers only) with the title typed, a reason, and the bound passkey gesture. - vtc-client: `boards_delete`. vta-sdk: the delete schemas in OpenAPI. - Pins vtc/boards/delete/0.1 and the updated vtc/boards/update/0.1. - docs/03-vtc/boards.md: closing, archiving, deleting, retention. - **console**: Group elections by the board they came from ([#2445](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2445)) A community board opens one election per accepted idea, so a busy board buries the community's own polls in a flat list. The console's Elections page and the member portal's now show stand-alone elections first, then one collapsible group per board, headed by its title, the count and (in the console) a stage summary such as "1 taking tickets · 1 voting", with a link to the board. Rows in a board's group show the idea's title without the generated identifier. The console adds a filter: all elections, stand-alone only, or one board. No wire change. An election a board opens is named `board..` (VTI-BRD-031); `lib/election-origin.ts`, a pure helper both bundles import, reads that and nothing else, so an id that only resembles it stays stand-alone. Titles come from `vtc/boards/list` — the console's signed read, the portal's own. A board the list does not name is "Deleted board" in the console and "A board no longer shown" in the portal (an archived board is hidden from members, not deleted); when the list cannot be read at all, each board is named by its identifier ("Board ff-8cTg0…") and the page still renders. The portal adds nothing about tickets or votes (VTI-VOT-001). - **portal**: A cleaner member home with live status per service ([#2440](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2440)) The member portal's home had grown into a grid of uneven cards, each a paragraph and a button. It is now: - one profile header: picture, greeting, status, role, member since, how the member signed in, their DID (copyable) and what other members see of their card; - "Needs your attention": open voting, tickets not yet taken, boards taking proposals, room offers waiting, a card with no name - each a link to where the member acts on it, shown only when there is one; - uniform tiles for Members, Groups, Boards, Elections, Data rooms and Repositories, each with a live status line; - passkeys under "Sign-in and security". Every status is read with the same query (key and function) as the page its tile opens, so the page shows what the tile said without asking again. Nothing on the home page prompts the wallet: it calls only the wallet's `rooms.list`, `rooms.offers` and `elections.list`, which never open a window. A passkey session, which holds no delegated key, is told to sign in with the wallet rather than shown an error. - **vti-vtn**: Verify the network's proof on every Trust Task answer ([#2439](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2439)) A client accepts a #response only with the network DID's valid authentication proof (ClientError::Unverified otherwise), and sends no task without a resolver (VtnClient::verifying). New `resolve` feature: VmKeyResolver, the purpose-checking DID resolver the VTC, the VTN and the NNM share. The VTC verifies every network answer; an unverified one is a mismatch. - **discovery**: Answer trust-task-discovery 0.4 and advertise the expiry horizon ([#2437](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2437)) The VTA, the VTC and the witness answer trust-task-discovery/0.4 (trust-tasks-tf #1030, trust-tasks-rs 0.37.2). Its acceptance window carries the thirty-day expiry horizon up to which a stated expiresAt is honoured (VTI-OPS-028), so a sender can state an expiry within it instead of issuing a new attempt every max_age (VTI-TRN-047). AcceptanceWindow gains expiry_horizon. VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW sets it to EXPIRY_HORIZON, and freshness_policy applies it, so the advertised horizon is the applied one by construction. Each node's test reads the horizon back out of its own answer and checks it against the spine's policy. The superseded 0.3 is still answered, with the same list and a window without the horizon, for the clients that still ask it (the SDK, the console and the git-ns bridge probe). ### Fixed - **portal**: Offer a board vote by the idea's election, not the board's window ([#2446](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2446)) #2433 held the vote button back until the board's `voting.opensAt`. But an idea's election keeps the window it was registered with: an idea accepted before a facilitator brought the board's voting window forward still opens on its old date, and the board then reads "Voting" while the member's VTA refuses the cast as `notOpen`. The portal now reads whether voting is open from the idea's own election (`election.state`): `registered` / `registration` take tickets but no ballot. The date shown is the board's `voting.opensAt` while that is still ahead; otherwise "Voting on this idea hasn't opened yet", since the board does not carry the election's own window. - **console**: Theme deciding pages, keep only their decision surfaces out of reach ([#2442](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2442)) vtc/community/theme/show/0.1 client item 2 requires every surface on which a person decides, approves, declines, consents, signs or is warned to be isolated from the theme. The console met it by isolating four whole pages (Actions, Join requests, Members, Repos), so their headers, filters, tables and empty states were drawn in the default look on a themed page: a box of another colour from the breadcrumb down, and a list with nothing to decide on it isolated anyway. The isolation now sits on the decision surfaces themselves: - Actions: each action card (verified summary, match code, the decision). - Join requests: the vetting card and the Decide card. - Members: the add-member form, entries without a membership, removed members; on a member, notes, step-up passkeys, approver devices, the vetter role and admin actions. - Repos: every form dialog and the signing dialog, and the break-glass and departed-grant warnings. Confirm dialogs, banners and the step-up page were already isolated. The page around a surface takes the theme. That is safe because the theme profile admits colours, fonts, borders, radii and gradients only - no position, z-index, margin or content - so a themed ancestor cannot cover, move or relabel an isolated surface. `Protected` gains a `card` ground: the card's colour, rounded to the console's `.card` and laid out as a grid, so a protected card shows no square corners and fills a stretched row. While a community theme is drawn, a protected card is outlined and marked "Protected area - standard look, not the community theme", from inside the isolation so no theme can hide it; without a theme nothing is marked. Fixes, both found while moving the boundary: - A protected surface ignored a pinned light / dark. The production build lowers light-dark() into custom-property toggles that the re-scoped :root rule resets to light inside the isolation, and only [data-theme] flips them back - so Dark pinned on a light OS drew every protected surface light (on main: the Actions, Join requests, Members and Repos pages, and every confirm dialog). The isolation's root now mirrors , followed live. Tests and the dev server never lower light-dark(), which is why nothing caught it. - Protected portals its children a render after it mounts, so a useModal above it ran before the dialog existed and never moved focus in. The Repos dialogs wrap their surface in Protected instead.

title: feat(rate-limit)!: VTA and VTC limits run on affinidi-rate-limit
body:
## Why

The VTA, the VTC (through `vti-common`), the mediator, the DID resolver cache and the DID hosting service each had their own copy of the trusted-proxy `X-Forwarded-For` rule. `affinidi-rate-limit` 0.1.4 now carries it, together with handler-side limits on any key and per-period quotas (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#982). This PR moves the VTA's and VTC's limits onto it. affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#329 does the same for the DID hosting service.

## What changes

- **`vti-common`:** `TrustedProxyKeyExtractor` delegates to the crate's `ClientIpExtractor`, and `clients()` exposes it. **Breaking:** `new` now returns a `Result`, because a range covering every address is refused.
- **VTA:** the five per-IP limiters and the per-step Trust Task limits run on `RateLimiterState::per_period`, with unchanged quotas. They share one extractor. Runtime quota swaps and the 429 contract (`x-rate-limit-source: vta`, `x-rate-limit-scope`, the legacy header) are unchanged.
- **VTC:** the unauthenticated chain uses the crate's layer at the same quota (burst 10, then one every 5 s). It shares its state with `trust_task_admission`, so an address still has one anonymous budget. The admission limits (signed address, signer, sign-in, room) run on the crate too. `vtc-service` no longer depends directly on `governor` or `tower_governor`; `tower_governor` still comes in through `vti-common`'s key extractor.
- **Config:** `trust_xff_cidrs` refuses `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` at load, in `vta-config` and the VTC config. The VTA setup wizard refuses one too.

## Behaviour changes (compared with `main`)

- **Unreadable chain.** An `X-Forwarded-For` chain from a trusted proxy that can't be read (a malformed entry, more than 64 entries) gets a **400** with `x-rate-limit-source` (`vta` or `vtc`) and a JSON body naming the limiter, on every path (VTA, VTC layer, VTC `/v1/trust-tasks`).
  - On `main` it was charged to the proxy's address, which gave its sender a second bucket and hid a misbehaving proxy.
  - The first such chain from a proxy each minute is logged as a warning naming it.
- **No peer address.** A request with no peer address gets a plain-text **403** with `x-rate-limit-source`, instead of a 500. That only happens through a wiring fault; production serves with `ConnectInfo`.
- **Catch-all range.** A `trust_xff_cidrs` range covering every address fails to load.
- **Tracked addresses.** Every per-IP limiter tracks at most 250,000 addresses. While that many are still within their budget, a new address gets a 429 with `Retry-After: 60` rather than the map growing without bound.
- **VTC unauthenticated 429 on the layer path.** It no longer carries tower_governor's informational `x-ratelimit-after` header, and its `message` is the shared limiter's generic text. `Retry-After`, the source header and the body's keys are unchanged.

## Not in this PR

- **GC sweep:** neither service runs the crate's minute-by-minute sweep (`spawn_gc`) yet. Each limiter's memory is bounded by the cap, which governor's maps were not; a sweep would reclaim idle keys sooner. Wiring it into the VTA's quota-swapping buckets needs a decision about which buckets the sweep follows.
- **Duplicate deserializer:** the `trust_xff_cidrs` deserializer is duplicated in `vta-config` and the VTC config. Sharing it through `vti-common` would make `vta-config` pull in the rate-limit stack.
- **`vti-common` key extractor:** its tower_governor `KeyExtractor` impl is now used only by its own tests. Removing it, and the `tower_governor` dependency with it, is a further public-API break, so it's left for a follow-up.

## Tests

- **vti-common:** the 23 extractor tests pass. The two fall-back-to-peer cases now expect the 400.
- **VTA:**
  - Router tests cover the 400, including that the proxy's own bucket isn't charged, and the plain-text 403.
  - The quota tests pin the crate limiter, not tower_governor.
- **VTC:**
  - A test covers the `/v1/trust-tasks` door's 400 and 403.
  - The integration tests `rate_limit_source` and `room_rate_limits` pass.
- **Config:** tests cover refusing catch-all ranges.
- **Library suites:** run for `vta-service`, `vtc-service` and `vta-config`. The one failure, `vti_08_context_create_fits_half_a_default_worker_stack`, overflows its stack on unchanged `main` too.
- **clippy:** the workspace reports nothing in the changed files.

Suggested squash message: this PR's title and the "What changes" and "Behaviour changes" sections. The individual commit messages describe intermediate states.

title: feat(rate-limit)!: VTA and VTC limits run on affinidi-rate-limit (#2414)
body:
feat(rate-limit)!: VTA and VTC limits run on affinidi-rate-limit (#2414)

* feat(rate-limit)!: VTA and VTC limits run on affinidi-rate-limit

The per-IP limits and the trusted-proxy client-address rule now come from
affinidi-rate-limit, the crate the mediator, the DID resolver cache and the
DID hosting service use, rather than three separate copies of the rule.

- vti-common's TrustedProxyKeyExtractor delegates to the crate's
  ClientIpExtractor. Its constructor now returns a Result: a range covering
  every address (0.0.0.0/0, ::/0) is refused.
- The VTA's limiters run on the crate with the same quotas, runtime quota
  swaps and 429 contract.
- The VTC's unauthenticated limiter is the crate's layer, sharing one
  budget with the Trust Task admission limits, which also run on the crate.

Behaviour changes. An X-Forwarded-For chain from a trusted proxy that
cannot be read (a malformed entry, more than 64 entries) is refused with
400 instead of being charged to the proxy, which gave its sender a second
bucket and hid a misbehaving proxy. trust_xff_cidrs refuses 0.0.0.0/0 and
::/0 at load, on the VTA and the VTC. The VTC's sign-in and room limiters
refuse a new address once 10,000 are live, where they used to sweep and
grow. The VTC's unauthenticated 429 no longer carries tower_governor's
informational x-ratelimit-after header; Retry-After is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>

* fix(rate-limit): one refusal shape, no new-address lockout, and review fixes

From the review of moving the VTA and VTC limits onto affinidi-rate-limit:

- A request the per-IP limiters cannot attribute is refused the same way on
  every path, as the shared limiter refuses it: 400 for an unreadable
  X-Forwarded-For chain from a trusted proxy and 403 with no peer address,
  each with x-rate-limit-source (vta or vtc) and a JSON body naming the
  limiter. The VTA and the VTC's /v1/trust-tasks door answered these with a
  plain-text 400, and 500 with no peer. The first unreadable chain from a
  proxy each minute is logged as a warning naming it.
- The VTC's sign-in and room limiters go back to the shared default of
  250,000 tracked addresses. A 10,000 cap let a flood of failing sign-ins
  from rotating IPv6 addresses refuse every new address.
- The VTA setup wizard refuses a trust_xff_cidrs range covering every
  address, rather than writing a config the VTA will not start with.
- Fixes a clippy result_large_err on the VTA limiter's client lookup.
- The VTC no longer depends on governor or tower_governor; the VTA keeps
  governor for its operation budgets only. The VTA's quota tests now pin the
  limiter production builds, not tower_governor. Stale comments in the VTA
  router docs, the Nitro enclave proxy and the VTC error-code census are
  updated.

Every per-IP limiter also now refuses a new address with 429 and
Retry-After: 60 while 250,000 addresses are still within their budget,
rather than growing without bound. The VTC's unauthenticated 429 message is
the shared limiter's generic text on the layer path.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>

* chore(rate-limit): take affinidi-rate-limit 0.1.4 from crates.io

0.1.4 is published, so the temporary [patch.crates-io] entry pointing at the affinidi-tdk-rs branch goes.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>

* fix(rate-limit): final review fixes

- Cargo.lock changes only what the switch needs: affinidi-rate-limit 0.1.4
  and its ipnet dependency, and governor/tower_governor dropped from the
  VTA and VTC. An earlier update had moved syn, base64 and windows-sys to
  older versions for unrelated crates.
- The VTA's limiters share one extractor per trusted-proxy list, so a
  proxy's unreadable chain is warned about once a minute, not once per
  limiter.
- Docs say what the refusals are: the 400 carries a JSON body naming the
  limiter, the 403 for a request with no peer address is plain text with
  x-rate-limit-source. Tests now check the 403 body, and the test that the
  proxy is not charged for a bad chain can fail.
- The layer-4 forwarder warning is back on TrustedProxyKeyExtractor, and
  comments that still named tower-governor describe the limiter in use.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>

* fix(rate-limit): sweep every limiter, key IPv6 per /64, one client rule

Review fixes for the affinidi-rate-limit move.

- Every keyed limiter is now swept of refilled buckets each minute
  (`vti_common::rate_limit::LimiterSweep`), stopping when its owner drops.
  Unswept, a limiter keeps a bucket per key until its 250,000-key cap and
  then refuses every new client, which a stranger cycling addresses could
  reach. This replaces the sign-in and room limiters' 10,000-key pruning.
- An IPv6 client is charged as its /64 (`IPV6_CLIENT_PREFIX`), so one host
  rotating addresses cannot take a bucket per address. Handlers still see
  the address itself (`Client { ip, key }`).
- One resolver for every limiter: `TrustedProxyKeyExtractor::client_of`.
  The tower_governor `KeyExtractor` impl and dependency are gone, as is the
  VTA's process-global extractor cache: each router builds one extractor
  and passes it to its limiters.
- `trust_xff_cidrs` is checked on load by the rule the extractor builds
  with (`deserialize_trusted_proxy_cidrs`, `check_trusted_proxy_cidrs`),
  in vta-config, the VTC config and the setup prompt.
- A zero period no longer turns a limiter off: the VTC's `quota()` refuses
  one and both services assert a built limiter is enabled.
- The VTC unauthenticated chain answers with its own 429 again (limiter
  `unauth`, the route's explanation), from a middleware that charges the
  same state as the Trust Task door. The VTA's unattributable refusals carry
  `x-rate-limit-scope` like its other refusals.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(portal): offer a board vote by the idea's election, not the board's window
body:
#2433 held the vote button back until the board's `voting.opensAt`. But an
idea's election keeps the window it was registered with: an idea accepted
before a facilitator brought the board's voting window forward still
opens on its old date, and the board then reads "Voting" while the
member's VTA refuses the cast as `notOpen`.

The portal now reads whether voting is open from the idea's own
election (`election.state`): `registered` / `registration` take tickets
but no ballot. The date shown is the board's `voting.opensAt` while that
is still ahead; otherwise "Voting on this idea hasn't opened yet", since
the board does not carry the election's own window.

Follows #2433.

## Testing
- `vitest run src/members` (147, one new: the board says voting, the election says registration — no vote offered), `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`

title: feat(collection): claim a persona's collection before connecting it; answer notifications with the VTA's receipt
body:
**Draft until VGI publishes 0.33.0.** This PR depends on `did-git-sign` / `vgi-core` 0.33.0 (OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#197), which is not on crates.io yet. The committed `Cargo.toml` names crates.io versions only. `Cargo.lock` was resolved against a local, uncommitted `[patch]` of that PR, so its two `did-git-sign` / `vgi-core` entries have no `source` line, and CI can't resolve until 0.33.0 is published. After publishing, run `cargo update -p did-git-sign -p vgi-core` and push the lockfile.

## Collection claims (VTI-NTF-080 – 084)

A persona's mediator allows one connection per DID, and the VTA can collect for any persona whose keys it holds. OpenVTC now claims a persona before it connects it.

- **Where the check runs.** It's in `didcomm::add_listener`, so every path that brings a persona socket up goes through it: startup, joins, manual reconnects, the supervisor's rebuilds and the headless commands. It applies to personas of a VTA account, via `ListenerSpec.collection`. BIP32 accounts and R-DID (`did:peer`) listeners claim nothing.
- **Claim before connecting.** OpenVTC sends `vta/collection/claim/0.1` for the persona DID in its trust context, asking for 86400 s. It connects only once the claim is granted (VTI-NTF-083).
- **Renewal.** The claim is renewed at half the granted period. Unless a renewal lands, the socket closes `CLOCK_SKEW` (120 s) before `endsAt`. A claim that lapses because the VTA can't be reached is asked for again, and the socket reconnects once it is granted.
- **Stopping.** The socket closes first, then `vta/collection/release/0.1` is sent. For a listener that is removed, the release waits `RELEASE_GRACE` (30 s), so a reconnect (remove, then re-add) keeps the claim. `Messaging::shutdown` closes every socket, then releases every claim, bounded to 5 s.
- **Refusals.** The activity log says each one in words, once per change:
  - `claimHeld`, any other refusal, or an unreachable VTA: the socket stays closed, and the claim is asked again with backoff (1 to 15 min; 30 s base while the VTA can't be reached). That retry runs on its own loop, not the supervisor's once-a-minute rebuild.
  - `claimNotRenewable` at renewal: the socket closes before the last granted end and stays closed until it is reconnected by hand.
- **`notCollectable` connects without a claim.** This differs from the brief, which said not to connect. VTI-NTF-081 forbids a client to collect only for the identifiers VTI-NTF-080 requires the VTA to collect for. `notCollectable` is the VTA saying the identifier is not one of them (its own DID, an ACL subject, an identity provisioned for another party, an excluded one). So connecting evicts nobody, and refusing to connect would leave the persona with no collector at all. A VTA that predates claims (`unsupportedType`) is treated the same way, because it can't collect either.
- **Headless commands.** `openvtc join` gives its runtime the admin session. `openvtc repos …` now opens a VTA session for a VTA account so it can make the claim, and shuts the session down after the runtime.

## The notification receipt (VTI-NTF-054, VTI-NTF-055; the gap left by #519)

- **Before.** The sender's receipt depended on OpenVTC's own `verify_delivery`. A notice that failed it was deposited but not answered, so a second verifier, with its own resolver cache and clock, decided the answer.
- **Now.** The sender is answered with the receipt the VTA answers the deposit with. That is the deposit response, read against its schema, and it is the same whether the VTA held the notice or declined it. That is also the answer the VTA gives when it collects the document itself (VTI-NTF-086).
- **Not answered:** a deposit the VTA refuses (`notAddressedHere`, `documentInvalid`, `permissionDenied`) and a VTA that can't be reached. Neither is a decision about holding the notice, and the sender delivers it again. A document whose transport sender is not its issuer is also not answered, matching the VTA's own collect path. That check looks only at the delivery and is made before anything is decided.

## Versions

- `vta/collection/claim/0.1` and `vta/collection/release/0.1` are newly pinned, and their bundles are byte-identical to VTI main's `vti-specs-vta`. `trust-tasks check` passes: 61 pins match the lock. The commit body says 63; the correct number is 61.
- Dependencies:
  - vta-sdk 0.80, did-git-sign / vgi-core 0.33.
  - Dev only: vta-service 0.73, vti-vetting-pcs 0.13, vti-voting 0.9.
  - affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45, trust-tasks-rs / -capability-client 0.37.2, test mediator 0.50.
- With the patch applied, `cargo tree -d` shows one copy each of affinidi-*, trust-tasks-*, vta-* and vti-*.

## Tests

- **Unit:**
  - claim and release payloads;
  - how each answer is classified (grant, each declared refusal, `unsupportedType`, unreachable, a non-grant answer);
  - when a claim is renewed and when the socket must close;
  - retry backoff;
  - each notice said only once;
  - a superseded grant cancelling the older one;
  - no grant means no socket, and the persona waits for a retry instead of being stranded;
  - a listener with nothing to claim is not checked at all;
  - the receipt is the VTA's deposit answer.
- **MockVta e2e** (new `collection_e2e`): a VTA-minted persona advertising a mediator is granted the 24 h asked for; claiming it again is a renewal; once released, the next claim is a fresh one. A DID the VTA doesn't hold is `notCollectable`.
- **Run locally with the patch, all green:**
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`
  - `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
  - `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored` (every MockVta e2e)
  - `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`
  - `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides`
  - `cargo check -p openvtc-core --no-default-features --features arbitrary`
  - `cargo bench --workspace --no-run`

## Unsettled

- **`documentInvalid` gets no answer.** When the VTA collects a document itself, it answers an invalid one with a refusal. Here the sender gets no answer, because the deposit's `documentInvalid` does not say which check failed. One case is a document refused for being outside its acceptance window: it is re-sent by the sender's ordinary retry rather than by a VTI-TRN-046 refusal.
- **Sleep and wake.** Renewal timers run on tokio's monotonic clock, so after the Mac wakes, a socket can stay open briefly past `endsAt - skew` before the timer fires and closes it.
- **No live run** against a deployed VTA. Also, `collect_by_default` is off by default on VTAs, so no conflict was exercised end to end.

title: feat(collection): claim a persona's collection before connecting it; answer notifications with the VTA's receipt (#522)
body:
feat(collection): claim a persona's collection before connecting it; answer notifications with the VTA's receipt (#522)

* feat(collection): claim a persona's collection before connecting it (VTI-NTF-080 – 084); answer a notification with the VTA's receipt (VTI-NTF-055)

A persona's mediator permits one connection per DID, and the member's VTA can
collect for the personas whose keys it holds (VTI-NTF-080). A persona listener
of a VTA account now connects only once the VTA grants this client a
collection claim (vta/collection/claim/0.1), asked for 86400 s (VTI-NTF-083).
The claim is renewed at half the granted period, and the socket is closed
CLOCK_SKEW (120 s) before the end unless the renewal landed; a lapsed claim is
asked again and the socket reconnects once granted. A listener removed for good
is closed first and its claim released after (vta/collection/release/0.1),
30 s later so a reconnect keeps it; shutdown closes every socket, then releases
every claim.

claimHeld, any other refusal, and an unreachable VTA leave the socket closed;
the activity log says why in words, and the claim is asked again with backoff
(1 min to 15 min; 30 s base while the VTA is unreachable). claimNotRenewable at
renewal closes the socket before the last granted end and leaves it closed
until reconnected by hand. notCollectable is the VTA stating it never collects
for the identifier, so nothing is evicted and the socket connects without a
claim, as against a VTA that predates claims (unsupportedType). BIP32 accounts
and R-DID listeners claim nothing. The gate sits in add_listener, so startup,
joins, reconnects and the supervisor's rebuilds all pass through it; the
headless join and repos commands give their runtime a VTA session for it.

The sender of a notify or relay is now answered with the receipt the VTA
answers the deposit with (vta/notifications/deposit/0.1's response), the same
whether it held or declined the document (VTI-NTF-054, VTI-NTF-055). This
client no longer runs verify_delivery of its own to decide whether to answer:
a second verification could come out differently from the VTA's, and an answer
turned on it would set a document this client collected apart from one the VTA
collected (VTI-NTF-086). A document the VTA refuses, or one whose transport
sender is not its issuer, is not answered, so its sender delivers it again.

vta/collection/claim/0.1 and release/0.1 are pinned, byte-identical to VTI's
vendored bundles (63 pins). Dependencies: vta-sdk 0.80, vta-service 0.73
(dev), vti-vetting-pcs 0.13, vti-voting 0.9, did-git-sign / vgi-core 0.33,
affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45, trust-tasks 0.37.2, test
mediator 0.50.

title: fix(vta): provision from a context-scoped DID template
body:
Provisioning from a context-scoped DID template always failed. The VTA checks that the template exists in the provisioning context first, then global, then built-in, and that check passed. But the `did:webvh` create step it then calls was given `template_context: None`, so it searched only global and built-in and failed with:

```
not found: DID template 'vtn-host' not found (searched global, builtin)
```

This came up in a production VTN setup that followed the documented flow (`pnm did-templates create --file templates/vtn-host.json --context vtn`). The template listed fine under `pnm did-templates list --context vtn`, the precondition check passed, and provisioning still failed. Registering the template globally (super admin) worked around it.

**Fix**

- `provision_integration`: pass the provisioning context as `template_context`, so rendering searches the same scopes as the checks before it (context, then global, then built-in).
- The "not registered" hints in `mint.rs`, `mod.rs`, `preconditions.rs` and `templates.rs` gave `pnm did-templates create <name> --file <path>`. `create` takes no name (it's read from the file), so that command fails. They now give `pnm did-templates create --file <path> --context <context>` and say the file's `name` must match.

**Tests**

- No regression test. Nothing drives `create_did_webvh` through provisioning today: it needs a DID-hosting server, and `tests/it/provision_integration_provisionable.rs` says it leaves that surface untested.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, and the `vta-service` provisioning tests pass (74 unit, 10 integration).

title: feat(boards)!: closing a board ends its voting; delete closed boards, keeping tombstones for a set retention (VTI-BRD-005 – 008)
body:
Closing a board (open → closed, or straight to archived) now ends the
voting on it (VTI-BRD-006): each idea's election open for voting is
closed early, so its count is final; one not yet open, or not yet
registered, is cancelled and its idea not selected; one whose manifest
does not allow closing early runs on, and the close answers which
(`closing.runningToClose`). The board is stored closed first; each end
is recorded on its election (`ElectionRecord::pending_end`) before the
ballot box is asked, asked at once in the background, and retried by
the elections sweeper — its one retry owner — until answered. The
facilitator's request never waits for the ballot box. A closed board
opens no election (VTI-BRD-005). Every board election is opened with
`allowEarlyClose: true`, and a template stating `false` is
`templateInvalid` (VTI-BRD-030); the console and `cnm boards init`
starter templates allow it.

`vtc/boards/delete/0.1` (VTI-BRD-007, VTI-BRD-008): vtc.boards.manage
unqualified and a step-up bound to the request, spent only after every
check passed; a board that is open is `notClosed`, one with an election
still running `electionsRunning`. Audited before anything goes. Removes
the board, its ideas and notes, and each election's record and ticket
rows; each election keeps a `Tombstone` — identifier, manifest digest,
kept board heads, never title, roll or tickets — for
`[boards] tombstone_retention` (days, default 365; 0 keeps none;
"forever"). The sweeper removes tombstones past their retention.

- cnm: `boards delete <id> --reason`, `boards close` prints how the
  voting ended; refusals print the fix (close first, which elections
  run, the passkey gesture).
- console: "Close and end voting", the closing summary in the toast,
  and "Delete board" (closed boards, board managers only) with the
  title typed, a reason, and the bound passkey gesture.
- vtc-client: `boards_delete`. vta-sdk: the delete schemas in OpenAPI.
- Pins vtc/boards/delete/0.1 and the updated vtc/boards/update/0.1.
- docs/03-vtc/boards.md: closing, archiving, deleting, retention.

BREAKING CHANGE: `vtc_service::elections::store::ElectionRecord` gains
`pending_end` and `vtc_service::config::AppConfig` gains `boards`.

Specs: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#99, trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1032. **Merge after #1032** is published to trusttasks.org: the pins were made from a registry built from that branch (bundles are deterministic, so the digests match once it is published).

## Testing
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service` with and without `--features voting` (5 new board tests: closing ends voting, the sweeper retries an unanswered close, early-close templates, delete with tombstones, zero retention)
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli -p vta-sdk`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- admin-ui: `vitest run` (1474), `npm run lint`

## Follow-up
No task serves a deleted election's tombstone to a voter yet.

title: feat(console): group elections by the board they came from
body:
A community board opens one election per accepted idea, so a busy board
buries the community's own polls in a flat list. The console's Elections
page and the member portal's now show stand-alone elections first, then
one collapsible group per board, headed by its title, the count and (in
the console) a stage summary such as "1 taking tickets · 1 voting", with
a link to the board. Rows in a board's group show the idea's title
without the generated identifier. The console adds a filter: all
elections, stand-alone only, or one board.

No wire change. An election a board opens is named
`board.<boardId>.<ideaId>` (VTI-BRD-031); `lib/election-origin.ts`, a
pure helper both bundles import, reads that and nothing else, so an id
that only resembles it stays stand-alone. Titles come from
`vtc/boards/list` — the console's signed read, the portal's own. A board
the list does not name is "Deleted board" in the console and "A board
no longer shown" in the portal (an archived board is hidden from
members, not deleted); when the list cannot be read at all, each board
is named by its identifier ("Board ff-8cTg0…") and the page still
renders. The portal adds nothing about tickets or votes (VTI-VOT-001).

## Testing
- admin-ui `vitest run` (1484, 12 new), `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`

  that does not allow closing early is `templateInvalid` (VTI-BRD-030).

  show, list and update now allow closing early.

title: fix(setup): completion messages for a hosted DID log and the NNM
body:
Two `vtn setup` completion messages were wrong, found during a production setup:

- **The DID log:** it said `did_log=… (serve it at the URL the DID names)` even when a DID-hosting server (`webvh_server`) had already published the log. It now says the file is a copy and names the server that publishes it. The serve instruction stays for a self-hosted `url`.
- **The NNM step:** it said "Then sign in from the NNM". There is no sign-in any more: `nnm networks add` records the network, and every request is signed by the admin key. It now says "Then add it to the NNM (its key must be one of `admins`)".

fmt and clippy are clean, and the `vtn-service` unit tests pass.

  board election is opened allowing it.

title: fix(console): theme deciding pages, keep only their decision surfaces out of reach
body:
Deciding pages now take the community theme. Only their decision surfaces stay out of its reach, and those are marked as protected while a theme is drawn.

## Why

`vtc/community/theme/show/0.1` client item 2 requires every surface on which a person decides, approves, declines, consents, signs or is warned to be isolated from the theme. The console met it by isolating **four whole pages** (Actions, Join requests, Members, Repos). So their headers, filters, tables and empty states drew in the default look on a themed page: a box of another colour from the breadcrumb down, around a list with nothing on it to decide. Operators read that as missing CSS.

## What is isolated now

| Page | Out of the theme's reach | Takes the theme |
|---|---|---|
| Actions | each action card (verified summary, match code, approve / decline) | header, tabs, empty state, load more |
| Join requests | vetting card, Decide card | list, filter, summary, VP claims, policy JSON |
| Members | add-member form, entries without a membership, removed members; on a member: notes, step-up passkeys, approver devices, vetter role, admin actions | list, search, filters, identity, credentials, relationships |
| Repos | every form dialog and the signing dialog; break-glass and departed-grant warnings | overview, tables, repo detail |

Confirm dialogs, banners and the step-up page were already isolated and are unchanged.

**Why this stays within item 2:** the theme profile admits colours, fonts, borders, radii and gradients only: no `position`, `z-index`, margins or `content`. So a themed ancestor cannot cover, move or relabel an isolated surface. The surfaces themselves stay structurally isolated (shadow tree, own tokens, `all: initial`).

## The "Protected area" marker

While a community theme is drawn, each protected card is outlined (dashed amber) and tagged **"Protected area — standard look, not the community theme"**, so the colour difference explains itself. It is drawn from inside the isolation, so no theme can hide it. With no theme drawn, nothing is marked. The top bar's "Custom theme" chip mentions it.

## Fixes found on the way

- **Pinned Dark drew protected surfaces light (on `main` too).** The production build (lightningcss) lowers `light-dark()` into `--lightningcss-light/dark` toggles. The re-scoped `:root` rule resets them to light inside the isolation, and only `[data-theme]` flips them, which never matched there. So Dark pinned on a light OS drew every protected surface light: the four pages, and every confirm dialog. The isolation's root now mirrors `<html data-theme>` (and `data-community-theme`), followed live. Tests and the dev server don't lower `light-dark()`, which is why nothing caught it.
- **Repos dialogs would have opened without taking focus.** `Protected` portals its children a render after it mounts, so a `useModal` above it ran before the dialog existed. The dialogs now wrap their surface in `Protected` instead, as `ConfirmDialog` does.

## Testing

- `npx tsc -b --noEmit`: clean
- `npx vitest run` (admin-ui, rebased on #2440): 120 files, 1486 tests passed. New tests:
  - an action card's decision is in a shadow tree while the tabs are not
  - a Repos dialog in a shadow tree keeps its focus trap, and Escape returns focus to an opener in the themed page
  - the isolation follows the pinned light / dark live
  - the protected-area marker turns on and off with the theme
- Checked in headless Chrome with the real Join requests pages: `main` vs this branch, Forest theme, Dark pinned on a light OS; and Sunset in light mode. **Not yet run in a live console.**

square corners and fills a stretched row. While a community theme is drawn,
a protected card is outlined and marked "Protected area - standard look,
not the community theme", from inside the isolation so no theme can hide
it; without a theme nothing is marked.

Fixes, both found while moving the boundary:

- A protected surface ignored a pinned light / dark. The production build
  lowers light-dark() into custom-property toggles that the re-scoped
  :root rule resets to light inside the isolation, and only [data-theme]
  flips them back - so Dark pinned on a light OS drew every protected
  surface light (on main: the Actions, Join requests, Members and Repos
  pages, and every confirm dialog). The isolation's root now mirrors
  <html data-theme>, followed live. Tests and the dev server never lower
  light-dark(), which is why nothing caught it.
- Protected portals its children a render after it mounts, so a useModal
  above it ran before the dialog existed and never moved focus in. The
  Repos dialogs wrap their surface in Protected instead.

title: feat(portal): a cleaner member home with live status per service
body:
The member portal's home had grown into a grid of uneven cards, each a paragraph and a button. This reworks it into a page that says where things stand.

## What the member sees

- **Profile header**: "Your card" and "Your membership" are now one block: picture, greeting, status, role, member since, how they signed in, their DID (ellipsised, with a copy button), and what other members see of their card. **Edit your card** sits beside the greeting.
- **Needs your attention**: shown only when something is waiting: an election open for voting, a ticket not yet taken, a board taking proposals or voting, a room offer, a card with no name. Each item links to where the member acts on it.
- **Your community**: six tiles of the same size (Members, Groups, Boards, Elections, Data rooms, Repositories). Each is fully clickable, with one line of description and a live status, e.g. "Member of 2 groups · 1 pending", "1 open for voting · 1 taking tickets", "3 rooms shared · 1 offer waiting". Green means fine, amber means something to act on, grey means nothing there or it needs the wallet.
- **Sign-in and security**: passkeys with shorter wording, beside a smaller "Coming to the portal" note.

## How the statuses are read

- Each status uses the **same query key and function as the page its tile opens** (`["groups","list"]`, `["boards"]`, `["git","view"]`, `["member-rooms", host]`, `["member-room-offers", host]`, `["member-elections", host, did]`), so opening a tile shows what it said without asking again.
- **Nothing on the home page prompts the wallet**: it calls only `rooms.list`, `rooms.offers` and `elections.list`, which never open a window. Nothing about a ballot or a cast is read or shown (VTI-VOT-001); `ticketHeld` is the same field the elections list already shows.
- A passkey session holds no delegated key, so its tiles say "Sign in with your wallet to see this" instead of failing.
- The status logic is in pure functions (`home-status.ts`), with unit tests.

## Testing

- `npx tsc -b --noEmit`: clean
- `npx vitest run` (admin-ui): 120 files, 1482 tests passed (10 new in `home-status.test.ts`; the existing `Portal.test.tsx` assertions on the home page still pass unchanged)
- Checked in headless Chrome against mocked wallet and community answers: desktop dark, light, and 390 px phone width (no horizontal scroll). **Not yet run against a live community and wallet.**

title: feat(vti-vtn)!: verify the network's proof on every Trust Task answer
body:
A VTN signs every Trust Task answer for `authentication`, but the `vti-vtn` client never checked that signature. It took any well-formed answer naming the right network as issuer, so anything on the path could answer for the network. Now a client accepts a `#response` only with the network's valid proof.

**`vti-vtn` (breaking; release-plz should bump it to 0.4)**

- **Answers are verified:**
  - `read_answer` is now async and takes a `KeyResolver`.
  - A `#response` must name `network_did` as `issuer`. It must carry that DID's `authentication` proof, and the proof must verify.
  - Otherwise the new `ClientError::Unverified` is returned. That covers an unsigned answer, a missing issuer, a forged key, the network's key used for another purpose, and a document changed after signing.
- **Refusals:**
  - A signed `trust-task-error` is verified the same way.
  - An unsigned one is still returned as `Refused`. It grants nothing, and the spine answers unsigned when it has no key yet or signing fails (`vti_trust_task_server::sign_response`).
- **Fail-closed client:**
  - `VtnClient::verifying(Arc<dyn KeyResolver>)` sets what answers are verified with.
  - A client without one can still fetch the profile and artifacts. But `task`, `read_task` and `send_request*` return `Unverified` before anything is sent.
- **Shared resolver:**
  - New `resolve` feature with `resolve::VmKeyResolver`, which wraps `vta-sdk`'s `TrustTaskVmResolver` with the purpose check (VTI-KEY-022).
  - Constructors: `network(resolver_url)`, `offline()`, and `From<TrustTaskVmResolver>` to share an existing DID cache.
  - It replaces the copies the VTC and the VTN each kept. The NNM uses it too.
- **Dependencies:** `vta-sdk` (`proof-verify`) and `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` are optional and only enabled by `resolve`. Neither is new to the workspace.

**`vtc-service` networks**

- Every network client verifies answers through the community's resolver (`VmKeyResolver::from(state.trust_task_vm_resolver())`). The local `Resolver` wrapper is gone.
- An unverified answer maps to `NetError::Mismatch`, the same as a URL that answers as another DID. `own_listing` keeps that error as a mismatch rather than reporting it as "not listed".

**Tests**

- **`vti-vtn`:**
  - new: an answer signed by the network reads; every unverified case listed above is refused; an unsigned refusal is still a refusal; a forged one is not.
  - new: a client with no resolver sends nothing.
  - new: `VmKeyResolver::offline` checks the purpose.
- **`vtc-service`:**
  - The fake networks in `networks/tests.rs` and `tests/it/networks.rs` now sign every answer as their network DID, the way the spine does.
  - New `an_answer_not_signed_by_the_network_is_a_mismatch`: a network that answers in its name with another key is refused, and nothing is saved.
- **Results:**
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.
  - `vti-vtn`: 27, 4 and 1 pass.
  - `vtc-service`: 2165 and 1376 pass.
  - The `vta-sdk` census tests pass.
  - `vti-vtn` builds with no features, with `client` alone and with `resolve` alone.

**Follow-up:** OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network uses this once released. `vtn-service`'s `Network::client` and the cascade tests verify parent and child networks' answers, and `nnm` gains `--resolver-url`. That branch passes all 23 VTN tests against this one.

title: feat(service): /health liveness and /health/ready readiness probes
body:
The VTN had no health check route. This adds liveness and readiness probes for an orchestrator or load balancer. Neither needs a signature, and the directory's `visibility` doesn't gate them.

| Route | Answer |
|---|---|
| `GET /health` | Liveness. Always `200 {status: "ok", version, did}`; nothing is checked. |
| `GET /health/ready` | Readiness. `200 {status: "ready", checks: {store: "ok"}}` when a point read through the store succeeds. Otherwise `503 {status: "unavailable", checks: {store: "failed"}}`, with the cause logged rather than returned. |

- **Path and shape:** they follow the VTC's and the VTA's `/health`. It returns only what's already public (the network DID is also at `/.well-known/vtn`) and no infrastructure detail.
- **What readiness checks:** the network identity is loaded before the service starts, and the service doesn't start without it. So readiness checks only the store. It doesn't probe the DID resolver, because that's an external dependency and a resolver outage shouldn't pull the network out of rotation.
- **Docs:** the README route table, `trust-tasks.md` ("What stays REST") and A9 list the new routes.
- **Tests:** new `health_and_readiness_answer_without_a_signature`, run on an admins-only network. The 503 path isn't covered by a test. fmt and clippy are clean, and all 24 tests pass.
