title: feat(discovery): answer trust-task-discovery 0.4 and advertise the expiry horizon
body:
## What

The VTA, the VTC and the witness now answer `trust-task-discovery/0.4` (trust-tasks-tf #1030, published in trust-tasks-rs 0.37.2). Its acceptance window adds `expiryHorizonSeconds`: how long after `issuedAt` a stated `expiresAt` is honoured in place of the maximum age. Each VTI node advertises its thirty-day horizon (VTI-OPS-028, VTI-TRN-047). With it, a sender can state an expiry within the horizon instead of issuing a new attempt every ten minutes.

## How

- **One value.** `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::AcceptanceWindow` gains `expiry_horizon`. `VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW` sets it to `EXPIRY_HORIZON`, and `freshness_policy()` applies it. The advertised horizon and the applied one therefore come from the same field.
- **Rounding.** `advertised()` rounds the horizon down to whole seconds. It leaves out a horizon under one second, which tells the discoverer the maximum age applies to everything: narrower than applied, never wider.
- **Shared builder.** `respond_v0_4` is the shared answer.
- **0.3 still served.** 0.3 is now superseded upstream but is still answered, through `respond_v0_3` and `advertised_v0_3()`. It returns the same list with the maximum age and skew, and no horizon. The SDK, the VTC console and the git-ns bridge probe still ask 0.3, and an older node only answers 0.3, so clients stay on it for now.
- **Registration.** `TASK_TRUST_TASK_DISCOVERY_0_4` is registered in `vta_sdk::trust_tasks`, the retry-safety table, the VTA dispatch table and the conformance witness. The VTC routes both versions, and the witness lists and routes both.
- **Version floor.** The workspace floor for `trust-tasks-rs` moves to 0.37.2. In the lockfile, only trust-tasks-rs changes.

## Tests

- **Shared:** the advertised horizon is 2,592,000 s, it reads back to `VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW`, a fractional horizon rounds down and a sub-second one is omitted.
- **Per node:** the VTA and the VTC each read the horizon out of their own 0.4 answer and compare it with the spine's policy. The VTA also checks that a document stating a one-year expiry is accepted at the advertised horizon plus skew, and refused a second later.
- **0.3 answers:** the VTC, the witness and vti-common each check that a 0.3 answer is schema-valid and carries no horizon.

## Checks run locally

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, the VTC `vetting-pcs,voting` clippy and the VTA rest-only clippy are clean.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo metadata --locked` pass.
- nextest on vti-common, vta-sdk, vta-service, vti-witness and vti-trust-task-server: 4,638 passed.
- nextest on vtc-service: 3,541 passed.

title: feat(service): browser sign-in with a wallet (auth/oob, A13)
body:
Builds against the VTI crates from release #2436: `vti-oob-server` 0.1, `vti-specs-core` 0.4, `vti-specs-vtn` 0.2, `vti-common` 0.56, `vti-secrets` 0.29, `vta-sdk` 0.80, `vti-trust-task-server` 0.2 and `vti-vtn` 0.3.

This adds browser sign-in (A13). A wallet approves the landing page's own key through `auth/oob/*`, and the page can then read a members-only or admins-only directory as the approver.

**Server (`vtn-service`)**

- **`tasks/oob.rs`: the network as an `OobHost`** for `vti-oob-server`, the crate extracted from the VTC in #2425. The check order, the records and the refusals all come from the crate.
  - **Who may approve:** an administrator, or a listed or member community or network. This is decided from local records before the DID is resolved (T15), and checked again at `redeem` (T18).
  - **What the key may sign** (`SIGNING_SCOPE`): `vtn/directory`, `vtn/graph`, `vtn/entries`, `vtn/roles` and `vtn/rooms/list`. Nothing administrative; that stays with `nnm`.
  - **`redeem`:** records a delegation of `K_b` to the approver, until the earlier of the grant's end and `[auth] browser_key_hours` (default 8, at most 24, per A20). No session and no cookie.
  - Step responses are signed for `assertionMethod`. Carried documents are verified with the network's resolver, and their ids are claimed in the store-backed accepted-ids record.
- **Dispatch:**
  - the spec policy covers `vtn/*` and `auth/oob/*` (`vti-specs-core`);
  - `before_proof` runs the crate's `did:key` precheck (T21);
  - `auth/oob` types are routed to the crate;
  - a request signed by a key with a live delegation that covers its task is read as the approver's. Their standing is decided afresh on each request.
- **HTTPS door:** `/v1/trust-tasks` now has its own handler. It supplies `HttpContext` (peer address, `User-Agent`, `Origin`, `Host`), which `request` and `redeem` require. `vtn serve` now uses connect info. Behind a reverse proxy the address is the proxy's, so the per-address limits on pending sign-ins are shared.
- **Store:** new keyspace `oob`, holding the requests and delegations. It's swept every 10 minutes along with the accepted ids.
- **Config:** new `[auth]` section with `browser_key_hours` and `link_host` (default `link.trustoverip.org`, checked against the crate's rules and against the network's own domain). `/.well-known/vtn` now publishes `signIn { linkHost, flow, scope }`.
- **`templates/vtn-host.json`:** adds `TrustTaskHTTPS` (`{API_URL}/v1`) and `SignInPortal` (`{API_URL}/`), which a wallet needs to find the network. A network that is already provisioned needs these services added to its DID document.

**Landing page**

- **The page's key (`K_b`):** generated with WebCrypto as an Ed25519 key, non-extractable. Documents are signed `eddsa-jcs-2022` for `authentication`, using JCS and base58btc ported from the VTC admin UI.
- **Sign-in flow:** "Sign in with a wallet" shows the trigger link (Open in wallet / Copy) and then the number to type into the wallet. It long-polls `redeem`, and Cancel sends `auth/oob/cancel`.
- **After approval:** the key is kept in this browser's IndexedDB until it expires. A session bar shows who you're signed in as, until when, and offers Sign out.
- **No QR code:** the page's CSP allows no external scripts, and I didn't write a QR encoder inline.

**What a person can't do yet:** a person holding a member community's credential (VMC) can't sign in this way, because the network has no record of them before their DID resolves (T15). They present the credential with each request instead. Keys delegated by an administrator (`auth/signing-key/*`) are also still to come.

**Tests**

- `tests/browser_sign_in.rs` runs the full flow through the router with real signatures:
  1. request, claim, a pending `redeem` (which returns the match number), prove, respond, redeem;
  2. the page's key then reads the members-only directory and its own entry as the approving community;
  3. it is refused for anything outside the scope;
  4. the delegation is capped at 8 hours even though the grant asked for 2 days.

  It also checks that a stranger gets `auth/oob:notAuthorized`, that an administrator may approve, and that a non-`did:key` issuer gets `auth/oob:keyUnsupported`.
- **Page signatures against the Rust verifier:** the page's signing code, taken from `index.html` and run in Node, produced a document (non-ASCII, quotes and newlines in the payload) that `vti_vtn::verify::verify_document` accepts. I ran this once by hand; it isn't in CI.
- **Live smoke test:** against `vtn serve`, the page's code opened a sign-in request through the real HTTPS door and got a signed answer. A read signed by the key was refused with `permissionDenied` until it was approved.
- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass (6 cascade, 11 network API, 3 browser sign-in, 3 unit).

title: vtc-service-v0.21.0
body:
### Added

- **console**: Edit a board from its page ([#2434](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2434))

A facilitator could close or archive a board in the console but change
  nothing else; every other change took `cnm` or a hand-built
  `vtc/boards/update`. The board's page now has **Edit board**, a form
  filled from the board as read: title, description, audience, the
  proposal and voting windows, topics, formats, ideas per member, the
  selection rule and the timetable.

  Only the fields that differ are sent (`boardChanges`), compared to the
  minute since a datetime input holds whole minutes, so an untouched
  voting window or audience never reaches the board after voting opens,
  where it is refused as `fixedAfterVotingOpens`; the form also shows
  both as fixed then. Timetable slots keep their identifiers, so a
  selected idea stays placed, and a new slot takes one no other slot has
  used. The election template is not edited here (it takes
  `vtc.elections.manage` as well).

- **trust-task-push**: Pushed documents state their delivery deadline as expiresAt (VTI-TRN-048) ([#2428](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2428))

A pushed document stated no expiry, so a recipient accepted it for ten
  minutes after its issuedAt. A push runs for hours or days (thirty for a
  removal notice), so a copy a mediator held while the recipient was offline
  was refused as stale when collected, and the engine had to keep issuing new
  documents under VTI-TRN-046 for the delivery to land. Since #2423 a VTI
  consumer accepts a document until its stated expiresAt, up to thirty days
  (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028), so stating the deadline keeps the document
  acceptable for as long as it is pursued.

  vti-common trust_task_push:
  - `state_delivery_expiry` stamps an unsigned document's expiresAt at its
    push's deadline, counted from issuedAt in whole seconds, keeping an earlier
    expiry the task already states, and refusing a signed document. New
    attempts already carry it unchanged.
  - The engine places a document by its acceptance end (VTI-TRN-044): the
    stated expiry, bounded by the horizon, or issuedAt + the maximum age
    without one. It no longer issues new attempts at ten minutes for a
    document that is still acceptable, and counts a copy collected inside its
    stated expiry as delivered.

  Stated at every push whose window outlasts the ten-minute maximum age: the
  VTC's removal, authority-reduced, authority-reduction-pending, step-up passkey
  and break-glass notices, its notifications, and its consent requests (the
  action's expiry, capped at a week); the VTA's credential-exchange steps.
  The VTA's step-up and consent pushes run five to ten minutes, inside the
  maximum age, and are unchanged.

- **trust-tasks**: Honour a stated expiresAt up to 30 days, and keep the replay record to the acceptance end (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028, VTI-OPS-029) ([#2423](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2423))

trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1021), with
  affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45 (affinidi-tdk-rs #983) and
  mediator 0.50 (affinidi-messaging-mediator #55), which move with it.

  Acceptance. A document that states an expiresAt is accepted until then, up to
  thirty days after its issuedAt, whatever the ten-minute maximum age
  (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028). An expiry beyond the horizon is clamped, not
  refused. A document without one keeps the ten-minute window. The horizon is
  `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::EXPIRY_HORIZON`, applied by
  `AcceptanceWindow::freshness_policy`, so every VTI consumer takes it.

  Retention. Every record of an accepted document was capped at
  issuedAt + max_age + skew, relying on the freshness check to refuse anything
  older. Under 0.37 that check accepts a document with a later expiresAt, so
  the record would be dropped while its document was still acceptable and a
  replay would execute twice. One rule now decides retention for every consumer,
  `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::retain_until`: the acceptance end plus the
  skew (VTI-OPS-029), bounded by the horizon. It is used by the shared receive
  pipeline (VTA and VTC accepted-id records), the VTC's spent step-up approver
  statements, vti-witness and room-host.

  Behaviour change for producers: a document stating a long expiresAt is no
  longer refused as stale after ten minutes. Step-up approver statements are
  included, as VTI-OPS-028 requires of any document that states an expiry.

  Not here: idempotency records still live 24 hours although a keyed document
  can now be acceptable for 30 days (VTI-OPS-066, next step); room-host's replay
  record is still in memory and lost on restart (VTI-OPS-029).

- **vtc-service**: Talk to networks over vtn/* Trust Tasks ([#2422](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2422))

The community's VTN client signs each request as the community (vtn/entries/show,
  vtn/membership/{offer,acknowledge,repudiate}, the signed vtn/groups/register
  request) instead of signing in and calling the REST routes the VTN removed.
  Answers are read as their generated #response types.

- **vtc-service**: Community boards — members propose ideas and leave notes, each accepted idea is its own election (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080) ([#2420](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2420))

* build(vti-specs-vtc): pin vtc/boards/*/0.1

  The thirteen Community Boards tasks (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080): create, update, list and show a board; propose, update, withdraw, decide and select ideas; add, list, withdraw and hide notes. Resolved against a local build of dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/vtc-boards — re-pin against trusttasks.org once that publishes.



### Changed

- **vtc-service**: Wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate ([#2425](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2425))

* refactor(vtc-service): wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate

  The auth/oob key-grant flow (a wallet approving a browser's key K_b)
  moves out of vtc-service into a new workspace crate, so the VTN service
  can serve the same flow instead of a copy.

  The crate owns the request store and compare-and-set, the claim and
  decision clocks, the redeem long poll and its caps, the did:key precheck
  (T21), the carried-document checks (T7, T15) and the check order of
  request, claim, prove, respond, redeem and cancel. A host implements
  OobHost: records keyspace, DID, origin and name, step signer,
  carried-proof verifiers, accepted-id record, a per-audience gate at three
  fixed points, signingScope, audit, and redeem's completion. Audiences
  are the host's associated type, and the default is never stored or
  signed, so VTC rows and signatures are byte for byte unchanged. The
  generic half of delegated signing (scope match, exclusions, record,
  armed over the host's row and liveness) moves too.

  vtc-service keeps SessionAudience, the member and admin gates,
  PORTAL_SIGNING_SCOPE, the audit events, session and cookie minting, its
  delegation row, the session liveness check, and the DID-document checks.
  Behaviour is unchanged. Every existing test passes unmodified.



### Fixed

- **portal**: Offer a board vote only once voting opens ([#2433](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2433))

An idea accepted before the board's `voting.opensAt` gets an election
  whose voting window starts then; its ticket can be taken at once
  (VTI-VOT-033), but a cast is refused by the voter's VTA as `notOpen`.
  The portal offered "Vote in your wallet" for every open idea, so a
  member who took a ticket early was sent to the wallet only to be told
  "voting is not open".

  Until voting opens the idea now reads "Voting soon" and "Voting opens
  <date>", keeps "Take your ticket", and in place of the vote button
  says the ticket is ready and when to come back.

- **vtc,voting**: Recover a TSP relationship the peer forgot ([#2427](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2427))

A ballot box restarted under a live community stopped answering it: the
  voting service kept TSP relationships in memory, so after a restart (or
  a reconnect, which builds a fresh ATM) it held none with the community
  and, by TSP §7.2.2, dropped every frame unanswered. The VTC's durable
  half still read "related", so it never re-invited, and every election
  registration timed out for good.

  Both halves are fixed:

  - vtc-service: `PeerTasks::exchange` resets the TSP relationship on a
    reply timeout (D4 of tsp-relationship-recovery.md, as the registry
    client already does), so the caller's next attempt re-forms it through
    `send_reestablishing`. Repair only; the caller's backoff stays the one
    retry owner.
  - vti-common: `IdentitySession::with_relationship_store` lets a host
    service keep its relationships in a durable store.
  - vti-voting-service: keeps them in `data_dir/store` (`tsp_relationships`)
    and runs the store's maintenance loop once per process.

title: vta-service-v0.73.0
body:
### Added

- **trust-task-push**: Pushed documents state their delivery deadline as expiresAt (VTI-TRN-048) ([#2428](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2428))

A pushed document stated no expiry, so a recipient accepted it for ten
  minutes after its issuedAt. A push runs for hours or days (thirty for a
  removal notice), so a copy a mediator held while the recipient was offline
  was refused as stale when collected, and the engine had to keep issuing new
  documents under VTI-TRN-046 for the delivery to land. Since #2423 a VTI
  consumer accepts a document until its stated expiresAt, up to thirty days
  (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028), so stating the deadline keeps the document
  acceptable for as long as it is pursued.

  vti-common trust_task_push:
  - `state_delivery_expiry` stamps an unsigned document's expiresAt at its
    push's deadline, counted from issuedAt in whole seconds, keeping an earlier
    expiry the task already states, and refusing a signed document. New
    attempts already carry it unchanged.
  - The engine places a document by its acceptance end (VTI-TRN-044): the
    stated expiry, bounded by the horizon, or issuedAt + the maximum age
    without one. It no longer issues new attempts at ten minutes for a
    document that is still acceptable, and counts a copy collected inside its
    stated expiry as delivered.

  Stated at every push whose window outlasts the ten-minute maximum age: the
  VTC's removal, authority-reduced, authority-reduction-pending, step-up passkey
  and break-glass notices, its notifications, and its consent requests (the
  action's expiry, capped at a week); the VTA's credential-exchange steps.
  The VTA's step-up and consent pushes run five to ten minutes, inside the
  maximum age, and are unchanged.

- **idempotency**: Keep a keyed operation's record until the latest acceptance end under its key (VTI-OPS-066) ([#2426](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2426))

A keyed Trust Task's idempotency record lived 24 hours (the NonDestructive
  class TTL). The attempts at one operation are separate documents, and since
  #2423 a document stating an expiresAt is acceptable for up to thirty days
  (VTI-OPS-028), so an attempt arriving after the 24 hours would perform the
  operation again. VTI-OPS-066 requires the record to last until the latest
  acceptance end, plus the skew, of any document carrying the key that the node
  has accepted.

- **trust-tasks**: Honour a stated expiresAt up to 30 days, and keep the replay record to the acceptance end (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028, VTI-OPS-029) ([#2423](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2423))

trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1021), with
  affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45 (affinidi-tdk-rs #983) and
  mediator 0.50 (affinidi-messaging-mediator #55), which move with it.

  older. Under 0.37 that check accepts a document with a later expiresAt, so
  the record would be dropped while its document was still acceptable and a
  replay would execute twice. One rule now decides retention for every consumer,
  `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::retain_until`: the acceptance end plus the
  skew (VTI-OPS-029), bounded by the horizon. It is used by the shared receive
  pipeline (VTA and VTC accepted-id records), the VTC's spent step-up approver
  statements, vti-witness and room-host.

  longer refused as stale after ten minutes. Step-up approver statements are
  included, as VTI-OPS-028 requires of any document that states an expiry.

  can now be acceptable for 30 days (VTI-OPS-066, next step); room-host's replay

- **vta**: Collection for the principal's identifiers — claims, the collector, collection by default off (VTI-NTF-080 – 093) ([#2421](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2421))

* feat(vti-specs): pin vta/collection/{claim,release,list} 0.1

  From trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1023 and #1024: a client's
  collection claim on a persona DID, its release, and the listing of who
  collects for each of a context's identifiers (VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-093).



### Fixed

- **vta-service**: A re-admitted room member acts on the room's later grant instead of being locked out ([#2424](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2424))

A member removed from a room and offered it again holds the room's first
  AuthorityCredential and MembershipCredential beside the re-issued ones:
  accepting stores the new credentials and nothing retires the old. The
  presentation oracle refused any persona holding two of a kind from one
  room, so from the accept on every action in that room failed with
  "which one to attenuate from is not a question this can answer safely",
  at every VTA version, with no way out short of archiving the older
  credential by hand.

  The oracle now uses, of each kind separately, the credential with the
  latest validFrom among those in force (one not yet valid never displaces
  one that is). That is the room's own rule rather than a guess: a removal
  withdraws the member with a subject entry covering every credential
  issued before its revokedAt (rooms/revocations/put, Matching), so after
  re-admission the earlier credential is the withdrawn one. Only two
  equally recent credentials are still refused, and the refusal now names
  their vault ids so the holder can archive the one it does not mean.

  Reported from Keyring (berkmancenter/keyring-wallet
  docs/upstream/2026-11-rooms-findings.md, finding 1).

- **contexts**: Purge every context-scoped record on delete ([#2419](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2419))

vta/contexts/delete removed a context's keys, DIDs, ACL scope, DID
  templates, app state and memory ([#2415](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2415)), but every other store that holds
  data for a context kept its rows. Most are keyed by the context id, or by a
  digest of it, so a context later created under the same id inherited them.

  Seen with OpenVTC: a context deleted and recreated under the same id failed
  vta/pcs/root-request with memberMismatch. The vetter engine record
  (pcs_engine vetter:<sha256(ctx, community)>) had survived, still pinned to
  the old member DID and to a derivation path under the old context's base.

  delete_context now purges, for every context in the subtree:

  - pcs_engine: vetter, applicant, voter and trustee records whose contextId
    is the context, with the wrapped state beside each (secret:<key>, and a
    voter's secret:voter-casts:<digest>). The keys are digests, so the purge
    scans each record prefix and matches the record's own contextId.
  - persona: every context-scoped prefix (pb, pc, pcr, pca, pcl, pd, plp, plb),
    driven from PREFIX_SCOPES so a new context-scoped prefix is purged without
    anyone remembering to; and the agent-scoped face-value edges that name one
    of the context's local profiles.
  - vault: credentials in the context's custody (with their index rows) and
    vault entries, hard-deleted whatever their lifecycle state.
  - notifications: held records with their dedup and bound rows (the sweep's
    removal, factored out and shared).
  - consent: grants decided in, and pending requests scoped to, the context;
    consent_approvers: its approver bindings.
  - external_accounts / external_secrets: each live account deleted the way
    external/accounts/delete deletes one (secret gone, id retired).
  - contexts: the daily quota counters (quota:<ctx>:...).
  - imported_secrets / internal_keys: the material of each key record the
    purge removes, as revoke_key does for an imported key.

  Each store purges itself next to the code that writes it, and the counts go
  in the deletion's log line. As in #2415 none of this is in the not-empty
  gate: the gate must agree with preview-delete, whose wire shape has no
  member for these, so surfacing them needs a spec revision.

  Kept on purpose: the audit log; issued credentials (revoked through the DID
  cascade, never deleted); operator policy; room groups and invitations (keyed
  by persona DID / credential id, unreachable from a recreated context); and
  external accounts' retired: tombstones, which hold no data and stop a
  recreated context reusing an account id a provider-side trust policy may
  still name.

  The census is now a claim the code is held to:

  - vta_keyspaces::context_delete_effect classifies every keyspace for a
    context deletion (Purged / Retained / Lapses / Unrelated), and
    context_delete_labels_match_the_cascade ties the Purged set to the
    cascade's own list.
  - did_delete_effect labelled most keyspaces Cascade (and five Blocks) though
    the DID deletion reaches only keys, webvh, acl, sessions, issued
    credentials and contexts. Those labels are now Orphaned, with the intended
    effect beside each, and did_delete_labels_match_the_cascade holds
    Cascade / Blocks / Revoke to DID_DELETE_REACHES.

- **contexts**: Purge every context-scoped record on delete ([#2419](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2419))

  templates, app state and memory ([#2415](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2415)), but every other store that holds
  data for a context kept its rows. Most are keyed by the context id, or by a
  digest of it, so a context later created under the same id inherited them.

  vta/pcs/root-request with memberMismatch. The vetter engine record
  (pcs_engine vetter:<sha256(ctx, community)>) had survived, still pinned to
  the old member DID and to a derivation path under the old context's base.

    is the context, with the wrapped state beside each (secret:<key>, and a
    voter's secret:voter-casts:<digest>). The keys are digests, so the purge
    scans each record prefix and matches the record's own contextId.

    driven from PREFIX_SCOPES so a new context-scoped prefix is purged without
    anyone remembering to; and the agent-scoped face-value edges that name one
    of the context's local profiles.
  - vault: credentials in the context's custody (with their index rows) and
    vault entries, hard-deleted whatever their lifecycle state.

    removal, factored out and shared).

    consent_approvers: its approver bindings.

    external/accounts/delete deletes one (secret gone, id retired).

    purge removes, as revoke_key does for an imported key.

title: vti-trust-task-server-v0.2.0
body:
### Added

- **trust-tasks**: Honour a stated expiresAt up to 30 days, and keep the replay record to the acceptance end (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028, VTI-OPS-029) ([#2423](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2423))

trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1021), with
  affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45 (affinidi-tdk-rs #983) and
  mediator 0.50 (affinidi-messaging-mediator #55), which move with it.

  Acceptance. A document that states an expiresAt is accepted until then, up to
  thirty days after its issuedAt, whatever the ten-minute maximum age
  (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028). An expiry beyond the horizon is clamped, not
  refused. A document without one keeps the ten-minute window. The horizon is
  `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::EXPIRY_HORIZON`, applied by
  `AcceptanceWindow::freshness_policy`, so every VTI consumer takes it.

  Retention. Every record of an accepted document was capped at
  issuedAt + max_age + skew, relying on the freshness check to refuse anything
  older. Under 0.37 that check accepts a document with a later expiresAt, so
  the record would be dropped while its document was still acceptable and a
  replay would execute twice. One rule now decides retention for every consumer,
  `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::retain_until`: the acceptance end plus the
  skew (VTI-OPS-029), bounded by the horizon. It is used by the shared receive
  pipeline (VTA and VTC accepted-id records), the VTC's spent step-up approver
  statements, vti-witness and room-host.

  Behaviour change for producers: a document stating a long expiresAt is no
  longer refused as stale after ten minutes. Step-up approver statements are
  included, as VTI-OPS-028 requires of any document that states an expiry.

  Not here: idempotency records still live 24 hours although a keyed document
  can now be acceptable for 30 days (VTI-OPS-066, next step); room-host's replay
  record is still in memory and lost on restart (VTI-OPS-029).

title: vti-common-v0.56.0
body:
### Added

- **trust-task-push**: Pushed documents state their delivery deadline as expiresAt (VTI-TRN-048) ([#2428](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2428))

A pushed document stated no expiry, so a recipient accepted it for ten
  minutes after its issuedAt. A push runs for hours or days (thirty for a
  removal notice), so a copy a mediator held while the recipient was offline
  was refused as stale when collected, and the engine had to keep issuing new
  documents under VTI-TRN-046 for the delivery to land. Since #2423 a VTI
  consumer accepts a document until its stated expiresAt, up to thirty days
  (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028), so stating the deadline keeps the document
  acceptable for as long as it is pursued.

  vti-common trust_task_push:
  - `state_delivery_expiry` stamps an unsigned document's expiresAt at its
    push's deadline, counted from issuedAt in whole seconds, keeping an earlier
    expiry the task already states, and refusing a signed document. New
    attempts already carry it unchanged.
  - The engine places a document by its acceptance end (VTI-TRN-044): the
    stated expiry, bounded by the horizon, or issuedAt + the maximum age
    without one. It no longer issues new attempts at ten minutes for a
    document that is still acceptable, and counts a copy collected inside its
    stated expiry as delivered.

  Stated at every push whose window outlasts the ten-minute maximum age: the
  VTC's removal, authority-reduced, authority-reduction-pending, step-up passkey
  and break-glass notices, its notifications, and its consent requests (the
  action's expiry, capped at a week); the VTA's credential-exchange steps.
  The VTA's step-up and consent pushes run five to ten minutes, inside the
  maximum age, and are unchanged.

- **idempotency**: Keep a keyed operation's record until the latest acceptance end under its key (VTI-OPS-066) ([#2426](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2426))

A keyed Trust Task's idempotency record lived 24 hours (the NonDestructive
  class TTL). The attempts at one operation are separate documents, and since
  #2423 a document stating an expiresAt is acceptable for up to thirty days
  (VTI-OPS-028), so an attempt arriving after the 24 hours would perform the
  operation again. VTI-OPS-066 requires the record to last until the latest
  acceptance end, plus the skew, of any document carrying the key that the node
  has accepted.

- **trust-tasks**: Honour a stated expiresAt up to 30 days, and keep the replay record to the acceptance end (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028, VTI-OPS-029) ([#2423](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2423))

trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1021), with
  affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45 (affinidi-tdk-rs #983) and
  mediator 0.50 (affinidi-messaging-mediator #55), which move with it.

  Acceptance. A document that states an expiresAt is accepted until then, up to
  thirty days after its issuedAt, whatever the ten-minute maximum age
  (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028). An expiry beyond the horizon is clamped, not
  refused. A document without one keeps the ten-minute window. The horizon is
  `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::EXPIRY_HORIZON`, applied by
  `AcceptanceWindow::freshness_policy`, so every VTI consumer takes it.

  Retention. Every record of an accepted document was capped at
  issuedAt + max_age + skew, relying on the freshness check to refuse anything
  older. Under 0.37 that check accepts a document with a later expiresAt, so
  the record would be dropped while its document was still acceptable and a
  replay would execute twice. One rule now decides retention for every consumer,
  `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::retain_until`: the acceptance end plus the
  skew (VTI-OPS-029), bounded by the horizon. It is used by the shared receive
  pipeline (VTA and VTC accepted-id records), the VTC's spent step-up approver
  statements, vti-witness and room-host.

  longer refused as stale after ten minutes. Step-up approver statements are
  included, as VTI-OPS-028 requires of any document that states an expiry.

  Not here: idempotency records still live 24 hours although a keyed document
  can now be acceptable for 30 days (VTI-OPS-066, next step); room-host's replay
  record is still in memory and lost on restart (VTI-OPS-029).

* build(vti-specs-vtc): pin vtc/boards/*/0.1

  The thirteen Community Boards tasks (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080): create, update, list and show a board; propose, update, withdraw, decide and select ideas; add, list, withdraw and hide notes. Resolved against a local build of dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/vtc-boards — re-pin against trusttasks.org once that publishes.



### Fixed

- **vtc,voting**: Recover a TSP relationship the peer forgot ([#2427](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2427))

A ballot box restarted under a live community stopped answering it: the
  voting service kept TSP relationships in memory, so after a restart (or
  a reconnect, which builds a fresh ATM) it held none with the community
  and, by TSP §7.2.2, dropped every frame unanswered. The VTC's durable
  half still read "related", so it never re-invited, and every election
  registration timed out for good.

  Both halves are fixed:

  - vtc-service: `PeerTasks::exchange` resets the TSP relationship on a
    reply timeout (D4 of tsp-relationship-recovery.md, as the registry
    client already does), so the caller's next attempt re-forms it through
    `send_reestablishing`. Repair only; the caller's backoff stays the one
    retry owner.
  - vti-common: `IdentitySession::with_relationship_store` lets a host
    service keep its relationships in a durable store.
  - vti-voting-service: keeps them in `data_dir/store` (`tsp_relationships`)
    and runs the store's maintenance loop once per process.

- **contexts**: Purge every context-scoped record on delete ([#2419](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2419))

vta/contexts/delete removed a context's keys, DIDs, ACL scope, DID
  templates, app state and memory ([#2415](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2415)), but every other store that holds
  data for a context kept its rows. Most are keyed by the context id, or by a
  digest of it, so a context later created under the same id inherited them.

  Seen with OpenVTC: a context deleted and recreated under the same id failed
  vta/pcs/root-request with memberMismatch. The vetter engine record
  (pcs_engine vetter:<sha256(ctx, community)>) had survived, still pinned to
  the old member DID and to a derivation path under the old context's base.

  delete_context now purges, for every context in the subtree:

  - pcs_engine: vetter, applicant, voter and trustee records whose contextId
    is the context, with the wrapped state beside each (secret:<key>, and a
    voter's secret:voter-casts:<digest>). The keys are digests, so the purge
    scans each record prefix and matches the record's own contextId.
  - persona: every context-scoped prefix (pb, pc, pcr, pca, pcl, pd, plp, plb),
    driven from PREFIX_SCOPES so a new context-scoped prefix is purged without
    anyone remembering to; and the agent-scoped face-value edges that name one
    of the context's local profiles.
  - vault: credentials in the context's custody (with their index rows) and
    vault entries, hard-deleted whatever their lifecycle state.
  - notifications: held records with their dedup and bound rows (the sweep's
    removal, factored out and shared).
  - consent: grants decided in, and pending requests scoped to, the context;
    consent_approvers: its approver bindings.
  - external_accounts / external_secrets: each live account deleted the way
    external/accounts/delete deletes one (secret gone, id retired).
  - contexts: the daily quota counters (quota:<ctx>:...).
  - imported_secrets / internal_keys: the material of each key record the
    purge removes, as revoke_key does for an imported key.

  Each store purges itself next to the code that writes it, and the counts go
  in the deletion's log line. As in #2415 none of this is in the not-empty
  gate: the gate must agree with preview-delete, whose wire shape has no
  member for these, so surfacing them needs a spec revision.

  Kept on purpose: the audit log; issued credentials (revoked through the DID
  cascade, never deleted); operator policy; room groups and invitations (keyed
  by persona DID / credential id, unreachable from a recreated context); and
  external accounts' retired: tombstones, which hold no data and stop a
  recreated context reusing an account id a provider-side trust policy may
  still name.

  The census is now a claim the code is held to:

  - vta_keyspaces::context_delete_effect classifies every keyspace for a
    context deletion (Purged / Retained / Lapses / Unrelated), and
    context_delete_labels_match_the_cascade ties the Purged set to the
    cascade's own list.
  - did_delete_effect labelled most keyspaces Cascade (and five Blocks) though
    the DID deletion reaches only keys, webvh, acl, sessions, issued
    credentials and contexts. Those labels are now Orphaned, with the intended
    effect beside each, and did_delete_labels_match_the_cascade holds
    Cascade / Blocks / Revoke to DID_DELETE_REACHES.

  collection claim on a persona DID, its release, and the listing of who
  collects for each of a context's identifiers (VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-093).



### Changed

- **vtc-service**: Wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate ([#2425](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2425))

* refactor(vtc-service): wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate

  The auth/oob key-grant flow (a wallet approving a browser's key K_b)
  moves out of vtc-service into a new workspace crate, so the VTN service
  can serve the same flow instead of a copy.

  The crate owns the request store and compare-and-set, the claim and
  decision clocks, the redeem long poll and its caps, the did:key precheck
  (T21), the carried-document checks (T7, T15) and the check order of
  request, claim, prove, respond, redeem and cancel. A host implements
  OobHost: records keyspace, DID, origin and name, step signer,
  carried-proof verifiers, accepted-id record, a per-audience gate at three
  fixed points, signingScope, audit, and redeem's completion. Audiences
  are the host's associated type, and the default is never stored or
  signed, so VTC rows and signatures are byte for byte unchanged. The
  generic half of delegated signing (scope match, exclusions, record,
  armed over the host's row and liveness) moves too.

  vtc-service keeps SessionAudience, the member and admin gates,
  PORTAL_SIGNING_SCOPE, the audit events, session and cookie minting, its
  delegation row, the session liveness check, and the DID-document checks.
  Behaviour is unchanged. Every existing test passes unmodified.

A push runs for hours or days (thirty for a removal notice), so a copy a mediator held while the recipient was offline was refused as stale when collected, and the engine had to keep issuing new documents under VTI-TRN-046 for the delivery to land. New attempts already carry it unchanged. - The engine places a document by its acceptance end (VTI-TRN-044): the stated expiry, bounded by the horizon, or issuedAt + the maximum age without one. It no longer issues new attempts at ten minutes for a document that is still acceptable, and counts a copy collected inside its stated expiry as delivered. The attempts at one operation are separate documents, and since #2423 a document stating an expiresAt is acceptable for up to thirty days (VTI-OPS-028), so an attempt arriving after the 24 hours would perform the operation again. VTI-OPS-066 requires the record to last until the latest acceptance end, plus the skew, of any document carrying the key that the node has accepted. - **trust-tasks**: Honour a stated expiresAt up to 30 days, and keep the replay record to the acceptance end (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028, VTI-OPS-029) ([#2423](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2423)) trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1021), with affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45 (affinidi-tdk-rs #983) and mediator 0.50 (affinidi-messaging-mediator #55), which move with it. ## [0.1.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/releases/tag/vti-oob-server-v0.1.0) — 2026-11-04 ### Changed - **vtc-service**: Wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate ([#2425](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2425)) * refactor(vtc-service): wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate The auth/oob key-grant flow (a wallet approving a browser's key K_b) moves out of vtc-service into a new workspace crate, so the VTN service can serve the same flow instead of a copy. The crate owns the request store and compare-and-set, the claim and decision clocks, the redeem long poll and its caps, the did:key precheck (T21), the carried-document checks (T7, T15) and the check order of request, claim, prove, respond, redeem and cancel. The generic half of delegated signing (scope match, exclusions, record, armed over the host's row and liveness) moves too. vtc-service keeps SessionAudience, the member and admin gates, PORTAL_SIGNING_SCOPE, the audit events, session and cookie minting, its delegation row, the session liveness check, and the DID-document checks. title: fix(release): a trust-tasks-rs range move is a breaking bump too
body:
The release job has failed on every push to main since #2425: the new
vti-oob-server 0.1.0 is packaged against the published vti-specs-core
0.3.0, built on trust-tasks-rs ^0.36, while the workspace moved to
^0.37 in #2423 — so its generated `auth/oob` types implement 0.36's
`Payload` and the crate needs 0.37's.

The Release PR would not have fixed it. release-plz gave vti-specs-core,
-rooms, -vtc and -vtn patch bumps, and check-release-bump-sizes.py did
not object: rules 2 and 3 only looked at internal dependencies, and
trust-tasks-rs is published from another repository. But every
generated vti_specs_* type implements its traits, so moving its range
breaks those crates' dependents exactly as moving a sibling's does
(#1795).

- Rules 2 and 3 now also track `SHARED_EXTERNAL` (trust-tasks-rs), so
  fix-release-bump-sizes.py raises those four to their next breaking
  version and moves vti-oob-server to vti-specs-core 0.4. Checked
  against the release-plz branch: one round, the guards pass, and
  `cargo check --workspace --locked` builds.
- A crate's first release no longer marks a run as a release. A new
  member sits unpublished on main until the release, and counting it
  would hold every feature PR to rule 3 — with trust-tasks-rs tracked,
  that turned main red for 18 crates. A Release PR always raises some
  published crate as well, which still sets it.

## Testing
- On `main`: `check-release-bump-sizes.py` passes (36 members).
- On `release-plz-2026-11-03T23-59-13Z`: it names exactly vti-specs-core, -rooms, -vtc, -vtn; `fix-release-bump-sizes.py` raises them (0.4.0 / 0.4.0 / 0.4.0 / 0.2.0) in one round, all guards then pass, `cargo check --workspace --locked` builds.

## After merge
The merge triggers a new Release PR. Its bot fix-up commit does not start CI (GITHUB_TOKEN), so close and reopen that PR to run CI on it.

title: fix(step-up): answer step-ups with auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7
body:
The VTC and the VTA moved every step-up answer to `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7` and stopped serving 0.4 and 0.6 (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2346). The wallet still pinned 0.6.

## What broke

Against a current VTC, the console's `approverSigned` flow failed at its last step. `approveStepUp` issued the statement, the console wrapped it in a 0.7 approve-response and asked the wallet to sign it as the subject, and the envelope missed the 0.6 carve-out in `approver-policy.ts` and fell through to `pageSignRefusal`'s generic refusal:

```
https://trusttasks.org/spec/auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7 cannot be signed for a page. A step-up approval is built only by the wallet's step-up flow (stepUpVta), which verifies the relying party's request and asks the holder first.
```

The same pin made the wallet's own answers to its VTA and to a relying party 0.6 documents, which those services no longer accept.

## What changes

- The pin moves to 0.7: `trust-tasks.toml`, `trust-tasks.lock`, the vendored bundle (digest as in `vti-specs-core`'s lock), and `src/specs/` regenerated with `npm run tasks:generate`. The lock holds one version per slug, so 0.6 goes.
- core: `vta/step-up.ts`, `rp-login/step-up.ts`, `persona/step-up.ts` and `trust-tasks/approver-attest.ts` import the 0.7 module. `APPROVE_RESPONSE_0_6_TYPE` is renamed `APPROVE_RESPONSE_0_7_TYPE`; nothing else in the repo used it.
- extension: the approver carve-out (`approverResponseRefusal`) and its dispatch in `background.ts` match the 0.7 type, so the console's wrapped statement is signed again.
- Tests and docs follow. The task-surface exemption for the 0.6 prefix is removed, since 0.7 is already in the vta-sdk snapshot.

The payload schema is byte-identical between 0.6 and 0.7. What changed in the specification is that a proof is no longer required by policy and the `assertionInvalid` reason enum is lowerCamelCase. The wallet signs unconditionally, so none of its answers change beyond the type URI.

## Verified

Built with the containerized build (lint, build, tests, CI assertions all pass). Loaded against vtc.oma.ic3.dev (vtc 0.18.0, vta 0.70.0): a community room create with an approver-signed step-up now completes.

## Worth a look

`rp-login/step-up.ts` now sends 0.7 to a did-hosting relying party as well. I have not verified that the did-hosting control plane serves 0.7; if it still serves 0.6 only, that flow needs its side moved too, since the wallet cannot speak both.

`pageSignRefusal`'s generic "cannot be signed for a page". The same pin also
made the wallet's own answers to its VTA and to a relying party 0.6
documents, which those services no longer accept.

The pin moves to 0.7 (`trust-tasks.toml`, `trust-tasks.lock`, the vendored
bundle, the regenerated `src/specs/`). The payload schema is unchanged
between 0.6 and 0.7; what changed is that a proof is no longer required by
policy and the `assertionInvalid` reason enum is lowerCamelCase. The wallet
signs unconditionally, so none of its answers change beyond the type URI.

- core: the four builders import the 0.7 module. `APPROVE_RESPONSE_0_6_TYPE`
  is renamed `APPROVE_RESPONSE_0_7_TYPE`.
- extension: the approver carve-out and its dispatch in `background.ts` match
  the 0.7 type, so the console's wrapped statement is signed once more.
- tests and docs follow; the task-surface exemption for the 0.6 prefix goes,
  since 0.7 is in the vta-sdk snapshot.

Verified against vtc.oma.ic3.dev (vtc 0.18.0): a community room create with
an approver-signed step-up now completes.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

* fix(step-up): route approver-signed approve-responses on their evidence, not their version

A version the wallet did not pin fell through to pageSignRefusal, whose
reason (use stepUpVta) is wrong for the console: the defect this PR fixes,
set up to recur at the next bump. isApproverSignedResponse routes on
evidence.kind === "approverSigned", as isApproverSignedDecision does, and
approverResponseRefusal refuses another version by name.

The extension now takes the type from core (APPROVER_RESPONSE_TYPE,
renamed without a version so a pin move renames nothing) rather than
spelling the URI a second time. Stale 0.6 wording in comments and test
names follows the pin.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: trust-tasks-https-v0.37.2
body:
### Added

- **trust-task-discovery**: Publish 0.4, a responder advertises the horizon up to which it honours a stated expiresAt ([#1030](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1030))

SPEC §7.2 (Bounding the record) applies a consumer's maximum age only where a
  document states no expiresAt, and since trust-tasks-rs 0.37 ([#1021](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1021))
  validate_freshness does so, honouring a stated expiry up to the policy's
  expiry_horizon. discovery 0.3 cannot describe that: its window "governs
  issuedAt only" and its responder refuses any document past
  issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds + clockSkewSeconds, whatever expiresAt it states. A
  responder that honours an expiry could only advertise a narrower window than
  it applies, and a producer could not learn that stating an expiry keeps a long
  delivery acceptable.

  - specs/trust-task-discovery/0.4: acceptanceWindow gains an optional
    expiryHorizonSeconds (whole seconds, at least 1), and the spec defines a
    document's acceptance end: issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds without an expiresAt;
    the earlier of expiresAt and issuedAt + expiryHorizonSeconds with one; and,
    where the window carries no horizon, the earlier of expiresAt and
    issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds, which is what a 0.3 window says.
    - Responder: MUST NOT advertise a horizon wider than it applies, nor one at
      all if it applies its maximum age whatever expiresAt states.
    - Discoverer: send bounds follow the acceptance end. MAY state an expiresAt
      within the horizon, no later than it will pursue delivery, instead of
      issuing a chain of new attempts; a new attempt carries it unchanged.
      Absent a horizon, it MUST assume the maximum age applies to every
      document.
    - AcceptanceWindow is closed in 0.3, so an added optional member is a MINOR
      increment (§5.2): a new version, not an edit.
    - Response-side invalid examples: a zero horizon, a duration string, and a
      fractional entry-level horizon.
  - trust-tasks-rs: DiscoveryRegistry::respond_to_v0_4 is the current answer.
    acceptance_window_from reads the policy's expiry_horizon, and
    expiry_horizon() sets one by hand. respond_to_v0_3 moves to
    discovery/superseded.rs and states the window without the horizon (narrower
    than applied, which 0.3 permits).
  - trust-tasks-https: enable_discovery answers 0.4, and 0.3 beside 0.2 and 0.1.
  - trust-tasks-dart-https: enableDiscovery answers 0.4. Dart's FreshnessPolicy
    has no horizon, so its window states none, which says the maximum age
    applies to every document. 0.3 moves to the superseded block.
  - Examples and tests that named the 0.3 types use 0.4.
  - Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart). 0.3 is superseded.

  Follows from #1021 and trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#96 (VTI-OPS-024,
  VTI-OPS-028, VTI-TRN-048), whose implementation in
  OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure states delivery deadlines as expiresAt.

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.13`) | `0.10.12` → `0.10.13` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.22` → `0.9.23` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_https` | pub.dev | `0.1.7` → `0.1.8` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_didcomm` | pub.dev | `0.1.2` → `0.1.3` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

Changelog

## `vti-specs-vta`

## [0.5.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-specs-vta-v0.4.0...vti-specs-vta-v0.5.0) — 2026-11-04 ### Added - **vta**: Collection for the principal's identifiers — claims, the collector, collection by default off (VTI-NTF-080 – 093) ([#2421](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2421)) * feat(vti-specs): pin vta/collection/{claim,release,list} 0.1 From trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1023 and #1024: a client's collection claim on a persona DID, its release, and the listing of who collects for each of a context's identifiers (VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-093).
## `vti-specs-vtc`
## [0.3.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-specs-vtc-v0.3.0...vti-specs-vtc-v0.3.1) — 2026-11-04 ### Added - **vtc-service**: Community boards — members propose ideas and leave notes, each accepted idea is its own election (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080) ([#2420](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2420)) * build(vti-specs-vtc): pin vtc/boards/*/0.1 The thirteen Community Boards tasks (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080): create, update, list and show a board; propose, update, withdraw, decide and select ideas; add, list, withdraw and hide notes. Resolved against a local build of dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/vtc-boards — re-pin against trusttasks.org once that publishes.
## `vta-sdk`
## [0.80.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.79.0...vta-sdk-v0.80.0) — 2026-11-04 ### Added - **vtc-service**: Community boards — members propose ideas and leave notes, each accepted idea is its own election (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080) ([#2420](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2420)) * build(vti-specs-vtc): pin vtc/boards/*/0.1 The thirteen Community Boards tasks (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080): create, update, list and show a board; propose, update, withdraw, decide and select ideas; add, list, withdraw and hide notes. Resolved against a local build of dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/vtc-boards — re-pin against trusttasks.org once that publishes. - **vta**: Collection for the principal's identifiers — claims, the collector, collection by default off (VTI-NTF-080 – 093) ([#2421](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2421)) * feat(vti-specs): pin vta/collection/{claim,release,list} 0.1 From trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1023 and #1024: a client's collection claim on a persona DID, its release, and the listing of who collects for each of a context's identifiers (VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-093). ### Changed - **vtc-service**: Wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate ([#2425](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2425)) * refactor(vtc-service): wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate The auth/oob key-grant flow (a wallet approving a browser's key K_b) moves out of vtc-service into a new workspace crate, so the VTN service can serve the same flow instead of a copy. The crate owns the request store and compare-and-set, the claim and decision clocks, the redeem long poll and its caps, the did:key precheck (T21), the carried-document checks (T7, T15) and the check order of request, claim, prove, respond, redeem and cancel. A host implements OobHost: records keyspace, DID, origin and name, step signer, carried-proof verifiers, accepted-id record, a per-audience gate at three fixed points, signingScope, audit, and redeem's completion. Audiences are the host's associated type, and the default is never stored or signed, so VTC rows and signatures are byte for byte unchanged. The generic half of delegated signing (scope match, exclusions, record, armed over the host's row and liveness) moves too. vtc-service keeps SessionAudience, the member and admin gates, PORTAL_SIGNING_SCOPE, the audit events, session and cookie minting, its delegation row, the session liveness check, and the DID-document checks. Behaviour is unchanged. Every existing test passes unmodified.
## `vti-common`
## [0.56.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-common-v0.55.0...vti-common-v0.56.0) — 2026-11-04 ### Added - **trust-task-push**: Pushed documents state their delivery deadline as expiresAt (VTI-TRN-048) ([#2428](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2428)) A pushed document stated no expiry, so a recipient accepted it for ten minutes after its issuedAt. A push runs for hours or days (thirty for a removal notice), so a copy a mediator held while the recipient was offline was refused as stale when collected, and the engine had to keep issuing new documents under VTI-TRN-046 for the delivery to land. Since #2423 a VTI consumer accepts a document until its stated expiresAt, up to thirty days (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028), so stating the deadline keeps the document acceptable for as long as it is pursued. vti-common trust_task_push: - `state_delivery_expiry` stamps an unsigned document's expiresAt at its push's deadline, counted from issuedAt in whole seconds, keeping an earlier expiry the task already states, and refusing a signed document. New attempts already carry it unchanged. - The engine places a document by its acceptance end (VTI-TRN-044): the stated expiry, bounded by the horizon, or issuedAt + the maximum age without one. It no longer issues new attempts at ten minutes for a document that is still acceptable, and counts a copy collected inside its stated expiry as delivered. Stated at every push whose window outlasts the ten-minute maximum age: the VTC's removal, authority-reduced, authority-reduction-pending, step-up passkey and break-glass notices, its notifications, and its consent requests (the action's expiry, capped at a week); the VTA's credential-exchange steps. The VTA's step-up and consent pushes run five to ten minutes, inside the maximum age, and are unchanged. - **idempotency**: Keep a keyed operation's record until the latest acceptance end under its key (VTI-OPS-066) ([#2426](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2426)) A keyed Trust Task's idempotency record lived 24 hours (the NonDestructive class TTL). The attempts at one operation are separate documents, and since #2423 a document stating an expiresAt is acceptable for up to thirty days (VTI-OPS-028), so an attempt arriving after the 24 hours would perform the operation again. VTI-OPS-066 requires the record to last until the latest acceptance end, plus the skew, of any document carrying the key that the node has accepted. - **trust-tasks**: Honour a stated expiresAt up to 30 days, and keep the replay record to the acceptance end (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028, VTI-OPS-029) ([#2423](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2423)) trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1021), with affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45 (affinidi-tdk-rs #983) and mediator 0.50 (affinidi-messaging-mediator #55), which move with it. Acceptance. A document that states an expiresAt is accepted until then, up to thirty days after its issuedAt, whatever the ten-minute maximum age (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028). An expiry beyond the horizon is clamped, not refused. A document without one keeps the ten-minute window. The horizon is `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::EXPIRY_HORIZON`, applied by `AcceptanceWindow::freshness_policy`, so every VTI consumer takes it. Retention. Every record of an accepted document was capped at issuedAt + max_age + skew, relying on the freshness check to refuse anything older. Under 0.37 that check accepts a document with a later expiresAt, so the record would be dropped while its document was still acceptable and a replay would execute twice. One rule now decides retention for every consumer, `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::retain_until`: the acceptance end plus the skew (VTI-OPS-029), bounded by the horizon. It is used by the shared receive pipeline (VTA and VTC accepted-id records), the VTC's spent step-up approver statements, vti-witness and room-host. Behaviour change for producers: a document stating a long expiresAt is no longer refused as stale after ten minutes. Step-up approver statements are included, as VTI-OPS-028 requires of any document that states an expiry. Not here: idempotency records still live 24 hours although a keyed document can now be acceptable for 30 days (VTI-OPS-066, next step); room-host's replay record is still in memory and lost on restart (VTI-OPS-029). - **vtc-service**: Community boards — members propose ideas and leave notes, each accepted idea is its own election (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080) ([#2420](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2420)) * build(vti-specs-vtc): pin vtc/boards/*/0.1 The thirteen Community Boards tasks (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080): create, update, list and show a board; propose, update, withdraw, decide and select ideas; add, list, withdraw and hide notes. Resolved against a local build of dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/vtc-boards — re-pin against trusttasks.org once that publishes. ### Fixed - **vtc,voting**: Recover a TSP relationship the peer forgot ([#2427](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2427)) A ballot box restarted under a live community stopped answering it: the voting service kept TSP relationships in memory, so after a restart (or a reconnect, which builds a fresh ATM) it held none with the community and, by TSP §7.2.2, dropped every frame unanswered. The VTC's durable half still read "related", so it never re-invited, and every election registration timed out for good. Both halves are fixed: - vtc-service: `PeerTasks::exchange` resets the TSP relationship on a reply timeout (D4 of tsp-relationship-recovery.md, as the registry client already does), so the caller's next attempt re-forms it through `send_reestablishing`. Repair only; the caller's backoff stays the one retry owner. - vti-common: `IdentitySession::with_relationship_store` lets a host service keep its relationships in a durable store. - vti-voting-service: keeps them in `data_dir/store` (`tsp_relationships`) and runs the store's maintenance loop once per process. - **contexts**: Purge every context-scoped record on delete ([#2419](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2419)) vta/contexts/delete removed a context's keys, DIDs, ACL scope, DID templates, app state and memory ([#2415](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2415)), but every other store that holds data for a context kept its rows. Most are keyed by the context id, or by a digest of it, so a context later created under the same id inherited them. ## [0.73.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-service-v0.72.0...vta-service-v0.73.0) — 2026-11-04 ### Added - **trust-task-push**: Pushed documents state their delivery deadline as expiresAt (VTI-TRN-048) ([#2428](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2428)) A pushed document stated no expiry, so a recipient accepted it for ten minutes after its issuedAt. A push runs for hours or days (thirty for a removal notice), so a copy a mediator held while the recipient was offline was refused as stale when collected, and the engine had to keep issuing new documents under VTI-TRN-046 for the delivery to land. Since #2423 a VTI consumer accepts a document until its stated expiresAt, up to thirty days (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028), so stating the deadline keeps the document acceptable for as long as it is pursued. vti-common trust_task_push: - `state_delivery_expiry` stamps an unsigned document's expiresAt at its push's deadline, counted from issuedAt in whole seconds, keeping an earlier expiry the task already states, and refusing a signed document. New attempts already carry it unchanged. - The engine places a document by its acceptance end (VTI-TRN-044): the stated expiry, bounded by the horizon, or issuedAt + the maximum age without one. It no longer issues new attempts at ten minutes for a document that is still acceptable, and counts a copy collected inside its stated expiry as delivered. Stated at every push whose window outlasts the ten-minute maximum age: the VTC's removal, authority-reduced, authority-reduction-pending, step-up passkey and break-glass notices, its notifications, and its consent requests (the action's expiry, capped at a week); the VTA's credential-exchange steps. The VTA's step-up and consent pushes run five to ten minutes, inside the maximum age, and are unchanged. - **idempotency**: Keep a keyed operation's record until the latest acceptance end under its key (VTI-OPS-066) ([#2426](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2426)) A keyed Trust Task's idempotency record lived 24 hours (the NonDestructive class TTL). The attempts at one operation are separate documents, and since #2423 a document stating an expiresAt is acceptable for up to thirty days (VTI-OPS-028), so an attempt arriving after the 24 hours would perform the operation again. VTI-OPS-066 requires the record to last until the latest acceptance end, plus the skew, of any document carrying the key that the node has accepted. - **trust-tasks**: Honour a stated expiresAt up to 30 days, and keep the replay record to the acceptance end (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028, VTI-OPS-029) ([#2423](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2423)) trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1021), with affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45 (affinidi-tdk-rs #983) and mediator 0.50 (affinidi-messaging-mediator #55), which move with it. An expiry beyond the horizon is clamped, not refused. A document without one keeps the ten-minute window. The horizon is `vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::EXPIRY_HORIZON`, applied by `AcceptanceWindow::freshness_policy`, so every VTI consumer takes it. Retention. Every record of an accepted document was capped at issuedAt + max_age + skew, relying on the freshness check to refuse anything older. Under 0.37 that check accepts a document with a later expiresAt, so the record would be dropped while its document was still acceptable and a replay would execute twice. It is used by the shared receive pipeline (VTA and VTC accepted-id records), the VTC's spent step-up approver statements, vti-witness and room-host. Behaviour change for producers: a document stating a long expiresAt is no longer refused as stale after ten minutes. Step-up approver statements are included, as VTI-OPS-028 requires of any document that states an expiry. ## [0.1.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/releases/tag/vti-oob-server-v0.1.0) — 2026-11-04 ### Changed - **vtc-service**: Wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate ([#2425](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2425)) * refactor(vtc-service): wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*) as the vti-oob-server crate The auth/oob key-grant flow (a wallet approving a browser's key K_b) moves out of vtc-service into a new workspace crate, so the VTN service can serve the same flow instead of a copy. The crate owns the request store and compare-and-set, the claim and decision clocks, the redeem long poll and its caps, the did:key precheck (T21), the carried-document checks (T7, T15) and the check order of request, claim, prove, respond, redeem and cancel. A host implements OobHost: records keyspace, DID, origin and name, step signer, carried-proof verifiers, accepted-id record, a per-audience gate at three fixed points, signingScope, audit, and redeem's completion. Audiences are the host's associated type, and the default is never stored or signed, so VTC rows and signatures are byte for byte unchanged. The generic half of delegated signing (scope match, exclusions, record, armed over the host's row and liveness) moves too. vtc-service keeps SessionAudience, the member and admin gates, PORTAL_SIGNING_SCOPE, the audit events, session and cookie minting, its delegation row, the session liveness check, and the DID-document checks. Behaviour is unchanged. Every existing test passes unmodified.

title: feat(trust-task-discovery): publish 0.4, a responder advertises the horizon up to which it honours a stated expiresAt (#1030)
body:
feat(trust-task-discovery): publish 0.4, a responder advertises the horizon up to which it honours a stated expiresAt (#1030)

SPEC §7.2 (Bounding the record) applies a consumer's maximum age only where a
document states no expiresAt, and since trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (#1021)
validate_freshness does so, honouring a stated expiry up to the policy's
expiry_horizon. discovery 0.3 cannot describe that: its window "governs
issuedAt only" and its responder refuses any document past
issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds + clockSkewSeconds, whatever expiresAt it states. A
responder that honours an expiry could only advertise a narrower window than
it applies, and a producer could not learn that stating an expiry keeps a long
delivery acceptable.

- specs/trust-task-discovery/0.4: acceptanceWindow gains an optional
  expiryHorizonSeconds (whole seconds, at least 1), and the spec defines a
  document's acceptance end: issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds without an expiresAt;
  the earlier of expiresAt and issuedAt + expiryHorizonSeconds with one; and,
  where the window carries no horizon, the earlier of expiresAt and
  issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds, which is what a 0.3 window says.
  - Responder: MUST NOT advertise a horizon wider than it applies, nor one at
    all if it applies its maximum age whatever expiresAt states.
  - Discoverer: send bounds follow the acceptance end. MAY state an expiresAt
    within the horizon, no later than it will pursue delivery, instead of
    issuing a chain of new attempts; a new attempt carries it unchanged.
    Absent a horizon, it MUST assume the maximum age applies to every
    document.
  - AcceptanceWindow is closed in 0.3, so an added optional member is a MINOR
    increment (§5.2): a new version, not an edit.
  - Response-side invalid examples: a zero horizon, a duration string, and a
    fractional entry-level horizon.
- trust-tasks-rs: DiscoveryRegistry::respond_to_v0_4 is the current answer.
  acceptance_window_from reads the policy's expiry_horizon, and
  expiry_horizon() sets one by hand. respond_to_v0_3 moves to
  discovery/superseded.rs and states the window without the horizon (narrower
  than applied, which 0.3 permits).
- trust-tasks-https: enable_discovery answers 0.4, and 0.3 beside 0.2 and 0.1.
- trust-tasks-dart-https: enableDiscovery answers 0.4. Dart's FreshnessPolicy
  has no horizon, so its window states none, which says the maximum age
  applies to every document. 0.3 moves to the superseded block.
- Examples and tests that named the 0.3 types use 0.4.
- Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart). 0.3 is superseded.

Follows from #1021 and trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#96 (VTI-OPS-024,
VTI-OPS-028, VTI-TRN-048), whose implementation in
OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure states delivery deadlines as expiresAt.

title: feat(console): edit a board from its page
body:
A facilitator could close or archive a board in the console but change
nothing else; every other change took `cnm` or a hand-built
`vtc/boards/update`. The board's page now has **Edit board**, a form
filled from the board as read: title, description, audience, the
proposal and voting windows, topics, formats, ideas per member, the
selection rule and the timetable.

Only the fields that differ are sent (`boardChanges`), compared to the
minute since a datetime input holds whole minutes, so an untouched
voting window or audience never reaches the board after voting opens,
where it is refused as `fixedAfterVotingOpens`; the form also shows
both as fixed then. Timetable slots keep their identifiers, so a
selected idea stays placed, and a new slot takes one no other slot has
used. The election template is not edited here (it takes
`vtc.elections.manage` as well).

docs/03-vtc/boards.md: *Changing a board*, including that an idea
already open for votes keeps the voting window its election was
registered with.

- `vitest run` in `vtc-service/admin-ui`: 1470 passed (three new in `plugins/Boards.test.tsx`: only changes are sent and an open vote's window never is; a voting window moves before voting opens; slot identifiers kept)

title: feat(cli): `pnm boards` and `cnm boards` for community boards
body:
Members and facilitators can now work a community board from the
command line (VTI-BRD-001 – 080), as the portal and console already do.

- vtc-client: `boards` — every `vtc/boards/*` task, each request read
  against its pinned schema before it is sent (`checked`), and each
  task's declared error codes (`declared`).
- vta-cli-common: `commands::boards` — a member's acts signed by their
  own VTA (`vault/sign-trust-task`), never a key the CLI holds, and
  checked to be the same document, proof aside, before sending.

title: fix(witness): keep TSP relationships on disk
body:
The witness kept its TSP relationships in memory, and `host_session`
builds a fresh ATM on every reconnect. After a restart or a dropped
socket it forgot every community, and TSP Rev 3 §7.2.2 has it drop —
unanswered — each frame from a VID it holds no relationship with, so
`witness/session` stopped silently while the community still held its
half. The voting service had the same fault (#2427).

Each identity's session now uses the durable store from
`vti_common::relationship_store`, in a `tsp_relationships` keyspace of
the witness's existing `<data_dir>/store`, opened once and shared with
the witness's own keyspaces. Records are keyed by `(our_vid, their_vid)`,
so up to ten identities share it safely. One maintenance loop runs per
process.

## Testing
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-witness` (78 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p vti-witness --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- Store durability itself is covered by `relationship_store::durability_tests::a_relationship_outlives_a_reopened_store` (#2427)

title: spec(process-attestation): label WritersProof as the Holder, and check that an implementation's role names a party
body:
Follow-up to #994 and #997.

- **`process-attestation/0.1`**: WritersProof is listed in the `{ url, role, name }` form #997 added (`role: Holder`), so the spec page says which party it plays.
- **Wording**: the outcome-evidence rule now says "a relying party MUST NOT" instead of "a consumer". The rule binds whoever relies on the citing artifact, and "consumer" means a document's recipient (SPEC §7.2). This was the non-blocking suggestion on #994.
- **`scripts/build-registry.mjs`**: a new `checkKnownImplementationRoles` fails the build when a `knownImplementations[].role` names none of the spec's `parties` and is not `both`. The meta-schema can only bound `role` as a string, and a typo would put a party the spec doesn't define on the page. It's a failure rather than a warning because nothing else uses `role` yet.

Verified locally: `npm run validate` and `npm run build` pass. Setting `role: Holdr` fails with:

```
process-attestation/0.1/spec.md: knownImplementations entry https://writersproof.com has role 'Holdr', which names none of this specification's parties ('Verifier', 'Holder') and is not 'both'. …
```

No library regeneration is needed: no generator or bundle reads `knownImplementations`, and the wording change is prose only.

title: fix(room-host): keep the accepted-document-id record in the store, so it survives a restart (VTI-OPS-029)
body:
room-host kept its record of accepted document ids (SPEC §7.2 item 11) in a
process-local InMemoryReplayGuard. A document accepted before a restart is
still inside its acceptance window after it, and since #2423 a document
stating an expiresAt is acceptable for up to thirty days (VTI-OPS-028), so a
restart inside a window is routine. A redelivery after one was executed again:
a records/put wrote a second version. VTI-OPS-029 requires the record to
survive a restart.

The host now uses vti-trust-task-server's StoreAcceptedIds, the record the
VTA and the VTC keep, over a new `accepted_ids` keyspace in its own store.
Retention is unchanged (the shared retain_until: acceptance end plus skew).
A claim is completed on success, with the response kept for consequential
tasks, and released on failure, as before. Expired rows are swept every five
minutes; reads already treat them as absent.

One host process owns its store, so a replicated host would still need the
record shared between replicas, as before.

## Tests
- New: `a_write_redelivered_after_a_restart_is_executed_once`: a put redelivered after reopening the store is answered from the record, the row is in the store keyspace, and the record stays at version 1
