title: feat(trust-task-push): pushed documents state their delivery deadline as expiresAt (VTI-TRN-048)
body:
A pushed document stated no expiry, so a recipient accepted it for ten
minutes after its issuedAt. A push runs for hours or days (thirty for a
removal notice), so a copy a mediator held while the recipient was offline
was refused as stale when collected, and the engine had to keep issuing new
documents under VTI-TRN-046 for the delivery to land. Since #2423 a VTI
consumer accepts a document until its stated expiresAt, up to thirty days
(VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028), so stating the deadline keeps the document
acceptable for as long as it is pursued.

vti-common trust_task_push:
- `state_delivery_expiry` stamps an unsigned document's expiresAt at its
  push's deadline, counted from issuedAt in whole seconds, keeping an earlier
  expiry the task already states, and refusing a signed document. New
  attempts already carry it unchanged.
- The engine places a document by its acceptance end (VTI-TRN-044): the
  stated expiry, bounded by the horizon, or issuedAt + the maximum age
  without one. It no longer issues new attempts at ten minutes for a
  document that is still acceptable, and counts a copy collected inside its
  stated expiry as delivered.

Stated at every push whose window outlasts the ten-minute maximum age: the
VTC's removal, authority-reduced, authority-reduction-pending, step-up passkey
and break-glass notices, its notifications, and its consent requests (the
action's expiry, capped at a week); the VTA's credential-exchange steps.
The VTA's step-up and consent pushes run five to ten minutes, inside the
maximum age, and are unchanged.

## Tests
- New: `a_stated_expiry_moves_the_acceptance_end`, `the_delivery_deadline_is_stated_as_the_expiry` (engine); `an_admin_removal_reaches_the_member_signed` now asserts the delivered notice states expiresAt = issuedAt + 30 days under its proof
- Workspace nextest 6886 passed; VTC nextest 3599 passed; doctests; clippy `-D warnings`; fmt

Step 5 of the expiresAt-window plan (#2423, #2426).

title: fix(vtc/voting): recover a TSP relationship the peer forgot
body:
## Problem

After the ballot box (`vti-voting-service`) restarted, every election a community sent it stayed `pendingRegistration` for good, and running elections got no more checkpoints. The voting service's debug log shows each frame from the VTC dropped:

```
ERROR affinidi_messaging_sdk::transport_adapter: cannot unpack an inbound TSP frame — … TSP message from …:first-vtc discarded: no relationship with …:device-bring
```

**Cause:**
- **The voting service forgets.** It keeps TSP relationships in the SDK's in-memory store, so a restart loses them. A mediator reconnect loses them too, because each session builds a fresh ATM.
- **The VTC never re-invites.** Its relationship record is durable and still reads "related", so it sends without re-forming the relationship. By TSP §7.2.2 the ballot box drops each frame unanswered.
- **The VTC has no recovery path.** On the reply timeout it returned `no reply … within 20s` and never repaired its record. The registry client already had that repair (D4, `tsp-relationship-recovery.md`); `PeerTasks::exchange` did not.

## Fix

- **vtc-service**: `PeerTasks::exchange` now resets the TSP relationship on a reply timeout. The caller's next attempt then re-forms it through `send_reestablishing`. This only repairs state and never resends; the caller's backoff remains the one retry owner. It covers every peer `PeerTasks` reaches, not only ballot boxes.
- **vti-common**: new `IdentitySession::with_relationship_store`, so a host service can keep its relationships in a durable store. The change is additive (the new field is private).
- **vti-voting-service**: relationships are now kept in `data_dir/store` (`tsp_relationships`), and the store's maintenance loop runs once per process. Documented in `docs/07-voting/README.md`.

Either fix alone recovers the stuck elections. Both are included so that a restart doesn't break delivery, and so that a peer which loses its relationships for any other reason is still recovered.

## Testing

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-voting-service -p vti-common -p vti-witness`: 909 of 909 pass.
- vtc-service tests matching election, board, outbound and peer: pass.
- New test `relationship_store::durability_tests::a_relationship_outlives_a_reopened_store`.
- The reset on timeout has no automated test. Nothing in the repo simulates a peer that silently drops frames, and the registry's identical path is not tested either. Verify it by deploying against a restarted ballot box.

## Follow-up

`vti-witness` builds its sessions through the same `host_session` and has the same weakness. Opting it in is now a two-line change, left out to keep this PR focused.
author: stormer78

title: fix(vtc,voting): recover a TSP relationship the peer forgot (#2427)
body:
fix(vtc,voting): recover a TSP relationship the peer forgot (#2427)

A ballot box restarted under a live community stopped answering it: the
voting service kept TSP relationships in memory, so after a restart (or
a reconnect, which builds a fresh ATM) it held none with the community
and, by TSP §7.2.2, dropped every frame unanswered. The VTC's durable
half still read "related", so it never re-invited, and every election
registration timed out for good.

Both halves are fixed:

title: feat(idempotency): keep a keyed operation's record until the latest acceptance end under its key (VTI-OPS-066)
body:
A keyed Trust Task's idempotency record lived 24 hours (the NonDestructive
class TTL). The attempts at one operation are separate documents, and since
#2423 a document stating an expiresAt is acceptable for up to thirty days
(VTI-OPS-028), so an attempt arriving after the 24 hours would perform the
operation again. VTI-OPS-066 requires the record to last until the latest
acceptance end, plus the skew, of any document carrying the key that the node
has accepted.

vti-common: IdempotencyStore::claim_retained takes the claiming document's
retention end. A new record expires at the later of it and the class TTL; a
repeat of the same request (completed, in flight or abandoned) extends the
record it finds, written conditionally on the row as read so a completion
landing meanwhile is not undone. A different request under the key is a
conflict and extends nothing. claim keeps its signature and behaviour.

vta-service: the keyed-task claim passes the document's acceptance end plus
skew (the same retain_until the accepted-id record uses). The sweeper already
goes by each record's own expiry.

## Tests
- New: `a_record_lasts_until_the_documents_acceptance_end`, `a_repeat_with_a_later_acceptance_end_extends_the_record` (store), `vti_ops_066_the_record_lasts_until_the_latest_acceptance_end` (VTA)
- Workspace nextest 6887 passed; VTC nextest 3599 passed; doctests; clippy `-D warnings`; fmt

Step 4 of the expiresAt-window plan, after #2423.

body:
fix(extension): an untitled room record is named by its first line, and a file record shows its caption

Keyring writes a room message as a record whose `body` holds the words and
which has no `title`, as SealedRecordBody allows. The records pane listed
every such record as "Untitled record", so a room of messages read as a

title: fix(vta-service): a re-admitted room member acts on the room's later grant instead of being locked out
body:
fix(vta-service): a re-admitted room member acts on the room's later grant instead of being locked out

A member removed from a room and offered it again holds the room's first
AuthorityCredential and MembershipCredential beside the re-issued ones:
accepting stores the new credentials and nothing retires the old. The
presentation oracle refused any persona holding two of a kind from one
room, so from the accept on every action in that room failed with
"which one to attenuate from is not a question this can answer safely",
at every VTA version, with no way out short of archiving the older
credential by hand.

The oracle now uses, of each kind separately, the credential with the
latest validFrom among those in force (one not yet valid never displaces
one that is). That is the room's own rule rather than a guess: a removal
withdraws the member with a subject entry covering every credential
issued before its revokedAt (rooms/revocations/put, Matching), so after
re-admission the earlier credential is the withdrawn one. Only two
equally recent credentials are still refused, and the refusal now names
their vault ids so the holder can archive the one it does not mean.

Reported from Keyring (berkmancenter/keyring-wallet
docs/upstream/2026-11-rooms-findings.md, finding 1).

title: feat(trust-tasks)!: honour a stated expiresAt up to 30 days, and keep the replay record to the acceptance end (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028, VTI-OPS-029)
body:
trust-tasks-rs 0.37 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1021), with
affinidi-tdk 0.37, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.45 (affinidi-tdk-rs #983) and
mediator 0.50 (affinidi-messaging-mediator #55), which move with it.

Acceptance. A document that states an expiresAt is accepted until then, up to
thirty days after its issuedAt, whatever the ten-minute maximum age
(VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028). An expiry beyond the horizon is clamped, not
refused. A document without one keeps the ten-minute window. The horizon is
`vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::EXPIRY_HORIZON`, applied by
`AcceptanceWindow::freshness_policy`, so every VTI consumer takes it.

Retention. Every record of an accepted document was capped at
issuedAt + max_age + skew, relying on the freshness check to refuse anything
older. Under 0.37 that check accepts a document with a later expiresAt, so
the record would be dropped while its document was still acceptable and a
replay would execute twice. One rule now decides retention for every consumer,
`vti_common::trust_task::acceptance::retain_until`: the acceptance end plus the
skew (VTI-OPS-029), bounded by the horizon. It is used by the shared receive
pipeline (VTA and VTC accepted-id records), the VTC's spent step-up approver
statements, vti-witness and room-host.

Behaviour change for producers: a document stating a long expiresAt is no
longer refused as stale after ten minutes. Step-up approver statements are
included, as VTI-OPS-028 requires of any document that states an expiry.

Not here: idempotency records still live 24 hours although a keyed document
can now be acceptable for 30 days (VTI-OPS-066, next step); room-host's replay
record is still in memory and lost on restart (VTI-OPS-029).

## Tests
- New: `vti_ops_028_*` and `vti_ops_029_*` in vti-common, vta-service and vtc-service (a day-long expiry accepted an hour on and retained to it; a far expiry clamped to the horizon; each acceptance end + skew)
- Workspace nextest 6884 passed; VTC nextest 3599 passed; doctests; clippy `-D warnings`; fmt

Step 3 of the expiresAt-window plan (spec #96, tt-tf #1021, VTI #2417).

title: feat(vtc-service)!: talk to networks over vtn/* Trust Tasks
body:
A community now talks to Verifiable Trust Networks over `vtn/*` Trust Tasks. Before this, it signed in and called REST routes that the VTN removed in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network#9. Until this merges, a VTC can't join, leave or repudiate a VTN on current main.

**`vtc-service` networks code (`vtc-service/src/networks`)**

- **No session:** each request is a `vtn/*` task signed as the community (`VtnClient::task` with the community's `Party`), addressed to the network DID the administrator named.
- **Profile check:** the network's profile is still read first, and a URL that answers as another DID is still a mismatch.
- **Task mapping:**

  | Step | Task |
  |---|---|
  | own entry and listing | `vtn/entries/show` |
  | membership offer | `vtn/membership/offer` |
  | acknowledge | `vtn/membership/acknowledge` |
  | repudiate a listing, or leave | `vtn/membership/repudiate` |
  | register a group | the signed `vtn/groups/register` request itself, sent unchanged |

- **Typed answers:** each network answer is read as its generated `#response` type, so an answer that doesn't match the spec is refused. A `...:notListed` refusal maps to `NetError::NotListed`; anything else maps to `NetError::Refused`, as before.
- **Relay unchanged:** broadcasts still reach the community at its relay endpoint as `{ envelope }`, until `vtc/networks` 0.2 (VTN A15).

**`vti-vtn` (breaking; release-plz should bump it to 0.3)**

- Removed `VtnClient::sign_in`, `VtnClient::sign_in_as`, the session token, and `SignInLink` (`vtn-signin:` links). No network serves `/v1/auth/*` any more. Browser sign-in returns with `auth/oob/*`.
- What's left: `profile`, `get`, `post`, `post_url`, `get_url`, the `tasks` client and `StatusChecker`.

**Tests**

- The fake networks in `networks/tests.rs` and `tests/it/networks.rs` are now Trust Task endpoints. They check each request's `authentication` proof and recipient, as a real network does, and answer with spec-shaped `#response` documents or `trust-task-error` documents.
- The removed `SignInLink` round-trip test went with `link.rs`.
- Results:
  - `cargo clippy -p vti-vtn -p vtc-service --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.
  - `vti-vtn` tests pass: 23, 4 and 1.
  - `vtc-service` networks tests pass: 5 unit and 3 integration.
  - The full `vtc-service` run: 2172 + 1376 passed, 0 failed.

title: feat(vtc-service): community boards — members propose ideas and leave notes, each accepted idea is its own election (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080)
body:
## What and why

A **board** is a shared space where members propose ideas and leave notes under their own name, a facilitator accepts, declines or merges each idea, every accepted idea is put to an **election of its own** from the board's template, and facilitators select among them with the result in view — an unconference, a roadmap, a retrospective, on the community's own voting.

- **`vtc-service`**: a `boards` module with its own backed-up keyspace, and the thirteen `vtc/boards/*/0.1` tasks. Members' acts accept the portal's session key (`vtc/boards` joins `PORTAL_SIGNING_SCOPE`); facilitators' never do. New capability `vtc.boards.manage`, qualifiable `board:<id>`; creating a board or changing its template also takes `vtc.elections.manage`.
- **Accepting an idea** opens its election through `elections::ops::check_create` + `create`, never parked. The idea stores only the election id: open / registering / refused, the ballot count and the result are read from the election record each time, so the board keeps no second copy of election state — and it never records or reports a ticket or a ballot. A crash between recording the id and creating the election leaves the idea plainly proposed; accepting again opens the same (deterministic) election.
- **Results without certification**: certify's checks move into `elections::ops::verify` (certify calls it unchanged); `verify_and_keep` keeps a verified, **uncertified** result on `ElectionRecord::verified` (serde-default, so existing records read) for facilitators who may not hold `vtc.elections.manage`. The election sweeper fills it once a board election closes, and checkpoints board elections every 30 min — spread over longer voting periods so the 256 kept heads never run out and the count keeps moving.
- **`vti-common`**: `AuditEvent::BoardChanged` (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so not breaking). **`vta-sdk`**: OpenAPI wrappers for the thirteen tasks.
- **Member portal**: `#/boards`, `#/boards/<id>` — lanes, idea panel with voting handed to the wallet, notes wall, timetable, proposing with the VTI-BRD-070 disclosure. "Take your tickets" uses the wallet's `elections.takeTickets` (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#413), else one `takeTicket` per election.
- **Console**: a Boards plugin for facilitators (create, decide, select into slots, hide notes, close/archive).
- **Docs**: `docs/03-vtc/boards.md`, `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-boards.md`, the flow entry in `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md`.

## Pin

`vti-specs-vtc` pins `vtc/boards/*/0.1` from trusttasks.org (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1025, published).

## Requirements

VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080 (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#98); touches VTI-VOT-020, 022, 025, 033, 052, 070, 071, 080, 081.

## Backport

none

## Tests

- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3609/3609 (default features), 3702/3702 (`--features vtc-service/voting`, incl. a concurrent-accept test), with the admin UI built.
- `vti-common` + `vta-sdk`: 2187/2187. Doc tests pass. `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean on both feature sets; `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- Admin UI: `tsc -b` clean, `wire:check` clean, vitest 1465/1465 (incl. 18 new board tests and the list-limit census).

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

### Cross-service (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new `reqwest::Client::new()` / bare fetch; the ballot box is reached only through the existing `elections::link` (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await — `boards::WRITE_LOCK` is released before the election is created over the link (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or resumable: an idea is `open` only once the ballot box registered its election; the recorded id is resumable by re-accepting (R2.1)
- [x] Retries bounded and backed off: registration redelivery stays with the existing election sweeper, the one retry owner (R1.4)
- [x] Wire types camelCase, generated from the pinned specs; schemas registered (R3.*)
- [x] Absence = most restrictive: without `voting`, `create` refuses every template (R5.*)
- [x] Logs claim only what was verified; a result is shown as "verified, not certified" unless certified (R6.*)

- Docs: docs/03-vtc/boards.md, docs/05-design-notes/vtc-boards.md, and the flow entry in vtc-service/CLAUDE.md.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-service): open an idea's election without holding the board lock (R1.3)

Accepting an idea held boards::WRITE_LOCK while elections::ops::create delivered the registration over the ballot box's link — a lock across a network await (vti-stack-development-guide R1.3). The lock is now released once the idea records its (deterministic) election id, and taken again to finish, re-reading the idea first.

With the lock released, two facilitators can accept one idea at once; the second finds the election the first created, and was answered as refused, which would have cleared a live election's id from the idea. OpenError::AlreadyOpening answers it with the idea as it stands instead, and a refusal clears the id only while it still names an election nobody created. title: feat(service)!: the API is vtn/* Trust Tasks
body:
`vtn-service` now serves its API as the `vtn/*` 0.1 Trust Tasks (trusttasks.org) at `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, all 33 of them. This is step 4 of `docs/trust-tasks.md`.

**How a request is handled**

Every document goes through the shared `vti-trust-task-server` pipeline, in this order:
1. size;
2. the 10-minute acceptance window;
3. the recipient must be this network;
4. the task's own spec policy;
5. the proof, made for `authentication` by the document's `issuer`;
6. the duplicate-id record;
7. dispatch.

The network signs every answer, refusals included.

- **Who is asking:** the proof's signer is the caller. There is no sign-in and no session (`auth.rs`).
- **Payloads and responses:** both are held to their published schemas. `tasks/wire.rs` maps the stored types to the `vtn/_shared` shapes. Storage formats don't change.
- **Refusals:** they carry the codes the specs declare (`vtn/<slug>:<local>`). Declared codes are read from `vti_specs_vtn::schema_index::error_codes_for`. A code a spec doesn't declare is sent as `taskFailed` instead.
- **Duplicate ids:** they are recorded in the store (keyspace `accepted_ids`), not in memory, so a document executes once even across a restart. Records are pruned every 10 minutes.

**What moved onto tasks**

- **Relay:** broadcasts reach a member network as `vtn/relay/deliver`, signed by the delivering network.
  - That network must be one the receiver joined, and the envelope's last hop must be its own.
  - A network registers its own `/v1/trust-tasks` as its group's endpoint.
  - Community inboxes still get `{ envelope }` over HTTPS until `vtc/networks` 0.2 (A15).
- **This network as a member:** joining, leaving and repudiating a parent use `vtn/*` tasks signed by this network. `memberships/join` and `memberships/repudiate` name the parent's DID; a URL that answers as another network is refused with `networkMismatch`.
- **nnm:** every command is a signed task. `nnm token` and `nnm login` are removed. `memberships join` and `memberships repudiate` take `--parent <did>`.
- **Landing page:** it reads the directory, counts and graph with unsigned tasks.

**Behaviour changes**

- Repeating a transition returns the entry unchanged instead of refusing (A22).
- `listings/update` changes only the fields named; an empty string clears a field.
- `groupTaken` is checked.
- A20 limits are applied in config: `[relay] ttl_hours` defaults to 24 and may be at most 168. A room `id` must match the spec pattern.

**Breaking**

- **REST removed:** the REST API is gone (A9). Only `/`, `/.well-known/vtn`, `/v1/status/*`, `/v1/index` and `/v1/credentials/{id}` remain.
- **Index and credentials:** these two are served only when the directory is public (new A21). The contract had said a signed document in the `Trust-Task` header would gate them. But in VTI that header carries a task's Type URI, not a signed document, so no such convention exists. In a restricted network the same credentials come through `vtn/entries/show` and `vtn/graph/show`.
- **Browser sign-in:** it returns with `auth/oob/*` (A13). Until then, a members-only or admins-only directory isn't browsable from the landing page; `nnm directory` still reads it.
- **VTC compatibility:** VTCs on the current `vtc-service` networks client still call REST, so they can't talk to a VTN on this branch until that client moves onto `vti_vtn::tasks`, which is the next VTI PR.

**Not in this PR**

- **Response signatures:** `vti_vtn::tasks::read_answer` checks the answer's issuer, recipient and thread, but not its proof. Credentials carried in answers are verified as before (A19).
- **Unsigned reads are still recorded:** the shared spine claims a duplicate-id record for unsigned public reads too, so each landing-page read writes a store row (pruned after its window).

**Tests**

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass: 6 cascade, 11 network API and 3 unit tests.
- New coverage:
  - a forged issuer, a proof made for the wrong purpose, the wrong recipient and a stale `issuedAt` are refused;
  - a replayed document returns the same answer, and a different document under the same id is refused with `idConflict`;
  - every one of the 33 Type URIs is routed;
  - unknown types and versions are refused;
  - partial update and the repeated transitions;
  - the spec codes for `rolesUnregistered` (with `details.roles`), `notMember`, `notEligible`, `chainInvalid`, `unknownRoom`, `networkMismatch` and `notListed`.
- Removed: the browser sign-in test (the flow is gone).

title: feat(extension): take a board's tickets in one decision — elections.takeTickets (VTI-BRD-034)
body:
## What

A community board (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#98) puts each accepted idea to its own election, so a member taking part in a dozen ideas faced a dozen ticket windows.

`window.vtaWallet.elections.takeTickets({ hostDid, electionIds, member? })`, 1–50 election ids:

- Passes the same gates as `takeTicket` (the page is the community's `SignInPortal`, the member is the wallet's).
- Reads each election as `takeTicket` does, but **never presents a membership just to read one**: an election shown only to a party's members (VTI-VOT-015) comes back `unavailable`, to be taken alone.
- Asks **once**, in one `kind: "tickets"` window listing every election and what each claim presents (VTI-VOT-025, 090).
- Then asks the community for **each ticket in its own request**, a random 1–6 s pause apart (CSPRNG), so they never arrive as one burst that ties the elections together in time. One refusal does not stop the rest.
- The page gets one outcome per election — `taken`, `held`, `unavailable`, `notEligible`, `failed` — all of which the community already knows.

Also names the new `vtc/boards` signing scope in the sign-in window ("proposing ideas and leaving notes as you — never voting").

## Tests

- 9 new gate tests in `tests/elections-page.test.mts` (49/49 in the file).
- `npm test` in `packages/extension`: 1465/1465. `npm run build` clean; `dist/background.js` has no dynamic `import()`.

## Companion PRs

The VTC portal uses it (falls back to one `takeTicket` per election on an older wallet); link in the next comment.

title: Add a Community Boards chapter: members propose ideas and leave notes, each accepted idea is put to its own election, and facilitators select among them (VTI-BRD-001 – VTI-BRD-080)
body:
## What

A new normative chapter, **Community Boards** (`spec/12c-vtc-boards.md`): a shared space where the members a board's audience admits propose ideas and leave notes under their own name, a facilitator accepts, declines or merges each idea, every accepted idea is put to an election of its own, and facilitators select among the ideas with the results in view. An unconference, a roadmap or a retrospective, run on the community's own voting.

- **Boards** (VTI-BRD-001 – 005): identifier, audience (all members or one group), proposal and voting windows, election template. Creating one takes `vtc.boards.manage` *and* `vtc.elections.manage`, because the template decides the elections its facilitators will open.
- **Ideas** (010 – 013): seven states; only the proposer edits or withdraws; facilitators accept/decline/merge, never their own idea while another facilitator exists.
- **Notes** (020 – 022): attributed, never edited, withdrawable by the author, hideable by a facilitator with a stated reason; never carried into any election.
- **Elections** (030 – 034): a template is a manifest less what the community fills per idea, never binding, roll = the board's audience. One election per idea, recorded open only once the ballot box registered it. **A board never shows or records whether a party took a ticket or voted**; while voting is open it shows at most the public board's ballot count. Taking several tickets at once is still one request per election.
- **Selection** (040 – 042): recorded with the result it was made with and whether it was certified; shown beside the result; grants nothing.
- **Members' acts and the portal** (050 – 051), **departure and erasure** (060 – 061), **disclosure** (070), **audit** (080).

Also: `vtc.boards.manage` registered in Appendix C.3 (qualifiable `board:<id>`), and the `BRD` prefix in the conformance table. Two open issues are recorded in the chapter: anonymous proposals, and the timing of batched ticket requests.

## Companion PRs

Wire specs, implementation and wallet follow; links in the next comment.

title: feat(vta)!: collection for the principal's identifiers — claims, the collector, collection by default off (VTI-NTF-080 – 093)
body:
Implements **collection for the principal's identifiers** (dtgwg-vti-spec #97, chapter 05a, VTI-NTF-080 – 093, Appendix F.3) over `vta/collection/{claim,release,list}/0.1` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1023, #1024).

The VTA decides who holds each persona DID's one mediator connection: the VTA itself, one client under a **collection claim** (a lease), or nobody and why. The VTA collects only when the operator turns on **collection by default**. It is **off** unless enabled (VTI-NTF-093), and claims are served either way.

## What is built

- **Pins.** `vta/collection/{claim,release,list}/0.1` and the shared `_shared/0.1` are pinned in `vti-specs-vta` with the `trust-tasks` CLI, at the bundles that include #1024 (category `notifications`, the `disabled` reason, the 24-hour lease).
- **The tasks** (`trust_tasks::collection`, `operations::collection`). All three need standing in the context.
  - **claim:** records the claim, then closes the VTA's connection, both under the identifier's lock, before it answers (VTI-NTF-082). The end is capped at `max_claim_secs`, at most thirty days, and the default grant is 24 hours. A renewal answers `renewed: true`.
  - **release:** a release by the claimant ends the claim at once. A release by anyone else makes it unrenewable; it still ends at its end, and the VTA waits out `clock_skew_secs` before collecting again (VTI-NTF-084).
  - **list:** shows `vta`, `client` with the claim, or `none` with `limit`, `conflict` or `disabled`, with paging and filters (VTI-NTF-091).
  - Every declared code is witnessed: `notCollectable`, `claimHeld`, `claimNotRenewable`.
- **Candidates** (VTI-NTF-080): every `did:webvh` the VTA holds in an existing context whose current, non-deactivated document advertises a `TSPTransport` or `DIDCommMessaging` endpoint naming a mediator DID. Services are matched on `type`. Excluded:
  - the VTA's own DID;
  - every ACL subject;
  - identities provision-integration minted for another party (now recorded as `provisioned:`);
  - the configured mediator;
  - `[collection] exclude`.
- **The collector** (`messaging::collector`):
  - **One session per collected DID:** its own TDK and ATM holding only that DID's keys, one profile, one websocket, and DIDComm and TSP on that socket. `CollectionControl::insert` refuses a second session for the same DID, and the collector never opens one for the VTA's own DID.
  - **Reconcile loop:** runs every 30 s, and at once after a claim, a release or a change of the setting. It closes sessions the plan no longer gives the VTA, and rebuilds a session when its keys or mediator change (VTI-NTF-090).
  - **Notifications** (VTI-NTF-086): a collected notify or relay goes through exactly the deposit path (`bind_document_to_sender` → `verify_delivery` → `admit_carried_document` at collection time → `receive`). The VTA answers as the persona, with the persona as issuer and the persona's proof, and the receipt is the same whatever it did.
  - **Everything else** (VTI-NTF-087, VTI-OPS-081): refused with `unsupportedType`, answered as the persona. It never reaches the dispatch spine and never names the VTA. A TSP relationship request and a DIDComm trust ping are answered as their transports require.
  - **Budgets** (VTI-TRN-029 / VTI-NTF-088): a sender without an ACL entry is charged to the single bound for senders without standing; one with an entry is charged to its own client bound. No bound is per identifier.
  - **Conflicts** (VTI-NTF-085): five connections that close within 30 s of opening, within 15 minutes, stop collection for that DID. It is recorded as a `conflict:` row and audited as `collection.conflict`, and a claim on the DID clears it.
  - **Shutdown:** the collector closes every connection before a soft restart's next generation starts.
- **Lifecycle:** a context deletion purges the context's claims, joining the #2419 purge set and its census. The sweep drops claims and conflicts on a DID that is no longer collectable. An `acl/grant` hand-off rollover and `acl/swap-key` carry claims to the successor.
- **Config:** a new `[collection]` section with `collect_by_default`, `max_identifiers` (64), `max_claim_secs`, `default_claim_secs`, `clock_skew_secs` and `exclude`.
  - `collect_by_default` is also settable in the tenant overlay. It is deliberately not a `config/patch` key, because a patch is lost on enclave restart.
  - A change is audited as `collection.enabled` / `collection.disabled` at the boot that applies it.
- **Keyspace `collection`:** backed up, because a restored VTA without its claims would be the second connection to every claimed persona. Classified in the backup partition, the DID-deletion census (`Orphaned`, swept) and the context-deletion census (`Purged`).
- **Client side:**
  - **SDK:** `TASK_VTA_COLLECTION_*`, with claim and release `RetrySafe` and list `ReadOnly`, and `VtaClient::collection_{claim,release,list}{,_json}` on the generated types.
  - **pnm:** `pnm collection claim|release|list`. `claimHeld` prints the `pnm collection release` command to run.
  - **vta-mcp:** `claim` is a mutating verb.
- **Docs:** `docs/02-vta/collection.md`, which includes what connections for different contexts reveal in common (VTI-TRN-027), and flow entries in both CLAUDE.md files.

## Not met, or open

- **VTI-NTF-090 (SHOULD):** the VTA does not keep collecting at the previous mediator after a mediator change. The new one takes over at once.
- **Personas collected:** only `did:webvh`. A `did:peer` relationship DID with a mediated service is not a candidate yet. A key held as an *internal* (non-extractable) key cannot be collected with, because the session needs the key in its secrets resolver.
- **Provisioned before this release:** an integration provisioned earlier carries no `provisioned:` marker. If it holds no ACL entry of its own, it is a candidate. The docs tell operators to list a context and use `[collection] exclude` before enabling collection.
- **Conflict detection:** the VTA infers a conflict from connections that die young. The SDK logs the mediator's `duplicate-channel` close reason but does not hand it to the caller, so a mediator that flaps the same way would also read as a conflict.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). The websocket connect is bounded at 30 s.
- [ ] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). **Deviation, deliberate:** the per-identifier lock is held across "write the claim, close the session" (grant) and "re-read the claim, open the session" (collector), which is what makes VTI-NTF-081 hold. It serialises only work on the same identifier, never unrelated ones.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable (R2.1). If the process dies after the claim is written and before the connection closes, the claim is in force and the VTA does not reopen; the client's retry is a renewal.
- [x] Every retry is bounded and backed off (R1.4). A session that fails to open is retried at 30 s doubling to 10 min, and the SDK's reconnect escalates on short-lived connections. Clients never blind-retry; the SDK classes are set.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). The reconcile loop logs and continues, and a session's inbound loop ends only on cancel or when its stream closes.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). The delivery layer's `subscribe` owns acks; a notification is held before the receipt.
- [x] New wire types (R3.*): none hand-written; all are generated, camelCase. Conformance witnesses are added and the schema index is pinned.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): collection is off unless enabled.
- [x] Logs and status claim only what was verified (R6.*). "Collecting" is logged only once the websocket is open, and the listing reads live session state, not a latch. Conflicts are audited.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): see above.
- [x] Deviations flagged: R1.3, above.

## Tests

- **Operations** (`operations/collection_tests.rs`):
  - candidates and their exclusions;
  - the setting off by default, `disabled` in the listing, and claims still served;
  - the setting's audit;
  - a grant closes the VTA's session before it answers;
  - the one-socket invariant;
  - lease cap, renewal and `claimHeld`;
  - release by another party (unrenewable, skew wait) and by the claimant (ends at once);
  - standing and collectability;
  - the plan's bound, conflict and claim handling across contexts;
  - rollover carry, context purge and the sweep;
  - list filters and paging.
- **Trust Tasks** (`trust_tasks/collection_tests.rs`):
  - a collected notify is held and answered as the persona with a verifying proof and no mention of the VTA's DID;
  - a repeat gets the same receipt;
  - a non-notification from a sender with admin standing is refused `unsupportedType` as the persona;
  - a document not bound to its sender is refused;
  - errors are not answered;
  - every declared code is driven through the handlers.
- **Collector:** the conflict bound and its window.

## For clients (OpenVTC)

A client that holds a persona's mediator connection must call `vta/collection/claim` **before** it connects. It should ask for 24 h and renew once half the granted period has passed. It must close the connection before `endsAt` minus its own skew unless it has renewed, and it must close first and then call `vta/collection/release` when it stops. On `claimHeld` or `notCollectable` it must not connect. It keeps depositing what it collects with `vta/notifications/deposit`. Operators should turn on `collect_by_default` only once every client in use does this (Appendix F.3).

  whether or not collection by default is on (VTI-NTF-093). A grant records
  the claim and closes the VTA's connection under the identifier's lock
  before it answers (VTI-NTF-082); the end is capped at the stated maximum
  (thirty days); a renewal answers renewed: true. Release by the claimant
  ends the claim at once; by another party it becomes unrenewable and ends at
  its end, and the VTA waits out its clock skew (VTI-NTF-084). A rollover or
  acl/swap-key carries the claim. Declared codes notCollectable, claimHeld,
  claimNotRenewable.
- Candidates (VTI-NTF-080) exclude the VTA's own DID, every ACL subject,
  identities provision-integration minted for another party (now recorded),
  the configured mediator and [collection] exclude.
- The collector (messaging::collector): one session — its own TDK and ATM,
  one websocket, DIDComm and TSP on it — per collected DID; a second for the
  same DID is refused, never the VTA's own. Collected notify/relay are taken
  exactly as a deposit and answered as the persona with the same receipt
  (VTI-NTF-086); every other operation is refused unsupportedType as the
  persona, never dispatched, never naming the VTA (VTI-NTF-087). Senders
  without standing share the node's one bound (VTI-NTF-088). Five
  short-lived connections in fifteen minutes stop collection, recorded and
  audited as a conflict until a client claims the identifier (VTI-NTF-085).
  A rotation or mediator change rebuilds the session (VTI-NTF-090).
- [collection] collect_by_default, off unless enabled (VTI-NTF-093), also in
  the tenant overlay; a change is audited at the boot that applies it.
- Keyspace `collection` (backed up, cascades with its DID); context deletion
  purges its claims.
- SDK: TASK_VTA_COLLECTION_* (claim/release RetrySafe, list ReadOnly),
  VtaClient::collection_{claim,release,list}{,_json}. pnm collection
  claim|release|list. vta-mcp: `claim` is a mutating verb.
- Docs: docs/02-vta/collection.md; flow entries in CLAUDE.md.

BREAKING CHANGE: vta_config::AppConfig gains `collection`;
vta_keyspaces::Keyspaces gains `collection`; vta_service::server::AppState
gains `collection_ks` and `collection`.

title: refactor!: use VTI's vti-vtn in place of vtn-core and vtn-client
body:
Builds against `vti-vtn` 0.2.0 from crates.io (released in VTI #2411).

`vtn-core` and `vtn-client` moved into VTI as `vti-vtn`, shared with the VTC. This PR deletes both and uses `vti-vtn` (feature `client`) everywhere. It's step one of moving onto Trust Tasks; the API itself is still REST.

**What `vti-vtn` 0.2 changes here**
- A group registration is the member's signed `vtn/groups/register` request; `servesRole` is retired. The network's `groupRegistered` acceptance binds its digest, proof included.
- Registered endpoints must be `https://`.
- Room passes last at most 24h, and broadcasts at most 7 days after `sentAt`.

**New setting:** `extra_root_certificates`, PEM files of certificate authorities this network trusts, beside the system's, when it calls another party over HTTPS. A closed deployment with a private CA needs it, and so do the tests.

**Tests:** endpoints are always `https://`, so the cascade tests now serve their networks, inboxes and status lists over real TLS under a test CA (`tests/support/tls.rs`: `rcgen` plus `tokio-rustls` behind axum's `Listener`, adding only `rcgen` as a new dev-dependency). The A13 sign-in link test completes the link by hand, because `SignInLink::complete` builds its own client; A13 goes in the Trust Tasks PR.

`cargo test --workspace`: cascade 7, network API 9, unit 3. Clippy is clean.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.37.0
body:
### Added

- **vta/collection**: Claim, release and list who collects a persona DID's messages at the mediator ([#1023](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1023))

Implements dtgwg-vti-spec's collection for the principal's identifiers
  (VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-092).

  A VTA collects, at the mediator each DID document advertises, the messages
  for every identifier whose messaging keys it holds in one of the principal's
  trust contexts — its personas — unless a client has claimed it. The mediator
  permits one connection per DID, so at most one party collects at a time.

  New tasks (family vta/collection, category messaging):

  - vta/collection/claim/0.1 — a client becomes an identifier's one collector
    until a stated end (a lease, at most thirty days), or renews its claim. The
    VTA stops collecting and closes its connection before it grants; the client
    connects only after the grant and closes before the end unless renewed.
    notCollectable, claimHeld, claimNotRenewable. Retry class 2.
  - vta/collection/release/0.1 — the claimant ends its claim at once, having
    stopped collecting; any other party with standing makes it unrenewable,
    and it still ends at its end. notCollectable. Retry class 2.
  - vta/collection/list/0.1 — who collects for each identifier of a context:
    the VTA, a claimant (with the end and whether renewable), or nobody, with
    the reason (limit, conflict).

- **rs**: A stated expiresAt replaces the maximum age, up to an expiry horizon ([#1021](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1021))

SPEC §7.2 (Bounding the record) applies the maximum age over issuedAt
  "where expiresAt is absent". validate_freshness applied it whatever the
  document stated, so a document whose producer stated a day-long expiry was
  refused as stale after five minutes, and a store-and-forward delivery could
  outlive only the consumer's maximum age.

  - validate_freshness applies max_age only to a document without an
    expiresAt. One with an expiresAt is bounded by it (validate_basic),
    clamped to issuedAt + expiry_horizon (+ skew): accepted until then,
    refused as expired after, never refused for stating a later instant.
  - FreshnessPolicy gains expiry_horizon and with_expiry_horizon;
    consequential() sets DEFAULT_EXPIRY_HORIZON (30 days). The default
    policy sets none.
  - record_expiry clamps the same way, so the replay record lasts exactly as
    long as the document is acceptable. Without an issuedAt the horizon has
    nothing to run from and the expiry stands: a horizon from first sight
    would drop the record while a copy is still acceptable.
  - FreshnessPolicy is now #[non_exhaustive].

  Breaking, in behaviour as well as API: a consumer that caps its replay
  record at issuedAt + max_age + skew, relying on validate_freshness to
  refuse older documents, must cap at record_expiry instead, or an
  expiresAt-bounded document accepted past its max age would execute twice.



### Specifications

- **vta/collection**: Category notifications, a disabled reason, and the 24-hour lease ([#1024](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1024))

Follows dtgwg-vti-spec#97's VTI-NTF-093 and lease recommendation.

  - Category messaging -> notifications for claim, release and list.
  - NotCollectedReason gains `disabled` (appended): the operator has not
    enabled collection by default (VTI-NTF-093). Claims are still granted,
    renewed, released and listed while it is off; notCollectable and list
    scope now refer to the identifiers VTI-NTF-080 names whether or not it is
    enabled, and a claimant's release resumes collection only where enabled.
  - Claim: a producer SHOULD request 86400 seconds and renew at half the
    period granted; the VTA's stated maximum SHOULD NOT exceed thirty days.

  Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its

`Dart API compatibility`).

edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(contexts)!: purge every context-scoped record on delete
body:
## What and why

`vta/contexts/delete` purged keys, ACL scope, DID templates, webvh DIDs, app state and memory (#2415), and nothing else. Every other store holding data *for* a context kept its rows. Most of them are keyed by the context id, or by a digest of it, so **a context recreated under the same id inherited them**.

Real failure: a context deleted and then recreated under the same id failed `vta/pcs/root-request` with `memberMismatch`. The vetter engine record (`pcs_engine` `vetter:<sha256(ctx\0community)>`) had survived. It was still pinned to the old member DID and to a derivation path under the old context's base.

### Now purged (for every context in the deleted subtree)

| Store | What goes |
|---|---|
| `pcs_engine` | vetter, applicant, voter and trustee records whose `contextId` is the context, plus the wrapped state beside each (`secret:<key>`, and a voter's `secret:voter-casts:…`). The keys are hashed, so the purge scans each prefix and matches the record's own `contextId`. Runs under the engine write lock. |
| `persona` | every context-scoped prefix (`pb pc pcr pca pcl pd plp plb`). It is driven from `PREFIX_SCOPES`, so a context-scoped prefix added later is purged without anyone having to remember. Also the agent-scoped face-value edges `pxf:…:l:<ctx>:…` that name the context's local profiles. |
| `vault` | credentials in the context's custody, with their `idx:` rows, and `vault:` entries. These are hard-deleted whatever their lifecycle state. |
| `notifications` | `held:<ctx>\0…` records plus their dedup and bound rows. Uses the sweep's removal, now factored out and shared. |
| `consent` / `consent_approvers` | grants and pending requests whose `context` is the context, and its `approver:<platform>\x1f<ctx>` bindings |
| `external_accounts` / `external_secrets` | each live account is deleted the way `external/accounts/delete` deletes one: secret gone, id retired. Stray `secret:external:<ctx>:` rows go too. |
| `contexts` | daily quota counters `quota:<ctx>:…` |
| `imported_secrets` / `internal_keys` | the material of every key record the purge removes. `revoke_key` already destroys an imported secret the same way. |

Each store purges itself next to the code that writes it (`purge_context` / `purge_context_*`). The counts are added to the `context (and subtree) deleted` log line.

**Preview / force gate:** unchanged, as in #2415. The not-empty gate must agree with `preview-delete`, whose wire shape has no member for any of these. A refusal the preview can't explain is the failure that function warns about. Listing these in the preview needs a spec revision of `vta/contexts/preview-delete`.

### Intentionally kept

- **audit / audit_key**: append-only. The record of the deletion must survive it.
- **issued_credentials**: third parties hold copies, so they are revoked (through the DID cascade), never deleted.
- **external accounts' `retired:<ctx>:<id>` tombstones**: they hold no data and resurrect nothing. They stop a recreated context from reusing an account id that a provider-side trust policy or audit row may still name, which is the reason they exist. The test asserts they stay.
- **policy**: an approval rule naming a context id is the operator's statement about that id, not data the context owned.
- **room_groups / room_invitations**: keyed by member persona DID and credential id, not by context. A recreated context's personas are new DIDs. A consumed invitation must stay consumed.
- **Lapses on its own** (TTL-bounded): sessions, task_consent, passkey_vms, idempotency, accepted_ids, witness_sessions.

### The census is now held to the code

- New `vta_keyspaces::context_delete_effect` classifies every keyspace for a context deletion as `Purged`, `Retained`, `Lapses` or `Unrelated`. A census test checks every keyspace is classified, and `context_delete_labels_match_the_cascade` ties the `Purged` set to the cascade's own list.
- `did_delete_effect` labelled most keyspaces `Cascade`, and five `Blocks`, but `delete_did_webvh_with` reaches only keys, webvh, acl, sessions, issued_credentials (revoke) and contexts (blocks). Those labels are now `Orphaned`, with the intended effect written beside each. `did_delete_labels_match_the_cascade` holds `Cascade` / `Blocks` / `Revoke` to `DID_DELETE_REACHES`, declared next to the cascade. The design note `did-deletion-cascade.md` is updated to match.

### Breaking (`!`)

- `vta_keyspaces::Keyspaces` gains `internal, vault, consent, consent_approvers, persona, pcs_engine, notifications, external_accounts, external_secrets`.
- `DidDeleteEffect` gains `Orphaned` and is now `#[non_exhaustive]`.

## Tests

- `delete_purges_every_context_scoped_store_and_a_recreated_context_inherits_nothing`:
  - Seeds every kind above into `acme`, `acme/eng` and the prefix-sharing sibling `acme2`, then force-deletes `acme`.
  - Recreates `acme` and `acme/eng` under the same ids and asserts nothing comes back (index rows included).
  - Asserts the retired external ids stay retired and that `acme2` keeps every kind.
- `a_context_recreated_under_a_deleted_ones_id_enrols_a_new_member` (PCS):
  - A vetter enrols as Alice, then its context is deleted and recreated.
  - Bob's `root-request` then succeeds, and the new engine's path is under the new base.
  - Confirmed failing with the PCS purge removed.
- The `context_delete_labels_match_the_cascade` and `did_delete_labels_match_the_cascade` tie tests, plus `every_keyspace_is_classified_for_context_deletion`.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6858 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3599 passed.
- Doctests for the touched crates: pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Live sessions**: a deleted context stays in the `contexts` claim of access tokens already issued, until they expire. Refresh re-reads the ACL, which the deletion has already narrowed. If the id is recreated within the access-token TTL, a stale token can act in the new context. Ordinary ACL removal has the same window, so the right fix is VTA-wide: revoke or rotate sessions on authority reduction. It isn't a context-delete special case.
- **DID-deletion cascade**: every `Orphaned` keyspace in `did_delete_effect`. A lone DID deletion still leaves vault, persona, PCS and other rows naming the DID, and doesn't check the "should block" keyspaces.
- **task_consent** pending items and grants whose `subject_context` names the deleted context are left to lapse on their TTL.
- **Preview**: surfacing these stores in `preview-delete` (and so in the not-empty gate) needs a spec revision.
- **Atomicity**: the per-context purge is a sequence of removals. Each step is idempotent and the context record goes last, so retrying the deletion completes it. It is not one atomic step.

## Requirements

VTI-CTX-001 (every stored datum belongs to a context), VTI-NTF-051 (contexts are walls), VTI-KEY-030 (PCS member keys derived under the context's base).

## Backport

none. This is a breaking change to `vta-keyspaces`; a release branch would need a non-breaking rework, which is a maintainer's call.

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

### Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new outbound calls
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): the PCS, notification and external write locks are held only across local store I/O
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the new purges are local-only and run after the existing host-copy settlement; every step is idempotent and the context record is removed last, so a retried delete completes
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none; no wire change
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): the log line reports counts actually removed; the census labels now claim only what the code does
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): see above
- [x] Deviations flagged: none

title: docs: the VTN over Trust Tasks
body:
Adds `docs/trust-tasks.md`, the contract the `vtn/*/0.1` specs are written from (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1020). It sets the decisions for moving `vtn-service` off REST:

- **REST is kept only for fetchable artifacts:** the landing page, `/.well-known/vtn`, status lists, the signed index and credential fetch.
- **Every request is a signed Trust Task.** Browser sign-in uses `auth/oob/*` and `auth/signing-key/*`.
- **Trust Tasks are the API; credentials are the proof (A19).** Group acceptance stays a revocable `groupRegistered` VSC, and `servesRole` is retired.
- **Short lifetimes (A20):** requests within 10 minutes; browser keys up to 24 hours; room passes up to 24 hours; broadcasts up to 7 days.

A9 and A13 are marked superseded, and A14 is amended. This is a docs-only change; the implementation follows in later PRs.

title: Collect for the principal's identifiers no client has claimed, under a lease that keeps one collector per identifier (VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-092)
body:
Follow-up to #95, from implementing VTI-NTF-* (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure). The tasks are in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (`vta/collection/{claim,release,list}/0.1`): trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1023 (merged), with the follow-up for this PR's later decisions in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1024.

## The gap

A persona the VTA mints at join advertises the VTA's mediator. A notification or relay addressed to it waits there until some party collects it, and the mediator permits **one connection per identifier** (a second evicts the first). A client that holds the persona's keys can hold that connection and hand over what it receives (VTI-NTF-054). A browser wallet cannot: the persona's keys, `keyAgreement` included, exist only at the VTA. So a relay to a wallet-only member (a party community relaying an election notice, say) was never collected, and its sender held collection evidence for a delivery that reached nobody.

## Design: the VTA collects by default; a client takes an identifier with a lease

New subsection *Collection for the principal's identifiers*, VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-093:

| Req | What it says |
|---|---|
| 080 | The VTA collects for every identifier whose `messaging` keys it holds in one of the principal's contexts and whose document advertises a mediated transport, from when it first does. Exceptions: its own durable identity (never claimable), other nodes' and provisioned integrations' identities (their holders collect), and identifiers under a claim. |
| 081 | At most one collector at a time. A client collects only while it holds a claim that is in force. |
| 082 | Claim: granted only to a client with authority in the context, only when no other client's claim is in force. **The VTA stops collecting and closes its connections before it answers the grant.** A claim has an end, capped at a maximum the VTA states. The claimant renews with the same operation. |
| 083 | The claimant connects only after the grant, and stops before the end less its skew tolerance unless it renews. It stops before it releases. |
| 084 | Release by the claimant ends the claim at once. Release by anyone else, or loss of the claimant's standing, makes the claim unrenewable, and it still ends at its end. Rollover and key rotation carry the claim to the successor. The VTA resumes only after the end plus its own skew tolerance. |
| 085 | A collector evicted by another connection backs off and stops after a stated bound. The VTA audits the conflict and lists the identifier as in conflict. |
| 086 | Collected notify/relay go through the hand-over's acceptance (VTI-NTF-055), with collection time as the hand-over time. The reply goes out as the persona, the same whoever collected (extends VTI-NTF-023/055). |
| 087 | Any other operation is refused as not served (VTI-OPS-081). It is never performed, held, relayed or treated as a request to the VTA, and no reply names the VTA's identity. Transport control messages are handled as the transport requires. |
| 088 | Bounds: senders without standing share the VTA's one bound (VTI-TRN-029). VTI-NTF-033's per-originator and per-relayer bounds are applied per context, across every collected identifier and every hand-over. Nothing is bounded per identifier. There is a stated cap on how many identifiers the VTA collects for, and one over it is listed as uncollected. |
| 089 | Collection happens inside the protection boundary that holds the messaging keys, so a TEE collects inside the enclave. No single connection collects for several contexts. The VTA documents what its connections reveal in common (VTI-TRN-027). |
| 090 | A rotation leaves the collector and the claim unchanged. On a mediator change, collect at the new mediator and SHOULD drain the old one. Deleting or deactivating the identifier, or deleting its context, stops collection and ends its claims. |
| 091 | A listing per context shows the collector of each identifier, each claim's claimant, end and renewability, and, where nobody collects, why. |
| 092 | Hand-over (deposit) is unchanged and still accepted with or without a claim. VTI-NTF-022 deduplicates. |
| 093 | Collection by default is behind an operator setting, **off unless the operator enables it**. While it is off, the VTA collects nothing under 080 but still grants, renews, releases and lists claims, listing each unclaimed identifier as collected by nobody. An operator SHOULD enable it only once its clients claim first. Turning it on or off is audited, and turning it off stops collection. 080 applies only while it is enabled. |

Lease sizing: a claimant SHOULD ask for 24h and renew at half the period granted (083), and the VTA's stated maximum SHOULD NOT exceed 30 days (082).

**Why default-VTA-collects plus a lease, and not the alternatives.** If the VTA collected only when a client opted in, a principal whose only client is a browser would stay exactly as stranded as today, and nothing would report it. Under default collection the failure case is a client that collects without claiming, and that case shows up as a conflict (085) the principal can see. A lease beats a standing assignment because the claimant can disappear without releasing (uninstalled, lost, revoked). With a lease the identifier returns to the VTA at the end, and the mediator holds whatever arrived in between. An early release by another party cannot cut the lease short, because the claimant is still connected and only its own clock tells it to stop. Ending the claim at once would make the VTA the second connection. TSP receive rides the same mediator connection, so a claim covers every protocol on it.

**Why refuse other operations, not drop or hold them.** A message the VTA collects and then discards is one its sender holds collection evidence for (VTI-TRN-040), so the sender records a delivery that performed nothing. A refusal is a protocol reply the sender acts on. Holding other operations for a client to fetch would make the VTA an inbox for operations nobody specified it to receive. That is left as an open issue.

## Also

- Plain-terms paragraph; the operations list in *What this chapter defines*; the VTI-NTF-054 rationale now names the claim.
- Conformance note (`Notifications` profile): MUST for a VTA; a client is bound by 081/083 where it collects.
- STRUCTURE.md row.
- Appendix F.3: an observed divergence for the current implementation, which collects only for its own identity. The resolution ships the client's claim before the VTA's default collection, and puts default collection behind the setting of 093.
- Open issue: a general inbox for operations other than notifications addressed to a collected persona. VTI-NTF-087 applies until it is specified. A refusal also shows the sender that the persona has no claiming client.
- Open issue: a revoked device that keeps a persona's messaging keys can collect without a claim. The remedy is rotating the persona's keys, which is not yet specified.

Rendered locally with `npm run render`: no errors.

body:
Collect for the principal's identifiers no client has claimed, under a lease that keeps one collector per identifier (VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-092) (#97)

* Collect for the principal's identifiers no client has claimed, under a lease that keeps one collector per identifier (VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-092)

A notification or relay addressed to a persona the VTA minted waits at the
persona's mediator until someone collects it, and the mediator permits one
connection per identifier. A client that holds the persona's keys can hold the
connection and hand over what it receives (VTI-NTF-054); a browser client
cannot, so nothing addressed to the persona of a browser-only member was ever
collected.

- The VTA collects for every identifier whose messaging keys it holds in a
  principal's context and that advertises a mediated transport, except its own
  durable identity, other nodes' and provisioned integrations' identities, and
  identifiers a client has claimed (VTI-NTF-080).
- At most one collector at a time (VTI-NTF-081). A client claims an
  identifier as a lease with a stated end; the VTA stops and disconnects before
  it grants, the client connects only after the grant and stops before the
  end unless it renews (VTI-NTF-082, VTI-NTF-083). Release by the claimant
  ends it at once; by anyone else, or after the claimant's entry loses
  standing, it becomes unrenewable and ends at its end (VTI-NTF-084).
- A collector evicted by another connection backs off and stops; the VTA
  audits the conflict and lists it (VTI-NTF-085).
- What the VTA collects: notify and relay are accepted exactly as a hand-over,
  and answered as the persona with the same reply whoever collected
  (VTI-NTF-086). Everything else is refused as not served, never performed,
  held or treated as a request to the VTA, and no reply names the VTA
  (VTI-NTF-087).
- Bounds are the node's, never per identifier (VTI-NTF-088, VTI-TRN-029);
  collection happens inside the boundary holding the messaging keys, and never
  over one connection for several contexts (VTI-NTF-089).
- Rotation, mediator change, deletion (VTI-NTF-090); listing (VTI-NTF-091);
  hand-over unchanged (VTI-NTF-092).

Also: plain-terms paragraph, conformance note, STRUCTURE.md row, a divergence
entry for the current implementation (F.3), and an open issue for operations
other than notifications addressed to a browser-only member's persona.

title: vtc-service-v0.20.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-service**: The accepted-document-id record in the store, shared with the VTC (VTI-OPS-026, VTI-OPS-027) ([#2417](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2417))

The VTA kept its record of accepted document ids (SPEC §7.2 item 11) in a
  process-local InMemoryReplayGuard, so a document accepted before a restart
  executed again when replayed after it, still inside its acceptance window
  (VTI-OPS-026).

  The VTC's store-backed record moves into vti-trust-task-server as
  StoreAcceptedIds (with its sweep and tests) and the VTA adopts it over a new
  `accepted_ids` keyspace: encrypted, excluded from backup, Unrelated to DID
  deletion, swept on the storage thread's timer. Rows keep the `accepted:<id>`
  shape, so the VTC needs no migration. admit_carried_document now returns the
  claim it took, and the deposit handler settles it.

  Also fixes a document refused after its claim (schema, spec policy, proof,
  idempotency) keeping its id spent as in-flight: the corrected resend under
  the same id was answered 202 and never ran. The post-claim work is now
  dispatch_claimed, and the caller settles the claim on every outcome.

  Retention is unchanged (issuedAt + max_age + skew); it moves to expiresAt when
  the nodes adopt trust-tasks-rs 0.37.

- **vti-vtn**: Group registration is the signed vtn/groups/register request; A20 lifetimes ([#2416](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2416))

- groups::register_as signs a vtn/groups/register/0.1 request; verify_registration checks
    its type, issuer, recipient and authentication proof. servesRole/1 is retired.
  - groupRegistered binds registration_digest: JCS over the request including its proof.
  - Registered endpoints are https.
  - room_pass refuses a lifetime over 24h; relay::new_message and relay::verify refuse a
    broadcast lasting more than 7 days after sentAt.
  - request::{request_document, sign_request} move out of the client feature;
    vti_vtn::specs re-exports the vtn/* types.

  `accepted_ids` keyspace: encrypted, excluded from backup, Unrelated to DID
  deletion, swept on the storage thread's timer. Rows keep the `accepted:<id>`
  shape, so the VTC needs no migration. admit_carried_document now returns the
  claim it took, and the deposit handler settles it.

  Also fixes a document refused after its claim (schema, spec policy, proof,
  idempotency) keeping its id spent as in-flight: the corrected resend under
  the same id was answered 202 and never ran. The post-claim work is now
  dispatch_claimed, and the caller settles the claim on every outcome.

  Retention is unchanged (issuedAt + max_age + skew); it moves to expiresAt when
  the nodes adopt trust-tasks-rs 0.37.



### Fixed

- **contexts**: Context deletion purges the context's app-state and agent memory ([#2415](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2415))

vta/contexts/delete removed a context's keys, DIDs, ACL entries and DID
  templates, but left its application state (app:/appv:/appc:/appt:<ctx>:…)
  and agent memory (mem:<ctx>:…) in place. Both are keyed by context id
  alone, so a context later created under the same id inherited them.

  Seen with OpenVTC: a profile wiped locally (config, keychain) and its VTA
  context deleted, then re-provisioned into a fresh context under the same
  id, synced the deleted profile's personas and communities straight back
  from vta/app-state — personas whose keys were gone, so every one failed to
  load with "not within the caller's scope".

  - operations::app_state::purge_context removes every record family for a
    context (records live and tombstoned, version index, write counters, reap
    watermarks), so a recreated context starts with an empty store and a
    change feed from zero.
  - operations::memory::purge_context removes the context's memory entries.
  - delete_context calls both for every context in the deleted subtree, and
    logs the counts.
  - Not added to the not-empty gate: the gate has to agree with
    preview-delete, whose wire shape has no member for either, and a refusal
    the preview cannot explain is the failure that function already warns
    about. Surfacing them in the preview needs a spec revision.

title: feat(vta/collection): claim, release and list who collects a persona DID's messages at the mediator
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#97 (VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-092).

A VTA collects the messages queued at the mediator for every DID whose messaging keys it holds in one of the principal's contexts (its personas), unless a client has claimed that DID. The mediator permits one connection per DID, so at most one party collects for a DID at a time. Without this, a browser wallet's personas, whose keys exist only at the VTA, were collected by nobody.

## New tasks (family `vta/collection`, category `notifications`)

| Task | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `vta/collection/claim/0.1` | A client becomes a DID's one collector until `endsAt` (a lease: `durationSeconds` 60 to 2592000, capped by the VTA's stated maximum), or renews its own claim (`renewed: true`). The VTA stops collecting and closes its connection **before** it grants. The client connects only after the grant and closes before `endsAt` less its skew tolerance unless it has renewed. Errors: `notCollectable` (not a DID the VTA collects for in `contextId`: no messaging keys there, no mediated transport, or the VTA's own, another node's, or a provisioned integration's identity), `claimHeld` (another client's claim is in force), `claimNotRenewable` (released by another party). Retry class 2; a repeat by the claimant is a renewal. |
| `vta/collection/release/0.1` | Release by the claimant, which has already stopped collecting, ends the claim at once. Release by anyone else with standing makes it unrenewable, leaves `endsAt` unchanged, and the VTA resumes only after `endsAt` plus its skew tolerance. With no claim in force it succeeds without `endsAt`. Errors: `notCollectable`. Retry class 2. |
| `vta/collection/list/0.1` | Who collects for each DID of a context: `vta`, `client` with its `claim` (claimant, `endsAt`, `renewable`), or `none` with `notCollectedReason` (`limit`, `conflict`, `disabled`). Filters `identifier` and `collector`; paged with `cursor`/`limit`. Its spec states why a filter suffices without a show twin. |

Shared: `vta/collection/_shared/0.1/collection.schema.json`. `CollectionEntry` ties `claim` and `notCollectedReason` to the `collector` value with `dependentSchemas` (not if/then/else).

All three are gated by standing in `contextId`. A claim confers nothing: no keys, no authority, and no say over the acceptance policy, which still decides everything the claimant hands over with `vta/notifications/deposit`.

## Collection by default is behind an operator setting (VTI-NTF-093)

The setting is off by default. While it is off, the VTA collects for no unclaimed DID, but it still grants, renews, releases and lists claims, and `list` shows each unclaimed DID as `none` / `disabled`. Clients can therefore adopt claims before any operator turns collection on. In `claim`, a producer SHOULD request `86400` seconds and renew at half the granted period, and the VTA's stated maximum SHOULD NOT exceed thirty days.

## Local validation

`npm run validate` and `npm run build` pass. `check-bindings` reports all four bindings agree. `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features vta --test conformance -- collection` passes 6 tests. Rust, TS, Go and Dart are regenerated.
