title: feat(elections): credential rolls, and notifications handed to the VTA (VTI-NTF-054, VTI-NTF-063, VTI-VOT-015 – 018, 025, 090)
body:
Election credential rolls and notifications, on VTI's vta-sdk 0.79 / vta-service 0.71 / vtc-service 0.19.

> **Blocked on a VGI release.** `did-git-sign` / `vgi-core` 0.31.0 are on `vta-sdk ^0.78`, and `git_signing` passes a `VtaClient` to `did_git_sign::vta::sign_sshsig`, so the workspace only builds with a did-git-sign on 0.79. This PR asks for **0.32.0**, which isn't published yet. The VGI change is a one-line dependency bump plus the release version (same shape as VGI #191). It's prepared on a local branch, `chore/vta-sdk-0.79`, but not pushed. Until 0.32.0 is on crates.io, CI fails at resolution. `Cargo.lock` already names the registry source for both crates, so once 0.32.0 is published, a CI re-run (or `cargo update -p did-git-sign -p vgi-core`) is all that's needed. Opened as a draft for that reason. Everything below was built and tested locally with a path patch to that branch.

## Credential rolls (VTI-VOT-015 – 018, 025, 090)

- An election under `roll.rule: credential` shows whose credential admits a voter, from `disclosure.rollCredential`. It also warns that taking a ticket shows the community that membership.
- **t** looks in the VTA vault (`vault/credentials/query`, `issuerDid` + `subjectDid`) for the membership credential **that party itself** issued the persona. It must be active and valid; if several match, it takes the one valid longest.
- The VTA then signs the whole `tickets/issue/0.3` claim, presentation included (`vta/pcs/voter/register/0.5` with `member` and `membershipCredential`). The claim goes to the community unchanged, on the membership's transport (TSP > DIDComm).
- Other rolls keep #514's persona-signed claim, with `register` sent without `member`.
- New refusals are explained in words:
  - from the community: `presentationRequired`, `membershipNotProven`, `membershipRevoked`, `rollUntrusted`, and `indeterminate` (nothing was recorded; try again later);
  - from the VTA: `membershipCredentialRequired`, `membershipCredentialUnusable`, `membershipCredentialMismatch`.

## Notifications (VTI-NTF-053, 054, 063)

- `notifications/notify/0.1` and `notifications/relay/0.1` pass the inbound gate, with a new census row.
- One addressed to a persona is deposited with the VTA as received: `VtaClient::notifications_deposit_json` with `{contextId, document}`, where `document` is the received JSON and the context is the persona's. There is no acceptance filter here.
- The sender gets the notify/relay receipt (`notificationId` and `revision` of the innermost notification). It's signed as the addressee and sent on the transport the notification arrived on. The receipt comes from the delivery as verified locally (`vta_sdk::notifications::verify_delivery`), never from the VTA's answer, so it's the same whatever the VTA did.
- Work runs off the loop, at most 8 hand-overs at once, starting as soon as the notification arrives.
- Nothing is opened, and nobody contacted, because a notification arrived.
- **Elections panel.** Beside the community's own list, the panel reads the VTA's held election notifications (`vta/notifications/list/0.1`, `kind: election`). It lists those held by this community or put to its members under **Told of**, shown only as notified: who holds it, its id, who it's put to, and its period.
- Opening a notified election reads it from the community holding it, presenting nothing at first.
  - If that community answers `electionUnknown` for an election put to another party's members, a disclosure screen says what presenting would show.
  - Only `y` presents. The VTA then signs the read (`vta/pcs/voter/read/0.6` with `memberOf` + `membershipCredential`).
  - Later reads, and the ticket and vote, present the same membership and nothing else.
- The holding community may be one the persona isn't a member of. Its answers are admitted only on a thread sent to it (`elections::expect_answer` / `is_awaited`, 120 s TTL, at most 64 outstanding). Every other document from it still has no standing.

## Versions

Only versions VTI currently serves are sent:

| Task | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `vtc/elections/list` | 0.3 | 0.5 |
| `vtc/elections/show` | 0.3 | 0.6 |
| `vtc/elections/tickets/issue` | 0.1 | 0.3 |
| `vta/pcs/voter/register` | 0.3 | 0.5 |
| `vta/pcs/vote` | 0.3 | 0.4 |
| `vta/pcs/vote-encrypted` | 0.4 | 0.5 |
| `vta/pcs/voter/read` | — | 0.6 |
| `notifications/notify`, `notifications/relay` | — | 0.1 |
| `vta/notifications/deposit`, `vta/notifications/list` | — | 0.1 |

- `voter/accept/0.1` was refreshed: description-only republish upstream.
- Every bundle is byte-identical to VTI main's. `trust-tasks check`: 59 pins OK.
- Dependencies: vta-sdk 0.79, vta-service 0.71 (dev), vti-vetting-pcs 0.12, vti-voting 0.8, did-git-sign / vgi-core 0.32. With the patch, `cargo tree -d` shows one vta-sdk and one vti-specs.

## Tests

- Core:
  - the credential-roll disclosure and warning;
  - the `register/0.5` claim, which names `member` and `membershipCredential` only under a credential roll;
  - the VTA's signed `ticketDocument` carried as answered;
  - the `read/0.6` presenting payload;
  - credential choice (the party's own, not a group's; valid, not archived; longest-lived);
  - refusal words, including `indeterminate`;
  - the awaited-answer registry;
  - the deposit carries the document byte for byte;
  - receipt document shape;
  - held-notification parsing (withdrawn ones and other kinds dropped);
  - a signed notify verified with its receipt read from it.
- TUI:
  - notified rows de-duplicated against the list;
  - nothing presented until `y`, and Back presents nothing;
  - signed reads and claims carried unchanged;
  - answers taken from the community the request went to;
  - dispatch hands a notification over as received (and not one for a DID we hold no persona for);
  - a non-member community's election answer is admitted only on our thread.
- MockVta e2e, run with `--include-ignored`:
  - `elections_vote_e2e` on register/0.5 and vote/0.4;
  - new `notifications_e2e`: a real deposit is refused `notAddressedHere` and read as an answer, not as an outage; an empty held list reads as empty.
- Run locally, all green: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo check -p openvtc-core --no-default-features --features arbitrary`.

## Unsettled

- **When the VTA can't be reached**, the notification is neither deposited nor answered, so the originator's retry (retry class 2) delivers it again. Whether to answer depends only on reachability, never on what the VTA decided. A document that doesn't verify locally, or whose sender isn't its issuer, is deposited but not answered, as VTI-NTF-023 answers verified documents.
- **Transport to a community the persona isn't a member of** uses TSP if the persona joined any community over TSP (and that community advertises `#tsp`), and DIDComm otherwise. It's a heuristic, not a check of the persona's own DID document.
- **`indeterminate`** is explained and left for the member to retry by hand. There is no automatic resend with backoff, unlike the wallet.
- **Dismissing** a held notification isn't offered yet, and there's no live run against a deployed VTC/VTA. A credential-roll claim isn't exercised end to end against MockVta: that needs a VTA-held persona with a VMC in the vault.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — VTA calls via VtaClient (20–30 s), sends via the existing transports
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — the awaited-thread registry is a std Mutex held only for map ops
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — nothing persisted; a lost claim is a later register, which the VTA answers with its kept request
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no new retry loops; held-notification listing is bounded at 5 pages
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — hand-over failures are logged and dropped, never panic the loop
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — a receipt only after the VTA answered the deposit
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, schema registered, all consumers updated (R3.*) — generated from pinned bundles; census updated
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no VTA: nothing deposited or answered; no membership chosen: nothing presented
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

body:

* feat(elections): credential rolls, and notifications handed to the VTA (VTI-NTF-054, VTI-NTF-063, VTI-VOT-015 – 018, 025, 090)

Credential rolls. An election whose roll is the holders of a membership credential for one DID
shows whose credential admits a voter and warns that taking a ticket shows that membership
(VTI-VOT-090). Taking a ticket finds the credential that party itself issued the persona in the
VTA's vault (issuerDid + subjectDid, active and valid, longest-lived) and has the VTA sign the
whole tickets/issue/0.3 claim with its presentation (vta/pcs/voter/register/0.5 with member and
membershipCredential); the claim is carried to the community unchanged. Other rolls keep the
persona-signed claim. The new refusals (presentationRequired, membershipNotProven,
membershipRevoked, rollUntrusted, indeterminate; the VTA's membershipCredential*) are said in
words.

Notifications. A notifications/notify or notifications/relay addressed to a persona passes the
inbound gate and is deposited with the VTA (vta/notifications/deposit/0.1) exactly as received,
with no acceptance filter here. The sender is answered with the notify/relay receipt
(notificationId, revision of the innermost notification) read from the delivery as verified
locally, never from the VTA's answer; an unreachable VTA leaves the document neither deposited
nor answered, so the sender's retry delivers it again. Nothing is opened because of one
(VTI-NTF-053).

The Elections panel lists, beside the community's own list, the held notifications of the kind
election that concern it (VTI-NTF-063), shown only as notified. Opening one reads it from the
community holding it, which may be one the persona is not a member of — its answer is admitted
only on a thread sent to it — first presenting nothing; on electionUnknown for an election put
to another party's members, a disclosure screen says what presenting shows and only `y` has the
VTA sign the read with the presentation (vta/pcs/voter/read/0.6, memberOf; VTI-VOT-015, 016).

Pins move to the versions VTI serves now: vtc/elections/list/0.5, show/0.6, tickets/issue/0.3;
vta/pcs/voter/register/0.5, read/0.6, vote/0.4, vote-encrypted/0.5; notifications/notify/0.1,
relay/0.1, vta/notifications/deposit/0.1, list/0.1. vta-sdk 0.79, vta-service 0.71 (dev),
vti-vetting-pcs 0.12, vti-voting 0.8, did-git-sign / vgi-core 0.32 (needs VGI's vta-sdk 0.79
release).

title: feat(vta/collection): claim, release and list who collects a persona DID's messages at the mediator (#1023)
body:
feat(vta/collection): claim, release and list who collects a persona DID's messages at the mediator (#1023)

Implements dtgwg-vti-spec's collection for the principal's identifiers
(VTI-NTF-080 – VTI-NTF-092).

A VTA collects, at the mediator each DID document advertises, the messages
for every identifier whose messaging keys it holds in one of the principal's
trust contexts — its personas — unless a client has claimed it. The mediator
permits one connection per DID, so at most one party collects at a time.

New tasks (family vta/collection, category messaging):

- vta/collection/claim/0.1 — a client becomes an identifier's one collector
  until a stated end (a lease, at most thirty days), or renews its claim. The
  VTA stops collecting and closes its connection before it grants; the client
  connects only after the grant and closes before the end unless renewed.
  notCollectable, claimHeld, claimNotRenewable. Retry class 2.
- vta/collection/release/0.1 — the claimant ends its claim at once, having
  stopped collecting; any other party with standing makes it unrenewable,
  and it still ends at its end. notCollectable. Retry class 2.
- vta/collection/list/0.1 — who collects for each identifier of a context:
  the VTA, a claimant (with the end and whether renewable), or nobody, with
  the reason (limit, conflict).

Shared: vta/collection/_shared/0.1 (Claim, Collector, NotCollectedReason,
CollectionEntry; the entry's members are tied to the collector by
dependentSchemas). Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

title: feat(vta-service): the accepted-document-id record in the store, shared with the VTC (VTI-OPS-026, VTI-OPS-027)
body:
The VTA kept its record of accepted document ids (SPEC §7.2 item 11) in a
process-local InMemoryReplayGuard, so a document accepted before a restart
executed again when replayed after it, still inside its acceptance window
(VTI-OPS-026).

The VTC's store-backed record moves into vti-trust-task-server as
StoreAcceptedIds (with its sweep and tests) and the VTA adopts it over a new
`accepted_ids` keyspace: encrypted, excluded from backup, Unrelated to DID
deletion, swept on the storage thread's timer. Rows keep the `accepted:<id>`
shape, so the VTC needs no migration. admit_carried_document now returns the
claim it took, and the deposit handler settles it.

Also fixes a document refused after its claim (schema, spec policy, proof,
idempotency) keeping its id spent as in-flight: the corrected resend under
the same id was answered 202 and never ran. The post-claim work is now
dispatch_claimed, and the caller settles the claim on every outcome.

Retention is unchanged (issuedAt + max_age + skew); it moves to expiresAt when
the nodes adopt trust-tasks-rs 0.37.

## Tests
- vta-service `accepted_ids_record`: replay after restart mints no second key; resend after a post-claim refusal runs; different document under an accepted id is `idConflict`
- vti-trust-task-server: restart survival of the record
- Workspace nextest, VTC suite (admin UI built), clippy `-D warnings`, doctests, fmt

Step 2 of the expiresAt-window plan (spec #96, tt-tf #1021). Next: nodes adopt trust-tasks-rs 0.37 once published.

title: feat(vti-vtn)!: group registration is the signed vtn/groups/register request; A20 lifetimes
body:
Brings `vti-vtn`'s protocol in line with the published `vtn/*` 0.1 specs, so the VTN can move onto Trust Tasks. Breaking for `vti-vtn` (0.1 → 0.2). **Best merged before release PR #2411**, so the first published `vti-vtn` with the Trust Task client carries it too.

**Group registration** (`vtn/groups/register/0.1`)
- `groups::register_as(member, network, role, group, endpoint)` returns the member's signed `vtn/groups/register` request. The signed request is the registration. `servesRole/1` is retired.
- `verify_registration` checks it's that type, issued by the member and addressed to the network, and signed by the member for `authentication`, then reads the generated payload type. It doesn't check freshness: the receiving spine checks the 10-minute window at arrival, and a registration in a room-pass chain is old by design.
- `registration_digest`: SHA-256 over the JCS form of the request **including** its proof, as the spec requires. A re-signed copy is a different registration. `acceptance` and `rooms::verify_link` use it.
- Endpoints must be `https://`. A community whose `public_url` is `http://` can no longer register groups.

**Lifetimes (A20)**
- `rooms::room_pass` refuses a lifetime that is zero or over 24h (`MAX_PASS_LIFETIME`; `DEFAULT_PASS_LIFETIME` is 60 min).
- `relay::new_message` refuses a lifetime over 7 days (`MAX_TTL`; `DEFAULT_TTL` is 24h). `relay::verify` refuses a received message whose `expiresAt` is more than 7 days after `sentAt`.

**Also**
- `request::{request_document, sign_request}` no longer need the `client` feature, so a server can build requests too.
- `vti_vtn::specs` re-exports `vti_specs_vtn::vtn`.
- `vtc-service` drops the `valid_from` argument at its one `register_as` call. It still posts the registration to the VTN's REST route until both sides move to Trust Tasks.

Tests: new ones for tampering, `http://` endpoints, the proof being in the digest, and both lifetime caps. `vti-vtn` (24 + 4 + 1) and `vtc-service` (2219 + 1416) pass, and workspace clippy is clean.

title: fix(contexts)!: context deletion purges the context's app-state and agent memory
body:
## Problem

`vta/contexts/delete` purges a context's keys, DIDs, ACL entries and DID templates, but never touches the `app_state` or `memory` keyspaces. Both are keyed by context id alone (`app:<ctx>:<ns>:<key>`, `appv:`, `appc:`, `appt:`, `mem:<ctx>:<key>`). So when a context is deleted and **recreated under the same id**, the new context inherits the old one's records.

Seen with OpenVTC. The user wiped a profile locally (config and keychain), deleted its VTA context, then recreated `openvtc-bob`. OpenVTC's account-state sync (namespace `openvtc`) pulled a full snapshot from an empty watermark, which brought the deleted profile's personas and communities straight back. Their keys were gone, so each persona failed to load with `forbidden: key … is not within the caller's scope`.

## Fix

- `operations::app_state::purge_context` removes every app-state record family for a context: live and tombstoned records, the version index, the per-namespace write counters, and the reap watermarks. A recreated context starts with an empty store and a change feed from zero.
- `operations::memory::purge_context` removes the context's memory entries.
- `delete_context` calls both for every context in the deleted subtree (online Trust Task, break-glass `vta contexts delete` CLI), and logs `app_state_records_removed` / `memory_entries_removed`.
- `vta_keyspaces::Keyspaces` gains `memory` and `app_state`. The unused `keyspaces_from_vta_state` is removed: `VtaState` holds neither keyspace and nothing called it.

### Deliberately not in the not-empty gate

The `force` gate has to agree with `preview-delete`. That function's comment covers exactly this: consumers decide `force` from the preview, and a refusal the preview can't explain is the bug it fixed. The preview's wire shape has no member for app-state or memory, so gating on them would bring that failure back. Listing them in the preview (and then gating on them) needs a spec revision of `vta/contexts/preview-delete`. That's a possible follow-up.

## Tests

- New `delete_purges_app_state_and_memory_across_the_subtree`:
  - Seeds records, a tombstone and memory in `acme`, `acme/eng` and the prefix-sharing sibling `acme2`, then force-deletes `acme`.
  - Asserts that no `app`/`appv`/`appc`/`appt`/`mem` keys remain for the subtree.
  - Asserts that a recreated `acme` reads `NotFound`.
  - Asserts that `acme2` is untouched.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib operations::contexts`: 19 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service -p vta-backup -p vta-keyspaces --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide)

- [x] No new outbound calls (R1.2/R1.4 n/a)
- [x] No wire-shape change; error text unchanged (R6.4 n/a)
- [x] Breaking API change to `vta-keyspaces` flagged in the commit (`!` + `BREAKING CHANGE`)

title: fix(review): harden replay evidence privacy and failure-path assurance
body:
Closes #54. Follow-up to the non-blocking observations in [Nicky's approving review of merged PR #40](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/40#pullrequestreview-5749032270).

## What changed
- Compare **raw** validator exit code/stdout/stderr across runs, then redact absolute input/local paths in publishable output. Keep distinct logical placeholders for known inputs.
- Record Python implementation/version and the two direct review-validator dependency versions (PyYAML and jsonschema).
- Record SHA-256 digests of raw stdout/stderr, while exposing only redacted text in the report.
- Add deterministic regressions for unstable output, redaction collision (different raw results that sanitize identically), input changes during replay, alternate acceptance-corpus bindings, path privacy and runtime provenance.
- Correct repeatability terminology, illustrative reviewer instructions, README footer placement and a fragmentary sentence.

## Why
PR #40 was approved and merged after its substantive review findings were resolved. The approving review identified residual gaps in portable retained evidence, environment provenance, negative-path regression tests and precise documentation claims.

## Scope and assurance boundaries
The helper still assesses **same-machine mechanical validator repeatability**, not evidence authenticity, independent analyst agreement, harm/risk acceptance, target conformance or a Task Force governance decision. There are no canonical `data/` or `method/` changes, new dependencies or universal evidence-sidecar contracts.

## Compatibility
The report now declares `rahp-review-replay-check/v2`. Existing `status`, `validation_accepted`, `machine_results_identical`, input hashes and CLI exit-code semantics are retained. The `observed_result.stdout` and `.stderr` fields are now redacted; consumers relying on byte-identical raw text must migrate and should compare explicit raw SHA-256 digests. Sanitization is not represented as comprehensive secret scanning.

## Evidence and reproduction
```sh
python3 -m unittest tests.test_review_replay_check -v
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
python3 tools/validate.py
python3 review/replay_check.py --review review/examples/worked-adoption/baseline-review.yaml --risks data/risks.yaml --repeat 2
```
Current-head RAHP validation run [#41642876868](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/41642876868) completed successfully; current-head DCO and EasyCLA also passed. CI exercised repository regression discovery, corpus validation and build; independent review is still required.

## Review questions
1. Is the v2 evidence representation and raw-before-redaction comparison appropriately fail-closed?
2. Does sanitization remove local path disclosures while retaining useful logical input context, without implying comprehensive free-text privacy assurance?
3. Are the negative cases deterministic and representative of the actual replay paths?
4. Is the environment metadata relevant and minimal for a first-use reproducibility assessment?
5. Are explicit cross-machine and independent-judgment limitations clear?

## AI assistance / accountability
Implementation and documentation prepared with AI assistance under the responsible contributor's direction. The contributor authorized DCO signing during this session. No independent review, risk acceptance or governance approval is claimed; upstream maintainers must review and accept this PR.

## Checklist
- [x] Scope, reason, non-goals and compatibility are documented.
- [x] Reproduction commands and concrete negative cases are included.
- [x] No generated `build/` files or canonical corpus records changed.
- [x] Required CI and DCO/CLA checks pass on the current PR head. ([RAHP run #41642876868](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/41642876868); DCO and EasyCLA successful on `3f2de70b3a4bdf170a074a0169164a53d84676ba`.)

title: feat(validation): require complete records for accepted risks
body:
## What changed

A risk acceptance with decision `accepted` or `accepted_with_conditions` must now fill in its required fields, or `tools/validate.py` fails. This is a new invariant, `INV-6`.

The required fields are the ones the header of `data/risk-acceptances.yaml` already lists: `authority`, `decided_by`, `decision_date`, `rationale`, `residual_risk`, `review_date` and `evidence`, plus `conditions` for `accepted_with_conditions`.

## Why

I raised this in [my review of #42](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/42#pullrequestreview-5734825790). If you change `RA-001` to `decision: accepted` and leave `authority` and `decided_by` empty, `tools/validate.py` still passes. With #28 merged, a review citing that record passes too. #42's checker doesn't look at this file, so this is the route someone would actually take.

## What this doesn't do

It **doesn't decide who may accept a risk**, and `GAP-3.1` stays open (#44). It checks that the fields are filled in, not that the named authority is genuine, or that the evidence or dates are any good. `RA-001` to `RA-003` stay `pending`.

I've kept it to the existing fields, so it doesn't depend on #42. If the TF adopts `authority_reference` or `deferred` from #42, the list can grow.

## Artefact IDs affected

None of the records change. `data/instance.yaml` gains `INV-6`, and the comment at the top of `data/risk-acceptances.yaml` now mentions it.

## Provenance

Review of #42 on 2 Nov 2026. Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). I decided the scope, and it wrote the check and tests and ran the checks below.

## Validation output

```
validate.py: 43 RK · 66 CT · 21 GR · 21 AT · 37 M · 36 US · 33 SC · 21 EPIC · 16 PERSONA · 9 REC · 3 RA · 3 GP · 0 errors · 32 warnings
```

The 32 warnings are already there on `main`.

## How to check it

```sh
python3 -m unittest tests.test_risk_acceptance_invariant -v
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

- All 68 tests pass, 7 of them new. With the check switched off, 4 of the new tests fail. The other 3 cover records that should pass, so they pass either way.
- It merges cleanly with #28, #31, #32, #40, #41 and #42. All 88 tests pass with #28 and #31 merged.

To see the original problem caught, change `RA-001` in `data/risk-acceptances.yaml` to `decision: accepted` and run `python3 tools/validate.py`.

## Limitations

- **A review validated on its own:** `review/validate_spec_review.py` run alone still passes a review citing an incomplete acceptance, because it only reads the decision. `tools/validate_all.py` and CI do fail, because they also run the corpus check. I've left the review validator alone to keep this small.
- **Dates:** the check doesn't look at the date format, or whether `review_date` comes after `decision_date`.
- **Where the rule lives:** `INV-6` sits in `data/instance.yaml` with `INV-3`, so an adopter could remove it. Whether rules like these belong in the method is a wider question I'd leave for later.

## Checklist

- [x] `python3 tools/validate.py` exits 0
- [x] Every new/changed record has a `provenance` block (no records changed)
- [x] New guardrails have an assurance test; new controls reach a metric (none added)
- [x] No generated file under `build/` was edited by hand
- [x] If a risk score changed, the evidence for the change is stated above (none changed)

Related: #42, #44, #28

title: fix(validation): reject incomplete accepted risk records
body:
## What changed

Consolidates the canonical accepted-risk validation fixes from #47 and #48 into one reviewable implementation. Risk-acceptance records marked `accepted` or `accepted_with_conditions` are checked through instance invariant `INV-6` using the existing canonical `tools/validate.py` entry point.

- Validates required authority, named deciders, rationale, evidence, residual severity and decision/review dates.
- Rejects malformed or out-of-order ISO dates, invalid/non-permitted residual-risk values (including `Critical`), and missing or blank conditions for conditional acceptance.
- Uses non-Critical values from the governed `method/vocabularies.yaml` severity vocabulary instead of duplicating allowed values.
- Emits one precise diagnostic per defect rather than duplicating the missing-`decided_by` message.
- Provides helper-level and real-file integration regression tests, including temporary data corpus mutation and a failing canonical validation exit status.
- Documents what the check establishes and its limitations in `docs/data-model.md`, `data/risk-acceptances.yaml`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.

Existing `RA-001`–`RA-003` remain `pending` and unchanged. No governance authority or acceptance decision is created.

## Why

Review of #42 identified a repository integrity gap: a risk-acceptance record could claim an accepted decision with empty documentary fields and still pass canonical validation. #47 and #48 independently addressed overlapping portions; this PR is now the sole proposed integration path.

## Scope and assurance boundaries

- **Provides:** structural/semantic documentary checks and canonical validator enforcement for declared accepted decisions.
- **Does not provide:** authentication of a purported decision-making body, mandate, signatories or evidentiary sufficiency; it does not settle GAP-3.1 or authorize risk acceptance. Those remain subject to #44.
- **Configurability:** `INV-6` is declared in the DTG instance. Removing the invariant disables that instance check, reducing validation coverage; it does not make an incomplete claim legitimate or establish conformance to a portable minimum. Whether this should be a non-optional portable method rule is distinct future governance work, not silently decided here.
- **Compatibility:** strengthens checks for future records claiming acceptance. Pending records continue to validate as before. No record schema or existing risk decisions changed.

## Evidence and reproduction

```sh
python3 -m unittest tests.test_risk_acceptance_validation -v
python3 tools/validate.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

The regression suite exercises both helper semantics and `tools/validate.py --data <isolated copy> --json` through `main()`; it tests valid pending/accepted records, incomplete acceptance, conditional acceptance, incorrect residual severity, invalid dates and date ordering.

- Signed source revision: `2e5e4ff84bf726ba6d36f1d53643bdaf901f9f3a`.
- RAHP validation: [workflow 41591136252](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/41591136252).
- DCO and EasyCLA: current-head checks (see Checks tab). Independent maintainer review remains required.

## Review questions

1. Is declaring `INV-6` in the instance the correct integration point for this bounded integrity requirement?
2. Does the acceptance/error boundary accurately preserve the distinction between documentary completeness and authorization?
3. Do the real-file regression tests cover the canonical path and protect against accidental removal of validation?
4. Are the governed vocabulary, date and conditional-acceptance rules proportionate and correct?
5. Are the remaining limitations sufficiently explicit?

## AI usage and contributor accountability

Prepared with AI assistance for implementation, consolidation and documentation. The responsible human contributor authorized the DCO sign-off. Repository validation evidence is reported from automated checks; no AI output is presented as independent review or task-force acceptance. An independent maintainer must inspect the changes and evidence before merge.

Supersedes the overlapping proposed implementation in #47 **after independent review and verification**. Related: #42, #44.

title: feat(vti-vtn): the vtn/* Trust Task client
body:
Adds `vti_vtn::tasks` behind the `client` feature: - `VtnClient::task::

(who, network_did, payload) -> P::Response`: signs a `vtn/*` request as the caller for `authentication`, with `recipient` set to the network the caller expects (never what the server claims), and `issuedAt` now (a network accepts it within 10 minutes, A20). Posts it to `/v1/trust-tasks`. The types are the generated ones, re-exported as `vti_vtn::tasks::specs`. - `read_task`: an unsigned read, for public directories. - `sign_request` / `send_request` / `send_request_to`: keep the signed document (`vtn/groups/register`, whose digest the network's `groupRegistered` credential binds), or relay one unchanged. - Answers are checked: they must be the request type's `#response`, from the expected network, addressed to the requester and on the request's thread. A `trust-task-error` becomes `ClientError::Refused { status, code, message, details }`, with `ClientError::code()`. Trust Tasks are the API; credentials stay the proof. The client hands back the credentials an answer carries, and the caller verifies them as before. The REST sign-in and `get`/`post` stay, because vtn-service still serves REST. They go when it moves onto `vti-trust-task-server`. Tests: three new ones (the signature verifies for `authentication`; wrong issuer or thread is refused; a refusal keeps its code and details). Workspace clippy is clean.

title: fix(startup): a persona whose keys the VTA refuses is not called a network blip
body:
## Problem

When the VTA answered `forbidden` / `notFound` / `gone` for a persona's key, the startup report filed it as `KeyUnavailable`, which is classed as transient. It then said:

> This looks temporary — the VTA or the network could not be reached… Restart OpenVTC once connectivity is back.

The VTA *was* reached, and restarting can never fix this. Seen after a VTA context was deleted and recreated under the same id: synced account state brought the old personas back without their keys, and every one failed with `forbidden: key … is not within the caller's scope`. The stale records themselves are a VTA bug, fixed in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2415.

## Fix

- New `DegradedReason::KeyNotAccessible`, chosen from the typed `VtaError` (`Forbidden | NotFound | Gone`), not from the message text. It is neither transient nor an interrupted write.
- `LoadIntegrity::has_inaccessible_keys()`.
- The startup advice now says the VTA refused the keys to this account and that a restart won't change it. It names the usual cause (a deleted or replaced VTA context) and what to do: remove the personas, or have the VTA admin restore access. An unreachable VTA still reads as temporary, and interrupted-write advice is unchanged (VTI R6.4).

## Tests

- `a_refused_key_is_neither_transient_nor_an_interrupted_write` (core)
- `a_refused_key_is_not_described_as_a_network_fault` (loading screen)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
author: stormer78

The stale records themselves come from the VTA not purging app-state on

title: feat(notifications): held notifications in the console, and notified elections in the member's view (VTI-NTF-050 – 063)
body:
The member's VTA holds the notifications it accepts in the context of the DID each was addressed to (VTI-NTF-050). This PR has the wallet read them. A notification is an originator's signed statement that a thing exists, such as an election. It says where the thing is held, its id there, and the audience it concerns. Notifications show up in two places:

- a general list in the console;
- the member's elections view (VTI-NTF-063), which shows the community's list together with the elections the agent was notified of.

Spec: dtgwg-vti-spec chapter 05a (VTI-NTF-001 – 074) and Appendix G. Schemas: dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf `notifications/*` and `vta/notifications/*`. Served by vta-service 0.71.0 and vtc-service 0.19.0 (vta-sdk 0.79.0). Following CLAUDE.md's "Nothing is deployed", the wallet sends only the versions VTI serves today.

## Changes

- **Core: `@openvtc/pnm-core/notifications`** (new layer-5 subpath).
  - `notificationsList` / `notificationsListAll`, `notificationsShow`, `notificationsDismiss`.
  - `notificationsDeposit` hands the received document to the VTA unchanged: the same object, never rebuilt from a typed form, never re-signed.
  - `inboundNotificationOf`, `notificationReceiptOf` (the innermost notification's `notificationId` / `revision`, within at most four relays) and `notifiedElectionOf`.
  - **Pins:** `notifications/notify/0.1`, `notifications/relay/0.1` and `vta/notifications/{list,show,dismiss,deposit}/0.1`. The bundles are byte-identical to VTI main's, and `task-surface.json` is resynced from vta-sdk 0.79.0, which only adds entries. Coverage goes from 235 to 242.
- **Console: a Notifications pane** (Data & credentials, context-scoped). With no context selected it lists every context.
  - Each card shows the kind, who said it, who passed it on, `heldBy`, the id, the audience, the period, the addressee, the context, and the status (available / withdrawn / lapsed / dismissed).
  - A kind the wallet does not know is shown as existing and nothing more (VTI-NTF-012).
  - Each card has *The document as received* (the `show` document) and *Dismiss*.
  - **Open the election** sends only `{contextId, recordId}` (`RUNTIME_NOTIFIED_ELECTION`, extension pages only).
    - `ElectionsPageGates.openNotified` reads the record again from the VTA, checks the community's endpoint is reachable, then reads the election from `heldBy` as the record's `addressee`, in its context, without presenting anything.
    - Only if the community answers `electionUnknown` does it return `needsPresent`. The console then says what presenting the membership of the audience shows, and sends `present: true` only from the member's click (VTI-VOT-016). The choice is remembered like a page's (`election-disclosed:`).
    - A withdrawn notification is not opened. Tickets and ballots stay in the portal flow.
- **Portal: `elections.list` answers `{ elections, notified }`.**
  - `notified` holds the election notifications held for this community in the member's context, in notified form only: id, audience, period and status. Elections already in the list are not repeated.
  - On `electionUnknown` with no `memberOf`, `show` and `vote` take `memberOf` from a held, unwithdrawn notification for that election. The `disclose` window still asks before anything is presented.
- **`page-task-policy.ts`** refuses `vta/notifications/*` from pages. A list of held notifications is a list of the member's relationships.
- **CLAUDE.md:** a new section, *Notifications: held at the agent, read by the wallet, opened only by the member*.

## Deposit: this wallet holds no persona socket

VTI-NTF-054 requires a client that holds a **persona** DID's mediator socket to deposit what it receives there. This wallet holds none:

- Its sessions are the holder's `did:key`, the approver and the onboarding ephemeral.
- A `did:key` advertises no transport, so nothing can be addressed to it (VTI-NTF-020).
- A persona's keys, keyAgreement included, live only at the VTA. The wallet can neither authenticate to the mediator as a persona nor open what is sealed to one.

So nothing reaches this wallet to deposit. Nothing is wired into the inbound pipeline, and no REST path or VTA-side decryption was invented to make up for it. `notificationsDeposit` is in core, tested to carry the document unchanged, for a client that does hold one.

**Open point for VTI:** a persona the join flow mints with `addMediatorService` advertises the VTA's mediator, and no party collects that socket today. A notification relayed to such a member, for example by a party community, is therefore never collected. The resolution belongs at the VTA, which holding its personas' sockets would make a direct delivery (VTI-NTF-050).

## Tests

- **core `notifications.mjs`:**
  - Each task's payload and addressing.
  - `listAll` follows cursors and stops on a repeated one.
  - A deposit carries the same object with its original timestamp spellings.
  - Recognising notify and relay documents, and the receipt through relays, including more than four.
  - `notifiedElectionOf`.
- **extension `elections-page.test.mts`:**
  - `list` merges notified elections in notified form only.
  - A notified election is opened as the audience's member after the disclose window.
  - A withdrawn notification names no party.
  - `openNotified`: read without presenting first; `needsPresent`, then presenting only with `present`, and remembered; `needsReach` before anything is read.
  - A page cannot drive `vta/notifications/*`.
- **extension `elections-page-offscreen.test.mts`:**
  - `notified` lists from the identity's context for this community only, and sends nothing to the community.
  - `notifiedShow` reads as the addressee, in the record's context, and presents only when told.
  - A withdrawn notification is not opened.
- **extension `notification-words.test.mts`:** kind, period and presentation wording.
- Commands run, all green:
  - `npm run lint`
  - `npm test`: core 1139, extension 1456, and the other workspaces
  - `npm run build`
  - `node packages/extension/scripts/check-task-versions.mjs`: 446 URIs OK
  - `trust-tasks -C packages/core check`: 281 pins match

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new fetch: VTA calls go through the existing channels, community reads through postCommunityTask
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — the disclosure is remembered only after the presenting read succeeded
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no new retry; dismiss is idempotent at the VTA
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a: nothing is added to the inbound path
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — generated from the pinned bundles; `elections.list` gains an additive `notified` member the VTI portal does not read yet
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no notification and no memberOf means no presentation; withdrawn names no party
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — contexts the agent would not list are named on the pane, not hidden
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — the only mutation is dismiss (idempotent); a lost presenting read is a fresh read
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

each was addressed to (VTI-NTF-050). The wallet now reads them.

  deposit}/0.1`, plus `inboundNotificationOf`, `notificationReceiptOf` and
  `notifiedElectionOf`. Pins `notifications/{notify,relay}/0.1` and the four

title: vtc-service-v0.19.0
body:
### Added

- **vetting**: Recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset, vta/pcs/vetter/recover) ([#2406](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2406))

* feat(vtc): recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset)

  A vetter is bound to the PCS identifier of their first enrolment, and a
  second identifier is refused with pcs-root:identifierRebound. The binding
  was never cleared, so a vetter whose key was lost was locked out of hidden
  vetting for as long as they stayed a member; revoking and re-granting the
  role did not help.

  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1: a member reads their own
    binding (identifier, enrolled labels, any pending reset), so their client
    can recover the matching key. Membership is the entitlement;
    notAMember otherwise.
  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/reset/0.1: an administrator holding
    vtc.vetting.manage (as vetters/grant) resets a member's binding with a
    reason. Idempotent; notBound for a member who never enrolled. Audited as
    HiddenVetterBindingReset, never with the identifier.
  - Enrolment after a reset: the recorded identifier cancels it
    (HiddenVetterResetCancelled); a new one is refused (identifierRebound)
    while any label the old one enrolled under is live, judged at each
    request against the caller's configuration and the stored one under the
    enrolment lock, and bound once none is (HiddenVetterRebound) with its
    labels afresh. The old labels are retired on the record.
  - vtc/vetting/hidden/publish refuses to make a retired label live again,
    checked before the consent gate and again under the enrolment lock
    before the write. publish/0.1 declares no code for it, so it is a
    validation refusal.
  - Admin console: a "Reset a hidden-vetting key" card under Vetting ->
    Vetters, shown when discovery lists the task.
  - EnrolmentRecord gains optional reset and retiredLabels members; rows
    without them read and write as before.

  The two specifications are pinned from a locally built registry ahead of
  their publication; trust-tasks.lock records that registry until they are
  re-pinned against trusttasks.org.

- **notifications**: Deposit to the VTA, a community's received notifications and relay decision, and four fixes (VTI-NTF-005, 034, 041, 047, 054 – 056, 070 – 074) ([#2405](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2405))

* feat(vti-specs): pin vta/notifications/deposit 0.1 and vtc/notifications/{list,show,relay} 0.1

  From trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1017: the client's hand-over of a
  notification received for a persona DID (vti-specs-vta), and a
  community's administrators' view and relay decision (vti-specs-vtc).
  notifications/notify and relay 0.1 changed in prose only; their pinned
  digests are unchanged.

- **vti-vtn**: Listings and repudiations use the registered DTG predicates ([#2403](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2403))
- **vtc**: A community's side of Verifiable Trust Network membership ([#2399](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2399))

* feat(vti-specs-vtc): pin vtc/networks/* 0.1

  list, show, join, repudiate, leave, groups/register, notice and evidence
  (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1014): a community's side of
  Verifiable Trust Network membership.

- **git-ns**: The VTC speaks bridge job 0.7 and event 0.6 ([#2401](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2401))

* feat(git-ns): the VTC speaks bridge job 0.7 and event 0.6

  Pin git-ns/bridge/job 0.7 and git-ns/bridge/event 0.6 in vti-specs-core
  (replacing job 0.6 and event 0.5; test deployments only, no fallback).

  - Jobs go out as git-ns/bridge/job/0.7 only, and only to a bridge that
    lists 0.7 in trust-task-discovery (vgi-bridge v0.31.0 or later). The
    schema is unchanged from 0.6.
  - The VTC serves git-ns/bridge/event/0.6 only. A bindCompleted carrying
    supersedes records it in the namespace's audit history
    (gitNs.namespace.superseded, the bridge as actor); nothing is restored
    from those ids.
  - Orphaned namespaces, VTC step 1: git-ns:unknownNamespace is answered to
    an event only when the namespace's record is positively absent. A store
    read failure, or a record that exists but cannot be read, is answered
    with the framework's unavailable, since a 0.6 bridge stops acting in a
    namespace on unknownNamespace. A bridge result whose job record cannot
    be read is likewise unavailable, never unknownJob.

  The registry also republished git-ns/bridge/job/list 0.4 with a
  description-only change (JobKind now names job 0.7); its new digest is
  locked here.

- **notifications**: Notify/relay, the VTA's held notifications and the election notice (VTI-NTF-001 – 063) ([#2397](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2397))

* feat(notifications)!: notifications/notify + relay, the VTA's held notifications, and the election notice to a member party (VTI-NTF-001 – 063)

  Implements the Notifications chapter of the VTI specification
  (dtgwg-vti-spec #91, VTI-NTF-001 – 063, Appendix G `election`) over the
  tasks pinned from dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1012: notifications/notify/0.1 and
  notifications/relay/0.1 (vti-specs-core), vta/notifications/{list,show,
  dismiss}/0.1 (vti-specs-vta).

  - vta-sdk: `notifications::verify_delivery` -> `VerifiedDelivery`, the one
    way to a notification's members: every layer's type and pinned schema,
    each proof over the JSON as received as its own issuer, each forwarded
    document addressed to the relay carrying it, at most four relays,
    `relayable` honoured (VTI-NTF-042). TASK_* constants, retry_safety
    (notify/relay/dismiss RetrySafe, list/show ReadOnly), typed and `_json`
    client methods for list/show/dismiss.
  - VTA: notify/relay are counterparty tasks (zero-authority claim for a
    sender the ACL does not know); the stated acceptance policy
    (`[notifications]`: an ACL entry, an issuer of a membership credential or
    a party of a relationship credential held in the context, `accept_from`,
    `accept_any`) counts the delivering relayer, never the originator
    (VTI-NTF-030/031); one record per (addressee, originator, notificationId),
    higher revision replaces, dismissal kept (VTI-NTF-022); the same receipt
    whatever was done (VTI-NTF-023); bounds per originator and deliverer
    (VTI-NTF-033); held per context in the new `notifications` keyspace
    (backed up), listed/read/dismissed only with standing there
    (VTI-NTF-050 – 052); lapsed records swept after `retain_lapsed_days`.
  - VTC as originator: an election under a credential roll naming a member
    party is notified to that party once registered and withdrawn (higher
    revision) if cancelled or closed before voting closes (VTI-NTF-060/061);
    the notice is recorded before it is sent and queued on the durable member
    push by the election sweeper, its one sender.
  - VTC as recipient and relayer: notify/relay on the open door, verified and
    held by its stated policy in its own `notifications` keyspace (backed up);
    a relay engine that refuses a decision which has not acknowledged what
    the relay discloses (VTI-NTF-046), relays the document exactly as
    received to every member, keeps whom it relayed to until the period ends
    (30 days without one) and relays every later revision, withdrawals
    included, to them (VTI-NTF-044). No remote surface for the relay decision
    yet: the specification defines no administrator task for it.
  - pnm: `pnm notifications list|show|dismiss`.

- **voting**: Credential rolls proven at the ticket claim, and elections shown only to whom they concern (VTI-VOT-015 – 018, VTI-VOT-025 – 029) ([#2395](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2395))

* build(specs): pin the credential-roll and election-privacy task versions

  voting/_shared/0.4 and every task carrying it (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1008,
  #1010, #1011): voting/election/register/0.4, show/0.4;
  vtc/elections/create/0.5, show/0.6, list/0.5, tickets/issue/0.3;
  vta/pcs/voter/register/0.5, voter/read/0.6, vote/0.4, vote-encrypted/0.5,
  trustee/{deal,justify,keys}/0.5, enrol/0.4, read/0.4. Older versions stay
  pinned.



### Changed

- **vtc-service**: The Trust Task receive pipeline as the vti-trust-task-server crate ([#2410](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2410))

The spine a received Trust Task goes through (size, parse, freshness,
  expiry and recipient, the spec's own policy, proof bound to issuer, the
  DIDComm/TSP sender binding, admission, the duplicate-id record, dispatch,
  signed replies) moves out of vtc-service into a new workspace crate, so the
  VTN service can speak Trust Tasks with the same pipeline instead of a copy.

  Service concerns are injected as traits: SpecPolicySource, SizeGate,
  ProofVerifier (ResolverProofVerifier over a TrustTaskVmResolver),
  SpineHooks (recipient, before/after-proof gates), VerifiedAdmission,
  AcceptedIdStore (InMemoryAcceptedIds for tests), Dispatcher and
  ResponseSigner. The crate also owns TrustTaskOutcome, ArrivalCtx/Transport,
  the reject and response helpers, typed payload/response validation, and an
  axum POST /v1/trust-tasks handler. It depends on no service and no
  vti-specs-* crate.

  vtc-service keeps its fjall-backed accepted-id record, its known-issuer
  size gate and large-document budget, the oob/install/delegation/did:scid
  hooks, the parked-operation submission scope, ACL and step-up, and its own
  HTTPS route (admission, cookies, event streams). JoinAuthCtx and
  JoinTransport are now the crate's ArrivalCtx and Transport. Behaviour is
  unchanged: four generic helper tests moved into the new crate.



### Fixed

- **vtc**: Census entries #2395 left stale ([#2400](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2400))

- list-limits: ElectionBuilder's members-list call now wraps across lines.
  - trust_task_manifest: feature-gated elections types now match what the
    console sends (create/0.5, list/0.5, show/0.6).

title: feat(rs)!: a stated expiresAt replaces the maximum age, up to an expiry horizon
body:
## Why

SPEC §7.2 (*Bounding the record*) applies the maximum age over `issuedAt` "where `expiresAt` is absent". `validate_freshness` applied it whatever the document said. As a result, a document whose producer stated a one-day expiry was refused as stale after five minutes under `consequential()`. A store-and-forward delivery could therefore last only as long as the consumer's maximum age.

This brings `trust-tasks-rs` in line with the specification it implements. It is needed by VTI spec trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#96 (VTI-OPS-024/028/029, VTI-TRN-048), which has merged. Under that spec a node accepts a document until its stated expiry, clamped to 30 days after issue.

## What changes

- **`validate_freshness`:**
  - `max_age` applies only to a document with no `expiresAt`.
  - A document with an `expiresAt` is bounded by it, as `validate_basic` already checks, but no later than `issuedAt + expiry_horizon` plus skew. Up to then it is accepted; after that it is refused as `expired`. A document is never refused for stating a later expiry; the expiry is clamped instead.
- **`FreshnessPolicy`:**
  - New field `expiry_horizon` and builder `with_expiry_horizon`.
  - `consequential()` sets `DEFAULT_EXPIRY_HORIZON` (30 days). `Default` sets none.
  - The struct is now `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- **`record_expiry`:** clamps the same way, so the replay record lasts exactly as long as the document is acceptable.
  - A document with no `issuedAt` gets no horizon: its record runs to its `expiresAt`. A horizon counted from first sight would drop the record while a later copy is still acceptable, so that copy would run again.

## Why `!`

The API changes: a new field, and `#[non_exhaustive]`. The behaviour change is the more important reason. A consumer that keeps its replay record only until `issuedAt + max_age + skew`, trusting `validate_freshness` to refuse anything older, has a double-execution hole once this lands. VTI's VTA does exactly that. Such a consumer must take its retention from `record_expiry` instead. A semver-compatible release would hand this change to every caret consumer silently.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`trust-task-discovery/0.3` says `acceptanceWindow` "governs `issuedAt` only", and that a responder refuses any document once `issuedAt + maxAgeSeconds + clockSkewSeconds` has passed.
- **Responder side:** after this change the advertised window is narrower than the one applied to documents that carry an `expiresAt`. Responder rule 1 permits that.
- **Producer side:** producers following rule 2 will still issue a new attempt at max age even when the document states a later expiry. That is wasteful, not unsafe.

A 0.4 could say the window applies where `expiresAt` is absent, and could advertise the horizon.

## Tests

- New tests:
  - `a_stated_expiry_replaces_the_maximum_age`
  - `an_expiry_beyond_the_horizon_is_clamped_to_it` (inside the horizon, within skew of it, past it; no horizon)
  - `the_horizon_needs_an_issued_at`
- The suites of `trust-tasks-rs`, `trust-tasks-https`, `trust-tasks-didcomm`, `trust-tasks-tsp` and `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` pass.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

title: feat(rs)!: a stated expiresAt replaces the maximum age, up to an expiry horizon (#1021)
body:
feat(rs)!: a stated expiresAt replaces the maximum age, up to an expiry horizon (#1021)

SPEC §7.2 (Bounding the record) applies the maximum age over issuedAt
"where expiresAt is absent". validate_freshness applied it whatever the
document stated, so a document whose producer stated a day-long expiry was
refused as stale after five minutes, and a store-and-forward delivery could
outlive only the consumer's maximum age.

- validate_freshness applies max_age only to a document without an
  expiresAt. One with an expiresAt is bounded by it (validate_basic),
  clamped to issuedAt + expiry_horizon (+ skew): accepted until then,
  refused as expired after, never refused for stating a later instant.
- FreshnessPolicy gains expiry_horizon and with_expiry_horizon;
  consequential() sets DEFAULT_EXPIRY_HORIZON (30 days). The default
  policy sets none.
- record_expiry clamps the same way, so the replay record lasts exactly as
  long as the document is acceptable. Without an issuedAt the horizon has
  nothing to run from and the expiry stands: a horizon from first sight
  would drop the record while a copy is still acceptable.
- FreshnessPolicy is now #[non_exhaustive].

Breaking, in behaviour as well as API: a consumer that caps its replay
record at issuedAt + max_age + skew, relying on validate_freshness to
refuse older documents, must cap at record_expiry instead, or an
expiresAt-bounded document accepted past its max age would execute twice.

title: vta-service-v0.71.0
body:
### Added

- **vetting**: Recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset, vta/pcs/vetter/recover) ([#2406](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2406))

* feat(vtc): recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset)

  A vetter is bound to the PCS identifier of their first enrolment, and a
  second identifier is refused with pcs-root:identifierRebound. The binding
  was never cleared, so a vetter whose key was lost was locked out of hidden
  vetting for as long as they stayed a member; revoking and re-granting the
  role did not help.

  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1: a member reads their own
    binding (identifier, enrolled labels, any pending reset), so their client
    can recover the matching key. Membership is the entitlement;
    notAMember otherwise.
  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/reset/0.1: an administrator holding
    vtc.vetting.manage (as vetters/grant) resets a member's binding with a
    reason. Idempotent; notBound for a member who never enrolled. Audited as
    HiddenVetterBindingReset, never with the identifier.
  - Enrolment after a reset: the recorded identifier cancels it
    (HiddenVetterResetCancelled); a new one is refused (identifierRebound)
    while any label the old one enrolled under is live, judged at each
    request against the caller's configuration and the stored one under the
    enrolment lock, and bound once none is (HiddenVetterRebound) with its
    labels afresh. The old labels are retired on the record.
  - vtc/vetting/hidden/publish refuses to make a retired label live again,
    checked before the consent gate and again under the enrolment lock
    before the write. publish/0.1 declares no code for it, so it is a
    validation refusal.
  - Admin console: a "Reset a hidden-vetting key" card under Vetting ->
    Vetters, shown when discovery lists the task.
  - EnrolmentRecord gains optional reset and retiredLabels members; rows
    without them read and write as before.

  The two specifications are pinned from a locally built registry ahead of
  their publication; trust-tasks.lock records that registry until they are
  re-pinned against trusttasks.org.

- **notifications**: Deposit to the VTA, a community's received notifications and relay decision, and four fixes (VTI-NTF-005, 034, 041, 047, 054 – 056, 070 – 074) ([#2405](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2405))

* feat(vti-specs): pin vta/notifications/deposit 0.1 and vtc/notifications/{list,show,relay} 0.1

  From trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1017: the client's hand-over of a
  notification received for a persona DID (vti-specs-vta), and a
  community's administrators' view and relay decision (vti-specs-vtc).
  notifications/notify and relay 0.1 changed in prose only; their pinned
  digests are unchanged.

- **notifications**: Notify/relay, the VTA's held notifications and the election notice (VTI-NTF-001 – 063) ([#2397](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2397))

* feat(notifications)!: notifications/notify + relay, the VTA's held notifications, and the election notice to a member party (VTI-NTF-001 – 063)

  Implements the Notifications chapter of the VTI specification
  (dtgwg-vti-spec #91, VTI-NTF-001 – 063, Appendix G `election`) over the
  tasks pinned from dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1012: notifications/notify/0.1 and
  notifications/relay/0.1 (vti-specs-core), vta/notifications/{list,show,
  dismiss}/0.1 (vti-specs-vta).

  - vta-sdk: `notifications::verify_delivery` -> `VerifiedDelivery`, the one
    way to a notification's members: every layer's type and pinned schema,
    each proof over the JSON as received as its own issuer, each forwarded
    document addressed to the relay carrying it, at most four relays,
    `relayable` honoured (VTI-NTF-042). TASK_* constants, retry_safety
    (notify/relay/dismiss RetrySafe, list/show ReadOnly), typed and `_json`
    client methods for list/show/dismiss.
  - VTA: notify/relay are counterparty tasks (zero-authority claim for a
    sender the ACL does not know); the stated acceptance policy
    (`[notifications]`: an ACL entry, an issuer of a membership credential or
    a party of a relationship credential held in the context, `accept_from`,
    `accept_any`) counts the delivering relayer, never the originator
    (VTI-NTF-030/031); one record per (addressee, originator, notificationId),
    higher revision replaces, dismissal kept (VTI-NTF-022); the same receipt
    whatever was done (VTI-NTF-023); bounds per originator and deliverer
    (VTI-NTF-033); held per context in the new `notifications` keyspace
    (backed up), listed/read/dismissed only with standing there
    (VTI-NTF-050 – 052); lapsed records swept after `retain_lapsed_days`.
  - VTC as originator: an election under a credential roll naming a member
    party is notified to that party once registered and withdrawn (higher
    revision) if cancelled or closed before voting closes (VTI-NTF-060/061);
    the notice is recorded before it is sent and queued on the durable member
    push by the election sweeper, its one sender.
  - VTC as recipient and relayer: notify/relay on the open door, verified and
    held by its stated policy in its own `notifications` keyspace (backed up);
    a relay engine that refuses a decision which has not acknowledged what
    the relay discloses (VTI-NTF-046), relays the document exactly as
    received to every member, keeps whom it relayed to until the period ends
    (30 days without one) and relays every later revision, withdrawals
    included, to them (VTI-NTF-044). No remote surface for the relay decision
    yet: the specification defines no administrator task for it.
  - pnm: `pnm notifications list|show|dismiss`.

- **voting**: Credential rolls proven at the ticket claim, and elections shown only to whom they concern (VTI-VOT-015 – 018, VTI-VOT-025 – 029) ([#2395](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2395))

* build(specs): pin the credential-roll and election-privacy task versions

  voting/_shared/0.4 and every task carrying it (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1008,
  #1010, #1011): voting/election/register/0.4, show/0.4;
  vtc/elections/create/0.5, show/0.6, list/0.5, tickets/issue/0.3;
  vta/pcs/voter/register/0.5, voter/read/0.6, vote/0.4, vote-encrypted/0.5,
  trustee/{deal,justify,keys}/0.5, enrol/0.4, read/0.4. Older versions stay
  pinned.



### Fixed

- **idempotency**: Never re-run a keyed Trust Task whose earlier attempt died ([#2409](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2409))

VTI-OPS-061 requires a node to perform a keyed operation at most once per
  key. The dispatcher claims the key, the handler commits its effect, then
  `record_outcome` marks the key done. Those are separate writes. A process
  that died between the effect and the record left an in-flight claim, and
  after the 10-minute grace `IdempotencyStore::claim` reclaimed it and ran the
  handler again. The new restart test shows the result: a retry of
  `keys/create` minted a second key ([#2402](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2402)).

  A stale in-flight claim is now `ClaimOutcome::Abandoned { claimed_at }` and
  is never reclaimed while its record lives. The VTA answers it with
  `taskFailed` ("outcome unknown", `details.claimedAt`). The caller checks
  whether the effect exists and uses a new key if it is still wanted. Inside
  the grace a retry still gets `unavailable`. An expired record is claimed
  afresh, as before.

  A store error while claiming now answers `unavailable` rather than
  dispatching unguarded. A keyed request run without its claim is one a
  later retry can run again.

  BREAKING CHANGE (vti-common): `ClaimOutcome` gains `Abandoned` and is now
  `#[non_exhaustive]`; `claim` no longer reclaims a stale in-flight record.

- **vta**: Room profile padding converges instead of oscillating ([#2408](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2408))

sign_padded aimed each retry at the last signed length. A base58
  Ed25519 proof is 88 characters about four times in five, so after a
  short proof it bet on the unlikely length again and could run out of
  attempts, which made a_curators_profile_is_accepted_and_padded_to_a_block
  fail about 1 run in 60.

  Aim at the longest unpadded length seen instead, and when the aim has
  not moved, add a whole block and keep it: Ed25519 is deterministic, so
  re-signing a body already tried returns the same short proof.
  300 consecutive runs pass.

title: vti-vetting-pcs-v0.12.0
body:
### Added

- **vetting**: Recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset, vta/pcs/vetter/recover) ([#2406](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2406))

* feat(vtc): recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset)

  A vetter is bound to the PCS identifier of their first enrolment, and a
  second identifier is refused with pcs-root:identifierRebound. The binding
  was never cleared, so a vetter whose key was lost was locked out of hidden
  vetting for as long as they stayed a member; revoking and re-granting the
  role did not help.

  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1: a member reads their own
    binding (identifier, enrolled labels, any pending reset), so their client
    can recover the matching key. Membership is the entitlement;
    notAMember otherwise.
  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/reset/0.1: an administrator holding
    vtc.vetting.manage (as vetters/grant) resets a member's binding with a
    reason. Idempotent; notBound for a member who never enrolled. Audited as
    HiddenVetterBindingReset, never with the identifier.
  - Enrolment after a reset: the recorded identifier cancels it
    (HiddenVetterResetCancelled); a new one is refused (identifierRebound)
    while any label the old one enrolled under is live, judged at each
    request against the caller's configuration and the stored one under the
    enrolment lock, and bound once none is (HiddenVetterRebound) with its
    labels afresh. The old labels are retired on the record.
  - vtc/vetting/hidden/publish refuses to make a retired label live again,
    checked before the consent gate and again under the enrolment lock
    before the write. publish/0.1 declares no code for it, so it is a
    validation refusal.
  - Admin console: a "Reset a hidden-vetting key" card under Vetting ->
    Vetters, shown when discovery lists the task.
  - EnrolmentRecord gains optional reset and retiredLabels members; rows
    without them read and write as before.

  The two specifications are pinned from a locally built registry ahead of
  their publication; trust-tasks.lock records that registry until they are
  re-pinned against trusttasks.org.

  `deleted: false` is no longer printed as "Context deleted": the
  specification says a consumer must not report the deletion as done on the
  response status alone.

  key. The dispatcher claims the key, the handler commits its effect, then
  `record_outcome` marks the key done. Those are separate writes. A process
  that died between the effect and the record left an in-flight claim, and
  after the 10-minute grace `IdempotencyStore::claim` reclaimed it and ran the
  handler again. The new restart test shows the result: a retry of
  `keys/create` minted a second key ([#2402](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2402)).

  A stale in-flight claim is now `ClaimOutcome::Abandoned { claimed_at }` and
  is never reclaimed while its record lives. The VTA answers it with
  `taskFailed` ("outcome unknown", `details.claimedAt`). The caller checks
  whether the effect exists and uses a new key if it is still wanted. Inside
  the grace a retry still gets `unavailable`. An expired record is claimed
  afresh, as before.

  A store error while claiming now answers `unavailable` rather than
  dispatching unguarded. A keyed request run without its claim is one a
  later retry can run again.

  BREAKING CHANGE (vti-common): `ClaimOutcome` gains `Abandoned` and is now
  `#[non_exhaustive]`; `claim` no longer reclaims a stale in-flight record.

- **store**: A templated test store copies the template's empty directories too ([#2388](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2388))

    each proof over the JSON as received as its own issuer, each forwarded
    document addressed to the relay carrying it, at most four relays,
    `relayable` honoured (VTI-NTF-042). TASK_* constants, retry_safety
    (notify/relay/dismiss RetrySafe, list/show ReadOnly), typed and `_json`
    client methods for list/show/dismiss.
  - VTA: notify/relay are counterparty tasks (zero-authority claim for a
    sender the ACL does not know); the stated acceptance policy
    (`[notifications]`: an ACL entry, an issuer of a membership credential or
    a party of a relationship credential held in the context, `accept_from`,
    `accept_any`) counts the delivering relayer, never the originator
    (VTI-NTF-030/031); one record per (addressee, originator, notificationId),
    higher revision replaces, dismissal kept (VTI-NTF-022); the same receipt
    whatever was done (VTI-NTF-023); bounds per originator and deliverer
    (VTI-NTF-033); held per context in the new `notifications` keyspace
    (backed up), listed/read/dismissed only with standing there
    (VTI-NTF-050 – 052); lapsed records swept after `retain_lapsed_days`.
  - VTC as originator: an election under a credential roll naming a member
    party is notified to that party once registered and withdrawn (higher
    revision) if cancelled or closed before voting closes (VTI-NTF-060/061);
    the notice is recorded before it is sent and queued on the durable member
    push by the election sweeper, its one sender.
  - VTC as recipient and relayer: notify/relay on the open door, verified and
    held by its stated policy in its own `notifications` keyspace (backed up);
    a relay engine that refuses a decision which has not acknowledged what
    the relay discloses (VTI-NTF-046), relays the document exactly as
    received to every member, keeps whom it relayed to until the period ends
    (30 days without one) and relays every later revision, withdrawals
    included, to them (VTI-NTF-044). No remote surface for the relay decision
    yet: the specification defines no administrator task for it.
  - pnm: `pnm notifications list|show|dismiss`.

- **voting**: Credential rolls proven at the ticket claim, and elections shown only to whom they concern (VTI-VOT-015 – 018, VTI-VOT-025 – 029) ([#2395](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2395))

* build(specs): pin the credential-roll and election-privacy task versions

  voting/_shared/0.4 and every task carrying it (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1008,
  #1010, #1011): voting/election/register/0.4, show/0.4;
  vtc/elections/create/0.5, show/0.6, list/0.5, tickets/issue/0.3;
  vta/pcs/voter/register/0.5, voter/read/0.6, vote/0.4, vote-encrypted/0.5,
  trustee/{deal,justify,keys}/0.5, enrol/0.4, read/0.4. Older versions stay
  pinned.



### Fixed

- **vta-sdk**: Do not treat missing host-cleanup evidence as an empty failure list ([#2407](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2407))

`host_cleanup_failures` read a `vta/contexts/delete:hostCleanupFailed`
  refusal whose `details.hostCleanupFailures` was absent, empty or malformed
  as `Some(vec![])`, so the CLI showed "0 DID(s)" and still offered to retry
  with `abandonHostCopies`. Nothing earlier checks those details: a
  `VtaError::Rejected` carries them as sent, and the generated error-code
  tables do not hold the code's `detailsSchema`.

  `host_cleanup_refusal` now classifies the refusal as `Evidenced` (one or
  more entries with non-empty `did` and `reason`, and `server` non-empty when
  present) or `Unreadable { why }`. It matches the exact declared code only,
  never a `taskFailed` that reads the same. `host_cleanup_failures` is
  deprecated and returns `None` for an unreadable refusal.

  The CLI offers the abandonment only for an `Evidenced` refusal, still behind
  its own confirmation, which `--yes` never answers. An `Unreadable` refusal is
  reported with the reason and the plain retry command. A success carrying
  `deleted: false` is no longer printed as "Context deleted": the
  specification says a consumer must not report the deletion as done on the
  response status alone.

title: vti-specs-vtc-v0.3.0
body:
### Added

- **vetting**: Recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset, vta/pcs/vetter/recover) ([#2406](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2406))

* feat(vtc): recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset)

  A vetter is bound to the PCS identifier of their first enrolment, and a
  second identifier is refused with pcs-root:identifierRebound. The binding
  was never cleared, so a vetter whose key was lost was locked out of hidden
  vetting for as long as they stayed a member; revoking and re-granting the
  role did not help.

  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1: a member reads their own
    binding (identifier, enrolled labels, any pending reset), so their client
    can recover the matching key. Membership is the entitlement;
    notAMember otherwise.
  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/reset/0.1: an administrator holding
    vtc.vetting.manage (as vetters/grant) resets a member's binding with a
    reason. Idempotent; notBound for a member who never enrolled. Audited as
    HiddenVetterBindingReset, never with the identifier.
  - Enrolment after a reset: the recorded identifier cancels it
    (HiddenVetterResetCancelled); a new one is refused (identifierRebound)
    while any label the old one enrolled under is live, judged at each
    request against the caller's configuration and the stored one under the
    enrolment lock, and bound once none is (HiddenVetterRebound) with its
    labels afresh. The old labels are retired on the record.
  - vtc/vetting/hidden/publish refuses to make a retired label live again,
    checked before the consent gate and again under the enrolment lock
    before the write. publish/0.1 declares no code for it, so it is a
    validation refusal.
  - Admin console: a "Reset a hidden-vetting key" card under Vetting ->
    Vetters, shown when discovery lists the task.
  - EnrolmentRecord gains optional reset and retiredLabels members; rows
    without them read and write as before.

  The two specifications are pinned from a locally built registry ahead of
  their publication; trust-tasks.lock records that registry until they are
  re-pinned against trusttasks.org.

- **notifications**: Deposit to the VTA, a community's received notifications and relay decision, and four fixes (VTI-NTF-005, 034, 041, 047, 054 – 056, 070 – 074) ([#2405](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2405))

* feat(vti-specs): pin vta/notifications/deposit 0.1 and vtc/notifications/{list,show,relay} 0.1

  From trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1017: the client's hand-over of a
  notification received for a persona DID (vti-specs-vta), and a
  community's administrators' view and relay decision (vti-specs-vtc).
  notifications/notify and relay 0.1 changed in prose only; their pinned
  digests are unchanged.

- **vtc**: A community's side of Verifiable Trust Network membership ([#2399](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2399))

  list, show, join, repudiate, leave, groups/register, notice and evidence

  Verifiable Trust Network membership.

- **voting**: Credential rolls proven at the ticket claim, and elections shown only to whom they concern (VTI-VOT-015 – 018, VTI-VOT-025 – 029) ([#2395](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2395))

body:
### Added

- **git-ns**: The VTC speaks bridge job 0.7 and event 0.6 ([#2401](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2401))

* feat(git-ns): the VTC speaks bridge job 0.7 and event 0.6

  Pin git-ns/bridge/job 0.7 and git-ns/bridge/event 0.6 in vti-specs-core
  (replacing job 0.6 and event 0.5; test deployments only, no fallback).

  - Jobs go out as git-ns/bridge/job/0.7 only, and only to a bridge that
    lists 0.7 in trust-task-discovery (vgi-bridge v0.31.0 or later). The
    schema is unchanged from 0.6.
  - The VTC serves git-ns/bridge/event/0.6 only. A bindCompleted carrying
    supersedes records it in the namespace's audit history
    (gitNs.namespace.superseded, the bridge as actor); nothing is restored
    from those ids.
  - Orphaned namespaces, VTC step 1: git-ns:unknownNamespace is answered to
    an event only when the namespace's record is positively absent. A store
    read failure, or a record that exists but cannot be read, is answered
    with the framework's unavailable, since a 0.6 bridge stops acting in a
    namespace on unknownNamespace. A bridge result whose job record cannot
