title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.36.10
body:
### Added

- **vtn**: The Verifiable Trust Network's own Trust Tasks (vtn/*/0.1) ([#1020](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1020))

A Verifiable Trust Network curates communities and networks into a
  nestable published set (VTI-VTN-001 - 063). Its API was interim REST;
  these are its Trust Tasks:

  - a listed party toward the network: entries/show, membership/{offer,
    acknowledge,repudiate}, groups/register, relay/deliver, roles/list,
    rooms/{list,pass}
  - reading the published set: directory/{search,federated,summary},
    graph/{show,member}
  - administration: listings/{create,update,suspend,reinstate,remove,list,
    show}, audit/list, groups/list, broadcasts/{send,list,show},
    outbox/{list,retry}
  - the network as a member of a parent: memberships/{list,join,repudiate,
    leave,groups/add}
  - vtn/_shared/0.1: entry, directory, graph, groups, relay, membership and
    rooms shapes

  Trust Tasks are the API; DTG credentials remain the evidence: lists/1,
  the VMC pair, repudiates/1, and a revocable groupRegistered acceptance
  binding the signed vtn/groups/register request by digest. Browser
  sign-in reuses auth/oob/* and auth/signing-key/*. Short lifetimes for
  anything not revocable: room passes at most 24 hours, broadcasts at
  most 7 days.

- **vetting**: Recover or reset a hidden-vetting key (vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/{show,reset}/0.1, vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1) ([#1018](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1018))

* feat(vtc,vta): recover or reset a hidden-vetting key — vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/{show,reset}/0.1 and vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1

  A community binds each vetter to one PCS identifier for good, so a vetter
  whose VTA engine lost track of its key was locked out of hidden vetting
  for as long as they stayed a member; revoking and re-granting the vetter
  role does not touch the binding.

  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1: a member reads their own
    binding, and the state of any reset.
  - vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1: the VTA searches the keys it can derive for
    the context and restores the bound one, while the engine's current key
    holds nothing a community issued.
  - vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/reset/0.1: an administrator resets the
    binding when the key is gone. A new identifier is bound only once no
    label the old one enrolled under is live, and a retired label never
    comes back, so the member is never counted twice.

  pcs-root/0.1 and the vta/pcs conventions point at the new tasks.

- **notifications**: Deposit to the VTA, the community's received notifications, and four fixes ([#1017](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1017))

Follow-up to #1012, implementing dtgwg-vti-spec's Notifications follow-up
  (VTI-NTF-006, 025, 034, 047, 054 – 056, 070 – 074).

  New tasks:

  - vta/notifications/deposit/0.1 — a client that receives a notify or relay
    for a DID whose keys its VTA holds (a persona DID whose mediator socket the
    client holds) hands the document to the VTA exactly as received. The VTA
    verifies it exactly as a direct delivery, counts for acceptance the party
    that delivered the document and never the depositing client, keeps one
    record per originator and notificationId, and answers with the same
    receipt whatever it did. Gated by standing in the context; retry class 2;
    notAddressedHere, documentInvalid.
  - vtc/notifications/list/0.1, show/0.1 — a community's administrators read
    the notifications addressed to the community (vtc.notifications.read).
  - vtc/notifications/relay/0.1 — an administrator's decision to relay one to
    all members, one group's or one role's (vtc.notifications.relay, qualified
    by group), refused until the disclosure is acknowledged; never to the
    community itself, the originator or any earlier relayer; later revisions
    follow without a further decision. destructive; retry class 2.

  Fixes to notifications/notify/0.1 and notifications/relay/0.1, prose only
  (no schema, error code or proof requirement changes):

  - relay producer item 2 now agrees with consumer item 2: a relayer may relay
    only where its relay makes at most four relays in all.
  - notification and relay proofs carry proofPurpose authentication with the
    operational key (VTI-KEY-081/082); examples updated from assertionMethod.
    VTI-KEY-107 applies to the relay received, not to forwarded layers.
  - a withdrawal keeps the period of the revision it replaces.
  - the originator re-checks VTI-NTF-005 for every revision it issues, except
    a withdrawal; election withdrawal covers an early close.
  - a relayer never relays to the originator or an earlier relayer.

The dispatcher claims the key, the handler commits its effect, then `record_outcome` marks the key done. Those are separate writes. A process that died between the effect and the record left an in-flight claim, and after the 10-minute grace `IdempotencyStore::claim` reclaimed it and ran the handler again. The new restart test shows the result: a retry of `keys/create` minted a second key ([#2402](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2402)). A store error while claiming now answers `unavailable` rather than dispatching unguarded. A keyed request run without its claim is one a later retry can run again. title: chore: release 11 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.36.9` → `0.36.10` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.36.9` → `0.36.10` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.36.9` → `0.36.10` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.36.9` → `0.36.10` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.36.9` → `0.36.10` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.36.9` → `0.36.10` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.36.9` → `0.36.10` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.36.9` → `0.36.10` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.28.10` → `0.28.11` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.10`) | `0.10.9` → `0.10.10` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.19` → `0.9.20` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: refactor(vtc-service): the Trust Task receive pipeline as the vti-trust-task-server crate
body:
This extracts the Trust Task receive pipeline from `vtc-service` into a new workspace crate, `vti-trust-task-server`, so a second service can reuse it instead of copying it. That service is `vtn-service`, which is moving from REST to Trust Tasks (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1020). `vtc-service`'s behaviour does not change.

## The crate

`Spine::new(policy, verifier, hooks, accepted_ids, dispatcher)` runs every received document through the same pipeline as before:
1. size
2. parse
3. freshness
4. expiry and recipient
5. spec policy
6. proof
7. sender match (DIDComm/TSP)
8. duplicate id
9. dispatch
10. a signed answer, refusals included

A service supplies the parts that differ through small traits:
- `SpecPolicySource`: any `Fn(&str) -> Option<SpecPolicy>`
- `SizeGate`
- `ProofVerifier`: `ResolverProofVerifier` wraps a `TrustTaskVmResolver`
- `SpineHooks`
- `VerifiedAdmission`
- `AcceptedIdStore`: `InMemoryAcceptedIds` is included for tests and small services
- `Dispatcher`
- `ResponseSigner`

The crate also holds:
- the generic `reject` helpers;
- typed `parse_spec_payload` and `respond`;
- the size peek helpers;
- a plain `http::routes` handler for `POST /v1/trust-tasks`.

It depends only on shared crates, never on `vtc-service` or a spec crate.

## What stays in vtc-service

These now plug into the spine as its implementations of the traits:
- the address-keyed size gate and large-document budget
- the fjall `AcceptedIds`
- the oob precheck
- install-DID refresh and did:scid recording
- the delegated-key-as-approver refusal
- `dispatch_typed`
- parked-operation answers
- `LocalSigner`
- ACL, capabilities and bound step-up
- room budgets, and its own HTTPS route, which needs admission, cookies and event streams

`JoinAuthCtx` and `JoinTransport` are now aliases of the crate's `ArrivalCtx` and `Transport`.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt`, and workspace clippy and `vtc-service --features test-support,voting` clippy with `-D warnings`.
- `vtc-service`, test-support with voting: 3633 passed, 1 skipped. That is 4 fewer than main, because the four generic helper tests moved into the new crate. None were dropped.
- `vti-trust-task-server`: 20 tests, covering stale and missing `issuedAt`, wrong recipient, missing or tampered proof, DIDComm/TSP sender rules, duplicate replay and `idConflict`, release on refused dispatch, unsupported type and version, oversized and non-document bodies, and the HTTPS route.
- Every census passes unchanged, with no allowlist touched. That covers DISPATCHED_URIS, conformance, error_code_census, spec_pin_census, REST_EXCEPTIONS, GOVERNED_UNAUTH, trust_task_manifest and openapi.
- `non_exhaustive_census` passes; the Nitro Dockerfile copies all 43 members.
- RELEASING.md ("28 of 37"), the CLAUDE.md crate table and `Dockerfile.nitro` are updated.

title: feat(vetting): recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset, vta/pcs/vetter/recover)
body:
## What and why

A community running hidden vetting binds each vetter's member DID to one PCS identifier for good. A vetter whose VTA engine lost track of its key (re-created engine record, restored VTA) was refused every enrolment with `pcs-root:identifierRebound`, for as long as they stayed a member — revoking and re-granting the vetter role does not touch the binding. Hit live on a community this week.

**VTC**
- `vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1` — a member reads their own binding and the state of any reset. Membership is enough.
- `vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/reset/0.1` — admin-only (`vtc.vetting.manage`, as `vetters/grant`), idempotent, `notBound` for a member who never enrolled. After a reset: the old identifier cancels it; a new identifier is refused while any label the old one held is live (evaluated per request, under `ENROL_LOCK`, against the stored config too); otherwise the new one is bound, labels restart, old labels are kept as retired.
- `hidden/publish` refuses to make a retired label live again (`labelRetired`), checked before consent and again under the lock.
- `EnrolmentRecord` gains optional `reset` / `retiredLabels` — old rows read and write as before.
- Audit: `HiddenVetterBindingReset`, `HiddenVetterResetCancelled`, `HiddenVetterRebound` — reason and labels, never the identifier.
- Admin console: "Reset a hidden-vetting key" under Vetting → Vetters (discovery-gated, required reason, confirm).

**VTA**
- `vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1` (`pcsVetter`): searches the context's allocated member-key paths under every held seed generation for the bound identifier, through a new audited custody door (`vta_keys::custody::authorize_pcs_search`, one `key.pcs_search` audit row, only `{path, seed_id}` leaves custody). Bound 4096 derivations; over it, searches nothing and answers `notFound`. Excludes paths held by other PCS engines (the identifier is a function of the key alone). Refuses `engineEnrolled` if the current key holds anything a community issued; `heldInAnotherContext` / `memberMismatch` as declared.
- `vta-sdk` helper (`RetrySafe`), `vta-mcp` classes it `Sensitive`, `vta-mobile-core` gains `PcsTask::VetterRecover` (native bindings not regenerated).

title: feat(vetting): recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset, vta/pcs/vetter/recover) (#2406)
body:
feat(vetting): recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset, vta/pcs/vetter/recover) (#2406)

* feat(vtc): recover or reset a lost hidden-vetting key (pcs-binding/show, pcs-binding/reset)

A vetter is bound to the PCS identifier of their first enrolment, and a
second identifier is refused with pcs-root:identifierRebound. The binding
was never cleared, so a vetter whose key was lost was locked out of hidden
vetting for as long as they stayed a member; revoking and re-granting the
role did not help.

- vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1: a member reads their own
  binding (identifier, enrolled labels, any pending reset), so their client
  can recover the matching key. Membership is the entitlement;
  notAMember otherwise.
- vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/reset/0.1: an administrator holding
  vtc.vetting.manage (as vetters/grant) resets a member's binding with a
  reason. Idempotent; notBound for a member who never enrolled. Audited as
  HiddenVetterBindingReset, never with the identifier.
- Enrolment after a reset: the recorded identifier cancels it
  (HiddenVetterResetCancelled); a new one is refused (identifierRebound)
  while any label the old one enrolled under is live, judged at each
  request against the caller's configuration and the stored one under the
  enrolment lock, and bound once none is (HiddenVetterRebound) with its
  labels afresh. The old labels are retired on the record.
- vtc/vetting/hidden/publish refuses to make a retired label live again,
  checked before the consent gate and again under the enrolment lock
  before the write. publish/0.1 declares no code for it, so it is a
  validation refusal.
- Admin console: a "Reset a hidden-vetting key" card under Vetting ->
  Vetters, shown when discovery lists the task.
- EnrolmentRecord gains optional reset and retiredLabels members; rows
  without them read and write as before.

The two specifications are pinned from a locally built registry ahead of
their publication; trust-tasks.lock records that registry until they are
re-pinned against trusttasks.org.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-pcs): vta/pcs/vetter/recover — restore the vetter key a community bound

A vetter's key is never stored: it is derived at a path the engine record
keeps. When that record is lost or replaced while the seed survives, the next
vta/pcs/root-request makes a fresh key and the community refuses it with
pcs-root:identifierRebound. The bound key is usually still derivable.

vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1 takes the identifier the community bound
(boundId, from vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show) and searches the keys
the VTA can derive for the context: every path the context's counter has
handed out, under every seed generation still held, less the paths another
PCS engine record names. If one matches it becomes the engine's key; the
engine is created if none existed, and enrolments and draws in flight under
the replaced key are discarded. Refused memberMismatch, engineEnrolled (the
current key holds a class credential, tokens or attestations),
heldInAnotherContext (an engine in another context the caller can act in
holds it) or notFound.

Key custody gets a bulk door for the search (vta_keys::custody::
authorize_pcs_search / AuthorizedPcsSearch::find, wrapped by
key_custody::search_pcs_member_keys): every candidate is held inside the
context's base, each seed generation is loaded once, no seed, key or node is
returned, and the search is bounded at PCS_SEARCH_MAX_DERIVATIONS (4096). A
context with more candidates is refused notFound, saying so, rather than
searched in part. The search is audited once (key.pcs_search: how many keys,
whether one matched), the recovery as pcs.vetter.recover; neither names an
identifier, a path or a seed.

vti-vetting-pcs gains scheme::MemberIds, which sets the scheme instance up
once for a search. The spec is pinned from the local trust-tasks-tf registry
build until it is published; trust-tasks.lock records that registry and is
re-pinned against trusttasks.org after publish.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): refuse a retired vetter label with hidden/publish:labelRetired

Re-pins pcs-binding/show, hidden/publish and pcs-root at their settled
drafts. publish/0.1 now declares labelRetired, so the refusal that kept
a retired label from going live again names its code instead of a bare
badRequest.

title: feat(vtn): the Verifiable Trust Network's own Trust Tasks (vtn/*/0.1)
body:
A Verifiable Trust Network (VTN) curates communities and networks into a nestable published set ([VTI spec 11a, VTI-VTN-001 – 063](https://trustoverip.github.io/dtgwg-vti-spec/)). Its reference implementation (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network) has had an interim REST API. This adds its Trust Tasks, so the VTN speaks Trust Tasks only. REST stays only for the artifacts verifiers fetch by URL: the profile, status lists, the signed index and credentials.

## Tasks (33, all draft)

| Group | Tasks |
|---|---|
| A listed party toward the network | `entries/show`, `membership/{offer,acknowledge,repudiate}`, `groups/register`, `relay/deliver`, `roles/list`, `rooms/{list,pass}` |
| Reading the published set | `directory/{search,federated,summary}`, `graph/{show,member}`. These are governed by the network's directory visibility (`public` / `members` / `admins`); a person proves membership with a VMC from a member community. |
| Administration | `listings/{create,update,suspend,reinstate,remove,list,show}`, `audit/list`, `groups/list`, `broadcasts/{send,list,show}`, `outbox/{list,retry}` |
| The network as a member of a parent | `memberships/{list,join,repudiate,leave,groups/add}`, which mirror `vtc/networks/*` |

Shared shapes are in `vtn/_shared/0.1`: entry, directory, graph, groups, relay, membership and rooms.

## Design points for review

- **Trust Tasks are the API; credentials are the proof.** No Trust Task document is evidence of a relationship. The evidence stays as DTG credentials, verifiable later against keys and status lists:
  - `lists/1` for a listing;
  - the VMC grant and acknowledgement pair for membership;
  - `repudiates/1` for a repudiation;
  - a revocable `groupRegistered` acceptance for a group serving a role. It binds the member's signed `vtn/groups/register` request by digest and replaces the old `servesRole` VSC.
- **Unacknowledged is never membership** (VTI-VTN-013). Every published entry carries `acknowledged`. A network grants nothing over a member's own members or keys (VTI-VTN-060 – 063).
- **Browser sign-in reuses existing specs.** It uses `auth/oob/*` and `auth/signing-key/*`, so there are no VTN-specific session tasks.
- **Short lifetimes for anything not revocable.** Room passes last at most 24 hours. A broadcast lasts at most 7 days, and a receiving network refuses one that claims longer.
- **Federation never chains membership** (VTI-VTN-033). Federated results carry their path, with each hop's own entry state. An unreachable member network is reported, not dropped (VTI-REG-012).

## Also

- The `vtc/networks/*/0.1` examples now show the registered `lists/1` and `repudiates/1` IRIs and `nodeType` (trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#33), replacing the interim IRIs and `kind`. These are example and prose changes only.
- The bindings are regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart). `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass, and the Rust conformance tests pass for `vtn` and `vtc`.

Follow-up: `vtc/networks/*/0.2` will move the community side onto `vtn/groups/register` and `vtn/membership/*`.

title: Close the acceptance window at a document's expiry, up to thirty days, and keep both records to that end across restarts (VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-028, VTI-OPS-029, VTI-OPS-066, VTI-OPS-067, VTI-TRN-048)
body:
## Why

Today an expiry can only **shorten** a document's acceptance. VTI-OPS-024 defined the window over the time of issue alone, and both node types refuse any document more than ten minutes (plus skew) past issue, whatever `expiresAt` says. [TRUST-TASKS] §7.2 ("Bounding the record") already says the opposite: where `expiresAt` is present it fixes both acceptance and the record of accepted documents, and the maximum age applies only where it is absent.

Two consequences:
- Every delivery longer than ten minutes depends on a chain of re-signed documents (VTI-TRN-046). A push runs up to a day, or thirty days for a removal notice.
- Under one idempotency key those documents can arrive after the agent's 24-hour key record has expired, and the operation is then performed again.

## What changes

| Requirement | Change |
|---|---|
| **VTI-OPS-024** | The window closes at the document's **acceptance end**: its expiry where stated, otherwise time of issue + maximum age. A document whose time of issue is in the future (beyond skew), or whose expiry is not after its time of issue, is refused (as in [TRUST-TASKS] item 13). |
| **VTI-OPS-028** (new) | **Expiry horizon = 30 days after time of issue.** A stated expiry is honoured up to it, whatever the node's maximum age. A longer expiry is **clamped**, not refused. The value is fixed rather than advertised because a long delivery is exactly the case where the recipient can't answer discovery (F.3, VTI-TRN-045). |
| **VTI-OPS-029** (new) | The record of accepted identifiers is kept to the acceptance end and **survives a restart**. |
| **VTI-OPS-066** (new) | The record of a keyed operation is kept to the latest acceptance end of any document accepted under that key, and survives a restart. |
| **VTI-OPS-067** (new) | An attempt with no recorded outcome is never performed again under its key. A repeat is refused as "outcome unknown", distinguishable from a refusal of the request. This codifies VTI #2409. |
| **VTI-TRN-048** (new) | A sender whose delivery can outlast the recipient's maximum age states an expiry no later than the close of its delivery window. New documents under VTI-TRN-046 carry it unchanged. |
| Transports chapter | The latest acceptable instant is restated over the acceptance end. VTI-TRN-046's SHOULD now reads "after its acceptance end". |
| 04, 90 | References updated. |

**Appendix F:**
- F.2: VTI-OPS-024/028 (*observed*: maximum age applied whatever the expiry; the community node caps its id record at it).
- F.2: VTI-OPS-029 (*observed*: the agent's id record is in memory and lost on restart; this has to be fixed first).
- F.3: VTI-TRN-048 (*observed*: the push engine states no expiry).
- F.7: closed VTI-OPS-061/067 (VTI #2409).

## Implementation order (VTI)

1. trust-tasks-rs: `validate_freshness` applies the maximum age only when there is no `expiresAt`, plus a `max_expiry` horizon that `record_expiry` also applies.
2. Agent: persist the record of accepted identifiers (VTI-OPS-029).
3. Both node types (and `vti-witness`, `room-host`): adopt the acceptance end. Keep idempotency records for max(24h, the latest acceptance end under the key).
4. Push engine: stamp the push deadline (≤ 30 days) as `expiresAt`.

title: fix(idempotency)!: never re-run a keyed Trust Task whose earlier attempt died
body:
Closes #2402.

## The hypothesis, measured

The VTA claims the key, then the handler commits its effect, then `record_outcome` marks the key done. These are separate writes. If the process died between the effect and the record, it left an in-flight claim. After the 10-minute grace, `IdempotencyStore::claim` took that claim over and ran the handler again.

The new test shows the result: a `keys/create` retry minted a **second key**. That breaks VTI-OPS-061, which requires a keyed operation to be performed at most once per key. With the old rule put back temporarily, `vti_ops_061_an_attempt_interrupted_after_its_effect_is_never_rerun` fails because the retry runs again.

## Fix

- **`vti-common`:** a stale in-flight claim is now `ClaimOutcome::Abandoned { claimed_at }` and is never reclaimed while its record lives. Only an *expired* record (past the 24h lifetime) is claimed afresh. `ClaimOutcome` is now `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- **`vta-service`:**

  | Situation | Answer |
  |---|---|
  | Earlier attempt claimed the key, within the grace | `unavailable` + `retryAfter` (unchanged) |
  | Earlier attempt claimed the key, past the grace | `taskFailed` "outcome unknown", with `details.claimedAt`. The caller checks whether the effect exists and uses a new key if it is still wanted. The refusal is terminal, so `VtaClient::idempotent` does not loop on it. |
  | Store error while claiming | `unavailable`. Previously the request was dispatched unguarded, which a later retry could run again. |
- **Docs:** `docs/05-design-notes/retry-and-idempotency.md` is updated, including reversing its "store error dispatches unguarded" rule.

## Test seam (test-only)

`TestAppOptions::data_dir: Option<PathBuf>`:
- `None` behaves exactly as before.
- An empty directory is seeded from the keyspace template.
- A directory that already holds a store is reopened with `Store::open` as it is.

No production API changes.

**Release is asserted.** fjall locks its directory while any handle on it lives. The test first asserts that a second open fails while app 1 is alive, then drops the router and context, then asserts the reopen succeeds before app 2 is built.

**Interruption.** The test rewrites the key's record to exactly what `claim` writes: `InFlight`, no response, `created_at` backdated. That is the on-disk state after a crash between the effect and the record. It needs no hook in the production path and no controllable clock.

## Tests (`vta-service/tests/it/idempotency_trust_task.rs`)

- **`vti_ops_061_a_keyed_effect_survives_a_restart_once`**: after a restart:
  - the same key on a fresh envelope returns the same `keyId`, with 1 key on disk;
  - the same key with a changed payload is refused, and nothing is created;
  - controls: another key and no key each create a key (3 total). So the convergence comes from the key, not from `keys/create` being convergent or from the envelope-id replay cache; every envelope is new.
- **`vti_ops_061_an_attempt_interrupted_after_its_effect_is_never_rerun`**: after a restart:
  - within the grace: `unavailable`;
  - past the grace: `taskFailed` with `claimedAt`, asked twice;
  - the key count stays 1 throughout, and the record is left untouched;
  - a new key then performs.
- `vti-common` store tests: an abandoned claim is never reclaimed; a different payload under it is still `Conflict`; an expired abandoned claim is claimed afresh; racing reclaims of an expired claim have one winner.

## Checks

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6791/6792 passed. The one failure was `approvals_breakglass_cli::policy_delete_redirects_away_from_the_declarative_row`. It runs the offline `vta` binary over its own tempdir and touches neither test_support nor idempotency. It passed on rerun, and the full `-p vta-service` suite then ran 2285/2285.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and doctests for `vti-common` and `vta-service` all pass.

## Open question: retention vs. the spec

VTI-OPS-061 has no time limit, but a key is remembered for 24h. That is ample for SDK clients, which retry for about a minute. It is **shorter** than the push engine's horizon: `trust_task_push` re-sends under the same `idempotencyKey` until the push deadline, which is up to 30 days for a removal notice. A push still retrying after 24h is performed again by the receiving VTA. This PR does not change that; it is proposed as a follow-up issue and an Appendix F divergence entry.

body:
fix(idempotency)!: never re-run a keyed Trust Task whose earlier attempt died (#2409)

VTI-OPS-061 requires a node to perform a keyed operation at most once per
key. The dispatcher claims the key, the handler commits its effect, then
`record_outcome` marks the key done. Those are separate writes. A process
that died between the effect and the record left an in-flight claim, and
after the 10-minute grace `IdempotencyStore::claim` reclaimed it and ran the
handler again. The new restart test shows the result: a retry of
`keys/create` minted a second key (#2402).

A stale in-flight claim is now `ClaimOutcome::Abandoned { claimed_at }` and
is never reclaimed while its record lives. The VTA answers it with
`taskFailed` ("outcome unknown", `details.claimedAt`). The caller checks
whether the effect exists and uses a new key if it is still wanted. Inside
the grace a retry still gets `unavailable`. An expired record is claimed
afresh, as before.

A store error while claiming now answers `unavailable` rather than
dispatching unguarded. A keyed request run without its claim is one a
later retry can run again.

BREAKING CHANGE (vti-common): `ClaimOutcome` gains `Abandoned` and is now
`#[non_exhaustive]`; `claim` no longer reclaims a stale in-flight record.

Tests: `TestAppOptions::data_dir` lets a test build the VTA twice over one
retained store. The second app is built only after fjall has released the
first's directory lock, and the test asserts that release. Two
`vti_ops_061_*` tests cover:
- the same key on a fresh envelope after a restart, which converges on the
  first effect;
- the same key with a changed payload, which is refused;
- another key and no key, which still perform (the controls);
- an attempt interrupted after its effect, which is never re-run.
The last fails under the old reclaim rule.

Closes #2402

title: fix(vta): room profile padding converges instead of oscillating
body:
Fixes the flaky `a_curators_profile_is_accepted_and_padded_to_a_block`, which failed once on #2403.

**Cause.** `sign_padded` pads a signed room profile to a 1 KiB block and retries because the proof's length varies: a base58 Ed25519 signature is 88 characters about 80% of the time, otherwise shorter. Each retry aimed at the *last* length. After a short proof, that bet on the unlikely length again, and the loop could run out of its 8 attempts. Locally this failed about 1 run in 60.

**Fix.**
- Aim at the longest unpadded length seen so far, which is the common case.
- When the aim hasn't moved, add a whole block and keep it. Ed25519 is deterministic, so re-signing a body already tried would return the same short proof. A first attempt without this made the failure rate worse by cycling between two bodies.

**Verified.** 300 consecutive runs pass, and all 25 `room_profile` tests pass. Clippy is clean.

title: fix(vta-sdk): do not treat missing host-cleanup evidence as an empty failure list
body:
Closes #2404.

## Was schema validation of the details guaranteed?

**No.** `VtaError::Rejected.details` is carried exactly as received (`vta-sdk/src/client/mod.rs`, the rejection decode), and `trust_tasks_rs::DeclaredErrorCode` (what `vti_specs::schema_index::error_codes_for` returns) holds only `code` and `retryable`, not the `detailsSchema`. So the consumer has to check the details itself, and this PR adds that check.

## Change

- **SDK**: new `host_cleanup_refusal(&VtaError) -> Option<HostCleanupRefusal>`. `HostCleanupRefusal` is `#[non_exhaustive]`:
  - `Evidenced(Vec<HostCleanupFailure>)`: at least one entry, each with a non-empty `did` and `reason`, and `server` non-empty when present. Unknown members are ignored.
  - `Unreadable { why }`: the code matched but the details are absent, empty or malformed.
  - Only the exact declared code matches. A generic `taskFailed`, or a `Protocol` string, never does.
- **Compatibility**: purely additive. `host_cleanup_failures` keeps its signature but is `#[deprecated]` and now returns `None`, not `Some(vec![])`, for an unreadable refusal. A caller that relied on `Some(vec![])` gets the original error through its `None` arm.
- **CLI** (`cmd_context_delete`):
  - Only an `Evidenced` refusal reaches the existing render-and-prompt path. The separate confirmation is still required, and `--yes` never answers it.
  - An `Unreadable` refusal prints the reason and the plain retry command, never offers `--abandon-host-copies`, and returns the original error.
- **Related**: a success with `deleted: false` is now an error, not "Context deleted". The spec says a consumer MUST NOT report the deletion as done on the response status alone. The issue left this out of scope; it is a one-function fix, so it is included here.

## Tests

- `vta-sdk`: tests for each case:
  - well-formed details
  - an unknown member
  - absent details
  - an empty list
  - malformed entries: missing or empty `did`/`reason`, empty `server`, wrong types. The deprecated helper is checked against these too.
  - `taskFailed`, `notEmpty` and `Protocol` with matching text
- `vta-cli-common`: `deleted: false` is refused; `deleted: true` returns the orphans.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk -p vta-cli-common -p pnm-cli -p cnm-cli --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `vta-sdk` doctests all pass.
- Not tested: an end-to-end CLI run against a VTA sending malformed details. The CLI branches only on the SDK enum, and the SDK tests cover that enum.

title: feat(vetting): recover a lost hidden-vetting key, or follow an admin reset
body:
## What and why

A vetter whose VTA engine lost track of its hidden-vetting key was refused at enrolment with `pcs-root:identifierRebound`, and the desk told them to "vet from the install that enrolled first" — wrong since the key moved into the VTA, and with no way out: revoking and re-granting the vetter role at the VTC does not change the binding. Hit live on a community this week.

On `identifierRebound`, the client now:

1. Reads its own binding from the community (`vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1`, new query type, at most every 15 min, inside the existing community-silence backoff).
2. If the VTA engine's key differs, asks the VTA to restore the bound key (`vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1`, 90 s timeout) and re-enrols once.
3. If the VTA cannot find it (`notFound`), tells the vetter to ask a community admin for a reset (`pcs-binding/reset/0.1`, admin-only at the VTC), then follows the reset on the desk — "waiting for vetter/2026-10 to retire" → "open — enrolling now".
4. `heldInAnotherContext`, `memberMismatch`, `engineEnrolled` and an unreachable VTA each get their own words (R6.4). Bounded: a second refusal after a retry stops; `r` on the Hidden vetting desk checks again.

The bound identifier is held in memory only, never written to the book. The decision logic is a pure `decide()` in `openvtc-core/src/vetting/binding.rs`.

Specs: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1018 (merged, published). Service side (VTC show/reset, VTA recover): verifiable-trust-infrastructure PR to follow — until that's deployed, a service that doesn't know the new tasks refuses them; the client shows that refusal with its code and stops the check (not yet exercised against a live service).

## Checklist

- [x] No version edits
- [x] `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` clean
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — recover is idempotent (`recovered: false` on repeat); state is re-derived from the community on restart
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, generated from pinned specs (R3.*)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed (R5.*) — n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] No deviations from the guide

title: review: record reviewer and local hypothesis namespace
body:
## Purpose

Implements #29 and the 14 October 2026 task-force decision recorded during review of #23.

## What changed

- Require a non-empty top-level `reviewer` on specification review records.
- Define reviewer identity as assessment accountability, not risk-acceptance authority.
- Permit explicit example-local risk identifiers using `EX-RK-*` alongside canonical `RK-*` identifiers.
- Migrate the standalone TRQP hypotheses from `RK-AU01` / `RK-TM01` to `EX-RK-AU01` / `EX-RK-TM01`.
- Migrate all repository review examples, including negative fixtures and the subsequently merged VRC baseline/reassessment, to carry reviewer identity.
- Rebind the TRQP evidence sidecar to changed review/risk bytes and update its risk-reasoning keys.
- Rebind both VRC evidence sidecars to the exact reviewer-bearing review bytes; retain original specification source pins and assessment findings.
- Add a VRC-specific negative regression proving that absent reviewer identity fails closed.
- Add regression coverage for missing reviewer and explicitly selected example-local risks.
- Document compatibility implications in `review/README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Assurance / review questions

1. **Assurance layer:** RAHP assessment record contract.
2. **Evidence produced or validated:** schema validation, review-risk resolution, retained sidecar digest bindings and regression tests.
3. **Judgment enabled:** identify who is accountable for the review while preserving explicit local-vs-canonical risk provenance.
4. **Judgment deliberately avoided:** reviewer identity does not establish authority to accept residual risk.
5. **Affected semantics:** review record schema and example-local risk identifiers.
6. **Experimental scope:** `EX-RK-*` is for explicitly selected example-local hypotheses; it does not extend the canonical DTG corpus.
7. **Independent reproduction:** run the repository test suite, the minimal review validator and the standalone TRQP examination.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
python3 review/validate_spec_review.py review/examples/minimal-review.yaml
python3 review/validate_spec_review.py review/examples/standalone-trqp/review.yaml --risks review/examples/standalone-trqp/risks.yaml
python3 review/examine.py
python3 review/examples/vrc-v03/evaluate.py
python3 tools/validate_all.py --review review/examples/minimal-review.yaml
```

## Integration repair and verification

The earlier [failed RAHP validation run](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/39562535006) resulted from VRC baseline/reassessment records added by merged #33 not yet carrying mandatory `reviewer`. Consequently the VRC regressions aborted at schema validation rather than reaching source-integrity, reassessment or stale-observation assertions. Commit `595dccb5ab64e9db5a050ac63a4cc83267aad473` migrates these records and refreshes their evidence SHA-256 bindings. It adds a reviewer-omission negative regression without weakening the contract.

- [x] VRC baseline and reassessment carry an accountable reviewer and updated exact-byte evidence bindings.
- [x] Reviewer-omission negative regression is added.
- [x] Integrated repository CI passed on commit `595dccb5ab64e9db5a050ac63a4cc83267aad473`: [RAHP validation run 39718904079](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/39718904079).
- [ ] Independent reviewer and maintainer acceptance.

## Compatibility

This is compatibility-significant for consumers that validate review records without `reviewer`. Existing repository records are migrated in this PR. No risk-acceptance authority or canonical risk meaning is changed.

## Provenance

Prepared with AI assistance following the #23 review and task-force decisions.

title: feat(notifications)!: deposit to the VTA, a community's received notifications and relay decision, and four fixes (VTI-NTF-005, 034, 041, 047, 054 – 056, 070 – 074)
body:
Implements the merged notification follow-up: dtgwg-vti-spec #95 (VTI-NTF-005, 006, 025, 034, 041, 042, 047, 054 – 056, 061, 070 – 074; Appendix C.3 `vtc.notifications.read` / `vtc.notifications.relay`) over the tasks from dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1017.

## Pins
- `vta/notifications/deposit/0.1` (vti-specs-vta); `vtc/notifications/{list,show,relay}/0.1` (vti-specs-vtc). notify/relay 0.1 changed in prose only; their digests are unchanged.

## VTA: `vta/notifications/deposit/0.1` (VTI-NTF-054 – 056)
- Standing in `contextId` is checked before the document is read. Then `notAddressedHere` unless the document's `recipient` is a DID the VTA holds keys of in that context.
- Verification is the direct-delivery path: `verify_delivery` checks every layer, then `trust_tasks::admit_carried_document` applies the acceptance window, `expiresAt` and the same replay guard to the deposited document at the time of the hand-over. Any failure is `documentInvalid`.
- `receive` counts the delivering party (originator or last relayer), never the depositing client. The receipt is the same whatever was done, and a repeat answers the same receipt (retry class 2).
- SDK `TASK_VTA_NOTIFICATIONS_DEPOSIT_0_1` (RetrySafe), `notifications_deposit{,_json}`; `pnm notifications deposit <file|-> --context`; vta-mcp verb `deposit` (mutating).

## VTC: `vtc/notifications/{list,show,relay}/0.1` (VTI-NTF-070 – 074)
- New capabilities `vtc.notifications.read` and `vtc.notifications.relay`. The relay capability can be qualified `group:<id>`, which limits it to that group's members. Both are inside community-admin's ceiling and are non-conferring.
- `relay` selects all members, one group or one role. The selection is resolved once, at the decision, to active members. It excludes the community, the originator and every relayer in the chain, and it never relays to the same party twice.
- `relay` is refused until the disclosure is acknowledged.
- A relay to `allMembers` takes the requester's bound step-up (VTI-NTF-074 SHOULD). Group and role relays do not.
- Each decision is recorded before anything is sent and audited as the new `AuditEvent::NotificationRelayDecided`. It records the selection and the count, never the members reached.
- All five relay codes and `show:notificationUnknown` are driven through the spine (`tests/it/notifications_admin.rs`, witnessed in the error-code census). Conformance witnesses cover all three tasks.

## Fixes to #2397
- **VTI-NTF-041:** the 4th relay is now allowed (a received chain of at most three relays). It was refused at three.
- **VTI-NTF-047:** the community never relays to the originator, an earlier relayer or itself. This is checked at the decision and again for every later revision.
- **VTI-NTF-034:** an acknowledged network membership in the community's own record now counts; a listing it never acknowledged does not. An expired ACL entry no longer counts.
- **VTI-NTF-005:** the member-party election notice re-checks that the party is still an active member before every revision that offers the election. Withdrawals go regardless and keep the period (VTI-NTF-025).

## Console
- A Notifications page under Membership: the list, the detail view with the document as received, and "Relay to members" with a target radio group and the disclosure acknowledgement.
- Gated by the two capabilities. Both are registered in the role editor.

## Breaking
- `vtc_service::acl::Capability` gains two variants.
- `notifications::inbox::ReceivedNotification` replaces `relay_decided_by`/`relay_decided_at` with `relay_decisions`.
- `relay_to_members` is now `relay(.., &Selection, ..)`.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). The inbox lock covers store reads only; the relays are queued on the durable member push.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable (R2.1). The relay decision is recorded before queueing and re-driven by `inbox::settle`.
- [x] Every retry is bounded and backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Deposit and relay are retry class 2.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New wire types come from the generated `vti-specs` modules. `Selection` is `deny_unknown_fields` and camelCase (R3.*).
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*). A relay is refused with `unavailable` when no audit writer is configured.
- [x] Logs and status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] No deviations

title: feat(vetting): recover or reset a hidden-vetting key (vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/{show,reset}/0.1, vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1)
body:
## Why

A community running hidden vetting binds each vetter to one PCS identifier for good (`pcs-root/0.1`, `identifierRebound`). A vetter whose VTA engine lost track of its key — re-created engine record, restored VTA — was locked out of hidden vetting for as long as they stayed a member. Revoking and re-granting the vetter role does not touch the binding. A vetter hit exactly this in a live community.

## What

- **`vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/show/0.1`** — a member reads their own binding (`bound`, `id`, `enrolledLabels`) and the state of any reset (`waitingOn`, `open`). Membership is enough; a vetter grant is not required.
- **`vta/pcs/vetter/recover/0.1`** — the VTA searches the member-key paths it has allocated for the context, under every seed generation it holds, for the bound identifier, and restores it while the engine's current key holds nothing a community issued. Never searches another context; never selects a key another PCS engine holds (the identifier is a function of the key alone). Bounded; over the bound it searches nothing and answers `notFound`.
- **`vtc/vetting/vetters/pcs-binding/reset/0.1`** — administrator-only fallback when the key is gone. A new identifier is bound only once no label the old one enrolled under is live (evaluated at each enrolment request), and enrolling with the old identifier cancels the reset. Nothing can count twice.
- **`vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1`** gains `labelRetired`: once a member is re-bound, the labels the old identifier held never become live again, for any vetter.
- `pcs-root/0.1` (error meaning + a "A lost key" section, no wire change) and `vta/_shared/0.4/CONVENTIONS.md` §3 point at the new tasks.

Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

## Implementations

Built and tested against a local registry build of this branch; those PRs follow once this is published:

- VTI — VTC `pcs-binding/show` + `reset` (with admin console card), `labelRetired`, and the VTA's `vta/pcs/vetter/recover` through a new audited key-custody search door.
- OpenVTC — on `identifierRebound`, read the binding → recover → re-enrol; otherwise follow the reset on the vetting desk.

title: fix(extension): a community's context id is a lowercase slug the agent accepts
body:
Joining a community failed before anything was sent: "malformed request: validation error: context id must contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters and hyphens".

`communityContextId` kept the portal host's dots, so it produced `vtc-first.openvtc.net`. The VTA accepts a context id only as a lowercase slug: `a-z 0-9 -`, not starting or ending with `-` (`vta_support::contexts::validate_slug`, enforced since VTI #700). This PR turns dots into hyphens, giving `vtc-first-openvtc-net`, then `vtc-first-openvtc-net-2`, and so on. The agent never accepted a context id containing a dot, so no context made earlier changes name.

Tests and the README now use the slug form. Extension: `tsc` is clean and all 1,442 tests pass.

title: Add lists/1 and repudiates/1 (draft)
body:
These implement item 3 of [dtgwg-cred-spec discussion #82](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/discussions/82), option (b): a Verifiable Trust Network's listing is a statement, separate from the membership grant. The design points follow @geoffturk's and @bmiller59's comments there.

## `lists/1`

A VTN attests that it lists a community or network in its published set, under a named governance framework and version.

- **Statement, not grant.** Membership is a completed VMC pair beside the listing. Revoking the listing is delisting (VTI-VTN-053); revoking the grant ends membership. These are two separate acts.
- **Acknowledgement state is derived, never asserted.** The listing alone means unacknowledged. Listing plus a completed VMC pair means acknowledged. Listing plus `repudiates/1` means repudiated. This covers VTI-VTN-011, and the network cannot misstate the state.
- **`object.value` is `{ nodeType: "VTC" | "VTN", framework: { iri, version } }`.** It reuses the `nodeType` values (#53) instead of adding a second vocabulary, and carries the framework version that VTI-VTN-023 and VTI-REG-002 require.
- **Minimum issuer scope is `public`.** The profile leaves what a listing means at `directed` scope open until cred-spec #75 settles.
- **The profile recommends** that a VTN publish a listing for every party it admits.

## `repudiates/1` (generic)

The party a credential is about states that it does not accept that credential.

- The issuer is the repudiated credential's subject, the subject is that credential's issuer, and the object is its digest.
- First uses: a listed party repudiates a listing (VTI-VTN-012), or a member departs by repudiating its grant.
- The predicate is generic so that "a statement made about a party without its agreement" gets a single identifier, per admission criterion 5.

## Admission

- **Criterion 7:** both predicates are needed by a DTG specification, the VTI specification's VTN chapter. Implementations are in [OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network) and in VTI's `vti-vtn` crate (in progress). They currently use interim OpenVTC-namespace IRIs and will move to these.
- **Criteria 2–3:** both are unilateral and on the attests side.

`npm run check` passes.

title: feat(notifications): deposit to the VTA, the community's received notifications, and four fixes (#1017)
body:
feat(notifications): deposit to the VTA, the community's received notifications, and four fixes (#1017)

Follow-up to #1012, implementing dtgwg-vti-spec's Notifications follow-up
(VTI-NTF-006, 025, 034, 047, 054 – 056, 070 – 074).

New tasks:

- vta/notifications/deposit/0.1 — a client that receives a notify or relay
  for a DID whose keys its VTA holds (a persona DID whose mediator socket the
  client holds) hands the document to the VTA exactly as received. The VTA
  verifies it exactly as a direct delivery, counts for acceptance the party
  that delivered the document and never the depositing client, keeps one
  record per originator and notificationId, and answers with the same
  receipt whatever it did. Gated by standing in the context; retry class 2;
  notAddressedHere, documentInvalid.
- vtc/notifications/list/0.1, show/0.1 — a community's administrators read
  the notifications addressed to the community (vtc.notifications.read).
- vtc/notifications/relay/0.1 — an administrator's decision to relay one to
  all members, one group's or one role's (vtc.notifications.relay, qualified
  by group), refused until the disclosure is acknowledged; never to the
  community itself, the originator or any earlier relayer; later revisions
  follow without a further decision. destructive; retry class 2.

Fixes to notifications/notify/0.1 and notifications/relay/0.1, prose only
(no schema, error code or proof requirement changes):

- relay producer item 2 now agrees with consumer item 2: a relayer may relay
  only where its relay makes at most four relays in all.
- notification and relay proofs carry proofPurpose authentication with the
  operational key (VTI-KEY-081/082); examples updated from assertionMethod.
  VTI-KEY-107 applies to the relay received, not to forwarded layers.
- a withdrawal keeps the period of the revision it replaces.
- the originator re-checks VTI-NTF-005 for every revision it issues, except
  a withdrawal; election withdrawal covers an early close.
- a relayer never relays to the originator or an earlier relayer.

title: Notifications: hand-off to the VTA, a community's received notifications, and clarifications (VTI-NTF-005, 006, 025, 034, 041, 042, 047, 054 – 056, 061, 070 – 074)
body:
Follow-up to #91, from what the first implementation (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2397) found. The tasks are trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1017 (`vta/notifications/deposit/0.1`, `vtc/notifications/{list,show,relay}/0.1`, and prose fixes to `notifications/{notify,relay}/0.1`).

## Gaps closed

**Hand-off to the VTA (new VTI-NTF-054 – 056).** A notification addressed to a member's persona identifier arrives at whichever party holds that identifier's transport — usually the principal's client, since the mediator permits one connection per identifier — not at the VTA that holds its keys, context and acceptance policy. The client now MUST hand the document to the VTA exactly as received (`vta/notifications/deposit/0.1`), MUST NOT apply a policy of its own, and answers the sender itself with the same reply whatever the VTA does. The VTA verifies and holds it exactly as a direct delivery (022, 030 – 033, 042 unchanged); the relationship counted is the delivering party's, never the client's authority; OPS-024/026/027 and KEY-107 apply at the hand-over. Gated by authority in the context and by the document being addressed to an identifier the VTA holds keys of there.

**A community's received notifications (new VTI-NTF-070 – 074).** Administrators list and read what the community was told (`vtc.notifications.read`) and decide a relay (`vtc.notifications.relay`, qualified by group): recipients are all members, one group's, or one role's, resolved from the community's records at the decision, active members only, never the parties 047 excludes or those already reached; later joiners need a new decision; later revisions follow. The decision is refused without the 046 acknowledgement, audited without naming whom it reached, not authority-conferring, and MAY (SHOULD for all members) be held for step-up/consent. Capabilities added to Appendix C.3. Closes the chapter's open issue for a community; a group with its own identifier and a network remain open.

**Relay depth (VTI-NTF-041).** The producer rule now matches the recipient's: a relay may be made only where it makes at most four relays in all (relay received directly or through up to three).

## Clarifications

- **Proof purpose (new VTI-NTF-006):** `authentication`, operational key. A notification is a Trust Task request document (KEY-081) asserting no decision about anyone (KEY-082); recipients rely on authorship and integrity only. `assertionMethod` would put every notification behind the VTA-held attestation key for no checked property and invite reading it as the attestation 004 says it is not. KEY-107 gains one sentence: it applies to the document received; a document carried inside it as evidence (042) is governed by the carrying operation — otherwise 042's "no acceptance window on forwarded layers" contradicted it.
- **Withdrawal keeps the period (new VTI-NTF-025):** same `validFrom`/`validUntil` as the revision replaced, since the period bounds recipients' and relayers' retention.
- **Early close (VTI-NTF-061):** withdraw if cancelled or closed early before the stated close.
- **Standing re-checked (VTI-NTF-005):** at each document issued (every revision and every TRN-046 re-issue); a withdrawal goes to every earlier addressee regardless.
- **A VTC's acceptance (new VTI-NTF-034):** ACL entry; relationship credential in force; or a community/network the community is itself a member of, as its own record shows — never an unacknowledged listing (VTN-011).
- **No relay back (new VTI-NTF-047):** never to the originator, an earlier relayer, or itself (a relay received is a report that it relayed — 043).

Also: conformance note, STRUCTURE.md row.

Rendered locally with `npm run render`: no errors.

title: Notifications: deposit to the VTA, a community's received notifications, and clarifications (#95)
body:
Notifications: deposit to the VTA, a community's received notifications, and clarifications (#95)

Follow-up to #91.

- Hand-off to the VTA (VTI-NTF-054 – 056): a client holding the transport of
  an identifier whose keys the principal's VTA holds hands every notification
  and relay for it to the VTA exactly as received; the VTA verifies and holds
  it exactly as a direct delivery, counting the delivering party and never the
  client, with the same reply.
- A community's received notifications (VTI-NTF-070 – 074): administrators
  list and read them (`vtc.notifications.read`) and decide a relay to all
  members, one group's or one role's (`vtc.notifications.relay`, qualified by
  group), only after acknowledging the disclosure; audited without naming
  whom it reached. Closes the open issue on a community's administrator view;
  a group's or network's remains open.
- Relay depth (VTI-NTF-041): the producer and recipient bounds agree, at most
  four relays in all.
- Proof purpose (VTI-NTF-006): `authentication` with the operational key; a
  notification is not an attestation artefact. VTI-KEY-107 applies to the
  document received, not to a document carried in it as evidence.
- Withdrawal keeps the period it replaces (VTI-NTF-025); withdrawal on an
  early close (VTI-NTF-061); VTI-NTF-005 applied at each revision issued,
  except a withdrawal.
- A VTC's acceptance policy (VTI-NTF-034): an ACL entry, a relationship
  credential in force, or a membership the community itself holds as its own
  record shows; never an unacknowledged listing.
- A relayer never relays to the originator or an earlier relayer
  (VTI-NTF-047).

title: feat(vtc): a community's side of Verifiable Trust Network membership
body:
Stacked on the `vti-vtn` PR; merge that first.

## What and why

This PR implements `vtc/networks/*` 0.1 ([dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1014](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1014), pinned from trusttasks.org): the community's side of Verifiable Trust Network membership.

| Task | Does |
|---|---|
| `join` | Checks that the network at the admin's URL answers as the DID they named, and verifies its listing. Then registers the assigned groups for the network's roles (required roles first), signs the acknowledgement as the community, and verifies the grant (VTI-VTN-013). |
| `repudiate` | Rejects a listing (VTI-VTN-012) |
| `leave` | Departs by repudiating the grant (VTI-VTN-053) |
| `groups/register` | Registers a community group for a network role |
| `list`, `show` | The memberships, and the credentials that evidence each one |
| `evidence` | A member gets the registration and acceptance linking their group to a network, for a network room pass |

**Gating:**
- Every write needs `vtc.config.admin` and a step-up bound to the document, as for enabling a capability module. Each write makes the community sign a statement to a third party.
- Reads need `vtc.config.admin`.
- `evidence` answers only for groups the signer is an active member of.

**Relay** (`POST /v1/networks/relay/{group_id}`, governed, unauthenticated). The route verifies a network's broadcast envelope end to end:
- the origin's signature;
- the hop chain;
- that the last hop is signed by a network the community is an acknowledged member of, delivering to the group it registered there.

It drops repeats by message id, then pushes the envelope unchanged to the group's active members as `vtc/networks/notice/0.1`. A delivery that doesn't verify gets `403`, which the network treats as final.

**Also in this PR:**
- `LocalSigner::sign_authentication_doc`: the primary key, `authentication` purpose, no envelope.
- `AuditEvent::NetworkMembershipChanged` in `vti-common`, labelled in the console's audit panel.
- `docs/03-vtc/networks.md`.

**Not registered as a capability module yet.** Enabling a module projects it to the trust registry, which has no `vtn-membership` module. Until then, the tasks are gated by the ACL alone.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`networks::tests`): run against a fake network that checks every signature the community sends. Covers join (including the refusals), relay (delivery, duplicate, a non-member network, a misaddressed group), evidence (members only, and the link verifies as a room-pass chain link), leave, and repudiate.
- **Integration** (`tests/it/networks.rs`): drives all 14 declared error codes through the spine with a passkey step-up. These tests are witnessed in the error-code census.
- **Conformance** witnesses for all seven served tasks. The relay route is classified in `REST_EXCEPTIONS` and `GOVERNED_UNAUTH`. `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated; the admin UI typechecks.
- **Test helper fix:** `GatedAdmin`'s gesture now addresses its approval to the VTC's configured DID rather than always `TEST_VTC_DID`, so suites with their own community DID can use it.
- **Results:** `vtc-service` passes 2,176 unit and 1,372 integration tests. `cargo fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` are clean.

## Requirements

VTI-VTN-010 – 013, 032, 033, 053; VTI-APV-015 (bound step-up); VTI-KEY-022.

## Backport

none

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main` (stacked on the `vti-vtn` PR)
- [x] No `version =` edits
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

  (VTI-VTN-053); groups/register a group for a network role; list, show.

  verifies. Writes need vtc.config.admin and a step-up bound to the
  document; reads need vtc.config.admin.
- Relay: POST /v1/networks/relay/{group_id} takes a network's broadcast
  envelope, verifies it end to end (origin signature, hop chain, last hop
  by a network the community is a member of, to the group it registered
  there), drops repeats by message id, and pushes it unchanged to the
  group's active members as vtc/networks/notice/0.1. A delivery that does
  not verify is 403, which a network treats as final.
- evidence: a member gets the registration and acceptance linking a group
  they are in to a network, for a network room pass.

LocalSigner gains sign_authentication_doc (primary key, authentication
purpose, no envelope sealing) for signing in to a network. vti-common
gains AuditEvent::NetworkMembershipChanged. Not registered as a

title: feat(git-ns): the VTC speaks bridge job 0.7 and event 0.6
body:
Pairs with OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#195 (VGI 0.31.0). **The two deploy together**: after this lands the VTC sends jobs only to a bridge that lists `git-ns/bridge/job/0.7`, and serves `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.6 only.

Normative: `git-ns/bridge/job/0.7` and `git-ns/bridge/event/0.6` (trusttasks.org), *Changes from* sections and *Orphaned namespaces*.

## Changes
- **Pins** (`vti-specs-core`): `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.6 → 0.7, `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.5 → 0.6, fetched from the registry with `trust-tasks update`. The registry also republished `git-ns/bridge/job/list` 0.4 with a description-only change (its `JobKind` now names job 0.7), so that digest moves too.
- **Job 0.7**: the VTC sends 0.7 only, and only to a bridge that lists it (vgi-bridge v0.31.0+). It has no fallback to 0.6, because these are test deployments. The schema is the same as 0.6.
- **Event 0.6**: when `bindCompleted` carries `supersedes`, the VTC writes a `gitNs.namespace.superseded` audit entry (actor: the bridge; detail `{"supersedes":[…]}`). It restores nothing from those ids. The audit action is a free string, so vti-common is unchanged.
- **`unknownNamespace` vs `unavailable`**: the only place that sends `git-ns:unknownNamespace` to the bridge is the namespace lookup in `handle_event`, and I audited it. The VTC now answers `unknownNamespace` only when the namespace's record is absent. A snapshot read failure gets `unavailable`, and so does a record that exists but cannot be read, which the snapshot skips silently. `handle_result` also answers `unavailable`, not `unknownJob`, when it cannot read the job.

## Tests
- `the_bind_job_goes_out_as_job_0_7`, `every_job_goes_as_0_7_to_a_bridge_that_lists_it`, `a_bridge_that_lists_only_job_0_6_is_sent_nothing`
- `bind_completed_records_supersedes_in_the_audit_history_and_restores_nothing`, `bind_completed_without_supersedes_records_none`
- `an_event_for_a_namespace_whose_record_is_unreadable_is_unavailable` (also checks that a truly unknown namespace still gets `unknownNamespace`)
- `an_event_before_0_6_is_refused`

## Note
Open PR #2397 (feat/notifications) also edits the `vti-specs-core` `trust-tasks.toml`/`.lock` and vendored bundles. Whichever PR lands second will need a mechanical rebase of those files (re-run `trust-tasks -C vti-specs-core update`).

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.18` → `0.9.19` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vti-vtn): the Verifiable Trust Network protocol as a workspace crate
body:
## What and why

This adds a new crate, **`vti-vtn`**: the Verifiable Trust Network protocol, which both sides use. A VTN curates a nestable set of communities and networks (VTI-VTN-001 – 063). The crate covers:
- listings, membership offers and acknowledgements, and repudiation;
- the entry lifecycle and Bitstring Status Lists;
- the signed network index, DTG graph and directory;
- role/group registration (`servesRole` / `groupRegistered`);
- signed broadcast envelopes and hop chains;
- network room passes.

**Why here.** `vtc-service` needs it to act as a network member (the next PR). The VTN service ([OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-network)) will depend on it from crates.io. That keeps dependencies one-way: the VTN repo depends on VTI, never the reverse.

**What changed from the VTN repo's `vtn-core` / `vtn-client`:**
- **Proof sets.** Verification accepts a proof set, which is how a VTC holding an ML-DSA key alongside its Ed25519 key signs. Every proof must come from a key of the expected signer, carry the expected purpose, and verify; at least one is required. `dtg-credentials`' `DTGCredential` carries a single proof, so the claims are parsed with the proof set split off. Covered by `tests/proof_sets.rs` (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-44; a foreign key or the wrong purpose fails the set).
- **`Party` trait.** Anything signing as a DID implements it, and `Identity` is the local implementation. The member-side builders come in unsigned forms (`member::acknowledgement`, `member::repudiation`, `groups::registration`) and `*_as` forms that take any `Party`, so a service signs through its own multi-key signer.
- **Feature `client`** (reqwest): `VtnClient`, whose DID sign-in is bound to the expected network DID; `vtn-signin:` links; and a `StatusChecker`.

The VTN profile predicates still use the interim `https://openvtc.org/vtn/vsc/` namespace. They move to the DTG registry's `lists/1` / `repudiates/1` once [dtgwg-vsc-registry#33](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry/pull/33) lands (decided in [dtgwg-cred-spec discussion #82](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/discussions/82)).

**Docs.** `CLAUDE.md` has a crate-table entry, and `RELEASING.md` lists the crate as published (27 of 36).

## Requirements

VTI-VTN-010 – 013, 030 – 033, 053; VTI-KEY-022 (purpose-checked key resolution).

## Backport

none

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in an existing `Cargo.toml`. The new crate starts at `0.1.0`.
- [x] Tests cover the change: 22 unit and integration tests. `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

**Note:** `cargo deny` fails on `main` today on RUSTSEC-2026-0429 (`zip`, via `nitro_attest`'s build script). That is unrelated to this change and left until `nitro_attest` moves to a fixed `zip`.

title: feat(notifications)!: notify/relay, the VTA's held notifications and the election notice (VTI-NTF-001 – 063)
body:
Implements the **Notifications** chapter of the VTI specification (dtgwg-vti-spec #91, VTI-NTF-001 – 063, Appendix G kind `election`) over the tasks of dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1012, pinned with the `trust-tasks` CLI: `notifications/notify/0.1`, `notifications/relay/0.1` (vti-specs-core) and `vta/notifications/{list,show,dismiss}/0.1` (vti-specs-vta).

## What

- **vta-sdk** — `notifications::verify_delivery` → `VerifiedDelivery` (typestate): every layer's type and pinned schema, each proof verified over the JSON as received as its own `issuer`, each forwarded document addressed to the relay carrying it, ≤ 4 relays, `relayable` honoured (VTI-NTF-042). `TASK_*` constants; `retry_safety` (notify/relay/dismiss `RetrySafe`, list/show `ReadOnly`); typed + `_json` client methods for list/show/dismiss.
- **VTA (recipient)** — notify/relay dispatch as counterparty tasks (zero-authority claim for a sender the ACL does not know). Stated acceptance policy (`[notifications]`): ACL entry, issuer of a membership credential or party of a relationship credential held in the context, `accept_from`, `accept_any`; a relay counts the delivering relayer, never the originator (VTI-NTF-030/031). One record per (addressee, originator identity, `notificationId`), higher revision replaces and keeps a dismissal (VTI-NTF-022); same receipt whatever happened (VTI-NTF-023); bounds per originator/deliverer (VTI-NTF-033). New `notifications` keyspace, **backed up**; reads gated by context standing (VTI-NTF-050 – 052); lapsed/withdrawn records swept after `retain_lapsed_days` (default 30).
- **VTC (originator, `election`)** — an election under a credential roll naming a member party is notified to that party once registered, and withdrawn by a higher revision if cancelled or closed before voting closes (VTI-NTF-060/061). The notice row is written before anything is sent; the election sweeper is its one sender, through the durable member push (TSP > DIDComm > REST, with escalation).
- **VTC (recipient + relayer)** — notify/relay on the open door, verified and held by the VTC's stated policy (ACL entry, or a relationship in force with the community DID) in its own backed-up `notifications` keyspace. Relay engine: refuses a decision that has not acknowledged what the relay discloses (VTI-NTF-046), relays the document exactly as received to each member, remembers whom it relayed to until the period ends (30 days without one), and relays every later revision — withdrawals included — to them (VTI-NTF-044).
- **pnm** — `pnm notifications list|show|dismiss`.

## Not in this PR

- No remote surface (console page / task) for a VTC administrator to list received notifications and decide a relay: the specification defines no administrator task for it (chapter's third open issue), and a new remote op needs an upstream spec first. The engine (`notifications::inbox::{list, disclosure, relay_to_members}`) is in place for it.

## Breaking

`vta_config::AppConfig` gains `notifications`; both services' `AppState` gain `notifications_ks`.

Tests: `vti_ntf_0xx_*` in `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/notifications_tests.rs` and `vtc-service/src/notifications/`.

body:
feat(bridge): orphaned namespaces and re-binding an owner (git-ns bridge event 0.6, job 0.7) (#193)

Move the bridge to git-ns/bridge/event 0.6 and job 0.7, with bundles
built from the unreleased specification (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1015).

- A verified git-ns:unknownNamespace answer from the VTC, threaded to an
  event the bridge sent naming the namespace, orphans it. While orphaned the
  bridge changes nothing on the forge, fails the check it posts, sends no
  event and drops queued ones, and keeps its forge-side state.
- A job naming an orphaned namespace binds it again, and its role map is
  reported.
- vgi-bridge namespace list|forget; orphan_retention_days (default 30, at
  least 30) with a sweep from the maintenance tick and daily warnings in
  the last week. Never orphaned or removed for being quiet.
- A beginBind for an owner already held under another id needs fresh proof
  (on GitHub the setup_action=update redirect with this job's state); on
  completion the forge-side state moves to the new id, the earlier ids are
  retired (answered unknownNamespace, never reused) and named in
  bindCompleted.supersedes. No governance carries over.

title: fix(bridge): connect to the mediator before restoring or starting anything else
body:
At start the bridge restored (outbox resend, role-map reports) and started its background loops, grant check and HTTP server before the mediator session was up, so the first sends failed with `not connected to the mediator` and the one-shot `git.commit.sign` grant check never ran.

- The bridge now waits for the first mediator session (connected, VTC offered a TSP relationship) before `restore()`, the GitHub App registration offer, the background loops, the VTA key refresh and the HTTP server.
- The first session serves no inbound documents until the restore has finished; the restore does that session's link-up. Later reconnects link up as before.
- A shutdown signal while waiting for the mediator stops cleanly.

Trade-off: with the mediator down at boot the HTTP server (webhooks) is not up either; GitHub redelivers.

title: feat(git-ns): bridge event 0.6 and job 0.7 — orphaned namespaces, and binding an owner again
body:
- **Orphaned namespaces (event 0.6).** A VTC's signed `git-ns:unknownNamespace` answer to an event orphans the namespace on the bridge: no forge changes, bridge-posted checks fail, no events (role-map reports included), forge-side state kept. Operators can list and remove orphaned namespaces; the bridge may remove them itself after a configurable retention period (at least 30 days). A job from the VTC naming the namespace returns it to bound. Inactivity alone never orphans or removes a namespace.
- **A VTC answers `unknownNamespace` only when it does not have the namespace**, and `unavailable` when it cannot read its records, since the bridge now acts on the answer.
- **`bindCompleted` may carry `supersedes`**: earlier namespace ids whose forge-side state the new binding took over. Audit only; nothing is restored from them.
- **Binding an owner again (job 0.7).** A `beginBind` for an owner the bridge already holds under another id needs the forge-side proof afresh (on GitHub, confirming the existing installation from the job's URL, nonce checked). On completion the new namespace takes over the forge-side state and the earlier ids are retired; no governance carries over. The bridge never re-creates a namespace at the VTC on its own.
- Current specs that linked job 0.6 / event 0.5 now point at the new versions; the four libraries are regenerated.

The VGI bridge implementation follows in verifiable-git-infrastructure.

title: feat(demo): interactive hidden-vetting walkthrough for a cryptographer audience
body:
## What

A paged, narrated walkthrough of hidden-vetter admission, `demo/examples/walkthrough.rs`, built for presenting to cryptographers.

```sh
cargo run -p pcs-vetting-prototype --release --example walkthrough
```

Enter goes to the next stage, `b` goes back, a number jumps to that stage, and `q` quits. `--auto` prints every stage at once.

There are 15 stages, grouped by a breadcrumb into Intro › Setup › Enrolment › Vetting › Admission › Privacy › Abuse › Withdrawal › Summary:

- **Setup:** pp, digest(pp), c₀, hvk with its well-formedness check, and the AllowList policy.
- **Enrolment:** the root request (C, T₀, π_root), PS blind issuance and unblinding, with the pairing equation checked live. Also the token drip under a separate key, tvk.
- **Vetting:** the applicant's fresh key and s = H₀(id), the attestation (T_j, cred\*_j, φ_j, π_j) with R_att and ctx_j written out, and the checks the applicant runs on receipt, including that tampering with the metadata breaks π_j.
- **Admission:** proofs for k = 1 (`requestMore`) and k = 2 (admitted). Then the submission in its wire form, the same JSON as `vti-vetting-pcs::wire::SubmissionWire`, with `proof` decoded byte by byte.
- **Privacy, Abuse, Withdrawal:** what the VTC learns, tag unlinkability across applicants, a token double-spend, and withdrawal by tag.
- **Summary:** which assumption each property rests on, and caveats.

Every group element on the wire is printed. The PS pairing checks, Tag_DDH evaluations and T₀ are recomputed live from the values shown. All stages are computed up front from a fixed seed, so the run is the same every time and going back is free.

## Engine changes (demo crate only)

Doc-hidden hooks the walkthrough needs:
- `enroll_traced` and `drip_traced` return what went over the wire.
- `usk_scalar` and `credential` expose secrets so the live checks can be shown.

`enroll` and `drip` now call the traced versions and behave as before.

## Checked

- All 23 live checks in the walkthrough pass.
- `cargo test -p pcs-vetting-prototype --release` passes all 14 tests.
- `cargo clippy --examples` reports nothing.
- The library itself is untouched, and `demo/` stays out of CI.
