title: Show an election put to a member party's members only to a reader who presents that membership (VTI-VOT-015, VTI-VOT-016, VTI-VOT-090)
body:
**The problem.** #88 added the credential roll. An election whose roll names a **member party** — another community, a group of another community, or a network that is itself a member of the community — concerns people the community holds no record of. Nothing in the chapter said who may read an election, and the Trust Tasks as merged (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1008, `vtc/elections/show/0.4` and `list/0.4`) showed such an election to any caller. Its title, questions and options were public.

**The change.**

- **VTI-VOT-015** (new): a VTC shows an election, or confirms that it exists, only to:
  - a holder of `vtc.elections.manage`; or
  - under the first three roll rules, a party the roll admits by the community's records; or
  - under a credential roll naming the community or one of its groups, its active members (and, for a group, the group's members); or
  - under a credential roll naming a member party, either that party itself (by its own active membership) or a reader who **presents their membership credential for that party in the read**. The presentation is bound to that read and checked as VTI-VOT-025 checks a ticket request's.

  Anyone else gets the same answer as for an election that does not exist. An indeterminate check gets that answer too.

  A list never asks for a presentation. It never includes a member-party election, **not even its identifier**, for anyone except the party itself and administrators. A presentation is not retained and is accepted once per read (VTI-CRD-022, VTI-CRD-042).
- **VTI-VOT-016** (new): a member's agent presents a credential in a read only by the member's choice, and binds it to that read alone.
- **VTI-VOT-090** (amended): the published statement says that reading such an election already shows the community the member's membership of the party, before they have seen the election.
- The registrar row of the party table now covers the read. So does the open issue on the registrar learning a foreign membership.

**Stub or no stub.** The requirement omits even a stub (`electionId`, `memberOf`, schedule) from lists. The rationale records the trade-off:
- **What a stub would cost.** A list proves nothing about its reader, so a stub would go to the world. It would publish that the election exists, its schedule and its identifier (which a community may make descriptive). It would also publish that the named party is a member of the community, which that party's directory listing may hide (VTI-DIR-040).
- **What omitting it costs.** Discovery. The party's members learn of the election from the party, which the list does show it to and which alone holds its roster, or from a link. They have no relationship with the community, so they had to learn of it from outside in any case.

**Not changed.** Visibility of elections under `members` / `membersAndListed` / `listed`, and under a credential roll naming the community or one of its groups. The ticket-claim checks (VTI-VOT-021 – 028).

No divergence-register entry: no implementation claims the rule yet.

The Trust Task change follows in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf: `vtc/elections/show/0.5` (optional `presentation`), `vtc/elections/list/0.5` (prose), `vta/pcs/voter/read/0.5` (the VTA presents the member's chosen credential).

`npm run render` passes locally.

title: feat(voting): a credential roll, proven when the ticket is claimed (voting/_shared/0.4, vtc/elections/tickets/issue/0.2)
body:
Follows trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#88, which adds a **credential roll**: a ticket goes to whoever holds a membership credential for the one DID the manifest names. That DID is the community, one of its groups, or a party that is itself an active member of the community, holding a VMC the community issued it: another community, a group of another community, or a network. Registry recognition is not membership. Eligibility is proven by a presentation when the party claims its ticket, and is never resolved when the election is created (VTI-VOT-021, VTI-VOT-025 – 028, VTI-VOT-090).

**Shared definitions: `voting/_shared/0.4`.** This is `0.3` with these changes:
- `RollRule.rule` appends `credential`, at the end of the enum.
- New `RollRule.memberOf`: a DID (`^did:[a-z0-9]+:\S+$`).
- `dependentSchemas` enforces that `memberOf` is required with `credential`, refused with every other rule, and that `listed` is refused with `credential`. I used `dependentSchemas` rather than `if`/`then`, because typify panics on `if`/`then`/`else`, and `oneOf`/`anyOf` turns `RollRule` into an enum of variants. With `dependentSchemas` all four generators keep `RollRule` a struct with an optional `memberOf`, and the runtime validators still enforce the rule. The negative examples prove it.
- `Disclosure` gains an optional `rollCredential` (`RollCredentialDisclosure`): `memberOf`, `memberOfKind` (`thisCommunity` | `communityGroup` | `memberParty`), an optional `memberOfName`, and `presenterDisclosed: true`.
- `CONVENTIONS.md` gains a *Credential roll* term and updates its authorization table.

**New task versions:**

| Task | New version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `voting/election/register` | 0.4 | request `manifest` |
| `voting/election/show` | 0.4 | response `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/deal` | 0.5 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/enrol` | 0.4 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/justify` | 0.5 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/keys` | 0.5 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/vote` | 0.4 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/vote-encrypted` | 0.5 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/voter/register` | 0.4 | request `manifest`. Also an optional `membershipCredential` (a vault handle): with `member`, the engine presents that credential inside the `ticketDocument` it signs, bound to that document and the community. `ticketDocument` is now `tickets/issue/0.2`. Two new codes: `membershipCredentialRequired`, `membershipCredentialUnusable` |
| `vtc/elections/create` | 0.5 | request `manifest`. New Conformance item 6 checks that `memberOf` is the community, one of its groups, or an active member of it (VTI-VOT-026). New code: `rollUntrusted`. Adds a credential-roll example and four invalid examples |
| `vtc/elections/show` | 0.4 | response `manifest` and `disclosure`, which carries `rollCredential` under a credential roll. Who sees a credential-roll election |
| `vtc/elections/list` | 0.4 (`extends: "0.3"`) | prose only: who sees a credential-roll election |
| `vtc/elections/tickets/issue` | 0.2 (`extends: "0.1"`) | optional `presentation` (a DI VP or an SD-JWT, with `nonce` = the document `id` and `domain`/`aud` = the community, as in `vtc/directory/card/present`). It is required under `credential` and refused (`malformedRequest`) under other rules. Conformance items 5, 6, 10 and 11 cover the checks, the dedup key and retention. Appended codes: `presentationRequired`, `membershipNotProven` (`details.reason`), `membershipRevoked`, `rollUntrusted`, `membershipIndeterminate` (retryable). `maxDocumentBytes.request` 98304 |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/read` | 0.4 | the signed `election` read names `voting/election/show/0.4` |
| `vta/pcs/voter/read` | 0.4 | the signed reads name `vtc/elections/list/0.4` and `vtc/elections/show/0.4` |

`voting/board/read/0.2` does not reach `Manifest` (the same reasoning as #1002), so it keeps its version. `vta/pcs/voter/accept/0.1` names `tickets/issue/0.1` only in a description. `tickets/issue/0.2` declares `extends: "0.1"`, so that reference stays current and `accept` keeps its version.

**Claim-time checks (`tickets/issue/0.2`, item 5), in order:**
1. A presentation is present.
2. `memberOf` is still trusted. For a member party, its own membership of the community must be active now, in the community's records and by the status of the VMC the community issued it; if it has lapsed or been revoked, the claim fails with `rollUntrusted`.
3. The proof verifies and is bound to this document; the holder and subject are the signer; the issuer is `memberOf`; for one of the community's own groups, the community's authorization credential to the group verifies; and the credential is valid now.
4. Neither the credential nor any authorization credential behind it is revoked or suspended, by status list or the issuer's trust registry. A group membership credential has no status, so it is checked by its expiry (VTI-DIR-085).
5. For the community or its groups, the community's own records agree.

**One ticket per participant (item 6, VTI-VOT-027).** The ticket is held against the credential subject, never against `memberOf`. For the community or its groups, it is held against the member record, so it follows rotation (VTI-MEM-041). For a member party, it is held against the subject DID.

- `npm run build-bundles` + `check-bundles`
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: 13 released files changed, all additively. These are prose-only stale-reference rewrites from `npm run fix-stale-references`.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features validate,voting,vtc,vta,vault --test conformance`: 1642 passed.
- `go vet` on the affected packages.
- `dart analyze --fatal-infos` on the affected libraries.

All four libraries are regenerated. The TS `tsc` / `npm test`, clippy and full-workspace builds are left to CI.

title: Let an election's roll be the holders of a membership credential for one DID — the community, its group, or a member party — proven when the ticket is claimed (VTI-VOT-021, VTI-VOT-022, VTI-VOT-025 – VTI-VOT-028, VTI-VOT-090, VTI-DIR-087)
body:
**The problem.** A roll can be a community's own members, a list of DIDs, or both. A community cannot put a question to the members of one of its groups, of a partner community or of a network, because it does not hold their roster and should not copy it.

**The change.** A fourth roll rule, a **credential roll**, admits whoever holds a membership credential for the one DID the manifest names. That DID is the community, one of its groups, or a party that is itself an active member of the community: another community, a group of another community, or a network. Eligibility is checked only when a party claims its ticket, from a presentation of that credential, and never when the election is created. So a member who joins after the election is called can vote, and a member removed in the meantime cannot.

**Requirements:**
- **VTI-VOT-021** (amended): the fourth rule. Under it, eligibility comes from the presentation, checked as VTI-VOT-025 requires.
- **VTI-VOT-022** (amended): a credential-roll issuance is recorded against the party VTI-VOT-027 names. Issuance records follow a member's identifier when it is rotated (VTI-MEM-041), so rotation never yields a second ticket.
- **VTI-VOT-025** (new): the checks made when a ticket is claimed:
  - the presentation is made by the credential's subject and satisfies VTI-CRD-020 – 022, with the community as its audience;
  - the proof verifies, and the issuer is the DID the roll names (for a group, the community's authorization credential to the group also verifies, VTI-DIR-083/086);
  - the credential is valid at that time, and the signer is its subject;
  - the credential and any authorization credential behind it are not revoked or suspended, by their status at that time;
  - for a party outside the community, that party's own membership of the community is still active and unrevoked, by the community's records and the status of the VMC it issued that party (VTI-VOT-026);
  - for the community or its groups, the community's own records show the subject as an active member (and group member).

  If a status list or registry cannot be reached, the outcome is indeterminate and no ticket is issued. The presentation is not retained.
- **VTI-VOT-026** (new): the roll names exactly one DID. It must be the community, one of its groups, or a party that is itself an active member of the community, holding a VMC the community issued it. For example, VTC A can name Group B of VTC B only if Group B's DID holds an active VMC from A. Registry recognition (VTI-REG-020) is not membership. Any other DID is refused at creation, and the outside party's membership is checked again at every claim. A roll admits the holders of the named party's own credentials, never the members of parties that party lists in turn (VTI-REG-024, VTI-VTN-022).
- **VTI-VOT-027** (new): the limit is one ticket per credential subject, never one per roll DID. For the community or its groups, the issuance is held against the member, so it survives rotation. For any other party, it is held against the subject's DID.
- **VTI-VOT-028** (new): the roll's size is not known, and no size is stated. Turnout is counted ballots against tickets issued (VTI-VOT-072).
- **VTI-VOT-090** (amended): the disclosure names the DID, what it is to the community (the community itself, one of its groups, or a member party), and that claiming a ticket shows the community the member's membership of it.
- **VTI-DIR-087** (amended): deciding ticket eligibility under a roll naming a group is not authority. The VTC verifies the group credential as an outside verifier would, and checks its own records as well.
- The registrar row of the chapter's party table now says what it learns under a credential roll.

**Open issues (non-normative), added to the chapter:**
- The registrar learns the requester's membership of a foreign party. A PCS predicate proof under a per-election pseudonym could avoid this. That is future work and is not specified here.
- The registrar cannot follow a rotation of the subject's DID at a foreign issuer. The count stays bounded by tickets issued (VTI-VOT-072), but one ticket per party then depends on the issuer's credentials carrying a DID that survives rotation, which nothing requires yet.

The existing `members`, `listed` and `membersAndListed` rules are unchanged. There is no divergence-register entry, because no implementation claims the rule yet.

The Trust Task schema change follows in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf:
- `voting/_shared/0.4` appends `credential` to the roll rule and adds `roll.memberOf` and a disclosure of it;
- every task carrying the manifest gets a new version;
- `vtc/elections/tickets/issue/0.2` carries the membership presentation, with new error codes;
- `vta/pcs/voter/register/0.4` lets the member's VTA attach its credential from the vault.

* Trust a roll's outside party only as a member of the community, not by recognition (VTI-VOT-025, VTI-VOT-026)

A credential roll may name the community, one of its groups, or a party that
itself holds an active membership credential the community issued it (another
community, a group of one, a network). Registry recognition is not enough.
The claim fails if that party's membership has lapsed or been revoked.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(validation): fail closed on missing schema dependency (Increment 4)
body:
## Increment 4 of #17 — validation closure and current-main reconciliation

### Problem

The corpus validator previously treated a missing `jsonschema` dependency as a warning and recorded schema validation as skipped/successful. That permits incomplete validation to appear complete.

The earlier version of this PR was stacked on #21 and referred to #14 as pending. Both dependencies are now merged. This branch has therefore been rebuilt as one signed-off commit on current `main`, containing only the remaining Increment 4 delta.

### Change

- Make `tools/validate.py` fail nonzero when `jsonschema` is unavailable.
- Add a focused negative regression that simulates only the missing schema dependency and proves that no PASS/skipped result is emitted.
- Extend the accepted #14 validation workflow to execute and retain:
  - composed corpus + explicitly selected review validation;
  - the retained-source TRQP examination;
  - existing corpus, regression, review and build evidence.
- Extend the workflow summary so corpus, regressions, review record, composed validation, TRQP examination and build outcomes remain individually visible.
- Update review documentation to describe the accepted CI/evidence path.

### Reconciliation against current upstream baseline (22 October 2026)

The PR branch has now integrated current `main` (`448e2ff4ca7f747ca899e0e845adfe45f750f094`) through DCO-signed merge commit `bbe06e3269a6330b64c52ce54ede4e74522ca292`. GitHub reports the PR mergeable, with no commits behind `main`. The intervening upstream work includes the accepted VRC v0.3 reassessment example (#33) and its documentation; the current PR remains limited to fail-closed corpus validation, CI execution/reporting, one negative regression and review documentation. The later `main` changes add material to `review/README.md`, so the eventual merge must retain both the VRC section and this PR's Increment 4 section. No credential-renewal or method-corpus change belongs in this PR.

The newly opened [upstream #37](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/37) (credential lifecycle authority/non-inheritance) and [upstream #38](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/38) (control-induced harms) are **separate research/corpus/method tracks** arising from [HTX Discussion #22](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-htx-tf/discussions/22). They neither block nor expand this Increment 4 validation repair. [Downstream #1106](https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/issues/1106) and [#1089](https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/issues/1089) remain separate downstream investigations.

### Assurance boundary

This establishes fail-closed repository validation and reproducible execution evidence. It does not establish target assurance, risk acceptance or independent human review.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Missing schema-validation dependencies cannot produce a misleading complete-validation result.
- [x] Failed, skipped and incomplete checks remain distinguishable in implementation and workflow reporting.
- [x] Relevant checks are wired into the accepted repository CI workflow.
- [x] CI output distinguishes repository integrity/reproduction from target assurance.
- [x] Reproduction commands and evidence retention are documented.
- [x] Current-head GitHub Actions execution succeeds and retained evidence is produced.
- [x] EasyCLA/contribution checks pass on the current head.
- [ ] Independent review and maintainer acceptance.
- [x] Final integration with current `main` preserves VRC reassessment documentation and has green RAHP validation on the integration head ([run 39718048319](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/39718048319)); EasyCLA is successful. Independent review and maintainer acceptance remain open.

### Reproduction

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 tools/validate.py --json
python3 tools/validate_all.py --review review/examples/minimal-review.yaml
python3 review/examine.py
```

The negative dependency case is included in normal test discovery through `tests/test_schema_dependency.py`.

### Observed CI evidence

The previous head `7c535c9a4f1bc1176dd88f7ca30884e359d7b269` passed [RAHP validation run `39522197711`](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/39522197711). The **integrated head** `bbe06e3269a6330b64c52ce54ede4e74522ca292` subsequently passed [RAHP validation run `39718048319`](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/39718048319). EasyCLA is successful on the integrated head.

Observed successful steps include dependency installation, corpus validation, repository/regression tests, the worked review record, composed validation, the retained-source TRQP examination, temporary build, generated-file binding, result summarization and evidence upload.

Retained artifact: `rahp-validation-39522197711-1` (artifact ID `12311850790`), digest `sha256:dc5d480b1a09ed3f578c01ecf069a2a565d42eed1e29ecfd43d93f3831a6300e`, retained through 4 November 2026.

EasyCLA is successful on the same head. Independent review and maintainer acceptance remain outstanding.

### Compatibility

No corpus semantics, warning thresholds, review schema or target-assurance semantics change. Environments that previously ran `tools/validate.py` without `jsonschema` must install the declared repository dependencies before validation can succeed. This is intentional fail-closed behavior.

### Provenance

Prepared with AI assistance for #17 Increment 4 and reconciled after #14, #19, #20 and #21 were accepted upstream.

title: Add Explore 03: put a GitHub organization under the VTC with the VGI bridge
body:
A third explore page: put a GitHub organization under the VTC with the VGI bridge, so a repository shows up in the admin console's Repos page and the member portal, and members hold rights to it. It was written from a run on an explore box set up by Explore 01 and 02 (the 2026-10-22 nightly), in the same shape as the walkthrough: a "Verified with" table, IDs to save, numbered steps with an expected result each, a members section, a verification list, and Known Issues.

- **Ten steps:** a check that the installed `cnm` is the server build, the `cnm` identity and its offline ACL grant, the bridge tarball with its checksum, the Nginx site and certificate, `vgi-bridge setup` with the `pnm` handoff and a systemd unit, the VTC `bridges` entry, GitHub App registration and Device Flow, bind and install, a passkey for the `cnm` identity, adopt, and grants.
- **Members:** link a GitHub account, set up `did-git-sign`, clone, and what the Verified badge needs.
- **Known Issues:** the keyring `cnm`, the step-up link printed on the API base (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2267), the `did-git-sign` credential missing from the VTA ACL, an empty repository's first branch becoming the protected default, and a registry started before the VTA.
- **Server Setup:** Step 5 installs `cnm-server` beside `pnm-server`, in both download channels and in the Option B source build, so Explore 03 finds the config-session `cnm` already on the box.
- **Index and walkthrough:** `sysop/explore/README.md` lists the page as item 3, and Explore 02 gains a Next section pointing to it.

One gap the page states openly: the mediator and Trust Registry versions are given only as the same day's nightly, since neither reports one on the box.

This PR waits for the build pipeline to publish `cnm-server` (ic3software/devops#150); the `cnm-server/nightly/cnm` path answers 404 until the next nightly has run.

title: Add Explore 03: put a GitHub organization under the VTC with the VGI bridge (#59)
body:
Add Explore 03: put a GitHub organization under the VTC with the VGI bridge (#59)

* Add Explore 03: put a GitHub organization under the VTC with the VGI bridge

A new explore page after the walkthrough: build the config-session cnm, give it a community-administrator identity, install and set up vgi-bridge in VTA mode behind Nginx, point the VTC at it, register the GitHub App, bind the organization, give the cnm identity a passkey for single-administrator self-grants, adopt a repository, grant rights, and what members do in OpenVTC to link, clone and sign. Verified on the 2026-10-22 nightly with vgi-bridge 0.20.0. The Known Issues section records what bit during that run: the keyring cnm build, the step-up link carrying /v1 (fixed in verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2267), a did-git-sign credential missing from the VTA's ACL, an empty repository's first branch becoming the protected default, and a registry started before the VTA.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

* Explore 03: install cnm-server from the download server

The devops build pipeline now publishes the config-session build of cnm as
cnm-server, next to pnm-server (ic3software/devops#150). Step 1 downloads
it the way Server Setup downloads the rest of the stack, with the same
no-checksum caveat, and keeps the source build only as the fallback for a
box that asks before the next nightly has run. The Verified-with note says
the run itself used a source build of the same nightly commit.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

* Install cnm-server in Server Setup, and have Explore 03 only check it

Explore 01's Step 5 now installs cnm-server beside pnm-server, in both
download channels and in the Option B source build, so the box has the
config-session cnm whether it was built or downloaded. Explore 03's Step 1
drops its own download and source-build instructions and the 404 fallback,
and only checks that the installed cnm is the server build; its Known
Issues entry points back to Server Setup.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

* Explore 03: add an "Upgrading the bridge" section

The bridge is released often, mostly to track the VTA, the mediator and
the VTC's Trust Task versions, so a bridge left on an older release stops
working against a newer stack. The new section walks an in-place upgrade:
download and verify the release tarball, stop the service and swap the
binary keeping the old one for rollback, move the verify-trust pin in
bridge.toml (setup pins it to its own release and nothing updates it),
start again and check after a short wait, with what the log should show.
It also notes that repositories bootstrapped under the old pin keep the
old workflow until the VTC resends their bootstrap job.

A Known Issues entry maps the minute-by-minute "TSP revision mismatch"
warning, which a 0.20.0 bridge logs once the mediator speaks TSP 1.0, to
that section. Verified upgrading 0.20.0 to 0.30.0 on 2026-11-02.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

* Explore 03: the verify-trust pin changes nothing under the bridge-posted check

The upgrade section said to have the VTC resend a repository's bootstrap
job after moving the pin, but on this page's Free-plan setup the guard is
the check the bridge posts itself, so no repository carries a workflow to
refresh. Say so, name the guards where the pin does matter, and be honest
that no cnm command sends a bootstrap on demand: the VTC sends one at
adoption, after an inspection finds a step missing, on a protectionChanged
event that drops the required check, or for a drift revert of drift the
bridge reported. Point at BRIDGE.md's per-guard upgrade steps for those.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

* Explore 03: say the page is a one-off run, kept as a guide for an AI

The page records one walk through the bridge on the 2026-10-22 builds
and will not be re-verified as the bridge, the VTC and cnm move on. A
callout at the top says so, and tells a reader who wants the latest
versions to have their AI assistant read the page for the shape of the
work, then read the current VGI and VTI repositories to find which
versions go together and carry out the install from those, with the
Upgrading section as the worked example of that approach.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

* Explore 03: join the two top callouts into one blockquote

A blank line between two blockquotes is one blockquote with a blank line
inside it, which markdownlint rejects (MD028). A `>` continuation line
keeps the explore-stream warning and the one-off-run note together.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

title: feat(elections): vote where textReleaseThreshold is below 10, and warn first (VTI-VOT-065)
body:
VTI-VOT-065 now lets an election's `textReleaseThreshold` be as low as 1 (it SHOULD be at least 10). The voting/_shared/0.3 manifest carries the new minimum, and every task that carries the manifest moved a version (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1002, OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2379). A member could not vote in such an election, because the 0.2 show schema refuses a threshold below 10.

## Changes

- **Pins** (`openvtc-core/trust-tasks.toml`). Each bundle has the same digest VTI pins.

  | Task | Was | Now |
  |---|---|---|
  | `vtc/elections/show` | 0.2 | 0.3 (sent; its `#response` routed and admitted by the inbound gate) |
  | `vta/pcs/voter/register` | 0.2 | 0.3 |
  | `vta/pcs/vote` | 0.2 | 0.3 |
  | `vta/pcs/vote-encrypted` | 0.3 | 0.4 |

  OpenVTC has no trustee flow, sends no `vta/pcs/voter/read` and composes no manifest (`vtc/elections/create`), so nothing else moves.
- **Warning (VTI-VOT-090).** Below 10, the member sees *"Written answers are released once N ballots are counted. Below 10, a written answer may identify who wrote it."* in three places: on the election detail, before `t` takes a ticket; on the ballot; and on the cast confirmation. The text comes from `ShownElection::text_release_warning` / `elections::text_release_warning`.
- **Onto the VTI 0.78 stack.**
  - `vta-sdk` 0.75 → 0.78.
  - `did-git-sign` / `vgi-core` → 0.30 (VGI #191).
  - `trust-tasks-rs` floor → 0.36.2.
  - Test deps: `vta-service` 0.67 → 0.70, `vti-voting` 0.4 → 0.7, `vti-vetting-pcs` 0.8 → 0.11.
  - `affinidi-tdk` 0.36 and `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.44 are unchanged.
  - `cargo tree -d` shows one line of every VTI, VGI, trust-tasks and TDK crate.
- **Tests.** Core tests check that thresholds 1–9 are read and 0 is refused, and check the warning text, including the singular form for 1. A TUI render test checks the warning on the detail, ballot and confirm screens, and its absence at 10. `elections_vote_e2e` now runs a threshold-3 election against `MockVta` from `vta-service` 0.70.
- CHANGELOG: the elections entry names the new versions and the warning; a "Changed" entry records the stack move.

Members need a VTA and a community that serve these versions (`vta-service` 0.70, `vtc-service` 0.18). An older one answers `unsupportedVersion`.

## Checks (local)

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo nextest run --workspace`: 2205 passed
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --run-ignored ignored-only` (the MockVta suites, `elections_vote_e2e` included): 30 passed
- `cargo test --workspace --doc`: passed

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): flow unchanged
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): generated from the pinned specs
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutation touched
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(store): a templated test store copies the template's empty directories too
body:
Closes #2383.

## Cause

The audit-coverage test wasn't hung; it was slow, and the cause is in a test fixture.

- `test_fixture::open_with_keyspaces` builds a test store by copying a pre-built template database, because creating keyspaces needs fsyncs.
- The template snapshot recorded **files only**, so each empty tree's `tables/` folder was left out of the copy.
- When lsm-tree recovers a tree whose folder is missing, it creates it and fsyncs it (`recover_levels`). On macOS that means one `F_FULLFSYNC` per keyspace on every open, about 0.33 s for the VTA's keyspace set.
- `every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry` opens a fresh store for each of its 163 tasks. It sat idle for about 35 s waiting on those syncs. On a machine busy with other builds it passed nextest's 300 s limit while barely using the CPU, which is why it looked hung.

## Fix

The snapshot now records directories, empty ones included, and the copy recreates them. A new test checks that every directory in the template is in the snapshot.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| open one VTA-sized fixture | ~330 ms | ~54 ms |
| `every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry` | 37 s | 8.7 s |
| `nextest --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` (local) | 427 s | 310 s |
| `nextest -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (local) | 675 s | 387 s |

I also tried running that test's tasks in parallel. That only reached 23 s, because `F_FULLFSYNC` syncs queue behind each other at the drive, so I left the test unchanged.

Local results:
- workspace: 6751 passed
- vtc-service: 3591 passed
- clippy and fmt: clean

title: vtc-service-v0.18.0
body:
### Added

- **voting**: TextReleaseThreshold may be as low as 1, disclosed below 10 (VTI-VOT-065) ([#2379](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2379))

* build(specs): pin voting/election register+show 0.3, vta/pcs voter/vote/trustee next versions, vtc/elections create 0.4 + show 0.3

  The voting/_shared/0.3 manifest lets textReleaseThreshold be as low as 1
  (VTI-VOT-065); every task carrying the manifest moves a version. The old
  versions stay pinned; their bundles take the registry's deprecation note.

- **vtc**: Archive, unarchive and remove a community-owned data room ([#2380](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2380))

A community could create, describe and staff a room it owns, but never close
  or remove one. This adds the owner's lifecycle beside the host's computed one,
  stored on the owner's record: active -> archived (readOnly | noAccess) ->
  removalScheduled -> purging -> removed
  (vtc/rooms/community/{archive,unarchive,remove}/0.1,
  vtc/rooms/community/removal/cancel/0.1).

  - readOnly freezes the host record (vti_rooms::Room::frozen_at): the host
    refuses every task but a read, except the owner's own Admin acts. Open
    offers are withdrawn.
  - noAccess, and every removal, resets the room: one `room` withdrawal through
    rooms/owner/revoke, the only withdrawal a private room's host applies.
    Admitted members become `suspended`. The community's own credentials are
    re-issued after the second the reset falls in, because a credential whose
    validFrom is before revokedAt is withdrawn. The reset is recorded as a
    pending change before it is asked for, and rooms::community_lifecycle (the
    one retry owner) finishes it; a reset the host accepted is never repeated.
  - Unarchiving restores suspended members with fresh credentials (same actions
    and expiry), delivered as an offers/list renewal.
  - Removal only from archived, with a grace period (default 30 days,
    `[rooms.community] removal_grace_days`) or at once. The purge deletes host
    rows, every blob (including moved copies), usage, the storage assignment,
    group bindings and the served DID log; it asks the VTA to delete the DID (a
    SHOULD, reported and never holding the purge); and it keeps a tombstone.
  - get/list 0.4 carry `status`, members/list 0.2 and memberships/list 0.2 the
    `suspended` state, and members/add 0.2 refuses `wrongState`. The 0.3 and 0.1
    reads stay served: purged rooms are hidden from them, and a suspended
    admission reads as admitted. members/add 0.1 is no longer served.
  - The VTA serves rooms/keys/act 0.10, which adds memberships/list 0.2.
    vta-sdk and pnm move to it.
  - cnm rooms archive|unarchive|remove|cancel-removal, list --state; the admin
    console's state chips, filter, Lifecycle card and dialogs (remove requires
    typing the room's label); the member portal's room-state wording.



### Changed

- **vtc**: One radio-group pattern across the console ([#2387](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2387))

The console styled a group of choices seven ways — election-radios,
  gitns-fieldset/gitns-radio, storage-kind, community-choices,
  rooms-limits-mode, switch-field, and fieldset.field with a form-actions
  row — each with its own gap, legend and description treatment, and most
  radios in the system blue rather than the brand colour.

  Now every group is `fieldset.choice-group` (`.inline` for a row of short
  choices) with a `.field-label` legend, every choice the shared
  `label.checkbox` + `.checkbox-text`, and a choice's explanation a
  `.choice-hint` line under it. `.checkbox` inputs take the brand accent.
  The six dead rule sets are removed; vetting's bordered `vet-fieldset`
  section box stays, holding the shared choices. The sign-in key picker
  (`login-option`) is a card picker, not a radio group, and is unchanged.



### Fixed

- **rooms**: Key a room's rows by length-prefixed room ID, so no two rooms share a row ([#2386](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2386))

Room records, epoch links and relayed commits were stored at
  `<prefix><roomId>:<…>`. A room identifier is a DID and contains `:`, and a
  record key may too, so the key was ambiguous: `did:web:a`'s record `b:k` and
  `did:web:a:b`'s record `k` were one row, which either room could overwrite,
  and one room's scan prefix covered every room whose identifier extends it —
  its listing, tree head, chain and relay read the other's rows, and its prune
  deleted the other's epoch links.

  Rows are now stored at `<prefix>/v2:<len>:<roomId>:<…>`, where `<len>` is
  the identifier's length in bytes. The identifier is read by count, not by a
  separator it may contain, so two rooms never share a key or a scan prefix.
  `purge_room_rows` no longer needs to check each row against the room.

- **vtc**: The rest of the console speaks its form language ([#2385](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2385))

A sweep of every console screen against the stylesheets found the same
  defect classes #2376 fixed on Groups, on other screens:

  - 17 buttons with no class rendered as bare browser buttons — the console
    styles only .primary/.secondary/.destructive. Election create/next/
    certify, storage and room-limit submits, "New storage", "New community
    room", room moves, the step-up Copy buttons.
  - Undefined layout classes: elections' detail-list/warning-text/
    button-row/election-texts, storage-form, rooms-limits-form, cap-list,
    rooms-tags, action-buttons/action-acknowledged. Forms stacked with no
    gap, buttons touched, chips ran together, warnings had no styling.
  - The global `dd { word-break: break-all }` split every sentence in a
    definition list mid-word (action facts, room and storage details).
    `overflow-wrap: anywhere` still wraps a DID, between words otherwise.
  - Bare radio/checkbox labels (ACL invite kind, remove-now) and an inline
    `Label <input>` on step-up enrolment.

  Shared fixes: .checkbox covers radios, a .warning-text notice, a card's
  direct button keeps its width, a card's h2 loses the browser margins,
  .rooms-edit spaces its children. Screens use form-stack, form-actions,
  dl.kv and Field.

- **vtc**: The member portal's forms use its own form language ([#2378](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2378))

The portal's stylesheet styled text inputs only inside `.field`,
  `.passkey-add` and `.search`, and styled no `select` at all, so the
  directory card's choices, a group's join note and a member's name for
  someone rendered as the browser's defaults. Its Directory and Groups
  pages also used classes no portal stylesheet defines (`stack`,
  `inline-form`, `note`), copied from the console.

  Every text control, select and textarea in the portal now shares one
  rule. The stacked forms use the portal's `card-form` / `card-field`,
  the one-line forms a new `form-row`, checkboxes a new `check`, and the
  status notes on the Groups and Repositories pages the sign-in sheet's
  `alert alert-info` notice. Your name for someone is labelled by `for`,
  so its Save button is no longer part of the input's name.

### Fixed

- **rooms**: Key a room's rows by length-prefixed room ID, so no two rooms share a row ([#2386](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2386))

Room records, epoch links and relayed commits were stored at
  `<prefix><roomId>:<…>`. A room identifier is a DID and contains `:`, and a
  record key may too, so the key was ambiguous: `did:web:a`'s record `b:k` and
  `did:web:a:b`'s record `k` were one row, which either room could overwrite,
  and one room's scan prefix covered every room whose identifier extends it —
  its listing, tree head, chain and relay read the other's rows, and its prune
  deleted the other's epoch links.

  Rows are now stored at `<prefix>/v2:<len>:<roomId>:<…>`, where `<len>` is
  the identifier's length in bytes. The identifier is read by count, not by a
  separator it may contain, so two rooms never share a key or a scan prefix.
  `purge_room_rows` no longer needs to check each row against the room.

  or remove one. This adds the owner's lifecycle beside the host's computed one,
  stored on the owner's record: active -> archived (readOnly | noAccess) ->
  removalScheduled -> purging -> removed

title: fix(rooms)!: key a room's rows by length-prefixed room ID, so no two rooms share a row
body:
Closes #2382.

## The bug

Room records, epoch links and relayed commits were stored at `<prefix><roomId>:<…>`. Room IDs are DIDs, so they contain `:`, and record keys can contain `:` too (the spec only caps them at 512 characters). The issue described a scan problem, but this is worse:

- **Cross-room write:** `did:web:a`'s record `b:k` and `did:web:a:b`'s record `k` were the **same row**, so either room could overwrite the other's record.
- **Scan bleed:** one room's listing, tree head, epoch chain and commit relay included the rows of any room whose ID extends its own.
- **Prune:** a room's prune deleted another room's epoch links.

## The fix

- **Keys:** rows are now stored at `<prefix>/v2:<len>:<roomId>:<…>`, where `<len>` is the room ID's length in bytes. The ID is read by count, not by a separator it may contain, so two rooms can't share a key or a scan prefix.
- **Purge:** `purge_room_rows` no longer checks each row's suffix, since every key is now exact.
- **Migration:** `storage::migrate_room_keys` moves rows still in the old layout.
  - Each row is matched to its room by what it holds: a record's own key, or a 10-digit epoch.
  - A row that can't be matched to one room, or whose new key is already taken, is left in place and reported.
  - Each row moves in one atomic batch that also checks the row is unchanged and the new key is empty, so the migration can run again safely and resumes if interrupted.
  - The VTC runs it at boot and after a backup import, and room-host runs it at boot.

## Breaking

`vti_rooms::storage::RECORDS_PREFIX` and `EPOCH_LINKS_PREFIX` are no longer public. Use `storage::record_storage_key` instead. Neither openvtc nor the browser plugin uses them.

## Tests

New tests in `vti-rooms` storage:
- the cross-room write
- the chain, relay and prune staying inside one room
- the migration: attribution, rows it can't attribute, a new key that's already taken, a rerun, and a store with no old-layout rows

Local runs:
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6750 passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3591 passed
- `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `fmt --check` are clean

title: fix(vtc): the rest of the console speaks its form language
body:
This follows #2376: a sweep of every admin console screen against the stylesheets on main.

**What was wrong**
- **17 unstyled buttons.** The console styles only `.primary`, `.secondary` and `.destructive`, so a classless `<button>` renders as the bare browser default. Affected:
  - election Create, Next and Certify
  - the storage-config, credential and room-limits submit buttons
  - "New storage", "New community room" and "Add a member"
  - the room-move buttons
  - the step-up Copy buttons
- **Undefined layout classes:**
  - Elections: `detail-list`, `warning-text`, `button-row`, `election-texts`
  - Storage and rooms: `storage-form`, `storage-set-credential`, `rooms-limits-form`, `rooms-tags`
  - Roles: `cap-list`
  - Actions: `action-buttons`, `action-acknowledged`

  As a result, forms stacked with no gap, the Close/Cancel buttons touched, tag chips ran together, warnings had no styling, and capabilities showed as a bulleted list.
- **Words split mid-word in definition lists.** The global `dd { word-break: break-all }` split every sentence in a definition list mid-word, on the action cards and the room and storage details ("consent to i / t"). It now uses `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, which still wraps a DID where it has to.
- **Loose controls.**
  - The ACL invite's radios were bare labels.
  - The room-removal "Remove now" checkbox was a bare label.
  - Step-up enrolment had an inline `Label <input>`.

**Shared fixes** in `components.css`:
- `.checkbox` now covers radios too.
- New `.warning-text` notice.
- A button placed directly in a `.card` keeps its own width instead of stretching.
- A card's `h2` loses the browser's heading margins.

Screens now use `form-stack`, `form-actions`, `dl.kv` and `Field`.

**Left alone**
- The theme preview bar is drawn in its own shadow tree on purpose.
- The theme switcher and rule-editor buttons are styled by their containers.
- Radio groups are still styled seven different ways. Consolidating those is a separate PR.

**Checks**
- `tsc -b --noEmit` is clean, and all 1414 tests pass.
- `wire:check` passes and the console builds.
- I screenshotted each changed screen, rendered from the existing tests: election detail and written answers, action cards, roles, the ACL invite, storage create and credential, room limits, and community-room tags.

title: chore: release 11 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.36.6` → `0.36.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.36.6` → `0.36.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.36.6` → `0.36.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.36.6` → `0.36.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.36.6` → `0.36.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.36.6` → `0.36.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.36.6` → `0.36.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.36.6` → `0.36.7` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.28.7` → `0.28.8` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.7`) | `0.10.6` → `0.10.7` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.16` → `0.9.17` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(rooms): archived and removed community rooms, and renewals collected
body:
The member side of archiving and removing community data rooms, OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2380 (spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1006).

**The record with room states.** The Rooms panel now reads `vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.2` instead of 0.1, so each room shows its own state beside your standing:
- `· read-only`
- `· closed for now`: suspended, restored if the room reopens
- `· being removed`: with the purge date
- `· room removed`

The new `suspended` member state has its own `Standing::Suspended`. `RoomCondition` reads `roomState`, `roomAccess` and `purgeAt`. Accepting is offered, and allowed, only in an active room; an archived room, or one being removed, admits nobody. The pin moved 0.1 → 0.2: a VTC before #2380 answers `unsupportedType`, which the panel explains.

**Renewals collected.** On every read, once a VTA is connected, the panel reads `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.4`'s `renewals`. `community_rooms::collect_renewals` has the VTA store each renewal it does not hold yet, replacing the credential it renews, as `pnm rooms offers renew` does. A renewal already held is skipped, and a read that renewed nothing doesn't read again. This is what restores a member suspended while a room was archived with no access, and it also picks up scheduled renewals of bound-group admissions.

**Not needed here: `rooms/keys/act/0.10`.** openvtc signs community requests with the persona's own key, not through the VTA's `act`, so neither the act pin nor the vta-sdk bump is required.

Docs: `docs/community-rooms.md` (*Archived and removed rooms*, *Renewed access*).

## Tests
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 2205 passed, 0 failed.
- New tests:
  - the room-condition table, plus `suspended` in the standing table (core)
  - a whole record checking for renewals, collecting them when listed and stopping when none are (TUI)
  - a closed room showing its members suspended (TUI)

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new `reqwest::Client::new()`. VTA calls go through `VtaClient`, and community calls keep the existing 30 s reply window (R1.2).
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3).
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect: nothing is persisted (R2.1).
- [x] Retries bounded: one renewal check per read, none after a read that renewed nothing (R1.4).
- [x] The loop survives failures: a refused or unanswered renewal check is a note, never a failed panel (R1.5).
- [x] Acks/deletes after durable handoff: n/a.
- [x] Wire types are the generated 0.2 types; the inbound census is updated (R3.*).
- [x] Config absence: n/a.
- [x] Status says only what was verified: "stored renewed access to N rooms" counts the vault's accepted receives (R6.*).
- [x] "Process dies on the next line": collection is idempotent (a held renewal is skipped).
- [x] No deviations.

title: feat(rooms): memberships/list 0.2 through act 0.10 — archived and removed room states, renewals collected
body:
A community can now archive and remove a room it owns: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2380 implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1006, and both are merged. Archiving with no access, or scheduling removal, resets the room's credentials and marks each admitted member `suspended`. Reopening the room re-issues their credentials as an `offers/list` renewal. The wallet showed none of this and collected no renewal, so a member restored after a no-access archive stayed locked out until they ran `pnm rooms offers renew`.

## What

- **Pins:** `rooms/keys/act` 0.9 → **0.10** (0.9's closed table plus `memberships/list/0.2`) and `vtc/rooms/memberships/list` 0.1 → **0.2**. This is a cut-over with no fold: nothing is deployed, and VTI serves both old and new.
- **Standing:** `roomStanding` gains `suspended`, and `roomCondition` maps the room's own state to `active` / `readOnly` / `closed` / `goingAway` (with `purgeAt`) / `removed`.
- **Views:** offer views, the portal's `PageOfferView` and `PageRoomView`, and the remembered room names carry `roomState`, `roomAccess`, `purgeAt` and `suspendedAt`. They are spelled exactly as vtc-service's member portal (`wallet-rooms.ts`) reads them, so the portal's "read-only / closed for now / removal scheduled" wording appears with no portal change. Values the schema does not allow are dropped, including from `chrome.storage`.
- **Renewals:** `collectRoomRenewals` (core) stores each `offers/list/0.4` renewal in the member's VTA **in place of** the credential it renews (`vault/credentials/{query,get,receive}`), as `pnm rooms offers renew` does. The offscreen listing runs it whenever the member is in one of the community's rooms.
  - It is idempotent: a credential already held is not sent again.
  - It refuses to guess between two held credentials of one kind.
  - It never fails the listing; a failure is logged and retried on the next read.
- `CLAUDE.md` and `task-surface.json` are updated (synced from vta-sdk 0.77.1).

## Tests

- Core: `tests/rooms.lifecycle.mjs`, 8 tests. They cover the suspended standing, `roomCondition`, names carrying state with bad values dropped, reading renewals across pages, storing in place, idempotency, a fresh store, and refusing two held credentials or non-JSON.
- Extension: 4 tests in `room-offers.test.mts`. They cover the listing carrying state and the portal view, renewals stored through the `list` op, a vault failure not failing the listing, and remembered names keeping state.
- `npm run build`, `npm run lint` and `npm test` pass: core 1120, extension 1413, and the rest green. `check-task-versions` passes (436 URIs at their pinned versions), and no page-reachable bundle names a rooms task.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new `fetch` / client; every call goes through the existing injected senders (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] Nothing is committed before its remote effect: a renewal is stored at the VTA, and the wallet keeps no record of it (R2.1)
- [x] No retry loop of its own; renewals are retried by the next listing (R1.4)
- [x] Listing survives a failed collection (R1.5)
- [x] n/a: no ack path touched (R1.6)
- [x] Wire types are the generated ones at the pinned versions; consumer names match the VTC portal (R3.*)
- [x] Absent room state reads as "active / nothing to say" (R5.*)
- [x] A failed renewal is logged with its room and reason, never reported as stored (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line": a renewal half-stored (membership but not authority) is finished on the next read, because each credential is checked against the vault on its own (R2.1)

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.36.7
body:
### Added

- **vtc/rooms/community**: Archive, unarchive, remove and removal/cancel 0.1; get/list 0.4, members/add+list 0.2, memberships/list 0.2 ([#1006](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/1006))

A community could create a room it owns and change its members, but never
  close or end one. This adds an owner's lifecycle for a community-owned room,
  distinct from the host's computed clock (live/lapsed/dormant/reclaimable):

  - active
  - archived, with an access: readOnly (members keep reading; the host refuses
    every write, upload and curation) or noAccess (the community's VTA resets
    the room — one `room` withdrawal — and re-issues the community's own
    credentials; each admitted member becomes `suspended`). Open offers are
    withdrawn either way. Reversible: vtc/rooms/community/unarchive restores
    suspended members in the background by re-issuing their membership and
    authority, collected as an offers/list renewal.
  - removalScheduled: only from archived (removal is the second of two
    deliberate acts). The room is noAccess and its content kept until purgeAt,
    after a grace period (graceDays, or the community's configured default;
    30 days in the reference implementation). vtc/rooms/community/removal/cancel
    returns it to archived/noAccess.
  - purging: graceDays 0, or the grace period ended. Deletes every record,
    epoch link, commit, revocation list, file in every storage config, transfer
    and the host record; drops kept credentials and owed removals; unbinds
    groups; stops serving a serverless DID log; SHOULD have the VTA delete the
    room's DID (a refusal there does not hold the purge). Retried with backoff,
    progress in status.purge, never reversible.
  - removed: a tombstone with the host record as it last stood.

  A change part-way through at the VTA (a reset the host accepted before the
  community's own credentials were re-issued) is reported as
  status.pendingChange and finished by the community.

  New shared definitions in vtc/_shared/0.5 (RoomState, ArchiveAccess,
  RoomStatus, PendingChange, PurgeProgress, CommunityRoomV3, MemberStateV2,
  RoomMemberV2, RoomMembershipV2). get/list 0.4 carry status (list gains a
  `states` filter; removed rooms only when asked for); members/add 0.2 refuses
  a room that is not active (wrongState); members/list 0.2 and
  memberships/list 0.2 add `suspended`, and memberships/list the room's own
  state so member surfaces can say read-only, closed or going away.
  rooms/keys/act 0.10 adds vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.2 to its table so a
  member's key holder can sign it.

  Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

`claimed`, `confirm` and `verified-value` are also undefined, but they are wrappers whose children are already styled, so they are left as hooks.

- `vitest run`: 116 files, 1397 tests pass

title: feat(voting)!: textReleaseThreshold may be as low as 1, disclosed below 10 (VTI-VOT-065)
body:
VTI-VOT-065 now says an election's textReleaseThreshold MUST be at least 1
and SHOULD be at least 10; below 10, the disclosure a member sees before
taking a ticket MUST say so, and that a written answer may identify its
author (VTI-VOT-090). The voting/_shared/0.3 manifest carries the new
minimum, and every task that carries the manifest moves a version
(dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1002).

| Task | Served | Sent |
|---|---|---|
| voting/election/register | 0.3, 0.2 | 0.3 (VTC; 0.2 to a ballot box that refuses 0.3, threshold >= 10 only) |
| voting/election/show | 0.3, 0.2 | 0.3 (trustee/read 0.3) |
| vtc/elections/create | 0.4, 0.3 | 0.4 (console, cnm, vtc-client) |
| vtc/elections/show | 0.3, 0.2 | 0.3 (console, voter/read 0.3) |
| vta/pcs/voter/register, vote | 0.3, 0.2 | 0.3 |
| vta/pcs/voter/read | 0.3 (signs show/0.3), 0.2 (signs show/0.2) | 0.3 |
| vta/pcs/vote-encrypted | 0.4, 0.3 | 0.4 |
| vta/pcs/trustee/enrol | 0.3, 0.2 | 0.3 |
| vta/pcs/trustee/deal, keys, justify | 0.4, 0.3 | 0.4 |
| vta/pcs/trustee/read | 0.3 (signs election/show/0.3), 0.2 (signs 0.2) | 0.3 |

- vti-voting reads the 0.3 manifest throughout. rules::check_manifest no
  longer refuses 1 - 9; the generated type is non-zero, so 0 is no
  manifest. A request under an old version is held to its own schema
  (minimum 10) before it is read as 0.3: no second gate.
- The ballot box (service::BallotBox::register_at / show_at,
  ElectionVersion) registers and shows at either version. A 0.2 show of
  an election below 10 is refused unsupportedVersion naming 0.3, never
  answered in a shape 0.2 forbids. The VTC's vtc/elections/show/0.2 does
  the same.
- The VTA serves both versions of each vta/pcs task through one handler,
  the spine holding each to its own schema; the two read tasks sign, and
  answer with, the show their own version names.
- Old versions stay served so existing clients keep working; none is
  dropped. The VTC lists create/0.3 and show/0.2 in discovery.
- The VTC registers at voting/election/register/0.3; if the ballot box
  refuses it unsupportedVersion and the threshold is 10 or more, it
  registers at 0.2 instead (a different request on a definite refusal;
  the sweeper stays the one redelivery owner).
- Console: the builder pins vtc/elections/create/0.4, allows 1 - 9 with a
  warning in Counting and Review (default stays 10); the election page's
  "What members are told" gains a "Written answers" row with the warning.
  The member portal shows the warning when the wallet passes the
  manifest's textReleaseThreshold on. pnm elections show/ticket print it;
  cnm manifest check and create warn the administrator.
- Action summaries: a template for vtc/elections/create/0.4, pinned in the
  build and the console.

Breaking: vti_voting's and vta-sdk's typed voting APIs take the 0.3
manifest types, and the SDK's typed vta/pcs voter and trustee methods use
the new versions' generated types.

## Upstream
- Spec: dtgwg-vti-spec#87 (VTI-VOT-065 MUST >= 1, SHOULD >= 10; VTI-VOT-090 disclosure below 10)
- Trust Tasks: dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1002 (voting/_shared/0.3 and the versions above), pinned in the first commit

## Tests
- `vti_vot_065_*` in vti-voting (rules, tally at 1), vti-voting-service (register/show at 0.2 vs 0.3), vtc-service IT (create 0.4/0.3, show 0.3/0.2, a ballot box serving register 0.2 only); pnm `vti_vot_090_*`; cnm; vta-service voter/trustee read at both versions; conformance witnesses for each new version with a threshold of 3; console builder, election page and portal tests.
- Local: fmt, workspace clippy, VTC clippy (default and `vetting-pcs,voting`), workspace nextest, VTC nextest (default and `vetting-pcs,voting`), doc tests, admin-ui lint + vitest.

## Follow-ups outside this repo
- vta-browser-plugin and OpenVTC: send the new versions, and show members the below-10 warning before a ticket (the disclosure has no member for it; derive it from `manifest.textReleaseThreshold`). The portal here shows it once the wallet passes `textReleaseThreshold` in its page-facing election view.

title: feat(elections): vote where written answers release below 10 ballots, and warn first
body:
VTI-VOT-065 (voting/_shared/0.3, dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #1003) lets a manifest's `textReleaseThreshold` go as low as 1, where 0.2 required at least 10. This moves the wallet to the versions carrying it and warns the member, as VTI-VOT-090 requires, before they take a ticket and again on the ballot.

Counterpart: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2379. That PR serves both the old and new versions. **Merge it, and deploy the VTA, before this one**: the wallet now sends only the new versions, with no fold back to the old ones (see CLAUDE.md, "Nothing is deployed").

## Changes

- **Pins**: `vta/pcs/voter/read` 0.3, `vta/pcs/voter/register` 0.3, `vta/pcs/vote` 0.3, `vta/pcs/vote-encrypted` 0.4 and `vtc/elections/show` 0.3. They replace 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.2, and the types are regenerated with `trust-tasks-gen-ts`. The vendored bundles are byte-identical to the ones #2379 vendors. `voter/read/0.3` signs a `show/0.3` read, and `postCommunityTask` accepts only `show/0.3#response` in reply.
- **Trustee tasks**: the wallet has no trustee flows, so `vta/pcs/trustee/*` is not pinned here.
- **Warning**: `textReleaseWarning(threshold)` in `@openvtc/pnm-core/vtc` returns "Written answers are released once N ballots are counted. Below 10, a written answer may identify who wrote it." It returns `null` at 10 or above. The value comes from the manifest because the community's disclosure has no member for it. The ticket and ballot windows show the warning inside the election's disclosure.
- **Page view**: `vtaWallet.elections.show` now returns an optional `textReleaseThreshold` (the manifest's value), which the VTI portal reads.
- **`task-surface.json`**: refreshed from `vta-sdk` 0.77.1 on #2379's branch. The refresh only adds entries (the new voter, vote and trustee versions).
- **Manifest validation**: the wallet does no runtime schema validation of manifests, and nothing in it enforced the old minimum of 10. The 0.3 types are the change that matters there.

## Tests

- core: the warning text at 1, 3 and 9, and none at 10, 25 or absent. A manifest with a threshold of 1 builds and casts. The new URIs are sent.
- extension: the ticket and ballot windows show the warning below 10 and not at or above it. `pageElectionViewOf` carries the threshold. The offscreen fixtures use the new versions.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (all workspaces green, 1412 extension tests), `npm run build`, `check-task-versions.mjs`, `trust-tasks check`.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new network code
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — unchanged flows
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — generated from the pinned registry bundles; the portal already reads the optional field
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — absent threshold shows no warning, but the manifest's field is required by schema
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no mutation added
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

title: feat(vtc)!: archive, unarchive and remove a community-owned data room
body:
A community could create, describe and staff a data room it owns, but never close or remove one. This implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#1006: the **owner's** lifecycle for a community-owned room, stored on the owner's record beside the host's computed lifecycle (which stays computed and never set).

```text
active ──archive──▶ archived(readOnly | noAccess) ──remove──▶ removalScheduled ──purgeAt──▶ purging ──▶ removed
  ▲                    │    ▲                                     │
  └────unarchive───────┘    └─────────── removal/cancel ──────────┘
```

**Draft until #1006 merges.** The pins in `vti-specs-vtc` and `vti-specs-rooms` were taken from that branch's built registry; once it is published, `trust-tasks -C <crate> update` must find the same digests.

## What it does

| State | Members | Host | Undo |
|---|---|---|---|
| archived, `readOnly` | keep reading | `Room::frozen_at`: every task but a read is refused (the owner's Admin acts excepted) | `unarchive` |
| archived, `noAccess` | `suspended`: a room **reset** withdraws every credential; the content is kept | refuses every member | `unarchive` restores them by renewal |
| `removalScheduled` | `suspended`, never restored | content kept until `purgeAt` | `removal/cancel` (no gesture) |
| `purging` → `removed` | — | records, epochs, commits, revocation list, every blob (incl. moved copies), usage, assignment, bindings and the served DID log are deleted; the VTA is asked to delete the DID | none |

- **Reset** = one `room` withdrawal (`rooms/owner/revoke`), the only withdrawal a private room's host applies. The community's own credentials are re-issued after the second the reset falls in (`validFrom < revokedAt` is withdrawn). The reset is recorded as a `Pending` change before it is asked for. `rooms::community_lifecycle` is the one retry owner: it finishes pending changes, starts due purges, purges, and restores suspended members. A reset the host accepted is never repeated.
- **Removal** starts only from archived. The grace period is `graceDays` 0–365, else `[rooms.community] removal_grace_days` (default 30). Both `cnm` and the console make the administrator type the room's label to confirm.
- **Reads:** `get`/`list` 0.4 (with `status`, and `list` filters by `states`), `members/list` 0.2 and `memberships/list` 0.2 (`suspended` and the room's own state). The 0.3/0.1 reads stay served: purged rooms are hidden from them, and a suspended admission reads as `admitted`. `members/add` moves to 0.2 (`wrongState`); 0.1 is no longer served.
- **VTA:** serves `rooms/keys/act/0.10` (adds `memberships/list` 0.2); `vta-sdk` and `pnm` move to it.
- **Surfaces:**
  - `cnm rooms archive|unarchive|remove|cancel-removal`, `list --state|--all`, with a fix printed for each `wrongState`.
  - Console: state chips and filter, a Lifecycle card, the archive and remove dialogs; only active rooms can be bound to groups.
  - Member portal and `pnm rooms memberships`: room-state wording.
- `docs/03-vtc/community-rooms.md` (*Archive and remove a room*), `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`.

**Breaking (`!`):** `vti_rooms::Room` gains a public field (`frozen_at`), and `vta-sdk`'s `room_act*` and `unsigned_*_request` take and return act 0.10 types.

## Tests

- `vtc-service`: 6 new end-to-end tests in `community_rooms.rs`. They cover:
  - read-only (writes refused, reads served)
  - no-access reset, suspend and restore by renewal, where the host honours the renewed credentials
  - a reset whose re-issue failed, finished by the worker without a second reset
  - schedule and cancel
  - instant purge with a tombstone and the 0.3 reads hiding it
  - every declared refusal

  Also: conformance samples for every new shape, error-code census witnesses, the manifest, and the live-channel fingerprint, which now includes `status`.
- `vti-rooms`: freeze gate, `purge_room_rows` (room-exact, resumable) and `BlobHost::purge_room`. The latter is checked for counters restored exactly, a failing store leaving rows for retry, a mid-migration purge, and leaving other rooms untouched.
- `cnm-cli` 142, admin-ui 1408 (vitest), `vta-sdk`/`vta-cli-common`/`pnm-cli`/`vta-mcp` 1523, `vta-service` room act and censuses.
- Workspace nextest: 6739 passed. The exception is `vta-service::trust_tasks::audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`, which times out; **it times out identically on `main` here** (filed separately). `vtc-service` + `vtc-client` all pass (admin-ui bundle built). Clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean.

## Not in this PR

- **pnm-browser-plugin / openvtc:** they need to pin act 0.10 and `memberships/list` 0.2 and show the new states. Neither collects `offers/list` renewals yet, so a member restored after `noAccess` regains access through `pnm rooms offers renew` until they do.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new `reqwest::Client::new()` / bare fetch (R1.2)
- [ ] **Deviation — R1.3:** `rooms::community_lifecycle` holds the community rooms' write lock (`CommunityRooms::lock`) across the VTA exchange (reset, re-issue), as `members/remove` already does. The lock is what keeps two changes of one room's membership from racing at the VTA, which holds one pending advance per room. `drive_pending` also waits under it up to one second for the re-issue to clear the reset's second. `BlobHost::purge_room` holds the blob lock across store deletes, as `sweep` does.
- [x] No local state before its remote effect; the reset is resumable through a recorded `Pending` (R2.1)
- [x] Retries bounded and backed off (30 s doubling to 1 h); the reset is re-asked only while its outcome is unknown (R1.4)
- [x] The worker loop survives transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Records/credentials dropped only after the host accepted the withdrawal (R1.6)
- [x] Wire types are the generated ones; console wire types regenerated (R3.*)
- [x] `removal_grace_days` absent → default 30, capped at 365; no new section is required (R5.*)
- [x] Purge, restore and pending-change failures are surfaced in `status` and `ext.org.openvtc.lifecycle`, and audited (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line": answered for reset → re-issue → close (`Pending`), for purge (idempotent steps, tombstone written last) and for restore (per member)

title: test(vtc-admin-ui): read argv back without an external printf that parses --help
body:
`Test (VTC admin UI)` has been red on `main` since the runner moved to ubuntu-26.04 (run 41364327307): four `shellQuote round-trips in {sh,bash,zsh,fish}` tests fail with `expected [] to deeply equal ['--help']`.

Cause: the test's argv echo was `env printf '%s\0' <words>`, and ubuntu-26.04's uutils `printf` treats a lone `--help` argument as its own option. `shellQuote` was correct.

Fix: read argv back through one fixed `sh` loop (`for a; do printf "%s\0" "$a"; done`), so each word reaches printf only as an argument after its format. The outer shell under test still does all the parsing. Test-only change; 85/85 pass locally.

title: test(vtc): read shellQuote's argv back through node, not an external printf
body:
`Test (VTC admin UI)` went red on main at 3139e00ec (a release commit with no code change). The cause is the runner, not the code: `ubuntu-latest` moved from 24.04 to 26.04 between the green run (41329057303) and the red one (41364327307).

Ubuntu 26.04 ships the uutils (Rust) coreutils. Its `printf` takes a `--help` argument as its own flag, even after the format string. The shellQuote round-trip harness ran `env printf '%s\0' <args>`, so for the `--help` value it got printf's help text back, which surfaced as `expected [] to deeply equal ['--help']`. That broke 4 tests, one for each shell.

`shellQuote` itself was correct. The bug was that the probe used a program that parses its own arguments. The harness now writes the argv back through a node script, because node reads no options after the script path. The intent is unchanged: an external program, so no shell builtin is involved.

All 85 tests in `actions.test.ts` pass locally.

title: feat(vtc/rooms/community): archive, unarchive and remove a community-owned room
body:
A community could create, describe and staff a data room it owns, but never close or remove one. This adds the owner's lifecycle for a community-owned room, beside the host's computed one (`live`/`lapsed`/`dormant`/`reclaimable`, which stays computed and never set):

```text
active ──archive──▶ archived(readOnly | noAccess) ──remove──▶ removalScheduled ──purgeAt──▶ purging ──▶ removed
  ▲                    │    ▲                                     │
  └────unarchive───────┘    └─────────── removal/cancel ──────────┘
```

- **`vtc/rooms/community/archive/0.1`**: `readOnly` (the host refuses every task but a read; open offers withdrawn) or `noAccess` (a room **reset**, meaning one `room` withdrawal through `rooms/owner/revoke`, the only withdrawal a `private` room's host can apply; admitted members become `suspended`; the community's own credentials are re-issued after the reset). A reset whose follow-up failed is recorded as a `pendingChange` and finished by the community, never reset twice.
- **`vtc/rooms/community/unarchive/0.1`**: reopens the room; suspended members are restored with fresh credentials (same actions and expiry), collected as an `offers/list` renewal.
- **`vtc/rooms/community/remove/0.1`** (`sideEffects: destructive`): only from `archived`; `graceDays` 0–365 (absent means the community's default; 0 means purge at once). The purge deletes everything the host holds and keeps a tombstone with a snapshot of the host record. Deleting the room's DID at the VTA is a SHOULD, because it needs the admin role on the context.
- **`vtc/rooms/community/removal/cancel/0.1`**: returns the room to archived with no access. It takes no step-up, so stopping a mistaken removal is never harder than making it.
- **New versions**: `get`/`list` 0.4 (`CommunityRoomV3` with `status`; `list` filters by `states`), `members/add` 0.2 (`wrongState`), `members/list` 0.2 and `vtc/rooms/memberships/list` 0.2 (the `suspended` member state and the room's own state for members), and `rooms/keys/act/0.10` (adds `memberships/list` 0.2 to act's closed table).
- **Shared definitions**: `vtc/_shared/0.5/community-room` adds `RoomState`, `ArchiveAccess`, `RoomStatus`, `PendingChange`, `PurgeProgress`, `CommunityRoomV3`, `MemberStateV2`, `RoomMemberV2` and `RoomMembershipV2`. Every 0.4 definition is unchanged.

The Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated. `fix-stale-references` updated links in 7 specs. Locally, `npm run build`, every generator, `check-bindings`, `check-published-schemas`, `build-bundles` and `check-bundles`, the Rust conformance tests with `--features validate` (3193) and the TS tests (126) all passed. The Dart tests were not run locally.

The VTI implementation (VTC, console, `cnm`, `pnm`, VTA act 0.10) follows in a separate PR that pins these versions.

title: feat(vtc/rooms/community): archive, unarchive, remove and removal/cancel 0.1; get/list 0.4, members/add+list 0.2, memberships/list 0.2 (#1006)
body:
feat(vtc/rooms/community): archive, unarchive, remove and removal/cancel 0.1; get/list 0.4, members/add+list 0.2, memberships/list 0.2 (#1006)

A community could create a room it owns and change its members, but never
close or end one. This adds an owner's lifecycle for a community-owned room,
distinct from the host's computed clock (live/lapsed/dormant/reclaimable):

- active
- archived, with an access: readOnly (members keep reading; the host refuses
  every write, upload and curation) or noAccess (the community's VTA resets
  the room — one `room` withdrawal — and re-issues the community's own
  credentials; each admitted member becomes `suspended`). Open offers are
  withdrawn either way. Reversible: vtc/rooms/community/unarchive restores
  suspended members in the background by re-issuing their membership and
  authority, collected as an offers/list renewal.
- removalScheduled: only from archived (removal is the second of two
  deliberate acts). The room is noAccess and its content kept until purgeAt,
  after a grace period (graceDays, or the community's configured default;
  30 days in the reference implementation). vtc/rooms/community/removal/cancel
  returns it to archived/noAccess.
- purging: graceDays 0, or the grace period ended. Deletes every record,
  epoch link, commit, revocation list, file in every storage config, transfer
  and the host record; drops kept credentials and owed removals; unbinds
  groups; stops serving a serverless DID log; SHOULD have the VTA delete the
  room's DID (a refusal there does not hold the purge). Retried with backoff,
  progress in status.purge, never reversible.
- removed: a tombstone with the host record as it last stood.

A change part-way through at the VTA (a reset the host accepted before the
community's own credentials were re-issued) is reported as
status.pendingChange and finished by the community.

New shared definitions in vtc/_shared/0.5 (RoomState, ArchiveAccess,
RoomStatus, PendingChange, PurgeProgress, CommunityRoomV3, MemberStateV2,
RoomMemberV2, RoomMembershipV2). get/list 0.4 carry status (list gains a
`states` filter; removed rooms only when asked for); members/add 0.2 refuses
a room that is not active (wrongState); members/list 0.2 and
memberships/list 0.2 add `suspended`, and memberships/list the room's own
state so member surfaces can say read-only, closed or going away.
rooms/keys/act 0.10 adds vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.2 to its table so a
member's key holder can sign it.

Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.
