title: feat(voting): textReleaseThreshold may be as low as 1, disclosed below 10 (voting/_shared/0.3)
body:
Follows trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#87, which amends **VTI-VOT-065**: the threshold at which text answers are released **MUST** be at least 1 and **SHOULD** be at least 10. Where it is below 10, the disclosure a member is shown before they request a ticket **MUST** say so, and **MUST** say that a written answer may identify its author (VTI-VOT-090). Small communities and surveys need written answers, so the risk is disclosed rather than forbidden.

**Shared definitions.** `voting/_shared/0.3` is `0.2` with one change: `Manifest.textReleaseThreshold` has `minimum: 1` (was 10). Its description carries the SHOULD and the disclosure rule. `0.2` is left as published, because consumers pin bundles by digest. `CONVENTIONS.md` gains a note on the 0.3 threshold.

**New task versions.** Each one is the current latest version, re-pinned to `_shared/0.3`, with a `Changes from` section:

| Task | New version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `voting/election/register` | 0.3 | request `manifest` |
| `voting/election/show` | 0.3 | response `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/deal` | 0.4 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/enrol` | 0.3 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/justify` | 0.4 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/keys` | 0.4 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/vote` | 0.3 | request `manifest` (adds an invalid example with threshold 0) |
| `vta/pcs/vote-encrypted` | 0.4 | request `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/voter/register` | 0.3 | request `manifest` |
| `vtc/elections/create` | 0.4 | request `manifest` |
| `vtc/elections/show` | 0.3 | response `manifest` |
| `vta/pcs/trustee/read` | 0.3 | the signed `election` read now names `voting/election/show/0.3` on the wire |
| `vta/pcs/voter/read` | 0.3 | the signed `show` read now names `vtc/elections/show/0.3` on the wire |

`voting/board/read/0.2` references `_shared/0.2`, but only `BoardEntry` and `ElectionId`, and neither reaches `Manifest`. So it keeps its version.

**Prose where the threshold is described:**
- `voting/election/register/0.3`: a threshold below 1 is `malformedRequest`. From 1 to 9 is valid, and a ballot box MUST NOT refuse it.
- `vtc/elections/show/0.3`: a client showing the disclosure MUST show the below-10 warning with it.
- `vtc/elections/create/0.4`: the `manifest` definition carries the SHOULD, and a composing client SHOULD warn the administrator.

`npm run fix-stale-references` updated the text links in current specs. `npm run extends-candidates` reports that the eleven manifest-carrying versions could declare `extends` on their predecessors (a loosened bound). None declares it here; prior shared-version bumps did not either. That can be added if wanted.

title: Let an election release text answers from a threshold of 1, disclosed below 10 (VTI-VOT-065, VTI-VOT-090)
body:
**The problem.** VTI-VOT-065 required the threshold at which text answers are released to be at least 10. A community or survey with fewer than 10 voters could not ask a written question at all.

**The changes:**
- **VTI-VOT-065:** the threshold MUST be at least 1 and SHOULD be at least 10. Where it is below 10, the statement a member is shown before they request a ticket MUST say so, and MUST say that a written answer may identify its author.
- **Rationale for VTI-VOT-065 (new):** a written answer can identify its author by what it says or how it is phrased, and the fewer ballots released together, the easier that is. Small communities and surveys still need written answers, so a low threshold is disclosed to the member rather than forbidden.
- **VTI-VOT-090:** the threshold warning is added to the list of things the disclosure statement covers, so the two requirements agree.

No other part of the specification states the old floor (checked the conformance tables, the appendix and the considerations).

The Trust Task schema change follows in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf: a new `voting/_shared/0.3` with `textReleaseThreshold` `minimum: 1`, and a new version of every task that references the manifest.

title: feat(elections): one ballot window that asks for the ballot box, shows each step, and remembers your vote
body:
Follow-up to #404 / #405, from a live test of voting from a community's portal.

## What changes for the member

The ballot window (`confirm.html?kind=election`, `election-consent.tsx`) is now a single window that goes from permission to receipt:

1. **Reach the ballot box** (only if needed). This used to be a refusal ("Allow it from the wallet's popup"). Now the window opens with `needsReach` and says: *"To vote, your wallet sends your ballot straight to the ballot box at <host>. Allow the wallet to reach it."* The **Allow** button calls `requestOriginPermission(origin)` as the first statement of the click. Once it is granted, the ballot form appears. The gates check `canReach` again before anything is sent.
2. **You voted** (only if this wallet remembers a vote): *"You voted on <date time>. The ballot box counted it (board entry N)"* or *"…replaced your earlier vote…"*. It offers **Change my vote** only when `disclosure.revote === "replace"` and voting is open. Otherwise it says the vote cannot be changed and shows **Close**. A small note says this is what this browser's wallet remembers.
3. **Ballot form.** The "Voting as <DID>" block is gone. In its place is **Your ticket** with the DID: *"Your ticket was taken as this identity. Your vote is sent with that blind ticket and a key made for this vote alone: it does not carry this identity, and neither <community> nor the ballot box can tell it is yours."* The ticket window's "Your ticket is for" gets the same explanation.
4. **Progress.** After **Cast my vote** the window stays open and shows each step as pending, active (with a soft pulse), done (✓) or failed (✕):
   - Checking your ballot against the election's rules
   - Your agent seals your ballot with a one-time key
   - Waiting a few seconds so your vote can't be timed to your ticket — live countdown of the real delay
   - Sending it straight to the ballot box at <host>
   - The ballot box counted it — checking its signed receipt

   It ends on **Your vote is in** (time, counted or replaced, board entry) or **Your vote was not cast**, which keeps the existing wording on voting again: the box never counts one ticket twice. There is a Close button. The animation stops completely under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Mechanics

- The offscreen `cast` op is split into three:
  - `castPrepare`: a fresh `show`, then `ballotRefusal`, the endpoint, and `pcsCast`.
  - `castPost`: sleeps the `delayMs` it is given (clamped to `[0, MAX_CAST_DELAY_MS]`), then runs `postCast`.
  - `castKeep`: runs `pcsVoterReceipt`.
- `ElectionsPageGates` drives these steps. It picks the delay with `castDelayMs()` and reports each `CastProgress` through a new `progress(window, state)` dep. The background writes it to `chrome.storage.session[election-progress:<consentId>]`, and the window follows it with `storage.onChanged`.
- `consentResultSender` gains `keepOpen`. The window stays open only if the background acknowledged a consent it was waiting for (`matched`). Any other result closes it as before.
- Closing the window early does not cancel the cast. `progress` returns false and the cast carries on. A counted vote is still remembered. A **failure** that can no longer be shown opens the old `kind: "cast"` window, which is now used only for that.
- When the ballot box returned a receipt but the agent could not keep it, the vote still counts. It is shown as done with a note, and it is remembered.
- A counted vote is stored in `chrome.storage.local` under `election-vote:` plus `ticketKey`, as `{at, status, leafIndex}`. Choices are never stored.
- The progress key is removed when the window closes.

## Privacy invariants (VTI-VOT-001)

The page-facing API and its param validation are unchanged. `vote` answers `{ ticketTaken: false }` whether the member cast, cancelled, failed, had already voted, or first had to allow the ballot box. A test pins this. The cast still goes wallet → ballot box directly.

## Tests

- `elections-page.test.mts`:
  - an unreachable box opens the window with `needsReach`, and a box still unreachable at cast time sends nothing
  - progress states arrive in order with the delay
  - a vote is remembered only once counted (and is remembered when only the receipt-keeping failed)
  - a window closed early does not stop the cast, and the failure fallback opens
  - a remembered vote and revote allowed or not
  - the page's answer is the same in every case
- `elections-page-offscreen.test.mts`: the three ops, delay capping, and a cast addressed to another box is never posted.
- `election-consent.render.test.mts`: the reach step, progress rendering and countdown, the failed step, the voted view with and without a revote, and the new ticket wording.
- `consent-window-race.test.mts`: the `keepOpen` semantics.

`npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (extension 1409, core 1112, tsp-js 123, demo-rp 6, reviewer-demo 9 — all pass) and `check-task-versions.mjs` all pass locally, along with the dist guards I ran.

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

The typed `pcs_voter_*` / `pcs_vote*` methods re-serialise timestamps (chrono), so a manifest published as `…T00:00:00.000Z` reaches the VTA as `…T00:00:00Z` — another digest, ticket refused — and signed reads/casts come back no longer the bytes their proofs cover.

- `vta-service/tests/it/voter_json_bytes.rs`: loopback test — JSON form sends the manifest as given; typed form rewrites it (pins the reason).

Additive only; no breaking change. Follows #2368 (pnm fix) and #2369 (member-vote e2e).

title: test(vtc): a member votes end to end with pnm through their own VTA
body:
## Why

The member's path through a community election had been tested only in pieces: the VTA's voter engine against an in-process ballot box, the community's registrar with a test-built voter, and the ballot box behind its own router. Nothing ran them together, so the member side of voting (now reachable from the portal, OpenVTC and `pnm`) had no end-to-end proof.

## What

New `vtc-service/tests/it/election_tasks.rs::a_member_votes_from_pnm_through_their_own_vta` (feature `voting`):

- **The member**: a key the member's VTA (`MockVta`) holds, seeded as an active member of the community.
- **The community**: this VTC, served over HTTP for the member.
- **The ballot box**: a real `vti-voting-service`. Its host session on the harness's mediator is the community's door (register, close, certify; VTI-VOT-005), and its HTTPS door on loopback is where the cast arrives (VTI-VOT-004). Its did:peer names both.
- **The flow**: `pnm elections`' own `cmd_ticket` (the VTA signs the read and the ticket request as the member; the community issues blind; the VTA unblinds), then, once voting opens, `cmd_vote` (the VTA builds the cast under a one-time key; `pnm` posts it to the ballot box and the VTA keeps the receipt).
- **The check**: the community closes and certifies from the board it reads back: `ballotsCounted == 1`, `{"alice": 1, "bob": 0}`.

Adds `vta-service` (`test-support`, `rest`) and `vta-cli-common` as path-only dev-dependencies of `vtc-service`.

## Tests

- New test passes locally in about 19 s, as do all 13 `election_tasks` tests. One existing test, `close_and_cancel_are_refused_for_each_rule_they_break`, is reported "leaky" by nextest; that is not new.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, with and without `--features voting`, is clean.

This covers the protocol path shared by `pnm`, the wallet (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#404) and OpenVTC (OpenVTC/openvtc#514). The wallet's browser UI and the OpenVTC TUI have their own tests in their repos.

title: fix(pnm): carry election documents exactly as received
body:
## Why

`pnm elections` asked the member's VTA through the SDK's typed `pcs_voter_*` / `pcs_vote*` wrappers. Those round-trip the payload and the answer through generated structs that hold timestamps as chrono `DateTime`s, so:

- **The manifest sent to `voter/register` / `vote` could change.** A manifest published as `…T00:00:00.000Z` reaches the VTA as `…T00:00:00Z`: another manifest with another digest. Taking a ticket then fails with "your VTA computed another manifest digest".
- **Documents the VTA signed came back re-serialised.** The member's read, the ticket request and the cast are no longer guaranteed to be the bytes their proofs cover.

Both fail safe (a refusal, never a wrong vote), but either one can stop a member voting. Found while building the same flow in OpenVTC (OpenVTC/openvtc#514), which carries these as JSON.

## What

Every voter task in `vta-cli-common/src/commands/elections.rs` now goes through `VtaClient::dispatch_trust_task` with the payload and the answer as JSON (`vta_task`). The manifest, the parameters and every signed document are carried exactly as received. The community's ticket answer reaches `voter/accept` without its `ext`, as that task requires. The SDK's public typed wrappers are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `the_manifest_is_registered_byte_for_byte`: a `.000Z` manifest reaches the register payload unchanged.
- `cargo test -p vta-cli-common --lib elections` (3 passed).
- `cargo test -p vti-e2e-tests --test voting_trustees` (passes; it drives the same module's trustee path against a real VTA and voting service).
- `cargo clippy -p vta-cli-common -p pnm-cli -p cnm-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

There is no end-to-end test of the member vote path through `pnm`. It needs a VTC as well as a VTA and a ballot box.

title: feat(elections): vote in a community's elections
body:
## Why

Communities can now run elections (VTI-VOT-001 – 100): the community issues blind tickets, a separate ballot box takes the casts, and the member's VTA holds every voter key (`vta/pcs/voter/*`, `vta/pcs/vote*`). `pnm elections` (VTI) and the browser wallet (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#404) let a member vote; OpenVTC could not. This adds the member side to the TUI. It complements VTI PR #2367 (the member portal) and plugin PR #404.

## What

- **`openvtc-core::elections`** (new) — the protocol, no UI:
  - builds and reads the community's tasks `vtc/elections/list/0.3`, `vtc/elections/show/0.2`, `vtc/elections/tickets/issue/0.1` through the generated types (`Request`, `parse_reply`, `Refusal::explain`);
  - the VTA calls `vta/pcs/voter/register/0.2` (no `member`), `voter/accept/0.1`, `vote/0.2`, `vote-encrypted/0.3`, `voter/receipt/0.1` (`register`, `accept`, `vote`, `keep_receipt`);
  - a mirror of VTI's `vti_voting::rules::check_ballot`, so a member hears a broken rule in words before anything is built (`check_ballot`, `BallotError`), and `BallotDraft` for the form;
  - the ballot box: `TrustTaskHTTPS` from its resolved DID document (matched on service `type`, https or loopback only), a random 0–20 s pause, the post, and `check_receipt` → `VerifiedReceipt` (typestate: only a receipt whose proof is the ballot box's, whose `threadId` is the cast's id and whose `recipient` is the cast's one-time key is ever handed to the VTA). Ballot-box refusal codes (`electionUnknown`, `notOpen`, `manifestMismatch`, `ballotInvalid`, `classMismatch`, `alreadyVoted`, `castInvalid`, `wrongLevel`) are each put in words.
- **Pins** (`trust-tasks -C openvtc-core add …`, `trust-tasks check` green, 52 versions): `vtc/elections/list/0.3`, `show/0.2`, `tickets/issue/0.1`, `vta/pcs/voter/{register/0.2,accept/0.1,receipt/0.1}`, `vta/pcs/vote/0.2`, `vta/pcs/vote-encrypted/0.3`, `voting/ballot/cast/0.1`, `voting/ballot/cast-encrypted/0.1` (the last two to read the receipt through its schema). Digests match VTI's vendored bundles.
- **TUI** — an Elections sub-page of a community, on the Rooms template: `e` on an Active community (hint added). Screens: list (voting open → tickets open → upcoming → over, with "ticket held"); detail with the disclosure (schedule, ballot-box operator, the `sameOperator` warning, board visibility, revote, secrecy, the coercion statement, the questions); the ballot (single choice as radio, multiple as checkboxes, ranking by toggle order, per-option scores with `+`/`-`, free text, `a`/`Ctrl-a` to leave an optional question blank); a confirmation (`y` only); the result (counted / replaced / already counted + board entry + what the VTA said of the receipt, or the refusal in words, with `r` to resend a cast whose answer was lost). Three dispatch lanes: `Elections` (community sends), `ElectionsVta`, `ElectionsCast`.

## Transport and privacy decisions

- **Community reads and the ticket request are signed locally as the persona** (`config.get_persona_keys_for`) and sent with `community_send` — TSP when the membership was joined over TSP, else DIDComm — exactly as rooms and git-ns are; answers come back on the inbound channel and are taken only when both the transport sender and the document `issuer` are the community the view asks (thread id is a correlation key, not a credential). The election reply types are in the inbound gate census.
- **Ticket:** the VTA's `register` (no `member`) returns `{electionId, manifestDigest, request}`; its digest must equal the community's `show` digest or no ticket is taken; the request becomes `vtc/elections/tickets/issue/0.1`; its answer, without `ext`, goes to `voter/accept`. `ticketHeld` reads as "already held".
- **Voting with no ticket held takes the ticket and stops**, telling the member to come back later (a cast straight after its ticket could be paired by time). The ballot screen warns when this app took the ticket less than an hour ago (kept in memory only — see below).
- **Vote:** `show` is read again first; the ballot is checked locally; `vote/0.2` (open) or `vote-encrypted/0.3` with `ceremony` from `show` (a clear refusal when it is absent). The ballot box DID is resolved through the TDK resolver with a 15 s timeout; the cast is posted **unchanged** to `<base>/trust-tasks` with `vta_sdk::http::foreign_fetch_client_for(EndpointPolicy::process_default())` after `guard_foreign_url` (finite timeouts, no redirects, no proxy, guarded DNS — R1.2), from this client's own connection, never the member's messaging session. **Nothing sent to the community carries a ballot, a cast or a receipt** — `Request` has no variant that could, and a test holds it.
- **Signed documents are carried as received.** The manifest goes to the VTA as the community sent it (its digest is over its JSON, and the generated type rewrites timestamps), and the cast is taken from the VTA's raw answer, never re-serialised from the generated type.
- **contextId** is the persona's own context (`community_context::persona_context`), as the hidden-vetting vetter does.
- **Ballots are not logged.** `BallotDraft` / `AnswerDraft` / `Cast` have redacting `Debug`; the form is dropped once its cast is built.

## Divergences from the brief, and why

- The VTA calls go through `VtaClient::dispatch_trust_task_document` with locally pinned generated payload types (the `vetting::pcs_vta` precedent) instead of the SDK's `pcs_voter_*` wrappers: the wrappers re-serialise the manifest and the cast through typed structs, and keep a refusal's code only as text. Same tasks, same transport, same client.
- "Ticket taken less than an hour ago" is held in memory (`ElectionsState::tickets_taken`), so it does not survive a restart. Persisting it would add a per-election timestamp to the encrypted config for a warning; left out deliberately.

## Tests

- core unit (`openvtc-core/src/elections/tests.rs`, 29): every ballot rule (manifest mismatch; choice count / unknown / repeated; full and partial ranking; scores complete and in bounds; text length in scalar values; abstain only when optional, and alone; every question exactly once; unknown question), the draft, payload shapes for register (no `member`, manifest as received) / accept (`ext` dropped) / vote (open vs encrypted, `NoCeremony`) / receipt (whole document), receipt checks (wrong signer, wrong thread, wrong recipient, wrong type/shape, unsigned), refusal wording (each cast code distinct; community and VTA codes), the endpoint selection, the bounded pause, and that nothing sent to the community carries a ballot or cast.
- state/reducer (`openvtc/src/state_handler/elections_actions/tests.rs`, 10, + 5 form tests in `main_page/elections.rs`): paging and ordering, forged answers dropped, vote → re-read → register, closed election, no-ticket vote takes the ticket and stops (and records it), held ticket opens the ballot, review before cast, resend only after a lost answer, community refusal in words, Back through the screens.
- TUI (`ui/pages/main/mod.rs`): `e` opens the panel; detail/ballot/confirm keys (incl. text answers taking `a` and `Ctrl-a` blanking); `TestBackend` render of the disclosure (operator, same-operator warning, coercion statement) and the ballot, with and without the recent-ticket warning; communities key hints.
- **Integration** (`openvtc-core/tests/elections_vote_e2e.rs`, `#[ignore]`d like the other MockVta suites, run by the coverage job): a real in-process VTA (`MockVta`) with VTI's own registrar and ballot box (`vti-voting` 0.4, new dev-dependency — the line `vta-service` 0.67 already runs): register → registrar signs blind → accept → `ticketHeld` on repeat → vote → ballot box counts → receipt checked → VTA keeps it; a receipt signed by anyone else is refused. The HTTPS post itself is not exercised (the hardened client refuses loopback); the receipt is built as the ballot box answers it.

### Local CI (what `ci.yml` runs), all green

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test --workspace` — 2202 passed, 0 failed, 30 ignored
- `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features` — 2202 passed, 0 failed, 30 ignored
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides` — 1022 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` — clean
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core --test elections_vote_e2e -- --include-ignored` — 1 passed
- `trust-tasks -C openvtc-core check` — 52 pinned versions match the lock
- `scripts/check-release-guards.py` — ok (no version edited)

## Pre-merge checklist (`vti-stack-development-guide.md` §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — the cast uses the SDK's hardened foreign-fetch client; the ballot-box resolve has a 15 s timeout; community sends have the 30 s reply window.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — all network work runs in background dispatch jobs over owned data.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable (R2.1) — nothing is persisted; every step answers a repeat with its first answer (VTA register repeats the request until held, the community answers a resend as before, the ballot box answers the same cast with its receipt). A lost cast answer is resent unchanged, never rebuilt.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retry loop is added; resend is a member's keypress on the same document.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a, no new loop.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — the cast is dropped only after a receipt or a refusal; the form only after the VTA built the cast.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered (R3.*) — no hand-written wire types; every payload and response is a pinned generated type. JS consumers: n/a.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*) — no new config. Loopback/private ballot boxes only under the SDK's existing process-wide opt-in.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — "voted" only after a receipt is verified as the ballot box's for this cast; lost answer vs refusal vs unreadable vs unproven are distinct messages; panicked jobs end the flow with a message.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — see above; the only in-app state is display state.
- [x] Deviations flagged: the two divergences above (dispatch path; in-memory ticket timing).

body:
## Why

Members should be able to see their community's active elections, take a ticket and vote from the member portal. The portal is the community's own code and knows who is signed in, and the community is **never trusted to learn how anyone voted or to link a ticket to a cast** (VTI-VOT-001, `docs/05-design-notes/community-voting-threat-model.md`). So the portal can't render a ballot. It hands off to the member's wallet, the same way portal data rooms and forge-account linking do.

## What

- **`#/elections`**: the elections the roll admits the member to, actionable ones first, with stage and "you have your ticket".

title: feat(elections): window.vtaWallet.elections — vote from a community's portal
body:
## Why

Members should be able to see their community's active elections, take a ticket and vote from the VTC member portal. The portal is the community's own code and knows who is signed in, and the community is **never trusted to learn how anyone voted or to link a ticket to a cast** (VTI `docs/05-design-notes/community-voting-threat-model.md`). So the portal can't host the ballot. It hands off to the wallet, the same way portal data rooms (P7b) and forge-account linking (#369) do.

## What

`window.vtaWallet.elections.{list, show, takeTicket, vote}`:

| Call | Prompts | Page gets |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | no | elections the roll admits + whether the community issued the member's ticket |
| `show` | no | questions, schedule, disclosure — not parameters, ceremony or checkpoints |
| `takeTicket` | ticket window | `{ ticketHeld, taken }` |
| `vote` | ballot window (or ticket window if none held) | `{ ticketTaken }` only — the same whether the member cast, cancelled or failed |

- **Ballot in the wallet's window only** (`election-consent.tsx`, `kind=election`): choice / ranking / score / text, validated live by `ballotRefusal`, which mirrors `vti_voting::rules::check_ballot`.
- **Cast never passes the community**: the VTA builds and signs it under a one-time key (`vta/pcs/vote/0.2`, `vote-encrypted/0.3`); the offscreen document posts it to the ballot box's `TrustTaskHTTPS` door after a random pause of up to 20 s. `postCast` believes the receipt only once it is the ballot box's (proof, threadId, addressed to the cast's key), then hands it to the VTA (`voter/receipt/0.1`).
- **Reads and the ticket request** are signed as the member by their VTA (`voter/read/0.2`, `voter/register/0.2`) and posted to the community unchanged via `postCommunityTask`; the issued ticket is unblinded by `voter/accept/0.1` (payload sent without `ext`).
- **Ticket and vote apart in time**: `vote` with no ticket takes one and stops; a ballot opened within an hour of this wallet taking the ticket warns that the two can be paired. Only the time is stored, never a choice.
- **Gates** (`elections-page.ts`): the git channel's four, plus a host permission for the ballot box's origin before a ballot opens.
- `requestTask` now refuses `vta/pcs/` and `vtc/elections/`.
- New pins: `vta/pcs/voter/{read 0.2, register 0.2, accept 0.1, receipt 0.1}`, `vta/pcs/vote 0.2`, `vta/pcs/vote-encrypted 0.3`, `vtc/elections/{list 0.3, show 0.2, tickets/issue 0.1}`. The regenerated `app-state` modules only rename a shared import (`Key` → `Key_VtaV0_1`).

The reference client is `pnm elections` (`vta-cli-common/src/commands/elections.rs` in verifiable-trust-infrastructure). The VTC portal page that calls this is a follow-up PR in that repo.

## Tests

- core `tests/vtc.elections.mjs`: task shapes, ballot rules, the cast post and receipt checks (wrong signer, wrong thread, wrong ballot box, refusal codes).
- extension `tests/elections-page.test.mts`: gates; a declined and a cast ballot look identical to the page; no choice reaches the page; a failed cast is shown only in the wallet's window; `requestTask` refusals.
- extension `tests/elections-page-offscreen.test.mts`: against a signing community and ballot box — nothing the community receives carries a ballot or cast; the cast reaches the ballot box unchanged after a pause; the receipt goes to the VTA.
- extension `tests/election-consent.render.test.mts`: Cast disabled until valid; ballot bound to the digest; Cancel sends none; recent-ticket warning.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (all suites green), `check-task-versions.mjs` OK.

Not yet exercised against a live VTA + VTC + voting service.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — `guardedFetch` + `withFetchTimeout`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable (R2.1) — the VTA answers a repeated `voter/register` with the same request until the ticket is held, and the community answers a resent request with its first answer; the ticket time is written only after `accept`
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retry loop added; a resent cast gets the first receipt
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — none added
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, schema registered (R3.*) — generated types only
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*) — no host permission for the ballot box = no ballot
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*) — "voted" only on a verified receipt
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered (R2.1) — see above
- [x] Deviations: none

  the ballot box's HTTPS door after a random pause of up to 20 s — never

  (`voter/read/0.2`, `voter/register/0.2`) and posted to the community
  unchanged; the issued ticket is unblinded into the VTA (`voter/accept/0.1`).
- Ticket and vote apart in time: `vote` with no ticket takes one and stops,
  and a ballot opened within an hour of the ticket says it can be paired.
- `requestTask` refuses `vta/pcs/` and `vtc/elections/`.

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.5`) | `0.10.4` → `0.10.5` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.14` → `0.9.15` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(voting-service): GET /health and /health/ready
body:
The voting service served only `POST /trust-tasks`: no health path for an operator, and nothing showed whether the mediator session — how communities register, close and cancel elections — was up.

## Changes

- **`vti_common::host_session::supervise_reporting`** (additive): `supervise`, also reporting on a `watch::Sender<bool>` whether the identity is reachable through its mediator. `true` only while a session is served **and** its socket reports `ConnState::Connected`; `false` again on a socket drop (SDK reconnect under a live session), a lost session, or return (drop guard). Driven by the transport's own state, never latched at first connect (R6.2). `supervise` keeps its signature and delegates.
- **`GET /health`**: always `200` while serving; body `{status, did, messaging}` with `messaging` = `connected` / `notConnected` / `disabled`. For a proxy's upstream check — casts arrive over HTTPS and keep working while the mediator is away, so this never pulls the cast door.
- **`GET /health/ready`**: `200` only while the mediator session is connected, `503` otherwise, and always `503` without an `[identity]` (no community can reach a test `did:key`). For alerting.
- `docs/07-voting/README.md`: a *Health checks* section.

Both reads are unauthenticated and carry nothing the service's DID document doesn't already publish.

## Tests

- `health_without_messaging_is_alive_but_never_ready`
- `readiness_follows_the_mediator_session_both_ways` — connected → disconnected flips readiness back to 503 (not latched); `/health` stays 200 throughout.
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-voting-service` (16/16), host_session + vti-witness (84/84), clippy `-D warnings` on vti-common / vti-voting-service / vti-witness clean.

title: feat(cnm): offline election manifest init and check
body:
## What

Two offline `cnm` commands for writing an election manifest, the CLI counterpart to the console builder (#2364):

```sh
cnm elections manifest init --ballot-box <DID> [--id …] [--title …] [--out poll.json] [--force]
cnm elections manifest check poll.json
```

- **`init`** writes a starting manifest for this community: one yes/no question, open voting by its members, tickets from now, voting for a week from a day after the next whole hour. It goes to stdout unless `--out` is given (the banner is on stderr, so `> file` is clean), and won't replace an existing `--out` without `--force`.
- **`check`** checks a manifest as the community will and prints `manifestDigest`. It honours `--json`.
- Neither opens a session or resolves a DID. The community's DID comes from `--vtc-did` or the profile, and the error says to pass `--vtc-did` when neither is set.

## One implementation of the rules

`check` validates against the pinned `vtc/elections/create/0.3` schema (`ValidatedPayload`), then calls **`vti_voting::rules::check_new_manifest`**. This new public function covers every check the community runs that needs only the manifest and the clock:

- the manifest is in the current 0.2 shape;
- `check_manifest`'s cross-field rules (VTI-VOT-010, VTI-VOT-060 – 064);
- voting has not already closed.

`vtc-service`'s `elections::ops::check_create` now calls the same function, so the offline check can't drift from the server. Effect on the VTC: a 0.1-shaped manifest is now refused by name (the `require_current_manifest` message) instead of as a serde "missing field". Every other refusal is unchanged.

Still checked only at `create`, because they need the community itself: the ballot box is trusted (VTI-VOT-082), and the identifier is unused.

An `invalidManifest` refusal from `cnm elections create` now suggests `cnm elections manifest check`.

## Dependency note

`cnm-cli` now depends on `vti-voting`, which brings the arkworks/PCS stack into `cnm`'s closure. That stack is already in the workspace build through `vta-service`, which depends on `vti-voting` unconditionally. I chose this over copying the rules into `cnm`.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p vti-voting --test rules_and_tally`: 10 pass, including the new `vot_010_a_new_manifest_is_checked_against_the_clock`.
- `cargo test -p cnm-cli --bin cnm elections`: 6 pass. They cover:
  - the starter manifest passes as written, with a pinned schedule;
  - a schema error, broken selection bounds, a past close and a community mismatch are each named;
  - the digest matches the community's;
  - the `invalidManifest` hint.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service --features voting -E 'test(/election/)'`: 21 pass.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings --all-targets` for `vti-voting`, `cnm-cli`, and `vtc-service --features voting`; `cargo fmt`.
- Smoke-tested the binary: init → check ok, refuses to overwrite, community mismatch exits 1.

title: feat(vtc): guided election manifest builder in the admin console
body:
## What

**Governance → Elections → New election** is now a guided form instead of a raw JSON textarea.

- Steps: **About** (title, identifier that follows the title until edited, description, binding) → **Questions** (choice / ranking / score / free text, option editor with keys that follow labels, presets, reorder) → **Who votes** (roll rule + listed DIDs) → **Schedule** (local-time pickers stored as UTC, duration readout, early close) → **Counting** (ballot box, secrecy with trustees/threshold, board visibility, auditors, revote, running totals, text-release threshold) → **Review**.
- The review shows a plain-language summary, the JSON, and the `manifestDigest` computed locally (JCS → SHA-256 multihash → base58btc), with a warning that nothing can change after registration. Every remaining issue is listed with a *Go to* link; **Create** stays disabled until there are none. A binding election's button reads *Create and send for approval*.
- **Start from a previous election** copies questions, voters and counting into a fresh identifier and schedule.
- **JSON view** is the same value. Switching back reads it into the form. A manifest with a member the form doesn't edit is refused there and stays in JSON instead of being trimmed.
- The draft is kept in `sessionStorage` until it is created or discarded.

## Checks (a convenience — the community re-checks on create)

- **Schema bounds:** `MANIFEST_LIMITS` is pinned to the vendored `vti-specs-vtc/.../vtc/elections/create/0.3.bundle.json` by `election-manifest.test.ts`, which also checks that the rendered manifest and each question variant use only declared members and include every required one. The schema itself isn't evaluated in the browser: the console's CSP (`script-src 'self'`) rules out a compiling validator.
- **Cross-field rules:** mirrors `vti_voting::rules::check_manifest` (VTI-VOT-010, VTI-VOT-060 – 064) — times ordered and closing in the future, `minSelections ≤ maxSelections ≤ options`, score `min < max`, unique question/option keys, listed rolls non-empty, auditors and trustees are neither the community nor the ballot box, `2 ≤ threshold ≤ trustees ≤ 64`, no running totals for encrypted levels, totals-only means choice questions only, `textReleaseThreshold ≥ 10`.

## Also

- `unsupportedSecrecy` hint said "only open elections are served"; all three levels are served now (`vti_voting::rules::SERVED_LEVELS`).
- `sampleManifest` removed (replaced by the builder's defaults); `Refusal` moved to `ElectionRefusal.tsx` so both pages share it.
- Docs: `docs/03-vtc/elections.md` (*Writing the manifest in the console*), `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md` elections flow entry.

## Not in this PR

- A dropdown of trusted ballot boxes. The console has no way to read `[voting] trusted_ballot_boxes` yet; that needs a read task, specification first. Until then the ballot box is a free-text DID with a hint.

## Testing

- `npm run lint` (tsc + wire check), `npm run build`
- `npx vitest run`: 115 files, 1381 tests pass. New: `election-manifest.test.ts` (schema pin, round trip, rules, digest vector computed independently), plus four builder flows in `Elections.test.tsx` (step through and create, Create blocked with *Go to* fixes, draft survives remount, JSON view refuses an unknown member and round-trips an edit).

title: fix(vtc): show the join page to a member already signed in to the portal
body:
## Problem

Clicking **Join this community** while signed in to the member portal skipped the join page entirely. `Portal.tsx` checks for a session before it looks at `?join`, so `/members/?join` with a live session rendered the member's own pages. That meant:
- the join code was never shown;
- the browser wallet never ran;
- the "Join with a new identity" offer from #2362 / OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#398 could never appear.

To the member it looked as though Join just signed them in.

## Change

- `/members/?join` now shows the join page whether or not there is a session.
- When there is one, the page says "You're already signed in as a member", names the DID, and links to `/members/`.
- A wallet sign-in from the join page, where the community admits on the spot, replaces the URL with `/members/`, so the browser moves on to the member pages instead of reloading the join page.
- Updated docs: `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md`.

## Tests

- New `Portal` test: opened to join with a session, the join page shows, names who is signed in, and links to the member pages.
- Admin UI `vitest`: 1364 passed.
- `tsc -b`: clean.
author: stormer78

title: feat(vtc): mark the join page's wallet code with data-oob-intent=join
body:
## Problem

The join page (`/members/?join`) shows the same trigger link as the sign-in page. When a browser wallet already signs in to this community and the person clicks **Join**, it signs them straight in. They have no way to join again with a new identity.

## Change

- `WalletSignIn` adds `data-oob-intent="join"` to the code's `<a>` on the join page only.
- The VTA Wallet extension (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#398) reads the attribute and, for a community it already signs in to, shows a choice instead of signing in: sign in, or **Join with a new identity**. The new identity is made in a fresh context (`vtc-<host>-2`, …).
- The attribute only changes what the wallet offers. The link, the request and the protocol are unchanged, and a wallet that ignores the attribute behaves as before.
- Updated docs: `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` ("Joining from the browser").

## Tests

- New `WalletSignIn` test: the join page's code link carries the attribute, and the sign-in page's does not.
- `vitest` (`WalletSignIn`, `Portal`): 38 passed.
- `tsc -b`: clean.

title: feat(sign-in): join a community again with a new identity from its join page
author: stormer78

title: feat(sign-in): join a community again with a new identity from its join page (#398)
body:
feat(sign-in): join a community again with a new identity from its join page (#398)

A member who clicked a community's Join button was signed straight in: the code
is the same as the sign-in page's, and with one identity the wallet claims
without asking. And "new identity" reused the community context vtc-<host>,
which already held the member's DID, so the request went in as the member.

The portal now marks its join page's code data-oob-intent="join". The content
script passes that on with the click; for a community the wallet already signs
in to, the confirm screen then waits, says the person is already a member, and
offers join-new beside signing in. join-new reads the manifest as for an
unknown community, leaves out the identities already used there, and makes the
new identity in the first of vtc-<host>, vtc-<host>-2, … holding none of them —
an unfinished join's context is still reused on retry.

The page's mark changes only what the person is offered; nothing is sent until
they choose (VTI-LNK-056 property 4 holds: nothing goes back to the page).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Updates `wrangler` from 4.151.3 to 4.154.0
Release notes

Sourced from wrangler's releases.

wrangler@4.154.0

Minor Changes

  • #16494 0968b08 Thanks @​petebacondarwin! - Enable Miniflare's development registry by default and centralize path resolution

    In Miniflare v5 beta, resolve the registry from CLOUDFLARE_DEV_REGISTRY_PATH, then the unsafeDevRegistryPath constructor option, then <Cloudflare config directory>/dev-registry/v5. The default is independent of legacy Wrangler directories and is scoped to the Miniflare major version. The Vite v2 beta plugin follows this new default, while current Wrangler and getPlatformProxy() retain Wrangler's legacy default for compatibility with existing Wrangler sessions. Vite v2 and Wrangler therefore require the same CLOUDFLARE_DEV_REGISTRY_PATH to discover each other; set it for both processes when mixing these tools.

    Add enableDevRegistry: false to disable registration and discovery explicitly. Shared storage now uses the resolved default without requiring an explicit path. As before, shared storage requires an enabled registry to elect a storage owner, so combining unsafeEnableSharedStorage: true with enableDevRegistry: false is rejected. Miniflare no longer reads MINIFLARE_REGISTRY_PATH; use CLOUDFLARE_DEV_REGISTRY_PATH instead. Expose resolveDevRegistryPath() for integrations that also read registry files. Wrangler uses the effective path for its runtime configuration, initial bindings display, and Flagship active-session check, so the canonical override cannot bypass that check. An explicitly disabled Wrangler registry remains disabled.

Patch Changes

  • #16499 f3c13b3 Thanks @​dinasaur404! - Preserve binding error codes and names in local development

    Errors from remote bindings and from Node.js binding proxies (getPlatformProxy() and Miniflare#getBindings()) now keep their machine-readable properties, such as Artifacts' code and numericCode. Previously these properties were dropped and the error name was folded into the message (for example "ArtifactsError: Repository not found"), so code could only branch on error text during local development.

    Node.js callers also keep custom error names such as ArtifactsError. Errors from remote bindings received inside a Worker keep their properties but are still named Error.

  • Updated dependencies [0968b08, f3c13b3]:

    • miniflare@5.20261023.1-beta

wrangler@4.153.0

Minor Changes

  • #14865 c0e915f Thanks @​TheSaiEaranti! - Add an --infer-origin-from-routes flag to wrangler dev

    When a config has routes, local dev infers the origin from the first route, so the Worker sees request.url, the Host header, and any Origin header rewritten to the route's host even though the client connected to localhost. That silently breaks Host/Origin-sensitive logic — for example a CORS check allowlisting http://localhost:* receives http://<route-host> instead and rejects the request only in local dev.

    The inference is intentional and remains the default. Passing --infer-origin-from-routes=false now opts out, preserving the real local origin without removing routes from the config. An explicitly configured --host, --local-upstream, or dev.host continues to take precedence either way. The flag only affects local development: in remote mode the route host still determines the preview session as before.

  • #15955 23ef63a Thanks @​ericclemmons! - Expand dotenv variable references in --secrets-file input

    Dotenv files supplied through --secrets-file to deploy, versions upload, and preview now expand $VAR and ${VAR} references using process values and earlier file values. Process environment values override matching file keys, including explicitly empty values. Treat dotenv secrets files as trusted input: they can read and upload any process environment value, such as a CI credential referenced by X=${GITHUB_TOKEN}. In CI, use secrets files whose contents untrusted contributors cannot modify.

    This changes how existing dotenv secrets files are interpreted: an unset reference becomes an empty string, so PASSWORD=pa$word becomes pa when word is unset. Escape literal dollar signs with a backslash (PASSWORD=pa\$word), or use a JSON secrets file to preserve values exactly. JSON input and bulk-secret commands, including piped stdin, retain their existing literal parsing.

Patch Changes

  • #16403 5f82a56 Thanks @​dependabot! - Update DEFAULT_COMPAT_DATE to 2026-10-22

    Use the bundled workerd release's compatibility date by default when scaffolding new projects or when no compatibility date is configured.

title: Refuse forked did:scid logs, and require witnesses for the did:scid form (VTI-KEY-162, VTI-KEY-165, VTI-KEY-168, VTI-VTA-034, VTI-VTA-038)
body:
Follow-up to #84. This comes from analysing what an attacker can do with a leaked update key.

**The threat.** To forge a did:webvh identity, an attacker needs the update key *and* write access to the host its identifier names. A did:scid names no host. So a fork signed with a leaked key and served from any host is the *same* identity, and it can be numbered past the latest version a node has verified.

**The changes:**
- **VTI-KEY-162:** refuse a log that does not contain the version already verified (a fork), not only an older log. This applies to the known-source cross-check too. Implemented in affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#981 (resolver 0.8.44).
- **VTI-KEY-165:** an identity may be presented as did:scid only if its log is **witnessed**, meaning:
  - every version, from the first one presented in that form, carries the witness approvals its threshold requires;
  - the threshold can't be met by witnesses the update-key holder controls;
  - each witness refuses to approve an entry that conflicts with one it already approved.

  New did:scid identities are witnessed from version 1. This puts back the second factor the host used to provide, including for a verifier that knows nothing about the identity yet.
- **VTI-KEY-168:** an existing log may switch to did:scid only once it is witnessed, and only once the node holds no private key that an unwitnessed version committed to as an update key. Witnesses approve only from the version after they are named, so a fork from an earlier version needs no approvals.
- **VTI-VTA-034 / VTI-VTA-038:** the VTA refuses to create a did:scid identity it cannot have witnessed from version 1. It refuses to switch an unwitnessed log, and never adds witnesses as part of a switch.
- **Rationale** explains all of this, and notes that witnesses do nothing against an old copy served from a former host (that copy carries genuine approvals). The version floor covers that case.

**Implementation note.** On VTI main, create/1.2 can present did:scid without witnesses. It will need to refuse, or attach the operator's witnesses, before it conforms. The switch task isn't implemented yet.

Refuse forked did:scid logs, and require witnesses for the did:scid form (VTI-KEY-162, VTI-KEY-165, VTI-KEY-168, VTI-VTA-034, VTI-VTA-038) (#85)

Under did:scid a fork signed with a leaked update key and served from any
host is the same identity, and can be numbered past the latest version a
node verified. VTI-KEY-162 now refuses a log that does not contain the
version verified, not only an older one, including against known sources.
VTI-KEY-165 requires an identity presented as did:scid to be witnessed by a
threshold the update-key holder cannot meet alone, with witnesses that refuse
a conflicting entry; VTI-KEY-168 lets an existing log switch only once it is

title: feat(sign-in): an identity that is already a member signs in instead of joining
body:
## Problem

A member whose wallet has no record of a community is shown the join flow. That happens when they joined from another wallet, or when the wallet's entry for the community was removed. If they then send a request as their member DID, it used to be queued and fail only once an administrator approved it. The same happens with the "new identity" option when the community's context (`vtc-<host>`) already holds their member DID, because creating that identity reuses the DID already in the context.

## Change

OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2360 makes the community refuse such a submission at once, with `vtc/join-requests/submit:alreadyMember`. On that answer the wallet now:

- keeps the vault entry it has just recorded for that DID,
- goes to the ordinary **Sign in to <host>?** screen for the same code, with `alreadyMember: true`,
- shows the note "You're already a member of <host>, so no request was sent", and doesn't skip the screen even for a single identity.

The wallet does not ask the community which of the person's DIDs are members beforehand. That would reveal their identities before they had chosen one (VTI-LNK-073).

Against a community that predates #2360, nothing changes: the request is queued as before.

## Tests

- `sign-in-flows`: on `alreadyMember` the flow goes to confirm, keeps the entry, and the claim proceeds.
- `sign-in-view.render`: the note is shown and no claim is sent automatically.
- `npm run build`, `npm run lint` and `npm test`: all pass (1366 extension tests).

title: feat(vtc): refuse a join submission from a current member at submit
body:
## Problem

A join request from a DID that is already a current member was accepted and queued for review. It was refused only when an administrator approved it, by the admit effect's duplicate-access-list guard (`ceremony/execute.rs`). So the administrator spent a review on a request that could never succeed, and the applicant was never told to sign in instead.

This now matters more because of the website's **Join this community** button (#2353). A member whose wallet has no record of the community lands on the join flow, and their member DID appears among the identities they can apply as.

## Change

- `submit_inner` refuses a DID present in the access list before anything is stored, with `SubmitRefusal::AlreadyMember`.
- The Trust Task surface answers it with `vtc/join-requests/submit:alreadyMember`. The code is consumer-minted under SPEC.md §8.5, the same way as `requestAlreadyOpen`. A client that doesn't recognise it falls back to `taskFailed`.
- The code is listed in the error-code census's `CONSUMER_MINTED` and exported as `vta_sdk::protocols::join_requests::JOIN_REQUEST_SUBMIT_ERR_ALREADY_MEMBER`.
- "Current" means present in the access list, matching the invitations route. A departed member, whose member record remains only as a tombstone, may still re-join.
- The admit-time guard stays, because it still catches someone admitted while their request was open.
- Updated docs: `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` ("Joining from the browser").

The browser wallet side is OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#397: on `alreadyMember` the wallet goes to the sign-in screen for the same code.

## Tests

- New: `rest_submit_refuses_a_current_member_before_review` checks the code is returned and nothing is queued.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3581 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p vta-sdk --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

title: fix(admin-ui): passkey admin invites sign, and the wallet claim finds a late wallet
body:
Two console bugs on admin invites.

**1. Minting a passkey invite: "Invite failed: JCS cannot encode value of type undefined".**
`CreateInviteForm` sent `{ did: undefined, … }`; the console signs over JCS (`lib/jcs.ts`), which deliberately refuses `undefined`. The same broke a wallet invite with a blank label, and *Regenerate* on a passkey invite. Optional members are now omitted.

Tests missed it because `test/signed-read.ts` (the signed-post stand-in) serialised with `JSON.stringify`, which drops `undefined`. It now runs `jcsCanonicalize` first, so every component test refuses what the real signer refuses — with that change alone, both existing invite tests failed with the production error.

**2. Wallet invitation install page shows no button.**
`Install` read `isWalletApproverEnrolmentAvailable()` once at first render, but the extension injects `window.vtaWallet` via a module `<script>` from its content script, which can run after the page renders. A wallet-kind token then hid the passkey button and never showed the wallet one. The page now re-probes for 3 s and on `vtawallet:ready` / `vtawallet:unlocked`; the fallback text now says the page cannot see the plugin and to check it has access to this site. The lead text no longer says "passkey ceremony" for wallet invitations.

Tests: `npx vitest run` — 1362 passed; `tsc --noEmit` clean. New test: a provider arriving after first render makes the wallet button appear.

title: vtc-service-v0.17.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A Join button on the landing page and a join page in the member portal ([#2353](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2353))

The default landing page's main call to action is now "Join this community",
  opening /members/?join: the member portal's sign-in page worded for a newcomer.
  It shows the same wallet code under "Join with your wallet", the browser
  wallet's install guide, and none of the options that need a membership
  (portal passkeys, the older SIOPv2 sign-in). The sign-in page links to it for
  visitors who are not members yet.

  The page changes words only. The wallet decides what a code means: for a
  community it holds no identity for, it offers to join (vtc/join-requests/*),
  which the VTA Wallet extension does by setting up a new identity for the
  community at the person's VTA. Under the default join criteria an
  administrator reviews the request, and the person then signs in on the
  ordinary page.

- **vtc**: The member portal adds files to open rooms ([#2350](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2350))

#2341 hid the portal's file upload on an open room, because a file's
  manifest could only travel inside a sealed body. rooms/records/put/0.4
  (trust-tasks-tf #987, VTI #2348) lets an open room's record carry its file
  and the random key it is sealed under, and the browser plugin writes and
  reads one (vta-browser-plugin #393).

  - The AddToRoom card offers a file on every tier. On an open room its note
    says a file is stored encrypted under a key its record carries in the
    clear, so the host can read it as well as its members.
  - A file on an open room is checked against the digest its record states,
    not one its author signed (the record is not signed by its author), and
    the record view says so.

- **rooms**: Files in open rooms — serve rooms/records/put/0.4 and rooms/keys/act/0.9 ([#2348](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2348))

An open room could hold notes and nothing else: a file's manifest only
  travelled inside a sealed body, and its key could only be derived from a
  storage key an open room does not have. rooms/records/put/0.4
  (trust-tasks-tf #987) puts the manifest in cleartext.file, with the random
  key its blob is sealed under in fileKey; rooms/keys/act/0.9 ([#990](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/990)) adds put
  0.4 to the closed table a member's VTA completes.

  Hosts (room-host, vtc-service, through vti-rooms):
  - Serve rooms/records/put/0.4 beside 0.3. The cleartext, file included, is
    stored and served as received (Host item 13).
  - On an open room, refuse as malformedRequest a record whose blobs is not
    exactly [cleartext.file.blobRef], or whose file has no fileKey — before
    blobNotFound and before anything changes (Host item 12). 0.3 is unchanged.

title: vta-service-v0.69.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Serve vta/webvh/dids/update/1.1 — list or remove an existing log's did:scid alias ([#2354](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2354))

* feat(vta)!: serve vta/webvh/dids/update/1.1 — list or remove an existing log's did:scid alias

  Every did:webvh log is also `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>`; the two forms are one
  subject only while the did:webvh document lists
  `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=<source>` in `alsoKnownAs` (VTI-KEY-164).
  create/1.2 lists it at creation. update/1.1 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#992)
  adds `scidAlsoKnownAs` so an operator can list or remove it on a log that
  already exists, without building the DID URL or sending a whole document.

  VTA (one handler serves 1.0 and 1.1; 1.1 extends 1.0):
  - `<source>` derived by `vta_sdk::did_scid::scid_forms` (`:` -> `/`,
    percent-encoding kept), applied to `document` or the current document.
    `true` appends unless listed and replaces a stale `src` in place; `false`
    removes every did:scid entry for the SCID.
  - `scidAliasRequired` when the VTA presents the identity as its did:scid
    (VTI-KEY-166): the `presented` flag create/1.2 records on the did:scid
    identity (`webvh_store::ScidIdentity`), or `vta_did` being this log's
    did:scid. Also refuses a supplied `document` that drops the alias, under
    1.0 too (as a validation error).
  - `noChange` when the resulting document and parameters equal the latest
    entry's: nothing published, no rotation.
  - Otherwise a document change: publishes and rotates the update key, so the
    task stays Destructive. The response reports `scidAlsoKnownAs` and
    `scidDidUrl`; 1.0 and rotate-keys responses are unchanged.
  - The did:scid identity record follows the published document, so the
    did:scid DID addresses the log exactly while the alias is listed.

- **rooms**: Files in open rooms — serve rooms/records/put/0.4 and rooms/keys/act/0.9 ([#2348](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2348))

An open room could hold notes and nothing else: a file's manifest only
  travelled inside a sealed body, and its key could only be derived from a
  storage key an open room does not have. rooms/records/put/0.4
  (trust-tasks-tf #987) puts the manifest in cleartext.file, with the random
  key its blob is sealed under in fileKey; rooms/keys/act/0.9 ([#990](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/990)) adds put
  0.4 to the closed table a member's VTA completes.

  Hosts (room-host, vtc-service, through vti-rooms):
  - Serve rooms/records/put/0.4 beside 0.3. The cleartext, file included, is
    stored and served as received (Host item 13).
  - On an open room, refuse as malformedRequest a record whose blobs is not
    exactly [cleartext.file.blobRef], or whose file has no fileKey — before
    blobNotFound and before anything changes (Host item 12). 0.3 is unchanged.

title: vti-voting-v0.6.0
body:
### Changed

- **specs**: Take every Trust Task wire type from the generated vti-specs crates ([#2343](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2343))

Every `trust_tasks_rs::specs::<family>` path becomes `vti_specs::<family>`
  (`vti_specs_rooms::rooms` in vti-rooms, which stays wasm-light), and every
  `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::*` call becomes `vti_specs::schema_index::*`,
  which answers for exactly the versions the vti-specs-* locks pin. The
  framework's own specs are re-exported from vti_specs unchanged.

  No crate turns a trust-tasks-rs spec family on any more: the workspace
  compiles none of the deprecated prebuilt modules, only `validate`.

  The generated types are the same generator's output at the same module paths,
  but they are distinct Rust types from the prebuilt ones: a downstream crate
  that passes a `trust_tasks_rs::specs` value into a vta-sdk API must move its
  import to `vta_sdk::specs` (a find-and-replace).

  CLAUDE.md's rule now points at the generated crates and says how to pin a
  version; the SPEC FAMILIES notes in Cargo.toml are replaced.



### Fixed

- **voting,witness,persona**: Board read at voting/board/read 0.2, witness evidence at witness/session 0.2 only, the persona timeline answer at 1.1 ([#2334](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2334))

trust-tasks-rs marks voting/board/read/0.1, witness/session/0.1,
  witness/session/submit/0.1 and persona/profile/timeline/1.0 superseded.
  Every party to each is in this workspace or has already moved, so each moves
  to its current version alone.

  voting/board/read 0.1 -> 0.2. A lifecycle entry's (opened, closed,
  closedEarly, cancelled) instant is `occurredAt`, as voting/_shared/0.2 and
  its CONVENTIONS §1 name it, not `at`.
  - The ballot box writes lifecycle entries with `occurredAt`, serves
    board/read at 0.2 only (0.1 is `unsupportedVersion`), and reads
    `occurredAt` when it replays its journal.
  - The VTC sends board/read at 0.2; the auditor (vti_voting::audit and its
    encrypted levels) reads `occurredAt`.
  - A leaf hash is over the entry's member names, so an entry journalled with
    `at` cannot be renamed without changing the board. Like a 0.1 manifest
    ([#2317](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2317)) it is refused by name: the ballot box will not restore a journal
    holding one, and the auditor reports it as unreadable rather than as
    "voting opened before votingOpensAt". Finish or cancel open elections
    before upgrading.

  witness/session 0.1 and submit 0.1. vti-witness and the VTA already serve
  only 0.2 ([#2147](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2147)), and openvtc main sends 0.2. The VTC no longer pairs outcome
  evidence from a 0.1 session with a submit/0.1 response: such evidence pairs
  with nothing.

  persona/profile/timeline 1.0 -> 1.1. The SDK already sent 1.1 but parsed the
  answer as the 1.0 response, whose events require `at`; a 1.1 answer names it
  `occurredAt`, so it failed to parse. `VtaClient::persona_profile_timeline`
  now returns the 1.1 response.

title: npm(deps): bump the npm-security group across 1 directory with 2 updates

Bumps the npm-security group with 2 updates in the / directory: [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) and [zod](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod). Updates `undici` from 7.29.1 to 7.30.1
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 · GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

When an originless Agent combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()), a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 · GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

An exception thrown by a downstream response handler from an asynchronous decompression callback could escape as an uncaught exception. A server could trigger this when decompress was composed with a handler such as dump with a size limit. This release converts downstream handler exceptions into per-request errors.

Subresource Integrity bypass with non-lowercase algorithm tokens

CVE-2026-109841 · GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472

fetch() treated valid mixed-case or uppercase SRI algorithm tokens, such as SHA256, as unknown and could accept a response whose body did not match the configured digest. This release normalizes algorithm tokens before validation and digest selection.

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

title: Switch an identity's presented form between did:webvh and did:scid (VTI-KEY-168, VTI-KEY-169, VTI-VTA-038, VTI-VTA-039, VTI-VTC-005)
body:
Closes #81. Follow-up to #80.

**Scope.** A held identity (trust context, persona, group, room) can be switched between the two forms in either direction. A node's own durable identity cannot: its form is part of the key of state that cannot follow it (mediator registration, deployment configuration, and a VTC's member pseudonyms, which are a digest over the community DID).

- **VTI-KEY-168 — switch.** Switching to did:scid requires the alias to be listed already, and a switch publishes no version. From the switch, the node names the identity in the new form wherever it names it as itself: sender, issuer, proof verification method, and a context's primary DID. Artefacts issued in the former form stay valid and are not re-issued.
- **VTI-KEY-169 — carrying standing.** This covers ACL entries, ownership, membership, administrator status, consent grants and credential subjects.
  - **Recognition (MUST):** standing carries if the webvh document has listed the alias in every version since the standing was recorded.
  - **Migration (MAY):** anything recorded before the alias (which VTI-KEY-167 refuses to carry) can be carried only by migration. That is a new grant by the recording node, on the subject's request signed in the new form, after it checks that the alias is listed now.
  - **Sessions never carry.**
- **VTI-KEY-164/165/167 amended** to point at these rules. VTI-KEY-164's open-ended "MAY treat as one subject" becomes "only as VTI-KEY-169 provides".
- **VTI-VTA-038 — the switch on the VTA.**
  - Gated as an update.
  - Refuses a switch to did:scid without the alias, and never lists the alias itself (listing rotates the update key and needs its own consent).
  - Refuses node identities and no-op switches.
  - Re-points the primary DID of every context naming either form, and reports the form it now presents.
- **VTI-VTA-039.** The VTA migrates its own records for the identity in the same change as the switch: ACL entries, consent grants, passkeys and issued-credential holders. It also ends sessions opened under the former form.
- **VTI-VTC-005.** A VTC recognises either form per VTI-KEY-169, and lets members and administrators migrate as it lets them rotate, without re-vetting. It never switches its own identity.

Trust Task and implementation follow once this reads right.

title: Switch an identity's presented form between did:webvh and did:scid (VTI-KEY-168, VTI-KEY-169, VTI-VTA-038, VTI-VTA-039, VTI-VTC-005) (#84)
body:
Switch an identity's presented form between did:webvh and did:scid (VTI-KEY-168, VTI-KEY-169, VTI-VTA-038, VTI-VTA-039, VTI-VTC-005) (#84)

VTI-KEY-168 lets the update authority switch the form a held identity (context,
persona, group, room) is presented in, either way, never a node's own durable
identity; switching to did:scid needs the alias listed and publishes nothing.
VTI-KEY-169 carries standing across forms by recognition when the alias has
been listed in every version since it was recorded, and otherwise by
migration on the subject's request in the new form; sessions never carry.
VTI-VTA-038/039 put the switch on the VTA, re-pointing contexts and migrating
the VTA's own records; VTI-VTC-005 has a VTC recognise and migrate members.

Closes #81.

body:
The Release PR #2349 fails `lockfile self-pins` / `release bump is large enough`: 15 crates move an internal dependency's floor (`vta-sdk` ^0.77, `vti-specs-*` ^0.2, …) on a patch bump.

publish.yml's fix step should have raised them, but it crashed:

```
error: failed to select a version for the requirement `vti-specs = "^0.1"`
required by package `vti-e2e-tests v0.6.0 (…/tests/e2e)`
```

**Cause:** `manifests()` globbed `*/Cargo.toml`, one level deep, so the raise never rewrote `tests/e2e/Cargo.toml`. That file has required `vti-specs` by version since #2343.

**Fix:** list the members with `cargo metadata --no-deps`, once, before the first edit. A tree whose requirements disagree doesn't load, so it can't be read later. Each crate's manifest and changelog are then found by that path.

**Verified:** I ran the fixed script on a scratch checkout of the #2349 branch. It converged in two rounds, raising 20 crates, and both guards pass:

```
release guard: 32 published members checked
no proposed version falls in a line a release branch owns
```

Once this merges, the next publish.yml run regenerates the Release PR and applies the raise automatically.

fix(scripts): fix-release-bump-sizes finds nested workspace members (#2358)

The script listed manifests with a one-level glob (`*/Cargo.toml`), so a raise
never reached `tests/e2e/Cargo.toml`, which requires `vti-specs` by version
since #2343. Raising vti-specs to 0.2.0 left that requirement at ^0.1, `cargo
update --workspace` refused the tree, and publish.yml's fix step failed on the
Release PR (#2349) instead of pushing the raise.

It now reads the members from `cargo metadata --no-deps` once, before the first
edit (a tree with disagreeing requirements does not load), and finds each
crate's manifest and changelog by that path rather than by its name.

title: docs(design-notes): key roles — the level is set per service through the DID template; retiring the old key on a raise is a SHOULD
body:
Docs only, no code. Records two maintainer decisions of 2026-10-31 in `docs/05-design-notes/key-roles.md`:

- **§5.4 The level is set per service.** The default key assurance level and a binding floor come from the service's DID template (`defaults.keyAssurance: { level, minimum }`), on the same one-way rule the template already applies to `portable`: it can tighten what a caller asked for, never loosen it. Resolution order is `--level`, then the template, then `[dids] default_level`, then 1. A proposed default and floor for every built-in template is tabled for confirmation: community, registry, witness, ballot box and the VTA's own identity default to 2; mediator, push gateway, rooms, integrations and the generic hosting shapes to 1; a VTN template, when one exists, to 3.
- **§15 The old key on a raise.** Retiring or revoking the replaced key is a SHOULD, not a MUST. `previousKeys` becomes `retire | revoke | keep`; a kept key is bound as `operational` only, which is the custody it already had, and VTI-KEY-201 keeps everything it signed a level-1 artefact.

Neither changes conformance. The draft spec PRs trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#82 and trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#993 still say MUST retire or revoke and are flagged for amendment. The visual summary is updated to match.

**Added in a second commit: §12.7 Post-quantum custody.** FROST cannot carry a post-quantum key, and no post-quantum threshold signature is standardised. The pre-rotation commitment is a hash and already quantum-safe; only the signature at recovery time must be post-quantum. The plan is FROST over Ed25519 now; when wanted, a hybrid custodian with one whole ML-DSA-44 key per custodian and a policy-enforced t-of-n proof set beside the FROST signature; later, a true post-quantum threshold scheme. Each step is one witnessed entry on the same DID. The visual summary carries the same note.

**Added in a third commit, after reviewer feedback: §1.1 Threat model and §12.0.** The note now defines the adversaries each level answers (A1–A7), as a primary classical model and a secondary quantum-capable model, which differ only at the recovery custodian. §12.0 answers the reviewer's question of whether threshold cryptography is needed at all: a policy threshold of whole, FIPS-approved keys does the job with no DKG, nonces or ceremonies and is post-quantum with ML-DSA. It is recommended as the baseline form, with FROST kept as an option within the primary model, pending the maintainer's decision (open question 10). The spec amendments that decision would need are listed.

**Fourth commit: FROST dropped.** Decided after review: the threshold custodian is a condition over whole keys (n members, each a whole recovery key, t must authorize, counted by the witness and verifiers). §12 rewritten, §12.0 records the reasoning, §12.7 simplified. trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#82 and trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#993 are amended to match (VTI-KEY-210–221 revised; `ThresholdRecoveryCommitment` on the wire; no ceremony tasks).

**Fifth commit: the three remaining decisions.** Per-template levels as tabled in §5.4 (every floor 1 except a future VTN's); two verifier profiles, `compatible` by default and `recommended` one setting away (§19.4); no recovery hold period (§18 item 5). No open question remains for the maintainer.
