title: feat(manager): list or remove a DID's did:scid alias (vta/webvh/dids/update 1.1)
body:
## What this does

An operator viewing a did:webvh DID in the console can see whether its document lists the log's did:scid alias, and list or remove it. Every did:webvh log is also `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>`, but the two forms are one subject only while the did:webvh document lists `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=<source>` in `alsoKnownAs` (VTI-KEY-164).

**Core** (`feat(core)`)
- `webvhDidUpdate` sends `vta/webvh/dids/update/1.1` and takes `scidAlsoKnownAs`. `false` is sent explicitly (`!== undefined`), never dropped as if it meant nothing. The client never builds the DID URL: the agent derives it and returns it as `scidDidUrl`.
- `trust-tasks.toml` moves the pin from 1.0 to 1.1 and `src/specs` is regenerated. 1.1 `extends` 1.0. `budget.ts`, test fixtures and example URIs follow the pin.

**Console** (`feat(manager)`)
- The DID detail reads the alias state from the latest log entry's `alsoKnownAs`. It is one of three: **listed**, **listed for an old location** (a did:scid entry for this SCID whose `src` is missing or is not where the log is served now), or **not listed**. `manager/scid-alias.ts` works out the current `src` only to compare against it, and never to build a request.
- The actions are *List the did:scid alias*, *List it for this location* and *Remove the did:scid alias*. They are `Destructive`s like Delete and Realign keys, so a `consentRequired` reply gets the match-code ceremony. The preview leads with the consequence the spec requires a consent surface to state: publishing **rotates the DID's update key**, and the entry is permanent. The request also sends `expectedVersionId`, the version the log was read at.
- Refusals are matched on their code. `noChange` is treated as an answer, not an error: nothing was published and the key did not rotate. `scidAliasRequired`, `versionConflict` and `notFound` are each explained in plain words. If the agent lists an identity as did:scid, the console does not offer removal.
- After publishing, the panel shows the reported `scidDidUrl` with a copy button, in the create pane's style (#392). The log and the list are then re-read.

## Pins

`vta/webvh/dids/update` 1.1 is pinned from the registry (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#992, deployed; digest `sha256:92f28b5b324f…`). `task-surface.json` is resynced from vta-sdk main, which serves 1.1 since OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2354.

The VTA has to serve 1.1 when this lands. Plugin and VTA cut over together, with no fold for an agent that only speaks 1.0.

## Tests

- `packages/core/tests/webvh.dids-servers-names.mjs` checks the type and the response type, and that the flag is sent when given (including `false`) and absent when not.
- `packages/extension/tests/scid-alias.test.mts` covers source derivation (a percent-encoded port stays encoded), the three states, a prefix SCID and a malformed `alsoKnownAs`.
- `packages/extension/tests/did-scid-alias.render.test.mts` covers each state on screen, and that the rotation copy appears before anything is sent. It checks the exact payload (`true` / explicit `false`, `expectedVersionId`, no DID URL), the `scidDidUrl` and copy button after success, `noChange` and `scidAliasRequired` by code, no removal for a did:scid identity, and the consent ceremony.

`npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` pass locally. `tests/specs.generated.mjs` passes against the local lock.

`scripts/check-task-versions.mjs` reports two errors, both outside this change: `rooms/records/put/0.3` and `rooms/keys/act/0.8` in the offscreen bundle. They were already there: CI on main (`0dcb2eb`, #393) is red.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — goes through the existing manager relay
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — nothing stored locally; `expectedVersionId` makes a stale retry refuse
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retries
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — the schema is from the 1.1 spec; errors are matched on code (R3.7)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — "published" only on the agent's reply; `noChange` says nothing was published
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — the console keeps no state; reopening the DID re-reads the log
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.36.4
body:
### Added

- **vta/webvh/dids/update**: 1.1 lists or removes an existing log's did:scid alias ([#992](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/992))

* feat(vta/webvh/dids/update): 1.1 lists or removes an existing log's did:scid alias

  Every did:webvh log is also a did:scid:vh:1 identity, but the two are distinct
  subjects until the did:webvh document lists the did:scid DID URL in
  alsoKnownAs (VTI-KEY-164). create/1.2 lists it in the first entry by default;
  a log created before it, or without it, had no way to get it but sending a
  whole replacement document with a hand-built DID URL — and the src encoding
  (`%3A` for a port, `/` for each `:`) is exactly what a client gets wrong.

  1.1 adds `scidAlsoKnownAs` (boolean): true lists the DID URL for the log's
  current location (replacing one left from before a move), false removes
  every did:scid entry naming this SCID. The agent derives the DID URL; the
  caller never writes it. The response reports `scidAlsoKnownAs` and
  `scidDidUrl`. New codes: `scidAliasRequired` (removing the alias of an
  identity the agent presents as did:scid, VTI-KEY-166) and `noChange` (an
  entry identical to the latest is not published, so the update key is not
  rotated for nothing).

  This is the pre-key-role path: vta/dids/update refuses every identity created
  before key roles (notKeyRoleIdentity), which is every did:webvh DID that
  exists today. Only adds, so 1.1 extends 1.0. All four bindings regenerated.

- **peer-check**: Peer-check/ask 0.1 — a signed yes or no from a peer's own device ([#973](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/973))

* feat(peer-check): peer-check/ask 0.1 — a signed yes or no from a peer's own device

  One party asks another a short question, such as "did you just ask me
  for this?", over a channel they already share. The responder's device
  prompts its user and returns a signed answer that echoes the challenge
  and carries the task digest of the request, so the asker can verify it
  against the responder's DID and it cannot be replayed against another
  ask.

  Draft. Specification, schema, negative examples and the regenerated Rust,
  TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings.

- **rooms/keys/act**: 0.9 completes rooms/records/put/0.4 ([#990](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/990))

rooms/records/put/0.4 ([#987](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/987)) lets a record on an open room carry a file,
  its description and random file key in cleartext.file. 0.8's table is
  closed (Recipient item 1) and names records/put at 0.1–0.3 only, so a
  conforming key holder refuses 0.4 with typeNotActable: a member whose keys
  their key holder holds could upload an open room's blob (upload/begin/0.2
  is in the table) but never write the record that names it, and the blob
  would sit unreferenced until collected.

  0.9 adds rooms/records/put/0.4 to the put row, write, presentation
  inserted, completed exactly as 0.3. The key holder neither mints nor checks
  the file key: the producer mints it (put 0.4 Producer item 7), the host
  checks the record (Host item 12), and the key holder signs what it was
  handed unaltered (Recipient item 6).

  Schemas are 0.8's and no error code is added; the table only widens, so
  0.9 declares extends: "0.8" and every spec naming 0.8 stays current. All
  four bindings regenerated.

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|

| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.36.3` → `0.36.4` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.28.3` → `0.28.4` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.4`) | `0.10.3` → `0.10.4` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.13` → `0.9.14` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: docs(design-notes): key roles — signing vs encryption keys, per-role rationale, a community in operation, principles and the balance
body:
Docs only, no code. Follow-up to #2352. Expands `docs/05-design-notes/key-roles.md` for readers who are not deep in the details, and records the reasoning behind choices the specification only states. Nothing normative changes.

- **§3 Signing keys and encryption keys.** Four of the five roles are signing keys; `messaging` is the only encryption key. What a stolen copy of each lets an attacker do (forge vs read), how each rotates, why one key must not do both (VTI-KEY-114, 184), and how TSP, DIDComm authcrypt and HTTPS use them. Also what the mediator cannot see, and which encryption keys are outside the DID document.
- **§4.2 Why each role is its own key.** Per role: the damage from a stolen copy, how long it lasts, how it is undone, and therefore how the key is held.
- **§10 A community in operation.** One VTC at level 3, its VTA, a witness and a FROST 2-of-3 recovery group: who holds what, a normal day, and three bad days.
- **§19 Principles, precedents and the balance.** Saltzer and Schroeder; NIST SP 800-57 and 800-63; DNSSEC KSK/ZSK; TUF; CAs; Matrix cross-signing; social-recovery wallets; did:webvh. Where simplicity and usability won, where security and privacy won. Two recommended defaults for the maintainer: **create new VTC/VTN identities at level 2**, **verify at level 1 with a recommended profile one setting away**; plus a recovery rehearsal mode.
- **Open questions** gain a witness-enforced hold period on recovery (the social-recovery veto window).
- The example document's second attestation key is now a valid Ed25519 multikey prefix (`z6Mkr…`, was `z2Sy…`).

Sections are renumbered and cross-references updated. The visual summary at https://claude.ai/artifact/9y9wbx1RAhrdbCk1hejtqT (private until shared) is updated to match: a signing-vs-encryption band, per-role "why" cards, the community mesh diagram, and the precedents and balance.

title: List or remove the did:scid alias of an existing did:webvh log (VTI-KEY-167, VTI-VTA-037)
body:
## Why

VTI-KEY-166 lists the `did:scid` alias only in a new log's first version. That leaves no stated way to link the two forms for an identity created without the alias: every log made before #75, and every one created with the alias turned off. Under VTI-KEY-164 the two forms of such an identity stay distinct subjects permanently.

## What

**VTI-KEY-167.** The holder of a log's update authority MAY list the alias in a later version, or remove it. Four conditions apply:

- **Current location.** The alias names the log's current location as `src`.
- **No stale `src`.** An entry naming an earlier location is replaced, not kept beside the new one. A former location is exactly where a replayed old log is served from (VTI-KEY-162).
- **Presented form.** The alias may not be removed while the identity is presented in the did:scid form (VTI-KEY-166).
- **Dated link.** The forms are one subject only from the version that lists the alias. Nothing authorised against an earlier version carries across, and the link ends at a version that removes the alias.

**VTI-VTA-037.** A VTA does this on request by name. It derives the DID URL itself, gates the request exactly like any other update to that identity, and never publishes a version that changes nothing, because every version of a pre-rotation log moves the update key.

The Trust Task is trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#992 (`vta/webvh/dids/update/1.1`). It is the path for identities created before key roles; `vta/dids/update` refuses those with `notKeyRoleIdentity`.

title: feat(vta/webvh/dids/update): 1.1 lists or removes an existing log's did:scid alias
body:
## Why

Every did:webvh log is also a `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>` identity: the same log verifies it, and `?src=` says where to fetch it (VTI-KEY-160, 161). The two forms are distinct subjects until the did:webvh document lists the did:scid DID URL in `alsoKnownAs` (VTI-KEY-164).

`vta/webvh/dids/create/1.2` lists that alias in the first entry by default. A log created before 1.2, or created without the alias, had only one way to get it: send a whole replacement document with a hand-built DID URL. The `src` encoding (`%3A` for a port, `/` for each `:`) is exactly the part a client gets wrong.

This has to live on the pre-key-role path. `vta/dids/update/1.0` (#986) refuses every identity created before key roles with `notKeyRoleIdentity`, and that is every did:webvh DID that exists today.

## What

`vta/webvh/dids/update/1.1` declares `extends: "1.0"`:

- **Request: `scidAlsoKnownAs: boolean`.**
  - `true` lists `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=<source>` for the log's current location. It replaces an alias left over from before a move rather than adding a second one.
  - `false` removes every did:scid entry that names this SCID.
  - It is applied to `document` when one is supplied, otherwise to the current document. The agent derives the DID URL; the caller never writes it.
- **Response: `scidAlsoKnownAs` and `scidDidUrl`.** The prose makes both MUST. The schema leaves them optional so the extension stays additive.
- **New error codes:**
  - `scidAliasRequired`: refuses removing the alias of an identity the agent presents in the did:scid form (VTI-KEY-166).
  - `noChange`: refuses to publish an entry identical to the latest one, so the update key is not rotated for nothing.
- **Consent.** Listing the alias publishes an entry, which rotates the update key, so the task stays `destructive`. A consent surface must say so.

## Checks

`npm run build`, `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, the TS, Go and Dart binding builds, and `npm run check-bindings` all pass. The Rust conformance suite passes (1998 tests).

title: feat(vta)!: serve vta/webvh/dids/update/1.1 — list or remove an existing log's did:scid alias
body:
Implements Trust Task `vta/webvh/dids/update/1.1` (`scidAlsoKnownAs`) in the VTA, vta-sdk and pnm. Spec and schema: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#992 (not merged, not on the registry yet).

> **Do not merge yet.** The last commit, `chore: DO NOT MERGE local patches for unreleased trust-tasks 1.1`, pins 1.1 from a local build of #992. It has to stay last, and it gets replaced once #992 is deployed (see below).

## What it does

Every did:webvh log is also `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>`. The two forms are one subject only while the did:webvh document lists `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=<source>` in `alsoKnownAs` (VTI-KEY-164). create/1.2 lists it when a DID is created. update/1.1 lets an operator list or remove it on a DID that already exists.

- **Deriving the URL:** the VTA builds it with `vta_sdk::did_scid::scid_forms`, the same derivation create/1.2 and the resolver use: `:` becomes `/` and percent-encoding is kept. The edit applies to `document` when one is supplied, otherwise to the latest document. The logic is in `operations/did_webvh/update/scid_alias.rs`.
- **`true`:** appends the URL after the existing entries unless it is already listed. If an entry names this SCID with a different `src`, it is replaced in place.
- **`false`:** removes every did:scid entry for this SCID, with or without `src`.
- **`scidAliasRequired`:** returned when the VTA presents this identity in its did:scid form (VTI-KEY-166). A supplied `document` that drops the alias is also refused, whether or not `scidAlsoKnownAs` is present. Under 1.0 that same document is refused as a validation error whose message starts with `scidAliasRequired`.
- **`noChange`:** returned when the resulting document and parameters (witnesses, watchers, ttl, pre-rotation) equal the latest entry's. Nothing is published and no key rotates. This check runs only when `scidAlsoKnownAs` is present. 1.0 label-only "resync" updates behave as before.
- **Key rotation:** any other alias change is a document change, so it rotates the update key just as `document` does. The task stays Destructive.
- **Response:** reports `scidAlsoKnownAs` (as published) and `scidDidUrl` (always). The 1.0 and rotate-keys responses are unchanged, because their closed schemas don't have these members.
- **Identity record:** the did:scid identity record (`webvh_store::ScidIdentity`) is updated to match the published document. The did:scid DID addresses the log exactly while the alias is listed.

### How the VTA knows it "presents the identity as did:scid"
create/1.2 already records this per DID: `ScidIdentity { presented, alias_listed }`, keyed `scid:<did:scid>` in the webvh keyspace. `presented` is true when the DID was created with `didMethod: scid`, and that includes the VTA's own DID created through setup. The check reads that flag. It also treats the VTA's configured `vta_did` as presented when it is this log's did:scid DID ("configured so since"). No new storage was needed.

One limit: the consent dry-run (`plan_did_webvh_update`) has no `vta_did`, so in a plan only the recorded flag counts. Execution checks both.

### 1.0 and 1.1 side by side
1.1 `extends` 1.0, so a 1.0 request is a 1.1 request with the same meaning. One handler serves both, and the handler branches on the Type URI only for the new member and the response fields. This follows how create/1.2 was introduced (#2257): served alongside the earlier versions, with the SDK sending the new version only when its new member is stated. `VtaClient::update_did_webvh_by_did` sends 1.1 only when `scid_also_known_as` is set, so ordinary updates still reach VTAs that serve only 1.0. 1.0 is **not** added to `SUPERSEDED_TASKS`, because our own SDK still sends it. It can be retired later in a #2316-style sweep.

## Gating (security)
Approval rules and typical operator Rego match one Type URI exactly (`input.request.typeUri == …`). Without a change, a rule like `pnm approvals require …/update/1.0 --consent` would **not** hold a 1.1 request.

- **Gate:** `policy_gate::GATED_AS` maps update/1.1 to update/1.0. `decide_with_extended` evaluates the request as itself and as 1.0, and the stricter result wins (deny > consent > step-up > allow). A rule that names only 1.1 still applies to 1.1. Everything goes through the one `decide`, so REST and Trust Task transports behave the same.
- **Dispatch class:** same as 1.0 (Destructive). The consent planner covers 1.1, so the approver sees the computed effects, including the key rotation. `retry_safety` (Keyed) and `budget::RELAYS_ONWARD` have 1.1 rows.
- **Other places that name the URI:**
  - `vta-policy/src/{approvals,defaults}.rs`, `vta-sdk/src/approvals/mod.rs`, `messaging/auth.rs`, `vta-mobile-core/src/consent.rs`, `ceremony.rs`, `task_consent.rs` and `helpers.rs` only use it as test fixtures. None of them is a gating table, so they are unchanged.
  - `vta-mcp` and the VTC delegation scope match by slug, so they already cover 1.1.
- **Tests:**
  - `a_reauth_rule_for_1_0_holds_1_1`
  - `a_consent_rule_for_1_0_holds_1_1`
  - `a_rule_naming_1_1_holds_1_1_only`
  - `the_stricter_decision_wins`
  - `extended_versions_share_handler_class_and_plan`
  - `update_1_1_is_gated_as_update_1_0`
- **Docs:** `docs/02-vta/approvals.md` explains the rule.

## pnm
`pnm did-mgmt dids scid-alias --did <did> --list|--remove` (aliases `--on`/`--off`), plus `--label` and `--no-confirm`.
- Pins `expectedVersionId` to the version it read.
- Before publishing, warns that the update key will rotate.
- Waits for consent the same way `dids edit` does.
- Prints `scidDidUrl`, the rotation consequence, and the serverless/redeploy hint.

## Files
- `vta-sdk`: `trust_tasks.rs` (constant), `protocols/did_management/update.rs` (fields), `client/webvh.rs` (`update_task_for`), `retry_safety.rs`, `budget.rs`.
- `vta-service`: `operations/did_webvh/update/{scid_alias.rs (new), orchestrator.rs, options.rs, errors.rs}`, `trust_tasks/{webvh.rs, mod.rs, planner.rs, policy_gate.rs, conformance.rs}`, `tests/it/api_integration.rs`.
- `vta-cli-common/src/commands/webvh.rs`, `pnm-cli/src/{cli.rs, commands/webvh.rs}`.
- `docs/02-vta/{did-webvh-update,approvals}.md`.
- Last commit only: `vti-specs-vta/trust-tasks.{toml,lock}` and `trust-tasks/vta/webvh/dids/update/1.1.bundle.json`.

## Tests
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-service`: 2268/2268 passed. This includes:
  - the new integration tests `vti_key_164_update_1_1_removes_and_lists_the_scid_alias`, `vti_key_166_a_presented_did_scid_keeps_its_alias` and `update_1_0_refuses_the_alias_and_1_1_always_reports_it`
  - the conformance sweep (a 1.1 witness was added)
  - the error-code census (`noChange` and `scidAliasRequired` are witnessed; 1.1's `notFound`/`versionConflict`/`invalidDocument` share wire codes with 1.0's existing baseline rows)
  - the schema test `the_scid_alias_is_a_1_1_member_only`
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-sdk -p vti-specs -p vti-specs-vta -p vta-cli-common -p pnm-cli -p vta-policy`: 1523/1523 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-mcp -p cnm-cli -p vta-mobile-core`: 260/260 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk -p vta-service -p vta-cli-common -p pnm-cli -p vti-specs-vta --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt`: clean.
- Not run: the full workspace nextest, the vtc-service suite, doctests and the e2e suite.

## Breaking
- New public fields on `UpdateDidWebvhBody`, `UpdateDidWebvhResultBody` (vta-sdk) and `UpdateDidWebvhOptions` (vta-service).
- New variants on the `#[non_exhaustive]` `UpdateDidWebvhError`.

## Spec notes
- 1.1's abstract says a VTA MUST refuse it for a key-role identity with `unsupportedVersion`. Key-role identities don't exist on `main` yet; that refusal belongs with the key-roles work (`feat/key-roles-1-method-profiles`).

## After #992 merges and the registry deploys
1. Drop the last commit and run `trust-tasks -C vti-specs-vta update vta/webvh/dids/update`, keeping `"vta/webvh/dids/update" = ["1.0", "1.1"]`. A local registry build shows the registry will also re-publish 1.0 in place with a "superseded by 1.1" note, which changes 1.0's digest.
2. Run `trust-tasks -C vti-specs-vta check`, rebuild, and re-run the suites above.
3. Until then, the first two commits don't build on their own; they need the pin in the last commit.

title: docs(design-notes): key roles design — why, the role model, recovery, benefits and implications (#2352)
body:
docs(design-notes): key roles design — why, the role model, recovery, benefits and implications (#2352)

* docs(design-notes): key roles design — why, the role model, recovery, approvals, benefits and implications

Expands the key-role work into a full design note beside the implementation plan: the problem with one key signing decisions, traffic and the DID log; the five roles; protection boundaries and custody; the external recovery key and why the VTA's own BIP-32 seed cannot hold it; rotation vs revocation; approvals; method profiles; no in-place migration; benefits, implications and open WG questions. Records the recovery-custodian decision and that implementation is paused. Docs only.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(design-notes): key roles revised to key assurance levels — DID classes, verifier policy, FROST recovery custodians

The first design made every single-key node identity non-conformant and
required an external recovery key for every key-role identity. The revision,
proposed in dtgwg-vti-spec#82 and dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#993:

- DID classes: relationship (single key normal, any method), persona (one
  key or passkeys; keyRoles marks only authenticator), service (VTA, VTC, VTN,
  registry, host services, mediator, integration).
- Key assurance levels 1 (single key), 2 (role-separated, VTA-held keys that
  may be derived and backed up), 3 (recoverable: generated, no backup,
  recovery custodian, witness), chosen by the operator; verifier policy sets
  the minimum per use. Every level is conformant, so today's DIDs are level 1.
- The recovery key is mandatory only at level 3, because it was needed only
  because of the no-backup rule.
- A verifier establishes the level from a declared `keyAssurance` member,
  capped by what the document and history show, with a lowered level read as
  level 1; what stays self-asserted is listed.
- Recovery custodians: a separately held key, a second VTA, or a FROST
  (RFC 9591) threshold group, with its security requirements, why Shamir
  reconstruct-then-sign is rejected, and why not for attestation keys.
- Raising a level in place (vta/dids/upgrade), never lowering it.
- Implementation plan re-ordered so that level 2 is reachable before any
  level-3 machinery; still paused.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(join): join a community as a new identity of its own
body:
## What

The join window ("Ask to join <host>") offers, first and preselected, **A new identity for <host>**. On *Send request* the wallet:

1. sets up a context of the community's own at the person's VTA — `vtc-<portal host>` (`vta/contexts/create/1.0`), skipped when it exists;
2. mints one DID in it (`vta/webvh/dids/create/1.2`), skipped when the context already holds one — no `didMethod`, so the agent's configured form (webvh or did:scid) is used; `addMediatorService` so the community can reach the agent; `setPrimary`; published through one of the agent's DID hosting servers (a picker appears when there is more than one);
3. carries on with the existing join: vault entry → `vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3` signed as that identity → under the default criteria, *Request sent — you can sign in once <host> approves it*.

An agent that won't list its hosting servers (not one this wallet administers) gets no offer; one with none shows the option disabled with why. A failure is reported at a new stage, `join-identity`, before anything about the person reaches the community.

Pairs with OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure `feat/vtc-website-join` (landing-page **Join this community** → `/members/?join`). Either can merge first: this one changes no wire shape.

## Tests

- `sign-in-flows.test.mts`: offer shape + context id; no offer when servers can't be listed; identity made before bind/sign/submit and the submit signed as it; failure stops before anything is sent; an unoffered server is out of order; `communityContextId` normalisation.
- `sign-in-view.render.test.mts`: preselected, server picker, submit sends `newIdentity`; disabled with no server.
- `npm test` (all workspaces) and `npm run lint` green locally; extension builds.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — reuses the VTA session
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable (R2.1) — context + DID are read-before-write, so a retried join reuses them
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retry added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*) — none; window↔offscreen message only
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*) — no servers / unlisted servers ⇒ no new identity
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered (R2.1) — dies after the DID is minted: the next attempt finds the context and its DID
- [x] Deviations flagged — TSP is not added to the new DID (`addTspService`); DIDComm only, as the existing DID form's default

title: fix(rooms): complete every member request at rooms/keys/act/0.9 and write records at rooms/records/put/0.4
body:
## Why

`main` is red since #393 + #388 landed together: `check-task-versions` fails because the offscreen bundle names `rooms/keys/act/0.8` and `rooms/records/put/0.3`. #393 pinned **two** versions of each and sent the older one for everything except an open room's file record, so a wallet kept working against a VTA that had not moved.

That is a compatibility fold. This repo doesn't keep those (nothing is deployed), and the lock's **one version per slug** rule (CLAUDE.md, *Repo mechanics*) is what makes that structural. So this fixes the cause, not the checker: the checker is unchanged.

## What

- Pin `rooms/keys/act` = 0.9 and `rooms/records/put` = 0.4 only; regenerate `src/specs` (0.8 / 0.3 removed).
- `roomsKeysAct` always completes at 0.9 (`actVersionFor` removed). VTI's 0.9 table is 0.8's plus `put/0.4` (`act_0_9_adds_put_0_4_to_0_8s_table`), so the community offer/membership types and every host-bound request are still covered.
- Every record put is 0.4: sealed records, cleartext notes and open-room files. 0.4 extends 0.3 with an open room's file.
- Tests, comments and CLAUDE.md updated. `task-surface.json` still lists what VTI serves (both act versions), and is untouched.

## Verified

- `npm run build` + `node packages/extension/scripts/check-task-versions.mjs`: **OK**, 417 task URIs.
- `npm test` (all workspaces): all pass. `npm run lint` clean.

Unblocks #395.

title: feat(rooms): files in open rooms, from the portal and the console
body:
## Why

An open room could hold notes only: `putRoomFile` refused it, because a file's manifest lived inside a sealed body and its key was derived from a storage key an open room doesn't have.

The spec now covers it:
- `rooms/records/put/0.4` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#987) puts the manifest in `cleartext.file`, with a random per-file key.
- `rooms/keys/act/0.9` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#990) lets a member's VTA complete that record.

VTI serves both since OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2348.

## What

**Put** (`putRoomFile` on an open room)
- Mints the file key here (32 random bytes), at the room's epoch.
- Seals the blob exactly as on every tier.
- Writes `rooms/records/put/0.4` with the manifest, `fileKey` included, in `cleartext.file`, and `blobs` exactly `[file.blobRef]`.
- Asks the VTA for neither `file-key` nor `seal`.

**Get** (`getRoomFile`)
- Reads an open record's manifest from its cleartext and holds the key to the tier: required in an open manifest, refused in a sealed one.
- Hands the opener the manifest without `fileKey`, so the published wasm reader, which predates the field, is unaffected.
- Never returns the key, and the console's records pane leaves it out of what it shows (`withoutFileKey`).
- `RoomFileGot` and both `got` messages gain `signed`. It is false on an open room, whose record its author didn't sign. Each surface then says the file matched the digest *its record states*, not one its author signed.

**Portal read** (`readView`)
- An open record's `cleartext.file` reaches the page as its name, size and media type, as a sealed body's file already does, so a portal can offer the download. `fileKey` never reaches the page.

**Act version** (`roomsKeysAct` / `actVersionFor`)
- Only `rooms/records/put/0.4` goes at `act/0.9`. Everything else stays at 0.8, so the wallet keeps working against a VTA that hasn't been upgraded.
- Open-room files need a VTA and a host built from VTI #2348 or later.

**Copy**
- The console's open-room note and the portal's write prompt now say what an open room's file exposes.
- The unused `openRoom` `RoomFileError` code is removed.

**Housekeeping**
- Pins `rooms/keys/act/0.9` and `rooms/records/put/0.4`.
- `trust-tasks update` also refreshed eleven draft bundles the registry had edited in place. Their changes are description and deprecation text only, with no schema change.
- `task-surface.json` is resynced from VTI main: it adds `act/0.9`, and approve-response moves from 0.6 to 0.7.
- `sync-task-surface.mjs` now reads VTI's `vti_specs::` paths. Since VTI #2343 it couldn't resync at all.

## Tests

- **Core engine**, against the real wasm cipher:
  - an open room's file round-trips through `put/0.4` at `act/0.9`, with no `file-key` or `seal` asked of the VTA;
  - only that one record goes at 0.9;
  - a manifest without a key is refused, and no derived key is fetched in its place;
  - a wrong key fails verification.
- **Extension**:
  - the preview shows "its record states" wording for an open-room file;
  - the page's `got` message carries `signed`;
- `readView` exposes an open record's file without its key.
- **Results**: `npm test` is green in every workspace (core 1102, extension 1337). `npm run lint` and the extension build pass.

Not covered by a test: `withoutFileKey` in the records pane.

title: ci: fail the build when a bundle names a task off its pinned version
body:
## Why

VTI keeps serving several superseded task versions only because this wallet was known to send them (VTI #2315's "kept for a deployed peer" list). To let VTI drop them, this PR answers: **does the wallet still send any superseded version?** It also makes sure the answer stays "no".

## Finding: no wire version moves are needed

#384–#387 already cut every task over. `trust-tasks.lock` pins one version per slug, and every pinned task is served at that version by its counterparty on `verifiable-trust-infrastructure` main (3e064e60d):

- re-running `npm run tasks:sync` against vta-sdk 0.75.0 leaves `task-surface.json` unchanged;
- the act-wrapped inner types (`rooms/info/0.3`, `rooms/records/list/0.5`, `rooms/records/put/0.3`, `rooms/records/curate/0.1`, `rooms/epoch/chain/0.2`, `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.4`, …) are all in the VTA's `ACT_TABLE_0_8` / `COMMUNITY_TYPES_0_8`.

A scan of the built `dist/` of both the extension and the PWA found exactly one task URI that was not a pinned version: `trust-task-error/0.1`. It came from the PWA's in-memory smoke VTA, and it never goes to an agent.

The task's starting list (persona 1.0, `rooms/keys/{seal,backfill,chain}` 0.1, act 0.1/0.5, join manifest 0.3, passkey-login 0.1) is already gone from `src/`. Every one of those slugs is pinned at its current version.

## What this changes

- **`packages/extension/scripts/check-task-versions.mjs`**, run in CI after the build. It reads what ships, not the source. Every `https://trusttasks.org/spec/<slug>/<version>` in the extension and PWA bundles must be the lock's version of that slug, and an unpinned slug fails. The only exemption is `trust-task-error`, which the wallet reads by slug across 0.x and never sends. It catches a hand-spelled URI or one a dependency brings in, which the lock and `specs.generated.mjs` cannot see. Checked both ways: it passes on this tree and fails on an injected `rooms/keys/act/0.5` and on an unpinned `vta/keys/list/0.1`.
- **The smoke VTA** now answers the way a current agent does: `TRUST_TASK_ERROR_TYPE_URI` with `unsupportedType`. Before, it sent `trust-task-error/0.1` with `unsupported_type`.
- **A stale comment in `provision/request.ts`**: it said `provision/integration/0.1` under an FPN dual-registration, but the wallet sends 0.3.

The title is not marked breaking because nothing on the wire or in the public API changes.

## Verified locally

`npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (2,561 tests, 0 failures) and the new guard all pass.

title: feat(vtc): the member portal adds files to open rooms
body:
## Why

#2341 hid the portal's file upload on open rooms, because a file's manifest could only travel inside a sealed body.

That's no longer true:
- `rooms/records/put/0.4` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#987) lets an open room's record carry its file and the random key the file is sealed under.
- Both VTI hosts serve it since #2348.
- The browser plugin writes and reads these records in OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#393.

## What

`vtc-service/admin-ui/src/members/Rooms.tsx`:

- **Upload:** the AddToRoom card offers a file on every tier. On an open room, its note says a file is stored encrypted under a key its record carries in the clear, so the host can read it as well as the room's members.
- **Download:** an open room's record isn't signed by its author. Its file is therefore checked against the digest the record states, and the record view says so instead of claiming the author's signature. The wording follows the record's `sealed` flag, so no new field is needed from the wallet.

## Depends on

- An open-room upload needs a wallet with vta-browser-plugin#393.
- A VTA and host built from #2348 or later.

With an older wallet, the upload fails with the wallet's own refusal, as before.

## Tests

`Rooms.test.tsx`:
- The open-room card test now expects the file field and the new notice.
- A new test checks that an open room's file says it is checked against the digest its record states.

Results: `npm run lint` passes, and `vitest run` passes all 1359 tests.

title: feat(manager): choose did:webvh or did:scid when creating a DID
body:
## Problem

The console's **New DID** form could only mint whatever form the agent was configured for, which is `did:webvh` by default. The core's `webvhDidCreate` has spoken `vta/webvh/dids/create/1.2` since #384 and takes `didMethod`, but `did-create.tsx` never set it, so the browser had no way to ask for a `did:scid`. #373 added did:scid for contacts, proofs and display, but not for creation.

## Change

- A new first section, **Which identifier it is**, with three choices:
  - **Your agent decides** (default). This sends no `didMethod`, so a VTA or VTC configured for did:scid (`[dids] default_did_method`) is not overruled by the console.
  - **did:webvh**, sent explicitly.
  - **did:scid**, sent explicitly.
- `scidAlsoKnownAs` is not sent. The agent's default is on, and did:scid is refused without the alias.
- The **Minted** card shows the other form of the same log, using the 1.2 response's `didMethod`, `webvhDid`, `scidDidUrl` and `scidAlsoKnownAs`:
  - for did:scid, the `?src=` DID URL to share (a bare did:scid names no source) and the did:webvh alias;
  - for did:webvh, the did:scid alias when the log lists one.
- The copy in the panel description and in "Where it is published" now covers both forms.

## Tests

`npm run lint`, `npm test` (all workspaces, 0 failures; extension 1341) and `npm run build` pass. New render tests in `did-create.render.test.mts`:

- the quiet path sends no `didMethod`;
- did:scid and did:webvh are sent when chosen, with no `scidAlsoKnownAs`;
- a did:scid mint shows the shareable DID URL and the webvh alias;
- a did:webvh mint shows the scid alias only when the log lists one.

title: feat(rooms)!: files in open rooms — serve rooms/records/put/0.4 and rooms/keys/act/0.9
body:
## Why

Until now an open data room could hold notes but no files. A file's manifest only travelled inside a sealed body, and its key could only be derived from a storage key, which an open room doesn't have.

Two spec changes close this:
- `rooms/records/put/0.4` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#987) puts the manifest in `cleartext.file`, together with the random key the blob is sealed under (`fileKey`).
- `rooms/keys/act/0.9` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#990) adds `put/0.4` to the closed table a member's VTA completes. Without it, pnm and the browser plugin are refused.

## What

**Hosts** (room-host and vtc-service, through vti-rooms)
- Serve `rooms/records/put/0.4` beside 0.3. The cleartext, including the file, is stored and served exactly as received (Host item 13).
- On an open room, refuse a record with `malformedRequest` if its `blobs` isn't exactly `[cleartext.file.blobRef]` or its file has no `fileKey` (Host item 12). This check runs before `blobNotFound` and before anything is written.
- 0.3 behaves as before.

**VTA**
- Serves `rooms/keys/act` 0.9 and 0.8, each checked against its own closed table (Recipient item 1). 0.9's table is 0.8's plus `put/0.4` as `write`.
- One handler serves both versions. 0.9 extends 0.8, so both are read and answered with 0.9's types.

**Clients**
- vta-sdk sends `act/0.9` only. `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_8` stays, because the VTA serves it for pnm-browser-plugin.
- `pnm rooms file put` and `get` work on open rooms:
  - the key is minted locally and carried in the manifest;
  - the record is written as `put/0.4` through `act/0.9`;
  - notes and sealed writes stay on `put/0.3`, which every deployed host serves.
- `vti_rooms::files::FileManifest` gains `file_key`. `carried_key(open_room)` holds a reader to the tier: the key is required on open rooms and refused on sealed ones. `Debug` is written by hand so the key never reaches a log.

**Pins**: `rooms/records/put/0.4` and `rooms/keys/act/0.9`. Wherever the superseded `put/0.3` or `act/0.8` is still sent or served, the use carries an `allow(deprecated)` with its reason.

## Breaking

- vta-sdk: `room_act`, `room_act_community`, `unsigned_room_request` and `unsigned_community_request` now take and return `act/0.9` types.
- vti-rooms: `FileManifest` has a new public field.

## Tests

- room-host:
  - an open-room file round-trips exactly as sent;
  - each Host item 12 refusal, including that it comes before `blobNotFound`;
  - a bad `fileKey` is refused by the schema;
  - 0.3 on an open room is unchanged.
- vtc-service: item 12 refusal, and that a valid record passes on to the blob lookup.
- vti-rooms: unit tests for the open-file rule (it doesn't apply on sealed tiers) and for `carried_key`.
- VTA: `act/0.9` completes `put/0.4` while 0.8 refuses it with `typeNotActable`, and 0.9's table is 0.8's plus that one row.

Local runs:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` | green |
| `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` | green |
| `cargo test --workspace --doc` | green |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` | green |
| `cargo fmt --check` | green |

## Follow-on

The browser plugin (portal and console) and the VTC portal's AddToRoom card get open-room file upload and download. The plugin needs `FileManifest.fileKey` in its wasm reader, and to send `act/0.9` for the `put/0.4`.

title: vtc-service-v0.16.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Move a community role with vtc/members/role/set/0.1 and stop serving acl/change-role/0.1 ([#2347](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2347))

* feat(vtc)!: move a community role with vtc/members/role/set/0.1 and stop serving acl/change-role/0.1

  The community-role move (member, moderator, issuer, admin, custom roles) is
  now `vtc/members/role/set/0.1`; `acl/change-role/0.1` is no longer served,
  sent or pinned. `acl/change-role/0.2` still moves the administrative role.

  The handler makes the specification's checks 1-7 in order, each with its
  declared code: vtc.roles.assign (permissionDenied), no self-move in either
  direction (VTI-OPS-050, VTI-ACL-052), notFound, roleNotRecognized
  (details.offendingRole) / roleNotAssignable (`application` onto or off),
  stateMismatch (details.currentRole), the requester covering the entry
  (VTI-ACL-050), and fromRole == toRole answered `changed: false` with no
  gesture and no write (SPEC 7.2).

  The role-change ceremony carries items 8-18: authority follows the role
  only where it is exactly the one the current role implies;
  delegationExceedsGranter (axes); lastRoleAssigner checked before the policy
  and again under the write's lock (VTI-APV-009); the policy sees whether the
  move confers or withdraws authority and may not choose a different role
  (deniedByPolicy); the bound step-up and parked consent (VTI-OPS-051,
  VTI-APV-018/019); the compare-and-swap re-checked under LAST_ADMIN_LOCK
  (item 14); the role credential returned as roleVac; and a new
  CommunityRoleSet audit event (from/to, authority before/after, approval,
  action id, reason).

  The response is the generated type: subject, role, previousRole, changed,
  approval, entry (AclEntry 0.2) and roleVac. vtc-client's acl_change_role
  becomes members_role_set; `cnm access change-role` and the admin console
  send the new task. Approver summary templates are added for the new task
  (server and console pins); the 0.1 templates stay for history.

- **auth**: Answer step-ups with auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7, and stop serving 0.4 and 0.6 ([#2346](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2346))

Every step-up answer moves to approve-response 0.7
  (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#983). A user-verified WebAuthn assertion
  by the approver's own registered passkey is evidence on its own, so the admin
  console answers unsigned. A delegated key's proof never counts as the
  approver's. A didSigned or approverSigned answer, and every denial, still
  needs the approver's own proof.

- **vtc**: Passkey admin invites from the console, vtc/admin/invites/{create,list}/0.2 ([#2345](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2345))

vtc/admin/invites/create/0.1 required `did`, so the console could issue only
  wallet invitations; a passkey invitation needed `vtc admin invite` on the host.
  trust-tasks-tf #989 adds create and list 0.2, which VTI now serves and sends in
  place of 0.1 (nothing outside VTI sent 0.1).

  Wire changes:
  - create 0.2: `did` optional. Present → wallet invitation (claimed with
    vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.3); absent → passkey invitation (claimed
    with vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1). The response gains a
    required `kind` (`wallet` | `passkey`); `aclEntryCreated` is false for a
    passkey invitation.
  - list 0.2: every entry gains a required `kind`; a passkey invitation's
    `targetDid` is absent until consumed, then the derived DID.
  - revoke stays at 0.1.

  Behaviour (create 0.2 items 3-4): a passkey invitation records an
  install::InvitedAuthority — community administrator with the full ceiling,
  delegated by the inviter, labelled with `label` — and writes nothing to the
  ACL; passkey/finish item 9 writes it for the derived DID. Since nobody is
  present to authorise it at the claim, issuing one always costs the inviter's
  bound gesture and another unrestricted administrator's consent, parked under
  the stable subject `urn:openvtc:vtc:admin-invite:passkey`. A consumed row now
  remembers it was a passkey invitation (`Consumed.passkey`) so list can report
  its kind.

- **specs**: Generate the Trust Task wire types VTI pins, with trust-tasks-build ([#2340](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2340))

* feat(specs): generate the Trust Task wire types VTI pins, with trust-tasks-build

  trust-tasks-rs 0.36 deprecates every prebuilt trust_tasks_rs::specs module.
  Five new crates generate the versions VTI uses instead:

  - vti-specs-rooms, vti-specs-vta, vti-specs-vtc, vti-specs-core: each
    build.rs runs trust-tasks-build (.index(true)) over its own
    trust-tasks.lock and vendored bundles. Each version is pinned in exactly
    one crate, so a type is the same type across the workspace. rooms stands
    alone so vti-rooms-wasm compiles nothing else.
  - vti-specs: re-exports every family at its trust_tasks_rs::specs path and
    merges the four Type URI indexes (type_index::lookup) into a drop-in
    schema_index, plus is_pinned. Framework specs fall through to
    trust_tasks_rs::schema_index.
  - vta-sdk re-exports it as vta_sdk::specs.

  664 versions are pinned: every version module the workspace names, plus the
  Type URIs it sends or serves as strings (registry/*, did-management/*,
  push/provision, ...).

  spec_pin_census in vta-service and vtc-service fails on a dispatched,
  served, sent or TASK_* Type URI no crate pins: an unpinned URI answers None
  from the index, and the gates that read None as nothing to check fail open.

  Nothing moves to the new crates yet; the import rewrite follows.

- **vtc**: The passkey install, vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1 ([#2338](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2338))

Implements trust-tasks-tf #976 and #978 (trust-tasks-rs 0.36.2) and stops
  serving vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.2, which those retire. A 0.2
  document is now `unsupportedVersion`, naming 0.3 as the slug's served
  version.

  The administrator's DID is the did:key of the passkey credential's own
  public key: Ed25519 (multicodec 0xed01, did:key:z6Mk…) or P-256 (the SEC1
  compressed point under multicodec 0x1200, did:key:zDn…). It is read from the
  attested credential data alone. It is never taken from the install token,
  which for this ceremony names no DID (start item 5, finish item 5).

  - start offers exactly EdDSA (-8) and ES256 (-7), puts no DID in `user`, and
    returns `assertionOptions`: a second fresh 256-bit challenge, single-use
    and bound to the registration, with no allowCredentials.
  - finish verifies the registration (`bindingInvalid`). It refuses any other
    algorithm with `unsupportedAlgorithm`; that refusal consumes nothing, and
    the registration stays open. It then derives the DID and verifies one
    WebAuthn assertion by the new credential over that challenge
    (`possessionUnproven`). Only after that does it consume the token, keep
    the passkey and mint the setup-session token (items 6–8). A refusal lifts
    the ceremony lock, so the installer can start again at once. A consumed
    token is `invalidToken`. The old idempotent replay, which re-minted a
    setup-session token without proof of possession, is gone.
  - The finish response carries a bearer token, so its proof is REQUIRED. The
    spine signs every answer, and finish refuses up front on a community with
    no signing key.
  - On a community that already has an administrator, finish writes the
    derived DID's ACL entry (item 9), with the authority the invitation was
    issued with. That authority is recorded on the token's row
    (`install::InvitedAuthority`). On a fresh community, vtc/admin/bootstrap
    writes it, as before.

  Two kinds of `vtc admin invite`:
  - with no `--did`: a passkey invitation. The token names no DID, no ACL
    entry is written now, and the authority is recorded on the invitation.
    The offline issue is queued as a break-glass, named by the invitation.
  - with `--did X`: a wallet invitation, claimed with vtc/install/claim/
    {start,finish}/0.3. The token names X, whose admin entry is written now
    if it has none.

  `vtc admin emergency-bootstrap` and `vtc setup` now mint passkey
  invitations. The setup's VTA admin DID is no longer what the install URL
  makes an administrator. The summary prints the offline `vtc acl add` that
  grants it.

  The admin console's install page reads which kind the token is. For a
  passkey invitation it creates the passkey, signs the possession assertion
  over `assertionOptions` with allowCredentials naming the new credential,
  and explains `possessionUnproven` and `unsupportedAlgorithm`. For a wallet
  invitation it offers the wallet claim only.

  The census witnesses the passkey install's six codes and 0.3's
  invalidToken and registrationMismatch, which 0.2's witnesses used to
  cover. The test harness gains P-256 and RS256 credentials and the install
  assertion.


  The claim finishes answer with their generated #response types (the
  generated-wire-types census).

- **vtc-portal**: Add notes to an open room from the member portal ([#2341](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2341))

The portal's "Add to this room" card said an open room takes nothing from the
  portal. The wallet now writes an open room's note in the clear, as the member
  (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#390), so the card offers the note form on every
  tier and says, for an open room, that a note there is readable by its host.
  Files stay attributed and private only: a file's description is sealed inside
  its record, and the card says so instead of offering the file input.

- **rooms**: Rooms/owner/group/remove 0.4 for attributed and private rooms ([#2337](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2337))

The VTA serves `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.4` (trust-tasks-tf #975), one
  version that removes a member from either sealed tier, and no longer serves
  0.1 or 0.3. trust-tasks-rs 0.36.2 marks both superseded by 0.4, and no client
  outside VTI sends them.

  - Attributed room: unchanged from 0.3. The member's credentials are withdrawn
    at the host first (the room's next revocation list, signed with
    `signingKeyId`), then the leaf is removed and the room advances. The
    response now carries `withdrawn: true`. A request naming no
    `signingKeyId` is refused `noSigningKey` (item 2).
  - Private room: the leaf is removed and the room advances. No revocation list
    is built, signed or sent, `signingKeyId`, `mirrors` and `until` are not
    needed, and the response is `{roomId, member, withdrawn: false, epoch}`
    (items 4 and 10). `privateRoom` is no longer declared.
  - Pending-removal settlement (item 8) is unchanged. A private room's removal
    now settles an earlier one with its own `earlierRemovalRefused`, where 0.1
    answered `hostRefused`. A pending removal with no list is settled by its
    epoch alone (item 8.3).



### Changed

- **specs**: Take every Trust Task wire type from the generated vti-specs crates ([#2343](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2343))

Every `trust_tasks_rs::specs::<family>` path becomes `vti_specs::<family>`
  (`vti_specs_rooms::rooms` in vti-rooms, which stays wasm-light), and every
  `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::*` call becomes `vti_specs::schema_index::*`,
  which answers for exactly the versions the vti-specs-* locks pin. The
  framework's own specs are re-exported from vti_specs unchanged.

  No crate turns a trust-tasks-rs spec family on any more: the workspace
  compiles none of the deprecated prebuilt modules, only `validate`.

  The generated types are the same generator's output at the same module paths,
  but they are distinct Rust types from the prebuilt ones: a downstream crate
  that passes a `trust_tasks_rs::specs` value into a vta-sdk API must move its
  import to `vta_sdk::specs` (a find-and-replace).

  CLAUDE.md's rule now points at the generated crates and says how to pin a
  version; the SPEC FAMILIES notes in Cargo.toml are replaced.

- **rooms**: Serve and send only the current rooms/* and vtc/rooms/* versions ([#2335](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2335))

The VTA serves rooms/keys/act 0.8 and rooms/keys/browse 0.3 only; the room
  hosts (room-host, vtc-service) serve rooms/records/put 0.3, records/list 0.5,
  info 0.3 and epoch/chain 0.2 only; the VTC serves vtc/rooms/offers/list 0.4
  only. The VTA's own requests to a host (browse, catch-up, anchor, the room's
  profile, group add/remove) send only those versions, with no fall-back for a
  host that predates them.

  pnm-browser-plugin sends only current versions since its cut-over
  (#384-#387); openvtc, vti-rooms-wasm and vta-mobile-core send no superseded
  room version.

  Kept, with a one-line #[allow(deprecated)] reason each:
  - rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1: 0.3 refuses a private room and points it at
    0.1; no successor yet (spec gap).
  - rooms/keys/act/0.8's own closed table (Recipient item 1) still names
    superseded host-bound versions and vtc/rooms/offers/list 0.1-0.3; the VTA
    completes them rather than diverge from the specification.

  Removed public API: vta-sdk TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_1, TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_5,
  TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_BROWSE_0_1; vti-rooms ROOMS_RECORDS_PUT_TYPE,
  ROOMS_RECORDS_PUT_V2_TYPE, ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_TYPE, ROOMS_EPOCH_CHAIN_TYPE,
  ROOMS_INFO_TYPE, blob_tasks::{info, put_v2_blobs, INFO_TYPE, PUT_V2_TYPE} and
  the Payload impls of PutRecordBody, ListRecordsBody and ChainBody; vtc-client's
  re-export of ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_TYPE.

- **vtc**: Approve-response 0.4 only for the console's unsigned answer; drop the unused acl/revoke 0.1 OpenAPI wrapper ([#2333](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2333))

The superseded auth/acl Trust Task versions, narrowed to what still needs
  them.

  auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4 (superseded by 0.6). The VTC now hears 0.4
  only as the admin console's unsigned session-passkey answer. Every signed
  answer — a member's step-up passkey beside their own proof, a refusal, a
  wallet's approver statement — is 0.6, and a signed 0.4 is refused with a
  pointer to 0.6. The 0.4 document is checked against 0.4's schema and then
  handled as the 0.6 payload it is wire-identical to, so
  `bound_step_up::approve` and everything past the door read 0.6 only. The
  console's Decline now sends 0.6.

  0.4 itself stays: approve-response 0.5 onward require the approver's own
  assertionMethod proof, and the console holds only a delegated key, which
  auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2 item 7 refuses as an approver's attestation. The
  console's unsigned answer has no successor in the specification yet.

  acl/change-role/0.1 (superseded by 0.2) stays as the community-role door,
  as #2323 kept it: 0.2 moves an AclEntry 0.2's administrative role, and the
  community role (member <-> admin, role-VAC re-mint, promotion serialisation)
  has no 0.2 task. Its uses now carry a per-item #[allow(deprecated)] naming
  that gap.

- **git-ns**: Speak only the current git-ns bridge versions (job 0.6, event 0.5, result 0.2) ([#2331](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2331))

The VTC sent `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4 and 0.5 beside 0.6, and served
  `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.1 to 0.4 and `git-ns/bridge/result` 0.1 beside the
  current versions, for the released bridge. `vgi-bridge` has sent only job
  0.6, event 0.5 and result 0.2 since v0.26.0, and nothing outside VTI speaks
  the older versions, so they go:

  - Jobs go out as `git-ns/bridge/job/0.6` only, and only to a bridge that
    lists 0.6 in its `trust-task-discovery` answer. `bridge_job_support` no
    longer records or picks 0.4 / 0.5 (`BridgeJobSupport::job_type`), and the
    downgrade to an older job version is gone. A bridge that lists only 0.4
    and 0.5 is sent nothing: in-line jobs are refused with "upgrade the
    bridge", queued jobs wait, and a queued `closePullRequest` is dropped and
    the namespace's administrators told the gate is not enforced. A discovery
    record stored by an earlier VTC still reads.
  - `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.1-0.4 and `git-ns/bridge/result` 0.1 are no
    longer served (refused `unsupportedVersion`); the read-as-0.5 and
    read-as-0.2 conversion shims are removed.
  - The VTC asks bridges with `trust-task-discovery/0.3` instead of 0.2. 0.3
    only adds the optional `acceptanceWindow` to the response; the request is
    unchanged, and `vgi-bridge` answers 0.3 since v0.26.0.

  Docs, vtc-service/CLAUDE.md, the cnm `notRevertible` guidance, the admin
  console's gate-unenforced label and the default git_ns.rego comments now
  name job 0.6.



### Fixed

- **vtc**: Bind an invited wallet administrator's approver at claim finish ([#2342](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2342))

A wallet invitation (`vtc admin invite --did`, vtc/admin/invites/create)
  claimed with vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3 parked its step-up approver binding
  for vtc/admin/bootstrap. On a community that already has an administrator —
  every invitation — bootstrap answers alreadyBootstrapped, so the binding never
  took effect: the invited administrator was left with no step-up factor and
  could do nothing that needs a step-up.

- **vtc-portal**: Show a shared open room as an open room, not "epoch ?" ([#2339](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2339))

An open room has no group, so the member's agent holds no keys and no epoch
  for it: the wallet reads it with the room's credentials, and since
  OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#389 reports a share of one as held with no epoch.
  The portal's "Your rooms here" row printed "epoch ?" for it, and "your agent
  no longer holds this room's keys" once the member left — keys an open room
  never had.

  The row now says "open room", and "you are no longer in this room" when an
  open room is no longer held.

- **voting,witness,persona**: Board read at voting/board/read 0.2, witness evidence at witness/session 0.2 only, the persona timeline answer at 1.1 ([#2334](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2334))

trust-tasks-rs marks voting/board/read/0.1, witness/session/0.1,
  witness/session/submit/0.1 and persona/profile/timeline/1.0 superseded.
  Every party to each is in this workspace or has already moved, so each moves
  to its current version alone.

  voting/board/read 0.1 -> 0.2. A lifecycle entry's (opened, closed,
  closedEarly, cancelled) instant is `occurredAt`, as voting/_shared/0.2 and
  its CONVENTIONS §1 name it, not `at`.
  - The ballot box writes lifecycle entries with `occurredAt`, serves
    board/read at 0.2 only (0.1 is `unsupportedVersion`), and reads
    `occurredAt` when it replays its journal.
  - The VTC sends board/read at 0.2; the auditor (vti_voting::audit and its
    encrypted levels) reads `occurredAt`.
  - A leaf hash is over the entry's member names, so an entry journalled with
    `at` cannot be renamed without changing the board. Like a 0.1 manifest
    ([#2317](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2317)) it is refused by name: the ballot box will not restore a journal
    holding one, and the auditor reports it as unreadable rather than as
    "voting opened before votingOpensAt". Finish or cancel open elections
    before upgrading.

  witness/session 0.1 and submit 0.1. vti-witness and the VTA already serve
  only 0.2 ([#2147](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2147)), and openvtc main sends 0.2. The VTC no longer pairs outcome
  evidence from a 0.1 session with a submit/0.1 response: such evidence pairs
  with nothing.

  persona/profile/timeline 1.0 -> 1.1. The SDK already sent 1.1 but parsed the
  answer as the 1.0 response, whose events require `at`; a 1.1 answer names it
  `occurredAt`, so it failed to parse. `VtaClient::persona_profile_timeline`
  now returns the 1.1 response.

- **vtc-admin-ui**: Fall back to the gradient mark for a logo the sign-in pages cannot show ([#2329](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2329))

The member portal and the console's login page rendered the community's
  logoUrl as-is in their shared top bar (CommunityTopbar). The VTC serves
  both with `img-src 'self' data:`, so a logo on another origin was blocked
  (a broken image plus a CSP violation in the console), and a URL that is
  not an image (a home page) showed broken too.

  The console's own top bar already filtered through displayableLogo and
  fell back on load error. The sign-in top bar now does the same.
  displayableLogo moves to a dependency-free lib/display-logo.ts so the
  member bundle can use it without importing the console's plugins;
  community-identity re-exports it.

- **step-up**: One approve-request version, 0.5, across the VTA, the VTC and the mobile approver ([#2327](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2327))

`auth/step-up/approve-request` was minted at three versions: the VTA at 0.2
  (a hand-built JSON payload), vtc-service at 0.4 (inline in a refusal) and the
  did-hosting RP at 0.5. An approver therefore had to read all three, and
  vta-mobile-core read only 0.1 and 0.2 — so it could answer the VTA but not
  the RP or the VTC.

  - vta-service mints 0.5, built through the generated
    `approve_request::v0_5::Payload` and its schema check (as vtc-service
    already does) rather than a hand-written `json!`; the type URI comes from
    `<Payload as trust_tasks_rs::Payload>::TYPE_URI`. On the wire:
    `acceptableEvidence` -> a required `accepts`, `ttl` -> `ttlSeconds`;
    `sessionId` is still sent, since this is a session step-up.
  - vtc-service's inline request moves 0.4 -> 0.5 (`ttl` -> `ttlSeconds`).
    `bound_step_up::ApproveRequest` is now the 0.5 payload, hence `!`.
  - vta-mobile-core's `parse_step_up_request` accepts 0.5 only, matched
    exactly, and reads `accepts`. `approverSigned` is surfaced as
    `approver-signed` rather than dropped. The UniFFI record keeps its shape: a
    request that names no session (0.5 makes `sessionId` optional) surfaces an
    empty `session_id`, the convention `stepup`'s response draft already reads.
  - The VTC console reads `accepts` only (the 0.3 `acceptableEvidence`
    fallback is gone) and shows `ttlSeconds`.

  The browser wallet cuts over with this: pnm-browser-plugin matches the
  agent's request at 0.2 today and moves to the single 0.5 pin it already
  holds for the RP.

title: vta-service-v0.68.0
body:
### Added

- **auth**: Answer step-ups with auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7, and stop serving 0.4 and 0.6 ([#2346](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2346))

Every step-up answer moves to approve-response 0.7
  (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#983). A user-verified WebAuthn assertion
  by the approver's own registered passkey is evidence on its own, so the admin
  console answers unsigned. A delegated key's proof never counts as the
  approver's. A didSigned or approverSigned answer, and every denial, still
  needs the approver's own proof.

- **specs**: Generate the Trust Task wire types VTI pins, with trust-tasks-build ([#2340](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2340))

* feat(specs): generate the Trust Task wire types VTI pins, with trust-tasks-build

  trust-tasks-rs 0.36 deprecates every prebuilt trust_tasks_rs::specs module.
  Five new crates generate the versions VTI uses instead:

  - vti-specs-rooms, vti-specs-vta, vti-specs-vtc, vti-specs-core: each
    build.rs runs trust-tasks-build (.index(true)) over its own
    trust-tasks.lock and vendored bundles. Each version is pinned in exactly
    one crate, so a type is the same type across the workspace. rooms stands
    alone so vti-rooms-wasm compiles nothing else.
  - vti-specs: re-exports every family at its trust_tasks_rs::specs path and
    merges the four Type URI indexes (type_index::lookup) into a drop-in
    schema_index, plus is_pinned. Framework specs fall through to
    trust_tasks_rs::schema_index.
  - vta-sdk re-exports it as vta_sdk::specs.

  664 versions are pinned: every version module the workspace names, plus the
  Type URIs it sends or serves as strings (registry/*, did-management/*,
  push/provision, ...).

  spec_pin_census in vta-service and vtc-service fails on a dispatched,
  served, sent or TASK_* Type URI no crate pins: an unpinned URI answers None
  from the index, and the gates that read None as nothing to check fail open.

  Nothing moves to the new crates yet; the import rewrite follows.

- **rooms**: Rooms/owner/group/remove 0.4 for attributed and private rooms ([#2337](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2337))

The VTA serves `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.4` (trust-tasks-tf #975), one
  version that removes a member from either sealed tier, and no longer serves
  0.1 or 0.3. trust-tasks-rs 0.36.2 marks both superseded by 0.4, and no client
  outside VTI sends them.

  - Attributed room: unchanged from 0.3. The member's credentials are withdrawn
    at the host first (the room's next revocation list, signed with
    `signingKeyId`), then the leaf is removed and the room advances. The
    response now carries `withdrawn: true`. A request naming no
    `signingKeyId` is refused `noSigningKey` (item 2).
  - Private room: the leaf is removed and the room advances. No revocation list
    is built, signed or sent, `signingKeyId`, `mirrors` and `until` are not
    needed, and the response is `{roomId, member, withdrawn: false, epoch}`
    (items 4 and 10). `privateRoom` is no longer declared.
  - Pending-removal settlement (item 8) is unchanged. A private room's removal
    now settles an earlier one with its own `earlierRemovalRefused`, where 0.1
    answered `hostRefused`. A pending removal with no list is settled by its
    epoch alone (item 8.3).



### Changed

- **specs**: Take every Trust Task wire type from the generated vti-specs crates ([#2343](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2343))

Every `trust_tasks_rs::specs::<family>` path becomes `vti_specs::<family>`
  (`vti_specs_rooms::rooms` in vti-rooms, which stays wasm-light), and every
  `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::*` call becomes `vti_specs::schema_index::*`,
  which answers for exactly the versions the vti-specs-* locks pin. The
  framework's own specs are re-exported from vti_specs unchanged.

  No crate turns a trust-tasks-rs spec family on any more: the workspace
  compiles none of the deprecated prebuilt modules, only `validate`.

  The generated types are the same generator's output at the same module paths,
  but they are distinct Rust types from the prebuilt ones: a downstream crate
  that passes a `trust_tasks_rs::specs` value into a vta-sdk API must move its
  import to `vta_sdk::specs` (a find-and-replace).

  CLAUDE.md's rule now points at the generated crates and says how to pin a
  version; the SPEC FAMILIES notes in Cargo.toml are replaced.

- **rooms**: Serve and send only the current rooms/* and vtc/rooms/* versions ([#2335](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2335))

The VTA serves rooms/keys/act 0.8 and rooms/keys/browse 0.3 only; the room
  hosts (room-host, vtc-service) serve rooms/records/put 0.3, records/list 0.5,
  info 0.3 and epoch/chain 0.2 only; the VTC serves vtc/rooms/offers/list 0.4
  only. The VTA's own requests to a host (browse, catch-up, anchor, the room's
  profile, group add/remove) send only those versions, with no fall-back for a
  host that predates them.

  pnm-browser-plugin sends only current versions since its cut-over
  (#384-#387); openvtc, vti-rooms-wasm and vta-mobile-core send no superseded
  room version.

  Kept, with a one-line #[allow(deprecated)] reason each:
  - rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1: 0.3 refuses a private room and points it at
    0.1; no successor yet (spec gap).
  - rooms/keys/act/0.8's own closed table (Recipient item 1) still names
    superseded host-bound versions and vtc/rooms/offers/list 0.1-0.3; the VTA
    completes them rather than diverge from the specification.

  Removed public API: vta-sdk TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_1, TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_5,
  TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_BROWSE_0_1; vti-rooms ROOMS_RECORDS_PUT_TYPE,
  ROOMS_RECORDS_PUT_V2_TYPE, ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_TYPE, ROOMS_EPOCH_CHAIN_TYPE,
  ROOMS_INFO_TYPE, blob_tasks::{info, put_v2_blobs, INFO_TYPE, PUT_V2_TYPE} and
  the Payload impls of PutRecordBody, ListRecordsBody and ChainBody; vtc-client's
  re-export of ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_TYPE.

- **vta**: Serve and send only vta/contexts/delete/1.1 ([#2332](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2332))

* refactor(vta)!: serve and send only vta/contexts/delete/1.1

  vta/contexts/delete/1.0 is superseded by 1.1 (trust-tasks-tf #967). The
  VTA now dispatches only 1.1 and the SDK sends only 1.1:

  - `VtaClient::delete_context` sends 1.1 with `abandonHostCopies: false`,
    so a host copy that cannot be confirmed removed is refused
    (`vta/contexts/delete:hostCleanupFailed`) with nothing deleted, instead
    of being dropped silently as the 1.0 call did.
  - `delete_context_with_outcome`, `TASK_CONTEXTS_DELETE_1_0` and the
    hand-written 1.0 payload `DeleteContextBody` are removed; use
    `delete_context_settling_hosts`.
  - `pnm`/`cnm contexts delete` no longer falls back to 1.0.
  - retry_safety, the conformance sweep, the error-code census baseline,
    the deprecation-table fixture, the vta-mcp guard test and the docs follow.

  The offline break-glass `vta contexts delete` keeps the report-after
  host-copy policy, which is no longer a wire contract.



### Fixed

- **step-up**: One approve-request version, 0.5, across the VTA, the VTC and the mobile approver ([#2327](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2327))

`auth/step-up/approve-request` was minted at three versions: the VTA at 0.2

### Added

  now `vtc/members/role/set/0.1`; `acl/change-role/0.1` is no longer served,
  sent or pinned. `acl/change-role/0.2` still moves the administrative role.

  The handler makes the specification's checks 1-7 in order, each with its
  declared code: vtc.roles.assign (permissionDenied), no self-move in either
  direction (VTI-OPS-050, VTI-ACL-052), notFound, roleNotRecognized
  (details.offendingRole) / roleNotAssignable (`application` onto or off),
  stateMismatch (details.currentRole), the requester covering the entry
  (VTI-ACL-050), and fromRole == toRole answered `changed: false` with no
  gesture and no write (SPEC 7.2).

  The role-change ceremony carries items 8-18: authority follows the role
  only where it is exactly the one the current role implies;
  delegationExceedsGranter (axes); lastRoleAssigner checked before the policy
  and again under the write's lock (VTI-APV-009); the policy sees whether the
  move confers or withdraws authority and may not choose a different role
  (deniedByPolicy); the bound step-up and parked consent (VTI-OPS-051,
  VTI-APV-018/019); the compare-and-swap re-checked under LAST_ADMIN_LOCK
  (item 14); the role credential returned as roleVac; and a new
  CommunityRoleSet audit event (from/to, authority before/after, approval,
  action id, reason).

  The response is the generated type: subject, role, previousRole, changed,
  approval, entry (AclEntry 0.2) and roleVac. vtc-client's acl_change_role
  becomes members_role_set; `cnm access change-role` and the admin console
  send the new task. Approver summary templates are added for the new task
  (server and console pins); the 0.1 templates stay for history.

- **auth**: Answer step-ups with auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7, and stop serving 0.4 and 0.6 ([#2346](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2346))

Every step-up answer moves to approve-response 0.7
  (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#983). A user-verified WebAuthn assertion
  by the approver's own registered passkey is evidence on its own, so the admin
  console answers unsigned. A delegated key's proof never counts as the
  approver's. A didSigned or approverSigned answer, and every denial, still
  needs the approver's own proof.



### Changed

- **specs**: Take every Trust Task wire type from the generated vti-specs crates ([#2343](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2343))

Every `trust_tasks_rs::specs::<family>` path becomes `vti_specs::<family>`
  (`vti_specs_rooms::rooms` in vti-rooms, which stays wasm-light), and every
  `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::*` call becomes `vti_specs::schema_index::*`,
  which answers for exactly the versions the vti-specs-* locks pin. The
  framework's own specs are re-exported from vti_specs unchanged.

  No crate turns a trust-tasks-rs spec family on any more: the workspace
  compiles none of the deprecated prebuilt modules, only `validate`.

  The generated types are the same generator's output at the same module paths,
  but they are distinct Rust types from the prebuilt ones: a downstream crate
  that passes a `trust_tasks_rs::specs` value into a vta-sdk API must move its
  import to `vta_sdk::specs` (a find-and-replace).

  CLAUDE.md's rule now points at the generated crates and says how to pin a
  version; the SPEC FAMILIES notes in Cargo.toml are replaced.

- **git-ns**: Speak only the current git-ns bridge versions (job 0.6, event 0.5, result 0.2) ([#2331](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2331))

The VTC sent `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4 and 0.5 beside 0.6, and served
  `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.1 to 0.4 and `git-ns/bridge/result` 0.1 beside the
  current versions, for the released bridge. `vgi-bridge` has sent only job
  0.6, event 0.5 and result 0.2 since v0.26.0, and nothing outside VTI speaks
  the older versions, so they go:

  - Jobs go out as `git-ns/bridge/job/0.6` only, and only to a bridge that
    lists 0.6 in its `trust-task-discovery` answer. `bridge_job_support` no
    longer records or picks 0.4 / 0.5 (`BridgeJobSupport::job_type`), and the
    downgrade to an older job version is gone. A bridge that lists only 0.4
    and 0.5 is sent nothing: in-line jobs are refused with "upgrade the
    bridge", queued jobs wait, and a queued `closePullRequest` is dropped and
    the namespace's administrators told the gate is not enforced. A discovery
    record stored by an earlier VTC still reads.
  - `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.1-0.4 and `git-ns/bridge/result` 0.1 are no
    longer served (refused `unsupportedVersion`); the read-as-0.5 and
    read-as-0.2 conversion shims are removed.
  - The VTC asks bridges with `trust-task-discovery/0.3` instead of 0.2. 0.3
    only adds the optional `acceptanceWindow` to the response; the request is
    unchanged, and `vgi-bridge` answers 0.3 since v0.26.0.

  Docs, vtc-service/CLAUDE.md, the cnm `notRevertible` guidance, the admin
  console's gate-unenforced label and the default git_ns.rego comments now
  name job 0.6.
