  sent or pinned. `acl/change-role/0.2` still moves the administrative role.

  The handler makes the specification's checks 1-7 in order, each with its
  declared code: vtc.roles.assign (permissionDenied), no self-move in either
  direction (VTI-OPS-050, VTI-ACL-052), notFound, roleNotRecognized
  (details.offendingRole) / roleNotAssignable (`application` onto or off),
  stateMismatch (details.currentRole), the requester covering the entry
  (VTI-ACL-050), and fromRole == toRole answered `changed: false` with no
  gesture and no write (SPEC 7.2).

  The role-change ceremony carries items 8-18: authority follows the role
  only where it is exactly the one the current role implies;
  delegationExceedsGranter (axes); lastRoleAssigner checked before the policy
  and again under the write's lock (VTI-APV-009); the policy sees whether the
  move confers or withdraws authority and may not choose a different role
  (deniedByPolicy); the bound step-up and parked consent (VTI-OPS-051,
  VTI-APV-018/019); the compare-and-swap re-checked under LAST_ADMIN_LOCK
  (item 14); the role credential returned as roleVac; and a new
  CommunityRoleSet audit event (from/to, authority before/after, approval,
  action id, reason).

  The response is the generated type: subject, role, previousRole, changed,
  approval, entry (AclEntry 0.2) and roleVac. vtc-client's acl_change_role
  becomes members_role_set; `cnm access change-role` and the admin console
  send the new task. Approver summary templates are added for the new task
  (server and console pins); the 0.1 templates stay for history.

- **auth**: Answer step-ups with auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7, and stop serving 0.4 and 0.6 ([#2346](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2346))

Every step-up answer moves to approve-response 0.7
  (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#983). A user-verified WebAuthn assertion
  by the approver's own registered passkey is evidence on its own, so the admin
  console answers unsigned. A delegated key's proof never counts as the
  approver's. A didSigned or approverSigned answer, and every denial, still
  needs the approver's own proof.



### Changed

- **specs**: Take every Trust Task wire type from the generated vti-specs crates ([#2343](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2343))

Every `trust_tasks_rs::specs::<family>` path becomes `vti_specs::<family>`
  (`vti_specs_rooms::rooms` in vti-rooms, which stays wasm-light), and every
  `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::*` call becomes `vti_specs::schema_index::*`,
  which answers for exactly the versions the vti-specs-* locks pin. The
  framework's own specs are re-exported from vti_specs unchanged.

  No crate turns a trust-tasks-rs spec family on any more: the workspace
  compiles none of the deprecated prebuilt modules, only `validate`.

  The generated types are the same generator's output at the same module paths,
  but they are distinct Rust types from the prebuilt ones: a downstream crate
  that passes a `trust_tasks_rs::specs` value into a vta-sdk API must move its
  import to `vta_sdk::specs` (a find-and-replace).

  CLAUDE.md's rule now points at the generated crates and says how to pin a
  version; the SPEC FAMILIES notes in Cargo.toml are replaced.

- **vtc**: Approve-response 0.4 only for the console's unsigned answer; drop the unused acl/revoke 0.1 OpenAPI wrapper ([#2333](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2333))

The superseded auth/acl Trust Task versions, narrowed to what still needs
  them.

  auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4 (superseded by 0.6). The VTC now hears 0.4
  only as the admin console's unsigned session-passkey answer. Every signed
  answer — a member's step-up passkey beside their own proof, a refusal, a
  wallet's approver statement — is 0.6, and a signed 0.4 is refused with a
  pointer to 0.6. The 0.4 document is checked against 0.4's schema and then
  handled as the 0.6 payload it is wire-identical to, so
  `bound_step_up::approve` and everything past the door read 0.6 only. The
  console's Decline now sends 0.6.

  0.4 itself stays: approve-response 0.5 onward require the approver's own
  assertionMethod proof, and the console holds only a delegated key, which
  auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2 item 7 refuses as an approver's attestation. The
  console's unsigned answer has no successor in the specification yet.

  acl/change-role/0.1 (superseded by 0.2) stays as the community-role door,
  as #2323 kept it: 0.2 moves an AclEntry 0.2's administrative role, and the
  community role (member <-> admin, role-VAC re-mint, promotion serialisation)
  has no 0.2 task. Its uses now carry a per-item #[allow(deprecated)] naming
  that gap.



### Fixed

- **step-up**: One approve-request version, 0.5, across the VTA, the VTC and the mobile approver ([#2327](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2327))

`auth/step-up/approve-request` was minted at three versions: the VTA at 0.2
  (a hand-built JSON payload), vtc-service at 0.4 (inline in a refusal) and the
  did-hosting RP at 0.5. An approver therefore had to read all three, and
  vta-mobile-core read only 0.1 and 0.2 — so it could answer the VTA but not
  the RP or the VTC.

  - vta-service mints 0.5, built through the generated
    `approve_request::v0_5::Payload` and its schema check (as vtc-service
    already does) rather than a hand-written `json!`; the type URI comes from
    `<Payload as trust_tasks_rs::Payload>::TYPE_URI`. On the wire:
    `acceptableEvidence` -> a required `accepts`, `ttl` -> `ttlSeconds`;
    `sessionId` is still sent, since this is a session step-up.
  - vtc-service's inline request moves 0.4 -> 0.5 (`ttl` -> `ttlSeconds`).
    `bound_step_up::ApproveRequest` is now the 0.5 payload, hence `!`.
  - vta-mobile-core's `parse_step_up_request` accepts 0.5 only, matched
    exactly, and reads `accepts`. `approverSigned` is surfaced as
    `approver-signed` rather than dropped. The UniFFI record keeps its shape: a
    request that names no session (0.5 makes `sessionId` optional) surfaces an
    empty `session_id`, the convention `stepup`'s response draft already reads.
  - The VTC console reads `accepts` only (the 0.3 `acceptableEvidence`
    fallback is gone) and shows `ttlSeconds`.

  The browser wallet cuts over with this: pnm-browser-plugin matches the
  agent's request at 0.2 today and moves to the single 0.5 pin it already
  holds for the RP.

  version that removes a member from either sealed tier, and no longer serves

title: feat(peer-check): peer-check/ask 0.1 — a signed yes or no from a peer's own device
body:
Hello, and thank you for looking at this. I would be glad to change any part of it, including the name and whether it belongs here at all.

**Update after review:** thank you @stormer78 for the detailed review. It is addressed in the commits after the first one; the sections below describe the task as it now stands, and the "Open questions" section records how each question was settled.

## Why

I looked for a live task that lets one peer ask another "did you just send or ask me this?" and get back an answer the asker can verify on its own. I did not find one. The closest candidates each assume something this case does not have:

- `confirm/request` and `confirm/response` 0.1 did this, but were retired in #156 in favour of `task-consent`.
- `task-consent/*` is an executor asking an enrolled approver device to authorise a pending privileged task. There is no executor, pending task or enrolment between two peers on a phone call.
- `auth/step-up/*` raises the assurance level of a session; there is no session here.
- `auth/oob/*` approves a login through a service, `messaging/ping` checks liveness with no user involved, and `vtc/members/personhood/challenge` is specific to VTC communities.

The use I have in mind is generic: someone phones or messages you, you doubt it is who they say, and you send a short question to the other person's own device over a channel you already had. It is not tied to any one kind of scam.

## What this adds

One task, `peer-check/ask/0.1`, with a request and a `#response`, the schema, negative examples, and the regenerated Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings.

- **Request**, signed by the asker (`issuer`) to the party being asked (`recipient`): a challenge of at least 128 bits, a question (200 characters), an optional note (500 characters, untrusted display text), and a required `payload.expiresAt`, which is the deadline for the answer. The envelope `expiresAt` keeps its framework meaning (SPEC 7.2 item 12): it only bounds when the request is accepted, and the responder does not prompt for a stale request.
- **Response**, signed by the responder: the echoed challenge, the task digest of the request (SPEC 4.9.3), `decision` as `confirmed` or `notConfirmed`, `respondedAt`, and an optional `notConfirmedReason` from a small enum. The schema enforces that a reason only appears with `notConfirmed` (`dependentSchemas`), and there is an invalid example for it. A "no" is a successful response, not a `permissionDenied` refusal (SPEC 8, "A decision is not a failure").
- **Proofs** use `authentication` (SPEC 4.7.3). The task declares `retention: exchange` and no `outcomeEvidence`: the answer is between the two parties, and the asker keeps nothing.
- **A waiting prompt is a hold** (SPEC 8.6). While the prompt is open the responder answers with `trust-task-next-step` (`continuation: resubmit`) where the transport carries a reply, and answers a resubmission with the decision once it is known. A resubmission carries the same `challenge` and `payload.expiresAt`, and the answer's `requestDigest` covers the document it answers. On an asynchronous transport, silence is all the asker sees until the decision arrives.
- **Asker checks:** the issuer is the party it asked, the proof verifies under that party's `authentication` key, the challenge and request digest match, the answer is inside the payload deadline, and the key was valid when the check was made. Nothing there depends on the DID method.
- **Security and privacy:** the section says plainly what a yes proves (this key, on its device, a deliberate choice) and does not (that the person on the call is genuine). It makes no claim to defeat deepfakes, recommends a user-presence gate on the responder, and says the check is only worth much when it travels a different path from the suspicious contact. A "Responder disclosure" note records that `askerNotAccepted` and `noSurface` each tell the asker something about the responder (SPEC 12.6), and lets a responder stay silent instead of sending `askerNotAccepted` where the binding allows.

## Why it is not a revival of confirm, and not task-consent

`confirm` was retired because a requester-authored `reason` is the wrong basis for a consent decision, and task-consent has the executor author the effects. This task authorises nothing, which is also why the decision values are `confirmed` / `notConfirmed` and not `approved` / `denied`. It asks a peer a question about what the peer did, treats the asker's text as untrusted throughout, and binds the answer to the exact request by digest. It reuses none of the retired members' meanings. Unlike task-consent there is no executor, approver set or enrolment.

## Open questions, and how they were settled

1. **Name and family.** `peer-check/ask` in a new family, as proposed. `persona/*` is about identity attributes, and the retired `confirm/*` meaning is avoided.
2. **Proof purpose.** `authentication`, per SPEC 4.7.3, since the answer is between the two parties and not an attestation a third party relies on.
3. **`outcomeEvidence`.** Left out, consistent with `retention: exchange`. If a signed yes ever needs to be citable later, the consistent set would be `assertionMethod` plus `retention: durable` plus an `outcomeEvidence` declaration, and the response would need the request's `id` since `requestDigest` alone is not the item 20.5 binding.
4. **User-presence claim.** Left out: an unverifiable claim adds nothing the SHOULD does not already say.
5. **Category.** `authentication`.

Please say if any of these should go the other way.

## Not included

No transport binding choice, no UI requirements beyond how the question and note are shown, no VRC or credential linkage, no rate-limiting rules, and no claim about identifying the human on the other end. Keyring (a wallet) is a planned reference implementation; it is not referred to in the spec.

## Related

While working through the review I collected some ideas on authoring guidance and pre-submission checks in #984. Nothing in this PR depends on it.

## Checks

Run locally and passing: `npm run validate`, `npm run check-bindings`, `build-bundles` with `check-bundles`, `check-published-schemas`, regeneration of the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings with no drift, the `peer-check` Rust conformance tests, `go build` of the family, `dart analyze` of the generated package and `tsc --noEmit`. Every example in the spec validates against the schema, and each negative example fails for its stated reason. A trial merge into the latest `main` is clean with no generator drift. The Dart bindings were formatted with Dart 3.13, because the local 3.5 does not accept `--language-version`.

title: feat(peer-check): peer-check/ask 0.1 — a signed yes or no from a peer's own device (#973)
body:
feat(peer-check): peer-check/ask 0.1 — a signed yes or no from a peer's own device (#973)

* feat(peer-check): peer-check/ask 0.1 — a signed yes or no from a peer's own device

One party asks another a short question, such as "did you just ask me
for this?", over a channel they already share. The responder's device
prompts its user and returns a signed answer that echoes the challenge
and carries the task digest of the request, so the asker can verify it
against the responder's DID and it cannot be replayed against another
ask.

Draft. Specification, schema, negative examples and the regenerated Rust,
TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(peer-check): address review feedback

Add a required payload.expiresAt as the answer deadline and leave the
envelope expiresAt with its framework meaning. Sign with the
authentication purpose. Treat a prompt waiting on the user as a hold
answered with trust-task-next-step. Enforce deniedReason with
dependentSchemas and add an invalid example. Rename the decision values
to confirmed and notConfirmed. Note that askerNotAccepted and noSurface
disclose responder state and allow silence instead. Explain why both
respondedAt and issuedAt exist. Regenerate the Rust, TypeScript, Go and
Dart libraries.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(peer-check): tighten hold semantics and examples

- Reconcile hold resubmission with the asker's checks: a resubmission keeps
  the same challenge and payload.expiresAt, no second prompt is raised, and
  requestDigest names the request document being answered.
- Reword the hold rule to "answer with a next step where the transport
  carries a reply, never an error"; only askerNotAccepted may be answered
  with silence, and a silent responder applies its asker policy before any
  hold. Note that noSurface is retryable and discloses device state.
- Make the example envelope expiresAt the shorter bound, compute the real
  requestDigest, sign the hold example, and declare identifierScope: any.
- Rename deniedReason to notConfirmedReason (and notRecognised to
  notRecognized); use US spelling throughout.
- Explain why notConfirmed is a successful response, not permissionDenied.
- Regenerate Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* fix(peer-check): name the resubmission's threadId, correct the challenge-length note

A resubmission's threadId is the original's threadId, or the original's id
where it carried none (SPEC §4.9); the example request carries none, so
"the same threadId" had nothing to point at. The short-challenge invalid
example said 128 bits is 16 base64url characters; it is 16 bytes, 22
characters.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
Co-authored-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc)!: move a community role with vtc/members/role/set/0.1 and stop serving acl/change-role/0.1
body:
Replaces the VTC's community-role door, `acl/change-role/0.1`, with `vtc/members/role/set/0.1` (trust-tasks-tf `specs/vtc/members/role/set/0.1`), and stops serving, sending and pinning `acl/change-role/0.1`. `acl/change-role/0.2` still moves the administrative role on its own. This removes the last `#[allow(deprecated)]` items for change-role 0.1 (vtc-service `acl_tasks.rs`, `trust_tasks/mod.rs` `ACL_CHANGE_COMMUNITY_ROLE_TYPE`; vtc-client `acl.rs` ×2).

## What changed

- **Pinning.** `vtc/members/role/set/0.1` is pinned in `vti-specs-vtc`. `acl/change-role/0.1` is removed from `vti-specs-core`, which now pins `"0.2"` only.
- **Handler** (`trust_tasks/member_role_tasks.rs`). It makes checks 1–7 in the spec's order, each with its declared code:
  1. `vtc.roles.assign` from the live, unexpired, unsuspended entry, else `permissionDenied`.
  2. No self-move in either direction (VTI-OPS-050, VTI-ACL-052). This is `permissionDenied`, and the refusal names this task.
  3. `notFound`.
  4. `roleNotRecognized` with `details.offendingRole`, and `roleNotAssignable` for `application` as `toRole` or as the role the entry holds.
  5. `stateMismatch` with `details.currentRole`.
  6. The requester covers the entry (VTI-ACL-050).
  7. `fromRole == toRole` answers `changed: false` and writes nothing. No gesture is asked and no credential is issued.
- **Ceremony** (`ceremony/orchestrate.rs`, `ceremony/execute.rs`, `routes/acl.rs::set_community_role`). It covers items 8–18:
  - Item 8: authority follows the role only when it is exactly the one `fromRole` implies.
  - Item 9: `delegationExceedsGranter` with `axes`.
  - Item 10: `lastRoleAssigner` is checked before the policy and any gesture, and again under the write's `LAST_ADMIN_LOCK` (VTI-APV-009).
  - Item 11: the role-change policy now also sees `confers_authority` / `withdraws_authority`. A policy that allows a different role is refused (`deniedByPolicy`). A deny is `deniedByPolicy`.
  - Items 12–13: the bound step-up and the parked consent are unchanged (VTI-OPS-051, VTI-APV-018/019).
  - Item 14: the compare-and-swap is now re-checked under the lock the write takes (`execute::remint_from`). A move onto a role implying `vtc.roles.assign` is serialised on `PROMOTE_LOCK`.
  - Item 16: the role credential is returned as `roleVac`.
  - Item 18: a new `AuditEvent::CommunityRoleSet` (vti-common, `#[non_exhaustive]` data) records from/to, authority before/after, approval, action id and reason.
- **Response.** It is the generated type: `subject, role, previousRole, changed, approval, entry` (AclEntry 0.2), `roleVac`.
- **Clients.**
  - vtc-client: `acl_change_role` / `acl::change_role` / `task::CHANGE_ROLE` become `members_role_set` / `acl::role_set` / `task::ROLE_SET`.
  - `cnm access change-role` sends the new task.
  - The admin console's promote and demote use `setCommunityRole` (`MEMBERS_ROLE_SET_TASK`).
- **Approver summaries.** There are two new pinned templates (grant/reduce) for `vtc/members/role/set/0.1`, in both the server and the console. The 0.1 templates are kept for history. The authority-reduction-pending notice computes the resulting administrative role for a role/set move.
- **Tests.**
  - `tests/it/members_role_set.rs` witnesses all seven declared codes in the error-code census. It also covers the moderator move (authority, `roleVac`, audit row) and a promotion to admin that is parked and then approved (VTI-APV-018).
  - `signed_step_up.rs` adds the self-move refusal (VTI-OPS-050) and the no-op.
  - Existing change-role tests are moved to the new task.
  - The conformance table has a `checked!` entry built from the handler's own projection.
- **Docs.** `docs/03-vtc/{admin-access,bootstrap-runbook,community-lifecycle}.md` now name the new task.

## Notes / known gaps

- **A policy `refer` is not parked yet.** Item 11 says the policy may refer a move for approval. As before, a `refer` on the signed door is answered `permissionDenied`; it is not parked. The default `role_change` policy only refers a promotion to admin without a step-up, which the signed door never sends, so this is reachable only through a custom policy.
- **`vtc/members/update/0.1` is unchanged.** It keeps `role` and refuses `admin` with `adminRoleForbidden`, per role/set's "update/0.1 also accepts a `role`, for any role but `admin`". It also refuses moves to or from `moderator` / `issuer` / administrator entries with the same code. That predates this PR: update/0.1's consumer text only says "If `role` is `admin`, return `adminRoleForbidden`". It is kept because those moves change administrative authority and need the bound gesture (VTI-OPS-051).
- **Parked 0.1 moves will not execute.** An action parked under `acl/change-role/0.1` before upgrade cannot execute after it, because the type is no longer served. It still renders in the history.
- **Approval for an unopposed demotion.** A demotion that nobody else could consent to (`unopposed`) is reported `approval: waived` in single-administrator mode and `policyAllowed` otherwise; the spec's `Approval` enum has no separate value. It is still audited `Critical` (`AuthorityReducedUnopposed`).

## Verification

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`: 0 warnings.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- nextest, workspace without vtc: 6686 passed.
- nextest, vtc-service + vtc-client: 3578 passed.
- Doc tests: green.
- admin-ui vitest: 1355 passed. `tsc -b`: clean.

title: docs(design-notes): why trigger links are not DIDComm out-of-band URLs
body:
## Summary

Adds `docs/05-design-notes/trigger-link-design.md` and an entry for it in
`docs/README.md` (Part V). Docs only; no change to the specification is
proposed.

The note explains design choices in the trigger-link chapter of the VTI
specification (`spec/07a-links.md`, VTI-LNK-001 to 124) that the chapter states
as rules but does not argue at length. It answers two questions raised in
discussion of the chapter:

- Was DIDComm's `?_oob=` encoding, or its `?_oobid=` short URL, considered, given
  that they would fit VCALM's affordances for bridging a QR code to DIDComm
  out-of-band?
- Does the choice mean a trigger link is always a new kind of QR code that
  DIDComm-only scanners do not read?

## What it covers

- Why the link names whom to contact and which flow to start, and leaves the
  protocol to the contact's DID document (VTI-LNK-053, VTI-LNK-057), and the
  mechanical reasons that `_oob` and `_oobid` do not suit (query visibility,
  fetch by reference, size, goal codes).
- What it costs: a DIDComm-only scanner does not act on a trigger link; how a
  wallet that reads both formats can share a scanner, and the limits
  (VTI-LNK-020: `too-long`, `query-form`); what released Credo does with a
  trigger link.
- Why `https` and not a custom scheme (VTI-LNK-010 to 013).
- What survives an outage of the link host versus the inviter's own DNS, site or
  DID host.
- Three DIDComm fallbacks, none specified, and why two codes on one page is the
  preferred one.
- VCALM section 3.7: the bridge sits beside a trigger link, not in it, and why
  one URL carrying both is ruled out by VTI-LNK-072.

## Checks

- Every VTI-LNK and VTI-TRN requirement cited exists on `dtgwg-vti-spec` `main`
  and says what the note says; checked line by line by a second reader.
- DIDComm, VCALM and RFC 8252 quotations checked against the published texts.
- Byte figures recomputed by script; assumptions are stated in the note.
- Credo behaviour read from the published `@credo-ts/didcomm` 0.7.4 and 0.6.3
  packages; not run.

## Not verified

No phone has tested these links. Camera hand-off during a link-host outage was
not checked. DIDComm readers other than Credo were not checked. No VCALM
implementation was tried. The note says so in its last section.

title: docs(design-notes): why trigger links are not DIDComm out-of-band URLs (#2336)
body:
docs(design-notes): why trigger links are not DIDComm out-of-band URLs (#2336)

* docs(design-notes): why trigger links are not DIDComm out-of-band URLs

Adds a design note explaining the trigger-link chapter of the VTI
specification (spec/07a-links.md) where it states rules without arguing
them: why a trigger link is an https URL with its parameters in the
fragment, and not a DIDComm out-of-band (_oob, _oobid) URL or a VCALM
interaction URL.

It records the cost (a scanner that only reads DIDComm out-of-band URLs
does not act on a trigger link, and what released Credo does with one),
how a wallet can read both formats and the limits of that, why a custom
scheme is not used, what survives an outage of the link host versus the
inviter, and three DIDComm fallbacks that stay open. Requirements are
cited by identifier. No change to the specification is proposed.

Signed-off-by: Brendan A. Miller <code+os@brendanmiller.com>

* docs(design-notes): trigger-link note: soften VTI-TRN citation, link spec and workspace docs

VTI-TRN-002/003 keep authorization independent of transport; they do not
govern links, so the note now calls the link design consistent with them
rather than the same stance. Links the spec chapter by URL, adds an
"In this workspace" section pointing at the sign-in docs, and shortens
the docs/README.md entry to match its neighbours.

body:
feat(rooms/keys/act): 0.9 completes rooms/records/put/0.4 (#990)

rooms/records/put/0.4 (#987) lets a record on an open room carry a file,
its description and random file key in cleartext.file. 0.8's table is
closed (Recipient item 1) and names records/put at 0.1–0.3 only, so a
conforming key holder refuses 0.4 with typeNotActable: a member whose keys
their key holder holds could upload an open room's blob (upload/begin/0.2
is in the table) but never write the record that names it, and the blob
would sit unreferenced until collected.

0.9 adds rooms/records/put/0.4 to the put row, write, presentation
inserted, completed exactly as 0.3. The key holder neither mints nor checks
the file key: the producer mints it (put 0.4 Producer item 7), the host
checks the record (Host item 12), and the key holder signs what it was
handed unaltered (Recipient item 6).

Schemas are 0.8's and no error code is added; the table only widens, so
0.9 declares extends: "0.8" and every spec naming 0.8 stays current. All
four bindings regenerated.

title: feat(auth)!: answer step-ups with auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7, and stop serving 0.4 and 0.6
body:
Moves every step-up answer to `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#983) and stops serving 0.4 and 0.6. This removes the last `#[allow(deprecated)]` items for approve-response, and the build has 0 warnings.

## Why

0.5 and 0.6 required the approver's own proof on every answer. A console holds only a delegated key, and `auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2` item 7 forbids that key's proof on any approve-response. So the VTC kept serving 0.4 for one purpose: the console's unsigned passkey answer. 0.7 resolves the conflict. A user-verified WebAuthn assertion by the approver's own registered passkey is evidence on its own, so a `webauthn` approval may come with no proof. A delegated key's proof never counts.

## What changes

**Specs pin.** In vti-specs-core, `auth/step-up/approve-response` is now `"0.7"`. Previously both `["0.4", "0.6"]` were pinned.

**VTC** (`vtc-service`)
- One handler serves 0.7, and the dispatcher no longer routes 0.4 or 0.6. The proof checks run before the pending step-up is looked up (consumer item 1a):
  - A proof by a console key is refused as `subjectMismatch` at the spine.
  - A proof by any signer other than the subject is also refused.
  - With no proof, the VTC hears only an approval carrying `webauthn` evidence. That answer must name the subject as `issuer`, and its credential must be registered here. A `didSigned` or `approverSigned` answer, or any denial, without a proof gets `proofRequired`.
- `bound_step_up::approve`:
  - A step-up passkey may now answer unsigned. 0.7 makes the passkey assertion evidence on its own. Session passkeys stop counting once a subject holds a step-up passkey, so refusing it unsigned would leave a console administrator who enrolled one with no way to answer.
  - Another subject's passkey now gets `subjectMismatch` (item 4).
  - A session passkey answering for a subject who holds a dedicated factor gets `assertionInvalid`/`credentialNotAccepted`.
  - `assertionInvalid`'s `details.reason` now uses 0.7's lowerCamelCase enum, mapped from the webauthn-rs error.

**Admin console** (`vtc-service/admin-ui`)
- The console's passkey answer is now an unsigned 0.7 document.
- Fixes the **Decline** button. It signed the refusal with the console key, which the VTC refuses. Under 0.7 (producer item 6) a denial must be `didSigned`, proved by the approver's own DID. The console now declines through the VTA wallet plugin, signed as the subject (`declineStepUp`). With no wallet it offers no Decline and tells the operator to let the request lapse.

**VTA** (`vta-service`)
- The VTA serves 0.7. The proof is now verified before the pending step-up is consumed, so a document refused for its proof leaves the challenge in place.
- A `webauthn` approval without a proof is accepted. For such an answer, `grantedAcr` is ignored and the level is the passkey's, `aal2` (item 4a).
- A missing proof on a `didSigned` answer or a denial gets `proofRequired`, and an invalid proof gets the framework's `proofInvalid`. Before this change it got the undeclared `…:proof_invalid`.

**SDK and clients**
- `vta_sdk::trust_tasks::TASK_AUTH_STEP_UP_APPROVE_RESPONSE_0_6` is renamed to `…_0_7`. This is a breaking change.
- `retry_safety` is updated.
- vtc-client `git_ns`, vta-mobile-core `stepup` and cnm-cli send 0.7. Their answers stay signed by the approver's own key.

**Policy** (`vta-policy`)
- `RETIRED_TASK_TYPES` maps approve-response 0.1–0.6 to 0.7. An approval rule that names a retired version therefore migrates instead of failing open.

## Tests

New or updated tests hold 0.7 consumer item 1a and item 4a:
- unsigned denial is refused;
- unsigned `didSigned` is refused;
- unsigned `webauthn` is recorded or elevated, with `grantedAcr` ignored;
- a step-up passkey answers unsigned;
- refusals leave the challenge unspent;
- a console-key proof gets `subjectMismatch`.

Console tests cover the wallet-signed Decline and the no-wallet case.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.36.3
body:
### Added

- **rooms/records/put**: 0.4 lets an open room's record carry a file ([#987](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/987))

An open room could hold notes and nothing else. A file's description
  (FileManifest) could only travel inside a sealed record body, and its key could
  only be derived from the room's per-epoch storage key, and an open room has
  neither: no sealed body, and no group to derive a key from. rooms/blobs/* never
  cared about the tier; the gap was entirely on the record side.

  - rooms/records/put/0.4 (extends 0.3): cleartext gains an optional `file`, a
    FileManifest, and `blobs` may name that file's blob. On an open room the
    host, which can read the record, refuses with malformedRequest a record whose
    `blobs` is not exactly `cleartext.file.blobRef`, names a blob without a
    `file`, or whose `file` carries no `fileKey`.
  - rooms/_shared/0.1 FileManifest gains an optional `fileKey` (additive): on an
    open room the uploader mints the file key at random for that one file and
    carries it there; it MUST be absent from a sealed body, where the key is
    derived. Padding, STREAM, associated data and reading are unchanged, so
    there is one blob format and one reader for every tier. The key in the clear
    withholds nothing from the host, which the open tier never did, but keeps
    the stored blob opaque to a party holding only the storage.
  - The descriptions of `name` and `digest` now say what holds on each tier.

  All four bindings regenerated.

- **vtc/admin/invites**: Create and list 0.2 — passkey invitations, with did optional ([#989](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/989))

* feat(vtc/admin/invites): create and list 0.2 — passkey invitations, with did optional

  vtc/admin/invites/create 0.1 required `did`, so an administrator could invite
  only someone who already held a DID in a wallet; a passkey invitation — whose
  administrator DID is derived from the passkey registered at
  vtc/install/claim/passkey/finish 0.1 — could be issued only by the operator on
  the host.

  create 0.2:
  - `did` is optional. Present: a wallet invitation (claimed with
    vtc/install/claim/{start,finish} 0.3). Absent: a passkey invitation.
  - `did`, when present, must begin `did:`.
  - Both kinds confer the same authority: an administrator entry with the
    community's full administrative authority, delegated by the inviter,
    labelled with `label`. A wallet invitation writes it now for a DID with no
    entry; a passkey invitation records it with the invitation and
    passkey/finish item 9 writes it for the derived DID.
  - A passkey invitation costs what an entry-writing wallet invitation costs
    (the inviter's step-up, another administrator's consent): at its claim no
    administrator is present to authorise it, so issuing it is the grant.
  - The response gains a required `kind` (`wallet` | `passkey`);
    `aclEntryCreated` is always false for a passkey invitation.

  list 0.2 (with vtc/_shared/0.2/invite): each InviteSummary gains a required
  `kind`; a passkey invitation's `targetDid` is absent until it is consumed, then
  the derived DID.

  revoke is unchanged (it takes only `jti`); its prose now links the 0.2
  versions.

- **vta/dids**: Method-neutral key-role family, creation and recovery, with per-method profiles ([#986](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/986))

* feat(vta/dids): method-neutral key-role family, creation and recovery, with per-method profiles

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.36.2` → `0.36.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.36.2` → `0.36.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-cli` | crates.io | `0.1.2` → `0.1.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.36.2` → `0.36.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.36.2` → `0.36.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.36.2` → `0.36.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.36.2` → `0.36.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.36.2` → `0.36.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.36.2` → `0.36.3` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.28.2` → `0.28.3` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.3`) | `0.10.2` → `0.10.3` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.12` → `0.9.13` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc)!: passkey admin invites from the console, vtc/admin/invites/{create,list}/0.2
body:
vtc/admin/invites/create/0.1 required `did`, so the console could issue only
wallet invitations; a passkey invitation needed `vtc admin invite` on the host.
trust-tasks-tf #989 adds create and list 0.2, which VTI now serves and sends in
place of 0.1 (nothing outside VTI sent 0.1).

Wire changes:
- create 0.2: `did` optional. Present → wallet invitation (claimed with
  vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.3); absent → passkey invitation (claimed
  with vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1). The response gains a
  required `kind` (`wallet` | `passkey`); `aclEntryCreated` is false for a
  passkey invitation.
- list 0.2: every entry gains a required `kind`; a passkey invitation's
  `targetDid` is absent until consumed, then the derived DID.
- revoke stays at 0.1.

Behaviour (create 0.2 items 3-4): a passkey invitation records an
install::InvitedAuthority — community administrator with the full ceiling,
delegated by the inviter, labelled with `label` — and writes nothing to the
ACL; passkey/finish item 9 writes it for the derived DID. Since nobody is
present to authorise it at the claim, issuing one always costs the inviter's
bound gesture and another unrestricted administrator's consent, parked under
the stable subject `urn:openvtc:vtc:admin-invite:passkey`. A consumed row now
remembers it was a passkey invitation (`Consumed.passkey`) so list can report
its kind.

Console: Access control → Admin invites → Invite admin asks "How will they
sign in?" — with a passkey (default; no DID needed) or with a wallet (their
DID). The list shows each invite's kind, and "created when claimed" for a
passkey invite's DID; Regenerate works for both kinds. The action summary for
create 0.2 is a new pinned template (0.1's kept for history) with a passkey
vector shared by both renderers.

Pinned with `trust-tasks -C vti-specs-vtc` (create/list 0.1 → 0.2); 0.1's
summary template stays only so an invite parked under it renders in history.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#989 (merged).

Local (rebased on #2343): `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client -p vti-specs -p vti-specs-vtc` (3573 passed), doc tests, clippy `-D warnings` (workspace), fmt, admin-ui lint + vitest (1355 passed). Before the rebase the full workspace run passed too (6686).

title: chore(lints): stop allowing deprecated, workspace-wide
body:
Last of three PRs (after #2340 and #2343). It removes `deprecated = "allow"` from `[workspace.lints.rust]` and from room-host, vti-rooms, vti-voting and vti-witness, which now inherit the workspace lints. It also removes every `#[allow(deprecated)]` the build no longer needs. Before the move these allows hid about 10,200 deprecation warnings.

`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` reports **0 warnings**, and so does `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## What still needs an allow

Each remaining allow sits on one item, with a comment giving the reason:

| Deprecated item | Where | Why it stays |
|---|---|---|
| `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.6` | vta-sdk `TASK_…_0_6`, vta-service `step_up.rs`, vtc-service `bound_step_up.rs` / `trust_tasks`, vtc-client `git_ns.rs`, vta-mobile-core `stepup.rs`, one VTC test | The registry has superseded it with 0.7, and VTI has not moved. |
| `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4` | vtc-service `handle_step_up_approve_response` | The console's unsigned answer. From 0.5 onward the spec requires a proof the console cannot make, a spec gap. |
| `vta/webvh/dids/update/1.0`, `rotate-keys/1.0` | vta-service conformance witnesses | Still served; whether to move them is a pending decision. |
| `acl/change-role/0.1` | vtc-service `acl_tasks.rs` / `trust_tasks`, vtc-client `acl.rs` | The community-role door. 0.2 cannot express it, a spec gap. |
| superseded rows of the `rooms/keys/act/0.8` table (`records/put` 0.1–0.2, `records/list` 0.1–0.4, `info` 0.1–0.2, `vtc/rooms/offers/list` 0.1–0.3, …) | vta-service `room_act.rs`, vta-sdk `is_offer_type` | The table is the specification's. |
| `AtomicU64/AtomicUsize::fetch_update` | vtc-service `server.rs`, vta-service `test_support.rs` | Not a Trust Task deprecation. The replacement, `try_update`, is newer than the 1.95 MSRV. |
| `fjall::DatabaseBuilder::max_write_buffer_size` | vti-common `store` | Not a Trust Task deprecation. It is still wired, and the existing note explains it. |

title: feat(rooms/records/put): 0.4 lets an open room's record carry a file
body:
## Problem

An `open` data room can hold notes but not files. `rooms/blobs/*` doesn't care which tier a room is; the gap is entirely on the record side:

- `rooms/records/put/0.3` item 6 puts a file's `FileManifest` only inside a sealed `SealedRecordBody`. An open room's `cleartext` has no `file` member, and the same item forbids naming a blob the body doesn't describe.
- The file key is `HKDF(storage_key(epoch), …)`. An open room has no group, so there is no storage key to derive it from.

## Change

**`rooms/records/put/0.4`** (`extends: "0.3"`, minor):
- `cleartext` gains an optional `file` (`FileManifest`), and `blobs` may name that file's blob.
- New producer item 7: on an open room, seal the blob under a key minted at random for that one file, and carry it in `fileKey`, with `epoch` set to the room's epoch at the time. On the sealed tiers the key is still derived, and `fileKey` must not be set.
- New host item 12: on an open room the host can read the record, so it refuses with `malformedRequest` a record whose `blobs` isn't exactly `cleartext.file.blobRef`, a record that names a blob without a `file`, or a `file` with no `fileKey`. Host item 13: a host stores `file` exactly as received, and a policy of "no files in this room" refuses at upload, not at the record.
- A new example, plus Security & Privacy text: an open room's file is readable by the host and is the host's word, just as the rest of an open record is.

**`rooms/_shared/0.1` `FileManifest`**, changed in place, additively:
- A new optional `fileKey` (32 bytes, base64url). It must be present on an open room and absent in a sealed body, and a reader refuses a file that breaks either rule.
- Padding, STREAM, associated data and the reading rules are unchanged, so every tier shares one blob format and one reader.
- The `name` and `digest` descriptions now say what holds on each tier.

**Why put the key in the clear rather than store plain bytes?** It keeps one format and one reader, and the stored blob stays opaque to anyone who holds only the storage (a bucket operator, a backup). It hides nothing from the host or from anyone the host serves the record to, and neither did the open tier before this change.

`rooms/records/get` and `rooms/keys/read` already return `cleartext` as an open object, so neither needs a new version.

## Checks

- `npm run validate`: 1153 specs pass, with no stale references.
- All four bindings are regenerated, and `npm run check-bindings` agrees.
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` succeeds.

Implementations follow in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure (host and `pnm`) and OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin (portal and console) after a `trust-tasks-rs` release.

title: refactor(specs)!: take every Trust Task wire type from the generated vti-specs crates
body:
Second of three PRs moving VTI off trust-tasks-rs's deprecated prebuilt `trust_tasks_rs::specs` modules (#2340 added the generated crates).

## What changes

- **Import paths.** Every `trust_tasks_rs::specs::<family>` path becomes `vti_specs::<family>`, across 281 files in 14 crates. In `vti-rooms`, which stays wasm-light, it becomes `vti_specs_rooms::rooms`. The module paths are unchanged, so this is a mechanical rewrite. The framework modules (`trust_task_discovery`, …) are re-exported from `vti_specs` unchanged.
- **Index lookups.** Every `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::*` call (about 60) becomes `vti_specs::schema_index::*`, which answers for exactly the versions the `vti-specs-*` locks pin.
- **No spec family features.** No crate turns a `trust-tasks-rs` spec family on any more. `cargo tree -e features -i trust-tasks-rs` now shows only `validate`, so the workspace compiles none of the deprecated prebuilt modules.
- **Manifests.** Each crate that names a spec depends on `vti-specs`, or `vti-specs-rooms` for `vti-rooms`. The "SPEC FAMILIES ARE DECLARED PER CRATE" notes in the root `Cargo.toml` are replaced by "SPEC VERSIONS ARE PINNED IN THE `vti-specs-*` CRATES".
- **CLAUDE.md.** "Trust Task wire types come from the generated `vti-specs` crates" replaces the old rule. The section says to look Type URIs up in `vti_specs::schema_index`, and a "Pinning a task version" section explains how to use `trust-tasks add` and `update`, and to commit the lock and the bundles. `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md` and `vti-voting/CLAUDE.md` follow.
- **`vta-sdk/tests/generated_wire_types_census.rs`** now reads the `vti-specs` index.

## Tests that asked "does the registry publish it" now ask "is it pinned"

- **`vtc-service` `trust_task_manifest`:** `NAMED_NOT_PINNED` lists the superseded versions the code names only in order to refuse them or map them to a successor: `confirm/response/0.1`, `git-ns` 0.1/0.3, `provision/integration` 0.1/0.2, and `witness/session` 0.1. A stale entry fails.
- **`vta-service` `produced_census::NOT_PRODUCED`:** the same idea for the strings named in `vta-service`.
- **`generated_wire_types_census` baseline:** loses the nine `acl_management` 0.1 body types (67 → 58), because `acl/*/0.1` is not pinned, so no generated module exists for those types to duplicate.
- **`the_spec_index_is_populated`:** checks `acl/grant/0.2`, the version VTI serves, instead of 0.1.

## Breaking for downstream

The generated types come from the same generator at the same paths, but they are **distinct Rust types** from the prebuilt ones. A downstream crate that passes a `trust_tasks_rs::specs` value into a `vta-sdk` API has to change its import to `vta_sdk::specs`, which is a find-and-replace.

## Checked locally

On this branch rebased on main, all of these pass:
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` (6686 passed)
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (3562 passed)
- both doctest runs
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`

title: feat(specs): generate the Trust Task wire types VTI pins, with trust-tasks-build
body:
First of three PRs moving VTI off trust-tasks-rs's prebuilt `trust_tasks_rs::specs` modules, which 0.36 deprecates (they go in about a quarter), onto types generated with `trust-tasks-build`. This one adds the crates and a census. Nothing uses them yet.

Stack:
1. **this PR**: the generated crates, the facade, `vta_sdk::specs` and the census
2. the import rewrite: every `trust_tasks_rs::specs` / `schema_index` use moves to `vti_specs`, and no crate turns a spec family on
3. removing `deprecated = "allow"` and every `#[allow(deprecated)]` that is no longer needed

## The crates

| Crate | Pins | Families |
|---|---|---|
| `vti-specs-rooms` | 62 | `rooms/*`, on its own so `vti-rooms-wasm` compiles nothing else |
| `vti-specs-vta` | 110 | `vta/*` |
| `vti-specs-vtc` | 210 | `vtc/*` |
| `vti-specs-core` | 282 | the other 25 families |
| `vti-specs` | — | the facade |

- **Generation.** Each family crate's `build.rs` runs `trust_tasks_build::Config::new().index(true).compile()` over its own `trust-tasks.toml`, `trust-tasks.lock` and `trust-tasks/` bundles. All three are committed and included in the package. The build checks every bundle against its locked digest and never uses the network.
- **One version, one crate.** Each version is generated in exactly one crate, so a type is the same type everywhere in the workspace. A test (`the_generated_tables_are_disjoint`) holds this.
- **The facade (`vti-specs`).** It re-exports every family at its `trust_tasks_rs::specs` path, plus the unlockable framework modules (`trust_task_discovery`, …). It also merges the four `INDEX` tables with `trust_tasks_rs::type_index::lookup` into a drop-in `schema_index`: `schema_for`, `spec_policy_for`, `error_codes_for`, `max_document_bytes_for`, plus `is_pinned` and `entry`. A `trust-task-*` / `trust-ceremony-*` URI falls through to `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index`. For any other URI, `None` means "not pinned".
- **`vta-sdk`** re-exports the facade as `vta_sdk::specs`, so downstream crates (pnm, cnm, openvtc, VGI) can fix their imports with a find-and-replace.
- **Publishing.** All five crates are published, because `vta-sdk` is, and they depend only on crates.io crates. `vti-specs-core` packages to 459 KiB compressed. `Dockerfile.nitro` copies them, and the member count and version requirements pass their checks.

## What is pinned: 664 versions

The versions VTI uses today, collected from the code rather than chosen:

1. **Every version module the workspace names.** I found these by building against a copy of trust-tasks-rs whose every version module carried a `#[deprecated(note = "VTIUSE <path>")]`. That listed 616 modules across every target with `--all-features`. The compiler then found 14 more that the lint does not report: paths in `<X as Payload>::TYPE_URI` position (the `rooms/keys/act/0.8` table in `room_act.rs`, and `messaging/account/update/0.2`).
2. **The Type URIs VTI sends or serves as strings.** This covers `registry/*` (0.1 and the current versions, both still sent), `did-management/*`, `push/provision/0.2`, `messaging/message/status/0.2`, `task-consent/granted/0.1`, `credential-exchange/present/0.1`, `git-trust/grant/0.1`, `auth/passkey/login/finish/0.2`, and the `vtc/join-requests`/`members` receipts.

I left out the superseded versions VTI only mentions in retirement maps or in refusal tests: `vta-policy` approvals, `provision/integration` 0.1/0.2, and the tests that check old URIs are refused.

## The census

`trust_tasks::spec_pin_census`, in `vta-service` and `vtc-service`, fails if any of these are not pinned:
- the VTA's dispatched, REST-routed and feature-gated URIs;
- every `TASK_*` constant, read from the source;
- every `const …: &str = "https://trusttasks.org/spec/<slug>/<M.N>"` in the non-test source of every workspace member;
- every URI the VTC serves (`discovery::served_uris()`).

The exceptions are explicit lists with reasons:
- `UNSPECCED_DISPATCHED_URIS`, which already exists: the registry has no spec for these.
- `NOT_PINNED`: the historical `provision/integration` 0.1/0.2 forms, and the `git-ns/right/grant/0.1` framework label.

Both lists fail when an entry goes stale. Without the census, a missing pin fails open: `schema_for` answers `None`, and the spine dispatches the payload unvalidated.

## Measurements

Measured on an Apple M-series machine with 64 GB, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` (no sccache), a fresh target directory per run, `/usr/bin/time -l cargo build --timings`, dev profile. "Before" is `main` at e6380bf1d. "After" is this PR plus the import rewrite (PR 2 of the stack), which is the state the workspace ends up in. Other builds were running on the machine at the same time, so treat wall times as ±10%.

| Build | Before: wall / peak RSS | After: wall / peak RSS | Spec code, before → after (`--timings` unit time) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-p vta-sdk` | 162 s / 17.2 GB | **103 s / 4.9 GB** | `trust-tasks-rs` with vta-sdk's 23 families: 139 s → runtime 4 s, plus vti-specs-{core 57, vtc 51, vta 14, rooms 7} s, built in parallel; build scripts 1–2.5 s each |
| `-p vti-rooms-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` | 71 s / 1.44 GB | **54 s / 1.09 GB** | `trust-tasks-rs[rooms]` 9.6 s → runtime 4.3 s + `vti-specs-rooms` 5.2 s (build script 0.8 s) |
| `--workspace` | 321 s / 18.0 GB | **261 s / 5.4 GB** | `trust-tasks-rs` with the union of families: 200 s → runtime 5 s + vti-specs-{core 44, vtc 28, vta 15, rooms 8} s |
| the spec code alone (vta-sdk's families vs `vti-specs`) | 132 s / 15.9 GB | 54 s / 4.9 GB | |
| the spec code alone (`rooms` vs `vti-specs-rooms`) | 15 s / 1.40 GB | 14 s / 0.96 GB | |

The before column is dominated by one rustc unit: `trust-tasks-rs` compiling every version of every enabled family, about 1,000 versions for vta-sdk. After, the 664 pinned versions are split across four units that build in parallel. `vti-specs-core` is now the longest of them (44–57 s). If it needs to come down further, splitting it in two is the next step.

## Not done here
- **No `declare_extends()` call.** The facade offers one. Today's runtime table is empty (`extends_index.rs` is `_ => None` in 0.36.1 and 0.36.2), so VTI does no forward-minor routing now. Calling it would turn routing on, which is a behaviour change, so it is left out of this PR.
- **`trust-tasks-rs` floor raised to 0.36.2.** That is the first release with `type_index`. This adds `trust-tasks-build = "0.1.3"`, the first release with `.index(true)`.

title: feat(vtc/admin/invites): create and list 0.2 — passkey invitations, with did optional (#989)
body:
feat(vtc/admin/invites): create and list 0.2 — passkey invitations, with did optional (#989)

* feat(vtc/admin/invites): create and list 0.2 — passkey invitations, with did optional

vtc/admin/invites/create 0.1 required `did`, so an administrator could invite
only someone who already held a DID in a wallet; a passkey invitation — whose
administrator DID is derived from the passkey registered at
vtc/install/claim/passkey/finish 0.1 — could be issued only by the operator on
the host.

create 0.2:
- `did` is optional. Present: a wallet invitation (claimed with
  vtc/install/claim/{start,finish} 0.3). Absent: a passkey invitation.
- `did`, when present, must begin `did:`.
- Both kinds confer the same authority: an administrator entry with the
  community's full administrative authority, delegated by the inviter,
  labelled with `label`. A wallet invitation writes it now for a DID with no
  entry; a passkey invitation records it with the invitation and
  passkey/finish item 9 writes it for the derived DID.
- A passkey invitation costs what an entry-writing wallet invitation costs
  (the inviter's step-up, another administrator's consent): at its claim no
  administrator is present to authorise it, so issuing it is the grant.
- The response gains a required `kind` (`wallet` | `passkey`);
  `aclEntryCreated` is always false for a passkey invitation.

list 0.2 (with vtc/_shared/0.2/invite): each InviteSummary gains a required
`kind`; a passkey invitation's `targetDid` is absent until it is consumed, then
the derived DID.

revoke is unchanged (it takes only `jti`); its prose now links the 0.2
versions.

title: fix(vtc): bind an invited wallet administrator's approver at claim finish
body:
A wallet invitation (`vtc admin invite --did`, vtc/admin/invites/create)
claimed with vtc/install/claim/finish/0.3 parked its step-up approver binding
for vtc/admin/bootstrap. On a community that already has an administrator —
every invitation — bootstrap answers alreadyBootstrapped, so the binding never
took effect: the invited administrator was left with no step-up factor and
could do nothing that needs a step-up.

trust-tasks-tf #988 adds finish 0.3 item 7: when the community already has an
administrator, the binding takes effect at finish, with the claim, as
vtc/install/claim/passkey/finish/0.1 item 9 writes an invited administrator's
entry at finish. claim_finish_v0_3 now binds the approver under the same
approver lock that checked it bindable, and audits `enrolled`; on a fresh
community it still parks the binding for bootstrap (item 6). The install
binding record and its audit are shared with bind_installed.

Test: claim_finish_v0_3_an_invitation_binds_the_approver_at_finish, which
failed before the fix (no approver bound) and checks the invited administrator
is then asked for, and can answer, an approver step-up.

title: feat(vtc)!: the passkey install, vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1
body:
Implements trust-tasks-tf #976 and #978 (released in trust-tasks-rs 0.36.2; this raises the workspace floor to it): the passkey install moves to `vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1`, and `vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.2` are no longer served.

## On the wire
- **New, served:** `vtc/install/claim/passkey/start/0.1` and `vtc/install/claim/passkey/finish/0.1`. Both are unsigned documents on the spine; the finish response is signed by the community (its proof is REQUIRED).
- **Removed:** `vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.2`. A 0.2 document now gets `unsupportedVersion`, which names 0.3 as the served version.
- **The administrator's DID** is the passkey's own `did:key`: Ed25519 `z6Mk…` or P-256 `zDn…` (compressed point, multicodec 0x1200). It is never taken from the install token. A token that names a DID belongs to the 0.3 wallet ceremony, and the passkey slug refuses it with `invalidToken`.
- **start** offers only COSE -8 and -7, puts no DID in `user`, and returns `assertionOptions`, a second fresh challenge.
- **finish** runs in the spec's order:
  1. Token → `invalidToken`. A consumed token is refused; the old idempotent replay is removed.
  2. registrationId → `registrationMismatch`.
  3. Registration → `bindingInvalid`.
  4. Algorithm → `unsupportedAlgorithm`. This consumes nothing, and the registration stays open.
  5. Derive the DID.
  6. Assertion over the second challenge → `possessionUnproven`.
  7. Only then: consume the token, store the passkey, mint the setup-session token, and write anything.
- **Invitations:** when the community already has an administrator, finish writes the derived DID's ACL entry, with the authority recorded on the invitation (`install::InvitedAuthority`). On a fresh community, `vtc/admin/bootstrap` writes it.

## Invites and recovery
- `vtc admin invite` with no `--did` is a **passkey invitation**. The token names no DID and no ACL entry is written beforehand. Issuing it offline is queued as a break-glass.
- `vtc admin invite --did X` is a **wallet invitation**. It uses the 0.3 ceremony, and X's entry is written now, as before.
- `vtc admin emergency-bootstrap` and `vtc setup` mint passkey invitations.
- The admin console's install page picks the ceremony from the token. For a passkey it runs create → get (assertion) → finish.

## For review
- **`vtc setup` behaviour change.** The first install URL no longer attaches the passkey to the VTA-minted admin DID; 0.2 did that, and it is retired. The founder is the passkey's own DID. The summary and runbook print the offline `vtc acl add` that grants the setup's admin DID as well.
- **Console invites (`vtc/admin/invites/create/0.1`) still require `did`**, so a console invite is a wallet invitation. A passkey invite from the running daemon needs a spec version with an optional `did`. Until then, `vtc admin invite` (offline) issues them.
- **Existing gap, not new:** a 0.3 claim on an invitation parks an approver binding that only bootstrap writes, and bootstrap answers `alreadyBootstrapped` for an invitation. So an invited wallet admin's approver is not bound at claim.

## Checks run locally
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo nextest` for the install, bootstrap, census, conformance and manifest tests
- admin-ui `npm run lint` and the full `vitest` run (1349 tests)

title: feat(vtc)!: the passkey install, vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1 (#2338)
body:
feat(vtc)!: the passkey install, vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1 (#2338)

Implements trust-tasks-tf #976 and #978 (trust-tasks-rs 0.36.2) and stops
serving vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.2, which those retire. A 0.2
document is now `unsupportedVersion`, naming 0.3 as the slug's served
version.

The administrator's DID is the did:key of the passkey credential's own
public key: Ed25519 (multicodec 0xed01, did:key:z6Mk…) or P-256 (the SEC1
compressed point under multicodec 0x1200, did:key:zDn…). It is read from the
attested credential data alone. It is never taken from the install token,
which for this ceremony names no DID (start item 5, finish item 5).

- start offers exactly EdDSA (-8) and ES256 (-7), puts no DID in `user`, and
  returns `assertionOptions`: a second fresh 256-bit challenge, single-use
  and bound to the registration, with no allowCredentials.
- finish verifies the registration (`bindingInvalid`). It refuses any other
  algorithm with `unsupportedAlgorithm`; that refusal consumes nothing, and
  the registration stays open. It then derives the DID and verifies one
  WebAuthn assertion by the new credential over that challenge
  (`possessionUnproven`). Only after that does it consume the token, keep
  the passkey and mint the setup-session token (items 6–8). A refusal lifts
  the ceremony lock, so the installer can start again at once. A consumed
  token is `invalidToken`. The old idempotent replay, which re-minted a
  setup-session token without proof of possession, is gone.
- The finish response carries a bearer token, so its proof is REQUIRED. The
  spine signs every answer, and finish refuses up front on a community with
  no signing key.
- On a community that already has an administrator, finish writes the
  derived DID's ACL entry (item 9), with the authority the invitation was
  issued with. That authority is recorded on the token's row
  (`install::InvitedAuthority`). On a fresh community, vtc/admin/bootstrap
  writes it, as before.

Two kinds of `vtc admin invite`:
- with no `--did`: a passkey invitation. The token names no DID, no ACL
  entry is written now, and the authority is recorded on the invitation.
  The offline issue is queued as a break-glass, named by the invitation.
- with `--did X`: a wallet invitation, claimed with vtc/install/claim/
  {start,finish}/0.3. The token names X, whose admin entry is written now
  if it has none.

`vtc admin emergency-bootstrap` and `vtc setup` now mint passkey
invitations. The setup's VTA admin DID is no longer what the install URL
makes an administrator. The summary prints the offline `vtc acl add` that
grants it.

The admin console's install page reads which kind the token is. For a
passkey invitation it creates the passkey, signs the possession assertion
over `assertionOptions` with allowCredentials naming the new credential,
and explains `possessionUnproven` and `unsupportedAlgorithm`. For a wallet
invitation it offers the wallet claim only.

The census witnesses the passkey install's six codes and 0.3's
invalidToken and registrationMismatch, which 0.2's witnesses used to
cover. The test harness gains P-256 and RS256 credentials and the install
assertion.


The claim finishes answer with their generated #response types (the
generated-wire-types census).

title: feat(vtc-portal): add notes to an open room from the member portal
body:
## Problem

The member portal's **Add to this room** card said that an open room takes nothing from the portal ("Adding from the portal is for attributed rooms"). This was true only because the wallet refused to write open-room notes.

## Change

OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#390 lets the wallet write an open room's note in plain text, as the member, after the usual confirmation. With that in place, the card now:
- offers the note form on every tier, and for an open room adds that a note there is readable by its host as well as its members
- still keeps files to attributed and private rooms, because a file's description is sealed inside its record. For an open room it says this instead of showing the file input

A wallet that predates #390 refuses the note, and the card shows that refusal's text as it does any other wallet error.

## Tests

`tsc -b` passes, and so do all 1346 admin-UI tests. A new test covers an open room: the readable-by-host notice is shown, there is no file input or Add file button, and a note goes to `wallet.putNote`.
author: stormer78

title: fix(vtc-portal): show a shared open room as an open room, not "epoch ?"
body:
## Problem

An open data room has no group, so the member's agent holds no keys and has no epoch for it. The wallet reads it with the room's credentials instead. Since OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#389, the wallet reports a portal share of an open room as `held: true` with no `epoch`. The member portal's **Your rooms here** row then printed `epoch ?`. Once the member left the room it printed "your agent no longer holds this room's keys", which is wrong for a room that never had keys.

## Fix

`RoomRow` now uses a small `holding()` helper:
- a held open room, or any held room with no epoch, shows **open room**
- an open room that is no longer held shows **you are no longer in this room**
- a sealed room is shown as before

The `PageRoom.held` doc comment now covers open rooms.

## Tests

`tsc -b` passes, and so do all 1345 admin-UI tests. A new test covers both open-room states and checks that no epoch or keys wording appears.
author: stormer78

title: feat(rooms): notes in open rooms from the portal, and open rooms in My rooms
body:
## Problem

After #389, a member who joined an open community room could share it with the portal, but:

- **Writing from the portal was refused.** `putNote` threw "this room is open: notes from the portal go in attributed rooms". The page write path only sealed records, and an open room has no group to seal under. The member held `write`, and nothing in the spec (`data-rooms-files.md` §8.5) forbids this.
- **The room wasn't in My rooms.** That tab lists `rooms/keys/list`, which is key custody, so an open room never appeared.

## Changes

- **Portal notes in open rooms:** `putNote` writes `rooms/records/put/0.3` with `cleartext` via `putCleartextAsMember`. Like every host request, it is completed as the member by `rooms/keys/act`; this is the same path `pnm rooms put` uses. It runs after the usual confirmation, which now says that the room is open and the note will be readable by its host. Files stay refused, because a file's manifest belongs inside a sealed body.
- **My rooms:** a new section, *Open rooms you are in*, built by `openRooms` from the communities' offers (joined, open, and not also held). Opening one shows its records only (`rooms-open.tsx`), read and written as the member against the community. `RoomRecords` and its parts now take a `RoomPlace` (room, member, actions), which both a held place and an open room are. The Communities lane's room name opens the room too.
- **Core:** `putCleartextAsMember` takes `description` and `tags`, and always sends a `body`, which put/0.3 requires (empty when the note has none). Added to the core CHANGELOG.
- CLAUDE.md records the rules.

## Tests

`npm run lint` and `npm test` pass in every workspace. New tests cover:
- the portal note for an open room: the prompt says it is open, and the write reaches the offscreen document
- the offscreen write: plain text, sent as the member, with no seal
- `putCleartextAsMember`: description, tags, and the empty body
- `openRooms` filtering
- the open-room card and detail: the detail lists records from the community as the member, without asking for the host

## Follow-up (VTI)

The member portal's *Add to this room* card says open rooms take nothing. It should offer notes for an open room, but not files. (Done in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2341.)
author: stormer78

title: fix(rooms): an open room joined is shareable with its portal and shown joined
body:
## Problem

After accepting an **open** community room, three surfaces disagreed:

- the member portal showed it `open · as you · joined` and offered **Open it here…**
- the share window it opens (`choose`) never listed the room ("Share 0 rooms")
- the console's Communities lane stopped at **Joined: not yet**

The join itself had succeeded. An open room has no group, so the VTA's `rooms/keys/list`, which answers "what can I open with a group key", never names it. The member reads it with the vaulted credentials the offer gave: `browse` / `read` present the authority credential, and no group is needed. `roomStanding` already counts it joined, but `choose`, a page's `list` and the lane's Joined step all read the VTA's listing and nothing else.

## Fix

- New offscreen op `openRooms`: the open rooms the community's record (`vtc/rooms/memberships/list`) says each identity is in (`admittedOpenRooms`: `state: admitted`, `visibility: open`). It is read each time and never kept, so a removal stops counting at once. A member whose record can't be read contributes nothing, and the community's own DID is never asked.
- `choose` offers these rooms beside the listing. A page's `list` reports a share of one as `held` with no `epoch`, and it asks the community only about shares the listing doesn't name.
- The lane's Joined step shows an open room as joined (`joinedOpen`), and a shared one reaches the `shared` stage.
- CLAUDE.md records the rule.

## Tests

`npm run lint` and `npm test` pass in every workspace (1330 extension tests). New tests cover: an open room offered, shared and listed as held, then no longer held once the record drops it; the community not asked when the listing already names every share; `admittedOpenRooms` filtering; the offscreen op reading per member, with one failure costing only its own; and the lane stages.

## Follow-up (VTI)

The portal's `RoomRow` prints `epoch ?` for a held room that has no epoch. It should say "open room" when `visibility === "open"`. (Done in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2339.)

title: Make key roles method-neutral, with a recovery key outside the VTA and method profiles (VTI-KEY-095 to 096, 116 to 119, 126 to 129, 154 to 155, 170 to 173, 180 to 184)
body:
## Summary

Key roles were written around did:webvh. This makes them method-neutral and closes the security gaps the method-neutral design exposed. The Trust Task side — the `vta/dids/*` family, its conventions and the method profiles — is trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf (linked below once open).

### What changes

| Area | Requirements | What |
|---|---|---|
| Method profiles | VTI-KEY-170 – 173 (new) | Six eligibility criteria. `did:key`, `did:jwk`, `did:peer` and `did:web` are refused. `did:webvh` and `did:scid:vh:1` are eligible. `did:webs` is **not eligible as published**: its document is derived from the KEL, every key-state key lands in both `authentication` and `assertionMethod`, and there is nowhere to put `keyRoles` or `revoked`. What the method leaves open is stated by a profile and only there. |
| Recovery key | VTI-KEY-116 (rewritten), 117 (aligned), 118, 119 (new) | Every version commits a **recovery key** held in a protection boundary other than the VTA's, and carries it forward unchanged. *Protection boundary* is defined, and an informative note says what plain, hardened and TEE VTAs are: one boundary each, because a hardened store key and a TEE's keys both sit behind the one seed or enclave. A one-boundary VTA (every VTA) takes the commitment, with a proof of possession, from an external custodian and refuses to create a key-role identity without one. Generated role keys are protected at rest under a key that does not derive from the seed and is in no backup. |
| Revocation encoding | VTI-KEY-126 – 129 (new); the VTI-KEY-120 open issue is closed | A revoked method stays in `verificationMethod`, out of every relationship and `keyRoles`, with the W3C Controlled Identifiers `revoked` property set to the compromise time, for the life of the identity. A planned retirement removes the method and never sets `revoked`. A recovery key is used once. Witnesses SHOULD enforce the continuity of the recovery commitment. |
| `keyRoles` | VTI-KEY-095, 096 (new) | `keyRoles` is a top-level document member, not a method parameter or a linked resource. The JSON-LD term is `https://w3id.org/vti#keyRoles` as an `@index` map. The only open item is the w3id registration. |
| Passkeys | VTI-KEY-154, 155 (new); `authenticator` added to the VTI-KEY-072 table | A passkey is an `authenticator` key. It appears only on its holder's own identity, never on a node's, and is valid only for WebAuthn assertions. |
| Approval | VTI-KEY-180 – 183 (new) | Changes need a step-up bound to a VTA-computed preview. A **quorum** is required to replace the recovery commitment. Revocation never needs more than one approval and is never blocked. Only the approver's own evidence counts: a delegated (console) key never does, consistent with approve-response 0.7. |
| Algorithms | VTI-KEY-184 (new) | No silent substitution, and no X25519 key computed from an Ed25519 key. |

Terms are added (*key-role identity*, *protection boundary*), `authenticator` joins *key role*, and [CID] joins the references.

### Appendix F (nothing is marked implemented)

- The key-role rows are re-filed against VTI-KEY-146 – 148, because the in-place migration of VTI-KEY-140 – 145 they cited is withdrawn. The creation path is now specified, but not implemented.
- The VTI-KEY-120 – 125 row moves from *open* to *observed*. The agent's rotation:
  - replaces every method at once;
  - keeps method ids;
  - re-derives successors from the seed;
  - has no staging or overlap;
  - records nothing that distinguishes rotation from compromise.
- Committed update keys are recorded as established: they are seed-derived and held in the same agent.
- New observed rows:
  - **VTI-KEY-118** — internal keys sit in the store, encrypted under a key derived from the seed, or unencrypted in plain mode. The backup carries the seed. Internal keys cannot be X25519 or ML-DSA.
  - **The recovery key** — none exists.
  - **VTI-KEY-154** — passkey VMs can be enrolled on any agent-managed DID, the agent's own included.
- **VTI-KEY-180 – 183** are recorded as *open*.

### Needs working-group review

1. **did:webs** (VTI-KEY-173 open issue). There are two routes:
   - (A) a did:webs extension that anchors role keys in the KEL and renders the key-state keys into no relationship (preferred);
   - (B) amend VTI-KEY-093 to tolerate key-state keys that the method itself renders.
   Until one lands, the rule refuses did:webs, which is the safest choice.
2. **did:webvh under VTA compromise.** Every entry is authorized by a committed key, and the routine successor sits in the VTA. A compromised VTA can therefore append an entry that drops the recovery commitment. VTI-KEY-129 makes witness enforcement a SHOULD, and the witness's way of telling which hash is the recovery hash is a profile convention. The WG should decide whether to make it a MUST for VTA/VTC/VTN identities.
3. **Refusing creation without a recovery commitment** (VTI-KEY-119) means no VTA can create a key-role identity until its operator supplies an external key. This is deliberate, and it is a deployment burden.
4. **The `revoked` encoding** (VTI-KEY-126) depends on generic Data Integrity verifiers honouring CID `revoked`.
5. **The 24-hour verifier cache cap** (VTI-KEY-134) is still a proposal.
6. **The w3id registration** for `keyRoles`.

Rendered locally with `npm run render`: no missing keys, and every new `[[ref:]]` resolves.

title: Make key roles method-neutral, with a recovery key outside the VTA, a revocation encoding, approval floors and method profiles (VTI-KEY-095, VTI-KEY-096, VTI-KEY-116 to VTI-KEY-119, VTI-KEY-126 to VTI-KEY-129, VTI-KEY-154, VTI-KEY-155, VTI-KEY-170 to VTI-KEY-173, VTI-KEY-180 to VTI-KEY-184) (#79)
body:
Make key roles method-neutral, with a recovery key outside the VTA, a revocation encoding, approval floors and method profiles (VTI-KEY-095, VTI-KEY-096, VTI-KEY-116 to VTI-KEY-119, VTI-KEY-126 to VTI-KEY-129, VTI-KEY-154, VTI-KEY-155, VTI-KEY-170 to VTI-KEY-173, VTI-KEY-180 to VTI-KEY-184) (#79)

Key roles were written around did:webvh. They now apply to every identifier
method that can carry them, with what depends on the method stated by a method
profile published beside the key-role Trust Tasks (vta/dids/*).

- VTI-KEY-170 to 173: eligibility criteria; did:key, did:jwk, did:peer and
  did:web refused; did:webvh and did:scid:vh eligible; did:webs not eligible as
  published (its document places every key-state key in authentication and
  assertionMethod), with the extension needed recorded as an open issue.
- VTI-KEY-116 rewritten, 118 and 119 added: every version commits a recovery key
  held in another protection boundary; a protection boundary is defined, with
  what plain, hardened and TEE VTAs are (one boundary each); generated role keys
  are protected at rest independently of the seed and of backups.
- VTI-KEY-126 to 129: a revocation is recorded with the Controlled Identifiers
  `revoked` property on a method kept in verificationMethod, closing the
  VTI-KEY-120 open issue; a recovery key is used once; witnesses SHOULD enforce
  the recovery commitment's continuity.
- VTI-KEY-095 and 096: keyRoles is a top-level document member with a fixed
  JSON-LD term definition; only the w3id registration stays open.
- VTI-KEY-154 and 155: a passkey is an `authenticator` key, on its holder's own
  identity only, never on a node's.
- VTI-KEY-180 to 184: preview-bound step-up, quorum to replace the recovery
  commitment, revocation never blocked, only the approver's own evidence counts,
  no silent algorithm substitution or curve conversion.

Appendix F: key-role rows re-filed against VTI-KEY-146 to 148 (the in-place
migration of VTI-KEY-140 to 145 is withdrawn), the rotation row turned from open
to observed, and new observed rows for VTI-KEY-118, the recovery key,
VTI-KEY-154 and the approval floors. Nothing is marked implemented.

title: feat(rooms)!: rooms/owner/group/remove 0.4 for attributed and private rooms
body:
This implements `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.4` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#975), one removal for both sealed tiers. The VTA no longer serves 0.1 or 0.3.

## Wire
- **Served:** `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.4` only. 0.1 and 0.3 are removed: trust-tasks-rs 0.36.2 marks both superseded by 0.4. These are 0.x drafts, so SPEC §5.2's keep-accepting rule for M.K doesn't apply. Nothing outside VTI sends either one. The pnm-browser-plugin's `task-surface.json` is only a snapshot of the SDK, so it needs a resync.
- **Attributed room:** works as at 0.3 (withdraw at the host first, then advance), and the response adds `withdrawn: true`. A request with no `signingKeyId` is refused `noSigningKey` (item 2) and nothing changes.

body:
fix(vtc-portal): show a shared open room as an open room, not "epoch ?" (#2339)

An open room has no group, so the member's agent holds no keys and no epoch
for it: the wallet reads it with the room's credentials, and since

never had.
