title: fix(rooms): an open room joined is shareable with its portal and shown joined (#389)
body:
fix(rooms): an open room joined is shareable with its portal and shown joined (#389)

An open room has no group, so the VTA's rooms/keys/list never names it: the
member reads it with the credentials the offer gave, and roomStanding counts
it joined. But the portal share window (choose) and a page's list built their
rooms from that listing alone, and the console's Communities lane drew its
Joined step from it too. So after accepting an open community room the
portal said "joined" and offered "Open it here…", the share window could
never list the room, and the lane stopped at "Joined: not yet".

- New offscreen op openRooms: the open rooms the community's record
  (vtc/rooms/memberships/list) says each identity is in, admitted and open
  (admittedOpenRooms). Read each time, never kept, so a removal stops
  counting at once; a member whose record cannot be read contributes none.
- choose offers them beside the listing; a page's list reports a share of
  one as held with no epoch, asking the community only about shares the
  listing does not name.
- The lane's Joined step shows an open room joined (joinedOpen), and a
  shared one reaches the "shared" stage.

title: trust-tasks-tsp-v0.36.2
body:
### Added

- **rs**: A guarded consumer for Trust Tasks of any type ([#969](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/969)) ([#980](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/980))

A consumer that opens a document of any type, routes on `type` and answers
  an unknown one `unsupportedType` could not be written: the bindings'
  pack/unpack required `P: Payload`, which `serde_json::Value` and
  `ErrorPayload` are not, and `TspConsumer` (like the DIDComm consumers) had
  no path that kept the duplicate-execution record for such a consumer.

  - The bindings' `pack_trust_task` / `unpack_trust_task` (TSP, DIDComm v2.1,
    DIDComm v1 `build_message`) take any `Serialize` / `DeserializeOwned`
    payload. None of them read a `Payload` constant; the bound only refused
    `TrustTask<Value>` and `ErrorResponse`. Loosening a bound is not a break.
  - `ErrorPayload` implements `Payload`. `TYPE_URI` is the version the library
    emits, now the one constant `TRUST_TASK_ERROR_TYPE_URI` (0.6) that
    `trust_task_error_type_uri()` parses; check-bindings reads it there. The
    policy constants are the 0.6 front matter's (recipient REQUIRED, proof
    RECOMMENDED).
  - `consume_dispatched` runs `consume_inbound`'s pipeline for a
    `TrustTask<Value>` routed by an `AsyncDispatcher`. The spec policy and
    payload schema come from the registration the document routes to (now
    recorded by `on_async`). `unsupportedType`, `unsupportedVersion` and a
    payload the handler's `P` cannot hold are refused before the item-11 record
    is written, so they never burn an `id`. The rest is the same code:
    `consume_inbound` and `consume_dispatched` both call one private
    `consume_core`, so freshness, the §4.8.1 cross-check, proof verification
    over the document as received, the per-spec checks and the record cannot
    diverge. Forward routes along a declared extension are pruned exactly as
    `AsyncDispatcher::dispatch` prunes them, which now shares the routing step.
  - `TspConsumer`, `DidcommConsumer` and `DidcommV1Consumer` gain
    `receive_dispatched` / `consume_dispatched` (and `receive_from_dispatched`
    for DIDComm v2.1), keeping each consumer's record and freshness policy.

  The HTTPS server already routes on `type` with its own record, so it needs
  nothing. TypeScript, Go and Dart have no dispatcher: their consume functions
  take the spec as a value and their unpack is untyped, so the caller routes
  then consumes; CLAUDE.md records the difference.

title: trust-tasks-https-v0.36.2
body:
### Fixed

- Stamp issuedAt in whole seconds in every library ([#970](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/970)) ([#979](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/979))

Rust wrote `issuedAt` with `Utc::now()`, which chrono serializes at the
  clock's precision: nine fractional digits on Linux, on every error response
  `dispatch_or_reject` / `reject_with` built and every response `respond_with`
  built. TypeScript wrote milliseconds with `toISOString()`. SPEC §13.1 item 3
  calls a full-precision timestamp a fingerprint and lets a producer round
  `issuedAt` down; readers with a narrower RFC 3339 profile refused these
  documents.

  Every instant the framework stamps is now UTC in whole seconds, rounded
  down, the form Go (`SystemClock`) and Dart (`systemClock`) already wrote:

  - trust-tasks-rs: new `issued_at_now()`, used by `reject_with_recipient`,
    `respond_with` and the dispatchers' error responses.
  - trust-tasks-https: the client's default `issuedAt` and the server's two
    fallback error documents.
  - trust-tasks-capability-client: built documents and `new_attempt`.
  - @openvtc/trust-tasks: new `issuedAtNow()`, the default clock of
    `rejectWithRecipient` / `rejectWith` / `respondWith`.
  - @openvtc/trust-tasks-capability-client: built documents and `newAttempt`.

  A whole second is inside every acceptance window a consumer applies, so no
  specification has to opt in; the minute or hour §13.1 permits is left to a
  specification that states its skew. Rounding down never future-dates a
  document (§7.2 item 13). Readers are unchanged and keep accepting any RFC
  3339 precision and offset; received documents are never re-stamped, so
  proofs and item-11 digests are unaffected.

  The same vectors are pinned in all four libraries (tests/issued_at_precision.rs,
  test/issued-at.test.ts, trusttasks/issued_at_test.go,
  test/issued_at_test.dart): what is written, and that 0, 1, 3, 6 and 9
  fractional digits and an offset are all read.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.36.2
body:
### Added

- **auth/step-up/approve-response**: 0.7 — the approver's own passkey assertion is evidence on its own ([#983](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/983))

0.5 and 0.6 required the approver's framework proof on every answer, and 0.6
  counted a console key's proof as the administrator's it acts for, while
  auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2 item 7 forbids a delegated key's proof on any
  approve-response. A console administrator therefore had no conforming answer:
  the console holds only a delegated key.

  0.7 resolves the contradiction in enroll's favour:
  - a delegated key's proof never counts as the approver's, for any gate
    (subjectMismatch);
  - approval evidence is the approver's own: a proof by its own DID
    (didSigned, approverSigned, every denial), or a user-verified WebAuthn
    assertion by a passkey the relying party registered to the approver, over
    the step-up challenge it bound to this approval — with no proof required;
  - an answer with no proof decides only what the assertion and the relying
    party's own state determine (decision approved, subject, session, bound
    operation, acr from the assertion; grantedAcr and ext ignored), and the
    pending step-up is taken atomically, since an unproved document's id is the
    sender's to choose;
  - proofRequirement is RECOMMENDED, conditional per gate;
  - assertionInvalid reasons are lowerCamelCase, adding userNotVerified and
    credentialNotAccepted.

  auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2's reference design (step 2) now answers with 0.7,
  unsigned, naming identityDid as issuer. Prose references to 0.6 elsewhere move
  to 0.7 (npm run fix-stale-references); approve-request/0.5 no longer says the
  answer is always signed.

- **vtc/members/role/set**: A community role moves with its own task ([#982](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/982))

vtc/members/role/set/0.1 moves a subject's community role — member,
  moderator, issuer, admin, or a custom role — with a compare-and-swap on
  fromRole. Until now the community role moved with acl/change-role/0.1, which
  0.2 superseded with a purely administrative-role move; the community role,
  its role credential and the community's role-change policy are the VTC's
  notions, not the access-control list's, so they get a VTC task and
  acl/change-role stays the generic operation.

  What the move carries:
  - the administrative authority the community role implies, when the entry's
    authority is exactly the one its current role implies; authority stated on
    its own (acl/grant or acl/update 0.2) is kept and only the role moves;
  - a role credential (role VAC) re-issued at the new role for a subject with a
    member record, returned as roleVac and delivered best-effort.

- **rs**: A guarded consumer for Trust Tasks of any type ([#969](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/969)) ([#980](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/980))

  nothing. TypeScript, Go and Dart have no dispatcher: their consume functions
  take the spec as a value and their unpack is untyped, so the caller routes
  then consumes; CLAUDE.md records the difference.

- **vtc/install/claim/passkey**: Passkey install ceremony under its own slug ([#976](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/976))

* feat(vtc/install/claim/passkey): passkey install ceremony under its own slug

  vtc/install/claim/{start,finish} 0.3 is a different ceremony from 0.2: the
  founder claims under a DID they already control, with a step-up approver.
  Because 0.3 is a later version of the same slug, it superseded 0.2, and the
  passkey install was scheduled for withdrawal with it, although 0.3 itself
  says "a passkey install keeps using 0.2".

  The two cannot share a 0.4: finish 0.3 declares `proof` REQUIRED (the
  founder's signature as their DID is the proof of control, enforced from the
  front matter by every consumer), and the passkey ceremony cannot carry one
  (the installer holds no key until the passkey exists). One version serving
  both would leave the wallet ceremony's proof requirement to prose.

  So the passkey ceremony moves, wire-unchanged, to
  vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1, and each ceremony versions on
  its own:

  - Payloads are 0.2's; framework Ext re-pinned to 0.4; Security & Privacy,
    Authorization, Request/Response examples written to current conventions.
  - passkey/finish declares the response `proof` REQUIRED and
    `discloses: secret`: it carries the bearer setup-session token (as
    finish 0.3's does). 0.2 declared neither.
  - vtc/install/claim/{start,finish} 0.2 are retired with `supersededBy`
    naming the passkey slug, so their deprecation note points at the right
    successor rather than at the wallet ceremony.
  - start 0.3's `tokenNamesNoDid` and the 0.3 change notes point at the new
    slug instead of 0.2.

  Also fixes persona/contact/put 1.2's Status paragraph, which still carried
  1.1's "Version 1.0 remains in force; 1.1 is a backwards-compatible MINOR
  increment".

- **rooms/owner/group/remove**: 0.4 — remove a private room's member from the group ([#975](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/975))

0.2 and 0.3 refused a `private` room with `privateRoom` and sent the owner
  to 0.1, which the spec called the way to remove a member of a private room.
  0.1 is superseded all the same, so once it is withdrawn no task could take
  a private-room member out of the MLS group.

  0.4 takes that tier in. On an `attributed` room it is 0.3: withdraw the
  member's credentials at the host first, then advance. On a `private` room
  it removes the leaf and advances the room, builds no revocation list (the
  host cannot be told whom to refuse), and answers `withdrawn: false`.

  - `privateRoom` is no longer declared.
  - `signingKeyId` is optional; still required (as `noSigningKey`) on any
    room that is not private.
  - The response gains a required `withdrawn` boolean; `revocation` is
    present only when it is true.
  - Item 8 (settling a pending removal) is 0.3's, with a pending removal that
    carries no list settled by its step 3 alone.
  - A producer MUST NOT report `withdrawn: false` as a withdrawal.

  Prose links to remove/0.3 in neighbouring rooms specs move to 0.4
  (fix-stale-references). vtc/rooms/community/members/remove 0.2 and
  rooms/owner/revoke 0.1 are clarified in place to allow 0.4 for a private
  room alongside 0.1.

- **build**: An opt-in Type URI index for generated tasks ([#974](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/974))


### Fixed

- Stamp issuedAt in whole seconds in every library ([#970](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/970)) ([#979](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/979))

Rust wrote `issuedAt` with `Utc::now()`, which chrono serializes at the
  clock's precision: nine fractional digits on Linux, on every error response
  `dispatch_or_reject` / `reject_with` built and every response `respond_with`
  built. TypeScript wrote milliseconds with `toISOString()`. SPEC §13.1 item 3
  calls a full-precision timestamp a fingerprint and lets a producer round
  `issuedAt` down; readers with a narrower RFC 3339 profile refused these
  documents.

  Every instant the framework stamps is now UTC in whole seconds, rounded
  down, the form Go (`SystemClock`) and Dart (`systemClock`) already wrote:

  - trust-tasks-rs: new `issued_at_now()`, used by `reject_with_recipient`,
    `respond_with` and the dispatchers' error responses.
  - trust-tasks-https: the client's default `issuedAt` and the server's two
    fallback error documents.
  - trust-tasks-capability-client: built documents and `new_attempt`.
  - @openvtc/trust-tasks: new `issuedAtNow()`, the default clock of
    `rejectWithRecipient` / `rejectWith` / `respondWith`.
  - @openvtc/trust-tasks-capability-client: built documents and `newAttempt`.

  A whole second is inside every acceptance window a consumer applies, so no
  specification has to opt in; the minute or hour §13.1 permits is left to a
  specification that states its skew. Rounding down never future-dates a
  document (§7.2 item 13). Readers are unchanged and keep accepting any RFC
  3339 precision and offset; received documents are never re-stamped, so
  proofs and item-11 digests are unaffected.

  The same vectors are pinned in all four libraries (tests/issued_at_precision.rs,
  test/issued-at.test.ts, trusttasks/issued_at_test.go,
  test/issued_at_test.dart): what is written, and that 0, 1, 3, 6 and 9
  fractional digits and an offset are all read.



### Specifications

- **vtc/install/claim/passkey**: Prove possession of the passkey before any authority ([#978](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/978))

A WebAuthn registration under the `none` attestation format, which most
  platform passkeys use, signs nothing: it names the key the administrator's
  DID is derived from but does not prove the installer holds it. The passkey
  install now proves possession before a setup-session token is minted or any
  administrator entry is written, whatever the attestation format.

  - start's response adds `assertionOptions` (required): request options with
    a second fresh challenge (>=128 bits, distinct from the creation
    challenge, single-use, bound to the registration), no allowCredentials.
  - finish's request adds `webauthnAssertion` (required): one
    navigator.credentials.get() assertion by the just-registered credential
    over that challenge. finish verifies it as WebAuthn §7.2 does, against
    the registered key (EdDSA/Ed25519 or ES256/P-256), before consuming the
    token, minting the setup-session token or writing an entry. Refusal:
    new declared code `possessionUnproven`, nothing consumed.
  - For an invitation of an additional administrator (the community already
    has one, so vtc/admin/bootstrap answers alreadyBootstrapped), finish
    writes the entry for the derived DID, after the assertion. On a fresh
    community bootstrap writes it from the setup-session token, as before.
  - Security & Privacy: possession is proven before any authority is granted.

  Tightened in place: both versions are `draft` and unreleased (merged in
  #976, held in Release PR #977), so SPEC §5.2's draft allowance applies and
  check-published-schemas has no released copy to compare against.
  vtc/admin/bootstrap/0.1 is unchanged and keeps working for its other caller,
  vtc/install/claim/finish 0.3: the assertion rides in finish, not bootstrap,
  because bootstrap never runs for an invited administrator.

  VTI note: `vtc admin invite` will have two kinds — `--did X` uses the 0.3
  wallet ceremony (token names X); no `--did` is a passkey invite, whose ACL
  entry is written from the derived DID at finish (or at bootstrap on a fresh
  community).

title: feat(auth/step-up/approve-response): 0.7 — the approver's own passkey assertion is evidence on its own (#983)
body:
feat(auth/step-up/approve-response): 0.7 — the approver's own passkey assertion is evidence on its own (#983)

0.5 and 0.6 required the approver's framework proof on every answer, and 0.6
counted a console key's proof as the administrator's it acts for, while
auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2 item 7 forbids a delegated key's proof on any
approve-response. A console administrator therefore had no conforming answer:
the console holds only a delegated key.

0.7 resolves the contradiction in enroll's favour:
- a delegated key's proof never counts as the approver's, for any gate
  (subjectMismatch);
- approval evidence is the approver's own: a proof by its own DID
  (didSigned, approverSigned, every denial), or a user-verified WebAuthn
  assertion by a passkey the relying party registered to the approver, over
  the step-up challenge it bound to this approval — with no proof required;
- an answer with no proof decides only what the assertion and the relying
  party's own state determine (decision approved, subject, session, bound
  operation, acr from the assertion; grantedAcr and ext ignored), and the
  pending step-up is taken atomically, since an unproved document's id is the
  sender's to choose;
- proofRequirement is RECOMMENDED, conditional per gate;
- assertionInvalid reasons are lowerCamelCase, adding userNotVerified and
  credentialNotAccepted.

auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2's reference design (step 2) now answers with 0.7,
unsigned, naming identityDid as issuer. Prose references to 0.6 elsewhere move
to 0.7 (npm run fix-stale-references); approve-request/0.5 no longer says the
answer is always signed.

title: feat(vtc/members/role/set): a community role moves with its own task (#982)
body:
feat(vtc/members/role/set): a community role moves with its own task (#982)

vtc/members/role/set/0.1 moves a subject's community role — member,
moderator, issuer, admin, or a custom role — with a compare-and-swap on
fromRole. Until now the community role moved with acl/change-role/0.1, which
0.2 superseded with a purely administrative-role move; the community role,
its role credential and the community's role-change policy are the VTC's
notions, not the access-control list's, so they get a VTC task and
acl/change-role stays the generic operation.

What the move carries:
- the administrative authority the community role implies, when the entry's
  authority is exactly the one its current role implies; authority stated on
  its own (acl/grant or acl/update 0.2) is kept and only the role moves;
- a role credential (role VAC) re-issued at the new role for a subject with a
  member record, returned as roleVac and delivered best-effort.

Checks: vtc.roles.assign covering the subject's entry, no self-move, notFound,
roleNotRecognized / roleNotAssignable (application), stateMismatch, a no-op
answered changed:false, delegationExceedsGranter, lastRoleAssigner, and
deniedByPolicy. Held moves follow the family: a re-authentication bound to the
document (approve-request/0.5 inline delivery) and parked moves answered with
trust-task-next-step to vtc/admin/actions/show/0.3. Execution is serialised,
applied at the next authorization decision, audited, and a demoted
administrator is sent vtc/members/authority-reduced-notice.

vtc/members/admit/0.1 now points its admin promotion at this task (prose, in
place on a draft).

title: spec(vta/contexts/delete): 1.1 bounds its acceptance of 1.0 by 1.0's withdrawal (#981)
body:
spec(vta/contexts/delete): 1.1 bounds its acceptance of 1.0 by 1.0's withdrawal (#981)

"A 1.1 consumer MUST still accept 1.0" read as a perpetual obligation. It
only restated SPEC §5.2, which requires an implementation at M.N to accept
every earlier MINOR, and §5.3.3 ends that obligation when the earlier version
is withdrawn. 1.1 now says so: until 1.0 is withdrawn a 1.1 consumer accepts it
and answers it as 1.0 specifies; afterwards it MAY refuse it with
unsupportedVersion, and a producer MUST NOT send it.

An in-place prose edit: 1.1 is a draft, and the change touches neither its
schema nor its front matter (SPEC §5.2, editorial changes to a draft).

title: feat(rs): a guarded consumer for Trust Tasks of any type (#969) (#980)
body:
feat(rs): a guarded consumer for Trust Tasks of any type (#969) (#980)

A consumer that opens a document of any type, routes on `type` and answers
an unknown one `unsupportedType` could not be written: the bindings'
pack/unpack required `P: Payload`, which `serde_json::Value` and
`ErrorPayload` are not, and `TspConsumer` (like the DIDComm consumers) had
no path that kept the duplicate-execution record for such a consumer.

- The bindings' `pack_trust_task` / `unpack_trust_task` (TSP, DIDComm v2.1,
  DIDComm v1 `build_message`) take any `Serialize` / `DeserializeOwned`
  payload. None of them read a `Payload` constant; the bound only refused
  `TrustTask<Value>` and `ErrorResponse`. Loosening a bound is not a break.
- `ErrorPayload` implements `Payload`. `TYPE_URI` is the version the library
  emits, now the one constant `TRUST_TASK_ERROR_TYPE_URI` (0.6) that
  `trust_task_error_type_uri()` parses; check-bindings reads it there. The
  policy constants are the 0.6 front matter's (recipient REQUIRED, proof
  RECOMMENDED).
- `consume_dispatched` runs `consume_inbound`'s pipeline for a
  `TrustTask<Value>` routed by an `AsyncDispatcher`. The spec policy and
  payload schema come from the registration the document routes to (now
  recorded by `on_async`). `unsupportedType`, `unsupportedVersion` and a
  payload the handler's `P` cannot hold are refused before the item-11 record
  is written, so they never burn an `id`. The rest is the same code:
  `consume_inbound` and `consume_dispatched` both call one private
  `consume_core`, so freshness, the §4.8.1 cross-check, proof verification
  over the document as received, the per-spec checks and the record cannot
  diverge. Forward routes along a declared extension are pruned exactly as
  `AsyncDispatcher::dispatch` prunes them, which now shares the routing step.
- `TspConsumer`, `DidcommConsumer` and `DidcommV1Consumer` gain
  `receive_dispatched` / `consume_dispatched` (and `receive_from_dispatched`
  for DIDComm v2.1), keeping each consumer's record and freshness policy.

The HTTPS server already routes on `type` with its own record, so it needs
nothing. TypeScript, Go and Dart have no dispatcher: their consume functions
take the spec as a value and their unpack is untyped, so the caller routes
then consumes; CLAUDE.md records the difference.

Fixes #969

title: refactor(rooms)!: serve and send only the current rooms/* and vtc/rooms/* versions
body:
Serve and send only the current version of every `rooms/*` and `vtc/rooms/*` task whose earlier versions the registry has superseded, so none of them is used through a deprecated `trust_tasks_rs::specs` module any more. The one exception is `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1` (see below).

`pnm-browser-plugin` has sent only current versions since its cut-over (#384–#387). The other clients outside this repo were checked too: `openvtc` sends `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.4` and `rooms/keys/key-package/0.2`, and `vti-rooms-wasm` and `vta-mobile-core` send no superseded room version. `dataroom-demo` still sends `rooms/{create,records/{get,put,list},epoch/chain}` at 0.1. It pins `vti-rooms` 0.11 and its own sample host, and this repo's hosts already refuse two of those (`create/0.1`, `records/get/0.1`), so it does not block anything here.

## No longer served

**VTA**
- `rooms/keys/act` 0.1 and 0.5: 0.8 only.
- `rooms/keys/browse/0.1`: 0.3 only.
- The SDK's `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_1`, `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_5` and `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_BROWSE_0_1`, with their retry-safety, budget, conformance and error-code-census rows. `operations::room_act::{ACT_TABLE, COMMUNITY_TYPES, actable, is_community_type}`, which were the tables of 0.1 and 0.5.

**Room hosts** (`room-host`, `vtc-service`)
- `rooms/records/put` 0.1 and 0.2: 0.3 only.
- `rooms/records/list/0.1`: 0.5 only.
- `rooms/info/0.1`: 0.3 only.
- `rooms/epoch/chain/0.1`: 0.2 only.
- Removed from `vti_rooms::wire`: `ROOMS_RECORDS_PUT_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_PUT_V2_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_TYPE`, `ROOMS_EPOCH_CHAIN_TYPE` and `ROOMS_INFO_TYPE`, and the `Payload` impls of `PutRecordBody`, `ListRecordsBody` and `ChainBody`. Those three types remain the shape every served version is read as. Also removed: `blob_tasks::{info, put_v2_blobs, INFO_TYPE, PUT_V2_TYPE}`.
- `create/0.1`, `records/get/0.1`, `records/prune/0.1`, `epoch/prune/0.1`, `blobs/get/0.1` and `blobs/upload/*/0.1` were already gone.

**VTC**
- `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2`: 0.4 only. 0.1 and 0.3 were already gone.

## No longer sent

The VTA's own requests to a room's host now use only the current versions, with no fallback for a host that predates them:
- browse: `records/list/0.5`, with no fall-back to 0.1.
- catch-up: `epoch/chain/0.2`, with no fall-back to 0.1.
- anchor: `records/list/0.5` (was 0.1).
- the room's profile: `info/0.3`, `records/list/0.5` and `records/put/0.3` (were 0.1).
- group add/remove: `info/0.3` (was 0.1).

`vtc-client` no longer counts `records/list/0.1` or `info/0.1` as reads, and no longer re-exports `ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_TYPE`.

## What stays, and why

- **`rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1`** (VTA serves it; the VTC and `pnm` send it). This is a gap in the specification: 0.3 refuses a `private` room (`privateRoom`), and its own text says to remove a private room's member with 0.1. Every use carries `#[allow(deprecated)]` with a one-line reason. A spec PR for a successor is in progress.
- **`rooms/keys/act/0.8`'s table** still names superseded versions: `records/put` 0.1/0.2, `records/get/0.1`, `records/list` 0.1–0.4, `records/prune/0.1`, `info` 0.1/0.2, `epoch/chain/0.1`, `blobs/get/0.1` and `vtc/rooms/offers/list` 0.1–0.3. Recipient item 1 makes the table closed, and the table belongs to the specification. Refusing those rows would be a silent divergence, so the VTA still completes them, even though no host in this repo serves them. `ACT_TABLE_0_8`, the offers constants and `vta_sdk::client::rooms::is_offer_type` each carry `#[allow(deprecated)]` with the reason. The fix belongs upstream, in a `rooms/keys/act` 0.9 whose table drops them.

## Spec notes

- `rooms/keys/act/0.8`'s table names superseded versions (above).
- `rooms/records/put/0.3` says a host that implements 0.3 **SHOULD** continue to accept 0.2 and 0.1. This PR stops doing so, a SHOULD-level deviation, because the registry marks both superseded. The two statements should agree.
- `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.3` points private rooms at 0.1, which the registry marks superseded.

Breaking: `vta-sdk`, `vti-rooms` and `vtc-client` lose public constants and functions, and the VTA, VTC and room hosts stop serving the versions above.

title: fix(vti)!: voting/board/read 0.2, witness/session 0.2 only, and the persona timeline at 1.1
body:
Moves four superseded Trust Task versions to their current ones. trust-tasks-rs marks each `superseded by` its successor; every party to each is in this workspace or has already moved.

| Task | Was | Now | Wire change |
|---|---|---|---|
| voting/board/read | 0.1 | 0.2 | a lifecycle entry's instant `at` → `occurredAt` (voting/_shared/0.2) |
| witness/session | 0.1 | 0.2 only | the VTC no longer pairs outcome evidence from a 0.1 session |
| witness/session/submit | 0.1 | 0.2 only | (with the above) |
| persona/profile/timeline | 1.0 | 1.1 | the SDK sent 1.1 but parsed the 1.0 response (`at`), so a 1.1 answer (`occurredAt`) failed to parse — a bug fix |

**voting/board/read 0.2**
- vti-voting: the ballot box writes lifecycle entries (`opened`, `closed`, `closedEarly`, `cancelled`) with `occurredAt`, and replay and both auditors read `occurredAt`.
- vti-voting-service serves board/read at 0.2 only; 0.1 gets `unsupportedVersion` (test extended).
- The VTC sends board/read at 0.2 (`box_version`); every other box task it sends stays at 0.1, which is current.
- A leaf hash covers the entry's member names, so an entry journalled with `at` can't be renamed without changing the board root and every receipt issued against it. As with a 0.1 manifest (#2317), it is **refused by name** (`rules::v0_1_lifecycle_entry`): the box won't restore a journal holding one, and the auditor reports it as unreadable instead of "voting opened before votingOpensAt". **Finish or cancel open elections before upgrading.**

**witness/session 0.2 only.** vti-witness and the VTA have served only 0.2 since #2147. openvtc `main` sends 0.2: its trust-tasks.lock pins `witness/session/0.2` and `submit/0.2`, and its inbound gate accepts only the 0.2 responses. (The local `openvtc-witness` checkout is a stale feature-branch clone of OpenVTC/openvtc at #494, not a separate witness implementation.) pnm-browser-plugin sends persona timeline 1.1 and nothing from the voting or witness families. affinidi-vti-enm uses none of these tasks.

**Breaking:** `VtaClient::persona_profile_timeline` now returns `persona::profile::timeline::v1_1::Response`.

Spec: VTI-VOT (voting/_shared/0.2 CONVENTIONS §1 already names the instant `occurredAt`); witness/session/0.2 *how the versions pair*; persona/profile/timeline/1.1 *Changes from 1.0*.

Local runs:
- Both workspace nextest runs are green. vta-service `audit_coverage` timed out at 300s under machine load in nextest, but passes on its own under `cargo test` (75s).
- Clippy (`-D warnings`), fmt and both doc-test runs are clean.

title: spec(vtc/install/claim/passkey): prove possession of the passkey before any authority (#978)
body:
spec(vtc/install/claim/passkey): prove possession of the passkey before any authority (#978)

A WebAuthn registration under the `none` attestation format, which most
platform passkeys use, signs nothing: it names the key the administrator's
DID is derived from but does not prove the installer holds it. The passkey
install now proves possession before a setup-session token is minted or any
administrator entry is written, whatever the attestation format.

- start's response adds `assertionOptions` (required): request options with
  a second fresh challenge (>=128 bits, distinct from the creation
  challenge, single-use, bound to the registration), no allowCredentials.
- finish's request adds `webauthnAssertion` (required): one
  navigator.credentials.get() assertion by the just-registered credential
  over that challenge. finish verifies it as WebAuthn §7.2 does, against
  the registered key (EdDSA/Ed25519 or ES256/P-256), before consuming the
  token, minting the setup-session token or writing an entry. Refusal:
  new declared code `possessionUnproven`, nothing consumed.
- For an invitation of an additional administrator (the community already
  has one, so vtc/admin/bootstrap answers alreadyBootstrapped), finish
  writes the entry for the derived DID, after the assertion. On a fresh
  community bootstrap writes it from the setup-session token, as before.
- Security & Privacy: possession is proven before any authority is granted.

Tightened in place: both versions are `draft` and unreleased (merged in
#976, held in Release PR #977), so SPEC §5.2's draft allowance applies and
check-published-schemas has no released copy to compare against.
vtc/admin/bootstrap/0.1 is unchanged and keeps working for its other caller,
vtc/install/claim/finish 0.3: the assertion rides in finish, not bootstrap,
because bootstrap never runs for an invited administrator.

VTI note: `vtc admin invite` will have two kinds — `--did X` uses the 0.3
wallet ceremony (token names X); no `--did` is a passkey invite, whose ACL
entry is written from the derived DID at finish (or at bootstrap on a fresh
community).

title: refactor(vta)!: serve and send only vta/contexts/delete/1.1
body:
Retire `vta/contexts/delete/1.0`. The VTA now serves, and the SDK now sends, only `vta/contexts/delete/1.1` (trust-tasks-tf #967). 1.0 is one of the superseded spec versions that the workspace's `deprecated = "allow"` hides.

## What changes

- **VTA.** The dispatch row and handler serve 1.1 only. The 1.0 branch is removed, along with the hand-written `DeleteContextBody` payload. The `ReportAfter` host-copy policy is no longer a wire contract; the offline break-glass `vta contexts delete` still uses it, because it prints every orphan it leaves.
- **SDK (breaking).**
  - `VtaClient::delete_context` now sends 1.1 with `abandonHostCopies: false`. If a host copy cannot be confirmed removed, it gets `vta/contexts/delete:hostCleanupFailed` and nothing is deleted. Under 1.0 the orphan was dropped silently, because this method discards the response.
  - `delete_context_with_outcome` is removed (it returned the 1.0 response). Use `delete_context_settling_hosts`.
  - `TASK_CONTEXTS_DELETE_1_0` and `DeleteContextBody` are removed.
- **CLI.** `pnm`/`cnm contexts delete` no longer falls back to 1.0 against a VTA that predates 1.1.
- **Tables and tests.**
  - `retry_safety`, the conformance sweep, the error-code census baseline and the deprecation-table test fixture are updated. The `vta-mcp` guard test and the docs now name 1.1.
  - A new test witnesses `vta/contexts/delete:notFound` on the 1.1 wire. The census had baselined that code under 1.0.

No outside client sends 1.0:
- `pnm-browser-plugin`'s `task-surface.json` is only a generated snapshot of vta-sdk.
- openvtc calls `delete_context`, which now sends 1.1.

## Not moved, and why

`vta/webvh/dids/update/1.0` → 2.1 and `vta/webvh/dids/rotate-keys/1.0` → 2.0 are left as they are. Their successors are not a new version of the same operation. They are the key-role model (trust-tasks-tf #638):
- per-role rotation with `activatesAt`/`overlapUntil`/`autoRetire`;
- `dryRun`/`previewId` plans;
- `update` refusing any change to key members (`keyMembersManaged`), because keys change only through `vta/webvh/dids/keys/*`. VTI implements none of those tasks.

Serving 2.x means implementing that model (VTI-KEY-120–125, open in Appendix F). Dropping 1.0 first would remove the only way to change a DID's keys.

## Spec note

`vta/contexts/delete/1.1` says: "A 1.1 consumer **MUST** still accept 1.0 and answer it as 1.0 specifies." This PR stops accepting 1.0, against that sentence. The sentence should be relaxed in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, to a SHOULD or a bounded transition. If the MUST is meant to stand, this PR should wait.

title: refactor(vtc)!: approve-response 0.4 only for the console's unsigned answer; drop the unused acl/revoke 0.1 OpenAPI wrapper
body:
The superseded auth/acl Trust Task versions, narrowed to what still needs
them.

auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4 (superseded by 0.6). The VTC now hears 0.4
only as the admin console's unsigned session-passkey answer. Every signed
answer — a member's step-up passkey beside their own proof, a refusal, a
wallet's approver statement — is 0.6, and a signed 0.4 is refused with a
pointer to 0.6. The 0.4 document is checked against 0.4's schema and then
handled as the 0.6 payload it is wire-identical to, so
`bound_step_up::approve` and everything past the door read 0.6 only. The
console's Decline now sends 0.6.

0.4 itself stays: approve-response 0.5 onward require the approver's own
assertionMethod proof, and the console holds only a delegated key, which
auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2 item 7 refuses as an approver's attestation. The
console's unsigned answer has no successor in the specification yet.

acl/change-role/0.1 (superseded by 0.2) stays as the community-role door,
as #2323 kept it: 0.2 moves an AclEntry 0.2's administrative role, and the
community role (member <-> admin, role-VAC re-mint, promotion serialisation)
has no 0.2 task. Its uses now carry a per-item #[allow(deprecated)] naming
that gap.

acl/revoke/0.1: `vta_sdk::openapi::AclRevoke01Response` is removed. It
documented a VTC `DELETE /v1/acl/{did}` route that no longer exists, and
nothing referenced it.

Also drops two stale #[allow(deprecated)] on vta-sdk's REST_ROUTED_URIS,
whose passkey-login 0.1 constants were already gone.

BREAKING: a signed auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4 to a VTC is refused;
send 0.6. `vta_sdk::openapi::AclRevoke01Response` is removed.

### Checked
- No outside client sends approve-response 0.4: vta-mobile-core and the browser plugin send 0.6; openvtc, affinidi-vti-enm, cierge and rp-sdk-js send no approve-response version at all.
- Passkey-login 0.1 URIs: already removed from VTI. This PR drops the two stale `#[allow(deprecated)]` left behind. No outside client (openvtc, cierge, rp-sdk-js, affinidi-vti-enm, vta-mobile-core) sends them.

### Spec problems
- `approve-response/0.5`/`0.6` consumer item 1a says that when a console key signs, the approver is the administrator it acts for. `auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2` item 7 forbids accepting a delegated key's proof on any approve-response. The two contradict each other.
- `auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2`'s reference design (step 2) has the console answer with approve-response 0.6 and webauthn evidence. 0.6 requires a proof the console cannot make, so there is no successor to the 0.4 unsigned answer.
- `acl/change-role/0.2` has no counterpart for a community-role change, so 0.1 is still the only door for that ceremony.

### Local CI
clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean. The workspace nextest run passes apart from two 300 s load timeouts, `audit_coverage` and `vta-backup restore_tests`, in code this PR does not touch; both are being rerun on their own. vtc-service nextest passes after a fix in `signed_step_up`: a console-key-signed 0.6 is refused with `subjectMismatch`. Doctests pass. The admin-ui tsc and vitest runs for StepUp, bound-step-up and theme-preview pass.

title: refactor(git-ns)!: speak only the current git-ns bridge versions (job 0.6, event 0.5, result 0.2)
body:
The VTC sent `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4 and 0.5 beside 0.6, and served
`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.1 to 0.4 and `git-ns/bridge/result` 0.1 beside the
current versions, for the released bridge. `vgi-bridge` has sent only job
0.6, event 0.5 and result 0.2 since v0.26.0, and nothing outside VTI speaks
the older versions, so they go:

- Jobs go out as `git-ns/bridge/job/0.6` only, and only to a bridge that
  lists 0.6 in its `trust-task-discovery` answer. `bridge_job_support` no
  longer records or picks 0.4 / 0.5 (`BridgeJobSupport::job_type`), and the
  downgrade to an older job version is gone. A bridge that lists only 0.4
  and 0.5 is sent nothing: in-line jobs are refused with "upgrade the
  bridge", queued jobs wait, and a queued `closePullRequest` is dropped and
  the namespace's administrators told the gate is not enforced. A discovery
  record stored by an earlier VTC still reads.
- `git-ns/bridge/event` 0.1-0.4 and `git-ns/bridge/result` 0.1 are no
  longer served (refused `unsupportedVersion`); the read-as-0.5 and
  read-as-0.2 conversion shims are removed.
- The VTC asks bridges with `trust-task-discovery/0.3` instead of 0.2. 0.3
  only adds the optional `acceptanceWindow` to the response; the request is
  unchanged, and `vgi-bridge` answers 0.3 since v0.26.0.

Docs, vtc-service/CLAUDE.md, the cnm `notRevertible` guidance, the admin
console's gate-unenforced label and the default git_ns.rego comments now
name job 0.6.

BREAKING CHANGE: a git-ns bridge older than vgi-bridge v0.26.0 is sent no
jobs, and its events and results are refused, until it is upgraded.

Part of the zero-deprecation-warnings work: removes 7 of the 44 superseded
spec versions the workspace still used (`git_ns::bridge::job::v0_4/v0_5`,
`event::v0_1..v0_4`, `result::v0_1`). Specs: `git-ns/bridge/job/0.6`,
`git-ns/bridge/event/0.5`, `git-ns/bridge/result/0.2`,
`trust-task-discovery/0.3` (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf).

Tested locally: `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli`
(git-ns tests 320/320 after the fix-up; the rest of the suite passed on the
first run), `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p cnm-cli --all-targets -D warnings`,
`cargo fmt --check`.

title: feat(vtc/install/claim/passkey): passkey install ceremony under its own slug
body:
vtc/install/claim/{start,finish} 0.3 is a different ceremony from 0.2: the
founder claims under a DID they already control, with a step-up approver.
Because 0.3 is a later version of the same slug, it superseded 0.2, and the
passkey install was scheduled for withdrawal with it, although 0.3 itself
says "a passkey install keeps using 0.2".

The two cannot share a 0.4: finish 0.3 declares `proof` REQUIRED (the
founder's signature as their DID is the proof of control, enforced from the
front matter by every consumer), and the passkey ceremony cannot carry one
(the installer holds no key until the passkey exists). One version serving
both would leave the wallet ceremony's proof requirement to prose.

So the passkey ceremony moves, wire-unchanged, to
vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1, and each ceremony versions on
its own:

- Payloads are 0.2's; framework Ext re-pinned to 0.4; Security & Privacy,
  Authorization, Request/Response examples written to current conventions.
- passkey/finish declares the response `proof` REQUIRED and
  `discloses: secret`: it carries the bearer setup-session token (as
  finish 0.3's does). 0.2 declared neither.
- vtc/install/claim/{start,finish} 0.2 are retired with `supersededBy`
  naming the passkey slug, so their deprecation note points at the right
  successor rather than at the wallet ceremony.
- start 0.3's `tokenNamesNoDid` and the 0.3 change notes point at the new
  slug instead of 0.2.

Also fixes persona/contact/put 1.2's Status paragraph, which still carried
1.1's "Version 1.0 remains in force; 1.1 is a backwards-compatible MINOR
increment".

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>


The administrator's DID is the did:key of the passkey credential's own
public key as registered: Ed25519 (multicodec 0xed01, did:key:z6Mk…) or
P-256, SEC1-compressed (multicodec 0x1200, did:key:zDn…). The install token
never names it; the community derives it from the attested credential data
alone.

- start offers exactly EdDSA (-8) and ES256 (-7) in pubKeyCredParams and
  puts no DID in the options' user members.
- finish verifies the registration as WebAuthn §7.1 does, and states that
  this registration is the proof of control; refuses any other COSE key with
  the new declared code `unsupportedAlgorithm`, consuming nothing.
- The response `adminDid` pattern admits both prefixes; a P-256 example is
  added, and the responses carry the REQUIRED proof.
- Security & Privacy says what a `none`-format attestation does and does not
  sign.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Do not merge without the maintainer: spec PR.

feat(vtc/install/claim/passkey): passkey install ceremony under its own slug (#976)

* feat(vtc/install/claim/passkey): passkey install ceremony under its own slug

vtc/install/claim/{start,finish} 0.3 is a different ceremony from 0.2: the
founder claims under a DID they already control, with a step-up approver.
Because 0.3 is a later version of the same slug, it superseded 0.2, and the
passkey install was scheduled for withdrawal with it, although 0.3 itself
says "a passkey install keeps using 0.2".

The two cannot share a 0.4: finish 0.3 declares `proof` REQUIRED (the
founder's signature as their DID is the proof of control, enforced from the
front matter by every consumer), and the passkey ceremony cannot carry one
(the installer holds no key until the passkey exists). One version serving
both would leave the wallet ceremony's proof requirement to prose.

So the passkey ceremony moves, wire-unchanged, to
vtc/install/claim/passkey/{start,finish}/0.1, and each ceremony versions on
its own:

- Payloads are 0.2's; framework Ext re-pinned to 0.4; Security & Privacy,
  Authorization, Request/Response examples written to current conventions.
- passkey/finish declares the response `proof` REQUIRED and
  `discloses: secret`: it carries the bearer setup-session token (as
  finish 0.3's does). 0.2 declared neither.
- vtc/install/claim/{start,finish} 0.2 are retired with `supersededBy`
  naming the passkey slug, so their deprecation note points at the right
  successor rather than at the wallet ceremony.
- start 0.3's `tokenNamesNoDid` and the 0.3 change notes point at the new
  slug instead of 0.2.

Also fixes persona/contact/put 1.2's Status paragraph, which still carried
1.1's "Version 1.0 remains in force; 1.1 is a backwards-compatible MINOR
increment".

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(vtc/install/claim/passkey): admin DID is the passkey's own Ed25519 or P-256 did:key

The administrator's DID is the did:key of the passkey credential's own
public key as registered: Ed25519 (multicodec 0xed01, did:key:z6Mk…) or
P-256, SEC1-compressed (multicodec 0x1200, did:key:zDn…). The install token
never names it; the community derives it from the attested credential data
alone.

- start offers exactly EdDSA (-8) and ES256 (-7) in pubKeyCredParams and
  puts no DID in the options' user members.
- finish verifies the registration as WebAuthn §7.1 does, and states that
  this registration is the proof of control; refuses any other COSE key with
  the new declared code `unsupportedAlgorithm`, consuming nothing.
- The response `adminDid` pattern admits both prefixes; a P-256 example is
  added, and the responses carry the REQUIRED proof.
- Security & Privacy says what a `none`-format attestation does and does not
  sign.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: feat(rooms/owner/group/remove): 0.4 — remove a private room's member from the group (#975)
body:
feat(rooms/owner/group/remove): 0.4 — remove a private room's member from the group (#975)

0.2 and 0.3 refused a `private` room with `privateRoom` and sent the owner
to 0.1, which the spec called the way to remove a member of a private room.
0.1 is superseded all the same, so once it is withdrawn no task could take
a private-room member out of the MLS group.

0.4 takes that tier in. On an `attributed` room it is 0.3: withdraw the
member's credentials at the host first, then advance. On a `private` room
it removes the leaf and advances the room, builds no revocation list (the
host cannot be told whom to refuse), and answers `withdrawn: false`.

- `privateRoom` is no longer declared.
- `signingKeyId` is optional; still required (as `noSigningKey`) on any
  room that is not private.
- The response gains a required `withdrawn` boolean; `revocation` is
  present only when it is true.
- Item 8 (settling a pending removal) is 0.3's, with a pending removal that
  carries no list settled by its step 3 alone.
- A producer MUST NOT report `withdrawn: false` as a withdrawal.

Prose links to remove/0.3 in neighbouring rooms specs move to 0.4
(fix-stale-references). vtc/rooms/community/members/remove 0.2 and
rooms/owner/revoke 0.1 are clarified in place to allow 0.4 for a private
room alongside 0.1.

title: feat(build): an opt-in Type URI index for generated tasks
body:
## Why

`trust_tasks_rs::schema_index` is a match over the prebuilt modules, gated per family. Since milestone 5 an application generates the tasks it pins with `trust-tasks-build`, which emitted no index. So an application that validates by Type URI loses its index when it drops a family feature, and a consumer reading `None` as "unknown, skip validation" fails open.

## What

- **`Config::index(true)`** (and `Target::index(bool)` for `generate_locked` callers) adds a `schema_index` module to the generated file. It is off by default, so the output is byte-for-byte unchanged without it, and `runtime_path` keeps the setting.
  - `schema_for`, `spec_policy_for`, `error_codes_for` and `max_document_bytes_for` have the signatures and semantics of `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index` (bare URI for the request, `#response` for the response; policy and error codes for the request only), over exactly the locked versions.
  - `TYPE_URIS: &[&str]` lists every request and `#response` URI, in lock order.
  - `INDEX: &[trust_tasks_rs::type_index::IndexEntry]` holds the same answers as data. The four functions are thin wrappers over it.
- **`trust_tasks_rs::type_index`** (new, additive, not feature-gated): `IndexEntry` (`#[non_exhaustive]`, with `const fn request(…)` and `response(…)`) and `lookup(&[&[IndexEntry]], uri)`. A facade over several generated crates combines their tables with `lookup(&[a::schema_index::INDEX, b::schema_index::INDEX], uri)` and needs no hand-written merge.
- The generated code names only public runtime items (`Payload`, `SpecPolicy::of`, `DeclaredErrorCode`, `type_index`), so no new `#[doc(hidden)]` door was needed.
- Framework specs cannot be locked and are not in the index; `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index` answers for them.

## Tests

- `trust-tasks-build` unit test: the index is opt-in and only appends to the file, covers both authorities, follows `runtime_path`, and refuses a family or source that collides with `schema_index`.
- `examples/consumer-app` turns the index on and uses it (step 7). `tests/index_equivalence.rs` compares every function, and `INDEX` through `lookup`, with `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index` for each locked URI in its bare, `#response` and `#request` forms, and for URIs neither index knows. It also checks that `TYPE_URIS` is exactly the URIs the prebuilt index has schemas for. It runs over the example's lock and over a second lock in `index-equivalence/` (acl/list 0.1, keys/sign-document 0.1, rooms/blobs/chunk 0.1, sync/event 0.1, vault/get 0.3), which covers request and response size bounds, a response-only bound, a task with no response, and superseded versions. The test enables those families as dev-dependency features; under resolver 2 the example binary still compiles no prebuilt module. A deliberately broken generator fails the test.
- The `consumer-app` CI job now runs `cargo test -p trust-tasks-example-consumer-app` and `trust-tasks check` on the second lock.
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen` produces no drift.
author: stormer78
significance_reasons: Interoperability, canonicalisation, conformance, or protocol behaviour

title: refactor(bridge): generate the git-ns/bridge types with trust-tasks-build instead of the deprecated prebuilt modules; release 0.27.2
body:
trust-tasks-rs 0.36 deprecates its prebuilt specification modules. The
bridge took git-ns/bridge/job 0.6, result 0.2 and event 0.5 from them and
allowed the deprecation crate-wide (and in three test files) to do so.

- vgi-bridge pins exactly those three versions in trust-tasks.toml /
  trust-tasks.lock (bundle digests, vendored under trust-tasks/), and its
  build.rs generates them with trust-tasks-build 0.1.2 as
  `vgi_bridge::specs`, at the module paths the prebuilt modules used.
  `wire::{job, result, event}` re-export them, so the bridge's API is
  unchanged. The generated modules are the prebuilt 0.36.1 ones up to the
  path they reach serde/chrono/regress by, so the wire is unchanged.
- The crate-level `#![allow(deprecated)]` in vgi-bridge and the ones in
  tests/{events,pr_gate,role_map}.rs are gone.
- `check_kind_members` drops its wildcard arm: `PayloadKind` is now this
  crate's own type, so `#[non_exhaustive]` no longer applies and a pinned
  job version that adds a kind fails to compile until it has a row.
- The workspace's trust-tasks-rs names no family (was `git-ns`). This does
  not shrink the build: trql-client takes trust-tasks-rs's defaults
  (`all-specs`) and vta-sdk enables its own families, so the release
  profile's opt-level 1 for trust-tasks-rs and the Linux swap stay.
- did-git-sign keeps one narrowly scoped `#[allow(deprecated)]` on
  `print_session_health`: `health_details()` returns vta-sdk's type, the
  prebuilt `vta/health/details/0.1`, whose fields trip the lint. It goes
  when vta-sdk moves off the prebuilt modules.

Still one trust-tasks-rs, one vta-sdk in Cargo.lock. Workspace and
internal crate versions 0.27.1 -> 0.27.2; bridge.example.toml pins v0.27.2.

Local: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` (default and `--all-features`), `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo audit` all clean.

title: feat(social-recovery): add the social-recovery task family (4 specs)
body:
This is the `social-recovery` family, split out per your review of #672 — one PR for the
categories, then one PR per family with its schemas. **CODEOWNERS routes this to the
`social-recovery` reviewers only.**

## What is here

- **4 specs**, each with a `payload.schema.json`.
- Categories used: **`key-management`** — all of them already in your enum. **This family
  does not depend on #672**, so it can be reviewed and merged independently of the
  category discussion.
- Additions only. The assembler stages the diff and **refuses to run if anything
  outside `specs/social-recovery/` changed, or if any path already exists upstream** — the
  clash check is exercised against a planted file each run, so a silent pass cannot
  be mistaken for a clean one.

## Validation

**596 specs validate against your own `spec.meta.schema.json`** — your
existing corpus plus these 4 — using **your unpatched 17-category schema**,
not a version of it we edited. 0 failures. Every spec declares `errorCodes`.

Payload schemas are draft 2020-12, `$id` on `https://trusttasks.org/spec/<slug>/<version>`,
`additionalProperties: false`, and reference `$defs/Ext` from
`_framework/0.2/framework.schema.json` — your convention, not one we invented.

## Why this family first

It is small, and it is one of only three of our families that is already
**lowerCamelCase-clean**, so it does not carry the §4.10 casing work we owe you on
the rest. **Please treat it as a shape template**: if the file layout, the spec
structure, the schema conventions or the commit/PR format are wrong, correcting them
here costs you one review instead of twenty-eight. We will not open the remaining
families until you have had a chance to say.

## Known-open, stated rather than hidden

- 🟡 **Worked examples are not yet round-trip verified against our implementation.**
  We tested this and the honest result is that some examples describe an intended
  API rather than the one our code accepts today. Where that is true of a spec in
  this family we would rather fix the example than quietly ship it — tell us if you
  want those corrected before merge or tracked separately.
- 🟡 **`ext` passthrough is declared but not universally implemented** on our side.
  The schemas model it per your `$defs/Ext`; our runtime honours it for some
  operations and not yet all.
- The `Security & Privacy` sections follow your house structure. Our earlier
  submission cited internal `src/...` paths in some spec bodies; **0 of your 592 do
  that**, so they are removed here.

## Casing

On your `sourceClass` point: **your conclusion was right and we are conforming.**
§4.10 items 3 and 4 govern it (your citation of §8.3 was the error-code table), and
we confirmed you hold your own corpus to it — zero unexplained snake_case enum values
across your 592 payload schemas. This family needed no changes. The rest is measured
and in flight; see the discussion on #672.

## Open questions for maintainer review

The `🟡 NEEDS-REVIEW:` convention this description promised is now actually in the
specs, under an **Open Questions for Registry Review** heading in each. Thank you for
catching that it was missing — it should have been there from the start.

It was missing for a reason on our side, now fixed: our own validator treated any spec
containing the marker as a failure, so the convention could not be used without turning
our own gate red. That encoded the wrong reading of our rule. A `NEEDS-REVIEW` marker
does not mean "we did not finish it" — it means "complete as far as we can take it, and
flagged for the reviewer who has to decide."

- **`social-recovery/buddies/list`** — in our reference implementation this is a
  same-device, owner-local read: a Settings-screen listing of the operator's own recovery
  buddies, not a request one party sends about another party's data. We documented it as
  the code behaves, but whether it belongs in a peer-facing registry at all is a call we'd
  like your judgment on.
- **`social-recovery/status/get`** — declares a `deviceNotFound` error code our
  implementation never emits (`localDeviceDid` is only checked for list membership, never
  looked up against an owner record). Flagged rather than silently resolved either way.
- **`social-recovery/buddies/add`** — same pattern: declares a `selfEnrollment` code our
  implementation never emits; nothing compares the buddy DID to the requester's own.

A fourth candidate was deliberately **not** marked: `buddies/list` publishing each buddy's
`publicKeyHex` is an intentional disclosure whose rationale is already in the spec text.
It is a decision, not an open question, and padding this list would cost you attention
rather than save it.

## Still red, and named rather than left to look handled

`bindings match specs`, both drift checks and `cargo test` are failing because no
generated client binding (Rust/TypeScript/Go/Dart) declares these four operations'
TYPE_URIs — codegen has not been run for this family. That is a generator run, not a
spec change. We are running it; this note is here so the red is not mistaken for a
spec defect.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(spec-meta): add 10 category values for domains the taxonomy has no home for
body:
## What this changes

Two files, and they have to move together:

1. `specs/spec.meta.schema.json` — ten values added to `#/properties/category/enum` (17 → 27).
2. `website/assets/data.js` — the matching ten `window.TT_CATEGORIES` entries.

Nothing else. No specs, no bindings, no version bumps, no CHANGELOG entry.

This is the first of the split series you asked for. The families and their specs
follow as one PR per family, so `CODEOWNERS` can route each one by slug.

## Why both files

`scripts/build-registry.mjs::checkCategoryTaxonomy()` fails the build on any enum
value with no `TT_CATEGORIES` entry — *"its specs would render without a
name/color and crash the spec page"* — and warns on the reverse. So the enum
patch alone would break `main`, and the `data.js` entries alone would be dead
weight. `CLAUDE.md` in this repo records this shipping for real once, when
`chat/message/1.0` went out broken on the live site.

We reproduced that check locally against a clean clone before opening this, in
four arms: pristine/pristine silent, patched-enum + unpatched-`data.js` failing on
exactly these ten, patched/patched clean, and unpatched-enum + patched-`data.js`
warning rather than failing. The third arm alone would not have told us whether
the check discriminates.

We also assert something the build does not: every `color` we set resolves to a
`--tt-<color>` token `tokens.css` actually defines, because `catColor()` emits
`var(--tt-${cat.color})` and an undefined token renders nothing rather than
failing. All ten use the existing six-token palette.

## The ten values

| Value | Family it serves | Why no existing value fits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `temporal-coordination` | `calendar` | Negotiating *when*, between parties |
| `automation` | `scheduler` | Scheduled or triggered execution with no human in the loop |
| `media` | `media` | Custody and delivery of recorded audio/video/image/book assets |
| `communications` | `call` | Real-time synchronous session setup — offer/answer, participants |
| `collaboration` | `canvas` | Concurrent multi-party editing of shared state |
| `matchmaking` | `matchmaking` | Mutual-interest discovery and introduction |
| `privacy` | `data-subject` | Data-subject rights against a controller |
| `storage` | `files` | Document custody on behalf of another party |
| `task-management` | `todo` | Human work tracking and assignment |
| `prediction` | `forecast` | A claim about the future plus the record that settles it |

**`privacy`** has a regulatory anchor (GDPR data-subject rights) the registry has
no home for today. `consent` covers a subject *granting* permission; it cannot
express a subject compelling a controller who would rather not comply.

**`prediction`** is the only temporally-directional value here. `reputation`
scores the past and `provenance` records it; neither can hold the claim half.

## Where we think you are right

You flagged `communications`, `matchmaking` and `media` as overlapping the
existing `chat`, `messaging` and `data-exchange`. We would rather discuss those
three than defend them, and we are happy to drop or merge any of them. If you
want the smallest possible first step, `privacy` and `prediction` are the two you
said make a good case, and this PR is easy to reduce to just those.

Separately, and this one is ours to fix rather than yours: all 36 `bridge/*`
specs we proposed declare `category: messaging`, and you are right that this
repo's `messaging` means operator-facing control of a mediator or relay, not an
application-level protocol bridge. That is a genuine misclassification on our
side. We will pick a better category for `bridge` in its own PR rather than
smuggle it through this one.

## Provenance

These ten values are not a taxonomy proposal in the abstract. Each one is the
category a family needed while implementing the Trust Task framework against this
registry, and every one of them is declared by specs we are submitting in the
follow-up PRs. If a value ends up with no family behind it, it should not land —
`checkCategoryTaxonomy()` would warn about it as dead weight, correctly.

title: fix(vtc-admin-ui): fall back to the gradient mark for a logo the sign-in pages cannot show
body:
The member portal and the console's login page rendered the community's
logoUrl as-is in their shared top bar (CommunityTopbar). The VTC serves
both with `img-src 'self' data:`, so a logo on another origin was blocked
(a broken image plus a CSP violation in the console), and a URL that is
not an image (a home page) showed broken too.

The console's own top bar already filtered through displayableLogo and
fell back on load error. The sign-in top bar now does the same.
displayableLogo moves to a dependency-free lib/display-logo.ts so the
member bundle can use it without importing the console's plugins;
community-identity re-exports it.
author: stormer78

title: fix(release): build the Linux binaries inside the runner's memory again; release 0.27.1
body:
Fixes the v0.27.0 Linux release binaries and releases **0.27.1**.

## What failed

v0.27.0's Release run (40832399878) lost both `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` legs, verify-trust and vgi-bridge, to the OOM killer (exit 143). The crates and the macOS and Windows binaries are unaffected.

This failure is older than #182. v0.25.0 (40314972216) had a single trust-tasks-rs and no workarounds, and it lost both Linux legs the same way. One trust-tasks-rs rustc at the release default (opt-level 3) peaks at 7-9 GB, which is the whole of an ubuntu runner, and `release.yml` adds no swap. v0.26.0's Linux legs survived only because #182 set `opt-level = 1`, and #183 reverted that.

## Fix

- The release profile builds `trust-tasks-rs` at **opt-level 1** again, which keeps it near 3 GB. It is serde code over small documents.
- `release.yml`'s Linux legs add the **16 GB swap file** that `ci.yml` and `bridge-image.yml` already use.
- **No `-j 1`.** CI, `publish.yml` and the Dockerfile keep normal parallelism.

Workspace and internal crate versions go from 0.27.0 to 0.27.1, and `bridge.example.toml` pins v0.27.1.

## Verification

PR CI does not run `release.yml`, so the Release workflow was also dispatched on this branch. On a branch it is a build-only dry run: the attest step and the Publish Release job only run for a `v*` tag. The run is linked in a comment below.

title: chore(deps)!: take trql-client 0.29 (registry/authorization 0.2); one trust-tasks-rs again, drop the serial-build workarounds; release 0.27.0
body:
Moves VGI onto **trql-client 0.29**, which is on trust-tasks 0.36, so the graph holds one trust-tasks-rs again. Reverts the serial-build workarounds #182 added for the second copy, and releases **0.27.0**.

## Dependencies

| Crate | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| trql-client | 0.28 | **0.29** (affinidi-trust-registry-rs#169) |
| trust-tasks-rs | 0.36.1 + 0.34.2 (alias) | **0.36.1 only** |

`Cargo.lock` has one `trust-tasks-rs` (0.36.1), and `cargo tree -d -e normal` lists no trust-tasks crate as a duplicate. The `trust-tasks-trql` alias is gone, and verify-trust names the workspace's `trust-tasks-rs` directly.

## ⚠️ trql-client 0.29 is a breaking release

- **Trust registry:** it asks `registry/authorization` **0.2**. If a registry refuses that with `unsupportedVersion`, it asks again at **0.1** and remembers that registry's answer. Registry releases up to 0.28 serve only 0.1, and the fallback covers them, so **an older registry needs no upgrade first**.
- **API:** `TrqlClient::authorization` returns trql-client's own `AuthorizationAnswer` instead of the trust-tasks payload type. `verify_trust::Registry::client()` exposes the client, so the change reaches VGI's public API, hence the `!`. VGI reads only `authorized`, so no call site changed.

The registry test fakes now answer 0.2 (`entityId`, `authorityId`, `evaluatedAt`), as in #181. A new test, `a_registry_on_authorization_0_1_still_authorizes`, covers a registry that refuses 0.2 and answers 0.1. RUNBOOK and the verify-trust README now say which version VGI asks and describe the fallback.

## Build memory: #182's workarounds reverted

With one trust-tasks-rs compile, these files are back to their state before #182 (each diffed against `4d1bb16`):

- `-j 1` is dropped from the CI Test job, the bridge Dockerfile, `release.yml` and `publish.yml`.
- The bridge-image job timeout is back to 45 minutes, from 90.
- `[profile.release.package.trust-tasks-rs] opt-level = 1` is removed.

## Version

Workspace and internal crate versions go from 0.26.0 to 0.27.0, and `bridge.example.toml` pins v0.27.0.

## Checks (local, default parallelism)

- `cargo fmt --all --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and so is the same run with `--all-features`.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 839 pass, 0 fail.
- `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` passes.
- `cargo audit --deny warnings` is clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no client change
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): no change
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): the 0.1 fallback is a single re-ask, inside trql-client
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): registry/authorization 0.2 is camelCase, with 0.1 kept as the fallback

title: fix: approve-only grants, webvh room DIDs, complete vault lookups, no snake_case preview fold
body:
Follow-ups from the trust-task cutover (#384–#386).

## Changes
- **Access pane: an "Approve only" grant.** With no context selected, Grant sends `act: {scope: "all"}`, and the VTA refuses that for any role except `admin` (`invalidActScope`). The form does not derive `none` from the role, because 0.2 forbids it. It now offers an explicit choice instead. "Approve only" sends the least-privilege approver from AclEntry 0.2:
  - `act: none`
  - `approve` set to where `act` would have reached
  - `approveCapabilities: ceiling`, stated because absent means none
  - `keys: none` and `capabilities: none`

  The entry is built by `grantEntry`, which has tests.
- **Rooms: room and host DIDs are `did:webvh`.** At `dids/create` 1.2, an agent configured for scid returns `did:scid:vh:…` when no method is named. Both mints in `rooms-create.tsx` now send `didMethod: "webvh"`, per VTI `data-rooms.md` §3.2. `did-create` and the persona editors still let the agent choose.
- **offscreen: vault lookups read past the first page.**
  - `doSignTrustTask` follows `nextCursor` (`collectPages`) before choosing the signer. Before, an identity on page two or later was refused as "not held".
  - `personaTaskSigner` fetches its entry by id with `vault/get` instead of searching one `vault/list` page.
- **`contextPreviewDelete`** now types the reply with the generated 1.0 response type and reads only its camelCase members. The snake_case compatibility fold is removed.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide)
- [x] No compatibility folds (one removed)
- [x] Wire types from generated specs
- [x] Listings read to the end (`collectPages`)
- [x] `npm run lint`, `npm test` (core 1098, extension 1325, all packages pass), `npm run build`

title: fix(step-up): one approve-request version, 0.5, for every party the wallet answers
body:
## Why
`auth/step-up/approve-request` was minted at three versions: the VTA at 0.2, a VTC's inline refusal at 0.4, and the did-hosting RP at 0.5. The wallet therefore kept a hand-written 0.2 literal for the agent, a 0.4 pin for the VTC, and read the RP's version out of `start/0.2`'s schema. That's one version per party, which is still a fold.

OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2327 moves the VTA and vtc-service to 0.5. This PR is the wallet's half of that cutover.

## What
- **One pin, one constant.** `approve-request` is pinned at 0.5. `STEP_UP_APPROVE_REQUEST_TYPE` replaces `AGENT_APPROVE_REQUEST_TYPES`, `RP_APPROVE_REQUEST_TYPES` and the `acceptTypes` option, and is matched with `===` whoever signed. A test holds the pin equal to the type `start/0.2` embeds, so the two cannot drift.
- **`accepts` is checked.** `verifyStepUpApproveRequest` refuses a request whose `accepts` (required in 0.5) does not list `didSigned`, the only evidence this wallet gives. The refusal happens before anyone is asked, instead of after the human approved and the agent answered `noGate`. The VTA drops `didSigned` once the subject holds a passkey.
- The VTC approver path (`approver-attest.ts`) reads the 0.5 payload type. The only wire change from 0.4 is `ttl` → `ttlSeconds`, which nothing in the wallet reads.

## Merge order
This must go in **with** VTI #2327. Until the VTA mints 0.5, an agent step-up (persona disclosure, a pushed step-up) is refused here as the wrong version. Nothing is deployed, so the two cut over together (CLAUDE.md: no compatibility folds).

## Verification
- From a clean worktree: `npm run lint` clean; tsp-js 123/123, core 1098/1098, extension 1322/1322, demo-rp 6/6, reviewer-demo 9/9; `npm run build` clean.
- New tests: a request without `didSigned` in `accepts` is refused; the pin equals `start/0.2`'s embedded type; 0.2 is refused.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new network paths
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): untouched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): untouched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): generated from the registry bundle; the Rust consumers are updated in VTI #2327
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(step-up)!: one approve-request version, 0.5, across the VTA, the VTC and the mobile approver
body:
## Why
`auth/step-up/approve-request` is minted at three different versions today:

| Producer | Version | Where |
|---|---|---|
| VTA | 0.2 | `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/step_up.rs` (hand-built `json!`) |
| VTC (inline in a refusal) | 0.4 | `vtc-service/src/acl/bound_step_up.rs` |
| did-hosting RP | 0.5 | affinidi-webvh-service `control_tasks/auth.rs` |

An approver has to read all three. `vta-mobile-core` reads only 0.1/0.2, so the phone can answer the VTA but not the RP or the VTC. The browser wallet has to keep one version per counterparty, which is exactly the fold its repo forbids.

## What
- **vta-service** mints **0.5**, built through the generated `approve_request::v0_5::Payload` with its schema check (the pattern vtc-service already uses) instead of a hand-written `json!`. The type URI comes from `<Payload as trust_tasks_rs::Payload>::TYPE_URI`. Wire changes: `acceptableEvidence` → required `accepts`, `ttl` → `ttlSeconds`. `sessionId` is still sent.
- **vtc-service**: the inline request moves 0.4 → 0.5 (`ttl` → `ttlSeconds`). `bound_step_up::ApproveRequest` is now the 0.5 payload, hence the `!`.
- **vta-mobile-core**: `parse_step_up_request` accepts 0.5 only (exact match) and reads `accepts`. `approverSigned` is surfaced as `approver-signed` rather than dropped. The UniFFI `StepUpRequest` record is unchanged: when a request names no session, `session_id` is empty, the convention `stepup`'s response draft already uses. The iOS app needs no change.
- **VTC console** (`admin-ui`): reads `accepts` only (the 0.3 `acceptableEvidence` fallback is removed), shows `ttlSeconds`, and rejects a refusal whose request has no `accepts`.
- Present-tense docs and comments updated. Historical "Done:" records left as written.

## Coordinating change
pnm-browser-plugin matches the VTA's request at 0.2 today. It moves to its existing single 0.5 pin (already used for the RP) together with this change; the follow-up PR is in that repo.

## Verification
Run locally, as CLAUDE.md lists:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` ✓
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✓
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6678 passed, 23 skipped
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3560 passed, 1 skipped
- `cargo test … --doc` (both sets) ✓
- `vtc-service/admin-ui`: `npm run lint` ✓, `vitest run` 1344/1344

New tests:
- the VTA mint carries `accepts` and `ttlSeconds` and no `acceptableEvidence` or `ttl`;
- the mobile approver refuses 0.1, 0.2 and 0.4, surfaces `approver-signed`, and gives an empty `session_id` for an operation-bound request;
- the console rejects a refusal without `accepts`.
