title: chore(deps)!: take vta-sdk 0.75, affinidi-tdk 0.36, messaging-sdk 0.44 and trust-tasks 0.36; bridge speaks job 0.6, result 0.2 and event 0.5; release 0.26.0
body:
Moves VGI onto the released upstream line and the current `git-ns/bridge` versions, and releases **0.26.0**. Supersedes #181 (vta-sdk 0.74), keeping its `allow(deprecated)` handling.

## Dependencies

| Crate | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| vta-sdk | 0.73 | **0.75** |
| affinidi-tdk | 0.32 | **0.36** |
| affinidi-messaging-sdk | 0.40 | **0.44** |
| trust-tasks-rs / trust-tasks-proof | 0.34.2 | **0.36.1** |
| affinidi-messaging-test-mediator | 0.45 | **0.48** |
| trql-client | 0.28 | 0.28 (latest release; 0.29 is unreleased, affinidi-trust-registry-rs#172) |

`cargo tree` has one copy each of vta-sdk, affinidi-tdk, affinidi-messaging-sdk and trust-tasks-proof. trust-tasks-rs has two: 0.36.1, plus 0.34.2 for trql-client 0.28. verify-trust names the second through the `trust-tasks-trql` alias again (as for the 0.73 step), and no trust-tasks type crosses into vta-sdk or the bridge.

## ⚠️ Protocol changes peers must follow

**vgi-bridge**

- It takes **`git-ns/bridge/job` 0.6** only, and lists only 0.6 in its `trust-task-discovery` answer. It refuses 0.1–0.5 with `unsupportedVersion`, after which the VTC drops its cached answer and asks again.
- It sends **`git-ns/bridge/result` 0.2** and **`git-ns/bridge/event` 0.5** only. **The VTC must serve both**, and VTI `main` does. An acknowledgement of any older event or result version still clears the outbox, so documents queued before the upgrade are not stuck.
- `event_version` takes `"0.5"` only. `"0.1"` to `"0.4"` now fail the start instead of being ignored. `roleMapReported` and `pullRequestOpened` are always sent.
- It answers `trust-task-discovery` **0.3** as well as 0.2, each in the version asked (discovery 0.3 says a responder SHOULD).

**VTA:** vta-sdk 0.75 speaks `keys/list/0.2` (cursor paging) and `vta/app-state/{list,put}/1.1` (`nextCursor`, `wasCreated`). did-git-sign and the bridge's VTA mode therefore need **vta-service 0.67 or later**, because 0.66 serves only the older versions. Key listing now pages by cursor instead of reading one 1000-record page.

**Trust registry:** `registry/authorization` stays at **0.1** through trql-client 0.28, which is what released registries (≤0.28) serve. It moves to 0.2 with trql-client 0.29, and the test fakes move with it (the part of #181 that waits on 0.29).

A nested repository path, which job 0.6 now admits for GitLab, cannot reach a GitHub or Forgejo adapter as one: both call `require_owner_repo` first, so such a job reports a failure.

## Build memory

trql-client 0.28 takes trust-tasks-rs 0.34 with default features, so every family is compiled twice, once per copy. Each rustc for it is a multi-GB compile, 10 GB or more unoptimised. Two at once ran the first runs' Test job and bridge-image build out of RAM and swap (143/137), at `-j 4` and `-j 2` alike. Until a trql-client on trust-tasks 0.36 removes the second copy:

- Every job that builds the whole graph builds **serially** (`-j 1`): the Test job, the bridge image (Dockerfile; its job timeout goes 45 → 90 min), `release.yml`'s binaries and `publish.yml`'s `cargo package`. The peak is then one trust-tasks-rs compile, as on main.
- The release profile builds `trust-tasks-rs` at opt-level 1, which cut its macOS peak from 8.6 to 3.2 GB. It is serde code over small documents.

Each change says to revert it once that trql-client exists.

## Deprecations

trust-tasks-rs 0.36 deprecates its prebuilt `specs::*` modules. Following #181, vgi-bridge allows the deprecation at crate level, as do the three test files that read payloads. did-git-sign allows it around vta-sdk's health answer. Generating these types with `trust-tasks-build` is a follow-up.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and so is the same run with `--all-features`.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 630 pass, 0 fail.
- `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` passes.
- `cargo audit --deny warnings` is clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no client change
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): outbox entries are re-signed at send time under the new versions
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): job 0.6 / result 0.2 / event 0.5, served by VTI main
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): an old `event_version` fails the start
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: `allow(deprecated)` above, until generated specs

title: chore: release @openvtc/trust-tasks-gen 0.1.2
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-gen` | npm | `0.1.1` → `0.1.2` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(ts-gen): qualify a bare component's nested branch types when their titles collide
body:
## Problem
`trust-tasks-gen-ts` 0.1.1 refuses a lock that pins both `device/list` 0.3 (or `device/register` 0.2) and `auth/oob/claim` 0.2 (or `prove` 0.3):

```
trust-tasks-gen-ts: the components module declares counter-suffixed duplicates: Service1
```

Under that lock `ConsumerKind` has one shape, so it stays bare, and its `oneOf` branches keep their own titles, `Companion` and `Service`. `auth/oob` has a shared definition named `Service` too. json-schema-to-typescript numbers the second one `Service1`, and the generator, correctly, refuses to emit it.

The prebuilt package never runs into this: across the whole registry `ConsumerKind` has two shapes, so it is qualified and `tagNestedTitles` tags its branches `_DeviceV0_2`.

Found by pnm-browser-plugin, which generates the tasks it pins and needs `auth/oob` beside `device/*`.

## Fix
In `compileComponents`, a bare component's nested titles are now tagged with its family/version (`_${tag}`, the same suffix a qualified component would get) when any of them collides with a component name or with another bare component's nested title. `displayNames` records the original, so modules still bind the plain name (`Service_DeviceV0_2 as Service`). A lock with no collision is unchanged.

## Tests
- New: `a bare component's nested branch types` in `test/generate.test.ts`. It uses two real registry bundles vendored under `test/fixtures/registry/`:
  - Colliding lock: auth/oob's `Service` stays bare, device's branch is `Service_DeviceV0_2` (the package's name for it), there is no `Service1`, and both modules import the plain name.
  - Lock without a collision: `ConsumerKind = Companion | Service`, unchanged.
- The colliding case fails on `main` (29 pass / 1 fail) and passes with this change (30/30).
- `npm run equivalence`: `equivalent ✓`, unchanged.

Once released as 0.1.2, pnm-browser-plugin will bump to it.

title: feat!: cut over to the task versions served today, generated from a lock
body:
## Why
The VTA moved to newer Trust Task versions and stopped serving the old ones. Sign-in failed with `unsupported version: https://trusttasks.org/spec/vault/list/0.3 — this VTA serves …/vault/list/0.4` (`sign-in/failed`). Resyncing `task-surface.json` from vta-sdk 0.75.0 showed 64 tasks behind.

## What
**Library + generation**
- `@openvtc/trust-tasks` ^0.27.2 → ^0.28.1. Its prebuilt per-task modules are deprecated (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #954), so core now pins what it speaks in `packages/core/trust-tasks.toml` / `trust-tasks.lock` (vendored bundles in `trust-tasks/`) and generates with `@openvtc/trust-tasks-gen` into `packages/core/src/specs/`. Source imports `../specs/<slug>/<M.N>/payload.js`; only `@openvtc/trust-tasks/runtime` and the framework `trust-task-discovery` come from the package.
- The lock holds **one version per slug**, so a second version cannot be imported without moving the pin: the no-folds rule is now enforced by the compiler.
- `tests/specs.generated.mjs` regenerates into a temp dir and fails on drift or a hand edit. `npm run tasks:generate -w @openvtc/pnm-core` regenerates. `specs` is a layer-0 module and a `./specs` subpath.
- Most of the +113k lines are `src/specs/` and the vendored bundles, all generated or downloaded; the hand-written diff is about 3k/3k lines.

**Version moves**, checked against vta-sdk/vta-service 0.75.0, affinidi-webvh-service, vtc-service, vti-rooms and affinidi-messaging-mediator 0.48.0
- 64 VTA tasks moved, shapes adapted (mostly renames to `nextCursor` / `wasCreated` / `occurredAt` / `…Seconds`, plus RFC 3339 times). ACL 0.2/0.3 has a new entry model (`act` / `keys` / first-class `capabilities`); `admin/acl*.ts` and the Access pane are rewritten onto it.
- `persona/facet/*` → `persona/world/*` (the VTA refuses the retired spelling).
- did-hosting: `did/{enable,disable}` and `domain/disable` → `*/set-state/0.1`; `did/publish` retired, so `publishHostedDid` (no callers) is removed.
- Room host / RP / VTC: `auth/authenticate` 0.3, `auth/refresh` 0.2, `auth/step-up/start` 0.2, `approve-response` 0.6 everywhere, `rooms/keys/act` 0.8, `rooms/{info 0.3, records/list 0.5, records/put 0.3, epoch/chain 0.2, create 0.2}`, `rooms/keys/browse` 0.3, `vtc/rooms/offers/list` 0.4, `vtc/join-requests/manifest` 0.4, `vta/contexts/delete` 1.1.
- Folds removed: multi-version accept lists in step-up, the join manifest, room records, `rooms/keys/act` and `rooms/keys/list`; the bare `auth/authenticate/0.1` DIDComm login (`loginViaDidcomm` now requires `signing`).
- Mediator lens: `account/{get,list,update}` 0.2 and `monitor/event` 0.2; `MEDIATOR_VERSION_FLOOR` 0.28.36 → 0.48.0.
- CI bundle guards re-pointed at the pinned versions. They named URIs that no longer existed anywhere, so they checked nothing.
- `task-surface.json` resynced; coverage 231 → 229 (two did-hosting retirements); stale `NOT_IN_SDK` entries dropped. CLAUDE.md updated.

**Coordinating change needed:** `auth/step-up/approve-request` is minted at 0.2 by the VTA, 0.4 by the VTC (`acl/bound_step_up.rs`) and 0.5 by the did-hosting RP. Each is matched with `===`, and the VTA's is a single commented literal until they align. `vta/webvh/dids/{update,rotate-keys}` stay at 1.0, because the VTA dispatches only 1.0 although the registry has newer versions.

## Verification
- `npm run lint` and `npm test` from a clean core: tsp-js 123/123, core 1095 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped, extension 1323/1323, demo-rp 6/6, reviewer-demo 9/9.
- `npm run build` plus every `dist/` guard step from `ci.yml` run locally: all pass. The Web Store zip step was not run (needs `npm run package`).

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new fetch paths; room host and RP calls go through the existing injected channels
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): version-fallback retries removed; new cursor loops go through `collectPages` (`MAX_PAGES`)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): untouched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path untouched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): types are generated from the registry bundles
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): `movePlan` ordering is unchanged under the world rename
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

## Open questions
1. Grant with no context sends `act: all`, which the VTA accepts only for `admin`. Should the Access pane offer an explicit "nowhere (approver only)"?
2. `webvh/dids/create` 1.2 lets the agent choose `did:scid` or `did:webvh`. Should room and host DIDs pin `webvh`?
3. Out of scope, still present: the `auth/oob` 0.2 → 0.1 fallback; snake_case reads in `contextPreviewDelete`; two first-page-only `vault/list` reads in `offscreen.ts`.

  speaks in trust-tasks.toml/.lock (vendored bundles in trust-tasks/) and
  generates them with @openvtc/trust-tasks-gen into src/specs/. The lock
  holds one version per slug, which makes "no compatibility folds"
  structural. tests/specs.generated.mjs fails on drift or a hand edit;
  `npm run tasks:generate -w @openvtc/pnm-core` regenerates.

Version moves (checked against vta-sdk 0.75.0, affinidi-webvh-service,
vtc-service, vti-rooms and affinidi-messaging-mediator 0.48.0)
- 64 VTA tasks moved, shapes adapted; ACL 0.2/0.3 has a new entry model
  (act / keys / capabilities).
- persona/facet/* -> persona/world/* (the VTA refuses the old spelling).
- did-management did/{enable,disable}, domain/disable -> */set-state;
  did/publish retired (publishHostedDid removed).
- Remaining folds removed: multi-version accept lists in step-up, join
  manifest, room records, rooms/keys/act and rooms/keys/list; the bare
  auth/authenticate/0.1 DIDComm login.
- Mediator lens floor 0.48.0 (account/* 0.2, monitor/event 0.2).
- CI bundle guards re-pointed at the pinned versions; they named URIs
  that no longer existed and so checked nothing.

Known gap: auth/step-up/approve-request is minted at 0.2 by the VTA, 0.4
by the VTC and 0.5 by the did-hosting RP; the VTA's is a single literal
until those align.

title: chore(deps): take trust-tasks-rs 0.36, affinidi-tdk 0.36 and affinidi-messaging-didcomm-service 0.29
body:
Moves the gateway onto the current Trust Tasks and Affinidi stack — the same set VTI main is on (vta-sdk 0.75 / vta-service 0.67).

| crate | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| trust-tasks-rs / -proof / -tsp | 0.24 | 0.36.1 |
| affinidi-tdk | 0.20 | 0.36 (affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.44) |
| affinidi-messaging-didcomm-service | 0.15 | 0.29 |
| affinidi-data-integrity | 0.7 | 0.8 |
| affinidi-secrets-resolver | 0.5.12 | 0.5.15 |
| affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk | 0.8.42 | 0.8.43 |

No source changes. The gateway models the `push/*` 0.2 bodies in `src/types.rs` and enables no `trust-tasks-rs` spec family, so 0.36's deprecation of the prebuilt `specs::` modules does not reach it.

**Push protocol:** no change. The gateway already serves `push/{register,provision,wake}/0.2` only (issue #20). VTI main sends 0.2 for all three: `vta-mobile-core/src/push.rs` sends register, `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/device.rs` sends provision, and `step_up.rs` sends wake. The remaining `0.1` URIs are in `tests/api.rs` and only assert that the retired forms are refused.

**cargo-deny** (red on main since #38):
- crypto-bigint 0.7 is now locked at 0.7.10, which fixes RUSTSEC-2026-0387.
- The 0.5.5 copy that is still in the tree comes in through p256 0.13. web-push-native requires p256 0.13 in every release up to 0.5.0, so the gateway can't drop it. It is ignored, and `deny.toml` gives the condition for removing the ignore.
- The RUSTSEC-2025-0134 ignore no longer matches anything, so it is removed.

Checked locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-targets` (145 passed) and `cargo deny check` all pass.

title: vtc-service-v0.15.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Serve acl/*/0.2 and acl/list/0.3, keeping change-role/0.1 for the community role ([#2323](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2323))

* feat(vtc)!: serve acl/*/0.2 and acl/list/0.3, keeping change-role/0.1 for the community role

  The VTC stops serving the superseded `acl/*` versions:

  - `acl/{grant,show,update,revoke}/0.1` are gone; `acl/*/0.2` (AclEntry 0.2, every authority axis explicit) is the only form.
  - `acl/list/0.2` → `acl/list/0.3`: `pageSize` → `limit`, response `cursor` → `nextCursor` (absent on the last page), `truncated` removed. The cursor stays bound to the filters and direction it was minted under (`acl/list:cursorMismatch`).
  - `acl/change-role/0.2` moves the **administrative** role.

  **Kept on 0.1: `acl/change-role/0.1`.** It is still the only door onto the **community**-role ceremony (member ↔ admin, role-VAC re-mint, promotion serialisation, the bound step-up and VTI-APV-018/019 consent). `acl/change-role/0.2` moves the administrative role only, and the community role has no 0.2 task of its own, so dropping 0.1 would remove the operation outright. It is served beside 0.2 as `ACL_CHANGE_COMMUNITY_ROLE_TYPE`; the consent gate, the summary templates and the bound step-up now name it explicitly rather than through the 0.2 constant.

- **auth**: Serve only the current passkey invite, approver invite, passkey revoke and login versions ([#2321](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2321))

The VTC now serves:

  - auth/passkey/enroll/invite/0.3 (was 0.2) and
    auth/step-up/approver/invite/0.2 (was 0.1): the invite lifetime is
    `ttlSeconds`, not `ttl`. Nothing else in either payload moved.
  - auth/passkey/revoke/{start,finish}/0.2 for an administrator's own
    session (login) passkeys too, which were still on 0.1. One Type URI
    now serves both purposes: start resolves the credential among the
    subject's session and step-up credentials, and finish routes the
    handle back to whichever started it. For a session credential, per
    0.2: lastCredential is refused at start before a challenge is issued
    (and re-checked at finish), the handle is bound to its producer
    (another producer's handle is revocationNotFound), the assertion must
    carry the UV flag, and the response carries `subject` and
    `purpose: "session"`. An administrator naming another administrator's
    session passkey as `subject` is notAuthorized: a login passkey is
    revoked only by its owner on this door.

  The VTA's REST passkey-login routes declare only
  auth/passkey/login/{start,finish}/0.2; the 0.1 constants are removed
  from vta-sdk (TASK_AUTH_PASSKEY_LOGIN_{START,FINISH}_0_1). The routes
  never read `purpose`, the only member 0.1 spelt differently
  (`step-up` vs `stepUp`), so no wire behaviour changes there. The VTC
  already served login 0.2.

  The admin console sends ttlSeconds and the 0.2 revoke URIs; openapi.json
  and wire.ts are regenerated for the revoke/finish response.

- **voting**: Register and show elections at voting/election 0.2, and serve vtc/elections create 0.3, list 0.3, show 0.2 ([#2317](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2317))

* feat(voting)!: register and show elections at voting/election 0.2, and serve vtc/elections create 0.3, list 0.3, show 0.2

  trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and
  withdraws each about 90 days later. Every party to an election is in this
  workspace, so all of them move to the current versions together, and the old
  ones are refused `unsupportedVersion`. Every current version is already in
  trust-tasks-rs 0.35.3.

  | Task | Was | Now | What changed on the wire |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | voting/election/register | 0.1 | 0.2 | the manifest (voting/_shared/0.2) names its instants `registrationOpensAt`, `votingOpensAt`, `votingClosesAt` |
  | voting/election/show | 0.1 | 0.2 | the same manifest in the answer |
  | vtc/elections/create | 0.1 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest; a parked binding election's next step expects `vtc/admin/actions/show/0.3` |
  | vtc/elections/list | 0.1 | 0.3 | `next` is `nextCursor` (0.2); items' `votingOpens`/`votingCloses` are `votingOpensAt`/`votingClosesAt` (0.3) |
  | vtc/elections/show | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/voter/register | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/voter/read | 0.1 | 0.2 | signs `vtc/elections/list/0.3` or `show/0.2` |
  | vta/pcs/vote | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/vote-encrypted | 0.2 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/trustee/enrol | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/trustee/{deal,keys,justify} | 0.2 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/trustee/read | 0.1 | 0.2 | an `election` read signs `voting/election/show/0.2` |

  - vti-voting reads the 0.2 manifest throughout (rules, tally, audit, the
    encrypted levels, the voter's checks).
  - vti-voting-service (the ballot box) dispatches by version: register and show
    at 0.2, every other voting/* task at 0.1, its current version. A known task
    at another version is refused `unsupportedVersion` naming the one served
    (was `unsupportedType`).
  - The VTC sends register 0.2 and serves the elections tasks above. The VTA's
    voter and trustee tasks (`vta/pcs/*`) carry the manifest too, so they move
    in the same change: a 0.2 manifest does not parse in the 0.1 task. `cnm`,
    `pnm`, vta-sdk, vta-mobile-core, vtc-client and the admin console move with
    them.
  - Action summaries: a template for `vtc/elections/create/0.3` (pointers
    `/manifest/votingOpensAt` and `/manifest/votingClosesAt`), pinned in the
    build and in the console. The 0.1 template stays so a binding election
    parked under it still renders in the history.

  **Elections registered before this build are not carried over.** A manifest's
  digest — which every ticket, cast and certification is bound to — is over its
  member names, so a 0.1 manifest cannot be re-read as 0.2 without becoming a
  different election. Rather than fail as a manifest "missing
  registrationOpensAt", every reader refuses it by name with
  `vti_voting::rules::require_current_manifest`:

  - the ballot box will not start while its journal holds such an election
    (restore fails, as for any journal entry that no longer parses), with
    "election <id> was registered under voting/election/register/0.1 … this
    build reads only the 0.2 manifest and cannot carry it over. Finish or cancel
    it on the previous release, or remove it";
  - the VTC's `vtc/elections/show` answers that election with the same message
    and its audit and decryption steps fail it the same way.
    `vtc/elections/list` still lists it.

  Finish or cancel open elections before upgrading.

- **vta**: Serve only the current vta/* and messaging/ping versions ([#2316](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2316))

The VTA and its clients move off superseded `vta/*` versions, and the VTA
  stops serving the old ones:

  - vta/did-templates/{list,create,get,update} 2.0/3.0 -> 3.1: the record's
    `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are RFC 3339 instants (`vta/_shared/0.7`). A record
    stored with integer seconds still reads.
  - vta/app-state/{put,put-many} 1.0 -> 1.1 (`created` -> `wasCreated`),
    vta/app-state/list 1.0 -> 1.1 (`limit`/`nextCursor`).
  - vta/attestation/mnemonic-export 1.0 -> 1.1, mnemonic-status 0.1 -> 0.2
    (`windowRemainingSecs` -> `windowRemainingSeconds`).
  - vta/credentials/list 0.1 -> 0.2 (`limit`/`nextCursor`).
  - vta/passkey-vms/enroll-submit 0.1 -> 0.2 (`clientDataJSON`; the REST twin
    still reads `clientDataJson`).
  - vta/services/{list,get,enable,disable,drain/list} 1.0 -> 1.1,
    {update,rollback} 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2, report 0.1 -> 0.2 (`drainTtlSeconds`,
    `handshakeTimeoutSeconds`, `drainEndsAt`, `firstSeenAt`/`lastSeenAt`).
  - vta/backup/{initiate-export,initiate-import,finalize-import} 1.0 -> 1.1,
    vta/contexts/update-did 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/webvh/dids/create 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2,
    vta/webvh/agent-name/list 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/witness/list 0.1 -> 0.2.
  - messaging/ping 0.1 -> 0.2 (`serverTime` -> `respondedAt`).

- **auth**: Serve only the current auth, audit/list, policy, task-consent and discovery versions ([#2313](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2313))

The VTA, the VTC and every client in the workspace move off superseded Trust
  Task versions of these families, and the services stop serving the old ones:

  - auth/authenticate 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (proxied-login members; a `principal` that
    is not the signer is refused `delegationNotRecognized`), auth/refresh 0.1 ->
    0.2, auth/revoke-session -> 0.2, auth/signing-key/enroll 0.1 -> 0.2.
  - auth/step-up/approve-response 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> 0.6 on the VTA (one typed
    handler; vta-mobile-core builds 0.6, a bound approval may carry no
    `sessionId`).
  - auth/oob/{request,redeem,claim} 0.1 -> 0.2, grant 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3, respond
    0.1 -> 0.3 (`claimClosesAt`, `decisionClosesAt`, `sessionEndsAt` as RFC 3339
    instants rather than epoch seconds), on the VTC and the member portal.
  - audit/list 0.1 -> 0.2 and policy/list 0.2 -> 0.3 (`limit`/`nextCursor`),
    policy/upsert 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (`created` -> `wasCreated`), on both services
    and their clients.
  - task-consent/decision 0.1 -> 0.2, trust-task-discovery 0.1 -> 0.3.

  An approval rule names its task by exact versioned Type URI, so a stored rule
  naming a version the VTA no longer serves would never match again and the task
  it gated would run ungated. `vta_policy::approvals::RETIRED_TASK_TYPES` maps
  each retired version to its successor; boot moves stored rules onto it, and the
  policy write path refuses a new rule naming a retired type.

  Deliberately not moved, because a peer outside this workspace pins them:

  - auth/step-up/approve-request stays at 0.2 on the VTA: the fielded approvers
    (vta-mobile-agent-ios, which routes by a hard-coded 0.1/0.2 type list, and the
    browser plugin) accept only 0.1 and 0.2.
  - the VTC still serves auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4 beside 0.6, for the
    console's unsigned session-passkey answer, which 0.5 onward forbids.

- **external**: Serve and send only the current external/* versions ([#2311](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2311))

trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and withdraws each about 90 days later. Every current `external/*` version is already in 0.35, so the VTA serves it now and stops serving the old one, and every client in the workspace sends it.

  Served now (the old versions are refused `unsupportedVersion`/`unsupportedType`):

  - `external/accounts/{list,get,create,update,bindings/grant,bindings/revoke,probe,keys/rotate,suspend,resume,archive,restore}` 0.2 (from 0.1). `secret/set`, `setup` and `delete` stay at 0.1, their current version.
  - `external/credentials/issue` 0.3 only (0.1 and 0.2 are no longer served).

  On the wire:

  - An account's `lastProbe` (`AccountProbeReport`, `external/_shared/0.2`) names when the probe ran `probedAt`, not `at`. A report stored by an earlier VTA is answered under the new name; nothing is rewritten.
  - Issuance is 0.3's: a `scope` for every brokered model but `s3-static-presign`, which takes a `presign` batch of at most 64 operations (a 65th is `malformedRequest`); a batch whose sealed answer would not fit is `responseTooLarge` and costs none of the binding's rate. 0.1's single, unbound presigned request is gone with it.

  Clients move with it:

  - `vta-sdk`: `TASK_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNTS_*_0_1` become `_0_2`; `TASK_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIALS_ISSUE_0_1`/`_0_2` are removed. `VtaClient::external_credentials_issue` sends 0.3 (it took the 0.1 payload); `external_credentials_issue_v2`/`_v3` are removed, and `external_credentials_issue_presign` no longer falls back to 0.2.
  - `vta-external`: `batch::PresignBatch`/`PresignRequest` are 0.3's types and `MAX_OPERATIONS` is 64; `MAX_OPERATIONS_0_3` is removed.
  - `pnm external issue` drops `--object-key` (0.3's `scope` takes none; an `s3-static-presign` account is asked with `--presign`).
  - The VTC (`auth: vta-account` storage) asks its VTA only at 0.3: the account check is a one-`get` batch on the canary, reads and deletes are batches of one, and a write the VTC makes itself is presigned as a `put` bound to its length and SHA-256 (`PresignedBlobs::put` hashes the staged file whenever its presigner `presigns_ops`). It no longer falls back to 0.2 for a VTA without 0.3.

- **git-ns**: Serve and send only the current git-ns/* versions ([#2314](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2314))

trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and
  withdraws each about 90 days later. Every current git-ns version is already
  in 0.35, so the VTC moves to it and stops serving the old ones (refused
  `unsupportedVersion`).

  Served now, at the current version only:
  - git-ns/namespace/bind 0.2 (from 0.1), namespace/reseat 0.4 (from 0.3)
  - git-ns/repo/adopt 0.3, repo/archive 0.3, repo/transfer 0.3 (from 0.1),
    repo/create 0.4 (from 0.3)
  - git-ns/right/grant 0.4 and right/revoke 0.4 (from 0.3),
    right/break-glass 0.2 and right/ratify 0.2 (from 0.1)
  - git-ns/drift/resolve 0.4 (from 0.1 revert-only and 0.3)
  - git-ns/roles/reproject 0.2 (from 0.1)
  - git-ns/view 0.6 (from 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 and 0.5): one handler for the member's
    view and `scope: administrator`
  - the administrator's reads: namespace/list 0.2, repo/list 0.2,
    right/list 0.3, right/issued-by-departed 0.3, bridge/job/list 0.4 (from
    0.1 and 0.2), projection/show 0.3, account/list 0.2, activity/list 0.3
  - git-ns/right/break-glass-notice is sent at 0.2 (from 0.1)

  On the wire: a record's `breakGlass.at` is `recordedAt`
  (git-ns/_shared/0.6), a break-glass notice's `at` is `occurredAt`, an
  activity item's `at` is `occurredAt`, and a repository's `lastCheck.at` is
  `concludedAt`. Ratifying names `breakGlassAt` as before, read from
  `breakGlass.recordedAt`.

  Nested repository paths (git-ns/_shared/0.6): a repository resource is
  `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>` with 1 to 21 path segments of up to 255
  characters, so `gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli` is one repository of the
  namespace `gitlab.com/acme`. A repository contains only itself: a right on
  `gitlab.com/acme/platform` is no right on `gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli`.

  The bridge's own tasks keep their older versions beside the current ones,
  because the released bridge (OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure
  `vgi-bridge` v0.25.0) still speaks only them: it sends `git-ns/bridge/event`
  0.3 by default (0.1, 0.2 or 0.4 as configured) and `git-ns/bridge/result`
  0.1, and takes `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4 and 0.5. So the VTC now accepts
  bridge/event 0.1 to 0.5 and bridge/result 0.1 and 0.2, and sends each job
  as the newest bridge/job version the bridge lists in `trust-task-discovery`
  — 0.6, else 0.5, else 0.4 — and a job naming a repository only 0.6 can
  carry to no bridge without 0.6 (bridge/job 0.6, *Changes from 0.5*). Those
  older bridge versions go once a bridge release speaking the current ones is
  deployed.

  One divergence kept, not introduced here: git-ns/drift/resolve 0.3 and 0.4
  read an unreported role map as the default one; this VTC still refuses an
  adopt with `git-ns:roleMapUnknown` until the bridge reports its map,
  failing closed.

  Clients move with it: the admin console (Repos plugin, member portal,
  openapi.json and wire.ts regenerated, list-limits.json), `cnm git`, and
  vtc-client, whose `git_ns_view` now takes `administrator` and `break_glass`
  and replaces `git_ns_view_v2`, `git_ns_view_v4` and `git_ns_view_v5`;
  `git_ns_drift_resolve` (0.4) replaces `git_ns_drift_resolve_v3` and the
  deprecated 0.1 form, and `GIT_NS_DRIFT_RESOLVE_TYPE` replaces
  `GIT_NS_DRIFT_RESOLVE_V3_TYPE`. vta_sdk::openapi's `GitNsView01*` wrappers
  are `GitNsView06*`.

- **rooms**: Serve and send only the current rooms tasks, keeping what pnm-browser-plugin sends ([#2315](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2315))

The rest of the `rooms` family, and `vtc/rooms/offers/list`, move off their superseded versions (part of the migration off the versions trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates, trust-tasks-tf #921). Every sender in this workspace goes at the current version with no fallback. The versions `pnm-browser-plugin` still sends stay served (below).

title: vta-service-v0.67.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Speak AclEntry 0.2 — acl/*/0.2 and acl/list/0.3 ([#2324](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2324))

The VTA moves its ACL surface to AclEntry 0.2 (`acl/_shared/0.2`), where every
  authority axis is explicit, and stops serving acl/{grant,show,update,
  change-role,revoke}/0.1 and acl/list/0.1. `operations::acl_v0_2` maps each
  0.2 value onto the stored (role, contexts) model and refuses the ones the
  store cannot hold (`act: all` on a non-admin, `act: none` on admin →
  invalidActScope) rather than approximating them. change-role carries the act
  scope across unchanged; update never narrows act (revoke {kind: act} does);
  list/0.3 pages with signed, filter-bound cursors and honours role,
  subjectPrefix and capability. RETIRED_TASK_TYPES moves approval rules naming
  the 0.1 URIs to their successors at boot.

- **policy**: A requireConsent decision states its quorum and requester exclusion (policy/_shared 0.4) ([#2322](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2322))

trust-tasks-rs 0.36 publishes policy/_shared/0.4 and policy/evaluate/0.4,
  which make requireConsent.minApprovals and excludeRequester REQUIRED with no
  default (SPEC §6.6 rule 5: a shared component supplies no governance
  default). Under 0.3 a decision omitting either meant a quorum of one, or a
  requester allowed to approve itself, with nothing on the wire to show it.

  vta-policy's mirror of the schema moves to 0.4: RequireConsent no longer
  defaults either member, so a policy whose decision omits one no longer
  deserialises and the PDP fails closed (deny), as for any other malformed
  decision. The declarative approvals generator (vta-sdk::approvals) and the
  VTC already emit both members; hand-written operator policies that omit
  them must add them.

  policy/evaluate is still not served (its PolicyInput.site remains required
  in 0.4), so there is no wire version to move.

- **vta**: Finish deleting a context whose DID host is gone (vta/contexts/delete/1.1) ([#2320](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2320))

* chore(deps)!: trust-tasks-rs 0.36, affinidi-tdk 0.36, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.44, mediator 0.48

  One trust-tasks-rs in the graph again, at 0.36.1 — the first release
  carrying vta/contexts/delete/1.1 (trust-tasks-tf #967). TDK moved in
  lockstep (affinidi-tdk-rs #978: affinidi-tdk 0.36, affinidi-messaging-sdk
  0.44) and so did the mediator (affinidi-messaging-mediator #46, released as
  0.48.0: test-mediator, mediator-admin, mediator-tui).

  trust-tasks-rs 0.36 emits trust-task-error/0.6, which adds the
  unsupportedExtension and indeterminate standard codes (framework 0.7,
  SPEC §8.3). Both services' framework_error_type_uri() move to 0.6 so an
  unrouted refusal speaks the same version as a routed one — the drift
  unrouted_and_routed_errors_agree_on_the_type_uri exists to catch — and the
  fixtures standing in for this workspace's own refusals follow, keeping
  one error version in vtc-service's binding census. Fixtures for foreign
  peers (a DID host) keep 0.5: a consumer still accepts it (SPEC §5.2).
  vta-sdk and the admin console recognise any trust-task-error/ version.

  0.36 also marks every prebuilt spec module deprecated in favour of
  trust-tasks-build. The workspace already allows `deprecated`;
  vta-external, vti-vetting-pcs and vta-persona did not inherit the
  workspace lints, and now do.

- **auth**: Serve only the current passkey invite, approver invite, passkey revoke and login versions ([#2321](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2321))

The VTC now serves:

  - auth/passkey/enroll/invite/0.3 (was 0.2) and
    auth/step-up/approver/invite/0.2 (was 0.1): the invite lifetime is
    `ttlSeconds`, not `ttl`. Nothing else in either payload moved.
  - auth/passkey/revoke/{start,finish}/0.2 for an administrator's own
    session (login) passkeys too, which were still on 0.1. One Type URI
    now serves both purposes: start resolves the credential among the
    subject's session and step-up credentials, and finish routes the
    handle back to whichever started it. For a session credential, per
    0.2: lastCredential is refused at start before a challenge is issued
    (and re-checked at finish), the handle is bound to its producer
    (another producer's handle is revocationNotFound), the assertion must
    carry the UV flag, and the response carries `subject` and
    `purpose: "session"`. An administrator naming another administrator's
    session passkey as `subject` is notAuthorized: a login passkey is
    revoked only by its owner on this door.

  The VTA's REST passkey-login routes declare only
  auth/passkey/login/{start,finish}/0.2; the 0.1 constants are removed
  from vta-sdk (TASK_AUTH_PASSKEY_LOGIN_{START,FINISH}_0_1). The routes
  never read `purpose`, the only member 0.1 spelt differently
  (`step-up` vs `stepUp`), so no wire behaviour changes there. The VTC
  already served login 0.2.

  The admin console sends ttlSeconds and the 0.2 revoke URIs; openapi.json
  and wire.ts are regenerated for the revoke/finish response.

- **voting**: Register and show elections at voting/election 0.2, and serve vtc/elections create 0.3, list 0.3, show 0.2 ([#2317](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2317))

* feat(voting)!: register and show elections at voting/election 0.2, and serve vtc/elections create 0.3, list 0.3, show 0.2

  trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and
  withdraws each about 90 days later. Every party to an election is in this
  workspace, so all of them move to the current versions together, and the old
  ones are refused `unsupportedVersion`. Every current version is already in
  trust-tasks-rs 0.35.3.

  | Task | Was | Now | What changed on the wire |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | voting/election/register | 0.1 | 0.2 | the manifest (voting/_shared/0.2) names its instants `registrationOpensAt`, `votingOpensAt`, `votingClosesAt` |
  | voting/election/show | 0.1 | 0.2 | the same manifest in the answer |
  | vtc/elections/create | 0.1 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest; a parked binding election's next step expects `vtc/admin/actions/show/0.3` |
  | vtc/elections/list | 0.1 | 0.3 | `next` is `nextCursor` (0.2); items' `votingOpens`/`votingCloses` are `votingOpensAt`/`votingClosesAt` (0.3) |
  | vtc/elections/show | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/voter/register | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/voter/read | 0.1 | 0.2 | signs `vtc/elections/list/0.3` or `show/0.2` |
  | vta/pcs/vote | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/vote-encrypted | 0.2 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/trustee/enrol | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/trustee/{deal,keys,justify} | 0.2 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest |
  | vta/pcs/trustee/read | 0.1 | 0.2 | an `election` read signs `voting/election/show/0.2` |

  - vti-voting reads the 0.2 manifest throughout (rules, tally, audit, the
    encrypted levels, the voter's checks).
  - vti-voting-service (the ballot box) dispatches by version: register and show
    at 0.2, every other voting/* task at 0.1, its current version. A known task
    at another version is refused `unsupportedVersion` naming the one served
    (was `unsupportedType`).
  - The VTC sends register 0.2 and serves the elections tasks above. The VTA's
    voter and trustee tasks (`vta/pcs/*`) carry the manifest too, so they move
    in the same change: a 0.2 manifest does not parse in the 0.1 task. `cnm`,
    `pnm`, vta-sdk, vta-mobile-core, vtc-client and the admin console move with
    them.
  - Action summaries: a template for `vtc/elections/create/0.3` (pointers
    `/manifest/votingOpensAt` and `/manifest/votingClosesAt`), pinned in the
    build and in the console. The 0.1 template stays so a binding election
    parked under it still renders in the history.

  **Elections registered before this build are not carried over.** A manifest's
  digest — which every ticket, cast and certification is bound to — is over its
  member names, so a 0.1 manifest cannot be re-read as 0.2 without becoming a
  different election. Rather than fail as a manifest "missing
  registrationOpensAt", every reader refuses it by name with
  `vti_voting::rules::require_current_manifest`:

  - the ballot box will not start while its journal holds such an election
    (restore fails, as for any journal entry that no longer parses), with
    "election <id> was registered under voting/election/register/0.1 … this
    build reads only the 0.2 manifest and cannot carry it over. Finish or cancel
    it on the previous release, or remove it";
  - the VTC's `vtc/elections/show` answers that election with the same message
    and its audit and decryption steps fail it the same way.
    `vtc/elections/list` still lists it.

  Finish or cancel open elections before upgrading.

- **vta**: Serve only the current vta/* and messaging/ping versions ([#2316](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2316))

The VTA and its clients move off superseded `vta/*` versions, and the VTA
  stops serving the old ones:

  - vta/did-templates/{list,create,get,update} 2.0/3.0 -> 3.1: the record's
    `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are RFC 3339 instants (`vta/_shared/0.7`). A record
    stored with integer seconds still reads.
  - vta/app-state/{put,put-many} 1.0 -> 1.1 (`created` -> `wasCreated`),
    vta/app-state/list 1.0 -> 1.1 (`limit`/`nextCursor`).
  - vta/attestation/mnemonic-export 1.0 -> 1.1, mnemonic-status 0.1 -> 0.2
    (`windowRemainingSecs` -> `windowRemainingSeconds`).
  - vta/credentials/list 0.1 -> 0.2 (`limit`/`nextCursor`).
  - vta/passkey-vms/enroll-submit 0.1 -> 0.2 (`clientDataJSON`; the REST twin
    still reads `clientDataJson`).
  - vta/services/{list,get,enable,disable,drain/list} 1.0 -> 1.1,
    {update,rollback} 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2, report 0.1 -> 0.2 (`drainTtlSeconds`,
    `handshakeTimeoutSeconds`, `drainEndsAt`, `firstSeenAt`/`lastSeenAt`).
  - vta/backup/{initiate-export,initiate-import,finalize-import} 1.0 -> 1.1,
    vta/contexts/update-did 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/webvh/dids/create 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2,
    vta/webvh/agent-name/list 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/witness/list 0.1 -> 0.2.
  - messaging/ping 0.1 -> 0.2 (`serverTime` -> `respondedAt`).

- **auth**: Serve only the current auth, audit/list, policy, task-consent and discovery versions ([#2313](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2313))

The VTA, the VTC and every client in the workspace move off superseded Trust
  Task versions of these families, and the services stop serving the old ones:

  - auth/authenticate 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (proxied-login members; a `principal` that
    is not the signer is refused `delegationNotRecognized`), auth/refresh 0.1 ->
    0.2, auth/revoke-session -> 0.2, auth/signing-key/enroll 0.1 -> 0.2.
  - auth/step-up/approve-response 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> 0.6 on the VTA (one typed
    handler; vta-mobile-core builds 0.6, a bound approval may carry no
    `sessionId`).
  - auth/oob/{request,redeem,claim} 0.1 -> 0.2, grant 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3, respond
    0.1 -> 0.3 (`claimClosesAt`, `decisionClosesAt`, `sessionEndsAt` as RFC 3339
    instants rather than epoch seconds), on the VTC and the member portal.
  - audit/list 0.1 -> 0.2 and policy/list 0.2 -> 0.3 (`limit`/`nextCursor`),
    policy/upsert 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (`created` -> `wasCreated`), on both services
    and their clients.
  - task-consent/decision 0.1 -> 0.2, trust-task-discovery 0.1 -> 0.3.

  An approval rule names its task by exact versioned Type URI, so a stored rule
  naming a version the VTA no longer serves would never match again and the task
  it gated would run ungated. `vta_policy::approvals::RETIRED_TASK_TYPES` maps
  each retired version to its successor; boot moves stored rules onto it, and the
  policy write path refuses a new rule naming a retired type.

  Deliberately not moved, because a peer outside this workspace pins them:

  - auth/step-up/approve-request stays at 0.2 on the VTA: the fielded approvers
    (vta-mobile-agent-ios, which routes by a hard-coded 0.1/0.2 type list, and the
    browser plugin) accept only 0.1 and 0.2.
  - the VTC still serves auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4 beside 0.6, for the
    console's unsigned session-passkey answer, which 0.5 onward forbids.

- **vta**: Serve only the current keys/list, consent/list, persona and did-management versions ([#2318](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2318))

The VTA and its clients move off these superseded versions, and the VTA stops
  serving the old ones:

  - keys/list 0.1 -> 0.2: paging moves from `offset`/`total` to `cursor` +
    `limit` -> `nextCursor`. The VTA pages by key id under a cursor bound to the
    filters it was minted for, and refuses one it did not issue. The did-secrets
    bundle export, `fetch_context_secrets` and pnm's mediator console follow the
    cursor; `pnm`/`cnm keys list` take `--cursor` in place of `--offset` and print
    the next one.
  - consent/list 1.0 -> 1.1 (`since` -> `syncToken`, `cursor` ->
    `nextSyncToken`; the VTA offers neither yet, so only the version moves).
  - persona/correlation/analyze 1.0 (retired) and 1.1 -> 1.2 (a finding's `why`
    -> `reason`), persona/profile/timeline 1.0 -> 1.1 (an event's `at` ->
    `occurredAt`; an event stored as `at` still reads). The retired
    persona/facet/{put,list,delete}/1.0 aliases are no longer routed: use
    persona/world/*.
  - The VTA's outbound did-management vocabulary: did/list 0.1 -> 0.2, which the
    hosting service already serves (`cursor`/`nextCursor` in place of
    `offset`/`total`; the reconcile reads until no cursor is offered),
    server/register and registry/admin-register 0.1 -> 0.2, and the retired
    did/{publish,enable,disable} and domain/disable replaced by did/set-state and
    domain/set-state.

- **external**: Serve and send only the current external/* versions ([#2311](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2311))

trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and withdraws each about 90 days later. Every current `external/*` version is already in 0.35, so the VTA serves it now and stops serving the old one, and every client in the workspace sends it.

  Served now (the old versions are refused `unsupportedVersion`/`unsupportedType`):

  - `external/accounts/{list,get,create,update,bindings/grant,bindings/revoke,probe,keys/rotate,suspend,resume,archive,restore}` 0.2 (from 0.1). `secret/set`, `setup` and `delete` stay at 0.1, their current version.
  - `external/credentials/issue` 0.3 only (0.1 and 0.2 are no longer served).

  On the wire:

  - An account's `lastProbe` (`AccountProbeReport`, `external/_shared/0.2`) names when the probe ran `probedAt`, not `at`. A report stored by an earlier VTA is answered under the new name; nothing is rewritten.
  - Issuance is 0.3's: a `scope` for every brokered model but `s3-static-presign`, which takes a `presign` batch of at most 64 operations (a 65th is `malformedRequest`); a batch whose sealed answer would not fit is `responseTooLarge` and costs none of the binding's rate. 0.1's single, unbound presigned request is gone with it.

  Clients move with it:

  - `vta-sdk`: `TASK_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNTS_*_0_1` become `_0_2`; `TASK_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIALS_ISSUE_0_1`/`_0_2` are removed. `VtaClient::external_credentials_issue` sends 0.3 (it took the 0.1 payload); `external_credentials_issue_v2`/`_v3` are removed, and `external_credentials_issue_presign` no longer falls back to 0.2.
  - `vta-external`: `batch::PresignBatch`/`PresignRequest` are 0.3's types and `MAX_OPERATIONS` is 64; `MAX_OPERATIONS_0_3` is removed.
  - `pnm external issue` drops `--object-key` (0.3's `scope` takes none; an `s3-static-presign` account is asked with `--presign`).
  - The VTC (`auth: vta-account` storage) asks its VTA only at 0.3: the account check is a one-`get` batch on the canary, reads and deletes are batches of one, and a write the VTC makes itself is presigned as a `put` bound to its length and SHA-256 (`PresignedBlobs::put` hashes the staged file whenever its presigner `presigns_ops`). It no longer falls back to 0.2 for a VTA without 0.3.

- **rooms**: Serve and send only the current rooms tasks, keeping what pnm-browser-plugin sends ([#2315](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2315))

The rest of the `rooms` family, and `vtc/rooms/offers/list`, move off their superseded versions (part of the migration off the versions trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates, trust-tasks-tf #921). Every sender in this workspace goes at the current version with no fallback. The versions `pnm-browser-plugin` still sends stay served (below).

### Build & CI

- **deps**: Compile only the trust-tasks-rs spec families each crate uses ([#2326](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2326))

The workspace `trust-tasks-rs` entry enabled `all-specs`, so every crate that
  depends on it, and every consumer of a published VTI crate, compiled all 34
  generated spec families (~70 MB of Rust, 14 GB peak rustc RSS). The workspace
  entry now enables `validate` only, and each crate lists the families it names:
  a `trust_tasks_rs::specs::<family>` path, or a Type URI it sends, serves or
  looks up in `schema_index`.

  sync, vrc, webvh) appear nowhere in VTI: no path, no Type URI, no handler. A
  received document of one of those types was already refused as unsupported;
  it is now dispatched to that refusal without a schema check first.

  What shrinks: `vti-rooms-wasm` compiles `rooms` alone (trust-tasks-rs dev
  build 14.2 GB / 174 s -> 1.5 GB / 7 s). Everything that depends on vta-sdk
  still needs 23-29 families, so the workspace, service and mobile builds are
  roughly unchanged (mobile `check` 12.9 -> 11.1 GB); the swap safety nets stay.

title: chore(deps)!: take vta-sdk 0.74, affinidi-tdk 0.33, messaging-sdk 0.41, trust-tasks 0.35 and trql-client 0.29; release 0.26.0
body:
Moves VGI onto the VTI #2300 line so openvtc (OpenVTC/openvtc#512) keeps a single `vta-sdk`: `vta-sdk` 0.74, `affinidi-tdk` 0.33, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.41, `trust-tasks-rs`/`-proof` 0.35, `trql-client` 0.29, and test mediator 0.46. The workspace and its internal pins go to **0.26.0**, as do `bridge.example.toml` and the tag `v0.26.0`.

## ⚠️ Draft: waiting on trql-client 0.29

`trql-client` 0.29 comes from affinidi/affinidi-trust-registry-rs#172 and the registry release after it, and isn't on crates.io yet. **`Cargo.lock` isn't updated in this commit**, because it can't resolve until then. Once 0.29 is published I'll run `cargo update`, commit the lockfile, and mark this ready.

## Changes

- **Registry test fakes answer `registry/authorization/0.2`.** trql-client 0.29 asks at 0.2 (lowerCamelCase: `entityId`, `authorityId`, `evaluatedAt`) first and falls back to 0.1 only on `unsupportedVersion`. The fakes in verify-trust and vgi-bridge answered 0.1 snake_case, which 0.29 refuses as a contract violation. That caused 4 verify-trust test failures before this change.
- **`#[allow(deprecated)]` for trust-tasks-rs 0.35's prebuilt spec modules.** vgi-bridge allows it at crate level, plus three test files. Its `git-ns/bridge/{job,result,event}` types come from those modules. In did-git-sign it covers `print_session_health`, because vta-sdk's `health/details` answer comes from them too. The real fix is generating those types with `trust-tasks-build`, as openvtc now does. That's a follow-up; this PR is a dependency move.

## Checks

These were run against the registry branch, patched in through an untracked `.cargo/config.toml`:

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`: 842 pass, 0 fail.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- `cargo tree` has one copy each of `vta-sdk`, `trust-tasks-rs`, `affinidi-tdk` and `affinidi-messaging-sdk`.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no client change
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): registry queries go out as 0.2 via trql-client 0.29; fakes updated
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: `allow(deprecated)` above, until generated specs

title: vta-vault-v0.26.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Serve only the current vault/* and device/* versions ([#2309](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2309))

The VTA, its SDK, CLI and MCP bridge move off the superseded vault and device
  Trust Task versions, and the VTA stops serving the old ones:

  - vault/list 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> 0.4: request `pageSize` -> `limit`, response
    `truncated`/`cursor` -> `nextCursor`. The VTA now pages for real (keyset on
    entry id, the cursor bound to the filters it was minted for) and answers a
    foreign cursor `vault/list:cursorInvalid`, since 0.4 requires a `nextCursor`
    whenever more entries match.
  - vault/get 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3, vault/upsert 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> 0.4 (`created` ->
    `wasCreated`), vault/release, proxy-login and sign-trust-task 0.1 -> 0.2.
  - vault/credentials/get 0.1 (retired) -> 0.2, which carries the body as stored
    in the member its format calls for: `credential` for a Data Integrity
    credential, `credentialBase64` for an SD-JWT or an mdoc (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf
    #919). 0.1 could only answer with a JSON object, so every SD-JWT VC in the
    vault failed to fetch.
  - device/register, wipe, set-wake 0.1 -> 0.2, device/list 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3
    (`limit`/`nextCursor`, keyset paging), device/heartbeat 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3
    (`serverTime` -> `respondedAt`). The device handlers parse the generated
    payloads and emit camelCase enum values themselves.

  The `wire_v0_2` edge transform no longer retypes a request to a 0.1 URI and
  dispatches it through a 0.1 handler: the dispatch table registers the served
  version, and the transform only rewrites the vault enum values between the
  wire's camelCase and the storage types' kebab-case. The JWE-sealing handlers
  always seal camelCase cleartext, so the task-local wire version is gone. The
  vault and device rows leave `deprecation::SUPERSEDED_TASKS`.

  `vault/_shared/0.3`'s `VaultEntry` no longer declares the archival-lifecycle
  members `vault/_shared/0.1` carried (`status`, `archivedAt`, `deletedAt`,
  `graceUntil`) and is `additionalProperties: false`, so an archived or deleted
  entry now carries them in `ext["org.openvtc.vault-lifecycle"]` (SPEC §4.5.1);
  an active entry carries none, as before. Restoring them to the shared
  component is a registry change.

title: vta-policy-v0.23.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Speak AclEntry 0.2 — acl/*/0.2 and acl/list/0.3 ([#2324](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2324))

The VTA moves its ACL surface to AclEntry 0.2 (`acl/_shared/0.2`), where every
  authority axis is explicit, and stops serving acl/{grant,show,update,
  change-role,revoke}/0.1 and acl/list/0.1. `operations::acl_v0_2` maps each
  0.2 value onto the stored (role, contexts) model and refuses the ones the
  store cannot hold (`act: all` on a non-admin, `act: none` on admin →
  invalidActScope) rather than approximating them. change-role carries the act
  scope across unchanged; update never narrows act (revoke {kind: act} does);
  list/0.3 pages with signed, filter-bound cursors and honours role,
  subjectPrefix and capability. RETIRED_TASK_TYPES moves approval rules naming
  the 0.1 URIs to their successors at boot.

- **policy**: A requireConsent decision states its quorum and requester exclusion (policy/_shared 0.4) ([#2322](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2322))

trust-tasks-rs 0.36 publishes policy/_shared/0.4 and policy/evaluate/0.4,
  which make requireConsent.minApprovals and excludeRequester REQUIRED with no
  default (SPEC §6.6 rule 5: a shared component supplies no governance
  default). Under 0.3 a decision omitting either meant a quorum of one, or a
  requester allowed to approve itself, with nothing on the wire to show it.

  vta-policy's mirror of the schema moves to 0.4: RequireConsent no longer
  defaults either member, so a policy whose decision omits one no longer
  deserialises and the PDP fails closed (deny), as for any other malformed
  decision. The declarative approvals generator (vta-sdk::approvals) and the
  VTC already emit both members; hand-written operator policies that omit
  them must add them.

  policy/evaluate is still not served (its PolicyInput.site remains required
  in 0.4), so there is no wire version to move.

- **auth**: Serve only the current auth, audit/list, policy, task-consent and discovery versions ([#2313](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2313))

The VTA, the VTC and every client in the workspace move off superseded Trust
  Task versions of these families, and the services stop serving the old ones:

  - auth/authenticate 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (proxied-login members; a `principal` that
    is not the signer is refused `delegationNotRecognized`), auth/refresh 0.1 ->
    0.2, auth/revoke-session -> 0.2, auth/signing-key/enroll 0.1 -> 0.2.
  - auth/step-up/approve-response 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> 0.6 on the VTA (one typed
    handler; vta-mobile-core builds 0.6, a bound approval may carry no
    `sessionId`).
  - auth/oob/{request,redeem,claim} 0.1 -> 0.2, grant 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3, respond
    0.1 -> 0.3 (`claimClosesAt`, `decisionClosesAt`, `sessionEndsAt` as RFC 3339
    instants rather than epoch seconds), on the VTC and the member portal.
  - audit/list 0.1 -> 0.2 and policy/list 0.2 -> 0.3 (`limit`/`nextCursor`),
    policy/upsert 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (`created` -> `wasCreated`), on both services
    and their clients.
  - task-consent/decision 0.1 -> 0.2, trust-task-discovery 0.1 -> 0.3.

  An approval rule names its task by exact versioned Type URI, so a stored rule
  naming a version the VTA no longer serves would never match again and the task
  it gated would run ungated. `vta_policy::approvals::RETIRED_TASK_TYPES` maps
  each retired version to its successor; boot moves stored rules onto it, and the
  policy write path refuses a new rule naming a retired type.

  Deliberately not moved, because a peer outside this workspace pins them:

  - auth/step-up/approve-request stays at 0.2 on the VTA: the fielded approvers
    (vta-mobile-agent-ios, which routes by a hard-coded 0.1/0.2 type list, and the
    browser plugin) accept only 0.1 and 0.2.
  - the VTC still serves auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4 beside 0.6, for the
    console's unsigned session-passkey answer, which 0.5 onward forbids.

title: vta-persona-v0.28.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Serve only the current keys/list, consent/list, persona and did-management versions ([#2318](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2318))

The VTA and its clients move off these superseded versions, and the VTA stops
  serving the old ones:

  - keys/list 0.1 -> 0.2: paging moves from `offset`/`total` to `cursor` +
    `limit` -> `nextCursor`. The VTA pages by key id under a cursor bound to the
    filters it was minted for, and refuses one it did not issue. The did-secrets
    bundle export, `fetch_context_secrets` and pnm's mediator console follow the
    cursor; `pnm`/`cnm keys list` take `--cursor` in place of `--offset` and print
    the next one.
  - consent/list 1.0 -> 1.1 (`since` -> `syncToken`, `cursor` ->
    `nextSyncToken`; the VTA offers neither yet, so only the version moves).
  - persona/correlation/analyze 1.0 (retired) and 1.1 -> 1.2 (a finding's `why`
    -> `reason`), persona/profile/timeline 1.0 -> 1.1 (an event's `at` ->
    `occurredAt`; an event stored as `at` still reads). The retired
    persona/facet/{put,list,delete}/1.0 aliases are no longer routed: use
    persona/world/*.
  - The VTA's outbound did-management vocabulary: did/list 0.1 -> 0.2, which the
    hosting service already serves (`cursor`/`nextCursor` in place of
    `offset`/`total`; the reconcile reads until no cursor is offered),
    server/register and registry/admin-register 0.1 -> 0.2, and the retired
    did/{publish,enable,disable} and domain/disable replaced by did/set-state and
    domain/set-state.



### Build & CI

- **deps**: Compile only the trust-tasks-rs spec families each crate uses ([#2326](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2326))

The workspace `trust-tasks-rs` entry enabled `all-specs`, so every crate that
  depends on it, and every consumer of a published VTI crate, compiled all 34
  generated spec families (~70 MB of Rust, 14 GB peak rustc RSS). The workspace
  entry now enables `validate` only, and each crate lists the families it names:
  a `trust_tasks_rs::specs::<family>` path, or a Type URI it sends, serves or
  looks up in `schema_index`.

  The workspace union is 29 families. The five dropped (chat, process-attestation,
  sync, vrc, webvh) appear nowhere in VTI: no path, no Type URI, no handler. A
  received document of one of those types was already refused as unsupported;
  it is now dispatched to that refusal without a schema check first.

  What shrinks: `vti-rooms-wasm` compiles `rooms` alone (trust-tasks-rs dev
  build 14.2 GB / 174 s -> 1.5 GB / 7 s). Everything that depends on vta-sdk
  still needs 23-29 families, so the workspace, service and mobile builds are
  roughly unchanged (mobile `check` 12.9 -> 11.1 GB); the swap safety nets stay.



### Chore

- **deps**: Trust-tasks-rs 0.36, affinidi-tdk 0.36, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.44, mediator 0.48 ([#2319](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2319))

One trust-tasks-rs in the graph again, at 0.36.1 — the first release
  carrying vta/contexts/delete/1.1 (trust-tasks-tf #967). TDK moved in
  lockstep (affinidi-tdk-rs #978: affinidi-tdk 0.36, affinidi-messaging-sdk
  0.44) and so did the mediator (affinidi-messaging-mediator #46, released as
  0.48.0: test-mediator, mediator-admin, mediator-tui).

  trust-tasks-rs 0.36 emits trust-task-error/0.6, which adds the
  unsupportedExtension and indeterminate standard codes (framework 0.7,
  SPEC §8.3). Both services' framework_error_type_uri() move to 0.6 so an
  unrouted refusal speaks the same version as a routed one — the drift
  unrouted_and_routed_errors_agree_on_the_type_uri exists to catch — and the
  fixtures standing in for this workspace's own refusals follow, keeping
  one error version in vtc-service's binding census. Fixtures for foreign
  peers (a DID host) keep 0.5: a consumer still accepts it (SPEC §5.2).
  vta-sdk and the admin console recognise any trust-task-error/ version.

  0.36 also marks every prebuilt spec module deprecated in favour of
  trust-tasks-build. The workspace already allows `deprecated`;
  vta-external, vti-vetting-pcs and vta-persona did not inherit the
  workspace lints, and now do.

title: vta-external-v0.11.0
body:
### Added

- **external**: Serve and send only the current external/* versions ([#2311](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2311))

trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and withdraws each about 90 days later. Every current `external/*` version is already in 0.35, so the VTA serves it now and stops serving the old one, and every client in the workspace sends it.

  Served now (the old versions are refused `unsupportedVersion`/`unsupportedType`):

  - `external/accounts/{list,get,create,update,bindings/grant,bindings/revoke,probe,keys/rotate,suspend,resume,archive,restore}` 0.2 (from 0.1). `secret/set`, `setup` and `delete` stay at 0.1, their current version.
  - `external/credentials/issue` 0.3 only (0.1 and 0.2 are no longer served).

  On the wire:

  - An account's `lastProbe` (`AccountProbeReport`, `external/_shared/0.2`) names when the probe ran `probedAt`, not `at`. A report stored by an earlier VTA is answered under the new name; nothing is rewritten.
  - Issuance is 0.3's: a `scope` for every brokered model but `s3-static-presign`, which takes a `presign` batch of at most 64 operations (a 65th is `malformedRequest`); a batch whose sealed answer would not fit is `responseTooLarge` and costs none of the binding's rate. 0.1's single, unbound presigned request is gone with it.

  Clients move with it:

  - `vta-sdk`: `TASK_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNTS_*_0_1` become `_0_2`; `TASK_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIALS_ISSUE_0_1`/`_0_2` are removed. `VtaClient::external_credentials_issue` sends 0.3 (it took the 0.1 payload); `external_credentials_issue_v2`/`_v3` are removed, and `external_credentials_issue_presign` no longer falls back to 0.2.
  - `vta-external`: `batch::PresignBatch`/`PresignRequest` are 0.3's types and `MAX_OPERATIONS` is 64; `MAX_OPERATIONS_0_3` is removed.
  - `pnm external issue` drops `--object-key` (0.3's `scope` takes none; an `s3-static-presign` account is asked with `--presign`).
  - The VTC (`auth: vta-account` storage) asks its VTA only at 0.3: the account check is a one-`get` batch on the canary, reads and deletes are batches of one, and a write the VTC makes itself is presigned as a `put` bound to its length and SHA-256 (`PresignedBlobs::put` hashes the staged file whenever its presigner `presigns_ops`). It no longer falls back to 0.2 for a VTA without 0.3.

body:
### Added

- **vta**: Serve only the current vta/* and messaging/ping versions ([#2316](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2316))

  stops serving the old ones:

  - vta/did-templates/{list,create,get,update} 2.0/3.0 -> 3.1: the record's
    `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are RFC 3339 instants (`vta/_shared/0.7`). A record
    stored with integer seconds still reads.
  - vta/app-state/{put,put-many} 1.0 -> 1.1 (`created` -> `wasCreated`),
    vta/app-state/list 1.0 -> 1.1 (`limit`/`nextCursor`).
  - vta/attestation/mnemonic-export 1.0 -> 1.1, mnemonic-status 0.1 -> 0.2
    (`windowRemainingSecs` -> `windowRemainingSeconds`).
  - vta/credentials/list 0.1 -> 0.2 (`limit`/`nextCursor`).
  - vta/passkey-vms/enroll-submit 0.1 -> 0.2 (`clientDataJSON`; the REST twin
    still reads `clientDataJson`).
  - vta/services/{list,get,enable,disable,drain/list} 1.0 -> 1.1,
    {update,rollback} 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2, report 0.1 -> 0.2 (`drainTtlSeconds`,
    `handshakeTimeoutSeconds`, `drainEndsAt`, `firstSeenAt`/`lastSeenAt`).
  - vta/backup/{initiate-export,initiate-import,finalize-import} 1.0 -> 1.1,
    vta/contexts/update-did 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/webvh/dids/create 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2,
    vta/webvh/agent-name/list 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/witness/list 0.1 -> 0.2.
  - messaging/ping 0.1 -> 0.2 (`serverTime` -> `respondedAt`).

    {update,rollback} 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2, report 0.1 -> 0.2 (`drainTtlSeconds`,
    `handshakeTimeoutSeconds`, `drainEndsAt`, `firstSeenAt`/`lastSeenAt`).

    vta/contexts/update-did 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/webvh/dids/create 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2,
    vta/webvh/agent-name/list 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/witness/list 0.1 -> 0.2.
  - messaging/ping 0.1 -> 0.2 (`serverTime` -> `respondedAt`).

- **auth**: Serve only the current auth, audit/list, policy, task-consent and discovery versions ([#2313](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2313))

The VTA, the VTC and every client in the workspace move off superseded Trust
  Task versions of these families, and the services stop serving the old ones:

  - auth/authenticate 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (proxied-login members; a `principal` that
    is not the signer is refused `delegationNotRecognized`), auth/refresh 0.1 ->
    0.2, auth/revoke-session -> 0.2, auth/signing-key/enroll 0.1 -> 0.2.
  - auth/step-up/approve-response 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> 0.6 on the VTA (one typed
    handler; vta-mobile-core builds 0.6, a bound approval may carry no
    `sessionId`).
  - auth/oob/{request,redeem,claim} 0.1 -> 0.2, grant 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3, respond
    0.1 -> 0.3 (`claimClosesAt`, `decisionClosesAt`, `sessionEndsAt` as RFC 3339
    instants rather than epoch seconds), on the VTC and the member portal.
  - audit/list 0.1 -> 0.2 and policy/list 0.2 -> 0.3 (`limit`/`nextCursor`),
    policy/upsert 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (`created` -> `wasCreated`), on both services

  naming a version the VTA no longer serves would never match again and the task
  it gated would run ungated. `vta_policy::approvals::RETIRED_TASK_TYPES` maps
  each retired version to its successor; boot moves stored rules onto it, and the
  policy write path refuses a new rule naming a retired type.

    (vta-mobile-agent-ios, which routes by a hard-coded 0.1/0.2 type list, and the

    console's unsigned session-passkey answer, which 0.5 onward forbids.

  serving the old ones:

    `limit` -> `nextCursor`. The VTA pages by key id under a cursor bound to the

    cursor; `pnm`/`cnm keys list` take `--cursor` in place of `--offset` and print
    the next one.

    `nextSyncToken`; the VTA offers neither yet, so only the version moves).
  - persona/correlation/analyze 1.0 (retired) and 1.1 -> 1.2 (a finding's `why`
    -> `reason`), persona/profile/timeline 1.0 -> 1.1 (an event's `at` ->

    hosting service already serves (`cursor`/`nextCursor` in place of
    `offset`/`total`; the reconcile reads until no cursor is offered),
    server/register and registry/admin-register 0.1 -> 0.2, and the retired
    did/{publish,enable,disable} and domain/disable replaced by did/set-state and
    domain/set-state.

trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and withdraws each about 90 days later. Every current `external/*` version is already in 0.35, so the VTA serves it now and stops serving the old one, and every client in the workspace sends it.

  Served now (the old versions are refused `unsupportedVersion`/`unsupportedType`):

  - `external/accounts/{list,get,create,update,bindings/grant,bindings/revoke,probe,keys/rotate,suspend,resume,archive,restore}` 0.2 (from 0.1). `secret/set`, `setup` and `delete` stay at 0.1, their current version.
  - `external/credentials/issue` 0.3 only (0.1 and 0.2 are no longer served).

  On the wire:

  - An account's `lastProbe` (`AccountProbeReport`, `external/_shared/0.2`) names when the probe ran `probedAt`, not `at`. A report stored by an earlier VTA is answered under the new name; nothing is rewritten.
  - Issuance is 0.3's: a `scope` for every brokered model but `s3-static-presign`, which takes a `presign` batch of at most 64 operations (a 65th is `malformedRequest`); a batch whose sealed answer would not fit is `responseTooLarge` and costs none of the binding's rate. 0.1's single, unbound presigned request is gone with it.

  Clients move with it:

  - `vta-sdk`: `TASK_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNTS_*_0_1` become `_0_2`; `TASK_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIALS_ISSUE_0_1`/`_0_2` are removed. `VtaClient::external_credentials_issue` sends 0.3 (it took the 0.1 payload); `external_credentials_issue_v2`/`_v3` are removed, and `external_credentials_issue_presign` no longer falls back to 0.2.
  - `vta-external`: `batch::PresignBatch`/`PresignRequest` are 0.3's types and `MAX_OPERATIONS` is 64; `MAX_OPERATIONS_0_3` is removed.
  - `pnm external issue` drops `--object-key` (0.3's `scope` takes none; an `s3-static-presign` account is asked with `--presign`).
  - The VTC (`auth: vta-account` storage) asks its VTA only at 0.3: the account check is a one-`get` batch on the canary, reads and deletes are batches of one, and a write the VTC makes itself is presigned as a `put` bound to its length and SHA-256 (`PresignedBlobs::put` hashes the staged file whenever its presigner `presigns_ops`). It no longer falls back to 0.2 for a VTA without 0.3.

- **rooms**: Serve and send only the current rooms tasks, keeping what pnm-browser-plugin sends ([#2315](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2315))

The rest of the `rooms` family, and `vtc/rooms/offers/list`, move off their superseded versions (part of the migration off the versions trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates, trust-tasks-tf #921). Every sender in this workspace goes at the current version with no fallback. The versions `pnm-browser-plugin` still sends stay served (below).
