title: ci(release): run the API check once and skip crates already raised to breaking
body:
A release took 4–5 h from the last merge to crates.io, nearly all of it cold cargo-semver-checks builds, made twice.

| Stage | Before | After (expected) |
|---|---|---|
| `Release-plz PR` (every merge to main) | 40–135 min, 2h13m today, restarted by each merge | ~2 min (release-plz with no crate to check always took that) |
| `release bump is large enough` (Release PR) | 2h13m on #2299 | minutes when the PR proposes breaking versions. Against the current Release PR (`release-plz-2026-10-28T00-06-59Z`) every one of the 12 checked crates is already breaking, so it checks none. Hours remain only when crates are proposed as patches, and a re-run on the same PR restores the baselines' rustdoc |
| `Release-plz release` | 86 min | lower, unmeasured until the next release: verify builds have no debuginfo or incremental state |

**Changes**
- `release-plz.toml`: `semver_check = false` workspace-wide. Bumps now come from conventional commits. The per-crate entries are gone, and `EXCLUDED` in `semver-report.sh` is the one list of what the API check covers.
- `publish.yml` `release-plz-pr`: removes the cargo-semver-checks install, the swap step, the flock gate and its log, plus `libtss2-dev`. All of them existed only for that check. Timeout is 30 min, down from 300. `fix-release-bump-sizes.py` needs none of them, because it runs no build.
- `semver-report.sh`: in enforce mode, a crate is skipped when its proposed version is already a breaking bump over its newest crates.io version. Below 1.0 that is the minor field, at 1.0 and above the major. The output lists each skipped crate with both versions, and the coverage assertion expects only the rest. On an under-bump it prints `<crate>: proposed X is too small — … needs Y or later` and the one-step fix (`fix-release-bump-sizes.py --raise …`), and writes `semver-raise.txt`. Report mode is unchanged.
- `ci.yml` guard: stays blocking. It caches `target/semver-checks/cache`, the baselines' rustdoc JSON, on the PR ref, keyed by rustc and by the names of the entries. On a breaking finding it applies `fix-release-bump-sizes.py --raise` and pushes the result with `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`. The push happens only if the branch is still at the commit that was checked and the PR is not from a fork. The token goes to git, never to the script.
- `publish.yml` `release-plz-release`: sets `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`. `cargo publish` verification is unchanged.

**No compiled build cache** for the guard or the release job. The repository's 25 GB cache allowance already holds 25.7 GB of main's CI caches. A multi-GB cache would evict them, and a cold `Test (workspace)` is ~28 min against its 30-minute budget. For the guard it would not help anyway: each check builds in a placeholder workspace of its own, resolved without the lockfile.

Docs: RELEASING.md and workspace-engineering-notes.md.

title: feat(vta)!: speak AclEntry 0.2 — acl/*/0.2 and acl/list/0.3
body:
The VTA moves its ACL surface from AclEntry 0.1 to **AclEntry 0.2** (`acl/_shared/0.2`) and stops serving 0.1:

| was | now |
|---|---|
| `acl/grant/0.1` | `acl/grant/0.2` |
| `acl/show/0.1` | `acl/show/0.2` |
| `acl/update/0.1` | `acl/update/0.2` |
| `acl/change-role/0.1` | `acl/change-role/0.2` |
| `acl/revoke/0.1` | `acl/revoke/0.2` |
| `acl/list/0.1` | `acl/list/0.3` |

`acl/swap-key/0.1` is unchanged (it has no later version).

## The explicit access-scope model

0.2 states every authority axis — `act`, `keys`, `capabilities` (REQUIRED), `approve`, `approveCapabilities` (absent = none) — in one of three explicit shapes, and an empty list is never a fourth one. The VTA still stores `(role, allowed_contexts, capabilities, approve_scope, allowed_keys)`, where an empty context list is unrestricted on `admin` and nowhere on any other role. `operations::acl_v0_2` maps each 0.2 value to exactly one stored value, and **refuses** the ones the store cannot hold rather than approximating them:

- `act: all` on a non-admin role, and `act: none` on `admin` → `invalidActScope` (grant item 2).
- `capabilities: none`, a listed scope naming only additive capabilities on a role with a non-empty ceiling, a resource qualifier, and `approveCapabilities: listed` → refused as malformed (the VTA has no form for them).
- `approve` with `approveCapabilities` absent or `none` is stored as approving nothing — both confer nothing (CONVENTIONS §7).

Every entry the VTA returns states every axis; `approve` is stated as `none` rather than omitted, and `delegatedBy` is the granter.

Because role and act scope are independent in 0.2 (§4 rule 3), nothing computes one from the other any more:

- **`acl/change-role/0.2` carries the act scope across unchanged** and refuses a move the store cannot hold with the same act scope. Promoting a `reader` that acts nowhere to `admin` used to make it an unrestricted super-admin (empty list, read through the new role); it is now refused, and the operator states the act scope with `acl/update` / `acl/revoke` first.
- **`acl/update/0.2` never narrows `act`** (`narrowingNotPermitted`); `acl/revoke/0.2 {kind: act}` does (`notNarrowing` unless strictly narrower). `label: null` clears the label, `expiresAt: null` makes the entry permanent (bounded like a grant, VTI-ACL-053), `stepUp.approver: null` clears the approver.
- `acl/grant/0.2` refuses a grant to an existing subject with a different role (grant item 6).
- `acl/show/0.2` answers `entry: null` for an absent entry, or one the caller may not see, instead of `notFound`.
- `acl/list/0.3` pages for real (`limit` default 100, ceiling 500; `nextCursor` signed with a `CursorKey` and bound to the caller and every filter → `acl/list:cursorMismatch`), requires `direction` with `context`/`resource` and refuses it without, and now honours `role`, `subjectPrefix` and `capability` (against the **effective** capability set) — 0.1's `role` / `subjectPrefix` were accepted and silently ignored.

Refusals carry the codes each task declares (`roleNotRecognized`, `invalidActScope`, `unknownCapability`, `capabilityOutsideCeiling`, `additiveWithinCeiling`, `notFound`/`subjectNotPresent`, `narrowingNotPermitted`, `notNarrowing`, `stateMismatch`, `cursorMismatch`). The granter-bound refusals (`delegationExceedsGranter`, `approveWiderThanGranter`, `additiveRequiresUnrestricted`) still answer `permissionDenied` from the shared operations, as they did on 0.1.

Payloads are parsed and answered through the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::acl` types; the SDK adds only the shared `acl/_shared/0.2` components (`vta_sdk::protocols::acl_management::v0_2`) and payload builders, so the generated-wire-types census stays at its baseline.

## SDK and CLI

`VtaClient`'s ACL methods keep their signatures and speak 0.2 / 0.3:

- `CreateAclRequest` serialises an explicit entry (`to_entry_v0_2`): `act` is the contexts if any, else `all` for `admin` and `none` otherwise — the VTA's documented reading of an empty list, now on the wire. "Role plus `persona-holder`" is sent as the role's ceiling enumerated plus the additive grant (0.2 has no other spelling); `vta_sdk::acl::role_capability_ceiling` / `ADDITIVE_CAPABILITIES` carry the tables, pinned equal to `vti-common`'s by a test.
- `update_acl` with new contexts reads the stored entry and splits the change: a widening is an update, a narrowing is `acl/revoke {kind: act}`, and a lateral move widens to the union then narrows, so the subject never holds a context it neither had nor was meant to get.
- `list_acl*` follows `nextCursor` to the last page; `get_acl` maps `entry: null` to `NotFound`.
- `AclEntryResponse` decodes AclEntry 0.2 (and 0.1, for `acl/swap-key/0.1`) and exposes the explicit `act()`.

## Approval rules

`RETIRED_TASK_TYPES` gains the six retired `acl/*` URIs, so a declarative approval rule naming `acl/grant/0.1` (the documented example) is moved to `acl/grant/0.2` at boot rather than silently gating nothing. Docs and help text name 0.2.

## Who else must change

- Anything that sends `acl/*/0.1` to a VTA directly (scripts, other agents, non-Rust clients) must move to 0.2 / `acl/list/0.3` and state every axis. Clients on `vta-sdk` need only upgrade.
- Operators who relied on a role change re-reading an empty context list (e.g. promoting an entry that acts nowhere to `admin` to make it unrestricted) must now grant the act scope explicitly.

BREAKING: the VTA no longer serves `acl/{grant,show,update,change-role,revoke}/0.1` or `acl/list/0.1`; `vta_sdk::trust_tasks` drops their constants for `TASK_ACL_*_0_2` / `TASK_ACL_LIST_0_3`.

title: feat(vtc)!: serve acl/*/0.2 and acl/list/0.3, keeping change-role/0.1 for the community role
body:
The VTC stops serving the superseded `acl/*` versions:

- `acl/{grant,show,update,revoke}/0.1` are gone; `acl/*/0.2` (AclEntry 0.2, every authority axis explicit) is the only form.
- `acl/list/0.2` → `acl/list/0.3`: `pageSize` → `limit`, response `cursor` → `nextCursor` (absent on the last page), `truncated` removed. The cursor stays bound to the filters and direction it was minted under (`acl/list:cursorMismatch`).
- `acl/change-role/0.2` moves the **administrative** role.

**Kept on 0.1: `acl/change-role/0.1`.** It is still the only door onto the **community**-role ceremony (member ↔ admin, role-VAC re-mint, promotion serialisation, the bound step-up and VTI-APV-018/019 consent). `acl/change-role/0.2` moves the administrative role only, and the community role has no 0.2 task of its own, so dropping 0.1 would remove the operation outright. It is served beside 0.2 as `ACL_CHANGE_COMMUNITY_ROLE_TYPE`; the consent gate, the summary templates and the bound step-up now name it explicitly rather than through the 0.2 constant.

Also:

- `vtc-client` and `cnm access` speak 0.2 / 0.3.
- Admin console: the listing is `acl/list/0.3` (`limit` / `nextCursor`), removal is `acl/revoke/0.2` `{kind: entry}`. The 0.1 summary-template pins are removed on both sides (the server dropped the templates; the console had renamed them onto 0.2 keys with 0.1 digests). The shared template vectors are regenerated for 0.2 payloads, and `acl/list/0.3` joins the list-limit census.
- `acl/grant/0.2` never narrows (grant item 6), so it no longer appears as a raiser of `ReduceUnrestricted` in the template census.

Tests ported to the 0.2 wire (`acl_canonical`, `acl_trust_tasks`, `signed_step_up`): grants state every axis (a community role no administrative role implies rides `ext["org.openvtc"].communityRole`), removals send `revocation: {kind: entry}`, listings page by `limit` / `nextCursor`, and an absent subject reads `entry: null`. Assertions whose meaning moved with the spec:

- a grant to an existing subject with another role is `permissionDenied` naming `acl/change-role` (grant item 6), not 422;
- granting past the granter's expiry answers `acl/grant:delegationExceedsGranter` with `axes: ["expiresAt"]` (VTI-ACL-053), not a bare 403;
- the list `role` filter reads the administrative role;
- a same-role re-grant must restate the held entry, since 0.2's grant refuses any narrowing; `vti_ops_050` restates the caller's own authority so the self-edit (VTI-ACL-052) remains the refusal under test.

Deleted: `admin_roles::a_0_1_reader_sees_only_what_0_1_can_express`, which tested the 0.1 rendering of 0.2 entries — there is no 0.1 reader left. The OpenAPI snapshot and `wire.ts` drop the REST-era `AclListResponse`.

Finishes the uncommitted work left in the `migrate-acl` worktree.

BREAKING: a client still sending `acl/{grant,show,update,revoke}/0.1` or `acl/list/0.2` to a VTC is refused as an unknown task. The admin console in this PR is updated; other clients (cnm via `vtc-client`, scripts) must move to 0.2 / 0.3.

- `acl/change-role/0.2` moves the **administrative** role.

**Kept on 0.1: `acl/change-role/0.1`.** It is still the only door onto the **community**-role ceremony (member ↔ admin, role-VAC re-mint, promotion serialisation, the bound step-up and VTI-APV-018/019 consent). `acl/change-role/0.2` moves the administrative role only, and the community role has no 0.2 task of its own, so dropping 0.1 would remove the operation outright. It is served beside 0.2 as `ACL_CHANGE_COMMUNITY_ROLE_TYPE`; the consent gate, the summary templates and the bound step-up now name it explicitly rather than through the 0.2 constant.

Also:

- `vtc-client` and `cnm access` speak 0.2 / 0.3.
- Admin console: the listing is `acl/list/0.3` (`limit` / `nextCursor`), removal is `acl/revoke/0.2` `{kind: entry}`. The 0.1 summary-template pins are removed on both sides (the server dropped the templates; the console had renamed them onto 0.2 keys with 0.1 digests). The shared template vectors are regenerated for 0.2 payloads, and `acl/list/0.3` joins the list-limit census.
- `acl/grant/0.2` never narrows (grant item 6), so it no longer appears as a raiser of `ReduceUnrestricted` in the template census.

Tests ported to the 0.2 wire (`acl_canonical`, `acl_trust_tasks`, `signed_step_up`): grants state every axis (a community role no administrative role implies rides `ext["org.openvtc"].communityRole`), removals send `revocation: {kind: entry}`, listings page by `limit` / `nextCursor`, and an absent subject reads `entry: null`. Assertions whose meaning moved with the spec:

- a grant to an existing subject with another role is `permissionDenied` naming `acl/change-role` (grant item 6), not 422;
- granting past the granter's expiry answers `acl/grant:delegationExceedsGranter` with `axes: ["expiresAt"]` (VTI-ACL-053), not a bare 403;
- the list `role` filter reads the administrative role;
- a same-role re-grant must restate the held entry, since 0.2's grant refuses any narrowing; `vti_ops_050` restates the caller's own authority so the self-edit (VTI-ACL-052) remains the refusal under test.

Deleted: `admin_roles::a_0_1_reader_sees_only_what_0_1_can_express`, which tested the 0.1 rendering of 0.2 entries — there is no 0.1 reader left. The OpenAPI snapshot and `wire.ts` drop the REST-era `AclListResponse`.

Finishes the uncommitted work left in the `migrate-acl` worktree.

BREAKING: a client still sending `acl/{grant,show,update,revoke}/0.1` or `acl/list/0.2` to a VTC is refused as an unknown task. The admin console in this PR is updated; other clients (cnm via `vtc-client`, scripts) must move to 0.2 / 0.3.

title: feat(policy)!: a requireConsent decision states its quorum and requester exclusion (policy/_shared 0.4)
body:
trust-tasks-rs 0.36 publishes `policy/_shared/0.4` and `policy/evaluate/0.4`, which make `requireConsent.minApprovals` and `excludeRequester` **required with no default** (SPEC §6.6 rule 5). Under 0.3 a decision omitting either meant a quorum of one, or a requester allowed to approve itself, with nothing on the wire to show it.

- `vta-policy::types::RequireConsent` (the mirror of `policy/_shared`) moves to 0.4: neither member defaults, so a decision omitting one no longer deserialises and the PDP fails closed (`deny`), like any other malformed decision.
- The declarative approvals generator (`vta-sdk::approvals`) and the VTC already emit both members. Test policies that relied on the defaults now state them.
- `policy/evaluate` is still not served (`PolicyInput.site` remains required in 0.4), so there is no wire version to move.

The dependency moves (trust-tasks-rs 0.36.1, affinidi-tdk 0.36, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.44, mediator 0.48) and `trust-task-error/0.6` already landed in #2319.

**Breaking:** a stored Rego policy returning `requireConsent` without `minApprovals` and `excludeRequester` now denies instead of asking one approver.

## Not in this PR: removing the workspace `deprecated = "allow"`
trust-tasks-rs 0.36 marks every prebuilt `specs::<family>` module `#[deprecated]` (generate with `trust-tasks-build` instead). Without the allow, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` reports ~9,770 prebuilt-module warnings against ~310 superseded-version ones, and one lint cannot tell them apart. Removing it needs the trust-tasks-build migration first.

- `cargo test -p vta-policy`: 41 passed

title: feat(vta)!: finish deleting a context whose DID host is gone (vta/contexts/delete/1.1)
body:
A context deletion got stuck when one of its did:webvh DIDs was hosted
on a server that had gone away. Two causes:

- A DID whose hosting server was no longer registered was a hard
  pre-flight blocker for the whole subtree, and the only way out was the
  offline `vta did-mgmt dids delete --local-only` with the VTA stopped.
- A registered but unreachable host cost a full reply timeout (30s, more
  with TSP recovery) per DID, one after another, before any local work
  — longer than the client's own 30s timeout, so the operator saw a
  failure on every attempt.

Serve vta/contexts/delete/1.1 (trust-tasks-tf #967). Every host copy in
the subtree is removed first, concurrently and within one 20s budget,
before any local record goes (VTI R2.1). A host that answers notFound or
alreadyDeleted has removed it (alreadyDeleted now maps to Gone, not
Conflict). Any copy not confirmed removed — unregistered server, no VTA
DID, refusal, no transport, timeout — refuses with
vta/contexts/delete:hostCleanupFailed listing each DID, its server and
why, and nothing local is deleted, so a retry completes once the host
is back. With abandonHostCopies the deletion completes and reports the
abandoned copies in daemonCleanupErrors.

`pnm`/`cnm contexts delete` send 1.1 and, on hostCleanupFailed, print
the DIDs loudly and ask whether to delete anyway (leaving those logs for
the operator to remove) or wait and retry. `--abandon-host-copies`
answers in advance for scripts; `--yes` does not, because it is a
different decision. Against a VTA that predates 1.1 they fall back to
1.0.

1.0 keeps its contract through the same handler (orphans reported after
the fact, an unregistered host refused) but gains the bounded,
concurrent host settle, so it no longer outlasts its client either. The
offline break-glass path keeps 1.0 semantics.

Breaking: `ContextDidCleanup` gains `host_copies`, and
`cmd_context_delete` gains `abandon_host_copies`.

## Stacked on #2319
This branch includes #2319's commit (`trust-tasks-rs` 0.36.1 is the first release with `vta/contexts/delete/1.1`). It targets `main` so CI runs; merge #2319 first, and this diff shrinks to its own commit.

## Verification (local, on `3e3c65b12` + this commit)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6658 run; the one failure (`payload_ext_census`) is fixed in this commit and re-run green
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3564 passed
- both `--doc` runs: pass
- New wire tests: a gone host refuses 1.1 with `hostCleanupFailed` and deletes nothing; `abandonHostCopies` completes and names the orphan; an unreachable registered host is answered within the 20s budget; `alreadyDeleted` maps to `Gone`.

title: feat(auth)!: serve only the current passkey invite, approver invite, passkey revoke and login versions
body:
Moves the remaining superseded auth tasks to their current versions.

## Wire changes

| Task | Was | Now | What changes on the wire |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth/passkey/enroll/invite` (VTC, `purpose: stepUp`) | 0.2 | **0.3** | `ttl` → `ttlSeconds` |
| `auth/step-up/approver/invite` (VTC) | 0.1 | **0.2** | `ttl` → `ttlSeconds` |
| `auth/passkey/revoke/{start,finish}` for an administrator's own **session** passkeys (VTC) | 0.1 | **0.2** | see below |
| `auth/passkey/login/{start,finish}` (VTA REST) | 0.1 + 0.2 declared | **0.2** only | none: the routes never read `purpose`, the only member 0.1 spelt differently (`step-up` vs `stepUp`) |

The VTC already served `revoke/{start,finish}/0.2` for members' step-up passkeys, and `login/{start,finish}/0.2`.

### revoke 0.2: one Type URI for both purposes

`revoke/start/0.2` now resolves `credentialId` among the subject's session **and** step-up credentials (0.2 step 3); `revoke/finish/0.2` hands the handle back to whichever store started it. For a session credential:

- `lastCredential` is refused at **start**, before a challenge is issued (0.2 step 4), and re-checked at finish under the lock.
- The handle is bound to its producer; another producer's `revocationId` is `revocationNotFound` and is left intact.
- The assertion must carry the UV flag, not only a valid signature.
- The response adds `subject` and `purpose: "session"`.
- Naming another administrator's session passkey as `subject` is `notAuthorized`: a login passkey is revoked only by its owner on this door (the spec leaves who may revoke another subject's credentials to the consumer).

## Breaking

- `vta-sdk`: `TASK_AUTH_PASSKEY_LOGIN_START_0_1` / `TASK_AUTH_PASSKEY_LOGIN_FINISH_0_1` removed.
- VTC: `enroll/invite/0.2`, `approver/invite/0.1`, `revoke/{start,finish}/0.1` are no longer served.

## Other parties

- **Admin console**: updated here (`ttlSeconds`, revoke 0.2 URIs, regenerated `openapi.json` / `wire.ts`).
- **iOS / Android apps, browser plugin**: anything that *sends* `auth/step-up/approver/invite/0.1` or `auth/passkey/enroll/invite/0.2` must move to 0.2 / 0.3 and send `ttlSeconds`; anything revoking an admin's login passkey must use `revoke/*/0.2` and expect `lastCredential` from start. Redeeming an invite (`approver/redeem/*`, `enroll/redeem/*`) is unchanged.
- **Passkey-login clients of the VTA**: no change needed; send `purpose: "stepUp"` if you send one.

Out of scope and unchanged: `auth/step-up/approve-request` stays at 0.2 (the iOS app and the plugin accept only 0.1/0.2), and the VTC keeps `approve-response/0.4` beside 0.6.

title: feat(voting)!: register and show elections at voting/election 0.2, and serve vtc/elections create 0.3, list 0.3, show 0.2
body:
trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and
withdraws each about 90 days later. Every party to an election is in this
workspace, so all of them move to the current versions together, and the old
ones are refused `unsupportedVersion`. Every current version is already in
trust-tasks-rs 0.35.3.

| Task | Was | Now | What changed on the wire |
|---|---|---|---|
| voting/election/register | 0.1 | 0.2 | the manifest (voting/_shared/0.2) names its instants `registrationOpensAt`, `votingOpensAt`, `votingClosesAt` |
| voting/election/show | 0.1 | 0.2 | the same manifest in the answer |
| vtc/elections/create | 0.1 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest; a parked binding election's next step expects `vtc/admin/actions/show/0.3` |
| vtc/elections/list | 0.1 | 0.3 | `next` is `nextCursor` (0.2); items' `votingOpens`/`votingCloses` are `votingOpensAt`/`votingClosesAt` (0.3) |
| vtc/elections/show | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/voter/register | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/voter/read | 0.1 | 0.2 | signs `vtc/elections/list/0.3` or `show/0.2` |
| vta/pcs/vote | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/vote-encrypted | 0.2 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/trustee/enrol | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/trustee/{deal,keys,justify} | 0.2 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/trustee/read | 0.1 | 0.2 | an `election` read signs `voting/election/show/0.2` |

- vti-voting reads the 0.2 manifest throughout (rules, tally, audit, the
  encrypted levels, the voter's checks).
- vti-voting-service (the ballot box) dispatches by version: register and show
  at 0.2, every other voting/* task at 0.1, its current version. A known task
  at another version is refused `unsupportedVersion` naming the one served
  (was `unsupportedType`).
- The VTC sends register 0.2 and serves the elections tasks above. The VTA's
  voter and trustee tasks (`vta/pcs/*`) carry the manifest too, so they move
  in the same change: a 0.2 manifest does not parse in the 0.1 task. `cnm`,
  `pnm`, vta-sdk, vta-mobile-core, vtc-client and the admin console move with
  them.
- Action summaries: a template for `vtc/elections/create/0.3` (pointers
  `/manifest/votingOpensAt` and `/manifest/votingClosesAt`), pinned in the
  build and in the console. The 0.1 template stays so a binding election
  parked under it still renders in the history.

**Elections registered before this build are not carried over.** A manifest's
digest — which every ticket, cast and certification is bound to — is over its
member names, so a 0.1 manifest cannot be re-read as 0.2 without becoming a
different election. Rather than fail as a manifest "missing
registrationOpensAt", every reader refuses it by name with
`vti_voting::rules::require_current_manifest`:

- the ballot box will not start while its journal holds such an election
  (restore fails, as for any journal entry that no longer parses), with
  "election <id> was registered under voting/election/register/0.1 … this
  build reads only the 0.2 manifest and cannot carry it over. Finish or cancel
  it on the previous release, or remove it";
- the VTC's `vtc/elections/show` answers that election with the same message
  and its audit and decryption steps fail it the same way.
  `vtc/elections/list` still lists it.

Finish or cancel open elections before upgrading.

title: feat(voting)!: register and show elections at voting/election 0.2, and serve vtc/elections create 0.3, list 0.3, show 0.2 (#2317)
body:
feat(voting)!: register and show elections at voting/election 0.2, and serve vtc/elections create 0.3, list 0.3, show 0.2 (#2317)

* feat(voting)!: register and show elections at voting/election 0.2, and serve vtc/elections create 0.3, list 0.3, show 0.2

trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and
withdraws each about 90 days later. Every party to an election is in this
workspace, so all of them move to the current versions together, and the old
ones are refused `unsupportedVersion`. Every current version is already in
trust-tasks-rs 0.35.3.

| Task | Was | Now | What changed on the wire |
|---|---|---|---|
| voting/election/register | 0.1 | 0.2 | the manifest (voting/_shared/0.2) names its instants `registrationOpensAt`, `votingOpensAt`, `votingClosesAt` |
| voting/election/show | 0.1 | 0.2 | the same manifest in the answer |
| vtc/elections/create | 0.1 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest; a parked binding election's next step expects `vtc/admin/actions/show/0.3` |
| vtc/elections/list | 0.1 | 0.3 | `next` is `nextCursor` (0.2); items' `votingOpens`/`votingCloses` are `votingOpensAt`/`votingClosesAt` (0.3) |
| vtc/elections/show | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/voter/register | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/voter/read | 0.1 | 0.2 | signs `vtc/elections/list/0.3` or `show/0.2` |
| vta/pcs/vote | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/vote-encrypted | 0.2 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/trustee/enrol | 0.1 | 0.2 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/trustee/{deal,keys,justify} | 0.2 | 0.3 | the 0.2 manifest |
| vta/pcs/trustee/read | 0.1 | 0.2 | an `election` read signs `voting/election/show/0.2` |

- vti-voting reads the 0.2 manifest throughout (rules, tally, audit, the
  encrypted levels, the voter's checks).
- vti-voting-service (the ballot box) dispatches by version: register and show
  at 0.2, every other voting/* task at 0.1, its current version. A known task
  at another version is refused `unsupportedVersion` naming the one served
  (was `unsupportedType`).
- The VTC sends register 0.2 and serves the elections tasks above. The VTA's
  voter and trustee tasks (`vta/pcs/*`) carry the manifest too, so they move
  in the same change: a 0.2 manifest does not parse in the 0.1 task. `cnm`,
  `pnm`, vta-sdk, vta-mobile-core, vtc-client and the admin console move with
  them.
- Action summaries: a template for `vtc/elections/create/0.3` (pointers
  `/manifest/votingOpensAt` and `/manifest/votingClosesAt`), pinned in the
  build and in the console. The 0.1 template stays so a binding election
  parked under it still renders in the history.

**Elections registered before this build are not carried over.** A manifest's
digest — which every ticket, cast and certification is bound to — is over its
member names, so a 0.1 manifest cannot be re-read as 0.2 without becoming a
different election. Rather than fail as a manifest "missing
registrationOpensAt", every reader refuses it by name with
`vti_voting::rules::require_current_manifest`:

- the ballot box will not start while its journal holds such an election
  (restore fails, as for any journal entry that no longer parses), with
  "election <id> was registered under voting/election/register/0.1 … this
  build reads only the 0.2 manifest and cannot carry it over. Finish or cancel
  it on the previous release, or remove it";
- the VTC's `vtc/elections/show` answers that election with the same message
  and its audit and decryption steps fail it the same way.
  `vtc/elections/list` still lists it.

Finish or cancel open elections before upgrading.

* test(voting): the VTC's election tests send each elections task at its served version

body:
The VTA and its clients move off superseded `vta/*` versions, and the VTA
stops serving the old ones:

- vta/did-templates/{list,create,get,update} 2.0/3.0 -> 3.1: the record's
  `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are RFC 3339 instants (`vta/_shared/0.7`). A record
  stored with integer seconds still reads.
- vta/app-state/{put,put-many} 1.0 -> 1.1 (`created` -> `wasCreated`),
  vta/app-state/list 1.0 -> 1.1 (`limit`/`nextCursor`).
- vta/attestation/mnemonic-export 1.0 -> 1.1, mnemonic-status 0.1 -> 0.2
  (`windowRemainingSecs` -> `windowRemainingSeconds`).
- vta/credentials/list 0.1 -> 0.2 (`limit`/`nextCursor`).
- vta/passkey-vms/enroll-submit 0.1 -> 0.2 (`clientDataJSON`; the REST twin
  still reads `clientDataJson`).
- vta/services/{list,get,enable,disable,drain/list} 1.0 -> 1.1,
  {update,rollback} 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2, report 0.1 -> 0.2 (`drainTtlSeconds`,
  `handshakeTimeoutSeconds`, `drainEndsAt`, `firstSeenAt`/`lastSeenAt`).
- vta/backup/{initiate-export,initiate-import,finalize-import} 1.0 -> 1.1,
  vta/contexts/update-did 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/webvh/dids/create 1.0/1.1 -> 1.2,
  vta/webvh/agent-name/list 1.0 -> 1.1, vta/witness/list 0.1 -> 0.2.
- messaging/ping 0.1 -> 0.2 (`serverTime` -> `respondedAt`).

`AgentSession::ensure_enrolled` now sends `device/register/0.2`'s camelCase
`serviceKind` (`aiAgent`); a kebab-case configuration is camel-cased rather
than refused by the VTA's schema.

`deprecation::SUPERSEDED_TASKS` is empty: every version it named is now
retired outright. The machinery stays for the next supersession, and the unit
tests exercise the notice path against a test-only stand-in table.

Not moved here: vta/webvh/dids/update 1.0 -> 2.1 and rotate-keys 1.0 -> 2.0
(2.0 manages key members through the key-role tasks and adds a dryRun preview
and bound approval — a behaviour change of its own), and the vta/pcs voter and
trustee tasks, whose successors carry `voting/_shared/0.2`'s `Manifest` and
move with the voting family.

BREAKING: the VTA no longer serves the superseded versions above.
`vta_sdk::trust_tasks` drops their constants; `AppStatePutResponse`,
`WriteResult`, `AppStateListBody`/`AppStateListResponse`,
`ListCredentialsBody`/`ListCredentialsResponse` and
`MnemonicExportResultBody` follow the renamed wire members.

title: feat(auth)!: serve only the current auth, audit/list, policy, task-consent and discovery versions
body:
The VTA, the VTC and every client in the workspace move off superseded Trust
Task versions of these families, and the services stop serving the old ones:

- auth/authenticate 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (proxied-login members; a `principal` that
  is not the signer is refused `delegationNotRecognized`), auth/refresh 0.1 ->
  0.2, auth/revoke-session -> 0.2, auth/signing-key/enroll 0.1 -> 0.2.
- auth/step-up/approve-response 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> 0.6 on the VTA (one typed
  handler; vta-mobile-core builds 0.6, a bound approval may carry no
  `sessionId`).
- auth/oob/{request,redeem,claim} 0.1 -> 0.2, grant 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3, respond
  0.1 -> 0.3 (`claimClosesAt`, `decisionClosesAt`, `sessionEndsAt` as RFC 3339
  instants rather than epoch seconds), on the VTC and the member portal.
- audit/list 0.1 -> 0.2 and policy/list 0.2 -> 0.3 (`limit`/`nextCursor`),
  policy/upsert 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3 (`created` -> `wasCreated`), on both services
  and their clients.
- task-consent/decision 0.1 -> 0.2, trust-task-discovery 0.1 -> 0.3.

An approval rule names its task by exact versioned Type URI, so a stored rule
naming a version the VTA no longer serves would never match again and the task
it gated would run ungated. `vta_policy::approvals::RETIRED_TASK_TYPES` maps
each retired version to its successor; boot moves stored rules onto it, and the
policy write path refuses a new rule naming a retired type.

Deliberately not moved, because a peer outside this workspace pins them:

- auth/step-up/approve-request stays at 0.2 on the VTA: the fielded approvers
  (vta-mobile-agent-ios, which routes by a hard-coded 0.1/0.2 type list, and the
  browser plugin) accept only 0.1 and 0.2.
- the VTC still serves auth/step-up/approve-response/0.4 beside 0.6, for the
  console's unsigned session-passkey answer, which 0.5 onward forbids.

BREAKING: the VTA and VTC no longer serve the superseded versions above.
`vta_sdk::trust_tasks` drops their constants and adds
`TASK_AUTH_STEP_UP_APPROVE_RESPONSE_0_6`, `TASK_AUDIT_LIST_0_2`,
`TASK_POLICY_LIST_0_3`, `TASK_POLICY_UPSERT_0_3` and
`TASK_TASK_CONSENT_DECISION_0_2`; the SDK, CLI, MCP and mobile-core clients
send the current versions.

title: feat(vta)!: serve only the current keys/list, consent/list, persona and did-management versions
body:
The VTA and its clients move off these superseded versions, and the VTA stops
serving the old ones:

- keys/list 0.1 -> 0.2: paging moves from `offset`/`total` to `cursor` +
  `limit` -> `nextCursor`. The VTA pages by key id under a cursor bound to the
  filters it was minted for, and refuses one it did not issue. The did-secrets
  bundle export, `fetch_context_secrets` and pnm's mediator console follow the
  cursor; `pnm`/`cnm keys list` take `--cursor` in place of `--offset` and print
  the next one.
- consent/list 1.0 -> 1.1 (`since` -> `syncToken`, `cursor` ->
  `nextSyncToken`; the VTA offers neither yet, so only the version moves).
- persona/correlation/analyze 1.0 (retired) and 1.1 -> 1.2 (a finding's `why`
  -> `reason`), persona/profile/timeline 1.0 -> 1.1 (an event's `at` ->
  `occurredAt`; an event stored as `at` still reads). The retired
  persona/facet/{put,list,delete}/1.0 aliases are no longer routed: use
  persona/world/*.
- The VTA's outbound did-management vocabulary: did/list 0.1 -> 0.2, which the
  hosting service already serves (`cursor`/`nextCursor` in place of
  `offset`/`total`; the reconcile reads until no cursor is offered),
  server/register and registry/admin-register 0.1 -> 0.2, and the retired
  did/{publish,enable,disable} and domain/disable replaced by did/set-state and
  domain/set-state.

BREAKING: `VtaClient::list_keys` takes `cursor: Option<&str>` in place of
`offset: u64`, and `ListKeysResultBody` carries `next_cursor` in place of
`total`/`offset`/`limit`; `vta_sdk::trust_tasks` drops the superseded
constants (adds `TASK_KEYS_LIST_0_2`, `TASK_CONSENT_LIST_1_1`,
`TASK_PERSONA_CORRELATION_ANALYZE_1_2`, `TASK_PERSONA_PROFILE_TIMELINE_1_1`,
`TASK_DID_MANAGEMENT_DID_LIST_0_2`, `..._SERVER_REGISTER_0_2`,
`..._REGISTRY_ADMIN_REGISTER_0_2`, `..._DID_SET_STATE_0_1`,
`..._DOMAIN_SET_STATE_0_1`); the `--offset` flag of `keys list` is gone.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.36.1
body:
### Added

- **vta/contexts/delete**: 1.1 — settle host copies first; abandonHostCopies ([#967](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/967))

1.0 removed every local record and reported a host copy it could not
  remove in daemonCleanupErrors after the fact, so the caller learned that
  DIDs were still resolving only once the records — and the keys that
  could remove them — were gone. A DID whose hosting server was no longer
  registered refused the whole deletion, with no way to complete it through
  this task: a context whose host had gone for good could not be deleted.

  1.1 settles every host copy before anything local is removed. A copy
  that cannot be confirmed removed (host down, refusing, unanswered, or no
  longer known to the VTA) refuses with the new
  vta/contexts/delete:hostCleanupFailed — retryable, details pinned by a
  detailsSchema listing each DID, its server and why — and nothing local
  is deleted. A producer shows those DIDs to a human and asks whether to
  wait for the host or retry with the new abandonHostCopies, which
  completes the deletion and reports the abandoned copies in
  daemonCleanupErrors. A host answering that it no longer holds the log has
  removed it, so a retry after a partial settle completes. The consumer
  SHOULD bound the time spent on hosts, in total, to answer within the
  requester's timeout.

  abandonHostCopies is an explicitness flag like force, not a privilege,
  and a producer MUST NOT set it on a first attempt without being told to.
  A 1.1 consumer still accepts 1.0 and answers it as 1.0 specifies.

  Regenerated the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings; 1.0 is now
  marked superseded. The stale-reference fixer moved create/1.0 and
  preview-delete/1.0's links to 1.1.

title: chore: release 11 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.36.0` → `0.36.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.36.0` → `0.36.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.36.0` → `0.36.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.36.0` → `0.36.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.36.0` → `0.36.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.36.0` → `0.36.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.36.0` → `0.36.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.36.0` → `0.36.1` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.28.0` → `0.28.1` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.10.1`) | `0.10.0` → `0.10.1` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.10` → `0.9.11` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —

title: feat(external)!: serve and send only the current external/* versions
body:
trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and withdraws each about 90 days later. Every current `external/*` version is already in 0.35, so the VTA serves it now and stops serving the old one, and every client in the workspace sends it.

Served now (the old versions are refused `unsupportedVersion`/`unsupportedType`):

- `external/accounts/{list,get,create,update,bindings/grant,bindings/revoke,probe,keys/rotate,suspend,resume,archive,restore}` 0.2 (from 0.1). `secret/set`, `setup` and `delete` stay at 0.1, their current version.
- `external/credentials/issue` 0.3 only (0.1 and 0.2 are no longer served).

On the wire:

- An account's `lastProbe` (`AccountProbeReport`, `external/_shared/0.2`) names when the probe ran `probedAt`, not `at`. A report stored by an earlier VTA is answered under the new name; nothing is rewritten.
- Issuance is 0.3's: a `scope` for every brokered model but `s3-static-presign`, which takes a `presign` batch of at most 64 operations (a 65th is `malformedRequest`); a batch whose sealed answer would not fit is `responseTooLarge` and costs none of the binding's rate. 0.1's single, unbound presigned request is gone with it.

Clients move with it:

- `vta-sdk`: `TASK_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNTS_*_0_1` become `_0_2`; `TASK_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIALS_ISSUE_0_1`/`_0_2` are removed. `VtaClient::external_credentials_issue` sends 0.3 (it took the 0.1 payload); `external_credentials_issue_v2`/`_v3` are removed, and `external_credentials_issue_presign` no longer falls back to 0.2.
- `vta-external`: `batch::PresignBatch`/`PresignRequest` are 0.3's types and `MAX_OPERATIONS` is 64; `MAX_OPERATIONS_0_3` is removed.
- `pnm external issue` drops `--object-key` (0.3's `scope` takes none; an `s3-static-presign` account is asked with `--presign`).
- The VTC (`auth: vta-account` storage) asks its VTA only at 0.3: the account check is a one-`get` batch on the canary, reads and deletes are batches of one, and a write the VTC makes itself is presigned as a `put` bound to its length and SHA-256 (`PresignedBlobs::put` hashes the staged file whenever its presigner `presigns_ops`). It no longer falls back to 0.2 for a VTA without 0.3.

Compatibility: a VTC from this release needs a VTA that serves `external/credentials/issue/0.3` — any `vta-service` since 0.61.0 (#2127). A VTC and a VTA older than that is the only mixed deployment that breaks, and the remedy is to upgrade the VTA, which this workspace releases together with the VTC. A client sending `external/accounts/*/0.1` must move to 0.2.

title: feat(vta/contexts/delete): 1.1 — settle host copies first; abandonHostCopies
body:
1.0 removed every local record and reported a host copy it could not
remove in daemonCleanupErrors after the fact, so the caller learned that
DIDs were still resolving only once the records — and the keys that
could remove them — were gone. A DID whose hosting server was no longer
registered refused the whole deletion, with no way to complete it through
this task: a context whose host had gone for good could not be deleted.

1.1 settles every host copy before anything local is removed. A copy
that cannot be confirmed removed (host down, refusing, unanswered, or no
longer known to the VTA) refuses with the new
vta/contexts/delete:hostCleanupFailed — retryable, details pinned by a
detailsSchema listing each DID, its server and why — and nothing local
is deleted. A producer shows those DIDs to a human and asks whether to
wait for the host or retry with the new abandonHostCopies, which
completes the deletion and reports the abandoned copies in
daemonCleanupErrors. A host answering that it no longer holds the log has
removed it, so a retry after a partial settle completes. The consumer
SHOULD bound the time spent on hosts, in total, to answer within the
requester's timeout.

abandonHostCopies is an explicitness flag like force, not a privilege,
and a producer MUST NOT set it on a first attempt without being told to.
A 1.1 consumer still accepts 1.0 and answers it as 1.0 specifies.

Regenerated the Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings; 1.0 is now
marked superseded. The stale-reference fixer moved create/1.0 and
preview-delete/1.0's links to 1.1.

Consumer: verifiable-trust-infrastructure (pnm/cnm `contexts delete` got stuck when a context's DID host was gone; the VTI change that serves 1.1 follows once this is released).

title: feat(git-ns)!: serve and send only the current git-ns/* versions
body:
trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and
withdraws each about 90 days later. Every current git-ns version is already
in 0.35, so the VTC moves to it and stops serving the old ones (refused
`unsupportedVersion`).

Served now, at the current version only:
- git-ns/namespace/bind 0.2 (from 0.1), namespace/reseat 0.4 (from 0.3)
- git-ns/repo/adopt 0.3, repo/archive 0.3, repo/transfer 0.3 (from 0.1),
  repo/create 0.4 (from 0.3)
- git-ns/right/grant 0.4 and right/revoke 0.4 (from 0.3),
  right/break-glass 0.2 and right/ratify 0.2 (from 0.1)
- git-ns/drift/resolve 0.4 (from 0.1 revert-only and 0.3)
- git-ns/roles/reproject 0.2 (from 0.1)
- git-ns/view 0.6 (from 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 and 0.5): one handler for the member's
  view and `scope: administrator`
- the administrator's reads: namespace/list 0.2, repo/list 0.2,
  right/list 0.3, right/issued-by-departed 0.3, bridge/job/list 0.4 (from
  0.1 and 0.2), projection/show 0.3, account/list 0.2, activity/list 0.3
- git-ns/right/break-glass-notice is sent at 0.2 (from 0.1)

On the wire: a record's `breakGlass.at` is `recordedAt`
(git-ns/_shared/0.6), a break-glass notice's `at` is `occurredAt`, an
activity item's `at` is `occurredAt`, and a repository's `lastCheck.at` is
`concludedAt`. Ratifying names `breakGlassAt` as before, read from
`breakGlass.recordedAt`.

Nested repository paths (git-ns/_shared/0.6): a repository resource is
`<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>` with 1 to 21 path segments of up to 255
characters, so `gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli` is one repository of the
namespace `gitlab.com/acme`. A repository contains only itself: a right on
`gitlab.com/acme/platform` is no right on `gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli`.

The bridge's own tasks keep their older versions beside the current ones,
because the released bridge (OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure
`vgi-bridge` v0.25.0) still speaks only them: it sends `git-ns/bridge/event`
0.3 by default (0.1, 0.2 or 0.4 as configured) and `git-ns/bridge/result`
0.1, and takes `git-ns/bridge/job` 0.4 and 0.5. So the VTC now accepts
bridge/event 0.1 to 0.5 and bridge/result 0.1 and 0.2, and sends each job
as the newest bridge/job version the bridge lists in `trust-task-discovery`
— 0.6, else 0.5, else 0.4 — and a job naming a repository only 0.6 can
carry to no bridge without 0.6 (bridge/job 0.6, *Changes from 0.5*). Those
older bridge versions go once a bridge release speaking the current ones is
deployed.

One divergence kept, not introduced here: git-ns/drift/resolve 0.3 and 0.4
read an unreported role map as the default one; this VTC still refuses an
adopt with `git-ns:roleMapUnknown` until the bridge reports its map,
failing closed.

Clients move with it: the admin console (Repos plugin, member portal,
openapi.json and wire.ts regenerated, list-limits.json), `cnm git`, and
vtc-client, whose `git_ns_view` now takes `administrator` and `break_glass`
and replaces `git_ns_view_v2`, `git_ns_view_v4` and `git_ns_view_v5`;
`git_ns_drift_resolve` (0.4) replaces `git_ns_drift_resolve_v3` and the
deprecated 0.1 form, and `GIT_NS_DRIFT_RESOLVE_TYPE` replaces
`GIT_NS_DRIFT_RESOLVE_V3_TYPE`. vta_sdk::openapi's `GitNsView01*` wrappers
are `GitNsView06*`.

title: feat(rooms)!: serve and send only the current rooms tasks, keeping what pnm-browser-plugin sends
body:
The rest of the `rooms` family, and `vtc/rooms/offers/list`, move off their superseded versions (part of the migration off the versions trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates, trust-tasks-tf #921). Every sender in this workspace goes at the current version with no fallback. The versions `pnm-browser-plugin` still sends stay served (below).

## Old → current

| Task | Was served | Now served | What changed on the wire |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rooms/keys/act` (VTA) | 0.1–0.6 | **0.8**, and 0.1 and 0.5 (kept) | 0.8's request and response schemas are 0.6's. Its closed table adds, from 0.7, `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.4`, `rooms/records/put/0.3`, `rooms/records/list/0.3`–`0.5`, `rooms/info/0.2`–`0.3` and `rooms/epoch/chain/0.2`, and from 0.8 `rooms/records/prune/0.1`/`0.2` and `rooms/records/retention/set/0.1` as `admin`, with a presentation. 0.1 and 0.5 keep their own tables and refuse those `typeNotActable`. |
| `rooms/keys/browse` (VTA) | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.3**, and 0.1 (kept) | `lastPrune` passed through from `rooms/records/list/0.5`, its instant named `prunedAt`. |
| `rooms/owner/register` (VTA) | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | Unchanged. The 0.1 refusal of a failed list delivery is gone. |
| `rooms/info` (hosts) | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.3**, and 0.1 (kept) | `lastPrune.at` → `prunedAt` (`rooms/_shared/0.2`). |
| `rooms/records/list` (hosts) | 0.1–0.3 | **0.5**, and 0.1 (kept) | `cursor` → `nextCursor` (0.4); `lastPrune.at` → `prunedAt` (0.5). |
| `rooms/records/prune` (hosts) | 0.1 | **0.2** | `prune.at` → `prunedAt`. |
| `vtc/rooms/offers/list` (VTC) | 0.1–0.3 | **0.4**, and 0.2 (kept) | `renewals[].renews` → `renewsAt`. |

Hosts are `vtc-service` and `room-host` (through `vti-rooms`); the act and browse key holder is `vta-service`.

Senders moved:
- **vta-sdk:** `room_act` and `room_act_community` send `rooms/keys/act/0.8` only and return its types; `room_owner_register` sends 0.2 only. `is_offer_type` / `is_community_type` include `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.4`. `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_{2,3,4,6}`, `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_BROWSE_0_2` and `TASK_ROOMS_OWNER_REGISTER_0_1` are removed; `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_8` and `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_BROWSE_0_3` are added.
- **vtc-client:** `room_info` sends `rooms/info/0.3` (`room_info_v2` and `RoomInfoV2Response` are gone); `prune_records` sends `rooms/records/prune/0.2`; `list_records` sends `rooms/records/list/0.5`.
- **pnm (vta-cli-common):** `rooms list`, `put` and the tier read go through act 0.8 at `records/list/0.5`, `records/put/0.3` and `info/0.3`; `rooms offers list|renew|accept` list at `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.4` only.
- **vti-rooms:** `RecordPrune::to_wire` writes `prunedAt`; `ROOMS_INFO_V3_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_V5_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_PRUNE_V2_TYPE` replace `ROOMS_INFO_V2_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_V3_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_PRUNE_TYPE`; `ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_V2_TYPE`, `record_tasks::list_v3_response` and `blob_tasks::list_v2_response` are gone.

`retry_safety`, `budget`, `ALL_URIS`, the policy gate's subject rule, both services' conformance tables and error-code censuses are updated. Docs are updated, except design-note version histories.

## Kept for a deployed peer

`pnm-browser-plugin` (`@openvtc/pnm-core`, outside this workspace) sends these today, so they stay served until it moves:
- `rooms/keys/act/0.1` and `rooms/keys/act/0.5`
- act-wrapped `rooms/info/0.1`, `rooms/records/list/0.1`, `rooms/records/put/0.1` and `0.2`, `rooms/epoch/chain/0.1`
- `rooms/keys/browse/0.1`
- `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2`

`rooms/owner/register/0.2`, which it also sends, is current.

Also kept: `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1`, the only task that removes a member of a `private` room from its group (the specification problem recorded in #2295).

## Breaking changes

- **API:** the public `vta-sdk`, `vtc-client` and `vti-rooms` surfaces above change.
- **Wire:** a client sending a dropped version gets `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion`. The SDK and `pnm` no longer fall back: an agent or community that does not serve the current version is reported for upgrade.

## Not done here

- `pnm rooms put` still refuses provenance on an `open` room. Act 0.8 now completes `rooms/records/put/0.3`, which `pnm` sends, but it does not yet write the provenance members into the cleartext.
- `pnm-browser-plugin` needs a follow-up there to move to act 0.8, and the versions above can then go.

| `rooms/owner/register` (VTA) | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | Unchanged. The 0.1 refusal of a failed list delivery is gone. |
| `rooms/info` (hosts) | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.3**, and 0.1 (kept) | `lastPrune.at` → `prunedAt` (`rooms/_shared/0.2`). |
| `rooms/records/list` (hosts) | 0.1–0.3 | **0.5**, and 0.1 (kept) | `cursor` → `nextCursor` (0.4); `lastPrune.at` → `prunedAt` (0.5). |
| `rooms/records/prune` (hosts) | 0.1 | **0.2** | `prune.at` → `prunedAt`. |
| `vtc/rooms/offers/list` (VTC) | 0.1–0.3 | **0.4**, and 0.2 (kept) | `renewals[].renews` → `renewsAt`. |

Hosts are `vtc-service` and `room-host` (through `vti-rooms`); the act and browse key holder is `vta-service`.

Senders moved:
- **vta-sdk:** `room_act` and `room_act_community` send `rooms/keys/act/0.8` only and return its types; `room_owner_register` sends 0.2 only. `is_offer_type` / `is_community_type` include `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.4`. `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_{2,3,4,6}`, `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_BROWSE_0_2` and `TASK_ROOMS_OWNER_REGISTER_0_1` are removed; `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_8` and `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_BROWSE_0_3` are added.
- **vtc-client:** `room_info` sends `rooms/info/0.3` (`room_info_v2` and `RoomInfoV2Response` are gone); `prune_records` sends `rooms/records/prune/0.2`; `list_records` sends `rooms/records/list/0.5`.
- **pnm (vta-cli-common):** `rooms list`, `put` and the tier read go through act 0.8 at `records/list/0.5`, `records/put/0.3` and `info/0.3`; `rooms offers list|renew|accept` list at `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.4` only.
- **vti-rooms:** `RecordPrune::to_wire` writes `prunedAt`; `ROOMS_INFO_V3_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_V5_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_PRUNE_V2_TYPE` replace `ROOMS_INFO_V2_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_V3_TYPE`, `ROOMS_RECORDS_PRUNE_TYPE`; `ROOMS_RECORDS_LIST_V2_TYPE`, `record_tasks::list_v3_response` and `blob_tasks::list_v2_response` are gone.

`retry_safety`, `budget`, `ALL_URIS`, the policy gate's subject rule, both services' conformance tables and error-code censuses are updated. Docs are updated, except design-note version histories.

## Kept for a deployed peer

`pnm-browser-plugin` (`@openvtc/pnm-core`, outside this workspace) sends these today, so they stay served until it moves:
- `rooms/keys/act/0.1` and `rooms/keys/act/0.5`
- act-wrapped `rooms/info/0.1`, `rooms/records/list/0.1`, `rooms/records/put/0.1` and `0.2`, `rooms/epoch/chain/0.1`
- `rooms/keys/browse/0.1`
- `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2`

`rooms/owner/register/0.2`, which it also sends, is current.

Also kept: `rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1`, the only task that removes a member of a `private` room from its group (the specification problem recorded in #2295).

## Breaking changes

- **API:** the public `vta-sdk`, `vtc-client` and `vti-rooms` surfaces above change.
- **Wire:** a client sending a dropped version gets `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion`. The SDK and `pnm` no longer fall back: an agent or community that does not serve the current version is reported for upgrade.

## Not done here

- `pnm rooms put` still refuses provenance on an `open` room. Act 0.8 now completes `rooms/records/put/0.3`, which `pnm` sends, but it does not yet write the provenance members into the cleartext.
- `pnm-browser-plugin` needs a follow-up there to move to act 0.8, and the versions above can then go.

title: feat(vtc): ask the trust registry in the current registry/* versions, falling back to 0.1
body:
The VTC already wrote membership records with `registry/record/put/0.3`
and read them with `registry/record/query/0.3`, falling back to 0.1 when a
registry answers `unsupportedVersion`. Every other registry call now does the
same:

| Call | Was sent | Now sent first |
|---|---|---|
| member removal, projection record delete | `registry/record/delete/0.1` | `registry/record/delete/0.2` |
| recognition check | `registry/recognition/0.1` | `registry/recognition/0.2` |
| git-namespace projection write | `registry/record/put/0.1` | `registry/record/put/0.3` |
| projection / operator enumeration | `registry/record/query/0.1` | `registry/record/query/0.3` |
| health probe | `registry/record/query/0.1` | `registry/record/query/0.3` |

The newer versions name the record key lowerCamelCase (`entityId`,
`authorityId`, `recordType`; registry `_shared/0.2`). The projection keeps
its one record shape: records are renamed going out and back coming in, at
the wire.

Kept: the fallback to 0.1. Every released trust registry
(affinidi-trust-registry-rs up to 0.28.0) serves only the 0.1 versions; the
lowerCamelCase versions are on its main branch (#168) for 0.29. Removing the
fallback would break every deployed registry, so it stays until that release
is the floor.

title: feat(vtc)!: serve only the current action list, live channel, storage, website, relationship-lifecycle and step-up notice versions
body:
trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and
withdraws each about 90 days later. The VTC moves to the current version of
each task below and stops serving the old ones, which are now refused
`unsupportedVersion`. Every current version is already in trust-tasks-rs
0.35.3.

| Task | Was served | Now |
|---|---|---|
| vtc/admin/actions/{list,show,cancel,acknowledge} | 0.1, 0.2 | 0.3 |
| vtc/admin/events/subscribe (stream of event) | 0.1–0.4 (event 0.1–0.4) | 0.6 (event 0.5) |
| vtc/operator/offline-write (record type) | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| vtc/storage/configs/{create,update} | 0.1, 0.2 | 0.3 |
| vtc/storage/configs/retire | 0.1 | 0.3 |
| vtc/storage/credentials/set | 0.2 | 0.3 |
| vtc/rooms/storage/assign | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| vtc/rooms/storage/migrate | 0.1, 0.2 | 0.3 |
| vtc/website/files/list | 0.1 | 0.3 |
| vtc/relationships/{suspend,restore} | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| vtc/members/step-up-passkey-notice (sent) | 0.1 | 0.2 |

On the wire:
- An action's approvals name their instant `decidedAt` (was `at`,
  actions/_shared/0.3). A cooling-off is always category `coolingOff` with
  `landsAt` and `cancellableBy`; 0.1's `ext.coolingOff` rendering is gone.
- An operator's offline write is raised under `offline-write/0.2`, its record
  naming the instant `writtenAt`. Items raised before this build are stored
  under 0.1 and shown as 0.2 (`at` read as `writtenAt`), so no stored action
  needs a migration.
- The live channel's request names its resume token `resumeToken` (was
  `since`), and its hints name their instant `observedAt` (was `at`). The
  topic set is 0.4's; there is no per-version topic set any more.
- Every parked storage operation's next step expects
  `vtc/admin/actions/show/0.3`.
- storage/configs/retire 0.3 item 3: a config is refused `migrationsInbound`
  (with `details.migrations`) while a migration of room files onto it is
  queued, running or paused — including one that kept its target after the
  room was reassigned. The check is made again when a parked retirement
  executes, under the storage lock, and a fresh migration's target is
  re-checked under the same lock, so no migration onto a config starts between
  the check and the config leaving `active`. 0.1 had no such refusal.
- website/files/list 0.3: an item's `modifiedAt` is `updatedAt`, and
  `nextCursor` is absent on the last page, never `null`.
- relationships suspend/restore 0.2: a superseded or withdrawn edge's
  `state.at` is `endedAt` (vtc/_shared/0.4/relationship-lifecycle).
- step-up-passkey-notice 0.2: the notice names its instant `occurredAt`.

Action summaries: templates are added for the current storage task versions
(pinned in the build and in the console). The templates for the versions no
longer served stay, so an action recorded under one still renders in the
history. A parked storage operation recorded under a version no longer served
cannot execute after an upgrade; it fails its recheck and must be asked again.

Clients move with it: the admin console (live channel at 0.6 with no
discovery-based version choice, the action list and storage at the current
versions; openapi.json and wire.ts regenerated), vtc-client (`list_actions`,
`show_action`, `cancel_action` at 0.3) and `cnm actions watch` (subscribe
0.6, event 0.5), `cnm storage` (credentials/set 0.3).

Kept: `vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.2`. 0.3 is the DID-founder path and
its own text says "a passkey install keeps using 0.2", so 0.2 is not replaced.

title: chore: release 3 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-proof` | npm | `0.1.5` → `0.1.6` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-tsp` | npm | `0.1.1` → `0.1.2` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks-capability-client` | npm | `0.1.1` → `0.1.2` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vta)!: serve only the current vault/* and device/* versions
body:
The VTA, its SDK, CLI and MCP bridge move off the superseded vault and device
Trust Task versions, and the VTA stops serving the old ones:

- vault/list 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> 0.4: request `pageSize` -> `limit`, response
  `truncated`/`cursor` -> `nextCursor`. The VTA now pages for real (keyset on
  entry id, the cursor bound to the filters it was minted for) and answers a
  foreign cursor `vault/list:cursorInvalid`, since 0.4 requires a `nextCursor`
  whenever more entries match.
- vault/get 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3, vault/upsert 0.1/0.2/0.3 -> 0.4 (`created` ->
  `wasCreated`), vault/release, proxy-login and sign-trust-task 0.1 -> 0.2.
- vault/credentials/get 0.1 (retired) -> 0.2, which carries the body as stored
  in the member its format calls for: `credential` for a Data Integrity
  credential, `credentialBase64` for an SD-JWT or an mdoc (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf
  #919). 0.1 could only answer with a JSON object, so every SD-JWT VC in the
  vault failed to fetch.
- device/register, wipe, set-wake 0.1 -> 0.2, device/list 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3
  (`limit`/`nextCursor`, keyset paging), device/heartbeat 0.1/0.2 -> 0.3
  (`serverTime` -> `respondedAt`). The device handlers parse the generated
  payloads and emit camelCase enum values themselves.

The `wire_v0_2` edge transform no longer retypes a request to a 0.1 URI and
dispatches it through a 0.1 handler: the dispatch table registers the served
version, and the transform only rewrites the vault enum values between the
wire's camelCase and the storage types' kebab-case. The JWE-sealing handlers
always seal camelCase cleartext, so the task-local wire version is gone. The
vault and device rows leave `deprecation::SUPERSEDED_TASKS`.

`vault/_shared/0.3`'s `VaultEntry` no longer declares the archival-lifecycle
members `vault/_shared/0.1` carried (`status`, `archivedAt`, `deletedAt`,
`graceUntil`) and is `additionalProperties: false`, so an archived or deleted
entry now carries them in `ext["org.openvtc.vault-lifecycle"]` (SPEC §4.5.1);
an active entry carries none, as before. Restoring them to the shared
component is a registry change.

BREAKING: the VTA no longer serves the superseded vault/* and device/*
versions. `vta_sdk::trust_tasks` drops their constants (adds
`TASK_VAULT_LIST_0_4`, `TASK_VAULT_UPSERT_0_4`, `TASK_DEVICE_HEARTBEAT_0_3`,
`TASK_DEVICE_LIST_0_3`); `VtaClient::cred_vault_get` returns
`trust_tasks_rs::specs::vault::credentials::get::v0_2::Response`; the vault and
device client methods send the current versions, so callers passing raw JSON
must use camelCase enum values (`webOrigin`, `oauthTokens`, `didcommAuthcrypt`,
`aiAgent`, `cacheAndKeys`).

title: feat(vtc)!: serve only the current vtc/rooms, storage, groups, directory, registry and relationships tasks
body:
trust-tasks-rs 0.35 deprecates every superseded Trust Task version and
withdraws each about 90 days later. Every current version below is already
in 0.34, so the VTC moves to it now and stops serving the old one.

Served now (old versions refused `unsupportedVersion`):
- vtc/directory/entries/list 0.2, vtc/directory/export 0.2,
  vtc/directory/notes/list 0.2 (from 0.1)
- vtc/groups/list, vtc/groups/members/list, vtc/groups/requests/list 0.2
  (from 0.1)
- vtc/registry/records/list 0.2, vtc/registry/sync-jobs/list 0.2,
  vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry 0.2 (from 0.1)
- vtc/relationships/list 0.3 (from 0.2), vtc/relationships/revoke 0.2
  (from 0.1)
- vtc/rooms/community/create 0.4 (from 0.1-0.3), get 0.3 and list 0.3
  (from 0.1-0.2), update 0.3 (from 0.1-0.2), members/remove 0.2 (from 0.1)
- vtc/rooms/get 0.3 (from 0.1-0.2), vtc/rooms/list 0.2 (from 0.1)
- vtc/storage/configs/get and list 0.2 (from 0.1)

On the wire: a paged response's `nextCursor` is absent on the last page,
never null; a hosted room's `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `epochExpiresAt`
are RFC 3339 strings (vtc/_shared/0.3/room-storage); sync-jobs/retry
reports an in-flight job `inFlight` (was `notFailed`). A community room is
always created with its profile written into it, and a removal always
withdraws the member at an open or attributed room's host.

Clients move with it: the admin console (openapi.json and wire.ts
regenerated), vtc-client, and `cnm rooms`, which no longer falls back to
older versions and tells the operator to upgrade a VTC that does not
serve the current one. vta_sdk::openapi drops the superseded wrappers.

title: docs: Explain complete cost and resource comparisons
body:
The guide asks implementers to compare complete profiles, but leaves the CPU boundary, legitimate proof reuse and memory scope implicit. This adds an informative “Comparing complete costs” subsection to the evidence chapter and links it from construction selection, addressing the measurement question in [WG-03](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-spec/blob/main/spec/implementation-guide.md) and [discussion #23, question 3](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-tf/discussions/23).

The guidance distinguishes aggregate CPU from elapsed time, charges required production and verification work, explains the conditional `P + nV < nR` comparison, and makes audience/freshness restrictions on proof reuse explicit. It also covers privacy boundaries, uncertainty, failed observations, process-wide memory scope and qualification under one configuration. It selects no backend, fixed reader count, resource threshold or evidence-state change.

An optional [lab worksheet and arithmetic checker](https://github.com/mitchuski/dtgwg-zkp-mage/pull/4) is proposed separately. Its synthetic tests check accounting and metadata, not measurements or security. It creates no guide dependency or adopted report format.

Validation: Node 22.23.3; `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `npm run render`, `npm run check`, and `git diff --check` passed. A separate focused review found no accounting or proof-reuse issue. Generated output and dependencies are excluded from the commit.

Formal review run 2: record 025's formal block, scope lines that say what the models encode, the rotation-tag check, the evidence revision pinned (#23)

* spec: post-quantum horizon — Security Considerations item 8, WG-18, a quantum horizon on every record, the proving-system PQ split, D3 proposal

Following the 8 September call's point that the credential signature scheme is the non-swappable choice. Security Considerations item 8 reads soundness apart from zero-knowledge and forgery apart from confidentiality: pairing-based soundness and discrete-log unforgeability fall under a cryptographically relevant quantum computer, perfect zero-knowledge and information-theoretic hiding do not, so there is no retroactive loss and every record's exposure is forward-looking forgery (the one confidentiality case is the Tag_DDH pseudonym stream of the PCS route). The issuance pattern with a post-quantum realisation at presentation cost today is the published-commitment branch of X3 — a post-quantum signature over the root or leaf commitment, checked outside the proof, the proof verifying no signature. Where the sibling DTG specifications stand is recorded.

Every construction record gains quantumHorizon { forgery, confidentiality }, rendered under Horizon (schema, renderer, validator). Every proving-system entry states post-quantum soundness and post-quantum zero-knowledge separately. WG-18 (post-quantum issuance contract) opened beside WG-02 with its appendix row and changelog entry; ADR-001's D3 carries a proposed resolution, status unchanged. References added: ETSI TR 119 476-1, NIST IR 8547, FIPS 204 and 205, W3C Quantum-Resistant Cryptosuites, Chiesa–Manohar–Spooner 2019, the 2025–26 proximity-gap results, the DTG VTI and Trust Tasks framework specifications. title: trust-tasks-https-v0.36.0
body:
### Added

- **ts, go**: Trust-task-error/0.6 and the unsupportedExtension and indeterminate standard codes ([#961](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/961))

* feat(ts)!: trust-task-error/0.6 and the unsupportedExtension and indeterminate standard codes

  Framework 0.7.0 added unsupportedExtension to the standard codes, and the
  indeterminate ruling (SPEC §8.3) adds indeterminate: the recipient could
  not decide because something it needed and does not control could not
  be obtained or checked, which is neither a refusal nor a failed
  verification. Both live in the closed code list of the trust-task-error
  payload schema, so they need a new version.

  - specs/trust-task-error/0.6: both codes appended to the enum, and
    extends: "0.5", which the build checks. References to 0.5 across the
    registry therefore stay current, and no other spec changes.
  - All four libraries recognize both codes and emit 0.6:
    trust_task_error_type_uri(), TRUST_TASK_ERROR_TYPE_URI,
    TrustTaskErrorTypeURI and trustTaskErrorTypeUri move together.
    Rust's StandardCode is hand-written (trust-task-error is in
    SKIP_SLUGS) and gains UnsupportedExtension and Indeterminate, with
    indeterminate retryable by default as §8.3 gives it.
  - The HTTPS binding's status table maps unsupportedExtension to 422 and
    indeterminate to 503, in the binding prose, trust-tasks-https and
    trust_tasks_https. The Dart package spells the new codes out so it
    still builds against a core that predates them.

  Breaking for @openvtc/trust-tasks only: StandardCode is a closed union
  there, so an exhaustive switch over it stops compiling. Rust's
  StandardCode is #[non_exhaustive] and Go's and Dart's are open string
  types, so the change is additive for them.

  Part of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#42.

### Specifications

- **policy**: A consent decision carries its quorum and self-approval rule ([#960](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/960))

policy/_shared/0.3 gave requireConsent.minApprovals a default of 1 and
  requireConsent.excludeRequester a default of false. JSON Schema defaults
  are annotations, but generators apply them, so a decision that omitted
  either sent a quorum of one, or let the requester approve itself, with
  nothing on the wire to show that nobody had chosen it. SPEC §6.6 rule 5
  now forbids a governance default in a shared schema component.

  - policy/_shared/0.4: both members required, defaults removed.
    task-consent/request/0.1 already requires both, so the policy decision
    and the consent request now agree.
  - policy/evaluate/0.4: policy/evaluate/0.3 re-pinned to the new
    component, which is its only change; the Security & Privacy section
    gains the four sub-headings a new version must carry.
  - policy/get/0.1 and policy/active/0.1 stay on 0.3: they use only
    PolicyModule, which is unchanged.
  - Stale references in task-consent prose moved to policy/evaluate/0.4.
  - Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart regenerated. 0.1 to 0.3 of
    policy/evaluate are now marked superseded by 0.4.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: ci(ts): the sibling range check holds siblings to the newest published core while the Release PR's is unpublished
body:
check-sibling-core-ranges failed the Release PR (#963) that takes
@openvtc/trust-tasks from 0.27.9 to 0.28.0, asking for the siblings'
floors to be raised to ^0.28.0 first. That cannot be done: the siblings
build and test against the core from npm, so a ^0.28.0 floor breaks
npm ci in every sibling job until 0.28.0 is published, and on main the
same check fails it against the 0.27.9 core in the checkout.

When the core version in the checkout is not on npm, the TypeScript
siblings are now held to the newest published core, and a range that
will not admit the new core is a warning naming the floor to raise once
the release publishes. After it publishes, the check is strict again and
fails every PR until the floors move. If npm cannot be reached it stays
strict. Dart is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Unblocks #963.

npm ci in every sibling job until 0.28.0 is published, and on main the
same check fails it against the 0.27.9 core in the checkout.

When the core version in the checkout is not on npm, the TypeScript
siblings are now held to the newest published core, and a range that
will not admit the new core is a warning naming the floor to raise once
the release publishes. After it publishes, the check is strict again and
fails every PR until the floors move. If npm cannot be reached it stays
strict. Dart is unchanged.

title: Post-quantum horizon: Security Considerations item 8, WG-18, a quantum horizon on every record, the proving-system split
body:
Following the 8 September call's point that the credential signature scheme is the critical, non-swappable choice — a post-quantum proof system does not mask a pre-quantum signature — this revision gives the specification a post-quantum reading it can be held to, without adopting a construction or promoting a state.

**Security Considerations item 8** now reads soundness apart from zero-knowledge and forgery apart from confidentiality. Soundness of pairing-based proof systems and unforgeability of discrete-log signatures and commitments fall under a cryptographically relevant quantum computer; zero-knowledge and hiding are information-theoretic and do not. So there is no retroactive loss, every record's exposure is forward-looking forgery (the one confidentiality case is the Tag_DDH pseudonym stream of the PCS route, records 023/024 option 1), and the credential signature is the layer a software update cannot swap. The issuance pattern with a post-quantum realisation at presentation cost today is the published-commitment branch of X3: a post-quantum signature over the root or leaf commitment, checked outside the proof, the proof verifying no signature — the set-root primitive of cred-tf #40 and the transition ETSI TR 119 476-1 §9.3 describes for salted-hash credentials. Where the sibling specifications stand is recorded: the Trust Tasks framework pins `mldsa44-jcs-2024` / `slhdsa128-jcs-2024`, VTI defines hybrid proof sets (VTI-KEY-103..105), the credential specification names `eddsa-jcs-2022` alone.

**Every construction record** carries a *quantum horizon* under its Horizon — which clauses or options fall to forgery, which lose confidentiality — as a new optional record field (`quantumHorizon { forgery, confidentiality }`; schema, renderer and validator updated). **Every proving-system entry** states post-quantum soundness and post-quantum zero-knowledge separately beside the existing `postQuantum` line: Groth16 falls / holds; Flock and ProveKit's core plausible / plausible, with the Groth16 wrapper named as where ProveKit stops being post-quantum and the 2025–26 proximity-gap results named as the bound a cost row must state; Longfellow plausible at the argument, classical at the statement.

**WG-18 — Discuss before implementation: post-quantum issuance contract**, opened beside WG-02: route (b) — signature over a published commitment, checked outside the proof — as the first profile's default or a reasoned alternative; the post-quantum root suite (ML-DSA-65, or SLH-DSA-128s for long-lived registry roots) as the profile's horizon rather than a V1 blocker; the hybrid overlap rule by reference to VTI; a decision on ADR-001's D3 against hash-based proof sizes. **D3** carries that proposed resolution; its status stays open.

**References added:** ETSI TR 119 476-1, NIST IR 8547, FIPS 204 and 205, W3C Quantum-Resistant Cryptosuites (FPWD 2026-06-16), Chiesa–Manohar–Spooner 2019, the proximity-gap results (Diamond–Gruen; Crites–Stewart; Ben-Sasson et al.; Kambiré), the DTG VTI and Trust Tasks framework specifications.

Appendix D and E updated; Appendix B pins evidence commit `0f7657f`. `validate` 24/24, conformance tests pass, render clean. No state promoted; nothing adopted.

Companion: [dtgwg-zkp-tf PR #29](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-tf/pull/29) carries the explanatory chapter (*Post-quantum considerations*) and the proposed LIV-ALG-09; either merges first.
