title: feat(git-workspace): nested GitLab group paths in repository coordinates
body:
Repository coordinates accept nested GitLab group paths, e.g. `gitlab.com/group/sub/repo`, up to GitLab's 20 subgroup levels. Cloning, the workspace layout, remote matching and the SSH URL handle the extra segments.

The check stays host-neutral, since a self-hosted GitLab cannot be recognised by name; empty, `..` and leading-`-` segments are still refused at any depth.

Follow-up: listing nested repositories in the Repos panel needs `git-ns/view/0.6`, which arrives with the `vta-sdk` 0.73 / trust-tasks 0.34 line.

* fix(git-workspace): harden nested repository paths

- github.com, bitbucket.org and codeberg.org keep exactly <owner>/<repo>,
  so a browse URL is not rewritten into an SSH remote
- a folder inside another checkout is not a checkout (show-toplevel), so
  account set-up never writes into the parent repository's config
- a repository right covers only that repository; only a namespace
  contains others
- gh_can_push says nothing for a nested path
- distinct errors for too deep and too long (512 chars) a path
- segments ending in .git are refused

title: docs: an extended error code is read against the Type URI it answers, in SPEC.md and all four libraries
body:
Follow-up to trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#35.

**SPEC.md**, regenerated from canonical main:
- **§8.5 now says it:** an extended code carries a slug but no authority. So a party resolves it against the Type URI of the document the error reports on (`inResponseTo.typeUri`, else the request correlated through `threadId`), never by its string alone.
- **Spelling:** the namespace is always the slug's `/` form, and the local code contains no colon.
- **§8.2:** its "hints at the family" note now says the code doesn't hint at the authority.
- **Also brings in spec #33** (declared `extends`, and `withdrawn` after a version is superseded). trusttasks.org already serves it, since CI regenerates `SPEC.md` from canonical before every build; the committed copy hadn't caught up. The registry build passes against this text: 1,132 specs, and 4,687 links into SPEC.md resolve.

**Libraries:** the same rule, in a few lines, where a reader meets extended codes:
- Rust's `TrustTaskCode::Extended`
- TypeScript's `extendedCode`
- Go's `ExtendedCode`
- Dart's `extendedCode`

Doc comments only, with no code change. `cargo fmt`, `gofmt` and `dart format` are clean.

title: feat(vtc)!: serve current vtc/auth, list, manifest and resend Trust Task versions only
body:
Migrates the `vtc/auth`, `vtc/join-requests`, `vtc/members`, `vtc/endorsements`, `vtc/endorsement-types` and `vtc/vetting` families off superseded Trust Task versions (trust-tasks-rs 0.35 marks them `#[deprecated]`). The VTC serves only the current version of each; every in-repo sender moves.

## Old → current

| Task | Old | Current | What changed on the wire |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vtc/auth/admin-session` | 0.1 | 0.2 | response `expiresAt` is an RFC 3339 date-time, not Unix seconds |
| `vtc/auth/recognise/challenge` | 0.1 | 0.2 | response `expiresAt` RFC 3339 |
| `vtc/auth/recognise` | 0.2 | 0.3 | response `data.accessExpiresAt` RFC 3339 |
| `vtc/members/list` | 0.1 | 0.2 | `nextCursor` absent on the last page, never `null` |
| `vtc/join-requests/list` | 0.1 | 0.2 | same |
| `vtc/endorsements/list` | 0.1 | 0.2 | same |
| `vtc/endorsement-types/list` | 0.1 | 0.2 | same |
| `vtc/join-requests/manifest` | 0.3 (and 0.2's generated vocabulary) | 0.4 | 0.3 no longer served; 0.4 adds `directoryDisclosure` |
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend` | 0.1 | 0.2 | 0.1 no longer served; 0.2 adds the administrator's `memberDid` |

### Notes

- **`nextCursor`** is fixed at the cause: `vti_common::pagination::Paginated` now omits a `None` cursor instead of sending `null`. No list schema in the registry requires `nextCursor`, so lists still on 0.1 (nullable, optional) conform too; every console reader already treats absence as "last page".
- **Manifest vocabulary**: `VettingRequirements`, `CommunityBranding`, `ResponseRequestedAttributesItem` and `Criterion` now come from `manifest::v0_4` everywhere (vta-sdk `protocols::vetting` re-exports, vtc-client, cnm-cli, vtc-service). `vta_sdk::openapi`: `JoinManifest02*` → `JoinManifest04*`, `JoinManifest03Response` removed, `VetterResend01Response` → `VetterResend02Response`.
- **Resend**: `VETTING_VETTER_RESEND_TYPE` now names 0.2; the `*_0_2_*` constants are gone. A vetter who is not an administrator and names `memberDid` is refused `permissionDenied` (0.2 Conformance item 2).
- Admin console: `admin-session` response type, manifest 0.4, list URIs; `openapi.json` / `wire.ts` regenerated.

## Left on the old version

- **`vtc/install/claim/{start,finish}/0.2`** stays served. 0.3 is not a replacement: it claims under a DID the founder already holds, with a step-up approver, and its own specification says *"a passkey install keeps using 0.2"* (`tokenNamesNoDid` tells the installer to use 0.2). Retiring 0.2 would remove passkey install. This looks like a specification problem: 0.2 should not be marked superseded by 0.3 while it is the only passkey ceremony.
- Historical text left as written: the `Cargo.toml` dependency-floor comment naming `manifest/0.3`, and design notes recording past counts/decisions (`vtc-console-signing.md`, `vtc-service-migration-plan.md`, `vtc-trust-task-registry-migration.md`, `vtc-trust-task-proof-enforcement.md` §counts, `vtc-action-list.md`). `openapi.json` / `wire.ts` still contain the `vtc/schemas/accepts` specification's own description text, which names `manifest/0.3`.

## Tests

- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (local, `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`: the admin-ui embedding tests fail only because the bundle was skipped; one rooms test flaked under load and passes alone)
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`, doc tests
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- admin-ui: `npm run lint`, `npx vitest run` (1347 passed)

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers

title: feat(rooms)!: room hosts serve only the current create, records/get, epoch/prune and blobs versions
body:
Room hosts (`vtc-service`, `room-host`) stop serving the superseded versions of the room-host tasks whose current version is already in `trust-tasks-rs` 0.34, and every sender in this workspace moves to the current one. Part of the migration off superseded Trust Task versions (trust-tasks-tf#921); the `rooms/keys/*` and `rooms/owner/group/*` half is a separate PR.

## Old → current

| Task | Old (no longer served) | Current |
|---|---|---|
| `rooms/create` | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| `rooms/records/get` | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| `rooms/epoch/prune` | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| `rooms/blobs/get` | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/begin` | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/chunk` | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/commit` | 0.1 | 0.2 |
| `rooms/blobs/upload/abort` | 0.1 | 0.2 |

## What changes on the wire

- **create 0.2**: adds the optional `recordRetention`; the response echoes it. A 0.1 body is a valid 0.2 body.
- **records/get 0.2**: the response also names the record's `blobs`.
- **epoch/prune 0.2**: the response carries the room's `epochFloor` (required). The 0.1 response did not, though both raised the floor. `pnm rooms prune` no longer falls back to 0.1.
- **blobs 0.2**: a proxied upload's chunk, commit and abort are signed by the single-use `uploadKey` the begin names, never by the member (begin/0.2 items 3, 14–15). A 0.1 upload, whose chunks the uploader signed, can no longer be opened. `rooms/blobs/get/0.2` answers with `mode` and, when proxied, `downloadId`, as 0.1 did. The download chunk, `rooms/blobs/chunk/0.1`, is still the current version.
- `vtc-client` loses `begin_upload`, `upload_chunk`, `commit_upload`, `abort_upload`, `get_blob`, `prune_epoch` and `epoch_chain`. The `_v2` methods replace them. `put_record` sends `rooms/records/put/0.3` and `put_sealed_record_with_blobs` sends 0.3 too. `create_room`, `get_record` and `prune_epoch_v2` send 0.2.
- In `vti_rooms::wire`, the constants for the removed versions are gone, and `CreateRoomBody` is now the generated `rooms/create/0.2` payload. `GetRecordBody` and `PruneBody` are no longer `Payload` impls; they remain as the 0.1 members a host reads out of the 0.2 request.

## Still served, and why

- **`rooms/records/put` 0.1 and 0.2, and `rooms/epoch/chain` 0.1.** A member writes and reads the chain through their VTA's `rooms/keys/act`. The newest act VTI serves is 0.6, and its table (Recipient item 1, a closed table) completes only `records/put` 0.1/0.2 and `epoch/chain` 0.1; act 0.7 is the first whose table adds `records/put/0.3` and `epoch/chain/0.2`. If hosts stopped serving these versions, every member write and chain read made through a VTA would break. They go with the act migration, which is not in this phase. Direct senders already moved here: `vtc-client` `put_record` sends put 0.3, and chain reads use `epoch_chain_v2`.
- **`ACT_TABLE` in `vta-service/src/operations/room_act.rs`** keeps `records/get/0.1` and `blobs/get/0.1`. This table is act 0.1–0.6's, fixed by that specification, and it moves with act.
- The `BlobHost` storage-layer methods `begin`, `put_chunk`, `commit`, `abort` and `open_download` stay as storage entry points. No host dispatches them any more, and their docs no longer name a task version.
- Two design notes mention `rooms/create/0.1` as history and were left unchanged: the gap table in `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms.md` and `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-epoch-anchoring.md`.

## Outside this repo

`pnm-browser-plugin`'s `@openvtc/pnm-core` exports host-direct helpers: `roomsCreate` sends `rooms/create/0.1` and `roomsRecordsGet` sends `records/get/0.1`. Nothing in that repo calls them. Once this lands, a host refuses both helpers with `unsupportedVersion`. They need a follow-up PR there. The extension's own file and act paths already send blobs 0.2, records/get 0.2 and act-wrapped put 0.1/0.2.

## Tests

- Local: `cargo check --all-targets` on every affected crate is clean. `cargo nextest run -p vti-rooms -p room-host -p vtc-client -p vta-cli-common -p vta-sdk` passed: 1650 tests, after one room-host test was moved off prune 0.1. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean.
- PR CI: Test (workspace), Test (VTC), Test (VTC, vetting-pcs), Test (VTC admin UI), Clippy, Format, the feature combos, the enclave build and the Android and iOS-simulator builds all pass.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): none added. Resume is `begin` again, which rebinds the upload key.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): `is_room_read` still lists only reads.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): not touched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): not touched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): generated types only. The JS consumer is noted above.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): not touched
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): not touched
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutation changed. An upload opened under 0.1 before the upgrade lapses on its own expiry and releases its reservation.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: feat(persona)!: serve only the current attribute/profile/world/contact task versions
body:
Moves the VTA's persona family off ten superseded Trust Task versions. The VTA now serves only the current version of each, and every sender in this repository uses it. The old versions are **no longer served**, so this is breaking on the wire.

## Old → current

| Task | Old (removed) | Current | What changed on the wire |
|---|---|---|---|
| `persona/attribute/put` | 1.0 | 1.1 | response `created` → `wasCreated` |
| `persona/attribute/promote` | 1.0 | 1.1 | response `promoted[].created` → `promoted[].wasCreated` |
| `persona/profile/put` | 1.0 | 1.1 | response `created` → `wasCreated` |
| `persona/profile/compose` | 1.0 | 1.1 | response `pooled[].created` → `pooled[].wasCreated` |
| `persona/local/profile/put` | 1.0 | 1.1 | response `created` → `wasCreated` |
| `persona/world/put` | 1.0 | 1.1 | response `created` → `wasCreated` |
| `persona/contact/lists/put` | 1.0 | 1.1 | response `created` → `wasCreated` |
| `persona/contact/put` | 1.0, 1.1 | 1.2 | response `created` → `wasCreated` (1.2 against 1.1). A 1.0 request is a valid 1.2 filing |
| `persona/contact/get` | 1.0 | 1.1 | already served beside 1.0. 1.1 adds the annotations and lets a linked contact omit `subjectDid` |
| `persona/contact/list` | 1.0 | 1.1 | already served beside 1.0. Same additions, plus the `starred` / `listId` / `directoryVtcDid` filters |

The payloads did not change for any of the `created` → `wasCreated` renames. Each spec's "Changes from" section confirms it.

## In this PR

- **vta-sdk**: replaced the `TASK_PERSONA_*` constants (`*_1_0` → `*_1_1`, `CONTACT_PUT_1_1` → `CONTACT_PUT_1_2`) and dropped `CONTACT_{PUT,GET,LIST}_1_0`. Updated the `retry_safety` table, and the client methods send the current URIs (`persona_contact_*` included) and return the current generated types (`attribute::promote::v1_1::Response`, `profile::compose::v1_1::*`, `world::put::v1_1::*`, `profile::put::v1_1::FaceReach`).
- **vta-service**: dispatch registrations, the `REACH` classification and the conformance witnesses now name the current versions. The 1.0 contact put/get/list handlers are deleted, and the 1.1 handlers take their names. Every success body touched answers `wasCreated`.
- **vta-cli-common**: `persona profile compose` reads `pooled[].was_created`. `--json` output therefore now prints `wasCreated`.
- **vta-persona**: the attribute-put pin tests now use 1.1.
- **Docs**: `docs/02-vta/contacts.md` and `docs/03-vtc/member-directory.md`, plus a comment in admin-ui `wallet-marks.ts`.

## Not covered by this PR

- **OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin** still sends every old version listed above: `contact/put` 1.0 and 1.1, `contact/get` 1.0, `contact/list` 1.0, `contact/lists/put` 1.0, `attribute/put|promote` 1.0, `profile/put|compose` 1.0 and `local/profile/put` 1.0 (`packages/core/src/persona/*.ts`). The VTA in this PR refuses those calls. The plugin has to move to the current versions before it can talk to this VTA.
- The `persona::*` hand-written client bodies in `vta_sdk::protocols::persona` (`PersonaContactPutBody` and the others) stay as they are. They match the current payloads, which did not change. Replacing them with the generated types is separate debt.

## Spec problems found

- The `persona/contact/put/1.2` spec.md Status paragraph still reads "Version 1.0 remains in force; 1.1 is a backwards-compatible MINOR increment", carried over from 1.1.

## Tests run

- Locally: `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` pass. In local `cargo nextest run --workspace …`, two persona integration tests failed because they read the 1.0 generated responses. The second commit fixes them. Three other failures came from load on a shared machine: two 300 s timeouts (`audit_coverage`, `vta-backup` restore round trip) and `tsp_stranded_reply`.
- CI: every job passes, including Test (workspace), Test (VTC), Test (VTC, vetting-pcs), Test (VTC admin UI), Clippy and the feature combos.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): none added
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): none added
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): no change to flow ordering
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): retry classes unchanged
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [ ] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): wire types come from `trust_tasks_rs::specs`. **vta-browser-plugin is not yet updated** (see above)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): n/a
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): handlers' store calls unchanged
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: R3 consumer gap above

title: feat(rooms)!: serve and send only the current rooms/keys and rooms/owner/group versions
body:
Moves the member key-holder (`rooms/keys/*`) and owner-group (`rooms/owner/group/*`) tasks off their superseded versions (part of migrating VTI off the versions `trust-tasks-rs` 0.35 deprecates). The VTA stops serving the old versions, and every sender goes at the current one with no fallback. The room-host half of the `rooms` family (create, epoch, records, blobs) is in a separate PR.

## Old → current

| Task | Was served / sent | Now | What changed on the wire |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rooms/keys/open` | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | Request unchanged. `unknownEpoch` now always carries `details.reason`, and `beyondChain` (a 0.1 bare validation failure) is `unknownEpoch` too. |
| `rooms/keys/file-key` | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | Unchanged request. A removed member's file is always `reason: removed` (0.1 said `notDelivered`). |
| `rooms/keys/seal` | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | `room_seal` sends 0.2 without `signAsPrincipal`, so it seals the bytes it is given, as 0.1 did. |
| `rooms/keys/key-package` | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | `invitation` is required. Returns the KeyPackage already held for the same room, member and invitation (`alreadyMinted`). The private half is kept for 14 days rather than 7. |
| `rooms/keys/list` | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | Each entry names its `member`. `includePersonal` is opt-in. |
| `rooms/keys/chain` | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | Relays and reports the epoch floor. |
| `rooms/keys/backfill` | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | Reports the floor. The VTA fetches with `rooms/epoch/chain/0.2` only; the fallback to `epoch/chain/0.1` is removed. |
| `rooms/owner/group/add` | 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 | **0.3** | Same schemas. A repeat is always answered with the kept Welcome (item 8). An earlier removal is reported as `earlierRemovalRefused`. |
| `rooms/owner/group/remove` | 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 | **0.1 and 0.3** | 0.2 is dropped, so `earlierRemovalRefused` replaces 0.2's `hostRefused` at `stage: revocation`. 0.1 is kept: see Exceptions. |
| `rooms/owner/group/renew` | 0.1, 0.2 | **0.2** | Same schemas. `earlierRemovalRefused`, and `hostUnreachable` carries `stage`. |

Senders moved:
- **vta-sdk:** `room_open`, `room_file_key`, `room_seal`, `room_group_add`, `room_group_renew` and `room_group_remove_v0_3` lose their fallbacks. `room_key_package` and `room_backfill` are now the 0.2 tasks; the 0.1 functions and the `_v0_2` names are gone. `room_keys_list` and `room_group_remove_v0_2` are removed.
- **vta-cli-common (pnm):** `keys key-package`, `keys list`, `keys backfill` and offer acceptance.
- **vtc-service:** a community's admission (`group/add`) and departure (`group/remove`) calls to its own VTA.

`retry_safety`, `budget`, `ALL_URIS`, the conformance witnesses and the error-code census are updated to match. Docs are updated too, except design-note version histories.

## Breaking changes
- **API:** the public vta-sdk surface changes. `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_{OPEN,FILE_KEY,SEAL,KEY_PACKAGE,LIST,CHAIN,BACKFILL}_0_1`, `TASK_ROOMS_OWNER_GROUP_{ADD_0_1,ADD_0_2,REMOVE_0_2,RENEW_0_1}` and the client methods above are removed. Return types move to the current versions' generated types.
- **Wire:** a client that sends the old versions gets `unsupportedType`.

## Exceptions
- **`rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1` stays served and sent, for `private` rooms.** `remove/0.3` refuses a `private` room (`privateRoom`), and its own error text and *What changed from 0.1* name 0.1 as "the way to remove a member of a `private` room from its group". There is no current version that does this. This is a specification problem; see below.
- **Not touched:** `rooms/keys/act` (its 0.8 needs `trust-tasks-rs` 0.35), and tasks not on this list.

## Outside this repo
`pnm-browser-plugin` (`@openvtc/pnm-core`, `packages/core/src/rooms/index.ts`) still sends three versions this PR stops serving, and needs a follow-up PR there:
- `rooms/keys/seal/0.1` (`roomsKeysSeal`)
- `rooms/keys/backfill/0.1`
- `rooms/keys/chain/0.1`

Its `rooms/keys/list/0.1` call is only a fallback behind 0.2.

## Specification problem
**`rooms/owner/group/remove` 0.1 is superseded, but nothing replaces it for `private` rooms.** 0.2 and 0.3 refuse a `private` room and send the caller back to 0.1. Once 0.1 is withdrawn in the quarterly batch, the owner of a `private` room has no task to take a member's leaf out of the group. The fix belongs in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, not here. Either:
- a `remove` version that, on a `private` room, removes the leaf without a per-member withdrawal, or
- 0.1 is not withdrawn.

## Tests
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`
- `cargo test --doc` (both sets)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: feat(rooms)!: serve and send only the current rooms/keys and rooms/owner/group versions (#2295)
body:
feat(rooms)!: serve and send only the current rooms/keys and rooms/owner/group versions (#2295)

The VTA stops serving the superseded member-key-holder and owner-group versions,
and every sender (vta-sdk, vta-cli-common/pnm, the VTC as a community's owner)
sends the current one with no fallback:

- rooms/keys/open 0.1 -> 0.2, file-key 0.1 -> 0.2, seal 0.1 -> 0.2,
  key-package 0.1 -> 0.2, list 0.1 -> 0.2, chain 0.1 -> 0.2,
  backfill 0.1 -> 0.2 (fetching with rooms/epoch/chain/0.2 only)
- rooms/owner/group/add 0.1, 0.2 -> 0.3; remove 0.2 -> 0.3; renew 0.1 -> 0.2

rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1 is kept, served and sent: 0.3 refuses a private
room (privateRoom) and names 0.1 as that tier's removal, so withdrawing 0.1
would leave no way to remove a member of a private room.

vta-sdk: room_key_package and room_backfill are now the 0.2 tasks (the 0.1
functions and the _v0_2 names are gone), room_keys_list and
room_group_remove_v0_2 are removed, room_seal goes at 0.2, and the
superseded TASK_ROOMS_* constants are removed.

Changelog

Sourced from aws-sigv4's changelog.

October 21st, 2026

New this release:

  • :tada: (all) Add an opt-in structure-prefix callback to schema-based CBOR serialization. The callback receives the value's schema and can write fields before modeled members, enabling RPC v2 CBOR error discriminators while retaining member names.

    Add opt-in definite-length encoding for lists and maps with known lengths, plus integer-list serialization that matches ordinary integer writes. ShapeSerializer provides default length-aware methods that delegate to existing implementations, so other codecs preserve their behavior.

  • :bug: (all, smithy-rs#4924) Enforce the event stream protocol's header value length limit when encoding messages. String and byte array header values longer than 32,767 bytes are now rejected instead of encoded. aws_sigv4::event_stream::sign_message now returns an error instead of panicking when a message cannot be encoded.

October 20th, 2026

New this release:

  • :bug: (client, smithy-rs#4921) Validate @hostLabel members are valid host labels. A @hostLabel value goes straight into the request authority, checked only by http::uri::Authority::from_str against the whole expanded prefix. That parser accepts a colon, and http::Uri then reads everything after it as an unparseable port and discards it. A label containing a colon therefore truncates the resolved host and drops the service suffix.

    The generated code now runs each host label through is_valid_host_label before building the prefix. Accepted labels narrow to [a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,63}. A value holding _ or . used to pass and now fails.

October 19th, 2026

Breaking Changes:

  • :warning::tada: (server, smithy-rs#4887, @​jeffzha) Add MetricsPool support to aws-smithy-http-server-metrics. The metrics layer now stores a SmithyMetricsPool producer handle in the request extensions. Independently-owned middleware and libraries that cannot name the service's metrics entry type can pull it out and contribute heterogeneous child metrics that flatten into the single per-request entry when the request finishes. Structs annotated with #[smithy_metrics] gain the backing pool automatically through a single hidden flattened field.

    This is a breaking change on two fronts.

    #[smithy_metrics] now injects a hidden __smithy_metrics field, so existing explicit struct literals no longer compile and __smithy_metrics is reserved as a field name. Construct these structs with ..Default::default() (or Default::default()) instead of naming every field:

    #[smithy_metrics]
#[metrics]

title: fix(spec): an extended error code is interpreted against the Type URI it answers, not its string
body:
A slug is unique only within its authority (§Type URI, §Private and Unpublished Trust Task Specifications), and an extended error code carries a slug but no authority. So the same code string can be emitted under two specifications: `vault/get:notFound` from the registry's `vault/get` and from a private one. The section said a consumer interprets a code "per that specification's declarations" without saying which specification, or that two equal strings can name different codes.

**Extension by Individual Trust Task Specifications** now states:
- **The namespace is always the slug's `/` form,** whatever form the Type URI takes. A URN-form specification emits `payments/settle:<local>`, never `payments:settle:<local>`.
- **The local code contains no colon,** so a code splits at its first colon without a registry lookup.
- **A party MUST resolve an extended code against the Type URI of the document the error reports on:** `inResponseTo.typeUri`, else the document correlated through `threadId`. It MUST NOT resolve the code by its string alone, or merge equal strings that resolve to different specifications.
- **The namespacing check** (own slug or family prefix) is made against that same Type URI's slug.
- **Anything keeping codes beyond the exchange** (logs, metrics, audit, retained evidence) SHOULD keep each with the Type URI it was resolved against. Retaining `inResponseTo` does it.

**Error Payload:** the note that a code's namespace hints at the family now adds that it does not hint at the authority.

**Why the authority stays out of the code:** codes stay short, every published code remains valid, and the Type URI that disambiguates a code is always available to the party entitled to interpret it.

**Impact:**
- **No wire change.** The new rules make explicit what the existing "per that specification's declarations" sentence relies on.
- **The one new constraint is "the local code MUST NOT contain a colon".** None of the 1,618 extended codes declared in the trusttasks.org registry has a second colon.
- **Tested against the registry:** `SPEC.md` generates cleanly from this branch. The registry build passes: 1,132 specs, and 4,687 links into the framework spec resolve.
- **No changelog entry,** following #24 and #33. It's written when the next framework version is released.

title: feat(dart): parse every SPEC §6.1 Type URI form, so third-party specs get extended codes and extends routing (#952)
body:
feat(dart): parse every SPEC §6.1 Type URI form, so third-party specs get extended codes and extends routing (#952)

The Dart runtime recognised only the public registry's Type URIs. A new
`TypeUri` (exported from the barrel, with `TypeUriVariant`, `TypeUriError`
and `TypeUriFormatException`) parses all three §6.1 forms — the registry's,
the path form under any authority (https URL, DID URL, …) and the URN form —
and refuses what trust-tasks-rs's `TypeUri` refuses: `http` in every form, a
`urn:` without `:spec:` or without an NID and prefix, a malformed or reserved
slug, and a version that is not MAJOR.MINOR.

- `slugFromTypeUri`, and with it `extendedCode` / `familyCode`, accept every
  form; codes stay authority-free `<slug>:<local>`, as Rust's
  `TrustTaskCode::Extended` renders them. Invalid input still throws
  `ArgumentError`.
- `extensionChain`, `extendsTo` and `readForVersion` walk a declared-extension
  chain with `TypeUri.withVersion`: same authority, form and slug, only the
  version changed, so a chain never crosses authorities and a third-party
  document never routes to a registry spec of the same slug.
- Fixes `_splitVersion`, which split the version on the last `/` and so found
  none in a URN-form Type URI: a URN document was never routed forward.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(ts): the runtime parses every SPEC §6.1 Type URI form, so extended codes and extends routing work for third-party specifications
body:
The TypeScript runtime now reads every Type URI form that SPEC §6.1 allows: the registry form, the path form under any authority (https, `did:web:…/spec/…`), and the URN form. It ports `trust-tasks-rs/src/type_uri.rs`; Go is #950.

**New, additive, from `/runtime` and the root** (api-compat against 0.27.8: only additions):
- `parseTypeUri`/`tryParseTypeUri` return `{ authority, form, slug, major, minor, variant }`;
- `formatTypeUri`, `typeUriWithVersion`, `sameSpecification`;
- `TypeUriError` carries a `kind`.

**Behaviour:**
- **More input accepted:** `slugFromTypeUri`, `extendedCode` and `familyCode` accept any authority. Codes stay `<slug>:<local>`, as in Rust. `extendsOf`/`extendsChain` now follow third-party chains.
- **Routing stays in its authority:** `readForSpec` matches only on the same authority, form, slug and variant. An `extends` chain is walked under the received authority and form, so a third-party `x/0.3` never routes to the registry's `x`, and the reverse holds too.
- **Stricter, as Rust is:** these are now refused:
  - a malformed version;
  - an unknown fragment;
  - a reserved `trust-task*` slug that isn't on the allowlist (a test holds it to `specs/spec.meta.schema.json`).

**Tests:** `npm test` passes 123 of 123; `tsc`, smoke and api-compat pass. They cover Rust's §6.1 vectors, every refusal, codes for each form, and third-party chains in path and URN form.

`trust-tasks-ts-capability-client` doesn't use these functions, and is unchanged.

title: feat(go): the runtime parses every SPEC §6.1 Type URI form, so extended codes and extends routing work for third-party specifications
body:
The Go runtime now reads every Type URI form that SPEC §6.1 allows, not only `https://trusttasks.org/spec/…`. Extended error codes, family codes and `extends` routing therefore work for third-party (SPEC §6.5) specifications, as they do in Rust (`trust-tasks-rs/src/type_uri.rs`, which this ports).

**New, additive:** `ParseTypeURI` returns a `TypeURI`, which exposes the authority (kept as written), whether it is the URN form, the slug, version and variant, plus `Bare`/`WithVersion`/`SameSpecification`. A failure is a `*TypeURIError` that says what was wrong.

**Behaviour:**
- **More input accepted:**
  - `SlugFromTypeURI`, `ExtendedCode`, `FamilyCode`, `ExtendsChainReaches` and `ReadForSpec(With)` now accept a Type URI under any authority.
  - Extended codes stay `<slug>:<local>`, with no authority, as in Rust.
- **Routing stays in its authority:** an `extends` chain is walked under the received document's own authority and form.
  - A third-party `widget/0.4` never routes along the registry's `widget` chain.
  - The same slug under another authority answers `unsupportedType`.
- **Stricter, as Rust is:** input the old prefix check let through is now refused:
  - a missing or malformed version (`…/spec/acl/grant` used to give the slug `acl`);
  - a reserved `trust-task*`/`trust-ceremony*` slug that isn't on the framework allowlist;
  - an unknown fragment.

body:
feat(go): the runtime parses every SPEC §6.1 Type URI form, so extended codes and extends routing work for third-party specifications (#950)

ParseTypeURI reads the public registry's form, the path form under any authority (https URLs, DID URLs, tag: URIs) and the URN form, refusing malformed input as trust-tasks-rs's TypeUri does: http in any form, a urn: not in the URN form, a bad slug or version, a reserved slug outside the framework allowlist, and an unknown fragment.

SlugFromTypeURI, and so ExtendedCode and FamilyCode, accept every form and still produce <slug>:<local>. ExtendsChainReaches and ReadForSpecWith compare authority, form and slug, and walk a declared-extension chain under the received URI's own authority, so a third-party specification never routes to a registry one sharing its slug.

title: fix: the TypeScript sibling packages share the application's core and load only its runtime
body:
Milestone 4, TypeScript. A survey of all four languages found that no hand-written package uses a generated task module outside its tests. So "generate only what you use" here comes down to depending on the runtime alone. Rust did this in #939; the Go and Dart siblings already import only the runtime. The design doc now records that.

**What was wrong**
- `@openvtc/trust-tasks-proof`, `-tsp` and `-capability-client` declared `"@openvtc/trust-tasks": "^0.19.0"` as a **regular dependency**. npm reads that as `<0.20.0`, so an app on core 0.27.8 that added one got a second core, 0.19.x, nested beside its own, with every prebuilt module in it.
- The published versions have the same problem: `npm view @openvtc/trust-tasks-proof dependencies` shows `^0.19.0`.
- Their own lockfiles built and tested against 0.19.8.
- They imported from the package root, which loads every prebuilt module, but used only runtime items.

**The fix**
- Each sibling takes core as a **peer dependency** at `^0.27.8`, plus a matching devDependency to build and test against.
- Each imports from `@openvtc/trust-tasks/runtime`.
- All three build and pass their tests against 0.27.8: 26, 14 and 17 tests.

**A guard so it can't drift again:** `npm run check-sibling-core-ranges` runs in `ts.yml`'s `bindings match specs` job. It fails when:
- a TypeScript sibling lists core anywhere but `peerDependencies`;
- a TypeScript or Dart sibling's caret range doesn't admit the core version in the checkout.

I checked both failure paths against modified manifests. On a Release PR that moves core across a `0.x` minor, it fails until the siblings' ranges are raised. That's deliberate: the siblings then release alongside the core that needs them. Documented in CLAUDE.md.

**Release:** all three siblings release with this change.

title: trust-tasks-build-v0.1.2
body:
### Added

- **build**: Bundles record the $defs order and each shared definition's origin ([#938](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/938))

* feat(build): bundles record the $defs order and each shared definition's origin

  A bundle's schemas are key-sorted, so the TypeScript, Go and Dart generators
  could not declare a schema's definitions in the order their in-repo
  counterparts do (1,100 of 1,127 Go files and 662 Dart files differed only in
  that order), and the TypeScript generator could not tell one shared component
  copied into many bundles from unrelated definitions that share a name.

  Two members, both additive within bundleVersion 1 (readers ignore them, and
  treat them as {} when absent):

  - defsOrder: /schema and /responseSchema -> the root $defs names in the
    order the TS/Go/Dart inliners leave them: the payload schema's own as
    authored, then each spliced definition in the order a last-in-first-out
    $ref frontier, collected in document order, reaches it. The builder
    replays that walk over the authored documents and refuses a bundle whose
    replay does not name exactly its $defs.
  - defOrigins: each spliced definition -> <its document's $id>#/$defs/<name>,
    or, for a document with no $id, its path under the specifications root
    below the Type URI prefix.

  check-bundles verifies both without the Rust builder: defsOrder against the
  $defs order of the TypeScript module's schemas (all 1,127 agree, as they do
  with Go's embedded schema text), and every origin against the $ids and $defs
  of the shared schemas in specs/.

  Every bundle's digest changes once when this deploys. The by-digest store is
  append-only, so existing locks still build, check and fetch; `trust-tasks
  update` takes the new bytes and says so.

title: trust-tasks-tsp-v0.35.3
body:
### Fixed

- **rs**: The transport crates depend on trust-tasks-rs's runtime only ([#939](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/939))

trust-tasks-didcomm, -didcomm-v1, -tsp, -https, -proof and
  -capability-client depended on trust-tasks-rs with its default features,
  which are every specification family. Cargo unifies features across the
  graph, so an application that generates only the tasks it pins
  (trust-tasks-build) still compiled every prebuilt module as soon as it
  depended on any transport, and the facade route in GETTING-STARTED
  (`trust-tasks` with default-features = false and runtime_path) got every
  family anyway.

  None of these crates uses a specification module outside its tests,
  examples and doc examples, so each now depends on the runtime alone
  (default-features = false) and enables `acl` (and `task-consent` for
  trust-tasks-https) as a dev-dependency feature for those.

  Verified per crate in isolation, so no other workspace member can switch
  the families back on: `cargo tree -e features` shows trust-tasks-rs with
  no features for each, and each crate's tests, examples and doctests pass
  with --all-features.

  An application that reached a family's types only because a transport
  switched every family on must now enable that family (or the `all-specs`
  default) on trust-tasks-rs itself.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(cli): trust-tasks generate --lang runs a language's generator over a verified lock
body:
`trust-tasks generate --lang <rs|ts|go|dart> --out <dir> [-- <args>]` is milestone 3's last piece. It runs `check`, and only if the lock verifies does it run that language's generator from the project directory:

| `--lang` | runs | needs |
|---|---|---|
| `ts` | `npx --no-install trust-tasks-gen-ts` | `npm i -D @openvtc/trust-tasks-gen` |
| `go` | `go run …/trust-tasks-go/cmd/trust-tasks-gen` | a module requiring `trust-tasks-go` |
| `dart` | `dart run trust_tasks:generate` | a package depending on `trust_tasks` |
| `rs` | nothing; it checks and points at `build.rs` | `trust-tasks-build` |

`--lock` and `--out` are passed as absolute paths, and anything after `--` goes to the generator unchanged. The command installs nothing; a missing tool gives an error saying what to add.

**Examples fixed:** the TypeScript example had no `trust-tasks.toml`, and the Dart example's manifest omitted the third-party task its lock pins, so neither passed `check`. Both manifests now match their locks.

**Verified locally through the new command:**
- the Go and TypeScript examples regenerate with no diff;
- the Dart example generates and runs;
- `--lang rs` checks the Rust example.

A new CLI test runs it against a stand-in `npx`, covering the working directory, arguments, `--` pass-through, the missing-tool error, a required `--out`, `--lang rs`, and no generator run on a lock that doesn't verify.

title: feat(dart): dart run trust_tasks:generate generates only the tasks an application pins
body:
Milestone 3, Dart: an application generates only the tasks it pins in `trust-tasks.lock`. Stacked on #938; it will retarget to `main` when that merges.

**What's in it**
- **`dart run trust_tasks:generate --lock … --out …`** (`trust-tasks-dart/bin/generate.dart`, `lib/src/generator/`).
  - It checks each vendored bundle's digest before generating, with a SHA-256 implemented in the package.
  - It writes one library per version, the same shape as `lib/specs`.
  - Third-party sources go under their own namespace and Type URI.
  - It declares `$defs` in the bundle's `defsOrder`, and falls back to key order for older bundles.
- **`examples/consumer-app-dart`** pins the Rust example's tasks and round-trips each document. It has a CI job in `dart.yml`.

**Equivalence over all 1,127 bundles** (`scripts/check-dart-consumer-generation.mjs`, in CI)
- **1,106 of 1,120 libraries:** byte-identical apart from the header and the embedded schema text, which is JSON-equal because bundles are key-sorted. Before #938, 458 were.
- **14 libraries (`vtc/directory/*`, `vtc/groups/*`):** the same declarations in a different order.
  - Each has an object whose `propertyNames` and `additionalProperties` both `$ref` a definition, and the prebuilt follows the authored keyword order.
  - A bundle doesn't keep that order, and the registry writes the pair both ways round.
  - The test allows only this case, names the 14 libraries, and fails on any other reordering.
- **Not generated, by design:** 140 shared and 12 framework libraries, and 7 framework bundles. The extends index matches.

**Release:** `feat(dart)` releases `trust_tasks`. The change is additive: a new `bin/` entry point and generator library.

body:
feat(dart): dart run trust_tasks:generate generates only the tasks an application pins (#942)

* feat(dart): generate only the tasks an application pins, with dart run trust_tasks:generate

`trust-tasks-dart/bin/generate.dart` reads a trust-tasks.lock and the bundles
vendored beside it, checks each bundle's SHA-256 against the lock, and writes
one library per pinned version to <out>/<slug>/v<M>_<N>/payload.dart plus an
extends_index.dart — the same API as the prebuilt lib/specs/ libraries,
importing the runtime as package:trust_tasks. An independent port of
scripts/build-dart-bindings.mjs with bundles as input; no new dependencies
(SHA-256 and the lockfile reader are in-package).

scripts/check-dart-consumer-generation.mjs runs it over every bundle in the
registry and compares with the prebuilt tree: 458 libraries identical, 662
identical declaration for declaration in a different top-level order (the
bundle does not carry $defs order), every embedded schema JSON-equal.
examples/consumer-app-dart pins the same three tasks as examples/consumer-app.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(dart): generate third-party tasks from lock sources, under their own namespace and Type URI

trust-tasks.lock may now declare [sources.<name>] tables and a per-task `source`. A sourced bundle is read from trust-tasks/@<source>/<slug>/<M.N>.bundle.json and generated under <out>/<source>/…; its Type URI is taken from the bundle, never rebuilt from the slug. Refused: a source named for an official task's first segment, a sourced bundle under https://trusttasks.org/, an official bundle whose Type URI is not the registry's, and a framework slug from a source. examples/consumer-app-dart pins one sourced fixture, payments/settle 1.0 from https://tasks.example.com.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(dart): declare $defs in the bundle's defsOrder, as the prebuilt tree does

The consumer generator now reorders a bundle's root $defs by its
`defsOrder` (the order the in-repo inliner leaves them in) before reserving
names and emitting declarations, so it declares types in the prebuilt
tree's order. A bundle older than `defsOrder` keeps the bundle's key order.

Against every registry bundle, 1106 libraries are now byte-identical apart
from the header and the embedded schema's key order (was 458), and 14 differ
only in top-level declaration order. Those 14 each have a schema object
whose `propertyNames` and `additionalProperties` both $ref a definition:
the dependency walk follows keyword order, which the key-sorted bundle does
not carry, and the registry writes the pair both ways round (30 and 9), so
no fixed keyword order would be right.

The equivalence check now allows a reordering only for that cause, and
fails one in a bundle without `defsOrder`.

* feat(go): trust-tasks-gen generates an application's locked tasks from vendored bundles

trust-tasks-go/cmd/trust-tasks-gen (standard library only, go 1.22 floor) is an
independent port of scripts/build-go-bindings.mjs whose input is a

skips framework specs and withdrawn versions with a note, owns its out

from the bundle's typeUri.

title: feat(ts-gen): an application generates only the TypeScript tasks it pins, byte-identical to the prebuilt modules
body:
Milestone 3, TypeScript: an application generates only the tasks it pins in `trust-tasks.lock`. Stacked on #938; it will retarget to `main` when that merges.

**What's in it**
- **New package `trust-tasks-ts-gen/`** (`@openvtc/trust-tasks-gen`, bin `trust-tasks-gen-ts --lock … --out …`). It checks each vendored bundle against its locked digest before generating. Its output directory carries a `.trust-tasks-generated` marker.
- **Shared definitions** are hoisted by the bundles' `defOrigins` and declared in `defsOrder`, the way `build-ts-bindings.mjs` does it.
- Third-party definitions are tagged with their source name, so they never take an official name.
- **`@openvtc/trust-tasks`** gains a `"./runtime"` export and `declareExtends`, which generated code needs.
- **`examples/consumer-app-ts`** pins the same tasks as the Rust example, plus a sourced one, and round-trips each document. It has a CI job in `ts.yml`.

**Equivalence over all 1,127 bundles** (`trust-tasks-ts-gen/scripts/equivalence.mjs`, in CI)
- **Modules:** every module's imports, types and re-exports are byte-identical to the committed `trust-tasks-ts/src`, with one exception. The 7 `registry/record/*` import lines name `TrustRecord_RegistryV0_1` where the prebuilt says `TrustRecord`. The prebuilt keeps a name once it has shipped (`component-names.lock.json`), and a bundle has no naming history. The test accepts only that rename, after checking the declarations are identical.
- **Shared components:** 686 of 688 declarations are byte-identical. `TrustRecord` is the rename above. `FileManifest` is reached only from a shared file, never a payload, so it is in no bundle.
- **Schema constants:** JSON-equal, with `properties` and root `$defs` order matching. They are not byte-identical, because bundles are key-sorted.
- **Fails on anything else:** checked by injecting a change into a module and into a shared declaration.

**Design notes**
- **Shared names depend on the lock.** A 3-task app gets `AclEntry` where the full library has `AclEntry_AclV0_2`. For that reason the generated `index.ts` doesn't export the shared module. Each task module re-exports its definitions under their own names.
- **Older bundles still work.** Without `defOrigins`, each module declares its own definitions; the tests cover this.

**Fix along the way:** the lock helper in the tests dropped `source`. That broke 7 tests once #934's example pinned `vault/get` 0.3 from both the registry and `acme`.

**Release:** `@openvtc/trust-tasks-gen` is not in `TS_PACKAGES` or the publish matrix yet. Its first npm publish is manual (RELEASING.md), and the wiring follows that.

when importing the package root. CI: ts.yml gen-equivalence and

in TS_PACKAGES or the publish-npm matrix (RELEASING.md).

them to do what scripts/build-ts-bindings.mjs does: every $defs entry spliced
in from a shared document is declared once in <out>/_shared/components.ts —
one origin is one component, grouped by fully-resolved shape and named bare
or family/version-qualified as the in-repo registry names it — and each
module compiles its payload schema as authored (own $defs only, in defsOrder
order), imports what it uses and re-exports it under its own name. The
schema constants carry $defs in defsOrder order.

vendored bundles are) still gets a self-contained module.

byte-identical from its first import to its last constant (banner aside) —

declarations byte-identical, the other the same historical name. The two
differences a bundle cannot remove: TrustRecord (registry 0.1) is
TrustRecord_RegistryV0_1 here, because component-names.lock.json keeps a name
that shipped bare before a second shape appeared and a bundle has no history;
and FileManifest, which only a shared schema file reaches, is in no bundle.
Schema constants stay JSON-equal (bundles are key-sorted), with properties and

the generated tree.

title: fix(rs): the transport crates depend on trust-tasks-rs's runtime only
body:
## Summary

`trust-tasks-didcomm`, `-didcomm-v1`, `-tsp`, `-https`, `-proof` and `-capability-client` depended on `trust-tasks-rs` with its default features, which switch on every specification family. Cargo unifies features across the graph, so:

- an application that generates only the tasks it pins (`trust-tasks-build`, #930) still compiled every prebuilt module as soon as it depended on any transport or on `trust-tasks-proof`;
- the facade route in GETTING-STARTED (#936: `trust-tasks` with `default-features = false` plus `runtime_path("::trust_tasks")`) got every family anyway.

None of these crates uses a specification module outside its tests, examples and doc examples. Each now depends on the runtime alone (`default-features = false`) and enables `acl` (plus `task-consent` for `trust-tasks-https`) as a dev-dependency feature for those.

Found while moving `affinidi-messaging-sdk` to build-time generation: with this change, the whole `affinidi-tdk-rs` workspace has one `trust-tasks-rs` node with no features; without it, `trust-tasks-proof` alone brings every family back.

## Verification

Each crate checked **in isolation** (`-p <crate>`), so no other workspace member can switch the families back on:

- `cargo tree -p <crate> --all-features -e normal,features` shows `trust-tasks-rs` with no features for all six;
- `cargo test -p <crate> --all-features --all-targets` and `--doc` pass for all six (182 tests, plus doctests).

## Compatibility

An application that reached a family's types only because a transport switched every family on must enable that family (or the `all-specs` default) on `trust-tasks-rs` itself, or, with the facade, keep its `all-specs` default. No public API of these crates changes, and none re-exports `trust_tasks_rs`.

title: feat(build): bundles record the $defs order and each shared definition's origin
body:
Milestone 3 decision A: registry bundles carry what canonical form loses, so the TypeScript, Go and Dart consumer-side generators can reproduce the prebuilt output exactly.

- **`defsOrder`**: the root `$defs` order the TS/Go/Dart inliners produce (own definitions as authored, then the last-in-first-out `$ref` frontier). `trust-tasks-build` replays the walk in `publish/order.rs` and refuses a bundle whose replay doesn't name exactly its `$defs`.
- **`defOrigins`**: each spliced definition maps to `<$id>#/$defs/<name>`, so the TS generator can hoist one shared component across bundles.

Both are additive within `bundleVersion` 1. `trust-tasks-cli` 0.1.1 and `trust-tasks-build` 0.1.1 read the new bundles unchanged.

**Verified**
- All 1,127 bundles' `defsOrder` equals the `$defs` order of the TypeScript module's `PAYLOAD_SCHEMA` and of Go's embedded `PayloadSchemaJSON`.
- `check-bundles` now asserts the TS comparison and checks every origin against `specs/`. A tampered order or origin fails it.
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen` produces no diff, since Rust doesn't read the new members.
- New unit tests cover the LIFO order, `$id` origins, and the no-`$id` fallback under https and URN prefixes.

**On deploy** every digest changes once. The by-digest store is append-only, so existing locks keep building and fetching. `trust-tasks list --remote` reports "changed upstream" until `trust-tasks update`.

Next: the three generator branches (TS, Go, Dart) switch to these members and re-run their equivalence tests.

title: feat(build): bundles record the $defs order and each shared definition's origin (#938)
body:
feat(build): bundles record the $defs order and each shared definition's origin (#938)

* feat(build): bundles record the $defs order and each shared definition's origin

A bundle's schemas are key-sorted, so the TypeScript, Go and Dart generators
could not declare a schema's definitions in the order their in-repo
counterparts do (1,100 of 1,127 Go files and 662 Dart files differed only in
that order), and the TypeScript generator could not tell one shared component
copied into many bundles from unrelated definitions that share a name.

Two members, both additive within bundleVersion 1 (readers ignore them, and
treat them as {} when absent):

- defsOrder: /schema and /responseSchema -> the root $defs names in the
  order the TS/Go/Dart inliners leave them: the payload schema's own as
  authored, then each spliced definition in the order a last-in-first-out
  $ref frontier, collected in document order, reaches it. The builder
  replays that walk over the authored documents and refuses a bundle whose
  replay does not name exactly its $defs.
- defOrigins: each spliced definition -> <its document's $id>#/$defs/<name>,
  or, for a document with no $id, its path under the specifications root
  below the Type URI prefix.

check-bundles verifies both without the Rust builder: defsOrder against the
$defs order of the TypeScript module's schemas (all 1,127 agree, as they do
with Go's embedded schema text), and every origin against the $ids and $defs
of the shared schemas in specs/.

Every bundle's digest changes once when this deploys. The by-digest store is
append-only, so existing locks still build, check and fetch; `trust-tasks
update` takes the new bytes and says so.

title: trust-tasks-cli-v0.1.1
body:
### Added

- **cli, build, rs**: Pin and generate tasks from third-party sources beside the registry's ([#934](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/934))

* feat(cli, build, rs): pin and generate tasks from third-party sources beside the registry's

  SPEC §6.1/§6.5 already allow specifications under another authority, with
  a slug unique only within its authority. An application can now pin them
  from a third-party registry and generate them with the official ones.

  trust-tasks-cli
  - trust-tasks.toml gains [sources.<name>] (url = "https://…" or
    path = "<dir>"); tasks are named "<source>:<slug>", and on the command
    line `trust-tasks add acme:payments/settle/1.0`. add, update, check,
    fetch, list and remove all take sourced tasks; a source serves the
    trusttasks.org layout (index.json, bundle.json, by-digest).
  - The lock (still version 1) records [sources.*] and `source =`, sorted
    official first, then source, slug, version; bundles vendor to
    trust-tasks/@<source>/…. Every lock read or written is also held to
    trust-tasks-build's reading of it.
  - Refused: a sourced bundle under https://trusttasks.org/ (SPEC §6.5
    item 1) and an official one outside it; a framework slug from a source;

    trust-tasks-codegen so the registry and third parties share one
    builder. The codegen's official bundles and trust-tasks-rs modules are

    exactly; http stays refused (its error text claimed otherwise).

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.35.1` → `0.35.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-build` | crates.io | `0.1.0` → `0.1.1` | patch |

| `trust-tasks-cli` | crates.io | `0.1.0` → `0.1.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.35.1` → `0.35.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.35.1` → `0.35.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.35.1` → `0.35.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.35.1` → `0.35.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.35.1` → `0.35.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.35.1` → `0.35.2` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  the commit subjects.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

Every bump follows the commit subjects; an undeclared API break is refused on its
pull request by that language's API compatibility check (`rs`, `ts`, `go` and
`Dart API compatibility`).

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat: did:scid personas
body:
did:scid personas in OpenVTC (spec trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#75).

- Account `preferred_did_method` / `scid_also_known_as` (optional, unset = unchanged behaviour); per-persona choice in create-persona and join; mint via `create_did_webvh_presented`, key ids match the native document; `PersonaRecord.did_locator` seeds the resolver's did:scid sources at load.
- Display, validation, context naming, agent-name host, health labels and copy handle did:scid.
- proof_check, VRC issuer binding, authenticated sender, rooms/repos reply checks compare by DID ignoring `src`; did:scid ≠ its did:webvh.
- A did:scid persona speaks as its locator so peers can resolve it.
- Also tolerates vta-sdk's new non-exhaustive enums (VTI #2196).

**Dependencies (all published on crates.io; no `[patch]`):**

- `vta-sdk` 0.73 (`vta_sdk::did_scid`, OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2257); dev: `vta-service` 0.65, `vti-vetting-pcs` 0.6
- `affinidi-tdk` 0.32, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.40, dev `affinidi-messaging-test-mediator` 0.45 (TSP 1.0)
- `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` 0.8.43 (native did:scid, affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#965)
- `didwebvh-rs` 0.8.1 (decentralized-identity/didwebvh-rs#56)
- `trust-tasks-rs` / `trust-tasks-capability-client` 0.34.2 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#862, #863)
- `did-git-sign` / `vgi-core` 0.25 (OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure#168, v0.25.0), on vta-sdk 0.73, so the graph keeps one vta-sdk / TDK / trust-tasks (`cargo tree -d` is clean for the stack)

**Behaviour change from vta-sdk 0.73:** an unresolvable `did:web` VTA is refused rather than synthesized into `https://<domain>`, so TSP discovery reports `Unavailable` instead of `NotAdvertised` (both stay on DIDComm). The test that pinned the old outcome is now `an_unresolvable_did_web_is_unavailable`.

**Tests:** `cargo fmt --check`; clippy `-D warnings` (all features, default, `dev-overrides`); `cargo test` all features (2148 passed, 0 failed), `--no-default-features`, `dev-overrides`, `--ignored`; `cargo doc`. All pass locally.

Deferred: rebuild-from-VTA brings a did:scid persona back as did:webvh (VTA list/get gap); peers' `src` not persisted.

title: feat: did:scid personas (#503)
body:
feat: did:scid personas (#503)

* fix: tolerate vta-sdk's non-exhaustive RemovalCode, VtaEvent and DiagStatus (#2196)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(persona): mint a persona as did:webvh or did:scid, and remember a did:scid's locator (VTI-KEY-160 to VTI-KEY-165, VTI-VTA-036)

The account gains `preferred_did_method` and `scid_also_known_as`, both
optional and off the wire when unset: an account that states nothing sends
`vta/webvh/dids/create/1.1` exactly as before and the VTA's `[dids]` decides.
A persona mint goes through `create_did_webvh_presented` with the operator's
choice for that persona (join flow) or the account's preference.

The VTA's `did` is the identity in the applied form, so key ids stay
`{did}#key-N`, which is what a did:scid's own document lists (VTI-KEY-161).
A did:scid persona's DID URL with `src` is recorded on its PersonaRecord as
`did_locator`. It is the persona's ATM profile DID, so what it sends carries
the source a first-contact peer needs (VTI-KEY-163). At load it seeds the
resolver's did:scid sources, so the bare DID resolves after a restart
(VTI-KEY-162). Orphaned-key detection recognises did:scid persona keys.

`create_did_via_server` returns a `MintedDid` rather than a tuple; its unread
mnemonic is dropped.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat: did:scid personas and communities in display, validation and the mint choice (VTI-KEY-160, VTI-KEY-163)

- Display: `shorten_webvh` elides a did:scid:vh:1's SCID too, keeping its
  `?src=` locator, where its host and path are.
- `validate_did` admits a did:scid DID URL whose only query is `src`, by
  validating its identity and the locator as a host and path. No other
  query, and no other method's, is admitted.
- Context tokens and rebuilt sub-contexts take a did:scid community's SCID,
  never its locator, whose `?` and `/` have no place in a context id. Health
  labels name a did:scid by its `src` path.
- Agent names: the host of a did:scid is its `src` host; a bare did:scid has
  none, so the identity panel carries the persona's locator.
- The create-persona overlay (`m` on the path screen) and the join
  identity choice (`m` on "Be someone new") choose the new persona's form:
  the account's preference, did:webvh, or did:scid. The worked example
  follows the choice. A minted did:scid persona is shown and copied as its
  DID URL with `src`, which is what a community needs to resolve it.
- Setup and join examples, and a loading tip, mention did:scid.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat: did:scid signers, senders and personas compared by DID, and a did:scid persona speaks as its locator (VTI-KEY-161, VTI-KEY-163, VTI-KEY-164)

- proof_check: a did:scid signer, and its verificationMethod, may be named
  with the `?src=` locator its document was resolved through. The document
  and its keys are under the bare DID, so both are compared without it. The
  method's DID must still be the signer's, and a did:webvh of the same log is
  not the did:scid.
- A VRC's issuer binding, a picked-up message's authenticated sender, and
  the rooms and repos reply checks compare by DID, ignoring a did:scid `src`.
  The picked-up sender is still returned as presented, as the live path
  returns it, so both route a message the same way.
- A did:scid persona's listener speaks as its DID URL with `src`
  (`Config::presented_did`), so what it sends, and the `skid` the TDK
  derives from it, carry the source a first-contact peer needs. The listener
  id and the persona's secrets stay under the identity.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(deps): take vta-sdk 0.73, affinidi-tdk 0.32, messaging-sdk 0.40, trust-tasks 0.34 and did-git-sign 0.25

The published stack the did:scid personas need:

- vta-sdk 0.73 (`vta_sdk::did_scid`, VTI #2257), with vta-service 0.65
  and vti-vetting-pcs 0.6 in the dev graph
- affinidi-tdk 0.32, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.40 and
  affinidi-messaging-test-mediator 0.45 (TSP 1.0)
- affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.43 (native did:scid resolution)
- didwebvh-rs 0.8.1 (the did:scid presentation of a did:webvh)
- trust-tasks-rs / trust-tasks-capability-client 0.34.2
- did-git-sign / vgi-core 0.25 (VGI #168), on vta-sdk 0.73, so the
  graph keeps one vta-sdk; 0.24 hands 0.72's VtaClient across its API

vta-sdk 0.73 resolves a VTA with OnUnresolved::Refuse, so an unresolvable
did:web is no longer turned into a synthesized https://<domain> endpoint:
TSP discovery reports Unavailable rather than NotAdvertised, and both
keep trust tasks on DIDComm. The test pinning that outcome is updated.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* ci: add swap to the jobs that build the workspace

On vta-sdk 0.73, affinidi-tdk 0.32 and trust-tasks 0.34, Benchmarks and
Coverage outgrew the runner's memory: vta-sdk turns on every generated
trust-tasks-rs spec, and the runner was shut down mid compile with exit code
143 and no compiler error. Every job that builds the workspace now gets a
16 GB swapfile (the test matrix on Linux only), as VGI's CI does.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(cli, build, rs): pin and generate tasks from third-party sources beside the registry's
body:
SPEC §6.5 already lets a third party publish Trust Task specifications under its own authority (an https URL, a DID URL or a URN — never `https://trusttasks.org`), and a slug is unique only within its authority. This makes the consumer-side tooling use that: an application pins an ecosystem's tasks beside the registry's and generates them together.

## For an application

```toml
# trust-tasks.toml
[sources.acme]
url = "https://tasks.acme.example"   # https only; or: path = "../acme-registry"

[tasks]
"vault/get" = "0.3"
"acme:payments/settle" = "1.0"
```

- `trust-tasks add acme:payments/settle/1.0`; `update`, `check`, `fetch`, `list`, `remove` all work for sourced tasks. Bundles vendor to `trust-tasks/@acme/…`; the lock (still `version = 1`) gains `[sources.*]` and `source = "acme"`.
- `trust-tasks-build` generates them under a source-named module: `tasks::acme::payments::settle::v1_0`. Identity is always the bundle's Type URI, so `acme:vault/get` and the registry's `vault/get` are different types and never route into each other.
- Digests pin content and builds never touch the network, exactly as for official tasks. `TRUST_TASKS_CA_FILE` names a PEM bundle for a source behind an internal CA.

**Refused**, with an error naming both sides: a sourced bundle under `https://trusttasks.org/`; an official bundle outside it; a framework slug (`trust-task*`, `trust-ceremony*`) from a source; two pins with one Type URI; a source named like a pinned official family; a source name that is not a slug segment (or not a Rust module name); a bundle whose Type URI, slug and version disagree with each other or the lock.

## For a third-party publisher

`trust-tasks registry build --specs <dir> --type-uri-prefix <prefix> --out <dir> [--official-specs <dir>]` turns a `specs/<slug>/<M.N>/` tree into the layout trusttasks.org serves — bundles, `index.json`, the append-only by-digest store — ready for any static host. The bundle builder moved out of `trust-tasks-codegen` into `trust-tasks-build`'s new `publish` feature so there is one builder; **all 1,127 official bundles and `index.json` regenerate byte-identically**. Absolute `$ref`s to trusttasks.org shared components resolve from `--official-specs` or by fetching (publisher side only).

What the builder checks: front matter and policy, slug/version grammar, reserved slugs, the authority rule, `$id` = Type URI, `$schema` 2020-12, every `$ref` resolves, `extends` names an existing version. **Not** ported from the JS build: `spec.meta.schema.json` validation, the additive-`extends` proof, casing/wire-conventions/stale-references lints, example validation, link checks.

## `trust-tasks-rs` (behaviour, both widening)

- `TypeUri` parses every §6.1 form — DID URL and URN as well as https — and round-trips `Display`; adds `TypeUri::new_urn`. (`http` was already refused; only the error text said otherwise.)
- Dispatchers and `read_as` classify another authority's same-slug document as **unsupported type**, not unsupported version. Routing was already keyed by full URI.

## Tests

- `trust-tasks-build` 55 (all features), `trust-tasks-cli` 37 incl. new `tests/sources.rs` (directory source, mock https source with its own CA, `registry build`, every refusal).
- `examples/consumer-app` pins `acme:vault/get/0.3` from `fixture-registry/` beside the three official tasks (unchanged) and dispatches each `vault/get` to its own handler; a CI step rebuilds the fixture registry and fails on drift.
- Re-verified locally before opening.

## Follow-ups (not here)

- TS, Go and Dart runtimes parse only registry Type URIs for extended error codes and `extends` routing; their generators (milestone 3, separate PRs) already handle sources.
- Extended error codes are namespaced by slug, so `acme:vault/get:notFound` is spelled like the registry's — a spec question.
- The CLI now depends on `trust-tasks-build` (`publish` feature), so `cargo install trust-tasks-cli` compiles typify/syn.

Also adds `trust-tasks-build/README.md` (its crates.io page was blank). Merge after #933.

title: ci(release): the crates' API is checked on every pull request, and the Release PR job no longer runs cargo-semver-checks
body:
## Why

The Release PR job ran `cargo-semver-checks` (release-plz's `semver_check`) after **every merge to main**, over every generated module:

- ~12.6 GB resident for `trust-tasks-rs` alone, repeatedly killed for memory on a 16 GB runner (the swap, `flock` serialisation and OOM sampler in `publish.yml` all existed to fight that);
- 8 to 40 minutes before the Release PR was ready to merge;
- and a break was found only *after* the PR that made it had merged.

The npm, Go and Dart packages are already checked on the pull request. This puts the crates with them.

## What changes

- **`rs API compatibility`** (new job in `rust.yml`, `scripts/check-rs-api-compat.sh`): `cargo semver-checks --baseline-rev <crate>-v<x.y.z>` for each published crate, the same verdict rule as the Go/TS/Dart jobs (passes when the title's `!` names a releasing scope, or a break merged since the tag already makes the release breaking).
  - `trust-tasks-rs` over the runtime + `validate` + the `acl` family only — the other families are the same generator's output, and schema changes are judged by `published schemas change only additively`. Measured locally: **24 s cold, ~200 MB**.
  - The facade (`--only-explicit-features`, 10 s) and `trust-tasks-ceremony` (16 s) always.
  - A binding crate only when the PR changes its directory: it compiles every family through its dependency (measured 280 s, 13.3 GB RSS), so the job adds swap.
  - Verified both ways locally: making `TypeUri::canonical` private fails (`inherent_method_missing`, exit 100); marking it `#[deprecated]` passes.
- **`release-plz.toml`**: `semver_check = false` — crate bumps now come from the commit subjects, like every other package's. The withdrawal batch title already carries `rs` in its `!` scope, so batches stay breaking.
- **`publish.yml` `release-pr`**: no cargo-semver-checks install, wrapper, swap or OOM sampler; timeout 90 → 30.
- RELEASING.md, CLAUDE.md's CI table, and comments in `release-pr.sh`, `withdraw.yml`, `ts.yml` and `release-bump-ts.sh` updated to match.

## Trade-off

A break in generated code of a family other than `acl`, that the schema-additivity check cannot see, would now surface only after release. Codegen changes apply uniformly to every family, so `acl` is a representative sample.

## Also observed

Release #931's crates.io publish took **81 s** — the previous release timed out after 30 minutes waiting on the 10 MB crate, before #926 shrank it.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.35.1
body:
### Added

- **rs, build, cli**: An application generates only the tasks it pins, and builds three of them in 8 s instead of 140 s ([#930](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/930))

* feat(rs, build, cli): an application generates only the tasks it pins, and builds three of them in 8 s instead of 140 s

  Milestone 2 of consumer-side generation (docs/design/consumer-side-generation.md).

  - trust-tasks-cli: the `trust-tasks` command — add, remove, update, fetch,
    check, list. trust-tasks.toml is the intent, trust-tasks.lock the
    resolution; bundles are vendored by digest from the append-only
    /specs/by-digest/ store, which deploy now writes and never deletes.
  - trust-tasks-build: an application's build.rs generates the versions its
    lock pins, after verifying each vendored bundle against the lock. The
    per-module generator moved here from trust-tasks-codegen, which now goes
    spec → bundle → generate_module and regenerates the repo byte-identically.
  - trust-tasks-rs (additive): a hidden `__private` re-export of serde,
    serde_json, regress and chrono, `extension::declare_extends` so the
    dispatchers route along app-generated `extends` chains, and a hidden
    `DeclaredErrorCode::__from_declaration`.
  - Bundles carry `propertyOrder`, the authored member order the canonical
    form sorts away.
  - examples/consumer-app pins three tasks: cold build 8.1 s / 0.41 GB, against
    140.2 s / 17.4 GB for trust-tasks-rs with every prebuilt module.

  Both new crates are `release = false` until their manual first publish.

- **specs**: Registry/* in lowerCamelCase, with a validity window on trust records ([#925](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/925))

* feat(specs): registry/* in lowerCamelCase, with a validity window on trust records

  New versions of every live registry/* spec move the family from TRQP's
  snake_case to the registry-wide lowerCamelCase convention, and give trust
  records an optional validity window so a query's `context.time` has
  something to be judged against (TRQP v2.0, Identifiers: `time` is "the
  datetime as of which the target authority statement is valid").

  - registry/_shared 0.2: TrustRecord members entityId, authorityId,
    recordType; new optional validFrom (inclusive) / validUntil (exclusive).
  - registry/authorization 0.2, registry/recognition 0.2: entityId,
    authorityId; time_evaluated -> evaluatedAt and time_requested -> asOf,
    per the `<event>At` / `asOf` instant conventions. New Evaluation section:
    outside the window the answer is false; a registry evaluating at its own
    clock MAY start a record up to 60 s before validFrom, never extends
    validUntil, and evaluates an explicit context.time exactly. A TRQP field
    names table gives the mapping a registry applies on the plain HTTP
    TRQP binding.
  - registry/record/put 0.3, registry/record/query 0.3,
    registry/record/delete 0.2: renamed members; put defines the window and
    rejects validFrom >= validUntil as malformedRequest.
  - registry/did/rotate 0.2: preRotationCount, newScid, newVersionId.

  The superseded versions stay published. Stale prose links in git-trust and
  vtc/directory/card/publish are moved to the new versions, and the TRQP
  instant-name allowlist entries are dropped, since no current spec uses them.
  Libraries regenerated.

- **rs, https, dart-https**: Answer trust-task-discovery 0.3, and move every hand-written use off the versions the first withdrawal batch removes ([#924](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/924))

* ci: warn about hand-written imports of versions due in the next withdrawal batch, and fail inside 30 days of it



### Fixed

- **rs**: Keep the published crate well under crates.io's 10 MB upload limit ([#926](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/926))

* fix(rs): keep the published crate well under crates.io's 10 MB upload limit

  `cargo package -p trust-tasks-rs` produced a 9.96 MB .crate: the next release
  adding a few spec versions would have failed to publish. Three changes, none
  visible in the API, take it to 7.80 MB:

  - Exclude the generated conformance tests (tests/conformance, 1,057 files)
    from the package. They run in this repository's CI; a consumer never
    compiles another crate's integration tests.
  - Drop the `<details><summary>JSON schema</summary>` block typify writes into
    every generated type's doc comment. It restated the type's schema, nested
    types included, once per enclosing type — 11–14 MB of source. The prose
    description is kept; the schema itself is PAYLOAD_SCHEMA and the published
    document at the Type URI.
  - Emit PAYLOAD_SCHEMA compact rather than pretty-printed. The value is the same
    JSON (check-bindings parses it and agrees across all four languages); only
    the whitespace a validator never reads is gone.

  Generated source: 87 MB → 71 MB. clippy --all-features -D warnings, the acl
  tests and rustdoc -D warnings pass.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps follow the commit subjects; an undeclared API break in
any of them is refused on its pull request by that language's API compatibility
check, as `cargo-semver-checks` refuses one in the crates here.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.
