title: feat(specs): registry/* in lowerCamelCase, with a validity window on trust records
body:
## Why

Two problems with the `registry/*` family:

1. **Casing.** It is the one family still in snake_case, because its members were copied verbatim from TRQP v2.0. The registry convention is lowerCamelCase. TRQP's names belong to the plain HTTP TRQP binding, so a registry should map to them there, not carry them through every Trust Task.
2. **No validity window.** TRQP v2.0 says `context.time` "MUST be interpreted as the datetime as of which the target authority statement is valid" (`core/identifiers.md:59`). A `TrustRecord` has no validity window to judge that against. Consumers have worked around this: vtc-service stores `activeFrom`/`activeTo` inside the opaque `context`. (Found while fixing affinidi/affinidi-trust-registry-rs#161.)

## What

New versions. The superseded ones stay published and go through the normal deprecation and withdrawal cycle.

| Spec | New | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `registry/_shared` | 0.2 | `TrustRecord`: `entityId`, `authorityId`, `recordType`. New optional `validFrom` (inclusive) and `validUntil` (exclusive). |
| `registry/authorization` | 0.2 | `entityId`, `authorityId`; `time_evaluated` → `evaluatedAt`, `time_requested` → `asOf`. New **Evaluation** section and a **TRQP field names** mapping table. |
| `registry/recognition` | 0.2 | Same as authorization. |
| `registry/record/put` | 0.3 | Renamed record members. Defines the window; `validFrom >= validUntil` → `malformedRequest`. |
| `registry/record/query` | 0.3 | Renamed filters and records; records carry their window. |
| `registry/record/delete` | 0.2 | Renamed members. |
| `registry/did/rotate` | 0.2 | `preRotationCount`, `newScid`, `newVersionId`. |

**Evaluation rules** (authorization and recognition):

- No bounds → the record holds at every instant. Existing records keep working unchanged.
- Evaluation instant outside the window → `authorized` / `recognized` is `false`, and `message` SHOULD say why.
- Evaluating at the registry's own clock (no `context.time`): it MAY start a record up to 60 s before `validFrom`, to absorb clock skew. It MUST NOT extend `validUntil`.
- An explicit `context.time` is evaluated exactly.
- The registry keeps current records, not their history. This is stated in the spec.

`timeEvaluated` / `timeRequested` would break the `<event>At` instant convention, so they are `evaluatedAt` and `asOf`. That also lets the two TRQP allowlist entries in `wire-conventions-allowlist.json` go.

Also:

- Prose links in `git-trust/grant`, `git-trust/revoke` and `vtc/directory/card/publish` moved to the new versions (`npm run fix-stale-references`).
- The new specs carry all four Security & Privacy sub-headings, rather than joining the allowlist.
- Libraries regenerated: Rust (then `cargo fmt --all`), TS, Go and Dart.

## Checks run locally

- `npm run build`: passes; 0 wire-convention or casing violations; the new specs are not on the S&P allowlist.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four libraries agree.
- `npm run check-published-schemas`: no released schema changed.
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`: clean.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features registry`: 89 passed.

## Consumers

The registry implementation (affinidi-trust-registry-rs) and vtc-service move in follow-up PRs, after a `trust-tasks-rs` release carries these modules. The registry will accept both the old and new versions during the transition.

feat(specs): registry/* in lowerCamelCase, with a validity window on trust records (#925)

* feat(specs): registry/* in lowerCamelCase, with a validity window on trust records

New versions of every live registry/* spec move the family from TRQP's
snake_case to the registry-wide lowerCamelCase convention, and give trust
records an optional validity window so a query's `context.time` has
something to be judged against (TRQP v2.0, Identifiers: `time` is "the
datetime as of which the target authority statement is valid").

- registry/_shared 0.2: TrustRecord members entityId, authorityId,
  recordType; new optional validFrom (inclusive) / validUntil (exclusive).
- registry/authorization 0.2, registry/recognition 0.2: entityId,
  authorityId; time_evaluated -> evaluatedAt and time_requested -> asOf,
  per the `<event>At` / `asOf` instant conventions. New Evaluation section:
  outside the window the answer is false; a registry evaluating at its own
  clock MAY start a record up to 60 s before validFrom, never extends
  validUntil, and evaluates an explicit context.time exactly. A TRQP field
  names table gives the mapping a registry applies on the plain HTTP
  TRQP binding.
- registry/record/put 0.3, registry/record/query 0.3,
  registry/record/delete 0.2: renamed members; put defines the window and
  rejects validFrom >= validUntil as malformedRequest.
- registry/did/rotate 0.2: preRotationCount, newScid, newVersionId.

The superseded versions stay published. Stale prose links in git-trust and
vtc/directory/card/publish are moved to the new versions, and the TRQP
instant-name allowlist entries are dropped, since no current spec uses them.
Libraries regenerated.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(ts): regenerate after #929 — the published TrustRecord keeps its name, and registry/_shared/0.2's is TrustRecord_RegistryV0_2

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: vta-service-v0.65.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-vault**: Narrow a vault query to one subject with subjectDid (vault/credentials/query/0.1) ([#2284](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2284))

vault/credentials/query/0.1 gained a `subjectDid` request member
  (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #884, in trust-tasks-rs 0.34): it narrows the other
  constraints to credentials whose subject — the DID a presentation of the
  credential is made as — is that DID. The VTA now honours it, matching the
  stored `subject_did` (Data Integrity `credentialSubject.id`, SD-JWT `sub`).

  It narrows only. On its own it is no filter, so a query naming nothing
  but `subjectDid` is still refused as an enumeration.

  This lets a wallet offer a VTC member-directory verification only the
  credentials bound to the member's DID, which is the only holder the
  VTC accepts.

- **vta**: The voter engine keeps no clear member-to-cast pairing, and pnm takes the ticket in its own run ([#2278](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2278))

Two privacy gaps from the community-voting threat model (CONVENTIONS §5 item 3, §6 items 3–4):

  - The VTA's voter record kept the member-signed ticket request beside every cast's board leaf
    hash, readable without the seed, and never discarded either. The member's documents and the
    blinded request now go once the ticket is held; leaf hashes and receipts are wrapped under the
    seed in their own secret (`voter-casts:`). The storage sweeper discards the ticket when voting
    closes and the record, casts and receipts `RECEIPT_RETENTION` (30 days) later, with the voter
    key's path. Nothing is audited: a row naming the election would be the pairing VTI-VOT-100
    forbids.
  - `pnm elections vote` took the ticket and cast in one run, so the community and the ballot box
    could pair them by their clocks. `pnm elections ticket` is now its own step; `vote` with no
    ticket held takes one and stops unless given `--now`.

- **vta**: Did:scid:vh:1 identities, create/1.2, and VTA/VTC presentation config ([#2257](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2257))

* feat(vta-sdk): did:scid:vh:1 identity rules and did:scid secret kids (VTI-KEY-160 to VTI-KEY-164)

- **vta**: Operation budgets for Trust Task work (VTI-TRN-029) ([#2264](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2264))

* feat(vta)!: operation budgets for Trust Task work (VTI-TRN-029)

  A VTA offered more Trust Task work than it can serve stops answering in
  time; on a TEE appliance health checks then fail and the watchdog restarts
  the enclave. Three budgets now bound that work, each unset by default:

  - operation_rate_limit_per_sec (+ _burst): the whole appliance, shared by
    REST, DIDComm and TSP.
  - operation_rate_limit_per_subject_per_sec: each client with standing, by
    its DID, charged before the appliance budget.
  - operation_rate_limit_unauthenticated_per_sec: DIDComm / TSP senders
    without an ACL entry (login steps, public tasks, counterparties,
    approvers, refusals), apart from the clients' budget. Past it there is no
    reply, so a flood cannot cost a signature per message.

  A task is charged its weight in signs (vault release 2, DID create and
  delete 10, others 1), after authentication and before it runs. REST
  answers 429 with x-rate-limit-source: vta and scope operations or
  operations-subject; DIDComm and TSP a signed, retryable unavailable with
  retryAfter. A refused document is not recorded (VTI-OPS-026), so a resend
  is a retry.

  The keys are config and tenant-overlay only, never config/patch, so a TEE
  enclave restart keeps them. A zero is refused at load. pnm and cnm explain
  operations and operations-subject refusals.

- **rooms**: Record provenance, record retention and prune, and the epoch floor ([#2272](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2272))

* feat(rooms)!: a record says what kind of claim it is and when it lapses — rooms/records/put 0.3 and provenance in the sealed body

- **vta**: Vault/credentials/present — present a held credential to a verifier the client names ([#2265](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2265))

Serves vault/credentials/present/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #871): the VTA
  presents a credential from its principal's vault to the audience the
  client names, bound to the client's nonce, as the persona the
  credential is held by. A Data Integrity credential is wrapped in a VP
  signed by the holder; an SD-JWT-VC is presented with a kb-jwt naming
  the audience and nonce, disclosing only the requested claims. A request
  that would disclose more than it names is refused wouldOverDisclose
  unless the client allows it.

  Gated on the new credentialPresent capability, classified in
  retry_safety, audited at the dispatch spine, and guarded in vta-mcp
  like the other vault writes. Bumps trust-tasks-rs to 0.33.2, whose
  record_expiry now includes the skew allowance; the retention test
  expects that bound.

- **pnm**: Select the TEE claim key by its DID, not by slug ([#2207](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2207))

* feat(pnm): select the TEE claim key by its DID, not by slug

  The claim DID is minted before the VTA exists, so no slug can be known then.
  `claim-did create` stores the key under its DID and `bootstrap connect
  --claim-did` selects it; `--slug` only names the VTA locally (default: the
  VTA DID's tail). A malformed or unknown claim DID is refused before any
  network call, and the not-found error no longer suggests minting a new claim
  DID, which the VTA would not accept.

  Older command lines keep working: without `--claim-did`, connect uses the key
  stored under the slug, as earlier pnm did; with it, a slug-keyed key is used
  only if it holds that DID. `claim-did create/show/discard --slug` stay as
  hidden flags.

  A VTA whose enclave predates vta-service 0.63 cannot parse the v2 claim and
  answers 422; connect now says so and names the workaround.

- **vta**: Star a directory member whose DID you have not been shown — persona/contact/put/1.1 linking form ([#2255](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2255))
- **voting**: Pnm elections trustee, vta/pcs/trustee/read, end-to-end tests over a mediator, and the voting service guide ([#2248](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2248))

* feat(voting): pnm elections trustee {status,step} — a trustee runs its round from the command line; vta/pcs/trustee/read (trust-tasks-tf #855)

  Nothing drove a trustee's part in a sealed or tallied-encrypted election: the VTA served every
  step, but no client carried them, and on a private board a trustee's client could not even read
  the election — the trustee tasks take its manifest, and the reads are answered only to a party
  signing as a trustee, whose key the VTA holds.

  - vta/pcs/trustee/read: the VTA signs voting/trustees/status or voting/election/show as the
    trustee, addressed to the ballot box, and nothing else. pcsTrustee; RetrySafe; not audited
    (it keeps nothing), as voter/read is not.
  - The ballot box answers voting/election/show to every trustee the manifest names on any board.
  - pnm elections trustee step <id> [--watch]: reads both, then takes every step the ceremony needs
    of this trustee now — enrol, deal, confirm (with any justifications), answer complaints against
    its dealing, keep its key share, decrypt after close — carrying each signed document to the
    ballot box's HTTPS door. Idempotent; --watch repeats every 30 s until the result is out.
    `status` shows where the ceremony stands.
  - Temporary [patch.crates-io] onto #855's branch until it is released.

- **vta**: A contact's star, petname, lists and directory link — persona/contact/*/1.1 and persona/contact/lists/*/1.0 ([#2245](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2245))

The VTA side of the member directory's personal layer (P3): what a member
  keeps *about* other people — a star, a petname, their own lists, a link to the
  community directory entry a contact was met through — lives in their own VTA,
  never at a community, so no operator holds the graph of who watches whom.

  - `persona/contact/put/1.1`: a filing may carry annotation changes, applied
    with it or not at all; the annotating form (`contactId`, no document) changes
    them without appending a revision or moving `rev`. Each annotation given
    replaces, each `removeX` removes, `lists` replaces the set; a list the
    context does not hold is `listUnknown` and changes nothing; an unchanged
    request answers `annotationsChanged: false` and writes nothing. Petnames and
    notes are kept exactly as written.
  - `persona/contact/get/1.1`: the current annotations with any revision, `lists`
    naming only lists that still exist.
  - `persona/contact/list/1.1`: `starred` always, `petname`, `lists`,
    `directoryRef` and the contact's own `displayName` (never the DID or the
    petname); filters `knownByPersona`, `changedSince`, `starred`, `listId`
    (`listUnknown`), `directoryVtcDid`; a stable order and a cursor bound to the
    filters (`cursorInvalid`).
  - `persona/contact/lists/{put,list,show,delete}/1.0`: names unique in the
    context, compared exactly (`nameTaken`), at most 256 (`tooManyLists` with
    its limit); listed by order then name with contact counts; deleting one takes
    it off every contact in one batch, revising none, echoing nothing.
  - Storage (`vta_persona::annotations`): annotations beside the contact
    (`pca:`), lists `pcl:`, both context-scoped and in the persona keyspace (so
    backed up); deleting a contact discards its annotations. No petname, note or
    list name reaches a log or the audit trail.

- **voting**: Community voting — polls, surveys and elections with blind tickets, a separate ballot box and trustee-encrypted levels (VTI-VOT-001 – 100) ([#2239](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2239))

* feat(voting): vti-voting, PCS voting tickets, casts and the ballot box

  Phase 0 of community voting (design: community voting, draft VTI-VOT-*):
  the cryptographic core on the Predicate Credential System, no wire types
  until the voting/* Trust Task family is specified.

  - registrar: the community's voting helper key, under its own deployment
    label (`<community>#voting-pcs`) and key-derivation info, so it is never
    the vetting key. Issues tickets blind under `voter/<election>`,
    sequentially under one lock.
  - voter: a fresh key per election, the blinded ticket request, the cast:
    `attest_in_context` for a hash-to-curve election point, with the
    community, election, manifest digest and ballot bytes bound into the
    context (VOT-012).
  - ballot_box: verifies on the published `hvk` alone (VOT-007); the tag is
    the per-election nullifier, recorded once under the revote rule
    (VOT-002) through an atomic NullifierStore.

  Measured (examples/scale.rs, 500 voters, release, M5 Max): issuance
  2.0 ms (~500/s per VTC), cast 3.2 ms, admit 3.0 ms (~330/s per core),
  recount 0.21 ms per ballot on 18 threads (~1 min for 300,000); a cast's
  attestation is 248 bytes compressed.

  publish = false until its first published consumer.

- **vta**: VtaPin and remoteApprover UV keys for wallet sign-in ([#2228](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2228))

Browser wallets without a PRF passkey could not approve auth/oob/grant.
  Two new UV key kinds:

  - vtaPin: the browser enrols K = PBKDF2(PIN) as verifier; a grant is
    approved by a transport-key decision plus HMAC-SHA256(K,
    "org.openvtc.uv-pin/v1|" + D), checked in constant time against a
    persisted, CAS-updated guess limit (5 wrong -> 15 min lock, doubling
    to 24 h, reset on success). Refusals oobUvPinWrong (attemptsRemaining)
    and oobUvLocked (lockedUntil). Replacing a PIN on heartbeat requires
    ext org.openvtc.uv-key-change.pinProof. The verifier is never returned,
    audited or logged (PinVerifier redacts Debug).
  - remoteApprover: the grant is approved on the member's phone. The VTA
    raises a task-consent request bound to the enrolled approver and the
    grant digest (PendingTaskConsent::bound_approver), pushes the signed
    task-consent/request/0.1, and answers oobUvPending (matchCode,
    expiresAt) until the phone's task-consent/decision/0.1 approves;
    oobUvDeclined / oobUvExpired otherwise. The approver must be
    designated by the operator (the device's stepUpApprover or an
    approver-set member), not created by the device. Candidates are
    listed via heartbeat ext org.openvtc.uv-approvers.

- **vta**: Rooms/keys/act/0.6 — completes vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3, so a member collects the renewals of the rooms they hold ([#2226](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2226))

* build: trust-tasks-rs 0.32.6, which carries vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3 and rooms/keys/act/0.6 (trust-tasks-tf #843)

- **vta**: A PRF-sealed UV key for wallet sign-in approvals (`prfSealedKey`) ([#2208](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2208))

The VTA signs an auth/oob/grant only on a task-consent/decision made by the
  device's enrolled UV key. Two kinds existed: a phone's biometric-gated
  hardware key, which signs the decision itself, and a WebAuthn passkey, whose
  assertion the device's transport key carries as evidence. The browser plugin
  used the second, which needs its own ES256 credential beside the wallet's PRF
  unlock passkey — on Chrome on Linux, a security key and three PIN rounds.

- **vta-sdk**: The vtc-group built-in DID template, a community group's own identity ([#2206](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2206))

`vtc/groups/create` has the community's VTA mint each group a DID of its own,
  which then issues the group's membership credentials under an authorization
  credential from the community. `vtc-group` is that identity's shape.

  It is a did:webvh with a signing key (assertion and authentication) and a
  key-agreement key. It has no service, because nothing delivers messages to a
  group yet; group messaging will add one by a DID update. It has no name,
  description or label, so resolving the DID says nothing about the group. It
  requires `WEBVH_SERVER`; `WITNESSES` is optional. Its methods are numbered from
  `#key-1`, and the key records follow the document, as the `room` template's do.

- **vta**: Keys/sign-document — a Data Integrity proof made only as the DID a document names ([#2200](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2200))

The VTA now serves keys/sign-document/0.1: an eddsa-jcs-2022 proof over a JSON document from a key that never leaves the VTA. It is what lets a member whose key their agent holds sign their external directory card (vtc/directory/card/publish, whose card names the membership DID as `issuer` for exactly this), and it is how a producer issues a credential as a DID without holding its key.

  The checks run in the specification's order:
  1. The `sign-document` capability. `sign` is not accepted in its place, because this VTA frames keys/sign payloads and a `sign` grant was never given with an issuer binding.
  2. The document's own checks: `proofPresent`; `documentInvalid` for `noSigner`, `signerMalformed` or `notCanonicalizable` (integers beyond 2^53 are refused, not rounded).
  3. The key: in scope, active, Ed25519.
  4. The issuer binding. The key must be a verification method of the DID the document names in `issuer` or `controller` (`issuerMismatch`), listed under the requested purpose (`purposeNotAuthorized`).
  5. `created` within five minutes of the VTA's clock.

  The signer DID's document is never taken from the request. A did:key's is read from the identifier, a did:peer's derived from it (`persona::own_document`), a did:webvh this VTA minted read from its own log, and anything else resolved.

  The VTA builds the proof configuration and the 64 bytes of hash data itself (`sign_formats`), with the document's @context, and `challenge` and `domain` when they are given. It signs those bytes as ProtocolDefined through the same chokepoint as keys/sign, so scope, signing policy and quota apply. The audit row names signer, method, purpose, the document's id and type, and the SHA-256 of the hash data, never the document.

- **rooms**: Rooms/owner/group/add 0.3 and renew 0.2 settle a pending removal like remove 0.3 (trust-tasks-tf #824) ([#2197](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2197))
- Growth types in published crates are #[non_exhaustive] ([#2196](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2196))

A new variant on a public enum, or a new field on a public struct a consumer
  can build with a literal, is a breaking change in a published crate. It kept
  happening on types that were always going to grow (#1231, #1234, #1244, #1247,
  #1250); #1262 fixed it for Capability and AuditEvent only.

  This marks the rest once. 143 enums are marked: every error and refusal enum
  (VtaError, AppError, ...) and the growth vocabularies (kinds, statuses,
  reasons, codes, transports, SealedPayloadV1). 32 structs are marked: config
  and response bags that no caller builds with a literal. Adding the attribute
  is itself breaking, once. After it, additions to these types are minor
  changes.

  Left exhaustive on purpose, and pinned that way by the census:
  VerifiedAssertion, AssertionProof, ActScope, ApproveScope, ContextDirection,
  SigningDomain, TokenStatus and Role. For each of these, every arm must be
  considered, and a downstream wildcard would be the bug.

  Every downstream match in the workspace gets a `_ =>` arm that takes the most
  restrictive or most generic reading: an internal error, a hidden or refused
  entry, a stale attribute. None is unreachable!().

  vta-sdk/tests/non_exhaustive_census.rs fails on a public enum in a published
  library crate whose name ends in Error, Refusal, Violation, Kind, Event,
  Status, Capability, Reason or Code and that is not #[non_exhaustive], unless
  it is listed as deliberately exhaustive with a reason. It also fails when a
  listed enum gains the attribute or disappears.

- **vtc**: The member portal's directory — signing delegated by auth/oob 0.2 ([#2190](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2190))

A member reads the directory and edits their own card from the portal, signed
  by the browser's sign-in key the member lets act for them in the directory for
  that session (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #820, auth/oob/grant/0.2).



### Documentation

- Move per-flow detail out of the workspace CLAUDE.md ([#2263](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2263))

The workspace CLAUDE.md had grown to 155k characters, loaded into every
  session. It is now 39.9k, under Claude Code's 40k warning.

  - The 38 integration-flow entries move verbatim to the CLAUDE.md of the
    crate that owns them (vta-service, vtc-service, vti-witness), which
    loads when working in that crate. The root keeps an index naming every
    flow and where it lives.
  - The versioning, test-suite and CI sections move verbatim to
    docs/04-reference/workspace-engineering-notes.md; the root keeps the
    rules and the CI command block.
  - The longest crate-map rows (vti-voting, vti-voting-service, vta-mcp,
    vti-witness) move to new crate CLAUDE.md files; the hot-spots list
    moves to vta-service/CLAUDE.md.
  - Rationale and incident history elsewhere is shortened; no rule is
    dropped.



### Fixed

- **vta**: Say why the offline dids edit could not publish, and what to run instead ([#2275](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2275))

* fix(vta): say why the offline dids edit could not publish, and what to run instead

  `vta did-mgmt dids edit` holds no mediator session, so the outbound seam
  can initiate REST and nothing else. Against a DID host whose document
  advertises only `TSPTransport` and `DIDCommMessaging` (what a host
  provisioned through a VTA with a mediator gets) it stopped with
  `publish error: publish_did: no transport in common with ...: it
  advertises [tsp, didcomm] and this agent can initiate [rest]`, and left
  the operator to work out that the new log entry was already committed
  locally and that the running VTA is the one that can publish it.

  The offline command now keeps that commit (it persists the store before
  returning, as the success path does) and prints what happened and the
  fix: the entry is pending, the running VTA re-publishes it before its
  next update of the DID, and the command to make the change there is
  `pnm did-mgmt dids edit --did <did> --document <file> --no-confirm`.
  When the publish error is the no-transport refusal it also explains the
  HTTPS-only reach of the offline command and what the host would have to
  advertise (`TrustTaskHTTPS`, or `WebVHHosting` at an https:// origin).
  The hint keys on the text `NoMatchingProtocol` renders; a test pins
  that coupling.

  Three doc comments said the offline seam "falls to DIDComm" when no TSP
  socket is held (`Outbound::from_parts`, `WebvhDeps::tsp`,
  `bootstrap_cli`). That is true of a DIDComm handler, which holds the
  live bridge, and false of the offline CLI and the wizards, which hold a
  signing-only bridge. They now say so.

  `docs/03-vtc/community-lifecycle.md` gains the `TrustRegistry` referral
  entry as a worked example of a post-mint document change, and a note on
  what the offline command can and cannot publish to.

- **vta**: Register the vsock REST listener with AsyncFd::register (tokio 1.54) ([#2276](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2276))

tokio 1.54 deprecates AsyncFd::new as unsound (RUSTSEC-2026-0386): its safe
  constructor accepts any AsRawFd. The listener owns its descriptor for its
  whole life, which is register's contract, so the all-features build stops
  tripping -D deprecated.

- **vta**: Bound each client and unauthenticated peers by default (VTI-TRN-029) ([#2274](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2274))

VTI-TRN-029 is a MUST: a node bounds what any one subject can consume, and
  bounds unauthenticated peers separately. The operation budgets shipped unset,
  so a VTA nobody sized met neither clause. The per-client share now defaults to
  100 operations a second and the budget for DIDComm / TSP senders without
  standing to 50; there is no setting that turns either off, and a higher value
  loosens them. The appliance budget stays unset by default: its right value is
  a property of the hardware.

  The budgets read an injectable clock (`BudgetClock`), so their tests run on a
  manual clock that does not refill while they run, rather than racing the
  monotonic one. Two tests that send more than the default share in under a
  second (every dispatched verb from one stranger; filling the contact-list cap)
  size the budget they need.

- **voting**: Trustees and voters act only on signed steps, the community authorizes decryption, the key needs t dealers, ballots bind their tag ([#2254](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2254))

* chore(deps)!: trust-tasks-rs 0.33, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.38, affinidi-tdk 0.29 and the mediator 0.44 crates; an mdoc presentation binds the OpenID4VP 1.0 handover

  The release train behind trust-tasks-rs 0.33 (affinidi-tdk-rs #963, affinidi-messaging-mediator
  #25). These versions move together because the messaging SDK's public API carries
  `trust_tasks_rs` types, so the workspace takes them in one step:
  - trust-tasks-rs 0.33.1, which carries the voting hardening specifications of trust-tasks-tf
    #860;
  - the trust-tasks-* transport crates at 0.33;
  - affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.38;
  - affinidi-tdk 0.29;
  - affinidi-messaging-mediator-{admin,tui} and affinidi-messaging-test-mediator 0.44.

  affinidi-tdk 0.29 re-exports affinidi-mdoc 0.4 (affinidi-tdk-rs #961), which implements
  OpenID4VP 1.0 Final's mdoc handover (Appendix B.2.6.1): `[client_id, nonce, jwk_thumbprint,
  response_uri]`. That replaces ISO 18013-7's `mdocGeneratedNonce`. A DeviceAuth signed over the
  old handover verifies at no 1.0 verifier, so the holder's `Oid4vpSession` changes shape:

  - **Breaking (vta-sdk):** `mdoc_generated_nonce` is removed. In its place is an optional
    `jwk_thumbprint`, the base64url SHA-256 thumbprint (RFC 7638) of the key the verifier
    encrypts its `direct_post.jwt` response to. It is absent for an unencrypted response, which
    the handover encodes as CBOR `null`. The field has no specification of its own and nothing in
    the workspace sent it.
  - A new test checks that the DeviceAuth verifies against exactly that transcript, and against
    none without the thumbprint or with another nonce.

  The test mediator 0.44 still asks for affinidi-tdk 0.28, so dev builds hold that copy beside
  0.29. Both share one messaging SDK and one trust-tasks-rs, and nothing passes a type between
  them.

- **vta**: Offline did-mgmt commands sign what they send a DID-hosting server ([#2251](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2251))

* fix(vta): offline did-mgmt commands sign what they send a DID-hosting server

  `vta did-mgmt dids create --server <id>` (and the offline publish, register
  and delete paths) always failed with "could not sign the DID-management task
  with this VTA's operational key", however the VTA was configured. Every
  document sent to a DID-hosting server carries this VTA's proof, and the signer
  is installed on the DIDComm bridge only when the daemon starts; the offline
  CLI handed the operation a bare placeholder bridge with no signer.

  The offline commands now build `DIDCommBridge::signing_only`: a placeholder
  that signs as this VTA with the key the daemon signs with
  (`{vta_did}#key-0`, read from the same store through the new
  `operations::credentials::load_vta_issuer_secret_from_store`). With no
  mediator session the request reaches the host over its HTTPS endpoint, where
  the proof is the whole of the authentication.

  A signing key that will not load is a warning, not an error, so a local-only
  delete, which signs nothing, still works as a break-glass. A VTA with no
  `vta_did` keeps the bare placeholder, and the hosting client still refuses it
  by name before anything is signed.

  * test(vta): sign a push/wake document in the offline-bridge tests, not a new Trust Task literal

  The fixture named did/check-name/0.1, a URI vta-service produces with no
  published schema, which produced_census rightly flags. push_wake_document is a
  document this VTA already produces and the census already accounts for.

- **rooms**: A room host's DID advertises TrustTaskHTTPS, and rooms/create accepts retentionPolicy ([#2247](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2247))

Found setting up a room from the wallet's console, which stopped at step 2 for
  a host minted from the room-host template.

  - The room-host template published its rooms/* surface as VTARest. A room host
    is not a VTA; the HTTPS binding's service type is TrustTaskHTTPS, which is
    what every Trust Task client — the wallet's console included — looks for, so
    the console found no endpoint and refused to continue. The VTA's own sender
    reads either; this makes the template say the right thing. Hosts minted from
    the old template need their DID updated.
  - rooms/create/0.1 declares retentionPolicy (and ext), and rooms/owner/register
    0.2 forwards retentionPolicy, but both hosts parsed rooms/create into a
    hand-written type with deny_unknown_fields that had neither — so any room
    registered with a retention policy was refused as malformed, and the policy
    was hard-coded to chained. CreateRoomBody gains both members and room-host
    and the VTC store the owner's choice (chained when absent); a fromJoin room
    then refuses epoch links, as it already would.
  - data-rooms §8.1: --listen is opt-in and when it is needed, enrolment and the
    scoped admin grant room-host prints, the TrustTaskHTTPS endpoint, and that a
    private room is not served yet.

- **audit**: Bounded chain-head recovery and paged audit readers ([#2229](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2229))

* fix(audit): bounded chain-head recovery and paged audit readers

  Chain-head recovery read the whole audit keyspace to find one row, which
  cannot work over vsock where the result must fit a single 16 MiB frame.
  Recovery now scans the newest rows under the writer's own prefix, falling
  back to a bounded deep scan only while a legacy log is being migrated, and
  failing closed rather than silently re-anchoring.

  Adds `ScanOpts` / `KeyspaceHandle::scan_raw` (a bounded, directional read
  with an exclusive resume key) across both backends, and `OP_SCAN` on the
  enclave proxy with the usual capability negotiation. `ScanPager` decides its
  strategy once per walk, so a proxy that cannot bound a read is asked for the
  range once rather than once per page.

  Audit verification and listing walk through the pager instead of
  materialising the keyspace.

- **rooms**: A read catches up on missed commits and the room's history before refusing; the portal says why a record will not open ([#2231](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2231))

In any room with more than two members, every membership change left every other
  member a commit behind, and every new member held nothing sealed before they
  joined. The only repairs were `pnm rooms keys commit --host` and `pnm rooms keys
  backfill`, by hand, and the wallet and member portal ran neither, so records showed
  "Did not open" in both directions.

  rooms/keys/read now repairs before it refuses (trust-tasks-tf #848, amending the
  read/0.1 draft): it fetches and applies the commits the host relays for a newer
  epoch, or fetches the epoch links for an older one, from the same host, as the same
  persona, under the same read grant, at most once per read, never for a removed
  member. It is serialised per member, and waiters time out rather than queue behind a
  wedged host (R1.3). What still does not open is the declared
  rooms/keys/read:cannotOpen with details.{epoch, reason}, not malformedRequest, and
  read and backfill answer the declared hostUnreachable / hostRefused.

  Member portal: a record that does not open says why in plain words; a joined room
  has one way to open it (a direct link once shared, else "Open it here…" through
  the wallet, then straight to the room) instead of two buttons and a red
  "Joined" box.

- **vtc,vta**: Creating a community group no longer fails "addTspService: this document names no DIDComm mediator" ([#2230](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2230))

`vtc/groups/create` failed against a VTA whose stack and mediator carry TSP. The
  VTA refused the group's mint `malformedRequest` with: addTspService: this document
  names no DIDComm mediator. Two defects met:

  - The VTC asked for the group's identity without saying anything about
    transports. The `vtc-group` template carries no service: nothing delivers
    messages to a group yet. The mint now says so explicitly
    (`addMediatorService: false`, `addTspService: false`).
  - The VTA turned its own default into a demand. A caller that names no
    `addTspService` gets whatever this VTA and its mediator can carry ([#1652](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1652)), and
    for a rendered template that answer reached `with_tsp_in_rendered_document`
    as if the caller had asked. That path refuses a document with no DIDComm
    mediator, which is right when the caller asked for `#tsp` and wrong when
    nobody did. Only an explicit request refuses now; a defaulted one mints the
    document as rendered.



### Chore

- **deps**: TSP 1.0 and trust-tasks-rs 0.34 (affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.40, affinidi-tdk 0.32, mediator 0.45) ([#2282](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2282))

title: fix(ts): a published shared-component name never changes when a new shape appears (#929)
body:
fix(ts): a published shared-component name never changes when a new shape appears (#929)

The TS generator hoists every cross-file `$def` into one declaration and
names it from scratch each run: a name with one shape is bare, a name with
several is qualified with every shape's family and version. Adding a new
`_shared` version that changes a definition therefore renamed the
already-published one. Adding `registry/_shared/0.2` turned every exported
`TrustRecord` into `TrustRecord_RegistryV0_1` and removed
`SharedComponents.TrustRecord`, so `ts API compatibility` failed an
additive spec change (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#925).

The generator now records the name it gives each component in
`trust-tasks-ts/component-names.lock.json` and reuses it. Only a component
without a recorded name is named by the old rules, so a new shape beside
a published bare name is the one that gets qualified. With no lock the
rules are unchanged, which is how the lock was seeded: regenerating `main`
with it produces no change under `src/`.

The drift job now diffs the lock with `src/`, so a regeneration that
names something new has to commit it. The lock is outside `src/` and not
in the package's `files`, so it is not published.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

**Every hand-written use of a due version moves to its successor**, in all four languages — test specimens, smoke tests, examples, doc examples, READMEs, GETTING-STARTED. What a test pinned is kept, re-anchored where the property no longer exists in the old version's form:

- The `extends` routing tests use the current version against a fictional successor (any real older version is itself due within a quarter).
- Shared cross-language proof fixtures are byte-identical; examples consume them as JSON.
- Every `#[allow(deprecated)]` / `deprecated_member_use` ignore added only for those specimens is gone.

**`trust-task-discovery` 0.3** (additive): `trust-tasks-rs` `DiscoveryRegistry::respond_to_v0_3` plus acceptance-window builders (`acceptance_window`, `acceptance_window_from(&FreshnessPolicy)` — rounded down so the claim is never wider than what is enforced); `trust-tasks-https` `with_discovery`/`enable_discovery` serve 0.3, `enable_discovery` stating the server's own freshness window; `trust_tasks_https` (Dart) `enableDiscovery` likewise. **0.1/0.2 support is kept until the batch**, in blocks opened by `// --- trust-task-discovery 0.1 / 0.2 (superseded)` and closed by `// --- end` (Rust: `discovery/superseded.rs`, `server/superseded_discovery.rs` and their `mod` lines; Dart: marked blocks in `server.dart` and its test). The batch deletes them; each language was trialled with every due version withdrawn and the blocks deleted, and builds and tests clean.

**Withdrawal readiness** (`scripts/check-withdrawal-readiness.mjs`, own workflow, per PR + push + weekly): lists every hand-written import of a version due in the next batch — a warning until 30 days before it, a failure inside that window; `(superseded)` blocks are listed as the batch's deletions, never failed on. title: feat(codegen): every specification version is published as a content-addressed registry bundle, with an index
body:
Milestone 1 of consumer-side generation (design: #927, whose doc this branch carries too and which drops out on rebase if #927 merges first).

`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen -- --bundles <dir>` (`npm run build-bundles`) writes `<dir>/<slug>/<M.N>/bundle.json` for every version (withdrawn included, `trust-task-error` excluded — modelled by hand in every runtime) and `<dir>/index.json`, in ~1.3 s. deploy.yml runs it into `website/specs`, so they are served at `https://trusttasks.org/specs/<slug>/<M.N>/bundle.json` and `/specs/index.json` (`/specs/` is already an asset prefix; no CloudFront change).

**Same code paths as generation.** The inlining/response-wrapping in `generate_one` and the eight policy readers are factored into `spec_schemas()` and `read_spec_policy()`, called by both — so a bundle's `schema`/`responseSchema` are by construction the generated module's `PAYLOAD_SCHEMA`s. A test runs `generate_one` on five varied specs and asserts both schemas, every policy const, `DEPRECATION`, `EXTENDS` and the digest agree.

**Canonical and content-addressed.** Compact JSON, keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit, JCS string escaping; `digest = sha256:<hex>` of the file bytes. Deterministic (two full runs, byte-identical trees).

**Independent check.** `scripts/check-bundles.mjs` (`npm run check-bundles`, run in deploy) verifies every digest and canonical form, that the index lists exactly the bundles on disk, and that each bundle's schemas agree with the *TypeScript* generator's — independent of the Rust one. A tampered byte and an unindexed bundle are both caught.

Regenerating all four libraries is drift-free; codegen tests (39), clippy, fmt and actionlint pass. Sizes: 1,121 bundles, 14.6 MB total, 13 KB average, 57 KB max; index 350 KB.

The design doc now records four things building this settled for milestone 2: carry the authored member order (digest over JCS, not file bytes), an append-only by-digest store, a per-slug index at scale, and resolving `supersededBy`.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.34.2` → `0.35.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.34.2` → `0.35.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.34.2` → `0.35.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.34.2` → `0.35.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.34.2` → `0.35.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.34.2` → `0.35.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.34.2` → `0.35.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.34.2` → `0.35.0` | breaking |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.27.5` → `0.27.6` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.9.6`) | `0.9.5` → `0.9.6` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.5` → `0.9.6` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_proof` | pub.dev | `0.1.3` → `0.1.4` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_https` | pub.dev | `0.1.3` → `0.1.4` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_didcomm` | pub.dev | `0.1.1` → `0.1.2` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps follow the commit subjects; an undeclared API break in
any of them is refused on its pull request by that language's API compatibility
check, as `cargo-semver-checks` refuses one in the crates here.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat: did:scid signers, VTCs and bridge identities
body:
did:scid in VGI (spec trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#75).

- vgi-core / verify-trust: `Signed-by-DID` keeps a did:scid's `?src=` so verifiers can resolve it; `same_signer` / `signer_identity`; registry queried with the bare identity.
- vgi-cli: `--vtc/--owner/--registry` accept a did:scid DID URL whose only query is `src`; bare did:scid refused.
- did-git-sign `init --did-method/--scid-also-known-as` via `create_did_webvh_presented`; signs as did:scid only when the log lists the alias.
- vgi-bridge `setup --did-method/--scid-also-known-as`; keys, ages, reconcile matched by identity; Trust Task proofs name the key in the issuer's form.

**Dependencies (all published):** vta-sdk 0.73, affinidi-tdk 0.32, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.40, trust-tasks-rs / trust-tasks-proof 0.34.2, affinidi-did-common 0.4.4 (`scid` module), affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.43 (native did:scid), didwebvh-rs 0.8.2, affinidi-messaging-test-mediator 0.45. Workspace version 0.24.0 -> 0.25.0 (`bridge.example.toml` pins v0.25.0).

**Known split:** trql-client 0.27, still the registry's latest release, requires trust-tasks ^0.32. verify-trust's `TrqlTransport` impls name its `TrustTask` through a `trust-tasks-trql` alias, as was done for the 0.56 move. No trust-tasks type crosses into vta-sdk or the bridge, and did-git-sign has no trql-client edge. The alias goes when a trql-client on trust-tasks 0.34 is published.

Also: one collapsible_match clippy fix (clippy 1.99) in did-git-sign's provisioning event loop.

Tests: `cargo test --workspace --all-features`: 842 passed, 0 failed. fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`, default and all features) and `cargo audit --deny warnings` are clean.

title: feat: did:scid signers, VTCs and bridge identities (#168)
body:
feat: did:scid signers, VTCs and bridge identities (#168)

* feat: a did:scid signer claim keeps its src locator; signers compare by identity

A did:scid:vh:1 identity is the DID; its ?src= is where its log is found
(VTI-KEY-160). The Signed-by-DID claim used to drop every query, so a
did:scid signer's claim reached verify-trust as a bare DID that a
stranger's resolver holds no source for, and every commit it signed was
UnresolvedSigner.

vgi_core::signer_did now keeps a did:scid's ?src= (only when it is the
sole query) and strips everything else as before. same_signer compares two
claims by identity, which conflicting_signer_dids, did-git-sign's
committer guard and the bridge's re-sign checks use, so a trailer with
?src= and a committer without it agree. A did:scid and the did:webvh of
its log stay different signers (VTI-KEY-164). verify-trust asks the
registry about the bare identity, for the signer and the VTC alike.

vgi-core takes affinidi-did-common (default features off) for the rule,
which needs 0.4.4 (the scid module).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

nothing else, and a bare did:scid:vh:1 is refused with a message naming
the form to give (VTI-KEY-163). Every other DID is held to the DID-core
production as before.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(did-git-sign): sign as a did:scid identity, and choose how a new DID is presented

init gains --did-method (webvh|scid) and --scid-also-known-as. A DID
created there goes through vta/webvh/dids/create 1.2 when either is
given. A DID signs as its did:scid identity when asked, or when its
context's primary DID is that did:scid; the key id is then given with
the ?src= a verifier needs (did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=…#key-N). Signing
as did:scid refuses a log that does not list the alias (VTI-KEY-166).

DiagStatus need (verifiable-trust-infrastructure #2196).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

setup gains --did-method and --scid-also-known-as for a DID minted into
the bridge's context (vta/webvh/dids/create 1.2 when either is given). A
bridge presented as did:scid is addressed by its DID URL with ?src=.

method ids and exports secrets under the bare did:scid, and the resolved
document lists keys under the bare DID (VTI-KEY-161). Key fingerprints,
key ages, reconcile and listed_keys now match by the bare identity and map
log-named records to their did:scid ids. Trust Task proofs and the
Signed-by-DID trailer name the signing key with the identity's ?src=, so
issuer and verificationMethod are in one form (VTI-KEY-163); DIDComm
secrets keep the document's bare ids. Also adds the wildcard arm vta-sdk's
#[non_exhaustive] DiagStatus needs (#2196).

The end-to-end proof test is ignored until trust-tasks-proof ships the
did:scid src fix (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf 6c893c09e).

`VtaEvent::Connected`; the pattern moves into the match arm.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

vta-sdk 0.73 is the release that admits a did:scid identity, which
did-git-sign and the bridge now sign as. It is on trust-tasks 0.34,
affinidi-tdk 0.32 and affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.40 (TSP 1.0), so those

module), affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.43 (native did:scid),
didwebvh-rs 0.8.2, trust-tasks-proof 0.34.2 and the test mediator 0.45.

title: ci(release): the npm, Go and Dart APIs are checked on every pull request, and a spec-scoped ! no longer makes them breaking
body:
Rust has `cargo-semver-checks`; TypeScript, Go and Dart had nothing, so an undeclared API break shipped as a patch — and, the other way round, their bump scripts counted **any** `!`, so `feat(vault)!:` (#919) and `fix(codegen)!:` (#917, the Rust generator) were about to make the next npm, Go and Dart releases MINORs with no API change in them.

**Scope-aware bumps.** `release-bump-{ts,go,dart}.sh` count a `!` only when its scope list names that package (`ts`, `go`, `dart`, their `-bindings`, or a sibling's own scope), when it is unscoped, or on a `BREAKING CHANGE` trailer — the rule commit-lint now enforces on new titles. On the real history the next Go release becomes a patch, which apidiff confirms is right.

**An API compatibility job per language**, comparing the PR with the last published release (all three pass on main):
- **Go** — `golang.org/x/exp/cmd/apidiff` over every package of the core module against the last `trust-tasks-go/v*` tag (~10–25 s). Generated schema-text, `Deprecation`, `Extends` and `Version` constant values move by design and are not counted.
- **TypeScript** — `@microsoft/api-extractor` (pinned devDependency) over every `.d.ts` against the published npm tarball (~1 min, ~5 GB peak, run per side). A value appended to a string union or to `STANDARD_CODES` is compatible by policy — the unions stay closed so a misspelled value remains a compile error (codes.ts records why widening was rejected).
- **Dart** — `dart_apitool` (pinned, with the SDK it runs on) over the runtime and every generated library against pub.dev (~1–2 min). Two tool defects (extension types dropped, typedefs crashing the diff) are worked around by rewriting both sides identically; see the script header.

**One verdict rule in all three:** a break passes only if the title has a `!` scoped to that package (the withdrawal batch's `feat(rs, ts, go, dart)!:` qualifies) or a change merged since the release already made the next one breaking by the bump script's own scoped rule; otherwise the PR fails with each break listed. The title is read live from the API, so retitling and re-running the job is enough.

Proved locally for each: main passes; a deliberate removal fails under a non-package title and under another package's `!`; the same removal passes with the package's own `!`; appended union / enum values and new optional members pass. The hand-written sibling packages are not checked yet — each script's header says what that takes.

Updates `undici` from 7.29.1 to 7.30.1
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Cache poisoning and cross-user disclosure through cross-origin redirects

CVE-2026-109829 · GHSA-4w7w-5xrc-9h26

When an originless Agent combined redirect and shared-cache interceptors as compose(redirect(), cache()), a response from a cross-origin redirect could be stored under the original URL. This could allow persistent cache poisoning or disclosure of user-specific responses to later callers. This release verifies the response origin before caching and preserves redirect-hop cache-control policy.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through the decompress interceptor

CVE-2026-87029 · GHSA-55wc-3pg8-jfw6

An exception thrown by a downstream response handler from an asynchronous decompression callback could escape as an uncaught exception. A server could trigger this when decompress was composed with a handler such as dump with a size limit. This release converts downstream handler exceptions into per-request errors.

Subresource Integrity bypass with non-lowercase algorithm tokens

CVE-2026-109841 · GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472

fetch() treated valid mixed-case or uppercase SRI algorithm tokens, such as SHA256, as unknown and could accept a response whose body did not match the configured digest. This release normalizes algorithm tokens before validation and digest selection.

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

title: feat(spec): declared extensions, and a withdrawn status after a version is superseded
body:
Two lifecycle gaps the registry keeps paying for.

A MINOR increment at draft may break (Compatibility Rules), so nothing can
rely on a newer MINOR being compatible: forward minor-version processing is
unsafe at draft, and every specification that names another by version has
to publish a new version of itself whenever the one it names moves. The
optional `extends` front-matter field (Specification Requirements item 22)
lets a version promise, at every maturity level, that it is a
backwards-compatible extension of an earlier version of its slug — it keeps
every member, type, required member, enumerated value, constraint and
definition, and only adds. Consumers SHOULD then accept its documents by
ignoring members they do not know, and a specification naming the earlier
version MAY treat it as satisfied by the extension, so an additive change
cascades nowhere. Without the declaration, forward minor-version processing
SHOULD NOT be applied at draft.

Nothing ever leaves an implementation. Every version stays supported
forever, and a generated library cannot drop one without breaking its own
users. A version is now **superseded** when a later version of its slug is
published at an equal or higher maturity (a condition, not a status), and a
version superseded or retired for at least 90 days MAY become `withdrawn`:
its schema and prose stay published and frozen so issued documents remain
verifiable, but producers MUST NOT emit it, consumers MAY reject it with
unsupportedVersion, and implementations MAY remove it. The registry policy
decides when withdrawals take effect and MAY batch them. `retired` moves
only to `withdrawn`, which is terminal; the bare-URL redirect, Stability,
supersededBy and shared schema components follow.

New text sits at the end of its section or list, so no existing section or
item number moves.

The registry side — the `extends` check, forward-minor routing in the libraries, the `withdrawn` status in the meta-schema and codegen — is in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf.

published at an equal or higher maturity (a condition, not a status), and a
version superseded or retired for at least 90 days MAY become `withdrawn`:
its schema and prose stay published and frozen so issued documents remain
verifiable, but producers MUST NOT emit it, consumers MAY reject it with
unsupportedVersion, and implementations MAY remove it. The registry policy
decides when withdrawals take effect and MAY batch them. `retired` moves
only to `withdrawn`, which is terminal; the bare-URL redirect, Stability,
supersededBy and shared schema components follow.

New text sits at the end of its section or list, so no existing section or
item number moves.

title: feat(specs): a version may declare it extends an earlier one, and every library reads the newer version as the older
body:
The registry side of SPEC §5.2 "Declared extension" (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#33). A MINOR at `draft` may break, so until now nothing could rely on a newer MINOR being compatible: every spec naming another had to publish a new version whenever its target moved, and a consumer had to be rebuilt for every MINOR. A version that only adds can now say so.

**The declaration.** `extends: "<M.K>"` in front matter (meta-schema), promising the version keeps everything `M.K` has and only adds. The build checks it with the published-schema engine (`scripts/lib/schema-compat.mjs`, titles excepted across versions) plus the front-matter rules (same `proofRequirement`, every error code kept). Tested: `auth/authenticate/0.2 extends 0.1` passes; `persona/contact/get/1.1 extends 1.0` is refused with its three real breaks.

**No more cascades.** The stale-references check treats a reference to any version the latest one's chain reaches as current, so an additive change asks nothing of the specs that name the older version.

**The libraries read the newer version as the older.** Every generated module carries its direct declaration (`EXTENDS` / `Extends` / `extendsVersion`), each library generates an index from Type URI to it, and `check-bindings` holds all four to the front matter. Rust's `Dispatcher` and `AsyncDispatcher` route a miss to the highest registered version the chain reaches (`extension::read_as` for callers without one); TS `readForSpec`, Go `ReadForSpec`, Dart `readForVersion` do the same for a caller holding a `Spec`. The payload is pruned to the members the implemented schema knows; the document keeps its received `type`, so the answer is `<received>#response`. **Proofs are verified over the document as received, never the pruned copy**, and item 11 digests the received document, so documents differing only in an extension member are an `idConflict`. Everything is additive: no existing signature changed.

**Dormant until declared.** No spec declares `extends` yet. `npm run extends-candidates` lists the 83 existing version pairs whose schemas already qualify; an author declares one after checking meaning, which the build cannot.

Verified on the merged branch: regeneration drift-free; check-bindings agrees (deprecation and extends) across 1,126 specs; an end-to-end declaration of the auth/authenticate chain produces the same index in all four languages; Rust `clippy --all-features -D warnings` and the acl tests, TS build/test (99)/smoke, Go vet/test/gofmt, Dart `analyze --fatal-infos`/test (98) all pass.

body:
feat(specs): a version may declare it extends an earlier one, and every library reads the newer version as the older (#922)

* feat(specs): an extends declaration the build checks, and that keeps references along its chain current

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build: check-bindings verifies each module's extends constant, and extends-candidates lists pairs an author could declare

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(dart): read a document of a later version along its declared extends chain

Every generated library carries extendsVersion (the direct extends
declaration, or null), and lib/specs/extends_index.dart maps every bare
request Type URI that declares one to the version it extends.

The runtime gains readForVersion, which reads a received document as the
version an application implements: unchanged for that version, pruned to
the implemented schema for a later version whose extends chain reaches it
(keeping the received type, so the response is typed as received), and
refused unsupportedVersion otherwise. extensionChain, extendsTo and
prunePayload are exported alongside it.

consumeInbound takes an optional received map: proofs verify over it rather
than the typed re-encoding, and a forward document's item-11 digest is
keyed on it, so documents differing only in a pruned member still conflict.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(ts): accept a later MINOR whose extends chain reaches the implemented version

Every generated TypeScript spec module now exports EXTENDS (string | null),
the version its front matter declares it extends, and the generated
src/_extends.ts indexes them as EXTENDS_BY_TYPE_URI (bare Type URI ->
version), so the runtime can walk a chain without the caller importing the
later module.

The runtime gains readForSpec(received, spec, { index? }), which re-reads a
received document for the version the application implements: unchanged
for that exact version, payload pruned against spec.payloadSchema for a later
version whose extends chain reaches it (type kept as received, so
respondWith answers <received type>#response), refused unsupportedVersion
otherwise. Also exported: extendsOf, extendsChain, prunePayload,
receivedDocumentOf, ExtendsLookup, ReadForSpecResult.

consumeInbound verifies the proof and computes the item-11 digest over the
document as received (receivedDocumentOf), never the pruned copy. Additive:
no existing signature changes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(go): route a document of an extending version to the version it extends

Every generated Go package carries `const Extends` — the MAJOR.MINOR its front
matter declares it extends, or "" — and a registry-wide index,
specs/extends.go (package specs, ExtendsOf), maps each declaring bare Type URI
to it, so the runtime can walk a chain without importing the extending
version's package.

trusttasks gains ExtendsLookup, RegistryExtends, ExtendsChainReaches and
ReadForSpec / ReadForSpecWith: given the received JSON and the implemented
Spec, they return the received bytes unchanged for the exact version, the
document with its payload pruned to the implemented schema for a version whose
extends chain reaches it, or an unsupportedVersion / unsupportedType refusal.

ConsumeOptions gains an optional Received: when set, the proof is verified over
those bytes rather than a re-encoding of Doc, and a Doc that is not a reading
of them is refused proofInvalid. The response keeps the received type, since
RespondWith already takes it from the document.

All additive: new constants, functions and an optional field.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(specs): the extends front-matter field in the meta-schema

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(rust): route a declared extension to the version a consumer implements

Every generated module carries pub const EXTENDS: Option<&str> (the direct
front-matter extends declaration), and a generated, ungated table backs
trust_tasks_rs::extension::extends_for (re-exported from schema_index).

Dispatcher and AsyncDispatcher route a document whose exact MAJOR.MINOR has
no handler to the highest registered version its extends chain reaches,
pruning the payload to what that version's schema knows; the document keeps
its received type, so respond_with answers <received type>#response.
extension::read_as does the same for one payload type, and consume_inbound's
VerifyReceived accepts such a document while verifying the proof over the
document as received.

title: vti-vetting-pcs-v0.6.0
body:
### Added

- Growth types in published crates are #[non_exhaustive] ([#2196](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2196))

A new variant on a public enum, or a new field on a public struct a consumer
  can build with a literal, is a breaking change in a published crate. It kept
  happening on types that were always going to grow (#1231, #1234, #1244, #1247,
  #1250); #1262 fixed it for Capability and AuditEvent only.

  This marks the rest once. 143 enums are marked: every error and refusal enum
  (VtaError, AppError, ...) and the growth vocabularies (kinds, statuses,
  reasons, codes, transports, SealedPayloadV1). 32 structs are marked: config
  and response bags that no caller builds with a literal. Adding the attribute
  is itself breaking, once. After it, additions to these types are minor
  changes.

  Left exhaustive on purpose, and pinned that way by the census:
  VerifiedAssertion, AssertionProof, ActScope, ApproveScope, ContextDirection,
  SigningDomain, TokenStatus and Role. For each of these, every arm must be
  considered, and a downstream wildcard would be the bug.

  Every downstream match in the workspace gets a `_ =>` arm that takes the most
  restrictive or most generic reading: an internal error, a hidden or refused
  entry, a stale attribute. None is unreachable!().

  vta-sdk/tests/non_exhaustive_census.rs fails on a public enum in a published
  library crate whose name ends in Error, Refusal, Violation, Kind, Event,
  Status, Capability, Reason or Code and that is not #[non_exhaustive], unless
  it is listed as deliberately exhaustive with a reason. It also fails when a
  listed enum gains the attribute or disappears.

  stored under the slug, as earlier pnm did; with it, a slug-keyed key is used
  only if it holds that DID. `claim-did create/show/discard --slug` stay as
  hidden flags.

title: feat(codegen): superseded and retired spec versions are deprecated in every library, and withdrawn ones leave them in a quarterly batch (#921)
body:
feat(codegen): superseded and retired spec versions are deprecated in every library, and withdrawn ones leave them in a quarterly batch (#921)

* feat(go): mark superseded and retired spec versions deprecated, and omit withdrawn ones

Every generated request package now exports `const Deprecation` (empty for a
current version, otherwise "superseded by <slug>/<M.N>", "retired; use
<slug>/<M.N>" or "retired"), and a deprecated version's Payload and Response
types carry a `// Deprecated:` paragraph. A version with `status: withdrawn`
gets no package at all. The rule is derived independently from front matter,
per SPEC "Superseded and Withdrawn Versions".

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(ts): mark superseded and retired spec versions deprecated, and skip withdrawn ones

Every generated spec module now exports DEPRECATION (null while current,
otherwise the lifecycle note), and a deprecated module carries @deprecated
on its root request/response payload types and the Payload/Response
aliases. A version with status: withdrawn is not generated at all.

The smoke test now pins acl/grant/0.2, a current version, since 0.1 is
superseded and will eventually be withdrawn.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(dart): mark deprecated spec versions and skip withdrawn ones in the generated bindings

Every generated request library now carries `const String? deprecation`,
null for a current version and the byte-exact note otherwise
(`superseded by S`, `retired; use S`, `retired`). A deprecated version's
root `Payload` and `Response` also carry `@Deprecated(note)`. A version with
`status: withdrawn` is not generated at all (SPEC "Superseded and Withdrawn
Versions").

Sibling packages that use a now-deprecated version: the didcomm and tsp
examples move to trust-task-discovery 0.3; the https server (which still
answers discovery 0.1/0.2), its example and test, and the proof example and
test (whose fixture is an acl/grant 0.1 document) keep their versions under
narrowly scoped `deprecated_member_use` ignores, so `--fatal-infos` stays clean.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(specs): a withdrawn status, the quarterly withdrawal batch, and a check that all four libraries agree on the lifecycle

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(codegen): deprecate superseded and retired spec versions, and generate nothing for withdrawn ones

Implements SPEC "Superseded and Withdrawn Versions" in the Rust generator.
Every generated module now carries `pub const DEPRECATION: Option<&str>`;
a superseded or retired version also marks its root `Payload` and
`Response` types `#[deprecated(note = ...)]` ("superseded by S",
"retired; use S" or "retired"). A `status: withdrawn` version gets no
module, mod.rs entry, schema-index arm or conformance test.

Generated code that names its own deprecated types (the module itself,
schema_index.rs, the conformance test) allows the lint. Hand-written tests,
examples and the discovery 0.1/0.2 responders that deliberately pin
superseded versions carry a narrowly scoped #[allow(deprecated)].

* fix(rs): allow deprecated in the validate-gated tests and the facade example, which pin superseded specimens

title: vta-external-v0.9.0
body:
### Added

- Growth types in published crates are #[non_exhaustive] ([#2196](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2196))

A new variant on a public enum, or a new field on a public struct a consumer
  can build with a literal, is a breaking change in a published crate. It kept
  happening on types that were always going to grow (#1231, #1234, #1244, #1247,
  #1250); #1262 fixed it for Capability and AuditEvent only.

  This marks the rest once. 143 enums are marked: every error and refusal enum
  (VtaError, AppError, ...) and the growth vocabularies (kinds, statuses,
  reasons, codes, transports, SealedPayloadV1). 32 structs are marked: config
  and response bags that no caller builds with a literal. Adding the attribute
  is itself breaking, once. After it, additions to these types are minor
  changes.

  Left exhaustive on purpose, and pinned that way by the census:
  VerifiedAssertion, AssertionProof, ActScope, ApproveScope, ContextDirection,
  SigningDomain, TokenStatus and Role. For each of these, every arm must be
  considered, and a downstream wildcard would be the bug.

  Every downstream match in the workspace gets a `_ =>` arm that takes the most
  restrictive or most generic reading: an internal error, a hidden or refused
  entry, a stale attribute. None is unreachable!().

  vta-sdk/tests/non_exhaustive_census.rs fails on a public enum in a published
  library crate whose name ends in Error, Refusal, Violation, Kind, Event,
  Status, Capability, Reason or Code and that is not #[non_exhaustive], unless
  it is listed as deliberately exhaustive with a reason. It also fails when a
  listed enum gains the attribute or disappears.

title: vta-support-v0.23.0
body:
### Fixed

- **vta-support**: The versionTime wait budgets whole-millisecond sleeps ([#2262](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2262))

wait_until_not_future charged each sleep as the exact time remaining, but
  Tokio's timer sleeps in whole milliseconds. Once the clock sat microseconds
  short of the target, every pass slept 1ms and was charged microseconds, so the
  total sleep could run past MAX_WAIT_SECONDS. Under paused time this showed up
  as waits_for_rapid_back_to_back_calls failing intermittently with
  elapsed=5.252s against the 5s budget.

  Each sleep is now rounded up to a whole millisecond and counted as such, so
  the budget matches what is slept. A new test drives a clock that creeps by a
  microsecond per pass and fails on the old accounting.

title: vta-config-v0.26.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Did:scid:vh:1 identities, create/1.2, and VTA/VTC presentation config ([#2257](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2257))

* feat(vta-sdk): did:scid:vh:1 identity rules and did:scid secret kids (VTI-KEY-160 to VTI-KEY-164)

- **vta**: Operation budgets for Trust Task work (VTI-TRN-029) ([#2264](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2264))

* feat(vta)!: operation budgets for Trust Task work (VTI-TRN-029)

  A VTA offered more Trust Task work than it can serve stops answering in
  time; on a TEE appliance health checks then fail and the watchdog restarts
  the enclave. Three budgets now bound that work, each unset by default:

  - operation_rate_limit_per_sec (+ _burst): the whole appliance, shared by
    REST, DIDComm and TSP.
  - operation_rate_limit_per_subject_per_sec: each client with standing, by
    its DID, charged before the appliance budget.
  - operation_rate_limit_unauthenticated_per_sec: DIDComm / TSP senders
    without an ACL entry (login steps, public tasks, counterparties,
    approvers, refusals), apart from the clients' budget. Past it there is no
    reply, so a flood cannot cost a signature per message.

  A task is charged its weight in signs (vault release 2, DID create and
  delete 10, others 1), after authentication and before it runs. REST
  answers 429 with x-rate-limit-source: vta and scope operations or
  operations-subject; DIDComm and TSP a signed, retryable unavailable with
  retryAfter. A refused document is not recorded (VTI-OPS-026), so a resend
  is a retry.

  The keys are config and tenant-overlay only, never config/patch, so a TEE
  enclave restart keeps them. A zero is refused at load. pnm and cnm explain
  operations and operations-subject refusals.

- Growth types in published crates are #[non_exhaustive] ([#2196](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2196))

A new variant on a public enum, or a new field on a public struct a consumer

  is itself breaking, once. After it, additions to these types are minor
  changes.

  VerifiedAssertion, AssertionProof, ActScope, ApproveScope, ContextDirection,
  SigningDomain, TokenStatus and Role. For each of these, every arm must be
  considered, and a downstream wildcard would be the bug.

  Every downstream match in the workspace gets a `_ =>` arm that takes the most
  restrictive or most generic reading: an internal error, a hidden or refused
  entry, a stale attribute. None is unreachable!().

  vta-sdk/tests/non_exhaustive_census.rs fails on a public enum in a published
  library crate whose name ends in Error, Refusal, Violation, Kind, Event,
  Status, Capability, Reason or Code and that is not #[non_exhaustive], unless
  it is listed as deliberately exhaustive with a reason. It also fails when a
  listed enum gains the attribute or disappears.



### Fixed

- **vta**: Bound each client and unauthenticated peers by default (VTI-TRN-029) ([#2274](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2274))

VTI-TRN-029 is a MUST: a node bounds what any one subject can consume, and
  bounds unauthenticated peers separately. The operation budgets shipped unset,
  so a VTA nobody sized met neither clause. The per-client share now defaults to
  100 operations a second and the budget for DIDComm / TSP senders without
  standing to 50; there is no setting that turns either off, and a higher value
  loosens them. The appliance budget stays unset by default: its right value is
  a property of the hardware.

  The budgets read an injectable clock (`BudgetClock`), so their tests run on a
  manual clock that does not refill while they run, rather than racing the
  monotonic one. Two tests that send more than the default share in under a
  second (every dispatched verb from one stranger; filling the contact-list cap)
  size the budget they need.

title: vta-audit-v0.21.0
body:
### Fixed

- **audit**: Bounded chain-head recovery and paged audit readers ([#2229](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2229))

* fix(audit): bounded chain-head recovery and paged audit readers

  Chain-head recovery read the whole audit keyspace to find one row, which
  cannot work over vsock where the result must fit a single 16 MiB frame.
  Recovery now scans the newest rows under the writer's own prefix, falling
  back to a bounded deep scan only while a legacy log is being migrated, and
  failing closed rather than silently re-anchoring.

  Adds `ScanOpts` / `KeyspaceHandle::scan_raw` (a bounded, directional read
  with an exclusive resume key) across both backends, and `OP_SCAN` on the
  enclave proxy with the usual capability negotiation. `ScanPager` decides its
  strategy once per walk, so a proxy that cannot bound a read is asked for the
  range once rather than once per page.

  Audit verification and listing walk through the pager instead of
  materialising the keyspace.
