title: fix(sign-in): pin the page's origin on an approved trigger-link sign-in, so a console can set up signing
body:
Fixes #377.

## The problem

A trigger-link sign-in (`auth/oob/*`) is the first option on a VTC operator console's login page, and it was the only wallet sign-in that seeded no origin → relying-party pin (`origin-pin.ts`, M5). The console's **Set up signing with your wallet** calls `signTrustTask`, which is bound to that pin and deliberately never seeds one. So a wallet administrator who signed in the recommended way was refused with `<origin> has no relying party pinned …` and could never enrol a console signing key. Only the two page-bridge SIOP sign-ins, now labelled deprecated on that login page, left a pin.

## The change

- **Pin on approval** (`background.ts`). When a trigger-link flow ends with an approved grant, `handleSignInStep` pins the click's browser-attested origin to the community DID the link names, through the existing `pinOrigin`. That is the pairing the flow already verified: it refused unless that origin was the portal the community's own DID document names (VTI-LNK-105). The link is parsed with `now: 0`, as `handleTriggerLinkNumber` does, so a link that lapsed while the person was approving still names its community.
- **The changed-pairing warning is kept.** M5's rule is that a page asking for a different relying party than it was pinned to gets a loud prompt, as the page-bridge logins give it. On `prepare` the background now forwards what the origin is currently pinned to (`pinnedDid`). The flow (`sign-in-flows.ts`) adds `changedFromDid` to the confirm screen when the link's community differs. The window (`sign-in-view.tsx`) shows a danger note naming the previous community and no longer skips the confirm screen for a single identity in that case, so the warning is seen before anything is sent.
- **Types** (`bridge-protocol.ts`): `pinnedDid?` on the offscreen prepare request, `changedFromDid?` on the confirm result. Both optional and additive.
- **Tests**: a flow test that the confirm screen carries `changedFromDid` only when the pinned DID differs from the link's community, and a render test that the warning is shown, no claim goes out on its own, and Continue is offered.

`page-task-policy.ts` is unchanged: no pin still means no signature.

## Judgment calls for the reviewer

1. **Where the pin is seeded.** The background pins from the stored flow record (the attested click origin) and the link's `from`, rather than the flow returning the pairing it verified in its `done` result. This keeps `SignInStepResult`'s `done` shape stable and leaves four `deepEqual` assertions on it untouched. The two are equal by construction today (the flow's `vtcDid` is `link.from.value`, and it refuses unless `origin` matches the portal), but if you would rather the flow report what it verified, `done` could carry `{ vtcDid, portalOrigin }` on an approve and the background would pin from that instead. Happy to switch.
2. **Overwriting an existing pin.** An approved sign-in overwrites a pin to a different community, as the page-bridge logins do once the person approves past the loud prompt. The alternative of refusing to overwrite would leave the person with no way back short of clearing extension storage, which has no UI. The warning on the confirm screen is what makes the overwrite an informed one; it is also why a single identity no longer skips that screen when the pairing changed.

## Verification

Built with the Docker workflow from the working tree: lint, `tsc`, `npm test` (1317 + 6 + 9 passing, the two new tests among them) and CI's post-build assertions all pass. The unpacked build loads with the pinned extension ID.

Exercised end to end against a live VTC (`test-vtc.openvtc.net`, operator console, a `did:webvh` persona with `community-admin`): after **Sign in with your wallet** the origin is pinned and **Set up signing with your wallet** succeeds, where the same steps on the previous build were refused with `has no relying party pinned`.

title: fix(codegen)!: model an anyOf of required members as optional fields, not an untagged enum (#917)
body:
fix(codegen)!: model an anyOf of required members as optional fields, not an untagged enum (#917)

* fix(codegen)!: model an anyOf of required members as optional fields, not an untagged enum

A payload schema saying "at least one of these members" with an `anyOf` of
bare `{"required": [..]}` branches was rendered by typify as an untagged
enum, one variant per branch holding only that branch's member under
`deny_unknown_fields`. A payload carrying two of the members — valid by the
schema, and the normal case for rooms/keys/chain/0.2's `links` + `epochFloor`
— deserialized into no variant.

The codegen now drops such an `anyOf` from the copy of the schema handed to
typify (as `desugar_oneof_with_compound_not` does for its `oneOf`). The wire
schema behind `ValidatedPayload::validate_value` is captured first, so the
constraint is still enforced at runtime.

BREAKING CHANGE: `Payload` in rooms::keys::chain::v0_2,
rooms::records::curate::v0_1, rooms::keys::profile::write::v0_1 and
vtc::directory::notes::append::v0_1 changes from an untagged enum to a struct
whose clause members are all optional.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(codegen): import json only where the feature-gated cases use it

title: feat(build): fail the build on a reference to a superseded spec version, and bring every current spec up to date
body:
A new check, scripts/lib/stale-references.mjs, run by the registry build:
no latest, non-retired spec may name another spec at a version that spec
has since superseded — in a schema, a description, a prose link or
mention, or an example. `npm run fix-stale-references` rewrites the text
references (links, mentions, descriptions; a lone version in a moved
link's label moves with it; a link whose #anchor the new version lacks is
left for a person) and lists what it will not touch: wire pins and
normative values (they take a new version) and examples (their payloads
must be checked against the new version). History is exempt — Changes
from / "What 0.4 changed" sections, version runs ending at the latest,
"since"/"added in", "or later" — and anything else deliberate goes in
stale-references-allowlist.json with its reason.

Run once over the registry, in place in draft specs:

- 728 text references across about 280 files, mostly prose links.
- Examples moved after checking their payloads against the new version:
  trust-task-discovery's supportedTypes, trust-task-error's inResponseTo,
  auth/oob/grant's directory listing, keys/derive-and-sign-document's
  authenticate document.
- git-ns/bridge/event 0.5 says what it meant: a bridge that lists
  git-ns/bridge/job 0.5 or later (the closePullRequest kind).
- Two allowlisted: rooms/records/get and list say a record written by
  rooms/records/put/0.1 has no blobs.

New versions, because the reference is a value an implementation emits —
the `expects` entry of a deferred operation's next-step named
vtc/admin/actions/show/0.2, which #907 superseded:

- vtc/elections/create 0.3, vtc/rooms/storage/assign 0.2,
  vtc/rooms/storage/migrate 0.3, vtc/storage/configs/create 0.3,
  retire 0.3 and update 0.3, vtc/storage/credentials/set 0.3.

title: fix(voting): the ballot box registers only the communities it serves, checks casts off its lock, and pages reads by size
body:
Three gaps from the community-voting threat model:

- Registrations: any DID could register elections until the box's store was full. The service
  config gains `[communities]` — `allowed` community DIDs, or `allow_any = true` for an open box;
  without it nothing registers — and `max_unfinished` (default 20) elections per community not
  yet tallied or cancelled. Another community's registration is `permissionDenied`; one past the
  quota is `unavailable`, which the VTC delivers again until one finishes. A repeat of a
  registration already held is never refused.
- Locking: a cast's costly checks (the attestation's pairing, a tallied ballot's proofs) ran
  under the one lock over every box, so a flood of casts stalled every other community.
  `BallotBox::cast_check` / `cast_encrypted_check` take the cheap checks and what the costly ones
  need; `CastCheck::run` proves the cast without the box, on a blocking thread (at most one per
  core); `cast_verified` / `cast_encrypted_verified` re-run the cheap checks under the lock and
  admit that one cast. `cast` and `cast_encrypted` still do it all in place.
- Board reads: a `voting/board/read` page carries at most 256 KiB of entries (always at least
  one), fewer than `limit` where entries are large (read item 4).

title: fix(voting): the ballot box registers only the communities it serves, checks casts off its lock, and pages reads by size (#2283)
body:
fix(voting): the ballot box registers only the communities it serves, checks casts off its lock, and pages reads by size (#2283)

Three gaps from the community-voting threat model:

- Registrations: any DID could register elections until the box's store was full. The service
  config gains `[communities]` — `allowed` community DIDs, or `allow_any = true` for an open box;
  without it nothing registers — and `max_unfinished` (default 20) elections per community not
  yet tallied or cancelled. Another community's registration is `permissionDenied`; one past the
  quota is `unavailable`, which the VTC delivers again until one finishes. A repeat of a
  registration already held is never refused.
- Locking: a cast's costly checks (the attestation's pairing, a tallied ballot's proofs) ran
  under the one lock over every box, so a flood of casts stalled every other community.
  `BallotBox::cast_check` / `cast_encrypted_check` take the cheap checks and what the costly ones
  need; `CastCheck::run` proves the cast without the box, on a blocking thread (at most one per
  core); `cast_verified` / `cast_encrypted_verified` re-run the cheap checks under the lock and
  admit that one cast. `cast` and `cast_encrypted` still do it all in place.
- Board reads: a `voting/board/read` page carries at most 256 KiB of entries (always at least
  one), fewer than `limit` where entries are large (read item 4).

title: feat(vta-vault)!: narrow a vault query to one subject with subjectDid (vault/credentials/query/0.1)
body:
vault/credentials/query/0.1 gained a `subjectDid` request member (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #884, in trust-tasks-rs 0.34, taken by #2282). The VTA now honours it: the query is narrowed to credentials whose stored `subject_did` matches. For Data Integrity that is `credentialSubject.id`; for SD-JWT it is `sub`.

`subjectDid` only narrows. On its own it is no filter, so a query naming nothing but `subjectDid` is still refused as an enumeration (`subject_did_alone_is_refused_as_an_enumeration`).

Why: a wallet verifying a VTC member-directory field should only offer credentials bound to the member's DID, because that is the only holder the VTC accepts. Browser plugin PR #376 (draft) queries with `subjectDid: <member DID>`.

BREAKING: `vta_vault::CredentialQuery` gains a public field, `subject_did`.

Changes:
- `vta-vault/src/query.rs`: the field, a post-filter after the custody gate, and two tests
- `vta-service` conformance fixture: carries `subjectDid`
- SDK doc line on `cred_vault_query`, and credential-architecture design note §14

Local runs:
- fmt and clippy (`-D warnings`): clean
- Workspace nextest: 6666/6667 passed. The one failure, `every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`, timed out under load and passes alone.
- Doctests: pass
- VTC nextest: 3555/3565 passed. The 10 failures were load timeouts and all pass when rerun individually.

title: ci(release): the Release PR only releases, and its regeneration runs one semver check at a time
body:
The Release PR changes only versions, lockfile entries and changelogs. What it
releases is main, which CI already built and tested commit by commit, and its
merge is a push to main that runs the whole graph again. So on a release-plz-*
head, ci-affects.sh answers run=false for every build and test job, and the
Docker images are not built. fmt, cargo-deny, lockfile resolves, lockfile
self-pins, branch rules, commit lint and the release bump guard still run.

The Release-plz PR job died twice in a row after #2282, about 10 minutes into
"Checking API compatibility" with no output: the runner lost under two
concurrent vta-service-sized semver checks. The gate now admits one check at a
time, and the job's timeout goes from 120 to 300 minutes to pay for the serial
run. The release bump guard, the one long job left on the Release PR, goes
from 90 to 180 after hitting 90 on the same Release PR.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

**After merging:** the merge is a push to main, so it starts a fresh Release-plz PR run with these settings. That run cancels the attempt currently in flight, which still uses two slots. Avoid merging other PRs to main until it finishes, because each push cancels and restarts the regeneration.

title: feat(vtc/storage): vtc/storage/configs/retire 0.2 — refuse while a migration targets the config (#912)
body:
feat(vtc/storage): vtc/storage/configs/retire 0.2 — refuse while a migration targets the config (#912)

* feat(vtc/storage): vtc/storage/configs/retire 0.2 — refuse while a migration targets the config

retire 0.1 refused only while rooms were assigned to the config or it was
the default. vtc/rooms/storage/migrate 0.2 fixes a migration's toConfig at
approval and keeps it across a reassignment, and a migration can wait
queued or paused. So: start moving room R onto config X, reassign R to Y,
retire X (no rooms assigned) — X leaves `active` and the move into it can
never finish; it pauses with cause `destination` and retries forever.

0.2 adds vtc/storage/configs/retire:migrationsInbound (retryable: false,
details.migrations ≥ 1): the community MUST refuse while any migration
whose toConfig is the config is queued, running or paused, MUST make the
check again when a parked retirement executes, and MUST make the check and
the state change as one step with respect to a migration starting.
Migrations off the config are unaffected. The converse order is already
closed by migrate 0.2's configNotActive and assign's refusal of a
non-active config. A community serving 0.1 beside 0.2 SHOULD apply the
same refusal to a 0.1 request, reporting it with the same slug-namespaced
code (SPEC §8.5); a 0.1 producer falls back to taskFailed.

Request and response schemas are unchanged from 0.1.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(vtc/storage): retire 0.2 — state the converse order precisely

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: Make npm run check pass again and run it in CI
body:
## Summary

Nothing ran the type check: CI only runs the tests and the deploy only runs the esbuild-based build, which strips types without checking them. Meanwhile `tsc --noEmit` had been failing on TypeScript 6's deprecation of `moduleResolution=node10` and, behind that, on four real type errors, and prettier flagged 60 files. This fixes each cause and adds `npm run check` to CI so it stays green.

## Changes

- **tsconfig.json**: set `ignoreDeprecations` to `"6.0"`. Switching to `"bundler"` resolution surfaces four more errors from Quartz's deep imports (`remark-parse/lib`, `satori/wasm`, `preact/src/jsx`, `micromorph`), so that migration waits for upstream.
- **quartz.config.ts**: analytics was the string `"null"`, which is not a provider. It only disabled analytics because it matched no branch. Use the typed value `null`; the build still emits no analytics script.
- **ArticleTitle.tsx**: drop the import and parameter left unused by the local "Remove extra title" change.
- **ofm.ts**: pass the callout class list as an array, which is what the current hast property types expect. Rendered output is unchanged: `class="callout note is-collapsible is-collapsed"`.
- **.prettierignore**: skip `content` (reviewed prose under CODEOWNERS) and `docs` (vendored Quartz documentation that prettier 3.9 also fails to format idempotently, splitting a sentence in hosting.md into three paragraphs). Format the one remaining file, README.md.
- **ci.yaml**: run `npm run check` before the tests.

## Verification

In a `node:22-slim` container: `npm run check` clean, `npm test` with 78 of 78 passing, a full `quartz build`, a test page confirming collapsed and plain callouts render with the correct classes, and a grep confirming no analytics script in the output.

title: chore(deps): bump toml from 4.3.0 to 5.0.1
body:
Bumps [toml](https://github.com/BinaryMuse/toml-node) from 4.3.0 to 5.0.1.
Changelog

Sourced from toml's changelog.

5.0.1 - October 12 2026

  • Address four security advisories, each reachable by parsing untrusted input:
    • GHSA-h895-cgqg-jf52, in which a crafted document could still write to Object.prototype. Two distinct key paths could render to the same bookkeeping string, letting an array-of-tables header clear the guard on an unrelated key, after which a dotted key could descend through a date value into its prototype chain. The compiler now records how each table was defined on the table itself rather than in string-keyed sets, so paths cannot collide and key paths can only descend through tables the compiler created.
    • GHSA-9j65-hcg3-gc64, in which dotted keys, table headers, and inline-table keys with many segments took quadratic time to resolve.
    • GHSA-4qx8-w7c3-pj3p, in which every array-of-tables header rescanned all paths defined so far, so documents with many such headers took quadratic time.
    • GHSA-9qmh-m7c6-f92p, in which integer literals were converted to BigInt before any size check, so a multi-megabyte literal consumed super-linear CPU time before being rejected. Literals with more digits than any 64-bit integer are now rejected before conversion.

5.0.0 - July 14 2026

  • Breaking: Integers outside JavaScript's safe range (beyond ±Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) now throw a parse error instead of silently returning a rounded value (#28). Opt in to lossless handling of the full 64-bit range with toml.parse(input, { bigint: true }), which returns all integer values as BigInt.
  • Breaking: Integers outside TOML's 64-bit signed integer range now throw a parse error in either mode, as required by the spec. Previously they were silently rounded.

title: Clear open Dependabot security alerts in the lockfile
body:
## Summary

Clears 22 of the 24 open [Dependabot alerts](https://github.com/OpenVTC/wiki/security/dependabot). All of them are denial-of-service or ReDoS advisories in build-time tooling, so nothing here reaches the published site, but the alerts were accumulating because the weekly Dependabot version-update PRs only follow package.json entries and never touch nested transitive copies in the lockfile. Dependabot security updates are now enabled on the repo as well, so future transitive alerts will arrive as PRs instead of sitting open.

## Changes

- Bump `toml` from 4.3.0 to 5.0.1, the only direct dependency with an open alert (three quadratic-complexity DoS advisories in `toml.parse()`). The frontmatter transformer only calls `toml.parse()`, and 5.x keeps that API, so no code change is needed.
- Run `npm audit fix` to refresh the transitive copies: brace-expansion 1.1.14 to 1.1.21 and 5.0.9 to 5.0.12, js-yaml 3.14.1 to 3.15.2 (under gray-matter), immutable 5.1.5 to 5.1.9, picomatch 2.3.1 to 2.3.2, source-map-js 1.2.1 to 1.2.2, and fflate 0.7.4 to 0.7.5.

## Not addressed

Two alerts remain and need major bumps in upstream packages: katex 0.16 to 0.18 (via rehype-katex and remark-math) and the fflate 0.7.3 copy that satori pins exactly. Both are build-time only and are candidates for dismissal as tolerable risk.

## Verification

In a `node:22-slim` container: clean `npm ci`, a TOML frontmatter smoke test against toml 5.0.1, `npm test` with 78 of 78 passing, and a full `quartz build` of all 57 content files. Note that `npm run check` already fails on `v4` because TypeScript 6 rejects the deprecated `moduleResolution=node10` setting in tsconfig.json; that predates this change and is left alone here.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.34.2
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Rooms/keys/act 0.8 — records prune and retention set ([#910](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/910))

rooms/keys/act's table is closed, so a key holder conforming to 0.7
  refuses rooms/records/prune (0.1, 0.2) and rooms/records/retention/set/0.1
  with typeNotActable. A member's own client therefore cannot make either
  request as the member: it falls back to rooms/keys/present and signs with
  its own key, and the host records the client key, not the member, as the
  administrator who changed the room's retention or pruned it.

  0.8 adds both to the table with action admin and a presentation inserted,
  as their own specifications require. Both name a room, so the member is
  resolved by Recipient item 2; the private-room same-subject binding and
  the producer's REQUIRED reason are already covered by Recipient items 4
  and 6. No error code is added and the schemas are 0.7's.

  rooms/epoch/prune stays absent. The table section now states why a
  records prune may ride act and an epoch prune may not: a records prune
  removes only what the room's record retention (stated in advance,
  readable by every member, set only by admin via retention/set) already
  made eligible, leaves the room's keys and its ability to read its past
  intact, carries a reason and is recorded; an epoch prune destroys key
  history to an epoch the request names, against no rule stated in
  advance.

  A MINOR increment per SPEC §5.2; 0.7 remains published. Bindings
  regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

- **build**: Lint that every instant is named <event>At, and rename serverTime to respondedAt ([#911](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/911))

The wire-conventions lint gains an `instant-name` rule: a `date-time`
  string is named `<event>At`, unless it is a bound or filter (`since`,
  `until`, `from`, `to`, `asOf`, or a name ending in Until/Since/From/After/
  Before/To) or the Data Integrity `created`. `timestamp-name` also refuses
  a bare `at`.

  Two specs had their own non-At instant, renamed in new versions:

  - device/heartbeat 0.3: serverTime -> respondedAt
  - messaging/ping 0.2: serverTime -> respondedAt (and its Security &
    Privacy section now carries the four sub-headings)

  External vocabularies are allowlisted with their source: TRQP's `time`,
  `time_evaluated` and `time_requested` (registry/*), and did:webvh's
  `versionTime` (did/log) and `latestVersionTime` (did/info).

  Depends on #760, which renames the git-ns bare `at` members this rule
  also catches.

- **specs**: Naming consistency — event instants, one spelling per concept, durations name their unit, in 69 new spec versions ([#907](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/907))

* feat(build): the wire-conventions lint requires an integer duration to name its unit



### Specifications

- **git-ns**: Nested repository paths for forges with subgroups ([#760](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/760))

* spec(git-ns): copy each affected version to its next version, unchanged

  Mechanical copy so the next commit shows only what the new versions change.

title: chore: release 11 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.34.1` → `0.34.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.34.1` → `0.34.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.34.1` → `0.34.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.34.1` → `0.34.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.34.1` → `0.34.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.34.1` → `0.34.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.34.1` → `0.34.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.34.1` → `0.34.2` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.27.4` → `0.27.5` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.9.5`) | `0.9.4` → `0.9.5` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.4` → `0.9.5` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: chore(deps)!: TSP 1.0 and trust-tasks-rs 0.34 (affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.40, affinidi-tdk 0.32, mediator 0.45)
body:
The ecosystem move to **TSP 1.0** (`YTSP-BAA`, trustoverip/tswg-tsp-specification#86), together with **trust-tasks-rs 0.34**.

| Dependency | From | To | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `affinidi-tdk` | 0.30 | **0.32** | affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#967 (TSP 1.0), #972 (trust-tasks 0.34) |
| `affinidi-messaging-sdk` | 0.38.1 | **0.40** | same; brings `affinidi-tsp` 0.3 |
| `trust-tasks-rs`, `-proof` | 0.33.2 | **0.34.1** | carries trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#884 (vault/credentials/query `subjectDid`) |
| `trust-tasks-https`, `-didcomm`, `-tsp`, `-capability-client` | 0.33 | **0.34** | `trust-tasks-tsp` 0.34 is on `affinidi-tsp` 0.3 |
| `affinidi-messaging-test-mediator`, `-mediator-admin`, `-mediator-tui` | 0.44 | **0.45** | affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator#30, #32 |

The lockfile now holds one `affinidi-tdk` (0.32; previously 0.28 and 0.30), one SDK and one `trust-tasks-rs`. No source change, and no `version =` edits.

**Wire-breaking for TSP.** A VTA on this release cannot exchange TSP messages with a peer still on Rev 3 (`affinidi-tsp` 0.2.x, `tsp_sdk` < 0.16), in either direction. DIDComm is unaffected. Deploy order:
1. Mediator 0.45 first; it routes both Rev 3 and 1.0.
2. Then the VTA together with the wallet (`@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` 0.4).
3. Then webvh-service and vti-push-gateway.

**Unblocks** feat/vault-query-subject-filter (vault `subjectDid`), which rebases onto this.

**Tested locally:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo deny --all-features check advisories` (ok); `cargo test --workspace` running, result to follow in a comment.

### Pre-merge checklist
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — N/A
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — N/A, dependency bump
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — N/A
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — N/A
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — N/A
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*) — TSP wire version Rev 3 → 1.0, with a stricter receive rule (NULL sender refused in confidential payloads); Trust Task types from 0.34 (additive)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed (R5.*) — an unknown TSP MAJOR and a NULL confidential sender are refused
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*) — N/A
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — no mutations
- [x] Deviations flagged: **R3.6**: a wire-breaking TSP change, coordinated with the mediator (already released), the wallet (vti-tsp-js 0.4, published), webvh-service and vti-push-gateway (to follow)

title: spec(git-ns): nested repository paths for forges with subgroups
body:
Lets git-ns govern repositories under GitLab subgroups: a repository resource becomes `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>` (1–21 path segments, e.g. `gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli`). The namespace stays the top-level owner; a subgroup is not a resource. Segments up to 255 characters.

**Reviewing:** four commits. The first copies each affected version unchanged and the third regenerates bindings — skip both. The second is the change (key hunks below); the fourth adds nested-path examples and invalid examples.

Open: Go and Dart bindings not yet regenerated. Question: may a draft shared schema be widened in place instead of re-versioning 24 tasks?

### The rule — `_shared/0.6` vs `0.5`
```diff
--- a/specs/git-ns/_shared/0.5/git-ns.schema.json
+++ b/specs/git-ns/_shared/0.6/git-ns.schema.json
@@ -3 +3 @@
-  "$id": "https://trusttasks.org/spec/git-ns/_shared/0.5/git-ns",
+  "$id": "https://trusttasks.org/spec/git-ns/_shared/0.6/git-ns",
@@ -5 +5 @@
-  "description": "Shapes used by more than one git-ns/* task: forge-qualified resources, the five git rights, namespaces, repositories, rights records, forge accounts and drift. 0.5 adds `AdminRightRow` and `RightOrigin`: the row shape the administrator's rights console shows, which is either a `RightRecord` restated with membership facts (`recorded`) or a v0.1 `[hooks.git-trust] grant_on_role` grant that is not a record at all (`roleDerived`) — used by git-ns/right/list and git-ns/right/issued-by-departed. Every other definition is unchanged from 0.4. Not itself a Trust Task specification. A VTC is the source of truth for all of these; the Trust Registry and the forge are projections of them.",
+  "description": "Shapes used by more than one git-ns/* task: forge-qualified resources, the five git rights, namespaces, repositories, rights records, forge accounts and drift. 0.6 admits repositories on forges with nested groups, such as GitLab: a repository resource is `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>`, where the repository path holds the subgroups between the top-level owner and the project (`gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli`), up to 21 segments; and a segment may be up to 255 characters. The namespace is still the top-level owner alone, so a resource of two segments is a namespace and one of three or more a repository. Every 0.5 document remains valid. Every other definition is unchanged from 0.5. Not itself a Trust Task specification. A VTC is the source of truth for all of these; the Trust Registry and the forge are projections of them.",
@@ -9 +9 @@
-      "description": "The lowercased DNS host of a forge: `github.com`, a GitHub Enterprise Server host, `codeberg.org`, or a self-hosted Forgejo instance such as `git.example.org`. No scheme, no port, no path. The host is a segment of every resource, so a right never crosses forges.",
+      "description": "The lowercased DNS host of a forge: `github.com`, a GitHub Enterprise Server host, `codeberg.org`, `gitlab.com`, or a self-hosted Forgejo or GitLab instance such as `git.example.org`. No scheme, no port, no path. The host is a segment of every resource, so a right never crosses forges.",
@@ -17 +17 @@
-      "description": "One lowercased owner or repository name. Forges compare these case-insensitively, so the wire form is always lowercase and a producer lowercases before sending. A leading `.` is refused, which rules out `.` and `..`.",
+      "description": "One lowercased owner, group or repository name. Forges compare these case-insensitively, so the wire form is always lowercase and a producer lowercases before sending. A leading `.` is refused, which rules out `.` and `..`. Up to 255 characters, the longest name GitLab allows; GitHub and Forgejo names are shorter.",
@@ -20 +20 @@
-      "maxLength": 100,
+      "maxLength": 255,
@@ -25 +25 @@
-      "description": "A forge-qualified resource: `<forge-host>/<owner>` for a namespace, or `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo>` for one repository, all lowercase — `github.com/acme`, `github.com/acme/widgets`, `codeberg.org/acme`. The forge is never implied: `acme/widgets` alone is not a resource. Containment is by whole segment: `github.com/acme` contains `github.com/acme/widgets` and does not contain `github.com/acme-labs/x` or `codeberg.org/acme/widgets`.",
+      "description": "A forge-qualified resource, all lowercase: `<forge-host>/<owner>` for a namespace, or `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>` for one repository — `github.com/acme`, `github.com/acme/widgets`, `codeberg.org/acme`. On a forge with nested groups (GitLab) the repository path holds the subgroups between the top-level owner and the project: `gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli` is one repository of the namespace `gitlab.com/acme`, and a subgroup such as `gitlab.com/acme/platform` is not a resource. A repository path has 1 to 21 segments (GitLab: 20 levels of subgroup and the project); GitHub and Forgejo repository paths are always one. The forge is never implied: `acme/widgets` alone is not a resource. Containment is by whole segment: `github.com/acme` contains `github.com/acme/widgets` and does not contain `github.com/acme-labs/x` or `codeberg.org/acme/widgets`.",
@@ -27,2 +27,2 @@
-      "maxLength": 455,
-      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(?:\\.[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)+(?:/[a-z0-9_-][a-z0-9._-]{0,99}){1,2}$"
+      "maxLength": 5885,
+      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(?:\\.[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)+/[a-z0-9_-][a-z0-9._-]{0,254}(?:/[a-z0-9_-][a-z0-9._-]{0,254}){0,21}$"
@@ -32 +32 @@
-      "description": "A forge-qualified resource naming exactly one repository: `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo>`, lowercase.",
+      "description": "A forge-qualified resource naming exactly one repository: `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>`, lowercase, where the repository path has 1 to 21 segments (see `Resource`).",
@@ -34,2 +34,2 @@
-      "maxLength": 455,
-      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(?:\\.[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)+/[a-z0-9_-][a-z0-9._-]{0,99}/[a-z0-9_-][a-z0-9._-]{0,99}$"
+      "maxLength": 5885,
+      "pattern": "^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(?:\\.[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)+/[a-z0-9_-][a-z0-9._-]{0,254}(?:/[a-z0-9_-][a-z0-9._-]{0,254}){1,21}$"
@@ -84 +84 @@
-      "description": "An identifier the forge itself assigns — a repository id, a user or organisation id — carried as a string so a forge whose ids are not numbers needs no new version. GitHub and Forgejo ids are decimal integers written as strings (`\"812736451\"`). Unlike a name, it survives renames and transfers, which is why rights and bindings are keyed by it.",
+      "description": "An identifier the forge itself assigns — a repository id, a user or organisation id — carried as a string so a forge whose ids are not numbers needs no new version. GitHub, Forgejo and GitLab ids are decimal integers written as strings (`\"812736451\"`). Unlike a name, it survives renames and transfers, which is why rights and bindings are keyed by it.",
@@ -143 +143 @@
-          "description": "Whether the owner is an organisation or a personal account, as the forge reports it. Present once known: a bridge-mode namespace learns it when binding completes, and a manual-mode namespace MAY never learn it."
+          "description": "Whether the owner is an organisation or a personal account, as the forge reports it; a GitLab top-level group is an `organization`. Present once known: a bridge-mode namespace learns it when binding completes, and a manual-mode namespace MAY never learn it."
```

### The meaning — `right/grant/0.4`, *Resources*
```diff
--- a/specs/git-ns/right/grant/0.3/spec.md
+++ b/specs/git-ns/right/grant/0.4/spec.md
@@ ### Resources @@
-Resources are forge-qualified and lowercase — `<forge-host>/<owner>` or `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo>` — and are never accepted without their forge. A producer lowercases before sending, because forges compare owner and repository names case-insensitively and the registry compares by exact string. Rights on a repository are keyed internally by the forge's repository id, so that when the forge renames a repository the VTC moves its rights to the new resource, and a new repository later created at the old name inherits nothing.
+Resources are forge-qualified and lowercase — `<forge-host>/<owner>` for a namespace, or `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>` for one repository — and are never accepted without their forge. The owner is always one segment: the organisation or user, or on a forge with nested groups the top-level group. The repository path is the rest of the repository's path on the forge: one segment on GitHub and Forgejo, and on GitLab the subgroups between the top-level group and the project followed by the project, 1 to 21 segments (`gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli`). title: fix(vtc)!: a backup restore closes ticket issuance on every election that could have issued since the backup
```
body:
A restore loses every ticket record written after the backup was taken, so those holders could
take a second ticket and vote twice (VTI-VOT-022). The import now closes issuance for good on
every restored election whose registration had opened and whose voting had not closed: tickets
already taken still vote; a member who took none before the backup cannot take one, and the
remedy is to cancel the election and create it again. An election whose registration had not
opened issued nothing in the gap and is left as it was.

It runs whether or not the build serves elections, so a later build that does cannot issue
either, and before the import's sentinel is cleared, so a failure leaves an interrupted import.
Each closed election is audited (`ElectionChanged`, change `issuanceClosedByRestore`) and logged.

Breaking: `vtc_service::elections::store::ElectionRecord` gains `issuance_closed_by_restore`.

title: feat(specs): naming consistency — event instants, one spelling per concept, durations name their unit, in 69 new spec versions
body:
A naming-consistency pass over every current spec, following #901. An inventory of the 2,000+ member names in the latest version of each spec (following shared `$ref`s) found the places where the registry says one thing several ways; this renames them to the majority spelling or to the rule. Every rename is a member-name change on the wire, so — as in #901 — each affected spec gets a **new version** whose `## Changes from <old>` says exactly what moved, and each changed shared definition gets a new shared version its users re-pin to. All are `draft`, so each break is a MINOR under SPEC §5.2; the old versions stay published.

**69 new spec versions**, and new shared versions `did-management/_shared/0.3`, `external/_shared/0.2`, `messaging/_shared/0.3`, `rooms/_shared/0.2`, `voting/_shared/0.2`, `vta/_shared/0.8`, `vtc/_shared/0.4`, `vtc/admin/actions/_shared/0.3`.

| Rule | Renames |
|---|---|
| An instant that records an event is `<event>At` | `votingOpens`/`votingCloses`/`registrationOpens` → `…At`; `lastSeen`/`firstSeen`/`lastHealthCheck` → `…At`; `renews` → `renewsAt`; a bare `at` named for its event: `occurredAt`, `observedAt`, `startsAt` (a bucket), `reachedAt` (a message status), `prunedAt`, `probedAt`, `decidedAt`, `endedAt`, `writtenAt` |
| One spelling per concept | `drainUntil` **and** `drainsUntil` (both in one file) → `drainEndsAt`; `modifiedAt` → `updatedAt`; `why` → `reason`; `clientDataJson` → WebAuthn's own `clientDataJSON` |
| A duration names its unit, spelled out | `…Secs` → `…Seconds` (`windowRemainingSeconds`, `drainTtlSeconds`, `handshakeTimeoutSeconds`); bare `ttl` → `ttlSeconds` |

**Re-pins.** Four specs sign or stream a version this PR (or #901) superseded, and get a new version that names the current one: `rooms/keys/act` 0.7 (its closed table also gains five newer rooms versions it had never listed), `vta/pcs/trustee/read` 0.2, `vta/pcs/voter/read` 0.2, `vtc/admin/events/subscribe` 0.6 (streams `event/0.5`).

**In place, editorial only** (no member or shape change): prose and descriptions that named the old members without carrying them — `voting/_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md`, `voting/election/close`, `vtc/elections/close`, `vtc/elections/tickets/issue`, `vta/services/drain/cancel`, `vtc/members/authority-reduction-pending-notice`.

**Lint.** The wire-conventions lint gains `duration-unit`: an integer `…Secs`/`…Mins` or a bare `ttl`/`timeout`/`duration`/`interval`/`delay` fails. Exceptions can now be keyed by a shared schema's family, which is how WebAuthn's `timeout` (external vocabulary, `auth/_shared`) is excepted everywhere it is reached.

The last commit regenerates all four libraries: `check-bindings` agrees across 1089 specs; `cargo check`, `tsc`, `go build` and `dart analyze` pass; `npm run validate` shows 0 non-conforming for both lints and 0 Security & Privacy gaps outside the allowlist (24 new versions had the four sub-headings written in, from existing text, adding no new MUST/SHOULD/MAY).

### Calls worth a reviewer's eye
- **`did-management/registry/admin-register`** reaches `_shared/0.1`'s `ServiceInstance`, which differs from 0.2's by far more than the rename. Re-pinning would have changed its response, so `_shared/0.3` carries a renamed copy of the 0.1 shape as `RegisteredInstance` (a distinct `$defs` name, so generated TypeScript does not collide).
- **Normative text kept, not dropped.** `vta/services/update` and `rollback` held drain rules inside their old "Changes from" sections; they move verbatim to a new "The drain window" section. `vtc/rooms/offers/list`'s "MAY renew a direct admission" moves to its Abstract.
- **The trustee/voter reads and the event stream accept the new target only**, not old and new: each new signer pairs with the new target.
- **Not renamed:** range bounds and filters (`since`, `until`, `validFrom`/`validUntil`, `graceUntil`, `retireAfter`); external vocabulary (WebAuthn `timeout`, W3C `created`, TRQP `time_evaluated`, did:webvh `versionTime`); `serverTime` (a clock reading, not an event); boolean `is`/`has` prefixes (7 vs 241 without) and list-response collection names (`items`/`entries`/`records`, which mostly name the thing listed).

### Not in this PR
- **`git-ns`'s four bare `at` sites** (`activity/list`, `repo/list`, `right/break-glass-notice`, shared `BreakGlass`) sit in exactly the folders #760 is creating new, unreleased versions of. They go there or after it lands, with a lint rule against a bare `at`.
- **Stale pins that predate #901**, left alone: `auth/step-up/start/0.1` carries `approve-request/0.3` (0.4 existed already); `sync/event` and `task-consent/decision` mention older versions in passing.

title: feat(vta)!: the voter engine keeps no clear member-to-cast pairing, and pnm takes the ticket in its own run
body:
Two privacy gaps from the community-voting threat model (CONVENTIONS §5 item 3, §6 items 3–4):

- The VTA's voter record kept the member-signed ticket request beside every cast's board leaf
  hash, readable without the seed, and never discarded either. The member's documents and the
  blinded request now go once the ticket is held; leaf hashes and receipts are wrapped under the
  seed in their own secret (`voter-casts:`). The storage sweeper discards the ticket when voting
  closes and the record, casts and receipts `RECEIPT_RETENTION` (30 days) later, with the voter
  key's path. Nothing is audited: a row naming the election would be the pairing VTI-VOT-100
  forbids.
- `pnm elections vote` took the ticket and cast in one run, so the community and the ballot box
  could pair them by their clocks. `pnm elections ticket` is now its own step; `vote` with no
  ticket held takes one and stops unless given `--now`.

Breaking: `vta_cli_common::commands::elections::cmd_vote` takes a `now` argument.

title: feat(vtc): seal a storage credential in the console (vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.2)
body:
The console now sets a `sealed` config's credential itself. The administrator
enters an S3 key pair, a Google service-account key file or a Sui key, and the
browser seals it to the community before anything is sent, as
`vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.2` requires of a producer: HPKE base mode
(X25519-HKDF-SHA256, HKDF-SHA256, ChaCha20-Poly1305, info
`vta-sealed-transfer/v1`) to the X25519 form of the community DID's `#key-0`,
read from the DID log the VTC serves at `/.well-known/did.jsonl`. Only the
armored block, its digest and the reason are sent; the change parks for
approval like every storage change, and approvers see the digest.

- `admin-ui/src/lib/sealed-transfer.ts` ports the sealing side of
  `vta_sdk::sealed_transfer`: CBOR chunk framing, the AAD, 32 KiB chunking,
  ASCII armor with CRC-24, and the multibase sha2-256 digest. Built on
  `@hpke/core`, `@hpke/chacha20poly1305`, `@hpke/dhkem-x25519`,
  `@noble/curves` and `cborg`.
- Shared vectors (`sealed-transfer.vectors.json`) hold the two sides together.
  The console test reproduces them byte for byte, and the `storage_credentials`
  tests open them with the community's own opener, including a two-chunk block
  and a refused replay into another config.
- The cleartext is sealed before any mutation sees it and cleared from the
  form once sealed. Where the browser cannot seal (no DID log served here, or
  no console key), the page says so and shows `cnm storage credentials set`,
  which stays the terminal route.
- `vta_sdk::openapi` gains wrappers for the payload, response and
  `SealedCredentialCleartext`, so the console's types are the specification's.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

### Tests
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (after the manifest fix), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, doctests: green.
- Workspace nextest: green except `audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`, which timed out at 300s under load and passes alone in 39s (it was already near the limit).
- admin-ui: `npm run lint`, `npx vitest run` green.
- Not tried against a live VTC with a real bucket.

title: chore(deps): clear RUSTSEC-2026-0387 by moving off crypto-bigint 0.5 and onto 0.7.6 (#908)
body:
chore(deps): clear RUSTSEC-2026-0387 by moving off crypto-bigint 0.5 and onto 0.7.6 (#908)

cargo deny fails every branch on RUSTSEC-2026-0387 (vulnerability): crypto-bigint has operations meant to be constant-time that are not. The graph carried two copies.

- crypto-bigint 0.7.5 -> 0.7.6, the patched release.
- crypto-bigint 0.5.5 has no patched release in its line. It arrived through the RustCrypto elliptic-curve 0.13 family (k256/p256/p384/p521 0.13), which reached us only through affinidi-crypto 0.2.6. affinidi-crypto 0.2.11 — semver-compatible with our requirement — has moved to the 0.14 family, so updating it (with affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.43 and affinidi-did-web 0.1.6) removes the whole 0.13 line, crypto-bigint 0.5.5 with it. No advisory ignore is needed.

Lockfile only: no manifest requirement moves, so no published crate's dependency range changes. cargo deny check passes (advisories, bans, licenses, sources).

title: fix(vta): say why the offline dids edit could not publish, and what to run instead
body:
## What happened

An operator on a Kubernetes stack ran the offline `vta did-mgmt dids edit --did <vtc did> --document document.json --no-confirm` to add a `TrustRegistry` referral to an existing VTC DID, and got `publish error: publish_did: no transport in common with <host did>: it advertises [tsp, didcomm] and this agent can initiate [rest]`. The host is a did-hosting-daemon provisioned through a VTA with a mediator, which gets `did-host-didcomm` and advertises no HTTPS endpoint. The offline command holds no mediator session (`DIDCommBridge::signing_only`, `tsp: None`), so `Outbound::initiable_for` yields `[rest]` and `pick_transport` has nothing to pick. The new log entry had already been committed locally; the error said nothing about that, nor that the running VTA, which holds the mediator session, is the one that can publish it.

## What changes

- `webvh_cli::run_edit_did` matches `UpdateDidWebvhError::Publish`, persists the store (the orchestrator commits before it publishes, and the running VTA re-publishes an unconfirmed head before its next update, so the commit is kept on purpose, as the success path keeps it), and returns a message that says the entry is pending and prints the online command verbatim: `pnm did-mgmt dids edit --did <did> --document <file> --no-confirm`. When the publish error is the no-transport refusal it also explains the HTTPS-only reach of the offline command and what the host would have to advertise (`TrustTaskHTTPS`, or `WebVHHosting` at an `https://` origin). This follows the workspace rule that an operator error suggests the fix.
- The hint keys on the text `vti_common::error::NoMatchingProtocol` renders. A unit test formats that error and asserts the marker, so a rewording there fails here instead of silently turning the hint off. Two more tests cover the message with and without the transport case.
- Three doc comments claimed the offline seam "falls to DIDComm" when no TSP socket is held (`Outbound::from_parts`, `WebvhDeps::tsp`, `bootstrap_cli`). True of a DIDComm handler, false of the offline CLI and the wizards. Corrected.
- `docs/03-vtc/community-lifecycle.md`, "Changing the community's transports after mint": the `TrustRegistry` referral entry as a worked example, the note that `[registry] did` in the VTC config is a separate setting, and what the offline command can and cannot publish to.

Not changed: the offline command still cannot reach a TSP/DIDComm-only host, and `dids register` / `dids create` offline have the same reach without the hint. The seam itself is right; the fix for a mediator-only host is the running VTA.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p vta-service --bin vta webvh_cli`: 3 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

`vta did-mgmt dids edit` holds no mediator session, so the outbound seam
can initiate REST and nothing else. Against a DID host whose document
advertises only `TSPTransport` and `DIDCommMessaging` (what a host
provisioned through a VTA with a mediator gets) it stopped with
`publish error: publish_did: no transport in common with ...: it
advertises [tsp, didcomm] and this agent can initiate [rest]`, and left
the operator to work out that the new log entry was already committed
locally and that the running VTA is the one that can publish it.

The offline command now keeps that commit (it persists the store before
returning, as the success path does) and prints what happened and the
fix: the entry is pending, the running VTA re-publishes it before its
next update of the DID, and the command to make the change there is
`pnm did-mgmt dids edit --did <did> --document <file> --no-confirm`.
When the publish error is the no-transport refusal it also explains the
HTTPS-only reach of the offline command and what the host would have to
advertise (`TrustTaskHTTPS`, or `WebVHHosting` at an https:// origin).
The hint keys on the text `NoMatchingProtocol` renders; a test pins
that coupling.

Three doc comments said the offline seam "falls to DIDComm" when no TSP
socket is held (`Outbound::from_parts`, `WebvhDeps::tsp`,
`bootstrap_cli`). That is true of a DIDComm handler, which holds the
live bridge, and false of the offline CLI and the wizards, which hold a
signing-only bridge. They now say so.

`docs/03-vtc/community-lifecycle.md` gains the `TrustRegistry` referral
entry as a worked example of a post-mint document change, and a note on
what the offline command can and cannot publish to.

Signed-off-by: Geoff Turk <geoff@ic3.dev>

* fix(vta): offline dids edit says whether the failed publish left a new entry

A publish error can arrive before the commit point (re-publishing an
unconfirmed head) as well as after it, so the CLI now asks the orchestrator
which, through update_did_webvh_reporting_commit, instead of always saying
the new entry was written.

title: feat(verify-trust): accept P-256 and FIDO (sk-) SSH signing keys
body:
Closes #169 (key types). The `context.time` item is deferred — see the [issue comment](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure/issues/169#issuecomment-6384284807).

- verify-trust accepts `ssh-ed25519`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256`, `sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com`, `sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com`; other algorithms remain `malformed`.
- vgi-core: `signing_keys_from_doc` → `PublishedKey` (Ed25519, or compressed P-256 via multicodec `0x1200`), same `assertionMethod`/`controller` rules. `ed25519_signing_keys_from_doc` stays for did-git-sign / bridge signing paths.
- **FIDO policy:** signature must carry the user-presence flag (ssh-key 0.6.7 verifies `sk-` signatures without checking it), and the key's application must be `ssh:`. Otherwise `malformed` with the reason.
- Tests sign real commits with all four types; cover untouched FIDO signatures, a foreign application, an unpublished P-256 key and a tampered payload. The sk-ecdsa fixture works around an ssh-key 0.6.7 *encoder* bug (trailer placed inside the signature string); its decoder, which verification uses, matches OpenSSH.
- Docs: verify-trust README, RUNBOOK status tables.

Local: `cargo test -p verify-trust -p vgi-core`, clippy `-D warnings` on verify-trust/vgi-core/did-git-sign/vgi-bridge, fmt.
author: stormer78
significance_reasons: Normative requirement language changed

title: feat(verify-trust): accept P-256 and FIDO (sk-) SSH signing keys (#177)
body:
feat(verify-trust): accept P-256 and FIDO (sk-) SSH signing keys (#177)

verify-trust accepted only ssh-ed25519 and reported the other OpenSSH signing
types as malformed, refusing exactly the signers with hardware-protected keys.
It now accepts ssh-ed25519, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com
and sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com.

DID documents may publish compressed P-256 keys (multicodec 0x1200) under
assertionMethod alongside Ed25519; vgi-core gains signing_keys_from_doc and a
PublishedKey type, with ed25519_signing_keys_from_doc kept for the Ed25519-only
signing paths.

A FIDO signature must carry the user-presence flag (OpenSSH's default; ssh-key
does not check it) and its key must be enrolled under the ssh: application.

Closes #169

title: fix(verify-trust): treat a retryable trust-task-error as registry unavailable
body:
Closes #170.

A `trust-task-error` with `retryable: true` now yields `RegistryUnavailable` (fails closed, fallback not asked) instead of `Unauthorized`. `retryable: false` remains a denial and the fallback resource is still queried.

Tests drive real `trust-task-error` documents through trql-client's parsing: retryable (`unavailable`, and `permissionDenied` marked retryable) → unavailable after one query; non-retryable `permissionDenied` → unauthorized after the fallback.

Local: `cargo test -p verify-trust`, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt.
author: stormer78
significance_reasons: Authority, delegation, approval, or revocation semantics

title: fix(verify-trust): treat a retryable trust-task-error as registry unavailable (#176)
body:
fix(verify-trust): treat a retryable trust-task-error as registry unavailable (#176)

A registry that answers with a trust-task-error marked retryable (e.g. its
data is stale) could not decide; verify-trust counted it as a denial and told
the signer they were unauthorized. It now fails closed as RegistryUnavailable,
as for an unreachable registry, without asking the fallback. A non-retryable
rejection stays a denial, so the fallback resource can still grant.

Closes #170

title: security(deps): crypto-bigint 0.7.6 for RUSTSEC-2026-0387
body:
`cargo-deny` is red on `main` since RUSTSEC-2026-0387 (2026-10-23).

- `Cargo.lock`: crypto-bigint 0.7.5 → 0.7.6, the patched release. This is the line the workspace's own P-256 / secp256k1 keys use (p256 / k256 0.14).
- `deny.toml`: ignore for the 0.5.5 residue, which has no patched release. It is reached only through elliptic-curve 0.13 (OpenMLS's provider for vti-rooms, whose ciphersuite is X25519/Ed25519; rPGP in cnm, verify-only; bls12_381_plus under affinidi-bbs). The advisory's named findings (`UintRef`, `BoxedMontyForm::invert`, ctutils masks) are 0.7-only APIs. Drop when elliptic-curve 0.13 leaves the graph.

title: fix(vta): register the vsock REST listener with AsyncFd::register (tokio 1.54)
body:
#2257 moved the lockfile to tokio 1.54.1 for RUSTSEC-2026-0386. tokio 1.54 deprecates `AsyncFd::new` as unsound, so the all-features clippy step (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`) fails on main in `vta-service/src/server.rs` (`VsockRestListener::adopt`).

This fix was pushed to the #2257 branch after it merged, so it missed main.

`VsockListener` owns its descriptor for its whole life, which is `AsyncFd::register`'s safety contract. The change is one constructor plus a SAFETY note; behaviour is unchanged.

Verified locally:
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on main and is clean with this change.
- `cargo check -p vta-service --no-default-features --features tee,rest,didcomm` passes.

title: ci(release): fail the npm job when npm stages the version instead of publishing it
body:
npm stages a CI upload — holding it out of public view until a maintainer
approves it with 2FA — when the package's trusted publisher lacks "Allow npm
publish", which npm leaves unticked by default for configs created since
2026-09-03. `npm publish` still exits 0. @openvtc/trust-tasks@0.27.4 sat
staged for 85 minutes in release #903 with every job green, and only a
registry check noticed.

publish-npm now ends with "Confirm the version is public on npm": it polls
`npm view` for up to 8 minutes and then fails with the approve/reject
commands and the setting to tick. It runs after the tag step on purpose: a
staged version already holds its number, the tag anchors the next Release
PR, and a re-run once the version is approved finds it on npm and skips
every step. A failed publish job also holds release-pr back, as it already
did, so the next Release PR is not computed on top of a half-published one.

The publish step itself now explains npm's opaque "409 Cannot publish over
previously staged version" — what a re-run hits while the version is still
staged. The job timeout goes from 20 to 30 minutes to cover the wait.

Both steps were exercised locally against a fake npm: a staged 409, a normal
publish, a version that appears, and one that never does. RELEASING.md says
to tick "Allow npm publish" when adding a package's trusted publisher, and
what to do when the new check fails.

body:
Bumps [aws-lc-rs](https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs) from 1.18.1 to 1.18.2.
Release notes

Sourced from aws-lc-rs's releases.

aws-lc-rs v1.18.2

What's Changed

  • Implement Eq and PartialEq for RSA and EdDSA parameters by @​dsykes16 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1228
    • RsaParameters can now be compared directly against RSA verification constants. Algorithms with different digests, padding schemes, or modulus-size ranges compare unequal. EdDSAParameters also gains equality support.
  • Add wasm32-wasip2 and wasm32-wasip3 support by @​ricochet in aws/aws-lc-rs#1239
    • Adds non-FIPS builds using universal bindings, with CI coverage under Wasmtime and wasi-sdk 34. WASIp3 requires nightly Rust.
    • Direct aws-lc-sys consumers must disable the default all-bindings feature for these targets.
  • Publish the intended RandomizedNonceKey::open_in_place documentation by @​Serophots in aws/aws-lc-rs#1227
    • Makes the existing nonce, ciphertext/tag layout, and buffer-on-error contract visible in rustdoc. No runtime behavior changes.

Upstream AWS-LC

  • aws-lc-sys v0.46.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.11.0 (previously v5.7.0). See also the release notes for v5.8.0, v5.9.0, and v5.10.0.
    • The Ed25519 C-implementation decoder now rejects non-canonical public keys, matching the assembly-optimized implementations: aws/aws-lc#3457
    • Includes ChaCha20-Poly1305 key-material zeroization and fixes ML-KEM CPU feature detection to avoid illegal-instruction failures on x86-64 CPUs with AVX2 but no BMI2: aws/aws-lc#3552 and aws/aws-lc#3596
  • aws-lc-fips-sys v0.14.3 updates its bundled AWS-LC FIPS 4.2.0 snapshot and regenerates bindings. It remains on the FIPS 4.x release line.

Build Improvements

  • Raise the minimum system AWS-LC version to 5.7.0 by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1243
    • Non-FIPS system-library installations must now provide AWS-LC 5.7.0 or newer, previously 1.68.0. Bundled-source builds and FIPS version requirements are unchanged.
  • Fix static FIPS system-library linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1236
    • Fixes unresolved FIPS_mode references with GNU ld.bfd when linking a prebuilt static FIPS library, including binaries that do not call crypto and builds where LTO removes those calls.
    • Uses whole-archive linking to retain libcrypto, including in downstream Rust staticlib outputs. This can increase binary size; dynamic FIPS and non-FIPS linking are unchanged.
  • Fix Cranelift linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1234
    • Normalizes binding link names to avoid undefined-symbol failures, including when Cranelift is selected through Cargo profiles rather than RUSTFLAGS. The AWS_LC_SYS_NO_U1_BINDINGS workaround is no longer needed.
  • Fix jitterentropy builds with optimizing CFLAGS and newer cc versions by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1254
    • Keeps filtered flags in effect throughout the jitterentropy builder's lifetime, preventing cached environment reads from allowing flags such as -O2 to override its required -O0.
  • Honor AWS_LC_SYS_CC in the main library build by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1255
    • Applies crate-specific compiler overrides before compiler lookup in both CC and CMake build paths, keeping compiler selection and capability probes consistent when cc caches environment reads.
  • Improve archive reproducibility through symlinked build paths by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1238
    • Prevents the non-Windows CC builder from incorporating symlink-resolved absolute build paths into archive member names, avoiding unnecessary downstream compile-cache misses. Windows short-path handling is unchanged.
  • Upgrade bindgen to 0.73 by @​xtqqczze in aws/aws-lc-rs#1244
  • Document the system-library trust model by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1218
    • Clarifies that supplied paths and pkg-config results are trusted build inputs, and that FIPS validation can execute candidate library code before accepting or rejecting it. Documents runner requirements and how to disable automatic system-library detection.

Issues Being Closed

  • Cranelift builds fail with codegen-backend = "cranelift" -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1231
  • Upgrade bindgen to v0.73 -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1245
  • Undefined FIPS_mode when linking a prebuilt FIPS module into a binary that does not use crypto -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1246
  • Jitterentropy fails with "must not be compiled with optimizations" in aws-lc-rs v1.18.1 / aws-lc-sys v0.45.0 -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1252

Other Merged PRs

  • docs: align pull request template with AWS-LC by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1219

title: chore(deps): Bump redb from 4.3.0 to 4.4.0
body:
Bumps [redb](https://github.com/cberner/redb) from 4.3.0 to 4.4.0.
Release notes

Sourced from redb's releases.

4.4.0

New features

  • Implement Value and Key for the NonZero integer types, NonZeroU8 to NonZeroU128 and NonZeroI8 to NonZeroI128.
  • Add Value::NICHE, an optional byte string that a type never encodes to. When a type declares one, Option of that type encodes None as it, in place of a tag byte. Adding a niche to a type changes the encoding of Option of it, and its type name with it, so the two are not equivalent types: a table that stores Option of the type from before it declared the niche fails to open with TableTypeMismatch instead of being misread, and can be read through a copy of the type that declares no niche.
  • Stabilize ReadableTable::lower_bound() and ReadableTable::upper_bound(), which return a read-only Cursor, modeled on the standard library's BTreeMap cursors.
  • Stabilize Table::lower_bound_mut() and Table::upper_bound_mut(), which return a CursorMut modeled on the standard library's BTreeMap cursors. Inserting sorted data through insert_before() can be around 3x faster than insert().

Bug fixes

  • Fix a bug where check_integrity() could report that it repaired corruption, after a transaction that grew the file size was aborted.
  • Fix Database::create() repairing the database it had just created, which failed with RepairAborted under a repair callback that aborts.
  • Fix unbounded memory growth in the page cache under write workloads, when the cache never reached its configured size limit.
  • Fix Durability::None commits being lost on a clean close, after a panic was caught inside an earlier write transaction.
  • Fix compact() leaving free regions at the end of the file, when the compaction emptied more of them than it made commits.
  • Fix compact() waiting forever when the caller holds a write transaction. It fails with CompactionError::TransactionInProgress, as it does for a read transaction.

Adding a niche to a type changes the encoding of Option of it, and its type name with it, so the two are not equivalent types: a table that stores Option of the type from before it declared the niche fails to open with TableTypeMismatch instead of being misread, and can be read through a copy of the type that declares no niche.
  • Stabilize ReadableTable::lower_bound() and ReadableTable::upper_bound(), which return a read-only Cursor, modeled on the standard library's BTreeMap cursors.
  • Stabilize Table::lower_bound_mut() and Table::upper_bound_mut(), which return a CursorMut modeled on the standard library's BTreeMap cursors. Inserting sorted data through insert_before() can be around 3x faster than insert().

Bug fixes

  • Fix a bug where check_integrity() could report that it repaired corruption, after a transaction that grew the file size was aborted.
  • Fix Database::create() repairing the database it had just created, which failed with RepairAborted under a repair callback that aborts.
  • Fix unbounded memory growth in the page cache under write workloads, when the cache never reached its configured size limit.
  • Fix Durability::None commits being lost on a clean close, after a panic was caught inside an earlier write transaction.
  • Fix compact() leaving free regions at the end of the file, when the compaction emptied more of them than it made commits.
  • Fix compact() waiting forever when the caller holds a write transaction. It fails with CompactionError::TransactionInProgress, as it does for a read transaction.

## What changed

Progresses #17 with a bounded fit assessment before any transfer. Adds `docs/baseline-assessment/README.md`, `inventory.json` and `execution.json`: eight candidate groups, 46 SHA-256-identified source assets at immutable upstream/downstream revisions, upstream overlap, interfaces/dependencies/consumers, proposed dispositions, retained execution evidence and a smallest-next-contribution proposal.

The recommendation is to adapt a real-source replay to the existing upstream review contract. Maintainers should choose TRQP adaptation or the requested VRC 0.3 example. Downstream pressure-test vocabularies are not equivalent to the upstream review contract. Consolidation, ownership, independent review and merge rights remain explicit decisions. Pending CI #14 is distinguished from accepted main. No code transfer, schema/corpus change, workflow change or enforcement change is included.

## Artefact IDs affected

Assessment-local C1–C8. No canonical RAHP record IDs changed.

## Provenance — what triggered this change?

Issue #17 and the maintainer proposal on #9. Upstream source: ab191485b48bca805ea2cc962c2ea9476a65db66. Downstream source: af58247e83d0aff4d47650d929bfc6280d9e41d3. Prepared with AI assistance; recommendations are not task-force decisions or independent review.

## Validation output

```text
Upstream: 12 tests passed; corpus 0 errors / 32 warnings; minimal review and temporary build exit 0.
Downstream: 3 standalone TRQP tests, 4 engine-contract tests and 6 freshness tests passed; retained replay matched.
Inventory: 46 source digests verified; eight candidate groups and eight successful executions; local document links verified.
```

The initial environment lacked jsonschema. Review tests failed and corpus schema checks were skipped; requirements were installed and all recorded checks rerun. Full outputs, dependency versions and limitations are retained in execution.json. No complete downstream suite, unfamiliar-adopter trial, live authorization/revocation, independent review or deployed Pages verification is claimed.

## Decisions and residual gaps

Keep #17 open: candidate acceptance, first target, vocabulary/validator architecture, maintenance ownership and GAP-5.1 independent review remain pending. This assessment supplies its inventory/mapping/disposition/proposal deliverables without implementing unsettled decisions.

The contributor reviewed PR #18 and explicitly authorized DCO sign-off using the existing author identity. The amended head `fec5ed096354518486ec73cf4b4bc92d11bdad94` preserves the original file tree and has a passing DCO check. Independent review and maintainer acceptance remain required. No automatic merge is enabled.

title: feat(vta)!: did:scid:vh:1 identities, create/1.2, and VTA/VTC presentation config
body:
did:scid:vh:1 support in the VTA and VTC (spec trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#75: VTI-KEY-160..166, VTI-VTA-034..036, VTI-VTC-004).

**VTA**
- `[dids] default_did_method` (webvh) and `scid_also_known_as` (true) with env overrides, runtime config keys, setup prompt; TEE allowlist admits did:scid where it admits did:webvh.
- Serves `vta/webvh/dids/create/1.2` alongside 1.0/1.1 (precedence request → VTC → VTA → defaults; `scidAliasRequired`; swiyu-verifier keeps the alias off).
- Native did:scid identities: bare DID is the identity, secrets under the did:scid key ids, the webvh/dids family accepts either form, resolver seeded at boot with each identity's source.
- Hardcoded did:webvh checks and identity comparisons accept did:scid by DID (ignoring `src`); Trust Task issuer↔VM binding stays exact, signer methods returned in the issuer's form.
- CLI `--did-method` / `--scid-also-known-as`; `VtaClient::create_did_webvh_presented` (`DidPresentation`), sends 1.2 only when stated.

**VTC**
- `[dids]` preference (None inherits the VTA), console card, sent on group/room/setup mints.
- did:scid members accepted and recorded as presented; verified sources persisted and seeded at boot.

Tests: nextest 6550/6550 (workspace excl. VTC) and 3511/3511 (vtc-service, vtc-client), doctests, admin-ui 1320 passed; fmt/clippy clean.

Open: TEE autogen presents did:webvh only; interactive `vtc setup` has no presentation prompt; list/get don't carry the presented form (needs a spec field).

**Depends on (all released):** didwebvh-rs 0.8.1 (decentralized-identity/didwebvh-rs#56), affinidi-tdk-rs#965/#966 (affinidi-did-common 0.4.4 `scid` module, resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.43 native did:scid with durable floors, messaging-sdk 0.38.1), trust-tasks 0.33.2 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#862 create/1.2, #863 trust-tasks-proof fix). Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#75 and #76 (VTI-KEY-160..166).

Every dependency resolves from crates.io: no `[patch.crates-io]`. The deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy workspace also moves to resolver 0.8.43.
