title: feat(vta)!: did:scid:vh:1 identities, create/1.2, and VTA/VTC presentation config (#2257)
body:
feat(vta)!: did:scid:vh:1 identities, create/1.2, and VTA/VTC presentation config (#2257)

* feat(vta-sdk): did:scid:vh:1 identity rules and did:scid secret kids (VTI-KEY-160 to VTI-KEY-164)

vta_sdk::did_scid holds the string rules every consumer needs without a DID library: a durable identity is a did:webvh or a did:scid:vh:1 (VTI-KEY-001); a did:scid's ?src= is a locator, so references compare by DID and fragment (VTI-KEY-160, VTI-KEY-163); the two forms of one log are distinct identities (VTI-KEY-164). DidMethod names the form a new log is presented as (webvh by default).

select_secret_kid publishes a did:scid identity's secrets under the did:scid DID, from key records named by its did:webvh log's method ids, because that is where the identity's resolved document lists its keys (VTI-KEY-161). A did:webvh bundle is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-config)!: [dids] default_did_method and scid_also_known_as (VTI-VTA-034, VTI-VTA-035)

AppConfig gains [dids]: default_did_method (webvh, the default, or scid) and scid_also_known_as (default true). Env: VTA_DIDS_DEFAULT_DID_METHOD and VTA_DIDS_SCID_ALSO_KNOWN_AS, blocked under KMS like every other override. Runtime: dids.default_did_method and dids.scid_also_known_as on config/show and config/patch, applied to the next DID created. The setup wizard asks how to present the VTA's DIDs when it mints a did:webvh, and from_toml takes [dids].

A TEE allowed_did_methods list that admits did:webvh admits did:scid:vh:1 too: its log is a did:webvh log.

Breaking: AppConfig and WizardInputs gain a field.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vti-common): validate_did admits a did:scid DID URL with its src locator (VTI-KEY-160)

A did:scid identity is given out as did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=<host>/<path> wherever a recipient may not hold a source (VTI-KEY-163), so every DID guard refused it on '?', '=' and '/'. The DID before ?src= is still held to the method-specific-id class, and the src to that class plus '/'. No other query, and no query on another method, is admitted.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-webvh): record the did:scid identity of a did:webvh log

ScidIdentity, keyed by the bare did:scid DID under a scid: prefix (clear of the did: prefix list_dids scans), says which log verifies it, whether the DID is presented as the did:scid (VTI-KEY-165) and whether the log lists the alias (VTI-KEY-166). It sits beside the record because the published WebvhDidRecord's schema refuses unknown members. log_did_for maps either name of a log to its did:webvh, so the webvh/dids family can take the did:scid.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta)!: serve vta/webvh/dids/create/1.2 and present new DIDs as did:scid (VTI-VTA-034 to VTI-VTA-036, VTI-KEY-165, VTI-KEY-166)

create/1.2 takes didMethod and scidAlsoKnownAs. Each falls back to [dids], then to did:webvh with the did:scid alias listed. A did:scid identity always lists its alias, so refusing it, a template forbidding alsoKnownAs (defaults.scidAlsoKnownAs: false), or a supplied did_log without it is answered with the declared scidAliasRequired. The response states didMethod, scidAlsoKnownAs, webvhDid and scidDidUrl; did is the identity applied. 1.0 and 1.1 refuse 1.2's request members and answer in their own shapes, with [dids] still applied, as the spec requires.

A DID presented as did:scid is used natively: its identity is the bare DID; the context records it with its src (VTI-KEY-163); key records keep the log's method ids and its secrets are registered under the identity's own. Every webvh/dids task accepts either name of a log. Deleting a log retires both names: credentials, ACL entries and sessions held under the did:scid go too, and a VTA or context presenting the did:scid blocks the delete as the did:webvh would.

The resolver gets a log's native did:scid document and source whenever the log lists its alias (VTI-KEY-161), and at boot for every did:scid identity the VTA holds, so a bare did:scid resolves after a restart, serverless ones included. The VTA's own identity can be a did:scid: its key records are found under its log, and its secrets registered under the bare DID and the configured DID URL.

CLI: vta create-did-webvh, vta webvh create-did and vta did-mgmt dids create take --did-method and --scid-also-known-as; provision-integration takes the DID_METHOD and SCID_ALSO_KNOWN_AS vars. Setup mints the mediator as did:webvh: whether it can be addressed as a did:scid is the mediator's to support.

Breaking: CreateDidWebvhBody, CreateDidWebvhResultBody and CreateDidWebvhParams gain fields.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vti)!: accept did:scid:vh:1 identities natively (VTI-KEY-160 to VTI-KEY-164)

Identity comparisons go by DID, ignoring a did:scid src locator, and never by converting to did:webvh: the DIDComm sender binding (whose proven sender is the bare did:scid DID authorization then sees), the trust-task proof's document/method/controller check, the lightweight DIDComm key lookup and the re-resolve-on-miss check. The issuer/verificationMethod binding stays exact; a producer writes both in one form (VTI-KEY-163).

Network-resolved method lists (the host-session gate, the mediator readiness gate) and the log-URL and REST-URL derivations take a did:scid:vh:1 as the log its src names (vta_sdk::did_scid::webvh_did). A did:scid persona signs with its log's keys under the did:scid as named; its own document is derived from the log. A VTA presenting a did:scid lists its services and self-hosts its log as its did:webvh would. TEE genesis lists the did:scid alias per [dids].

DID shortening abbreviates a did:scid's SCID and src host like a did:webvh's, in vta_sdk::display_name and the admin console, with shared vectors.

The SDK client gains create_did_webvh_presented and DidPresentation, sending create/1.2 only when a 1.2 member is stated, so callers and VTAs that predate it are untouched; pnm did-mgmt dids create takes --did-method and --scid-also-known-as.

Breaking: vta-cli-common's cmd_webvh_did_create_with_files takes a DidPresentation.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-sdk): a did:scid signs a Trust Task as itself and a stranger verifies it (VTI-KEY-161 to VTI-KEY-163)

The holder names its key under the did:scid DID URL with its src and writes issuer in the same form; a verifier with no prior knowledge resolves it through the src to the identity's own document and accepts the proof. A bare did:scid verifies only where the verifier holds a source, and the right key under another SCID is refused.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): a did:scid signer named with its src gets its proof method in that form (VTI-KEY-163)

keys/sign-document picks the method from the signer's own document, whose ids are under the bare did:scid DID. For an issuer written as the DID URL with src, the method is now named the same way, so issuer and verificationMethod agree in form, as the exact issuer binding requires.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): state the community's did:scid preference on the identities it mints (VTI-VTC-004)

[dids] default_did_method and scid_also_known_as (absent: the VTA's [dids] decides), with VTC_DIDS_DEFAULT_DID_METHOD / VTC_DIDS_SCID_ALSO_KNOWN_AS and the runtime keys dids.default_did_method / dids.scid_also_known_as, layered env > stored > file like dids.webvh_server. Group and community-room mints send them on vta/webvh/dids/create/1.2, and 1.1 when the community states nothing, so an unconfigured community sends what it did before. A group or room presented as did:scid is given out as its DID URL with src (VTI-KEY-163); a log this community serves is recorded under its did:webvh.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): accept did:scid members and state the community's own DID form at setup (VTI-VTC-004, VTI-KEY-164)

Key rotation takes a did:scid:vh:1 new DID, verified by its own document, and records the member under its identity, the bare DID. The messaging signer/sender binding and the issuer/holder check compare by identity, ignoring a did:scid src. The VTC's log label, root host and self-hosting follow a did:scid VTC DID to the log its src names. swiyu issuers stay did:webvh: the Swiss profile requires it.

vtc setup --from takes did_method and scid_also_known_as, sends them as the vtc-host template's DID_METHOD / SCID_ALSO_KNOWN_AS vars and writes them to [dids].

provision-integration hands a did:scid integration its DID URL with src, and its bundle keys under the bare DID, where its document lists them (VTI-KEY-161, VTI-KEY-163).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): the console sets how group and room identities are presented (VTI-VTC-004)

A Groups-page card beside 'Where identities are published' writes dids.default_did_method and dids.scid_also_known_as: did:webvh or did:scid, and whether the alias is listed (always, for a did:scid). Unset, the card says the community's VTA decides.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): the swiyu-verifier template keeps the did:scid alias off its log (VTI-KEY-166)

The Swiss Profile Anchor forbids alsoKnownAs, so the template now says so with the binding defaults.scidAlsoKnownAs: false, and the [dids] default alias no longer lands in its signed state. A did:scid presentation of it is refused with scidAliasRequired. Also answers the setup wizard's new presentation prompt in the scripted existing-keys test, and a clippy fix.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): remember where each verified did:scid was found, and seed the resolver at boot (VTI-KEY-162)

Members, administrators and peers are recorded by the bare did:scid DID, so after a restart the resolver could not resolve one until it next presented its src. Every proof the trust-task spine verifies under a did:scid DID URL with src now records that source, keyed by the bare DID and replaced when a newer one is presented; boot seeds DIDCacheClient::scid_sources() from the rows, as the VTA does for its own identities. The rows live in the members keyspace under a scid_source: prefix, clear of member listing and backed up with it. A source stays a hint: the resolver verifies the log and refuses an older one.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build(deps)!: the did:scid floors — affinidi-tdk 0.30, messaging-sdk 0.38.1, resolver 0.8.42, did-common 0.4.4, didwebvh-rs 0.8.1

The did:scid work calls APIs these releases introduce: the native did:scid resolution, source book and rollback guard (resolver 0.8.42), the scid reference helpers and src-tolerant lookups (did-common 0.4.4), the did:scid form of a log (didwebvh-rs 0.8.1), and a did:scid sender's DIDComm (messaging-sdk 0.38.1), all under affinidi-tdk 0.30 (affinidi-tdk-rs #965). trust-tasks-rs carries vta/webvh/dids/create/1.2 from its next release (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #862); its floor moves when that is published.

Breaking: affinidi-tdk moves a minor.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vti-common): durable did:scid version floors (VTI-KEY-162)

A did:scid identity's `?src=` is the presenter's choice. did:webvh
verification binds each log entry to the host its own DID names, but a
portable log that has moved still names its former host in its early
entries, so whoever holds that host can serve the log as it stood before
the move. The resolver's source book refuses a log older than one it has
verified and checks an unknown source against known ones; this keeps what
it knows across a restart.

`scid_floors` stores the resolver's `ScidSourceRecord` (sources + version
floor) as `scid_floor:<bare did>` rows in a keyspace the node chooses,
merging on write so a floor is never lowered. `seed` loads them into a
resolver at boot. `spawn` persists records as the book changes them, through
the book's listener into a bounded channel (the listener never blocks), and
on a periodic sweep that also catches an identity resolved before it was
authorised, for the identities an `Authorised` predicate accepts.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta): an ACL subject's did:scid version floor survives a restart (VTI-KEY-162)

The VTA seeds its resolver's did:scid source book from the `scid_floor:`
rows in its `acl` keyspace at boot, and persists the book's records for every
ACL subject as they change (`vti_common::scid_floors::spawn`, ended with the
server's other tasks). The rows sit beside the `acl:` entries, which are read
by prefix, so they are not ACL entries, and travel with the keyspace in a
backup. The VTA's own did:scid identities are unaffected: their logs are held
locally and preloaded.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): did:scid version floors for members and administrators survive a restart (VTI-KEY-162)

`scid_sources` now keeps `vti_common::scid_floors` records — every source a
did:scid identity was verified at and the latest version — in the `members`
keyspace, in place of a single DID URL. Boot migrates the `scid_source:` rows
written before (read the old shape, write the record, then remove the row) and
seeds the resolver with sources and floor, so a former host serving a member's
moved log as it stood before the move is refused from the first request. The
resolver's records are persisted for every member and ACL subject as they
change (`scid_sources::spawn`, ended with the server's other tasks).
`record` / `source_of` keep their behaviour.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build(deps): affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.43, for durable did:scid version floors

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vti-common): the did:scid floor writer test names its live resolver apart from the helper

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

and trust-tasks-proof 0.33.2 verifies a did:scid key named with its src

title: fix(vta)!: bound each client and unauthenticated peers by default (VTI-TRN-029)
body:
## What and why

VTI-TRN-029 is a MUST: *a node MUST bound the resources any one subject can consume, and MUST bound those available to unauthenticated peers separately.* #2264 added the operation budgets but left all three unset, so an unsized VTA met neither clause.

- **Per client** (`operation_rate_limit_per_subject_per_sec`): absent now means **100/s** (`vta_config::DEFAULT_OPERATION_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SUBJECT_PER_SEC`).
- **Unauthenticated** (`operation_rate_limit_unauthenticated_per_sec`): absent now means **50/s**.
- No setting turns either off; a higher value loosens them. Zero is still refused at load. Read through `ServerConfig::operation_per_subject_per_sec()` / `operation_unauthenticated_per_sec()`.
- **Appliance** (`operation_rate_limit_per_sec`) stays unset by default: its right value follows the hardware, and TRN-029 does not require it.

The defaults are generous on purpose: they stop a runaway client or a flood, not ordinary heavy use. Refusals are retryable (REST 429 / signed `unavailable`), and `VtaClient::idempotent` already honours them.

## Test clock

The budgets read an injectable `BudgetClock`. Budget tests run on `BudgetClock::manual()`, which does not refill while the test runs, instead of racing the monotonic clock (the DIDComm spine tests assumed ten signed dispatches finish inside one second). `TestAppOptions::operation_budget_clock` carries it into REST integration tests; the resend test advances the clock instead of sleeping.

Two existing tests sent more than the new default in under a second, from one subject: every dispatched verb from one stranger (`envelope_only_carriage`), and filling the contact-list cap (`the_contact_annotation_tasks_refuse_what_they_declare`). Each now sizes the budget it needs, since the budget is not what it tests.

## Breaking

`OperationBudget` no longer implements `Default`; `TestAppOptions` gains `operation_budget_clock`.

## Requirements

- VTI-TRN-029: both clauses now hold with no configuration.

## Checks

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6627 run, all pass after the two test fixes (both re-run)
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3558 passed
- `cargo test -p vta-service -p vta-config --doc`: pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

## Backport

none

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.34.0` → `0.34.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.34.0` → `0.34.1` | patch |

| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.34.0` → `0.34.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.34.0` → `0.34.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.34.0` → `0.34.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.34.0` → `0.34.1` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.27.3` → `0.27.4` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.9.4`) | `0.9.3` → `0.9.4` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.3` → `0.9.4` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(build): a lint that keeps the wire conventions
body:
Stacked on #901 (base `feat/spec-wire-conventions`); GitHub retargets it to `main` when #901 merges.

CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md "Wire conventions for common members" spells
instants, pagination, `since` and `created` one way each; #901 gave every
offender a new version. scripts/lib/wire-conventions.mjs keeps it so: the
build fails when the latest version of a non-retired spec — or any shared
definition it $refs, followed transitively — carries an integer instant,
a bare `timestamp`, pageSize/pageToken/continuationToken, `offset` beside a
cursor or limit, a nullable `nextCursor`, `truncated` beside `nextCursor`, a
response-side `cursor` or string `next`, a `since` that is not a date-time,
or a boolean `created`.

Superseded versions are not checked: they keep the spelling they were
published with, which is why their successors exist. Shapes that only look
like a convention go in wire-conventions-allowlist.json, keyed by slug,
with the reason; the one entry today is messaging/queue/list's `truncated`,
a survey-coverage flag. A stale entry warns.

Following $refs is what found the five vta instants #901 picked up in its
last commit; a scan of payload schemas alone had missed them. Every rule
was exercised against the superseded versions and a planted spec.

title: feat(specs): one spelling for instants, pagination, since and created, in 74 new spec versions
body:
Aligns the registry on one spelling for four recurring shapes, as written down in CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md "Wire conventions for common members" (#899). Every affected spec gets a **new version** — no existing version folder changes — and each new `spec.md` opens with a `## Changes from <old>` section an implementer can migrate from alone. All affected specs are `draft`, so each break is a MINOR increment under SPEC §5.2; the old versions stay published.

**74 new spec versions**, plus new shared components: messaging/_shared/0.2, vta/_shared/0.7, vtc/_shared/0.3 

| Convention | What moved | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| Instants are RFC 3339 strings, event instants named `*At` | 22 Unix-seconds members: `auth/oob/*` (`decisionDeadline` → `decisionClosesAt`, `claimDeadline` → `claimClosesAt`, `notAfter` → `sessionEndsAt`), `vtc/auth/*`, `messaging` `Account`/`AuditEntry` (`timestamp` → `recordedAt`), vtc `HostedRoom`, vta `DidTemplateRecord` and `AgentNameEntry` (found by the follow-up lint, which follows shared `$ref`s) | 1–3, 9 |
| Pagination is `cursor` + `limit` → `nextCursor`, absent on the last page | `pageSize`/`truncated` (10 specs), `offset`/`total` (keys, did-management), response `cursor`/`next` (rooms/records, vtc/elections), nullable `nextCursor` (14 vtc, 6 git-ns, registry/query) | 2–4, 6–7 |
| `since` is an inclusive time filter | `vtc/admin/events/subscribe` `since` → `resumeToken`; `consent/list`'s delta token → `syncToken`/`nextSyncToken` | 3, 7 |
| `created` is a timestamp | boolean `created` → `wasCreated` in 13 persona/policy/registry/vault/vta specs (incl. `vta/_shared/0.7` `WriteResult`) | 5 |

The last commit regenerates all four libraries: 1020 specs checked against TypeScript, Rust, Go and Dart — all agree. `cargo check`, `tsc`, `go build/vet` and `dart analyze` pass locally.

### Calls worth a reviewer's eye
- **Retired specs get no version.** `messaging/account/change-queue-limits`, `change-type` and `messaging/admin/audit-log` are retired, so they stay on `messaging/_shared/0.1`.
- **Not pagination, so not changed:** `messaging/queue/list` and `messaging/stats/show` `truncated` (a survey that stopped early), `git-ns` bind/job `next` (a redirect), `vtc/website/files/show` `offset` (a byte offset), `voting/board/read` `from`/`next` (transparency-log positions). `vault/sync` is a feed that always returns its position, so it renames `pageSize` → `limit` and keeps `truncated`.
- **"More exists but I can't page" is gone.** `acl/list` 0.2 and `vault/list` 0.3 allowed `truncated: true` with no cursor; the new versions require a `nextCursor` whenever more matching entries exist.
- **`totalEstimate` stays** in four vtc lists: an approximate count, not a paging mechanism.
- **`wireCompatibleWith` removed** from six new versions whose predecessors declared it — a member rename is not wire-identical.
- **Security & Privacy.** 24 new versions inherited a section without the four lint sub-headings from predecessors on the allowlist; rather than grow that debt list, each was restructured under Data carried / Correlation / Retention / Consent/purpose, moving existing text and adding no new MUST/SHOULD/MAY.
- **`auth/oob` family docs** (`_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md`, `TRIGGER-LINK.md`) are edited in place: they now describe the current versions, and the trigger link's `_exp` stays integer seconds, computed from `claimClosesAt` when the link is built.
- **Not swept:** 43 `date-time` names that don't end in `At` — mostly range bounds and filters (`since`, `until`, `validFrom`/`validUntil`) or external vocabulary (`created`, `notBefore`, `retryAfter`). A bare `at` (15 specs), `serverTime`, `lastSeen` and `votingOpens`/`votingCloses` are candidates for a later pass.

title: chore: release 5 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go/didcomm` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/didcomm/v0.2.1`) | `0.2.0` → `0.2.1` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_proof` | pub.dev | `0.1.2` → `0.1.3` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_https` | pub.dev | `0.1.2` → `0.1.3` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_didcomm` | pub.dev | `0.1.0` → `0.1.1` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_capability_client` | pub.dev | `0.1.0` → `0.1.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(dart): the sibling packages require the current trust_tasks core
body:
Every published sibling (trust_tasks_https, _proof, _didcomm, and the
unreleased _tsp and _capability_client) declared `trust_tasks: ^0.1.0`,
which pub reads as `>=0.1.0 <0.2.0`. A consumer therefore got core 0.1.19,
missing every fix since, and an app already on trust_tasks 0.9.x could not
add a sibling at all: the constraints conflict. tag-dart's release check
did not notice, because it verifies against the newest published core the
constraint admits. The floor is now ^0.9.3.

That core releases the replay claim itself when a handler throws (#876),
so the HTTPS server and the DIDComm and TSP consumers no longer release it
a second time. Their release also fired when the guard failed to record a
response after the handler had run, freeing a document whose effect had
already happened; the core keeps the claim in that case, and so do they now.

They also pass `responseToJson` (#878), so a persistent ReplayGuard caches
the success response as JSON and a resend is answered with it.

title: ci(release): give the publish job the semver job's swap, so the verify build of a new crate survives
body:
The release job has died on the last three pushes to main (fe9f24d6, b82fb17a, 416b04c9) while
publishing vti-voting for the first time: "The runner has received a shutdown signal", about
five minutes into cargo publish's verify build. vti-voting is not on crates.io, so vta-service
and vtc-service (which depend on it) cannot publish either, and the release is half-shipped.

The cause is memory. Measured cold with a RUSTC_WRAPPER recording each rustc's peak RSS,
trust-tasks-rs 0.33 peaks at 9.75 GB and 10.39 GB in the two rustc invocations that build it;
nothing else in the tree exceeds 1.1 GB. The runner has 16 GB of RAM and a 4 GB swapfile. The
release PR job already replaces that swapfile with a 12 GB one for the same reason; the publish
job did not.

After merge: run the **Release-plz** workflow manually (workflow_dispatch, `package` empty) to publish vti-voting and everything behind it. The next push to main would also do it.

Upstream note: one crate needing ~10 GB to compile in debug is worth raising in trust-tasks-tf (splitting the generated specs behind features), but the swap unblocks the release now.

title: trust-tasks-tsp-v0.34.0
body:
### Added

- **tsp**: The Trust Tasks TSP binding speaks TSP 1.0 ([#881](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/881))

affinidi-tsp 0.2 -> 0.3. The ToIP TSP specification released 1.0
  (trustoverip/tswg-tsp-specification#86, YTSP-BAA): Rev 3's wire with the
  ESSR sender VID mandatory in every confidential payload. 1.0 and Rev 3 do not
  interoperate in either direction, so a consumer of this binding moves with
  its peers - hence the !.

  No source or API change here: affinidi-tsp 0.3 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#967)
  keeps every signature this binding uses. MetaEnvelope::parse, which a relay
  calls before unpack, now reads any TSP version.

  Unblocks verifiable-trust-infrastructure, which cannot move to affinidi-tsp
  0.3 while this binding resolves 0.2 beside it.



### Fixed

- **trust-tasks-tsp**: A sender mismatch maps to proofRequired, as the DIDComm bindings' sender failures do ([#882](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/882))
- Binding rejection reasons carry a category, not the error's text ([#877](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/877))

The DIDComm v2.1, DIDComm v1 and TSP bindings built the malformedRequest
  reason in `into_reject_reason` from the error's `Display`. That text holds the
  deserializer's member names and line/column offsets, sender DIDs and VIDs,
  verkeys, and upstream envelope and resolver failures. A caller that answered
  with the reason put all of it on the wire, which SPEC §10.4 forbids. The HTTPS
  binding already avoided this.

  - A body that does not deserialise now maps through
    `RejectReason::malformed_from_serde`, as the HTTPS binding's does.
  - A thread disagreement names the header and member, not their values.
  - Every other malformedRequest carries one constant reason per binding.

  The error's `Display` is unchanged, so logs keep the detail. The codes are
  unchanged; only the reason text differs.

- Proofs are verified over the document as received, so a genuine proof survives a typed re-encoding ([#875](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/875))

Every Rust consumer verified a proof over its parsed TrustTask re-serialised:
  consume_inbound through ProofVerifier::verify, the HTTPS server through
  DynProofVerifier::verify_json on a TrustTask<Value>. Re-serialisation
  reproduces the signed bytes only when every member round-trips, and several
  do not — a generated `#[serde(default)]` member the producer omitted comes
  back as `false`, a member the payload type does not model is dropped, and a
  framework timestamp written `+00:00` is re-rendered as `Z`. A genuine proof
  over any such document was refused proofInvalid.

  - ProofVerifier and DynProofVerifier gain a provided `verify_received(&Value)`;
    the affinidi Verifier overrides it with its exact `verify_raw`, and
    ErasedVerifier forwards it. Existing implementations keep the old,
    re-serialising behaviour by default.
  - ProofPolicy gains `VerifyReceived(&V, &Value)` and `with_received`, which
    turns a caller's `Verify` into it. consume_inbound re-parses the received
    value and refuses proofInvalid when it is not the document being consumed,
    since a proof over one document vouches for nothing about another.
  - The TSP, DIDComm v2 and DIDComm v1 `receive` paths keep the document as
    received and apply `with_received`, so their callers change nothing.
  - The HTTPS server verifies over the request body parsed as a Value, keeping
    the typed parse that refuses a duplicated top-level member.
  - DynProofVerifier's doc no longer claims the erasure is lossless.

  All additive: cargo semver-checks reports no update required for
  trust-tasks-rs, trust-tasks-proof or trust-tasks-https.

title: trust-tasks-https-v0.34.0
body:
### Fixed

- The HTTPS servers check expiry, recipient and freshness before identity, as consume_inbound does ([#879](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/879))

The Rust and Dart HTTPS servers ran identity resolution (§7.2 item 6) before
  expiry, recipient and freshness (items 4 and 5a). consume_inbound and every
  other binding run them in §7.2 order. So a document failing both kinds of
  check was refused identityMismatch over HTTPS, and expired or wrongRecipient
  everywhere else.

  Both servers now use §7.2 order when the sender is authenticated. With no
  authenticated sender, identity still runs first. Then the only identity that
  can disagree is the recipient, and §8.1 suppresses that refusal. Checking the
  recipient first would answer wrongRecipient instead, telling an
  unauthenticated prober which VIDs the server is not, and undoing the PR #75
  suppression both servers' regression tests pin. Those tests are unchanged and
  pass.

title: feat(vta)!: operation budgets for Trust Task work (VTI-TRN-029)
body:
## What and why

A VTA offered more Trust Task work than it can serve stops answering in time: on a TEE appliance the load balancer returns 502s, health checks fail and the watchdog restarts the enclave. Only unauthenticated REST routes were limited, per IP.

This adds three budgets, each unset by default so existing deployments are unchanged:

- **Appliance** (`operation_rate_limit_per_sec`, `_burst`): all clients together, across REST, DIDComm and TSP.
- **Per client** (`operation_rate_limit_per_subject_per_sec`): each client with standing, keyed by DID, charged first so one client's excess never spends the shared budget.
- **Unauthenticated** (`operation_rate_limit_unauthenticated_per_sec`): DIDComm / TSP senders without an ACL entry, including login steps and refusals, kept apart from the clients' budget. Past it there is no reply. Anonymous REST stays on the existing per-IP limiters.

Tasks are charged their cost in signs (vault release 2, DID create/delete 10, others 1), after authentication and before they run. Refusals: REST `429` with `x-rate-limit-source: vta` and `x-rate-limit-scope: operations` / `operations-subject`; DIDComm and TSP a signed, retryable `unavailable` with `retryAfter`. A refused document is not recorded, so resending it is a retry.

The keys come from config or the TEE tenant overlay's `server` block (delivered every boot), never `config/patch`, which a TEE restart would drop. A zero is refused at load. `render-tenant-overlay.sh` gains matching flags; `pnm`/`cnm` explain the new refusals.

Tests: budget unit tests (weights, per-client isolation, separate unauthenticated bound); REST integration (429 contract, per-client scope, unconfigured VTA, resend after refusal); DIDComm spine (clients and strangers bounded separately, login steps over DIDComm/TSP, silent drop past the unauthenticated budget); overlay and config validation; CLI hints.

Known limits, documented: a client's share is spent even when the appliance budget then refuses; one stranger can use up the shared unauthenticated budget; unmeasured tasks cost 1. The passkey-VM REST routes are not Trust Tasks and are not charged.

## Requirements

- VTI-TRN-029: bound what one subject can consume, and unauthenticated peers separately (implemented).
- VTI-OPS-026 / 027: a refused document is not recorded as accepted.

## Backport

none

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean (except existing lints in `vti-voting`, `vta-mobile-core` and `sign_formats.rs`, which this PR does not touch)

feat(vta)!: operation budgets for Trust Task work (VTI-TRN-029) (#2264)

* feat(vta)!: operation budgets for Trust Task work (VTI-TRN-029)

A VTA offered more Trust Task work than it can serve stops answering in
time; on a TEE appliance health checks then fail and the watchdog restarts
the enclave. Three budgets now bound that work, each unset by default:

- operation_rate_limit_per_sec (+ _burst): the whole appliance, shared by
  REST, DIDComm and TSP.
- operation_rate_limit_per_subject_per_sec: each client with standing, by
  its DID, charged before the appliance budget.
- operation_rate_limit_unauthenticated_per_sec: DIDComm / TSP senders
  without an ACL entry (login steps, public tasks, counterparties,
  approvers, refusals), apart from the clients' budget. Past it there is no
  reply, so a flood cannot cost a signature per message.

A task is charged its weight in signs (vault release 2, DID create and
delete 10, others 1), after authentication and before it runs. REST
answers 429 with x-rate-limit-source: vta and scope operations or
operations-subject; DIDComm and TSP a signed, retryable unavailable with
retryAfter. A refused document is not recorded (VTI-OPS-026), so a resend
is a retry.

The keys are config and tenant-overlay only, never config/patch, so a TEE
enclave restart keeps them. A zero is refused at load. pnm and cnm explain
operations and operations-subject refusals.

Breaking: TestAppOptions (test-support) gains two public fields.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): steady the budget resend test; name the operation budget in the unavailable hint

The resend test ran at 10/s, where a token refills every 100 ms, so ten
requests on a slow runner could let the document through on its first
send. At 1/s the window is a second.

Over DIDComm and TSP a budget refusal surfaces as VtaError::Unavailable,
whose hint spoke only of the idempotency layer (VTI-TRN-029).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.34.0
body:
### Added

- **vault**: Vault/credentials/query subjectDid narrows to credentials presented as one identity ([#884](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/884))

An optional request member: the maintainer returns only credentials whose subject — the DID vault/credentials/present would present them as — is the named DID. It narrows the other constraints and does not satisfy the at-least-one-filter requirement on its own.

  A verifier that requires a particular holder (a community directory accepts a verified field only from a presentation its member holds) refuses a credential bound to a separate holder key; a wallet offering the holder a choice can now offer only the credentials that verifier will accept. A request member rather than a descriptor member, because every generated descriptor reader denies unknown members: a new descriptor member would break existing consumers, while a maintainer that predates this filter refuses it rather than ignoring it.



### Fixed

- Proofs are verified over the document as received, so a genuine proof survives a typed re-encoding ([#875](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/875))

Every Rust consumer verified a proof over its parsed TrustTask re-serialised:
  consume_inbound through ProofVerifier::verify, the HTTPS server through
  DynProofVerifier::verify_json on a TrustTask<Value>. Re-serialisation
  reproduces the signed bytes only when every member round-trips, and several
  do not — a generated `#[serde(default)]` member the producer omitted comes
  back as `false`, a member the payload type does not model is dropped, and a
  framework timestamp written `+00:00` is re-rendered as `Z`. A genuine proof
  over any such document was refused proofInvalid.

  - ProofVerifier and DynProofVerifier gain a provided `verify_received(&Value)`;
    the affinidi Verifier overrides it with its exact `verify_raw`, and
    ErasedVerifier forwards it. Existing implementations keep the old,
    re-serialising behaviour by default.
  - ProofPolicy gains `VerifyReceived(&V, &Value)` and `with_received`, which
    turns a caller's `Verify` into it. consume_inbound re-parses the received
    value and refuses proofInvalid when it is not the document being consumed,
    since a proof over one document vouches for nothing about another.
  - The TSP, DIDComm v2 and DIDComm v1 `receive` paths keep the document as
    received and apply `with_received`, so their callers change nothing.
  - The HTTPS server verifies over the request body parsed as a Value, keeping
    the typed parse that refuses a duplicated top-level member.
  - DynProofVerifier's doc no longer claims the erasure is lossless.

  All additive: cargo semver-checks reports no update required for
  trust-tasks-rs, trust-tasks-proof or trust-tasks-https.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.33.2` → `0.34.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.33.2` → `0.34.0` | breaking |

| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.33.2` → `0.34.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.33.2` → `0.34.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.33.2` → `0.34.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.33.2` → `0.34.0` | breaking |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.27.2` → `0.27.3` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.9.3`) | `0.9.2` → `0.9.3` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.2` → `0.9.3` | patch |
| `trust_tasks_https` | pub.dev | `0.1.1` → `0.1.2` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(rooms)!: record provenance, record retention and prune, and the epoch floor
body:
Implements trust-tasks-tf #865, #868 and #869, one commit each.

**Provenance (#865).** `rooms/records/put/0.3` on both hosts; `SealedRecordBody` carries basis/confidence/evidence/validFor/validUntil inside the signature. Provenance is display and weighting, never authority; checked against the schema and kept as received; no host acts on `validUntil`. `pnm rooms put --basis/--confidence/--cite-*/--purpose/--valid-until`.

**Retention and prune (#868).** Host-neutral `vti_rooms::record_tasks` serves `rooms/records/prune/0.1`, `rooms/records/retention/set/0.1`, `rooms/create/0.2`, `rooms/info/0.2`, `rooms/records/list/0.3` on room-host and the VTC alike. Prune is admin only and removes only what the retention in force makes eligible; the mark takes the next version and `headVersion` is max(highest record, mark), with reads taking the head under the prune's lock. VTA: `rooms/keys/browse/0.2`. `pnm rooms records prune` (dry run first) and `pnm rooms records retention {show,set}`.

**Epoch floor (#869).** Floor = `beforeEpoch − 1`, raised by both prune versions, never lowered; no rung at or below it stored or served. Members' VTAs keep the floor, discard rungs below it, apply it in every chain walk and never take one back (`rooms/keys/{chain,backfill}/0.2`, catch-up); `vti-rooms-wasm` gets `applyEpochFloor`. `pnm rooms prune` sends 0.2, and its warning's off-by-one is fixed (`--before-epoch 5` makes 1–3 unreadable).

**Breaking:** `vti_rooms::Room` gains `record_retention`, `last_prune`, `epoch_floor`; `vtc_client`'s `SealedRecordBody` gains five public fields. New enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`.

**Known gaps / follow-ups:**
- `rooms/keys/act` (≤ 0.6) has no rows for the new versions, so `pnm` refuses provenance on open rooms and records prune/retention set go through `rooms/keys/present` (hosts record the CLI key). Needs `act` 0.7 in the spec.
- Codegen: `rooms/keys/chain/0.2`'s generated payload is an untagged enum that cannot hold links and a floor together; the request is checked against the schema instead.
- A room-host read mirror pulls with list 0.1 and does not follow its primary's prune.
- No host cap on retention yet (`retentionNotPermitted` never raised).

Local: clippy `-D warnings` (plus the vta-service, vtc-service and vti-rooms `mls` feature combos) and fmt clean; workspace nextest 6598 passed; vtc-service/vtc-client 3523 passed; room-host `--features didcomm` and wasm32 checks passed before the rebase.

title: feat(rooms)!: record provenance, record retention and prune, and the epoch floor (#2272)
body:
feat(rooms)!: record provenance, record retention and prune, and the epoch floor (#2272)

* feat(rooms)!: a record says what kind of claim it is and when it lapses — rooms/records/put 0.3 and provenance in the sealed body

trust-tasks-tf #865. A record's provenance (`basis`, `confidence`,
`evidence`, `validFor`) and expiry (`validUntil`): display and weighting
only, never authority; expiry is a reader's rule and no host acts on it.

- vti-rooms: `provenance` — the five members, checked against the
  specification's generated types and kept as received (a typed round trip
  would rewrite a `validUntil`), `RecordBasis`, `is_expired`.
  `ROOMS_RECORDS_PUT_V3_TYPE`; `blob_tasks::{put_v3_parts, put_v3_as_v0_1}`.
- Hosts (room-host and the VTC, one shared path): `rooms/records/put/0.3`
  served beside 0.2 and 0.1. An open room's `cleartext` is stored and served
  exactly as received (consumer item 11); 0.2 still refuses those members in
  its closed cleartext.
- vtc-client: `SealedRecordBody` carries the five members inside the
  author's signature, checked on signing and on reading;
  `SealedRecordBody::is_expired`; `VtcClient::put_cleartext_record_v3`.
- vta-service: `rooms/keys/seal` signs bodies carrying them (checked, never
  acted on); the profile reader accepts them and keeps them off a profile.
- pnm: `rooms put --basis/--confidence/--cite-record/--cite-credential/
  --purpose/--use-note/--valid-until`; `declared` by default on a sealed
  room. `rooms get` shows the basis beside the author and marks an expired
  record. An open room's provenance needs put 0.3, which `rooms/keys/act`
  (0.1-0.6) does not complete, so pnm refuses it there rather than sign as
  itself.

BREAKING: `vtc_client::rooms::body::SealedRecordBody` gains five public
fields.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(rooms)!: a room states how long it keeps its records, and an administrator prunes what that makes eligible

trust-tasks-tf #868. A room's record retention ({tombstoneDays,
recordDays}, by the host-visible updatedAt, pinned records exempt from
recordDays; absent or {} makes nothing eligible) is the rule; a prune by a
holder of `admin`, with a reason, is the act. Hosts never prune on their own.

- vti-rooms: `record_retention` (RecordRetention, PruneKind, is_eligible,
  RecordPrune) and `record_tasks`, the host-neutral tasks both hosts call:
  `rooms/records/prune/0.1` (admin only, roomNotLive, noRetention with the
  retention in details, dryRun changes nothing, removed records go outright
  with their blobs released, the next version taken as the `lastPrune` mark,
  nothing of a removed record kept), `rooms/records/retention/set/0.1`
  (replaced whole, expectedRetention -> retentionConflict, `{}` clears,
  nothing removed), `rooms/create/0.2` (recorded as given and echoed),
  `rooms/info/0.2` (recordRetention, lastPrune), `rooms/records/list/0.3`
  (lastPrune on every page). `Room` gains `record_retention` and
  `last_prune`. `HeadVersion` is the higher of the highest record and the
  latest prune (`storage::room_tree_head{,_with_trace}`), and every listing
  and read now takes its head under the record-write lock a prune holds, so
  a root and its head stay one snapshot. `BlobHost::records_lock`.
- room-host and the VTC serve all five beside the old versions, through
  the same shared code; both audit `room.records.prune` /
  `room.records.retention.set` with the mark, reason, rule and kinds — never
  a removed record (VTC: new `AuditEvent::RoomRetention`). The VTC reads
  `rooms/records/put/0.3`, `rooms/create/0.2` and
  `rooms/records/retention/set/0.1` from the document's JSON as received.
- vta-service: `rooms/keys/browse/0.2` lists with list 0.3 (0.1 for a host
  that predates it) and passes `lastPrune` through; at 0.1 a sinceVersion
  below a prune is ignored and the whole room listed.
- vtc-client: `room_info_v2`, `prune_records`, `set_record_retention`.
- pnm: `rooms records prune` (always a dry run first, then confirm or
  `--yes`), `rooms records retention {show,set}` (set is conditional on the
  rule just read).
- Docs: data-rooms.md §2, §9, §10.5, §11, §12.

BREAKING: `vti_rooms::Room` gains two public fields;
`vti_common::audit::AuditEvent` gains a variant (non_exhaustive).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(rooms)!: the host keeps a room's epoch floor, and members' VTAs forget what they hold below it

trust-tasks-tf #869. Erasing the host's rungs left every member's key
holder able to derive what the owner decided nobody should. The epoch
floor (`beforeEpoch - 1`: rung N survives and still yields N-1) is now kept
by the host and applied by members' key holders.

- vti-rooms: `Room::epoch_floor`; `storage::prune_chain_to_floor` raises it
  (written before the rungs go, monotonic, also where nothing is dropped) at
  every prune version; `servable_epoch_links` never serves a rung at or
  below it; `put_epoch_link_above_floor` never stores one.
  `EpochKeyChain::apply_floor` / `SealedRoom::apply_epoch_floor`: rungs at or
  below the floor and keys below it (memoised ones included) discarded, a
  derivation below it answered `EpochUnreachable` with an earliest epoch at
  or above it, such rungs never stored again from any source.
- Hosts (room-host and the VTC, one shared response path):
  `rooms/epoch/prune/0.2` (required `epochFloor`), `rooms/epoch/chain/0.2`
  (`epochFloor` on every response once pruned, empty `links` too) beside 0.1,
  which also stops serving rungs at or below the floor.
- vta-service: the floor in its own `room-epoch-floor` row per member,
  applied in every chain walk (open, file key, profile locations, reach, the
  owner's add/remove/renew); `room_groups::apply_epoch_floor` discards the
  rungs before answering. `rooms/keys/chain/0.2` (floor relayed with rungs or
  alone; read against its schema, because the generated untagged `Payload`
  cannot hold links and a floor together), `rooms/keys/backfill/0.2` (fetches
  with epoch/chain 0.2, falls back to 0.1, applies and reports the floor, never
  asks below it). A read's catch-up fetches with epoch/chain 0.2 and applies
  the floor; 0.1 chain/backfill still never keep a rung at or below it.
- vti-rooms-wasm: `applyEpochFloor` / `epochFloor`, kept in the snapshot.
- SDK/CLI: `VtaClient::{room_backfill_v0_2, room_chain_v0_2}`,
  `VtcClient::{prune_epoch_v2, epoch_chain_v2}`; `pnm rooms prune` sends 0.2
  (0.1 for an older host, saying it keeps no floor) and its warning now
  states the off-by-one correctly (epochs 1 to N-2 become unreadable) and that
  the prune reaches conforming key holders; `pnm rooms keys backfill` reports
  the floor.
- Docs: data-rooms.md §2, §10.4, §12; CLAUDE.md integration flow for room
  records (provenance, retention and prune, the epoch floor).

BREAKING: `vti_rooms::Room` gains `epoch_floor`.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc)!: rooms/storage/migrate 0.2 and rooms/get 0.2 — fixed target, one retry owner, resume without consent, queueing
body:
Implements trust-tasks-tf #867, served beside 0.1 (one engine, each version answered at its own).

- **Fixed target (item 9):** `toConfig` is fixed at approval and kept through a reassignment; uploads after it go to the new config.
- **One retry owner (item 10):** the migration worker. Capped backoff + jitter while `running`; `paused` only after 8 failures in a row, then it retries itself ~every 30 minutes (jittered). A target not `active` → cause `destination`; no usable credential → `credential`; each is an ordinary failed attempt. `capacity` is never a cause (bytes reserved at approval).
- **Resume without re-consent (item 5):** re-issuing at either version answers the open move; a paused one resumes at once, not parked, keeping `toConfig` and `reason`; audited with the requester (`automatic: true` when the worker resumes it).
- **Pause reporting (item 11):** `pausedCause`, `lastError` (scrubbed of URL queries, tokens, the room id/prefix/hash and the blob ref) and `nextAttemptAt`.
- **Orphans (item 12):** never planned or counted; one orphaned mid-move is dropped at once, never counted twice.
- **Queueing (item 13):** one move per target config; others `queued` with bytes reserved, started in approval order. 0.1 reports `queued` as `running`.
- **`vtc/rooms/get/0.2`:** `storage.migration` per the shared `room-migration` schema.
- Console: destination (incl. "reassigned; this move keeps going to X"), queued moves, last error, pause cause and next attempt, "Resume now".

**Breaking:** `vti_rooms::BlobHost::next_migration` is replaced by `running_migrations` and `promote_queued`.

**Spec gap (not invented here):** if a move's target config is retired, the move pauses as `destination` and retries forever, holding up later moves to that config only. Needs a spec rule (refuse the retire, or end the move).

Rebased onto #2271 (storage auth); the shared lists (task registry, summary templates, console pins → 54) are unions.

Local, after that rebase: clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean; vtc-service/vtc-client nextest 3554 passed; workspace (excluding those) 6586 passed; admin-ui lint clean, vitest 1329 passed.

title: feat(vtc)!: rooms/storage/migrate 0.2 and rooms/get 0.2 — fixed target, one retry owner, resume without consent, orphans, pause reporting, queueing (#2273)
body:
feat(vtc)!: rooms/storage/migrate 0.2 and rooms/get 0.2 — fixed target, one retry owner, resume without consent, orphans, pause reporting, queueing (#2273)

Serves vtc/rooms/storage/migrate/0.2 and vtc/rooms/get/0.2 (trust-tasks-tf
engine and behave the 0.2 way. The migration is reported through
vtc/_shared/0.1/room-migration.

vti_rooms::blobs::migrate:

- item 9: toConfig is the room's assignment at approval and is kept through a
  reassignment; a later migration moves everything once this one finishes.
- item 10: the runner is the one retry owner. A failed copy, read, write or
  credential request backs off (capped, full jitter) and the migration stays
  `running`; only after MIGRATION_MAX_ATTEMPTS in a row is it `paused`, and the
  runner then tries again by itself at nextAttemptAt (PAUSED_RETRY_SECS,
  jittered; BlobHost::resume_due). `capacity` is never a pause cause here: the
  bytes are reserved at approval.
- item 11: PauseCause (source / destination / credential / capacity) and a
  lastError naming step, config and backend error, scrubbed of URL queries,
  tokens, the room id, prefix and hash, and the blob ref.
- item 12: orphans are never planned or counted; a blob orphaned or collected
  while a migration is open is dropped at once (drop_from_migration): plan row
  and reservation before its switch, an `mdone:` row's done and total counts
  after. skip() adjusts only while the plan row exists, so nothing counts twice.
- item 13: one migration per target config runs at a time; another to the same
  config is `queued` (reserved, nothing copied) and promote_queued starts it in
  approval order once those ahead are complete or failed.
- item 5: a request for a room with a queued, running or paused migration is
  answered with it, a paused one resumed at once, never parked, keeping its
  toConfig and reason; a requested rate is adopted.

vtc-service: the runner checks the target before each step (not `active` ->
destination, no usable store -> credential) and counts it as a failed attempt;
steps every running migration in turn; audits a self-resumption as
migrationResumed with "automatic": true. A restore pauses a running migration
with cause destination and no nextAttemptAt. 0.1 answers report `queued` as
`running` and carry none of the new members. A parked 0.2 request has its own
action-list template (kind rooms.storage.migrate), pinned in server and
console.

Console: the room page reads rooms/get 0.2 and sends migrate 0.2; it shows
the move's destination (and that a reassigned room's move keeps it), queued
moves, the backoff error while running, and a paused move's cause, last error
and the community's next attempt; "Resume now" needs no new approval.

A target retired under an open move is a gap in the specification: the move
pauses as destination and retries at nextAttemptAt indefinitely, holding up
later moves to that config only.

title: feat(vtc/config): did-hosting/list 0.1 — the hosting servers the community's VTA can publish its identities through
body:
A community's administrator chooses where the identities it mints (its groups'
and its own rooms') are published. The community either serves each `did:webvh`
log itself, or has its VTA publish it on a hosting server registered there.
Without a list of those servers the choice is typed blind.

- vtc/config/did-hosting/list/0.1: for holders of `vtc.config.admin`. The
  community asks its own VTA (`vta/webvh/servers/list`), as itself, over the
  link it keeps to it. It answers with each server's `id`, `did` and `label`,
  and nothing else of the VTA's record. A server whose id the configuration
  could not name is left out.
- Codes: noKeyHolder (no VTA link), keyHolderUnavailable (no answer,
  retryable), keyHolderRefused (the VTA's own code and message in `details`).

Regenerated Rust, TS, Go and Dart. Locally: `npm run validate`, `check-bindings` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` pass.

title: fix(trust-tasks-dart): consumeInbound can cache a success response as JSON, so a persistent replay guard stores it
body:
The Dart pipeline handed ReplayGuard.recordResponse a refusal as a JSON map
but a success as the TrustTaskDocument object itself. A guard backed by a
store cannot serialise that object. The failure was swallowed (recording is
best-effort), so such a guard cached no success response, and a resend was
absorbed with nothing to return instead of the original response. The Rust,
TypeScript and Go runtimes always record JSON.

consumeInbound takes an optional `responseToJson`. With it, a success reaches
the guard, and later DuplicateOutcome.priorResponse, as the same JSON map
shape as a refusal. Without it, behaviour is unchanged, so this is additive.
The guard and pipeline docs now say a persisting guard needs it.

The Dart HTTPS, DIDComm and TSP bindings already accept either shape when
they emit a prior response. They can pass their response encoder once they
require a core that has this parameter.

## Tests
`test/replay_test.dart`: a guard that keeps only what `jsonEncode` can write records a success, and a resend returns it as a JSON map. dart analyze is clean and all 75 tests pass.
author: stormer78

title: fix: a handler that fails without refusing releases its replay claim, so the document can be resent
body:
In the Go, TypeScript and Dart pipelines, a handler error that was not a
Refusal (an exception in TS and Dart) propagated straight out of
consumeInbound, leaving the item-11 claim in flight. Every resend of the
document was then absorbed as an in-flight duplicate until the record expired:
the task could not be retried, and the producer was never told why.

The claim is now released, best-effort, before the error propagates. The
handler did not finish, so nothing records that the effect happened. A
Refusal is unchanged: a retryable one releases the claim, a final one settles
it. Rust is unaffected, because its handler returns a Result and cannot fail
any other way.

The Go and Dart TSP/DIDComm bindings and the Dart HTTPS server released the
claim themselves after the core returned. Those workarounds stay until each
binding requires a core that includes this fix. The TypeScript TSP binding had
no workaround and is fixed by this change.

## Tests
A regression test in each of `trust-tasks-go/trusttasks/replay_test.go`, `trust-tasks-ts/test/replay.test.ts` and `trust-tasks-dart/test/replay_test.dart`: the handler throws, then a resend is handled rather than reported as an in-flight duplicate. Each test fails with the fix reverted. The full Go, TS (81) and Dart (75) suites pass; go vet and dart analyze are clean.
author: stormer78

title: fix: a replay record is kept until the skew-extended window closes, so a late replay cannot execute twice
body:
## Problem

Freshness accepts a document until `issuedAt + maxAge + skew`, but `recordExpiry` kept the replay record only until `issuedAt + maxAge`. A replay arriving in the final `skew` interval (60 s under the consequential defaults) passed freshness, found its record already dropped, and the guard answered `Fresh` — so the handler ran a second time. That is the double execution SPEC §7.2 item 11 forbids, and it breaks the "same bound" rule `record_expiry`'s own docs claim.

Example (`consequential()`: 5 min window, 60 s skew): `issuedAt = T`, first delivery at T+1m, replay at T+5m30s → accepted, record gone at T+5m, executes again.

Affected all four runtimes, and `trust-tasks-https` via `FreshnessPolicy::record_expiry`.

## Fix

`recordExpiry` now returns `issuedAt + maxAge + skew` in Rust (`freshness.rs`), TypeScript (`_runtime/freshness.ts`), Go (`trusttasks/freshness.go`) and Dart (`runtime/freshness.dart`). The `expiresAt` branch is unchanged — expiry is checked without skew, so it was already exact.

## Tests

- New boundary regression test in Rust and TS: a document 5m30s old is accepted *and* its record outlives `now`. The TS test was confirmed to fail without the fix.
- Existing Go/Dart/Rust record-expiry expectations updated to include the skew.
- Passing locally: `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --lib`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-https`, `npm test` (trust-tasks-ts), `go test ./trusttasks/`, `dart test test/replay_test.dart`; `cargo fmt --check` and `gofmt -l` clean.

Behavioural change only (records retained `skew` longer); no API change → patch.
author: stormer78

title: feat(voting): vta/pcs/trustee/read, and trustees read voting/election/show on any board
body:
A trustee could not run its part of a sealed or tallied-encrypted election on a private board
from a client: the trustee tasks take the manifest, which voting/election/show answers only to
the community and the auditors there; and a trustee's client, which holds no trustee key, had no
way to sign the reads a private board answers only to a trustee.

- vta/pcs/trustee/read/0.1 (new): the VTA signs voting/trustees/status or voting/election/show
  as the trustee, addressed to the ballot box — the trustee's counterpart of vta/pcs/voter/read.
  Its payload is fixed to { community, electionId }; `read` is closed. Gated on pcsTrustee.
- voting/election/show answers every trustee the manifest names on any board (CONVENTIONS §4
  gains its own row; §9.6's "Who reads the ceremony" names both reads).
- vta/pcs/trustee/decrypt: `closedAt` is the board's close entry, or for a client that cannot
  read the board any time at or after the close and not in the future — the election's summary,
  which the field used to point at, carries no close time.

Additive: cargo semver-checks against 0.32.9 reports no semver update required.

title: ci: package trust-tasks-rs once, with validate, and guard the assumption that makes that enough
body:
The `cargo package (trust-tasks-rs)` job packaged and verify-compiled the
crate twice, once with default features and once with `validate`, taking
about 9 minutes. The verify compile exists to catch an `include_str!` of a
file outside the crate root, which the tarball drops. But nothing in
trust-tasks-rs compiles only when `validate` is off: there is no
`cfg(not(feature = "validate"))` and no build script. So the default build is
a strict subset of the validate build, and its verify compile could only fail
when the validate one also did. It is dropped, saving roughly 4 minutes.

and says to restore the default-feature package. That keeps the assumption
checked rather than remembered. The job's name is unchanged, so required-check
settings are unaffected.

title: ci: build test dependencies without debug info
body:
`[profile.test]` keeps line tables so a failing test's backtrace has
file:line, which is all it needs and what keeps the trust-tasks-rs test build

title: feat(vault): vault/credentials/query subjectDid narrows to credentials presented as one identity
body:
An optional request member: the maintainer returns only credentials whose subject — the DID vault/credentials/present would present them as — is the named DID. It narrows the other constraints and does not satisfy the at-least-one-filter requirement on its own.

A verifier that requires a particular holder (a community directory accepts a verified field only from a presentation its member holds) refuses a credential bound to a separate holder key; a wallet offering the holder a choice can now offer only the credentials that verifier will accept. A request member rather than a descriptor member, because every generated descriptor reader denies unknown members: a new descriptor member would break existing consumers, while a maintainer that predates this filter refuses it rather than ignoring it.

Generated payload structs gain a member (additive on the wire; struct-literal consumers need a one-line edit). Consumers: VTI VTA (filter), vta-browser-plugin `directory.presentCredential` (offers only member-bound credentials).
author: stormer78

title: fix: a replay guard's unrecognised verdict fails closed in the TypeScript and Go pipelines
body:
consumeInbound in TypeScript and Go switched on the guard's verdict with cases
for fresh, duplicate and conflict and no default. A verdict outside those
three fell through, and the handler ran with no claim held. Item 11 was
skipped without anything noticing. In Go that includes the zero
ReplayVerdict a guard returns with a nil error. In TypeScript it includes a
plain-JS guard with a mistyped kind. Rust (an enum) and Dart (a sealed class)
cannot express such a verdict.

The default now refuses the document unavailable and retryable, the same as
a guard that cannot answer at all. Nothing is said about the guard on the wire.

## Tests
`TestItem11FailsClosedOnAVerdictItDoesNotKnow` (Go, a zero-verdict guard) and "fails closed on a verdict it does not know" (TS) both check the handler does not run. Both fail with the fix reverted. The Go suite passes and go vet is clean. TS: 82 tests pass.
author: stormer78

title: ci(release): run cargo-semver-checks one crate at a time, so the Release PR job stops running out of memory
body:
#890's in-step sampler caught the cause in run 39869780457. release-plz runs
cargo-semver-checks for every changed crate at once: four in parallel, each
compiling trust-tasks-rs into its own target directory. Memory filled within
about two minutes. Over the next nine, swap climbed to the full 16 GB, with
three rustc at ~3 GB each and one rustdoc at ~6 GB. The kernel's OOM killer
then killed rustdoc in the runner agent's cgroup ("Out of memory: Killed
process (rustdoc)"), the hosted-compute agent shut down ("Runner agent failed
with unexpected exit code"), and the job got the SIGTERM (exit 143) it has
been ending with since 2026-10-22. One check alone peaks at ~13 GB, which fits
in 16 GB of RAM plus 16 GB of swap.

release-plz has no setting for that parallelism, so after install the
cargo-semver-checks binary is replaced by a two-line wrapper that takes a
`flock` lock and then execs the real binary. It replaces the binary in place,
because cargo searches $CARGO_HOME/bin before PATH when it resolves
`cargo semver-checks`. The checks now run one after another, so the job
timeout rises from 60 to 90 minutes. The swap and the sampler stay.

## Evidence (run 39869780457, from the step's own log)
```
[sample 23:11:17] mem used=15093M avail=896M swap used=3M ...
[sample 23:20:19] mem used=15697M avail=292M swap used=16311M; top rss: rustdoc=6089M rustc=3272M rustc=3013M
kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 9073 (rustdoc) ... anon-rss:6528236kB
hosted-compute-agent: Runner agent failed with unexpected exit code
```
The OOM dump lists four `cargo-semver-checks` processes, each driving its own `cargo`.

## Checks
actionlint is clean. I tested the wrapper locally with stand-ins for `cargo-semver-checks` and `flock`: the generated script is correct and arguments pass through unchanged. `flock` itself is util-linux, which the Ubuntu runner has.

title: test(trust-tasks-rs): every spec family builds and tests on its own, and CI keeps it so
body:
trust-tasks-rs has one Cargo feature per spec family, so
`--no-default-features --features vault` should build only the vault family.
The library did, but its tests did not compile: five unit-test modules and six
integration test files named `acl` (and error_codes.rs also `keys`, `vta`,
`vtc`, `rooms` and `vault`) with no feature gate. A one-family test build
failed on the first ungated reference, so the features were unusable for
working on a single family.

- The acl-specimen unit-test modules in consume, async_dispatch, discovery,
  dispatcher and payload are `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "acl"))]`, as is the
  one acl test in guards/acl.rs.
- audience_binding, dispatcher, generated_specs, replay_guard and
  spec_const_emission open with `#![cfg(feature = "acl")]`. error_codes is
  gated on keys/vta/vtc, and its details module also on rooms/vault.
- A new `test-single-family` job in rust.yml runs the trust-tasks-rs suite
  with only acl, only vault and only keys, so a new ungated reference fails
  CI.
- CLAUDE.md records the rule.

Measured locally: a cold `--features vault` test build takes 13 s and 1.0 GB
(160 tests). A cold workspace test build takes 258 s and 6 GB. The default
build is unchanged: all 1805 trust-tasks-rs tests run and pass.

## Checks
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features X` passes for acl (256 tests), vault (160) and keys (169).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` is clean for vault-only and keys-only.
- The default-feature suite passes, 1805 tests. clippy and fmt are clean.
- actionlint is clean.

title: ci(release): print resource samples and kill evidence into the Release PR step's live log
body:
#888's sampler wrote to a file for a later `if: failure()` step to print. In
run 39864674704 that step was skipped, and so was every post step. The
Release PR step is not failing. The runner is going away under it, so no
later step ever runs. The run left no evidence.

The Release PR step now prints everything into its own live log as it runs:
- a sample every 30 seconds of memory used and available, swap used, free
  disk on /, and the three largest processes by RSS;
- kernel messages about OOM, kills, memory or hung tasks, as the kernel
  writes them (`dmesg -w`);
- on SIGTERM, from a trap, the journal's recent lines about OOM, kills,
  memory, shutdown or the runner, before the step exits 143.

release-pr.sh runs in the background under `wait`, so the trap fires
promptly. The report step stays for the case where the step does fail
normally.

## Checks
actionlint is clean. One shellcheck false positive (SC2329, `report` is called from the trap) is suppressed. I tested the trap locally with a stand-in for release-pr.sh: samples streamed, SIGTERM printed the report, and the step exited 143.

title: feat(vtc): ambient and sealed storage auth, GCS, and vtc/storage/* 0.2
body:
Implements trust-tasks-tf #866: `vtc/storage/configs/{list,get,create,update}` 0.2 served beside 0.1 (each answered at its own version), and `vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.2`.

- **Host gating**: new optional `[rooms.files.auth]` (`ambient`, `sealed` — both off by default — `aws_role_arn`, `aws_source_ip`, `gcs_service_account`). Refusals `authNotAllowed` with `details.reason`. A config whose mode the host withdraws stays, reports `notAllowed`, and can be moved to a permitted mode.
- **Room-scoped credentials** (`rooms/storage_auth/`): one per config × scope (a room's prefix, or `probe/`) × access; never bucket-wide; dropped at 15 minutes, in memory only; no fallback to an unscoped credential.
  - S3 ambient: STS `AssumeRole` with the config's `roleArn` (kept in the storage config), else the host's role; session policy built by a JSON encoder, optional `aws:SourceIp`. S3 sealed: `GetFederationToken` on AWS; elsewhere the key only presigns single objects under the room's prefix.
  - **GCS backend** via `object_store`, one downscoped token per room and access under a Credential Access Boundary (CEL literals escaped). Ambient: application default credentials, or the named service account impersonated for 900 s. Sealed: token minted at Google's own endpoint, never the key file's `token_uri`.
- **Sealed credentials**: opened with the X25519 derivation of the community key (new `SealedPayloadV1::StorageCredential`; the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so not breaking), schema-checked as received, stored encrypted in a new `storage_credentials` keyspace excluded from backup, shown only as an HMAC fingerprint, never returned/logged/audited. New action kind `storage.credential.set`.
- **Console**: storage pages at 0.2 (S3/GCS, VTA account/ambient/sealed, `roleArn`); **cnm**: `cnm storage {list,get,credentials set}`; docs: new `docs/03-vtc/room-storage.md`.

**Divergence (pending a decision):** the spec has the console seal a sealed credential in the browser. This PR seals in `cnm` and the console shows the command to run; the console has no HPKE library yet. Either browser sealing follows in a separate PR, or this goes in the divergence register.

**Gaps (spec SHOULDs):** credential issuance is logged, not audited (needs a new vti-common audit variant); approvers can't probe proposed settings.

Local: clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean; `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` 3546 passed; workspace (excluding those) 6580 passed; admin-ui lint clean.

title: feat(build): lint payload member names and enumerated values for SPEC §4.10 casing
body:
SPEC §4.10 says payload member names (rule 3) and specification-defined
enumerated values (rule 4) SHOULD be lowerCamelCase. Names and values fixed by
an external vocabulary (rule 5) MUST be carried verbatim. Only the error-code
local parts were checked. Across the 1074 schemas under specs/, 17 member
names and 141 values are not lowerCamelCase, and nothing stopped more.

scripts/lib/member-casing.mjs sweeps every schema's `properties` names and its
string `enum` and `const` values, and fails the build on any that is not
lowerCamelCase unless scripts/lib/member-casing-allowlist.json names it:
- `external`: 13 member names and 37 values, each mapped to the vocabulary
  that owns it (JSON-LD, OpenID4VP, OID4VCI, TRQP, JOSE/JWK, HTTP, SameSite,
  WebAuthn, W3C Data Integrity, X.500, RFC 6238, IANA hash names, GCP
  service-account keys). Accepted anywhere.
- `frozen`: the other 126 pre-lint deviations, keyed by spec family.
  Re-casing is a breaking change, so a family keeps its own across versions,
  but no other family can adopt one. An entry no longer used is reported
  stale.

Values containing `:` or `/` (URIs, DID methods, media types) are out of
scope, as slugs are under rule 6. Dotted lowerCamelCase identifiers such as
`git.repo.create` conform. Retired specs are skipped and counted, as in the
error-code casing lint.

Today it reports 0 non-conforming. A snake_case member or a kebab-case value
added to a draft spec now fails the build, including a value frozen for a
different family.

## Checks
`npm run validate` passes and reports "1074 schema(s) swept; 132 external-vocabulary occurrence(s), 149 frozen pre-lint deviation(s), 0 non-conforming". To check the lint fails, I temporarily added a `grant_mode` member with values `vault-read` and `fast` to `acl/grant/0.1`. The build failed on both `grant_mode` and `vault-read`. I then restored the file.

## For review
The `external` attributions are mine. Anything I could not attribute with confidence is in `frozen` instead (`record_type`, `new_scid`, `new_version_id`, `pre_rotation_count`, `Secp256r1`, `sev-snp`, …), so the lint does not claim an external owner it cannot name. Please correct any attribution that is wrong.

title: feat(vtc): the console's live channel at 0.4 — the communityRooms topic
body:
Serves `vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.4` and `event/0.4` (trust-tasks-tf #864) beside 0.1–0.3, each stream answered at its own version.

- **Topic `communityRooms`**: the rooms the community owns, as their owner sees them. Heard by holders of `vtc.rooms.manage` (the capability the owner reads check); `vtc.rooms.admin` alone does not qualify. Standing re-checked as for every topic.
- **What prompts it**: every write to the owner's record that `vtc/rooms/community/{list,get}` or `members/list` shows, after it lands (`rooms::community::changed`), plus every `rooms` seam, since those reads embed the hosted room and its storage config. Fingerprinted over what the reads show, so nothing else hints. A clock-driven lifecycle change wakes it, as for `rooms` (the wake is now per topic).
- **Hints only**: no room, member, DID or credential, in any member.
- **Console**: subscribes at 0.4 when discovery lists it; the community rooms pages re-read on a hint and poll slowly while the stream carries it. `cnm actions watch` stays at 0.1.
- Docs: `website-and-admin.md` (*Live updates*), `community-rooms.md`, and the live-channel entry in `vtc-service/CLAUDE.md`.

Spec reading worth confirming: event rule 8 gives a host-side change to `rooms` "unless the owner's reads also show it" — the owner's reads embed the hosted room and storage config, so those changes also hint `communityRooms`.

Local: `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` 3519 passed; clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean; admin-ui lint clean (vitest 1320 passed before the rebase onto main).
