feat(vtc): the console's live channel at 0.4 — the communityRooms topic (vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.4) (#2270)

`vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.4` and `event/0.4` (trust-tasks-tf #864) are
served beside 0.1 – 0.3, each stream answered at its own version. 0.4 adds one
topic, `communityRooms`: the rooms the community itself owns, as their owner
sees them.

- Who hears it: holders of `vtc.rooms.manage`, who are answered on
  `vtc/rooms/community/list`, `get` and `members/list`. `vtc.rooms.admin` alone
  does not qualify — that is the host's authority, and the `rooms` topic's.
  Standing is re-checked as for every topic; losing `vtc.rooms.manage` ends a
  stream carrying it.
- What prompts it (event 0.4 producer rule 8): every write to the owner's
  record the reads show, after the record lands — a room created or its label,
  description or tags changed (`put_room_details` now hints); a member's record
  (offered, withdrawn, accepted, renewed, removed); a removal owed, including on
  departure, retried, settled or dropped; the profile write's and the authority
  renewal's records. Every `rooms` seam prompts it too, because the owner's
  reads embed the hosted room and name its storage config.
- Fingerprinted over what those reads show: each room's details, the hosted
  room, its storage config, each member's rendered record, the removals owed
  and the profile/renewal `ext`. So a host-side change they do not show (a
  holdings write, a room the community does not own) and a write no read shows
  (a served room-identity log, a renewal's vault handles) send nothing. A room
  lifecycle moving with the clock wakes the stream, as for `rooms` (the wake is
  now per topic).
- Not a count topic. The hint names no room, member, DID, offer or credential
  (rule 9).

The console subscribes at 0.4 when `trust-task-discovery` lists it; the
Community rooms tab, a community room's page, its members and the room-name
lookup re-read on a `communityRooms` hint (key `["rooms", "community"]`) and
poll slowly while the stream carries it. `cnm actions watch` stays at 0.1.

title: feat(go-release): release trust-tasks-go/capabilityclient on its own tag, and stop its changes releasing the core
body:
The Go capability wire client had no release wiring. It had no version.go, no
publish-go matrix leg, no GO_MODULES entry and no release-bump-go.sh case, so it
was never tagged. `go get` resolved it only as a pseudo-version, while the
website listed it as shipped. Worse, the core module's release watch excluded
proof, didcomm and tsp but not capabilityclient, so a change under
trust-tasks-go/capabilityclient bumped and re-tagged the core module.

This wires it exactly as #503 wired proof and didcomm:
- version.go with `const Version = "0.1.0"` (the manifest surrogate
  publish-go reads) and an empty CHANGELOG.md for the release automation;
- a publish-go matrix leg, which builds, vets and tests before tagging;
- a GO_MODULES entry in release-pr.sh and a case in release-bump-go.sh;
- the core's watch now excludes trust-tasks-go/capabilityclient;
- RELEASING.md and CLAUDE.md list it with the other nested modules.

Go is self-bootstrapping, with no manual first publish. On merge, publish-go
tags trust-tasks-go/capabilityclient/v0.1.0. A Go tag cannot be retracted.

> ⚠️ **Merging publishes.** `publish-go` will push `trust-tasks-go/capabilityclient/v0.1.0`, and proxy.golang.org caches a tag permanently.

## Checks
In `trust-tasks-go/capabilityclient`: gofmt is clean and go vet and go test pass. `bash -n` passes for both scripts. shellcheck reports nothing new; its one warning (SC2209, line 160) is already on main.

title: fix(cnm): build the step-up and enrol links on the console's origin, not the API base
body:
## What

`cnm git` printed the operation-bound step-up link, and the step-up passkey enrollment link, by appending `/admin/step-up` to the profile's VTC base. That base is the `VTCRest` endpoint from the DID document and carries the API mount (`https://vtc.example/v1`), so the link became `/v1/admin/step-up`. On a VTC serving a community website that path falls through to the home page, and the operator following the printed link never saw the step-up form. The console is a sibling mount on the same host, so the link must be built on the origin.

## Change

- New `console_url(base, page)` in `cnm-cli/src/git.rs`: parse the base, keep scheme, host and port, set the path to `/admin/<page>`, drop query and fragment. A base that is not a URL falls back to appending, as before.
- `step_up_url` and `enrol_url` both use it.
- Test `console_links_are_built_on_the_origin_not_the_api_base` pins `https://vtc.example/v1` → `https://vtc.example/admin/step-up#request=…` (and the enrol link), plus the query/fragment stripping and the fallback. The existing tests with a bare origin still pass.

## How it was found

Recording `git.repo.own` for the operator's own `cnm` identity on a single-administrator community (the VTI-APV-022 waiver). `cnm` printed `https://vtc.oma.ic3.dev/v1/admin/step-up#request=…`, which showed the website; `https://vtc.oma.ic3.dev/admin/step-up#request=…` with the same fragment showed the step-up page and the grant completed.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p cnm-cli`: 133 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p cnm-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

title: feat(vault): vault/credentials/query subjectDid narrows to credentials presented as one identity (#884)
body:
feat(vault): vault/credentials/query subjectDid narrows to credentials presented as one identity (#884)

An optional request member: the maintainer returns only credentials whose subject — the DID vault/credentials/present would present them as — is the named DID. It narrows the other constraints and does not satisfy the at-least-one-filter requirement on its own.

A verifier that requires a particular holder (a community directory accepts a verified field only from a presentation its member holds) refuses a credential bound to a separate holder key; a wallet offering the holder a choice can now offer only the credentials that verifier will accept. A request member rather than a descriptor member, because every generated descriptor reader denies unknown members: a new descriptor member would break existing consumers, while a maintainer that predates this filter refuses it rather than ignoring it.

title: fix: a replay guard's unrecognised verdict fails closed in the TypeScript and Go pipelines (#883)
body:
fix: a replay guard's unrecognised verdict fails closed in the TypeScript and Go pipelines (#883)

consumeInbound in TypeScript and Go switched on the guard's verdict with cases
for fresh, duplicate and conflict and no default. A verdict outside those
three fell through, and the handler ran with no claim held. Item 11 was
skipped without anything noticing. In Go that includes the zero
ReplayVerdict a guard returns with a nil error. In TypeScript it includes a
plain-JS guard with a mistyped kind. Rust (an enum) and Dart (a sealed class)
cannot express such a verdict.

The default now refuses the document unavailable and retryable, the same as
a guard that cannot answer at all. Nothing is said about the guard on the wire.

title: fix(trust-tasks-tsp): a sender mismatch maps to proofRequired, as the DIDComm bindings' sender failures do
body:
`TspError::into_reject_reason` mapped SenderMismatch (the envelope claims one
VID and another VID's key verified it) to malformedRequest. The DIDComm v2.1
and v1 bindings map every failure that leaves no transport-authenticated
sender, including their own sender-key mismatches, to proofRequired: only an
in-band proof could still attribute such a document. The same failure now gets
the same code from all three Rust bindings.

Binding §4 puts an authentication failure outside the framework pipeline, and
`receive` still returns it as an error rather than answering. Only callers that
fold transport errors into a RejectReason see the change.

## Tests
A new unit test in `trust-tasks-tsp/src/error.rs` checks the mapping. The #877 leak test now uses `WrongEnvelopeType` as its malformedRequest example. Lib tests pass and clippy `-D warnings` is clean.

title: feat(tsp)!: the Trust Tasks TSP binding speaks TSP 1.0
body:
`affinidi-tsp` 0.2 → 0.3. The ToIP TSP specification released **1.0** ([tswg-tsp-specification#86](https://github.com/trustoverip/tswg-tsp-specification/pull/86), `YTSP-BAA`). It is Rev 3's wire with the ESSR sender VID **mandatory in every confidential payload**. 1.0 and Rev 3 **do not interoperate in either direction**, so a consumer of this binding moves with its peers — hence the `!`.

**No source or API change.** `affinidi-tsp` 0.3 ([affinidi-tdk-rs#967](https://github.com/affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs/pull/967)) keeps every signature this binding uses. One behaviour change worth knowing: `MetaEnvelope::parse`, the keys-free parse a relay runs before `unpack`, now reads any TSP version, so a relay on 0.3 still forwards Rev 3 traffic. `unpack` requires 1.0.

The lockfile moves `affinidi-tsp` 0.2.0 → 0.3.0 and adds `salsa20` 0.11, which 0.3 uses. No `affinidi-*` crate is duplicated.

**Why now:** this unblocks `verifiable-trust-infrastructure`, which can't move to `affinidi-tsp` 0.3 / `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.39 while this binding resolves 0.2 alongside it. In that case its TSP binding would keep speaking Rev 3 while the rest of the VTA spoke 1.0.

**Tests:** `cargo test -p trust-tasks-tsp --all-features` passes (15 passed, 2 ignored, as before), and clippy with `-D warnings` is clean.

**Not changed here:** `bindings/tsp/0.1/spec.md` still says TSP structure follows "Implementers Draft, Rev 2", which was already stale at Rev 3. Updating that prose is a `spec(tsp)` edit, better done separately.

title: fix: the HTTPS servers check expiry, recipient and freshness before identity, as consume_inbound does
body:
The Rust and Dart HTTPS servers ran identity resolution (§7.2 item 6) before
expiry, recipient and freshness (items 4 and 5a). consume_inbound and every
other binding run them in §7.2 order. So a document failing both kinds of
check was refused identityMismatch over HTTPS, and expired or wrongRecipient
everywhere else.

Both servers now use §7.2 order when the sender is authenticated. With no
authenticated sender, identity still runs first. Then the only identity that
can disagree is the recipient, and §8.1 suppresses that refusal. Checking the
recipient first would answer wrongRecipient instead, telling an
unauthenticated prober which VIDs the server is not, and undoing the PR #75
suppression both servers' regression tests pin. Those tests are unchanged and
pass.

CLAUDE.md's note on the Dart server's step order is updated to match.

## Tests
In each server, a new test sends an authenticated document whose issuer contradicts the token and which is addressed elsewhere. It is now refused `wrongRecipient`. The test fails with the fix reverted. The PR #75 suppression tests still pass. Rust trust-tasks-https: 49 end-to-end tests pass and clippy `-D warnings` is clean. trust_tasks_https (Dart): 56 tests pass and analyze is clean.

title: fix: the TypeScript and Dart runtimes refuse a timestamp with no zone designator, as Rust and Go do
body:
`issuedAt` and `expiresAt` are RFC 3339 date-times (SPEC §4.2). The TypeScript
runtime parsed them with Date.parse and the Dart runtime with
DateTime.tryParse. Both read "2026-01-01T00:00:00" as the consumer's local
time, and both accept forms RFC 3339 does not: a bare date, a free-text date
(TS), a space or no separators (Dart). So the freshness window, the expiry
check and the replay record's retention all moved with the consumer's time
zone. Rust (chrono) and Go (time.RFC3339) refuse these.

title: fix: the TypeScript and Dart runtimes refuse a timestamp with no zone designator, as Rust and Go do (#880)
body:
fix: the TypeScript and Dart runtimes refuse a timestamp with no zone designator, as Rust and Go do (#880)

`issuedAt` and `expiresAt` are RFC 3339 date-times (SPEC §4.2). The TypeScript
runtime parsed them with Date.parse and the Dart runtime with
DateTime.tryParse. Both read "2026-01-01T00:00:00" as the consumer's local
time, and both accept forms RFC 3339 does not: a bare date, a free-text date
(TS), a space or no separators (Dart). So the freshness window, the expiry
check and the replay record's retention all moved with the consumer's time
zone. Rust (chrono) and Go (time.RFC3339) refuse these.

Both runtimes now parse with a strict RFC 3339 matcher. A timestamp without
`Z` or a numeric offset is refused malformedRequest with the message these
paths already use for an unparseable timestamp. The parser is internal in
both: not re-exported from the TS runtime index, and in a Dart file the barrel
does not export.

Documents these runtimes used to accept are now refused. Every one of them
was outside the spec and already refused by the Rust and Go consumers.

title: feat(directory): verify a directory field with a credential your agent holds (window.vtaWallet.directory.presentCredential) (#375)
body:
feat(directory): verify a directory field with a credential your agent holds (window.vtaWallet.directory.presentCredential) (#375)

A member fills their card's credential-sourced fields — a verified employer, a professional registration — from a credential their own agent holds. The portal asks with one new call, window.vtaWallet.directory.presentCredential({ hostDid, member?, fields }), naming the fields and nothing else: never the claims, never the credential.

Gates: the call is well formed (1 to 16 distinct field keys); the page is the community's portal by its DID document; the member is one of the wallet's identities there. Then the wallet reads the community's field schema as the member (vtc/directory/fields/list): every named field must be active, credential-sourced and a claim field, and all of one credential type. It finds the member's credentials that answer them (vault/credentials/query, valid, active, from an issuer every field accepts) and asks the person, in the wallet's own window, which one to present — showing the community, the fields and every claim it discloses. A closed window, or an answer naming a credential the prompt did not offer, presents nothing.

The agent then presents the chosen credential (vault/credentials/present/0.1, trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#871): audience the community's DID, nonce the id of the vtc/directory/card/present document that will carry it, so the community's binding check holds. A credential that cannot hide claims the fields do not read is refused by the agent with wouldOverDisclose — matched on the code, never the message — and the wallet asks again, naming those claims, before presenting with them; declined, nothing more is presented. The card/present document is signed as the member and sent; the page gets back the verified values now on the card.

A page may no longer drive vault/credentials/present through the generic task path (page-task-policy): it is a disclosure under the subject's signature to a verifier the caller names, which a generic prompt cannot show.

core: credVaultPresent (vault/credentials.ts); vtc/directory-present.ts (credentialAskFor, claimNameOf, buildCardPresent, verifiedValuesOf). @openvtc/trust-tasks 0.27.2; task-surface.json synced, family count 230 → 231.

Depends on the VTA serving vault/credentials/present/0.1 (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure, branch feat/vault-credentials-present, not yet merged); against a VTA without it the call fails at the agent with unsupportedType.

title: fix(trust-tasks-dart): consumeInbound can cache a success response as JSON, so a persistent replay guard stores it (#878)
body:
fix(trust-tasks-dart): consumeInbound can cache a success response as JSON, so a persistent replay guard stores it (#878)

The Dart pipeline handed ReplayGuard.recordResponse a refusal as a JSON map
but a success as the TrustTaskDocument object itself. A guard backed by a
store cannot serialise that object. The failure was swallowed (recording is
best-effort), so such a guard cached no success response, and a resend was
absorbed with nothing to return instead of the original response. The Rust,
TypeScript and Go runtimes always record JSON.

consumeInbound takes an optional `responseToJson`. With it, a success reaches
the guard, and later DuplicateOutcome.priorResponse, as the same JSON map
shape as a refusal. Without it, behaviour is unchanged, so this is additive.
The guard and pipeline docs now say a persisting guard needs it.

The Dart HTTPS, DIDComm and TSP bindings already accept either shape when
they emit a prior response. They can pass their response encoder once they
require a core that has this parameter.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: fix: binding rejection reasons carry a category, not the error's text
body:
The DIDComm v2.1, DIDComm v1 and TSP bindings built the malformedRequest
reason in `into_reject_reason` from the error's `Display`. That text holds the
deserializer's member names and line/column offsets, sender DIDs and VIDs,
verkeys, and upstream envelope and resolver failures. A caller that answered
with the reason put all of it on the wire, which SPEC §10.4 forbids. The HTTPS
binding already avoided this.

- A body that does not deserialise now maps through
  `RejectReason::malformed_from_serde`, as the HTTPS binding's does.
- A thread disagreement names the header and member, not their values.
- Every other malformedRequest carries one constant reason per binding.

The error's `Display` is unchanged, so logs keep the detail. The codes are
unchanged; only the reason text differs.

## Tests
A new unit test in each crate's `error.rs` checks that no serde offset, VID, thread id or envelope detail reaches the reason. The DIDComm, DIDComm v1 and TSP lib tests pass (4, 16 and 1), and clippy `-D warnings` is clean.

title: fix: a handler that fails without refusing releases its replay claim, so the document can be resent (#876)
body:
fix: a handler that fails without refusing releases its replay claim, so the document can be resent (#876)

In the Go, TypeScript and Dart pipelines, a handler error that was not a
Refusal (an exception in TS and Dart) propagated straight out of
consumeInbound, leaving the item-11 claim in flight. Every resend of the
document was then absorbed as an in-flight duplicate until the record expired:
the task could not be retried, and the producer was never told why.

The claim is now released, best-effort, before the error propagates. The
handler did not finish, so nothing records that the effect happened. A
Refusal is unchanged: a retryable one releases the claim, a final one settles
it. Rust is unaffected, because its handler returns a Result and cannot fail
any other way.

The Go and Dart TSP/DIDComm bindings and the Dart HTTPS server released the
claim themselves after the core returned. Those workarounds stay until each
binding requires a core that includes this fix. The TypeScript TSP binding had
no workaround and is fixed by this change.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: fix: proofs are verified over the document as received, so a genuine proof survives a typed re-encoding
body:
Every Rust consumer verified a proof over its parsed TrustTask re-serialised:
consume_inbound through ProofVerifier::verify, the HTTPS server through
DynProofVerifier::verify_json on a TrustTask<Value>. Re-serialisation
reproduces the signed bytes only when every member round-trips, and several
do not — a generated `#[serde(default)]` member the producer omitted comes
back as `false`, a member the payload type does not model is dropped, and a
framework timestamp written `+00:00` is re-rendered as `Z`. A genuine proof
over any such document was refused proofInvalid.

- ProofVerifier and DynProofVerifier gain a provided `verify_received(&Value)`;
  the affinidi Verifier overrides it with its exact `verify_raw`, and
  ErasedVerifier forwards it. Existing implementations keep the old,
  re-serialising behaviour by default.
- ProofPolicy gains `VerifyReceived(&V, &Value)` and `with_received`, which
  turns a caller's `Verify` into it. consume_inbound re-parses the received
  value and refuses proofInvalid when it is not the document being consumed,
  since a proof over one document vouches for nothing about another.
- The TSP, DIDComm v2 and DIDComm v1 `receive` paths keep the document as
  received and apply `with_received`, so their callers change nothing.
- The HTTPS server verifies over the request body parsed as a Value, keeping
  the typed parse that refuses a duplicated top-level member.
- DynProofVerifier's doc no longer claims the erasure is lossless.

All additive: cargo semver-checks reports no update required for
trust-tasks-rs, trust-tasks-proof or trust-tasks-https.

## Tests
- `trust-tasks-proof/tests/raw_and_relationships.rs`: consume_inbound verifies the received form; a received document that is not the one consumed is refused; the erased verifier verifies as received.
- `trust-tasks-https/tests/end_to_end.rs`: a did:key-signed body with a `+00:00` issuedAt is accepted.
- Each new test fails with the fix reverted. Workspace: 2875 passed, 0 failed; clippy `-D warnings` clean.

title: feat!: target TSP 1.0 (YTSP-BAA); probe the mandatory ESSR sender
body:
Moves the suite to the **released TSP 1.0** specification ([tswg-tsp-specification#86](https://github.com/trustoverip/tswg-tsp-specification/pull/86), `ccda6b3`): Rev 3's wire, with the ESSR sender VID **mandatory in every confidential payload**, at `YTSP-BAA`.

**Suite**
- Fixture re-extracted with `tools/extract_spec_vectors.py` from the 1.0 Appendix A: eleven vectors, including the new `control-rfi-referral`. It is value-for-value identical to affinidi-tsp 0.3.0's file, which was itself checked against `tsp_sdk` 0.16.0's JSON.
- **Expected version:** the runner now expects 1.0 (`SPEC_VERSION`).
- **ESSR sender rule:** a confidential payload's ESSR sender must be the envelope sender; NULL is accepted only in signed-only payloads.
- **Interop:** `scs/hpke-base/payload-sender-null` → `…-null-refused`. A packer must decline the request; any error passes.
- **Referral check:** the `Signature_new` oracle now accepts only the challenge with the sender's VID in it.
- **New negative case `sealed/hpke-base-scs/essr-sender-null`:** no conformant 1.0 packer can produce this probe, so the runner seals it itself with RFC 9180 HPKE-Base (`runner/src/seal.rs`, `hpke` crate — a crypto primitive, not a TSP implementation). A control sealed the same way but naming the sender must open first. That also confirms the runner's sealing against every implementation.
- **Version mutations:** new mutation `draft-version-rev3` (`-BAA` → `-AAC`); `unknown-major-version` is now `-CAA`; the re-signed MINOR cases are `BAB` and `BBA`.
- **`pack-exact`** now passes a vector's referral (VID_new plus its published key), so `control-rfi-referral` re-packs byte for byte.

**Drivers**
- **reference-rust → `tsp_sdk` 0.16.0.** It now names the relationship digests by role, so the driver's invite side-table is gone.
- **affinidi-rust (0.3.0) and tsp-js (0.4.0)** refuse a NULL sender in a confidential payload. tsp-js now classifies `E_TSP_REVISION` by its `major` field rather than by the message text.

**Findings**
- **New `sdk-null-essr-sender-confidential` (spec-violation):** `tsp_sdk` 0.16.0 moved its send side to 1.0 but still accepts the NULL-sender probe. `crypto/tsp_hpke.rs` `open_payload` still treats the field as optional (`if let Some(id) = sender_identity && …`, under a comment that still says it is optional). Worth reporting upstream.
- **New `go-rev3` / `dart-rev3`** (plus `-inner` variants for nested messages): both libraries' `main` is still Rev 3, so every pairing with a 1.0 implementation fails on MAJOR. Separately, the Dart driver no longer builds from a fresh checkout: `affinidi-tsp-dart` became a workspace (`packages/affinidi_tsp`), and `drivers/dart/pubspec.yaml` still points at the repo root.
- **`sdk-non-canonical-lead-bytes`, `sdk-trailing-bytes` and `sdk-signed-only-essr`** all pass on 0.16.0 and are marked `fixed`. I didn't bisect which release fixed them.

**Report** (`--seed 20261022`): among affinidi-tsp 0.3.0, `tsp_sdk` 0.16.0 and tsp-js 0.4.0, every case passes or skips except the one `tsp_sdk` finding above. Every failure in the report is attributed. Built from worktrees of affinidi-tdk-rs main and vta-browser-plugin main (listed under "Local overrides"); the note under the title records the commits.

`cargo test` (runner): green.

### Pre-merge checklist
- [x] R1.2 / R1.3 / R1.4 / R1.5 / R1.6 / R2.1 — N/A (test harness; no services, locks, retries or state)
- [x] R3.* — driver protocol: a request for a NULL sender in a confidential payload must now be refused (documented in `docs/driver-protocol.md`); the Go and Dart drivers are unchanged
- [x] R5.* / R6.* — the report attributes every failure; nothing is excused by a catch-all except Go and Dart, whose entries say to remove them when those libraries move to 1.0
- [x] Deviations — none

title: A did:scid version floor survives a restart, and a new source is checked against the known ones (VTI-KEY-162)
body:
Tightens VTI-KEY-162 (from #75) after a security review of the implementation.

A portable did:scid log that has moved still names its former host in its early entries, so whoever holds that host later can serve the pre-move log — with rotated-away keys — under the same did:scid identity (did:webvh verification already stops a host the log never named from serving it). VTI-KEY-162 now requires:
- checking a DID URL with an unknown `src` against the sources already known for that identity, refusing it when they serve a later version;
- persisting the sources and latest verified version of every did:scid identity the node authorises (ACL subjects, owners, members, administrators), so a restart doesn't reset the floor.

The rationale paragraph explains the moved-log replay. Implemented in affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#966 (resolver 0.8.43).

title: feat(tsp-js)!: TSP 1.0 (YTSP-BAA) — refuse the Rev 2 and Rev 3 drafts, require the sender VID
body:
Moves `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` to the **released TSP 1.0** specification ([tswg-tsp-specification#86](https://github.com/trustoverip/tswg-tsp-specification/pull/86), `ccda6b3`), in step with `affinidi-tsp` 0.3.0 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#967, published) and the reference `tsp_sdk` 0.16.0.

**The change**
- **Packs `YTSP-BAA` (1.0)**, was `YTSP-AAC` (Rev 3). `unpack`, `decodeEnvelope` and `peekRevision` refuse every MAJOR but 1 as `E_TSP_REVISION`, naming the version found — Rev 3 (`AAC`), its pre-merge draft (`ABA`) and Rev 2 (`AAB`) included, all of which this package used to read.
- **The sender VID is required in every confidential payload** (spec §3.2, §3.7 step 7). Rev 3 allowed the NULL VID under HPKE-Base; a NULL sender field is now refused. Packing is unchanged — we always wrote the VID.
- **The Rev 2 reader is deleted** (the "one `rm`" CLAUDE.md anticipated), with its dispatcher arm, `UnpackKeys.senderEncryptionKey`, the `revision` field/type and the Rev 2 `cesr` constants. `src/rev3/` → `src/v1/`. `KNOWN_MINORS` → `KNOWN_VERSIONS`; `describeVersion` added. CLAUDE.md's "TSP Rev 2 exception" paragraph now says the exception is gone and why.
- **core** takes `^0.4.0` and stops passing the Rev 2-only sender X25519 key.

**Not backwards compatible on the wire.** The wallet and any VTA it talks TSP to must both be on 1.0 — VTA on `affinidi-tsp` 0.3 / `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.39. A VTA on 0.2.x is refused by name (`E_TSP_REVISION`), and refuses ours.

**Evidence**
- Appendix A 1.0 vectors (`tests/fixtures/spec-v1-vectors.json`, identical to affinidi-tsp 0.3.0's, checked against the spec text and `tsp_sdk` 0.16.0's JSON): all HPKE-Base vectors open; the six we can pack re-pack byte for byte; new `control-rfi-referral` opened and its `Signature_new` verified.
- **Both directions against the published `affinidi-tsp` 0.3.0**: a message it packed opens here with a matching thread digest (`tests/interop.rust-vector.mjs`), and a message packed here with the same fixed keys was opened by its `direct::unpack` — payload, sender, receiver, digest all match.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` all green across workspaces: tsp-js 123/123, core 1070 pass / 0 fail (2 pre-existing schema skips), extension 1308/1308.

**Release**: `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js` 0.3.0 → 0.4.0 (needs publishing for core's `^0.4.0` to resolve outside the workspace). `@openvtc/pnm-core` has an Unreleased CHANGELOG entry.

### Pre-merge checklist
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no network code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — N/A
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1) — N/A, codec change
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off (R1.4) — N/A
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — N/A; a draft-version inbound frame surfaces as a typed `E_TSP_REVISION` like any other refused frame
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — N/A
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*) — TSP wire 0.2 → 1.0 and a stricter receive rule; matches affinidi-tsp 0.3.0 (already published), verified in both directions
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*) — unknown MAJOR and NULL confidential sender both refused
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*) — refusals carry the version found
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" (R2.1) — no mutations
- [x] Deviations flagged: **R3.6** — wire-breaking; the VTA side shipped in affinidi-tdk-rs#967. No compatibility fold kept, per this repo's CLAUDE.md

title: trust-tasks-proof-v0.33.2
body:
### Fixed

- **trust-tasks-proof**: A did:scid key named with its src locator verifies ([#863](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/863))

* fix(trust-tasks-proof): a did:scid key named with its src locator verifies

  A did:scid identity is the bare DID `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>`; its resolved
  document lists its keys under it. A signer may name its key with the `?src=`
  locator a verifier needs to fetch the log (`did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=host#key-1`),
  and `CachedDidResolver` compared that reference, and the DID it carries, to the
  document's ids by exact string, so the proof never verified.

  The resolver now strips a did:scid `src` (affinidi_did_common::scid, which
  touches nothing else) before checking the document id, the relationship
  listing and the controller. The issuer binding is unchanged and stays exact
  (SPEC §4.8): a signer writes `issuer` and its verificationMethod in the same
  form, and a test pins that a mixed pair is still refused.

  Needs affinidi-did-common 0.4.4 (the `scid` module) once it is released.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.33.2
body:
### Added

- **vault/credentials/present**: Present a held credential to a verifier the client names, bound to its nonce, disclosing only the named claims ([#871](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/871))

* feat(vault/credentials/present): present a held credential to a verifier the client names, bound to its nonce, disclosing only the named claims

  A client that holds no holder key (a browser wallet, a phone) could not
  carry a presentation to a verifier that takes one inside its own request
  document, such as vtc/directory/card/present: credential-exchange/present
  answers only a verifier that asks the agent. The maintainer now signs as the
  credential's subject for a named audience and nonce, refuses over-disclosure
  of a credential without selective disclosure (wouldOverDisclose), records the
  disclosure before answering, and conflates custody failures as notFound.

- **vta/webvh/dids/create**: 1.2 chooses the did:scid identity and the alsoKnownAs alias ([#862](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/862))

* feat(vta/webvh/dids/create): 1.2 chooses the did:scid identity and the alsoKnownAs alias

  A did:webvh log can be presented as its did:scid:vh:1 DID, an identity
  the same log verifies but which does not name its host (VTI-KEY-160 to
  VTI-KEY-166 of the VTI specification). 1.2's request may name `didMethod`
  (`webvh` or `scid`) and `scidAlsoKnownAs`. Each falls back to the VTA's
  configuration, then to `webvh` and `true`.

  The response REQUIRES both as applied, plus `webvhDid` (the log) and
  `scidDidUrl` (the did:scid with the `src` a recipient needs to resolve it).
  `did` is the identity in the applied form, the bare did:scid DID when
  `didMethod` is `scid`, and the family's other tasks accept either `did` or
  `webvhDid`.

  Asking for the did:scid identity when the alias cannot be listed (refused by
  the request, forbidden by the template, or absent from a supplied log) is
  refused with the new `scidAliasRequired` code.

  1.2 is a new version because 1.1's response refuses unknown members. The
  request members are additive, but a 1.1 client would refuse the response.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

- **rooms/records/prune**: A room states how long it keeps its records, and an administrator prunes what that rule makes eligible ([#868](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/868))

Records only had room-level lifecycle: a room could not keep a meeting note
  for a month and a decision for years, and nothing ever removed a retracted
  record's tombstone.

  - rooms/_shared/0.1 (in place, additive): RecordRetention ({tombstoneDays,
    recordDays}, by host-visible updatedAt; pinned records exempt from
    recordDays; absent or {} means nothing is eligible) and RecordPrune (the
    mark a prune leaves: version, time, count — never which records or what
    they said). HeadVersion answers the note it carried about erasure: a prune
    takes the next version, and on a pruned room headVersion is the higher of
    the highest record version and the latest prune's, so two roots straddling
    a prune never share a version.
  - rooms/records/prune 0.1 (new): admin only, never curate; kinds retracted |
    aged; required reason; dryRun. Removes eligible records outright, releases
    their blobs, records lastPrune. noRetention when the room states no rule
    for the kinds asked. Hosts never prune on their own. Audit keeps the mark,
    reason, requester where the tier discloses one, and the retention applied,
    never content; a reader holding an earlier listing can check every
    disappearance against the reported retention.
  - rooms/records/retention/set 0.1 (new): admin replaces the retention whole,
    with a reason and an optional expectedRetention precondition.
  - rooms/create 0.2: recordRetention at creation. rooms/info 0.2: serves
    recordRetention and lastPrune to every reader. rooms/records/list 0.3 and
    rooms/keys/browse 0.2: lastPrune on every page; a reader synced below it
    rebuilds and drops what is gone.
  - rooms/records/curate 0.1: editorial pointer to the prune.
  - Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

  Refs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2118.

- **vtc/rooms/storage**: Migrate 0.2 and rooms/get 0.2 — reassignment, retry ownership, resume without re-consent, orphans, pause reporting, queueing ([#867](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/867))

migrate/0.2 fixes a migration's toConfig at approval and keeps it if the room
  is reassigned (new uploads go to the new assignment; a second migration may
  follow); makes the community the one retry owner (capped exponential backoff
  with jitter before `paused`); answers a request for a room with a migration in
  progress at once, resuming a paused one, without parking it for consent again;
  does not migrate or count orphaned blobs; reports `pausedCause`, `lastError`
  and `nextAttemptAt`; and permits one migration at a time with a `queued`
  state.

  rooms/get/0.2 reports the same migration through the new shared component
  vtc/_shared/0.1/room-migration, and adds the required `toConfig`.

- **vtc/storage**: Ambient and sealed storage auth — roleArn, room-scoped credential rules, sealed cleartext schema, host gating ([#866](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/866))

vtc/_shared/0.2/room-storage adds `roleArn` to `ambient` auth (S3 only), the
  `notAllowed` credential status, and `SealedStorageCredential` — the cleartext a
  `sealed` credential is carried in (s3 access-key pair with optional session
  token, gcs service-account key file, walrus suiprivkey), naming its configId
  inside the seal.

  vtc/storage/configs/{create,update,get,list}/0.2 re-pin to it. create/0.2 makes
  room-scoped credentials normative for ambient (and sealed where the backend can
  mint them): one per (config, room), limited to the room prefix
  `rooms/<32 hex of SHA-256(roomId)>/` and the object actions needed, built by a
  JSON encoder / CEL builder and never by interpolation, at most 15 minutes,
  never used for another room. A host MAY refuse ambient or sealed by
  configuration (`authNotAllowed`, now with `details.reason`), and SHOULD label
  sealed as offering no protection against the machine's operator.

  vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.2 requires the sealed cleartext to be a
  SealedStorageCredential for the request's config, and refuses sealed when the
  host does not permit it.

- **vtc/admin/events**: 0.4 adds a communityRooms topic — the owner's view of the rooms the community owns ([#864](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/864))

The console's Community rooms tab polls every 60 s, because no topic covers
  it: `rooms` is the host's view (storage, limits, lifecycle) for holders of
  `vtc.rooms.admin`, carries no room's details, and is not readable by a
  `vtc.rooms.manage` holder who lacks `vtc.rooms.admin`.

  - vtc/admin/events/_shared/0.4: Topic gains `communityRooms` (10 topics).
  - vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.4: `topics` maxItems 10; "What 0.4 adds";
    Authorization row — holders of `vtc.rooms.manage`, prompting
    vtc/rooms/community/list 0.2, get 0.2 and members/list 0.1;
    `vtc.rooms.admin` alone does not qualify.
  - vtc/admin/events/event/0.4: producer rules 8–9 — hint when anything those
    reads show changes (a room created or its label, description or tags
    changed; an admission offered, withdrawn, accepted or renewed; a removal
    owed, retried, settled or failed, including on departure; the profile
    write's state; the authority-renewal state). No room, member, DID, offer,
    credential or record identifier in any member, ext included. Not a count
    topic. Coalescing, standing re-checks and stream-ending on a shrink are
    unchanged.
  - vtc/rooms/community/update 0.1 and 0.2 (draft, editorial in place):
    "Live updates" now points at `communityRooms` in events 0.4 instead of
    "a later version".

  0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 are unchanged; a community serving several versions answers
  each subscription at its own.



### Fixed

- A replay record is kept until the skew-extended window closes, so a late replay cannot execute twice ([#872](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/872))

Freshness accepts a document until issuedAt + maxAge + skew, but the replay
  record was retained only until issuedAt + maxAge. A replay arriving in the
  final skew interval (60s under the consequential defaults) passed freshness,
  found its record already dropped, and executed again — the double execution
  SPEC §7.2 item 11 forbids, and a break of the "same bound" rule the record
  expiry documents.

  recordExpiry now returns issuedAt + maxAge + skew in Rust, TypeScript, Go and
  Dart. The expiresAt branch is unchanged: expiry is checked without skew, so it
  was already exact. Rust and TS gain a regression test at the boundary.



### Specifications

- **rooms/epoch/prune**: 0.2 — the host keeps the room's epoch floor, and members' key holders forget what they hold below it ([#869](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/869))

* spec(rooms/epoch/prune): 0.2 — the host keeps the room's epoch floor, and members' key holders forget what they hold below it

  Each member's key holder keeps its own copy of a room's epoch chain, so
  erasing the host's rungs left every key holder able to derive what the owner
  had decided nobody should.

  - rooms/_shared/0.1 (in place, additive): EpochFloor — the earliest epoch
    whose key the room still lets anybody derive; monotonic. Hosts keep it,
    never store or serve a rung at or below it, and serve it. A member's key
    holder that learns a higher floor discards rungs at or below it and every
    storage, file or cached key below it (including keys derived in passing
    while catching up), never stores them again from any source, refuses to
    derive below it (beyondChain), and keeps the floor. States plainly that
    nothing already read, decrypted or exported is recalled, and that the
    floor is honoured, not enforced.
  - rooms/epoch/prune 0.2: the host raises the floor to beforeEpoch − 1 (also
    where nothing is dropped: a gap, a fromJoin room) and returns it as the
    required epochFloor. beforeEpoch keeps 0.1's meaning; the off-by-one is
    stated with a table, and two 0.1 misstatements are corrected.
  - rooms/epoch/chain 0.2: epochFloor on every response once pruned; never a
    rung at or below it.
  - rooms/keys/chain 0.2: the member relays the floor (alone if need be); the
    key holder applies it. rooms/keys/backfill 0.2: fetches with epoch/chain
    0.2, applies and reports the floor.
  - Editorial pointers in rooms/keys/open 0.2, rooms/keys/file-key 0.2,
    rooms/keys/read 0.1 and rooms/epoch/prune 0.1.
  - Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

  Refs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2118.

- **rooms/records**: A record says what kind of claim it is, what it cites, what it may be used for, and when it lapses ([#865](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/865))

A sealed record proves who wrote it and whether a member or an agent did,
  but not what kind of claim it is: an agent's inference read the same as an
  observed fact or a credential-backed statement. And records could not
  expire individually — a meeting note and a decision lived equally long.

  - rooms/_shared/0.1 (in place, additive, as `roomProfile` was):
    SealedRecordBody gains optional `basis` (declared | observed | verified |
    inferred), `confidence` (0–1), `evidence` (record or credential
    citations, discriminated by `kind`), `validFor` (purposes as IRIs plus a
    plain-text note) and `validUntil`, all inside the author's signature.
    Provenance is display and weighting only, never authority; writers
    SHOULD set `basis`, agent writers that do not know SHOULD write
    `inferred`. Readers hide a record past its `validUntil` from default
    listings, search and recall and MAY show it on explicit request; no host
    enforces it and nothing about it is in the clear on sealed tiers.
    Records written before verify unchanged; readers that predate the
    members refuse bodies carrying them by rule (1), showing nothing rather
    than something wrong.
  - rooms/records/put 0.3 (new): an open room's `cleartext` carries the same
    five members, stored and served as received, never acted on by the
    host. `sealed` writes are unchanged.
  - Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

  Refs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2117, #2118.

title: fix(trust-tasks-ts-proof): ecdsa-jcs-2019 hashes once and accepts high-S, so P-256/P-384 proofs interoperate
body:
## Problem

`@openvtc/trust-tasks-proof`'s `ecdsa-jcs-2019` (P-256 / P-384) didn't interoperate with any other implementation:

- **Double hash.** `sign.ts` passed `SHA(hashData)` to `@noble/curves`, whose `prehash` option defaults to `true` (v2), so noble hashed it again. TS signatures were over `SHA(SHA(hashData))`. The verifier did the same, so TS↔TS round-trips passed while every standard ECDSA signature — including the Go backend's (`trust-tasks-go/proof`, single hash) — failed, in both directions.
- **Low-S only.** noble's `verify` defaults to `lowS: true`. Go's `ecdsa.Sign` doesn't normalise S, so about half of Go's signatures would have been refused even after the hashing fix.

Only Ed25519 had a cross-language fixture, so nothing caught either.

## Fix

- `sign.ts`: `sign(digest(hashData), key, { prehash: false })` — the explicit suite digest *is* the ECDSA message hash.
- `verifier.ts`: `verify(sig, digest(hashData), key, { prehash: false, lowS: false })`.

Ed25519 is untouched.

## Tests

- **node:crypto as an independent ECDSA**, P-256 and P-384: a `signTrustTask` signature verifies as standard ECDSA-with-SHA over `hashData` (r‖s); and a node-signed proof verifies with the TS verifier in both its low-S and high-S form. All four fail on the old code.
- **Shared fixture** `ecdsa-jcs-2019.fixture.json`, copied into `trust-tasks-ts-proof/test/` and `trust-tasks-go/proof/testdata/` (as the eddsa fixture is): `ts-p256`/`ts-p384` signed by TS (RFC 6979, so the TS test reproduces them byte for byte) and `go-p256`/`go-p384` signed by Go and picked with a **high S**. Both suites verify all four.
- Passing locally: `npm test` in `trust-tasks-ts-proof` (26/26); `go vet` / `go test ./...` in `trust-tasks-go/proof`; `gofmt -l` clean.

## Compatibility

ECDSA proofs produced by an earlier version of this package **no longer verify** (they were never valid ecdsa-jcs-2019). Trust Task documents are short-lived under freshness, so the practical exposure is small. This PR is titled `fix:` (patch); if you consider it a breaking behaviour change for consumers who stored such documents, retitle with `!`.

Not covered here: the Rust (`trust-tasks-proof`, via affinidi) and Dart (`trust_tasks_proof`, via `ssi`) ECDSA paths aren't yet in the shared fixture — worth adding both to it as a follow-up.

title: ci(release): give the Release PR job swap so cargo-semver-checks is not killed under memory pressure
body:
## Problem

The `Release PR` job in `publish.yml` failed on the push of #871 ([run 39787449295](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/actions/runs/39787449295)) and again on its re-run: `Process completed with exit code 143` (SIGTERM) roughly 2–2.5 minutes into `Checking API compatibility with cargo-semver-checks...`, with no error from the tool. The previous push succeeded, with that step taking 6.5 min. Release PR #870 is consequently missing #871.

Running `cargo semver-checks -p trust-tasks-rs --baseline-version 0.33.1` locally peaks at **12.6 GB resident** (`/usr/bin/time -l`). A standard `ubuntu-latest` runner has 16 GB, and SIGTERM-with-no-message under memory pressure is how systemd-oomd ends a process. #871's additional generated code is the likely tipping point. (The run log has no memory figures, so this is a strong inference, not a captured OOM event.)

## Change

A new step before `Open or update the Release PR`:

- stops `systemd-oomd` (tolerating its absence), so pressure alone doesn't end the job;
- replaces the image's swap with a swapfile of up to 16 GB on whichever of `/` and `/mnt` has more free space, always leaving 8 GB free for the rustdoc builds (skips with a warning below 4 GB);
- prints `free -h` so the next failure, if any, shows what it had.

Swap keeps `semver_check = true` on every crate, which `release-plz.toml` asks for on crates that own an API; the alternatives were a paid larger runner or switching the check off for `trust-tasks-rs`.

## Verification

`actionlint` clean (including shellcheck of the step). The job only runs on push to `main`, so merging this is its test — the `Release PR` job on this merge should succeed and bring #870 up to date.

title: fix: a replay record is kept until the skew-extended window closes, so a late replay cannot execute twice (#872)
body:
fix: a replay record is kept until the skew-extended window closes, so a late replay cannot execute twice (#872)

Freshness accepts a document until issuedAt + maxAge + skew, but the replay
record was retained only until issuedAt + maxAge. A replay arriving in the
final skew interval (60s under the consequential defaults) passed freshness,
found its record already dropped, and executed again — the double execution
SPEC §7.2 item 11 forbids, and a break of the "same bound" rule the record
expiry documents.

recordExpiry now returns issuedAt + maxAge + skew in Rust, TypeScript, Go and
Dart. The expiresAt branch is unchanged: expiry is checked without skew, so it
was already exact. Rust and TS gain a regression test at the boundary.

carry a presentation to a verifier that takes one inside its own request
document, such as vtc/directory/card/present: credential-exchange/present
answers only a verifier that asks the agent. The maintainer now signs as the
credential's subject for a named audience and nonce, refuses over-disclosure
of a credential without selective disclosure (wouldOverDisclose), records the
disclosure before answering, and conflates custody failures as notFound.

title: fix(trust-tasks-proof): a did:scid key named with its src locator verifies
body:
`CachedDidResolver` compared a proof's `verificationMethod`, its DID and the controller to the resolved document's ids by exact string. A did:scid identity's document lists keys under the bare `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>`, while a signer names its key with the `?src=` locator a verifier needs to fetch the log (`did:scid:vh:1:<scid>?src=host#key-1`, VTI-KEY-163 in trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#75), so such a proof never verified.

The resolver now strips a did:scid `src` (`affinidi_did_common::scid::strip_scid_src`, which touches nothing but a did:scid DID URL whose only query is `src`) before checking the document id, the relationship listing and the controller. **The issuer binding is unchanged and stays exact (SPEC §4.8)**: producers write `issuer` and the verificationMethod in the same form; a test pins that a mixed pair is still refused.

Tests in `trust-tasks-proof/tests/proof_purpose.rs` (bare and `src` forms verify; another SCID refused; mixed issuer/VM refused).

Floors: affinidi-did-common 0.4.4 (the `scid` module) and affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.42 (native did:scid documents; every DID URL of one did:scid shares a cache entry), both published from affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#965. Tests: 44 passed; clippy clean; workspace check passes.

form, and a test pins that a mixed pair is still refused.

body:
New version `vta/webvh/dids/create/1.2` for presenting a did:webvh log as its `did:scid:vh:1` identity (VTI-KEY-160..166, VTI-VTA-034..036 — trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#75).

- Request may name `didMethod` (`webvh` | `scid`) and `scidAlsoKnownAs`; each falls back to the VTA's configuration, then `webvh` / `true`.
- Response REQUIRES both as applied, plus `webvhDid` (the log) and `scidDidUrl` (the did:scid with the `src` a recipient needs). `did` is the identity in the applied form — the bare did:scid DID when `didMethod` is `scid`; the family's other tasks accept either `did` or `webvhDid`.

the same log verifies but which does not name its host (VTI-KEY-160 to

configuration, then to `webvh` and `true`.

`scidDidUrl` (the did:scid with the `src` a recipient needs to resolve it).
`did` is the identity in the applied form, the bare did:scid DID when
`didMethod` is `scid`, and the family's other tasks accept either `did` or
`webvhDid`.

Asking for the did:scid identity when the alias cannot be listed (refused by
the request, forbidden by the template, or absent from a supplied log) is
refused with the new `scidAliasRequired` code.

1.2 is a new version because 1.1's response refuses unknown members. The
request members are additive, but a 1.1 client would refuse the response.

title: spec(rooms/epoch/prune): 0.2 — the host keeps the room's epoch floor, and members' key holders forget what they hold below it
body:
## What

`rooms/epoch/prune` now **reaches members' key holders**. Each member's key holder keeps its own copy of the room's epoch chain (that is what lets it open old records unaided), so erasing the host's rungs alone left every key holder able to derive what the owner decided nobody should.

- `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json` (in place, additive): `EpochFloor` — the earliest epoch whose storage key the room still lets anybody derive. Monotonic (only rises; every party keeps the highest it has learnt from any source). Normative rules for:
  - **hosts**: keep it per room, never store/accept/serve a rung at or below it, serve it wherever a response can carry it;
  - **member key holders** (and any member client that keeps rungs/keys): on learning a higher floor, **MUST** discard rungs `≤ F` and every storage key, file key or cached key below `F` (including keys derived in passing while applying commits through those epochs); **MUST NOT** store them again from any source (principal, backfill, repair, catch-up, an unpruned mirror) or ask for them; **MUST** refuse to derive below `F`, answering `beyondChain`; keep `F` itself while holding anything for the room; SHOULD learn it whenever fetching rungs / catching up and at least as often as it otherwise reads the room;
  - an honest **"what a floor does not do"**: it recalls nothing already read, decrypted, downloaded, exported or extracted, and is honoured by conforming parties rather than enforced; the cryptographic guarantee is still only "never derived ⇒ never derivable".
- `rooms/epoch/prune/0.2` — host keeps and raises the floor (`max(held, beforeEpoch − 1)`, also on `fromJoin` rooms and gap-y chains where nothing is dropped), new **required** response member `epochFloor`. `beforeEpoch` keeps exactly 0.1's meaning; the off-by-one (rung `N` survives and yields `N − 1`) is now stated with a table. Corrects two 0.1 misstatements (sideEffects said "no member retained the outgoing keys"; `notAhead` said "drop every rung"). Mirrors: prune at every host; the floor learnt from any host keeps an unpruned mirror's rungs out.
- `rooms/epoch/chain/0.2` — `epochFloor` on **every** response once pruned (any `fromEpoch`/`limit`, empty `links` too — so a one-rung read is a cheap floor check); never a rung at or below it; a relaying client MUST relay it.
- `rooms/keys/chain/0.2` — request carries `epochFloor` (relayed from the host), `links` optional so a floor can be passed on alone (`anyOf`); response reports the floor held; rungs at/below it are silently not stored. 0.1 requests are subject to the held floor too.
- `rooms/keys/backfill/0.2` — fetch with `epoch/chain` 0.2, apply the floor, never ask below it, report `epochFloor`.
- Editorial pointers (no wire change): `rooms/keys/open/0.2`, `rooms/keys/file-key/0.2` (below the floor ⇒ `beyondChain`), `rooms/keys/read/0.1` (a repair never restores below the floor), `rooms/epoch/prune/0.1` (→ 0.2).
- Rust / TypeScript / Go / Dart bindings regenerated.

## Why

Maintainer decision on OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2118 ("crypto-deletion verb" + "prune_epoch_links_before … no verb reaches it"): epoch prune is only meaningful for "delete everything before X" if members' agents stop being able to read before X too.

## Version-set reasoning (kept minimal)

- New versions only where the **wire** changes: `epoch/prune` 0.2, `epoch/chain` 0.2 (the read key holders use to sync the chain), `keys/chain` 0.2, `keys/backfill` 0.2.
- `rooms/info` was considered and **not** used: member key holders do not read it to sync the chain (in VTI only owner-side group code calls it), and the record-retention PR already mints `info/0.2` — adding the floor there would make the two PRs collide. Easy to add later if surfaces want it.
- `rooms/epoch/commits` not versioned: a key holder catching up SHOULD read `epoch/chain` 0.2 (it needs links then anyway), and keys derived in passing below the floor must be discarded per `EpochFloor`.
- `keys/open`, `keys/file-key`, `keys/read`, `keys/profile/read`, `keys/list`: no new reason code needed — below the floor is exactly the existing `beyondChain` (`earliestEpoch` at or above the floor). The obligation itself lives in the shared `EpochFloor` definition, following the family's precedent of reader rules living in `_shared` (`SealedRecordBody`, `RoomProfileStatement`); only pointer sentences were added in place.

## Naming

The wire member is `epochFloor`, not `prunedBefore`: what parties act on is the earliest *readable* epoch (`beforeEpoch − 1`), which matches the existing `earliestEpoch` / `earliestReadableEpoch` vocabulary. Naming it after `beforeEpoch` would invite the off-by-one that 0.1's own prose fell into.

## `fromJoin` rooms

No rungs exist and the host drops nothing (`pruned: 0`), but the host still raises the floor, and key holders discard any storage/file keys they cached for epochs below it. A `fromJoin` member could not walk back anyway; the floor reaches their caches.

## Open questions

1. **Commits below the floor.** Hosts keep relaying commits (`epoch/commits`) so a member stuck below the floor can catch up; the member's key holder must discard what it derives in passing. Dropping commits instead would strand such members (re-Welcome needed). Kept as is; worth a maintainer view.
2. **Owner surface.** `rooms/epoch/prune` is deliberately absent from `rooms/keys/act`, so an owner whose surface can reach only its agent has no way to send it (VTI: "no verb reaches it"). A dedicated owner-side key-holder task (like `rooms/owner/register`) is likely needed — follow-up.
3. `rooms/keys/act` 0.6 lists actable versions; `epoch/chain` 0.2 needs an `act` 0.7. Suggest one `act` bump after the three companion PRs land.
4. The floor is cooperative. A malicious or stale key holder keeps what it had — stated plainly in the spec.

## Validation

`npm run validate` ✓ (928 specs) · `npm run check-bindings` ✓ · `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --test conformance -- rooms::` ✓

Companion PRs: #865 (record provenance + `validUntil`), #868 (record retention + `rooms/records/prune`). All three edit `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json` in different `$defs`; whichever merges later should re-run the four generators.

title: feat(rooms/records/prune): a room states how long it keeps its records, and an administrator prunes what that rule makes eligible
body:
## What

A room states **how long it keeps its records**, and an administrator can **prune** what that rule makes eligible.

- `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json` (in place, additive):
  - `RecordRetention` — `{tombstoneDays?, recordDays?, ext?}`, integer days. Absent or `{}` = nothing is ever eligible by age. Age is the host-visible `updatedAt` (a curation restarts it); pinned records are exempt from `recordDays`.
  - `RecordPrune` — the mark a prune leaves: `{version, at, removed}`. Never which records, never anything they said.
  - `HeadVersion` description — answers the note it carried ("a family that exposes [erasure] owes this definition another look"): a prune takes the next version from the room's counter, and on a pruned room `headVersion` is `max(highest record version, latest prune's version)`, so a root before and a root after a prune are never labelled with one version (which would read as equivocation). Rooms never pruned are unaffected.
- `rooms/records/prune/0.1` (new) — **`admin` only** (not `curate`). `kinds: ["retracted" | "aged"]`, REQUIRED `reason`, optional `dryRun`. Removes eligible records outright (tombstones included), releases blobs only they named, takes a version, records `lastPrune`. Response reports `removed`, `blobsReleased`, the `recordRetention` eligibility was decided under, and the `prune` mark. `noRetention` when the room states no rule for the kinds asked (removing under an unstated rule is refused, not answered `removed: 0`). Hosts never prune on their own initiative or on a timer.
- `rooms/records/retention/set/0.1` (new) — `admin` changes the record retention (whole replacement, `{}` clears), REQUIRED `reason`, optional `expectedRetention` precondition (`retentionConflict`), `retentionNotPermitted` for host governance; response carries `previous`.
- `rooms/create/0.2` — `recordRetention` at creation (+ echo). Adds the Authorization/Request/Response sections 0.1 lacked.
- `rooms/info/0.2` — serves `recordRetention` and `lastPrune` to every reader, so no record is removed under a rule its readers could not have read.
- `rooms/records/list/0.3` — `lastPrune` on every page; a reader whose copy was synced below `lastPrune.version` MUST rebuild from a full listing and drop what is gone (a prune removes the tombstones incremental sync relied on).
- `rooms/keys/browse/0.2` — passes `lastPrune` through from the host, same reader rule.
- `rooms/records/curate/0.1` — editorial pointer: the "separate, higher-trust act" that removes tombstones is `rooms/records/prune`.
- Rust / TypeScript / Go / Dart bindings regenerated.

## Why

VTI issue OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2118 (room record retention + a prune verb). Records only had room-level lifecycle (`retentionDays` after lapse); a room could not keep meeting notes for a month and decisions for years, and nothing removed tombstones.

## Audit and Merkle trail

- The host keeps the `RecordPrune` mark (version, time, count), the reason, the requester **where the tier discloses one** (nothing on `private`), and the retention applied. It MUST NOT keep anything a removed record said or carried and SHOULD NOT keep removed keys (on `open` rooms keys may be descriptive).
- The record tree loses leaves; `RecordCount` drops; `HeadVersion` moves to the prune's version; older witnessed anchors read as `ahead`. A reader holding an earlier listing **can check a prune**: every record that disappeared must have been eligible at `prune.at` under the reported `recordRetention`.
- Honest scope: a prune removes records from **the host**, not from members' copies, exports, mirrors or published ciphertext. The erasure that reaches copies is `rooms/epoch/prune` (companion PR).

## Naming: why `recordRetention`

`retentionPolicy` (chained|fromJoin) is the key chain's reach and is immutable; `retentionDays` is how long a host keeps a lapsed room. This is a third, **mutable** question — how long a live room keeps its records — so it gets its own name.

## Compatibility

All new versions are MINOR increments of draft specs with closed payloads. Hosts implementing them SHOULD keep serving the earlier versions. **Known gap:** `rooms/records/list` 0.1/0.2 and `rooms/keys/browse` 0.1 cannot carry `lastPrune`, so an incremental reader at those versions keeps pruned records (and sees a record retracted while it was away as current) until it fully rebuilds. browse 0.2 SHOULD ignore `sinceVersion` for a 0.1 caller of a pruned room.

## Judgment calls / open questions

1. **No automatic host pruning.** Every removal is an attributable `admin` act with a reason; the room's own agent can run it on a schedule. Alternative: hosts apply the retention on their own — rejected because it is a destructive act nobody signed.
2. **No notice period** on a shortened retention; `retention/set` says a host or governance MAY delay it and SHOULD say so. Worth deciding whether to require one.
3. **The room profile record** (`RoomProfileStatement`) is indistinguishable to the host, so `recordDays` can remove it; the prune spec says rooms with `recordDays` SHOULD keep the profile pinned. An alternative is to have `rooms/keys/profile/write` pin it — a follow-up.
4. `validUntil` (companion PR #865) is sealed and never host-visible, so it is never a prune criterion; a curator's agent retracts expired records and `tombstoneDays` ages them out.
5. `rooms/keys/act` 0.6's table lists actable versions; `create/0.2`, `info/0.2`, `list/0.3` need an `act` 0.7 to be reachable via the key holder. `prune` and `retention/set` are deliberately not added (like `rooms/epoch/prune`), which leaves an owner surface that can only reach its agent without a path — same open question as epoch prune. Suggest one `act` follow-up after the three companion PRs land.
6. `rooms/owner/register` 0.2 passes create params through but not `recordRetention`; left for a later register version.

## Validation

`npm run validate` ✓ (930 specs) · `npm run check-bindings` ✓ (TS/Rust/Go/Dart agree; 2343 error codes) · `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --test conformance -- rooms::` ✓

Companion PRs: #865 (record provenance + `validUntil`), #869 (epoch prune reaching members' key holders).

If merged after #865 (both edit `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json` in different `$defs`), re-run the four generators on the merge.

title: feat(vtc/rooms/storage): migrate 0.2 and rooms/get 0.2 — reassignment, retry ownership, resume without re-consent, orphans, pause reporting, queueing
body:
## What

Clarifies `vtc/rooms/storage/migrate` in a **0.2** (0.1 untouched), and carries the reporting into **`vtc/rooms/get/0.2`**, which returns the same migration under `storage.migration`.

- **Reassignment during a migration** (item 9): the migration's `toConfig` is fixed when it is approved and is kept if the room is reassigned; uploads after the reassignment go to the new assignment (as `assign` already requires); a second migration may follow once the first is `complete` or `failed`.
- **Retry ownership** (item 10): the community retries failing copy/read/write/credential steps itself with capped exponential backoff and jitter before setting `paused` (except `capacity`, which retrying cannot clear); it is the one retry owner. A verification failure is still `failed`, not retried.
- **Resume without re-consent** (item 5 + Authorization): a request for a room with a migration `queued`/`running`/`paused` is answered at once with it — resuming a paused one — and is **not parked**; it changes neither `toConfig` nor `reason`, MAY adopt the new `maxBytesPerSecond`, and is audited.
- **Orphans** (item 12): orphaned blobs are not migrated and not counted; one orphaned mid-migration is dropped from it.
- **Pause reporting** (item 11): optional `pausedCause` (`capacity` | `source` | `destination` | `credential`), `lastError` (≤ 500 chars, never a credential / presigned URL / signed request / room id) and `nextAttemptAt`; the last two MAY appear on a `running` migration waiting out a backoff.
- **Queueing** (item 13): a community MAY run one migration at a time (per community or per config) and hold the rest as a new **`queued`** state.
- New shared component **`vtc/_shared/0.1/room-migration.schema.json`** (`MigrationState`, `MigrationPauseCause`, `MigrationLastError`) so migrate and rooms/get describe one migration the same way.
- **`vtc/rooms/get/0.2`**: `storage.migration` gains required **`toConfig`** (after a mid-migration reassignment the assigned config is not where blobs are going) and the fields above; present while `queued`/`running`/`paused`, MAY remain for the last finished one.
- New examples (a paused migration) and invalid fixtures (unknown cause, unbounded `lastError`, unknown member; rooms/get migration without `toConfig`, unknown state).
- Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

## Why

Maintainer decisions on the open behaviours of migrate (VTI `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` §7.3); without them, two VTCs would disagree on what happens to a reassigned room's migration and whether resuming needs another approval.

## Versioning / compatibility

`migrate/0.1` is `draft`, but these add members and a state value and change normative behaviour, so per SPEC §5.2 this is a MINOR version, not an in-place edit (in-place is reserved for editorial/normalisation changes). `rooms/get` needs a 0.2 because `storage.migration` is its own inline shape.

- Requests are unchanged in both tasks.
- Response readers must accept `queued` and the new optional members; `rooms/get/0.2` producers must send `toConfig`.

## Validation

- `npm run validate` — 926 specs, OK
- `npm run check-bindings` — all four languages agree
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --test conformance -- vtc::rooms` — 92 passed (includes the new invalid fixtures)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (trust-tasks-ts), `go vet ./specs/vtc/...`, `dart analyze` on the new libraries — clean

## Open questions

1. **Destination retired mid-migration.** `retire` refuses only while rooms are *assigned* to a config, so after a reassignment a migration's `toConfig` can be retired (→ `draining`) while the migration still targets it. This PR pauses it with cause `destination`, but there is no task to abandon a paused migration, and item 5 keeps answering with it — so the room cannot start a new one. Options: `retire` refuses while a config is any migration's `toConfig`; or a re-issue ends a migration whose `toConfig` is no longer `active` and (with consent) starts a new one; or a `vtc/rooms/storage/migrate/cancel`.
2. **Queue scope**: "per community or per config" is left to the host. Say if you want one fixed.
3. Anyone with `vtc.rooms.admin` can resume someone else's paused migration without consent (it is the approved operation). That matches the decision; flagging that it also lets them change the rate.
4. This PR and #866 (storage auth) both regenerate `schema_index.rs`, `components.ts`, `index.ts`, `tests/conformance/main.rs`; whichever merges second needs a rebase + regenerate.

`window.vtaWallet.directory` gains `marks`, `mark`, `putList`, `deleteList`. They talk only to the member's own agent, in the context their identity at the community lives in; nothing goes to the community. The first mark on an entry links it; later ones annotate the contact it made.

title: feat(vtc/storage): ambient and sealed storage auth — roleArn, room-scoped credential rules, sealed cleartext schema, host gating
body:
## What

Pins down the two non-VTA storage auth modes for data-room storage configs.

- **`vtc/_shared/0.2/room-storage.schema.json`** (new component version; 0.1 untouched)
  - `ambient` gains optional **`roleArn`** (`AwsRoleArn`, IAM role ARN in any partition, validated so it can go to STS and into a session policy safely). S3 only.
  - `CredentialState.status` gains **`notAllowed`** — the config's mode is one the host no longer permits; `roomsHoldingCredentials` now also applies to `ambient`/`sealed`.
  - New **`SealedStorageCredential`** — the cleartext inside a `sealed` block, by kind: `s3` (`accessKeyId`, `secretAccessKey`, optional `sessionToken`), `gcs` (`serviceAccountKey`, Google's key file verbatim), `walrus` (`suiPrivateKey`, Bech32 `suiprivkey`). Names `configId` inside the seal so a block can't be replayed into another config (same pattern as `external`'s `ExternalSecretPayload`).
- **`vtc/storage/configs/create/0.2`** — re-pins; new **Room-scoped credentials** section (modelled on `external/credentials/issue/0.3` items 9–12): per (config, room), limited to the room prefix `<prefix>rooms/<32 hex of SHA-256(roomId)>/` and the object actions needed; S3 = `AssumeRole` + inline session policy on `arn:<partition>:s3:::<bucket>/<room prefix>*`, `DurationSeconds` ≤ 900; GCS = STS token exchange with a Credential Access Boundary and `resource.name.startsWith(...)` condition; policy by JSON encoder / CEL builder, never interpolation; ≤ 15 min; never across rooms; no unscoped fallback. Sealed: same rules where the backend can mint (AWS `GetFederationToken`, GCS key → token → CAB), else single-object presigns ≤ 15 min. Host gating: a community **MAY** refuse `ambient`/`sealed` by configuration; `authNotAllowed` gains `details.reason` (`doesNotFitKind` | `roleArnNotApplicable` | `disabledByHost`). `sealed` **SHOULD** be labelled as no protection against the machine's operator. Adds an ambient+roleArn example and a refusal example.
- **`vtc/storage/configs/update/0.2`** — re-pins; same validation; drops cached room-scoped credentials on any auth change; accepts moving a `notAllowed` config to a permitted mode.
- **`vtc/storage/configs/{get,list}/0.2`** — re-pin (so responses can carry `roleArn` / `notAllowed`); report `notAllowed`; label sealed.
- **`vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.2`** — cleartext MUST be a `SealedStorageCredential` whose `kind` is the config's and `configId` the request's (`invalidCredential` otherwise); `authNotAllowed` when the host does not permit `sealed`. The type is declared in the payload schema's `$defs.SealedCredentialCleartext` (not a payload member) so all four generated bindings carry it.
- Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

## Why

Maintainer decisions for the VTC data-room files work (VTI `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` §7.4): ambient S3 should name its role in the config; downscoping for ambient/sealed needs to be normative rather than a sentence in a description; implementations must agree on what is inside the seal; ambient/sealed are host-operator choices.

## Versioning / compatibility

All touched specs are `draft`, but these are member additions/narrowings, not editorial, so per SPEC §5.2 / §6.6 they are MINOR versions with a new `_shared` component version, and only the tasks that embed `StorageAuth`/`CredentialState` re-pin (create, update, get, list, credentials/set). `probe`, `retire`, `vtc/rooms/*` stay on `_shared/0.1` — they reference only identifiers/limits that did not change.

- A 0.1 create/update request is valid at 0.2. A 0.2 request with `roleArn` is not valid at 0.1 (closed object).
- A get/list reader switching exhaustively on `credential.status` needs updating for `notAllowed`.
- TS: as in #710, the generator's hoisting renames `SharedComponents.StorageAuth` / `StorageConfig` / `CredentialState` / `StorageConfigFacts` to `_VtcV0_1` / `_VtcV0_2` variants (per-module imports are aliased, unchanged). Titled without `!` following #710's precedent — say if you want `!`.

## Validation

- `npm run validate` — 929 specs, OK
- `npm run check-bindings` — all four languages agree
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --test conformance -- vtc::storage` — 46 passed (includes the new invalid-example fixtures)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (trust-tasks-ts), `go vet ./specs/vtc/...`, `dart analyze` on the new libraries — clean

## Open questions

1. **Room prefix** is now defined normatively here (`<prefix>rooms/<first 32 lowercase hex of SHA-256(UTF-8 roomId)>/`), taken from the design note. Is `create/0.2` the right home, or should it live in `rooms/_shared` beside blobs?
2. **Walrus sealed** is included (`suiPrivateKey`, Bech32 `suiprivkey`) rather than deferred, so `set/0.2` does not make sealed Walrus impossible. Drop it if you'd rather defer.
3. **`roleArn` absent** on ambient S3: the community assumes its host-configured role, else the ambient identity's own role (which must trust itself). An alternative is to make `roleArn` required for ambient S3.
4. **GCS lifetime**: a CAB token inherits its source token's expiry, so the spec says SHOULD mint the source at ≤ 900 s (`generateAccessToken`) and MUST stop using any token after 15 min — a stolen token may still live up to the source's expiry. Tighten to MUST if acceptable for deployments.
5. **`notAllowed`** status is an addition beyond the decision list (the natural reporting for a mode the host later disables). Easy to drop.
6. The generated Rust `SealedStorageCredential` derives `Debug` like every generated type; implementations must keep it out of logs.
