title: spec(rooms/records): a record says what kind of claim it is, what it cites, what it may be used for, and when it lapses
body:
## What

A data-room record can now say **what kind of claim it is** and **when it lapses**:

- `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json` — `SealedRecordBody` gains five OPTIONAL members, all inside the author's signature:
  - `basis` — `declared | observed | verified | inferred` (`RecordBasis`)
  - `confidence` — number 0–1, the author's own estimate (`RecordConfidence`)
  - `evidence` — 1–32 citations (`RecordEvidence`), discriminated by `kind`: `{kind: "record", key, version?, roomId?}` or `{kind: "credential", credentialId, digest?}`
  - `validFor` — permitted use (`PermittedUse`): `purposes` (absolute IRIs, e.g. W3C DPV) and/or a plain-text `note`
  - `validUntil` — date-time (`RecordValidUntil`)
  
  plus reader rules in the body's description: provenance is display/weighting only and **never authority**; `basis: verified` never substitutes for checking `evidence`; citations are never fetched; `validFor.note` is never instructions. Readers **MUST** hide a record whose `validUntil` has passed from default listings, search and recall and **MAY** show it on explicit request, marked expired. Hosts do not enforce expiry and nothing about it is in the clear on sealed tiers. The room-profile record carries none of the new members.
- `rooms/records/put/0.3` (new) — an `open` room's `cleartext` carries the same five members (unsigned on that tier, stored and served as received, never acted on by the host). The `sealed` path is unchanged.
- Rust / TypeScript / Go / Dart bindings regenerated.

## Why

VTI issue OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2117 (provenance) and the per-record expiry half of OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2118. In a room used as shared memory or an evidence locker, an agent's inference ("customer is price-sensitive") read the same as an observed fact or a credential-backed statement; and a meeting note could not lapse sooner than the room.

## Compatibility

- `SealedRecordBody` is edited **in place**, following the `roomProfile` precedent (#807): it is a draft shared component that no host task carries (client to client), so no task's wire contract changes. Records written before still verify — the signing rules are unchanged and absent members mean "not stated", never a default.
- Readers that predate the members refuse bodies carrying them by reader rule (1) — "shows nothing rather than something wrong". In particular an old reader can never show an expired record as current. The same holds for a key holder sealing for a writer (`rooms/keys/seal` 0.2 `bodyInvalid`); a writer MAY retry without the provenance members but MUST NOT drop `validUntil` to get a record accepted.
- `put/0.2`'s `cleartext` is closed, so open rooms need a new version; hosts implementing 0.3 SHOULD keep accepting 0.2 and 0.1.

## Judgment calls

- **`validFor` is IRIs + a note, not a vocabulary of our own.** Purpose vocabularies already exist (W3C DPV); a short list here would be one more to translate between and wrong at its edges for every domain using rooms. The IRI space is the extension path; `note` carries nuance an identifier cannot. Neither is enforced — no host can see it on sealed tiers and every reader already holds the content — so it is a statement of the author's terms that an agent SHOULD honour.
- **`evidence` items are tagged objects**, following `RevocationEntry`'s `kind` discriminator, with an optional version pin (records can be rewritten under one key) and an optional credential digest (a reader holding a credential with that id can tell whether it is the one meant). References, never locators.
- **`confidence` is per-author**: readers MUST NOT rank across authors as though the numbers shared a scale.
- **Open rooms get the fields** (cheap, via `put/0.3`), with a Security note that they are unsigned there; a room wanting attributable provenance uses a sealed tier.
- Expiry hides, it does not delete: a curator's agent MAY retract expired records, which is how a sealed room reclaims storage without telling its host anything about expiry. (Time-based pruning by the host is the separate retention PR.)

## Open questions

- `rooms/keys/act` 0.6's table enumerates actable versions; `put/0.3` becomes actable through the key holder only with an `act` 0.7. Suggest one follow-up `act` bump after this and the two companion PRs (record retention + prune; epoch prune reaching members) land, rather than three competing `act/0.7`s.
- Should `RecordMetadataV2`-style listings on open rooms lift `basis` / `validUntil` the way they lift `title`? Not done here — readers already have `cleartext` on get.

## Validation

`npm run validate` ✓ · `npm run check-bindings` ✓ (925 specs; Rust/TS/Go/Dart agree) · `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --test conformance -- rooms::` ✓ (309 passed, includes the new invalid examples).

Companion PRs: #868 (record retention + `rooms/records/prune`), #869 (epoch prune reaching members' key holders). All three edit `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json` in different `$defs`; whichever merges later should re-run the four generators.

  SHOULD set `basis`, agent writers that do not know SHOULD write
  `inferred`. Readers hide a record past its `validUntil` from default
  listings, search and recall and MAY show it on explicit request; no host
  enforces it and nothing about it is in the clear on sealed tiers.
  Records written before verify unchanged; readers that predate the
  members refuse bodies carrying them by rule (1), showing nothing rather
  than something wrong.
- rooms/records/put 0.3 (new): an open room's `cleartext` carries the same

title: feat(vtc/admin/events): 0.4 adds a communityRooms topic — the owner's view of the rooms the community owns
body:
## Why

The VTC console's **Community rooms** tab polls every 60 s, because no live-events topic covers it. The `rooms` topic (0.2+) is the community's view as a **host** — storage, limits, lifecycle — for holders of `vtc.rooms.admin`, and carries no room's details. The community-rooms pages are its view as an **owner** (`vtc/rooms/community/*`), gated on `vtc.rooms.manage`, a different capability: a `vtc.rooms.manage` holder without `vtc.rooms.admin` cannot be sent `rooms` hints at all, and folding the owner's view into `rooms` would send hints to `vtc.rooms.admin` holders who cannot read what they point at. The topic set is closed per version, so the new topic is a new MINOR version of the component, as 0.2 did for `rooms` and 0.3 for `directory`/`groups`.

## What changes

- **`vtc/admin/events/_shared/0.4`** — `Topic` gains `communityRooms` (10 topics).
- **`vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.4`** — copy of 0.3; `topics` `maxItems` 10 (request and response); a "What 0.4 adds" section; an Authorization row: recipients are holders of `vtc.rooms.manage`, the reads prompted are `vtc/rooms/community/list` 0.2, `vtc/rooms/community/get` 0.2 and `vtc/rooms/community/members/list` 0.1; `vtc.rooms.admin` alone does not qualify. Correlation note for member-related timing.
- **`vtc/admin/events/event/0.4`** — copy of 0.3; producer rule 8: hint whenever anything those reads would show the recipient changes — a community room created or its label/description/tags changed; an admission offered, withdrawn, accepted or renewed; a removal owed, retried, settled or failed (including one owed because a member left the community); the profile write's state (`pending`/`written`); the community's authority-renewal state (where the reads show those last two, in `ext` or otherwise). Rule 9: no room id or DID, member DID, offer, credential, Welcome, KeyPackage or other record identifier in any member, `ext` included. Not a count topic. Coalescing (≤ 1 hint/topic/s), per-hint standing re-checks and ending the stream on a shrink are the existing subscribe rules, unchanged. One new example hint.
- Invalid examples: `roomId` / `member` / `state` on a `communityRooms` hint; a per-room `roomId` filter and an `offers` pseudo-topic on subscribe.
- **`vtc/rooms/community/update` 0.1 and 0.2** — editorial, in place (both `draft`, per CONTRIBUTING-SPECS "Version rules"): the "Live updates" section said a hint for the owner's view "would belong to a topic … in a later version"; it now points at `communityRooms` in events 0.4 (0.2 also mentions the profile write's `pending` → `written` change).
- Regenerated Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings (only the new 0.4 modules + indexes changed).

## Compatibility

Additive. 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 of subscribe/event/_shared are unchanged; a console asks for `communityRooms` only at 0.4, and a community serving several versions answers each subscription at its own version.

## Validation

- `npm run validate` — 926 specs validated, no errors.
- `npm run check-bindings` — all four languages agree.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features vtc --test conformance admin::events` — 21 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

title: fix(vta-support): the versionTime wait budgets whole-millisecond sleeps
body:
wait_until_not_future charged each sleep as the exact time remaining, but
Tokio's timer sleeps in whole milliseconds. Once the clock sat microseconds
short of the target, every pass slept 1ms and was charged microseconds, so the
total sleep could run past MAX_WAIT_SECONDS. Under paused time this showed up
as waits_for_rapid_back_to_back_calls failing intermittently with
elapsed=5.252s against the 5s budget.

Each sleep is now rounded up to a whole millisecond and counted as such, so
the budget matches what is slept. A new test drives a clock that creeps by a
microsecond per pass and fails on the old accounting.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc): move a room's files to another storage config (rooms/storage/migrate)
body:
Serves `vtc/rooms/storage/migrate/0.1` — phase **P10** of `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md` (§7.3): a holder of `vtc.rooms.admin` moves a hosted room's existing files onto the storage config it is assigned to. Each blob is copied, read back from the target and checked against every chunk digest and the whole-blob digest of its committed manifest, then switched; the old copy is deleted by the collection pass after the orphan grace window. No key is involved, and readers notice nothing (a blob is named by its digest; every read re-reads its entry).

## Design

**Engine — `vti-rooms/src/blobs/migrate.rs`** (shared host code; `room-host` has one config and does not serve the task):

- Rows in `room_blobs` (backed up): `migration:<room>` (the record: target, sources, totals/progress, state, requester, approvers, reason, attempts/backoff, the blob in flight and its copy), `mplan:<room>:<ref>` (one per blob still to move), `moved:<room>:<ref>:<migration>` (an old copy awaiting deletion).
- **The switch is one `Batch`** — entry, `moved:` row, counters, plan row, record — applied only while the entry is byte-for-byte what it was when the copy began (`require_unchanged`). A blob orphaned, collected or rewritten meanwhile is skipped (out of the totals, its reservation and copy given back). Orphaned blobs are never planned (left to collection).
- **Capacity (§6.1)**: bytes to move are reserved on the target config and the host-wide counter at start, so `capacityExceeded` is answered before anything is copied; each switch converts its blob's reservation; the old copy keeps counting against its config — and in `ConfigHoldings`, so a `draining` config does not retire — until collection actually deletes it.
- Before writing a copy, a pending `moved:` row of the same blob on the target (moved away and back within the grace) is reclaimed under the lock, so collection cannot delete what the switch is about to name.
- **Resumable**: the blob in flight and its copy are recorded; a restart re-verifies a recorded copy (made again if missing). Tests stop a step after *choosing*, *copying* and *verifying* (standing in for the process dying) and check the blob stays readable from its original config and the end state is exact.

**Service — `vtc-service`**:

- `storage_tasks::handle_migrate`: `permissionDenied` → `roomNotFound` → (a `running`/`paused` migration is the answer, a paused one resumed, **not parked again**) → `configNotActive` (assigned config not active or without a usable credential) → `capacityExceeded` (with `details`) → nothing to move completes at once, parks nothing (item 7) → otherwise parked as `Act::ChangeStorage`, kind `rooms.storage.migrate` (template pinned in the server and the console; single-administrator mode waives it as for `assign`), every check re-run on execution.
- `rooms::migration`: the runner — **the one retry owner**. One migration at a time per host, oldest first (the others are reported `running`). Capped exponential backoff with full jitter on a failed copy, `paused` after 8 in a row. A copy that does not verify is `failed`, never retried. Rate = request's `maxBytesPerSecond` bounded by the new optional `[rooms.files] migration_max_bytes_per_second` (default 8 MiB/s, floor 64 KiB/s).
- Audit: `RoomStorageChanged` rows `migrationStarted` / `migrationResumed` / `migrationCompleted` / `migrationPaused` / `migrationFailed`, with requester, approvers, room, configs and reason (item 8). Store errors kept or audited are scrubbed of URL queries and long tokens (a presigned URL's signature).
- `vtc/rooms/get` reports `storage.migration`. The `rooms` live-channel fingerprint includes each migration's **state** (not its per-blob progress); the console polls a running one every 3 s.
- Backup import pauses running migrations (audited); the blob in flight is re-verified on resume.
- Wiring: discovery/dispatch, `vta_sdk::openapi` wrappers → `openapi.json` → `wire.ts`, conformance sample, declared-error-code census witnesses, console task manifest.

**Console**: the room page shows a migration's progress, offers **Move existing files to `<config>`** while files remain on earlier storage (reason, optional MiB/s; warns before moving onto Walrus), and **Resume** when paused.

## Maintainer decisions applied
1. A room reassigned mid-migration keeps the migration's original `toConfig`.
2. Runner is the single retry owner; re-issuing resumes a paused migration without consent; a start while running/paused returns that migration.
3. Orphaned blobs are skipped.
4. One migration at a time per host.
5. Migration rows are in the backed-up `room_blobs`; a restored `running` migration comes back `paused` and re-verifies.

## Spec notes / ambiguities
- **`retry_safety`**: `vta_sdk::retry_safety` classifies only tasks the **VTA** serves (its census is over `vta_sdk::trust_tasks::ALL_URIS`); this task is VTC-only, like `storage/assign`, so it has no entry there.
- **Resuming a paused migration and `configNotActive`**: item 1 checks the room's *assigned* config; a paused migration keeps its own target (decision 1), so resume checks the migration's target instead.
- **`vtc/rooms/get` `storage.migration`** says "while one is running"; this reports the room's last migration in any state, so the console can show one finishing or failing.
- **Event 0.2 rule 4** does not name migrations; the `rooms` fingerprint now also moves on a migration's state change (still a hint naming nothing). Worth adding to the rule upstream.
- **Unusable target credential** has no declared code; answered `configNotActive` ("cannot receive the blobs").

## Tests
- `vti-rooms` unit tests (12): full move + verify + collection after grace with counters; nothing to move; capacity refusal; second request / resume / reassigned target kept; corrupt source → `failed`, blob stays; dying after each step; resumed copy re-verified (missing → copied again); blob changed under the copy → skipped; unreachable target → backoff → `paused`; moved back within the grace keeps the live object; error scrubbing; jitter bounds.
- `vtc-service` integration: through the action list (parked, approved, re-request returns the same migration, runner completes it, `rooms/get` reports it, audit rows with approvers); nothing-to-move completes without consent; `roomNotFound` / `configNotActive` / `capacityExceeded` (census witnesses).
- Console: move parks with reason + rate; paused progress + Resume.

title: feat(vtc): move a room's files to another storage config (rooms/storage/migrate) (#2261)
body:
feat(vtc): move a room's files to another storage config (rooms/storage/migrate) (#2261)

Serves vtc/rooms/storage/migrate/0.1 (data-rooms-files.md §7.3, phase P10):
a holder of vtc.rooms.admin moves a hosted room's existing blobs onto the
storage config it is assigned to. Each blob is copied, read back from the
target and checked against every chunk digest and the whole-blob digest of its
committed manifest, and only then switched; the old copy is deleted by the
collection pass after the orphan grace window. No key is involved and readers
notice nothing.

The engine is vti_rooms::blobs::migrate, shared host code over the blob index:

- the switch is one atomic store batch (entry, the old copy's `moved:` row,
  counters, plan row, migration record), applied only while the blob's entry
  is byte-for-byte what it was when the copy began; a blob orphaned,
  collected or rewritten meanwhile is skipped and its copy discarded;
- the bytes to move are reserved on the target (and the host's storage) at
  start, so capacityExceeded is answered before anything is copied; each
  switch converts its reservation, and the old copy keeps counting against
  its config until it is actually deleted (§6.1), so a draining config does
  not retire early (ConfigHoldings counts pending old copies);
- a pending old copy of the same blob on the target is reclaimed under the
  lock before the copy is written, so collection never deletes what a switch
  is about to name;
- progress is persisted (record, plan rows, blob in flight and its copy), so
  a restart resumes; tests stop a step after choosing, copying and verifying
  and check the blob stays readable and the end state is exact.

vtc-service runs one migration at a time (rooms::migration), the one retry
owner: capped exponential backoff with full jitter on a failed copy, then
`paused` after eight in a row. Re-issuing the task resumes a paused migration
without parking again, and a running or paused one is always the answer
(item 5). A copy that does not verify is `failed` (item 3). A new migration is
parked as Act::ChangeStorage (kind rooms.storage.migrate, template pinned in
the server and the console); single-administrator mode waives it as for
assign. A room with nothing to move completes at once and parks nothing
(item 7). Each start, resume, completion, pause and failure is a
RoomStorageChanged audit row with the requester, approvers, room, configs and
reason (item 8). A store error kept or audited is scrubbed of URL queries and
long tokens.

vtc/rooms/get reports storage.migration; the rooms live-channel fingerprint
includes each migration's state, and the console polls a running one. A
restored backup brings a running migration back paused; the blob in flight is
verified again on resume. New optional config: [rooms.files]
migration_max_bytes_per_second (default 8 MiB/s), which a request's
maxBytesPerSecond can only lower.

Console: the room page shows a migration's progress, offers "Move existing
files" when files remain on earlier storage (warning before moving onto
Walrus), and "Resume" when paused.

title: feat(rooms)!: pnm rooms prune sends rooms/epoch/prune, and both hosts audit it as a prune
body:
## What

`rooms/epoch/prune/0.1` was served by `room-host` and the VTC but nothing sent it. This adds the client path and fixes two host conformance bugs.

### Client: `pnm rooms prune --room <id> --host <url> [--host-did <did>] --before-epoch <n> --reason <text> [--yes]`
- Goes the same way as `pnm rooms renew`: the VTA presents `admin` for the CLI (`rooms/keys/present/0.2`), and the CLI signs and sends the document (`VtcClient::prune_epoch`, new). The payload is checked against the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::rooms::epoch::prune::v0_1::Payload`. The CLI never retries it.
- **Why not `rooms/keys/act`:** every act version (0.1–0.6) leaves `rooms/epoch/prune` out on purpose ("warrants a task of its own that states its consequences"). Adding it would diverge from the spec. Because the CLI signs, the host records the CLI's DID, not the persona's.
- The spec's *Consent/purpose* section asks for a warning. The command reads the room first (`rooms/info`: epoch and retention policy) and prints what becomes unreadable. It says that records stay and that members' VTAs keep the keys they already derived. It then asks `[y/N]` at a terminal. Without a terminal and without `--yes` it refuses and prints the command to run.
- If the floor is at or above the current epoch (`notAhead`), the command refuses before sending anything and prints the highest floor that works. If the host answers `permissionDenied`, it says the prune needs `admin` and names `issue-authority --action admin`. `pruned: 0` is reported as a success, and the reach shown is `earliestRung`.
- `--reason` is required in the CLI (it is optional in the spec) because it is the only record of intent a prune leaves.

### Hosts
- **Audit bug:** both `room-host` and `vtc-service` audited a prune as `RoomOperation::MintEpoch` (`room.epoch.mint`). There is now `RoomOperation::PruneEpoch` (`room.epoch.prune`, admin).
- **`notAhead`:** both hosts answered a floor at the current epoch with a generic validation error. They now answer the declared `rooms/epoch/prune:notAhead` with `details.epoch`, as the spec requires (`vti_rooms::blob_tasks::prune_floor_refused`).

### Breaking
`vti_rooms::audit::RoomOperation` (published, previously exhaustive) gains `PruneEpoch` and is now `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the next addition will not break anything.

### Docs
`docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md`: the §2 status row (it said "primitive only, no verb reaches it"), the §9 CLI list, the `act` paragraph, a new §10.4 *Pruning the epoch key chain*, and §11 refusal rows. `tasks/data-rooms-todo.md` X4.4 is marked done. The docs say plainly that today's prune erases the **host's** rungs only and members' VTAs keep their copies. A spec change to reach members is being drafted separately.

`vta_sdk::retry_safety` is unchanged: it classifies tasks the VTA serves. Prune is served by hosts, and the VTA task used here (`rooms/keys/present/0.2`) is already classified.

## Tests
- vti-rooms: `a_prune_is_admin_and_named_as_a_prune`, and the distinct-names census includes `PruneEpoch`.
- room-host: `a_prune_needs_admin_and_is_audited_as_a_prune` checks that a read chain gets 403 and no audit entry, that `notAhead` comes with `details.epoch`, and that a successful prune logs `room.epoch.prune` and no mint (log capture).
- vtc-service: the same test, reading the audit keyspace.
- vtc-client: the payload is the generated wire type, and the client does not retry it.
- vta-cli-common: the confirmation guard, the warning text, the `notAhead` and `permissionDenied` hints, and the outcome wording.
- pnm-cli: the printed hint command parses, and `--reason` and `--before-epoch` are required.

Local runs:
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 6542 passed. One test timed out at 300s under load: `vta-service audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry`. This PR doesn't touch vta-service, and the test passes alone in 293s.
- Doctests: ok.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3510 passed.

title: feat(vta): star a directory member whose DID you have not been shown — persona/contact/put/1.1 linking form
body:
The VTA side of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#858. A community's directory shows members' DIDs to other members only where each member chooses to, so most entries carry no DID to file a contact under — this lets the member's wallet star, name and list them anyway.

- **put/1.1 linking form** (`directoryRef` + `knownByPersona`, no `subjectDid` / document): `PersonaStore::link_contact` finds the contact this context keeps for that entry and persona, or makes one (rev 1, empty document, no DID), applies the annotations, appends no revision. A filing naming a DID is a contact of its own, never merged with a linked one (item 4).
- get/list 1.1 omit `subjectDid` for a linked contact; get/list **1.0**, which cannot omit it, do not show one.

The dependency moves this needed (trust-tasks 0.33, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.38, affinidi-tdk, mediator 0.44) are already on main, so the PR is the feature commit alone.

Unblocks vta-browser-plugin#370 (wallet marks) for entries whose DID isn't shown.

title: chore(deps)!: trust-tasks-rs 0.33, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.38, affinidi-tdk 0.29, mediator 0.44; an mdoc presentation binds the OpenID4VP 1.0 handover
body:
The release train behind trust-tasks-rs 0.33 (affinidi-tdk-rs #963, affinidi-messaging-mediator
#25). These versions move together because the messaging SDK's public API carries
`trust_tasks_rs` types, so the workspace takes them in one step:
- trust-tasks-rs 0.33.1, which carries the voting hardening specifications of trust-tasks-tf
  #860;
- the trust-tasks-* transport crates at 0.33;
- affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.38;
- affinidi-tdk 0.29;
- affinidi-messaging-mediator-{admin,tui} and affinidi-messaging-test-mediator 0.44.

affinidi-tdk 0.29 re-exports affinidi-mdoc 0.4 (affinidi-tdk-rs #961), which implements
OpenID4VP 1.0 Final's mdoc handover (Appendix B.2.6.1): `[client_id, nonce, jwk_thumbprint,
response_uri]`. That replaces ISO 18013-7's `mdocGeneratedNonce`. A DeviceAuth signed over the
old handover verifies at no 1.0 verifier, so the holder's `Oid4vpSession` changes shape:

- **Breaking (vta-sdk):** `mdoc_generated_nonce` is removed. In its place is an optional
  `jwk_thumbprint`, the base64url SHA-256 thumbprint (RFC 7638) of the key the verifier
  encrypts its `direct_post.jwt` response to. It is absent for an unencrypted response, which
  the handover encodes as CBOR `null`. The field has no specification of its own and nothing in
  the workspace sent it.
- A new test checks that the DeviceAuth verifies against exactly that transcript, and against
  none without the thumbprint or with another nonce.

The test mediator 0.44 still asks for affinidi-tdk 0.28, so dev builds hold that copy beside
0.29. Both share one messaging SDK and one trust-tasks-rs, and nothing passes a type between
them.



## Tests

Run locally:
- fmt and clippy (`--all-targets -D warnings`): clean.
- vtc-service + vtc-client nextest: 3508 passed.
- Doctests: pass.
- Workspace nextest: 6531 passed; 2 hit the 5-minute limit while the full suite was running. Those two (`vta-backup` keyspace round trip, `vta-service` audit coverage) pass on their own in 51 s and 72 s.

* fix(vtc): a rotation carries a member's election tickets to the new DID — one ticket per party, whatever key it signs with (VTI-VOT-022)

Tickets were keyed on the signer's DID, and neither acl/swap-key nor the member's own rotation
moved them: a member could take a ticket, rotate, and take a second under the new DID with a
fresh voter key — a second counted ballot, with tickets_issued rising so certification's
countExceedsTickets could not notice. Both rotations now copy every ticket the old DID holds to
the new one before they commit, under the issuance lock held until the rotation is done.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(voting)!: trustees and voters act only on signed steps, the community authorizes decryption, the key needs t dealers, ballots bind their tag (VTI-VOT-060 – 071)

An adversarial review of community voting found that a dishonest ballot box could take the
trustees' place, that one trustee could end up holding the election key alone, and that a voter
could copy someone else's encrypted ballot. The threat model, the attacks and what is still open
are in docs/05-design-notes/community-voting-threat-model.md. Specifications:
trust-tasks-tf #860.

Trustee VTAs (vta/pcs/trustee/{deal,keys,justify,decrypt}/0.2; 0.1 retired):
- Every step is taken from `ceremony`, the trustees' signed requests, each proof checked against
  its trustee's DID. Nothing is taken from what voting/trustees/status summarises.
- deal pins the transport keys it dealt to (`ceremonyChanged`).
- justify answers only a complaint in the complainant's own signed confirm (`noComplaint`).
- keys never replaces a share it holds (`keyMismatch`).
- decrypt decrypts only targets the community authorized, and once per election
  (`authorizationInvalid`, `alreadyDecrypted`).

Voter VTAs (vta/pcs/vote-encrypted/0.2):
- The VTA forms the election key itself from the signed steps that vtc/elections/show now
  carries as `ceremony`.
- An encrypted ballot's proofs, and a sealed ballot's AAD, bind the cast's tag
  (`Voter::tag_for`).

Ballot box (vti-voting, vti-voting-service):
- The key forms only from at least t qualified dealers and t confirmations.
- New task voting/trustees/authorize: a `decryptionAuthorized` board entry, required before
  any partial decryption.
- A copied ciphertext is refused, and a replacement ballot must differ.
- Payloads are schema-validated.
- A signed request must name its `recipient`. A consequential request needs `issuedAt`.
  Casts must be signed by a `did:key`.
- After a crash, a torn receipt record is truncated, and a decryption cut short is finished.
- Audit checks the board's order (CONVENTIONS §3.9, `orderInvalid` / `ceremonyInvalid`).

VTC:
- After close, the sweeper computes the decryption targets from the board it verified and signs
  them.
- Pre-credentials are discarded on tally or cancel.
- Untrusted ballot boxes are refused on every exchange.
- The final checkpoint is kept.
- Tickets are issued as the community, never with a console key.

pnm elections trustee sends the ceremony and waits for the community's authorization before
it decrypts.

title: Admit did:scid:vh:1 as a durable identity, used natively (VTI-KEY-160 to VTI-KEY-166, VTI-VTA-034 to VTI-VTA-036, VTI-VTC-004)
body:
Adds `did:scid:vh:1` as a durable identity alongside `did:webvh`, which stays the default.

**Identity and resolution (spec/04-identity-keys.md, new section after Identifier methods)**
- VTI-KEY-001 admits a `did:scid:vh:1` identifier whose source is a `did:webvh` log.
- VTI-KEY-160: the identity is the bare DID `did:scid:vh:1:<scid>`; `?src=` is a locator, so the log can move without the identity changing. One mapping to and from the `did:webvh` form.
- VTI-KEY-161: resolution returns the identity's own document (`id` is the bare DID, self-references under it, `alsoKnownAs` lists the `did:webvh` DID and the `src` DID URL), because DID Core requires the id to be the DID resolved.
- VTI-KEY-162: nodes remember the last verified source per SCID and refuse a log older than one already verified (a stale mirror can replay, not forge).
- VTI-KEY-163: presenters give `src` where the recipient may not hold a source; references (e.g. a DIDComm `skid`) may carry `src` and are dereferenced by DID and fragment; where a format binds a key to an issuer by exact string (Trust Tasks), both are written in the same form.
- VTI-KEY-164: a `did:scid` and its `did:webvh` are distinct identities, linked as one subject only where the `did:webvh` document lists the alias.
- VTI-KEY-165/166: logs are still `did:webvh`; the form presented defaults to `did:webvh`; new logs list the `did:scid` alias in `alsoKnownAs` by default.

**Configuration**
- VTI-VTA-034..036: VTA config for the presented form and the alias; precedence request → VTC → VTA → defaults.
- VTI-VTC-004: a VTC may state its preference; it accepts members presenting either form and records the identity presented.

**Trigger links (07a)**: a `did:scid:vh:1` contact must carry `src`, which makes it host-named (route A, host rules apply to the `src` host, displayed as its source). The three test vectors that sent it through route B are replaced.

Also adds [DID-SCID] to references, updates decision D7 in STRUCTURE.md, and fixes an appendix example with no SCID segment.

The wire change for VTA creation is trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf `vta/webvh/dids/create/1.2` (PR to follow).

title: Admit did:scid:vh:1 as a durable identity, used natively (VTI-KEY-160 to VTI-KEY-166, VTI-VTA-034 to VTI-VTA-036, VTI-VTC-004) (#75)
body:
Admit did:scid:vh:1 as a durable identity, used natively (VTI-KEY-160 to VTI-KEY-166, VTI-VTA-034 to VTI-VTA-036, VTI-VTC-004) (#75)

A did:scid:vh:1 identity is verified by a did:webvh log but is not bound to
the host serving it. VTI-KEY-001 admits it. The identity is the DID
did:scid:vh:1:<scid>; `src` is a locator, so the log can move without the
identity changing (VTI-KEY-160). Resolution returns the identity's own
document, with the did:scid DID as `id` and every self-reference under it
(VTI-KEY-161), because DID Core requires the id to be the DID resolved and a
verifier must find the keys under it.

Sources are untrusted but cannot forge: the SCID commits to the log. A node
remembers the last source per SCID and refuses a log older than one it has
verified, which a stale mirror could otherwise replay (VTI-KEY-162). A
presenter gives `src` wherever the recipient may not hold one; key references
stay under the DID (VTI-KEY-163). The two forms are distinct identities, linked
as one subject only where the did:webvh document lists the did:scid alias
(VTI-KEY-164).

title: fix(room-host): a document whose issuer is not the mediator sender is refused identityMismatch
body:
Over DIDComm and TSP, room-host compared nothing between a document's in-band
`issuer`/`recipient` and the parties the carrier authenticated, and answered
whoever delivered the frame. The DIDComm (0.2 §3) and TSP (0.1 §3) bindings
require them to agree (framework SPEC §7.2 item 6); a document signed by one
party and delivered by another is `identityMismatch`. The VTC already refuses
it.

The check runs before dispatch, using the bindings' own handlers
(`DidcommHandler`, `TspHandler`): DIDComm on the bare DID, TSP on the exact
VID, absent in-band members taking the carrier's values. The refusal goes to
the authenticated sender and echoes no document id (SPEC §8.1).

Nothing of ours relied on the old behaviour: the VTA sends persona-signed
documents over HTTPS only, and the wallet reaches hosts over HTTPS.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: ci: budget the cold-cache tail (30 -> 45 min) and prune superseded build caches so it stays the tail
body:
## Problem

`Test (workspace)` and the `Feature combos` groups were being **cancelled** at their 30-minute `timeout-minutes`, about a third of PR runs on 2026-10-21. That included #2251 and #2252, which each needed a rerun. An overrun reports as `cancelled`, so it reads like a human cancelled it.

Job timings from the last ~40 CI runs:

| Job | warm cache | cold cache |
|---|---|---|
| Test (workspace) | 11–16 min | 25–31 min |
| Feature combos (vta-service tests) | ~11 min | 21–30 min |
| Feature combos (mediator-backed) | ~10 min | 22–30 min |

Every slow run logs `No cache found.` for its exact key (e.g. `v0-rust-test-Linux-x64-1fbdb7d5-94d5cf1e`), even with the prefix fallback. Every fast one logs `Cache hit`.

## Cause: eviction, not a missing key

- main's caches total **~21 GB** of the repository's **25 GB** allowance (`actions/cache/storage-limit`).
- Keys end in the `Cargo.lock` hash, which changed **13 times in 3 days** on main.
- Each change saves a second ~21 GB generation next to the first, and GitHub evicts least-recently-used caches to fit, sometimes ones main had just saved. The test cache that served the fast runs was created at 21:42, after the slow run at 21:11 found none.
- A superseded generation is dead weight: the restore takes the exact key or the newest with the job's prefix, so the old one is never chosen again. It still occupies the allowance until its 7-day expiry.

## Change

- **`scripts/prune-superseded-caches.py`**: deletes main's caches that a newer generation of the same job supersedes. It groups by the job part of the key, ignoring the env and lock hashes, and keeps the newest of each group. It only touches the two key shapes this repo writes (`v0-rust-*` via `.github/actions/rust-cache`, `*-cargo-mobile-*`). It never touches a PR's cache or an unknown key. `--self-test` covers the grouping, including hyphenated job names (`test` vs `test-vtc`) and toolchain changes. A dry run against the live repo lists 16 main caches and 0 superseded (eviction has already cleaned up the last generation).
- **`.github/workflows/cache-prune.yml`**: runs the script on `workflow_run` of CI completed for a push to main, so the new generation has been saved by each job's post step. It also runs on `workflow_dispatch`. Its only write permission is `actions: write`.
- **The pruner's self-test** runs in the guard job beside `semver-build-failure.py --self-test`, because a wrong grouping would delete current caches.
- **Timeouts:** `Test (workspace)` and all six `Feature combos` groups go from 30 to 45 minutes. A cold cache should now be rare, but it's still the tail ("Budget the tail, not the mean"), and 45 is about 1.5× the cold time. The comment that justified 30 as "~3x the warm time" is updated to the measured cold figure.

Not changed: the mediator-backed group's cache (7.55 GB, the largest). Dropping it (`compiled: "false"`) would free space but make that job cold on every run (~25 min instead of ~10). With one generation held, the allowance has room for it.

## Checks

- `python3 scripts/prune-superseded-caches.py --self-test` passes.
- `bash scripts/check-workflow-action-pins.sh` passes; the new workflow's checkout is pinned to the same SHA as `ci.yml`.
- `actionlint` reports nothing for `cache-prune.yml`. The only findings are pre-existing SC2086 info hints in untouched `ci.yml` lines.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): n/a; the job itself has `timeout-minutes: 10`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): each delete is independent, and a failed or interrupted run leaves the rest for the next one
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries; the next main CI run is the retry
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): a failed delete (already expired or evicted) is reported and skipped, not fatal
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): deletes run only after CI completes, when the replacing generation is saved, and never touch a group's newest
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): n/a
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): an unknown key shape is never deleted
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): it prints each delete and counts failures
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): see R2.1 above
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(vta): offline did-mgmt commands sign what they send a DID-hosting server
body:
## Problem

An operator automating trust-registry provisioning on the VTA side reported:

```
vta did-mgmt dids create --context trust-registry-280 --server dids \
  --path myvtc-fs-trust-registry --mediator-service --pre-rotation 1
Error: internal error: could not sign the DID-management task with this VTA's operational key
```

That command could never succeed offline. Every document sent to a DID-hosting server carries this VTA's proof (`WebvhHostClient::call` → `DIDCommBridge::sign_outbound_request`). The signer is installed on the bridge only in `build_app_state`, that is, when the daemon starts. `webvh_cli` handed every operation a bare `DIDCommBridge::placeholder()`, so `create`, `edit` (publish), `register` and the non-local `delete` all hit the "no signing key installed" branch, whatever the VTA's configuration.

## Fix

- `DIDCommBridge::signing_only(vta_did, keyspaces…)` is a placeholder that signs as this VTA. It uses the key the daemon signs with (`{vta_did}#key-0`, with the verification method named by `vta_signing_vm`), read from the same store.
- `operations::credentials::load_vta_issuer_secret_from_store` is `load_vta_issuer_secret` over the keyspaces themselves, for callers with no `AppState`. The existing function delegates to it.
- The four offline call sites in `webvh_cli` build their bridge through `offline_signing_bridge`. With no mediator session, `Outbound` can initiate only REST, so the request goes to the host's HTTPS endpoint (`TrustTaskHTTPS`, or the base derived from `WebVHHosting`), where the proof is the whole of the authentication.
- A signing key that will not load produces a warning and the bare placeholder, so `delete --local-only`, which signs nothing, still works as a break-glass. With no `vta_did`, the bridge stays bare, and `create_path_host_client` still refuses by name.

## Tests

- `didcomm_bridge::tests::signing_only_signs_as_the_vta` signs a request through the offline bridge and verifies the proof against the VTA's DID with `verify_trust_task_proof_with`.
- `didcomm_bridge::tests::signing_only_without_a_vta_did_does_not_sign` checks that with no `vta_did` the bridge refuses and attaches no proof.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Not covered: an end-to-end offline run against a live did-hosting daemon.

Part of making the trust registry provisionable from a headless VTA flow. The companion changes are the `trust-registry` DID template (separate PR) and `trust-registry setup` in affinidi-trust-registry-rs.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients; it reuses `Outbound`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): unchanged; the operation layer's ordering is the online path's
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire change
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): no `vta_did` or no loadable key means nothing is signed
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): a key that fails to load is reported, not swallowed
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no new mutation
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.33.1
body:
### Fixed

- **voting**: Trustees and voters act only on signed evidence; the community authorizes decryption; the key needs t dealers; ballots bind their tag ([#860](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/860))

* fix(voting): trustees and voters act only on signed evidence; the community authorizes what is decrypted; the key needs t dealers; ballots bind their tag; the board is in order

  An adversarial review of community voting found that a dishonest ballot box could take the
  trustees' place, and a single corrupt trustee could hold the election key.

  - **The box could feed the trustees' VTAs.** They acted on values voting/trustees/status reported,
    which carry no trustee's proof. The box could:
    - substitute transport keys, and open the shares sealed to them;
    - invent complaints, and collect the shares revealed in answer;
    - replace dealings, and overwrite a key share;
    - list one voter's ciphertexts as a "total", or a cast before the close, and collect honest
      trustees' partials of it.
  - **One trustee could hold the key.** The key formed from a single qualified dealer, so a corrupt
    trustee complaining of every other dealer at the last moment was left holding it alone.
  - **The voter's VTA took any key.** It encrypted under whatever key it was handed, so a community
    could give one member a key it held.
  - **Ballots could be copied.** Nothing bound a ballot to its cast: a voter could re-cast another's
    encrypted ballot verbatim under their own tag (Cortier–Smyth).
  - **Certification ignored the lifecycle.** It accepted casts after close, a result before it, and
    an early close a manifest forbade.

  The changes:

  - **vta/pcs/trustee/{deal,keys,justify,decrypt}/0.2 and vta/pcs/vote-encrypted/0.2** (the 0.1
    versions retire) take the ceremony as its signed steps, which status now carries as `steps`. The
    VTA verifies each step itself (CONVENTIONS §9.6). In particular:
    - deal pins the transport keys it dealt to;
    - justify needs the complainant's own confirm;
    - keys never replaces a held share;
    - the voter's VTA forms the key itself;
    - vtc/elections/show carries `ceremony` for it.
  - **voting/trustees/authorize/0.1 (new).** After close the community computes the decryption
    targets from the board it checked, and signs their digest under the closing head. The box
    accepts it only if its own targets match, and appends a `decryptionAuthorized` entry. A
    trustee's VTA decrypts only an authorized set, once (decrypt/0.2). The box refuses partials
    before an authorization.
  - **CONVENTIONS §9.6 item 5:** the key forms only from at least t qualified dealers, with at least
    t confirmations.
  - **§9.3/§9.4:** an encrypted form's proofs, and a sealed form's AAD, bind the cast's tag. The box
    refuses a form whose ciphertexts are already on the board under another tag.
  - **§3.9 (new):** the board's order — opened, casts, close, authorization, partials, one result
    whose head is the board before it — enforced at certification (`orderInvalid`,
    `ceremonyInvalid` appended to boardInconsistent's faults).

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.33.0` → `0.33.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.33.0` → `0.33.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.33.0` → `0.33.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.33.0` → `0.33.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.33.0` → `0.33.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.33.0` → `0.33.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.33.0` → `0.33.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.33.0` → `0.33.1` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.27.0` → `0.27.1` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.9.1`) | `0.9.0` → `0.9.1` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.9.0` → `0.9.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat: a did:scid VTA binds the gateway to its src host, and a bare one fails closed
body:
feat: a did:scid VTA binds the gateway to its src host, and a bare one fails closed

A did:scid:vh:1 VTA is resolved through the host its ?src= names, so the
push gateway's host binding uses that host, and the pairing review shows
it as the VTA's domain. A did:scid given without ?src= names no host to
bind to; it is warned about (hostNotBoundToVta) instead of passing
silently as a method with no web domain does. Re-pairing a did:scid VTA
given with and without its src is not replacing a different VTA
(DidIdentity, VTI-KEY-160); a did:scid and the did:webvh of its log stay
distinct (VTI-KEY-164).

Display names come from the engine's shortenDid, which learns did:scid
when the engine is rebuilt against a TDK and vta-sdk that have it.

title: fix(voting): trustees and voters act only on signed evidence; the community authorizes decryption; the key needs t dealers; ballots bind their tag (#860)
body:
fix(voting): trustees and voters act only on signed evidence; the community authorizes decryption; the key needs t dealers; ballots bind their tag (#860)

* fix(voting): trustees and voters act only on signed evidence; the community authorizes what is decrypted; the key needs t dealers; ballots bind their tag; the board is in order

An adversarial review of community voting found that a dishonest ballot box could take the
trustees' place, and a single corrupt trustee could hold the election key.

- **The box could feed the trustees' VTAs.** They acted on values voting/trustees/status reported,
  which carry no trustee's proof. The box could:
  - substitute transport keys, and open the shares sealed to them;
  - invent complaints, and collect the shares revealed in answer;
  - replace dealings, and overwrite a key share;
  - list one voter's ciphertexts as a "total", or a cast before the close, and collect honest
    trustees' partials of it.
- **One trustee could hold the key.** The key formed from a single qualified dealer, so a corrupt
  trustee complaining of every other dealer at the last moment was left holding it alone.
- **The voter's VTA took any key.** It encrypted under whatever key it was handed, so a community
  could give one member a key it held.
- **Ballots could be copied.** Nothing bound a ballot to its cast: a voter could re-cast another's
  encrypted ballot verbatim under their own tag (Cortier–Smyth).
- **Certification ignored the lifecycle.** It accepted casts after close, a result before it, and
  an early close a manifest forbade.

The changes:

- **vta/pcs/trustee/{deal,keys,justify,decrypt}/0.2 and vta/pcs/vote-encrypted/0.2** (the 0.1
  versions retire) take the ceremony as its signed steps, which status now carries as `steps`. The
  VTA verifies each step itself (CONVENTIONS §9.6). In particular:
  - deal pins the transport keys it dealt to;
  - justify needs the complainant's own confirm;
  - keys never replaces a held share;
  - the voter's VTA forms the key itself;
  - vtc/elections/show carries `ceremony` for it.
- **voting/trustees/authorize/0.1 (new).** After close the community computes the decryption
  targets from the board it checked, and signs their digest under the closing head. The box
  accepts it only if its own targets match, and appends a `decryptionAuthorized` entry. A
  trustee's VTA decrypts only an authorized set, once (decrypt/0.2). The box refuses partials
  before an authorization.
- **CONVENTIONS §9.6 item 5:** the key forms only from at least t qualified dealers, with at least
  t confirmations.
- **§9.3/§9.4:** an encrypted form's proofs, and a sealed form's AAD, bind the cast's tag. The box
  refuses a form whose ciphertexts are already on the board under another tag.
- **§3.9 (new):** the board's order — opened, casts, close, authorization, partials, one result
  whose head is the board before it — enforced at certification (`orderInvalid`,
  `ceremonyInvalid` appended to boardInconsistent's faults).

Additive: cargo semver-checks against 0.33.0 reports no semver update required.

The trustee's VTA checks a complaint's steps against the manifest's trustees and threshold, so

publicly because it is board evidence.

title: refactor(rooms)!: rooms/create's payload is the generated type, not a hand-written copy
body:
## Why

`vti_rooms::wire::CreateRoomBody` was a hand-written copy of the `rooms/create/0.1` payload. It drifted from the spec: it refused `retentionPolicy` until #2247 patched it by hand. The workspace rule is to use the type `trust-tasks-rs` generates, and the census already listed this copy as migration debt.

## What changes

- `CreateRoomBody` is now a re-export of `trust_tasks_rs::specs::rooms::create::v0_1::Payload`. The next spec change reaches both hosts through a `trust-tasks-rs` bump, with no matching edit here.
- **`CreateRoomTerms::from_request`** reads what a host keeps, in vti-rooms' own types:
  - Visibility, retention policy and anchor cadence are mapped across by their shared wire values. A value the host doesn't know is refused, never defaulted.
  - Unstated terms default to `chained` and `manual`.
  - `retentionDays` (`NonZeroU64` on the wire) is refused, not truncated, past what a host's `u32` holds.

  room-host and the VTC both read their terms through it, and refuse unreadable terms as `malformedRequest`.
- **Census:** `PREDATES_GENERATED` shrinks by one (68 → 67). The conformance test for the old copy is removed, since there's no copy left to hold to the schema.

## Testing

- New unit tests: default terms; stated terms kept (`fromJoin`, `renewal`, 30 days, an `ext` member); an oversized `retentionDays` refused; a member the spec doesn't declare refused.
- #2247's `a_room_registered_from_join_is_stored_so` passes on the generated type.
- room-host 283, vti-rooms 156, vtc-service rooms 172, census 3/3; workspace clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean.

`!` because `CreateRoomBody`'s shape changes for any external user of vti-rooms (it's now `#[non_exhaustive]`, with the spec's enums and `NonZeroU64` days).

title: feat(vta-sdk): the trust-registry built-in DID template, so a trust registry can be provisioned headless
body:
## Why

An operator running the VTA farm full stack wants the trust registry provisioned in the same automated pipeline as the VTC, mediator and did-hosting daemon. Those all use the two-phase headless setup (`--setup-key-out`, then a VTA grant with `--admin-handoff`, then `setup --from <toml>`), which drives a template `FullSetup` through `vta_sdk::provision_client`. No built-in template described a trust registry's own DID document, so there was nothing to provision it from.

## What

`vta-sdk/templates/trust-registry.json`:
- `#key-0` for signing (`authentication` and `assertionMethod`) and `#key-1` for key agreement; portable, with 2 pre-rotation keys by default.
- Every service is an optional slot that defaults to `null` and is pruned when omitted: `SERVICE_DIDCOMM`, `SERVICE_REST` (`TRQPRest`), `SERVICE_TRUST_REGISTRY` (ToIP `TrustRegistry`, an **endpoint** whose `uri` is the TRQP URL) and `SERVICE_TSP`.
- `SERVICE_DIDCOMM` and `SERVICE_TSP` reuse the constants from `did_templates::transports`, and `SERVICE_TRUST_REGISTRY` reuses `TRUST_REGISTRY_SERVICE_VAR`.

The template doesn't spell the entries out because a registry advertises only what it serves (REST only with a public URL; DIDComm/TSP only when enabled). The registry's setup builds the entries with its own runtime `build_services` and fills the slots. The published document therefore matches the one the registry serves, which is the invariant `TransportFlags` exists for in that repo.

The template is registered in `BUILTIN_NAMES`, `load_embedded` and the assertion-method census, and listed in `docs/02-vta/did-templates.md`.

## Tests

- `trust_registry_renders_every_transport_it_is_given`
- `trust_registry_prunes_every_transport_it_is_not_given`: each slot renders alone
- The existing `every_builtin_parses_and_validates`, `every_builtin_document_lists_an_assertion_method_key` and `every_builtin_still_declares_the_historical_key_pair` cover the new template.

## Companion changes

- #2251: offline `vta did-mgmt` commands can sign (the bug the operator hit first).
- affinidi-trust-registry-rs: `trust-registry setup --setup-key-out` / `--from`, which names this template.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no code paths
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): new template data only; the service shapes are the existing ones the registry emits, and its consumers (trql-client) already read them
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): an omitted slot advertises nothing
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

A registry advertises exactly the transports it serves, so the registry's setup
builds the entries with its own runtime builder and passes them in. The
published document and the one the registry serves then cannot disagree.

not the referral a community publishes.

title: fix(rooms): a room file from before you joined, or after a missed update, opens — the agent repairs, then the wallet retries
body:
## Why

VTI #2231 made `rooms/keys/read` repair before refusing: it catches up on missed commits and fetches the room's earlier history from the host. Record reads in the portal now open. **File downloads didn't benefit.** The wallet opens a file's record with `rooms/keys/open` and gets its key with `rooms/keys/file-key`. Neither carries a host, so the agent can't fetch what it's missing. A file added before the member joined, or after a membership change their agent hadn't applied, never opened.

## What changes

- When `open` or `file-key` refuses `unknownEpoch` with reason `notDelivered` or `beyondChain`, the wallet **reads the same record once with `rooms/keys/read`**, which names the host, so the agent repairs its epoch state. Then it **retries once**. The agent is still the only party that repairs, and the wallet never fetches commits or links itself. `removed` is never repaired.
- `open` and `file-key` move to **0.2**. Its `unknownEpoch` carries `details.reason`, so the wallet acts on a declared reason, not message text (R3.7). The request shapes are identical, and the VTA serves both versions.
- The **CI guard** that keeps `file-key` out of every bundle except the offscreen document now matches the task's slug at any version. Naming `file-key/0.1` exactly would have made it match nothing after this switch.

## Testing

- New: for both `open` and `file-key`, refused with `beyondChain` and with `notDelivered`, the file opens after exactly one `rooms/keys/read` naming the host and the record. A `removed` refusal stands, and no read is made.
- Page policy: a page still can't open a sealed record at 0.1 or 0.2.
- core 1070 passing, extension 1302/1302, `npm run lint`. Built the extension and ran the updated guard: the task is present only in the offscreen chunk.

title: fix(vtc): audit every document the portal's sign-in key signs as the member, naming the key and the grant
body:
`auth/oob/grant/0.2` consumer item 7: the VTC MUST audit every document
accepted under a portal sign-in delegation against the member, naming the
starter key as the acting credential and the grant `id` as the authority.
Nothing did — the directory, groups and git-ns paths resolved the member
through `delegation::member_for` and wrote no row, and the delegation did
not keep the grant's id.

- The delegation records the grant's `id` at `redeem` (`Delegation.grant_id`).
- `delegation::accept` resolves the member and writes
  `AuditEvent::MemberPortalKeyUsed` (`member`, `startKeyDid`, `grantId`,
  `taskType`, `documentId`) before the document takes effect. Without an
  audit writer, or when the row cannot be written, the document is refused
  — a delegated document is never unaudited.
- The three acceptance sites — the directory and groups tasks and git-ns's
  `reader_as` — call `accept`. The admission budget and the size gate keep
  `member_for`: they only ask whether a key stands for a member and accept
  nothing, so they audit nothing.

`AuditEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new variant is additive.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

### Tests
- `member_portal_oob::every_document_the_portal_key_signs_is_audited_with_its_grant`: a directory read, a groups list and a git-ns view each write one `MemberPortalKeyUsed` row naming the member, `K_b` and the approved grant's id; an out-of-scope document writes none.
- `vti-common` `member_portal_key_used_round_trip`.
- Local: `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` 3508/3508; `cargo nextest run -p vti-common` 784/784; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. The workspace test job is left to CI.

title: fix(rooms): New room no longer strands a member at step 2, prints the grant room-host needs, and defaults to a tier hosts serve
body:
## Why

A member couldn't get from step 2 to step 3 of **New room**. An analysis of why listed several mismatches with verifiable-trust-infrastructure; I checked each against both codebases. Companion PR: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2247.

The specific case: the context's DID offered as "This context's DID is the host" was the member's own persona DID, which isn't a room host. The refusal didn't say so, and it pointed nowhere useful.

## What changes

- **Step 2's refusal is accurate and points somewhere.** A DID publishing no `TrustTaskHTTPS` endpoint can't host rooms here, because members' wallets move room files to the host over HTTPS. If the DID is the member's own identity, the message suggests using **a community they belong to** as the host (paste its DID), or minting a host with a URL. It no longer claims the agent reaches hosts over HTTPS only: the VTA speaks TSP, DIDComm or HTTPS, whichever the host advertises. The same correction is made in the mint-host text and the button hint.
- **Hosts minted from the `room-host` template pass.** That's a template fix in VTI (#2247: `TrustTaskHTTPS` instead of `VTARest`), so there's no dual-accept here, per this repo's no-fold rule.
- **The printed grant is `--role admin --contexts <context>`**, the grant room-host prints itself. The host fetches its DID's keys at startup, which needs `key-export`. The `application` grant left it unable to start as its DID.
- **Attributed is the default.** Private is shown but can't be chosen: hosts store a private room and refuse every request on it until the ZK profile is specified.
- **`rooms/owner/register/0.2`** with a retention-policy choice: whole history (`chained`), or from when a member joined (`fromJoin`). VTI #2247 makes the hosts accept it.
- **The room is recorded at the host the register reply names**, not the one requested.

## Testing

- New: private disabled and attributed by default; `fromJoin` goes out on `register/0.2`; the room is recorded at the replying host.
- Updated: the grant test (now `admin`, scoped), the default visibility, the step-2 message and the transport wording.
- `npm run lint`, extension 1302/1302, core 1065 passing.

title: test(vta-support): the versionTime wait test asserts the wait, not a whole second
body:
Flaky test, not a regression: `version_time::tests::waits_for_rapid_back_to_back_calls` failed CI on #2247 with `elapsed=851ms`.

The function waits from the real clock's sub-second position to the next whole second. So the wait is 851 ms when the call lands at x.149 s, not a full second. Under paused tokio time, a loaded runner can also carry the real clock past the target during the first (instant) virtual sleep. In that case the function returns, correctly, after 851 ms of test time. The old assertion (≥ 1 s) only holds when the call starts on a second boundary.

The test now asserts what the function promises: it waited, and within `MAX_WAIT_SECONDS`. The real-clock property (the result isn't future-dated on return) is covered by the next test, which runs on real time. Passes 5/5 locally; clippy is clean.

step, but no client carried them, and on a private board a trustee's client could not even read
the election — the trustee tasks take its manifest, and the reads are answered only to a party
signing as a trustee, whose key the VTA holds.

- pnm elections trustee step <id> [--watch]: reads both, then takes every step the ceremony needs
  of this trustee now — enrol, deal, confirm (with any justifications), answer complaints against
  its dealing, keep its key share, decrypt after close — carrying each signed document to the
  ballot box's HTTPS door. Idempotent; --watch repeats every 30 s until the result is out.
  `status` shows where the ceremony stands.

title: fix(rooms)!: a room host's DID advertises TrustTaskHTTPS, and rooms/create accepts retentionPolicy
body:
## Why

A user setting up a data room from the wallet's console was stuck at step 2. An analysis of why listed several mismatches between the console and this repo. I checked each against the code. Two are bugs here; the rest are in the extension (companion PR in pnm-browser-plugin).

## What changes

- **`room-host` template publishes `TrustTaskHTTPS`, not `VTARest`.** A room host isn't a VTA. `TrustTaskHTTPS` is the HTTPS binding's own service type, and it's what every Trust Task client looks for, the wallet's console included. Without it the console found no endpoint and refused step 3. The VTA's sender already reads either type, so VTA-to-host traffic was unaffected. Hosts minted from the old template need their DID updated.
- **`rooms/create` accepts `retentionPolicy` (and `ext`), as `rooms/create/0.1` declares.** `rooms/owner/register/0.2` forwards `retentionPolicy`, but both hosts parsed `rooms/create` into a hand-written `deny_unknown_fields` type that had neither member. So any registration with a policy was refused as malformed, and the policy was hard-coded to `chained`. Both hosts now store the owner's choice (`chained` when absent), and a `fromJoin` room then refuses epoch links as it already would.
- **`docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` §8.1**: `--listen` is opt-in, and the guide now says when it's needed. A VTA reaches a host over TSP, DIDComm or HTTPS; browsers need HTTPS for files. It also covers enrolment with the scoped `admin` grant room-host prints, and that `private` isn't served yet.

## Testing

- `room_host_builtin_advertises_trust_task_https_not_vta_rest` (vta-sdk); the canonical-order test is updated.
- `a_room_registered_from_join_is_stored_so` (room-host): `retentionPolicy: "fromJoin"` plus an `ext` member is accepted and stored as `FromJoin`.
- The schema conformance test covers the new members against the spec schema.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`; nextest vti-rooms / room-host / vta-sdk (1237) and vtc-service rooms (172).

`!` because `vti_rooms::wire::CreateRoomBody` gains public fields.

title: feat(vtc): your stars, petnames and lists in the member portal's directory, from your wallet
body:
Portal half of the member directory's personal layer (P3). Stars, petnames and lists are the member's own and live in their own VTA — this community stores none of them.

- When the wallet offers `window.vtaWallet.directory.marks` (vta-browser-plugin#370), the directory pages apply them **locally** to what the directory answered: stars first, *Your name for them* beside a member's own name (never in its place, per persona/contact/list/1.1), lists as filter chips. The directory is read exactly as without marks.
- A star toggle on each tile (beside the link, not inside it) and entry; an entry gets an **Only you see this** section — petname, list checkboxes, *Add to a new list*.
- The page never asks the wallet on its own: **Show my stars and lists** turns them on (the wallet asks once per community — decided with the user), remembered in this browser.

Related: VTI #2245 (VTA tasks), trust-tasks-tf#858 (linking form, so members whose DID isn't shown can be starred). Without a wallet that offers marks, nothing here appears.

## Verified locally

- portal vitest `src/members`: 105 passed (2 new: opt-in + local application; absent without wallet support); tsc clean

title: feat(persona)!: star a directory member whose DID you have not been shown — persona/contact/put/1.1 linking form
body:
A community's member directory shows members' DIDs to other members only where each member chooses to (`did` is admins-only by default), so most entries a holder reads carry no DID to file a contact under — and `persona/contact/put/1.1` needed one (`subjectDid`) to keep a star, a petname or a list on anyone. Found while building the VTI side (VTI #2245) of the member directory's personal layer.

- **put/1.1**: a third form, **linking** — `directoryRef` + `knownByPersona`, without `contactId`, `subjectDid`, `document` or `credentialRefs`. The agent finds the contact it keeps for that entry and persona, or makes one (rev 1, empty document, no `subjectDid`), and appends no revision. Item 4 now keys it on `(contextId, directoryRef, knownByPersona)` and never merges a linked contact with a filed one. Abstract, definitions, an example and two invalid examples added.
- **get/1.1, list/1.1**: `subjectDid` no longer required in the response — absent for a linked contact.

Both are drafts (SPEC §5.3), so changed in place; the generated Response types change shape, hence `!`.

## Checked

- `npm run validate` (918 specs), `check-bindings` (all four languages agree)
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features --tests`

title: feat(vta)!: a contact's star, petname, lists and directory link — persona/contact/*/1.1 and persona/contact/lists/*/1.0
body:
The VTA side of the member directory's personal layer (P3): what a member
keeps *about* other people — a star, a petname, their own lists, a link to the
community directory entry a contact was met through — lives in their own VTA,
never at a community, so no operator holds the graph of who watches whom.

- `persona/contact/put/1.1`: a filing may carry annotation changes, applied
  with it or not at all; the annotating form (`contactId`, no document) changes
  them without appending a revision or moving `rev`. Each annotation given
  replaces, each `removeX` removes, `lists` replaces the set; a list the
  context does not hold is `listUnknown` and changes nothing; an unchanged
  request answers `annotationsChanged: false` and writes nothing. Petnames and
  notes are kept exactly as written.
- `persona/contact/get/1.1`: the current annotations with any revision, `lists`
  naming only lists that still exist.
- `persona/contact/list/1.1`: `starred` always, `petname`, `lists`,
  `directoryRef` and the contact's own `displayName` (never the DID or the
  petname); filters `knownByPersona`, `changedSince`, `starred`, `listId`
  (`listUnknown`), `directoryVtcDid`; a stable order and a cursor bound to the
  filters (`cursorInvalid`).
- `persona/contact/lists/{put,list,show,delete}/1.0`: names unique in the
  context, compared exactly (`nameTaken`), at most 256 (`tooManyLists` with
  its limit); listed by order then name with contact counts; deleting one takes
  it off every contact in one batch, revising none, echoing nothing.
- Storage (`vta_persona::annotations`): annotations beside the contact
  (`pca:`), lists `pcl:`, both context-scoped and in the persona keyspace (so
  backed up); deleting a contact discards its annotations. No petname, note or
  list name reaches a log or the audit trail.

BREAKING CHANGE: `vta_persona::Contact` gains `received_at` — when the current
revision arrived, which `changedSince` reads (and list 1.0's `receivedAt` now
reports instead of the time of the read).

## Verified locally

- fmt, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`
- workspace nextest (excl. VTC): 6522 run, all green after marking the new error enums `#[non_exhaustive]`; vta-persona/vta-sdk doctests
- new: `persona_trust_task::{a_contacts_annotations_are_the_holders_and_append_no_revision, the_contact_annotation_tasks_refuse_what_they_declare}`; census witnesses every new code (baseline −2)

Next: the wallet channel and portal UI (vta-browser-plugin + VTC member portal).

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.32.10
body:
### Added

- **voting**: Vta/pcs/trustee/read, and trustees read voting/election/show on any board ([#855](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/855))

A trustee could not run its part of a sealed or tallied-encrypted election on a private board
  from a client: the trustee tasks take the manifest, which voting/election/show answers only to
  the community and the auditors there; and a trustee's client, which holds no trustee key, had no
  way to sign the reads a private board answers only to a trustee.

  - vta/pcs/trustee/read/0.1 (new): the VTA signs voting/trustees/status or voting/election/show
    as the trustee, addressed to the ballot box — the trustee's counterpart of vta/pcs/voter/read.
    Its payload is fixed to { community, electionId }; `read` is closed. Gated on pcsTrustee.
  - voting/election/show answers every trustee the manifest names on any board (CONVENTIONS §4
    gains its own row; §9.6's "Who reads the ceremony" names both reads).
  - vta/pcs/trustee/decrypt: `closedAt` is the board's close entry, or for a client that cannot
    read the board any time at or after the close and not in the future — the election's summary,
    which the field used to point at, carries no close time.

title: feat(voting): vta/pcs/trustee/read, and trustees read voting/election/show on any board (#855)
body:
feat(voting): vta/pcs/trustee/read, and trustees read voting/election/show on any board (#855)

A trustee could not run its part of a sealed or tallied-encrypted election on a private board
from a client: the trustee tasks take the manifest, which voting/election/show answers only to
the community and the auditors there; and a trustee's client, which holds no trustee key, had no
way to sign the reads a private board answers only to a trustee.

- vta/pcs/trustee/read/0.1 (new): the VTA signs voting/trustees/status or voting/election/show
  as the trustee, addressed to the ballot box — the trustee's counterpart of vta/pcs/voter/read.
  Its payload is fixed to { community, electionId }; `read` is closed. Gated on pcsTrustee.
- voting/election/show answers every trustee the manifest names on any board (CONVENTIONS §4
  gains its own row; §9.6's "Who reads the ceremony" names both reads).
- vta/pcs/trustee/decrypt: `closedAt` is the board's close entry, or for a client that cannot
  read the board any time at or after the close and not in the future — the election's summary,
  which the field used to point at, carries no close time.

Additive: cargo semver-checks against 0.32.9 reports no semver update required.

title: feat(vtc): the member portal shows your repositories, what is shared with you, and your forge accounts
body:
A Repositories page in the member portal (`/members/#/repos`): the member's
own git rights by repository or namespace, with who gave each and any
expiry; on repositories they own or administer, what every other member
holds there; every repository the community governs; and the forge
accounts linked to them.

The portal's wallet sign-in now offers `git-ns/view` and
`git-ns/account/link-status` in its `signingScope`, and nothing else under
`git-ns`. Only those two reads accept the portal key (`reader_as`), with
the member's standing read at execution time and a cooling-off suspension
refusing them as it refuses a change. The view is the member's, never the
administrator's (grant 0.2 consumer item 5).

Linking and unlinking a forge account are not signed by the portal key:
a link binds the account the forge gives the member's roles to, which
`auth/oob/grant/0.2` consumer item 6 excludes from a delegated key. The
page asks the member's wallet (`window.vtaWallet.git.linkAccount` /
`unlinkAccount`), which signs as the member and shows the forge's page
and device code in its own window, then follows the link with
`link-status`. Without that channel it shows `cnm git link --forge`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

### Pairs with
A plugin PR adding `window.vtaWallet.git` (link/unlink through the wallet) follows in OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin. Until it lands the page shows the `cnm git link` command in place of the Link button.

### Tests
- `member_portal_oob::the_portal_key_reads_the_members_repos_and_never_changes_them`: the portal key reads view/0.4 as the member; link, unlink and grant are refused; sign-out disarms it.
- `Repos.test.tsx`: view grouping, wallet link → link-status follow, unlink, no-wallet fallback.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3497 run, the one failure (manifest allowlist) fixed in this commit and rerun green. `npm run lint`, portal vitest, clippy `-D warnings` clean.

### Not in this PR
grant 0.2 consumer item 7 (audit every delegated document naming the key and grant id) is unmet for the directory and groups paths already; these reads follow them. Separate fix.
