title: fix(vtc): a signed-in member browsing the portal is charged their own rate budget, not the anonymous one
body:
## Why

Members browsing the portal got **429**s within a few clicks (`"limiter":"unauth"`, retry after 5 s).

Every directory and groups page signs its Trust Tasks with the browser's sign-in key `K_b`, which the member delegated those families to at sign-in (`auth/oob/grant/0.2` `signingScope`). Trust Task admission (`routing::trust_task_admission::known_principal`) recognised a member's own DID and an administrator's **console key**, but not a portal delegation. So every portal read paid the per-address **anonymous** governor: a burst of 10, then one every 5 s, shared by everyone behind the same address. None of these budgets is configurable, so there was no setting an operator could raise.

## What changes

`known_principal` now also resolves a **live portal delegation that covers the document's type** (`member_portal::delegation::member_for`, the same check the spine and the size gate use) to its member. When the member's ACL entry is live, the member's own signer bucket is charged (a burst of 60, then one every 500 ms) once the proof verifies, exactly as a console key is charged to its administrator.

The rest of the admission model is unchanged:
- A forged document naming `K_b` is charged the per-address ceiling before verification, and the anonymous governor too once it fails.
- A key outside its scope, or whose session has ended, is still a stranger.

## Testing

- `a_portal_key_browsing_the_directory_is_charged_to_its_member_not_the_anonymous_burst`: 30 directory reads from one address pass. **Fails without the fix** at the 11th read, refused by `unauth`.
- `a_portal_key_outside_its_scope_still_pays_the_anonymous_burst`: the same key on a task it wasn't delegated is refused at the anonymous burst.
- The existing `rate_limit_source` and portal delegation tests pass; clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean.

title: feat(vtc): dynamic groups — membership computed from a rule over verified facts, with opt-outs (VTI-DIR-011, VTI-DIR-103)
body:
`vtc/groups/create` now serves `kind: dynamic` (P6): a group whose members are
whoever its `DynamicRule` admits, recomputed by the community.

- **The rule** (`groups::dynamic::admits`): every condition must hold, each
  over a verified fact — community role, an `admin`- or `credential`-sourced
  directory field (a credential value compared by its claim), personhood on
  file, join date. Checked when written (`ruleInvalid`) and again at every
  evaluation against the schema as it stands: a field no longer verified
  admits nobody.
- **The recompute** (`groups::dynamic::recompute`, the one retry owner): admits
  each active member the rule includes and who has not opted out
  (`source: rule`, the group credential issued and offered first, as any
  admission), ends each rule-sourced membership it no longer includes, and
  audits both by reference. A sweeper runs every five minutes and is kicked by
  the `Members` / `Directory` event seams, by create, a rule change and an
  opt-out undone; a VTA that does not answer is retried on a capped, jittered
  backoff.
- **Opt-outs** (`gopt:<groupId>:<entryId>`): `leave` records one — before the
  rule reaches the member too — and ends any membership (`optedOut`;
  `alreadyOptedOut` a second time); `join` withdraws it and admits at once
  when the rule includes them (`joined`), else `optOutWithdrawn`. Joining one
  not opted out of is `notJoinable`. `myMembership` answers `optedOut`.
  Departure and deletion forget them.
- `members/add` / `members/remove` refuse `dynamicGroup`; `update` edits the
  rule (and refuses `joinPolicy` on a dynamic group); a dynamic group answers
  `kind` and `rule`, no `joinPolicy`, stores `closed`, and never carries
  authority (`groupNotEligible`; `groups::authority` skips it).
- Console: **New group → Members: By rule** with a rule builder offering only
  verified facts; Settings edit the rule; no hand add/remove or Authority
  section on a dynamic group. Portal: **Opt out of this group** / **Opt back
  in**.
- Census: `dynamicGroup` ×2 and `alreadyOptedOut` gain witnesses; create's
  `kindNotServed` moves to the baseline.

## Verified locally

- vtc-service + vtc-client nextest: 3500 passed; clippy clean
- admin-ui vitest 1299 passed; tsc clean

title: feat(git): link and unlink a member's forge account from the community's portal (window.vtaWallet.git)
body:
A community's member portal shows the member's repositories and the forge
accounts linked to them (VTI #2244). Its sign-in key may read them, but may
not sign `git-ns/account/link` or `git-ns/account/unlink`: a link binds the
account the forge then gives the member's roles to, which
`auth/oob/grant/0.2` consumer item 6 excludes from a delegated key. So the
page asks the wallet.

`window.vtaWallet.git.linkAccount({ hostDid, forge, member? })` and
`unlinkAccount({ hostDid, forge, accountId?, member? })` pass the same gates
as `directory.publishCard`: the page's browser-attested origin must be the
`SignInPortal` of `hostDid`'s verified DID document, the member must be one
of the wallet's identities there, and the person approves in the wallet's
window. The member's agent then signs the document as the vault entry they
sign in with (`vault/sign-trust-task`) and the wallet posts it to the
community.

For a link the wallet opens the forge's authorisation page itself, checked to
be a plain `https:` URL, and shows any device code in its own window; the
page gets only the link's id and expiry, to follow it with
`git-ns/account/link-status`. A page holding the code could finish the
authorisation with an account of its own choosing.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

### Pairs with
OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2244 — the portal's Repositories page, which calls this channel and falls back to `cnm git link` without it. Either can merge first.

### Tests
- `tests/git-page.test.mts`: params, portal gate, reach gate, identity gate, decline signs nothing, link returns only id+expiry (never the code) and opens the forge, unlink carries the last-read accountId, builders, https-only authorise URL.
- `core/tests/task-surface.mjs`: `git-ns/account/` added to NOT_IN_SDK (VTC is the counterparty).
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (all workspaces), `npm run build` green locally.

title: feat(voting): community voting — polls, surveys and elections with blind tickets, a separate ballot box and trustee-encrypted levels (VTI-VOT-001 – 100)
body:
Community voting for VTI communities (VTI-VOT-001 – 100): polls, surveys and elections in which only members — or holders of an unlinkable voting ticket — vote, the community never sees a ballot, and the ballot box never learns whose ballot it holds.

## Parties

- **The community (VTC) is the registrar** (`vtc/elections/*`, feature `voting`). It creates an election from a manifest, decides eligibility from its own records, and issues each eligible party one ticket, blind: a PCS class credential it signs without seeing. It certifies the result by re-verifying the whole board from its own voting key, with auditors' attestations beside it.
- **The ballot box is a host service** (`vti-voting-service`, `publish = false`), never the VTC: a VTA-provisioned `did:webvh` reached over TSP then DIDComm, with HTTPS kept only as the sessionless cast door VTI-VOT-004 requires. One instance holds boxes for any number of communities and never a roster. Its board is an RFC 9162 log, public or private as the manifest says.
- **The member's VTA is the voter** (`vta/pcs/voter/*`, `vta/pcs/vote`, `vta/pcs/vote-encrypted`): a fresh key per election, the blind ticket request, and a cast signed by a key made for it alone. `pnm elections {list,show,vote}` drives it.
- **Trustees** of a sealed or tallied-encrypted election are VTA personas (`vta/pcs/trustee/*`): a dealer-free t-of-n key generation on the board, then threshold decryption after close.

## Secrecy levels

- **open** — ballots on the board, counted by anyone.
- **sealed** — each ballot sealed to the trustees' threshold key, opened only after close.
- **tallied-encrypted** — exponential ElGamal with 0/1 and selection-count proofs; only each option's total is ever decrypted.

The cryptography (`vti_voting::trustees`) is Ristretto255 on `curve25519-dalek`: Feldman commitments with a proof of knowledge, transport keys and sealed shares, Belenios-style complaints and justifications, Chaum–Pedersen partial decryptions, and an ElGamal KEM with ChaCha20-Poly1305. It is unaudited protocol code over audited group operations.

Each step of the trustees' ceremony goes on the board as the trustee's own signed request (`trusteeStep`). The community forms the election key it shows voters from those verified steps alone, so a ballot box cannot deal in a trustee's name and hold the key itself.

## Surfaces

- VTC: `vtc/elections/{create,list,show,close,cancel,certify}` and `tickets/issue`. A binding election is parked for a second manager (VTI-VOT-081).
- `cnm elections …` and an Elections page in the admin console.
- VTA: the voter and trustee roles, each with its own capability (`pcsVoter`, `pcsTrustee`), classified for retry safety, the MCP guard and the dispatch table.
- `vti-voting`: the PCS core, the board, rules and tally, the ballot-box state machine with a journal rebuilt by replaying the board, and `audit`, which any auditor can run.

## Specification

The wire types are trust-tasks-rs's generated `voting/*`, `vtc/elections/*` and `vta/pcs/{voter,trustee}/*`:

trust-tasks-tf #834 – #853, all released; this branch takes trust-tasks-rs 0.32.9 from crates.io with no patch.

## Testing

- `vti-voting`: unit and end-to-end runs of every level, including restore-by-replay and doctored-board certification failures.
- `vti-voting-service`: HTTP tests.
- `vta-service`: the voter and trustee roles end to end against a real ballot box.
- `vtc-service --features voting`: create through certify against the real ballot box in process, including a sealed election on a private board and a board whose dealings carry no trustee's proof.

title: feat(voting): community voting — polls, surveys and elections with blind tickets, a separate ballot box and trustee-encrypted levels (VTI-VOT-001 – 100) (#2239)
body:
feat(voting): community voting — polls, surveys and elections with blind tickets, a separate ballot box and trustee-encrypted levels (VTI-VOT-001 – 100) (#2239)

* feat(voting): vti-voting, PCS voting tickets, casts and the ballot box

Phase 0 of community voting (design: community voting, draft VTI-VOT-*):
the cryptographic core on the Predicate Credential System, no wire types
until the voting/* Trust Task family is specified.

- registrar: the community's voting helper key, under its own deployment
  label (`<community>#voting-pcs`) and key-derivation info, so it is never
  the vetting key. Issues tickets blind under `voter/<election>`,
  sequentially under one lock.
- voter: a fresh key per election, the blinded ticket request, the cast:
  `attest_in_context` for a hash-to-curve election point, with the
  community, election, manifest digest and ballot bytes bound into the
  context (VOT-012).
- ballot_box: verifies on the published `hvk` alone (VOT-007); the tag is
  the per-election nullifier, recorded once under the revote rule
  (VOT-002) through an atomic NullifierStore.

Measured (examples/scale.rs, 500 voters, release, M5 Max): issuance
2.0 ms (~500/s per VTC), cast 3.2 ms, admit 3.0 ms (~330/s per core),
recount 0.21 ms per ballot on 18 threads (~1 min for 300,000); a cast's
attestation is 248 bytes compressed.

publish = false until its first published consumer.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(voting): name vti-voting's tests and docs after the final VTI-VOT requirement IDs

The VTI specification's Community Voting chapter (dtgwg-vti-spec, feat/community-voting) numbered the requirements VTI-VOT-001 – 100; the crate cited the design note's draft numbering.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): the board — an RFC 9162 Merkle tree log with inclusion and consistency proofs (VTI-VOT-050)

Append-only leaf log, MTH roots, PATH/PROOF generation and the RFC 9162 verification algorithms, which work on the path alone so an auditor needs no log. Checked against the Certificate Transparency reference roots for sizes 0-8, every inclusion and consistency proof of that tree, a rewritten-history refusal, and logarithmic proof sizes at 300,000 leaves.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): manifest and ballot rules and the count, over the generated voting wire types (VTI-VOT-010, 011, 032, 065, 070)

rules: the manifest digest (JCS SHA-256, as a multihash), the manifest's cross-field rules, and a ballot's: one answer per question, exactly one answer member, choices within bounds, complete rankings, every option scored within bounds, text within its length, abstain only where optional. tally: per-question totals from the counted ballots, text withheld below the release threshold and in every provisional count.

The wire types come from trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#834 through a renamed git dependency pinned to its commit (trust-tasks-voting). TEMPORARY: feature branch only, replaced by the workspace trust-tasks-rs once a release carries the voting family.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): the ballot box — every voting/* task as a state machine over the elections it holds (VTI-VOT-012 – 013, 040 – 052, 061, 070)

service::BallotBox: register (community-signed, digest-checked, idempotent, conflict on another manifest), the election's own clock (opened at votingOpens; closed and the result on the board at votingCloses), close/cancel by the community, cast (cheapest check first, exact resend = first receipt, revote replace/refuse with a replacement entry, receipt token), board head/read/inclusion/consistency, result (tallied, or provisional where the manifest allows). Private boards answer the community, named auditors and, for one leaf, its receipt token; everyone else sees electionUnknown. Transport, signing and storage stay the host's. voter::cast_wire builds the wire Cast over the ballot's JCS bytes.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): the ballot box journals what it accepts and rebuilds itself by replaying the board

A Journal receives, before any answer, the three things that cannot be recomputed: each registration as received, each board entry, and each receipt token (journalled before its cast's entry). BallotBox::restore re-registers from the stored manifest and parameters and replays the board for state, tag record, counted ballots and result, journalling nothing again. NoJournal and MemoryJournal (which refuses an out-of-order entry); a restart test checks the restored box gives the same head, the same receipt for a resend, and the same count.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): vti-voting-service — the ballot box as a host service over the HTTPS Trust Task binding

POST /trust-tasks serves every voting/* task: the document's own proof names the signer (it must be the issuer), registration/close/cancel/cast require one, reads may be anonymous; the BallotBox runs under one lock never held across an await; every answer — receipts, heads and refusals — is signed as the service's DID, and an answer that cannot be signed is not sent. Task refusals carry their slug (voting/ballot/cast:castInvalid). A FileJournal (election.json, length-prefixed entries.log and receipts.log, sync_data before answering, torn tail truncated) rebuilds the box on restart. Identity: a did:key minted into the data directory, owner-only.

Also: a receipt token is a bearer credential, so Admitted's Debug is written by hand (caught by the secret-Debug census); voting/election/register's conflicting repeat is alreadyRegistered (trust-tasks-tf#834 now defines it — the framework has no standard conflict code).

* build: trust-tasks-rs 0.32.3 — the voting wire types from crates.io; drop vti-voting's git dependency

trust-tasks-tf #834 (voting/*, vtc/elections/*, vta/pcs/voter/*, vta/pcs/vote) and #835 (pcsVoter appended) shipped in 0.32.3 as a patch release. vti-voting now uses the workspace trust-tasks-rs, so the graph holds one copy again and nothing on this branch blocks main.

* docs: vti-voting's wire types now come from trust-tasks-rs 0.32.3

* feat(vta): the voter role of the PCS engine — vta/pcs/voter/{register,accept,receipt} and vta/pcs/vote (VTI-VOT-020 – 053)

The VTA votes for its principal in a community's elections, as it already
vets and applies for them, so a client with no PCS implementation can vote
and never holds a key or a ticket (trust-tasks-tf #834, conventions
voting/_shared/0.1).

- operations::pcs_voter: a voter key per (context, community, election) at
  a fresh path under the context's base (VTI-VOT-023), re-derived on every
  use; the blinded ticket request (repeated unchanged until the ticket is
  held); unblinding the community's answer; the ballot checked against the
  manifest and the window, the cast built over the ballot's JCS bytes, and
  the voting/ballot/cast document returned signed by a did:key made for
  that cast alone and never kept (VTI-VOT-003); receipts verified as the
  registered ballot box's, matched to a cast this engine built by its board
  leaf hash, kept wrapped, and checked for inclusion in a head the
  community kept (VTI-VOT-053). Blinding state, ticket and receipts are
  wrapped in pcs_engine like every other PCS secret.
- trust_tasks::pcs: the four handlers, gated on the new pcs-voter capability
  (admin and initiator, never application, never sign); audit names the
  election, never a tag, a cast or a receipt (VTI-VOT-100).
- vti-common: Capability::PcsVoter, appended last so no variant moves.
- vta-sdk: URI constants, VtaClient::pcs_voter_* / pcs_vote, retry-safety
  (vote and accept keyed, register and receipt retry-safe).
- vta-mcp: vote is destructive (a host confirms every vote), receipt mutates.
- vta-mobile-core: PcsTask::{VoterRegister, VoterAccept, Vote, VoterReceipt}.
- Conformance witnesses, every declared error code witnessed, and an end to
  end test: register, blind issuance by a registrar, accept, vote, the
  ballot box admits the cast, a signed receipt and head, inclusion checked.
- vti-voting is now published (vta-service depends on it); Ticket::to_text /
  from_text for custody at rest.
- trust-tasks-rs 0.32.4: pcs-voter registered in device/_shared 0.1 too
  (#836), so a device binding publishes it rather than carrying it in ext.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): the ballot box over TSP and DIDComm — a VTA-provisioned identity, one dispatcher, HTTPS kept for sessionless casts (VTI-VOT-004, VTI-VOT-005)

Communities and auditors now reach the voting service over TSP, then DIDComm, through the service identity's own mediator session. The HTTPS door stays only for casts: a one-time key has no mediator session to take its receipt on, and an Affinidi mediator accepts nothing from a sender without one, so casting over messaging would mean opening a session as that key and handing the mediator an account, a relationship record and the voter's address and timing.

- vti-common `host_session` (feature `host-session`): the witness's mediator session, supervisor and TSP/DIDComm carriage, generalised over a `Responder`. vti-witness now runs on it; the ballot box is its second user.
- vta-sdk: the `ballot-box` built-in template (TSP, DIDComm, then `TrustTaskHTTPS`) and `ProvisionAsk::ballot_box`.
- vti-voting-service: `setup` (two-phase, VTA-provisioned, keys in `[secrets]`), `run` (mediator session beside the HTTPS door), `config.toml`; `dispatch::answer` serves both. Over messaging the document's issuer must be the transport-proven sender, and a reply or error is never answered.
- Fix: a request's `#request` fragment is optional; the bare type URI the generated payload types use was refused `unsupportedType`.
- Dockerfile.nitro copies vti-voting and vti-voting-service: vta-service depends on vti-voting, so the enclave image could not build without it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): community elections — vtc/elections/{create,list,show,close,cancel,certify} and tickets/issue, the community as registrar (VTI-VOT-001 – 100)

The community decides who may vote and issues each party the roll admits one ticket, blind; the ballot box the manifest names (a vti-voting-service) admits the casts and keeps the board. The community never handles a ballot and the ballot box never learns who holds a ticket.

- vtc-service `elections` (feature `voting`): records, the registrar's PCS key (HKDF from the signer's master, `vtc-voting-pcs-secret/v1`), and the link to ballot boxes over TSP > DIDComm as the community (VTI-VOT-005). Remote first: registered, closed and cancelled only after the ballot box answered; an unanswered registration is redelivered by the elections sweeper, the one retry owner, which also keeps board checkpoints and discards stored pre-credentials after close. Cancel stops issuance durably before it asks.
- Tickets: one per party per election, recorded before answering, under one lock; a resend is answered with its first answer; the audit row never carries the request's identifier, commitment or pre-credential. Unknown and unseen are the same `electionUnknown`.
- A binding election parks for a second holder of `vtc.elections.manage` (`Act::CreateBindingElection`, kind `election.binding.create`, VTI-VOT-081), template pinned in the console too.
- `certify` reads the result, head and every entry from the ballot box, never the requester, and re-verifies the board with `vti_voting::audit` (new): root, checkpoints, every cast, tags and replacements, the result, ballots ≤ tickets (VTI-VOT-072). Auditors' attestations are verified beside it.
- New capability `vtc.elections.manage`, keyspace `elections` (backed up), `[voting] trusted_ballot_boxes` (VTI-VOT-082), audit events `ElectionChanged` / `ElectionTicketIssued`.
- CI's feature job now runs `vetting-pcs,voting`. The OpenAPI snapshot is regenerated for the trust-tasks-rs 0.32.4 description change.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(cnm): cnm elections {create,list,show,close,cancel,certify}, and vtc-client's elections_* methods

An administrator runs the community's elections from cnm over the signed Trust Task door: create from a manifest file (sent exactly as written, since its digest binds every ticket and cast), list, show (with the disclosure members read), close, cancel, and certify with auditors' attestations. A binding creation answers with the parked action to follow; an untrusted ballot box prints the [voting] config the host operator adds; a taken identifier points at the election. vtc-client gains elections_{create,list,show,close,cancel,certify,ticket}, schema-checked before sending and decoded into the generated responses.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* style(voting): cargo fmt the auditor

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-ui): an Elections page in the admin console — create, close, cancel, certify

Under Governance, for holders of vtc.elections.manage: the community's elections, one election's page (what members are told — ballot box, operator, a warning when one operator runs both — tickets issued, board checkpoints, the certified result), and the four acts. Create takes the manifest as JSON (a sample to start from names this community and a ballot box); a binding election shows as sent for approval. Certify sends auditors' attestations exactly as given. The list-limit and template-pin censuses gain the new listing and the election.binding.create template. src/lib/wire.ts is regenerated: it had fallen behind the OpenAPI snapshot refreshed for trust-tasks-rs 0.32.4.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(vti-common): the host-session feature

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta): vta/pcs/voter/register signs the ticket request as the member (member, ticketDocument)

Implements trust-tasks-tf #841. With `member` — a persona this VTA holds an authentication key of, in a context the caller acts in — the register answer also carries ticketDocument: the vtc/elections/tickets/issue request signed as that member through the gated oracle (ProtocolDefined input the VTA built, as the witnessed party signs). The VTA signs only that document type with only that payload, under pcsVoter; the document is kept per member and returned unchanged on a repeat, so the community answers a resend with its first answer. A DID it holds no key of is memberNotHeld, before anything is allocated. Builds against the PR branch through a temporary [patch.crates-io], removed before the branch reaches main.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta): vta/pcs/voter/read — vtc/elections/list or show signed as the member; route #request-typed documents in VTA and VTC

Implements the voter/read half of trust-tasks-tf #841: the VTA signs exactly one of the two election reads as a persona it holds (pcsVoter and standing to act as the member; the read's payload checked against its own schema first), so a client without the member's key can read the election it votes in. Wired through vta-sdk (URI, retry class, pcs_voter_read), the dispatch table, conformance, the MCP guard (signs as the member, so never --read-only) and vta-mobile-core (PcsTask::VoterRead, appended).

Also: SPEC §4.4.1 makes a request's #request fragment optional, but both services dispatched on the type URI as written, so a #request-typed document was unsupportedType. They now route on TypeUri::for_routing(), which keeps #response.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(pnm): pnm elections {list,show,vote} — a member votes with every key in their VTA

list and show are vtc/elections reads the VTA signs as the member (vta/pcs/voter/read), carried to the community's HTTPS door; show prints what the member is told before a ticket (VTI-VOT-090), including when one operator runs both community and ballot box. vote takes the ticket if the VTA holds none — register with member, the ticketDocument carried unchanged, the community's answer unblinded by voter/accept — builds the cast in the VTA under a key made for it alone, posts it to the ballot box's TrustTaskHTTPS endpoint from this connection after a random pause of up to 20s (--no-delay to skip), and hands the receipt back to voter/receipt. Answers as --answer question=option, optional questions abstained; --ballot for a whole ballot. vtc-client gains send_signed_document for documents another party signed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(vtc): elections from cnm, the console and pnm

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build: trust-tasks-rs 0.32.5 from crates.io (vta/pcs/voter/read, register's member) — the feature-branch patch is gone

Also: the console's Elections page reads trust-task-discovery before anything else and, on a VTC built without the voting feature, says so instead of sending tasks nobody serves; the admin-UI task census lists the six election tasks as feature-gated, dispatched exactly when voting is compiled in.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): the trustees' cryptography for sealed and tallied-encrypted elections, on Ristretto (VTI-VOT-060 – 064)

vti_voting::trustees, over the curve25519-dalek the workspace already runs Ed25519 on (no new crate copy): dealer-free t-of-n joint key generation (Feldman commitments, a proof of knowledge of each dealer's constant term bound to its index and the election), partial decryptions with Chaum-Pedersen proofs against each trustee's public verification key, Lagrange combination of any t; sealed ballots as an ElGamal KEM with ChaCha20-Poly1305; tallied-encrypted ballots as exponential ElGamal per option with disjunctive proofs that each is 0 or 1 and that the question's selections sum to a count the manifest admits, homomorphic totals, and baby-step giant-step to read a total back. Every proof is Fiat-Shamir over SHA-512 bound to a caller's election context. Tests cover threshold opening (and refusal below it), forged shares, dealings, partials and ballots, cross-election replay, and tallies. The protocol layer is new and unaudited; the group operations are curve25519-dalek's. Not yet wired: the trustee tasks, the ballot box's encrypted levels, and the VTA's trustee role.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): transport keys, sealed shares and a key from the qualified dealers — the trustees' cryptography as CONVENTIONS §9 fixes it (VTI-VOT-062)

Shares ride the public board sealed to each recipient's transport key (Schnorr-proved under vti/vote/trustee/transport/v1, bound to the trustee's index), bound by AAD to the election, the dealer and the recipient. ElectionKey::from_dealings takes the qualified dealers' dealings — any non-empty set — and records them; a trustee key takes shares from exactly those dealers. Election::trustee_context and question_ctx give the contexts §9.2 and §9.3 name.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(voting): service's module doc names no private method

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): the trustees' ceremony as the ballot box runs it — enrol, deal, confirm, justify, form or fail, then decrypt (VTI-VOT-062, VTI-VOT-063)

vti_voting::ceremony: a state machine over the trustee cryptography. A step repeated exactly is a Repeat, a different one is refused; a complaint holds the key back until its dealer reveals a share that checks; at votingOpens the key forms from the qualified dealers, or the ceremony fails. Decryption takes exactly one verified partial per target from each trustee until t have decrypted. Each refusal names the task error code it answers as.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): the trustee rules of a sealed or tallied-encrypted manifest, held behind SERVED_LEVELS until the ballot box serves them (VTI-VOT-061, VTI-VOT-062, VTI-VOT-064)

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting): the ballot box runs sealed and tallied-encrypted elections — voting/trustees/*, voting/ballot/cast-encrypted, decryption and the result (VTI-VOT-060 – 064)

The box registers all three levels. Every trustee step is checked against the manifest's trustee at its index and appended to the board; the key forms when the ceremony completes or at votingOpens, or the ceremony fails and no cast is admitted. cast-encrypted admits a sealed payload or an encrypted ballot (each option 0/1 and each count admissible, proved) on the open cast's rules, the attestation over the form's JCS bytes. After close, trustees decrypt the sealed casts' KEMs or the options' totals; with t of them the box opens each ballot (unsealed, or spoiled when it does not open to a valid ballot) or reads each total, and publishes the result. Restore rebuilds the ceremony, the casts and the round by replaying the board. vti_voting::wire converts the wire forms; voter::encrypted_form and cast_encrypted_wire build a cast. Temporarily patched to trust-tasks-rs on trust-tasks-tf #845.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(voting-service): serve voting/trustees/* and voting/ballot/cast-encrypted (VTI-VOT-060 – 064)

Every trustee step and the encrypted cast must be signed; status is a read like the board's. A trustee's enrolment over HTTPS is tested end to end: unsigned is proofRequired, another trustee is permissionDenied.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(voting): cast-encrypted's receipt carries electionId and entryHash, as the open cast's does

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta): the trustee role and the encrypted cast — vta/pcs/trustee/* and vta/pcs/vote-encrypted; every level served end to end (VTI-VOT-060 – 073)

The VTA is a trustee's custodian (trust-tasks-tf #845): operations::pcs_trustee keeps
the transport key and the key share of a sealed or tallied-encrypted election and signs
each voting/trustees/* request as the trustee persona. The transport secret and the
dealing's polynomial are re-derived from a fresh path under the context's base, so a
repeated deal is the same dealing and justify reveals exactly the share dealt; the key
share, a sum of other trustees' shares, is kept wrapped (secret:trustee:…). decrypt is
refused before closedAt (VTI-VOT-063). Capability pcsTrustee (appended to Capability;
that hunk went out in a47971a7).

vta/pcs/vote-encrypted seals the ballot to the election key or encrypts it option by
option with its proofs, and the attestation binds the encrypted form; the cleartext
never leaves. voter/register now serves every level and vta/pcs/vote refuses a
non-open manifest; voter/receipt keeps a cast-encrypted receipt too.

SDK URIs, retry classes (vote-encrypted keyed, trustee tasks retry-safe), dispatch,
conformance witnesses, the MCP guard (justify and decrypt confirmed), mobile
PcsTask::VoteEncrypted, VtaClient::pcs_trustee_* and pcs_vote_encrypted.

vti-voting: rules::SERVED_LEVELS is all three; the auditor recounts an encrypted board
(audit_encrypted: the ceremony, every encrypted cast's attestation and proofs, every
partial, and the openings and totals they give); tally::tallied_rows shared by the box
and the auditor; a tallied election with no casts has no targets. The VTC creates
sealed and tallied-encrypted elections and certifies them.

unsupportedSecrecy (vta/pcs/voter/register, vtc/elections/create) can no longer occur
here, so both move to their census baselines (ceilings 373 and 10).

Tests: a sealed election through the VTA's own handlers against a real ballot box
(three trustee personas, a member, two decrypting); every declared trustee and
vote-encrypted code; a sealed election created, decrypted and certified through the
VTC; certification of both encrypted levels and of a doctored opening.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(pnm): elections vote casts sealed and tallied-encrypted ballots; trust-tasks-rs 0.32.7 from crates.io

pnm reads the election key from the ballot box's voting/trustees/status and has the VTA build the cast with vta/pcs/vote-encrypted. trust-tasks-rs 0.32.7 carries trust-tasks-tf #845 and #847; the feature-branch patch is gone. The VTC census baselines vtc/elections/create:unsupportedSecrecy only where the elections tasks are bound (feature voting).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(voting): encrypted elections on a private board — trustees read their ceremony, voters take the key from vtc/elections/show (trust-tasks-tf #852)

The ballot box answers voting/trustees/status to every trustee the manifest names on any board (CONVENTIONS §4, §9.6). The VTC's sweeper reads the formed election key from the box, keeps it only if the qualified dealings reported with it form it, and vtc/elections/show carries it (item 6). pnm elections vote takes the key from show and no longer asks the box. Tests: a sealed election run to its result on a private board, an outsider refused; through the VTC on a private board, a key its dealings do not form never shown. trust-tasks-rs 0.32.8 from crates.io.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(voting): each trustee step on the board is the trustee's signed request (trust-tasks-tf #853, VTI-VOT-062)

The board recorded each step of the trustees' ceremony as its payload alone, so nothing on it
showed who took a step. A ballot box could deal in a trustee's name — a polynomial of its own,
with matching shares sealed to that trustee's transport key — and every check would pass while it
held the election key, able to open sealed ballots before close.

- The ballot box appends each enrol, deal, confirm and justify as a `trusteeStep` entry carrying
  the request exactly as received, proof included, and rebuilds the ceremony from them on
  restore. The payload-only kinds are no longer written, and a board holding one is refused.
- `vti_voting::steps`: `read` takes a request as a step only when its issuer is the trustee the
  manifest names at its index and it names this election; `ProvenRequests` holds the signers a
  caller's verifier vouched for, since resolving DIDs is the caller's I/O.
- `audit` requires every step's signer to be proven (`Evidence::proven`); `audit::election_key`
  forms a key from proven steps alone.
- The VTC forms the key `show` carries by reading the board and verifying each step's proof
  against the trustee's DID — never from `voting/trustees/status` — and certify verifies them too.
- Temporary `[patch.crates-io]` onto #853's branch until it is released.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(vtc): the member portal's room page puts the open record beside the list, not below it
body:
## Why

On the member portal's room page, clicking a record (or wanting to add one) opened a panel **below the whole record list**, off-screen. The page used one auto-fit grid for three panels (*This room*, *Records*, and the record / add form), so the third wrapped under the tallest card. The room's six facts took a card of their own, and the page was capped at 64rem, which left wide margins on a desktop.

## What changes

- **Facts on one line** under the room's name: tier · epoch · room storage · your storage · "You are glenn-vta", with the attributed-tier note beneath.
- **List and detail side by side** (page widened to 84rem): records on the left; on the right, sticky below the top bar, the open record (with a close button) or the add form. **+ Add** in the Records header returns to the form.
- **Compact rows**: one meta line, `v12 · 19 Oct 2026, 20:22 · airport-electric`. Authors are shown by short name ("you" for the member's own), with the full DID on hover and in the record panel. Thumbnails are smaller. Retracted records fold under "N retracted records", and the count shows the records you can open.
- **Add form**: "signed as **glenn-vta**" instead of the full DID.
- **Phones**: one column; an opened record goes above the list and scrolls into view.

Checked visually against a fake wallet at desktop and 390px widths (throwaway harness, not committed).

## Testing

Two new tests: the open record and the add form share the side pane (Add and Close switch between them); authors are shown briefly and retracted records are folded. admin-ui vitest 1295 passing; `npm run lint` clean.

title: feat(vtc): the console gives a group authority — the group page's Authority section for grants and role bindings
body:
A group's page in the console now shows what the group gives its members and
lets its managers bind more: capabilities they hold themselves, or a role's
capabilities, on a closed group. A capability that creates authority is
marked, and the binding goes to the action list for another administrator's
approval (the existing `ParkedAction` toast). Ending one is a reduction of
every member and may wait for approval the same way. A group that is not
closed says why it cannot give authority. The Rooms section lists room
bindings only.

`vtc/groups/{show,list}` now answer `carriesAuthority` truthfully — it was
hardwired `false` from before grants bindings were served (#2237).

## Verified locally

- admin-ui vitest 1295 passed, tsc and lint clean
- vtc-service group tests (62) passed; clippy clean

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.32.9
body:
### Fixed

- **voting**: Each trustee step on the board is the trustee's signed request ([#853](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/853))

The board recorded each step of the trustees' ceremony as its payload alone, so nothing on it
  showed who took a step. A ballot box could enrol or deal in a trustee's name — a polynomial of its
  own choosing, with matching shares sealed to that trustee's transport key — and every check the
  community, the trustees and certification run would pass while the ballot box held the election
  key, able to open sealed ballots before close. The defence was only that the ballot box runs
  honestly, which VTI-VOT-062 does not let a deployment assume.

  - A new board entry, `trusteeStep` (appended), carries the trustee's `voting/trustees/enrol`,
    `deal`, `confirm` or `justify` request exactly as the ballot box received it, proof included.
    The `transportKey`, `dealing`, `confirmation` and `justification` kinds are no longer appended,
    and a consumer refuses a board holding one.
  - CONVENTIONS §9.6: whoever replays the ceremony takes a step only when its type, community and
    election are right, its issuer is the trustee the manifest names at the payload's index, and
    its proof is the issuer's. A `partials` entry needs no signature: its Chaum–Pedersen proofs
    already tie it to the trustee's share. `voting/trustees/status` is never evidence of who took a
    step.
  - `vtc/elections/show` item 6: the community forms the key itself by replaying the ceremony from
    the board (open to it on any board), never from `voting/trustees/status`.
  - `vtc/elections/certify` item 8 states the encrypted levels' recount: ceremony, casts and
    partials, from the board alone.

title: chore: release 11 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.32.8` → `0.32.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.32.8` → `0.32.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.32.8` → `0.32.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.32.8` → `0.32.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.32.8` → `0.32.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.32.8` → `0.32.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.32.8` → `0.32.9` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.32.8` → `0.32.9` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.27` → `0.26.28` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.28`) | `0.8.27` → `0.8.28` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.27` → `0.8.28` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): grants and role bindings — groups that carry authority, with the consent every change takes (VTI-DIR-103 – 105)
body:
The second half of grant and role bindings (P5), on the group-grants model:
`vtc/groups/bindings/add` now serves `grants` and `role` bindings, and every
change to what such a group confers is a grant or a reduction with the
consent either takes (VTI-DIR-104). "Groups give no way round consent."

- **bindings/add** (items 3 – 5, 8): a static `closed` group only
  (`groupNotEligible`); every capability one the registry knows
  (`unknownCapability`, naming them) or a defined role's ceiling
  (`unknownRole`); held by the requester themselves, never through a group
  (`exceedsBinderAuthority`, VTI-ACL-071). Binding an authority-conferring
  capability parks as `Act::GroupAuthority` (subject `group:<id>`) and is
  recorded only when the approval executes it, re-checked then; one that
  confers none takes the bound gesture. Members are provisioned before the
  answer. `kindNotServed` is no longer emitted.
- **members/add** (item 5): a member whose role ceiling does not admit what
  the group confers is refused `exceedsRoleCeiling`; admitting one is a grant
  to them, parked as `Act::GroupAuthority` (subject the member) when it confers
  authority.
- **members/remove**: a reduction of what the group gave them, through
  `settle_reduction_as(Act::ReduceGroupAuthority)` — third-party consent, or
  the unopposed path with its cooling-off and the subject's suspension, exactly
  as any reduction. **leave** is the member's own and needs nobody.
- **bindings/remove** and **delete** of a group carrying authority: one
  group-wide `Act::ReduceGroupAuthority` whose approvers exclude every member
  of the group; where nobody is left, the requester's gesture and a `Critical`
  `AuthorityReducedUnopposed` row per member, with no cooling-off (a
  cooling-off suspends one subject). Rows are withdrawn and the binding
  deleted before the answer. `delete` reports `bindingsRemoved`.
- **update**: a group carrying authority stays closed (`authorityGroupLocked`,
  VTI-DIR-103).
- The group acts' requester is the group's manager, who may hold no
  administrative role: `requester_still_authorized` asks `vtc.groups.manage`.
  The members a change reaches never approve it.
- Five summary templates (`acl.grant.authority` / `acl.reduce.authority` for
  the group tasks), pinned here and in the console.
- Census: six codes gain witnesses (`group_authority.rs`); `kindNotServed`
  moves to the baseline.

## Verified locally

- fmt, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`
- vtc-service + vtc-client nextest: 3496 passed
- admin-ui vitest: 1293 passed

Stacked on #2236; retarget to main once it merges (CI runs only on PRs to main).

Not here: a console form for grants bindings (approvals already render in the action list).

title: feat(vtc): group grants — capabilities a group provisions onto its members' entries (VTI-DIR-100 – 102)
body:
The first half of grant and role bindings (P5): the access-control model and
its one writer. `vtc/groups/bindings/add` still refuses a grants or role
binding `kindNotServed`; the tasks that take the consent such a binding needs
(VTI-DIR-104) follow, so nothing here can be reached from the wire yet.

- `VtcAclEntry.groupGrants` (`acl::group_grant`): one row per capability and
  binding, naming the group as its source and the binding's delegator
  (VTI-ACL-072). Two groups conferring a capability make two rows, so it goes
  only when its last source does (VTI-DIR-101).
- `VtcAclEntry::can` reads the rows beside the role. A row counts only inside
  the ceiling of the member's administrative role, and only while the entry may
  act — at every read, so narrowing the role inerts it at once (VTI-DIR-102,
  VTI-DIR-105). Rows confer nothing to approve (VTI-ACL-040).
- `VtcAclEntry::conferring` counts the rows, and `newly_conferred` /
  `lost_conferring` read it: a role change that brings a group's grant into
  force is a conferral the role change's own consent sees (VTI-APV-018).
- `groups::authority::provision` makes one entry's rows what its groups say:
  every capability of an active grants or role binding of a closed group the
  subject is a member of, that the binding's delegator holds **other than
  through a group** — a group cannot manufacture a capability nobody behind it
  held, or keep alive one its binder gave themselves through it. Under the
  git-namespace write lock; the binding reconciler runs it for every affected
  entry each pass. A suspended member keeps their rows.
- `acl/*` writes keep the rows as stored, as they keep resource grants; the
  entry's `ext["org.openvtc"].groupGrants` shows each with its group and
  whether it is in effect. A key rotation re-points rows and bindings.
- `AuditEvent::GroupGrantsChanged` records each change by reference: group,
  binding, member entry, capabilities.

## Verified locally

- fmt, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`
- vtc-service + vtc-client nextest: 3492 passed
- workspace nextest (excl. VTC): 6436 passed; vti-common doctests ok

The tasks (bindings/add for grants and role, members add/remove as grants and reductions, update lock, consent) follow in a stacked PR.

title: fix(voting): each trustee step on the board is the trustee's signed request
body:
The board recorded each step of the trustees' ceremony as its payload alone, so nothing on it
showed who took a step. A ballot box could enrol or deal in a trustee's name — a polynomial of its
own choosing, with matching shares sealed to that trustee's transport key — and every check the
community, the trustees and certification run would pass while the ballot box held the election
key, able to open sealed ballots before close. The defence was only that the ballot box runs
honestly, which VTI-VOT-062 does not let a deployment assume.

- A new board entry, `trusteeStep` (appended), carries the trustee's `voting/trustees/enrol`,
  `deal`, `confirm` or `justify` request exactly as the ballot box received it, proof included.
  The `transportKey`, `dealing`, `confirmation` and `justification` kinds are no longer appended,
  and a consumer refuses a board holding one.
- CONVENTIONS §9.6: whoever replays the ceremony takes a step only when its type, community and
  election are right, its issuer is the trustee the manifest names at the payload's index, and
  its proof is the issuer's. A `partials` entry needs no signature: its Chaum–Pedersen proofs
  already tie it to the trustee's share. `voting/trustees/status` is never evidence of who took a
  step.
- `vtc/elections/show` item 6: the community forms the key itself by replaying the ceremony from
  the board (open to it on any board), never from `voting/trustees/status`.
- `vtc/elections/certify` item 8 states the encrypted levels' recount: ceremony, casts and
  partials, from the board alone.

title: feat(vtc): the console offers the VTA's hosting servers — vtc/config/did-hosting/list/0.1
body:
The "Where identities are published" card on the Groups page asked an
administrator to type a hosting server's id at the community's VTA. It now
lists them: `vtc/config/did-hosting/list/0.1` (trust-tasks-tf #849, in
trust-tasks-rs 0.32.8) asks the community's VTA for its registered
`did:webvh` hosting servers and answers the ids `dids.webvh_server` would
accept.

- Needs `vtc.config.admin`, like the key it serves. The VTC holds no list of
  its own: every answer is the VTA's, read now, filtered through
  `did_hosting::validate` (so `local` and a malformed id never appear).
- Refusals are the specification's: `noKeyHolder` without a configured VTA,
  `keyHolderUnavailable` when it cannot be reached, `keyHolderRefused` when it
  refuses.
- The console shows a select of the listed servers, keeps a typed id as the
  fallback, and says why when the list cannot be read.

## Verified locally

- fmt, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`
- vtc-service + vtc-client nextest: 3483 passed
- vta-sdk (workspace build): 1369 passed
- admin-ui vitest: 1293 passed; tsc clean

title: docs(assurance): explain incremental RAHP assurance model
body:
## Purpose

Adds an explanatory design note for #17 describing how RAHP builds assurance incrementally across source preparation, evidence generation, RAHP assessment and assurance interpretation, while keeping human harm prevention as RAHP's governing purpose.

The note now reflects the task-force decisions made on 14 October 2026 and the upstream state that followed.

## What this note clarifies

- Why Increment 1 is part of RAHP even though it establishes reproducible source preparation and replay rather than a complete assessment.
- How observations, such as the TRQP time mismatch, should be treated before they become specification findings.
- Why validation and replay evidence do not by themselves establish assurance success.
- Why review vocabulary and reviewer accountability are method concerns, not merely implementation details.
- How example-local hypotheses remain distinct from canonical corpus risks.
- What future convergence PRs should explain up front.

## Review-driven updates

Following review on 20 October:

- anchors RAHP to the README's human-harm-prevention purpose rather than creating a competing general assurance definition;
- records the accepted vocabulary direction from #27 and #21;
- identifies #28 semantic enforcement as still under review rather than current behavior;
- records the task-force decisions on reviewer accountability and example-local risk identifiers;
- removes transient WG report-out text;
- links the note from README;
- leaves the separate architectural layer model raised from downstream #1007 for later convergence rather than expanding this PR.

Two executable follow-ups are now tracked separately:

- #29 / #31: reviewer accountability and example-local risk identifiers;
- #30 / #32: GAP-5.1 pull-request reviewability and contribution guidance.

## Scope boundary

This PR remains documentation-only. It does not change schemas, validators, corpus records, review records, examples or CI. The implementation and governance consequences identified during review are deliberately isolated in #31 and #32.

## Validation

The branch has been rebuilt as one signed-off commit on current `main`. Repository CI is expected to run on the current ready-for-review head.

## Provenance

Prepared with AI assistance following review discussion on #19, #20, #21, #23 and the #17 convergence plan.

body:
## Increment 5 of #17 — VRC examination and bounded reassessment

### Purpose

Demonstrate reuse beyond TRQP using the historical DTG Credentials v0.3 source and a real subsequent source revision. This is the #17 generality checkpoint: retain immutable inputs, derive reproducible observations, preserve earlier evidence, reassess after source change, and identify which evidence structures genuinely recur across specifications.

### Source provenance

Historical RAHP PR #6 was created at 2026-05-08 06:55:52 UTC but did not retain the specification bytes or immutable source revision used in its AI-assisted session.

For this new reproducible examination, the authoritative task-force source is reconstructed from Git history:

- `dtgwg-cred-tf#31` merged at `62bbd8a19d598078f50560948ca71ec0e034a6fc` on 30 April 2026.
- `dtgwg-cred-tf#33` merged at 2026-05-08 08:36:46 UTC.
- The #33 merge commit `200acbaa47a422b173652ed2c3dc961c4fbc9e7a` has `62bbd8a19d598078f50560948ca71ec0e034a6fc` as its parent.
- The baseline retained here is therefore the authoritative `main` revision immediately preceding #33 and contemporaneous with #6.
- The reassessment uses the real #33 changed-source revision.

This establishes the source for this examination. It does **not** claim that the unretained bytes uploaded into the historical #6 AI session were byte-identical.

### What changed

- Retain `dtg.md` at both immutable revisions with repository/commit/path, Git blob SHA and SHA-256 manifests.
- Add SR-201 baseline and SR-202 reassessment records using the existing `rahp-spec-review/v1` contract.
- Add example-local evidence sidecars binding target, method, review bytes, canonical risk corpus, fresh observations, source propositions and finding reasoning.
- Add a deterministic evaluator that verifies retained source identity, review/evidence bindings and finding transitions.
- Add negative/boundary tests for altered source, stale observations, reused revision, missing finding evidence, incorrect risk reasoning and unresolved source propositions.
- Add adoption documentation and a TRQP × VRC generality decision.
- Link the second real-source examination from `review/README.md`.

### Findings

- **F-001 / RK-SC02:** baseline general VRC ZKP guidance couples proof to shared-community membership evidence. #33 separates pairwise and community-anchored proof and explicitly removes shared membership as a general precondition. SR-202 resolves this documentary interpretation gap.
- **F-002 / RK-ID05:** M-DID bootstrapping remains permitted and migration to R-DIDs remains recommended rather than normatively triggered. The source change does not close the residual linkability window, so the finding remains open.

### Generality decision

The second case supports a reusable **minimal evidence-envelope proposition**: immutable target/method identity, review/corpus bindings, execution state, evidence identifiers, finding coverage, observation/inference separation, limitations and per-risk reasoning recur across TRQP and VRC.

The complete example-local sidecars are **not** promoted to a shared contract here. TRQP result pointers/fixtures and VRC source-section propositions remain subject-specific, as do observation payloads and unassessed dimensions. A shared schema would be a separate method decision after review of this second case.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] VRC source identity, scope and attribution are established for the new reproducible examination.
- [x] Checks and findings derive from actual retained source.
- [x] Earlier review/evidence is preserved alongside the reassessment.
- [x] Changed source cannot silently inherit the previous assessment.
- [x] Reassessment uses a real immutable changed-source revision rather than a constructed example.
- [x] Findings identify evidence, reasoning, limitations and treatment.
- [x] Generality is assessed without prematurely standardizing example mechanics.
- [x] Current-head repository CI passes.
- [x] Contribution checks pass.
- [ ] Independent review and maintainer acceptance.

### Reproduction

```sh
python3 review/examples/vrc-v03/evaluate.py
python3 review/validate_spec_review.py review/examples/vrc-v03/baseline-review.yaml
python3 review/validate_spec_review.py review/examples/vrc-v03/reassessed-review.yaml
python3 -m unittest tests.test_vrc_reassessment -v
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

### Observed validation evidence

Current head `461cde03758d4027525153e6e910a65174f17502` passed RAHP validation run `39523250399`.

The run completed canonical corpus validation, the full repository/review regression suite (including `tests/test_vrc_reassessment.py`), worked-review validation, temporary build, generated-file binding, summary generation and evidence upload.

Retained artifact: `rahp-validation-39523250399-1` (artifact ID `12311397680`), digest `sha256:435b79dd11ceed8cfdaa5baf3e31a4317675b362640182f8aa95c2dbd1ab1dab`, retained through 4 November 2026.

EasyCLA is successful on the same head. Independent review and maintainer acceptance remain outstanding.

### Dependency / merge boundary

This PR is prepared from accepted `main` only. It does not depend on unmerged #22, #28, #31 or #32 and does not silently consume their contracts.

#22 remains the Increment 4 delivery gate in #17. This PR may be reviewed in parallel, but Increment 5 should not be recorded as delivered upstream before the required convergence sequence is accepted.

### Assurance boundary

Successful reproduction establishes source identity, deterministic observations and internally consistent review/evidence bindings. It does not establish ZKP implementation correctness, deployed behavior, target-wide assurance, residual-risk acceptance or independent human review.

Prepared with AI assistance.

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.27`) | `0.8.26` → `0.8.27` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.26` → `0.8.27` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.32.8
body:
### Added

- **vtc/config**: Did-hosting/list 0.1 — the hosting servers the community's VTA can publish its identities through ([#849](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/849))

A community's administrator chooses where the identities it mints (its groups'
  and its own rooms') are published. The community either serves each `did:webvh`
  log itself, or has its VTA publish it on a hosting server registered there.
  Without a list of those servers the choice is typed blind.

  - vtc/config/did-hosting/list/0.1: for holders of `vtc.config.admin`. The
    community asks its own VTA (`vta/webvh/servers/list`), as itself, over the
    link it keeps to it. It answers with each server's `id`, `did` and `label`,
    and nothing else of the VTA's record. A server whose id the configuration
    could not name is left out.
  - Codes: noKeyHolder (no VTA link), keyHolderUnavailable (no answer,
    retryable), keyHolderRefused (the VTA's own code and message in `details`).



### Fixed

- **voting**: Encrypted elections on a private board — trustees read their ceremony, voters get the key from vtc/elections/show ([#852](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/852))

On a private board the ballot box answered voting/trustees/status only to the community and
  its auditors, so no trustee could take its next step (transport keys, dealings and targets are
  read from status) and no voter could obtain the election key: a sealed or tallied-encrypted
  election on a private board could not run.

  - CONVENTIONS §4 gains the rows the trustee tasks were missing; voting/trustees/status
    answers every trustee the manifest names on any board. Nothing the ceremony publishes is
    secret (§9.6, "Who reads the ceremony").
  - vtc/elections/show carries electionKey (optional, appended) once formed, read from the
    ballot box and refused unless the qualified dealings in the same answer form it. A voter
    gets it from the community it already asks for its ticket.

title: fix(audit): bounded chain-head recovery and paged audit readers
body:
## What and why

The VTA's audit hash-chain could not work inside an enclave. On the first write after a restart, `AuditWriter` recovered its chain head by reading the **entire** audit keyspace to find one row. Over vsock the whole result must fit a single 16 MiB frame, so on a real log that read simply fails — and the audit chain is the mechanism that makes the log tamper-evident.

**Recovery is now bounded.** It scans the newest `HEAD_LOOKBACK` (20) rows under the writer's own key prefix — `log:` on a VTA, which keeps `prune:watermark` from being read as the newest audit row. A full window of non-envelope rows is genuinely ambiguous, and both obvious answers are wrong: anchoring at genesis forks the chain if an envelope sits just below the window, and failing closed bricks the prefix permanently because no write can then succeed to clear the condition. So it pages further back (500 rows per read, no cap in total) until it finds an envelope or proves the prefix holds none. A cap would be the second wrong answer again: a pre-chain log larger than it is ordinary (one row per audited operation over the retention window), and failing closed there would lose the audit trail of every VTA upgrading from before chaining. That deep scan belongs to the one-time legacy-to-chained migration and runs at most once.

A failed recovery is reported once at `ERROR`, counted once in `audit_chain_recovery_failures_total`, and backed off for 60s. Recovery can fail only on a failed read — so a broken log does not re-read storage on every audited operation.

**New storage primitive.** `ScanOpts` / `KeyspaceHandle::scan_raw` — a bounded, directional read with an exclusive resume key — on both backends, plus `OP_SCAN` on the enclave proxy with the existing HELLO capability negotiation. An older proxy falls back to one full-prefix read filtered client-side; if that exceeds 16 MiB it is not retried and the caller gets a proxy-upgrade error.

`ScanPager` decides its strategy **once per walk** rather than per call. Without it, a reader looping on `scan_raw` would ask an old proxy for the whole prefix on every page — a walk of *n* pages transferring and decrypting the range *n* times. It re-checks per page, so a proxy downgraded mid-walk buffers the remainder once instead of reverting to a full read each time.

**Audit verification and listing** now walk through the pager instead of materialising the keyspace. `verify` also counts rows actually examined and stops at a break, matching the field's definition and the VTC's `verifier.index()`; it previously reported the whole log's size.

### Notes for review

- **Opcode allocation.** `OP_APPLY_BATCH` (#2106) landed in parallel and took `0x0C` / `1 << 4`. Scan took the next free byte and bit (`0x0D` / `1 << 5`). The collision would **not** have been a compile error on either side — the proxy would have dispatched one opcode to the other's handler — so both values are now pinned in `op_code_constants_match_proxy_wire_contract`.
- **Snapshot reads.** `scan_raw` reads through `read_snapshot` like every other lock-free read (#2113), and the proxy's `OP_SCAN` reads through a snapshot too. A plain `range` can observe a write batch half-applied, and a page of audit rows torn across a batch is exactly what a chain verifier reports as tampering.
- **Range-algebra parity.** The enclave's and proxy's `scan_bounds` are separate implementations in separate cargo workspaces. They are pinned to one table of conformance vectors (`vti-common/src/store/scan_range_vectors.json`), which each side runs through its own production path.
- **Accepted, documented trade-offs:** a selective `audit/list` filter reads to the end of the log (a strict `truncated` cannot be had alongside a bounded scan); the proxy refuses an oversized page rather than truncating it (a short page means *end of range*, so a capped page would end a walk early and, in recovery, fork the chain); the chain mutex is deliberately held across recovery I/O (releasing it would let two writers anchor concurrently).

## Requirements

VTI-AUD-004 (the audit trail is tamper-evident) — no new requirement, but the chain only satisfies it on a TEE deployment with this fix; recovery previously failed there, and the fail-closed behaviour is what prevents a silent re-anchor from forking the chain.

## Backport

**Proposed: none** — maintainer's call. It is a fix rather than a feature, so it is eligible, but it carries a new storage primitive and an enclave-proxy wire opcode, which is more surface than a release branch usually takes. Worth backporting only if a supported release ships the chained audit sink on a TEE.

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main` (or is a backport / `release-direct` PR into `release/<name>`)
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

## CI

Merged with `main`, which carries the `deny.toml` ignore for `RUSTSEC-2026-0374` (`basic-toml`) and the webpki fixes from #2232, so `cargo-deny` is green again. That red check had skipped every test job on the first run.

Checked locally on the pushed tree: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the workspace suite (6435 passed), the vtc-service/vtc-client suite (3481 passed) and `enclave-proxy`'s own suite (63 passed).

title: fix(audit): bounded chain-head recovery and paged audit readers (#2229)
body:
fix(audit): bounded chain-head recovery and paged audit readers (#2229)

* fix(audit): bounded chain-head recovery and paged audit readers

Chain-head recovery read the whole audit keyspace to find one row, which
cannot work over vsock where the result must fit a single 16 MiB frame.
Recovery now scans the newest rows under the writer's own prefix, falling
back to a bounded deep scan only while a legacy log is being migrated, and
failing closed rather than silently re-anchoring.

Adds `ScanOpts` / `KeyspaceHandle::scan_raw` (a bounded, directional read
with an exclusive resume key) across both backends, and `OP_SCAN` on the
enclave proxy with the usual capability negotiation. `ScanPager` decides its
strategy once per walk, so a proxy that cannot bound a read is asked for the
range once rather than once per page.

Audit verification and listing walk through the pager instead of
materialising the keyspace.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Yaroslava Kurash <yaroslava.k@affinidi.com>

* fix(store): refuse an oversized vsock response rather than resending it

The two matchers that recognise "this response did not fit one frame"
compared `AppError::to_string()` against the raw message. `AppError::Internal`
renders as `internal error: {0}`, so the rendered form never starts with the
message it was built from, and both matchers were dead code.

Two things followed, each the opposite of what the surrounding code says it
does:

  - the connection pool fell through to its reconnect path and resent the
    request, so an enclave whose audit log had outgrown the frame cap read the
    whole prefix twice per attempt instead of refusing it once;
  - the bulk-read fallback never mapped the failure, so an operator saw
    `vsock response too large: 36869978 > 16777216` rather than being told to
    upgrade the proxy.

Found running a new enclave image against a proxy without bounded scan over a
36 MB audit log: `pnm audit verify` reported the raw error and the parent
logged a reconnect for that read. The chain-head backoff was unaffected — it
sits above the store layer — so recovery still failed closed and counted once
per attempt; it was the I/O underneath that doubled.

The prefix is now a single constant shared by the construction site and both
matchers, and recognition matches the variant's payload instead of its
rendering.

What let this through was that nothing exercised the refusal. The existing
oversized test drives `round_trip` directly and never reaches the pool's retry
decision, and a caller sees the same error whether or not the request was
resent — so the only way to see it is to count what reaches the parent. The
new pool test does that (one frame means refused, two means resent), and the
matcher tests build the error the way production raises it rather than
asserting on rendered text.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Yaroslava Kurash <yaroslava.k@affinidi.com>

* fix(audit): walk a legacy log to its end rather than fail closed at a row cap; snapshot the proxy's scan

Chain-head recovery's deep scan gave up after 20,000 non-envelope rows and
then refused every audit write to the prefix. That is the answer its own
comments rule out: no write can succeed to clear the condition, so the next
attempt walks the same rows and fails again. A pre-chain log of that size is
ordinary — one row per audited operation over the 28-day retention window — so
a VTA upgrading from before chaining (#1420) would lose its audit trail until
retention pruned it below the cap. The old full read anchored such a log at
genesis.

The deep scan now has a page size but no total cap: it walks until it finds an
envelope or reaches the end of the prefix, which is paid once, since the
envelope the next write anchors is found by every later restart's lookback.
Recovery can now fail only on a failed read, so the `exhausted` reason and the
counter's `reason` label go; the backoff tests induce a storage refusal
instead.

The enclave proxy's OP_SCAN read with a plain `range`, which can observe a
write batch half-applied. It now reads through a snapshot, as the enclave's
local backend does (#2113).

Also corrects the design note's CAP_SCAN bit (5, not 4).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(pnm): collect a room's renewal — pnm rooms offers renew, and renewals listed from vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3
body:
A community renews the room admissions a group's binding gave its members, and
lists the renewals in `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3` (trust-tasks-tf #843). Until a
surface collects one, the member's admission lapses at its old expiry. `pnm` is
now such a surface.

- `pnm rooms offers list` asks for 0.3, completed with `rooms/keys/act/0.6`, and
  prints each renewal with the command that collects it. A VTA or VTC that does
  not serve 0.3 is read at 0.2 (act 0.4), then 0.1 (act 0.3), as before; those
  carry no renewals.
- `pnm rooms offers renew --room …` stores the renewal's membership and authority
  in the member's VTA in place of the ones they renew (list 0.3 surface items
  1–3). Each existing entry is found with `vault/credentials/query` by the room

body:
feat(pnm): collect a room's renewal — pnm rooms offers renew, and renewals listed from vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3 (#2234)

A community renews the room admissions a group's binding gave its members, and
lists the renewals in `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3` (trust-tasks-tf #843). Until a
surface collects one, the member's admission lapses at its old expiry. `pnm` is
now such a surface.

- `pnm rooms offers list` asks for 0.3, completed with `rooms/keys/act/0.6`, and
  prints each renewal with the command that collects it. A VTA or VTC that does
  not serve 0.3 is read at 0.2 (act 0.4), then 0.1 (act 0.3), as before; those
  carry no renewals.
- `pnm rooms offers renew --room …` stores the renewal's membership and authority
  in the member's VTA in place of the ones they renew (list 0.3 surface items
  1–3). Each existing entry is found with `vault/credentials/query` by the room
  as issuer, then the one whose subject is the member, and the renewal is
  received under that handle. A key holder holding two authorities from one room
  acts with neither, so more than one candidate is refused with the fix. Storing
  a renewal again is harmless, so any surface may collect it first.

title: feat(vtc): choose at runtime where the community's group and room identities are published — dids.webvh_server
body:
Where a group's or a community room's `did:webvh` was published was a host
setting: `[groups] webvh_server` and `[rooms.community] webvh_server` in
`config.toml`, absent meaning this community serves the log itself. Changing it
took an edit on the host and a restart.

- `dids.webvh_server` is a runtime key (`config/patch`, `vtc/config/import`,
  the Groups page's *Where identities are published*, `vtc.config.admin`).
  Its value is `local` (this community serves each identity, at
  `/group-dids/` and `/room-dids/`) or the id of a `did:webvh` hosting server
  registered at the community's VTA. One choice covers both kinds.
- `did_hosting::live` reads it at every mint: the environment
  (`VTC_DIDS_WEBVH_SERVER`), then the stored override, then `[dids]` in
  `config.toml`. Unset, each kind's own `webvh_server` applies, as before. A
  malformed value in any layer is ignored, and a patch refuses one.
- It applies to the next identity minted. One already minted stays where it is,
  because its DID names its host. It confers no authority, so it is audited
  like any configuration change and not held for consent.

### Console
The Groups page gains *Where identities are published*, for holders of `vtc.config.admin`: this community, or a hosting server at the VTA by its id. The VTA's registered servers are not listed yet; listing them would need a VTC task asking the VTA, which is a separate change.

Locally: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, the VTC suite (3481), doctests, the console suite (1290) and tsc pass.
