title: fix(rooms): a read catches up on missed commits and room history before refusing; the portal says why a record won't open
body:
## Why

Found live in the member portal on a three-member attributed room ("Keyring integration"): records showed **"Did not open"** for every member, from both directions.

- The member who joined at epoch 3 could not open v10/v11 (sealed under epoch 2): `the epoch key chain reaches back only to 3`.
- The existing member, still at epoch 2, could not open the new member's v12 (sealed under 3): `a commit has not been delivered`.

Both are the **normal** state of any room with more than two members: every membership change leaves every other member a commit behind, and every new member starts at the epoch they joined. The only repairs were `pnm rooms keys commit --host …` and `pnm rooms keys backfill`, by hand, per member, per change. The wallet and portal never ran either, so the portal could not show records at all once a room had a third member. And the refusal came back as **`malformedRequest`**, which `rooms/keys/read/0.1` does not declare. It declares `cannotOpen`, `hostUnreachable` and `hostRefused`.

## What changes

**VTA: `rooms/keys/read` repairs before it refuses** (trust-tasks-tf #848, amending the `read/0.1` draft):
- Record newer than the epoch held: fetch the commits the host relays (`rooms/epoch/commits`) and apply them in order. Record older than the chain reaches: fetch the epoch links (as `backfill`). Then open the record again.
- The repair uses the same host, the same persona and the same `read` grant as the read, so it discloses nothing the read did not. At most once per read. Never for a removed member.
- Serialised per member, so a page opening 25 records fetches each commit once. Waiters give up after 20 s instead of queueing behind a wedged host (R1.3).
- What still won't open is `rooms/keys/read:cannotOpen` with `details.{epoch, reason, heldEpoch|earliestEpoch|removedAtEpoch}` (open/0.2's words), plus why the repair stopped.
- `read` and `backfill` now answer the declared `hostUnreachable` / `hostRefused`. Previously a host DID that didn't resolve was reported as `malformedRequest`.
- New: `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/room_catch_up.rs`.

**Member portal (`/members`):**
- Records that don't open show why: "Waiting for a room update", "Added before you joined", "Added after you left", "Community unreachable". The record panel explains each in plain words, with the agent's own message beside it.
- *Rooms from this community*: a joined room offered **two** buttons ("Open it here…" on its row, and "Share it here…" in a red "Joined …" box) that did the same thing. Now there is one action. A room already shared here gets an **Open** link. One that isn't shared yet gets "Open it here…", which asks the wallet and then goes straight to the room. The acceptance notice disappears once the room's row shows it, and it uses a neutral style (`.alert-info`) instead of the danger style.

**Docs:** `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` §6 and §11.

## Testing

- 5 new end-to-end tests against a real `room_host` with two VTAs (`room_profile_tests.rs`): behind by a commit, then caught up and opened; joined late, then history fetched and opened; concurrent reads sharing one repair; a commit the host never received giving `cannotOpen` / `notDelivered`; an unreachable host giving `hostUnreachable`.
- Portal: updated the accept→open test; added tests for the direct Open link, the notice giving way to the row, and the plain-language reason.
- A sixth test makes read `hostRefused` and backfill's `hostRefused` / `hostUnreachable` happen; the error-code census baseline shrinks by five (372 → 367).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, workspace nextest (6372 pass; two heavyweight tests timed out under full-suite load and pass alone in 53 s / 68 s), admin-ui vitest (1289) and `npm run lint`.

title: fix: creating a community group no longer fails when the VTA's mediator carries TSP
body:
`vtc/groups/create` failed against a VTA whose stack and mediator carry TSP. The
VTA refused the group's mint `malformedRequest` with: addTspService: this document
names no DIDComm mediator. Two defects met:

- The VTC asked for the group's identity without saying anything about
  transports. The `vtc-group` template carries no service: nothing delivers
  messages to a group yet. The mint now says so explicitly
  (`addMediatorService: false`, `addTspService: false`).
- The VTA turned its own default into a demand. A caller that names no
  `addTspService` gets whatever this VTA and its mediator can carry (#1652), and
  for a rendered template that answer reached `with_tsp_in_rendered_document`
  as if the caller had asked. That path refuses a document with no DIDComm
  mediator, which is right when the caller asked for `#tsp` and wrong when
  nobody did. Only an explicit request refuses now; a defaulted one mints the
  document as rendered.



Tests: the VTA renders `vtc-group` under a defaulted TSP and mints it as rendered (`a_defaulted_tsp_on_a_document_with_no_mediator_mints_as_rendered`); an explicit request on a document with no mediator is still refused. The VTC group-create test asserts the mint says `addTspService: false` and `addMediatorService: false`.

Locally: clippy `-D warnings`, the VTC suite and the workspace suite pass, apart from timing tests that failed while the Mac slept mid-run (the push-delivery set passes in full on a re-run).

title: security: a credential's proof must be made by a key of its issuer
body:
## Defect

`DTGCredential::verify_proof_with_public_key` verified the Data Integrity proof under the key the caller passed, but never checked that the proof's `verificationMethod` belongs to the credential's `issuer`. A caller that resolves the method the proof names and then trusts `issuer()` accepted a credential naming any issuer, signed by any key. `verify_grant_with_public_key` already made this check; the credential-level entry point did not.

## Fix

One private helper, `check_proof_from_issuer`, now runs after the signature in both public verification entry points:

| Entry point | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `DTGCredential::verify_proof_with_public_key` | no binding | binding |
| `verify_grant_with_public_key` | binding (inline) | same binding, shared helper |

`authority::verify_chain` and `delegation::verify_chain` check no signatures themselves (by design, documented); they rely on each link having gone through `verify_proof_with_public_key`, so they gain the binding through it. No other public function verifies a proof.

A method belongs to the issuer when:
- the DID before its `#` is exactly the issuer (`did:x:a#key-1`), or
- it is the issuer itself, with no fragment, or
- it is a bare `#fragment`, read against the issuer (previously refused by the grant path).

Comparison is verbatim (a DID URL with a query or path before the fragment is not the issuer); an empty issuer matches nothing. On the grant path the issuer may be a string or an object with an `id`.

## Compatibility

- **Not API-breaking.** `DTGCredentialError::ProofNotFromIssuer` already existed and the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`. No version bump here; CHANGELOG entry under `[Unreleased]`.
- **Behaviour change:** a credential signed with a key whose id is not a method of the issuer no longer verifies. Two unit tests signed with randomly-named keys and were given issuer-bound key ids.

## Tests

`tests/issuer_binding.rs`, each case against both entry points: another DID refused; a DID that merely extends the issuer's refused; a DID URL with a query refused; a method of the issuer accepted; the issuer itself as the method accepted; a relative `#fragment` accepted; object-form issuer bound by its `id` (accept and refuse).

Locally: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-features`, `cargo test --no-default-features`, `cargo check` on 1.95.0, `cargo package`, and both examples run.

title: Add Apache 2.0 licence for source code
body:
## What

- Adds `LICENSE` with the full Apache License 2.0 text, so GitHub detects the repo as Apache-2.0.
- Adds a **Licensing** section to `README.md` and updates the header and footer:
  - **Source code** (`tools/`, `review/*.py`, `tests/`, `.github/workflows/`, schemas and other tooling): Apache 2.0
  - **Documentation and content** (the method, `data/`, Markdown docs): CC-BY 4.0, as currently declared
  - **Third-party material** (the TRQP source snapshot in `review/examples/standalone-trqp/source/`): keeps its own ToIP licences

## Why

Until now the repo had no licence file. The only statement was "CC-BY 4.0", which isn't meant for software, and the code had no licence at all. Sibling DTGWG task forces use Apache 2.0 (`dtgwg-htx-tf`, `dtgwg-zkp-tf`). ToIP spec repos put source code under Apache 2.0 through `SOURCE_CODE.md`.

## For the TF to decide

This PR keeps CC-BY 4.0 for content because that's what the repo already declares. If the TF would rather use Apache 2.0 for everything (as htx and zkp do), that's a small README change. Contributions so far were made under CC-BY, though, so that call belongs with the contribution-governance discussion (GAP-5.1).

body:
## Purpose

Queues **Increment 3 of #17**, explicitly stacked on #20 (which is stacked on #19). No main-branch merge is requested until the earlier increments have received maintainer review.

## Changes

- Add `tools/validate_all.py`, a supported entry point composing the existing corpus and **explicitly selected** review validators. Preserve `--data`, `--risks`, `--strict` behavior and failure exit codes.
- Check method vocabulary completeness and duplicate definitions, and detect drift in the review schema's control-plane, status and resolution type enumeration.
- Add negative regression tests for vocabulary changes, duplicates, failed review validation and review omission.
- Document usage and limitations in `review/README.md`.

The method and review vocabularies represent **different semantics**. This does not combine them into a single enum or change the existing schemas, records, corpus, or APIs.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
python3 tools/validate_all.py --review review/examples/minimal-review.yaml
python3 tools/validate_all.py --review review/examples/standalone-trqp/review.yaml --risks review/examples/standalone-trqp/risks.yaml
python3 tools/validate_all.py --strict
```

**Evidence state:** Implemented, regression tests written and three author-matching DCO trailers verified via Git commit objects; automated DCO status and complete-checkout execution remain unverified. No local end-to-end run was possible through the available connector environment. GitHub CI and independent reviewer verification are required; do not interpret this text as a passing test report.

## Acceptance boundary

- [x] Existing standalone validation commands are left intact.
- [x] Combined entry point accepts only explicitly selected review records.
- [x] Vocabulary/schema drift is treated as failure, not silently accepted.
- [x] Regression tests cover negative cases for new behavior.
- [x] Usage, warning policy and exit behavior documented.
- [ ] Run all tests and both documented worked-example commands in a complete checkout.
- [ ] Verify relevant repository CI, including interaction with pending #14.
- [ ] Contributor-matching DCO trailers are present on all three rewritten commits; automated current-head DCO check is still pending/unavailable.
- [ ] Independent review and maintainer acceptance.

**Dependency:** Merge/reconcile #19 then #20, then retarget/revalidate this PR against accepted `main`. Existing review records remain the authoritative review contract. This PR does not establish target assurance, risk acceptance, or CI policy.

**Provenance:** Prepared with AI assistance for #17 Increment 3. No maintainer acceptance is implied.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.32.7
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Rooms/keys/read repairs before refusing — catches up on commits and fetches links, then cannotOpen with a reason ([#848](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/848))

A key holder misses an epoch key in two ordinary ways — behind by a commit after any
  membership change, or joined late and holding nothing older — and the member's surface
  reaches only their agent, so the agent is the one party that can repair either.

  The recipient now SHOULD, before answering cannotOpen, fetch the commits the host relays
  (rooms/epoch/commits) and apply them in order, or fetch the epoch links as backfill does,
  from the same host, as the same principal, under the same read grant; at most once per
  request, serialised per member, never for a removed principal. cannotOpen carries
  details.reason (notDelivered / beyondChain / removed) in rooms/keys/open 0.2's words.
  sideEffects becomes mutating: the room is unchanged, the recipient's key state is not.

- **voting**: Sealed and tallied-encrypted elections — trustees, encrypted casts, VTA trustee role ([#845](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/845))

* feat(voting): sealed and tallied-encrypted elections — voting/trustees/*, voting/ballot/cast-encrypted, vta/pcs/trustee/* and vta/pcs/vote-encrypted

  The encrypted secrecy levels (VTI-VOT-060 – 064). CONVENTIONS §9 fixes the
  cryptography: Ristretto255, exponential ElGamal under a threshold key, and
  Fiat–Shamir Schnorr, Chaum–Pedersen and disjunctive proofs with their domains.

  The trustees generate the election key on the board (Pedersen DKG with
  Belenios-style complaints): enrol a transport key, deal (Feldman commitments
  plus every share sealed to its recipient), confirm or complain, and a dealer
  complained of justifies by revealing the share. The key forms from the
  qualified dealers. After close, each trustee publishes partial decryptions of
  every sealed cast's KEM, or of every option's homomorphic total, with
  Chaum–Pedersen proofs; voting/trustees/status tells everyone what is left.

  voting/ballot/cast-encrypted admits a cast whose attestation binds the sealed
  payload or the encrypted ballot, the latter with 0/1 proofs per option and a
  proof that each question's count is admissible.

  vta/pcs/trustee/{enrol,deal,keys,justify,decrypt} make the trustee's VTA the
  custodian of its transport key and key share, signing only the task's own
  document as the trustee; vta/pcs/vote-encrypted is vta/pcs/vote for the
  encrypted levels. The new capability pcsTrustee / pcs-trustee is appended to
  both device/_shared Capability enums.



### Fixed

- **vtc/elections**: Create serves the encrypted levels a community certifies ([#847](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/847))

* fix(vtc/elections): create serves the encrypted levels a community certifies, and holds them to their trustee rules

  Item 3: unsupportedSecrecy names a level the community does not serve; a community serving sealed or talliedEncrypted refuses a manifest that breaks the trustee rules with invalidManifest.

title: ci(release): pin release-plz to 0.3.171 in the Release PR job
body:
## Problem

Every push to `main` since #804 fails **Release PR** (`scripts/release-pr.sh` → `release-plz update`):

```
ERROR failed to determine next versions
  0: error while building changelog
  1: Template parse error:
 --> 1:1
  |
1 | # Changelog
  | ^---
  = stack limit reached
```

so no release can be cut (runs 38940602141, 38944076398, 38971273995, 38972100560).

## Root cause

Not the repo. `taiki-e/install-action` moved from release-plz **0.3.171** to **0.3.172** between the 15:32 run (0.3.171, built changelogs fine) and the 16:11 run on 2026-10-16. The 16:11 run was the #803 release merge: nothing to release, so it never rendered a changelog — it looked green only for that reason.

0.3.172 is the first release-plz on pest **2.9.3**, which added a native-stack guard (pest-parser/pest#1212): a parse fails with "stack limit reached" when `stacker::remaining_stack()` reports under 64 KiB. install-action installs the static **`x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`** build, and on musl `stacker` measures the main thread's stack via `pthread_getattr_np`, which reports only the part mapped so far (~128 KiB), so the guard trips on the first byte of the Tera header template. This is rust-lang/stacker#155 (open).

Evidence (Docker, `rust:1.95`, on `main` 4e5d281):

| binary | result |
|---|---|
| 0.3.172 `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` | fails exactly as CI (also with `ulimit -s unlimited`, `RUST_MIN_STACK=64MiB`) |
| 0.3.172 `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` | ok — 0.31.14 bumps |
| 0.3.171 `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` | ok — 0.31.14 bumps, changelogs for #804–#807 |
| 0.3.172 on macOS | ok |

## Fix

Pin the Release PR job's install to `release-plz@0.3.171` (still installed and checksum-verified by install-action), with a comment saying why and when to unpin. The publish job is unaffected — `release-plz/action@v0.5.131` installs its own pinned 0.3.160.

## After merge

The merge itself is a push to `main`, so the Release PR job re-runs and should open the 0.31.14 Release PR.

title: feat(rooms/keys/profile): a room's own profile — name and description sealed inside the room, readable only by its members
body:
## What

A room's own **profile** — name, optional description, tags and one emoji — that lives **inside the room**, sealed on `attributed`/`private` like every record, readable by every member (including later joiners and `fromJoin` rooms) and never by the host on a sealed tier.

| Spec | Version | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `rooms/_shared` | 0.1 (in place, draft, as #804) | `RoomProfile`, `RoomProfileStatement`; `SealedRecordBody.roomProfile` |
| `rooms/keys/profile/read` | **0.1 new** | key holder finds, fetches, verifies, returns newest accepted profile |
| `rooms/keys/profile/write` | **0.1 new** | key holder signs as member, seals, puts; clear = retract; epoch-advance re-write rule |
| `vtc/rooms/community/create` | **0.3** | VTA writes label/description as the profile; community authority = admin+write+curate; `roomProfile` in response |
| `vtc/rooms/community/update` | **0.2** | re-writes the profile when label/description change; `roomProfile` in response |
| `rooms/owner/group/{add 0.2, remove 0.2, renew 0.1}` | editorial | non-normative pointer to the re-write rule |
| `vtc/_shared` 0.1 | editorial | `RoomLabel`/`RoomDescription` say where they now go |

## Design, and the alternatives

**Location: a per-epoch derived key, not a well-known one.** `profile_key(E) = base64url(HKDF-SHA256(storage_key(E), info="openvtc/room/profile/v1"‖roomId‖u64be(E))[0..16])` — 22 characters, the shape of any random key, so the family's "sealed keys MUST be opaque" rule holds and the host cannot tell which record names the room. A new member finds it knowing only the room and the epoch. Open rooms (no storage key, nothing hidden) use the fixed key `room-profile`, with the signed body as `cleartext.body`.
- *Rejected — fixed key `profile` with existing `records/put` + `keys/read`:* tells the host which record is the room's name, when it changes, who changed it (attributed), its rough length, and makes withholding/rolling back the name a one-line policy. Violates the opaque-key MUST.
- *Rejected — random key, found by opening every record:* linear cost for every new member.
- *Rejected — in credentials, the host record, `rooms/owner/register`:* all host-visible; register explicitly forbids a name.
- *Rejected — signed by the room DID:* every change needs the room key, curators excluded, and on `attributed` the host records the presenting member as author, contradicting a room-signed body.

**Why two new tasks (`rooms/keys/profile/read|write`) rather than none.** On a sealed tier the location is derived from the storage key, which never leaves the key holder — so a client cannot even find the record without the key holder. And the profile's authorization is a chain check readers must do (below), which belongs with the keys, not in a wallet or portal page. One call each instead of a key-disclosure call + read + client-side chain verification.

**Who may write.** A host stores the record under `write` (it cannot tell the profile apart), so **readers** decide: the statement carries the author's authority chain, and readers MUST verify it (≤8 links, issuer-signed links, rooted in the room, no widening, leaf = `author`) confers **`curate` or `admin`**, valid at the signed `issuedAt`, with `issuedAt` within [updatedAt − 1h, updatedAt + 5m] of the host's record, plus the `SealedRecordBody` author-signature/location/attributed-author rules. A profile failing any check is ignored and reported (`rejected`), so a member with only `write` can overwrite the record but cannot rename the room.

**Which one is authoritative.** One record per key ⇒ one per epoch; the reader walks from its current epoch down and takes the **newest accepted**; a `retracted` record (curate-gated at the host) means deliberately cleared and stops the walk.

**Revocation (#804).** Not retroactive: a profile written while its author held the standing stays valid after removal/lapse/room reset. Backdating needs host collusion (the `updatedAt` window), a revoked party cannot write at all, and removal advances the epoch, after which the owner re-writes the profile anyway. A reader holding a `RevocationList` refuses a profile whose chain was revoked at or before `issuedAt`.

**Epochs / `fromJoin`.** A key holder that advances a sealed room's epoch (add/remove/renew, any version) SHOULD read the profile **before** the advance (a `fromJoin` holder can't open it after) and re-write it under the new epoch afterwards, as its principal; never failing or rolling back the advance; never retracting the earlier one (history; retracting would link the two for the host). Readers without one get `absent`/`stale` and fall back to the offer label.

**Community-owned rooms.** create 0.3 / update 0.2 relax item 8 exactly: label → `name`, description → `description` go to the community's own VTA in `rooms/keys/profile/write` and into the room sealed; still never the host record, credentials, register; **tags never** (admin filing). Profile-write failure doesn't fail the task (`roomProfile: pending`, retried). Rooms made with create ≤0.2 get their profile on the first update 0.2, after re-issuing the community authority with `write`+`curate`.

**Privacy.** Padding to 1 KiB multiples; emoji is text, never a fetched icon/URL (would be a tracking pixel per member). Residual leak: a host can *guess* the profile from pattern (owner writes one right after each advance) but cannot read it and can do nothing to it it couldn't do to any record. Readers render as plain text, never instructions.

## Implementation follow-ups (VTI)
- **VTA** (`vta-service`): serve `rooms/keys/profile/read` + `write` (HKDF location, chain embed + verify, padding, version-race retry → `contended`); the epoch-advance re-write in group/add, remove, renew; accept `roomProfile` in sealed bodies and hide profile records from `keys/read`/`browse` surfaces; classify both tasks in `vta_sdk::retry_safety`.
- **VTC** (`vtc-service`): create 0.3 / update 0.2 — community authority admin+write+curate, profile write via its VTA, `roomProfile` status, pending retry; first-update profile for older rooms.
- **vtc-client / pnm / cnm**: SDK methods for both tasks; `pnm rooms profile {show,set,clear}`; show room names in listings.
- **Browser plugin / portal**: show the profile in room lists via the wallet, render as text, surface `rejected` (somebody tried to rename the room) and `stale`.

## Checks run locally
`npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings` (all four languages agree), Rust conformance tests for the new/changed specs (87 passed), `go build`/`vet`, `tsc`, `dart analyze`, `cargo fmt --check`.

title: feat(rooms/keys/label): a member's own private name, description, notes and tags for a room they hold
body:
## Problem

A member holding several data rooms can tell them apart only by names other parties gave them: the room's own profile, which is drafted separately on `spec/room-profile` (a sealed in-room record that curators write and members read), or the label on a community's offer. Failing those, they have the DID. Those names belong to whoever wrote them. They may be missing or generic, or written for an audience the member is not part of. Nothing let a member keep **their own** name for a room.

A second problem sits next to it. `rooms/keys/list` 0.1 has no member field. A person who holds one room as two personas (their own place, and a seat they hold for an organisation) gets two entries with nothing to say whose each one is. VTI carries the member in `ext["org.openvtc.rooms"].held` to cope (VTI #2161), and that PR noted a spec field as the follow-up.

## Change

- **`rooms/keys/label` 0.1 (new):** sets, changes or removes the member's **personal label** for one room they hold, with these fields:
  - `label`: one line, up to 128 characters
  - `description`: up to 1000 characters
  - `notes`: up to 4000 characters
  - `tags`: 1 to 16 tags, each up to 32 characters, in any script

  Rules:
  - The label is kept by the member's key holder and keyed by **room and member**, so each persona has its own.
  - It is plain text. Line breaks are allowed only in `description` and `notes`, and no other control characters are allowed anywhere.
  - Proof and `issuedAt` are REQUIRED. The task is `mutating`, ingests `personal` data, and is retained `durable`.
- **`rooms/keys/list` 0.2:**
  - Each entry names its `member` (REQUIRED), giving one entry per room and member.
  - Entries cover only the members the caller may act as, and this is now normative.
  - A new `includePersonal` flag, off by default, returns an optional `personal` object on each entry.
- **`rooms/_shared/0.1/personal-label` (new):** `PersonalLabel` and the types for each field.
- Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings regenerated.

The two specs stay distinct from the room profile. A **profile** is one room's name for itself: curators write it and every member reads it. A **personal label** is one member's name for one room: that member writes it and nobody else ever sees it.

## Design decisions and the alternatives

**Where the label lives: the member's key holder (VTA), next to the group state for (room, member).**
- *In the room*, as a profile field: shared with every member, which is the opposite of what is wanted. That is the other PR's job.
- *At the community*, as part of the offer label: it would tell the community what the member thinks of its room, and the community has no reason to know.
- *In the vault (`vault/upsert`)*: vault entries are context-scoped secrets with `targets`, not keyed by room and member. Their lifecycle would not follow the room's state, and storing a name as a secret would be misleading.
- *Client-local storage (wallet or extension)*: not shared across a member's devices and clients (pnm, wallet, mobile), and not backed up. The VTA already holds per-room, per-member state and is the member's custodian.

**How it is read: inside `rooms/keys/list` 0.2, not a separate get/list.** Every screen that shows rooms already calls `list`. Putting the label on the entry gives a client one round trip and no ID join, and rooms are bounded by how many a person is in, so the response stays small. A separate `label/get` plus `label/list` would add two tasks and a join for no extra capability. `includePersonal` is **off by default** so that a caller that does not need labels, or will pass the list on (a wallet answering a portal), never receives them. That matches the rule that absence means the most restrictive reading. Adding `member` to the entry is part of the same bump: a label keyed by (room, member) cannot be written back without it, and it standardises VTI's `ext` stop-gap.

**How it is written: one task, `rooms/keys/label`, with patch semantics.**
- Each field given replaces the stored value, an absent field is unchanged, and `removeLabel`, `removeDescription`, `removeNotes` and `removeTags` each remove one field. This follows the `const: true` pattern of `vtc/rooms/community/update` 0.1. A nullable field cannot distinguish "unchanged" from "remove" in libraries that map both to `None`. `dependentSchemas` forbids giving a field and removing it in the same request.
- Removing the last field removes the label. There is no empty label, so `PersonalLabel` has `minProperties: 2`.
- The slug is `rooms/keys/label` rather than `label/set`: one verb, and there is no `get` to sit beside it.
- *Rejected: full replacement plus a revision precondition.* A revision needs tombstones (the ABA problem after a remove), costs every client a read before every write, and guards against a race between a person and themselves. With patch semantics, renaming a room on a phone does not clobber notes written on a laptop. The spec says "No optimistic concurrency" explicitly.
- *Rejected: `anyOf` for "at least one change".* typify turns a top-level `anyOf` into an untagged enum with `deny_unknown_fields`. That cannot hold a label that has both `label` and `description`, which I checked in the generated Rust. `minProperties` is used instead (counting `roomId`/`member`, or `updatedAt` on the response), as #805 does, and the one gap it leaves (a request whose only extra member is `ext`) is a prose `malformedRequest` (Recipient item 3).

**`member` is REQUIRED on `label`.** It is never inferred. A label written under the wrong persona would be shown in the wrong context, and with list 0.2 the client always has the member at hand. So there is no ambiguity error.

**Authorization.**
- The caller must act as the member, which is the same act-scope question every `rooms/keys/*` task asks.
- Delegates holding a chain from `rooms/keys/present` get `permissionDenied` (mirroring `rooms/keys/act` item 3): a delegate is given narrow authority in one room and does not become the member.
- `notHeld` is one answer for both "no group state for this room as this member" and "not a member you act as". A client scoped to one context therefore cannot learn whether another persona holds the room.

**Privacy.**
- The key holder MUST NOT send a label to the room, host, owner or a community, or put it in anything it completes, signs or seals (`act`, `seal`, `present`). It MUST NOT log the text or write it to an audit record.
- A client that receives a label is bound by the same rule.
- A wallet SHOULD NOT hand a label to a website (for example a member portal) unless the member chose to show it to that site, and SHOULD call `list` without `includePersonal` when answering one.

**Retention.**
- The label is kept, protected and backed up with the group state for that room and member, and discarded when that state is discarded.
- It is **not** discarded when the member is removed from the room, when the room lapses, or when its host or owner changes. A room the member can still open but no longer write in is the one they most need to recognise.
- No history of earlier values is kept.

**Display precedence (informative):** personal label, then the room's profile name, then the community's offer label, then the DID. A surface should keep the room's own name reachable next to a personal one, so a member can see that the room was renamed after they labelled it, and should mark the personal label as "your name for it".

**Retry safety:** `label` is idempotent. A repeated request answers `changed: false`, so it can be retried as it is. `list` is a read.

## Versions touched

- `rooms/keys/label/0.1`: new
- `rooms/keys/list/0.2`: new version; 0.1 unchanged
- `rooms/_shared/0.1/personal-label.schema.json`: new shared file

## What implementers must do (follow-ups, no VTI code in this PR)

- **VTA:**
  - Store the label per (room, member) next to the group state, in a backed-up keyspace, and discard it with that state.
  - Serve `rooms/keys/label/0.1`: act-scope check, `notHeld` with no difference in answer between its two causes, delegate refusal, patch semantics, `changed`, no logging of the text.
  - Serve `rooms/keys/list/0.2` with `member` and `includePersonal`, still answering 0.1. `held[i].member` in `ext` can be retired once clients move to 0.2.
- **SDK (`vta-sdk`):**
  - Typed `rooms_keys_label` and `rooms_keys_list(include_personal)` built on the generated types.
  - Classify `rooms/keys/label` as idempotent in `vta_sdk::retry_safety`.
- **pnm:**
  - `pnm rooms keys label <room> --member <did> [--label …] [--description …] [--notes …] [--tag …] [--remove-…]`.
  - `pnm rooms keys list` shows the personal label, and the member, per entry.
- **Browser plugin (wallet):**
  - Show and edit personal labels in the rooms view, preferring them as described above.
  - Call `list` **without** `includePersonal` when a portal page asks for rooms.
  - Never pass a label to a page unless the member opted in for that site.

title: fix(vtc/directory/images/upload): tooLarge also refuses a picture beyond the decoding bound
body:
images/upload declared `tooLarge` for `data` that decodes to more than 262144 bytes, and item 2 refuses it before decoding. But the payload schema already bounds `data` to exactly 262144 bytes, so a conforming community could never send the code. The schema answers malformedRequest first.

The bound that matters is the other one. A PNG of a few kilobytes can claim tens of thousands of pixels across, which is a decompression bomb, and nothing in the specification told a community to stop it. Item 2 now requires a community to bound what it decodes, the pixels a picture may claim and the memory its decoding may take, and to refuse a picture beyond either with `tooLarge`. The code's meaning says the same.

No schema change; the generated Rust carries the new meaning in its documentation.

`npm run validate` and `check-bindings` pass.

title: feat(vtc/rooms/memberships): list — every surface shows a member the same rooms, and finishes an acceptance any other began
body:
## The problem

A member reaches the rooms their community owns from several surfaces: the community's member portal (through the browser wallet), `pnm`, and OpenVTC. Each surface could see only what `vtc/rooms/offers/list` shows: offers open now, or accepted within the repeat window. Two things went wrong:

- **A room accepted in one surface vanished from the others** once the offer aged out of the list. No surface could say "you joined this", "you were removed", or "you accepted but your agent never joined".
- **An acceptance begun in one surface could not be finished in another.** Each surface asked the key holder for a KeyPackage with `rooms/keys/key-package/0.1`, which mints a new one every time. A repeated `vtc/rooms/offers/accept` with a different KeyPackage is `alreadyAccepted`. The Welcome the community kept for the first KeyPackage could never be used, because the key holder had overwritten its private half.

Surfaces worked around this by keeping their own record of acceptances in progress (the wallet had one in browser storage). That is precisely the one place they disagree.

## What changed

- **`vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1`** (new). The community's own record of the caller's admissions to rooms it owns, in every state (`offered`, `admitted` or `removed`), for as long as the community keeps the record. It carries no credentials; those are still collected with `offers/list` while an offer is open.
  - `repeatAcceptUntil` says, on a sealed room, until when the community keeps the Welcome.
  - The spec defines how a surface combines this record with the key holder's `rooms/keys/list`, so every surface derives the same standing: *offered*, *joined*, *unfinished*, *needs re-admission*, *removed*.
  - It forbids a surface from keeping its own record of acceptance.
- **`rooms/keys/key-package/0.2`**. A repeated request for the same room, member and invitation returns the outstanding KeyPackage (`alreadyMinted: true`, original `expiresAt`) instead of minting another. Concurrent requests get the same one. `invitation` and `expiresAt` are now required.
  - Mint, accept and Welcome now each answer a repeat with their first answer, so any surface can finish an acceptance another began.
- **`rooms/keys/act/0.5`**. Adds `vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1` to the table on the offer types' terms: no presentation inserted, `issuer` REQUIRED (the DID the community addresses its offers to), resolved by Recipient item 2b. It widens the `type` pattern to admit `vtc/rooms/memberships/`, and nothing else of the `vtc` family. An acceptance's KeyPackage may come from `key-package` 0.1 or 0.2.
- **`vtc/_shared/0.1/community-room`**: a new `RoomMembership` definition.
- **`vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.2`** and **`offers/accept/0.1`**: informative cross-links only. `accept` gains a subsection on finishing from another surface. The wire is unchanged (§5.2 editorial).
- **Bindings regenerated** (Rust, TS, Go, Dart): additive modules, plus index and conformance entries.

## Versioning (SPEC §5.2)

- **`act/0.5`, not an edit to `0.4`** (#810). The closed table admits a type a conforming `0.4` recipient refuses with `typeNotActable`. That is wire behaviour, so it gets a MINOR increment, exactly as `0.3` (#797) and `0.4` (#810) did.
- **`key-package/0.2`, not an edit to `0.1`**. A repeated request now returns the same KeyPackage instead of a new one, and the response gains required members.

## Checks

- `npm run build`
- `npm run check-bindings`: 823 specs; TS, Rust, Go and Dart agree.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features --test conformance`: 2,097 passed.
- TS `tsc --noEmit`
- `go build ./...`
- `dart analyze` on the new modules.

## Downstream (after this is merged and released)

Each downstream branch is built and tested against a local copy of this branch. Each will drop its local path dependency once this is released.

- **VTI** (`OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure`):
  - The VTC serves `memberships/list/0.1`.
  - The VTA serves `key-package/0.2`, plus `act/0.4` (the #810 follow-up) and `act/0.5`.
  - `pnm rooms memberships` is added.
  - The member portal shows a room in each standing.
- **OpenVTC**: a Rooms panel that reads the same record.
- **Browser wallet**: reads the record, and drops its own record of acceptances in progress.

title: feat(vtc/community/theme): show and update — a community's own stylesheet for its console and member portal
body:
A community could set an accent colour and a logo (vtc/community/branding),
and nothing else about how its pages look. Administrators want to restyle
their console and member portal at run time, without the operator-only
admin_ui directory mode.

vtc/community/theme/update/0.1 (new, draft):
- An administrator replaces one stylesheet; the empty string removes it.
  Proof and issuedAt REQUIRED; audited by digest, never by text.
- `dryRun: true` checks and answers with what would be stored, storing
  nothing, so a client can preview a theme exactly as stored.
- The theme profile (P1-P8): design tokens on :root (light/dark), plus a
  small set of cosmetic properties on ordinary elements — colours,
  gradients, bounded borders/radius, font family/weight. No url()/@import/
  @font-face (a theme loads nothing), no !important, no escapes or `<`, and
  nothing that can move, size, hide, overlay or add content.
  `outsideProfile` names the line, column and profile item broken.
- maxDocumentBytes 48 KiB both ways, for a 32 KiB stylesheet.

vtc/community/theme/show/0.1 (new, draft):
- Proof OPTIONAL and answerable to an unidentified caller: sign-in pages
  draw the theme before the visitor holds any identity.
- Client requirements: re-check the profile before applying; render every
  surface where a person decides, approves, consents, signs or is warned
  in structural isolation from the theme; mark that a custom theme is on.

Why no second-administrator consent: the profile and the isolation
together mean a theme cannot change what another administrator is asked
to approve, so it stays an ordinary configuration write.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

title: feat(vtc/rooms/offers): list 0.3 — renewals of the admissions a member holds; rooms/keys/act 0.6 completes it; groups bindings refuse an unserved kind
body:
A group's room binding says the community renews each admission it made "while
the member stays in the group". Nothing defined how an already-admitted member
receives renewed credentials. `offers/list` carries only an offer's three
credentials, and `memberships/list` carries none by design. So an admission
could only be carried past its `validUntil` by an administrator removing and
re-admitting the member.

- vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3: the response gains `renewals`. For an admission the
  caller holds, it lists the room's fresh membership and authority credentials,
  granting the same actions until a later `validUntil`. `renews` names the
  expiry of the ones they replace. There is no invitation: a renewal is never a
  second way in.
  The community issues a renewal through the room's key holder before
  recording it, and lists only the latest one per admission. A renewal stays
  listed on the first page until what it renews expires, the member is removed,
  or a later renewal supersedes it. The community records the renewed
  `validUntil` as the admission's own.
  A surface stores a renewal in place of the credentials it renews, never
  beside them, and treats storing it twice as success. It never accepts a
  renewal.
- vtc/_shared/0.1/community-room: `Renewal` and `RenewalCredentials`, additive.
- rooms/keys/act/0.6: the table adds vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3, in the offer
  types' row and on their terms. 0.5's table is closed, so a 0.5 key holder
  refuses 0.3 with `typeNotActable`.
- vtc/groups/bindings/add/0.1: item 6 renews a room binding's admissions
  through offers/list 0.3. New code `kindNotServed` (item 7): a community that
  serves room bindings only may refuse a grants or role binding after item 1,
  and never records a binding it does not provision.
- vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1: a row for an admitted room with a renewal
  listed, which the surface stores before anything else it offers.
- RoomBindingSpec's description points at the renewal path.



Regenerated Rust, TS, Go and Dart. Locally: `npm run validate`, `check-bindings`, `check-enum-append-only`, and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` pass.

VTI follow-up: the VTC serves offers/list 0.3, issues renewals and serves room bindings; the VTA serves rooms/keys/act 0.6. Member surfaces (portal through the wallet, OpenVTC) then collect renewals.

title: feat(vta/pcs/voter): the engine signs the voter's requests to the community as the member — register's ticketDocument, and voter/read
body:
A voter's membership DID usually lives in their VTA, so a client could not sign vtc/elections/tickets/issue as the member without a general signing oracle. The request may now name `member`; the engine then also returns `ticketDocument`, the tickets/issue request already signed as that DID for `authentication`, with exactly this response's payload, to send unchanged. The engine signs only that document type with only that payload — `member` confers no other signature — under pcsVoter and standing to act as the member, as vta/pcs/vote signs the cast.

On a repeat the engine returns the document it kept for that member, unchanged, so the community answers a resend with its first answer rather than as a second request. New code `memberNotHeld`, checked before anything is allocated. Additive: both members optional; trust-tasks-rs semver-checks report no update required.

title: ci: enum values are append-only — an insertion is a breaking release for the whole core group
body:
Inserting a value into an existing JSON Schema `enum` anywhere but its end shifts the implicit discriminant of every generated Rust variant after it. `cargo-semver-checks` reports this as `enum_no_repr_variant_discriminant_changed`. The eight Rust crates share one release-plz `version_group`, so one insertion makes all of them a **breaking minor**, which every downstream workspace can then only adopt in lockstep.

That has now happened twice:

- **#819** inserted `signDocument` into device `Capability` and made **0.32.0** breaking. The release run's log shows `ExternalAccountsManage 18 -> 19`, `PcsVetter 20 -> 21` and so on.
- **#834** inserted `pcsVoter` the same way and would have made **0.33.0** breaking, until #835 appended it instead and the release went out as 0.32.3.

## The check

`scripts/check-enum-append-only.mjs` walks every changed `specs/**/*.json` against its merge base with the PR's base commit. It requires each existing enum's values to be an unchanged prefix of the new array. Removing, reordering or inserting a value fails with the diff and the fix. New files and new enums are unconstrained.

It runs on every pull request (`rust.yml` → *enum values are append-only*) and locally as `npm run check-enum-append-only`.

## Tested

- A clean tree passes.
- A temporary commit inserting a value before `pcsVetter` fails, naming `/$defs/Capability/enum` and the inserted value.
- A temporary commit appending after `pcsVoter` passes.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.25` → `0.8.26` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix(sign-in): match the VTA's PIN and phone approval as it landed
body:
Follow-up to #367, which was merged before these changes. This brings the plugin in line with the VTA as it landed in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2228 (`docs/02-vta/wallet-sign-in-uv-keys.md`).

## Changes
- **Approver listing is a heartbeat, not a new task.** The wallet sends `device/heartbeat` with `ext["org.openvtc.uv-approvers"] = {}` and reads `{approvers: [{did, displayName?, formFactor?}]}` from the response's `ext`. The invented `TASK_DEVICE_UV_APPROVERS` URI is removed.
- **Recovery from the VTA's summary.** Every heartbeat response carries `ext["org.openvtc.uv-key"]`: `kind`, `salt`, `iterations`, `failedAttempts`, `lockedUntil` (null when not locked), and `approver` for a phone. Core reads it with `readUvKeySummary`.
  - When `pnm/uv-pin/v1/<vtaDid>` is missing, the wallet fetches it with a heartbeat, writes `{salt, iterations}` back and carries on. It no longer tells the person to re-register.
  - When the local `pnm/uv-key/enrolled/<vtaDid>` record is missing, the summary fills it in. This applies to the sign-in review and to the Settings rows.
- **Errors.**
  - `oobUvPinWrong` with `attemptsRemaining: 0` and `lockedUntil` (the wrong guess that imposes the lock) is shown as locked, not as a count.
  - Heartbeat refusals now covered: `uvPinWrong`, `uvKeyLocked`, `uvKeyChangeProofRequired`, `uvKeyChangeProofInvalid`, and `uvApproverNotPermitted`. The last one is matched on the message text, since the VTA puts it only there. Each has a plain message, kept in a new shared module, `sign-in-uv-messages.ts`, that the window and Settings both use.
- **Approver wording.** Shown when no phone is listed and on `uvApproverNotPermitted`: "Your phone can't approve for this browser yet. Connect the OpenVTC app on your phone to the same agent, then ask an administrator of the agent to make that phone this browser's approver." The README explains the designation rule and points to the VTA doc.
- **First-time PIN key derived once.** The enrolment hands K to the first proof. The flow wipes it once the grant is signed, and the enrolment wipes it if enrolment fails.

## Tests
- `npx tsc -b`: clean.
- core `npm test`: 1065 pass.
- extension `npm test`: 1290 pass.
- `npm run build`: clean.
- New tests cover the heartbeat-based listing, the summary (including `lockedUntil: null`), the new refusal codes, salt and record recovery, the lock on a wrong PIN, single derivation with K wiped, and the not-permitted message in both the window and Settings.

title: feat(vta)!: vtaPin and remoteApprover UV keys for wallet sign-in
body:
## Problem

A browser wallet with no PRF passkey (Linux Chromium without a security key, password managers that offer passkeys without PRF) cannot approve a wallet sign-in. The VTA signs an `auth/oob/grant` only on the device's UV-key approval, and the browser's only UV kind was `prfSealedKey`, sealed under a PRF passkey.

## What changed

Two new UV key kinds, enrolled like the others (`org.openvtc.uv-key` on `device/register` / `device/heartbeat`) and checked in `oob_sign_in::verify_uv_decision`. `hardwareKey`, `webauthn` and `prfSealedKey` behave exactly as before.

### `vtaPin` — a PIN the VTA checks

- Enrolment `{ kind: "vtaPin", salt (16..64 B), iterations (600 000..10 000 000), verifier (32 B), hardwareBacked: false, biometricGated: false }`. The VTA stores `K` and checks HMACs; it runs no PBKDF2.
- Approval `ext["org.openvtc.uv-consent"] = { decision, pinProof }`: the decision signed by the device's transport key, no `evidence`; `pinProof = HMAC-SHA256(K, "org.openvtc.uv-pin/v1|" + D)`, compared in constant time (`hmac` `verify_slice`).
- Guess limit (`operations/uv_pin.rs`): 5 consecutive wrong → 15 min lock; each wrong proof after a lock expires re-locks, doubled (15 m, 30 m, 1 h … 24 h cap); while locked the proof is not checked; a correct proof resets count and doubling. Persisted in the ACL keyspace at `uv-pin:<did>` (outside `acl:`), keyed to the enrolment instant, every update a conditional write (CAS) so concurrent guesses all count.
- Refusals: `oobUvPinWrong` `{ code, attemptsRemaining }` (+ `lockedUntil` on the proof that imposed a lock), `oobUvLocked` `{ code, lockedUntil }` (unix seconds). A malformed proof is `oobUvInvalid` and not counted.
- Replacing a `vtaPin` with any key via heartbeat needs `ext["org.openvtc.uv-key-change"].pinProof = HMAC(K_old, "org.openvtc.uv-pin/v1|change|" + sha256hex(JCS(new enrolment as sent)))`, on the same limit: `device:uvKeyChangeProofRequired`, `device:uvPinWrong` (`attemptsRemaining`), `device:uvKeyLocked` (`lockedUntil`), `device:uvKeyChangeProofInvalid`, all in `details`.
- Summary (`device/list`, register response, and now every heartbeat response under `ext["org.openvtc.uv-key"]`): `kind, salt, iterations, failedAttempts, lockedUntil` (+ the existing claims). The verifier is a `PinVerifier` newtype whose `Debug` prints `<redacted>`; it is in no summary, response, audit row or log.
- Audit: `device.uv-pin.failed`, `device.uv-pin.locked` (counts and instants only).

### `remoteApprover` — approve on the phone

- Enrolment `{ kind: "remoteApprover", approver: <DID>, hardwareBacked: false, biometricGated: false }`.
- **Approver rule** (`operations::device::uv_approver_eligible`): not the device itself; a live ACL entry; **designated by the operator** — the browser entry's `stepUpApprover` (set by another admin; self-modification is refused) or a member of an approver set (super-admin only); not created by the browser; and if it has a device binding, an active mobile/desktop companion. A browser that is a context admin can create ACL entries and register them as phones, so "is in the ACL" or "is a registered phone" alone is forgeable; the operator's designation is not. Re-checked on every approval. Refusal: `device:uvApproverNotPermitted`.
- Listing candidates: no new Trust Task URI (the registry has no spec for one, and the parity harness forbids unspecced URIs), so it rides heartbeat: request `ext["org.openvtc.uv-approvers"] = {}`, response `ext["org.openvtc.uv-approvers"] = { approvers: [{ did, displayName?, formFactor? }] }`.
- Approval `ext["org.openvtc.uv-consent"] = { "remote": true }`: the VTA raises a task-consent request **bound to the enrolled approver** (`PendingTaskConsent::bound_approver`, new) for exactly this grant digest, signs a normal `task-consent/request/0.1` (taskType = grant type, requester = browser DID, origin, subject = persona, one `signIn` effect naming origin, browser name and expiry) and pushes it with `push_signed_requests`. Refusal `oobUvPending` `{ code, matchCode, expiresAt }` (unix seconds); polling re-reads the same request and never re-pushes. The phone's existing `task-consent/decision/0.1` goes through the existing `handle_decision`, which for a bound request accepts only the bound approver; approval mints the usual single-use grant, which the next poll consumes **after** every other check passes. Decline → `oobUvDeclined` (sticky for the grant), lapse (120 s, capped at `notAfter`) → `oobUvExpired`. A `BoundRequestMark` (`bound:` rows, swept by the existing task-consent sweeper) remembers raised/declined so a late poll never re-asks.

## Security notes

- vtaPin threat model: a copied browser profile holds the transport key but cannot guess offline; every guess is counted by the VTA. Malware in the browser can capture the PIN; it is recorded as its own kind for policy and audit.
- remoteApprover: approval happens behind the phone's biometric; a decision for another digest or from another DID does not satisfy a request (tested).
- **Pre-existing, unchanged:** `device/heartbeat` lets a device replace a `hardwareKey` / `prfSealedKey` / `webauthn` (and now `remoteApprover`) UV key with no proof from the current key. Only `vtaPin` now requires the current factor. Documented in the new doc.
- TEE note: the PIN guard row and the bound marks live outside the integrity manifest (as the existing `oob-grant:` replay markers do), so an untrusted enclave host could roll them back.

## Docs

New `docs/02-vta/wallet-sign-in-uv-keys.md` (all five kinds, wire shapes, errors, lockout, approver rule, threat models); `task-consent.md` gains *Requests bound to one approver*; `docs/README.md` index.

## Tests

New integration tests in `vta-service/tests/it/vault_sign_in_oob.rs`: PIN enrol + approve (once); PIN decision must be the device's own and carry a proof; wrong PIN `attemptsRemaining`, reset on success; 5 wrong → 15 min lock, refused unchecked while locked, re-lock doubles to 30 min then 1 h after expiry (expiry simulated by moving the persisted `lockedUntil`), success resets the doubling; verifier never in register/list/heartbeat/refusal/audit; heartbeat change needs `pinProof` (missing / wrong / for another key / correct; same counter); locked PIN cannot be replaced; remoteApprover enrolment refuses self, unknown DID, undesignated ACL entry, malformed DID, an entry the browser created; approver-set members allowed; picker lists exactly the designated phone; pending → idempotent poll (same `matchCode`, one request) → phone `task-consent/decision/0.1` approve → browser retry signs → single use (`oobGrantReplayed`, nothing re-asked) → audit records `remoteApprover` + phone DID; decline (sticky) and lapse (`oobUvExpired`, late decision `noPending`); another ACL device's decision (`not a member`), wrong digest (`noPending`), crossed challenge refused, approving one grant's request signs that grant only.
Unit tests: SDK validation for both kinds and Debug redaction; lock arithmetic; approver rule; bound-request store (idempotent raise, sticky denial, sweep, withdraw); the pushed request verifies with `vta_sdk::task_consent::ConsentRequest::verify` under the VTA DID, addressed to the phone, with the browser's match code and a readable `signIn` effect.

Run locally:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — ok
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — ok; plus the three reduced-feature `vta-service` clippy builds CI runs — ok
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-service -p vta-sdk -p vti-common -p vta-policy` — 4326 run; all pass after marking two new enums `#[non_exhaustive]` (census) — `audit_coverage::every_consequential_task_records_an_audit_entry` hit the 300 s nextest timeout under full parallel load on macOS and passes alone in 55 s
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk -p vti-common --doc` — ok

## Not done

- No new Trust Task URI for listing approvers (heartbeat ext instead; see above).
- `oob-grant:` replay markers and `uv-pin:` rows are not swept (bounded by device/grant count).

title: feat(vta)!: vtaPin and remoteApprover UV keys for wallet sign-in (#2228)
body:
feat(vta)!: vtaPin and remoteApprover UV keys for wallet sign-in (#2228)

Browser wallets without a PRF passkey could not approve auth/oob/grant.
Two new UV key kinds:

- vtaPin: the browser enrols K = PBKDF2(PIN) as verifier; a grant is
  approved by a transport-key decision plus HMAC-SHA256(K,
  "org.openvtc.uv-pin/v1|" + D), checked in constant time against a
  persisted, CAS-updated guess limit (5 wrong -> 15 min lock, doubling
  to 24 h, reset on success). Refusals oobUvPinWrong (attemptsRemaining)
  and oobUvLocked (lockedUntil). Replacing a PIN on heartbeat requires
  ext org.openvtc.uv-key-change.pinProof. The verifier is never returned,
  audited or logged (PinVerifier redacts Debug).
- remoteApprover: the grant is approved on the member's phone. The VTA
  raises a task-consent request bound to the enrolled approver and the
  grant digest (PendingTaskConsent::bound_approver), pushes the signed
  task-consent/request/0.1, and answers oobUvPending (matchCode,
  expiresAt) until the phone's task-consent/decision/0.1 approves;
  oobUvDeclined / oobUvExpired otherwise. The approver must be
  designated by the operator (the device's stepUpApprover or an
  approver-set member), not created by the device. Candidates are
  listed via heartbeat ext org.openvtc.uv-approvers.

Breaking: new public fields on vti_common::task_consent::PendingTaskConsent
(bound_approver) and on OobDeps / UvApproval.

title: feat(sign-in): approve wallet sign-ins with a PIN or on your phone
body:
Browser wallets with no usable PRF passkey (Linux Chromium without a security key; 1Password, which can't answer an extension's WebAuthn calls) couldn't approve a wallet sign-in. This adds two more kinds of the device's user-verification (UV) key, `vtaPin` and `remoteApprover`, on the shared wire contract.

**Depends on the VTA PR implementing the same contract.** Plugin and VTA cut over together, so there are no compatibility shims.

## Wire (plugin side)
- **vtaPin**
  - Enrolment: `org.openvtc.uv-key` `{kind:"vtaPin", salt, iterations: 600000, verifier: K, hardwareBacked:false, biometricGated:false}`, where `K = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(utf8(NFC(pin)), salt, 600000, 32)`. Derived with WebCrypto.
  - Approval: `org.openvtc.uv-consent` `{decision, pinProof}`. The decision is `task-consent/decision/0.2` signed (assertionMethod) by the **device transport key** (the holder), with no evidence. `pinProof = b64url(HMAC-SHA256(K, "org.openvtc.uv-pin/v1|" + D))`.
  - Replacing a vtaPin key: `org.openvtc.uv-key-change` `{pinProof: HMAC(K_old, "org.openvtc.uv-pin/v1|change|" + sha256hex(JCS(newEnrolment)))}`.
  - Local storage: only `pnm/uv-pin/v1/<vtaDid>` = `{salt, iterations}`. The PIN and K are never stored, and K's bytes are wiped after each use.
- **remoteApprover**
  - Enrolment: `{kind:"remoteApprover", approver, ...}`.
  - Approval: `uv-consent {remote:true}`. The window polls by re-sending the same grant every 2 s while the VTA answers `oobUvPending`.
  - Approver listing: `https://trusttasks.org/openvtc/device/uv-approvers/0.1` (`TASK_DEVICE_UV_APPROVERS` in `core/src/vault/sign-oob.ts`). It must match the URI the VTA serves; this is the one place it is named.
- **Refusals**
  - `oobUvPinWrong` (attemptsRemaining), `oobUvLocked` (lockedUntil), `oobUvPending` (matchCode, expiresAt), `oobUvDeclined`, `oobUvExpired`, read by `vaultOobRefusalDetail`.
  - Heartbeat `uvPinWrong` / `uvKeyLocked` (code's last segment), read by `deviceUvRefusal`.
- `pnm/uv-key/enrolled/<vtaDid>` now records `kind`, plus `approver` for the phone.

## Screens
- **Review**: says "Approving asks for your passkey / your PIN / your phone." With nothing set up, it also has a link: **Use a PIN or my phone instead**.
- **Approve**:
  - Opens the chooser instead of making a passkey when `browserOffersPrf() === false`.
  - Also opens it when the passkey fails for lack of PRF (new typed `PrfUnavailableError`, or `PrfUnlockError("no-prf-output")`).
- **Chooser**: "How should this browser approve sign-ins?" offers **Set a PIN** or **Approve on my phone**.
- **Set a PIN**: 6+ characters, entered twice, then sent once with `setPin`.
- **Approve on my phone (picker)**:
  - Lists the phones the agent returns.
  - With none, it says to open the OpenVTC app on the phone and connect it to the same agent.
- **Enter your PIN**: password field. After a wrong PIN it shows "Wrong PIN. N tries left before it locks."; when locked, "Locked until <time>" with the input disabled.
- **Approve on your phone**: shows the match code and asks again every 2 s.
  - Cancel stops asking and goes back to the review.
  - If the decision deadline passes, it cancels the flow and says so.
- **Settings → Advanced → Sign-in approval**: one row per agent showing its method.
  - Change PIN (current PIN + new PIN twice).
  - Switch to phone approval / Switch to PIN. Moving away from a PIN needs the current PIN.

## Boundaries
- `RUNTIME_UV_SETTINGS` / `OFFSCREEN_UV_SETTINGS` are not page-facing. The background checks `isExtensionPageSender` and the offscreen checks `isExtensionContextSender`.
- `OFFSCREEN_SIGN_IN_STEP` now has the offscreen sender check too, since a PIN can travel in a step.
- A test pins all of this.

## Tests
- core `npm test`: 1064 pass. New `tests/vault.uv-pin.mjs` covers:
  - the PBKDF2 vector against `crypto.pbkdf2Sync`, including NFC;
  - the proof strings and the JCS change proof;
  - enrolment shapes and consent variants;
  - refusal details;
  - the approver listing and the params store.
- extension `npm test`: 1284 pass. New tests:
  - `sign-in-flows.test.mts`: vtaPin wrong → locked → success; first-time setPin; enrol failure; remoteApprover pending → poll → signed, declined, expired, cancel stops further signing; approver listing.
  - `sign-in-uv.test.mts`: the offscreen module (enrolment, change proofs, kept state, sender gates).
  - `sign-in-uv.render.test.mts`: the window screens, including the chooser when `browserOffersPrf()` is false.
  - `sign-in-approval-settings.render.test.mts`: the settings section.
- `npx tsc -b` clean; `npm run build` clean (the approver task URI is only in the offscreen chunk).

## Open points on the contract
- A cleared browser loses `{salt, iterations}`. The VTA's uv-key summary returns them, but this PR doesn't read them back yet. Without them the PIN can't be used or changed, so the wallet says to have the device disabled and connect again.
- `oobUvLocked.lockedUntil` and `oobUvPending.expiresAt` are read as epoch seconds and shown as local times.

title: feat(rooms): rooms/keys/read repairs before refusing (catch up on commits, fetch links), cannotOpen gives a reason
body:
## Why

Found live on a three-member attributed room: every membership change leaves every *other* member a commit behind, and every new member starts at the epoch they joined. Both read as \"Did not open\" in the member portal, and the member — whose surface reaches only their own agent — has no move of their own. Today `rooms/keys/read/0.1` names only `backfill` as a repair, says nothing about a member who is *behind*, and declares `sideEffects: none`.

## What changes (draft spec, no version bump — SPEC §5.2)

- **Repair before refusing.** Before `cannotOpen`, the recipient SHOULD fetch from the same host, as the same principal under the same `read` grant: the relayed commits (`rooms/epoch/commits`) when the record is newer than any epoch it holds, applied under `rooms/keys/commit`'s rules; the epoch links (as `rooms/keys/backfill`) when the record is older than its chain reaches. At most once per request, never another epoch's key, SHOULD serialise per member, MUST NOT for a removed principal.
- **`cannotOpen` says why**: `details.epoch` plus `details.reason` (`notDelivered` / `beyondChain` / `removed`) with `heldEpoch` / `earliestEpoch` / `removedAtEpoch`, exactly `rooms/keys/open` 0.2's words. Consumers act on the reason.
- **`sideEffects: mutating`**: the room is unchanged; the recipient's own key state can now advance. Class unchanged (it was already consequential via `discloses: secret` / `actsAsSubject`).

Bindings regenerated (Rust doc text only); `npm run check-bindings` passes.

Implementation: verifiable-trust-infrastructure (VTA `rooms/keys/read` handler).

title: feat(rooms): rooms/keys/read repairs before refusing — catches up on commits and fetches links, then cannotOpen with a reason (#848)
body:
feat(rooms): rooms/keys/read repairs before refusing — catches up on commits and fetches links, then cannotOpen with a reason (#848)

A key holder misses an epoch key in two ordinary ways — behind by a commit after any
membership change, or joined late and holding nothing older — and the member's surface
reaches only their agent, so the agent is the one party that can repair either.

The recipient now SHOULD, before answering cannotOpen, fetch the commits the host relays
(rooms/epoch/commits) and apply them in order, or fetch the epoch links as backfill does,
from the same host, as the same principal, under the same read grant; at most once per
request, serialised per member, never for a removed principal. cannotOpen carries
details.reason (notDelivered / beyondChain / removed) in rooms/keys/open 0.2's words.
sideEffects becomes mutating: the room is unchanged, the recipient's key state is not.

title: feat(vtc): a group's room bindings — vtc/groups/bindings/{add,remove,list}/0.1 — and renewals members collect from vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3
body:
A group can now be bound to a room the community owns (trust-tasks-tf #843).
Every member of the group is offered admission to it, keeps it while they stay
in the group, and loses it when they leave, unless something else still covers
them.

- bindings/add, remove, list: a manager of the group who also holds
  `vtc.rooms.manage`, after the gesture bound to the document that
  `vtc/rooms/community/members/add` takes. Room bindings are not parked:
  community room changes never are. A grants or role binding is refused
  `kindNotServed` (item 7) and nothing is stored. Codes witnessed: notFound,
  roomNotFound, bindingExists, tooManyBindings (64), kindNotServed;
  bindingNotFound; list's notFound, answered alike for a group that does not
  exist and one the caller may not manage.
- `groups::bindings` is the reconciler, the one owner of every effect. It runs
  each minute and whenever a group's members or bindings change.
  - Offers: it offers each active group member admission through the normal
    offer path, and records the offer only after the community's VTA issued its
    credentials.
  - Sources: it keeps `MemberRecord::sources`, the bindings (`gb_…`) that cover
    an admission, plus `direct` where an administrator admitted the member.
  - Removals: it drops a source when the member leaves the group or the binding
    goes. An admission with no source left is owed a removal
    (`DepartureCause::LeftGroup`), driven by the departures worker exactly like a
    departure from the community. A direct admission is never removed this way.
  - Renewals: within a third of `validFor` of expiry, it renews an admitted
    member's membership and authority, the same actions and never an
    invitation. The renewed `validUntil` becomes the admission's own.
  - Ending a binding: a binding being removed is deleted once nothing names it.
    Deleting a group puts its bindings into removal.
- vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3: 0.2's offers, and on the first page the `renewals`
  of the admissions the member holds, each listed until what it renews expires.
  A removal drops the pending renewal.

The error-code census ceiling rises from 15 to 19. bindings/add declares four
codes only a grants or role binding can reach: groupNotEligible,
unknownCapability, unknownRole and exceedsBinderAuthority. They are baselined
until grants are provisioned from groups.



### Console
A group's page shows the community rooms its members are admitted to, each with
its actions and how often admissions renew. A manager who also holds
`vtc.rooms.manage` binds another room (actions, days per admission, a reason)
or ends a binding. Each takes their passkey or step-up approver, bound to the
request. Ending one that still covers members shows that they are being removed.



**Needs your call:** the error-code census ceiling goes 15 → 19 (the four codes above). Room bindings take the bound gesture but are not parked for consent; the spec says a `curate` binding SHOULD be held, and this follows community rooms, whose changes never park.

Rebased onto `main` after #2226 merged. Locally, on 0.32.6, the whole stack passed the CI-equivalent run.

title: feat(vta): rooms/keys/act/0.6 — completes vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3, so a member collects the renewals of the rooms they hold
body:
`vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3` (trust-tasks-tf #843) also returns the renewals of
the admissions a member holds: fresh membership and authority credentials the
community issues before the ones held expire. Its request is signed as the DID
the community addresses its offers to, which the member's VTA holds. 0.5's
table is closed, so a 0.5 key holder refuses it with `typeNotActable`.

- VTA: serves `rooms/keys/act/0.6`, which is 0.5 with `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3`
  in the offer row on the same terms: no presentation inserted, `issuer`
  required and never picked, resolved without a room credential (recipient item
  2b). 0.5 and below still refuse the 0.3 listing. The member is the audit row's
  subject, as at 0.2 – 0.5.
- SDK: `TASK_ROOMS_KEYS_ACT_0_6` is classified retry-safe (a listing).
  `room_act_community` asks 0.6 first and falls back version by version, never
  below 0.6 for a 0.3 listing. 0.6's request and response schemas are 0.5's, so
  its signature keeps 0.5's generated types. `is_offer_type` /
  `is_community_type` include `vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3`.
- Docs: the act versions in data-rooms, community-rooms and the files design
  note.



Also raises `trust-tasks-rs` to 0.32.6, which carries vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3 and rooms/keys/act/0.6 (trust-tasks-tf #843).

title: feat(voting): sealed and tallied-encrypted elections — trustees, encrypted casts, VTA trustee role
body:
The encrypted secrecy levels (VTI-VOT-060 – 064). CONVENTIONS §9 fixes the
cryptography: Ristretto255, exponential ElGamal under a threshold key, and
Fiat–Shamir Schnorr, Chaum–Pedersen and disjunctive proofs with their domains.

The trustees generate the election key on the board (Pedersen DKG with
Belenios-style complaints): enrol a transport key, deal (Feldman commitments
plus every share sealed to its recipient), confirm or complain, and a dealer
complained of justifies by revealing the share. The key forms from the
qualified dealers. After close, each trustee publishes partial decryptions of
every sealed cast's KEM, or of every option's homomorphic total, with
Chaum–Pedersen proofs; voting/trustees/status tells everyone what is left.

voting/ballot/cast-encrypted admits a cast whose attestation binds the sealed
payload or the encrypted ballot, the latter with 0/1 proofs per option and a
proof that each question's count is admissible.

vta/pcs/trustee/{enrol,deal,keys,justify,decrypt} make the trustee's VTA the
custodian of its transport key and key share, signing only the task's own
document as the trustee; vta/pcs/vote-encrypted is vta/pcs/vote for the
encrypted levels. The new capability pcsTrustee / pcs-trustee is appended to
both device/_shared Capability enums.

Additive: cargo semver-checks against 0.32.5 reports no semver update required.

title: fix(wallet): accept a security key whose PRF output comes only on an assertion
body:
## Problem
On Linux Chromium there is no platform authenticator, so the wallet's passkey is usually made on a USB security key. Encrypting the wallet, or the first approval, failed with "authenticator does not support the PRF extension". This happened on keys that do support PRF: it was reported with a YubiKey 5 (firmware 5.7+, PIN set, Chrome reporting PRF available).

## Cause
`enrollOrLoadCredential` passes `prf: { eval: { first: salt } }` to `create()` and requires `prf.results.first` in the response.
- Platform passkeys (iCloud Keychain, Windows Hello) evaluate the salt at registration.
- Security keys without CTAP 2.2 `hmac-secret-mc` (YubiKey 5, Nitrokey 3) can only evaluate it on an assertion. The browser returns `prf.enabled: true` with no `results`.
- The wallet treated that as unsupported, threw, and left the new credential orphaned on the key. That's why the same steps worked on macOS.

## Fix
- New `registrationPrf()` sorts a registration result into three cases: output present, enabled but needs an assertion, or unsupported.
- **Needs an assertion:** one `get()` for the same credential and salt (a second touch and PIN). The credential and salt are stored only after that output is in hand.
- **Unsupported** (`enabled` absent or false): refused before anything is stored, with a message that says what to use instead.
- **Browser check:** `browserOffersPrf()` reads `getClientCapabilities()["extension:prf"]` (Chrome 133+).
  - If the browser says no, the wallet stops before making the passkey with "this browser doesn't offer PRF". An assertion that comes back without output gets the same message when the browser is the cause.
  - A browser that can't answer is allowed to try, as before.
- When a later assertion has no output, the message says to use the same key or phone with its PIN, or that a reset key no longer holds the passkey. It used to say "authenticator may have rotated keys".
- Credential ids are passed to `allowCredentials` as the decoded bytes, not as `.buffer`. On a view, `.buffer` is the whole backing store, which would be a different id.
- The README explains that a PIN is needed and the first setup takes two touches. It also says why a password-manager extension such as 1Password can't answer the wallet's prompt.

Existing users: a credential made by the old code was never stored, because the wallet threw first. So there is nothing to migrate. Users may want to delete the orphan "OpenVTC Wallet" passkey(s) from their key (`ykman fido credentials list` / `delete`).

## Tests
- `tests/webauthn-prf-registration.test.mts` covers the registration cases and the browser check.
- Extension suite: 1251 pass.
- Not tried on a physical security key. Please check it on Linux with a YubiKey or NK3 that has a PIN set.

* fix(wallet): accept a security key whose PRF output comes only on an assertion

Making the wallet's passkey asked the authenticator to evaluate the PRF salt
during create(). iCloud Keychain and Windows Hello do; a security key without
CTAP 2.2 hmac-secret-mc (YubiKey 5, Nitrokey 3) cannot, and the browser
reports prf.enabled: true with no results. The wallet read that as
"authenticator does not support the PRF extension" and gave up, so on Linux,
where a security key is the usual authenticator, encrypting the wallet and
the first approval failed, leaving an orphan credential on the key.

Now enabled-without-output runs one get() for the same credential (a second
touch) before anything is stored; only enabled absent or false is refused,
with a message that says what to use instead. A missing output on a later
assertion says to use the same key with its PIN, rather than suggesting the
keys rotated.

Before making the wallet's passkey, ask the browser (getClientCapabilities,
Chrome 133+) whether it offers PRF, and refuse with a browser message if it
says no rather than minting a credential that can never hold the wrap. An
assertion with no PRF output gives the same browser message when that is the

answer is let through, as before.

title: fix(sign-in): read the portal's number from the shadow root the code is in
body:
## Problem
On the VTC portals (member portal and operator console), clicking the sign-in code opened the wallet, but the wallet still asked for the number. On DID Hosting it filled in by itself.

## Cause
The VTC portals render the sign-in box inside an open shadow root (the `data-protected` wrapper). The click handler finds the anchor via `event.composedPath()`, which crosses shadow boundaries, so the click is routed. The C11 number watcher, however, used `document.querySelectorAll("[data-oob-match-number]")` and a `MutationObserver` on `document.documentElement`, and neither reaches into a shadow root. So the number was never read, the 6 s wait ran out, and the number screen appeared. DID Hosting renders in the light DOM.

## Fix
At the click, the shadow roots on the event's path are collected while the event is still dispatching. The watcher queries and observes each of them as well as the document. Nothing else changes: the scope is still that request id only, on that page, after that click.

## Verified
- New test: a portal whose code and number are inside an open shadow root. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.
- Extension suite: 1246 pass.
- Live: the patched watcher was injected into the real https://test-vtc.openvtc.net/members/ and /admin/ pages in headless Chrome. A trusted click on the code, then a claim from a script, and the watcher reported the number the page showed (`16` and `83`). The unpatched watcher reported nothing on the same page.

fix(sign-in): read the portal's number from the shadow root the code is in (#365)

The VTC member portal and operator console draw their sign-in box inside an
open shadow root. The click on the code still reached the wallet (an event's
composed path crosses the root), but the C11 watcher looked for the number
with document.querySelectorAll and a document MutationObserver, neither of
which sees into a shadow root, so the person was asked to type it. DID
Hosting renders in the light DOM, which is why it worked there.

The watcher now also queries and observes every open shadow root on the
click's path, read while the click is dispatched. Verified against the live
test-vtc member portal and operator console in Chrome.

title: Read the portal's number from an open shadow root around the code (VTI-LNK-107)
body:
VTI-LNK-107 lets a same-device reader read the number from "the element of that page". The VTC portals draw their sign-in box inside an open shadow root, and a reader that searched only the document missed it (vta-browser-plugin#365). This adds one clarifying sentence:
- an element inside an open shadow root that contains the activated link counts as part of that page;
- a closed shadow root hides the number from the reader, and the person enters it.

No change to what the reader may do, or to when it must ask.
