What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.32.6
body:
### Added

- **vtc/rooms/offers**: List 0.3 — renewals of the admissions a member holds; rooms/keys/act 0.6 completes it; groups bindings refuse an unserved kind ([#843](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/843))

A group's room binding says the community renews each admission it made "while
  the member stays in the group". Nothing defined how an already-admitted member
  receives renewed credentials. `offers/list` carries only an offer's three
  credentials, and `memberships/list` carries none by design. So an admission
  could only be carried past its `validUntil` by an administrator removing and
  re-admitting the member.

  - vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3: the response gains `renewals`. For an admission the
    caller holds, it lists the room's fresh membership and authority credentials,
    granting the same actions until a later `validUntil`. `renews` names the
    expiry of the ones they replace. There is no invitation: a renewal is never a
    second way in.
    The community issues a renewal through the room's key holder before
    recording it, and lists only the latest one per admission. A renewal stays
    listed on the first page until what it renews expires, the member is removed,
    or a later renewal supersedes it. The community records the renewed
    `validUntil` as the admission's own.
    A surface stores a renewal in place of the credentials it renews, never
    beside them, and treats storing it twice as success. It never accepts a
    renewal.
  - vtc/_shared/0.1/community-room: `Renewal` and `RenewalCredentials`, additive.
  - rooms/keys/act/0.6: the table adds vtc/rooms/offers/list/0.3, in the offer
    types' row and on their terms. 0.5's table is closed, so a 0.5 key holder
    refuses 0.3 with `typeNotActable`.
  - vtc/groups/bindings/add/0.1: item 6 renews a room binding's admissions
    through offers/list 0.3. New code `kindNotServed` (item 7): a community that
    serves room bindings only may refuse a grants or role binding after item 1,
    and never records a binding it does not provision.
  - vtc/rooms/memberships/list/0.1: a row for an admitted room with a renewal
    listed, which the surface stores before anything else it offers.
  - RoomBindingSpec's description points at the renewal path.

title: feat(vtc): the console's live channel at 0.3 — directory and groups topics (vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.3)
body:
`vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.3` and `event/0.3` are served beside 0.1 and 0.2,
each stream answered at its own version. 0.3 adds two topics:

- `directory` is the member directory as administrators see it. It is hinted
  when a field, card, value, external card or administrators' note is written
  or removed, to holders of `vtc.directory.admin` or `vtc.directory.notes`.
  Hints are coalesced to one per ten seconds, so one member's edits do not read
  as a rhythm (subscribe 0.3 §Correlation).
- `groups` is hinted when a group, membership, join request or manager's
  appointment changes, to holders of `vtc.groups.manage`. It is fingerprinted
  per recipient over the groups they may manage (each group, its members,
  requests and managers), so a manager qualified to one group (`group:<id>`) is
  never hinted about another group (subscribe 0.3 §Authorization).
  Losing the last appointment ends the stream, as any shrink of readable topics
  does.

Neither hint names an entry, a group or a member. The bus is fed from the
directory's and groups' own storage writes; an ACL write also prompts `groups`.

The console subscribes at the newest version `trust-task-discovery` lists. Its
directory, member and groups pages re-read on their topic's hint.



Locally: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, the VTC suite (3471; the three census failures it first found are fixed, and their 47 tests re-run green), doctests, and the console suite (1287).

title: feat(sign-in): offer to call the community by its own name when it differs from the wallet's record
body:
## Why
On test-vtc the wallet's record is "TEST VTC". The community's signed name is "Test and Development VTC for next generation release". Every sign-in therefore flags the difference (VTI-LNK-104) and asks for the number by hand. The plugin had no way to rename a record: the Vault panel offers only Use, Reveal and Delete, and deleting makes the community look unjoined.

## What
The name-mismatch note on the number screen gets a button: **"Call it <their name> in my wallet"**.
- New step `adopt-name`:
  - renames the entry at the VTA with `vault/upsert` (its own id, `expectedVersion`, context, targets and kind; label only, no secret, so the VTA keeps its secret);
  - then carries on as if there had been no difference: proves with the page's number when it has arrived (C11), otherwise shows the number screen with no warning.
- If the VTA refuses the rename, the flow keeps its claim, the warning stays, and the reason shows. The person can still type the number or decline.

### Added

title: feat(vtc): renewing community groups' credentials before they lapse — each group's authority and its members' group credentials
body:
`vtc/groups/create` item 5 says the community MUST renew a group's authority
credential well before it lapses; a member's group credential, which has no
status list, is renewed while they stay. `groups::renewal` is that sweeper.
No new task: there is no "renew now".

- A group's authority is renewed within `[groups] authority_renew_within_days`
  (new; default 30, or `credential_valid_days` where longer, never more than
  half the authority's life). The VTA signs a fresh one as the community **in
  the slot of the community's revocation list the group already holds**, so
  deleting the group revokes every authority it was issued with one bit. The old
  one is not revoked: members present it until their own credential is renewed.
- Each active member's credential is renewed within a third of its life (ten
  days of 30), signed as the group and offered with the group's current
  authority, as an admission offers it. A member no longer active in the
  community is not renewed, and expiry is the revocation (VTI-CRD-014).
- Remote first: the group's new authority or the membership's new credential is
  written last, under the directory's write lock. It is dropped if the group or
  membership went, or changed, while the VTA was asked.
- The sweeper is the only retry owner. Each item gets one attempt per pass and a
  capped, jittered backoff (1 minute doubling to 6 hours), kept in `grenew:`
  schedules beside the group and removed with the group or the membership.
  Failures are logged at `warn` and audited when a run begins
  (`authorityRenewalFailed` / `credentialRenewalFailed`); renewals are audited
  by reference (`authorityRenewed` / `credentialRenewed`).



Rebased onto `main` after #2218 merged.

title: fix(vtc): sign-in has its own rate-limit budget, and the portal waits out a 429
body:
## Symptoms (seen live on test-vtc)
After a sign-in or two, or a couple of page reloads, within a minute:
- The sign-in page showed **"Show sign-in code"** instead of making the code: its config fetch got a `429`.
- The page showed a bare **"429"** with "Try again": its redeem poll was refused, so no number appeared, and the browser plugin fell back to asking the person to type it.
- The plugin's sign-in window said **"This code can't be used"**: the wallet's own claim was refused, or the page had already replaced the code.

## Cause
Every `auth/oob/*` document is signed by a throwaway `did:key`: the page's `K_b` for `request`, `redeem` and `cancel`, and the wallet's `K_a` for `claim`, `prove` and `respond`. So `routing::trust_task_admission` charged all of them to the anonymous per-address governor: a burst of 10, then one every 5 s. `GET /v1/member/sign-in/config` sat behind the same governor. A same-device sign-in sends about ten documents from one address, so it used up nearly the whole budget. Everyone behind one NAT shares that budget too.

## Fix
- **A sign-in budget, like rooms'.** The closed set of `auth/oob/*` types (`oob_tasks::URIS`) is charged to its own per-address ceiling, limiter `sign-in-address`: a burst of **60**, then **one a second**. It is charged before anything is verified and never touches the anonymous governor, so a join or recognise flood doesn't cost an address its sign-ins, and the reverse.
  - **Why that size:** one sign-in is about 10 documents (request, a redeem answer per state change, claim, prove, respond, sometimes cancel). The burst covers several people signing in at once behind one address, and the refill sustains several sign-ins a minute.
  - **Bound on abuse:** before refusing, a document costs one signature check over a key it carries (a `did:key` resolves locally), plus the member's identify for `prove`. A document whose proof never verifies costs **10** more. Once its burst is spent, a flood of forgeries is held to about one every 10 s.
  - The redeem long-poll keeps its own per-address cap on open polls (`PollGuard`).
  - The budget is constants, like the known-signer budgets; the room budgets are the configurable ones.
- **`GET /v1/member/sign-in/config` leaves the governor.** It returns public settings and a cached DID self-check, and is read on every load of the member portal's and the console's sign-in page.
- **The portal waits out a 429.** `send()` and `fetchSignInConfig()` turn a limiter's `429` into `OobError("rateLimited")` carrying its `Retry-After`.
  - A redeem poll waits that long (capped at 10 s) and polls again.
  - A code request retries up to 3 times.
  - The config is tried 3 times on load.
  - A refusal that persists is shown in words, "Too many sign-in attempts from this network. Try again in a moment.", with **Try again**. It's never a bare "429" or a silent button.
  - Other non-JSON refusals read "The community refused the sign-in (HTTP n)."

## Tests
- `trust_task_admission` unit tests (14 pass):
  - sign-in documents never spend the anonymous budget
  - the sign-in ceiling refuses past its burst, per address
  - an anonymous flood doesn't cost sign-ins
  - a document that never verifies costs extra
- New integration test `member_portal_oob::sign_in_from_one_address_is_not_held_to_the_anonymous_governor`: 25 config reads and 20 redeems from one address are all answered. It fails without the fix.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service`:
  - `--lib oob rate_limit trust_task_admission`: 41 pass
  - `--test it member_portal rate_limit trust_task_door governor`: 60 pass
  - `--test it join_requests room_rate_limits rate_limit_source relationships`: 172 pass
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- admin-ui: `npm run lint` clean; `npx vitest run` 1275 pass, also with `--sequence.shuffle`. New tests: a 429 on a poll is waited out and the number follows; a refused code request is retried; one that stays refused is shown in words; the config is retried on load; a config that stays unreadable shows the reason and Try again.
- Not run: the full workspace nextest.

title: feat(vtc): community groups in the console and the member portal
body:
The console's Groups page (Membership) lists every group the administrator may
see, and a holder of `vtc.groups.manage` creates one there: name, description,
how members join, who sees the group and who sees its members (never wider than
the group), and whether it issues credentials.

A group's page shows its identity and credential authority, and members by
their directory name and picture. Its managers also see its settings, member
add and remove, requests to join with their notes (approve and decline), and
managers (appoint, and end an appointment), and can delete the group with a
reason.

In the member portal, Groups (`#/groups`) lists the member's own groups and the
others they may see. A group's page joins an open group, asks to join one by
request with an optional note for its managers, or leaves, and lists its
members where the group shows them, each linking to their directory entry. The
portal signs as the member with the key delegated `vtc/groups` at sign-in.

title: fix(sign-in): wait out the community's 429 instead of ending the sign-in
body:
## Symptom
On test-vtc's operator console, a sign-in ended with "Sign-in stopped: This code can't be used". The page beside it showed "429".

## Cause
The VTC's per-address rate limiter refused the wallet's `auth/oob` document with HTTP 429. The wallet shares an address with the page that started the sign-in. That page's config, code request and polls draw on the same small anonymous budget (burst 10, then one per 5 s). The VTC side is being fixed separately: sign-in gets its own budget, and the portal waits out a 429.

## Fix
`postCommunityTask` (used by every `auth/oob` step and the join requests) retries a 429:
- waits `Retry-After` (2 s if absent, at most 10 s), up to 3 retries, then refuses as before with `http-429`;
- resends the same signed document. The limiter refuses before the document is read, so nothing was consumed.

## Tests
- core: 429 is waited out for the time Retry-After asks and the same document goes again; a long Retry-After is capped and a limiter that never relents is a refusal. Core suite: 1052 pass, 0 fail (2 not run).
- extension: 1239 pass.

title: feat(vtc): appointing group managers — vtc/groups/managers/{add,remove}/0.1, with a departed granter's appointments reviewed
body:
A group manager is `vtc.groups.manage` qualified `group:<groupId>`: a resource
grant on the manager's access-control entry, beside its role and never inside
the role's ceiling. So a member with no administrative role may manage a group
(trust-tasks-tf #833).

- managers/add: a manager of the group, or a holder of the unqualified
  capability, appoints an active member. The grant is delegated by the signer,
  who covers it by managing the group. It is written under the git-namespace
  write lock, which `acl/*` writes re-read resource grants under, so a racing
  role change keeps it. Codes: notFound, entryNotFound, alreadyManager (by a
  grant or by managing every group).
- managers/remove: a manager steps down, or a holder of the unqualified
  capability ends another manager's appointment. Managers of one group do not
  remove one another. Holding the capability unqualified is no appointment
  (`notManager`).
- A delegated grant (VTI-ACL-071): when a granter leaves the community or no
  longer manages the group, the directory's pass puts the appointment under
  review. It raises an `acl.grants.review` item listing it under
  `groupGrants`. Approving re-affirms it under the approver, and declining or
  letting the deadline (the action lifetime) pass withdraws it. A granter back
  behind it clears the review.
- Deleting a group withdraws every appointment to it.

  `groupGrants`. Approving re-affirms it under the approver, and declining or
  letting the deadline (the action lifetime) pass withdraws it. A granter back
  behind it clears the review.
- Deleting a group withdraws every appointment to it.

title: fix(sign-in): a record labelled with the portal host is not a name the community's can differ from
body:
## Problem
On test-vtc (members and admin portals), the wallet still asked for the number. DID Hosting filled it in.

The wallet labels a service it records with the portal host, e.g. `test-vtc.openvtc.net` (`profileLabelFor`). The VTC's signed step 1 names it by its community name. `communityNameMismatch` counted those as different names. A name mismatch always shows the number screen so the warning gets read (C11), so every VTC sign-in from such a record fell back to typing the number. DID Hosting reports its host as its name, which is already exempt, so it wasn't affected.

## Fix
A record whose label is the portal host holds no name of the person's, so there's nothing for the community's name to differ from. VTI-LNK-104 already treats the host as "not a name" on the community's side; this applies the same on the wallet's side. A name the person gave the record (or any other label) still gets flagged as before.

## Tests
- New rule test: host label → no mismatch (any case); a person's name or another host still differs.
- `npm test` (extension): 1239 pass.

Spec clarification of VTI-LNK-104 to match: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec (PR linked below).
author: stormer78

title: fix(sign-in): a record labelled with the portal host is not a name the community's can differ from (#362)
body:
fix(sign-in): a record labelled with the portal host is not a name the community's can differ from (#362)

The wallet labels a service it records with the portal host
(profileLabelFor). A VTC's signed step 1 names it by its community name, so
every VTC sign-in from such a record flagged a name mismatch, and the
mismatch makes the person type the number (C11). The host label is the
wallet's own, not the person's: VTI-LNK-104 already treats the host as no
name on the community's side, and now does on the wallet's.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: A record named only by the portal host holds no name to differ from (VTI-LNK-104)
body:
VTI-LNK-104 already says a signed name that is the host of the verified portal origin is not a different name. This applies the same on the reader's side: a record whose name is that host holds the label the reader made for itself, so no signed name differs from it.

Without this, a reader that labels a recorded service with its host (as the browser plugin does) flags every named community on every sign-in. That falls the same-device path back to typing the number (VTI-LNK-107), and teaches people to ignore the warning.

Implementation: OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#362.
author: stormer78

title: A record named only by the portal host holds no name to differ from (VTI-LNK-104) (#72)
body:
A record named only by the portal host holds no name to differ from (VTI-LNK-104) (#72)

A reader that labels a contact it records with the portal host has no name
of the person's to compare. Flagging every signed name against that label
warns on every sign-in to a named community, which teaches people to ignore
the warning that matters.

Updates `aws-lc-rs` from 1.18.1 to 1.18.2
Release notes

Sourced from aws-lc-rs's releases.

aws-lc-rs v1.18.2

What's Changed

  • Implement Eq and PartialEq for RSA and EdDSA parameters by @​dsykes16 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1228
    • RsaParameters can now be compared directly against RSA verification constants. Algorithms with different digests, padding schemes, or modulus-size ranges compare unequal. EdDSAParameters also gains equality support.
  • Add wasm32-wasip2 and wasm32-wasip3 support by @​ricochet in aws/aws-lc-rs#1239
    • Adds non-FIPS builds using universal bindings, with CI coverage under Wasmtime and wasi-sdk 34. WASIp3 requires nightly Rust.
    • Direct aws-lc-sys consumers must disable the default all-bindings feature for these targets.
  • Publish the intended RandomizedNonceKey::open_in_place documentation by @​Serophots in aws/aws-lc-rs#1227
    • Makes the existing nonce, ciphertext/tag layout, and buffer-on-error contract visible in rustdoc. No runtime behavior changes.

Upstream AWS-LC

  • aws-lc-sys v0.46.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.11.0 (previously v5.7.0). See also the release notes for v5.8.0, v5.9.0, and v5.10.0.
    • The Ed25519 C-implementation decoder now rejects non-canonical public keys, matching the assembly-optimized implementations: aws/aws-lc#3457
    • Includes ChaCha20-Poly1305 key-material zeroization and fixes ML-KEM CPU feature detection to avoid illegal-instruction failures on x86-64 CPUs with AVX2 but no BMI2: aws/aws-lc#3552 and aws/aws-lc#3596
  • aws-lc-fips-sys v0.14.3 updates its bundled AWS-LC FIPS 4.2.0 snapshot and regenerates bindings. It remains on the FIPS 4.x release line.

Build Improvements

  • Raise the minimum system AWS-LC version to 5.7.0 by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1243
    • Non-FIPS system-library installations must now provide AWS-LC 5.7.0 or newer, previously 1.68.0. Bundled-source builds and FIPS version requirements are unchanged.
  • Fix static FIPS system-library linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1236
    • Fixes unresolved FIPS_mode references with GNU ld.bfd when linking a prebuilt static FIPS library, including binaries that do not call crypto and builds where LTO removes those calls.
    • Uses whole-archive linking to retain libcrypto, including in downstream Rust staticlib outputs. This can increase binary size; dynamic FIPS and non-FIPS linking are unchanged.
  • Fix Cranelift linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1234
    • Normalizes binding link names to avoid undefined-symbol failures, including when Cranelift is selected through Cargo profiles rather than RUSTFLAGS. The AWS_LC_SYS_NO_U1_BINDINGS workaround is no longer needed.
  • Fix jitterentropy builds with optimizing CFLAGS and newer cc versions by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1254
    • Keeps filtered flags in effect throughout the jitterentropy builder's lifetime, preventing cached environment reads from allowing flags such as -O2 to override its required -O0.
  • Honor AWS_LC_SYS_CC in the main library build by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1255
    • Applies crate-specific compiler overrides before compiler lookup in both CC and CMake build paths, keeping compiler selection and capability probes consistent when cc caches environment reads.
  • Improve archive reproducibility through symlinked build paths by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1238
    • Prevents the non-Windows CC builder from incorporating symlink-resolved absolute build paths into archive member names, avoiding unnecessary downstream compile-cache misses. Windows short-path handling is unchanged.
  • Upgrade bindgen to 0.73 by @​xtqqczze in aws/aws-lc-rs#1244
  • Document the system-library trust model by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1218
    • Clarifies that supplied paths and pkg-config results are trusted build inputs, and that FIPS validation can execute candidate library code before accepting or rejecting it. Documents runner requirements and how to disable automatic system-library detection.

Issues Being Closed

  • Cranelift builds fail with codegen-backend = "cranelift" -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1231
  • Upgrade bindgen to v0.73 -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1245
  • Undefined FIPS_mode when linking a prebuilt FIPS module into a binary that does not use crypto -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1246
  • Jitterentropy fails with "must not be compiled with optimizations" in aws-lc-rs v1.18.1 / aws-lc-sys v0.45.0 -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1252

Other Merged PRs

  • Add security review workflow by @​nhatnghiho in aws/aws-lc-rs#1226
  • docs: align pull request template with AWS-LC by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1219
  • ci: verify docs.rs build with read-only crate sources by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1209
  • ci: harden workflows and release tooling by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1216

Release notes

Sourced from quick-xml's releases.

v0.42.0 - String Ergonomics

What's Changed

0.42.0 -- 2026-08-22

This is a large release. The primary change is an ergonomic improvement across the entire API - quick_xml now makes use of &str and String types where possible instead of &[u8] and Vec<u8>. The MSRV has been raised to 1.86. We now use Rust 2024 Edition.

  • #963: Name types (QName, LocalName, Prefix, Namespace, PrefixDeclaration) now wrap &str instead of &[u8]. into_inner() returns &str, and AsRef<str> is implemented (AsRef<[u8]> has been removed). ResolveResult::Unknown now contains String instead of Vec<u8>, and NamespaceError variants contain String instead of Vec<u8>.
  • #963: Removed the decoder: Decoder field from event types (BytesStart, BytesText, BytesCData, BytesRef) and Attributes. The decoder() method is no longer available on these types. Decode methods on events now always assume UTF-8 input. Error::missed_end() no longer takes a Decoder parameter.
  • #963: Event types (BytesStart, BytesEnd, BytesText, BytesCData, BytesPI, BytesRef) now store Cow<str> internally instead of Cow<[u8]>. into_inner() on BytesText, BytesCData, BytesPI, and BytesRef now returns Cow<str>. BytesStart::set_name() now takes &str instead of &[u8].

title: feat(vtc): community group membership — vtc/groups/members/{add,remove,list}, join, leave, requests/{list,decide}, and each member's group credential
body:
Membership for static groups (design §9), built on the group lifecycle.

- members/add and members/remove are for the group's managers; members/list
  is for whoever the group shows its members to.
- join and leave are for an active member, for themselves: `open` joins where
  the `groups` policy allows, and `request` records a request. requests/list
  and requests/decide are for managers, and nobody decides their own request.
  An approval re-checks that the requester is still an active member and the
  group still takes requests.
- Where the group issues credentials, admitting a member first has the
  community's VTA sign, as the group's DID through `keys/sign-document`, a DTG
  `MembershipCredential` to the member's membership DID. It is offered with
  the group's authority credential on the credential-exchange path, and only
  then is the membership recorded. A VTA that does not answer or refuses
  records nothing. There is no status list per group (VTI-CRD-014): expiry is
  the revocation.
- members/list projects each member's fields exactly as
  `vtc/directory/entries/show` does for the caller. Pending members go only to
  managers, and `credentialValidUntil` only to the member and managers. A
  request's note goes to managers only, and a declined requester never sees
  the reason. Every list cursor is bound to its caller and filters.
- The directory's `groups` audience now counts the groups both belong to
  whose member list the viewer may see, so a group hiding its members never
  reveals them through somebody's card. Groups now fill `Viewer.groups` and
  `Subject.groups`.
- Departure ends every membership and withdraws pending requests, before the
  card's own departure. Deleting a group withdraws its pending requests.
- The member portal's sign-in key may sign `vtc/groups` as the member
  (`signingScope`).
- New `GroupMembershipChanged` audit event, by reference only.

Four more declared codes are baselined until dynamic groups or authority
bindings exist, raising the error-code census ceiling from 11 to 15:
`members/add:dynamicGroup`, `members/add:exceedsRoleCeiling`,
`members/remove:dynamicGroup` and `leave:alreadyOptedOut`.



**Needs your call:** the census ceiling goes 11 → 15 here, as above.

Rebased onto `main` after #2215 merged.

Updates `aws-lc-rs` from 1.18.1 to 1.18.2
Release notes

Sourced from aws-lc-rs's releases.

aws-lc-rs v1.18.2

What's Changed

  • Implement Eq and PartialEq for RSA and EdDSA parameters by @​dsykes16 in aws/aws-lc-rs#1228
    • RsaParameters can now be compared directly against RSA verification constants. Algorithms with different digests, padding schemes, or modulus-size ranges compare unequal. EdDSAParameters also gains equality support.
  • Add wasm32-wasip2 and wasm32-wasip3 support by @​ricochet in aws/aws-lc-rs#1239
    • Adds non-FIPS builds using universal bindings, with CI coverage under Wasmtime and wasi-sdk 34. WASIp3 requires nightly Rust.
    • Direct aws-lc-sys consumers must disable the default all-bindings feature for these targets.
  • Publish the intended RandomizedNonceKey::open_in_place documentation by @​Serophots in aws/aws-lc-rs#1227
    • Makes the existing nonce, ciphertext/tag layout, and buffer-on-error contract visible in rustdoc. No runtime behavior changes.

Upstream AWS-LC

  • aws-lc-sys v0.46.0 aligns with AWS-LC v5.11.0 (previously v5.7.0). See also the release notes for v5.8.0, v5.9.0, and v5.10.0.
    • The Ed25519 C-implementation decoder now rejects non-canonical public keys, matching the assembly-optimized implementations: aws/aws-lc#3457
    • Includes ChaCha20-Poly1305 key-material zeroization and fixes ML-KEM CPU feature detection to avoid illegal-instruction failures on x86-64 CPUs with AVX2 but no BMI2: aws/aws-lc#3552 and aws/aws-lc#3596
  • aws-lc-fips-sys v0.14.3 updates its bundled AWS-LC FIPS 4.2.0 snapshot and regenerates bindings. It remains on the FIPS 4.x release line.

Build Improvements

  • Raise the minimum system AWS-LC version to 5.7.0 by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1243
    • Non-FIPS system-library installations must now provide AWS-LC 5.7.0 or newer, previously 1.68.0. Bundled-source builds and FIPS version requirements are unchanged.
  • Fix static FIPS system-library linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1236
    • Fixes unresolved FIPS_mode references with GNU ld.bfd when linking a prebuilt static FIPS library, including binaries that do not call crypto and builds where LTO removes those calls.
    • Uses whole-archive linking to retain libcrypto, including in downstream Rust staticlib outputs. This can increase binary size; dynamic FIPS and non-FIPS linking are unchanged.
  • Fix Cranelift linking by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1234
    • Normalizes binding link names to avoid undefined-symbol failures, including when Cranelift is selected through Cargo profiles rather than RUSTFLAGS. The AWS_LC_SYS_NO_U1_BINDINGS workaround is no longer needed.
  • Fix jitterentropy builds with optimizing CFLAGS and newer cc versions by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1254
    • Keeps filtered flags in effect throughout the jitterentropy builder's lifetime, preventing cached environment reads from allowing flags such as -O2 to override its required -O0.
  • Honor AWS_LC_SYS_CC in the main library build by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1255
    • Applies crate-specific compiler overrides before compiler lookup in both CC and CMake build paths, keeping compiler selection and capability probes consistent when cc caches environment reads.
  • Improve archive reproducibility through symlinked build paths by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1238
    • Prevents the non-Windows CC builder from incorporating symlink-resolved absolute build paths into archive member names, avoiding unnecessary downstream compile-cache misses. Windows short-path handling is unchanged.
  • Upgrade bindgen to 0.73 by @​xtqqczze in aws/aws-lc-rs#1244
  • Document the system-library trust model by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1218
    • Clarifies that supplied paths and pkg-config results are trusted build inputs, and that FIPS validation can execute candidate library code before accepting or rejecting it. Documents runner requirements and how to disable automatic system-library detection.

Issues Being Closed

  • Cranelift builds fail with codegen-backend = "cranelift" -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1231
  • Upgrade bindgen to v0.73 -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1245
  • Undefined FIPS_mode when linking a prebuilt FIPS module into a binary that does not use crypto -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1246
  • Jitterentropy fails with "must not be compiled with optimizations" in aws-lc-rs v1.18.1 / aws-lc-sys v0.45.0 -- aws/aws-lc-rs#1252

Other Merged PRs

  • docs: align pull request template with AWS-LC by @​justsmth in aws/aws-lc-rs#1219

title: chore: release 3 packages
body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.22` → `0.26.23` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.23`) | `0.8.22` → `0.8.23` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.22` → `0.8.23` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): community groups — vtc/groups/{create,update,delete,list,show}/0.1, each group with its own VTA-held identity
body:
The first part of the member directory's groups (design §9). Static groups
only, for now with no members.

- Create (unqualified `vtc.groups.manage`, then the `groups` policy) has the
  community's VTA mint the group a `did:webvh` from the `vtc-group` template.
  Where the group issues credentials, the VTA then signs, as the community
  through `keys/sign-document`, the community's DTG `AuthorityCredential` to
  the group (`issue-membership`). That credential has an expiry and a slot in
  the community's revocation list.
- The group is stored only after both exist, so the VTC holds no group key
  (`noKeyHolder`). A served DID log is published first and withdrawn if a later
  step fails. `keyHolderUnavailable` names a DID already minted, and
  `keyHolderRefused` carries the VTA's own code.
- A dynamic group's rule is checked against verified facts only (never a
  `member`-sourced field), then refused `kindNotServed` (trust-tasks-tf #833).
- Update and delete need `vtc.groups.manage` for the group, unqualified or as a
  resource grant `group:<groupId>`, read from the live ACL entry. Deleting
  revokes the group's authority in the community's list and ends its
  memberships.
- List and show follow `visibility` and `showMembers`. A group the caller may
  not see is `notFound`, exactly as one that does not exist. `memberCount` goes
  only where the member list is visible, and `managers` and
  `credentialAuthorityValidUntil` only to managers. The list cursor is bound to
  the caller and the filters.
- New `Capability::GroupsManage` and `ResourceQualifier::Group`.
- New `groups` policy purpose (`vtc.groups`, refuse-only, default allow).
- New `[groups]` config (context, webvh_server, authority and credential
  validity).
- Serves `/group-dids/<id>/did.jsonl`.
- New `GroupChanged` audit event, by reference only.
- Storage is the `directory` keyspace, membership keyed by `entryId`.

Two declared codes are baselined until bindings exist, raising the error-code
census ceiling from 9 to 11: `update:authorityGroupLocked` and
`delete:keyHolderUnavailable`.

Membership, members' group credentials, managers (`managers/*`), bindings and
the console and portal pages follow.



Also raises `trust-tasks-rs` to 0.32.3 (the lock resolves 0.32.4), which carries the `vtc/groups/*` specifications (trust-tasks-tf #831, #833).

**Needs your call:** the error-code census ceiling (`UNWITNESSED_CEILING`) goes 9 → 11 here. The two codes are only reachable once bindings exist, so they are baselined with that reason in place of tests.

First of four stacked PRs: lifecycle → membership → managers → console/portal pages.

title: feat(vtc-admin-ui): show the sign-in code unasked and hand its number to the plugin
body:
Part of streamlining wallet sign-in in the member portal and the operator console. Both use the shared `WalletSignIn`.

## What changed
- **No "Show sign-in code" click.** The code is made once `GET /v1/member/sign-in/config` says wallet sign-in can work and the tab is in view. If the config fetch fails, the old button comes back, and clicking it fetches again and reports the error.
- **Unclaimed codes renew themselves.** A code renews when its claim window closes, and only while the tab is in view. A background tab makes no requests: the code goes to `lapsed` and is renewed when the tab comes back. A code that ends within 10 s of being made shows as expired, so a skewed clock or a VTC dropping requests can't make the page loop. A *claimed* code that expires still shows "The code expired" (someone scanned it).
- **Number hand-off to the browser plugin (sign-in contract C11).** In the claimed phase, the number's element carries `data-oob-request-id` and `data-oob-match-number`. The page posts nothing and reads nothing back. For a code the person clicked on this page, the plugin's content script reads these attributes and fills the number into the wallet. Phone wallets still have the person type it.
- The waiting state's hint now reads "Scan it with your wallet app, or click it…", since the idle hint is no longer seen.
- Docs: `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md`.

## Why
A desktop sign-in took about 8 interactions. Together with the companion browser-plugin PR, it comes down to: click the code, Approve, Touch ID. The plugin PR fills the number in from C11 and skips the identity picker when there's only one identity. The plugin keeps checking that the clicked page's origin is the community's `SignInPortal`, which is what blocks relayed or emailed codes when the person doesn't type the number. The VTC still checks the signed number.

## Tests
- `npx vitest run`: 108 files, 1270 tests pass. New tests cover: the code shows unasked; renewal in view; no request while hidden, then renewal when visible; a tab opened in the background; the immediate-expiry guard; and the C11 attributes.
- `npm run lint` (wire check + `tsc -b --noEmit`): clean.

title: fix(auth/oob): a same-device reader may enter the number it reads from the starter's page
body:
The auth/oob prose says the match number is \"the digits the member typed\". Under the new **VTI-LNK-106**, a same-device reader may instead read the number from the page and enter it for the member. This applies only when the reader received the link from the member's click on the verified portal (VTI-LNK-056 activation, VTI-LNK-105 page-origin check). The VTI-LNK-106 rule is being added to `dtgwg-vti-spec` in a parallel PR.

**Prose only. No schema, wire, or error-code change.** `identify` still carries `enteredNumber`, and `prove` still compares it with the match number.

### Changes
- `identify/0.1`: the summary, item 1, the `enteredNumber` definition, and the Authorization sentence now say the number is *entered*: typed by the member, or read from the page by a same-device reader. Consent/purpose gains a security paragraph: on that path, a relayed code (T1) and an out-of-band code are already refused by the page-origin check before anything is sent. The number is still carried and checked; the member just doesn't retype it.
- `prove/0.1`, `prove/0.2`, `claim/0.1`, `request/0.1`: \"typed\" becomes \"entered\" in the matching sentences.

### Left unchanged
- The `numberMismatch` error meaning (\"The typed number does not match\") is copied into the generated Rust bindings.
- The `enteredNumber` schema description (\"The two digits the member typed…\") is copied into the generated TS bindings.

Changing either means regenerating the bindings. That can follow if wanted.

### Implementations
- OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#361 (the plugin reads the number from the page)
- OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2214 (VTC member portal and operator console publish it)
- affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#287 (DID Hosting UI publishes it)

`npm run validate`: 900 specs validated.

title: Let a same-device reader take the click on the portal as Continue, and read the number from that page (VTI-LNK-106, VTI-LNK-107)
body:
## What

Two rules in the `sign-in` flow of the links chapter (`spec/07a-links.md`), plus cross-references in VTI-LNK-052, -057, -104 and the note on the exchange:

- **VTI-LNK-106:** a reader that received the link from the person's own click on a page whose origin matched the portal (VTI-LNK-056, VTI-LNK-105), for a service already in its records, MAY treat that click as the person continuing.
  - Only when it holds exactly one identity for the service. Records naming the same identifier count once.
  - With more than one identity, the person still chooses.
  - The click counts as continuing for every rule that waits for it, including the route B domain-linkage fetch. It approves nothing the exchange asks afterwards.
- **VTI-LNK-107:** while the portal shows the number, it SHOULD mark that element with `data-oob-request-id` (the handle) and `data-oob-match-number`.
  - Such a reader MAY read the number from that page, for that handle only, and enter it for the person.
  - It must send nothing to the page.
  - It falls back to asking the person when it can't find the number, or when the service's signed name differs from the reader's records (VTI-LNK-104).

## Why

On the same device, sign-in was: click the code → pick identity → Continue → type the number → Continue → Approve → passkey. The number and the Continue tap guard against a code relayed from an attacker's browser, or one sent by email or chat. A reader that saw the click itself has already refused both under VTI-LNK-105. The review of where the request came from, and the user verification on Approve, are unchanged. The phone (QR) path is unchanged.

## Implementations

- OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#361 (reader)
- OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2214 (VTC member portal and operator console)
- affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#287 (DID hosting UI)

The matching prose change to `auth/oob/identify` ("the digits the member typed") is a separate PR on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf.

title: Specify community voting: unlinkable tickets, a ballot box apart from the community, and results anyone permitted can recompute (VTI-VOT-001 – 100)
body:
A new Part C chapter, `spec/12b-vtc-voting.md`, for a community that offers polls, surveys and elections. A member proves only that they may vote, never who they are, and anyone permitted to read the ballots can count them again.

## What it requires

- **Separation** (VOT-001 – 004). The registrar (the VTC) and the ballot box (a voting host service) are kept apart. The VTC never handles a ballot, the ballot box never learns an identity, and a cast is signed by a key made for that cast alone. Linking a voter to a ballot takes the two colluding.
- **Manifests** (VOT-010 – 014). The community registers the manifest, and every cast is bound to its digest, so a member shown other questions casts nothing that counts.
- **Tickets** (VOT-020 – 024). Tickets are class credentials of a predicate credential system, issued blind.
  - One class per election, one ticket per eligible party.
  - They are issued under a voting key used for nothing else.
  - The voter's key is fresh for each election.
- **Casting** (VOT-030 – 033). A cast binds the community, the election, the manifest and the ballot's bytes. Its tag is the per-election nullifier.
- **The ballot box and board** (VOT-040 – 053).
  - It admits casts on the registration alone and counts one ballot per tag under the manifest's revote rule.
  - It answers every cast with a signed receipt.
  - The board is an RFC 9162 log whose heads the community checkpoints, and it is public or private.
- **Secrecy levels** (VOT-060 – 065).
  - The three levels are open, sealed and tallied encrypted.
  - Trustee keys are generated jointly, and neither the VTC nor the ballot box ever holds one.
  - Text answers are released only above a turnout threshold.
- **Results and audit** (VOT-070 – 073). The VTC verifies the board itself before certifying, and the ballots counted never exceed the tickets issued. Auditors' findings are verifiable credentials.
- **Governance** (VOT-080 – 082). `vtc.elections.manage` governs elections. A binding election, and any change to the trusted ballot boxes, take consent.
- **Disclosure** (VOT-090). The statement includes that coercion resistance is not provided.
- **Audit events** (VOT-100). No record pairs a voter's identifier with a tag, a cast or a ballot.

## Where it is registered

`specs.json`, `intro.md` (structure and reading tables), `STRUCTURE.md` (chapter map and status), `95-conformance.md` (`Community` profile, `VOT` area), `appendix.md` C.3 (`vtc.elections.manage`) and `96-references.md` (RFC 9162, PCS, Belenios).

## Related

- Wire: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, branch `feat/voting`. That branch defines the `voting/*`, `vtc/elections/*` and `vta/pcs/voter/*` + `vta/pcs/vote` families, with shared conventions in `specs/voting/_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md`.
- Reference implementation of the cryptographic core: `vti-voting` in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure, branch `feat/community-voting`. It has 17 tests and a benchmark: at 300,000 voters, issuance runs at about 500 tickets/s per VTC, admission at about 330 casts/s per core, and a full recount takes about a minute on 18 threads.

## Open issues recorded in the chapter

- **Coercion resistance.** Not provided.
- **Ranked questions at the tallied-encrypted level.** These need a verifiable shuffle, which is not yet specified.

title: chore(deps): bump regress from 0.11.1 to 0.12.0
body:
Bumps [regress](https://github.com/ridiculousfish/regress) from 0.11.1 to 0.12.0.
Release notes

Sourced from regress's releases.

v0.12.0

Highlights

  • Restored support for no_std + alloc builds. Use: --no-default-features --features alloc.
  • Added Unicode Script=Unknown property support.
  • Improved correctness for ECMAScript Unicode Sets (v mode), inline modifier groups, and several Unicode case-insensitive matching cases.
  • Hardened parsing against excessively nested expressions, avoiding stack-overflow failures.
  • Reduced downstream binary size by avoiding forced inlining of regex construction and search internals.

Fixes

  • Correctly propagate flags from inline modifier groups.
  • Correct handling of nested and negated character sets in v mode.
  • Correct parsing of invalid \x escapes as identity escapes where ECMAScript permits it.
  • Correctly detect start-anchored alternations.
  • Include the v flag in Flags formatting.
  • Make Regex::find_from clearly panic when given an index that splits a UTF-8 code point.
  • Fix big-endian matching.
  • Avoid overly aggressive loop unrolling.

Performance and implementation

  • Improve PikeVM handling of one-character loops and reduce state allocation overhead.
  • Improve Unicode string-set lowering and longest-match ordering.
  • Improve case-folding/literal lowering internals.
  • Add a safety limit for deeply nested patterns.
  • Allow downstream users to share regex internals rather than duplicating them through inlining.

title: feat(sign-in): fill in the portal's number and skip the identity screen when there is one identity
body:
Streamlines same-device wallet sign-in: **click the code → Approve → passkey**. Before, the flow was click → pick identity → Continue → type number → Continue → Approve → passkey.

Implements sign-in contract **C11** (design-docs `sign-in-trigger-link-contract.md`). Pairs with:
- OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2214 (VTC member portal + operator console)
- affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#287 (DID Hosting UI)

### What changes
- **The number comes from the page.** After a click it routed, the content script watches that page for the element carrying `data-oob-request-id` equal to the link's `_id` and a two-digit `data-oob-match-number`. It sends the number once (`RUNTIME_TRIGGER_LINK_NUMBER`, page-facing and origin-attested). The background hands it to the flow whose link has that id and whose click came from the same origin, and the claim proves with it. The community still checks the number. The flow waits up to 6 s for it, then shows the number screen. A community name that differs from the wallet's record always shows the number screen, so the warning is read.
- **One identity, no picker.** Vault entries naming the same DID are offered once, since they sign identically. With one identity the window claims as it opens, showing "Signing in to <community>…" meanwhile. This also applies after joining a DID hosting service.
- **What stays:** the review screen (where the request came from) and the passkey on Approve. Both portals' "Continue as…?" screen is unchanged.
- The review result now carries `decisionDeadline`, so the countdown still shows when the number screen was skipped.

### Why it's safe
The number answers T1 (an attacker relays a real code from their own browser) and T2 (a code sent by email or chat). On this path both already fail the origin check (C3 step 4) before anything is sent. The page learns nothing: the content script only reads the DOM.

### Tests
- `npm test` (extension): 1238 pass
- `npm run build`: OK
- New tests:
  - flows: number arrives during the wait or before the claim; no number, so the person types it; malformed numbers ignored; a name mismatch still asks; duplicate entries merged
  - content-script watcher: sends once, only for the clicked request, and only after a click
  - view: one identity goes straight to the review, or to the number screen when the page doesn't publish it; joining a DID host claims at once

Not yet tested end to end against deployed portals.

title: fix(vta-sdk): collect a stranded TSP reply, keep the DIDComm mediator on REST, refuse an unresolvable VTA DID (OpenVTC #501)
body:
## Why

OpenVTC/openvtc#501. `openvtc setup`, and `vtc setup` on 2026-10-10 with a 164 KB reply, sent `provision/integration` over TSP. The VTA minted the long-term admin and replied, and the mediator stored the reply without pushing it. That was a notify-before-store race, affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#957, fixed in mediator 0.43.0. `TspSession::request` timed out and gave up. The reply stayed in the inbox for days, holding the only copy of the new admin's key, and the setup DID's one-time hand-off was already spent. The VTA was left with an admin entry nobody could use.

The same report found two smaller faults in the sdk's provisioning path.

## What

- **`TspSession::request` collects a stranded reply.** On a reply timeout it reconnects the socket once and gives the still-registered waiter `STRANDED_REPLY_GRACE` (10 s) more. Raw-TSP sockets are flush-on-connect, so a reply the mediator stored but never pushed is delivered by the reconnect. Nothing is resent, so this is safe for keyed tasks such as `provision/integration`. The new socket opens before the old one is closed, so a failed reconnect leaves the session as it was. The connect is bounded by the grace window (R1.2). The D4 self-repair and its breaker still see a reply timeout as before, only later.
- **REST `VtaEvent::Connected` carries the advertised DIDComm mediator.** `dispatch_rest_leg` used to send `mediator_did: None`, so a consumer saving an account over REST saved no mediator. OpenVTC's persona mint then refused with "your VTA did not advertise a DIDComm mediator". The field doc now says what it holds per transport.
- **`provision_client::resolve_vta` refuses a DID that does not resolve.** `resolve_vta_endpoint` guesses a REST URL from the DID on a resolution failure, which suits session connect. For setup, though, a typo surfaced much later as "unexpected challenge response … (is this a VTA?)" against the guessed host. The provisioning resolve now returns `resolve <did>: the DID does not resolve: …`. Session connect keeps the guess (`OnUnresolved::GuessFromDid`), and a document that resolves but advertises no service still falls back to its domain. Both other callers already handle `Err`: the `vtc setup` wizard, whose comment already said "bail-fast on a typo", and `vti-witness` correlation.
- **`vtc setup` can force the provisioning transport.** The interactive wizard asks when the VTA advertises more than one transport, and `--from` takes `provision_transport = "tsp" | "didcomm" | "rest"`. The value is passed as `force_transport`. Automatic still moves on only when a transport fails to connect: a reply lost after the VTA acted is final, so this is the way round a mediator known to drop replies. The value is not persisted. The example TOML and `non-interactive-setup.md` document it.

Not changed: the TSP leg multiplexed on a DIDComm session (`DIDCommSession::await_tsp_reply`) rides the DIDComm socket's own delivery and is left as it is.

## Testing

- New e2e `tsp_stranded_reply` (embedded `TestMediator`): a reply landing after the first deadline is collected across the reconnect (an error before this change), and a request nobody answers still times out after the grace, bounded.
- New unit tests: an unresolvable DID is refused, not guessed (`seeded_discovery_tests`); `provision_transport` parses from the file and an unknown value is an error; the provisioning transports offered are the advertised ones, in order.
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-e2e-tests` on the `tsp_stranded_reply`, `tsp_ping_correlation`, `tsp_round_trip` and `tsp_vta_trust_task` binaries: 47 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-sdk --all-features -E 'test(/resolve|provision_client|tsp|session/)'`: 259 passed, including the existing `resolve_vta_endpoint_falls_back_to_rest_for_did_web`.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -E 'test(/setup|from_toml|provision/)'`: 57 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk -p vtc-service -p vti-e2e-tests -p vti-witness --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --all`: clean.
- Not run: the full workspace nextest, or a live setup against a deployed mediator.

The companion OpenVTC change (transport choice, keeping the mediator on REST, classing a lost reply) is OpenVTC/openvtc#502. It does not depend on this PR.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). The reconnect is bounded by `STRANDED_REPLY_GRACE`.
- [ ] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). **Deviation, flagged:** `reconnect` holds the session's own socket lock across the connect, as `pump_once` already holds it across a read. Releasing it would be worse: the mediator closes the old socket when the new one connects, and a request pumping the old one would fail with "closed by the mediator". Every other waiter stays bounded by its own deadline, because `await_reply` selects on it beside the lock.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). Nothing is persisted.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). The recovery reconnects once and resends nothing.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). No new loops.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). Plain `connect_websocket` is delete-on-send, unchanged.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). No wire change. `provision_transport` is a setup-TOML key under the existing `deny_unknown_fields`.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). Omitted means automatic, the existing behaviour.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). An unresolvable DID is now named as one.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). No mutation.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. R1.3, above.

`TspSession::request` gave up on a reply timeout even when the mediator
had stored the reply and not pushed it (affinidi-tdk-rs#957). For
`provision/integration` that reply held the only copy of a freshly
minted admin key. It now reconnects once — raw-TSP sockets are
flush-on-connect — and gives the still-registered waiter
`STRANDED_REPLY_GRACE` more. Nothing is resent.

The REST leg's `VtaEvent::Connected` now carries the advertised
`#DIDCommMessaging` mediator instead of `None`, so a consumer saving an
account over REST keeps the mediator its personas publish.

`provision_client::resolve_vta` refuses a DID that does not resolve
instead of guessing a REST URL from it; session connect keeps the guess.

`vtc setup` can force the provisioning transport: the wizard asks when
the VTA advertises more than one, and `--from` takes
